[Open English Translation, Readers' Version] [2025] [engOETrv]
[Genesis] [1]:[1] In the beginning, God created the heavens and the earth.
[Genesis] [1]:[2] The earth was formless and empty and darkness covered the surface of the deep waters and God’s spirit was hovering over the waters’ surface.
[Genesis] [1]:[3] Then God said, “Let there be light,” and light came into existence,
[Genesis] [1]:[4] and God observed that the light was good. Then he separated the light from the darkness.
[Genesis] [1]:[5] God named the light daytime, and the darkness he named nighttime. Then evening came, and later morning came, and that was the end of the first day.
[Genesis] [1]:[6] Then God said, “Let there be a large space in the middle of the waters, and let it separate the two lots of waters.”
[Genesis] [1]:[7] So God made the large space and separated between the waters that were underneath from the waters that were above it. Everything happened exactly as he commanded,
[Genesis] [1]:[8] and he named the space sky. Then evening came, and later morning came, and that was the end of the second day.
[Genesis] [1]:[9] Then God said, “Let the waters under the sky be gathered to one place, and let the dry ground appear.” Everything happened exactly as he commanded,
[Genesis] [1]:[10] and he named the ground that appeared land, and he named the gathered waters seas, and he saw that what he had done was good.
[Genesis] [1]:[11] Then God said, “Let the land sprout vegetation: every plant yielding seed, every fruit tree bearing its own fruit that has its seed inside it, on the earth.” Everything happened exactly as he commanded,
[Genesis] [1]:[12] so the land started producing vegetation, every plant producing its own seed, and every tree bearing fruit that has its seed inside it. And God saw that what he had done was good.
[Genesis] [1]:[13] Then evening came, and later morning came, and that was the end of the third day.
[Genesis] [1]:[14] Then God said, “Let there be lights in the sky to separate daytime from nighttime, so they’ll be signs, and for indicating seasons, and for tracking days and years.
[Genesis] [1]:[15] They must function as lights in the sky that shine light on the earth.” Everything happened exactly as he commanded,
[Genesis] [1]:[16] so God made the two large lights, the larger, brighter light to rule the day, and the smaller light to rule the night, and he also made the stars.
[Genesis] [1]:[17] He put those lights in the sky to shine light on the earth,
[Genesis] [1]:[18] and to oversee the daytime and the nighttime, and to distinguish between the light and the darkness. And God saw that what he had done was good.
[Genesis] [1]:[19] Then evening came, and later morning came, and that was the end of the fourth day.
[Genesis] [1]:[20] Then God said, “Let the waters be full of with swarms of living creatures, and let birds fly in the sky above the earth.”
[Genesis] [1]:[21] So God created the great sea creatures and every kind of living creature that moves which the waters swarm with, and every kind of winged bird. And God saw that what he had done was good,
[Genesis] [1]:[22] and he blessed them, saying, “Be fruitful and multiply and fill the waters in the seas, and let the birds multiply on the earth.”
[Genesis] [1]:[23] Then evening came, and later morning came, and that was the end of the fifth day.
[Genesis] [1]:[24] Then God said, “Let the land bring forth every kind of living creature: livestock and every crawling creature and every kind of living thing on the earth.” Everything happened exactly as he commanded,
[Genesis] [1]:[25] so he made every kind of creature of the earth, and every kind of livestock, and every kind of crawling creature on the ground. And God saw that what he had done was good.
[Genesis] [1]:[26] Then God said, “Let us make man in our image, according to our likeness, and let them rule over the fish in the sea and over the birds in the sky and over the livestock and over all the earth, and over every creature moving on the earth.”
[Genesis] [1]:[27] Then God created humankind in his image, yes, created in the image of God—male and female he created them.
[Genesis] [1]:[28] Then God blessed them and told them, “Be fruitful and multiply, and fill the earth and take control of it. You’re in charge of the fish in the sea and the birds in the sky and over every living thing that moves on the earth.”
[Genesis] [1]:[29] Then God said, “Look, I’ve given you every plant throughout the whole earth that yields seed, and every tree that has fruit with a seed or seeds inside it. They will be yours for food,
[Genesis] [1]:[30] and to every living thing on the earth, and to every bird in the sky, and to everything moving on the earth that has living breath in it, I’ve given every green plant for food.” Everything happened exactly as he commanded,
[Genesis] [1]:[31] and he saw everything that he’d made, and wow, it was very good. Then evening came, and later morning came, and that was the end of the sixth day.
[Genesis] [2]:[1] So the heavens and the earth were completed, along with everything in them.
[Genesis] [2]:[2] By the seventh day God had finished his work, so he rested on the seventh day from all his work that he’d done.
[Genesis] [2]:[3] Then God blessed the seventh day and declared it to be different from the other days, because on that first Saturday, he rested from all his work of creating.
[Genesis] [2]:[4] What follows tells more details about the history of what God did when he created the heavens and the earth: During the time when Yahweh God made the earth and the heavens,
[Genesis] [2]:[5] there weren’t yet any bushes growing on the earth, and no plants had yet sprung up in the countryside, because Yahweh God had not yet made it rain, and nor were there any people yet to till the ground.
[Genesis] [2]:[6] However, a mist came up from the ground and watered the entire surface of the land.
[Genesis] [2]:[7] Then Yahweh God formed the first man out of the dust on the ground and he breathed into his nostrils the breath of life, and the man became a living person.
[Genesis] [2]:[8] Now in the east, Yahweh God had planted a garden in Eden, and he put the man there that he had formed.
[Genesis] [2]:[9] He also caused all kinds of trees to grow there—some that are pleasant to look at and good for food. In the middle of the garden was the tree of life and the tree of the knowledge of good and evil
[Genesis] [2]:[10] A river flowed out of Eden to water the garden, and then from there it split into four rivers.
[Genesis] [2]:[11] The first river was named Pishon, and it winds around through the entire region of Havilah, where there’s gold.
[Genesis] [2]:[12] The gold from there is very pure, and there’s also a type of fragrant resin and onyx gemstones there.
[Genesis] [2]:[13] The second river was named Gihon, and it winds through the entire region of Kush (Ethiopia).
[Genesis] [2]:[14] The third river was named Hidekel, and it flowed east of the Ashur (Assyria) region, and then the fourth river was named Perat (Euphrates).
[Genesis] [2]:[15] Yahweh God took the man and put him in the garden at Eden to cultivate and maintain it
[Genesis] [2]:[16] and instructed him, “You can eat as much fruit as you want from any tree in the garden,
[Genesis] [2]:[17] but you mustn’t eat from the tree of the knowledge of good and evil, because the day you eat its fruit you’ll certainly die.”
[Genesis] [2]:[18] Then Yahweh God said, “It’s not good for the man to be alone, so I’ll make a suitable helper for him.”
[Genesis] [2]:[19] Now Yahweh God had formed every living thing of the countryside and every bird of the sky from the ground, so he brought them to the man to see what he would call them, and whatever the man called each living creature, that would become its name.
[Genesis] [2]:[20] The man gave names to all the various livestock and to the birds of the sky and to every living creature in the countryside, but none of them was a suitable companion to help him.
[Genesis] [2]:[21] So Yahweh God caused the man to go into a deep sleep, and then while he was sleeping, he removed one of his ribs and closed up over its place with flesh.
[Genesis] [2]:[22] Then Yahweh God used the rib which he had taken from the man to form into a woman, and he brought her to the man,
[Genesis] [2]:[23] and the man said: “Now this is bone from my bones and flesh from my flesh. She’ll be named ‘woman’ because she came from a man.”
[Genesis] [2]:[24] So that’s why a man leaves his father and mother, and becomes united to his wife, and the two of them become one being.
[Genesis] [2]:[25] At that time, both the man and his wife were naked, but they had no sense of shame.
[Genesis] [3]:[1] Now the snake was the craftiest of all the wild animals that Yahweh God had created, and one day he asked the woman, “Did God really command you to not eat fruit from any of the trees in the garden?”
[Genesis] [3]:[2] “No,” answered the woman, “we can eat the fruit from any of the trees in the garden,
[Genesis] [3]:[3] except from the tree that is in the centre. He commanded us to not eat that fruit or even touch it, because if we do, we will die!”
[Genesis] [3]:[4] But the serpent said to the woman, “It’s not definite that you’ll die.
[Genesis] [3]:[5] Actually, God knows that as soon as you eat fruit from that tree, you’ll understand new things, so that you will know what’s right and what’s wrong just like God does.”
[Genesis] [3]:[6] The woman saw that the tree’s fruit looked good to eat and that the tree itself was very attractive, plus she wanted to eat the fruit so that it would make her wise. So she picked some of the fruit and ate it and she also gave some of it to her husband who was there with her, and he ate it too.
[Genesis] [3]:[7] Immediately they both had new understanding and they felt their nakedness. So they sewed some fig leaves together and made skirts for themselves.
[Genesis] [3]:[8] Late that afternoon, during the cool time of the day, the man and his wife heard Yahweh God’s voice as he walked in the garden, but they hid from him behind some trees in the garden,
[Genesis] [3]:[9] so Yahweh God called out to the man, “Adam, where are you?”
[Genesis] [3]:[10] “I heard you walking in the garden,” he replied, “but I was scared because I was naked, so I hid myself.”
[Genesis] [3]:[11] “Who told you that you’re naked?” Yahweh God asked. “Have you eaten the fruit that I told you not to eat?”
[Genesis] [3]:[12] “The woman that you put here beside me,” answered the man, “she gave me some fruit from the tree and I ate it.”
[Genesis] [3]:[13] Then Yahweh God asked the woman, “What did you do?” “The snake tricked me, so I ate some of the fruit,” the woman replied.
[Genesis] [3]:[14] Then Yahweh God said to the snake, “Because you’ve done this you’ll be cursed more than all the livestock, and more than every wild animal. Now you’ll move along on your belly, and you’ll eat dust all the rest of your life.
[Genesis] [3]:[15] I’ll put hostility between you and the woman between your descendants and hers. He will crush your head and you’ll strike his heel.”
[Genesis] [3]:[16] To the woman God said, “I’ll sharply increase your pain in childbirth. You’ll produce children in pain. Your desire will be for your husband and he will rule over you.”
[Genesis] [3]:[17] Then God said to the man, “Because you did what your wife told you and ate from that tree that I’d told you not to eat from, then the ground will be cursed because of you. You’ll have to work hard to get food from it all the rest of your life.
[Genesis] [3]:[18] It’ll produce thorns and thistles for you although you’ll eat the crops from the countryside.
[Genesis] [3]:[19] You’ll eat bread with sweat drops on your nose until you return to the ground because you were taken out of the ground. Yes, you were created from dust, and you’ll return back to dust.”
[Genesis] [3]:[20] Then the man named his wife ‘Havah’ (Eve) (which means ‘living’) because she would become the mother of all future people.
[Genesis] [3]:[21] Then Yahweh God made clothes from animal skins for Adam and his wife and he dressed them.
[Genesis] [3]:[22] Then Yahweh God said, “See, the man has become like one of us, being aware of good and evil. But now, he mustn’t be allowed to reach out his hand and also take fruit from the tree of life and eat it and live forever.”
[Genesis] [3]:[23] So Yahweh God expelled them out of the garden in Eden to work the soil from which Adam had been taken.
[Genesis] [3]:[24] After he expelled them, he placed sentries on the east side of the garden in Eden, as well as a fiery sword that swung around in every direction to guard the path to the tree of life.
[Genesis] [4]:[1] Then Adam slept with his wife Havah (Eve), and she conceived and in due course gave birth to Kayin (Cain). “Yahweh has enabled me to produce a man,” she said.
[Genesis] [4]:[2] Eventually she also gave birth to Kayin’s brother, Hevel (Abel). Hevel became a shepherd, while Kayin became a crop farmer.
[Genesis] [4]:[3] Some months later, Kayin brought some of what he’d grown in the ground as an offering to Yahweh,
[Genesis] [4]:[4] and also Hevel brought the best portions from some of the firstborn of his flock. Now Yahweh was pleased with Hevel and his offering,
[Genesis] [4]:[5] but he didn’t even look towards Kayin and his offering. Kayin got very angry and his face showed his displeasure.
[Genesis] [4]:[6] Then Yahweh said to Kayin, “Why are you so angry? And why are you frowning like that?
[Genesis] [4]:[7] If you do what’s right, won’t you be honoured? But if you don’t do what’s right, sin is crouching in the doorway wanting to have you, but you have the control over it.”
[Genesis] [4]:[8] One day, Kayin spoke to his brother Hevel when they were out in the countryside, and then Kayin attacked him and killed him.
[Genesis] [4]:[9] Later Yahweh asked Kayin, “Where’s your brother Hevel?” “I don’t know,” he replied, “It’s not my job to look after my brother.”
[Genesis] [4]:[10] “What have you done?” Yahweh asked. “Your brother’s blood is calling out to me from the ground.
[Genesis] [4]:[11] So now you’re cursed and banished from the soil that your brother’s blood soaked into as a result of your actions.
[Genesis] [4]:[12] Whenever you till and plant the ground, it will no longer produce good yields for you. You’ll be a fugitive and wandering refugee on the earth.”
[Genesis] [4]:[13] “My punishment is more than I can bear,” Kayin complained to Yahweh.
[Genesis] [4]:[14] “Look, you’re now driving me away from the ground I’ve been cultivating to somewhere where you won’t be able to see me. I’ll be a wandering refugee on the earth, and anyone who finds me will kill me.”
[Genesis] [4]:[15] “Very well,”, replied Yahweh and declared, “If anyone kills Kayin, then that person will receive a seven times greater sentence.” Then Yahweh marked Kayin so that no one who found him would kill him,
[Genesis] [4]:[16] and Kayin left Yahweh’s presence and settled in the land of Nod to the east of Eden.
[Genesis] [4]:[17] Then Kayin (Cain) slept with his wife and she conceived and gave birth to Hanok (Enoch). Then Kayin founded a town and named it Hanok after his son.
[Genesis] [4]:[18] Eventually Hanok fathered Irad, and Irad fathered Mehuyael, and Mehuyael father Metushael, and Metushael fathered Lemek (Lamech).
[Genesis] [4]:[19] Lemek had two wives: the first was named Adah and the second was Tsilah (Zillah).
[Genesis] [4]:[20] Adah gave birth to Yaval who became the ancestor of people who live in tents and rear cattle.
[Genesis] [4]:[21] His brother’s name was Yuval and he became the ancestor of people who play stringed and wind instruments.
[Genesis] [4]:[22] Tsilah gave birth to Tuval-Kayin who forged all kinds of tools out of bronze and iron. His sister was named Na’amah.
[Genesis] [4]:[23] Then Lemek said to his wives: “Adah and Tsilah, listen to me. My wives, take notice of my words; I killed a man who had wounded me; I killed a young man who hurt me.
[Genesis] [4]:[24] If killers of Kayin (Cain) would be sentenced seven times as much, then anyone who kills me should be sentenced seventy-seven times as much.”
[Genesis] [4]:[25] Then Adam slept with his wife again and she bore a son and named him Shet (Seth) (which means ‘given’) because she had said, “God has given me another son in place of Hevel (Abel) who was killed by Kayin (Cain).”
[Genesis] [4]:[26] Eventually Shet also had a son and named him Enosh. That was when people began using Yahweh’s name when they prayed for help.
[Genesis] [5]:[1] This is the list of Adam’s descendants. When God had created humankind, he made them in his own likeness.
[Genesis] [5]:[2] He created them as male and female, and he blessed them and named them ‘humans’.
[Genesis] [5]:[3] When Adam was 130 years old, he had a son who was like him in many ways, and he named him Shet (Seth).
[Genesis] [5]:[4] After Shet’s birth, Adam lived another 800 years and had other sons and daughters.
[Genesis] [5]:[5] So Adam lived a total of 930 years, and then he died.
[Genesis] [5]:[6] When Shet was 105 years old, he had a son named Enosh.
[Genesis] [5]:[7] After Enosh’s birth, Shet lived another 807 years and had other sons and daughters.
[Genesis] [5]:[8] So Shet lived a total of 912 years, and then he died.

[Genesis] [5]:[17] So Mahalalel lived a total of 895 years, and then he died.

[Genesis] [5]:[19] After Hanok’s birth, Yered lived another 800 years and had other sons and daughters.
[Genesis] [5]:[20] So Yered lived a total of 962 years, and then he died.

[Genesis] [5]:[23] So Hanok lived a total of 365 years.
[Genesis] [5]:[24] Hanok walked with God, and then he was not there, because God took him away.
[Genesis] [5]:[25] When Metushelah was 187 years old, he had a son named Lemek (Lamech).
[Genesis] [5]:[26] After Lemek’s birth, Metushelah lived another 782 years and had other sons and daughters.
[Genesis] [5]:[27] So Metushelah lived a total of 969 years, and then he died.
[Genesis] [5]:[28] When Lemek was 182 years old, he had a son
[Genesis] [5]:[29] and he named him Noah (which sounds like the Hebrew word for ‘relief’) because he said, “This son will give us relief from the difficult work that we have to do because Yahweh has cursed the ground.”
[Genesis] [5]:[30] After Noah’s birth, Lemek lived another 595 years and had other sons and daughters.
[Genesis] [5]:[31] So Lemek lived a total of 777 years, and then he died.
[Genesis] [5]:[32] After Noah was 500 years old, he had sons whose names were Yefet (Japheth), Shem, and Ham.
[Genesis] [6]:[1] When people began to multiply on the earth’s surface, and they were having daughters,
[Genesis] [6]:[2] God’s sons saw that men’s daughters were beautiful, and they took any that they wanted for themselves as wives.
[Genesis] [6]:[3] Then Yahweh said, “My Spirit won’t tolerate people forever, because they are physical beings, therefore their remaining time will be 120 years.”
[Genesis] [6]:[4] The NEFILIM were on the earth in those days and also after that, when the sons of God went to the daughters of humankind and they bore children for them. INVESTIGATE They were the mighty warriors of long ago—those famous men.
[Genesis] [6]:[5] Then Yahweh saw that the humankind’s wickedness on the earth was extensive, and that every inclination of their inner thoughts was only evil all day long.
[Genesis] [6]:[6] So Yahweh regretted that he had made humankind on the earth and he was deeply saddened,
[Genesis] [6]:[7] so he said, “This humankind that I created, I will completely destroy them from the surface of the ground, along with the animals, and crawling creatures and the birds of the sky, because I regret that I made them.”
[Genesis] [6]:[8] However, Yahweh noticed Noah and was pleased with him.
[Genesis] [6]:[9] This is the account of Noah: He was a man who obeyed God, blameless among the people of his time and he walked around with God.
[Genesis] [6]:[10] Noah had three sons: Yefet (Japheth), Shem, and Ham.
[Genesis] [6]:[11] Now God noticed that humankind was corrupt and very violent.
[Genesis] [6]:[12] Yes, God looked at the earth, and wow, all the living creatures on the earth had corrupted their behaviour.
[Genesis] [6]:[13] So God told Noah, “I’ve decided to put an end to all people on earth because the earth is filled with violence because of them. So listen, I myself am going to destroy all of them, along with the earth.
[Genesis] [6]:[14] Make yourself a wooden chest out of cypress. Build rooms inside it, and seal it both inside and outside with resin.
[Genesis] [6]:[15] These are the dimensions for it: 140m long, 23m wide, and 14m high.
[Genesis] [6]:[16] It must have a roof, but the last half a metre between the sides and the roof should remain open. Put the door in its side, and build lower, middle, and upper decks.
[Genesis] [6]:[17] You see, I’m going to flood the earth with water to destroy every creature that breathes. Everything that’s on the earth will die.
[Genesis] [6]:[18] But I’ll make an agreement with you, so you must go into this chest along with your wife and sons and their wives,
[Genesis] [6]:[19] and you must take a pair, male and female, of everything that lives into the chest to keep alive with you.
[Genesis] [6]:[20] Pairs of every kind of bird and animal, including every kind of creature that moves on the ground, will come to you so that you keep them alive,
[Genesis] [6]:[21] and you must take with you some of every different kind of food and store it in there for you and them to eat.
[Genesis] [6]:[22] So Noah did that exactly as God had specified.
[Genesis] [7]:[1] Then Yahweh said to Noah, “Go into the ark, you and all your household, because I’ve seen that you’re the only one who obeys me in this generation.
[Genesis] [7]:[2] Take in seven male and female pairs of every kind of ‘clean’ animal, and one male and female pair of the ‘unclean’ animals,
[Genesis] [7]:[3] as well as seven male and female pairs of every kind of flying bird in order to preserve their kinds on the earth.
[Genesis] [7]:[4] Seven days from now I’ll send forty days and nights of rain on the earth, and I’ll eliminate every living thing that I’ve made that’s still on the ground.
[Genesis] [7]:[5] So Noah did everything that Yahweh had instructed him to do.
[Genesis] [7]:[6] Noah was 600 years old when the flood covered the earth,
[Genesis] [7]:[7] and he went into the wooden chest along with his wife, his three sons and their wives, in order to escape from the floodwaters.
[Genesis] [7]:[8] ‘Clean’ and ‘unclean’ animals, the birds, and everything that lived on the ground
[Genesis] [7]:[9] came to Noah in male and female pairs and went into the chest, just like God had instructed Noah.
[Genesis] [7]:[10] Then when the seven days were up, water started to flood the earth.
[Genesis] [7]:[11] When Noah was 600 years old (and around the beginning of May), deep underwater geysers in the ocean started spouting out water, and the skies began to drop heavy rain
[Genesis] [7]:[12] that continued day and night for forty days.
[Genesis] [7]:[13] That was the very day that Noah and Yefet (Japheth) and Shem and Ham and their wives had all entered the wooden chest.
[Genesis] [7]:[14] They had with them every kind of living creature, including every kind of livestock and every other kind of creature that lives on the land, and every kind of bird and everything else that flies.
[Genesis] [7]:[15] They had come to Noah in order to enter the chest—two by two of every creature with the breath of life.
[Genesis] [7]:[16] So pairs of males and females of every creature entered just as God had instructed Noah, then Yahweh closed the door and they were shut in.
[Genesis] [7]:[17] Then the flood came onto the earth for forty days, and the water rose so that the wooden chest was lifted up right off the land.
[Genesis] [7]:[18] The water continued to rise and get deeper on the earth, and the chest floated along on top of the water.
[Genesis] [7]:[19] Eventually the water on the earth got so deep that all the high mountains everywhere under the sky were under water—
[Genesis] [7]:[20] in fact the water rose over seven metres above the tops of them.
[Genesis] [7]:[21] By then every living creature that lived on the earth had drowned—birds, livestock, animals, every creature that swarms on the earth, and all humankind.
[Genesis] [7]:[22] Everything that had the breath of the spirit of life in its nostrils, everything that lived on dry land, died.
[Genesis] [7]:[23] That’s how Yahweh completely annihilated every living creature off the earth, including humankind and livestock and crawling creatures and even the birds. Everything was annihilated except for Noah and those with him in the floating chest,
[Genesis] [7]:[24] and the earth remained in full flood for 150 days.
[Genesis] [8]:[1] Then God considered Noah and all the living things and all the livestock that were with him in the floating chest, and he caused a wind to pass over the earth, and the waters started to subside
[Genesis] [8]:[2] and the underwater geysers and the rain was stopped.
[Genesis] [8]:[3] Then the water steadily receded from the earth and after five months the water had gone down enough
[Genesis] [8]:[4] that by October the wooden chest was left sitting on one of the Ararat mountains.
[Genesis] [8]:[5] The water continued to recede until December when the tops of the mountains became visible.
[Genesis] [8]:[6] Then after another forty days, Noah opened a window near the top of the chest
[Genesis] [8]:[7] and he released a raven which kept flying out and returning until the land started to dry out.
[Genesis] [8]:[8] Then Noah also released a dove to see if the land was really out of the water,
[Genesis] [8]:[9] but the dove didn’t find anywhere to land so it returned to the window because the surface of the earth was still wet, and he stretched out his arm and brought the dove back inside.
[Genesis] [8]:[10] Noah waited another week and then he released the dove again
[Genesis] [8]:[11] and it returned to him in the evening and wow, it had a fresh, green olive leaf in its beak. So now Noah knew that the land was out of the water.
[Genesis] [8]:[12] Then he waited another week, and released the dove again, but this time it didn’t come back to him.
[Genesis] [8]:[13] So it was when Noah was 601 years old (in the month of WHAT MONTH on the first day of the Jewish new year) the land was still drying out. So Noah made an opening in the top of the wooden chest and saw that the land surface there was almost dry.
[Genesis] [8]:[14] By the end of the next month, the land was fully dry.
[Genesis] [8]:[15] Then God said to Noah,
[Genesis] [8]:[16] “Leave the wooden chest along with your sons and each of your wives.
[Genesis] [8]:[17] Take out all the living creatures that are with you, including the birds and livestock, and everything that crawls (CHECK FOR WORD CONSISTENCY) on the ground, so that they’ll proliferate and increase their numbers all over the earth.
[Genesis] [8]:[18] So Noah went outside, along with his sons and each of their wives.
[Genesis] [8]:[19] Every living creature, every crawling thing and every bird, everything moving on the earth, went outside kind by kind.
[Genesis] [8]:[20] Then Noah built an altar to Yahweh, and he took some of every kind of clean animal and every kind of clean bird, and he offered them as burnt offerings on the altar.
[Genesis] [8]:[21] When Yahweh smelt the pleasing aroma, he said to himself, “I’ll never curse the ground because of humankind again, even though the humankind’s hearts are inclined from their youth to do evil things. And I’ll never again destroy every living thing again like I’ve just done.
[Genesis] [8]:[22] As long as the earth continues to exist, seedtime and harvest time, cold and heat, summer and winter, day and night, will never stop happening.
[Genesis] [9]:[1] Then God blessed Noah and his sons and said to them, “Be fruitful and multiply and fill the earth.
[Genesis] [9]:[2] Now every living creature on the earth will be afraid and terrified of you, including every bird that flies in the sky, along with every creature that moves on land, and all the fish in the ocean. I have put them all under your authority.
[Genesis] [9]:[3] From now on every creature that is alive and moves can be eaten as food—just like I previously provided you green plants for food, now I provide you everything for food—
[Genesis] [9]:[4] the only exception is meat with its life blood still in it.
[Genesis] [9]:[5] Also, I will certainly require blood as payment for people’s lives: if anyone murders another person, I require that the murderer must die, and even if an animal kills a human being, I require that it must die.
[Genesis] [9]:[6] Yes, if anyone sheds human blood, the others must shed the murderer’s blood, because God made human beings in his image.
[Genesis] [9]:[7] So then, be fruitful and multiply—have children on the earth and become numerous.
[Genesis] [9]:[8] Then God said to Noah and his sons,
[Genesis] [9]:[9] “Now listen, I am making an agreement with you and your future descendants,
[Genesis] [9]:[10] and it’s also with every living creature that is with you: with the birds, the livestock, and every living thing on the earth with you, from all that came out of the wooden chest to every future living thing on the earth.
[Genesis] [9]:[11] My agreement that I’m establishing with you is that all living things will never die from a flood again. That’s right, I will never use a flood again to destroy everything on the earth.”
[Genesis] [9]:[12] Then God added, “This is how I’ll show everyone that I’ve made this agreement with you and with all the living creatures that are with you, along with all future generations:
[Genesis] [9]:[13] I’ll place my rainbow among the clouds, and it’ll be a sign of the agreement between me and all life on the earth.
[Genesis] [9]:[14] So whenever I cause clouds to form in the sky and a rainbow is visible in the clouds,
[Genesis] [9]:[15] then I’ll remember my agreement that’s between me and you and every kind of living creature, and a flood will never again destroy everything living.
[Genesis] [9]:[16] So whenever a rainbow appears among the clouds, I’ll see it and remember my permanent agreement with every living creature that lives and will live on the earth.”
[Genesis] [9]:[17] Then God said to Noah, “The rainbow is the sign of the agreement that I have established between me and every living thing on the earth.”
[Genesis] [9]:[18] Noah’s sons who came out of the wooden chest after the flood were Yefet (Japheth), Shem, and Ham. (Ham became Kena’an’s (Canaan) father).
[Genesis] [9]:[19] They were Noah’s three sons and from them the whole earth became populated.
[Genesis] [9]:[20] After a while, Noah, who was a farmer, planted some grape vines,
[Genesis] [9]:[21] and in due course he drank some of his wine and got drunk, and he fell asleep naked in his tent.
[Genesis] [9]:[22] Then Ham (Kena’an’s father) saw his father’s nakedness then went outside and told his brothers what he’d seen.
[Genesis] [9]:[23] So Shem and Yefet took a robe, and holding it between their shoulders they walked backwards into the tent and covered their father’s nakedness. (Their faces were towards the tent entrance, so they didn’t see his nakedness.)
[Genesis] [9]:[24] Eventually, Noah woke up from his drunken sleep and found out what his youngest son (Ham) had done to him
[Genesis] [9]:[25] and said, “May Kena’an be cursed and become a slave of slaves to his brothers!”
[Genesis] [9]:[26] Then he added, “Praise Yahweh who’s Shem’s god. May Kena’an become Shem’s slave.
[Genesis] [9]:[27] May God expand Yefet’s territory and may he live in Shem’s tents. May Kena’an also become a slave of Yefet.”
[Genesis] [9]:[28] After the flood, Noah lived another 350 years,
[Genesis] [9]:[29] and so he was 950 years old when he died.
[Genesis] [10]:[1] These are the generations of Noah’s sons, Yefet (Japheth), Shem, and Ham, and their descendants born to them after the flood:
[Genesis] [10]:[2] Yefet’s (Japheth) sons were Gomer, Magog, Maday, Yavan, Tuval, Meshek, and Tiras.
[Genesis] [10]:[3] Gomer’s sons were Ashkenaz, Rifat, and Togarmah.
[Genesis] [10]:[4] Yavan’s sons were Elishah and Tarshish, and Kitim and Dodanim.
[Genesis] [10]:[5] From all those descendants, people spread out into areas near the coast, each group with their own language, and with all the clans making up their nations.
[Genesis] [10]:[6] Ham’s sons were Kush, Mitsrayim, Put, and Kena’an (Canaan).
[Genesis] [10]:[7] Kush’s sons were Seva, Havilah, Savtah, Raemah, and Savteka. Then Raemah’s sons were Sheva and Dedan.
[Genesis] [10]:[8] Kush was also the father of Nimrod who became a mighty warrior on the earth.
[Genesis] [10]:[9] Nimrod also became a terrific hunter noticed by Yahweh, so people said, “Like Nimrod, a terrific hunter noticed by Yahweh.”
[Genesis] [10]:[10] His kingdom began in the cities of Bavel, Erek, Akad, and Keleneh, all in the Shin’ar region.
[Genesis] [10]:[11] From that area he extended to Ashur (Assyria) where he built the cities of Nineveh, Rehovot-Ir, Kelah,
[Genesis] [10]:[12] and Resen, between Nineveh and the large city of Kelah.
[Genesis] [10]:[13] Mitsrayim fathered Ludim, Anamim, Lehavim, Naftuhim,
[Genesis] [10]:[14] Patrusi, and Kasluhim (who the Pelishtim came from), and Kaftorim.
[Genesis] [10]:[15] Kena’an (Canaan) fathered Tsidon (Sidon) his firstborn, then Het,
[Genesis] [10]:[16] Yevusi, Amori, Girgashi.
[Genesis] [10]:[17] Hivi, Arki, Sini,
[Genesis] [10]:[18] Arvadi, Tsemari, and Hamati. Later on, the Kena’an clans spread in all directions
[Genesis] [10]:[19] and their border went from Tsidon toward Gerar as far as Azah (Gaza), and then toward Sedom, Amorah (Gomorrah), Admah, and Tsevoim, as far as Lesha.
[Genesis] [10]:[20] Those are Ham’s descendants according to their clans, languages, regions, and nations.
[Genesis] [10]:[21] Shem (the younger brother of Yefet (Japheth)) also had some sons and became the ancestor of all the descendants of Ever.
[Genesis] [10]:[22] Shem’s sons were Eylam, Ashur, Arpakshad, Lud, and Aram.
[Genesis] [10]:[23] Aram’s sons were Uts (Uz), Hul, Geter, and Mash.
[Genesis] [10]:[24] Arpakshad fathered Shelah, then Shelah fathered Ever.
[Genesis] [10]:[25] Ever’s two sons were Peleg and Yaketan. (Peleg’s name means ‘division’, because it was during his lifetime that the earth was divided.)
[Genesis] [10]:[26] Yaketan fathered Almodad, Shelef, Hatsarmavet, Yerah,
[Genesis] [10]:[27] Hadoram, Uzal, Diklah,
[Genesis] [10]:[28] Oval, Avimael, Sheva,
[Genesis] [10]:[29] Ofir, Havilah, and Yovav. (All of those were the sons of Yaketan.)
[Genesis] [10]:[30] They lived in the area from Meysha then to Sefar in the eastern hills.
[Genesis] [10]:[31] Those are Shem’s descendants according to their clans, languages, regions, and nations.
[Genesis] [10]:[32] All of those are the clans of Noah’s sons, according to their generations and nations, and from them the nations spread out across the earth after the flood.
[Genesis] [11]:[1] Now the whole world had a single language and the same words,
[Genesis] [11]:[2] and as they migrated from the east, they discovered a plain in the Shin’ar region and settled there.
[Genesis] [11]:[3] Then they said to each other, “Come on, let’s make bricks and cure them with fire.” So they had bricks instead of stones, and they had tar for mortar.
[Genesis] [11]:[4] Then they said, “Come on, let’s build a city for ourselves and a tower with its top in the sky, and let’s make a reputation for ourselves, so that we don’t get scattered all over the whole earth.”
[Genesis] [11]:[5] Then Yahweh came down to see the city and the tower that the humans were building
[Genesis] [11]:[6] and he said, “Look, they’re just one people group, and they all speak the same language. This is only the beginning of what they can do together—soon they’ll be capable of doing anything they plan to do.
[Genesis] [11]:[7] Come on then, let’s go down and confuse their language so that they won’t be able to understand each other’s words.”
[Genesis] [11]:[8] So then they stopped building the city and Yahweh caused them to scatter over the whole world.
[Genesis] [11]:[9] That’s why they named the city ‘Bavel’ (meaning ‘mixed-up’) because it was there that Yahweh mixed up everyone’s language and then scattered them over the whole world.

[Genesis] [11]:[11] After Arpakshad was born, Shem lived another 500 years and had other sons and daughters.
[Genesis] [11]:[12] When Arpakshad was thirty-five years old, he had a son named Shelah.
[Genesis] [11]:[13] After Shelah was born, Arpakshad lived another 403 years and had other sons and daughters.
[Genesis] [11]:[14] When Shelah was thirty years old, he had a son named Ever.
[Genesis] [11]:[15] After Ever was born, Shelah lived another 403 years and had other sons and daughters.
[Genesis] [11]:[16] When Ever was thirty-four years old, he had a son named Peleg.
[Genesis] [11]:[17] After Peleg was born, Ever lived another 430 years and had other sons and daughters
[Genesis] [11]:[18] When Peleg was thirty years old, he had a son named Re’u.
[Genesis] [11]:[19] After Re’u was born, Peleg lived another 209 years and had other sons and daughters.
[Genesis] [11]:[20] When Re’u was thirty-two years old, he had a son named Serug.
[Genesis] [11]:[21] After Serug was born, Re’u lived another 207 years and had other sons and daughters.
[Genesis] [11]:[22] When Serug was thirty years old, he had a son named Nahor.
[Genesis] [11]:[23] After Nahor was born, Serug lived another 200 years and had other sons and daughters.
[Genesis] [11]:[24] When Nahor was twenty-nine years old, he had a son named Terah.
[Genesis] [11]:[25] After Terah was born, Nahor lived another 119 years and had other sons and daughters.
[Genesis] [11]:[26] After Terah was seventy years old, he had sons whose names were Avram, Nahor, and Haran.
[Genesis] [11]:[27] This is the record of Terah’s descendants: Terah’s sons were Avram, Nahor, and Haran and Haran had a son named Lot.
[Genesis] [11]:[28] While his father was still alive, Haran died in the land where he was born, in the city of Ur where the Kasdim (Chaldeans) lived.
[Genesis] [11]:[29] Meanwhile Avram married Saray (Sarai) and Nahor married Milkah. (Milkah and her sister Yiskah were the daughters of Nahor’s brother Haran.)
[Genesis] [11]:[30] However, Saray wasn’t able to get pregnant so they didn’t have any children.
[Genesis] [11]:[31] Then one day, Terah gathered his son Avram and his grandson Lot (who was Haran’s son), and his daughter-in-law Saray (who was Avram’s wife), and they all left from the city of Ur (where the Kasdim lived), to travel to the region of Kena’an (Canaan), but when they arrived at the city of Haran, they decided to live there.
[Genesis] [11]:[32] Then when Terah was 205 years old, he died there in Haran.
[Genesis] [12]:[1] Then Yahweh said to Avram, “You must leave your land and your relatives and your father’s house and go to the land that I’ll show you.
[Genesis] [12]:[2] I’ll bless you and make you into a great nation. I’ll make you famous and you’ll be a blessing to others.
[Genesis] [12]:[3] I’ll bless everyone who blesses you, but I’ll curse anyone who curses you. All the families on the earth will be blessed because of you.
[Genesis] [12]:[4] So Avram left there just as Yahweh had told him, and Lot also went with him. Avram was seventy-five years old when he left the city of Haran.
[Genesis] [12]:[5] He took his wife Saray (Sarai) and his nephew Lot and all their possessions that they had accumulated and the people who they had acquired in Haran, and they set out to go to the land of Kena’an (Canaan). When they arrived in the Kena’an region,
[Genesis] [12]:[6] they continued travelling as far as the city of Shekem, to Moreh’s oak tree. (The Kena’anim (Canaanites) were still living in that region at that time.)
[Genesis] [12]:[7] Then Yahweh came to Avram and told him, “I’ll give this land to your descendants.” So Avram built an altar there and made a burnt offering to Yahweh, who had appeared to him.
[Genesis] [12]:[8] Then from there he went on to the hills to the east of Beyt-El (Bethel) and pitched his tents, with Beyt-El on the west and Ay on the east. He built an altar to Yahweh there, and sacrificed and prayed to Yahweh
[Genesis] [12]:[9] before continuing south down toward the Negev desert.
[Genesis] [12]:[10] One time when there was a drought causing a severe food shortage, Avram and his household travelled west across to Mitsrayim (Egypt) to stay there.
[Genesis] [12]:[11] Just before they arrived in Mitsrayim, Avram said to his wife Saray (Sarai), “Listen, you’re a very beautiful woman,
[Genesis] [12]:[12] so when the Mitsrim (Egyptians) see you they’ll say, ‘This is his wife,’ and they’ll kill me but let you live.
[Genesis] [12]:[13] Please tell them that you’re my sister so they’ll treat me well because of you and let me live.”
[Genesis] [12]:[14] So that’s what happened when they entered Mitsrayim—the Mitsrim indeed noticed that Saray was very beautiful,
[Genesis] [12]:[15] and when Par’oh’s (Pharaoh) officials saw her, so they told him about her beauty, and she was taken into Par’oh’s palace.
[Genesis] [12]:[16] He treated Avram well (thinking he was the brother), so he was given flocks and herds, male and female donkeys, male and female slaves, and camels.
[Genesis] [12]:[17] But Yahweh directed terrible deadly diseases onto Par’oh and his household because of his taking Avram’s wife Saray.
[Genesis] [12]:[18] So Par’oh called for Avram and said, “What’s this you’ve done to me? Why didn’t you tell me that she’s your wife?
[Genesis] [12]:[19] Why did you say, ‘She’s my sister,’ so that I took her in as a wife? Now then, here’s your wife. Take her and get out of here.”
[Genesis] [12]:[20] Then Par’oh commanded his officers, and they sent Avram and his wife away and everything that belonged to him.
[Genesis] [13]:[1] Then Avram left Mitsrayim (Egypt) with his wife and everything that belonged to him, and their nephew Lot. They returned to the Negev
[Genesis] [13]:[2] and now Avram had become very wealthy, with both livestock, and silver and gold.
[Genesis] [13]:[3] Then they continued north through the Negev as far as Beyt-El (Bethel), to the place where his tents had been at the beginning—between Beyt-El and Ay—
[Genesis] [13]:[4] to the place where he’d previously built an altar, and Avram sacrificed and prayed to Yahweh there.
[Genesis] [13]:[5] Now Lot, who was travelling with Avram, also had flocks and herds and tents,
[Genesis] [13]:[6] but the land couldn’t support them all while they stayed together. Because the needs of their combined assets were so demanding, they couldn’t all thrive in one place
[Genesis] [13]:[7] and that led to strife between Avram’s and Lot’s herdsmen. Also, the Kena’anim (Canaanites) and the Perizim were living in the land at that time.
[Genesis] [13]:[8] So Avram said to Lot, “Let’s not have quarrelling between you and I, or between yours herdsmen and mine, because we’re relatives.
[Genesis] [13]:[9] Isn’t the whole land available to you? So let’s separate. If you go to the left then I’ll go right, or if you go to the right then I’ll go left.”
[Genesis] [13]:[10] Lot looked all around and saw that all the plain of the Yarden (Jordan) river valley was well-watered through towards Tsoar, just like Yahweh’s garden had been before he destroyed Sedom and Amorah (Gomorrah), and like the land of Mitsrayim (Egypt).
[Genesis] [13]:[11] Lot chose all of the Yarden plain for himself, and so he travelled to the east and they separated from each other.
[Genesis] [13]:[12] So Avram settled in the land of Kena’an (Canaan), and Lot settled in the cities of the plain and moved his tents as far as Sedom.
[Genesis] [13]:[13] However, the people of Sedom were extremely wicked, constantly disobeying Yahweh.
[Genesis] [13]:[14] After Lot had left, Yahweh told Avram, “Look all around you towards the north, the south, the east, and the west,
[Genesis] [13]:[15] because all that land that you can see, I’ll give it to you and to your descendants to have forever.
[Genesis] [13]:[16] I’ll make your descendants as numerous as dust particles. Your descendants will only be able to be counted if someone’s able to count all the dust particles on the earth.
[Genesis] [13]:[17] So, go and start walking throughout the land—through its length and its width, because I’m giving it all to you.”
[Genesis] [13]:[18] So Avram moved his tents and went and settled by the terebinth trees at Mamre (near Hevron), and he built an altar to Yahweh there.
[Genesis] [14]:[1] At the time when Amrafel was king of Shin’ar, Areyok was king of Elasar, Kedorla’omer was king of Eylam, and Tid’al was king of the Goyim,
[Genesis] [14]:[2] they went to war against Bera king of Sedom, Birsha king of Amorah (Gomorrah), Shin’av king of Admah, Shem’ever king of Tsevoim, and the king of Bela (also known as Tsoar).
[Genesis] [14]:[3] Those latter five kings joined forces in the Siddim valley (also known as the Salt Sea valley).
[Genesis] [14]:[4] They had been subject to King Kedorla’omer for twelve years, but in the thirteenth year they rebelled.
[Genesis] [14]:[5] Then in the fourteenth year, Kedorla’omer and the kings who were with him went and attacked the Refaim in Ashterot-Karnayim, and the Zuzim in Ham, and the Emim in Shaveh-Kiryatayim,
[Genesis] [14]:[6] and the Horim in the hill country of Se’ir as far as El Paran, which is near the wilderness.
[Genesis] [14]:[7] Then those four kings turned back and went to Eyn Mishpat (also called Kadesh) and they attacked the entire territories of the Amalekim and also the Amorim, who were living in Hazezon Tamar.
[Genesis] [14]:[8] Then the king of Sedom, the king of Amorah, the king of Admah, the king of Tsevoim, and the king of Bela (also called Tsoar) went out into the Sidim Valley and arranged their troops for battle
[Genesis] [14]:[9] against Kedorla’omer king of Eylam, Tid’al king of Goyim, Amrafel king of Shin’ar, Areyok king of Elasar—five kings defending themselves against the four.
[Genesis] [14]:[10] Now the Sidim Valley had many tar pits, and when the kings of Sedom and Amorah fled, they fell into the pits, but the rest fled up into the hills.
[Genesis] [14]:[11] Then the four attacking kings took all the peoples’ possessions from Sedom and Amorah and all their food and left.
[Genesis] [14]:[12] Avram’s nephew Lot and all his possessions also got taken because he was living in the city of Sedom,
[Genesis] [14]:[13] but someone who escaped came and reported this news to Avram the Ivri (Hebrew). At that time, Avram was still living by the terebinth trees of Mamre the Amori, the brother of Eshkol and the brother of Aner, and the three of them had formed an alliance together.
[Genesis] [14]:[14] When Avram heard that his nephew had been taken captive, he led out his 318 trained men who’d all been born in his house, and he pursued his enemies as far as the town of Dan.
[Genesis] [14]:[15] During the night, Avram split in his slaves into groups and they attacked the four kings and their soldiers and pursued them to Hovah (north of Damesek (Damascus)).
[Genesis] [14]:[16] They were able to bring back all the possessions, as well as his nephew Lot and his possessions, and also the women and the other people who’d been captured.
[Genesis] [14]:[17] After Avram returned from defeating Kedorla’omer and his allied kings, the king of Sedom went out to meet Avram in Shaveh valley (also called the king’s valley) .
[Genesis] [14]:[18] Then Malki-Tsedek (Melchizedek) the king of Shalem brought out bread and wine—he was a priest to the most high God.
[Genesis] [14]:[19] Malki-Tsedek blessed Avram, saying: “May Avram be blessed by the most high God, the owner of heaven and earth.
[Genesis] [14]:[20] Praise the most high God, who enabled you to defeat your enemies.” Then Avram gave to Malki-Tsedek a tenth of everything he had recovered.
[Genesis] [14]:[21] Then the king of Sedom said to Avram, “Give my people back to me, but keep the possessions for yourself.”
[Genesis] [14]:[22] But Avram said to the king of Sedom, “I promise by Yahweh, most high God, the owner of heaven and earth,
[Genesis] [14]:[23] that I won’t take anything of yours, not even the strap of a sandal, so that you won’t be able to say that it was you who made me wealthy.
[Genesis] [14]:[24] I’ll take nothing, except what the young fighters have eaten, and the share of the other men who went with me: Aner, Eshkol, and Mamre. Let them take their share.”
[Genesis] [15]:[1] After those events, Yahweh spoke to Avram in a vision, telling him, “Don’t be afraid, Avram, because I’ll protect you and I’ll generously and richly reward you.”
[Genesis] [15]:[2] “My master Yahweh,” replied Avram, “what will you give me, since we have no children and it’s Eliezer (my chief slave from Damesek (Damascus)) who’ll inherit all my possessions?”
[Genesis] [15]:[3] Then he continued, “Yes, you haven’t given me a child so wow, my heir is a slave from my household!”
[Genesis] [15]:[4] Then listen, Yahweh’s word came to Avram saying, “That man won’t be your heir, but on the contrary, it’ll be your biological son.”
[Genesis] [15]:[5] Then Yahweh took Avram outside and said, “Look up at the sky and see if you can count the stars.” Then he said to him, “Your descendants will be like that.”
[Genesis] [15]:[6] Avram believed in Yahweh, and Yahweh considered that faith of Avram’s as an act of obedience.
[Genesis] [15]:[7] Then Yahweh told Avram, “I’m Yahweh who brought you out of Ur (where the Kasdim (Chaldeans) lived) so I could give you this land to possess it.”
[Genesis] [15]:[8] “My master Yahweh,” Avram asked, “how will I know that I will possess it?”
[Genesis] [15]:[9] “Bring me a three-year-old heifer,” Yahweh replied, “and a three-year-old she-goat and a three-year-old ram and a turtledove and a young pigeon.”
[Genesis] [15]:[10] So Avram brought all those to Yahweh, and then he cut the animals (but not the birds) in half down the middle and laid the halves opposite to each other.
[Genesis] [15]:[11] Then some birds of prey flew down to the carcasses, but Avram shooed them away.
[Genesis] [15]:[12] Later as the sun was going down, Avram fell into a deep sleep, and it suddenly became completely dark and he became terrified,
[Genesis] [15]:[13] and Yahweh said to Avram, “Know for certain that your descendants will be strangers in a land that doesn’t belong to them, and they’ll serve the rulers of that land and those rulers will persecute them for 400 years.
[Genesis] [15]:[14] But just as certain, I’ll punish the nation that they serve and after that they’ll come out with many possessions.
[Genesis] [15]:[15] And as for you, you’ll go to your ancestors in peace—you’ll be buried at a good old age.
[Genesis] [15]:[16] Then in the fourth generation your descendants will come back here, because the Amorim’ sins won’t be complete until then.”
[Genesis] [15]:[17] Then the sun went down and darkness came, and wow, there was a smoking fire pot and a flaming torch that passed between those animal halves.
[Genesis] [15]:[18] On that day Yahweh made an agreement with Avram, saying, “I’ve given this land to your descendants, from Mitsrayim’s (Egypt) river to the famous Perat (Euphrates) River.
[Genesis] [15]:[19] That includes the land of the Keynim, the Kenizim, the Kadmoni,
[Genesis] [15]:[20] the Hitim, the Perizim, the Refaim,
[Genesis] [15]:[21] the Amorim, the Kena’anim (Canaanites), the Girgashim, and the Yevusim.”
[Genesis] [16]:[1] Now Avram’s wife Saray (Sarai) hadn’t been able to give him any children, but she had an Mitsri (Egyptian) slave named Hagar,
[Genesis] [16]:[2] so Saray said to Avram, “Listen, Yahweh has prevented me from having children so please sleep with my slave. Perhaps I can have a family through her.” Avram agreed to what Saray had suggested.
[Genesis] [16]:[3] So Saray, the wife of Avram, took Hagar, her Mitsri slave, after Avram had lived ten years in the land of Kena’an (Canaan), and gave her to Avram her husband as a wife for him.
[Genesis] [16]:[4] So he slept with Hagar and she got pregnant, but once she realised that she began to despise her mistress.
[Genesis] [16]:[5] So Saray complained to Avram, “This is all your fault. I let you sleep with my slave, but now that she’s pregnant she looks down on me. May Yahweh judge between me and you.”
[Genesis] [16]:[6] “Listen,” Avram replied, “She’s your slave to do what she’s told. Do whatever you think best.” So Saray started mistreating Hagar, and so she ran away.

[Genesis] [16]:[11] Then the messenger told her, “Listen here: you’re pregnant and will give birth to a son, and you’ll name him ‘Yishmael’ (Ishmael) (which means ‘God hears’) because Yahweh has heard your cries of misery.

[Genesis] [16]:[13] Then Hagar realised that it was Yahweh who had spoken to her and said, “You’re ‘The god who sees me’,” because she thought, “Did I really just see the back of the god who sees me?”

[Genesis] [17]:[11] This removal of the foreskin will be a physical mark confirming the agreement between me and you.

[Genesis] [17]:[13] Yes, they definitely must be circumcised either way if they’re born in your house or purchased as slaves. This way, my agreement will be manifested in your physical bodies as a never-ending agreement.
