[Genesis] [22]:[16] saying, “I, Yahweh, make this declaration by my authority and truth that because you did that and didn’t withhold your only son,
[Genesis] [22]:[17] I’ll bless you tremendously and I’ll cause your descendants to be as numerous as the stars in the sky and as the sand on the beach, and your descendants will be victorious over their enemies.
[Genesis] [22]:[18] Because you obeyed what I said, all the nations of the earth will be blessed through your descendants.”
[Genesis] [22]:[19] Then Avraham returned to his young men and they all continued on home together to Be’er-Sheva (Beersheba), and Avraham continued living there.
[Genesis] [22]:[20] Some time later, Avraham heard the news, Look, your brother Nahor’s wife Milkah has also given birth to sons:
[Genesis] [22]:[21] Uts (Uz) his eldest son, and Buz his brother and Kemuel, the father of Aram,
[Genesis] [22]:[22] Kesed, Hazo, Pildash, Yidlaf, and Betuel.”
[Genesis] [22]:[23] Those are the eight sons that Milkah gave birth to for Avraham’s brother Nahor, and Betuel went on to father Rivkah.
[Genesis] [22]:[24] In addition, Nahor’s slave-wife Re’umah also gave birth to four sons: Tevah, Gaham, Tahash, and Ma’akah.
[Genesis] [23]:[1] Sarah went on to be 127 years old
[Genesis] [23]:[2] when she died in the city of Kiryat-Arba (now called Hevron) in the Kena’an (Canaan) region. Avraham went in by her bed to weep and mourn for her.
[Genesis] [23]:[3] After a time, Avraham got up from beside his dead wife and he spoke to the Hitim, requesting,
[Genesis] [23]:[4] “I’m a foreigner and just staying among you. Give me property for a burial place on your land so that I can bury my dead wife.”
[Genesis] [23]:[5] Those descendants of Het replied to Avraham, telling him,
[Genesis] [23]:[6] “My master, listen to us. You’re a godly leader among us. Go ahead and bury your dead in the choicest of our burial places. We’ve all agreed not to prevent you from burying your dead in any of our cemeteries.”
[Genesis] [23]:[7] Then Avraham stood and bowed to the Hitim who were the land-owners,
[Genesis] [23]:[8] and asked them, “Since you’re all allowing me to bury my dead, listen to me and intercede for me with Tsohar’s son Efron,
[Genesis] [23]:[9] so that he’ll sell me Makpelah’s cave which belongs to him and which is at the end of his field. I’ll pay full price if he’ll give it to me to use as a burial place.”
[Genesis] [23]:[10] Now Efron (a Hiti) was sitting there among Het’s other descendants, so he responded to Avraham while the other land-owners were listening, along with everyone else at the city gate,
[Genesis] [23]:[11] “No, my master. Listen to me: I’ll give you the field and the cave that’s in it. I give it to you in front of all these others, then you can bury your dead.”
[Genesis] [23]:[12] Then Avraham bowed before the people of the land,
[Genesis] [23]:[13] and he told Efron while all the others were listening, “But if you would, please listen to me. I’ll pay the value of the field. Accept it from me, then I’ll bury my dead there.”
[Genesis] [23]:[14] Efron responded to Avraham,
[Genesis] [23]:[15] “My master, listen to me. That land’s worth 400 shekels of silver, but that’s nothing between me and you. Just go ahead and bury your dead.”
[Genesis] [23]:[16] So Avraham accepted Efron’s words and weighed out for Efron the price that he had mentioned in the hearing of Het’s descendants: 400 shekels of silver (the currency among the merchants).
[Genesis] [23]:[17] So Efron’s field that was in Makpelah which faced Mamre (including the field and the cave that was in it, and all the trees that were in the field that was within all of its surrounding borders) was deeded
[Genesis] [23]:[18] to Avraham as the new owner as witnessed by Het’s descendants and everyone else who had come to the city gate.
[Genesis] [23]:[19] Then after that, Avraham laid the body of his wife Sarah to rest in the cave in Makpelah’s field facing Mamre (also called Hevron, in the Kena’an (Canaan) region).
[Genesis] [23]:[20] So the field was deeded as property to Avraham by Het’s descendants, including the cave in it for a burial place.
[Genesis] [24]:[1] Avraham was now getting very old, and Yahweh had blessed him in every way.
[Genesis] [24]:[2] Then Avraham said to his oldest slave in his household who was in charge of everything that belonged to him, “Please put your hand under my thigh,
[Genesis] [24]:[3] and I want you to vow by Yahweh, the god of the heavens and the god of the earth, that you won’t select a wife for my son Yitshak (Isaac) from any of the Kena’ani (Canaanite) women in this area where we’re living.
[Genesis] [24]:[4] Rather, you should go back to my country and to my relatives, and find a wife for him there.”
[Genesis] [24]:[5] “Suppose the woman isn’t willing to come back with me to this place?” the slave asked. “Should I take your son back to the country that you came from?”
[Genesis] [24]:[6] “Make sure that you don’t take my son back there,” Avraham answered.
[Genesis] [24]:[7] “Yahweh, the god of the heavens, who took me from my father’s house and from the land of my relatives, and who spoke to me and who promised me, saying, ‘I’ll give this land to your descendants,’ he’ll send his messenger ahead of you, and you’ll be guaranteed to bring back a wife for my son from there.
[Genesis] [24]:[8] If it turned out that the woman isn’t willing to come back with you, then you’re released from this vow to me. But still in that case, don’t take my son back there!”
[Genesis] [24]:[9] Then the slave put his hand under the thigh of his master Avraham and promised his that he’d follow those instructions..
[Genesis] [24]:[10] Then the slave took ten of his master’s camels and loaded them with all kinds of good things from his master, and with his own slaves, he travelled to the city of Nahor in the Aram-Naharayim region.
[Genesis] [24]:[11] Then on that first evening, he made the camels kneel down outside the city by the well. It was the time that women come out to fetch water,
[Genesis] [24]:[12] and he prayed, “Yahweh, God of my master Avraham, please cause it to happen right in front of me today that you show kindness toward my master Avraham.
[Genesis] [24]:[13] See, I’m standing by this well, and the young women from the city will be coming out here to fetch water.
[Genesis] [24]:[14] Let it be that if I say to a young woman, ‘Please let me have a drink from your water jar,’ and she says, ‘Sure, and I’ll also get more for your camels,’ let her be the one you have appointed for your slave Yitshak (Isaac). And by finding her, I’ll know that you’ve shown kindness toward my master.”
[Genesis] [24]:[15] Now before he’d even finished speaking, then wow, Rivkah arrived with her empty water jar on her shoulder. (She was Betuel’s daughter—Betuel being the son of Avraham’s brother Nahor and his wife Milkah.)
[Genesis] [24]:[16] The young woman was very beautiful and a virgin who hadn’t slept with a man. She went down to the well and filled her jar and came back up.
[Genesis] [24]:[17] The slave ran to meet her and said, “Can I have a small drink of water from your jar.”
[Genesis] [24]:[18] “Drink, my master,” she said and quickly lowered her jar to her hands and gave him a drink,
[Genesis] [24]:[19] and after she’d finished giving him a drink, she said, “I’ll also get water for your camels until they have finished drinking.”
[Genesis] [24]:[20] Then she hurried and emptied her jar into the trough and ran back to the well to draw more water, and she drew enough water for all his camels
[Genesis] [24]:[21] while Avraham’s slave watched her silently to determine whether Yahweh had made his journey successful or not.
[Genesis] [24]:[22] Then when the camels had finished drinking, the slave took out an expensive gold nose ring and two solid gold bracelets for her arms.
[Genesis] [24]:[23] “Tell me, whose daughter are you?” he asked her. “Is there room at your father’s house for us to stay?”
[Genesis] [24]:[24] “I’m Betuel’s daughter. He’s the son of Nahor and Milkah,” she answered.
[Genesis] [24]:[25] “We’ve got plenty of both straw and fodder for the camels, and there’s also a room where you could stay.”
[Genesis] [24]:[26] Then the slave bowed down and worshipped Yahweh
[Genesis] [24]:[27] and said, “Praised be Yahweh, my master Avraham’s god, who hasn’t relented from his kindness and faithfulness toward my master. As for me, Yahweh has led me on the road to the home of my master’s relatives.”
[Genesis] [24]:[28] Then the young woman ran home and told her mother’s household what had happened.
[Genesis] [24]:[29] Now Rivkah had a brother named Lavan (Laban), and he ran out to the man at the well.
[Genesis] [24]:[30] He had seen the nose ring and the bracelets on his sister’s arms, and when he’d heard his sister Rivkah’s words saying, “This is what the man said to me,” then he went to the man, and indeed, he was there standing by the camels at the spring
[Genesis] [24]:[31] and he invited him, “Come, you who are blessed by Yahweh. Why are you standing out here? I’ve already prepared the house and a place for the camels.”
[Genesis] [24]:[32] So Avraham’s slave went to the house. Then he unloaded the camels and gave them straw and fodder, and water to wash his feet and the feet of the men who were with him.
[Genesis] [24]:[33] Then food was set out for them to eat, but Avraham’s slave said, “I won’t eat until I have said what I have to say.” “Speak then,” Lavan responded.
[Genesis] [24]:[34] “I’m one of Avraham’s slaves,” he said,
[Genesis] [24]:[35] and Yahweh has blessed my master a lot, so that he has become wealthy. Yahweh has given him cattle, sheep and goats, silver and gold, male and female slaves, and camels and donkeys.
[Genesis] [24]:[36] And my master’s wife Sarah gave birth to a son for my master despite her old age, and my master has given him everything that he owns.
[Genesis] [24]:[37] My master made promises, saying, ‘You mustn’t get a wife for my son from Kena’ani (Canaanite) women whose land I am living in,
[Genesis] [24]:[38] but rather you must go to my father’s house and to my clan, and find a wife for my son there.’
[Genesis] [24]:[39] Then I asked my master, ‘Suppose the woman refuses to come with me?’
[Genesis] [24]:[40] And he replied, ‘The god Yahweh that I obey, he’ll send his messenger with you and make your journey succeed, so that you’ll find a wife for my son from my clan, and from my father’s house.
[Genesis] [24]:[41] Then you’ll be free of your promise: When you go to my clan, and if they won’t allow her to return with you, then you’ll be clear from this promise.’
[Genesis] [24]:[42] “Then today I came to the well, and I said, ‘Yahweh, God of my master Avraham, if it’s what you want, make my journey succeed that I have come on.
[Genesis] [24]:[43] Listen, I’m standing by this well, so let it be that the young woman who comes out to fetch water and I say to her, “Please give me a little water to drink from your jar,”
[Genesis] [24]:[44] and she replies to me, “Sure, drink, and I will also get water for your camels,” let her be the wife that Yahweh has chosen for the my master’s son.’
[Genesis] [24]:[45] Before I’d finished speaking in my heart, then wow, Rivkah was coming out with her jar on her shoulder. And she went down to the well and drew water, and I asked her, ‘Can I have a drink.’
[Genesis] [24]:[46] So she hurried and lowered her jar from her shoulder and said, ‘Drink, and I’ll also water your camels.’ So I drank and she also watered the camels.
[Genesis] [24]:[47] Then I asked her, ‘Whose daughter are you?’ And she said, ‘The daughter of Betuel, a son of Nahor and his wife Milkah.’ Then I put the ring on her nose and the bracelets on her arms.
[Genesis] [24]:[48] Then I bowed down and worshipped and praised my master Avraham’s god Yahweh, who led me on the right way to find the daughter of my master’s brother for his son.
[Genesis] [24]:[49] And now if you all want to show kindness and faithfulness to my master, tell me. But if not, tell me, so that I can decide what to do next.”
[Genesis] [24]:[50] Then Lavan (Laban) and Betuel answered, “This matter has come from Yahweh, so we’re not able to tell you bad or good.
[Genesis] [24]:[51] But listen, Rivkah’s right here. Take her and go, and let her become the wife of your master’s son, as Yahweh has indicated.”
[Genesis] [24]:[52] Now when Avraham’s slave heard their reply, he bowed down to the ground before Yahweh.
[Genesis] [24]:[53] Then he brought out silver and gold jewellery, and clothing, and gave them to Rivkah. And he gave valuable things to her brother and her mother.
[Genesis] [24]:[54] Then Avraham’s slave and the men with him ate and drank and stayed there overnight. Then in the morning they got up, and he said, “Let me leave now and return back to my master.”
[Genesis] [24]:[55] But Rivkah’s brother and her mother said, “Let the girl stay with us a few days, at least ten. After that she can go.”
[Genesis] [24]:[56] “Don’t detain me,” he told them, “since Yahweh has made my journey successful. Send me off so that I can return to my master.”
[Genesis] [24]:[57] “Let’s call for the young woman and find out what she wants to do.” they responded.
[Genesis] [24]:[58] So they called for Rivkah and asked her, “Are you prepared to leave now with this man?” “Yes, I’ll go.” she answered.
[Genesis] [24]:[59] So they got ready to send off their sister Rivkah with Avraham’s slave and his men, along with her childhood nurse.
[Genesis] [24]:[60] They prayed a blessed for Rivkah, saying “Our sister, may you become the mother of thousands, and may your descendants defeat all of their enemies.”
[Genesis] [24]:[61] Then Rivkah got up with her maids, and they mounted the camels and went with the man. So the slave took Rivkah and left.
[Genesis] [24]:[62] Meanwhile Yitshak (Isaac) was living in the Negev region, and had just returned from visiting Be’er-Lahay-Ro’i.
[Genesis] [24]:[63] Late on afternoon, he went out to the countryside to meditate, and when he looked up, he saw some camels approaching.
[Genesis] [24]:[64] Rivkah also looked up and saw Yitshak, and dismounted from her camel,
[Genesis] [24]:[65] asking the slave, “Who’s that man out in the countryside who’s coming to meet us?” “He’s my master,” the slave replied, so she took the veil and covered herself.
[Genesis] [24]:[66] Then the slave reported everything that he’d done to Yitshak.
[Genesis] [24]:[67] Then Yitshak brought her into the tent of Sarah his mother, and he took Rivkah as his wife. And Yitshak loved her and he was comforted after his mother’s death.
[Genesis] [25]:[1] Then Avraham married another woman named Keturah,
[Genesis] [25]:[2] and she gave birth to Zimran, Yakeshan, Medan, Midyan, Yishbak, and Shuah.
[Genesis] [25]:[3] Yakeshan fathered Sheva and Dedan, and the descendants of Dedan were the Ashurim, the Letushim, and the Le’umim.
[Genesis] [25]:[4] Midyan’s sons were Eyfah, Efer, Hanok, Avida, and Elda’ah. All of those were Keturah’s descendants.
[Genesis] [25]:[5] Avraham went on to live to be 175 years old. He gave valuable gifts to all the sons of his slave-wives, then he forced them to move to the east to ensure that they would be removed from his son Yitshak (Isaac). Then he left everything else he owned to Yitshak.
[Genesis] [25]:[8] Then Avraham breathed his last and died at a good old age, elderly and satisfied, and he joined his ancestors in death.
[Genesis] [25]:[9] His sons Yitshak and Yishmael (Ishmael) buried him in Makpelah’s cave (in the field of Efron, Tsohar the Hiti’s son, which faced Mamre)—
[Genesis] [25]:[10] the field that Avraham had bought from Het’s sons. So Avraham’s body was laid there alongside that of his wife Sarah.
[Genesis] [25]:[11] After his death, God blessed his son Yitshak who lived near Be’er-Lahay-Ro’i.
[Genesis] [25]:[12] Now these are the generations of Yishmael (Ishmael) the son of Avraham, whom Hagar the Mitsri (Egyptian), Sarah’s female slave, had given birth to for Avraham.
[Genesis] [25]:[13] These are the names of Yishmael’s sons, by their names according to their births: Yishmael’s firstborn was Nevayot, then Kedar, Adbe’el, Mivsam,
[Genesis] [25]:[14] Mishma, Dumah, Masa,
[Genesis] [25]:[15] Hadad, Teyma, Yetur, Nafish, and Kedemah.
[Genesis] [25]:[16] Those were Yishmael’s sons, and those are their names by their settlements and by their camps—twelve rulers according to their tribes.
[Genesis] [25]:[17] Yishmael went on to live to be 137 years old, before breathing his last and dying and joining those who’d gone before.
[Genesis] [25]:[18] His descendants settled from Havilah to Shur (which is near Mitsrayim (Egypt) as you go toward Ashur (Assyria)). He fell in the face of all his brothers.
[Genesis] [25]:[19] These are the generations of Avraham’s son Yitshak (Isaac): Avraham fathered Yitshak
[Genesis] [25]:[20] and Yitshak was forty years old when he married Rivkah. (She was the daughter of Betuel the Aramean from Padan-Aram, the sister of Lavan (Laban) the Aramean.)
[Genesis] [25]:[21] In due course, Yitshak prayed to Yahweh on his wife’s behalf because she was barren. Yahweh answered his prayer and his wife Rivkah got pregnant,
[Genesis] [25]:[22] but the twins kept jostling each other within her womb, so she asked, “Why’s this happening to me?” She also asked Yahweh about it
[Genesis] [25]:[23] and he responded, “There’s two nations inside your womb— two different peoples will come from within you. One group will become stronger than the other, and the older will serve the younger.”
[Genesis] [25]:[24] When the time came to give birth, she gave birth to twin boys.
[Genesis] [25]:[25] The firstborn came out quite red and covered with hair like a fur coat, so they named him ‘Esav’ (Esau) (which means ‘hairy’).
[Genesis] [25]:[26] Then his brother was born and his hand grabbed Esav’s heel, so he was named ‘Ya’akov’ (Jacob) (which means ‘heel-grabber’). Yitshak (Isaac) was sixty years old when they were born.
[Genesis] [25]:[27] As the boys grew up, Esav (Esau) got good at hunting, a man of the outdoors, but Ya’akov (Jacob) was a quiet man who stayed around the tents.
[Genesis] [25]:[28] Yitshak (Isaac) liked the taste of game meat so he loved Esav, but Rivkah loved Ya’akov.
[Genesis] [25]:[29] One day, Ya’akov was cooking some stew when Esav arrived home from being out, and he was very hungry
[Genesis] [25]:[30] and asked Ya’akov, “I’m starving—can I have some of that yummy-looking red stuff.” (After that, Esav’s nickname became ‘Edom’, meaning ‘red’.)
[Genesis] [25]:[31] “Well, now,” Ya’akov answered, “sell me your future inheritance.”
[Genesis] [25]:[32] “Listen, I’m dying of starvation,” said Esav, “so what use would a future inheritance be to me?”
[Genesis] [25]:[33] “Well then, make a vow to me,” insisted Ya’akov. So Esav promised him, effectively selling his future inheritance to Ya’akov,
[Genesis] [25]:[34] and Ya’akov gave him some of the lentil stew and some bread. So Esav ate and drank and left again, thus despising his own inheritance as firstborn son.
[Genesis] [26]:[1] Then there was a famine in the region (a different one from the earlier famine that was in the days of Avraham) so Yitshak (Isaac) moved to Gerar, the region of Avimelek, the Pelishtim king.
[Genesis] [26]:[2] Then Yahweh appeared to Yitshak and told him, “Don’t go down to Mitsrayim (Egypt)—stay in the area that I’ll tell you.
[Genesis] [26]:[3] Stay as a guest in this region, and I’ll be with you and bless you, because I’ll give all this land to you and to your descendants, and I’ll confirm the oath that I made to your father Avraham.
[Genesis] [26]:[4] I’ll multiply your descendants to be as numerous as the stars in the sky, and I’ll give all this region to them. And all the nations on the earth will be blessed through your descendants,
[Genesis] [26]:[5] because Avraham obeyed me by keeping my requirements, my commands, my decrees, and my laws.”
[Genesis] [26]:[6] So Yitshak settled there in Gerar.
[Genesis] [26]:[7] Then the men of the place asked about his wife, and he said, “She’s my sister,” because he was afraid to say, “She’s my wife.” He was thinking, “What if the men in this place kill me because Rivkah is so beautiful to look at.”
[Genesis] [26]:[8] Then when he’d been in that area for quite a while, the Pelishti King Avimelek looked down from a window and saw that to his surprise, Yitshak was laughing together with his wife Rivkah.
[Genesis] [26]:[9] So Avimelek called for Yitshak and said, “Hey, she’s really your wife! So how could you say, ‘She’s my sister’?” “Because I said to myself, ‘I might die because of her.’,” Yitshak replied.
[Genesis] [26]:[10] “What’s this that you’ve done to us?” continued Avimelek. “One of my people might easily have slept with your wife and you would have brought condemnation onto us!”
[Genesis] [26]:[11] Then King Avimelek ordered all the people, “Anyone who touches this man or his wife will certainly be killed.”
[Genesis] [26]:[12] Then Yitshak planted a crop in that land and Yahweh blessed him and gave him one hundred times as much as he’d planted.
[Genesis] [26]:[13] Hence he became wealthier and that repeated until eventually he was very powerful.
[Genesis] [26]:[14] He also owned sheep and goats, and cattle, and many slaves. Because the Pelishtim now envied him,
[Genesis] [26]:[15] they blocked up all the wells that his father’s slaves had dug when his father Avraham had been alive, and they filled them with dirt.
[Genesis] [26]:[16] Then King Avimelek told Yitshak, “You all need to leave this area because you’ve become more powerful than us.”
[Genesis] [26]:[17] So Yitshak left that place and set up camp in the Gerar Valley and settled there.
[Genesis] [26]:[18] Then he returned and dug out the water wells that they had dug in the days of Avraham his father and that the Pelishtim had blocked up after Avraham’s death, and he called them similar names to the ones that his father had called them.
[Genesis] [26]:[19] Then Yitshak’s slaves dug in the valley and found an underground spring with flowing water there.
[Genesis] [26]:[20] But the herdsmen from Gerar quarrelled with Yitshak’s herdsmen, saying, “The water belongs to us.” So he named the well ‘Esek’ (which means ‘dispute’), because they disputed with him.
[Genesis] [26]:[21] Yitshak’s men dug another well, but they quarrelled over it too, so he named it ‘Sitnah’ (which means ‘opposition’).
[Genesis] [26]:[22] Then he moved from there and dug another well, and they didn’t quarrel over it, so he named it ‘Rehovot’ (which means ‘space’), and he said, “Because now Yahweh has made space for us and we’ll be productive in this area.”
[Genesis] [26]:[23] Then from there Yitshak moved down to Be’er-Sheva (Beersheba),
[Genesis] [26]:[24] and Yahweh appeared to him during that night and said, “I am the god of your father Avraham. Don’t be afraid, because I’m with you and I will bless you and multiply your descendants for the sake of my slave Avraham.”
[Genesis] [26]:[25] So Yitshak built an altar there and he prayed to Yahweh. He set up his tents there and his slaves dug a well there.
[Genesis] [26]:[26] Then King Avimelek came to Yitshak (Isaac) from Gerar along with his friend Ahuzat and Pikol the commander of his army
[Genesis] [26]:[27] and Yitshak asked them, “Why have you come here since you hate me and you forced me away from you?”
[Genesis] [26]:[28] “We have clearly seen that Yahweh has been with you,” they answered, “so we said, ‘There should be an agreement between us’—between us and you. So let us make an agreement with you,
[Genesis] [26]:[29] that you won’t do anything evil against us, just as we did not touch you, and just as we did only did good to you and sent you away in peace. Now you are blessed by Yahweh.”
[Genesis] [26]:[30] Then Yitshak prepared a feast for them, and they all ate and drank together.
[Genesis] [26]:[31] The visitors got up early the next morning and make promises to each other. Then Yitshak sent them on their way, and they left from there in peace.
[Genesis] [26]:[32] That very day, Yitshak’s slaves came and updated him about the well that they had just been digging and told him, “We’ve found water.”
[Genesis] [26]:[33] So Yitshak named the well ‘Shiv’ah’ (which sounds like the Hebrew word meaning ‘promise’), so that’s why that city is named ‘Be’er-Sheva’ (Beersheba) (meaning ‘well of the promise’) to this day.
[Genesis] [26]:[34] When Esav (Esau) was forty years old, he married two Hiti women: Be’eri’s daughter Yehudit (Judith) and Eylon’s daughter Basemat,
[Genesis] [26]:[35] but this brought grief to his parents Yitshak (Isaac) and Rivkah.
[Genesis] [27]:[1] When Yitshak (Isaac) grew old and could no longer see, he called his older son Esav (Esau) and said to him, “My son.” “I’m here,” Esav replied.
[Genesis] [27]:[2] “Please listen,” Yitshak continued, “I’m old and don’t know how long I’ve got before I die.
[Genesis] [27]:[3] So please take your weapons—your quiver, and your bow—and go out into the countryside and hunt game for me
[Genesis] [27]:[4] and cook me a tasty meal in the way that I love it, and bring it to me so I can eat it, so that I can bless you before I die.”
[Genesis] [27]:[5] Now Rivkah had been listening while Yitshak spoke to Esav. Then Esav went out to the countryside to hunt game and bring it back.
[Genesis] [27]:[6] Meanwhile Rivkah said to her son Ya’akov (Jacob), “Listen, I heard your father speaking to your brother Esav, saying,
[Genesis] [27]:[7] ‘Get some game meat for me and prepare me a tasty meal so that I can eat it, and then I can bless you in Yahweh’s presence before I die.’
[Genesis] [27]:[8] So now Ya’akov, listen to what I tell you:
[Genesis] [27]:[9] Go out to the flock and get me two of the best young goats so that I can prepare a tasty meal from them that your father loves.
[Genesis] [27]:[10] Then you can take it in to your father, and after he’s eaten it, he’ll bless you before he dies.”
[Genesis] [27]:[11] “Look,” Ya’akov said to his mother, “My brother Esav is very hairy, whereas my skin is smooth.
[Genesis] [27]:[12] What if my father touches me? Then he’ll think of me as a deceiver and he’ll curse me rather than bless me.”
[Genesis] [27]:[13] “Let your curse be on me, my son,” his mother replied, “Just do what I said and go get the young goats for me.”
[Genesis] [27]:[14] So he went and slaughtered them and brought them to his mother. Then she prepared tasty food the way his father loved it.
[Genesis] [27]:[15] She then got Esav’s best clothes that were in the house and got her younger son Ya’akov to put them on,
[Genesis] [27]:[16] and then she tied the skins of the young goats over his hands and around the smooth part of his neck.
[Genesis] [27]:[17] Then she handed the tasty food and the bread to Ya’akov,
[Genesis] [27]:[18] and he went in to his elderly father and said, “My father.” “I’m here,” he said, “Which son are you?”
[Genesis] [27]:[19] “I’m your oldest son Esav,” Ya’akov replied to his father. “I’ve done what you told me. Please get up, and come and sit up and eat some of my game, so that you’ll bless me.”
[Genesis] [27]:[20] “How did you find it so quickly, my son?” Yitshak (Isaac) asked. “Because your god Yahweh helped me when I went out hunting,” Ya’akov answered.
[Genesis] [27]:[21] Then Yitshak said to Ya’akov, “Please come close so that I can touch you, my son, and to be sure whether you’re really my son Esav or not.”
[Genesis] [27]:[22] So Ya’akov went close to his father and Yitshak felt his skin and said to himself, “It’s Ya’akov’s voice, but these are definitely Esav’s hands.”
[Genesis] [27]:[23] So he didn’t recognise that it was Ya’akov, because his hands were hairy like Esav’s hands, so he was about to bless him
[Genesis] [27]:[24] but asked once more, “Are you really my son Esav?” “Yes, I am,” Ya’akov answered.
[Genesis] [27]:[25] So Yitshak told him, “Bring the food here and I’ll eat some of my son’s game, so that I can then bless you.” So Ya’akov took it to him and he ate, and then he brought wine to him and he drank.
[Genesis] [27]:[26] Then Yitshak asked Ya’akov, “My son, please come close and kiss me.”
[Genesis] [27]:[27] So he went close and kissed him. His dad noticed the smell of his clothes, so he blessed him saying, “Ah yes, the smell of my son is like the pleasant fragrance of the countryside that Yahweh has blessed.
[Genesis] [27]:[28] May God give you dew from the sky and riches from the land, to produce plenty of grain and wine.
[Genesis] [27]:[29] May peoples serve you, and may nations bow down to you. Be master over your brothers, and may your mother’s sons bow down to you. May those who curse you be cursed, and may those who bless you be blessed.”
[Genesis] [27]:[30] Then just as Yitshak (Isaac) had finished blessing Ya’akov (Jacob), and as Ya’akov had only just gone out from his father’s presence, his brother Esav (Esau) his brother returned from his hunting.
[Genesis] [27]:[31] Then he too prepared some tasty food and brought it in to his father and said, “Let my father get up and eat from the game that his son hunted so that you can bless me.”
[Genesis] [27]:[32] But Yitshak asked him, “Which son are you?” “I’m your oldest son Esav.” he answered.
[Genesis] [27]:[33] Then Yitshak started to trembled badly and he said, “Then who was it that hunted game and brought it to me? I ate it all just before you came in, and I blessed that man and indeed, he’ll be blessed.”
[Genesis] [27]:[34] When Esav heard that, then he let out a very loud and exceedingly bitter wail, and then begged his father, “Bless me too, my father.”
[Genesis] [27]:[35] But Yitshak replied, “Your brother came in and deceived me and he’s taken your blessing!”
[Genesis] [27]:[36] “Yes, his name Ya’akov (Jacob) (meaning ‘deceiver’) suits him exactly!” said Esav. “First he took my inheritance and man, now he’s also taken my blessing!” Then he asked, “Haven’t you at least saved a blessing for me?”
[Genesis] [27]:[37] But Yitshak replied, “Listen, I’ve made him master over you, and I’ve given all his brothers to him as slaves. And I’ve sustained him with grain and wine. So then, what else can I do for you, my son?”
[Genesis] [27]:[38] “My father, Did you only have one blessing that you could give?” Esav asked. “Bless me too, my father!” Then Esav sobbed loudly.
[Genesis] [27]:[39] Then his father Yitshak responded and said to him, “Listen, you and your descendants will live away from the most fertile land on the earth in a place that doesn’t get dew from the sky.
[Genesis] [27]:[40] You and your descendants will live by your sword, and you’ll serve your brother. But when you become restless you’ll all break away from serving them.
[Genesis] [27]:[41] From that time onwards, Esav (Esau) hated Ya’akov (Jacob) because of the blessing that their father had blessed him with, and Esav said to himself, “My father’s funeral can’t be that far away—after that I’ll kill my brother Ya’akov.”
[Genesis] [27]:[42] But Rivkah got to hear about Esav’s plans, so she sent for her younger son Ya’akov and told him, “Listen, your brother Esav is coping with what happened by planning to kill you.
[Genesis] [27]:[43] So my son, listen to what I’m saying: for your own sake, pack up and flee to my brother Lavan’s (Laban) place in Haran
[Genesis] [27]:[44] and stay with him for a while until your brother cools down.
[Genesis] [27]:[45] When he’s no longer angry with you and forgets what you did to him, then I’ll send for you from there so you can return here. I don’t want to lose both of you on the same day.”
[Genesis] [27]:[46] Then Rivkah told her husband Yitshak (Isaac), “I’m quite disgusted with those daughters of Het. If Ya’akov (Jacob) chooses a wife like Het’s daughters from this culture around us here, I wouldn’t be able to bear it.”
[Genesis] [28]:[1] So Yitshak called for Ya’akov and blessed him, and instructed him, “Don’t take a wife from the Kena’ani (Canaanite) girls.
[Genesis] [28]:[2] Pack up and go to Padan-Aram—to the home of your mother’s father Betuel and get yourself a wife from there—from the daughters of your mother’s brother Lavan (Laban).
[Genesis] [28]:[3] And may the powerful God bless you and make you fruitful and multiply you so that you become a community of peoples.
[Genesis] [28]:[4] May he give the same blessing of Avraham to you—to you and to your offspring with you—so that you will own the land where you’ve been staying and which God gave to Avraham.”
[Genesis] [28]:[5] Then Yitshak sent Ya’akov away, and he went to Padan-Aram—to Lavan, the son of Betuel the Aramean and the brother of Ya’akov and Esav’s (Esau) mother Rivkah.
[Genesis] [28]:[6] Now Esav (Esau) noticed that Yitshak (Isaac) had blessed Ya’akov (Jacob) and sent him to Padan-Aram to take a wife for himself from there. He’d also noticed that when Yitshak had blessed him, he’d instructed him not to take a wife from the Kena’ani (Canaanite) girls,
[Genesis] [28]:[7] and that Ya’akov had listened to his parents and travelled to Padan-Aram.
[Genesis] [28]:[8] As a result, Esav realised that his father wasn’t happy about the Kena’ani girls
[Genesis] [28]:[9] so he went to Yishmael (Ishmael) and he took Mahalat as an additional wife. She was the daughter of Avraham’s son Yishmael, and was the sister of Nevayot.
[Genesis] [28]:[10] Meanwhile, Ya’akov (Jacob) had left Be’er-Sheva (Beersheba) and was enroute to Haran.
[Genesis] [28]:[11] One night after he’d stopped when the sun had gone down, he laid down in that place and used one of the stones there to put under his head for a pillow.
[Genesis] [28]:[12] While he was sleeping, he had a dream, and wow, a stairway was set up on the earth and its top reached to the heavens, and look, God’s messengers were ascending and descending on it.
[Genesis] [28]:[13] And look, Yahweh was standing above it and he said, “I am Yahweh, the god of Avraham your grandfather and the god of Yitshak (Isaac). I will give the land that you are lying on to you and to your descendants
[Genesis] [28]:[14] and they will be as numerous as dust particles, and you’ll all spread out to the west and to the east and to the north and to the south. And all the families of the earth will be blessed through you and your offspring.
[Genesis] [28]:[15] So listen, I’m with you and I’ll watch over you everywhere you go. I’ll bring you back to this land because I won’t leave you until I’ve done what I told you.”
[Genesis] [28]:[16] Then Ya’akov woke up and said to himself, “Yahweh is certainly here in this place, but I didn’t realise it.”
[Genesis] [28]:[17] So he was afraid and said to himself, “This place is spine-chilling—it’s nothing other than God’s house, and it’s heaven’s gateway.”
[Genesis] [28]:[18] Then in the morning Ya’akov got up early, and he took the stone that he’d put under his head and stood it up longways as a pillar, and he poured oil over the top of it.
[Genesis] [28]:[19] He named that place ‘Beyt-El’ (Bethel) (which means ‘God’s house’), even though that town had been named Luz before then.
[Genesis] [28]:[20] Then Ya’akov made a promise to God, saying, “If God will be with me and watch over me on this road that I’m walking on, and give me bread to eat and clothes to wear,
[Genesis] [28]:[21] and if I’m able to return safely to my father’s home, then I’ll make Yahweh my god,
[Genesis] [28]:[22] and this stone that I’ve stood up as a pillar will be God’s house, and I’ll give you a tenth of everything that you give to me.”
[Genesis] [29]:[1] Then Ya’akov (Jacob) got on the road again and went to the land of the eastern peoples.
[Genesis] [29]:[2] Close to his destination, he looked ahead, and wow, there was a well in the countryside, and what’s more, three flocks of sheep and goats were lying there near it, because the flocks were watered from that well but the stone over the mouth of the well was large and heavy.
[Genesis] [29]:[3] Once all the flocks were gathered there, then they would roll the stone from over the mouth of the well and water the animals. Then they would return the stone to its place over the mouth of the well.
[Genesis] [29]:[4] So Ya’akov asked the farmers, “My brothers, where are you from?” “We’re from Haran,” they replied.
[Genesis] [29]:[5] “Do you know Nahor’s grandson Lavan (Laban)?” Ya’akov asked. “Yes, we know him,” they replied.
[Genesis] [29]:[6] “Is he doing well?” Ya’akov asked. “Yes, he’s fine,” they said, “and here comes his daughter Rahel (Rachel) with their flock.”
[Genesis] [29]:[7] “Look, it’s still broad daylight,” Ya’akov told them. “It’s not time for the livestock to be brought it. Water the flock, and go pasture them.”
[Genesis] [29]:[8] “We can’t,” they said, “until all the flocks are gathered here and they roll the stone off the top of the well. Then we will water the sheep.”
[Genesis] [29]:[9] He was still talking with them when Rahel came with her father’s flock, because she was the one who looked after them.
[Genesis] [29]:[10] When Ya’akov saw Rahel (the daughter of his mother’s brother, Lavan (Laban)) with Lavan’s flock, he went over and rolled the stone off the top of the well and watered the sheep and goats.
[Genesis] [29]:[11] Then he gave Rahel a kiss and happily cried out loud.
[Genesis] [29]:[12] Then he told Rahel that he was a relative of her father and that he was a son of Rivkah. Then she ran and told her father,
[Genesis] [29]:[13] and when Lavan heard the news about his sister’s son Ya’akov, he ran out to meet him. Then he embraced him and kissed him and brought him to his house. Then Ya’akov told Lavan everything that had happened up until then,
[Genesis] [29]:[14] and Lavan told him, “You are indeed a close relative.” After Ya’akov (Jacob) had stayed with Lavan (Laban) and worked for him for a whole month,
[Genesis] [29]:[15] Lavan said to him, “Should you work for me for nothing just because you’re my relative? Tell me, what should I pay you?”
[Genesis] [29]:[16] Now Lavan had two daughters: the older one was named Le’ah, and the younger one was named Rahel (Rachel).
[Genesis] [29]:[17] Le’ah had pretty eyes, but Rahel was extremely beautiful in every way.
[Genesis] [29]:[18] Now Ya’akov was in love with Rahel, so he answered, “I’ll work for you for seven years so I can marry your younger daughter Rahel.”
[Genesis] [29]:[19] “Okay, stay with me then,” said Lavan. “It’s better for me to give her to you than to give her to some other man.”
[Genesis] [29]:[20] So Ya’akov worked seven years for Rahel, but it only seemed like a few days to him because of his love for her,
[Genesis] [29]:[21] then he said to Lavan, “Give me my wife to marry now because I’ve worked the agreed seven years.”
[Genesis] [29]:[22] So Lavan invited all the local people and held a wedding reception,
[Genesis] [29]:[23] but that evening Lavan brought his other daughter Le’ah to Ya’akov, and he slept with her.
[Genesis] [29]:[24] (Lavan also gave his female slave Zilpah to Le’ah to be her personal slave.)
[Genesis] [29]:[25] But in the morning, Ya’akov saw that wow, it was Le’ah! “Hey, what’s this that you’ve done to me?” Ya’akov demanded of Lavan. “Wasn’t it Rahel that I worked for you for? So why did you deceive me?”
[Genesis] [29]:[26] “It’s not our custom here,” Lavan answered, “for the younger daughter to marry before the older one.
[Genesis] [29]:[27] Stay with just this one for the marriage week, and then we’ll also give you the younger one in return for another seven year’s work.”
[Genesis] [29]:[28] So Ya’akov agreed and spent the week with Le’ah, then Lavan also gave him his daughter Rahel to be his wife.
[Genesis] [29]:[29] (Lavan also gave his female slave Bilhah to Rahel to be her personal slave.)
[Genesis] [29]:[30] So Ya’akov also slept with Rahel, but he also loved her more than Le’ah. Then he worked for Lavan for another seven years.
[Genesis] [29]:[31] Now Yahweh saw that Le’ah was spurned, so he allowed her to conceive, but Rahel (Rachel) was unable to get pregnant.
[Genesis] [29]:[32] So Le’ah got pregnant and gave birth to a son, and she named him ‘Re’uven’ (which means ‘Look, a son’) because she said, “Because Yahweh has looked on my misery, surely my husband will love me now.”
[Genesis] [29]:[33] Then she got pregnant again and gave birth to a second son, and she said, “Because Yahweh heard that I am hated, then he also gave me this son.” So she called his name ‘Shim’on’ (Simeon) (which means ‘he hears’).
[Genesis] [29]:[34] Then she got pregnant again and gave birth to a third son, and she said, “This time now my husband will hold me close to him, because I’ve given him three sons.” That’s why she named the baby ‘Levi’ (which means ‘hold close’).
[Genesis] [29]:[35] Then Le’ah got pregnant again and gave birth to a fourth son, and she said, “This time I will praise Yahweh.” That’s why she named him ‘Yehudah’ (Judah) (which means ‘praise’). Then she stopped getting pregnant.
[Genesis] [30]:[1] Now Rahel realised that she wasn’t producing any children for Ya’akov (Jacob), so she envied her sister Le’ah, and she demanded from Ya’akov, “Give me children, and if you don’t, I’ll die!”
[Genesis] [30]:[2] But Ya’akov’s anger flared up against Rahel and he asked, “Am I in the place of God who’s kept you from getting pregnant?”
[Genesis] [30]:[3] Rahel answered, “Listen, here’s my slave Bilhah. Sleep with her so that she’ll have children on my behalf and I’ll also be able to have a family through her.”
[Genesis] [30]:[4] Then she gave Bilhah to him as a slave wife and Ya’akov slept with her,
[Genesis] [30]:[5] so then Bilhah got pregnant and produced a son for Ya’akov.
[Genesis] [30]:[6] Rahel said, “God has vindicated me, and indeed he’s listened to my request and given me a son!” That’s why she named him ‘Dan’ (which means ‘he judged (in my favour)’).
[Genesis] [30]:[7] Later on, Rahel’s slave Bilhah got pregnant again and gave birth to a second son for Ya’akov

[Genesis] [30]:[9] Now when Le’ah noticed that she wasn’t getting pregnant any more, she gave her female slave Zilpah to Ya’akov as a slave wife.
[Genesis] [30]:[10] Then eventually Le’ah’s slave Zilpah produced a son for Ya’akov,
[Genesis] [30]:[11] and Le’ah said, “What good fortune!” So she named him ‘Gad’ (which means ‘fortunate’).
[Genesis] [30]:[12] Then Le’ah’s slave Zilpah produced a second son for Ya’akov,
[Genesis] [30]:[13] and Le’ah said, “How blessed I am because women will call me blessed.” So she named him ‘Asher’ (which means ‘blessed’).
[Genesis] [30]:[14] One day during the wheat harvest, Re’uven went out and found some mandrake plants in the countryside and brought them home to Le’ah his mother. Then Rahel asked Le’ah, “Please give me some of your son’s mandrakes.”
[Genesis] [30]:[15] “Is it a small matter you have taken my husband?” Le’ah snapped back. “And would you also take my son’s mandrakes?” “Well, he can sleep with you tonight in exchange for your son’s mandrakes.” Rahel answered.
[Genesis] [30]:[16] So that evening when Ya’akov came home from the countryside, Le’ah went out to meet him and told him, “You must come to me tonight because I’ve hired you with my son’s mandrakes.” So he slept with her that night.
[Genesis] [30]:[17] God listened to Le’ah and she got pregnant and produced a fifth son for Ya’akov,
[Genesis] [30]:[18] saying, “God has given me my reward because I gave my slave to my husband to sleep with.” So she named him ‘Yisakar’ (Issachar) (which means ‘reward’).
[Genesis] [30]:[19] Then Le’ah got pregnant again and produced a sixth son for Ya’akov,
[Genesis] [30]:[20] saying, “God has given me a nice present. This time my husband will honour me because I have produced six sons for him.” So she called his name ‘Zevulun’ (which might mean ‘honour’).
[Genesis] [30]:[21] Later on, Le’ah had a daughter and named her Dinah.
[Genesis] [30]:[22] Then God paid attention to Rahel and listened to her and enabled her to conceive,
[Genesis] [30]:[23] so she got pregnant and produced a son, and said, “God has taken away my disgrace.”
[Genesis] [30]:[24] She named him ‘Yosef’ (Joseph) (which means ‘may he give another’), saying, “May Yahweh add another son to me.”
[Genesis] [30]:[25] Sometime after Rahel (Rachel) had given birth to Yosef (Joseph), Ya’akov (Jacob) said to Lavan (Laban), “Send me off now, so that I can return to my place and to my land.
[Genesis] [30]:[26] Let me take my wives that I worked for you for, and take my children so that I can leave, because you yourself know how long and hard I’ve worked for you.”
[Genesis] [30]:[27] But Lavan replied, “Please stay, if I’ve found favour in your eyes because I’ve learnt by divination that Yahweh has blessed me because of you.”
[Genesis] [30]:[28] Then he added, “Tell me how much you want and I’ll pay you that.”
[Genesis] [30]:[29] “You yourself know how well I’ve served you and how your livestock have prospered with me.” Ya’akov replied.
[Genesis] [30]:[30] Before I came, you didn’t have much, but now you have plenty because Yahweh has blessed you wherever I was involved. But now, when will I also do something for my own household?”
[Genesis] [30]:[31] “What should I give you?” Lavan asked. “You don’t have to give me anything,” Ya’akov replied. “If you’ll do this one thing for me, I’ll continue taking care of your flocks:
[Genesis] [30]:[32] Let me look through all your flocks today and separate out from them all the lambs that are speckled, spotted, or dark-coloured, and all the young goats that are spotted or speckled. They will be my pay.
[Genesis] [30]:[33] So in the future, you’ll be able to see that I’ve been honest because you’ll be able to see it for yourself: any goat that’s not speckled and spotted, and any sheep that’s not dark-coloured, if it’s in my flock then it must have been stolen.”
[Genesis] [30]:[34] “Okay then, let’s do it your way.” Lavan agreed.
[Genesis] [30]:[35] But that very day, he removed the male goats that were streaked and spotted, and all the female goats that were speckled and spotted, any that had white on it, and all the dark-coloured ones among the lambs. Then he gave them to his sons to look after,

[Genesis] [30]:[37] Then Ya’akov got some freshly cut branches of poplar and almond and plane trees, and peeled white stripes in them by exposing the white that was inside the branches.
[Genesis] [30]:[38] Then he put the branches that he had peeled in the water troughs where the flocks would see them when they came to drink, and they mated when they came to drink.
[Genesis] [30]:[39] Thus the flocks would mate by the striped branches, and they would bear young who were streaked, speckled, and spotted.
[Genesis] [30]:[40] Then Ya’akov separated out those young animals into a separate flock, and he made the older flocks look at the streaked and all the dark-coloured animals in Lavan’s flocks. So he kept his own flocks by themselves and didn’t mix them with Lavan’s flocks.
[Genesis] [30]:[41] So whenever the strong animals were ready to mate, then Ya’akov put the branches in the troughs in front of the flocks so that they would mate by the branches,
[Genesis] [30]:[42] but when the animals were weak, he didn’t put them in. So the weak animals went to Lavan and the strong ones to Ya’akov
[Genesis] [30]:[43] so he became very wealthy, and he owned large flocks as well as male and female slaves, and camels and donkeys.
[Genesis] [31]:[1] One day, Ya’akov (Jacob) overheard the words of Lavan’s (Laban) sons who were saying, “Ya’akov has taken everything that belonged to our father, and from what originally belonged to our father he has gained all this wealth.”
[Genesis] [31]:[2] Then Ya’akov also noticed that Lavan’s attitude towards him had changed, and he wasn’t in favour of him like he’d been in the past.
[Genesis] [31]:[3] Then Yahweh told Ya’akov, “Go back to the land of your ancestors and to your relatives, and I’ll be with you.”
[Genesis] [31]:[4] So Ya’akov sent for Rahel (Rachel) and Le’ah to come to him out in the countryside where he was with his flocks
[Genesis] [31]:[5] and he told them, “I’ve noticed your father’s attitude and that he’s not positive toward me like he was a few days ago, but my father’s god has been with me.
[Genesis] [31]:[6] You both know that I’ve served your father with all my strength,
[Genesis] [31]:[7] but your father has deceived me and changed my wages ten times. However, God hasn’t allowed him to harm me.
[Genesis] [31]:[8] When he told me: ‘The speckled animals will be your wages,’ then all the flocks bore speckled young. But when he told me: ‘The streaked ones will be your wages,’ then all the flocks bore streaked young.
[Genesis] [31]:[9] In that way, God took your father’s animals away from him and gave them to me.
[Genesis] [31]:[10] “One day during the season when the flocks were mating, I looked up and saw in a dream that, wow, the male goats that were mounting the flocks were streaked, speckled, and spotted.
[Genesis] [31]:[11] Then God’s messenger said to me in the dream, ‘Ya’akov!’ and I said, ‘I’m listening.’
[Genesis] [31]:[12] Then he told me, ‘Please look up and observe that all the male goats that are mounting the flocks are streaked, speckled, and spotted, because I have seen everything that Lavan (Laban) is doing to you.
[Genesis] [31]:[13] I’m the god of Beyt-El (Bethel), where you anointed a pillar—where you vowed a vow to me. Now pack up and depart from this land, and return to the land where you were born.’ ”
[Genesis] [31]:[14] Then Rahel (Rachel) and Le’ah replied, “Yes, we’re not expecting any portion or inheritance from our father’s property.
[Genesis] [31]:[15] Doesn’t he just treat us like foreigners now? Yes, he sold us and then he frittered away all the money that should have been ours,
[Genesis] [31]:[16] so all the wealth that God took from our father belonged to us and to our children anyway. So yes, go ahead and do everything that God’s told you to do.”
[Genesis] [31]:[17] So Ya’akov packed up and put his wives and children on the camels.
[Genesis] [31]:[18] Then he drove all his livestock and all his property that he had acquired—the livestock in his possession that he had acquired in Padan-Aram—to go back to Yitshak (Isaac) his father in the Kena’an (Canaan) region.
[Genesis] [31]:[19] Now Lavan had gone off for several days to shear his sheep, so Rahel stole the idols that belonged to her father,
[Genesis] [31]:[20] and Ya’akov deceived Lavan (the Arami (Syrian)) by not telling him that they all were leaving.
[Genesis] [31]:[21] So Ya’akov took his household and everything that belonged to them and crossed the Perat (Euphrates) River and headed upward toward the hill-country of Gilead.
[Genesis] [31]:[22] Three days later, Lavan (Laban) was informed that Ya’akov (Jacob) had fled with his family,
[Genesis] [31]:[23] so he took some of his relatives with him and chased after Ya’akov and his family for seven days until they overtook them in the hill-country of Gilead.
[Genesis] [31]:[24] But that night God appeared to Lavan the Arami (Syrian) in a dream and told him, “Watch yourself that you don’t say anything to Ya’akov, either good or bad.”
[Genesis] [31]:[25] When Lavan had caught up to Ya’akov, Ya’akov had pitched their tents in the hills, so Lavan with his relatives also pitched theirs on the Gilead hills.
[Genesis] [31]:[26] Then Lavan said to Ya’akov, “What have you done? You’ve deceived me and carried away my daughters like prisoners of war.
[Genesis] [31]:[27] Why did you flee secretly and deceive me and not tell me? I would have sent you all off with music and singing and a cheery party.
