[Genesis] [36]:[33] Then Bela died, and Zerah’s son Yovav from Batserah reigned in his place.
[Genesis] [36]:[34] Then Yovav died, and Husham from the land of the Teymanin reigned in his place.
[Genesis] [36]:[35] Then Husham died, and Bedad’s son Hadad reigned in his place, and the name of his city was Avit. He was the one who attacked the Midyanites in the countryside in Moav (Moab).
[Genesis] [36]:[36] Then Hadad died, and Samlah from Masrekah reigned in his place.
[Genesis] [36]:[37] Then Samlah died, and Shaul from Rehovot by the river reigned in his place.
[Genesis] [36]:[38] Then Shaul died, and Akbor’s son Ba’al-Hanan reigned in his place.
[Genesis] [36]:[39] Then (Akbor’s son) Ba’al-Hanan died, and Hadar reigned in his place, and the name of his city was Paeu. His wife’s name was Meheytavel (and she was the daughter of Matred’s daughter and the granddaughter of Mey-Zahav).
[Genesis] [36]:[40] And these are the names of the chiefs of Esav (Esau), according to their clans, according to their places, by their names: Chief Timna, Chief Alvan, Chief Yetet,
[Genesis] [36]:[41] Chief Oholivamah, Chief Elah, Chief Pinon,
[Genesis] [36]:[42] Chief Kenaz, Chief Teyman, Chief Mivtsar,
[Genesis] [36]:[43] Chief Magdiyel, and Chief Iram. They were the chiefs of Edom, according to their dwellings in the land of their possession. That was the record about Esav, the ancestor of the Edomim.
[Genesis] [37]:[1] Yisrael (Israel) (also called Ya’akov (Jacob) ) lived in the area where his father Yitshak (Isaac) had stayed, in the Kena’an (Canaan) region.
[Genesis] [37]:[2] This is the record of his descendants: When Yosef (Joseph) was seventeen, he was shepherding the flocks with his brothers. He was younger than his brothers who were the sons of his father’s slave wives Bilhah and Zilpah. One day Yosef gave a tell-tale bad report about them to their father.
[Genesis] [37]:[3] Now Yisrael loved Yosef more than all of his other sons because he was born to him when he was already old, so he made a multicoloured robe for him.
[Genesis] [37]:[4] When his brothers saw that their father loved Yosef more than all of his brothers, they hated him and couldn’t make themselves say anything nice to him.
[Genesis] [37]:[5] One night Yosef had a dream, and he told his brothers about it, but that made them hate him even more.
[Genesis] [37]:[6] He told them, “Please listen about this dream that I had:
[Genesis] [37]:[7] See, we were tying up bundles of grain stalks in the middle of a field, and wow, my bundle got up and stood upright. Then would you believe it, your bundles gathered around and bowed down to my one.”
[Genesis] [37]:[8] “Will you really reign over us?” his brothers retorted. “Do you think you’ll really rule over us?” So they continued to hate him even more because of his dreams and because of what he said.
[Genesis] [37]:[9] Then Yosef had another dream, and again he told his brothers, “Listen, I had another dream, and wow, the sun and the moon and eleven stars were bowing down to me.”
[Genesis] [37]:[10] When he told his father and his brothers, his father scolded him, “What’s this dream that you had? Will your mother and I and your brothers actually come to bow down to the ground to you?”
[Genesis] [37]:[11] Consequently his brothers envied him, but his father kept pondering it.
[Genesis] [37]:[12] Sometime after that, Yosef’s (Joseph) brothers went to shepherd their father’s flocks near Shekem.
[Genesis] [37]:[13] One day, Yisrael (Israel) said to Yosef, “Aren’t your brothers away shepherding near Shekem? Come we’ll get some supplies and I’ll send you to them.” “Sure,” Yosef replied.
[Genesis] [37]:[14] Then he told him, “Please go and see how your brothers are doing and the flocks as well, then come and let me know.” So he sent Yosef off from the Hevron valley, and he went to Shekem.
[Genesis] [37]:[15] When he got there, a man noticed him wandering around the countryside and asked him, “What are you looking for?”
[Genesis] [37]:[16] “I’m looking for my brothers,” he answered. “Please tell me where they’re looking after our flocks.”
[Genesis] [37]:[17] “They’ve left here,” the man responded. “I heard them say, ‘Let’s go to Dotan.’ ” So Yosef continued on after his brothers and found them at Dotan,
[Genesis] [37]:[18] but they saw him from a distance and before he got close to them, they made plans among themselves to kill him.
[Genesis] [37]:[19] “Look, that master dreamer is coming,” they said to each other.
[Genesis] [37]:[20] “Here’s our chance to kill him and throw his body into one of the pits around here. We’ll say that a wild animal attacked him. Then we’ll see what his dreams turn into.”
[Genesis] [37]:[21] But Re’uven heard what they were saying, and he tried to rescue Yosef by insisting, “Let’s not take his life.”
[Genesis] [37]:[22] “Don’t shed blood,” he continued. “Throw him into that pit in the wilderness, but don’t wound him.” He said this because he was planning to rescue Yosef later and return him home to their father.
[Genesis] [37]:[23] So when Yosef reached his brothers, they grabbed him and ripped off the coloured robe that he was wearing.
[Genesis] [37]:[24] Then they took him and dropped him into the pit. (The pit was empty with no water in the bottom).
[Genesis] [37]:[25] Then they sat down to eat, and a bit later when they looked up, look, there was a caravan of Yishmaelim (Ishmaelites) coming towards them. They had left Gilead carrying spices and balm and myrrh on their camels that they were going to take down to Mitsrayim (Egypt).
[Genesis] [37]:[26] Then Yehudah (Judah) said to his brothers, “What will we gain if we kill our brother and cover up his blood?
[Genesis] [37]:[27] Let’s sell him to these Yishmaelim so we won’t be guilty of killing him. After all, he’s our brother—our own flesh and blood.” And his brothers agreed.
[Genesis] [37]:[28] So when the Midyanite traders came past, the brothers pulled Yosef up and lifted him out of the pit and sold him to the Yishmaelim for twenty pieces of silver. Then the traders took Yosef onwards with them to Mitsrayim.
[Genesis] [37]:[29] Later on, Re’uven returned to the pit, but wow, Yosef wasn’t down there, so he tore his clothes in despair
[Genesis] [37]:[30] and returned to his brothers and said, “The boy isn’t there. What am I going to do?”
[Genesis] [37]:[31] Then they slaughtered a young goat and took Yosef’s robe and dipped it in the blood.
[Genesis] [37]:[32] Then they sent the coloured robe back to their father with this message: “We found this. Please examine whether or not it’s your son’s robe.”
[Genesis] [37]:[33] Yisrael (Israel) recognised it and said, “It is my son’s robe. A wild animal must have eaten him. Yosef was almost certainly torn to pieces.”
[Genesis] [37]:[34] Then Ya’akov (Jacob) ripped his clothes and put sackcloth around his waist, and he mourned for his son many days.
[Genesis] [37]:[35] All his other sons and all his daughters came to comfort him, but he refused to be comforted and said, “I will go down to my son in the grave mourning.” So his father wept for him.
[Genesis] [37]:[36] Meanwhile, the Midyanites arrived in Mitsrayim (Egypt) and sold him to Potifar—Par’oh’s (Pharaoh) captain of the guards.
[Genesis] [38]:[1] Around that time, Yehudah (Judah) went down the hills from where his brothers were and settled near an Adulami man named Hirah.
[Genesis] [38]:[2] There Yehudah saw the daughter of a Kena’ani (Canaanite) man named Shua, and he took her as a wife. He slept with her
[Genesis] [38]:[3] and she got pregnant and in due course, gave birth to a son who Yehudah named Er.
[Genesis] [38]:[4] Then she got pregnant again and gave birth a another son, and she named him Onan.
[Genesis] [38]:[5] Then she got pregnant yet again and gave birth to a third son, and she named him Shela. (Yehudah was in Keziv when she Onan was born.)
[Genesis] [38]:[6] In due course, Yehudah took a wife for Er his firstborn, and her name was Tamar.
[Genesis] [38]:[7] But Er was evil in Yahweh’s eyes, so Yahweh killed him.
[Genesis] [38]:[8] Then Yehudah said to Onan, “Go to your brother’s wife and perform your brotherly duty to her to produce children for your brother.”
[Genesis] [38]:[9] However, Onan knew that any children wouldn’t be his, so whenever he slept with his brother’s wife, he spilled his semen on the ground so that he wouldn’t give children to his late brother.
[Genesis] [38]:[10] But Yahweh considered what he did to be evil, so he killed him also.
[Genesis] [38]:[11] Then Yehudah told his daughter-in-law Tamar, “Remain a widow in your father’s house until my son Shela grows up.” This was because he’d said, “So that he doesn’t also die like his brothers!” So Tamar went and lived in the house of her father.
[Genesis] [38]:[12] A long time afterwards, Yehudah’s wife (Shua’s daughter) died. After Yehudah had finished mourning, he and his friend Hirah (the Adulami) went to Timnah to where the men were shearing his sheep.
[Genesis] [38]:[13] Then Tamar was told, “Look, your father-in-law is going to Timnah to shear his sheep.”
[Genesis] [38]:[14] So she changed out of her widow’s clothes and covered herself with a veil and wrapped herself up. Then she sat at the entrance of Enayim which is on the road to Timnah. She was doing this because she had seen that Shela had grown up, but she hadn’t been given to him as a wife.
[Genesis] [38]:[15] In due course, Yehudah saw her and because she had covered her face, he thought she was a prostitute.
[Genesis] [38]:[16] So he turned to her beside the road and asked, “Please let me lie with you,” because he didn’t know that she was his daughter-in-law. “What will you give me in exchange?” she asked.
[Genesis] [38]:[17] “I’ll send you a young goat from my flock,” he replied. “But what about something to keep now as a pledge until you send it,” she bartered.
[Genesis] [38]:[18] “What pledge should I give you?” he asked. “Your signet ring and its cord, and your staff that you’re holding.” So he handed them to her and went and lay with her, and she became pregnant as a result.
[Genesis] [38]:[19] Then Tamar got up and left, and she took off her veil and put her widow’s clothes back on.
[Genesis] [38]:[20] Then Yehudah (Judah) sent his friend the Adulami to take the young goat and get the pledge back from the woman, but he couldn’t find her,
[Genesis] [38]:[21] so he asked some of the local men, “Where’s the temple prostitute who was at Enayim beside the road?” But they answered, “There’s never been a temple prostitute around here.”
[Genesis] [38]:[22] So Hirah returned to Yehudah and told him, “I couldn’t find her. What’s more, the men of the place said that there hasn’t been a temple prostitute at that place.”
[Genesis] [38]:[23] “Oh well,” said Yehudah. “Let her keep those things for herself so that we don’t become a laughingstock. Anyway, I did my duty by sending the goat, but you couldn’t find her.”
[Genesis] [38]:[24] About three months later, Yehudah was told, “Your daughter-in-law Tamar has prostituted herself, and not only that, she’s pregnant from doing it.” “Bring her out and let her be burnt to death.” Yehudah demanded.
[Genesis] [38]:[25] So they got her and brought her out, but she sent a message to her father-in-law, saying, “It was the man who these things belong to that got me pregnant.” Then she added, “Please identify whose signet ring and cords and staff these are.”
[Genesis] [38]:[26] When Yehudah recognised the items, he admitted, “She’s more in the right than I am, because I didn’t give my son Shela to her.” But he didn’t lie with her again.
[Genesis] [38]:[27] When the time came for Tamar to give birth, wow, she was going to have twins.
[Genesis] [38]:[28] While she was giving birth, one of the babies poked out a hand and the midwife tied a scarlet thread around its wrist, saying, “This one came out first.”
[Genesis] [38]:[29] However, it pulled its hand back in, then wow, its brother was delivered first. Then she said, “How did you manage to break out first?” So he named him ‘Perets’ (which means ‘break out’).
[Genesis] [38]:[30] After that, his brother who had the scarlet thread on his wrist was delivered, and he named him Zerah.
[Genesis] [39]:[1] Meanwhile, Yosef (Joseph) had been taken down to Mitsrayim (Egypt), and an Mitsri (Egyptian) man named Potifar had bought him from the Yishmaelim (Ishmaelites) who had taken him down there. Potifar was the chief of the guards for Par’oh (Pharaoh).
[Genesis] [39]:[2] Yosef lived in the house of his Mitsri master, and Yahweh was with him and he was successful at his work.
[Genesis] [39]:[3] His master noticed that Yahweh was with him and that Yahweh made everything that he did succeed,
[Genesis] [39]:[4] so Yosef earned his favour as he served him. Then Potifar put him in charge of his entire household and everything that he owned.
[Genesis] [39]:[5] From that time onwards, Yahweh blessed that Mitsri household because of Yosef, and Yahweh’s blessing even extended from everything in the home all the way out to the countryside.
[Genesis] [39]:[6] Potifar left all his belonging in Yosef’s charge, so much so that he didn’t have to think about anything else beyond what he wanted to eat. Now Yosef had developed into a well-built and handsome young man,
[Genesis] [39]:[7] and after a while, his master’s wife started to develop a crush on him and told him, “Come to bed with me.”
[Genesis] [39]:[8] But he refused and told her, “Listen, with me here, my master doesn’t have to think about what’s in the house and he’s put me in charge of everything.
[Genesis] [39]:[9] In this house, he doesn’t even have more authority than I do and he hasn’t kept anything back from me, except for you, his wife. How could I do this very wicked thing and sin against God.
[Genesis] [39]:[10] But she kept persisting with Yosef day after, but he wouldn’t lie with her like she wanted.
[Genesis] [39]:[11] Then one day when he went into the house to do his work and there were no other men of the house around,
[Genesis] [39]:[12] Potifar’s wife grabbed Yosef’s cloak and demanded, “Come to bed with me.” But he pulled away and fled outside the house, leaving her there holding his cloak.
[Genesis] [39]:[13] As soon as it registered that he’d fled outside leaving his cloak behind,
[Genesis] [39]:[14] she yelled for the other male slaves and told them, “Look, he brought a Ivri (Hebrew) here man to mock at us. He tried to get me onto the bed, but I yelled out loudly.
[Genesis] [39]:[15] When he grasped that I was screaming for help, he left his cloak here and just took off outside.”
[Genesis] [39]:[16] Potifar’s wife kept the cloak beside her until her husband, Yosef’s master, got home,
[Genesis] [39]:[17] then she told him the same story, “That Ivri slave that you brought into our home came to me to mock me,
[Genesis] [39]:[18] but when I yelled out, he left his cloak here and took off outside.”
[Genesis] [39]:[19] When Yosef’s master heard his wife tell what his slave had tried to do to her, he became furious.
[Genesis] [39]:[20] He took him and threw him into the prison built for the king’s prisoners.
[Genesis] [39]:[21] But Yahweh was with Yosef and was kind to him and caused the prison warden to be pleased with him,
[Genesis] [39]:[22] so the warden put him in charge of all the other prisoners and Yosef ended up being in charge of everything that happened inside.
[Genesis] [39]:[23] Then the warden didn’t need to concern himself with anything that was going on because Yahweh was with Yosef and helped him succeed in everything he did.
[Genesis] [40]:[1] Sometime after that the Mitsri (Egyptian) king’s cupbearer and baker sinned against their master, also known as Par’oh (Pharaoh).
[Genesis] [40]:[2] Par’oh was angry at those two officials
[Genesis] [40]:[3] and he put them in the custody of the chief of the guards—in the prison where Yosef (Joseph) was also being held.
[Genesis] [40]:[4] There the chief of the guards assigned Yosef to serve them. After they’d been in custody for quite some time,
[Genesis] [40]:[5] the king’s cupbearer and baker in prison each had separate dreams on the same night, and each man’s dream had its own interpretation.
[Genesis] [40]:[6] The next morning, Yosef came to them, and wow, they were worried,
[Genesis] [40]:[7] so he asked the two former officials of Par’oh, “Why are you looking so upset today?”
[Genesis] [40]:[8] “We each had a dream last night,” they answered, “but there’s no one here who can tell us what our dreams mean.” “God is the only one who gives someone the ability to interpret the meaning of dreams,” Yosef replied. “Please tell me what you dreamed.”
[Genesis] [40]:[9] Then the chief of the cupbearers went first and told his dream to Yosef, “Listen, in my dream there was a grapevine in front of me
[Genesis] [40]:[10] with three branches on it. Then as soon as the buds appeared on the branches, its blossoms came out straight away and its clusters ripened into grapes.
[Genesis] [40]:[11] Then I was holding Par’oh’s cup and I took the grapes and squeezed them into it and I gave the cup to Par’oh.”
[Genesis] [40]:[12] “This is the interpretation,” Yosef responded. “The three branches represent three days.
[Genesis] [40]:[13] Within three days, Par’oh will display you publicly and then restore you to your position. Then you’ll place Par’oh’s cup into his hand, just like you used to before when you were his cupbearer.
[Genesis] [40]:[14] But when it all goes well for you, if you remember me then please be kind and mention me to Par’oh to get me out of this prison,
[Genesis] [40]:[15] because indeed I was trafficked from the land of the Ivrim (Hebrews). And even here, I didn’t do anything to deserve being held in this pit.”
[Genesis] [40]:[16] Now when the chief of the bakers saw that this first dream was interpreted so favourably, he told Yosef, “I also was in my dream, and listen, there were three baskets of white bread on my head.
[Genesis] [40]:[17] In the top basket there were various kinds of food for Par’oh—baker’s goods—but the birds were eating them out of the basket on my head.”
[Genesis] [40]:[18] “This is the interpretation,” Yosef responded. “The three baskets are three days.
[Genesis] [40]:[19] Within three days, Par’oh will display you publicly and then impale you on a pole, and the birds will eat your flesh off your bones.”
[Genesis] [40]:[20] Then three days later, it was Par’oh’s birthday and he held a feast for all his officials and he got the chief of the cupbearers and the chief of the bakers brought in to stand publicly in the middle of everyone.
[Genesis] [40]:[21] Then he restored the chief of the cupbearers to his position, and the man carried the cup across to Par’oh,
[Genesis] [40]:[22] but he had the chief of the bakers executed, just like Yosef had described in the interpretation of the dream.
[Genesis] [40]:[23] However, the chief of the cupbearers completely forgot about Yosef.
[Genesis] [41]:[1] Some two years later, King Par’oh (Pharaoh) had a dream and in it, he was standing beside the Nile River.
[Genesis] [41]:[2] Then, wow, seven fine-looking and well-fed cows came up out of the river, and they grazed among the reeds.
[Genesis] [41]:[3] But wow, seven ugly, skinny cows came up out of the river after them, and they stood beside the other cows on the river bank.
[Genesis] [41]:[4] Then the ugly, skinny cows ate the seven nice, fat cows, and then Par’oh woke up.
[Genesis] [41]:[5] Then he fell asleep again and had a second dream. And wow, seven good, fat heads of grain came up on one stalk.
[Genesis] [41]:[6] But wow, seven thin heads of grain sprouted after them—these heads of grain had been scorched by the hot, desert wind.
[Genesis] [41]:[7] Then the thin heads of grain swallowed up the seven good, fat heads. At that point, Par’oh woke up, and realised that it had been a dream.
[Genesis] [41]:[8] That morning, Par’oh’s spirit was troubled, so he sent for all the sorcerers and wise men of Mitsrayim (Egypt) and he told them his dreams, but no one could interpret them for the king.
[Genesis] [41]:[9] Then the chief of the cupbearers spoke with Par’oh saying, “I’ve just remembered my broken promise today.
[Genesis] [41]:[10] The king had been angry with his servants, and he put me in the custody of the chief of the guards in his prison—me and the chief of the bakers.
[Genesis] [41]:[11] The two of us each had a dream one night, and each of the dreams had different interpretations.
[Genesis] [41]:[12] There was a young Ivri (Hebrew) man in there with us—a slave of the chief of the guards. When we told him our dreams, he interpreted our two different dreams for us.
[Genesis] [41]:[13] And it all happened just as he’d interpreted them—I was restored to my position and the baker was executed.
[Genesis] [41]:[14] So Par’oh sent for Yosef (Joseph), and they quickly brought him in from the pit. When he’d shaved and changed his clothes, he was brought in to the king
[Genesis] [41]:[15] who told him, “I had a dream but no one could interpret it. However, I heard that you could listen to a dream and explain what it means.”
[Genesis] [41]:[16] “No, it’s not my ability,” Yosef responded, “but God will answer the king to give him peace.”
[Genesis] [41]:[17] “In my dream,” Par’oh told Yosef, “wow, I was standing on the river bank
[Genesis] [41]:[18] and then listen, up from the river came seven cows. They were well-fed and good-looking, and they grazed among the reeds.
[Genesis] [41]:[19] Then listen, seven other cows came up after them. They were in poor condition and very ugly and skinny—I haven’t seen cows that ugly anywhere in Mitsrayim (Egypt).
[Genesis] [41]:[20] Then the skinny, ugly cows ate the first seven fat cows,
[Genesis] [41]:[21] but you wouldn’t know it because their bellies were just as skinny as before and they looked just as ugly as they had before. Then I woke up.
[Genesis] [41]:[22] “Then I had another dream, and listen, seven heads of grain came up on one stalk. They were full and good.
[Genesis] [41]:[23] Then listen, seven more heads of grain sprouted after them, but they were withered and thin, and scorched by the east wind.
[Genesis] [41]:[24] Then the thin heads of grain swallowed up the seven good heads of grain. I told these dreams to the sorcerers, but no one could explain them to me.”
[Genesis] [41]:[25] Then Yosef (Joseph) said to Par’oh (Pharaoh), “The king’s dreams are one and the same. God has shown Par’oh what he’s going to do.
[Genesis] [41]:[26] The seven good cows are seven years, and the seven good heads of grain are seven years—both dreams mean the same.
[Genesis] [41]:[27] And the seven thin and ugly cows that came up after them are seven years, and so are the seven thin heads of grain scorched by the east wind. There will be seven years of drought.
[Genesis] [41]:[28] That’s why I told Par’oh that God has shown him what he’s going to do.
[Genesis] [41]:[29] Listen, there’s seven years coming of plentiful harvests throughout all of Mitsrayim,
[Genesis] [41]:[30] but seven years of drought will follow after them, such that the years of plenty will be quickly forgotten and famine will devastate the land.
[Genesis] [41]:[31] Yes, the time of plenty won’t be remembered because of the famine that follows—it’ll be very severe.
[Genesis] [41]:[32] And as for having two dreams with the same meaning, it’s because the matter has been established by God, and God will do it soon.
[Genesis] [41]:[33] “So now the king should find a man who’s discerning and wise, and appoint him over all Mitsrayim (Egypt).
[Genesis] [41]:[34] Then the king should get him to appoint supervisors all across the country to collect twenty percent of the crops during the seven years of plenty.
[Genesis] [41]:[35] They should collect that surplus food in the coming good years, and store it in the cities under the king’s authority. It should be kept
[Genesis] [41]:[36] and used as a reserve for the seven years of famine that will affect the country, so that the people will survive.
[Genesis] [41]:[37] This idea sounded good to Par’oh (Pharaoh) and to all his servants,
[Genesis] [41]:[38] so he asked them, “Do we have any other man like this who has God’s spirit in him?”
[Genesis] [41]:[39] Then he told Yosef (Joseph), “Since God has shown you all this, there’s no one as discerning and wise as you.
[Genesis] [41]:[40] You’ll be over my household, and all my people will obey your every word. Only I on the throne will be greater than you.”
[Genesis] [41]:[41] Then he added, “See, I’ve put you over all the entire country.”
[Genesis] [41]:[42] Then he removed his signet ring from his hand and put it on Yosef’s hand, and he had him dressed in fine linen clothes, and put a gold chain around his neck.
[Genesis] [41]:[43] He had Yosef ride in his #2 chariot, and they called out in front of him, “Bow down!” So the king put him over the entire country of Mitsrayim (Egypt).
[Genesis] [41]:[44] Par’oh also told him, “I’m Par’oh, and no person in all Mitsrayim will lift their hand or foot without your permission.”
[Genesis] [41]:[45] Then Par’oh gave him the Mitsri (Egyptian) name ‘Tsofnat-Pa’neah’ (which means ‘the one who reveals secrets’), and he presented him with Esenat, the daughter of Poti-Fera the priest of On, as a wife. And Yosef travelled throughout the land of Mitsrayim.
[Genesis] [41]:[46] Yosef was thirty years old when he’d been called to stand before Par’oh king of Mitsrayim. When he left Par’oh’s presence, he travelled throughout the land of Mitsrayim
[Genesis] [41]:[47] and the land produced outstanding harvests during the seven years of plenty.
[Genesis] [41]:[48] For seven years, he gathered all the food throughout the land of Mitsrayim and had it stored in the cities. The food from the countryside that surrounded each city, he put inside that city.
[Genesis] [41]:[49] So Yosef stored up so much grain that it was like sand on the beaches, until he eventually stopped measuring it because it too much to calculate.
[Genesis] [41]:[50] Before the years of the famine came, Yosef had two sons that Esenat (the daughter of Poti-Fera, the priest of On) gave birth to.
[Genesis] [41]:[51] Yosef named the oldest son ‘Menasheh’ (Manasseh) (which means ‘forget’), because he said, “God has made me forget all my hardships and all of my family.”
[Genesis] [41]:[52] His second son he named ‘Efrayim’ (Ephraim) (which means ‘fruitful’), because he said, “God has made me fruitful in the land of my difficulties.”
[Genesis] [41]:[53] Then the seven years of plenty in Mitsrayim came to an end
[Genesis] [41]:[54] and the seven years of famine started, just as Yosef had said. The famine covered the entire wider region, but it was different in Mitsrayim.
[Genesis] [41]:[55] All the land of Mitsrayim became famished, and the people cried to the king for food, so Par’oh (Pharaoh) said to all the Mitsrim (Egyptians), “Go to Yosef and do whatever he tells you.”
[Genesis] [41]:[56] The famine was right across the country, so Yosef opened all the grain stores and sold grain to the Mitsrim. But the famine in Mitsrayim was really severe.
[Genesis] [41]:[57] Then people from much further away started coming to Mitsrayim to buy grain from Yosef, because the famine was severe in the entire wider region.
[Genesis] [42]:[1] Meanwhile (up in the Kena’an (Canaan) region), Ya’akov (Jacob) heard that there was grain available in Mitsrayim (Egypt), so he said to his sons, “Why are you just standing there looking at each other?
[Genesis] [42]:[2] Listen, I’ve heard that they’re selling grain in Mitsrayim. Go down there and buy some for us so that we won’t just starve to death here.”
[Genesis] [42]:[3] So ten of Yosef’s (Joseph) brothers travelled down to Mitsrayim to buy grain,
[Genesis] [42]:[4] but Ya’akov wouldn’t send Benyamin (Yosef’s youngest brother) with the others, because he said, “I don’t want any harm to come to him.”
[Genesis] [42]:[5] So Yisrael’s (Israel) sons found themselves among many others who went to buy grain, because the famine was also throughout the Kena’an region.
[Genesis] [42]:[6] Now Yosef was the governor over all of Mitsrayim and he was the one there who was selling grain to all the people. So Yosef’s brothers approached and bowed down to him with their noses to the ground.
[Genesis] [42]:[7] When Yosef saw his brothers, he recognized them and acted like a stranger to them, and he spoke harshly with them (through an interpreter), “Where are you lot from?” “From the land of Kena’an to buy food,” they answered.
[Genesis] [42]:[8] Yosef had recognised his brothers, but they hadn’t recognised him,
[Genesis] [42]:[9] and just then he remembered the dreams that he had dreamed about them, so he said to them, “You are spies. You’ve all come to discover any weak points in this country’s defences.”
[Genesis] [42]:[10] “No, my master,” they answered. “Your servants have only come to buy food.
[Genesis] [42]:[11] We’re all sons of the same man. We’re being honest. Your servants are not spies.”
[Genesis] [42]:[12] “No, you’ve definitely all come here to see where our land is vulnerable,” Yosef insisted.
[Genesis] [42]:[13] “Your servants are twelve brothers,” they protested. “We’re all sons of one man in the Kena’an (Canaan) region. It’s all true—the youngest is home with our father, and one has passed away.”
[Genesis] [42]:[14] “Yes, it’s just as I said,” retorted Yosef. “You’re spies!
[Genesis] [42]:[15] But this is how we’ll test you all: On Par’oh’s (Pharaoh) life, you won’t ever leave this place unless your youngest brother comes here.
[Genesis] [42]:[16] Select one among you to go and get your brother, and the rest of you will be imprisoned. Then we’ll find out if you’ve all been telling the truth. And if not, on Par’oh’s life, you’re certainly spies.”
[Genesis] [42]:[17] Then he had them locked up together for three days.
[Genesis] [42]:[18] On the third day, Yosef told them, “I’m a man who reveres God. So if you do exactly what I say, I’ll let you live.
[Genesis] [42]:[19] If you are actually honest, leave one of your brothers in prison here, and you others go and take grain back to feed your families.
[Genesis] [42]:[20] Then when you will bring me your youngest brother so that I can verify your statements, then you won’t die.” So they agreed,
[Genesis] [42]:[21] saying to each other (in Hebrew), “We are truly guilty concerning our brother Yosef, because we saw the distress of his soul when he pleaded with us, but we didn’t take any notice. That’s why this predicament has happened to us.”
[Genesis] [42]:[22] “Didn’t I beg you all not to sin against the lad?” Re’uven spoke up. “But you wouldn’t listen, so now, see, now we’re having to account for his blood.”
[Genesis] [42]:[23] (But they didn’t know that Yosef understood them, because he and them had been speaking through an interpreter.)
[Genesis] [42]:[24] Yosef turned away from them briefly so they couldn’t see his tears, then he turned back toward them and spoke to them. Then he had Shim’on (Simeon) separated from the group and tied up in front of them.
[Genesis] [42]:[25] Then Yosef ordered his servants and they filled their bags with grain, and he quietly ordered them to return each man’s silver back to his sack and to give them provisions to them for the road. After Yosef (Joseph) had provided for his brothers,
[Genesis] [42]:[26] they loaded their grain onto their donkeys and departed.
[Genesis] [42]:[27] At a lodging place that night, one of them opened his sack to feed his donkey and to his horror, he saw his silver inside the top of the sack.
[Genesis] [42]:[28] “My silver’s been returned,” he told his brothers, “and it’s right here in my sack!” Then their stomachs tightened, and trembling, they asked each other, “What’s this that God’s doing to us?”
[Genesis] [42]:[29] When they got home to Ya’akov (Jacob) their father in Kena’an (Canaan), they told him everything that had happened to them,
[Genesis] [42]:[30] “This man, the master of Mitsrayim (Egypt), spoke harshly to us and treated us as if we were spying out his country,
[Genesis] [42]:[31] but we told him, ‘We’re honest—we’re not spies.
[Genesis] [42]:[32] We’re twelve brothers, the sons of our father. One is no longer alive, and the youngest is with our father today back in Kena’an.’
[Genesis] [42]:[33] Then that man told us, ‘I’ll find out if you’re honest: Leave one of your brothers with me, and take grain for your families and go.
[Genesis] [42]:[34] Then bring me your youngest brother so that I’ll know you’re not spies—that you’re telling the truth. Then I’ll release your brother and you can trade here freely.’ ”
[Genesis] [42]:[35] Then when they started emptying their sacks, wow, each man’s pouch of silver was inside his sack. When the brothers and their father saw their pouches of silver, they were afraid.
[Genesis] [42]:[36] “You’ve deprived me of another son,” Ya’akov exclaimed. Yosef (Joseph) is gone! Shim’on’s (Simeon) gone! And then you want to take Benyamin as well! Why’s everything going so wrong for me?”
[Genesis] [42]:[37] Then Re’uven offered to his father, “You can kill my two sons if I don’t bring Benyamin back to you. Let me take responsibility for him, and I’ll make sure that he returns to you.”
[Genesis] [42]:[38] “My son will not go with you,” Ya’akov countered, “because his brother is dead, and he alone is left. And if harm were to meet him on the road that you’re going on, then you’d bring my grey head down to the grave in grief.”
[Genesis] [43]:[1] However, the famine in the region was still very severe,
[Genesis] [43]:[2] so when they’d used up all the grain that they’d brought from Mitsrayim (Egypt), their father instructed them, “Go back there and buy some food for us.”
[Genesis] [43]:[3] But Yehudah (Judah) challenged him, “That man told us that he won’t even see us unless our brother is with us.
[Genesis] [43]:[4] We can only go there to buy food for you if you’ll agree to send our youngest brother with us.
[Genesis] [43]:[5] If you don’t, it’s not even worth going, because that man clearly told us that he won’t even see us unless our brother is with us.
[Genesis] [43]:[6] “Why did you all treat me badly by telling the man you have a younger brother?” their father Yisrael (Israel) asked.
[Genesis] [43]:[7] “The man kept asking about us and our relatives,” they answered. “He asked, ‘Is your father still alive? Do you have another brother?’ We just answered what he asked. How could we possibly know that he would insist that we bring our youngest brother there?”
[Genesis] [43]:[8] Then Yehudah said to his father, “Entrust the young man to me, and we’ll pack up and go so that both we and you and our little ones will live and not die.
[Genesis] [43]:[9] I myself will guarantee him. If anything happens to him, you can charge it to me. If I don’t get him safely back to you, then I’ll personally carry the blame for the rest of my life.
[Genesis] [43]:[10] If we hadn’t sat around here doing nothing for so long, certainly by now we could have been there and back twice!”
[Genesis] [43]:[11] “Well, if that’s our only choice,” their father acceded, “then do this: Take some of the best produce from around here in your bags, and take it down to the man as a gift: a little balm, a little honey, spices and myrrh, and some pistachio nuts and almonds.
[Genesis] [43]:[12] And take double the amount of silver, because you must repay the silver that was returned in the tops of your sacks. Perhaps it was a mistake.
[Genesis] [43]:[13] So take your brother and go and return to the man.
[Genesis] [43]:[14] May the provider God Almighty cause the man to treat you kindly, and may he send your other brother and Benyamin back with you. And as for me, if I lose another son, I’ll just have to mourn him.”
[Genesis] [43]:[15] So the brothers took the gifts and double the amount of silver. Then taking Benyamin, they travelled down to Mitsrayim (Egypt) and presented themselves to Yosef (Joseph).
[Genesis] [43]:[16] When Yosef saw Benyamin with them, he told his head house-servant, “Take these men to the house, and slaughter an animal and prepare a meal, because they’ll eat with me at noon.”
[Genesis] [43]:[17] The man did what he’d been instructed and brought the men to Yosef’s house.
[Genesis] [43]:[18] But the brothers were afraid when they found out that they’d been brought to wait outside Yosef’s house, and said to each other, “We must have been brought here because of the silver that was returned in our sacks the first time. He wants to overpower us, then arrest us and confiscate our donkeys and take us as slaves.”
[Genesis] [43]:[19] So they approached the head servant and spoke to him at the entrance of the house,
[Genesis] [43]:[20] explaining, “Please, my master, honestly, we came down here the first time to buy food.
[Genesis] [43]:[21] But when we got to our lodging place that evening, we opened our sacks and got a shock because each man’s silver was in the top of his sack—the full amount of our silver was there. So we’ve brought it back here on this trip,
[Genesis] [43]:[22] plus we’ve brought more silver to buy food. We don’t know who put that silver in our sacks.”
[Genesis] [43]:[23] But he said, “Peace to you—don’t be afraid. Your god and the god of your father has given you hidden treasure in your sacks—I received your previous payment.” Then he brought Shim’on (Simeon) out to them.
[Genesis] [43]:[24] Then the servant took the brothers into Yosef’s house. He had water given to them and they washed their feet, and he had fodder given to their donkeys.
[Genesis] [43]:[25] Then they got theirs gifts ready for when Yosef would arrive at midday, because they’d heard that they would be given lunch there.
[Genesis] [43]:[26] When Yosef arrived there, they brought their gifts and they bowed to the ground in front of him.
[Genesis] [43]:[27] Then he asked them about their living situation at home and questioned, “Is everything ok for your elderly father that you told me about? Is he still alive?”
[Genesis] [43]:[28] “Things are well for your servant our father. And yes, he’s still alive.” Then they bowed their heads and bowed to the ground again.
[Genesis] [43]:[29] Then Yosef looked around and saw his full-brother Benyamin, and asked, “Is this your youngest brother that you spoke to me about?” Then he said, “May God be gracious to you, my son.”
[Genesis] [43]:[30] At that point, Yosef had to hurry out of the room, because he was so overcome with emotion for his younger brother that he needed to cry, so he went to his inner room and cried there.
[Genesis] [43]:[31] Then he washed his face and came out, controlling himself and ordering, “Serve the meal.”
[Genesis] [43]:[32] So the servants served Yosef at his own table, and served the brothers separately and the Mitsrim (Egyptians) who were eating with him separately again (because Mitsrim won’t eat together with Ivrim (Hebrews), because Mitsrim would find that demeaning).
[Genesis] [43]:[33] At their table, the brothers were astonished to discover that they had been seated in order from the oldest to the youngest.
[Genesis] [43]:[34] Then they were served food Yosef’s table, but Benyamin’s serving was five times larger than any of the others, and they drank and they and Yosef all got a bit tiddly.
[Genesis] [44]:[1] Then Yosef (Joseph) commanded his head servant, “Fill the men’s sacks with grain, as much as they are able to carry, and put each man’s payment back into the top of his sack.
[Genesis] [44]:[2] And put my own silver cup in the top of the youngest one’s sack along with his payment.” So he did what he was instructed.
[Genesis] [44]:[3] The next morning at daylight, the brothers and their donkeys were sent off to start their trip home.
[Genesis] [44]:[4] They hadn’t gone very far out of the city when Yosef told his head servant, “Get up and, follow after those men. When you overtake them, ask them, ‘Why did you repay good with evil?
[Genesis] [44]:[5] Isn’t this the cup that my master drinks from and indeed, what he divines with? You’ve done evil taking that.’ ”
[Genesis] [44]:[6] So the servant overtook them and did exactly what he’d been instructed to do.
[Genesis] [44]:[7] But they asked him, “Why does my master say that? Far be it from your servants to do something like that.
[Genesis] [44]:[8] Listen, we brought the silver that we found in the top of our sacks back to you from the land of Kena’an (Canaan). So why would we then steal silver or gold from the house of your master?
[Genesis] [44]:[9] If you find anything stolen with any of us, that person can be executed, and the rest of us can also be taken as slaves for my master.”
[Genesis] [44]:[10] “Indeed,” the servant replied, “according to your words, that’s how it’ll be: the one who is found with the stolen cup will become my slave, but you others will be free to go.”
[Genesis] [44]:[11] So each of the brothers quickly lowered his sack to the ground, and each one opened his sack.
[Genesis] [44]:[12] Then Yosef’s servant searched beginning with the oldest and ending with the youngest, and the cup was found in Benyamin’s sack.
[Genesis] [44]:[13] Seeing this, the brothers tore their clothes (as a sign of their distress), and each one loaded up his donkey, and they all returned to the city.
[Genesis] [44]:[14] When Yehudah (Judah) and his brothers got to Yosef’s (Joseph) house, he was still there, and they fell to their knees and bowed to the ground in front of him.
[Genesis] [44]:[15] “What’s this that you’ve done?” Yosef demanded. “Didn’t you know that a man like me can certainly divine the truth?”
[Genesis] [44]:[16] “What can we say to my master?” Yehudah answered. “What words could we speak? How could we possibly justify ourselves? God has exposed the sin of your servants. So now, we are slaves for my master—both we and the one who was found with the cup.”
[Genesis] [44]:[17] “Far be it from me to do that.” Yosef corrected them. “Only the man who had the cup will become my slave, and the rest of you can go back to your father in peace.”
[Genesis] [44]:[18] Then Yehudah (Judah) went closer to Yosef (Joseph) and said quietly, “Please, my master, please let your servant speak a word in my master’s ears, and don’t get angry with me, since you’re as powerful as Par’oh (Pharaoh).
[Genesis] [44]:[19] My master previously asked his servants if we had a father or another brother?
[Genesis] [44]:[20] And we answered to my master, ‘Yes, we have an elderly father and also the youngest son of his old age. But that son’s brother is dead, so he alone is left of his mother’s children, and his father loves him.’
[Genesis] [44]:[21] Then you told your servants, ‘Bring the other son here so I can see him myself.’
[Genesis] [44]:[22] And we said to my master, ‘The young man isn’t able to leave his father, because if he does, then the old man will die.’
[Genesis] [44]:[23] But then you said to your servants, ‘If your youngest brother doesn’t come with you, you won’t get access to me again.’
[Genesis] [44]:[24] “After all that, when we went back to your servant my father, we explained your words to him, my master.
[Genesis] [44]:[25] Eventually, our father told us, ‘Return there to buy some food for us.’
[Genesis] [44]:[26] But we told him, ‘We can’t go back unless our youngest brother is with us, because we wouldn’t be able to get access to that man if our youngest brother wasn’t with us.’
[Genesis] [44]:[27] Then your servant my father told us, ‘You know that my wife gave birth to two sons for me.
[Genesis] [44]:[28] One of them went away from me, and I’ve assumed that he was torn to pieces, and I’ve never seen him again.
[Genesis] [44]:[29] So if you also take this son away and something happened to him, then you’d bring my grey head down to the grave in misery.’
[Genesis] [44]:[30] “So now, if I was to return home to your servant my father without that young man, since his father’s soul is bound to his soul,
[Genesis] [44]:[31] then as soon as he sees that the young man isn’t will us, then he’ll have a heart attack and so your servants will bring the grey head of your servant our father down to the grave in misery.
[Genesis] [44]:[32] But your servant guaranteed the young man to my father, saying, ‘If I don’t get him back to you, then I will have sinned against my father all my life.’
[Genesis] [44]:[33] “So now, please let your servant stay as a slave for my master instead of the young man, and let the young man go home with his brothers.
[Genesis] [44]:[34] So now, how could I possibly go home to my father if that young man isn’t with me? I wouldn’t be able to cope with my father’s misery.”
[Genesis] [45]:[1] By now, Yosef (Joseph) wasn’t able to control himself in front of everyone who was standing around, and he called out, “Send everyone else out!” So Yosef was alone when he revealed himself to his brothers,
[Genesis] [45]:[2] but he cried so loudly that many Mitsrim (Egyptians) heard it and Par’oh’s (Pharaoh) household listened.
[Genesis] [45]:[3] “I’m Yosef!” he told his brothers. “Is my father still alive?” But his brothers weren’t able to answer him because they were terrified there in front of him.
[Genesis] [45]:[4] “Please come close to me,” he said. So they came close, and he explained, “I’m your brother Yosef that you sold to be taken to Mitsrayim (Egypt).
[Genesis] [45]:[5] But don’t be upset now or troubled that you sold me here, because it was God who sent me ahead of you so that lives would be saved.
[Genesis] [45]:[6] There’s already been two years of famine in this region, but there’s still five more years to come without any ploughing or harvesting.
[Genesis] [45]:[7] So God sent me ahead of you all so that some of you would be kept alive by this miracle and your children would be preserved.
[Genesis] [45]:[8] You see, it wasn’t you who sent me here, but God. And he’s made me like a father to Par’oh, and master over all his house and the ruler in all the land of Mitsrayim.
[Genesis] [45]:[9] “So hurry back to my father and tell him, ‘This is what your son Yosef says, “God has made me master over all Mitsrayim. Come down to me—don’t delay.
[Genesis] [45]:[10] You can live in the Goshen region so that you’ll be near to me—you and your children and your children’s children and your flocks and your herds and everything that belongs to you.
[Genesis] [45]:[11] I’ll provide for you here because there’s still five years of famine to come. That way, you won’t end up poor—you and your household and everyone with you.” ’
[Genesis] [45]:[12] Look at me! You yourselves and even my brother Benyamin can see that it’s really me who’s speaking to you.
[Genesis] [45]:[13] So go and tell my father about all my very high position in Mitsrayim and everything else that you’ve seen. Then hurry and bring my father down here.”
[Genesis] [45]:[14] Then he hugged his brother Benyamin and cried, and Benyamin cried too while they hugged.
[Genesis] [45]:[15] Then he kissed all his brothers and cried over them, and after that his brothers talked with him.
[Genesis] [45]:[16] When the report about the arrival of Yosef’s (Joseph) brothers reached Par’oh’s (Pharaoh) house, both him and his servants were pleased.
[Genesis] [45]:[17] Then Par’oh instructed Yosef, “Tell your brothers, ‘Do this: Load your animals and leave. Go to Kena’an (Canaan)
[Genesis] [45]:[18] and get your father and your households, and come back here to me, and I’ll give to you the best of the land in Mitsrayim, and you’ll eat the best of the country.’
[Genesis] [45]:[19] And you’re commanded, ‘Do this: Take carts with you from here for your little ones and for your wives, and get your father and come.
[Genesis] [45]:[20] Don’t be upset about anything you have to leave behind, because the best of all the land in Mitsrayim will be yours.’ ”
[Genesis] [45]:[21] Then Yisrael’s (Israel) sons did what they had been instructed and Yosef gave them carts as per Par’oh’s orders as well as provisions for the journey.
[Genesis] [45]:[22] Then he gave changes of clothes to each of them, but he gave three hundred pieces of silver and five changes of clothes to Benyamin.
[Genesis] [45]:[23] To his father he sent ten male donkeys loaded with the best of Mitsrayim, and ten female donkeys loaded with grain and bread and provisions for his father for the road.
[Genesis] [45]:[24] Then he sent off his brothers, and as they left, then he told them, “Don’t quarrel on the road.”
[Genesis] [45]:[25] So they left Mitsrayim and went back home to their father Ya’akov (Jacob) in Kena’an (Canaan)
[Genesis] [45]:[26] and told him, “Yosef is still alive! In fact, he’s the ruler over all of Mitsrayim.” But Ya’akov was totally stunned and he couldn’t really believe them.
[Genesis] [45]:[27] Then they told him everything that Yosef had told them. When he saw the carts that Yosef had sent to carry him, then he started to recover from the shock.
[Genesis] [45]:[28] Then Yisrael exclaimed, “Enough! I accept that my son Yosef is still alive. I’ll go and see him before I die.”
[Genesis] [46]:[1] So Yisrael (Israel) started his trip, taking everything he had. When they stopped in Be’er-Sheva (Beersheba), he offered sacrifices to the god of his father Yitshak (Isaac).
[Genesis] [46]:[2] During the night, God spoke to Yisrael in visions sayings, “Ya’akov (Jacob), Ya’akov.” “I’m listening,” he answered.
[Genesis] [46]:[3] Then God told him, “I’m God, the god of your father. Don’t be afraid to go down to Mitsrayim (Egypt), because I’ll make you into a great nation there.
[Genesis] [46]:[4] I myself will go down with you to Mitsrayim, and I myself will also surely bring you back here. And Yosef (Joseph) will be there with you when you die.”
[Genesis] [46]:[5] Then Ya’akov departed from Be’er-Sheva, and his sons carried their father and their little ones and their wives in the carts that Par’oh (Pharaoh) had sent to carry him.
[Genesis] [46]:[6] They had also brought along all their livestock and their possessions that they had acquired in Kena’an (Canaan). Then they arrived in Mitsrayim—Ya’akov and all of his offspring with him:
[Genesis] [46]:[7] his sons and his sons’ sons with him, and his daughters and his sons’ daughters. So he brought all his offspring with him to Mitsrayim.
[Genesis] [46]:[8] These are the names of Yisrael’s sons who went to Mitsrayim, that is Ya’akov and his sons: Ya’akov’s firstborn was Re’uven,
[Genesis] [46]:[9] and Re’uven’s sons were Hanok and Palu and Hetsron and Karmi.
[Genesis] [46]:[10] Shim’on’s (Simeon) sons were Yemuel, Yamin, Ohad, Yakin, Tsohar, and Shaul, the son of a Kena’ani (Canaanite) woman.
[Genesis] [46]:[11] Levi’s sons were Gereshon, Kohat, and Merari.
[Genesis] [46]:[12] Yehudah’s (Judah) sons were Er, Onan, Shela, Perets, and Zerah, but Er and Onan had died in Kena’an. Perets’ sons were Hetsron and Hamul.
[Genesis] [46]:[13] Yisakar’s (Issachar) sons were Tola, Puah, Iyov (Job), and Shimron.
[Genesis] [46]:[14] Zevulun’s sons were Sered, Eylon, and Yahle’el.
[Genesis] [46]:[15] Those were all Le’ah’s sons that she bore for Ya’akov in Padan-Aram, along with his daughter Dinah. The total number of those descendants was thirty-three.
[Genesis] [46]:[16] Gad’s sons were Tsifyon,Hagi, Shuni, Etsbon, Eri, Arod, and Areli.
[Genesis] [46]:[17] Asher’s sons were Yimnah, Yishvah, Yishvi, Beriah, and their sister Serah. And Beriah’s sons were Hever and Malkiel.
[Genesis] [46]:[18] Those were all Zilpah’s sons, the slave woman that Lavan (Laban) had given to his daughter Le’ah, and she gave birth to those sixteen descendants for Ya’akov.
[Genesis] [46]:[19] Ya’akov’s wife Rahel’s (Rachel) sons were Yosef (Joseph) and Benyamin.
[Genesis] [46]:[20] Yosef’s sons Menasheh (Manasseh) and Efrayim (Ephraim) were born in Mitsrayim (Egypt). Esenat, the daughter of Poti-Fera the priest of On, gave birth to them for Yosef.
[Genesis] [46]:[21] Benyamin’s sons were Bela, Beker, Ashbel, Gera, Na’aman, Ehi, Rosh, Mupim, Hupim, and Ard.
[Genesis] [46]:[22] Those were all Rahel’s descendants—a total of fourteen.
[Genesis] [46]:[23] Dan’s son was Hushim.
[Genesis] [46]:[24] Naftali’s (Naphtali) sons were Yahtse’el, Guni, Yetser, and Shilem.
[Genesis] [46]:[25] Those two were both Bilhah’s sons, the slave woman that Lavan had given to his daughter Rahel, and she gave birth to those seven descendants for Ya’akov.
[Genesis] [46]:[26] The total count of those who went to Mitsrayim with Ya’akov who were his descendants (not counting his daughters-in-law) was sixty-six.
[Genesis] [46]:[27] As well as that, Yosef’s two sons were born in Mitsrayim so that added up to a grand total of seventy.
[Genesis] [46]:[28] As they all approached Mitsrayim (Egypt) , Ya’akov (Jacob) sent Yehudah (Judah) ahead of the others to find out from Yosef (Joseph) how to get to Goshen. As they all arrived in the Goshen area,
[Genesis] [46]:[29] Yosef hooked up his chariot and went to meet his father Yisrael (Israel) there. He went up to his father, and hugged him for a long time as he cried.
[Genesis] [46]:[30] “Now I can die,” Yisrael said to Yosef, “since I’ve seen your face—seen that you’re still alive.”
[Genesis] [46]:[31] Then Yosef spoke to his brothers and to his father’s household, “I’ll go and report to Par’oh (Pharaoh) and explain to him that my brothers and my father’s household who were living in Kena’an (Canaan) have come to join me.
[Genesis] [46]:[32] I’ll tell him that you’re herders of sheep—livestock farmers—and that you’ve brought your flocks and herds and everything that you own.
[Genesis] [46]:[33] So when Par’oh calls for you and asks what your work is,
[Genesis] [46]:[34] then you should answer, ‘Your servants have been livestock men from our youth and until now, both we and also our fathers,’ so that you can settle here in Goshen, because Mitsrim (Egyptians) despise sheep herders.”
[Genesis] [47]:[1] Then went Yosef to Par’oh and told him, “My father and brothers and their flocks and herds and everything that belongs to them, have come from Kena’an and they’re here now Goshen area.”
[Genesis] [47]:[2] Then he took five of his brothers and presented them to Par’oh,
[Genesis] [47]:[3] and Par’oh asked them, “What’s your occupation?” “Your servants have been shepherds for several generations,” they replied.
[Genesis] [47]:[4] Then they explained, “We’ve come to stay here for a while because in Kena’an, there’s no pasture for our flocks because the drought is very severe. So now, please let your servants settle in the Goshen area.”
[Genesis] [47]:[5] Then Par’oh turned to Yosef, “Your father and your brothers have come to you.
[Genesis] [47]:[6] The entire country of Mitsrayim (Egypt) is in front of you. Settle your father and your brothers in the best land, so let them settle in the Goshen area. And if you’re aware that some of them have special talents, then appoint them as overseers of my own livestock as well.”
[Genesis] [47]:[7] Then Yosef brought his father Ya’akov (Jacob) and presented him to Par’oh, and Ya’akov blessed Par’oh.
[Genesis] [47]:[8] “How old are you?” Par’oh asked him.
[Genesis] [47]:[9] “I’ve been moving from place to place for 130 years,” Ya’akov replied. “My life has been short and with many difficulties, so I haven’t reached the longer ages of my ancestors in their moving around.”
[Genesis] [47]:[10] Then he blessed Par’oh again and departed from his presence.
[Genesis] [47]:[11] So Yosef gave his father and his brothers some of the best land in Mitsrayim and helped them settle there—in the Ra’meses district just as Par’oh had commanded.
[Genesis] [47]:[12] He also provided his father and his brothers and all his father’s household with bread—each family according to the number of children.
[Genesis] [47]:[13] Then the time came when there was no bread in that entire part of the world, because the drought was now extremely severe, and both Mitsrayim (Egypt) and Kena’an (Canaan) were suffering from food shortages.
[Genesis] [47]:[14] People all over came to buy grain, and over time Yosef (Joseph) had received in payment all the silver that could be found in Mitsrayim and Kena’an, and he in turn took it to Par’oh’s (Pharaoh) house.
[Genesis] [47]:[15] So once there was no more silver left in Mitsrayim and in Kena’an, all the Mitsrim (Egyptians) demanded from Yosef, “Give us food. Why should we die right here in front of you? All our money is gone!”
[Genesis] [47]:[16] “Bring your livestock,” Yosef answered, “and I’ll give grain to you in exchange for them, since the silver is gone.”
[Genesis] [47]:[17] So the people brought their livestock to him, and he gave them grain in exchange for their horses and sheep and cattle and donkeys. So he provided them with food that year in exchange for all their livestock.
[Genesis] [47]:[18] The next year they came to Yosef and begged, “We can’t hide it from our master that since there’s no silver left and since all the livestock now belongs to our lord, there’s nothing left to offer other than our bodies and our lands.
[Genesis] [47]:[19] Why should we die right in front of you—both we and our land? Buy us and our land in exchange for food, and we and our land will be slaves to Par’oh. And give us seed so that we’ll live and not die, and so that the land won’t be barren.”
[Genesis] [47]:[20] So Yosef bought all the farmland of Mitsrayim for Par’oh, because every Mitsri (Egyptian) sold his field. In that way, all the land became Par’oh’s because the famine was so extreme.
[Genesis] [47]:[21] As for the people, he moved them to the cities from one end of Mitsrayim to the other.
[Genesis] [47]:[22] The only land he didn’t buy was that of the priests, because they were given a regular allowance by Par’oh. Because they could live on what they were supplied with, they didn’t need to sell their land.
[Genesis] [47]:[23] Then Yosef told the people, “Listen, now that I’ve bought you and your land for Par’oh, here is seed for you so that you can work the ground.
[Genesis] [47]:[24] Every time you harvest a crop, you must give a fifth of it to Par’oh. The other four parts will be for you to use as seed and as food for yourselves and your households and your young children.”
[Genesis] [47]:[25] “You’ve kept us alive,” they agreed. “Master, continue to show us your favour, and we’ll be slaves for Par’oh.”
[Genesis] [47]:[26] So Yosef established it as a law to this day concerning the Mitsri farmland: that the fifth belongs to Par’oh. (Only the priests’ land didn’t become Par’oh’s.)
[Genesis] [47]:[27] So Yisrael (Israel) (also called Ya’akov (Jacob) ) and his descendants settled in the Goshen region of Mitsrayim (Egypt) and prospered. The had many children and quickly increased in number.
[Genesis] [47]:[28] Ya’akov resided there for seventeen years, and by then he was 147 years old
[Genesis] [47]:[29] and he was getting close to death, so he called for his son Yosef (Joseph) and asked him, “If, please, I have found favour in your eyes, please give me your hand and promise to deal with me in kindness and faithfulness. Please don’t bury me in Mitsrayim.
[Genesis] [47]:[30] When I die, I want to be buried with my ancestors, so carry me out of Mitsrayim and bury me in their tomb.” “I’ll do what you’ve requested,” Yosef agreed.
[Genesis] [47]:[31] “Promise me,” he insisted. So Yosef promised him and Yisrael bowed at the head of the bed.
[Genesis] [48]:[1] Some time after that, Yosef (Joseph) was told, “Listen, your father is sick.” So Yosef went to him, taking his two sons with him—Menasheh (Manasseh) and Efrayim (Ephraim).
[Genesis] [48]:[2] When someone told Ya’akov (Jacob) that Yosef had arrived, he exerted himself and sat up in bed,
[Genesis] [48]:[3] then he told him, “God the provider appeared to me at Luz in Kena’an (Canaan), and he blessed me
[Genesis] [48]:[4] and said to me, ‘Listen, I’ll make you fruitful, and I’ll multiply you and make you into a community of peoples. And I’ll give this land to your offspring after you to be their possession forever.’
[Genesis] [48]:[5] “And now, your two sons, who were born for you here in Mitsrayim (Egypt) before I came here, I adopt them as my own—Efrayim and Menasheh—just as Re’uven and Shim’on (Simeon) are mine.
[Genesis] [48]:[6] Any other children that you father after them will be yours. Their inheritance will only be through their older brothers.
[Genesis] [48]:[7] As for me, when I was coming into Kena’an from Padan, Rahel (Rachel) died beside on the way when we were still quite some distance from Efrat, and I buried her there beside the road of Efrat (which is Beyt-Lehem (Bethlehem)).”
[Genesis] [48]:[8] Then Yisrael (Israel) noticed Yosef’s two sons and asked, “Who are these?”
[Genesis] [48]:[9] “They are my sons that God has given me here in this place.” Yosef replied to his father. “Please bring them to me, and I will bless them,” Ya’akov (Jacob) requested.
[Genesis] [48]:[10] Now Yisrael’s sight was poor in his old age, so he wasn’t able to see much. So Yosef brought them over to him, and Yisrael kissed them and embraced them.
[Genesis] [48]:[11] “I never expected to see you again” he said to Yosef, “but wow, God has even let me see your children as well.”
[Genesis] [48]:[12] Then Yosef removed his sons from his father’s knees and bowed with his face to the ground.
[Genesis] [48]:[13] Then Yosef took both of them—Efrayim (Ephraim) on his right toward Yisrael’s left and Menasheh (Manasseh) (the eldest) on his left toward Yisrael’s right—and brought them close to him.
[Genesis] [48]:[14] But Yisrael intentionally extended his right hand and placed it on the Efrayim’s head (the younger one), and crossing his arms, he placed his left hand on Menasheh’s head.
[Genesis] [48]:[15] Then he blessed Yosef saying, “May the god who my grandfather Avraham and my father Yitshak (Isaac) served, the god who has been shepherding me for my entire life,
[Genesis] [48]:[16] the messenger who’s turned all harm intended for me into good, may he bless these young men. May they be recognised as my descendants, and as descendants of Avraham and Yitshak, and grow to increase in number on the earth.
[Genesis] [48]:[17] Then Yosef (Joseph) noticed that his father had placed his right hand on Efrayim’s (Ephraim) head and he was upset about it, so he picked up his father’s hand to move it across to Menasheh’s (Manasseh) head,
[Genesis] [48]:[18] telling his father, “My father, that’s wrong because that one is my oldest son. Put your right hand on his head.”
[Genesis] [48]:[19] But his father pushed back, “I know, my son, I know. Menasheh will also become a people, and he will also be great. Nevertheless his younger brother will be the greater one, and his descendants will become a multitude of nations.”
[Genesis] [48]:[20] So Yisrael (Israel) blessed Efrayim and Menasheh that day saying, “After this, my descendants will bless people by saying, ‘May God make you like Efrayim and like Menasheh.’ ” (Notice that he put Efrayim before Menasheh.)
[Genesis] [48]:[21] Then Yisrael told Yosef, “Listen, I’m about to die, and God will be with you and take you back to the land of your ancestors.
[Genesis] [48]:[22] I’m giving Shekem to you as an additional inheritance over that of your brothers. I captured it with my sword and my bow from the descendants of Amor and it’s now yours.”
[Genesis] [49]:[1] Then Ya’akov (Jacob) called for all his sons and said, “Gather together, and I’ll reveal to you what will happen to you all in the years ahead.
[Genesis] [49]:[2] Gather around and listen you sons of Ya’akov, listen to your father Yisrael (Israel).
[Genesis] [49]:[3] Re’uven you’re my eldest, my power and the beginning of my strength. With excellence in dignity, and excelling in power.
[Genesis] [49]:[4] But you’re destructive like strong waters. You climbed into my bed (with my slave-wife). You got onto my couch and defiled it.
[Genesis] [49]:[5] Shim’on (Simeon) and Levi are alike. Their swords are weapons of violence.
[Genesis] [49]:[6] Don’t let my thoughts enter into their discussion. Don’t let my honour join in their assembly. They killed a man in their anger, and they hamstrung an ox just for their pleasure.
[Genesis] [49]:[7] Their fierce anger is cursed, and their severe anger is determined. I will divide them out among Ya’akov’s (Jacob) descendants, and scatter them across Yisrael (Israel).

[Genesis] [49]:[11] He’ll tie his donkey to the grapevine, and the donkey’s colt to the best branch. He’ll wash his clothes in wine and his robes in the blood of grapes.
[Genesis] [49]:[12] His eyes will be darker than wine, and his teeth will be white from milk.
[Genesis] [49]:[13] Zevulun will settle near the coast, and be like a safe harbour for ships. His border will extend up to Tsidon (Sidon).
[Genesis] [49]:[14] Yisakar (Issachar) (Yisakar) is a strong donkey lying down between the sheep pens.

[Genesis] [49]:[16] Dan (which means ‘judge’) will judge his people like one of Yisrael’s (Israel) tribes.

[Genesis] [49]:[18] Yahweh, I’m waiting for you to save us.

[Genesis] [49]:[20] Asher will enjoy delicious food, and he’ll provide delicacies for a king.
[Genesis] [49]:[21] Naftali (Naphtali) is a doe that’s been untied. He says beautiful words.
[Genesis] [49]:[22] Yosef (Joseph) is part of a fruit-bearing vine— part of a fruit-bearing vine at a spring. His branches will climb over the wall.
[Genesis] [49]:[23] Expert archers will attack him, and shoot and harass him.
[Genesis] [49]:[24] But his bow will stay steady and his arms will be made agile by the hands of the mighty one of Ya’akov (Jacob), because of the shepherd who’s Yisrael’s (Israel) rock,
