[Genesis] [49]:[26] I’ve been blessed more than my ancestors were— even with being gifted those ancient hills. May those blessings now transfer to Yosef (Joseph)— the one who was separated from all his brothers.
[Genesis] [49]:[27] Benyamin is a ravenous wolf. In the morning he devours his prey, and in the evening he divides the plunder.
[Genesis] [49]:[28] Those are Yisrael’s (Israel) twelve sons (that led to the twelve tribes) and that’s what their father said to them from his bed as he blessed each one of them—each one blessed appropriately.
[Genesis] [49]:[29] Then Ya’akov (Jacob) instructed them, “I’m about to go and join my ancestors. Bury me with them in the cave in the field that was bought from Efron the Hiti,
[Genesis] [49]:[30] in the cave that is in Makpelah’s field in front of Mamre in Kena’an (Canaan). That’s the cave that my grandfather Avraham bought with the field from Efron the Hiti as property for a burial place.
[Genesis] [49]:[31] Avraham and his wife Sarah were buried there, along with their son Yitshak (Isaac) and his wife Rivkah, and I also buried my wife Le’ah there.
[Genesis] [49]:[32] That field and the cave in it was bought from the descendants of Het.
[Genesis] [49]:[33] When Ya’akov finished giving those instructions to his sons, he pulled his feet up into the bed and lay and breathed his last and his spirit joined his ancestors.
[Genesis] [50]:[1] Then Yosef (Joseph) hugged his father and cried over him and kissed him.
[Genesis] [50]:[2] Then he commanded those of his servants who were physicians to embalm his father. So Yisrael’s (Israel) body was embalmed
[Genesis] [50]:[3] over the next forty days (which is the normal time for embalming), and the Mitsrim (Egyptians) mourned for him for seventy days.
[Genesis] [50]:[4] After those mourning days were over, Yosef spoke to Par’oh’s (Pharaoh) servants, saying, “Please, if I have found favour in your eyes, please tell Par’oh that
[Genesis] [50]:[5] my father made me swear, saying, ‘Listen, I am dying. You must bury me in my grave that I dug for myself in Kena’an (Canaan).’ So now, please ask Par’oh to let me go up there and bury my father, then I’ll return.”
[Genesis] [50]:[6] “Go up and bury your father just like he made you promise.” was the reply back from Par’oh.
[Genesis] [50]:[7] So Yosef went up to Kena’an to bury his father. Par’oh’s servants went with him, along with the elders from Par’oh’s household and all the elders of the land of Mitsrayim (Egypt).
[Genesis] [50]:[8] Yosef’s own household also went, along with his brothers and his father’s household. They only left their children and their livestock behind in Goshen.
[Genesis] [50]:[9] There were chariots as well as soldiers mounted on horses so it was a very large procession.
[Genesis] [50]:[10] After they crossed the Yarden (Jordan) river, they arrived at Atad’s threshing floor, and they mourned there for seven days with very loud wailing.
[Genesis] [50]:[11] The local Kena’ani (Canaanite) people saw the mourning at Atad’s threshing floor, and they said, “This is very serious mourning for the Mitsrim (Egyptians).” That’s why they then named that place across the Yarden ‘Avel-Mitsrayim’ (which means ‘the Mitsrim mourned here’).
[Genesis] [50]:[12] So Ya’akov’s (Jacob) sons did everything just how he’d instructed them.
[Genesis] [50]:[13] They carried his embalmed body to Kena’an and buried him in the cave in Makpelah’s field. Avraham had bought with the field with the included cave from Efron the Hiti as property for a burial place, in front of Mamre.
[Genesis] [50]:[14] Then after his father’s burial was completed, Yosef returned to Mitsrayim (Egypt) along with his brothers and everyone who had gone up with him to bury him.
[Genesis] [50]:[15] Now that their father was no longer alive, Yosef’s (Joseph) brothers said to each other, “What if Yosef hates us and now he decides to repay us for all the evil things that we did to him?”
[Genesis] [50]:[16] So they sent a messenger to Yosef to tell him, “Before he died, your father ordered that
[Genesis] [50]:[17] you be given this message: ‘I beg you, please forgive your brothers’ crime and their sin, because they did evil things to you.’ So now, please forgive the crime of the servants of your father’s god.” When Yosef heard their message, he started crying.
[Genesis] [50]:[18] Then his brothers also came and bowed to the ground in front of him and pleaded, “Here we are. We belong to you as slaves.”
[Genesis] [50]:[19] “Don’t be afraid,” Yosef answered. “I’m not God and it’s not my job to decide on your punishment.
[Genesis] [50]:[20] You all plotted evil things against me, but God intended it for good in order to do what he’s doing this very day: to save many people.
[Genesis] [50]:[21] So now, don’t be afraid. I’ll support you and your little ones.” So he reassured them and he spoke kindly to them.
[Genesis] [50]:[22] Yosef (Joseph) continued to live in Mitsrayim (Egypt), along with the rest of his father Ya’akov’s (Jacob) family, until he was 110 years old.
[Genesis] [50]:[23] He lived long enough to see his son Efrayim’s (Ephraim) children, grandchildren, and great-grandchildren. The children of his grandson Makir, who was Menasheh’s (Manasseh) son, also grew up around him.
[Genesis] [50]:[24] Then one day Yosef said to his brothers, “I’m about to die, but God will definitely help you all and take you and your descendants from this country to the land that he vowed to give to Avraham, Yitshak (Isaac), and Ya’akov.
[Genesis] [50]:[25] When God does that, you must take my body back to Kena’an (Canaan) with you and bury it there.” Then Yosef had his brothers and the rest of the descendants of Yisrael (Israel) vow that they would do that.
[Genesis] [50]:[26] Then Yosef died at the age of 110, and the specialists embalmed his body and it was put in a coffin in a tomb in Mitsrayim.
[Exodus] [1]:[1] These are the names of Yisrael’s (Israel) descendants who accompanied Ya’akov (Jacob) when he moved his household to Mitsrayim (Egypt):
[Exodus] [1]:[2] Re’uven, Shim’on (Simeon), Levi, Yehudah (Judah),
[Exodus] [1]:[3] Yisakar (Issachar), Zevulun, Benyamin,
[Exodus] [1]:[4] Dan, Naftali (Naphtali), Gad, and Asher.
[Exodus] [1]:[5] At that time, Ya’akov had a total of seventy descendants (including Yosef (Joseph) and his sons who were already in Mitsrayim.)
[Exodus] [1]:[6] As the years progressed, Yosef and his brothers died—all of that generation,
[Exodus] [1]:[7] but they’d had many children who went on to have their own children and grandchildren, and so they became a large and powerful group there in Mitsrayim.
[Exodus] [1]:[8] Eventually a new king came to power in Mitsrayim who had never known Yosef
[Exodus] [1]:[9] and he told his people, “Listen, those descendants of Yisrael (Israel) are becoming more numerous and powerful than us.
[Exodus] [1]:[10] So, let’s deal wisely with them, in case they continue to multiply. Then if war was to break out, they could easily take the other side and fight against us, and then leave our country.”
[Exodus] [1]:[11] Then they appointed overseers to work them in slave gangs, and using them as forced labour, they built the store cities at Piton and Ra’meses for Par’oh (Pharaoh).
[Exodus] [1]:[12] However, the more they oppressed them, the more they multiplied and spread out, and the more the Mitsrim (Egyptians) came to dread the Israelis.
[Exodus] [1]:[13] So they made the Israelis work long, hard hours,
[Exodus] [1]:[14] and they made their lives bitter with the hard slavery. They were forced to make mortar and bricks, as well as all kinds of slave labour in the fields—all the work they had to do was strenuous and tiring.
[Exodus] [1]:[15] Then the king of Mitsrayim spoke to Shifrah and Puah, the two Ivri (Hebrew) midwives,
[Exodus] [1]:[16] saying, “When you assist the Ivri women as midwives, as you sit there on your stool, if you see that it’s a male, do something so he’ll die, but if it’s a female, then let her live.”
[Exodus] [1]:[17] But the midwives were godly women and didn’t do according to what the Mitsri (Egyptian) king had instructed them, and they let the boys live.
[Exodus] [1]:[18] So the king called the midwives back, and he demanded, “Why have you done that and let their sons live?”
[Exodus] [1]:[19] “Because the Ivri women aren’t like Mitsri women,” the midwives answered. “They’re more active and give birth before the midwife even gets to them.”
[Exodus] [1]:[20] So God rewarded the midwives, and meanwhile, the people continued to increase in number and become more powerful,
[Exodus] [1]:[21] and because the midwives had demonstrated their desire to obey God, he gave them families of their own.
[Exodus] [1]:[22] Then Par’oh (Pharaoh) commanded all of his people, “You all need to toss every newborn boy into the river, but you can let the girls live.”
[Exodus] [2]:[1] During this period, a man from the tribe of Levi married a woman who was also a Levite,
[Exodus] [2]:[2] and she conceived and gave birth to a son. When she saw that he was a healthy boy, she hid him away for three months,
[Exodus] [2]:[3] but then she wasn’t able to hide him any longer. So she got a basket made from woven reeds and plastered it with bitumen and pitch. Then she put the baby in it, and floated the basket in the reeds along the riverbank,
[Exodus] [2]:[4] leaving the baby’s sister to watch from a distance to see what would happen to him.
[Exodus] [2]:[5] After a while, Par’oh’s (Pharaoh) daughter came down to the river to wash herself, and she and her young attendants were walking along the riverbank. She saw the container among the reeds and sent one of her slave women to get it.
[Exodus] [2]:[6] She opened it and saw the baby inside, and wow, he started crying. She felt sorry for him and said, “This baby must be one of the Ivri (Hebrew) children.”
[Exodus] [2]:[7] Then his sister approached and asked the princess, “Would you like me to go and find a Ivri woman who’ll be able to breastfeed the baby for you?”
[Exodus] [2]:[8] “Yes, go,” answered Par’oh’s daughter, and the girl went and got the baby’s mother.
[Exodus] [2]:[9] “Take this baby,” said the princess, “and breastfeed him for me, and I’ll pay you for doing it.” So the woman took the baby and looked after him.
[Exodus] [2]:[10] When the boy had grown enough, she brought him back to Par’oh’s daughter and he became her son. She named him ‘Mosheh’ (Moses) (which means ‘pulled out’) because she said that she’d plucked him out of the river.
[Exodus] [2]:[11] Later on when Mosheh (Moses) was fully grown, he went out to visit the Ivrim (Hebrews) and saw their forced labour, and he saw an Mitsri (Egyptian) man beating a Ivri (Hebrew) man—one of his own people.
[Exodus] [2]:[12] Mosheh looked around to check that no one was watching, then he hit the Mitsri, killing him, then he hid his body in the sand.
[Exodus] [2]:[13] The next day, he went out again and wow, two Ivri men were fighting each other, and he said to the man in the wrong, “Why are you hitting your fellow Ivri?”
[Exodus] [2]:[14] “Who made you the ruler and judge over us?” the man replied. “Are you planning to kill me like you killed that Mitsri?” Then Mosheh was afraid because he realised that what he’d done had probably become widely known.
[Exodus] [2]:[15] Indeed, when Par’oh (Pharaoh) heard about it, he ordered Mosheh to be killed. So Mosheh had to flee from the king and he took off east to live in Midyan and he stayed near the well.
[Exodus] [2]:[16] The priest there in Midyan had seven daughters, and they would come to the well to draw water out and fill up the troughs there so their father’s sheep and goats could drink.
[Exodus] [2]:[17] Now some male shepherds came along and started to shoo their flock away, but Mosheh got involved and helped them so that their animals could drink.
[Exodus] [2]:[18] When they got home to their father Re’uel, he asked, “How come you got home so early today?”
[Exodus] [2]:[19] “There was an Mitsri man,” they answered, “who stood up for us against those other shepherds. And he even drew water for us and gave our flock water to drink.”
[Exodus] [2]:[20] “Where is he now?” he asked them. “What’s this—you mean you all just left him there? Go and get him so we can give him a meal.”
[Exodus] [2]:[21] Later it turned out that Mosheh was prepared to live with the man, and in due course he gave his daughter Tsiporah to Mosheh in marriage.
[Exodus] [2]:[22] When she gave birth to a son, he named him ‘Gereshom’ (which means ‘foreigner’) because he said, “I’ve become a foreigner living in a foreign land.”
[Exodus] [2]:[23] Eventually Mitsrayim’s (Egypt) king died, but the Israelis groaned from the slavery they were still under and they cried out, and their cry for freedom from slavery went up to God.
[Exodus] [2]:[24] He heard their groaning and remembered his agreement with Avraham, with Yitshak (Isaac), and with Ya’akov (Jacob),
[Exodus] [2]:[25] and he looked down on the Israelis and he was concerned about them.
[Exodus] [3]:[1] One time Mosheh (Moses) was shepherding the flock of his father-in-law Yitro (Jethro) (or Yitro, the priest at Midyan), and he led the flock beyond the wilderness and came to a hill. (This was later known as the mountain of God at Horev).
[Exodus] [3]:[2] While he was there. Yahweh’s messenger appeared to him in a flame coming from the middle of a bush, and as Mosheh looked, to his surprise he saw that the bush was burning in the fire yet not actually being burnt up.
[Exodus] [3]:[3] “I’ve got to go and see this amazing sight,” Mosheh said to himself. “How come that bush isn’t burning up?”
[Exodus] [3]:[4] When Yahweh saw that he’d left his path in order to look, God called to him from the middle of the bush, “Mosheh, Mosheh.” “I’m here,” he replied.
[Exodus] [3]:[5] “Don’t come any closer,” Yahweh said. “Take off your sandals because the place where you’re standing is HOLY ground.
[Exodus] [3]:[6] I’m the god of your father and the god of Avraham, Yitshak (Isaac), and Ya’akov (Jacob).” So Mosheh covered hid his face because he was scared to look at God.
[Exodus] [3]:[7] “I’ve certainly noticed the suffering of my people in Mitsrayim (Egypt),” Yahweh continued, “I’ve heard their cries as the slave drivers oppress them—I’m unmistakingly aware of their pain.
[Exodus] [3]:[8] So I’ve come down to set them free from Mitsri (Egyptian) control and to bring them up from there to a good and wide land—a land flowing with milk and honey. It’s currently the place of the Kena’anim (Canaanites), the Hitim, the Amorim, the Perizim, the Hivim, and the Yevusim.
[Exodus] [3]:[9] Yes, the cry of the Israelis has now reached me and what’s more, I’ve seen how much the Mitsrim (Egyptians) are oppressing them.
[Exodus] [3]:[10] So go now and I’ll send you to Par’oh (Pharaoh) and bring my people—Yisrael’s (Israel) descendants—out from Mitsrayim.”
[Exodus] [3]:[11] “Who am I, that I should go to Par’oh,” Mosheh asked God, “and that I should be the one to bring out the Israelis out from Mitsrayim?”
[Exodus] [3]:[12] “I’ll certainly be with you,” God replied, “and this will be your sign so that you’ll know that I have sent you: when you bring the people out from Mitsrayim, you all will serve God on this very hill.”
[Exodus] [3]:[13] “But listen,” Mosheh told God, “If I’m about to go to the Israelis and if I told them, ‘Your ancestors’ god has sent me to you.’ then they’d ask me, ‘Oh yeah, what’s his name?’ then what would I tell them?”
[Exodus] [3]:[14] “I AM WHO I AM,” God told Mosheh. “You’ll tell them this: ‘I AM (Yahweh) sent me to you.’ ”
[Exodus] [3]:[15] Then he continued, “This is what you need to tell the Israelis: ‘Yahweh, the god of your ancestors, the god of Avraham, Yitshak (Isaac), and Ya’akov (Jacob), sent me to you. This is my name forever, and this is my memorial throughout the generations.’
[Exodus] [3]:[16] Go and gather the Israeli elders, and tell them, ‘Yahweh, the god of your ancestors, appeared to me, the god of Avraham, Yitshak, and Ya’akov, to say, “I’ve certainly noticed you all and how you’re all being treated in Mitsrayim,
[Exodus] [3]:[17] and I’ve promised to take you all from your mistreatment in Mitsrayim, away to the land where the Kena’anim (Canaanites), Hitim, Amorim, Perizim, Hivim, and the Yevusim are currently living—to a land flowing with milk and honey.” ’
[Exodus] [3]:[18] Then the people will listen to what you tell them, and you and the Israeli elders will go to the Mitsri (Egyptian) king and you’ll all tell him, ‘Yahweh, the god of the Ivrim (Hebrews), has met with us. So now, please let us go three days’ journey into the wilderness, so we can sacrifice to Yahweh, our god.’
[Exodus] [3]:[19] But I know that the Mitsri king won’t let you go until he’s forced to.
[Exodus] [3]:[20] So I will use force and I’ll strike Mitsrayim with several supernatural acts, and after those, he’ll let you all go.
[Exodus] [3]:[21] Then I’ll make the Mitsri people favour you all in such a way that when you go, you won’t leave empty-handed.
[Exodus] [3]:[22] For example, an Israeli woman will ask her Mitsri neighbour (or from someone staying where she lives) for gold and silver items and for clothing. Then you’ll put them on your sons and daughters, and in this way you’ll all plunder the Mitsrim (Egyptians).”
[Exodus] [4]:[1] “But listen,” Mosheh (Moses) responded, “they won’t believe me and won’t listen to what I say, because they’ll say, ‘Yahweh never showed himself to you.’ ”
[Exodus] [4]:[2] “Well, what’s that in your hand?” Yahweh asked. “My shepherd’s staff,” he said.
[Exodus] [4]:[3] “Throw it on the ground,” Yahweh said. So Mosheh he threw it onto the ground and it became a snake, and he quickly moved back away from it.
[Exodus] [4]:[4] “Pick it up by its tail.” Yahweh told him. So Mosheh picked it up by the tail and it became a staff in his hand again.
[Exodus] [4]:[5] “That’s so that they’ll believe that I appeared to you: Yahweh—the god of their ancestors—the god of Avraham, Yitshak (Isaac), and Ya’akov (Jacob).”
[Exodus] [4]:[6] “Now put your hand on your chest—inside your robe.” Yahweh added. So Mosheh did that, and when he pulled it out again, his hand had gone totally white with disease.
[Exodus] [4]:[7] Then Yahweh said, “Now, put your hand back in again.” So Mosheh did it again, and when he pulled it out, wow, it had returned to normal.
[Exodus] [4]:[8] “So, if they don’t believe you, and if the first miracle doesn’t convince them, then they’ll believe that second miracle.
[Exodus] [4]:[9] And then, even if they don’t believe those two miracles and won’t believe what you tell them, then you should take some water from the river and pour it onto the dry land. Then the water which came from the river will turn into blood there on the dry land.”
[Exodus] [4]:[10] “Oh my master,” Mosheh responded, “I’m not very good at speaking to others—I never have been and still aren’t. I seem to get tongue-tied easily.”
[Exodus] [4]:[11] “Who was it that made people’s mouths?” Yahweh said. “Who makes someone mute or deaf, or seeing or blind? Isn’t it me, Yahweh?
[Exodus] [4]:[12] So get going now, and I’ll look after your mouth and show you what you to say.”
[Exodus] [4]:[13] But Mosheh replied, “Oh master, please send someone else.”
[Exodus] [4]:[14] Then Yahweh got angry with Mosheh and told him, “Isn’t Aharon (Aaron) a fellow Levite and your brother? I know that he can speak well, and what’s more, he’ll come from Mitsrayim (Egypt) to meet you, and when he does, he’ll be very happy.
[Exodus] [4]:[15] He’ll become your speaker and you’ll be able to talk to him and tell him what to say. I’ll be helping both of you speak and I’ll teach you both what you should do.
[Exodus] [4]:[16] So in that way, he’ll be like a mouth for you and speak to the people for you, and you’ll be like God to him.
[Exodus] [4]:[17] In addition, you’ll have that staff with you in order to do those miracles.”
[Exodus] [4]:[18] Then Mosheh (Moses) went back to his father-in-law Yitro (Jethro), and told him, “Can I please leave so I can return to my relatives in Mitsrayim (Egypt) and see whether they’re still alive.” “Go in peace,” Yitro answered.
[Exodus] [4]:[19] Meanwhile Yahweh had told Mosheh in Midyan, “Leave here and return to Mitsrayim because all those who wanted to kill you are now dead.”
[Exodus] [4]:[20] Then Mosheh took his wife and sons and put them on a donkey and returned towards Mitsrayim with them, and Mosheh took the staff that God had turned into a snake.
[Exodus] [4]:[21] On the way, Yahweh said to Mosheh, “When you return to Mitsrayim, all those miracles that I gave you, you’ll be able to demonstrate them in front of Par’oh (Pharaoh), but as for me, I’m going to make him stubborn so that he won’t let your people leave.
[Exodus] [4]:[22] But tell Par’oh, ‘Yahweh has stated that Yisrael (Israel) is like his oldest son
[Exodus] [4]:[23] and he asked you to let that son go so that he can serve him. But you refused to let Yisrael go, so Yahweh will kill your oldest son.’ ”
[Exodus] [4]:[24] One night as they were overnighting at a lodging place near the road, Yahweh confronted Mosheh and would have killed him,
[Exodus] [4]:[25] but his wife Tsiporah took a flint knife and cut off her son’s foreskin and threw it at Mosheh’s feet saying, “You’re definitely a bloody husband to me.”
[Exodus] [4]:[26] (That was referring to circumcision.) So then Yahweh left them alone.
[Exodus] [4]:[27] Meanwhile Yahweh had told Aharon (Aaron), “Go out into the wilderness to meet Mosheh.” So he went and met him at the hill of God, and he kissed him.
[Exodus] [4]:[28] Then Mosheh told Aharon everything that Yahweh had told him and how he had sent him, and all the miracles that he commanded him to demonstrate.
[Exodus] [4]:[29] Then Mosheh and Aharon went to Mitsrayim (Egypt) and they assembled all the Israeli elders
[Exodus] [4]:[30] and Aharon told them everything that Yahweh had spoken to Mosheh. Then Mosheh did the miracles in front of them,
[Exodus] [4]:[31] and the people believed. Then they heard how Yahweh had paid attention to the Israelis and that he had seen their suffering, and they bowed and prostrated themselves in thankfulness.
[Exodus] [5]:[1] After that, Mosheh (Moses) and Aharon (Aaron) went in and said to Par’oh (Pharaoh), “This is what Yisrael’s (Israel) god Yahweh says: ‘Let my people go, so they can celebrate me out in the wilderness.’ ”
[Exodus] [5]:[2] But the king said, “Who’s this ‘Yahweh’ that I should listen to him telling me to let Yisrael go? I don’t know Yahweh, and what’s more, I won’t let the Israelis go anywhere.”
[Exodus] [5]:[3] “The god of us Ivrim (Hebrews) has met with us,” they replied, “Please, let us go three days into the wilderness so we can sacrifice to our god Yahweh, because we don’t want him to strike us with deadly diseases or with war.”
[Exodus] [5]:[4] “Mosheh and Aharon,” the king of Mitsrayim (Egypt) answered, “why are you causing the people to slacken off from their tasks? Get back to your work.”
[Exodus] [5]:[5] And Par’oh continued, “Listen, there’s many of you and you two have caused them to rest from their duties.”
[Exodus] [5]:[6] Then on that very same day, Par’oh ordered the people’s slave masters and supervisors,
[Exodus] [5]:[7] “Don’t give straw to the people to make bricks with as you’ve done up till now. They can go and gather straw for themselves.
[Exodus] [5]:[8] But keep the same quota of bricks as before—don’t decrease it because they must be idle if they have time to say, ‘Let us go—let us sacrifice to our god.’
[Exodus] [5]:[9] Give the men more work so they’ll be too busy to worry about deceptive words.”
[Exodus] [5]:[10] So the slave masters and supervisors of the people went out and told them all, “The king has said that he won’t give you any more straw,
[Exodus] [5]:[11] so you’ll all have to go and get your own straw from wherever you can find it, because there’ll be no reduction to your quota.”
[Exodus] [5]:[12] So the people dispersed throughout all of Mitsrayim (Egypt) to gather stubble for straw,
[Exodus] [5]:[13] and the taskmasters were hassling them, saying, “Hurry up and finish your day’s work, the same as when you were given straw.”
[Exodus] [5]:[14] Then the Israeli foremen that Par’oh’s slave masters had appointed were beaten and told, “Why haven’t you met your required brick making quota yesterday or today? It’s just the same as in the past.”
[Exodus] [5]:[15] So the Israeli foremen went and complained to Par’oh, “Why are you treating your servants like this?
[Exodus] [5]:[16] We haven’t been given any straw and yet they’re telling us to keep making bricks. And see, we your servants get beaten, but it’s your people’s mistake.”
[Exodus] [5]:[17] “You’re all lazy—plain lazy!” the king responded. “That’s why you’re saying, ‘Let us go sacrifice to Yahweh.’
[Exodus] [5]:[18] So go now! Back to work! And you won’t be given straw, but you still have to meet the quota of bricks.”
[Exodus] [5]:[19] When the Israeli foremen heard that the quota wasn’t going to be reduced, they realised how serious their problem was,
[Exodus] [5]:[20] so when they left Par’oh they confronted Mosheh (Moses) and Aharon (Aaron) who were waiting to meet them,
[Exodus] [5]:[21] “May Yahweh see what you’ve done and judge you for it because you’ve raised a big stink in Par’oh’s mind and with his servants. Now they have their excuse to kill us!”
[Exodus] [5]:[22] Then Mosheh (Moses) went back to Yahweh and asked, “My master, why have you taken it out on our people? Was this why you sent me?
[Exodus] [5]:[23] Ever since I went to Par’oh (Pharaoh) to deliver your message, he’s made these people suffer and you clearly haven’t rescued them.”
[Exodus] [6]:[1] Then Yahweh said to Mosheh, “Now you’ll see what I’ll do to Par’oh. I’ll use my power to force him to let them go, and then using my power again he’ll actually drive them out of his country.”
[Exodus] [6]:[2] Then God spoke to Mosheh (Moses) again, “I am Yahweh
[Exodus] [6]:[3] and I revealed myself to Avraham, to Yitshak (Isaac), and to Ya’akov (Jacob) as El Shaddai (God the provider) but they didn’t know me by my name Yahweh.
[Exodus] [6]:[4] What’s more, I made an agreement with them: to give them the Kena’an (Canaan) region—the area which they had been staying in.
[Exodus] [6]:[5] Furthermore, I’ve heard the complaints from the Israelis who have been enslaved by the Mitsrim (Egyptians), and I have remembered my agreement.
[Exodus] [6]:[6] Therefore, tell the Israelis, ‘I am Yahweh and I will help you escape from the control of the Mitsrim and rescue you from their slavery. I’ll buy you out of slavery using my power and by punishing the Mitsrim for this injustice.
[Exodus] [6]:[7] I’ll take you all to be my own people, and I’ll be your god. Then you’ll know that I am Yahweh your god—the one rescuing you all from the Mitsri (Egyptian) oppression.
[Exodus] [6]:[8] Then I’ll take you all to the land that I promised to give to Avraham, to Yitshak, and to Ya’akov, and I’ll give it to you as your own. I am Yahweh.’ ”
[Exodus] [6]:[9] So Mosheh passed all that on to the Israelis, but they wouldn’t listen to Mosheh, because they were both discouraged and worn out from the slavery.
[Exodus] [6]:[10] Then Yahweh told Mosheh,
[Exodus] [6]:[11] “Go and speak to the Mitsri king Par’oh (Pharaoh) and tell him that he needs to let the Israelis leave his country.”
[Exodus] [6]:[12] And Mosheh said in front of Yahweh, “Look, the Israelis haven’t listened to me, so why would Par’oh listen? And I have difficulty speaking.”
[Exodus] [6]:[13] Then Yahweh spoke to Mosheh and Aharon (Aaron), and he gave them a command to pass on to the Israelis and to the Mitsri king Par’oh: to take the Israelis out of Mitsrayim (Egypt).
[Exodus] [6]:[14] The following were the leaders of the clans: The sons of Re’uven (Yisrael’s (Israel) eldest son) were Hanok, Palu, Hetsron, and Karmi, and they headed the clans of Re’uven.
[Exodus] [6]:[15] Shim’on’s (Simeon) sons were Yemuel, Yamin, Ohad, Yakin, Tsohar, and Shaul—the son of a Kena’ani (Canaanite) woman, and they headed the clans of Shim’on.
[Exodus] [6]:[16] Levi’s sons were Gereshon, Kohat, and Merari. Levi was 137 years old when he died.
[Exodus] [6]:[17] Gereshon’s sons were Livni and Shimei, and they headed their clans.
[Exodus] [6]:[18] Kohat’s sons were Amram, Yitshar, Hevron, and Uziel. Kohat was 133 years old when he died.
[Exodus] [6]:[19] Merari’s sons were Mahli and Mushi, and all of those headed the clans of Levi.
[Exodus] [6]:[20] Amram married his aunt Yokeved, and she gave birth to Aharon (Aaron) and Mosheh (Moses). Amram lived to be 137 years old.
[Exodus] [6]:[21] Yitshar’s sons were Korah, Nefeg, and Zikri.
[Exodus] [6]:[22] Uziel’s sons were Mishael, Elitsafan, and Sitri.
[Exodus] [6]:[23] Aharon married Elisheva, Aminadav’s daughter and the sister of Nahshon, and she gave birth to Nadav, Avihu, Eleazar, and Itamar.
[Exodus] [6]:[24] Korah’s sons were Asir, Elkanah, and Aviasaf, and they headed the clans of Korah.
[Exodus] [6]:[25] Aharon’s son Eleazar took a wife for himself from the daughters of Putiel and she gave birth to Pinhas. All of those headed the clans of Levi.
[Exodus] [6]:[26] It was to Aharon and Mosheh that Yahweh had said, “Bring the Israelis out of Mitsrayim (Egypt) by their tribes.”
[Exodus] [6]:[27] They were the ones who spoke to the Mitsri (Egyptian) king Par’oh (Pharaoh), to bring the Israelis out of Mitsrayim.
[Exodus] [6]:[28] On the day that Yahweh spoke to Mosheh (Moses) in Mitsrayim (Egypt),

[Exodus] [6]:[30] “Please listen to me,” Mosheh responded. “I’m not a good speaker, so why should Par’oh listen to me?”
[Exodus] [7]:[1] Yahweh answered, “Listen, I’ve made you like God to Par’oh, and your brother Aharon (Aaron) will be your prophet.
[Exodus] [7]:[2] You’ll quietly say everything that I tell you to and then your brother Aharon will relay it to Par’oh and tell him that he must let the Israelis leave his country.
[Exodus] [7]:[3] But I’ll make Par’oh stubborn and so I’ll increase the signs and miracles that I’ll do in Mitsrayim.
[Exodus] [7]:[4] Par’oh won’t listen to you so I’ll pressure Mitsrayim, and I’ll use severe judgements to ensure that I bring my armies—my people the Israelis—out Mitsrayim.
[Exodus] [7]:[5] The Mitsrim (Egyptians) will know that I am Yahweh when I demonstrate my power to Mitsrayim by taking the Israelis out from the middle of them.”
[Exodus] [7]:[6] So Mosheh and Aharon did everything that Yahweh told them to do.
[Exodus] [7]:[7] (Mosheh was eighty and Aharon was eighty-three when they were interacting with Par’oh.)

[Exodus] [7]:[11] Then Par’oh also called for his wise men and sorcerers, and the Mitsri (Egyptian) magicians did the same thing using their magic—
[Exodus] [7]:[12] each of them threw down his staff and they became snakes, except that Aharon’s staff swallowed up their staffs.
[Exodus] [7]:[13] But Par’oh’s mind was made up and he took no notice of them as Yahweh had said earlier.
[Exodus] [7]:[14] Then Yahweh told Mosheh (Moses), “Par’oh (Pharaoh) is very stubborn and he’s refused to let the people go.
[Exodus] [7]:[15] So go to Par’oh. Listen, every morning he goes down to the river, so station yourself to meet him on the bank. Take the staff with you that turned into a snake,
[Exodus] [7]:[16] and tell him, ‘Yahweh, the god of the Ivrim (Hebrews), previously sent me to you to say, “Let my people go so they can serve me in the wilderness.” But listen, until now you haven’t done it
[Exodus] [7]:[17] so Yahweh says, “Now you will know that I am Yahweh because of this: See, I’m about to use my staff to strike the water in the Nile and it will turn to blood
[Exodus] [7]:[18] and the fish in the river will die and the river will stink. Then your people will gag to drink the water from the river.” ’
[Exodus] [7]:[19] “Tell Aharon (Aaron) to take his staff and stretch out his hand over the waters of Mitsrayim (Egypt): over their streams, their canals, and their pools, and over every reservoir of their water, and the water will become blood. Then there’ll be blood in the entire country—even in wooden or stone containers of water.”
[Exodus] [7]:[20] So And Mosheh and Aharon did exactly what Yahweh had commanded: Aharon raised the staff and struck the river, while Par’oh and his servants watched, and the entire river turned to blood.
[Exodus] [7]:[21] Then the fish in the river died and the river stank, so the Mitsrim (Egyptians) couldn’t drink water from the river, and the blood was all over Mitsrayim.
[Exodus] [7]:[22] But the Mitsri (Egyptian) sorcerers did the same with their magic, and so Par’oh stayed stubborn and wouldn’t listen to them, just as Yahweh had said earlier.
[Exodus] [7]:[23] The Par’oh turned around and went back to his house, and he put all of that out of his mind.
[Exodus] [7]:[24] Meanwhile, all the Mitsrim dug holes around the river to get water to drink, because river water was undrinkable.
[Exodus] [7]:[25] So a week went by since Yahweh had struck the river
[Exodus] [8]:[1] and he said to Mosheh (Moses), “Go to Par’oh (Pharaoh) and tell him, ‘Yahweh says that you must let my people go so they can serve me.
[Exodus] [8]:[2] But if you refuse to let them go, then look, I’m about to pound your entire territory with frogs.
[Exodus] [8]:[3] The frogs will swarm in the river, then they’ll climb out and go into your house and in your bedroom and onto your bed. They’ll go into your servants’ houses and among your people, and in your cooking bowls and into your ovens.
[Exodus] [8]:[4] They’ll climb on you and on your people and on all your servants.’ ”
[Exodus] [8]:[5] Then Yahweh said to Mosheh, “Tell Aharon (Aaron): Hold your staff out over the canals, the streams, and the pools, and cause the frogs to come up onto the land of Mitsrayim (Egypt).”
[Exodus] [8]:[6] So Aharon reached out his hand over the Mitsri (Egyptian) water supplies and frogs came up and covered the land of Mitsrayim.
[Exodus] [8]:[7] But the sorcerers did the same with their magic, and they too brought up frogs over the land of Mitsrayim.
[Exodus] [8]:[8] Then Par’oh called for Mosheh and Aharon, and told them, “Ask Yahweh to take the frogs away from me and from my people. Then I’ll let your people go, and they can sacrifice to Yahweh.”
[Exodus] [8]:[9] Mosheh answered, “I’ll pray for you and your servants and your people, praying that the frogs will keep away from you and your homes and only be left in the river. And I’ll give you the honour of specifying when it’ll happen.”
[Exodus] [8]:[10] “Tomorrow morning,” the king replied. “Just as you say,” Mosheh responded, “so that you’ll know that there’s no one else like our god Yahweh.
[Exodus] [8]:[11] Tomorrow the frogs will leave you and go away from your houses, and from your servants and your people. They’ll only be left in the river.”
[Exodus] [8]:[12] Then Mosheh and Aharon left Par’oh and Mosheh called out to Yahweh concerning the retraction of the frogs that he’d sent against the king.
[Exodus] [8]:[13] So Yahweh did what Mosheh had requested and the frogs died off from the houses and the courtyards, and from the fields.
[Exodus] [8]:[14] The people collected them into many piles and the whole country stank.
[Exodus] [8]:[15] But when Par’oh saw that there was relief from the frogs, he firmed his resolve and didn’t listen to Mosheh and Aharon, just as Yahweh had said previously.
[Exodus] [8]:[16] Then Yahweh said to Mosheh (Moses), “Tell Aharon (Aaron): Stretch out your staff and strike the dust on the ground, and it will turn into lice all over Mitsrayim (Egypt).”
[Exodus] [8]:[17] So Aharon held out his staff and struck the dust with it, and the dust became lice on the people and on the animals. All over Mitsrayim, the dust turned into lice
[Exodus] [8]:[18] and the sorcerers tried to do the same with their magic but they were unable to. So there were lice on people and animals
[Exodus] [8]:[19] and the magicians said to Par’oh (Pharaoh), “This is God’s finger.” But Par’oh was stubborn and he didn’t listen to them, just as Yahweh had said previously.
[Exodus] [8]:[20] Then Yahweh said to Mosheh (Moses), “Get up early in the morning and when you see Par’oh (Pharaoh) coming down to the river, station yourself in front of him and tell him, ‘Yahweh saw that you must let my people go so they can serve me.
[Exodus] [8]:[21] Certainly if you don’t release my people immediately, then take note: I’m about to send the swarm at you and your servants and at your people and into your houses. The Mitsrim’ (Egyptians) houses will be full of the swarm and even the ground that they’re on.
[Exodus] [8]:[22] But when it happens, I’ll distinguish the Goshen region where my people live so the swarm won’t be there, so that you’ll be able to see that I’m Yahweh and I’m right here in this land.
[Exodus] [8]:[23] This sign will happen tomorrow and you’ll see how I plan to set my people free from your people.’ ”
[Exodus] [8]:[24] So Yahweh did what he’d said and a heavy swarm came to Par’oh’s house and the houses of his servants and all the Mitsrim—the country was ruined by the arrival of the swarm.
[Exodus] [8]:[25] Then Par’oh called for Mosheh and to Aharon (Aaron) and told them, “Go and sacrifice to the god of you all, but here in Mitsrayim (Egypt).”
[Exodus] [8]:[26] “It wouldn’t be right to do that,” Mosheh replied, “because our sacrifices to Yahweh our god would be offensive to Mitsrim. Listen, if we made sacrifices in front of the Mitsrim that are repulsive to them, wouldn’t they throw rocks at us to try to kill us?
[Exodus] [8]:[27] We need to travel into the wilderness for three days, then we’ll sacrifice to our god Yahweh there, just like he’s telling us to.”
[Exodus] [8]:[28] So Par’oh relented, “I’ll let you all go into the wilderness and sacrifice to Yahweh your god—except you definitely can’t go very far. Now, ask God for me for the plague to stop.”
[Exodus] [8]:[29] “Listen, I’m about to leave now,” Mosheh responded, “and I’ll pray to Yahweh and he’ll withdraw the swarm from Par’oh tomorrow, and from his servants and his people. But may Par’oh not be dishonest again and fail to let our people go to sacrifice to Yahweh.”
[Exodus] [8]:[30] Then Mosheh left Par’oh and prayed to Yahweh
[Exodus] [8]:[31] and Yahweh did what Mosheh asked him and he withdrew the swarm from Par’oh, and from his servants and his people. Not one remained.
[Exodus] [8]:[32] But Par’oh changed his mind and remained stubborn and he wouldn’t let the Israelis leave.
[Exodus] [9]:[1] Then Yahweh said to Mosheh (Moses), “Go in to Par’oh (Pharaoh) and tell him: ‘This is what the god of the Ivrim (Hebrews). Yahweh, says: Let my people go so they can serve me.
[Exodus] [9]:[2] Certainly if you’re unwilling to release them and if you keep holding onto them,
[Exodus] [9]:[3] then listen. Yahweh is about to inflict a very serious deadly disease onto your livestock which are in the fields—on the horses, the donkeys, the camels, the cattle, and on the flock.
[Exodus] [9]:[4] But Yahweh will distinguish between the livestock of the Israelis and the Mitsrim (Egyptians)—none of the Israelis’ animals will die.’ ”
[Exodus] [9]:[5] Then Yahweh said when it would happen, “Yahweh will do this to Mitsrayim (Egypt) tomorrow.”
[Exodus] [9]:[6] So the next day Yahweh did what he’d said and all of the livestock of the Mitsrim died, yet none at all from the livestock of the Israelis died.
[Exodus] [9]:[7] Par’oh sent people to investigate, and wow, not even one of the livestock of the Israelis had died. But Par’oh was strong-willed and wouldn’t let the people go.
[Exodus] [9]:[8] Then Yahweh told Mosheh (Moses) and Aharon (Aaron), “Take handfuls of ash out of a furnace, then Mosheh should toss it up in the air in front of Par’oh (Pharaoh).
[Exodus] [9]:[9] It will become a powder over all Mitsrayim (Egypt) and then it will turn into boils—bursting blisters—on people and on animals all over Mitsrayim.”
[Exodus] [9]:[10] So they took some ash from a furnace, and standing in front of Par’oh, Mosheh tossed it up into the air and it turned into boils with bursting blisters on the people and the animals.
[Exodus] [9]:[11] Because of the boils, the sorcerers weren’t even able to stand there with Mosheh because the sorcerers suffered with them along with all the Mitsrim (Egyptians).
[Exodus] [9]:[12] But Yahweh caused Par’oh to remain stubborn and he didn’t listen to them, just as Yahweh had told Mosheh previously.
[Exodus] [9]:[13] Then Yahweh told Mosheh (Moses), “Get up early in the morning, and stand in front of Par’oh (Pharaoh) and say to him, ‘This is what Yahweh, the god of the Ivrim (Hebrews), says: Let my people go so they can serve me
[Exodus] [9]:[14] because this time, I’m about to send all my plagues to you and your servants, and your people. You’ll all be deeply distressed by them, in order that you might know that there is no one else like me in all the world.
[Exodus] [9]:[15] By this time, I could have reached out and struck you and your people with such deadly disease or destruction that you would all have been obliterated from the land.
[Exodus] [9]:[16] However, I’ve kept you for this reason: to show you my power and in order to proclaim my name all over the world.
[Exodus] [9]:[17] You’re still considering yourself to be greater than my people by failing to release them.
[Exodus] [9]:[18] Now listen: I’m about to cause extremely heavy hail to rain down at this time tomorrow. It’ll be hail like which has never been seen before in Mitsrayim (Egypt) from the day it was founded until now.
[Exodus] [9]:[19] So send for your livestock and everything you own in the country now, and bring it in under cover because the hail will come down on every person and animal that is found in the countryside and not sheltering under a roof, and they will die.’ ”
[Exodus] [9]:[20] Some of Par’oh’s servants who believed what Yahweh said, quickly brought their slaves and their livestock back into their houses,
[Exodus] [9]:[21] but those people who didn’t believe Yahweh just left their slaves and their animals out in the countryside.
[Exodus] [9]:[22] “Raise your arm up toward the sky,” Yahweh told Mosheh (Moses), “and hail will strike all over Mitsrayim—on the people and animals and on every plant in the Mitsri (Egyptian) countryside.”
[Exodus] [9]:[23] So Mosheh lifted his staff to the sky, and Yahweh sent thunder and hail, and lightning caused fires on the land, and so Yahweh rained hail down onto Mitsrayim.
[Exodus] [9]:[24] There was hail, and also fire coming down in the middle of the hail. It was very heavy, such as had never been in all of Mitsrayim since it became a nation.
[Exodus] [9]:[25] The hail struck everything in Mitsrayim—everything that was in the countryside, from people to animals. It also struck every plant and broke every tree out in the countryside.
[Exodus] [9]:[26] Only in the Goshen region where the Israelis were, was there no hail.
[Exodus] [9]:[27] Then Par’oh sent for Mosheh and Aharon (Aaron) and told them, “I’ve sinned this time. Yahweh is righteous, and me and my people are guilty.
[Exodus] [9]:[28] Pray to Yahweh to stop it, because the thunder of God and hail are too much. Then I’ll release you all—you won’t have to remain here.”
[Exodus] [9]:[29] “As I’m leaving the city,” Mosheh replied, “I’ll spread my palms out to Yahweh. The thunder will stop and the hail won’t continue so that you will be able to see that the earth belongs to Yahweh.
[Exodus] [9]:[30] But as for you and your servants, I know that you still don’t fear Yahweh God.”
[Exodus] [9]:[31] (Now the flax and the barley were flattened by the hail because the barley was full grown and starting to fill out and the flax was in bloom.
[Exodus] [9]:[32] But the wheat and the spelt weren’t destroyed because they come later in the season.)
[Exodus] [9]:[33] So Mosheh left Par’oh, and as he was leaving the city, he spread his palms out to Yahweh and the thunder and hail ceased, and the rain stopped pouring down on the land.
[Exodus] [9]:[34] But when Par’oh saw that the rain and hail and thunder had stopped, he added to his sins and he firmed his resolve—he and his servants.
[Exodus] [9]:[35] And so Par’oh remained stubborn and didn’t let the Israelis leave, just as Yahweh had said through Mosheh previously.
[Exodus] [10]:[1] Then Yahweh told Mosheh (Moses), “Go in to Par’oh (Pharaoh) because I’ve made him and his servants stubborn in order to be able to demonstrate these miracles of mine among them,
[Exodus] [10]:[2] and so that in the future you’ll be able to tell your descendants that I made Mitsrayim (Egypt) look foolish, and my miracles which I demonstrated among them—and so that you will know that I am Yahweh.”
[Exodus] [10]:[3] So Mosheh and Aharon (Aaron) went in to Par’oh and told him, “This is what Yahweh, God of the Ivrim (Hebrews) says: how long before you’ll submit to me? Let my people go so they can serve me,
[Exodus] [10]:[4] because if you refuse to release them, then listen, I’ll bring locusts into your territory tomorrow.
[Exodus] [10]:[5] They’ll cover the ground so that no one will even be able to see it, and they’ll devour whatever remains after the hail. Plus they’ll devour every tree growing in the countryside.
[Exodus] [10]:[6] They’ll fill your houses and the houses of all your servants and the houses of all the Mitsrim (Egyptians). It’ll be nothing like anything which your parents generation ever saw, nor anything seen by the previous generations from the day they came to be on the earth until today.” Then Mosheh turned around and went out from Par’oh with Aharon.
[Exodus] [10]:[7] Then Par’oh’s servants asked him, “How much longer is this going to cause trouble for us? Let the men go and they’ll worship their god Yahweh. Don’t you understand yet that Mitsrayim is being destroyed?”
[Exodus] [10]:[8] So Mosheh and Aharon were brought back to Par’oh, and he told them, “Go and worship your god Yahweh. Who are the ones who’ll be going?”
[Exodus] [10]:[9] “We’ll take our children and our old folks,” Mosheh answered. “We’ll go with our sons and daughters, and with our flocks and herds, because the festival of Yahweh is for all of us.”
[Exodus] [10]:[10] “You’d need Yahweh with you if I ever let you and your children go together,” Par’oh responded. “You’re clearly plotting an evil trick!
[Exodus] [10]:[11] Well that won’t happen! The men may go and worship Yahweh since that’s what you’ve been wanting.” Then he drove them out of the room.
[Exodus] [10]:[12] Then Yahweh told Mosheh, “Extend your hand over Mitsrayim and let the locusts rise up over the land, and let them devour all the plants—everything which the hail had spared.”
[Exodus] [10]:[13] So Mosheh stretched his staff out over Mitsrayim, and Yahweh sent an east wind over the land all that day and all night. Then morning came, and the east wind had brought the locusts.
[Exodus] [10]:[14] The locusts covered across all the land of Mitsrayim and came to rest everywhere within the country’s borders. They were extremely numerous—never before were there so many locusts, and it’ll never be repeated again.
[Exodus] [10]:[15] The cloud of locusts blocked the sun and prevented people from being able to see very far. They devoured all the plants on the land and all of the fruit on the trees that the hail had left, and no piece of greenery remained on any tree or plant in the entire Mitsri (Egyptian) countryside.
[Exodus] [10]:[16] Par’oh quickly summoned Mosheh and Aharon (Aaron) and said, “I’ve sinned against your god Yahweh and against you.
[Exodus] [10]:[17] So now just this once, please overlook my sin and pray to your god Yahweh and just let him take this deathly plague away from me.”
[Exodus] [10]:[18] So Mosheh left Par’oh and went out and prayed to Yahweh,
[Exodus] [10]:[19] and Yahweh caused a very strong sea wind. The wind carried away the locusts and drove them into the Red Sea—not a single locust remained anywhere in Mitsri territory.
[Exodus] [10]:[20] But Yahweh caused Par’oh to remain stubborn and he wouldn’t release the Israelis.
[Exodus] [10]:[21] Then Yahweh told Mosheh (Moses), “Raise your hand up toward the sky and let it become dark over all Mitsrayim (Egypt)—darkness that can be felt.”
[Exodus] [10]:[22] So Mosheh stretched his hand out towards the sky, and a thick darkness was in all Mitsrayim for three days.
[Exodus] [10]:[23] No one could see anyone else, and for three days no one was able to go anywhere, yet there was light in the region where the Israelis lived.
[Exodus] [10]:[24] Then Par’oh (Pharaoh) summoned Mosheh and told him, “Go serve Yahweh. Your children can go with you all, but your flocks and your herds must remain behind.”
[Exodus] [10]:[25] “On top of that,” Mosheh responded, “you must also give us the sacrifices and offerings to be burnt when we will sacrifice to Yahweh our god.
[Exodus] [10]:[26] And even our livestock needs to go with us. Not a hoof will be left behind because we’ll choose from them to serve Yahweh our god. You see, we won’t know what we must sacrifice to Yahweh until we arrive there.”

[Exodus] [10]:[29] “Yes,” Mosheh responded. “It’s just as you say: I’ll never see you again!”
[Exodus] [11]:[1] Then Yahweh told Mosheh (Moses), “I’ll send one more plague to Par’oh (Pharaoh) and Mitsrayim (Egypt). After that he’ll let you all go from here. What’s more, when he does he’ll actually chase you all right out of here.
[Exodus] [11]:[2] Go and quietly tell the people that both men and women should ask their Mitsri (Egyptian) neighbours for items of gold and silver.”
[Exodus] [11]:[3] Then Yahweh gave the Israelis favour in the eyes of the Mitsrim (Egyptians). What’s more, Mosheh was very prestigious in the eyes of Par’oh’s servants and in the eyes of the Mitsri people.
[Exodus] [11]:[4] Then Mosheh told Par’oh, “This is what Yahweh says: Sometime around the middle of the night I’ll go out around Mitsrayim,
[Exodus] [11]:[5] and every oldest son in Mitsrayim will die, from the oldest son of Par’oh who sits on his throne, to the oldest son of the slave girl who lives behind the mill, as well as every oldest male offspring of your livestock.

[Exodus] [11]:[7] But amongst the Israelis, the dogs won’t growl at any person or animals so that you’ll know that Yahweh distinguishes between Mitsrayim and Yisrael (Israel).

[Exodus] [11]:[10] Mosheh and Aharon (Aaron) had done all those miracles in front of Par’oh but Yahweh had made Par’oh stubborn so he hadn’t let the Israelis leave his country.
[Exodus] [12]:[1] Then Yahweh told Mosheh (Moses) and Aharon (Aaron) in Mitsrayim (Egypt),
[Exodus] [12]:[2] “This month is to become the beginning of the months for you all—from now on it will be the first month of the new year.
[Exodus] [12]:[3] Assemble the people and tell them that on the tenth of this month, every man who’s the head of the household must select a lamb or young goat for his family.
[Exodus] [12]:[4] But if the household’s too small to cook a whole animal, then neighbours can combine and share—budgeting on how much each person eats.
[Exodus] [12]:[5] You all can choose either a sheep or a goat, but it must be a perfect, one-year-old male—without any defects.
[Exodus] [12]:[6] You all must take special care of those animals until the fourteenth day of this month, then every Israeli household will slaughter their animal early that evening.
[Exodus] [12]:[7] Then they must take some of the blood and put it on both doorposts and on the lintel of the houses that they’ll be in when they eat it.
[Exodus] [12]:[8] They must roast them on the fire and eat the meat that night, along with flat bread and bitter herbs.
[Exodus] [12]:[9] Don’t eat any of the meat raw and don’t boil it in water—it must be roasted over the fire with its head, legs, and internal organs.
[Exodus] [12]:[10] Nothing must be left by morning—anything that’s not eaten must be burnt in the fire.
[Exodus] [12]:[11] And this is how you all must eat it: with your belts fastened on your waists, your sandals on your feet, and your staffs in your hands. You all must eat it in a hurry. It is the Passover to Yahweh.
[Exodus] [12]:[12] Then during that night, I will move throughout Mitsrayim (Egypt) and I will kill all the oldest males—both people and animals. I will execute judgement on all the gods of Mitsrayim. I am Yahweh.
[Exodus] [12]:[13] That blood on the doorposts and lintel will be your sign on the houses which you are all in. I will see the blood and will pass over above you all, and the plague won’t affect you all with destruction as I strike against Mitsrayim.
[Exodus] [12]:[14] Then this day will become a memorial for you all, and you’ll celebrate it as a festival to Yahweh for future generations—a statute that you’ll all celebrate forever.
[Exodus] [12]:[15] For seven days you all must only eat flat bread made without yeast. Yes, on the first day you all must remove any yeast from your houses, because anyone who eats bread with yeast during those seven days, that person must be permanently driven out of Yisrael (Israel).
[Exodus] [12]:[16] On the first day, you all must gather for a sacred assembly, and similarly on the seventh day. No work can be done on those days other than meal preparation.
[Exodus] [12]:[17] You all must regularly observe the Flat Bread Celebration, because on this very day I will have brought your divisions out from Mitsrayim (Egypt). You all must observe this day throughout future generations—a statute that you’ll all celebrate forever.
[Exodus] [12]:[18] Starting on 14th of the first month in the evening, you all must eat only flat bread until the 21st day of the month in the evening.
[Exodus] [12]:[19] For seven days you all must have no yeast in your homes, because anyone who eats bread with yeast in it, that person must be driven out from the Israeli people whether they’re a foreigner or a native.
[Exodus] [12]:[20] You all mustn’t eat anything made with yeast. Wherever you live, you all must only eat flat bread.
[Exodus] [12]:[21] Then Mosheh (Moses) summoned the Israeli elders and told them, “Go ahead and select a lamb or young goat for each family and slaughter it.
[Exodus] [12]:[22] Then you all must take a bunch of leafy hyssop stalks, and dip it in the basin with the blood from the sacrifice and paint the blood onto the lintel and both doorposts. After that, absolutely no one should go out the door of your houses until morning.
[Exodus] [12]:[23] Then Yahweh will pass through out Mitsrayim (Egypt) to strike the Mitsrim (Egyptians) and when he sees the blood on the lintel and on the two doorposts, he’ll ‘pass over’ that doorway and won’t permit ‘the destroyer’ to enter into your houses to strike.
[Exodus] [12]:[24] All of you and your descendants must maintain this as a law and celebrate it forever,
[Exodus] [12]:[25] so when you all enter into the land that Yahweh will give to you just as he promised, then you must observe this ceremony.
[Exodus] [12]:[26] Then when it occurs, your children will ask, ‘What does this ceremony mean to you?’
[Exodus] [12]:[27] you all must tell them, ‘It’s the sacrifice of ‘pass-over’ to Yahweh, who passed over the houses of the Israelis in Mitsrayim when he struck the Mitsrim and rescued our families.’ ” And the people bowed their heads and prostrated themselves,
[Exodus] [12]:[28] and the Israelis went and did just as Yahweh had commanded through Mosheh and Aharon (Aaron).
[Exodus] [12]:[29] Then, in the middle of the night, Yahweh struck all the oldest males in Mitsrayim (Egypt), from the oldest son of Par’oh (Pharaoh) who sat on his throne, to the firstborn of the prisoner in the dungeon and all oldest male offspring of the animals.
[Exodus] [12]:[30] During the night, all the Mitsrim (Egyptians) got up, including Par’oh and all his servants. There was tremendous wailing throughout Mitsrayim because it was a very rare house where there wasn’t someone dead.
[Exodus] [12]:[31] Par’oh called for Mosheh (Moses) and Aharon (Aaron) in the night and told them, “Pack up and get out from among my people—you two and all the other Israelis. Go and serve Yahweh as you’ve said.
[Exodus] [12]:[32] Also take your flocks and your herds as you’ve said, and go. And bless me as well.
[Exodus] [12]:[33] The Mitsrim urged the Israelis, hurrying to let them go from the land because they said, “We’re all dying.”
[Exodus] [12]:[34] So the people carried their bread dough before it could rise. Their bread-making bowls were wrapped in their clothes on their shoulders.
[Exodus] [12]:[35] The Israelis did everything that Mosheh had instructed them, including asking for items of gold and silver, and clothing from the Mitsrim.
[Exodus] [12]:[36] Yahweh gave the people favour in the eyes of the Mitsrim, so by their requests, they were able to strip the Mitsrim of their wealth.
[Exodus] [12]:[37] Then the Israelis walked from Ra’meses toward Sukot—about 600,000 strong men on foot, not counting women and children.
[Exodus] [12]:[38] A large assortment of other people also went with them, along with large numbers of sheep and goats, and cattle.
[Exodus] [12]:[39] They baked the dough that they brought from Mitsrayim (Egypt) into flat bread since it hadn’t had time to rise, because they were driven out of Mitsrayim in a hurry and hadn’t had time to prepare food to take.
[Exodus] [12]:[40] The descendants of Yisrael (Israel) (also called Ya’akov (Jacob) ) had lived in Mitsrayim for 430 years
[Exodus] [12]:[41] to the day, because that very day was when all the various divisions of Yahweh’s people left Mitsrayim.
[Exodus] [12]:[42] It was a time when they stayed awake all night as Yahweh took them out of Mitsrayim—a night to be observed in that same way by every future generation.
[Exodus] [12]:[43] Then Yahweh told Mosheh (Moses) and Aharon (Aaron), “This is the statute of the ‘pass-over’: No foreigners may share in the meal that night,
[Exodus] [12]:[44] unless it’s a slave that you bought and who’s been circumcised—
[Exodus] [12]:[45] no foreigner or hired helper can join in the meal.
[Exodus] [12]:[46] Each animal must be eaten in only one house—don’t take any of the meat outside. And don’t break any of the animals bones.
[Exodus] [12]:[47] Every Israeli must observe it,
[Exodus] [12]:[48] and if someone is living among you and wants to join in Yahweh’s ‘pass-over’, then every male in their family must be circumcised. Only then will they be allowed to observe it, and then they should be considered like a native of the land. No uncircumcised person may eat it.
[Exodus] [12]:[49] This one law will apply to both the natives, and those who live among you all.”
[Exodus] [12]:[50] All the Israelis followed those instructions that Yahweh had given through Mosheh and Aharon,
[Exodus] [12]:[51] and so on that very day, Yahweh took all the Israelis out of Mitsrayim (Egypt) grouped by their family divisions.
[Exodus] [13]:[1] Then Yahweh told Mosheh (Moses),
[Exodus] [13]:[2] “All firstborn offspring are to be consecrated to me—the first product of every womb, whether human or animal, belongs to me.”
[Exodus] [13]:[3] Then Mosheh (Moses) told the people, “Always remember this day, that you went out of Mitsrayim (Egypt), rescued from slavery, because Yahweh used his power to bring you out from there. And nothing with yeast in it can be eaten when you celebrate this.
[Exodus] [13]:[4] Today you are leaving in the month of Aviv,
[Exodus] [13]:[5] and when Yahweh brings you into the area occupied by the Kena’anim (Canaanites), Hitim, Amorim, Hivim, and the Yevusim (which he swore to your fathers to give to you—a land flowing with milk and honey) you must observe this ceremony in this same month.

[Exodus] [13]:[9] It’ll be like a reminder written on your hand and hanging from your forehead, so that you’ll remember to pass on Yahweh’s instructions because he used his power to bring you out of Mitsrayim.
[Exodus] [13]:[10] So you must follow those instructions at the appointed time year after year.
[Exodus] [13]:[11] Later, when Yahweh brings you into the land of the Kena’anim (Canaanites) as he promised to you and your ancestors, and he gives it to you,
[Exodus] [13]:[12] then hand over to Yahweh all your oldest sons, and all the oldest, male animal offspring that are yours. They will then belong to Yahweh.
[Exodus] [13]:[13] In the case of the oldest donkey foal, you must buy it back by killing a lamb instead of it. If you don’t buy it back, you must kill the donkey by breaking its neck. You must buy back every one of your oldest sons,
[Exodus] [13]:[14] and in the future when your son asks you, ‘What’s that about?’ then you must tell him, ‘We were enslaved in Mitsrayim (Egypt) , but Yahweh used his incredible power to bring us out.
[Exodus] [13]:[15] And so it was that when Par’oh (Pharaoh) was too stubborn to let us go, then Yahweh struck all of the oldest sons and oldest male animals in Mitsrayim. That’s why we offer all the oldest offspring to Yahweh, and why we need to buy back all our oldest sons.’
[Exodus] [13]:[16] So you must place a reminder on your hand and hanging on your forehead that Yahweh used his incredible power to bring us out of Mitsrayim.”
[Exodus] [13]:[17] When Par’oh (Pharaoh) released the people, God didn’t lead them through the area occupied by the Pelishtim, although that way was shorter, because he said, “It’s best if the people don’t have to face war immediately, or they might change their minds and then want to return to Mitsrayim (Egypt).”
[Exodus] [13]:[18] So God caused the people to take the path going towards the wilderness and the Red Sea. The Israeli left Mitsrayim in formation as if ready for battle.
[Exodus] [13]:[19] Mosheh (Moses) ensured that Yosef’s (Joseph) bones were taken with them, because many years back Yosef had made the Israelis promise, saying, “God will certainly take notice of you all, and you must take my bones out from here with you.”
[Exodus] [13]:[20] The people travelled on from Sukot and camped at Etam on the edge of the wilderness.
[Exodus] [13]:[21] During the day, Yahweh went ahead of them in a pillar of cloud to lead them on the way, and at nighttime, he went in a pillar of fire to be light to them, so they could travel both in the daytime and at night.
[Exodus] [13]:[22] The daytime pillar of cloud and the nighttime pillar of fire, didn’t ever leave their place ahead of the people.
[Exodus] [14]:[1] Then Yahweh told Mosheh (Moses),
[Exodus] [14]:[2] “Tell the Israelis that they should turn and camp in front of Pi-Hahirot, between Migdol and the sea, in front of Ba’al-Tsefon. You all are to camp by the sea opposite it.
[Exodus] [14]:[3] Then Par’oh (Pharaoh) will say, ‘They are confused and lost—the wilderness has boxed them in.’
[Exodus] [14]:[4] I’ll strengthen Par’oh’s resolve and he’ll chase after them. Then because of Par’oh and all his army, I’ll be honoured and the Mitsrim (Egyptians) will know that I am Yahweh.” So the Israelis camped where they were instructed.
[Exodus] [14]:[5] When the king of Mitsrayim (Egypt) was told that the Israelis had fled, he and his servants started thinking about their own people and they asked, “What have we done by letting the Israeli slaves go free?”
[Exodus] [14]:[6] Then he hitched up his chariot and took his army with him.
[Exodus] [14]:[7] He took 600 of the best chariots as well as all the other Mitsri (Egyptian) chariots and officers to supervise them.
[Exodus] [14]:[8] Yahweh strengthened the Mitsri king’s resolve and so Par’oh pursued after the Israelis after they had confidently marched out of Mitsrayim.
[Exodus] [14]:[9] The Mitsrim pursued them, then all of Par’oh’s horses and chariots, along with his mounted soldiers and his foot army, overtook them camping above the sea above Pi-Hahirot, across from Ba’al-Tsefon.
[Exodus] [14]:[10] As the Mitsrim approached, the Israelis looked back, and to their horror, saw the army coming after them. They were extremely afraid and cried out to Yahweh.
[Exodus] [14]:[11] They complained to Mosheh, “Is it because there weren’t any graves in Mitsrayim that you brought us here to die in the wilderness? What have you done to us? Why did you bring us out from Mitsrayim?
[Exodus] [14]:[12] Isn’t this exactly what we told you in Mitsrayim when we said, ‘Just leave us alone and let us serve the Mitsrim’? Because serving the Mitsrim sounds a lot better to us than dying out here in the wilderness.”
[Exodus] [14]:[13] Then Mosheh (Moses) told the people, “You mustn’t be afraid. Stand still and see how Yahweh saves you all—he’s going to do it today, because any Mitsrim that you see today, you’ll never, ever see them again.
[Exodus] [14]:[14] Yahweh himself will fight for you all—all you need to do is to remain calm.”
[Exodus] [14]:[15] Then Yahweh scolded Mosheh, “Why are you still here crying out to me? Talk to the Israelis and get them moving forward.
[Exodus] [14]:[16] As for you, raise your staff and stretch your arm out over the sea and divide it. Then the Israelis will go on onto dry ground through the middle of the sea.
[Exodus] [14]:[17] Yes, watch me! I’ll strengthen the resolve of the Mitsrim and they’ll enter between the sea after them. Then I’ll be honoured because of what will happen to Par’oh (Pharaoh) and all his army, and his chariots and his horsemen.
[Exodus] [14]:[18] The honour that I gain through that will cause the Mitsrim to know that I’m Yahweh.”
[Exodus] [14]:[19] Then God’s messenger who travelled ahead of the Israelis, moved and went behind them. Also the pillar of cloud moved from in front of them and stood behind them
[Exodus] [14]:[20] and so it was then between the coming Mitsrim and the Israelis. Then the cloud became darkness on the Mitsri (Egyptian) side, yet it lit up the other side, and no one could approach it all night.
[Exodus] [14]:[21] Then Mosheh stretched his arm out over the sea and Yahweh sent a strong east wind. It blew all night and divided the sea on each side and dried the strip of land in the middle.
[Exodus] [14]:[22] So then the Israelis entered through the middle of the sea on dry ground with a wall of water on each side of them.
[Exodus] [14]:[23] However, the Mitsrim pursued after them. Every one of Par’oh’s horses and chariots and his horsemen also entered into the middle of the sea.
[Exodus] [14]:[24] By now morning was coming and Yahweh looked down through the pillar of fire and cloud, and he caused confusion for the Mitsri army.
[Exodus] [14]:[25] He caused the wheels of their chariots to turn unevenly so they became difficult to drive, and the Mitsrim complained, “Let’s retreat from following the Israelis, because Yahweh is fighting against Mitsrayim (Egypt) and for them.”
[Exodus] [14]:[26] On the other side, Yahweh told Mosheh, “Stretch your arm out over the sea and the waters will flow back onto the Mitsrim and onto Par’oh’s chariots and his horsemen.”
[Exodus] [14]:[27] So Mosheh stretched his arm out over the sea, and as the day broke, the sea began to return to its normal place. The Mitsrim turned and fled before its impact but Yahweh shook the Mitsrim off their horses and chariots in the middle of the sea.
[Exodus] [14]:[28] So the sea returned and covered the chariots and the horsemen—even Par’oh’s entire army that had entered into the sea after the Israelis. Not even one of the pursuers remained.
[Exodus] [14]:[29] But the Israelis had walked through the middle of the sea on dry ground with a wall of water on each side of them.
[Exodus] [14]:[30] So Yahweh saved Yisrael (Israel) from Mitsrayim’s power that day, and the Israelis saw the Mitsrim’ bodies washed up on the shore.
[Exodus] [14]:[31] All the Israelis saw the incredible power that Yahweh had used against the Mitsrim, and the people revered Yahweh, and put their trust in him and his servant Mosheh.
[Exodus] [15]:[1] Then Mosheh (Moses) and the Israelis sang this song to Yahweh: “I will sing to Yahweh because he’s been so successful— he’s thrown both the horses and their riders into the sea.
[Exodus] [15]:[2] I will sing about Yahweh, my source of strength, and the one who saves me. I will praise him because he’s my god— he’s my father’s god and I will honour him.
[Exodus] [15]:[3] Yahweh is a warrior. Yahweh is his name.
[Exodus] [15]:[4] He threw Par’oh’s (Pharaoh) chariots and his army into the sea. His hand-picked officers have been sunk in the sea.
[Exodus] [15]:[5] The deep waters cover them. They descended into the depths like a stone.
[Exodus] [15]:[6] Yahweh’s right arm is so powerful. Yahweh’s right arm shattered our enemy.
[Exodus] [15]:[7] You toss away your adversaries with your great power. Your burning anger consumes them like straw in a fire.
[Exodus] [15]:[8] It was your breath that made the waters pile up. They stood up like a heap. The deep water seemed like it was solid.
[Exodus] [15]:[9] Our enemies thought that they could chase after us and overtake us. They had planned to satisfy themselves by sharing out the plunder. They were ready to use their swords and swing their arms to destroy us.
[Exodus] [15]:[10] But you blew with your breath. The sea covered them. They sank like lead in that terrible surge.
[Exodus] [15]:[11] Which other god is like you, Yahweh? Who else is so powerful and yet sinless, receiving praises for doing miracles?
[Exodus] [15]:[12] You stretched out your powerful arm. The earth swallowed them up.
[Exodus] [15]:[13] You are leading the people you bought back, because you committed yourself to love them. You used your strength to lead them to your sinless home.
[Exodus] [15]:[14] Other countries have heard, and they tremble. Anguish has struck the inhabitants of Peleshet.
[Exodus] [15]:[15] The chiefs of Edom have panicked. Trembling has seized the leaders of Moav (Moab). The inhabitants of Kena’an (Canaan) have melted away.
[Exodus] [15]:[16] Terror and dread have fallen on them. After seeing your great power, they’ve stayed as still as stone until your people have all marched past, Yahweh. Until the people you bought have all gone past them.
[Exodus] [15]:[17] Bring them into the land and establish them on the mountain of your inheritance. The place you’ve chosen to become your home, Yahweh— a sanctuary built by your hands, master.
[Exodus] [15]:[18] Yahweh will reign as king forever and ever.
[Exodus] [15]:[19] Par’oh’s (Pharaoh) horse went into the sea, along with his chariots and horsemen, and Yahweh brought the water back over them, after the Israelis had walked through on dry ground in the middle of the sea.”
[Exodus] [15]:[20] Then Aharon’s (Aaron) sister Miryam (Miriam) who was a prophetess, picked up a tambourine and went outside. All the other women did likewise and followed her out to dance together
[Exodus] [15]:[21] so Miryam sang this response: “Sing to Yahweh and tell of his amazing victory— He tossed the horses and their riders into the sea.”
[Exodus] [15]:[22] Then Mosheh (Moses) lead the Israelis away from the Red Sea and they moved into the wilderness at Shur. They went through the wilderness for three days and finally found some water,
[Exodus] [15]:[23] but it was so bitter that they couldn’t drink it. So they named that place ‘Marah’ (which means ‘bitter’),
[Exodus] [15]:[24] and the people grumbled about Mosheh saying, “So what will we drink then?”
[Exodus] [15]:[25] So Mosheh cried out to Yahweh, and Yahweh showed him a tree. When he threw it into the water, the water became safe to drink. Yahweh made a statue at that place, and a rule, and he tested Mosheh there,
[Exodus] [15]:[26] saying, “If you carefully listen to the voice of Yahweh your god, and you do what’s right in my eyes, and you listen to my commands and you keep all of my laws, then I won’t inflict you with any of the diseases that I put on the Mitsrim (Egyptians), because I’m Yahweh your healer.”
[Exodus] [15]:[27] Then they moved on and came to Eylim where there were twelve springs and seventy palm trees, and they camped there by the water.
[Exodus] [16]:[1] Then they left Eylim, and all the Israelis entered into the wilderness at Sin (between Eylim and Sinay) around six weeks after leaving Mitsrayim (Egypt),
[Exodus] [16]:[2] and all the Israelis murmured against Mosheh (Moses) and Aharon (Aaron) there in the wilderness,
[Exodus] [16]:[3] saying, “If only Yahweh had killed us in Mitsrayim, where we’d be sitting by a pot of meat eating bread until we’re full, because you’ve brought us out into this wilderness to starve us all to death.”
[Exodus] [16]:[4] Then Yahweh told Mosheh, “Just watch me make food rain down from the sky for you all. Then the people will be able to go out every day and gather enough for that day so that I can test them: Will they obey my law or not?
[Exodus] [16]:[5] But every Friday they can gather and prepare twice as much as what they gather on the other days.”
[Exodus] [16]:[6] So Mosheh and Aharon told all the Israelis, “This evening you’ll all know that Yahweh was the one who brought you out from Mitsrayim.
[Exodus] [16]:[7] In the morning you’ll all see Yahweh’s greatness as he’s heard your murmurings against him. I mean, who are we that you’d murmur against us?”
[Exodus] [16]:[8] Then Mosheh continued, “So Yahweh will give you all meat to eat in the evening and enough bread in the morning to make you all full. Yes, Yahweh has heard your murmurings against him. As for us, we’re insignificant. Your murmuring isn’t against us, but against Yahweh.”
[Exodus] [16]:[9] Then Mosheh told Aharon, “Summon everyone to come and face Yahweh, because he’s heard their murmurings.”
[Exodus] [16]:[10] And so while Aharon spoke to all the Israelis, they turned toward the wilderness, and wow, Yahweh’s dazzling brightness appeared in the cloud!
[Exodus] [16]:[11] Then Yahweh told Mosheh,
[Exodus] [16]:[12] “I’ve heard the murmurings of the Israelis. Speak to them saying, ‘In the evenings, you’ll all eat meat, and in the mornings you’ll all be satisfied with bread. Then you’ll all know that I’m your god, Yahweh.’ ”
[Exodus] [16]:[13] And so that evening, quail appeared and covered the camp. And in the morning, something like dew was lying all around the camp,
[Exodus] [16]:[14] and when it evaporated, wow, it left behind thin flakes—thin like frost on the ground there in the wilderness.
[Exodus] [16]:[15] When the Israelis saw it, they asked each other, ‘What is it?’ because they didn’t know what it was. And Mosheh told them, “It’s the food that Yahweh has given you all to eat.
[Exodus] [16]:[16] These are Yahweh’s instructions: Gather enough of it according to how many people you’re feeding—about two litres per person who lives in your tents.”
[Exodus] [16]:[17] So the Israelis went ahead and gathered it—some collecting a lot, and others, less,
[Exodus] [16]:[18] but when they measured it out, those who’d collected a lot didn’t have any extra, and those who hadn’t gathered so much still had enough to eat—each person had gathered just enough.
[Exodus] [16]:[19] Then Mosheh told them, “Don’t save any of it for tomorrow,”
[Exodus] [16]:[20] but some of them didn’t take any notice of him and kept it until the next morning. However, by then it was full of maggots and smelt rotten, and Mosheh was very angry at them.
[Exodus] [16]:[21] So from that day onwards, they gathered it every morning, depending on how many they were feeding, and then when the sun got hot, the rest melted away.
[Exodus] [16]:[22] On the Friday, they gathered twice as much—around four litres for each person—and all the leaders of the community came and informed Mosheh
[Exodus] [16]:[23] and he told them, “This is what Yahweh said: Tomorrow is a rest day to be set aside for Yahweh. So bake or cook your food, and keep the left-overs overnight to use in the morning.”
[Exodus] [16]:[24] So they did what Mosheh had told them and kept the left-overs until the morning, and it didn’t stink or have any bugs in it.
[Exodus] [16]:[25] On that Saturday morning, Mosheh told them, “Go ahead and eat the previously cooked food because today is set aside for Yahweh and so you all won’t find any more on the ground—
[Exodus] [16]:[26] you’ll gather it for six days each week, but on the Saturday, there won’t be any.”
[Exodus] [16]:[27] However, some people did go out to collect it, but they couldn’t find any,
[Exodus] [16]:[28] and Yahweh said to Mosheh, “For how long will you all keep refusing to obey my commands and my laws?
[Exodus] [16]:[29] Listen, Yahweh has given you the Rest Day, so on the Friday he gives you food for two days. On the Saturday, everyone should stay where they are—there’s no need for anyone to go outside searching.”
[Exodus] [16]:[30] So the people didn’t work on the Saturday.
[Exodus] [16]:[31] The Israelis named it ‘manna’ (which sounds like Hebrew ‘What is it?’). It was white like coriander seed, and it tasted like wafers with honey.
[Exodus] [16]:[32] Then Mosheh said, “This is the procedure that Yahweh has commanded: Keep a full measure of it for preservation for your descendants so that they can see the food which I fed you in the wilderness, when I brought you out from Mitsrayim (Egypt).”
[Exodus] [16]:[33] So Mosheh said to Aharon (Aaron), “Take a jar and fill it with the full two litres of manna. Place it in front of Yahweh for preservation for your descendants.”
[Exodus] [16]:[34] So Aharon prepared the jar and kept it (and would eventually place it in the box with the stone tablets.)
[Exodus] [16]:[35] The Israelis ate manna for forty years, until they eventually left the wilderness and came to the borders of the region of Kena’an (Canaan).
