[Exodus] [26]:[16] and each one must be five metres high and 0.75m wide.
[Exodus] [26]:[17] Each frame must have two protrusions so it can be connected to the frame next to it.
[Exodus] [26]:[18] Assemble twenty frames for the south side of the residence
[Exodus] [26]:[19] along with forty silver bases to go underneath them—two bases supporting each frame, and each frame having two protrusions at the bottom to go into the bases.
[Exodus] [26]:[20] For the north side, assemble twenty frames
[Exodus] [26]:[21] along with forty silver bases—two under each frame.
[Exodus] [26]:[22] For the rear of the residence facing west, assemble six frames
[Exodus] [26]:[23] plus two extra frames for bracing the two back corners—
[Exodus] [26]:[24] they must be joined on at the bottom and then both of them have their tops attached to a ring.
[Exodus] [26]:[25] Then assemble eight frames with their sixteen silver bases—two bases supporting each frame.
[Exodus] [26]:[26] Make crossbars from acacia wood—five of them to go across the frames on the northern side,
[Exodus] [26]:[27] five for the south side, and five for the frames at the rear of the residence on the western side.
[Exodus] [26]:[28] The middle crossbar in the centre of the frames will go right through from one end to the other.
[Exodus] [26]:[29] Overlay the frames and the crossbars with gold, and make the rings for holding the crossbars with gold.
[Exodus] [26]:[30] Then you must assemble my residence exactly as per the plan that you were shown on the mountain.
[Exodus] [26]:[31] You must have a skillful workman make a curtain from twisted finely-spun linen, with winged-creatures embroidered on them using blue, purple, and scarlet thread.
[Exodus] [26]:[32] Hang it from gold clips on four pillars made from acacia wood overlaid with gold on four silver bases.
[Exodus] [26]:[33] Hang the curtain under the clips, then bring the box that contains the agreement inside the curtain. That curtain will separate for you between the sacred section and the very sacred interior.
[Exodus] [26]:[34] Install the atonement platform as the lid on the box there in the very sacred interior.
[Exodus] [26]:[35] Set the table up outside the curtain on the north side, with the lampstand on the south side opposite the table.
[Exodus] [26]:[36] Then make a curtain out of twisted finely-spun linen for the entrance of the tent. It should be embroidered with blue, purple and scarlet yarn.
[Exodus] [26]:[37] Make five pillars for the curtain from acacia wood overlaid with gold. The hooks on them must be made of gold, and their five bases must be cast with bronze.
[Exodus] [27]:[1] Make an altar from acacia wood that’s 2.5m square and 1.5m high
[Exodus] [27]:[2] and as part of that same piece of wood, include a carved projection like a horn on each of the top corners of the altar. Overlay the altar with bronze.
[Exodus] [27]:[3] Make pots for the ashes out of bronze, along with the necessary shovels, sprinkling bowls, meat forks, and fire-trays.
[Exodus] [27]:[4] Then make a bronze grating for it with four rings of bronze on the four corners.
[Exodus] [27]:[5] Fit it down onto a ledge inside the altar so that it sits inside the altar about halfway up.
[Exodus] [27]:[6] Also, make poles from acacia wood for the altar and overlay them with bronze.
[Exodus] [27]:[7] They’ll be able to be put into rings on two sides of the altar for carrying it.
[Exodus] [27]:[8] The altar should be hollow in the middle and made from wooden planks just like you were shown on the mountain.
[Exodus] [27]:[9] Make curtains of twisted finely-spun linen to form a courtyard around the residence. The south side will require fifty metres of curtain
[Exodus] [27]:[10] with twenty bronze pillars and their twenty bases. The hooks on the pillars and the clips must be made of silver.
[Exodus] [27]:[11] Similarly on the north side, another fifty metres of curtain with twenty pillars and their bases and their hooks and clips.
[Exodus] [27]:[12] The west side will require twenty-five metres of curtain with ten pillars and bases.
[Exodus] [27]:[13] The east side of the courtyard must also be twenty-five metres wide.
[Exodus] [27]:[14] On one side of the gate, the curtain will be 7.5m long with three pillars and bases,
[Exodus] [27]:[15] and the same on the other side.
[Exodus] [27]:[16] The entrance curtain must be made of twisted finely-spun linen. It’ll be ten metres wide and hang on four pillars with their bases, and must be embroidered with blue, purple, and scarlet yarn.
[Exodus] [27]:[17] All the pillars for the courtyard must have silver decorations around them, as well as their silver hooks and bronze bases.
[Exodus] [27]:[18] So the courtyard will be fifty metres by twenty-five metres and the curtain enclosure will be 2.5m high. All the curtains will be made of finely-spun linen, and the bases under all the pillars will be bronze.
[Exodus] [27]:[19] All the equipment for the operation of the residence and all the tent pegs and pegs for the courtyard must be made of bronze.
[Exodus] [27]:[20] Order the Israelis to bring you pure, pressed olive oil for the lamps so they can be kept burning continually.
[Exodus] [27]:[21] In the outer portion of the sacred tent (outside the curtain where the sacred box is kept), Aharon (Aaron) and his sons must attend to the lampstand in front of Yahweh from evening to morning. This regulation will apply continually to all future generations of Israelis.
[Exodus] [28]:[1] Now, have your brother Aharon (Aaron) and his sons brought to you from among the Israelis. Aharon, Nadav, Avihu, Eleazar, and Itamar will become my priests.
[Exodus] [28]:[2] Make sacred clothes for Aharon—they must be uniquely beautiful
[Exodus] [28]:[3] so speak to all the skilled craftsmen who’ve been given the spirit of wisdom, and they can make Aharon’s clothes to dedicate him as my priest.
[Exodus] [28]:[4] These are the clothes that they’ll need to make: a small pouch to hang around the neck and an apron, a robe and a tunic of woven work, and a turban and a waistband. They must make those sacred clothes for your brother Aharon and for his sons to serve as my priests.
[Exodus] [28]:[5] The skilled craftsmen must be given gold wire and blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, and finely-spun linen.
[Exodus] [28]:[6] They must make the sacred apron from twisted finely-spun linen with gold wire and blue, purple, scarlet yarn embroidered onto it by a skilled craftsman.
[Exodus] [28]:[7] It should have two shoulder pieces attached to the top two corners so it can be fastened.
[Exodus] [28]:[8] Then the waistband for the apron shall be made with similar workmanship from twisted finely-spun linen with gold wire and blue, purple, and scarlet yarn skillfully embroidered into it.
[Exodus] [28]:[9] Then get two onyx stones and engrave the names of Yisrael’s (Israel) twelve sons onto them—
[Exodus] [28]:[10] six names on one stone and six on the other, in their birth order.
[Exodus] [28]:[11] A stone craftsman with experience at making signet rings should do the engravings, and then mount the two stones in decorative gold settings.
[Exodus] [28]:[12] Then attach the two stones to the shoulder pieces of the apron as a reminder about Yisrael’s sons. That way Aharon (Aaron) will carry their names on his two shoulders as a reminder every time he goes to face Yahweh.
[Exodus] [28]:[13] Make the decorative settings for the two stones from gold,
[Exodus] [28]:[14] and then make two twisted chains of pure gold like a cord that you can attach to the decorative settings.
[Exodus] [28]:[15] Make a sacred chest pouch for important decision making. A skilled craftsman should make it from twisted finely-spun linen like the apron, embroidered with gold wire and blue, purple, and scarlet yarn.
[Exodus] [28]:[16] It needs to be 23cm square when folded over double,
[Exodus] [28]:[17] and it will have four rows of three gemstones on it: a red ruby, a yellow topaz, a green emerald,
[Exodus] [28]:[18] then a turquoise, a blue sapphire, a diamond,
[Exodus] [28]:[19] then a red jacinth, a white agate, a purple amethyst,
[Exodus] [28]:[20] and in the last row, a yellow beryl, an onyx, and a green jasper. All those stones must be mounted in decorative gold settings,
[Exodus] [28]:[21] and so they’ll represent the twelve tribes of Yisrael (Israel). The names of the twelve sons must be engraved on the stones similar to how signet rings are made.
[Exodus] [28]:[22] Make two twisted chains of pure gold like a cord that you can attach to the pouch,
[Exodus] [28]:[23] then make two gold rings and attach them to the two top corners of the pouch.
[Exodus] [28]:[24] Attach the two gold chains to the rings on the corners
[Exodus] [28]:[25] with the other ends fastened to the two decorative settings around the stones and then attached to the front side of the shoulder straps.
[Exodus] [28]:[26] Make two more gold rings and attach them on the inside to the two bottom corners of the pouch,
[Exodus] [28]:[27] and another two gold rings to be attached to the bottom of the two shoulder pieces near where the shoulder straps join the apron just above the crafted waistband.
[Exodus] [28]:[28] Then tie the rings on the sacred pouch to the rings on the apron with a blue cord so that the pouch sits above the waistband and can’t come loose from the apron.
[Exodus] [28]:[29] Then whenever Aharon (Aaron) enters the sacred inner room to stand in front of me, he’ll be carrying the names of Yisrael’s sons over his heart on the sacred pouch that’ll be used for making decisions.
[Exodus] [28]:[30] Then place the ‘Urim’ and the ‘Tumim’ in the sacred pouch so they’ll be over Aharon’s heart when he goes in before Yahweh, thus Aharon will continually bear the decisions of the Israelis over his heart before Yahweh.
[Exodus] [28]:[31] Make the robe to be worn under the sacred apron entirely from blue material
[Exodus] [28]:[32] with an opening for his head in the middle of it. A border will be needed around the opening so it can’t tear—this should be woven like openings in regular clothes.
[Exodus] [28]:[33] Then on the bottom hem, make decorations that look like pomegranates—they must be made from blue, purple, and scarlet yarn. Gold bells should hang in between the pomegranates
[Exodus] [28]:[34] so as you go around the hem of the robe there’ll be a gold bell, then a pomegranate, then a gold bell, then a pomegranate, etc.
[Exodus] [28]:[35] Aharon (Aaron) must wear this robe when he’s serving, so when he goes into my presence in the sacred inner room, I’ll hear the bells when he enters and when he leaves, so he won’t die.
[Exodus] [28]:[36] Make a plate from pure gold and engrave ‘Dedicated to Yahweh’ on it like you would on a signet ring.
[Exodus] [28]:[37] Attach it to the front of the turban using a blue cord
[Exodus] [28]:[38] so it’ll be on Aharon’s forehead. In this way, it’ll bear the deficiencies of human sinfulness when Israelis attempt to make sacred objects and attempt to make sacred offerings. Thus it’ll be on his forehead continually so that I will see it and accept those things.
[Exodus] [28]:[39] The tunic must be woven from finely-spun linen, and similarly for the turban. An embroiderer must make the waistband.
[Exodus] [28]:[40] You must also make tunics, waistbands and headbands for Aharon’s sons so they’ll look splendid and beautiful.
[Exodus] [28]:[41] Put these clothes on your brother Aharon and his sons, then anoint them with oil and ordain and consecrate them as priests to me.
[Exodus] [28]:[42] Make underwear out of linen to cover their bare flesh from the waist to the thighs—
[Exodus] [28]:[43] they must wear it whenever they enter the sacred tent and whenever they approach the altar to offer sacrifices so they won’t be disobeying and die. Aharon and his descendants must obey that rule forever.
[Exodus] [29]:[1] Now this is how you should consecrate them to be priests to me: Take a young bull from the herd and two rams without defects.
[Exodus] [29]:[2] Also, using finely-ground wheat flour, bake flat bread, flat cakes with olive oil in them, and flat wafers sprinkled with olive oil.
[Exodus] [29]:[3] Put the baking into a basket, and bring the basket to me along with the bull and two rams.
[Exodus] [29]:[4] Then take Aharon (Aaron) and his sons near to the entrance of the sacred tent and wash them with water.
[Exodus] [29]:[5] Take the clothes and dress Aharon in the tunic and the robe that goes with the apron, then the sacred apron and the sacred pouch, and tie the waistband around the apron.
[Exodus] [29]:[6] Put the turban on his head and attach the sacred gold ornament to it,
[Exodus] [29]:[7] then take the anointing oil and pour it over his head to dedicate him.
[Exodus] [29]:[8] Next, bring his sons and put tunics on them
[Exodus] [29]:[9] and wrap waistbands around them and tie on their headbands. They and their descendants will be priests forever, and you must ordain both Aharon and his sons.
[Exodus] [29]:[10] Then bring the bull to the front of the sacred tent and get Aharon and his sons to put their hands on its head,
[Exodus] [29]:[11] then slaughter the bull before me at the entrance of the sacred tent.
[Exodus] [29]:[12] Take some of that blood and smear it on the top projections of the altar with your finger, then pour the rest of it on the ground at the base of the altar.
[Exodus] [29]:[13] Take all the fat covering the innards including the lobe above the liver, as well as both kidneys and the fat on them, and burn it all on the altar,
[Exodus] [29]:[14] but the bull’s meat and hide and intestines must be burnt outside the camp. Sacrificing the bull’s fat like that is an act of purification.
[Exodus] [29]:[15] Then take one of the rams and have Aharon and his sons place their hands on its head,
[Exodus] [29]:[16] then slaughter it. Catch the blood and sprinkle it all over the sides of the altar.
[Exodus] [29]:[17] Then cut the ram into pieces and wash its innards and its legs, and put those bits together with the head and the other pieces.
[Exodus] [29]:[18] Then burn it all on the altar. That will be a burnt offering to me—a pleasing aroma from the offering by fire.
[Exodus] [29]:[19] Then take the second ram, and have Aharon and his sons place their hands on its head,
[Exodus] [29]:[20] then slaughter it. Catch the blood and smear some of it on the tip of Aharon and his sons’ right ears and on their right thumbs and big toes. Then sprinkle the rest all over the sides of the altar.
[Exodus] [29]:[21] Take some of the blood that is on the altar and some of the anointing oil, and sprinkle that on Aharon and his clothes, and on his sons and their clothes. That will consecrate Aharon and his sons and their priestly clothes.
[Exodus] [29]:[22] Take the fat of that second ram, and its fat tail, the fat covering its innards and the lobe above the liver, the two kidneys and that fat that’s on them, and the right thigh, because this ram is for consecration.
[Exodus] [29]:[23] Also take one round bread loaf, one cake of bread made with oil in it, and one wafer from that basket of flat breads that’s offered to me.
[Exodus] [29]:[24] Put all those into the hands of Aharon and his sons, and they must wave them before me as a wave offering.
[Exodus] [29]:[25] Then take them from their hands and burn them completely on the altar on top of the burnt offering. That also will be a fire offering to me, and its aroma will please me.
[Exodus] [29]:[26] Take the breast meat of the ram (the second one for the consecration of Aharon) and wave it as a wave offering before me. Then after that it will be your share to cook and eat.
[Exodus] [29]:[27] So you should consecrate the breast of the wave offering and the thigh of the contribution from the ram of consecration for Aharon and his sons.
[Exodus] [29]:[28] Those will belong to Aharon and his sons as their regular portion from the Israelis—it will be a contribution from the Israelis from their peace offerings to me.
[Exodus] [29]:[29] The sacred clothes that belong to Aharon will be used for his male descendants to wear in turn when they’re anointed and consecrated.
[Exodus] [29]:[30] The priest who succeeds him from among his sons, who comes into the sacred tent to serve in the sacred inner room must wear them for seven days.
[Exodus] [29]:[31] Take the ram of consecration and boil its meat in a sacred place,
[Exodus] [29]:[32] then Aharon and his sons should eat the meat of the ram as well as the breads that are in the basket at the entrance to the tent.
[Exodus] [29]:[33] They must eat those things used to make atonement for them and to consecrate them. No one else can eat them, because they’ve been made sacred.
[Exodus] [29]:[34] If any meat of the consecration or any of the bread remains until the morning, then you must burn the remainder—it can’t be eaten because it’s been made sacred.
[Exodus] [29]:[35] So that’s what you must do for Aharon and his sons, just like I’ve commanded you. You’ll consecrate them for seven days,
[Exodus] [29]:[36] and each day you must sacrifice a bull to purify the altar and compensate for the altar’s imperfections. You must also anoint it each day with olive oil to make it sacred.
[Exodus] [29]:[37] After making atonement for the altar and making it sacred for seven days, it will then be so sacred that anything that touches it will also become sacred.
[Exodus] [29]:[38] After all that, you must continually offer two, year-old lambs every day—
[Exodus] [29]:[39] one in the morning and the other around twilight.
[Exodus] [29]:[40] With the morning lamb, also offer 2kg of finely-ground wheat flour mixed with a litre of pressed olive oil and a litre of wine.
[Exodus] [29]:[41] With the twilight lamb, offer the same grain offering as in the morning, and the same drink offering. That will be a fire offering to me and the aroma will please me.
[Exodus] [29]:[42] This must be a continual offering to me at the entrance of the sacred tent even in following generations, and I’ll meet with you all there to speak to you there
[Exodus] [29]:[43] and I’ll meet with the Israelis there, and my splendour will sanctify it.
[Exodus] [29]:[44] I’ll consecrate the sacred tent and the altar, and I’ll sanctify Aharon (Aaron) and his sons to be my priests.
[Exodus] [29]:[45] Then I’ll live there among the Israelis and I will be their god,
[Exodus] [29]:[46] and they will know that I’m their god Yahweh, who brought them out of Mitsrayim (Egypt) so I could live among them. I am Yahweh their god.
[Exodus] [30]:[1] You must make an altar out of acacia word for burning incense on.
[Exodus] [30]:[2] It should be square—half a metre on each side—and a metre high. Make projections that look like horns on top out of that same block of wood.
[Exodus] [30]:[3] It must be overlaid with pure gold—its top and all around its sides and its projections—plus you shall make a gold moulding all around it.
[Exodus] [30]:[4] Make two gold rings and attach them to the altar below the moulding—one on each side to hold the poles for carrying it with.
[Exodus] [30]:[5] Make the two poles from acacia wood and overlay them with gold.
[Exodus] [30]:[6] Put this incense altar outside the curtain that hangs in front of the sacred chest—the box containing the stone slabs and with a platform on it where I will meet with you.
[Exodus] [30]:[7] Aharon (Aaron) must burn fragrant incense on this altar every morning when he looks after the lamps
[Exodus] [30]:[8] and again every evening when he lights the lamps, so incense must be continually burning before me throughout your generations.
[Exodus] [30]:[9] Don’t offer up any incense or burnt offering or grain offering on it that’s different from these instructions, and don’t pour a drink offering on it.
[Exodus] [30]:[10] Once a year, Aharon must take the purifying blood from the annual atonement sacrifice and put it on the projections of the altar to compensate for the altar’s imperfection. Each high priest will cover the altar’s flaws this way throughout all future generations. The altar will be very sacred—dedicated to me.
[Exodus] [30]:[11] Then Yahweh told Mosheh (Moses):
[Exodus] [30]:[12] Whenever you take a census of the Israeli men, each man must pay a ransom to Yahweh for his life when they’re counted, and then the counting won’t cause deadly diseases among them.
[Exodus] [30]:[13] As each man crosses over to stand with those who’ve been counted, he must pay give a half-shekel coin as an offering to me. (That’s half of the official shekel weight of 12 grams.)
[Exodus] [30]:[14] Every man who’s twenty or older must pay this contribution to me when he’s counted—
[Exodus] [30]:[15] the wealthy aren’t expected to pay more, and the poor must not pass less than this amount when they pay this ransom to me to make atonement for your lives.
[Exodus] [30]:[16] Then you must take that money from the Israelis and use it for work on the sacred tent—it will be a reminder to me that you all have made atonement for your lives.
[Exodus] [30]:[17] The Yahweh told Mosheh (Moses):
[Exodus] [30]:[18] Make a bronze washbasin with a bronze base. Place it between the sacred tent and the altar, and fill it with water
[Exodus] [30]:[19] and Aharon (Aaron) and his sons must wash their hands and feet in it.
[Exodus] [30]:[20] Before they go into the sacred tent, they must wash with water so that won’t die, and also when they’re going to the altar to burn offerings to me—
[Exodus] [30]:[21] they must wash their hands and feet so they won’t die. This will be a rule for them and for all their descendants throughout the generations.
[Exodus] [30]:[22] Then Yahweh told Mosheh (Moses):
[Exodus] [30]:[23] Then you yourself must collect these spices: 6kg of fragrant sap named myrrh, then 3kg of fragrant cinnamon, 3kg of fragrant cane,
[Exodus] [30]:[24] and 6kg of fragrant casia bark. (Use the official weight for everything.) Also, four litres of olive oil.
[Exodus] [30]:[25] Get a professional perfumer to make this into a sacred, fragrant, anointing oil.
[Exodus] [30]:[26] Use it to anoint the sacred tent and the box containing the stone slabs,
[Exodus] [30]:[27] as well as the table and all its utensils, the lampstand and its utensils, the incense altar,
[Exodus] [30]:[28] the altar for burnt offerings and all its equipment, and the basin and its base.
[Exodus] [30]:[29] That will make them sacred and dedicated to me, and anything that touches them will also become sacred.
[Exodus] [30]:[30] Then anoint Aharon (Aaron) and his sons, and dedicate them to become my priests.
[Exodus] [30]:[31] Approach the Israelis and tell them, “This recipe will be my sacred anointing oil for all generations.
[Exodus] [30]:[32] It must not be poured on anyone’s body, and you all must not use any similar recipe for yourselves—it’s sacred and must be treated as such.
[Exodus] [30]:[33] Anyone who mixes together anything like that, or who puts any of it on a stranger, must be expelled from the community.
[Exodus] [30]:[34] Then Yahweh told Mosheh (Moses): Collect equal amounts of stacte, onycha, and galbanum spices, and pure frankincense,
[Exodus] [30]:[35] and get a professional ointment mixer to add salt and make it into pure incense that will be sacred.
[Exodus] [30]:[36] Pulverise some of it into a fine powder and put it in front of the box containing the stone slabs inside the sacred tent. This incense must be regarded as being very sacred.
[Exodus] [30]:[37] No one else should make any incense for yourselves with this same recipe—it must be regarded as sacred to me.
[Exodus] [30]:[38] Anyone who makes anything similar for its fragrance must be expelled from the community.
[Exodus] [31]:[1] Then Yahweh told Mosheh (Moses):
[Exodus] [31]:[2] Listen, I’ve chosen a man named Betsalel (son of Uri, son of Hur, from Yehudah’s (Judah) descendants)
[Exodus] [31]:[3] and I’ve filled him with my spirit with wisdom, ability, knowledge, and general craftsmanship.
[Exodus] [31]:[4] He’s capable of designing and creating gold, silver, and bronze works,
[Exodus] [31]:[5] as well as cutting and setting gemstones, wood-carving, and other crafts.
[Exodus] [31]:[6] And what’s more, I’ve appointed Oholiav (son of Ahisamak, from Dan’s descendants) to help him, and I’ve also given special ability to other skilled men so that they can make everything that I’ve instructed you:
[Exodus] [31]:[7] the sacred tent, the box containing the stone slabs with the atonement platform on top of it, all the equipment for inside the sacred tent,
[Exodus] [31]:[8] the table and its utensils, the gold lampstand and all its utensils, the altar for burning incense,
[Exodus] [31]:[9] the altar for the burnt offerings and all its utensils, the washbasin with its base,
[Exodus] [31]:[10] the woven clothes: the sacred clothes for Aharon (Aaron) the priest and his sons,
[Exodus] [31]:[11] the anointing oil, and the fragrant incense for the sacred tent. Those craftsmen must make everything exactly according to my instructions.
[Exodus] [31]:[12] Then Yahweh told Mosheh (Moses):
[Exodus] [31]:[13] Tell the Israelis that you all must certainly observe the weekly rest day because the rest day is a sign between me and you all throughout your generations, so that you will know that I am Yahweh, who wants to distinguish you from other nations.
[Exodus] [31]:[14] So you all must observe the rest day because it’s sacred for you. Anyone who treats it as an ordinary day must be put to death. Anyone who works on it must be expelled from the community.
[Exodus] [31]:[15] There’s six days for working, and then the seventh is a rest day—dedicated to me. Anyone who works on it must certainly be put to death.
[Exodus] [31]:[16] The Israelis must observe the rest day for all future generations. There’s no ending to this agreement
[Exodus] [31]:[17] between me and the Israelis. It’s a never-ending sign that I made the heavens and the earth in six days, and then rested on the seventh day and was refreshed.
[Exodus] [31]:[18] When Yahweh finished speaking to Mosheh, he gave Mosheh the two stone slabs with the transcript that he had engraved on them with his own finger.
[Exodus] [32]:[1] Meanwhile, the people had noticed that Mosheh (Moses) had been up on the mountain for a long time, so they gathered themselves around Aharon (Aaron) and told him, “Come on. Make some gods for us that can go ahead of us, because we don’t know what’s happened to that Mosheh—the man who brought us out of Mitsrayim (Egypt).”
[Exodus] [32]:[2] Aharon replied, “Go and get the gold earrings off your wives and your sons and daughters, and bring them to me.”
[Exodus] [32]:[3] So the people took off all their gold earrings and brought them to Aharon,
[Exodus] [32]:[4] and he took them and smelted and crafted the gold into the form of a young bull. Then the people said, “These are your gods, Yisrael (Israel), who brought you out of Mitsrayim.”
[Exodus] [32]:[5] When Aharon saw that, he built an altar in front of the bull and announced, “Tomorrow will be a festival to honour Yahweh.”
[Exodus] [32]:[6] So they got up early the next day and offered burnt offerings and brought peace offerings. Then the people sat down to eat and drink, then stood up to make merry.
[Exodus] [32]:[7] Then Yahweh told Mosheh, “Go on down because your people that you brought out of Mitsrayim have gone bad—
[Exodus] [32]:[8] they’ve quickly deviated from what I instructed them. They’ve made a metal bull for themselves and have bowed down to it and sacrificed to it and they’ve said, ‘Yisrael, these are your gods that brought you out of Mitsrayim.’ ”
[Exodus] [32]:[9] Then Yahweh said to Mosheh, “I’ve seen this people, and look, they’re so stubborn.
[Exodus] [32]:[10] So leave me alone now and let my anger rage against them. I will destroy them and make you into a great nation.”
[Exodus] [32]:[11] But Mosheh pleaded with his god Yahweh and asked, “Yahweh, why are you angry at your people that you have brought out of Mitsrayim with your incredible power and actions?
[Exodus] [32]:[12] If you did that, the Mitsrim (Egyptians) would say, ‘Ha, he brought them out with evil plans to kill them in the mountains and to destroy them from off the earth.’ Turn from your anger and repent from any idea of doing evil to your people.
[Exodus] [32]:[13] Remember Avraham and Yitshak (Isaac) and Yisrael—your servants that you swore to them yourself and told them, ‘I will cause your descendants to increase like the stars in the sky, and I will give your descendants all this land which I told you about, and they will inherit it forever.’ ”
[Exodus] [32]:[14] So Yahweh repented from the evil that he’d said he’d do to his people.
[Exodus] [32]:[15] Then Mosheh turned and went down the mountain carrying the two tablets with the transcript. The tablets were engraved on both sides—front and back.
[Exodus] [32]:[16] They were God’s work—it was his writing and he had inscribed it on the tablets.
[Exodus] [32]:[17] As they descended, Yehoshua (Joshua) heard the sounds of people shouting and said to Mosheh, “It sounds like a war going on down there in the camp!”
[Exodus] [32]:[18] But Mosheh responded, “It’s not a victory march, and it’s not moans of defeat—it’s singing that I can hear!”
[Exodus] [32]:[19] Then as they approached the camp, they saw the bull and the dancing, and Mosheh got very angry and threw the tablets down at the bottom of the mountain and they shattered.
[Exodus] [32]:[20] He took the bull they had made and burnt it in the fire, then he ground it down until it was powder and sprinkled it on top of pots of water and made the Israelis drink it.
[Exodus] [32]:[21] Then Mosheh demanded from Aharon (Aaron), “What did these people do to you to make you bring such a terrible sin on them?”
[Exodus] [32]:[22] Aharon responded, “Don’t be angry with me, my master. You know the people—they’re intent on evil.
[Exodus] [32]:[23] They insisted, saying, ‘Make a god for us to lead us. As for that Mosheh—the man that brought us out of Mitsrayim (Egypt)—we don’t know what’s happened to him.’
[Exodus] [32]:[24] So I told them, ‘Anyone who has gold jewellery, take it off yourself,’ and they gave it to me and I threw it into the fire, and this bull came out.”
[Exodus] [32]:[25] Mosheh saw that the people were out of control because Aharon had let them go wild, and now they were subject to mockery from any group that stood up against them.
[Exodus] [32]:[26] Then Mosheh stood at the camp entrance and asked, “Anyone who’s for Yahweh, come to me.” And all the men from the clan of Levi gathered around him.
[Exodus] [32]:[27] Then he told them, “This is what Yahweh, the god of Yisrael (Israel), says: ‘Each man must strap his sword on his side. Pass through and return from gate to gate in the camp and kill the unfaithful men—even if it’s your brother, or friend, or neighbour.’ ”
[Exodus] [32]:[28] The Levite men did what Mosheh ordered and they killed about three thousand Israeli men that day.
[Exodus] [32]:[29] Then Mosheh told them, “Consecrate yourselves to Yahweh today, because any man who stood against his son or his brother today has placed a blessing on himself.”
[Exodus] [32]:[30] The next day, Mosheh told the people, “You all have committed a terrible sin, but now I will go up to Yahweh—perhaps I can atone for your sin.”
[Exodus] [32]:[31] So Mosheh returned to Yahweh and said, “Please, these people have committed a terrible sin and made gods for themselves out of gold.
[Exodus] [32]:[32] But now, maybe you’ll forgive their sin, but if not, please blot me out of your book that you’ve written.”
[Exodus] [32]:[33] But Yahweh said to Mosheh, “It’s anyone who sinned against me that I’ll blot out of my book.
[Exodus] [32]:[34] So go now and lead the people to where I’ve spoken to you. See, my angel will go ahead of you, but on the day that I settle accounts, then I’ll punish them for their sin.”
[Exodus] [32]:[35] Then Yahweh sent deadly diseases onto the people because they had got Aharon (Aaron) to make the gold bull.
[Exodus] [33]:[1] Then Yahweh told Mosheh (Moses), “Go and pack up from here, you and the people that you brought out of Mitsrayim (Egypt). Go to the land which I promised to Avraham, to Yitshak (Isaac), and to Ya’akov (Jacob), when I told them that I’d give it to their descendants.
[Exodus] [33]:[2] I’ll send an angel ahead of you, and I’ll drive out the Kena’anim (Canaanites), the Amorim, the Hitim, the Perizim, the Hivim, and the Yevusim.
[Exodus] [33]:[3] It’s a land flowing with milk and honey, but I won’t stay among you in case I decide to destroy you on the way because you’re stubborn people.”
[Exodus] [33]:[4] When the people heard this angry comment, they mourned and none of them put on anything fancy.
[Exodus] [33]:[5] Yahweh had told Mosheh, “Tell the Israelis, ‘You’re all stubborn people. If I went with you for even one moment, then I’d destroy you. So now, take off your jewellery and anything fancy that you’re wearing, and then I’ll know what I’ll do to you.’ ”
[Exodus] [33]:[6] So from Mt. Sinay onwards, the Israelis stripped themselves of their jewellery and fancy things.
[Exodus] [33]:[7] From that day onwards, Mosheh (Moses) would take a tent and would put it up at a distance outside the camp—he called it ‘the tent of meeting’. Then anyone who wanted a decision from Yahweh would go out to that tent of meeting outside the camp.
[Exodus] [33]:[8] Whenever Mosheh went out to the tent, all the people would stand up at the entrance of their own tents, and they would watch Mosheh go out until he went into the tent.
[Exodus] [33]:[9] Once he entered the tent, the pillar of cloud would come down and stand at the entrance of the tent, and Yahweh would speak with him.
[Exodus] [33]:[10] When all the people saw the pillar of cloud standing at the entrance of the tent, they would get up and bow down at the entrance of their own tents.
[Exodus] [33]:[11] Yahweh would speak to Mosheh face to face like someone speaks to their friend. Then Mosheh would return to the camp, but his servant Yehoshua (Joshua) (a young man who was the son of Nun) would not leave the inside of the tent.
[Exodus] [33]:[12] Then Mosheh (Moses) said to Yahweh, “Listen, you’ve been saying to me, ‘Take these people onwards,’ but you haven’t let me know who you’ll send with me, although you have said, ‘I know you by name, and you’ve also found favour in my sight.’
[Exodus] [33]:[13] So now please, if I’ve found favour in your sight, please help me to know your ways. Then I’ll know you so that I can find favour in your sight. And don’t forget that this nation is your people.”
[Exodus] [33]:[14] Yahweh replied, “My presence will go with you and I will help you to be able to rest.”
[Exodus] [33]:[15] Mosheh replied to him, “If your presence isn’t coming with us, then don’t make us leave here.
[Exodus] [33]:[16] How would anyone know that I’ve found favour in your sight—me and your people that is—if you didn’t come with us? How could I and your people be distinguished from all the other people groups in the world?”
[Exodus] [33]:[17] Yahweh replied to Mosheh, “Okay, I’ll also do what you’ve asked because you’ve found favour in my sight and I know you by name.”
[Exodus] [33]:[18] Then Mosheh, “Please show me your splendour.”
[Exodus] [33]:[19] Yahweh replied, “I myself will cause all my goodness to pass over in front of you, and I will say my name of Yahweh in front of you. I will favour anyone I want, and I’ll be compassionate to whoever I want.”
[Exodus] [33]:[20] But he said, “You won’t be able to see my face, because no human can see me and still live.”
[Exodus] [33]:[21] He continued, “Look, there’s a place near me where you can stand there on the rock.
[Exodus] [33]:[22] Then while my splendour passes over, I’ll put you in a crevice in the rock, and my hand will cover you until I’ve gone past.
[Exodus] [33]:[23] Then I’ll take my hand away and you’ll be able to see my back, but you mustn’t try to look at my face.”
[Exodus] [34]:[1] Then Yahweh continued speaking to Mosheh (Moses), “Carve two slabs of stone for yourself just like the first ones. Then the words that were on the first tablets that you broke, I’ll write them again on the slabs.
[Exodus] [34]:[2] Be ready by morning, and in the morning come up to Mt. Sinay, and present yourself there to me up on the top.
[Exodus] [34]:[3] Don’t bring anyone with you, and also don’t let anyone be on the mountain at all—don’t even let their flocks and herds graze at the base of that mountain.”
[Exodus] [34]:[4] So Mosheh carved out two slabs of stone like the first ones, and he got up early in the morning and went up to Mt. Sinay as Yahweh had commanded him, carrying up the two slabs of stone.
[Exodus] [34]:[5] Then Yahweh came down in the cloud and stood with him there, and he pronounced his name ‘Yahweh’.
[Exodus] [34]:[6] Yahweh passed over above his face and proclaimed, “I am Yahweh, a compassionate and gracious God, slow to get angry but exuding faithfulness and trustworthiness.
[Exodus] [34]:[7] I display faithfulness to thousands of generations—forgiving disobedience, transgression, and sin. But I certainly won’t let the guilty get away with it—visiting the iniquity of the parents onto the children and onto the grandchildren—to the third and the fourth generations.”
[Exodus] [34]:[8] Mosheh hurried and bowed to the ground and worshipped Yahweh
[Exodus] [34]:[9] and said, “Please, if I have found favour in your sight, my master, please go with us, because these are stubborn people. And forgive our disobedience and our sin and take us as your inheritance.”
[Exodus] [34]:[10] Yahweh said, “Listen, I’m about to make an agreement in front of all your people. I will do miracles that have not been done before anywhere on the earth or in any country of the world. All the people that you’re among will see my work, because what I’m going to do with you is awe-inspiring.
[Exodus] [34]:[11] Be sure to obey what I’m telling you today. See, I’m about to force the Amorim, the Kena’anim (Canaanites), the Hitim, the Perizim, the Hivim, and the Yevusim out of the land ahead of you.
[Exodus] [34]:[12] Be very careful not to make any treaties with any of the current inhabitants of the land that you’re about to enter, in case it ends up trapping you.
[Exodus] [34]:[13] What you must do instead is to break down their altars and smash their pillars, and cut down the poles used to worship their god Asherah.
[Exodus] [34]:[14] You must not bow down to any other god because Yahweh is a jealous God—jealous to protect his name.
[Exodus] [34]:[15] So don’t make an agreement with the inhabitants of the land, because when they prostitute themselves to their gods and sacrifice to them, and then they invite you to join them and you eat some of their sacrifice,
[Exodus] [34]:[16] then you’ll end up by allowing your sons to marry their daughters who’ll prostitute themselves to their gods, and then your sons will do the same.
[Exodus] [34]:[17] Don’t make cast metal gods for yourselves.
[Exodus] [34]:[18] You must observe the Flat Bread Celebration every year as I instructed you. For seven days you must eat only bread that hasn’t been risen, at the appointed time in late March or early April because that’s when you came out of Mitsrayim (Egypt).
[Exodus] [34]:[19] All of your eldest male offspring belong to me, including your sons and the first males born from your cattle and sheep and goats.
[Exodus] [34]:[20] If it’s a male donkey, a lamb can be given as a ransom instead, but if you don’t pay a ransom then you must kill the donkey. It’s compulsory to ransom your eldest sons. Don’t come to worship me without bringing something.
[Exodus] [34]:[21] Each week, you should only work for six days, then you must rest on the seventh day—even during ploughing and harvest times.
[Exodus] [34]:[22] In the spring when you begin to harvest the first wheat crop, you must have a Celebration of Weeks, and at the end of the year in the autumn, have a Finished Harvest Celebration.
[Exodus] [34]:[23] Three times every year, all your men must present themselves before me—Yisrael’s (Israel) god, the master Yahweh.
[Exodus] [34]:[24] I will drive out the people groups ahead of you and expand your borders, and no one will think of taking your land when they know that you present yourselves to me three times a year.
[Exodus] [34]:[25] Don’t wave bread that’s been risen when offering a sacrifice. Don’t allow any part of the sacrifice for the ‘pass-over’ celebration to still be there in the morning.
[Exodus] [34]:[26] You must bring the best of the first parts of your harvests to my residence. Don’t boil a young goat in its mother’s milk.
[Exodus] [34]:[27] Yahweh told Mosheh (Moses), “Write down these words for yourself, because it’s in accordance with these words that I’ve made an agreement with you and with Yisrael.”
[Exodus] [34]:[28] Mosheh was there with Yahweh for forty days and nights, and during that time he didn’t eat or even drink water, and he wrote the ten commands of the agreement on the stone slabs.
[Exodus] [34]:[29] So when Mosheh came down from Mt. Sinay, he was carrying the two stone slabs with the transcript of the ten commands, but what he didn’t know as he descended was that the skin on his face was shining after his talking with Yahweh.
[Exodus] [34]:[30] When Aharon (Aaron) and the Israelis saw Mosheh, wow, his face radiated light and they were afraid to go close to him.
[Exodus] [34]:[31] But Mosheh called them over, and Aharon and all of the community leaders returned back to him, and he spoke with them.
[Exodus] [34]:[32] After that, the Israelis came closer, and Mosheh gave them all the instructions that Yahweh had told him on Mt. Sinay.
[Exodus] [34]:[33] Then when he’d finished talking to them, Mosheh put a veil over his face,
[Exodus] [34]:[34] and whenever he would go in to speak with Yahweh, he would remove the veil until he came out. Whenever he did come out, he’d tell the Israelis what he’d been instructed,
[Exodus] [34]:[35] and they would see how his face shone. Then Mosheh would put the veil back over his face until he went in the next time to speak with Yahweh.
[Exodus] [35]:[1] Mosheh (Moses) assembled all the Israelis and told them, “These are the things that Yahweh has instructed you to do.
[Exodus] [35]:[2] Every week, you can work for six days, but the seventh day will be a sacred rest day, dedicated to Yahweh. Anyone who works on that day must be put to death.
[Exodus] [35]:[3] Don’t light a fire in any of your homes on the rest days.”
[Exodus] [35]:[4] Then Mosheh (Moses) told all the assembled Israelis, “This is what Yahweh instructed:
[Exodus] [35]:[5] Take up an offering for Yahweh—everyone who wants to participate should bring to Yahweh their contribution of gold, silver, bronze,
[Exodus] [35]:[6] blue, purple, or scarlet yarn, finely-spun linen and goats’ hair,
[Exodus] [35]:[7] reddened ram skins, sea-cow hides, and acacia wood,
[Exodus] [35]:[8] olive oil for the lamps and spices to make the anointing oil and the fragrant incense,
[Exodus] [35]:[9] and onyx and other gemstones for the priest’s sacred apron and chest pouch.
[Exodus] [35]:[10] Everyone among you all who’s highly skilled should come and make everything that Yahweh has instructed—
[Exodus] [35]:[11] the tent for the residence and its covering, its clasps and frames, its bars, pillars, and bases,
[Exodus] [35]:[12] the box with its poles and the atonement platform to go on top, the curtain for screening it,
[Exodus] [35]:[13] the table and its poles and all its utensils and the sacred bread,
[Exodus] [35]:[14] the lampstand for light with its lamps and utensils and oil to burn,
[Exodus] [35]:[15] the incense altar and its poles, the anointing oil and fragrant incense, the curtain for the entrance of the residence,
[Exodus] [35]:[16] the altar for the burnt offerings with its bronze grate, its poles and all of its utensils, the washbasin with its base,
[Exodus] [35]:[17] the courtyard curtains with their pillars and bases, and the curtain for the courtyard gate,
[Exodus] [35]:[18] the tent pegs and ropes for the residence and the courtyard,
[Exodus] [35]:[19] the finely-woven clothing for serving in the Holy Place, the sacred clothes for Aharon (Aaron) the priest, and the clothes for his sons to serve as priests.”
[Exodus] [35]:[20] Then all the Israelis who’d been assembled in front of Mosheh (Moses) went away,
[Exodus] [35]:[21] and everyone who felt to do so came back bringing their contributions to Yahweh for the work on the sacred tent and all its components, and for the sacred clothes.
[Exodus] [35]:[22] This included both men and women who were wanting to contribute, and they brought necklaces and earrings and ornaments—all made of gold. They held them up high as a raised offering of gold to Yahweh.
[Exodus] [35]:[23] Many people who had blue or purple or scarlet yarn, or finely-spun linen or goats’ hair, reddened ram skins or sea-cow hides brought them.
[Exodus] [35]:[24] Others who could, brought a contribution of silver or bronze to Yahweh, and those with acacia wood brought it for all the construction of the tent components.
[Exodus] [35]:[25] All the women who were skilled at making cloth brought blue, purple, or scarlet yarn and fine, hand-spun linen thread,
[Exodus] [35]:[26] and all those women who felt to do so spun goats’ hair.
[Exodus] [35]:[27] The leaders brought onyx stones and other gemstones to be mounted on the sacred apron and for the sacred pouch,
[Exodus] [35]:[28] along with the spices and olive oil to be used for the maps, the anointing oil, and the fragrant incense.
[Exodus] [35]:[29] Thus the Israelis brought a voluntary offering to Yahweh—every man and woman who felt to do so brought something for all the work which Yahweh had instructed them through Mosheh to do.
[Exodus] [35]:[30] Then Mosheh (Moses) said to the Israelis, “Listen, Yahweh has called Betsalel by name (the son of Hur’s son Uri, from the tribe of Yehudah (Judah))
[Exodus] [35]:[31] and he has filled him with his spirit, with skill and understanding, and with knowledge and with all kinds of craftsmanship.
[Exodus] [35]:[32] He can design designs, work in gold, silver, and bronze,
[Exodus] [35]:[33] in cutting gemstones for setting, and in wood-carving—to do all kinds of design and crafting.
[Exodus] [35]:[34] Yahweh has also given him the desire to teach, along with Oholiav (Ahisamak’s son from the tribe of Dan).
[Exodus] [35]:[35] He’s given them both skills to do all the work of craftsmen and of skillful workmen and of embroiderers in blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, and in the fine linen and of weavers—both as designers as well as the various, actual crafts.
[Exodus] [36]:[1] Betsalel and Oholiav will do the work of constructing all the components of the sacred tent along with any others who are like-minded and who have been given the necessary skills and understanding by Yahweh.”
[Exodus] [36]:[2] So Mosheh (Moses) summoned Betsalel and Oholiav, as well as anyone else who felt to help and had been given the appropriate skills by Yahweh,
[Exodus] [36]:[3] and they took away all the contributions that the Israelis had brought to Mosheh to be used for the construction of the sacred tent. However the people still continued to bring voluntary offerings every morning.
[Exodus] [36]:[4] So all those skilled people came over to start on the work of making the sacred tent, Holy Place came, leaving behind the work that they had been doing,
[Exodus] [36]:[5] and they informed Mosheh, “The people are bringing way more than enough to use for the work that Yahweh has instructed us to do.”
[Exodus] [36]:[6] So with Mosheh’s agreement, they spread a message around the camp saying, “Please don’t bring any more contributions for the sacred tent.” So the people—men and women—stopped bringing donations
[Exodus] [36]:[7] as they had already collected more than enough materials for all the work.
[Exodus] [36]:[8] Then all the most-skilled men out of the workmen made the ten strips of curtaining for the residence from twisted finely-spun linen and blue, purple, scarlet yarn used to embroider winged-creatures on them.
[Exodus] [36]:[9] Each strip was 14.5m long and two metres wide—they were all the same size.
[Exodus] [36]:[10] Five strips were sewn together as one set, and the other five as another set.
[Exodus] [36]:[11] They made loops of blue on the edge of the first curtain at the edge of the set, and similarly for the second set—
[Exodus] [36]:[12] fifty matching loops on the edge of each set so they were aligned with each other.
[Exodus] [36]:[13] They also made fifty gold clips and used them to join the two curtain sets to each other to make the wall of the sacred tent.
[Exodus] [36]:[14] Then they made eleven goats’ hair curtain sections for the tarpaulin over the sacred tent.
[Exodus] [36]:[15] All eleven sections were the same size at fifteen metres long and two metres wide,
[Exodus] [36]:[16] and they joined five sections to each other for one set and six for the other.
[Exodus] [36]:[17] Then they attached fifty blue loops onto one edge of each of the two sets
[Exodus] [36]:[18] and made fifty bronze clips for connecting them into one continuous cover.
[Exodus] [36]:[19] They then made a tarpaulin from red rams skins to go over the tent, and the top waterproof tarpaulin of sea-cow hides.
[Exodus] [36]:[20] Then they made forty-eight upright frames from acacia wood for the sacred tent.
[Exodus] [36]:[21] Each frame was five metres long and 0.75m wide
[Exodus] [36]:[22] with two protrusions on each frame for connecting them together, so all the frames were made in this way.
[Exodus] [36]:[23] They made twenty frames for the south side
[Exodus] [36]:[24] with their forty silver bases—two bases under each frame that two more protrusions fitted down into,
[Exodus] [36]:[25] then two more for the north side
[Exodus] [36]:[26] with their forty silver bases—two bases under each frame.
[Exodus] [36]:[27] Six frames were made for the west side
[Exodus] [36]:[28] as well as two frames for the back corners of the sacred tent.
[Exodus] [36]:[29] At the two corners, the frames were connected together at the bottom, and similarly at the top before being attached to a single ring
[Exodus] [36]:[30] so that made eight frames with their sixteen silver bases—two bases under each frame.
[Exodus] [36]:[31] Then they made crossbars from acacia wood—five for the frames on the north side of the sacred tent,
[Exodus] [36]:[32] five for the south side, and five crossbars for the frames on the west side along the back.
[Exodus] [36]:[33] The middle crossbar was made to pass through from one end to the other in the centre of the frames,
[Exodus] [36]:[34] and the frames were overlaid with gold. They then made gold rings to be the holders for the crossbars, and they too were overlaid with gold.
[Exodus] [36]:[35] They made a curtain from twisted finely-spun linen, and a skillful workman embroidered winged creatures on them with blue, purple, scarlet yarn.
[Exodus] [36]:[36] They made four pillars of acacia wood overlaid with gold, as well as their gold hooks and four bases cast from silver.
[Exodus] [36]:[37] They made a curtain for the tent entrance—an embroiderer made it from twisted finely-spun linen and blue, purple, and scarlet yarn,
[Exodus] [36]:[38] along with its five pillars and their hooks. The tops of the pillars were overlaid with gold, and their five bases were made of bronze.
[Exodus] [37]:[1] Then Betsalel made the sacred chest from acacia wood—it was 1.2m long, 0.75m wide, and 0.75m high.
[Exodus] [37]:[2] He overlaid both the inside and the outside with pure gold, and made a gold moulding all around it,
[Exodus] [37]:[3] and he cast four rings of gold and attached them to its four feet—two rings on each one side.
[Exodus] [37]:[4] He made two acacia wood poles and overlaid them with gold,
[Exodus] [37]:[5] and he put the poles into the rings on the sides of the box for carrying it.
[Exodus] [37]:[6] Then he made the atonement platform from pure gold to fit as the lid for the box, so it was also 1.2m long and 0.75m wide,
[Exodus] [37]:[7] then from the ends of the lid, he hammered the gold to form two winged creatures.
[Exodus] [37]:[8] There was a winged creature sitting on each end of the atonement platform made from its two ends,
[Exodus] [37]:[9] and they were spreading their wings upwards to cover over the platform. They faced each other, looking down towards the atonement platform.
[Exodus] [37]:[10] He made the bread table from acacia wood—one metre long, half a metre wide, and three-quarters of a metre high.
[Exodus] [37]:[11] It was overlaid with pure gold and had a gold moulding all around it.
[Exodus] [37]:[12] He made an 8cm wide rim all around it, and a gold moulding around the rim.
[Exodus] [37]:[13] He moulded four gold rings from gold and attached them to the four corners of the table. Each ring was close to each table leg
[Exodus] [37]:[14] near the rim to hold the poles for carrying the table.
[Exodus] [37]:[15] He made two acacia wood poles and overlaid them for gold—they were for carrying the table.
[Exodus] [37]:[16] He also made the utensils that would be on the table—its plates and pans, and its bowls and pitchers to be used for pouring out the wine offerings—all made from pure gold.
[Exodus] [37]:[17] Then he made the lampstand from pure gold. The base and shaft of the lampstand were hammered into shape, along with its cups, and its buds and blossoms.
[Exodus] [37]:[18] There were six branches going out from the shaft of the lampstand—three on each side.
[Exodus] [37]:[19] Each branch had three gold cups on it that looked like almond flowers with buds and petals. It was the same for each of the lampstand’s six branches.
[Exodus] [37]:[20] On the lampstand shaft there were four cups that also looked like almond blossoms, each one with flower buds and petals.
[Exodus] [37]:[21] He made one flower bud beneath every pair of branches (that were going out from opposite sides). The bud was attached to each pair of branches as if they were growing out of it—all six lampstand branches were attached like that.
[Exodus] [37]:[22] The buds and the branches coming out of them were all hammered out of one piece of pure gold.
[Exodus] [37]:[23] Then he made the seven lamps out of pure gold, along with the tongs and trays.
[Exodus] [37]:[24] He made the lampstand and tongs and trays using 33kg of pure gold.
[Exodus] [37]:[25] Then he made the altar for burning incense out of acacia wood. It was square—half a metre on each side—and one metre high. Its projections on the top four corners were part of it.
[Exodus] [37]:[26] He overlaid it with pure gold—all four sides including the projections—and put a gold moulding all around it.
[Exodus] [37]:[27] Then he made two gold rings and attached them below the moulding—two on each side for holding the poles for carrying the altar.
[Exodus] [37]:[28] The two poles were made from acacia wood and then overlaid with gold.
[Exodus] [37]:[29] He got a professional ointment maker to make the sacred anointing oil and the pure, fragrant incense.
[Exodus] [38]:[1] Then Betsalel made the altar for burning offerings from acacia wood. It was square—2.5m on each side—and 1.5m tall.
[Exodus] [38]:[2] From the same piece of wood, he made horn-like projections for each of the four corners, then he overlaid it all with bronze.
[Exodus] [38]:[3] He made all the utensils for the altar: the pots and shovels, basins and meat-forks, and the firepans—all made from bronze.
[Exodus] [38]:[4] He made a grating for the altar—a bronze lattice that fitted down in the middle of the altar,
[Exodus] [38]:[5] and he cast the grating with rings on the four corners as holders for the carrying poles.
[Exodus] [38]:[6] He made the acacia wood poles and overlaid them with bronze
[Exodus] [38]:[7] and he put the poles into the rings on the sides of the altar so they could carry it with them. He made the altar hollow using boards.
[Exodus] [38]:[8] Then he made a bronze washbasin and base. They were made with the bronze from the mirrors of the serving women who served at the entrance of the sacred tent.
[Exodus] [38]:[9] Then Betsalel worked on the courtyard. For the south side, the courtyard curtains were fifty metres of twisted finely-spun linen
[Exodus] [38]:[10] with their twenty bronze pillars and their bases. The hooks on the pillars and their rings were made of silver.
[Exodus] [38]:[11] On the north side, there were fifty metres of curtains with their twenty bronze pillars and bases, and their silver hooks and rings.
[Exodus] [38]:[12] On the west side, there were twenty-five metres of curtains with their ten pillars and bases, and their silver hooks and rings,
[Exodus] [38]:[13] and another twenty-five metres on the east side.
[Exodus] [38]:[14] The curtains for one side of the entrance were 7.5m long with their three pillars and their bases.
[Exodus] [38]:[15] On the other side, opposite the courtyard entrance, the curtains were 7.5m long with their three pillars and their bases.
[Exodus] [38]:[16] All of the courtyard curtains were made with twisted finely-spun linen.
[Exodus] [38]:[17] The bases for the pillars were bronze, but the hooks on them and their rings were silver. All of the courtyard pillars had decorative silver caps fitted to their tops.
[Exodus] [38]:[18] The curtain for the courtyard gate was done by an embroiderer. It was made from twisted finely-spun linen embroidered with blue, purple, and scarlet yard. The curtain was ten metres long and 2.5m high, just like the other courtyard curtains
[Exodus] [38]:[19] with its four bronze pillars and their bases and their silver hooks and rings, and with silver caps.
[Exodus] [38]:[20] All the tent pegs for the sacred tent and for around the courtyard were made with bronze.
[Exodus] [38]:[21] These are the records from making the sacred tent (where the stone transcripts were kept). They were recorded by the Levites according to Mosheh’s (Moses) instructions and supervised by Itamar (a son of Aharon (Aaron) the priest).
[Exodus] [38]:[22] Betsalel (son of Uri son of Hur, from the tribe of Yehudah (Judah)) made everything that Yahweh had instructed Mosheh to make.
[Exodus] [38]:[23] Oholiav (son of Ahisamak, from the tribe of Dan) worked with him—he was an engraver and a designer and an embroiderer in blue, purple, and scarlet, and in fine linen.
[Exodus] [38]:[24] The gold that they used for the construction of the sacred tent was measured at 965kg. This was the gold from the wave offering and was weighed using the official standard weights.
[Exodus] [38]:[25] The silver contributed by the people was measured at 3,420kg also using the official weights.
[Exodus] [38]:[26] During the census, every male who was twenty years old or older paid a 5g silver coin—a total of 603,550 men.
[Exodus] [38]:[27] They’d used 3,400kg of silver to make the bases under the pillars that supported the sacred tent’s curtains (34kg for each of one hundred bases)
[Exodus] [38]:[28] and the other twenty kilograms were used for the hooks for the pillars and for the caps on the tops of them.
[Exodus] [38]:[29] The bronze from the wave offering came to 2,400kg
[Exodus] [38]:[30] and it was used to make the bases for the pillars at the tent entrance and for the altar and its grating and all the utensils,
[Exodus] [38]:[31] and for the bases for the posts for the curtains around the courtyard and at the entrance, and for the tent pegs for the main structure and around the courtyard.
[Exodus] [39]:[1] They used the blue, purple, and scarlet cloth to make the sacred clothes to be used in the sacred tent. They made Aharon’s (Aaron) clothes just as Yahweh had instructed Mosheh (Moses).
[Exodus] [39]:[2] Betsalel made the sacred apron from twisted finely-spun linen embroidered with gold wire, and blue, purple, and scarlet yarn.
[Exodus] [39]:[3] They hammered thin sheets of gold and he cut them into thread of wire for a skillful craftsman to embroider into the fine linen along with the blue, purple, and scarlet yarn.
[Exodus] [39]:[4] They made joined shoulder pieces for it—joined on two corners
[Exodus] [39]:[5] and the skillfully woven waistband which is attached to the apron was made of the same material of twisted finely-spun linen, and had similar embroidery using gold wire, and blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, just as Yahweh had instructed Mosheh (Moses).
[Exodus] [39]:[6] They cut two onyx stones and mounted them in decorative gold settings. The names of the twelve sons of Yisrael (Israel) were engraved on them similar to how a signet ring is engraved,
[Exodus] [39]:[7] and he put them on the shoulder pieces of the sacred apron as stones of reminder for the sons of Yisrael, as Yahweh had instructed Mosheh.
[Exodus] [39]:[8] Then he made the sacred chest pouch which took the work of a skilled craftsman like making the sacred apron. It too was made of twisted finely-spun linen and embroidered with gold wire, and blue, purple, and scarlet yarn.
[Exodus] [39]:[9] When the material was folded over double, it made a square pouch that was 23cm long and 23cm wide,
[Exodus] [39]:[10] and they attached four rows of gemstones onto the front. The first row had a red ruby, a yellow topaz, and a red garnet.
[Exodus] [39]:[11] The second row had a green emerald, a blue sapphire, and a diamond.
[Exodus] [39]:[12] The third row had a red jacinth, a white agate, and a purple amethyst.
[Exodus] [39]:[13] The fourth row had a yellow beryl, an onyx, and a green jasper. All the stones were mounted in decorative gold settings.
[Exodus] [39]:[14] The gemstones were engraved with the names of the twelve sons of Yisrael (Israel) similar to how a signet ring is engraved, and they represented the twelve tribes.
[Exodus] [39]:[15] They attached two twisted chains of pure gold crafted like a cord onto the pouch,
[Exodus] [39]:[16] and made two decorative gold settings and two gold rings, and attached them to the upper corners of the sacred pouch.
[Exodus] [39]:[17] They attached one end of each gold chain to one of the rings on the top corner of the pouch,
[Exodus] [39]:[18] and they attached the other end of each chain to the two decorative settings that enclose the stones. Then they put those on the front side of the shoulder straps of the sacred apron.
[Exodus] [39]:[19] Then they made two more gold rings and attached them to the lower corners of the sacred pouch on the inside edges next to the sacred apron.
[Exodus] [39]:[20] They made two more gold rings and attached them to the lower part of the front of the shoulder straps near where the shoulder straps join with the sacred apron just above the waistband.
[Exodus] [39]:[21] They tied the rings on the sacred pouch to the rings on the sacred apron with a blue cord, so that the sacred pouch was above the waistband and would not come loose from the apron. They did these things exactly as Yahweh had instructed Mosheh (Moses) to do.
[Exodus] [39]:[22] Betsalel had a weaver make the robe that would be worn under the sacred apron entirely from blue material.
[Exodus] [39]:[23] It opened down the middle like other clothes and had a border around this opening so that it wouldn’t tear,
[Exodus] [39]:[24] and the bottom hem had decorative pomegranates on it that were made from blue, purple, and scarlet yarn.
[Exodus] [39]:[25] They also made small bells from pure gold and attached them between the pomegranates around the bottom of the robe,
[Exodus] [39]:[26] so it alternated between a bell and a pomegranate going around the hem, just as Yahweh had instructed Mosheh (Moses).
[Exodus] [39]:[27] A weaver made tunics for Aharon (Aaron) and his sons from fine linen,
[Exodus] [39]:[28] along with the turban and caps from fine linen, the underwear made from twisted finely-spun linen,
[Exodus] [39]:[29] and the waistband from fine linen with blue, purple, and scarlet embroidery, just as Yahweh had instructed Mosheh.
[Exodus] [39]:[30] They made a decorative plate (to represent a holy crown) from pure gold and they engraved ‘Dedicated to Yahweh’ on it (like you’d do for a signet ring).
[Exodus] [39]:[31] They put a blue cord on it to attach it to the front of the turban, just as Yahweh had instructed Mosheh.
[Exodus] [39]:[32] And so all the components of the residence, the tent for meeting God, were finished—the Israelis had done just what Yahweh had instructed Mosheh (Moses).

[Exodus] [40]:[1] Then Yahweh told Mosheh (Moses),
[Exodus] [40]:[2] “On the first day of the first month, you should set up the tent where we’ll meet.
[Exodus] [40]:[3] Put the box for the transcript slabs in its place and hang the curtain to screen it from sight.
[Exodus] [40]:[4] Then bring in the bread table and arrange its utensils, and bring in the lampstand and set up the lamps,
[Exodus] [40]:[5] and put the gold incense altar in front of the sacred box and set up the entrance curtain for the tent.
[Exodus] [40]:[6] Put the altar for burning sacrifices in front of the entrance to the sacred tent where we’ll meet.
[Exodus] [40]:[7] Put the washbasin between the sacred tent and that altar, and fill it with water.
[Exodus] [40]:[8] Set-up the curtains around the outside to make the courtyard, and also set up the courtyard’s entrance curtain.
[Exodus] [40]:[9] Then take the sacred anointing oil and smear it on the sacred tent and everything that’s in it, then none of those things should be touched by others—it will all be sacred.
[Exodus] [40]:[10] Also anoint the altar for burnt offerings and all its utensils. After that, the altar shouldn’t be touched by others—it will be very sacred.
[Exodus] [40]:[11] Anoint the washbasin and its base, and then prohibit others from using it.
[Exodus] [40]:[12] Now bring Aharon (Aaron) and his sons to the entrance of the sacred tent and wash them with water.
[Exodus] [40]:[13] Then put the sacred garments on Aharon and anoint him and make him sacred, so he can now serve as a priest to me.
[Exodus] [40]:[14] Also bring his sons and dress them in tunics
[Exodus] [40]:[15] and anoint them like you anointed their father, and they will serve as priests to me. Their anointing will cause them to be a priesthood forever throughout their generations.”
[Exodus] [40]:[16] So Mosheh (Moses) did everything that Yahweh had instructed him to do.
[Exodus] [40]:[17] It was the first day of the first month of their second year when they set up the sacred tent.

[Exodus] [40]:[19] He spread the two tarpaulin layers over the tent just as Yahweh had instructed him.

[Exodus] [40]:[21] and brought the box into the residence. He set up the curtain to conceal the box with the transcript, just as Yahweh had instructed him.
[Exodus] [40]:[22] He put the table into the sacred tent on the north side of the residence, outside the curtain,
[Exodus] [40]:[23] and arranged the bread on it to display it to Yahweh, just as Yahweh had instructed him.
[Exodus] [40]:[24] He put the lampstand inside the sacred tent across from the table, on the south side of the residence,

[Exodus] [40]:[26] Then he put the gold incense altar inside the sacred tent in front of the curtain that screened the sacred box from view,

[Exodus] [40]:[31] so that Mosheh (Moses), and Aharon (Aaron) and his sons, could wash their hands and feet from it.
[Exodus] [40]:[32] Whenever they went into the sacred tent or whenever they went near the altar, first they would wash themselves, just as Yahweh had commanded Mosheh.
[Exodus] [40]:[33] He erected the courtyard curtains around the residence and the altar, and he set up the courtyard gate curtain. And so Mosheh finished the work.
[Exodus] [40]:[34] Then a cloud covered the sacred tent and Yahweh’s power and bright light filled the residence
[Exodus] [40]:[35] and Mosheh (Moses) was unable to enter the tent because the cloud had settled on it and Yahweh’s splendour had filled the residence.
[Exodus] [40]:[36] From then onwards, whenever the cloud went up from over the residence, the Israelis would pack their camp and set out on their travels,
[Exodus] [40]:[37] but while the cloud remained, they would stay in that place until the cloud lifted.
[Exodus] [40]:[38] Yahweh’s cloud would be there during the day but it would become fire at night, and so the Israelis could always see it.
[Leviticus] [1]:[1] Yahweh summoned Mosheh (Moses) to the sacred tent and told him,
[Leviticus] [1]:[2] “Tell the Israelis that when anyone presents an offering to Yahweh, it must be presented from their own herd or flock.
[Leviticus] [1]:[3] If it’s from the herd, it must be a bull with no defects. It must be presented in front of the entrance to the sacred tent to be acceptable to Yahweh.
[Leviticus] [1]:[4] The owner must place his hand on the head of that offering to be burnt, and then it will be accepted make him right with Yahweh.
[Leviticus] [1]:[5] Then he must slaughter the bull in front of Yahweh, and the priests (Aharon’s (Aaron) descendants), must present the blood and splash it all around the altar which is by the entrance of the sacred tent.
[Leviticus] [1]:[6] Then the presenter must skin the bull and cut it into pieces,
[Leviticus] [1]:[7] Meanwhile, the priest Aharon’s sons must put fire on the altar and arrange wood on the fire,
[Leviticus] [1]:[8] and then they must arrange the pieces (including the head and the fat portions) on top of the burning wood on the altar.
[Leviticus] [1]:[9] Then the presenter must wash the innards and the feet with water, and the priest must place it on the altar, ensuring that every part is completely burnt up as a pleasing aroma for Yahweh.
[Leviticus] [1]:[10] “If the offering is from the flock (i.e., a sheep or a goat), then it must be a healthy male that’s presented,
[Leviticus] [1]:[11] and then it must be slaughtered on the northern side of the altar facing Yahweh, and Aharon’s sons, the priests, must splash its blood on the altar, all around.
[Leviticus] [1]:[12] Then the presenter must cut it into pieces and they must arrange them (including the head and fat portions) on top of the burning wood on the altar.
[Leviticus] [1]:[13] Then the presenter must wash the innards and the feet with water, and the priest must place it on the altar, ensuring that every part is completely burnt up as a pleasing aroma for Yahweh.
[Leviticus] [1]:[14] “However, if his burnt offering to Yahweh will be a bird, then it must be either a dove or a young pigeon.
[Leviticus] [1]:[15] The priest must present it at the altar, and then twist its head off and burn the head on the altar as he drains the blood out onto the outer edge of the altar.
[Leviticus] [1]:[16] Then he must pull out the crop with its contents, and throw it down on the eastern side of the altar where the ashes are.
[Leviticus] [1]:[17] He will then tear the bird mostly apart by its wings (but making sure that it stays as one piece), and place it on the altar, ensuring that every part is completely burnt up as a pleasing aroma for Yahweh.
[Leviticus] [2]:[1] “When someone presents a grain offering to Yahweh, it must be as fine, wheat flour mixed with olive, and with frankincense added to the top of it.
[Leviticus] [2]:[2] It must be taken to the priest Aharon’s (Aaron) sons who will take it from them, then take a handful out, being sure to get flour, oil, and some frankincense, and throw that memorial portion onto the altar to get completely burnt up as a pleasing aroma for Yahweh.
[Leviticus] [2]:[3] Then the rest of that grain offering will be for Aharon and his sons—it’s a very sacred part from the gifts for Yahweh.
[Leviticus] [2]:[4] “When someone presents something baked as their grain offering, it must be baked without leaven: either wheat flour mixed with olive oil and baked into flat buns, or else wheat flour biscuits with olive oil spread on top.
[Leviticus] [2]:[5] Or if your grain offering is done on the flat pan, it must be wheat flour mixed with olive oil and made into flat biscuits
[Leviticus] [2]:[6] that should then be crumbled and have oil poured over them as your grain offering.
[Leviticus] [2]:[7] Or if your grain offering is deep-fried in a pot, it must be made from wheat flour with olive oil.
[Leviticus] [2]:[8] “Any of the above types of grain offering to Yahweh must be presented to the priest, and he will take it to the altar.
[Leviticus] [2]:[9] Then he must take a handful as a memorial portion to the altar to get completely burnt up as a pleasing aroma for Yahweh.
[Leviticus] [2]:[10] Then the rest of that grain offering will be for Aharon and his sons—it’s a very sacred part from the gifts for Yahweh.
[Leviticus] [2]:[11] “Anything that’s presented to Yahweh as a grain offering must not be made with any rising agent, because any leaven or honey mustn’t be burnt as a gift to Yahweh.
[Leviticus] [2]:[12] Foods containing those can be presented as a first-fruits offering, but they mustn’t be burnt on the altar.
[Leviticus] [2]:[13] However, every grain offering must be salted—the salt in the grain offering is a reminder of our agreement, so it must always be present.
[Leviticus] [2]:[14] “Finally, if you want to offer ripe grain as a grain offering to Yahweh, then it must be a young ear of grain that’s been roasted over the fire and presented as a grain offering of your first ripe grains
[Leviticus] [2]:[15] with olive oil on it and some frankincense on top. That also becomes a grain offering,
[Leviticus] [2]:[16] and the priest must burn a memorial portion from it with some of the crushed grains and some of the oil and some of the incense, to be burnt to become smoke as a gift to Yahweh.
[Leviticus] [3]:[1] “Now if it’s a sacrifice for a peace offering, if it’s from the herd, then either a male or female can be presented to Yahweh as long as it has no defects.
[Leviticus] [3]:[2] The presenter must lay their hand on the head of the bull or cow, then he must slaughter it in front of the sacred tent. Then the priest Aharon’s (Aaron) sons will splash the blood on the altar on each side.
[Leviticus] [3]:[3] From that peace offering, he must present the fat covering the innards and which is part of the innards as a gift to Yahweh,
[Leviticus] [3]:[4] along with both kidneys and the fat that’s attached to them, and the lobe on the liver (all of which need to be removed from the animal).
[Leviticus] [3]:[5] Then Aharon’s sons must burn them on the wood that’s burning on the altar as a gift—to become smoke as a pleasing aroma for Yahweh.
[Leviticus] [3]:[6] “However, if the sacrifice for a peace offering is from the flock, then either a male or a female can be presented to Yahweh as long as it has no defects.
[Leviticus] [3]:[7] When the offering is being presented, it must be presented in front of Yahweh,
[Leviticus] [3]:[8] and the presenter will put his hand on the head of the animal being offered, and slaughter it in front of the sacred tent. Then Aharon’s sons must splash its blood on the altar, on each side.
[Leviticus] [3]:[9] From that peace offering, he must present the fat as a gift to Yahweh, along with the entire fatty tail (cut off near the backbone), the fat covering the innards and which is part of the innards,
[Leviticus] [3]:[10] both kidneys and the fat that’s attached to them, and the lobe on the liver (all of which need to be removed from the animal).
[Leviticus] [3]:[11] Then the priest must burn them on the altar as a food offering made to Yahweh by fire.
[Leviticus] [3]:[12] “Similarly, if the offering is a goat, then it can be presented to Yahweh.
[Leviticus] [3]:[13] The presenter will put his hand on its head, and slaughter it in front of the sacred tent. Then Aharon’s sons must splash its blood on the altar, on each side.
[Leviticus] [3]:[14] From that peace offering, he must present the fat as a gift to Yahweh, along with the fat covering the innards and which is part of the innards,
[Leviticus] [3]:[15] both kidneys and the fat that’s attached to them, and the lobe on the liver (all of which need to be removed from the animal).
[Leviticus] [3]:[16] Then the priest must burn them on the altar as a food offering made to Yahweh by fire as a pleasing aroma. All the fat belongs to Yahweh.
[Leviticus] [3]:[17] “This regulation must be permanent for all future generations: All of you must never eat fat or blood.”
[Leviticus] [4]:[1] Then Yahweh told Mosheh (Moses),
[Leviticus] [4]:[2] “Tell the Israelis that if a person breaks any of Yahweh’s regulations unintentionally, or does anything that he said shouldn’t be done, then this is the procedure:
[Leviticus] [4]:[3] “If it’s the high priest who’s done it, that causes the nation to be guilty, and for his transgression he must present a bull with no defects to Yahweh as a sin offering.
[Leviticus] [4]:[4] He must bring the bull before Yahweh at the entrance of the sacred tent, then he must place his hand on its head and slaughter it in front of Yahweh.
[Leviticus] [4]:[5] Then the high priest must get some of the bull’s blood and bringing it into the sacred tent,
[Leviticus] [4]:[6] he must dip his finger into it and seven times he must flick the blood towards the front of the curtain of the sanctuary in front of Yahweh.
[Leviticus] [4]:[7] Then the high priest must put some of the blood on the four projecting corners of the incense altar (located inside the sacred tent in front of Yahweh and used for burning fragrant incense). Then he must go back outside and pour the rest of the bull’s blood out at the base of the altar for burnt offerings (which is out at the entrance to the sacred tent).
[Leviticus] [4]:[8] Then the high priest must remove all the fat from the bull being offered as a sin offering, including the fat covering the innards and which is a part of the innards,
[Leviticus] [4]:[9] both kidneys and the fat that’s attached to them, and the lobe on the liver (all of which need to be removed from the animal)
[Leviticus] [4]:[10] just like you’d do for the bull of the peace offering. Then the priest must burn them on the altar for the burnt offering.
[Leviticus] [4]:[11] However, the bull’s hide and its meat, plus its head and feet, and innards and dung,
[Leviticus] [4]:[12] must be taken outside the camp to the clean place where they pour out the ashes, and they must make a fire with wood there on top of the ashes and burn it there.
[Leviticus] [4]:[13] “If it’s the whole community that unintentionally transgresses by doing something that Yahweh prohibited, then they’ll be guilty even if the community didn’t actually notice.
[Leviticus] [4]:[14] When they become aware of what they’ve done wrong, then the community must present a young bull in front of the sacred tent as a sin offering.
[Leviticus] [4]:[15] Then the community elders must place their hands of the bull’s head in front of Yahweh, and slaughter it there.
[Leviticus] [4]:[16] The high priest must take some of the bull’s blood into the sacred tent
[Leviticus] [4]:[17] and seven times he must dip his finger in it and flick the blood towards the front of the curtain of the sanctuary in front of Yahweh.
[Leviticus] [4]:[18] Then he must put some of the blood on the four projecting corners of the incense altar (located inside the sacred tent in front of Yahweh). Then he must go back outside and pour the rest of the bull’s blood out at the base of the altar for burnt offerings (which is out at the entrance to the sacred tent).
[Leviticus] [4]:[19] Then he must remove all the fat from the slaughtered bull and burn up that fat on the altar,
[Leviticus] [4]:[20] and he should process the bull just the same as for a sin offering. Then the priest will have made them right with God and they’ll be forgiven.
[Leviticus] [4]:[21] Then he must take the remaining parts of the bull outside the camp and burn it as described above and it will be the sin offering for the community.
