[Leviticus] [4]:[22] “If it’s a leader that unintentionally transgresses by doing something that his god Yahweh prohibited, then he’ll be guilty.
[Leviticus] [4]:[23] Alternatively, maybe someone else will point out his failing to him. Then he must bring an offering of a male goat with no defects.
[Leviticus] [4]:[24] He must place his hand on its head and slaughter it in the place where the animals for the burnt offering are slaughtered. It will be a sin offering,
[Leviticus] [4]:[25] and the priest must take some of the blood of that sin offering and with his finger, put some of the blood on the four projecting corners of the altar for burnt offerings.
[Leviticus] [4]:[26] He must burn up all the fat on the altar just like the fat from the peace offering, and that way, the priest will make that leader right with God and he’ll be forgiven.
[Leviticus] [4]:[27] “If it’s an ordinary person who unintentionally transgresses by doing something that Yahweh prohibited, then they’ll be guilty.
[Leviticus] [4]:[28] Alternatively, maybe someone else will point out their failing to them. Then due to their transgression, that person must bring an offering of a female goat with no defects.
[Leviticus] [4]:[29] He must place his hand on the head of the goat that’s a sin offering, and slaughter it at the place for burnt offerings.
[Leviticus] [4]:[30] Then the priest must take some of the blood and with his finger, put some of the blood on the four projecting corners of the altar for burnt offerings, and then pour the rest of the blood at the altar’s base.
[Leviticus] [4]:[31] Then the presenter must pull out all the fat (just like it’s done for the peace offering), and the priest will burn it on the altar to make a pleasing aroma for Yahweh, and to make that person right with God, and they’ll be forgiven.
[Leviticus] [4]:[32] “But if it’s a lamb that the individual wants to bring as their sin offering, then it must be a female with no defects.
[Leviticus] [4]:[33] The presenter must put their hand on the head of the lamb and slaughter it as a sin offering at the place where burnt offerings are slaughtered.
[Leviticus] [4]:[34] Then the priest must take some of the blood and with his finger, put some of the blood on the four projecting corners of the altar for burnt offerings, and then pour the rest of the blood at the altar’s base.
[Leviticus] [4]:[35] Then the presenter must pull out all the fat (just like it’s done for the peace offering), and the priest will burn it on the altar to make a pleasing aroma for Yahweh, and to make that person right with God, and they’ll be forgiven.
[Leviticus] [5]:[1] “If someone is a witness to a case because of something they saw or knew about, and hears an oath in court but doesn’t testify, then they’ll become guilty.
[Leviticus] [5]:[2] “If someone touches anything ‘unclean’ (e.g., a dead domestic or wild animal, or some creature) without realising it, they still become ‘unclean’ and is guilty.
[Leviticus] [5]:[3] “If someone touches anything ‘unclean’ from another person, even if they initially didn’t realise what it was, they become guilty.
[Leviticus] [5]:[4] “If someone makes a rash promise, whether it’s to do something good or something bad, and even if they were just speaking carelessly but find out later, they become guilty.
[Leviticus] [5]:[5] “So then the person that became guilty from any of the above, must confess their wrongdoing
[Leviticus] [5]:[6] and present a penalty to Yahweh to address that wrongdoing, and must present a female lamb or young goat as a sin offering, and the priest will act on their behalf to make them right with God.
[Leviticus] [5]:[7] “However if that person can’t afford a sheep, then for their guilt offering because of their transgression, they must bring two doves or young pigeons to Yahweh—one for a sin offering and one for a burnt offering.
[Leviticus] [5]:[8] The presenter must take them to the priest who will present the sin offering first—twisting the bird’s head off from the neck, but not pulling the body in half.
[Leviticus] [5]:[9] Then he must sprinkle some of the blood from that sin offering onto the side of the altar, and then drain out the rest of the blood at the altar’s base. That will be the sin offering.
[Leviticus] [5]:[10] The second bird will be for a burnt offering as per the regulation. The priest will make the presenter right with God after their wrongdoing, and they’ll be forgiven.
[Leviticus] [5]:[11] “However if that person still can’t afford those two doves or young pigeons, then they can present a kilogram of fine wheat flour for a sin offering. It mustn’t have oil or frankincense in it because it’s a sin offering.
[Leviticus] [5]:[12] The presenter must take it to the priest who will then take a handful of it, and burn that memorial portion on the altar for burnt offerings to Yahweh. That will be the sin offering.
[Leviticus] [5]:[13] The priest will make the presenter right with God after their wrongdoing as per one of the above, and they’ll be forgiven. The rest of the flour will be for the priest, similar to a grain offering.”
[Leviticus] [5]:[14] Then Yahweh told Mosheh (Moses),
[Leviticus] [5]:[15] “If someone acts unfaithfully but unintentionally desecrates something that’s sacred to Yahweh, then because of their guilt, that person must present ram with no defects from the flock, or silver coins using the official valuation, as a guilt offering.
[Leviticus] [5]:[16] They must also compensate for the sacred item, but with an extra twenty percent. That must all be given to the priest who will make the presenter right with God with that ram as the guilt offering, and they’ll be forgiven.
[Leviticus] [5]:[17] “If someone transgresses by violating even one of Yahweh’s regulations or prohibitions, even if they didn’t realise it, they become guilty and must bear responsibility for that guilt.
[Leviticus] [5]:[18] Then that person must take a ram from the flock that has no defects to the priest for a guilt offering. Then the priest will make the presenter right with God after that transgression (even if they weren’t aware of it), and they’ll be forgiven.
[Leviticus] [5]:[19] That’s a guilt offering, because they were clearly guilty before Yahweh.”
[Leviticus] [6]:[1] Then Yahweh told Mosheh (Moses),
[Leviticus] [6]:[2] “Someone who transgresses against Yahweh by cheating with respect to a deposit or a pledge, or by theft or extortion,
[Leviticus] [6]:[3] or by finding lost property and then denying it, or making an oath that was knowingly false, or by any other typical transgression that people do,
[Leviticus] [6]:[4] then they’ve become guilty as a result of that transgression. That person must return what was stolen or extorted, or return the deposit or the lost property,
[Leviticus] [6]:[5] or make amends for a false oath. They must return the full value plus an extra twenty percent as soon as the guilt is discovered.
[Leviticus] [6]:[6] Then that person must take a ram from the flock with no defects to the priest as a guilt offering to Yahweh,
[Leviticus] [6]:[7] and the priest will make the presenter right with Yahweh after whatever that transgression was to make them guilty, and they’ll be forgiven.
[Leviticus] [6]:[8] Then Yahweh told Mosheh (Moses),
[Leviticus] [6]:[9] “Tell Aharon (Aaron) and his sons that these are the regulations for the burnt offerings: The burnt offering must remain on the altar’s hearth, on the altar all night until the morning and the fire must be kept burning on it.
[Leviticus] [6]:[10] Then the priest must put on his linen underwear and linen robe and remove the fatty ashes from the burnt offerings on the altar, and pile them beside it.
[Leviticus] [6]:[11] After that, he’ll get changed again into his regular clothes and take those ashes outside the camp to a ‘clean’ place.
[Leviticus] [6]:[12] Meanwhile, the fire on the altar must be kept burning—it must never go out. Every morning the priest must put more wood on the fire, then he must arrange more offerings on the fire—he should burn the fat of the fellowship offerings on that fire so the smoke rises.
[Leviticus] [6]:[13] Yes, the fire must burn continually on the altar—never going out.
[Leviticus] [6]:[14] “Here’s the regulations for the grain offering: Aharon’s (Aaron) sons must present it before Yahweh in front of the altar.
[Leviticus] [6]:[15] The priest must take a handful of the flour from that grain offering, being sure it includes some of the oil and the incense, and burn it on the altar as a memorial portion to become a pleasing aroma for Yahweh.
[Leviticus] [6]:[16] The remainder of that flour will be used as food for Aharon and his sons—they must eat the flat bread in a sacred place, i.e., in the courtyard of the sacred tent.
[Leviticus] [6]:[17] It must not be baked with any rising agent. I give that to them from what’s given to me. It’s very sacred just like the sin offering and the guilt offering.
[Leviticus] [6]:[18] Any of Aharon’s male descendants can eat it—it’ll be their portion from Yahweh’s gifts throughout the generations. Anyone who touches Yahweh’s gifts will become sacred themself.”
[Leviticus] [6]:[19] Then Yahweh told Mosheh (Moses),
[Leviticus] [6]:[20] “On the day when one of Aharon’s (Aaron) male descendants is consecrated as a priest, this is what he must present to Yahweh: a continual grain offering of a kilogram of fine wheat flour—half for the morning and half for the evening.
[Leviticus] [6]:[21] It must be mixed with olive oil then cooked with oil on a flat pan. It must then be broken into pieces and presented as a grain offering to make a pleasing aroma for Yahweh.
[Leviticus] [6]:[22] The priest who’s next in line to become high priest must offer it and it must be completely burnt for Yahweh. This is a permanent regulation.
[Leviticus] [6]:[23] Any grain offering by a priest must be completely burnt—it must not be eaten.”
[Leviticus] [6]:[24] Then Yahweh told Mosheh (Moses),
[Leviticus] [6]:[25] “Tell Aharon (Aaron) and his sons that these are the regulations for the sin offerings: The sin offering must be slaughtered in front of Yahweh at the place where the burnt offerings are slaughtered. It’s a very sacred activity.
[Leviticus] [6]:[26] The priest who offers the sin offering must be the one to eat it. It must be eaten in a sacred place, i.e., in the courtyard of the sacred tent.
[Leviticus] [6]:[27] Everything that touches the animal’s body will become sacred. Anyone who gets the blood on their clothes, must wash them in a sacred place.
[Leviticus] [6]:[28] Any clay pot that it’s been boiled in, must then be shattered, but if it’s boiled in a bronze pot, then that must be scoured and rinsed with water.
[Leviticus] [6]:[29] Any male in the priests’ families may eat it—it’s very sacred.
[Leviticus] [6]:[30] However, every sin offering that has its blood taken inside the sacred tent to make someone right with God, then that meat mustn’t be eaten—it must be completely burnt up.
[Leviticus] [7]:[1] “Then these are the regulations for the very sacred guilt offerings:
[Leviticus] [7]:[2] The guilt offering must be slaughtered at the same place as the burnt offerings, and the blood must be splashed on each side of the altar.
[Leviticus] [7]:[3] The presenter must present all the fat including the fatty tail, the fat covering the innards,
[Leviticus] [7]:[4] both kidneys and the fat that’s attached to them, and the lobe on the liver (all of which need to be removed from the animal).
[Leviticus] [7]:[5] Then the priest must burn those on the altar as a guilt offering to Yahweh.
[Leviticus] [7]:[6] Any male in the priests’ families may eat it—it’s very sacred.
[Leviticus] [7]:[7] The regulations are the same for the guilt offering as for the sin offering—the priest who offers the guilt offering must be the one to eat it.
[Leviticus] [7]:[8] “Whenever a priest presents someone’s burnt offering, the skin of the animal that was presented belongs to that priest.
[Leviticus] [7]:[9] Any grain offering that’s baked in an oven, or cooked in a pan or on a griddle, will belong to the priest who presents it.
[Leviticus] [7]:[10] Any grain offering that’s either dry or mixed with oil, belongs to all of Aharon’s (Aaron) male descendants without any distinction.
[Leviticus] [7]:[11] “Then these are the regulations for sacrificing peace offerings to present to Yahweh:
[Leviticus] [7]:[12] If it’s presented from thankfulness, then the sacrifice must be accompanied by thanksgiving flat bread buns (made from flour mixed with olive oil), and flat biscuits smeared with oil, and buns made from fine wheat flour mixed with oil,
[Leviticus] [7]:[13] plus risen bread rolls. All that must accompany the peace offering from thankfulness.
[Leviticus] [7]:[14] Then he must present one of each kind of bread as a contribution to Yahweh. Those will belong to the priest who splashes the blood for the peace offerings.
[Leviticus] [7]:[15] The meat of the thankfulness sacrifice of those peace offerings must be eaten the same day that it’s offered—none of it can be left until morning.
[Leviticus] [7]:[16] However, if the sacrificed offering is a vow or freewill offering, then it can be eaten that same day and also the next day,
[Leviticus] [7]:[17] but any left-over meat must be burnt up on the fire on the third day.
[Leviticus] [7]:[18] If any of that meat from the sacrifice was eaten on the third day, the presenter won’t be accepted and they won’t be forgiven. It is spoilt, and anyone who eats any of it will bear their own guilt.
[Leviticus] [7]:[19] If any meat touches anything that’s ‘unclean’, then it must not be eaten—it must be burnt up in the fire. However, any long as the meat remains ‘clean’, it can be eaten by any person who’s ‘clean’.
[Leviticus] [7]:[20] If a person who was ‘unclean’ were to eat any of the meat from the sacrifice for a peace offering, then that person must be cut off from the community.
[Leviticus] [7]:[21] Similarly, when a person touches anything ‘unclean’ (e.g., human uncleanness, or an unclean animal, or a detestable creature), and then they eat some of the meat of the sacrifice for a peace offering that now belongs to Yahweh, that person must be cut off from the community.
[Leviticus] [7]:[22] Then Yahweh told Mosheh (Moses),
[Leviticus] [7]:[23] “Tell the Israelis that you all must not eat the fat from cattle or sheep or goats,
[Leviticus] [7]:[24] plus you all definitely must not eat the fat from an animal that died naturally or was killed by wild animals although you can use it for other purposes.
[Leviticus] [7]:[25] Anyone who does eat the fat from an animal presented as a gift to Yahweh must be cut off from the community.
[Leviticus] [7]:[26] “Also, you all must not eat blood from either a bird or an animal, no matter where you’re living.
[Leviticus] [7]:[27] Any person who does eat blood must be cut off from the community.”
[Leviticus] [7]:[28] Then Yahweh told Mosheh (Moses),
[Leviticus] [7]:[29] “Tell the Israelis that anyone who offers a peace offering to Yahweh must take some of it as his peace offering to Yahweh.
[Leviticus] [7]:[30] They must personally carry Yahweh’s gift which will be the breast with its fat and raise it in front of Yahweh as a wave offering,
[Leviticus] [7]:[31] and the priest must burn that fat up on the altar but the breast will be for Aharon (Aaron) and his sons.
[Leviticus] [7]:[32] The right thigh from the sacrifices of your peace offerings must be given to the priest—
[Leviticus] [7]:[33] whichever priest (Aharon’s descendant) who handled the blood of the peace offerings and the fat, that right thigh will be his portion
[Leviticus] [7]:[34] because I took the breast from the wave offering and the thigh from the contribution of the Israelis’ peace offerings, and I gave them to Aharon the priest and his sons as an ongoing portion from the Israeli people.
[Leviticus] [7]:[35] That’s the share for Aharon and his sons from the gifts to Yahweh since Mosheh presented them to Yahweh as priests.
[Leviticus] [7]:[36] Yahweh commanded them to be given to them back on the day when he anointed them out of all the Israeli people and made it a permanent regulation for future generations.
[Leviticus] [7]:[37] Those are the regulations for the burnt offerings, the grain offerings, the sin offerings, the guilt offerings, the ordination offerings, and the peace offerings
[Leviticus] [7]:[38] that Yahweh gave to Mosheh at Mt. Sinay on the day when he ordered the Israelis to present their offerings to Yahweh when they were there in the Sinay wilderness.
[Leviticus] [8]:[1] Then Yahweh told Mosheh (Moses),
[Leviticus] [8]:[2] “Take Aharon (Aaron) and his sons with their clothes and the anointing oil, and the bull for the sin offering and two rams, and a basket of unleavened bread,
[Leviticus] [8]:[3] and assemble the entire community at the entrance to the sacred tent.”
[Leviticus] [8]:[4] So Mosheh did exactly has Yahweh had commanded him, and the people assembled at the entrance of the sacred tent.
[Leviticus] [8]:[5] Then Mosheh told the assembled people, “This ceremony is what Yahweh has told us to do.”
[Leviticus] [8]:[6] Then Mosheh presented Aharon and his sons and after washing them with water,
[Leviticus] [8]:[7] he put the tunic on Aharon and wrapped the sash around him, and then put the robe on him. Then he put the sacred apron on him, tying its finely woven waistband to fasten it onto him.
[Leviticus] [8]:[8] Then he attached the chest pouch and put the Urim and Tumim into the pouch.
[Leviticus] [8]:[9] Finally he placed the turban on his head, and fastened the golden flower-shaped plate (that sacred crown that demonstrates that Aharon is set apart to only serve Yahweh) to the front of the turban, exactly as Yahweh had instructed Mosheh.
[Leviticus] [8]:[10] Then Mosheh took the anointing oil and anointed Yahweh’s residence and everything in it, thus consecrating it all.
[Leviticus] [8]:[11] Seven times he flicked some of it onto the altar—anointing the altar and all its utensils and the basin and its base, thus consecrating them.
[Leviticus] [8]:[12] He poured some of the anointing oil over Aharon’s head, thus anointing him to consecrate him.
[Leviticus] [8]:[13] Then Mosheh presented Aharon’s sons and dressed them in tunics and wrapped sashes around each of them, and tied their headbands onto them, just as Yahweh had instructed Mosheh.
[Leviticus] [8]:[14] Then he brought the bull for the sin offering, and Aharon and his sons placed their hands on its head.
[Leviticus] [8]:[15] Then Aharon slaughtered it, and Mosheh took the blood and used his finger to put some on the four projecting corners of the altar, thus purifying the altar. Then he poured the rest of the blood out at the altar’s base, sanctifying it so it could be used for making people right with God.
[Leviticus] [8]:[16] Then Mosheh took all the far that was on the innards and the lobe of the liver, and the two kidneys and their fat, and he burnt them up on the altar.
[Leviticus] [8]:[17] However, he burnt up the rest of the bull including its hide, flesh, and dung, outside the camp, just as Yahweh had told him.
[Leviticus] [8]:[18] Then Mosheh presented the ram for the burnt offering, and Aharon and his sons placed their hands on its head.
[Leviticus] [8]:[19] Then Aharon slaughtered it, and Mosheh splashed the blood on each side of the altar.
[Leviticus] [8]:[20] Then Aharon cut the ram into pieces, and Mosheh burnt up the head, and the pieces and the fat.
[Leviticus] [8]:[21] However, Aharon washed the innards and the legs, then Mosheh also burnt those up on the altar as a burnt offering that was pleasing aroma for Yahweh, just as Yahweh had instructed Mosheh.
[Leviticus] [8]:[22] Then Mosheh presented the second ram for the ordination offering, and Aharon and his sons placed their hands on the ram’s head.
[Leviticus] [8]:[23] Then Aharon slaughtered it, and Mosheh took some of its blood and put it on the lobe of Aharon’s right ear, on his right thumb, and on his right big toe.
[Leviticus] [8]:[24] Then he presented Aharon’s sons and put some of the blood on their right earlobes, and their right thumbs, and their right big toes. Then Mosheh splashed the blood on each side of the altar.
[Leviticus] [8]:[25] He collected the fat and the fatty tail, and all the fat that was on the innards and the lobe of the liver, and the two kidneys with their fat, and the right thigh,
[Leviticus] [8]:[26] Then from the basket of unleavened bread that was there in front of Yahweh, he took one flat bread bun, and one flat bread that had been smeared with oil, and one flat biscuit, and placed them on top of the fat and the right thigh.
[Leviticus] [8]:[27] He place all that onto the open hands of Aharon and his sons who raised them as a wave offering in front of Yahweh.
[Leviticus] [8]:[28] Then Mosheh took it all again, and burnt it all up on the altar with the burnt offering. That ordination offering on the fire became a pleasing aroma for Yahweh.
[Leviticus] [8]:[29] Then Mosheh took the breast meat from the ram for the ordination offering, and raised it as a wave offering in front of Yahweh, just as Yahweh had instructed him.
[Leviticus] [8]:[30] Then Mosheh took some of the anointing oil and some of the blood from on the altar, and he flicked them onto Aharon and his clothes, his sons and their clothes, thus consecrating Aharon and his clothes, and his sons and their clothes.
[Leviticus] [8]:[31] Then Mosheh told Aharon and his sons, “Boil the meat at the entrance to the sacred tent and eat it, along with the flat bread that’s in the basket as part of the ordination offering, just as I had instructed that Aharon and his sons should eat it.
[Leviticus] [8]:[32] Any meat or bread that’s leftover must be burnt in the fire.
[Leviticus] [8]:[33] None of you may leave the entrance to the sacred tent for seven days. That’s because Yahweh will ordain you all over those seven days.
[Leviticus] [8]:[34] What’s been done today has been initiated by Yahweh in order to make you all right with him,
[Leviticus] [8]:[35] so remain here day and night at the entrance of the sacred tent for seven days as per Yahweh’s instructions and you all won’t die, because that’s what I’ve been commanded.”
[Leviticus] [8]:[36] So Aharon and his sons did everything that Yahweh had instructed them via Mosheh.
[Leviticus] [9]:[1] On the eighth day, Mosheh (Moses) summoned Aharon (Aaron) and his sons, along with Yisrael’s (Israel) elders,
[Leviticus] [9]:[2] and he told Aharon, “Get a healthy, young, male calf for a sin offering for yourself, and a ram without defects for a burnt offering, and present them to Yahweh.
[Leviticus] [9]:[3] Then tell the Israeli people to take a male goat for a sin offering, and a calf and a lamb, both a year old and without defects for a burnt offering,
[Leviticus] [9]:[4] as well as a bull and a ram to sacrifice to Yahweh as peace offerings, and a grain offering mixed will oil, because Yahweh will appear to you all today.”
[Leviticus] [9]:[5] So they brought everything to the sacred tent that Mosheh had instructed them, and the whole assembly presented them as they stood before Yahweh,
[Leviticus] [9]:[6] then Mosheh said, “You’ve done what Yahweh told you, so now you’ll all see his brightness appear.”
[Leviticus] [9]:[7] Then he told Aharon, “Go to the altar and make your sin offering and your burnt offering to make yourself and the people right with God. Then make the people’s offering to make them right with God, just as Yahweh commanded.”
[Leviticus] [9]:[8] So Aharon approached the altar and slaughtered the calf for his own sin offering,
[Leviticus] [9]:[9] and his sons presented the blood to him. Dipping his finger into the blood, he smeared it on the altar’s four projecting corners, then he poured the rest of the blood out at the altar’s base.
[Leviticus] [9]:[10] He burnt up the fat and the kidneys, and the lobe from the liver for the sin offering on the altar, just as Yahweh had instructed Mosheh,
[Leviticus] [9]:[11] but the meat and the skin, he burnt up in a fire outside the camp.
[Leviticus] [9]:[12] Then Aharon slaughtered the burnt offering, and his sons brought the blood to him and he splashed it on each side of the altar.
[Leviticus] [9]:[13] Then they brought him the head and the cut-up pieces, and he burnt them up on the altar.
[Leviticus] [9]:[14] He washed the innards and the legs, and then also burnt them up on the altar.
[Leviticus] [9]:[15] Then Aharon presented the people’s offering. He took the goat for the people’s offering and slaughtered it, then offered it as a sin offering like the other one.
[Leviticus] [9]:[16] He presented the burnt offering—following all the instructions when he did it.
[Leviticus] [9]:[17] Then he presented the grain offering, and taking a large handful, he burnt it on the altar, in addition to the morning’s burnt offering.
[Leviticus] [9]:[18] Then Aharon slaughtered the bull and the ram which were the people’s peace offering, and his sons brought the blood to him and he splashed it on each side of the altar.
[Leviticus] [9]:[19] He took the fat from the bull and the ram, including their fatty tails and the fat covering the innards, the kidneys, and the lobe of the liver,
[Leviticus] [9]:[20] and placed it all on top of those animals breast meat, then burnt up the fat on the altar.
[Leviticus] [9]:[21] Finally, he raised the breast meat and the right thigh as a wave offering in front of Yahweh, just as Mosheh (Moses) had instructed.
[Leviticus] [9]:[22] Then Aharon raised his arms towards the people and blessed them, and then he stepped down, having finished making the sin offering, the burnt offering, and the peace offerings.
[Leviticus] [9]:[23] Mosheh and Aharon entered the sacred tent, and when they came back out, they blessed the people and Yahweh’s brilliance appeared to all the people.
[Leviticus] [9]:[24] Then flames shot out from Yahweh’s front and evaporated the burnt offering and the fat on the altar. They people saw that happen, and they yelled out and fell down onto their knees with their faces to the ground.
[Leviticus] [10]:[1] Then two of Aharon’s (Aaron) sons, Nadav and Avihu each took their incense-burning pans and put fire in them, and put incense on the fire, thus offering unauthorised fire to Yahweh that he hadn’t instructed them to do.
[Leviticus] [10]:[2] So flames shot out from Yahweh’s front and consumed then so they died there in front of Yahweh.
[Leviticus] [10]:[3] Then Mosheh (Moses) told Aharon, “That’s what Yahweh meant when he said, ‘I will reveal my holiness to those who approach me, then I’ll be honoured in the sight of all the people.’ ”
[Leviticus] [10]:[4] Then Mosheh summoned Mishael and Elitsafan, the sons of Aharon’s Uncle Uziel, and told them, “Come and help by carrying your cousins’ bodies from the sacred place here to a place outside the camp.”
[Leviticus] [10]:[5] So they came and carried the two corpses by their clothes to a place outside the camp just as Mosheh had told them to do.
[Leviticus] [10]:[6] Then Mosheh told Aharon and his sons Eleazar and Itamar, “Don’t leave your hair loose, and don’t tear your clothes, so that you won’t die and so that Yahweh won’t be angry at the entire community. But meanwhile, all the Israelis must mourn because Yahweh was angry enough to burn those two.
[Leviticus] [10]:[7] Also, don’t leave the entrance to the sacred tent, as you might die because you all still have Yahweh’s anointing oil on you.” So they did everything that Mosheh said.
[Leviticus] [10]:[8] Then Yahweh told Aharon (Aaron),
[Leviticus] [10]:[9] “Neither you or your sons should drink wine or strong drink when you’re going to go into the sacred tent so that you won’t die. This regulation is permanent and for future generations.
[Leviticus] [10]:[10] You must carefully distinguish between what’s sacred and what’s common, and what’s ‘unclean’ and ‘clean’.
[Leviticus] [10]:[11] and you must teach the Israelis all the instructions that Yahweh has given them via Mosheh (Moses).”
[Leviticus] [10]:[12] Then Mosheh told Aharon and his remaining sons Eleazar and Itamar, “Take the remainder of the grain offering after the memorial portion has been given to Yahweh, and eat that flat bread there beside the altar, because it’s very sacred.
[Leviticus] [10]:[13] You all must eat it in a sacred place, because it’s the portion for you and your sons from the gifts to Yahweh, because that’s what I’ve been instructed.
[Leviticus] [10]:[14] Also, you all must eat the breast meat from the wave offering and the thigh from the contribution offering in a ‘clean’ place. Your sons and daughters can join you all for that, because that food has been given as the portion for you and your children from the peace offering sacrifices from the Israelis.
[Leviticus] [10]:[15] Yes, those thighs from the contribution offering and the breast meat from the wave offering, in addition to the gifts of the fat portions, must be brought before Yahweh as a raised offering, and then they’ll always become the portion for you and your families, just as Yahweh instructed.”
[Leviticus] [10]:[16] Then Mosheh looked for the goat meat from the sin offering, but was shocked to discover that it had been burnt up on the altar, so he was angry with Aharon’s remaining sons Eleazar and Itamar, telling them,
[Leviticus] [10]:[17] “Why didn’t you eat that sin offering in the sacred place, because it’s very sacred and he gave it to you to bear the community’s guilt then to make them right with Yahweh.
[Leviticus] [10]:[18] Listen here! Its blood wasn’t taken into the inner sacred place, so you must eat it in the sacred place just like I told you to do!”
[Leviticus] [10]:[19] Then Aharon explained to Mosheh, “Listen, they presented their sin offering and their burnt offering to Yahweh today, and yet I lost two of my sons. But if I’d eaten the sin offering today, would it have pleased Yahweh?”
[Leviticus] [10]:[20] When Mosheh heard that, he was satisfied.
[Leviticus] [11]:[1] Then Yahweh told Mosheh (Moses) and Aharon (Aaron):
[Leviticus] [11]:[2] Tell the Israelis that the following creatures on the earth are the ones that you all can eat:
[Leviticus] [11]:[3] You all can eat any animal that has hooves which are completely split in two and that also chew the cud.
[Leviticus] [11]:[4] However you mustn’t eat those without both traits, for example camels chew the cud but don’t have divided hooves, so they are ‘unclean’ for you.
[Leviticus] [11]:[5] The rock badger likewise, because although it chews the cud, it too doesn’t have divided hooves,
[Leviticus] [11]:[6] and the rabbit is ‘unclean’ for you all because although it chews the cud, it doesn’t have divided hooves.
[Leviticus] [11]:[7] Pigs have divided hooves that are split completely, but don’t chew the cud, so they’re ‘unclean’ for you all—
[Leviticus] [11]:[8] you mustn’t eat their meat or touch their carcasses because they’re ‘unclean’ for you all.
[Leviticus] [11]:[9] You all can eat everything that lives in the water, whether the oceans or rivers, as long as it has both fins and scales.
[Leviticus] [11]:[10] In contrast, anything in the oceans or rivers without both fins and scales, whether they’re swarming creatures or otherwise, they’ll all be detestable for you all.
[Leviticus] [11]:[11] So anything that’s detestable to you all, you mustn’t eat their meat and you must detest their carcasses.
[Leviticus] [11]:[12] Anything in the water that doesn’t have both fins and scales will be detestable for you all.
[Leviticus] [11]:[13] From the birds, the ones that you’ll all detest and avoid eating will include: the eagle and any kind of vulture,
[Leviticus] [11]:[14] the kite and any kind of falcon,
[Leviticus] [11]:[15] any kind of crow,
[Leviticus] [11]:[16] any kind of owl, gull, or hawk,
[Leviticus] [11]:[17] the cormorant,
[Leviticus] [11]:[18] the osprey,
[Leviticus] [11]:[19] the stork, any kind of heron, the hoopoe, and bats.
[Leviticus] [11]:[20] Everything that swarms with wings and walks on four legs must be detestable for you all.
[Leviticus] [11]:[21] However, you all can eat anything that swarms with wings and walks on four legs that has its legs above its feet for hopping on the ground.
[Leviticus] [11]:[22] You all can eat any kind of locust or cricket or grasshopper,
[Leviticus] [11]:[23] but anything that swarms with wings and walks on four legs must be detestable for you all.
[Leviticus] [11]:[24] The following will make you ‘unclean’—anyone who touches their carcasses will become ‘unclean’ until the evening,
[Leviticus] [11]:[25] plus anyone who carries their carcass must wash their clothes and will be ‘unclean’ until the evening:
[Leviticus] [11]:[26] Any animal with a divided hoof but not completely split in two or that doesn’t chew the cud will be ‘unclean’ for you all—anyone who touches them will become ‘unclean’.
[Leviticus] [11]:[27] Also, any four-footed animal that walks on its paws is ‘unclean’ for you—anyone who touches their carcass will become ‘unclean’ until the evening,
[Leviticus] [11]:[28] plus anyone who carries their carcass must wash their clothes and will be ‘unclean’ until the evening because they’re ‘unclean’ for you all.
[Leviticus] [11]:[29] These are the ‘unclean’ creatures from the ones that swarm on the ground: rats, mice, lizards
[Leviticus] [11]:[30] of any kind, geckos, skinks, and chameleons.
[Leviticus] [11]:[31] Out of all the swarming things, those are ‘unclean’ for you—anyone who touches them when they’ve died will be ‘unclean’ until the evening.
[Leviticus] [11]:[32] Also, anything that their dead bodies fall on will become ‘unclean’, whether it’s a wooden, cloth, leather, or sackcloth object, or any container used for work, so then it must be immersed in water and it will be ‘unclean’ until the evening when it will become ‘clean’ again.
[Leviticus] [11]:[33] If one of those creatures falls into a clay container, everything in it will become ‘unclean’ and you must break that container.
[Leviticus] [11]:[34] If water from that container got onto any food, it will become ‘unclean’, and any drink take from that container will be ‘unclean’.
[Leviticus] [11]:[35] Anything that the dead body of one of those creatures falls onto will become ‘unclean’—any oven or stove must be smashed. They have become ‘unclean’ and would always remain so.
[Leviticus] [11]:[36] However a spring or a cistern for collecting water will be ‘clean’, but anyone touching that dead body will be ‘unclean’.
[Leviticus] [11]:[37] If the dead body fell on some seeds that will be planted, that seed is still ‘clean’,
[Leviticus] [11]:[38] but if the seeds are wet when the dead body falls on it, then it’s ‘unclean’ for you.
[Leviticus] [11]:[39] If any animal that you all can eat dies, then any person touches its carcass will be ‘unclean’ until the evening.
[Leviticus] [11]:[40] Anyone who eats any part of that dead body, and anyone who moves it, must wash their clothes and will be ‘unclean’ until the evening.
[Leviticus] [11]:[41] Every creature that swarms along the ground is detestable—it mustn’t be eaten.
[Leviticus] [11]:[42] Everything that moves on its belly, and any swarming thing that moves along the ground on four or more feet mustn’t be eaten because they’re detestable.
[Leviticus] [11]:[43] Don’t make yourselves detestable with any of those swarming creatures, and don’t make yourselves ‘unclean’ by touching or eating them,
[Leviticus] [11]:[44] because I am your god Yahweh. You all must keep yourselves holy, and you’re a holy people because I’m holy. So don’t make yourselves ‘unclean’ with any swarming creatures that creep across the ground
[Leviticus] [11]:[45] because I am Yahweh, the one who brought you all out of Mitsrayim (Egypt) to be your god, and you must be holy because I am holy.
[Leviticus] [11]:[46] The above are the regulations about livestock, birds, creatures that move in the water, and creatures that swarm across the ground,
[Leviticus] [11]:[47] to distinguish between the ‘unclean’ and the ‘clean’, i.e., those that can be eaten and those that must not be eaten.
[Leviticus] [12]:[1] Then Yahweh told Mosheh (Moses):
[Leviticus] [12]:[2] Tell the Israelis that when a woman gets pregnant and then gives birth to a boy, she will then be ‘unclean’ for seven days similar to how her impurity during her monthly period makes her ‘unclean’.
[Leviticus] [12]:[3] Then on the eighth day, the baby boy’s foreskin must be circumcised.
[Leviticus] [12]:[4] The mother will remain impure from the blood for thirty-three days—she must not touch any sacred thing and may not enter the sanctuary until her purification time is completed.
[Leviticus] [12]:[5] However, if she gave birth to a girl, she’ll be ‘unclean’ for two weeks similar to how her impurity during her monthly period, and her purification time will be sixty-six days.
[Leviticus] [12]:[6] When the mother’s purification time is completed for either a son or a daughter, she must take a one-year-old lamb as a burnt offering and a young pigeon or dove as a sin offering to the priest at the entrance to the sacred tent.
[Leviticus] [12]:[7] Then he must present them to Yahweh to make her right with God, and then she’ll be purified from her flow of blood. That’s the regulation for a woman who gives birth to either a male or a female.
[Leviticus] [12]:[8] If she’s unable to afford a lamb, then she must take two young pigeons or doves—one for the burnt offering and one for the sin offering. Then the priest will make her right with God, and then she’ll will have been purified.
[Leviticus] [13]:[1] Then Yahweh told Mosheh (Moses) and Aharon (Aaron):
[Leviticus] [13]:[2] If someone discovers a raised area on their skin, or a scab or a bright spot, and it seems like an infectious skin disease, then that person should be taken to a priest (Aharon or one of his sons),
[Leviticus] [13]:[3] and the priest must examine their skin. If the hair in the infected spot has turned white and the infection appears to be deeper under the skin, then it’s confirmed as an infectious skin disease and so the priest must pronounce the person as ‘unclean’.
[Leviticus] [13]:[4] However, if it’s a white spot that doesn’t seem to be deep, and the hair hasn’t turned white, then the priest must order the person to be quarantined for seven days.
[Leviticus] [13]:[5] Then on the seventh day, if the infection is still there but hasn’t spread, then the priest must order a further seven days of quarantine.
[Leviticus] [13]:[6] After that next seven days, if the infection has faded and not spread, the priest must pronounce the person as ‘clean’—it was just a sore so the person must wash their clothes and then they’ll be ‘clean’.
[Leviticus] [13]:[7] However, if the spot does spread across the skin after the priest has pronounced the person to be ‘clean’, then they must return to the priest a second time.
[Leviticus] [13]:[8] The priest must re-examine that person and if the spot on the skin has spread, then the priest must pronounce them ‘unclean’ because they have a skin disease.
[Leviticus] [13]:[9] Anyone who develops an infectious skin disease must be taken to a priest
[Leviticus] [13]:[10] to be examined. If it’s a white spot on the skin and the hair has turned white, and there’s raw flesh visible in the swelling,
[Leviticus] [13]:[11] then it’s a chronic skin disease, and the priest must pronounce that person as ‘unclean’ and can’t just be temporarily quarantined.
[Leviticus] [13]:[12] However, if the disease has broken out and spread across the entire body from head to toe as far as can be observed by the priest,
[Leviticus] [13]:[13] then after the priest’s confirmation that it covers the entire body, that person can be pronounced as ‘clean’ again as all of it has turned white.
[Leviticus] [13]:[14] However, if any raw flesh shows itself, then they’ll become ‘unclean’ that same day.
[Leviticus] [13]:[15] The priest must examine that raw flesh and must pronounce that person as ‘unclean’ due to their skin disease.
[Leviticus] [13]:[16] Afterwards, if it heals over and goes white, then they can return to the priest
[Leviticus] [13]:[17] to be reexamined, and if the infection has indeed gone white, then the priest can pronounce it as not being infectious and the person as ‘clean’ again.
[Leviticus] [13]:[18] When someone has a boil on their skin, but it heals
[Leviticus] [13]:[19] leaving behind a white swelling or a reddish-white bright spot, then that person must show themself to the priest.
[Leviticus] [13]:[20] The priest will examine it, and if it is indeed more than just skin deep and its hair has turned white, then the priest must pronounce that person as ‘unclean’ because an infectious skin disease has broken out from the original boil.
[Leviticus] [13]:[21] However, if the priest’s examination finds not white hair on it, and it’s not more than skin deep, and it’s fading, then he will order that person quarantined for seven days,
[Leviticus] [13]:[22] and if it spreads further on their skin, then the priest must declare that person as ‘unclean’ because it’s infectious.
[Leviticus] [13]:[23] But if the bright spot hasn’t spread during the quarantine, then it’s just the scar from the boil and the priest can pronounce the person as ‘clean’.
[Leviticus] [13]:[24] If someone gets a burn on their skin, and the burn area becomes reddish-white or a white spot,
[Leviticus] [13]:[25] then the priest must examine it, and if the hair on the spot has turned white and the infection looks more than skin deep, then a skin disease has broken out in the burn, and the priest must pronounce that person as ‘unclean’ because it’s infectious.
[Leviticus] [13]:[26] However, if the priest sees that there’s no white hair in the spot, and it’s not more than skin deep, and it’s fading, then he will order that person quarantined for seven days.
[Leviticus] [13]:[27] On the seventh day, the priest will re-examine the person, and if it’s spread further, he must pronounce that person as ‘unclean’ because it’s an infectious skin disease.
[Leviticus] [13]:[28] But if the bright spot hasn’t spread on the skin, and it faded more, then it was just swelling from the burn. Then the priest will pronounce that person to be ‘clean’ because it was just the scar caused by their burn.
[Leviticus] [13]:[29] If a man or woman has an infection in their scalp or under their beard,
[Leviticus] [13]:[30] then the priest should inspect the infection. If it appears to be more than skin deep, and there’s any thin yellow hairs in it, then the priest must pronounce that person as ‘unclean’ because it’s an itchy and infectious skin infection on the scalp or face.
[Leviticus] [13]:[31] However, if the priest notices an itchy infection yet it’s only skin deep and there’s no black hair on it, then he should quarantine that person for seven days.
[Leviticus] [13]:[32] On the seventh day, the priest will re-examine that person and if the spot hasn’t widened and still only appears to be skin deep,
[Leviticus] [13]:[33] then that person should shave their head, and then the priest should quarantine them for a further seven days.
[Leviticus] [13]:[34] Then again on the seventh day, the priest will inspect it, and if the spot hasn’t widened after being shaved and it doesn’t seem to be more than skin deep, then the priest can pronounce that person as ‘clean’ once they’ve washed their clothes.
[Leviticus] [13]:[35] However, if it did spread on their skin after that,
[Leviticus] [13]:[36] then the priest must inspect it again, and if it’s spread then that person is ‘unclean’ (whether or not there’s any yellow hair).
[Leviticus] [13]:[37] But if it seems that the spot hasn’t spread and dark hair is growing in it again, then that person’s not infectious and the priest can pronounce them as ‘clean’.
[Leviticus] [13]:[38] If a man or woman finds very white spots on their skin,
[Leviticus] [13]:[39] then the priest must examine them. If the spots on their skin are dull white, then it’s a skin rash that’s broken out and they are ‘clean’.
[Leviticus] [13]:[40] If a man’s head has become bare, then he’s gone bald and is still ‘clean’.
[Leviticus] [13]:[41] Similarly, if the hair is receding from the front corners, he’s going bald and is still ‘clean’.
[Leviticus] [13]:[42] However, if there’s a balding spot with a reddish-white infection, it’s a skin disease breaking out via that spot
[Leviticus] [13]:[43] and the priest must examine him. If it’s a balding spot with a reddish-white infection that looks like a contagious skin disease,
[Leviticus] [13]:[44] then he’s contagious and ‘unclean’. The priest must pronounce his as ‘unclean’ because of that infection on his head.
[Leviticus] [13]:[45] Anyone who’s developed an infectious skin disease must tear their clothes and leave their hair loose, and must cover their mouth and call out, ‘Unclean, unclean.’
[Leviticus] [13]:[46] They will remain ‘unclean’ as long as they still have that infection, and must live alone outside the camp.
[Leviticus] [13]:[47] When a piece of clothing has a mould growing on it, whether it’s made of wool or linen,
[Leviticus] [13]:[48] or whether it’s something woven from wool or linen, or something made from leather,
[Leviticus] [13]:[49] if the growth is greenish or reddish in colour, then it’s something that can spread and it must be shown to the priest.
[Leviticus] [13]:[50] The priest must examine the growth, and quarantine the article for seven days.
[Leviticus] [13]:[51] On the seventh day, if the growth has spread on that piece of material or leather equipment, and it’s confirmed as spreadable and is ‘unclean’.
[Leviticus] [13]:[52] The owner must burn the piece of clothing or equipment that contains the infection because it’s contagious, so it must be completely burnt up.
[Leviticus] [13]:[53] However if the priest notices that the growth hasn’t spread on the clothing or on the woven or leather material,
[Leviticus] [13]:[54] then the priest must order that the material be washed and then quarantined for a further seven days.
[Leviticus] [13]:[55] On the seventh day, the priest must inspect that washed material, and if the growth hasn’t changed its appearance, even if it hasn’t spread, then it’s ‘unclean’ and must be burnt in the fire—it’s a mildew that’s on the front or back of the material.
[Leviticus] [13]:[56] However, if the priest notices that the growth has faded after being washed, then it can be torn out of the clothing or piece of leather or woven material.
[Leviticus] [13]:[57] If it then reappears on that clothing or material, then it’s breaking out, so then that article must be burnt in the fire.
[Leviticus] [13]:[58] On the other hand, if the growth vanished after being washed, then it must be washed a second time and then it will be ‘clean’.
[Leviticus] [13]:[59] The above are the regulations concerning any growth on a piece of woollen or linen clothing or fabric, or any leather article, to pronounce it ‘clean’ or ‘unclean’.
[Leviticus] [14]:[1] Then Yahweh told Mosheh (Moses):
[Leviticus] [14]:[2] These are the regulations for the purification of a person who had a skin disease. They must be taken to a priest
[Leviticus] [14]:[3] who’ll go outside the camp to meet them. The priest must inspect that person, and if the skin disease has indeed left them,
[Leviticus] [14]:[4] then the priest will order them to bring him two live, ‘clean’ birds, some cedar wood, some scarlet thread, and some hyssop twigs.
[Leviticus] [14]:[5] The priest must tell the person to slaughter one bird so the blood runs into a clay jug containing water from a spring or creek.
[Leviticus] [14]:[6] Then the priest will take the live bird, along with the cedar wood, the scarlet thread, and the hyssop twigs, and dip them all into that blood of the slaughtered bird (mixed with the fresh water),
[Leviticus] [14]:[7] and flick it seven times onto the person who’s being purified from the skin disease. Then the priest can pronounce them as ‘clean’ enough to re-enter the community, and release the live bird to fly into the countryside.
[Leviticus] [14]:[8] The person who’s being purified must then wash their clothes, shave all their hair, and then bathe in flowing water. After that, they can re-enter the camp but must live outside their tent for seven more days.
[Leviticus] [14]:[9] On the seventh day, that person must shave off all their hair (including eyebrows and beard if appropriate), wash their clothes and bathe themself in flowing water, then they’ll be ‘clean’.
[Leviticus] [14]:[10] Then on the eighth day, that person must get two one-year-old male lambs, and one female lamb, all with no defects, along with three kilograms of fine flour mixed with oil as a grain offering, as well as half a litre of olive oil.
[Leviticus] [14]:[11] That must be taken to the priest who’d pronounced them as ‘clean’ will accompany them and all those offerings to stand in front of Yahweh at the entrance to the sacred tent.
[Leviticus] [14]:[12] Then the priest must take one of the male lambs and the container of oil and present it as a guilt offering, then he’ll raise them as a wave offering in front of Yahweh.
[Leviticus] [14]:[13] Then that person must slaughter that lamb in the sacred place where sin offerings and burnt offerings are slaughtered, because this guilt offering is like a sin offering in that it’s for the priest—it’s very sacred.
[Leviticus] [14]:[14] Then the priest must take some of the blood from that guilt offering, and put it on the lobe of the right ear of the person being purified, and on their right thumb and right big toe.
[Leviticus] [14]:[15] Then the priest must take the container of olive oil and pour some into his left hand.
[Leviticus] [14]:[16] Then he’ll dip his right finger into that oil on his left palm, and with that same finger, flick it seven times towards Yahweh.
[Leviticus] [14]:[17] Then the priest must put some of the remaining oil on his palm onto the lobe of the right ear of the person being purified, and on their right thumb and right big toe—on top of the blood from the guilt offering.
[Leviticus] [14]:[18] Then the priest will put all the remaining oil from his palm onto the head of the person being purified, and the priest will then make that person right with Yahweh.
[Leviticus] [14]:[19] Then the priest must make the sin offering and make that person right after being purified from their ‘uncleanness’. After that that person will slaughter lamb for the burnt offering.
[Leviticus] [14]:[20] Then the priest must offer that burnt offering and the grain offering on the fire on the altar and he will make that person right again and he will be ‘clean’.
[Leviticus] [14]:[21] However, if that person is poor and cannot afford the multiple lambs, then they must take one lamb to wave as the guilt offering and to make them right again, along with one kilogram of fine flour mixed with oil for the grain offering, and the half litre of oil,
[Leviticus] [14]:[22] plus two doves or young pigeons—whichever they can afford—one for a sin offering and the other for the burnt offering.
[Leviticus] [14]:[23] Then on that eighth day, he’ll take them to the priest at the entrance of the sacred tent for purification in front of Yahweh.
[Leviticus] [14]:[24] Then the priest should take the guilt offering lamb and the container of oil and lift them up as a wave offering in front of Yahweh.
[Leviticus] [14]:[25] Then the person should slaughter that guilt offering lamb, and the priest must take some of that blood and put it on the lobe of the right ear of the person being purified, and on their right thumb and right big toe.
[Leviticus] [14]:[26] Then he must pour some of the oil onto his left palm
[Leviticus] [14]:[27] and with his right finger he must flick it seven times towards Yahweh.
[Leviticus] [14]:[28] Then the priest must put some of the oil from his palm onto the lobe of the right ear of the person being purified, and on their right thumb and right big toe—on top of the blood from the guilt offering.
[Leviticus] [14]:[29] Then the priest will put all the remaining oil from his palm onto the head of the person being purified, and the priest will then make that person right with Yahweh.
[Leviticus] [14]:[30] Then he must offer one of the birds (dove or pigeon—whatever that person could afford)
[Leviticus] [14]:[31] as a sin offering and the other as a burnt offering along with the grain offering and he will make that person right again with Yahweh.
[Leviticus] [14]:[32] The above are the regulations for anyone who has a skin disease but who couldn’t afford the regular purification offerings.
[Leviticus] [14]:[33] Then Yahweh told Mosheh (Moses) and Aharon (Aaron):
[Leviticus] [14]:[34] “When you enter into the land of Kena’an (Canaan) which I’m giving you all as a possession, and if I cause an infection in one of your homes in that land,
[Leviticus] [14]:[35] then the homeowner must go and inform the priest that something like an infection has appeared in their house.
[Leviticus] [14]:[36] The priest must order that everything be removed out of the house before he comes to inspect it so that it won’t all be pronounced as ‘unclean’. After that’s done, he’ll go to see the house
[Leviticus] [14]:[37] and examine the growth. If the growth is greenish or reddish and seems more than surface deep,
[Leviticus] [14]:[38] then the priest must leave the house via the main entrance and quarantine the house for seven days.
[Leviticus] [14]:[39] On the seventh day, the priest must return and examine it again, and if the growth has spread on the house walls,
[Leviticus] [14]:[40] then he must order that those infected stones be pulled out of the wall and thrown outside the city into a place that’s considered ‘unclean’.
[Leviticus] [14]:[41] Then the homeowner must scrape all the plaster off the inside walls and also dispose of that at that ‘unclean’ place.
[Leviticus] [14]:[42] Then they can replace the stones that were removed, and apply fresh plaster to the house.
[Leviticus] [14]:[43] However, if the growth returns and breaks out again in the house even after the stones were replaced and the walls were replastered,
[Leviticus] [14]:[44] then the priest must come back and reexamine it. If the growth has spread on the walls, then it’s a malignant growth and the house is ‘unclean’.
[Leviticus] [14]:[45] The owner must tear the house down—its stones and timber and all the mortar, must be carted outside the city into a place that’s considered ‘unclean’.
[Leviticus] [14]:[46] Any person that enters that house after the priest had quarantined it, will be ‘unclean’ until that evening.
[Leviticus] [14]:[47] Any person who lies down or eats in that house, must wash their clothes.
[Leviticus] [14]:[48] However, if the priest came back after the house was replastered and after his inspection, find that the growth hasn’t reappeared, then he can pronounce the house as ‘clean’ because the growth has gone.
[Leviticus] [14]:[49] Then he must take two birds, cedar wood, scarlet thread, and some hyssop twigs,
[Leviticus] [14]:[50] and slaughter one bird so the blood runs into a clay jug containing water from a spring or creek.
[Leviticus] [14]:[51] Then the priest must take the live bird, along with the cedar wood, the scarlet thread, the hyssop twigs and the live bird, and dip them all into that blood of the slaughtered bird (mixed with the fresh water), and flick it seven times onto the house.
[Leviticus] [14]:[52] In that way, he’ll purify the house with the bird’s blood and the fresh water, and with the live bird and the cedar wood, the hyssop twigs and the scarlet thread.
[Leviticus] [14]:[53] Then he must release the live bird to fly into the countryside, thus making the house right with God, and then it’ll be ‘clean’.
[Leviticus] [14]:[54] The above are the regulations concerning any serious skin diseases and itchiness,
[Leviticus] [14]:[55] as well as growths on clothing and buildings
[Leviticus] [14]:[56] and swellings, rashes, and bright spots on the skin,
[Leviticus] [14]:[57] so that you’ll know how to determine what’s ‘unclean’ or ‘clean’. Those are the regulations for infectious growths.
[Leviticus] [15]:[1] Then Yahweh told Mosheh (Moses) and Aharon (Aaron):
[Leviticus] [15]:[2] Tell the Israelis that whenever any man has a discharge from his genitals, then he becomes ‘unclean’.
[Leviticus] [15]:[3] He becomes ‘unclean’ whether his body secretes the flow or if it’s blocked—either way he’s ‘unclean’.
[Leviticus] [15]:[4] Any bed that he was lying on during or after the discharge becomes ‘unclean’, as does anything he sits on.
[Leviticus] [15]:[5] Anyone who touches that bed must wash their clothes and bathe themself in water, and that person will be ‘unclean’ until the evening.
[Leviticus] [15]:[6] Similarly, anyone who sits on the place where he sat must wash their clothes and bathe themself in water, and that person will be ‘unclean’ until the evening.
[Leviticus] [15]:[7] Anyone who touches the man who had a discharge must wash their clothes and bathe themself in water, and that person will be ‘unclean’ until the evening.
[Leviticus] [15]:[8] If that man who had a discharge spits on some person who was ‘clean’, then that person must wash their clothes and bathe themself in water, and they’ll be ‘unclean’ until the evening.
[Leviticus] [15]:[9] Any thing that the man who had a discharge rides on, will become ‘unclean’,
[Leviticus] [15]:[10] and anyone who touches it will be ‘unclean’ until the evening, plus anyone who carries any of those things, must wash their clothes and bathe themself in water, and they’ll be ‘unclean’ until the evening.
[Leviticus] [15]:[11] Anyone the man who had a discharge touches and do didn’t rinse their hands in water, must wash their clothes and bathe themself in water, and they’ll be ‘unclean’ until the evening.
[Leviticus] [15]:[12] Any container that the man who had a discharge touches, must be smashed if it’s made from clay and rinsed with water if it’s made from wood.
[Leviticus] [15]:[13] When the man’s discharge ceases, he must mark off seven days for his purification, and then he must wash his clothes and bathe himself in water, and after that, he’ll be ‘clean’.
[Leviticus] [15]:[14] Then on the eighth day, he must take two doves or young pigeons, and stand in front of Yahweh at the entrance to the sacred tent. There he should give them to a priest,
[Leviticus] [15]:[15] and the priest must offer one as a sin offering and the other as a burnt offering, thus making the man right with Yahweh for his discharge.
[Leviticus] [15]:[16] Now when a man has an emission of semen, then he must bathe his entire body in water, and he’ll be ‘unclean’ until the evening.
[Leviticus] [15]:[17] He must also wash all his clothing, and any leather articles on him that came into contact with the semen and all of that will be ‘unclean’ until the evening.
[Leviticus] [15]:[18] When a man and a woman ‘sleep together’, then they must both bathe in water, and they’ll both be ‘unclean’ until the evening.
[Leviticus] [15]:[19] When a woman has her menstrual period, she’ll be ‘unclean’ for seven days, and anyone who touches her during that time will be ‘unclean’ until the evening.
[Leviticus] [15]:[20] Anything that she lies on or sits on during that time will become ‘unclean’.
[Leviticus] [15]:[21] Anyone who touches her bed must wash their clothes and bathe in water, and they’ll be ‘unclean’ until the evening.
[Leviticus] [15]:[22] Anyone who touches anything that she sat on must wash their clothes and bathe in water, and they’ll be ‘unclean’ until the evening,
[Leviticus] [15]:[23] i.e., whether it’s her bed or something she sat on, anyone who touches it will be ‘unclean’ until the evening.
[Leviticus] [15]:[24] If a man sleeps with a menstruating woman and gets blood on him, then he’ll be ‘unclean’ for seven days, and any bed that he lies on will also become ‘unclean’.
[Leviticus] [15]:[25] If any woman has a blood flow when it’s not her period, or keeps bleeding beyond her menstrual period, all those days will be regarded the same as her menstruation so she’ll be ‘unclean’.
[Leviticus] [15]:[26] Any bed that she lies on as long as she’s discharging blood will be regarded the same as during her menstruation and will be ‘unclean’, as will anything she sits on.
[Leviticus] [15]:[27] Also, any person who touches them will be ‘unclean’ and they must wash their clothes and bathe in water, and they’ll be ‘unclean’ until the evening.
[Leviticus] [15]:[28] Once the flow stops, then the woman must count off seven days, and then she’ll be ‘clean’ after that.
[Leviticus] [15]:[29] Then on the eighth day, she must take two doves or young pigeons and give them to a priest at the entrance to the sacred tent,
[Leviticus] [15]:[30] and he will offer one as a sin offering and the other as a burnt offering, thus making her right with Yahweh from her ‘unclean’ flow.
[Leviticus] [15]:[31] You two must keep the Israeli people separate from their ‘uncleanness’, then they won’t defile my residence that’s among them, and cause their own death.
[Leviticus] [15]:[32] The above are the regulations for any man with a discharge or a seminal emission that makes him ‘unclean’,
[Leviticus] [15]:[33] plus any woman who is menstruating or has a bodily discharge, as well as any man who sleeps with an ‘unclean’ woman.
[Leviticus] [16]:[1] Yahweh spoke to Mosheh (Moses) after the death of two of Aharon’s (Aaron) sons when they approached Yahweh wrongly and died,
[Leviticus] [16]:[2] and he told Mosheh: Tell your brother Aharon that if he doesn’t want to die, then he mustn’t just enter the holiest room inside the curtain at any old time. The atonement lid is on the sacred box, and I will appear in a cloud over that lid.
[Leviticus] [16]:[3] This is how Aharon must enter the sacred tent: he must acquire a young bull for a sin offering, and a ram for a burnt offering.
[Leviticus] [16]:[4] He must bathe himself in water and then put on linen underclothes, followed by his sacred linen tunic and tie the linen sash around it. Then he must wrap the linen turban on. Those are all sacred clothes.
[Leviticus] [16]:[5] Then Aharon must acquire two young goats for a sin offering and one ram for a burnt offering.
[Leviticus] [16]:[6] He must present the bull as a sin offering for himself to make both him and his household right with God.
[Leviticus] [16]:[7] Then he must take the two goats and make them stand in front of Yahweh at the entrance to the sacred tent,
[Leviticus] [16]:[8] and throw dice to decide which one is for Yahweh, and one is to be the ‘scapegoat’.
[Leviticus] [16]:[9] Then Aharon must present the goat that’s for Yahweh, and offer it as a sin offering,
[Leviticus] [16]:[10] but the chosen ‘scapegoat’ must be kept standing there in front of Yahweh, because it’ll be used to make the people right with Yahweh, and be sent into the wilderness.
[Leviticus] [16]:[11] Then Aharon must present the bull for his own sin offering to make him and his household right with God, then he’ll slaughter the bull for the sin offering for himself.
[Leviticus] [16]:[12] Then he must get a panful of burning coals off the altar in front of Yahweh as well as two handfuls of finely-ground, fragrant incense, and take them inside the curtain
[Leviticus] [16]:[13] where he’ll put the incense on the coals in Yahweh’s presence. Then the smoke cloud from the incense will cover the atonement lid on the sacred chest, and he won’t die.
[Leviticus] [16]:[14] Then he must take some of the bull’s blood, and using his finger, he must flick the blood seven times onto the eastern the side of the lid and seven times onto the front of the lid.
[Leviticus] [16]:[15] Then Aharon must slaughter the goat for the people’s sin offering, and take its blood inside the curtain, and do the same with it that he did to the bull’s blood—flicking it onto the side and front of the atonement lid,
[Leviticus] [16]:[16] thus making the Israeli people right with Yahweh for their uncleanness and their rebellion and disobedience. That’s also for the sacred tent which is among the people with their uncleanness.
[Leviticus] [16]:[17] No one else can enter the sacred tent when Aharon enters to make atonement in the sacred room until he leaves again. He must make atonement for himself and his household, as well as for the whole Israeli community,
[Leviticus] [16]:[18] then he’ll go out to the altar that’s in front of Yahweh and make atonement for that—he must take some of the bull’s blood and some of the goat’s blood and put it on the four projecting corners of the altar.
[Leviticus] [16]:[19] Then he must flick blood on to it seven times with his finger, thus purifying it and removing the uncleanness of the Israeli people from it.
[Leviticus] [16]:[20] When Aharon (Aaron) has finished purifying the sacred room, the sacred tent, and the altar, then he should present the live goat.
[Leviticus] [16]:[21] He must place both his hands on the goat’s head, and confess all of Yisrael’s (Israel) disobedience, rebellion, and shortcomings—symbolically placing them onto the goat’s head, and then he must choose a man that’s nearby to take it into the wilderness.
[Leviticus] [16]:[22] Then he’ll release the goat there in the wilderness, and the goat will carry all their sins into that barren land.
[Leviticus] [16]:[23] Then Aharon must enter the sacred tent and take off the linen garment that he’d put on as he’d entered into the sacred room and leave them there.
[Leviticus] [16]:[24] Then he must wash himself in water in a sacred place, put on his regular clothes, and go out and make his burnt offering and the burnt offering for the people, thus making both himself and the people right with Yahweh.
[Leviticus] [16]:[25] Then he must burn the fat from the sin offering up on the altar.
[Leviticus] [16]:[26] Also, the person who led away the ‘scapegoat’ must wash his clothes and bathe himself in water, and then he can reenter the camp.
[Leviticus] [16]:[27] Then the remains of the bull and the goat from the sin offerings (whose blood was taken into the sacred room to make atonement) must be taken to a place outside the camp where they must be burnt—skins, flesh, and dung.
[Leviticus] [16]:[28] The man who burnt them must then wash his clothes and bathe his body in water, and then he can reenter the camp.
[Leviticus] [16]:[29] This will be a permanent regulation for you all: On the 10th of the seventh month (of Tishrei—around September/October), all of you including those who are native-born as well as foreigners living among you, must humble yourselves and not work that day
[Leviticus] [16]:[30] because on that day, the high priest will purify you all from your sins to make you right with Yahweh, and you’ll be ‘clean’.
[Leviticus] [16]:[31] It’ll be a very sacred rest day for you, and you all must humble yourselves—a permanent regulation for you all.
[Leviticus] [16]:[32] The priest who’s anointed and ordained to succeed his father as high priest must be the one to make atonement, and he must be wearing his sacred linen clothes.
[Leviticus] [16]:[33] He will first purify the sacred room and the sacred tent, and the altar, and then make all the priests right with Yahweh and finally, the entire community.
[Leviticus] [16]:[34] That will become a permanent regulation every year to make all the Israelis right with Yahweh because of their sins. So Mosheh (Moses) did exactly as Yahweh had instructed him.
[Leviticus] [17]:[1] Then Yahweh told Mosheh (Moses):
[Leviticus] [17]:[2] Tell Aharon (Aaron) and his sons and all the Israelis that these are the instructions from Yahweh:
[Leviticus] [17]:[3] No Israeli is allowed to slaughter a bull or lamb or goat either inside the camp or outside it.
[Leviticus] [17]:[4] If they’re not taken to the entrance to the sacred tent to be presented as an offering to Yahweh in front of his residence, then that person will be held guilty of its blood—they’ve shed blood so they must be cut off from his people.
[Leviticus] [17]:[5] The Israelis must stop sacrificing their animals in the countryside, and instead bring them to Yahweh at the entrance to the sacred tent, i.e., they must bring them to the priest and sacrifice them as peace offerings to Yahweh.
[Leviticus] [17]:[6] Then the priest will splash the blood onto Yahweh’s altar at the tent entrance, and burn up the fat to become a soothing aroma for Yahweh.
[Leviticus] [17]:[7] Then they won’t be able to continue offering their sacrifices to the goat demons that they’re prostituting themselves to. The above will be a permanent regulation throughout the generations.
[Leviticus] [17]:[8] You must tell them that if an Israeli or a foreigner living among them, makes a burnt offering or sacrifice
[Leviticus] [17]:[9] without bringing it to Yahweh at the sacred tent entrance, then that person must be cut off from the community.
[Leviticus] [17]:[10] If there’s any Israeli or foreigner living among them, who eats blood, then I’ll oppose that person and remove them from the community
[Leviticus] [17]:[11] because the body’s life is in the blood. I myself have given you blood to make atonement for your lives at the altar, because it’s the blood that can atone for life.
[Leviticus] [17]:[12] That’s why I told the Israelis that none of them must eat blood—not even the foreigners that live among them may eat blood.
[Leviticus] [17]:[13] So any person (Israeli or foreigner living among them) who catches wild game (including birds) to eat, they must pour its blood out and cover it with soil
[Leviticus] [17]:[14] because the life of their bodies is the blood that’s in them. Again, that’s why I’ve told the Israelis not to eat the blood of any living thing because the life is in the blood, and anyone who eats it must be cut off from the community.
[Leviticus] [17]:[15] Anyone who eats part of a carcass they found or one that was killed by wild animals, must wash their clothes and bathe in water, and they’ll be ‘unclean’ until the evening, and then they’ll be ‘clean’ again.
[Leviticus] [17]:[16] However, if that person doesn’t wash their clothes or bathe, then they must bear the punishment for their own disobedience.
[Leviticus] [18]:[1] Then Yahweh told Mosheh (Moses):
[Leviticus] [18]:[2] Tell the Israeli that I am their god Yahweh.
[Leviticus] [18]:[3] They mustn’t behave as if they’re still there in Mitsrayim (Egypt), nor should they behave like the Kena’anim (Canaanites) that were living in the land that I’m taking you all into, and don’t emulate their customs and practices.
[Leviticus] [18]:[4] You all must imbibe my values and follow my instructions. I am your god Yahweh.
[Leviticus] [18]:[5] You all must follow my instructions and my values—those who do so will live. I am your god Yahweh.
[Leviticus] [18]:[6] None of you may ever flirt with any close relative to try to get them to undress. I am Yahweh.
[Leviticus] [18]:[7] You must never mess with your father’s naked body, or your mother’s—no, she’s your mother so don’t ever take advantage of her nakedness.
[Leviticus] [18]:[8] Don’t ever mess with any of your father’s wives, because their naked bodies are the realm of your father.
[Leviticus] [18]:[9] Don’t flirt with your sister’s nakedness, whether she’s a full sister, a half sister, or an adopted sister.
[Leviticus] [18]:[10] Don’t flirt with your grandchildren’s nakedness, because you’d be absolutely shaming yourself.
[Leviticus] [18]:[11] Don’t flirt with your step-sister’s nakedness, because she’s your sister and her nakedness isn’t yours to enjoy.
[Leviticus] [18]:[12] Don’t flirt with your aunts nakedness on your father’s side, because she’s closely related to your father.
[Leviticus] [18]:[13] Don’t flirt with your aunt’s nakedness on your mother’s side, because she’s closely related to your mother.
[Leviticus] [18]:[14] Don’t flirt with your uncle’s nakedness on your father’s side, and keep away from his wife, because she’s your aunt.
[Leviticus] [18]:[15] Don’t flirt with your daughter-in-law’s nakedness, because she’s your son’s wife and her nakedness isn’t yours to enjoy.
[Leviticus] [18]:[16] Don’t flirt with your sister-in-law, because her naked body is the realm of your brother.
[Leviticus] [18]:[17] Don’t flirt with the nakedness of both a woman and her daughter or her granddaughter, because they’re related to each other—that would be perverse.
[Leviticus] [18]:[18] Don’t take your wife’s sister to be a junior wife while your wife is still alive.
[Leviticus] [18]:[19] Don’t approach a woman who’s menstruating, to undress her, because she’s ‘unclean’.
[Leviticus] [18]:[20] Don’t sleep with someone else’s wife—your child with her would be ‘unclean’.
[Leviticus] [18]:[21] Don’t sacrifice your children to Molek so you don’t profane your god’s reputation. I am Yahweh.
[Leviticus] [18]:[22] Don’t have sexual relations with a man like with a woman—it’s an abomination.
[Leviticus] [18]:[23] Men, don’t have sexual relations with any animal as that would make you ‘unclean’. And women, don’t give yourself sexually to any animal as that’s perverse.
[Leviticus] [18]:[24] Don’t make yourselves ‘unclean’ in any of the above ways, because all of those things were done by the people groups that I’m driving out of this land ahead of you all.
[Leviticus] [18]:[25] The land had become ‘unclean’ so I made them pay for their wickedness and so the land will vomit out its inhabitants.
[Leviticus] [18]:[26] However, you all must obey my instructions and decisions and not tolerate any of that perverse behaviour—not you who are native-born, nor any foreigner living among you all,
[Leviticus] [18]:[27] because all that perversity was done by those living there before you all, and the land became ‘unclean’.
[Leviticus] [18]:[28] Don’t think that the land won’t vomit you all out just like it’s doing to the people groups that have been there before you,
[Leviticus] [18]:[29] because everyone who does any of those perversities will be cut off from their community.
[Leviticus] [18]:[30] So you all must carefully guard against practising any of those detestable customs which were previously done there and which would make you all ‘unclean’. I am your god Yahweh.
[Leviticus] [19]:[1] Then Yahweh told Mosheh (Moses):
[Leviticus] [19]:[2] Tell the entire Israeli community that they must be separate from others, because I, your god Yahweh, am holy (i.e., separated from impurity).
[Leviticus] [19]:[3] Everyone must respect and obey their parents, and observe my rest days. I am your god Yahweh.
[Leviticus] [19]:[4] Don’t turn to worthless idols, and don’t make cast metal gods for yourselves. I am your god Yahweh.
[Leviticus] [19]:[5] When you all sacrifice peace offerings, do it correctly so that you’ll all be accepted.
[Leviticus] [19]:[6] The meat from your sacrifice must be eaten that same day or the next day—anything left until the third day must be thrown into the fire.
[Leviticus] [19]:[7] If it was to be eaten on the third day, it would be ‘unclean’ and not acceptable,
[Leviticus] [19]:[8] and the people eating it would have to bear their own guilt for profaning Yahweh’s holiness, and that person must be cut off from the community.
[Leviticus] [19]:[9] When you all harvest your crops off your land, you mustn’t cut the grain right to the very edge of your field, and nor can you all pick up any dropped stalks.
[Leviticus] [19]:[10] In your vineyards, you must not pick every last grape or pick up any that fall on the ground, because they must be left for the poor and for the foreigners. I am your god Yahweh.
[Leviticus] [19]:[11] You all mustn’t steal or deceive, or defraud any fellow citizen,
[Leviticus] [19]:[12] and don’t use my name to seal a promise and then go ahead and ruin my reputation. I am Yahweh.
[Leviticus] [19]:[13] Don’t oppress your neighbours or steal from them. Don’t fail to pay a day-labourer as they finish each day’s work.
[Leviticus] [19]:[14] Don’t curse a deaf person, or put something in front of a blind person to trip them. You must respect and obey your god. I am Yahweh.
[Leviticus] [19]:[15] Don’t judge unfairly—showing partiality to the poor, or honouring those who are well-known—you must always judge your fellow citizens fairly.
[Leviticus] [19]:[16] Don’t go around slandering people. Don’t take advantage of your neighbour’s death. I am Yahweh.
[Leviticus] [19]:[17] You mustn’t hate your brother. Certainly rebuke those you interact with so you don’t get blamed for their bad behaviour.
[Leviticus] [19]:[18] Don’t try to get revenge against others or hold a grudge against any of your people, but instead, love your neighbour as yourself. I am Yahweh.
[Leviticus] [19]:[19] Follow my instructions—don’t crossbreed two different kinds of animals, don’t sow two different crops in your field, and don’t wear clothing made of different kinds of thread.
[Leviticus] [19]:[20] If a man impregnates a woman who’s destined to be someone else’s slave and she hasn’t been freed, compensation needs to be paid. They mustn’t be executed, because she hadn’t been freed.
[Leviticus] [19]:[21] However, that man must take a ram to Yahweh at the sacred tent’s entrance for a guilt offering,
[Leviticus] [19]:[22] and the priest will make him right with Yahweh by means of that guilt offering ram, and then he’ll be forgiven for his transgression.
[Leviticus] [19]:[23] When you all enter into the land and plant various kinds of fruit trees, you mustn’t eat the fruit for the first three years—it should be regarded as ‘uncircumcised’ for that duration.
[Leviticus] [19]:[24] Then in the fourth year, all that fruit must be regarded as ‘sacred’—praise offerings for Yahweh.
[Leviticus] [19]:[25] Finally, in the fifth year, you can eat that fruit and add that produce to your harvest. I am your god Yahweh.
[Leviticus] [19]:[26] Don’t eat anything with the blood still in it. Don’t practice divination or witchcraft.
[Leviticus] [19]:[27] Don’t have haircuts that round off your hair at the sides, and men, don’t trim the edges of your beards.
[Leviticus] [19]:[28] Don’t make cuts on your bodies when someone dies, and don’t tattoo yourselves. I am Yahweh.
[Leviticus] [19]:[29] don’t defile your daughter by making her prostitute herself, so the country doesn’t prostitute itself and become full of wickedness.
[Leviticus] [19]:[30] Keep my rest days, and respect my sanctuary. I am Yahweh.
[Leviticus] [19]:[31] Don’t turn to mediums and diviners—don’t make yourselves ‘unclean’ by means of them. I am your god Yahweh.
[Leviticus] [19]:[32] Stand up for those with grey hair, and honour the presence of the elderly. Honour and respect your god. I am Yahweh.
[Leviticus] [19]:[33] Don’t take advantage of foreigners when they stay in your land—
[Leviticus] [19]:[34] you all must treat foreigners the same as native-born Israelis and love them like you love yourselves, because you were all foreigners in Mitsrayim (Egypt). I am your god Yahweh.
[Leviticus] [19]:[35] Don’t allow injustice either in judging cases, or by trading with rigged weights and measures—
[Leviticus] [19]:[36] your scales and weights and measuring containers must be honest. I am your god Yahweh who brought you all out of Mitsrayim.
[Leviticus] [19]:[37] You all must obey my instructions and decisions and stick to them. I am Yahweh.
