[Leviticus] [21]:[2] apart from the body of a close relative like a parent, child, brother
[Leviticus] [21]:[3] or unmarried sister—the priest can become ‘unclean’ by means of one of them.
[Leviticus] [21]:[4] He must not make himself ‘unclean’ if it’s the death of a relative only by marriage.
[Leviticus] [21]:[5] They must not shave their heads or trim the edges of their beards or cut their bodies in grief.
[Leviticus] [21]:[6] The priests must stay separate for their God and they must not tarnish his reputation because they present the gifts to Yahweh—their god’s food
[Leviticus] [21]:[7] They mustn’t marry a woman who was a prostitute or who has defiled herself some other way or who is divorced from her husband, because they’re separated for their god.
[Leviticus] [21]:[8] You must treat him as set apart because he’s the one presenting your god’s food. He must be ‘holy’ for you, because I, Yahweh, am holy and I set you all apart as ‘holy’.
[Leviticus] [21]:[9] If a priest’s daughter prostituted herself, she would be profaning her father so must be burnt to death.
[Leviticus] [21]:[10] The priest who is chief of all his brothers and who had the anointing oil poured over his head, and who has the responsibility of wearing the special clothing, must not wear his hair loose, and he must not tear his clothes in grief.
[Leviticus] [21]:[11] He mustn’t approach any dead body—not even his own parents—he mustn’t make himself ‘unclean’.
[Leviticus] [21]:[12] Even for a death, he mustn’t leave his duties in the sanctuary, and he mustn’t profane the sanctuary of his god, because he’s been consecrated with the anointing oil. I am Yahweh.
[Leviticus] [21]:[13] He can only marry a virgin—
[Leviticus] [21]:[14] he mustn’t take a widow or a divorced woman, or a defiled prostitute. He can only marry an unmarried, Israeli girl,
[Leviticus] [21]:[15] then he won’t profane his offspring among his relatives, because I am Yahweh who sets him apart as ‘holy’.
[Leviticus] [21]:[16] Then Yahweh told Mosheh (Moses),
[Leviticus] [21]:[17] Tell Aharon (Aaron) that none of his descendants who have a deformity should ever approach to present the food for his god.
[Leviticus] [21]:[18] Yes, no man who has a deformity must approach to offer a sacrifice, i.e., no one who’s blind, lame, mutilated, or with a swelling,
[Leviticus] [21]:[19] or with a broken foot or hand,
[Leviticus] [21]:[20] or a hunchback or dwarf, or with an eye defect, with a scab or rash, or anyone with a crushed testicle.
[Leviticus] [21]:[21] Any descendant of Aharon the priest with a blemish mustn’t approach to preset a gift to Yahweh—no that person mustn’t approach to present god’s food.
[Leviticus] [21]:[22] However, they can eat those gifts for God, including the sacred and very sacred portions.
[Leviticus] [21]:[23] Despite that, they mustn’t enter past the curtain or approach the altar if they have a defect on their body. They mustn’t profane my sanctuary because I am Yahweh who sets them apart as ‘holy’.
[Leviticus] [21]:[24] So Mosheh (Moses) told all that to Aharon and his sons, and all the Israelis.
[Leviticus] [22]:[1] Then Yahweh told Mosheh (Moses):
[Leviticus] [22]:[2] Tell Aharon (Aaron) and his sons that they must carefully honour the holy things offered by the Israeli people, and they mustn’t profane my holy reputation. I am Yahweh.
[Leviticus] [22]:[3] Tell them that throughout the generations, any of your descendants who is ‘unclean’ and approaches things that have become holy because the people have consecrated them to Yahweh, that person will be cut off from me. I am Yahweh.
[Leviticus] [22]:[4] Any man who’s a descendant of Aharon, if he has a skin disease or a discharge, he mustn’t eat any of the sacred food until he’s ‘clean’ again. The same applies if he’s touched any ‘unclean’ corpse, anyone who’s had a seminal emission,
[Leviticus] [22]:[5] anyone who’s touched any swarming creature that makes him ‘unclean’ or touches another person who makes him ‘unclean’ (whatever that person’s uncleanness is).
[Leviticus] [22]:[6] No, the man who’s touched any of those will be ‘unclean’ until the evening and he mustn’t eat any of the sacred food until he’s washed his body with water.
[Leviticus] [22]:[7] When the sun sets, then he’ll be ‘clean’ and will be able to eat any of those sacred offerings because that’s his food.
[Leviticus] [22]:[8] But he must never eat an animal found dead or torn by wild animals and become ‘unclean’ in that way. I am Yahweh.
[Leviticus] [22]:[9] The priests must follow my instructions so they won’t have to bear their own disobedience and die from it because they profaned them. I am Yahweh who makes them sacred.
[Leviticus] [22]:[10] However, no stranger may eat the sacred food, e.g., someone staying with the priest, or his hired servant.
[Leviticus] [22]:[11] If the priest had purchased the person with cash, then that person can eat it, plus anyone that was born into the priest’s household.
[Leviticus] [22]:[12] A priest’s daughter who is married by someone who’s not a priest can no longer eat those sacred offerings.
[Leviticus] [22]:[13] However, in the future if she became a widow or was divorced without having had children, and if she has returned to her father’s house like when she was young, then she can eat the same food as her father, but no stranger may eat it.
[Leviticus] [22]:[14] If someone accidentally eats something that’s sacred, then they must pay back the full value plus 20% to the priest.
[Leviticus] [22]:[15] So in summary, the priests must not profane the sacred things contributed by the Israelis and which they’ve offered to Yahweh
[Leviticus] [22]:[16] or else they’ll cause themselves to bear the guilt from their disobedience concerning eating sacred food, because I am Yahweh who has separated them to be sacred.
[Leviticus] [22]:[17] The Yahweh told Mosheh (Moses):
[Leviticus] [22]:[18] Tell Aharon (Aaron) and his sons, and all the Israelis that any Israeli or outsider residing in Yisrael (Israel), when they present their burnt offering to Yahweh, whether it’s for a vow or for a freewill offering,
[Leviticus] [22]:[19] to be accepted it must be a male with no defects, whether it’s a cow, or a sheep, or a goat.
[Leviticus] [22]:[20] Anything that has a defect must not be presented because it wouldn’t be acceptable on your behalf.
[Leviticus] [22]:[21] When someone presents a sacrifice of peace offerings to Yahweh to fulfill a vow or as a freewill offering from the herd or the flock, to be accepted it must flawless with no defects—
[Leviticus] [22]:[22] not blind or with broken bones, and not maimed or with an oozing sore or rash or scab. You all mustn’t present anything like that to Yahweh, and must not even offering any part of them to Yahweh on the altar.
[Leviticus] [22]:[23] However, if a cow or a sheep has something enlarged or something stunted, it can be offered as a freewill offering, but it wouldn’t be accepted for a vow,
[Leviticus] [22]:[24] and you all must never present to Yahweh any animal that’s bruised or torn or cut. You mustn’t do that in your country.
[Leviticus] [22]:[25] You all mustn’t present any of those animals raised by foreigners to your god because they’ve been ruined and are defective, so they won’t be accepted for you.
[Leviticus] [22]:[26] Then Yahweh told Mosheh (Moses):
[Leviticus] [22]:[27] A newborn calf or lamb or goat must remain with its mother for seven days—it can be offered as a sacrifice to Yahweh from the eighth day onwards,
[Leviticus] [22]:[28] but you mustn’t slaughter a cow or a sheep and its offspring on the same day.
[Leviticus] [22]:[29] When you offer a thanksgiving sacrifice to Yahweh, it must be acceptable as a sacrifice
[Leviticus] [22]:[30] and you can eat it that same day but no part of it should be left until the morning. I am Yahweh.
[Leviticus] [22]:[31] You all must record my instructions and follow them. I am Yahweh.
[Leviticus] [22]:[32] You mustn’t profane the reputation of my holiness, and I will demonstrate my holiness among the Israeli people. I am Yahweh who separates you all to be sacred—
[Leviticus] [22]:[33] who brought you all out of Mitsrayim (Egypt) to be your god. I am Yahweh.
[Leviticus] [23]:[1] Then Yahweh told Mosheh (Moses):
[Leviticus] [23]:[2] Tell the Israelis that they must proclaim Yahweh’s scheduled festivals as sacred assemblies at the given times.
[Leviticus] [23]:[3] Work for six days, then the seventh is a rest day for a sacred assembly—don’t work on that day—wherever you live it’s a rest day to honour Yahweh.
[Leviticus] [23]:[4] The following are the scheduled festivals that you must proclaim at the appointed times as sacred assemblies:
[Leviticus] [23]:[5] The 14th of the first month (Nisan = March/April) each year at twilight is the start of the celebration to honour Yahweh with the ‘passover’.
[Leviticus] [23]:[6] Then the next day (the 15th) is the start of the festival of flat bread to honour Yahweh—you all must eat bread made without any rising agent for seven days.
[Leviticus] [23]:[7] On that first day you’ll hold a sacred assembly—no regular work may be done that day.
[Leviticus] [23]:[8] For seven days you all must present offerings to Yahweh, then the seventh day is another sacred assembly—again no regular work may be done that day.
[Leviticus] [23]:[9] Then Yahweh told Mosheh (Moses):
[Leviticus] [23]:[10] Tell the Israelis that when you enter the land that I’m giving you all, and you harvest your grain crops, then you all must bring a sheaf of the first part of your harvest to a priest,
[Leviticus] [23]:[11] and he will wave the sheaf in front of Yahweh to be accepted for you. That must be done the day after the rest day.
[Leviticus] [23]:[12] That same day, you all must offer a year-old lamb with no defects to Yahweh as a burnt offering,
[Leviticus] [23]:[13] and the associated grain offering will be two kilograms of fine wheat flour mixed with olive oil. That will be a gift to Yahweh with a pleasing aroma, and the associated drink offering will be a litre of wine.
[Leviticus] [23]:[14] You all may not eat any bread, or roasted or fresh grain, on that day, until after you’ve taken the offering to your god. That is a rule that will continue throughout your generations no matter where you live.
[Leviticus] [23]:[15] Then count seven rest days from the day after you brought the bundle of grain as a wave offering—seven full weeks.
[Leviticus] [23]:[16] Then that next day will make fifty days, and then you all must present a new grain offering to Yahweh.
[Leviticus] [23]:[17] From your homes, each family must bring two loaves of bread baked with a rising agent, as a firstfruits offering to Yahweh.
[Leviticus] [23]:[18] Along with the bread, you all must present seven year-old male lambs without defects, one young bull, and two rams. They will be a burnt offering to Yahweh, with their associated grain and drink offerings—a gift with a pleasing aroma for Yahweh.
[Leviticus] [23]:[19] You all must also offer a male goat as a sin offering and two one-year-old male lambs as a peace offering.
[Leviticus] [23]:[20] The priest must raise them along with the firstfruits bread as a wave offering in front of Yahweh, with the two lambs. They will become sacred to Yahweh, but for the priest to eat.
[Leviticus] [23]:[21] You all must proclaim a sacred assembly that same day—you mustn’t do any regular work. That is a permanent rule that will continue throughout the generations no matter where you live.
[Leviticus] [23]:[22] When you all harvest your crops, don’t reap to the very edge of your field and don’t pick up stalks that drop on the ground—they must be left for the poor and for foreigners without land. I am your god, Yahweh.
[Leviticus] [23]:[23] Then Yahweh told Mosheh (Moses),
[Leviticus] [23]:[24] “Tell the Israelis that on the 1st of the seventh month (Tishrei = September/October) each year, you must have a public holiday with a loud trumpet blast announcing the sacred assembly.
[Leviticus] [23]:[25] You all must not do any regular work on that day, and you all must present a fire-offering to Yahweh.”
[Leviticus] [23]:[26] Then Yahweh told Mosheh (Moses),
[Leviticus] [23]:[27] “The 10th of that seventh month is a day for making things right with Yahweh. You all must hold a sacred assembly and humble yourselves and present a fire-offering to Yahweh.
[Leviticus] [23]:[28] You mustn’t do any work on that particular day because it’s the day for making yourselves right in front of your god Yahweh,
[Leviticus] [23]:[29] because anyone who doesn’t humble themself on that day will be cut off from their people.
[Leviticus] [23]:[30] In addition, I will destroy anyone who works on that day—removing them from their people.
[Leviticus] [23]:[31] You all must not do any work. That’s a permanent rule that will continue throughout the generations no matter where you live—
[Leviticus] [23]:[32] it’s a very strict rest day and you all must humble yourselves from the evening of the 9th until the next evening when it will finish.
[Leviticus] [23]:[33] Then Yahweh told Mosheh (Moses):
[Leviticus] [23]:[34] Tell the Israelis that starting on the 15th of the seventh month (of Tishrei—around September/October), there will be a celebration in shelters to honour Yahweh.
[Leviticus] [23]:[35] The first day will be a sacred assembly—you all mustn’t do any regular work.
[Leviticus] [23]:[36] You all must present a gift to Yahweh each day for seven days, and then on the eighth day, there’ll be another sacred assembly and you’ll all present a gift to Yahweh. It’ll be a day to assemble—you all mustn’t do any regular work that day.
[Leviticus] [23]:[37] The above are the scheduled dates to proclaim sacred assemblies to present a gift to Yahweh: burnt offerings and grain offerings, sacrifices and drink offerings, on the appropriate days,
[Leviticus] [23]:[38] as well as Yahweh’s rest days, and alongside all your regular gifts and vows and freewill offerings that you all give to Yahweh.
[Leviticus] [23]:[39] So indeed, on the 15th of the seventh month when you have harvested your crops, you’ll all celebrate Yahweh’s festival for seven days with the first and eighth days being rest days.
[Leviticus] [23]:[40] On that first day, you’ll all bring the fruit from your trees, along with palm branches, leafy branches, and willow branches from beside the creeks, and you’ll all happily celebrate in front of your god Yahweh for seven days.
[Leviticus] [23]:[41] Do that for seven days each year as a festival to honour Yahweh. you all must celebrate it in the seventh month. That’s a permanent rule that will continue throughout the generations.
[Leviticus] [23]:[42] You all must live in shelters for seven days—all you native-born Israelis,
[Leviticus] [23]:[43] so that the future generations will know that I made their ancestors live in shelters when I brought them out of Mitsrayim (Egypt). I am your god Yahweh.
[Leviticus] [23]:[44] So Mosheh (Moses) passed all those scheduled dates from Yahweh, on to the Israelis.
[Leviticus] [24]:[1] Then Yahweh told Mosheh (Moses):
[Leviticus] [24]:[2] Order the Israelis to bring you pressed olive oil that’s pure, to supply lamps to give continual light.
[Leviticus] [24]:[3] The high priest (Aharon (Aaron)) must take care of them from evening until the morning to burn continually in front of Yahweh. That’s a permanent requirement that will continue throughout the generations.
[Leviticus] [24]:[4] He will arrange the lamps continually on the lampstand in front of Yahweh.
[Leviticus] [24]:[5] Each week you must take fine wheat flour and bake twelve loaves of bread, using two kilograms of flour for each loaf.
[Leviticus] [24]:[6] Arrange the loaves into two rows of six loaves on the pure table in front of Yahweh,
[Leviticus] [24]:[7] and put pure frankincense with each row to be a memorial portion for the bread as a gift to Yahweh.
[Leviticus] [24]:[8] Every rest day it will be placed in front of Yahweh representing the ongoing agreement with the Israelis.
[Leviticus] [24]:[9] Afterwards, it will belong to Aharon (Aaron) and his sons, and they must eat it in a sacred area because it’s a very sacred part of the gifts for Yahweh. That’s a permanent rule.
[Leviticus] [24]:[10] Once there was an Israeli woman and an Mitsri (Egyptian) man who had a son who lived among the Israelis, and he got into a fight with an Israeli man.
[Leviticus] [24]:[11] Then that son of the Israeli woman slandered Yahweh’s name and cursed, and so the people took him to Mosheh (Moses). (The mother was Shelomit, a daughter of Divri from the Dan tribe.)
[Leviticus] [24]:[12] They held him in custody while waiting for Yahweh’s decision.
[Leviticus] [24]:[13] Then Yahweh told Mosheh:
[Leviticus] [24]:[14] Take that man who cursed outside the camp, and everyone who heard him must place their hands on his head, and then all the people must execute him by throwing rocks at him.
[Leviticus] [24]:[15] Then tell the people that anyone who curses God must bear the results of their own wickedness.
[Leviticus] [24]:[16] Anyone who slanders Yahweh’s reputation must be executed. The gathered assembly must throw rocks at them. It makes no difference whether they’re a foreigner staying there, or a native-born Israeli.
[Leviticus] [24]:[17] Anyone who murders another person, must definitely be executed.
[Leviticus] [24]:[18] Anyone who kills someone else’s animal, must make restitution with the same kind of animal.
[Leviticus] [24]:[19] Anyone who injures a fellow citizen, must have the same done to them—
[Leviticus] [24]:[20] fracture for fracture, eye for eye, tooth for tooth—however they injured the other person, that’s what must be done to them.
[Leviticus] [24]:[21] Anyone who kills someone else’s animal must replace it, but anyone who kills another person must be executed.
[Leviticus] [24]:[22] There’s only one set of regulations for both the foreigner and the native-born citizen because I am your god Yahweh.
[Leviticus] [24]:[23] Mosheh (Moses) passed all that onto the people, and they took the man who had cursed Yahweh outside the camp where they executed him with rocks. The Israelis did exactly what Yahweh had commanded them via Mosheh.
[Leviticus] [25]:[1] Then on Mt. Sinay, Yahweh told Mosheh (Moses):
[Leviticus] [25]:[2] Tell the Israelis that when you all enter the land that I’m giving you, the land must observe a rest year for Yahweh.
[Leviticus] [25]:[3] You can plant your crops, prune your grapevines, and harvest all its produce for six years,
[Leviticus] [25]:[4] but during the seventh year, you must allow the land to rest to honour Yahweh. You mustn’t plant any crops or prune any grapevines.
[Leviticus] [25]:[5] Don’t systematically harvest the self-sown crops or the grapes from the untrimmed vines. It must be a rest year for the land.
[Leviticus] [25]:[6] However, during the rest year, the land will provide food for you and your servants, and for your hired workers and the foreigners who are living among you,
[Leviticus] [25]:[7] as well as your livestock and the wild animals across the land. Any produce from the land can be eaten.
[Leviticus] [25]:[8] Count off seven rest years, so seven times seven which is forty-nine years,
[Leviticus] [25]:[9] then after that, sound loud horn blasts on the 10th of the seventh month to announce throughout the land that it’s the day for making things right with Yahweh.
[Leviticus] [25]:[10] Then you all must declare that fiftieth year to be sacred. It’ll be a restoration celebration year when you announce freedom for all the inhabitants of the country—everyone can be free to return to their families, and all families can be free to return to their originally inherited land.
[Leviticus] [25]:[11] That fiftieth year will be a restoration celebration year. You all mustn’t plant crops and don’t systematically harvest the self-sown crops or the grapes from the untrimmed vines,
[Leviticus] [25]:[12] because it’s a restoration celebration year. You all must treat it as sacred and just eat what you take directly from the countryside.
[Leviticus] [25]:[13] In that restoration celebration year, you all should return to your inherited land.
[Leviticus] [25]:[14] In the other years when you buy or sell from your fellow citizens, you mustn’t cheat them
[Leviticus] [25]:[15] because the value of the land will depend on the number of years after the restoration celebration year, i.e., you must take into account the number of years of produce—
[Leviticus] [25]:[16] if there’s many years to go, the price will increase, and if the next rest year is close, the price will decrease because you’re selling the number of crops.
[Leviticus] [25]:[17] So don’t cheat eat other—you must respect and obey your god, because I am your god Yahweh.
[Leviticus] [25]:[18] You all must follow all my instructions and maintain my values—keeping them so that you’ll be able to live securely on the land.
[Leviticus] [25]:[19] The land will yield its crops and you’ll all have plenty to eat, and you’ll be able to live there securely.
[Leviticus] [25]:[20] But if you all wonder what you’ll eat in that seventh year when you’ll neither plant crops or do organised harvests,
[Leviticus] [25]:[21] well I’ll send my blessing to you all in the sixth year, and it’ll produce enough for three years
[Leviticus] [25]:[22] so you all can still eat that stored food while you plant crops in the eighth year to feed you all through the ninth year.
[Leviticus] [25]:[23] The land can not be irrevocably sold, because it belongs to me and you all are foreigners and temporary residents on my land.
[Leviticus] [25]:[24] so for all the land that you take possession of, there must be a way to get back the family land.
[Leviticus] [25]:[25] For example, if an Israeli man becomes poor and sells off some of his inherited land, then a close relative must have the right to go and buy back that land.
[Leviticus] [25]:[26] Even if he didn’t have a relative who could do that, and he prospers again in the future and is able to raise enough money,
[Leviticus] [25]:[27] then he can calculate the value of the years until the restoration celebration, and then for that amount he must be allowed to buy the land back from the person he’d sold it to.
[Leviticus] [25]:[28] However, if the original owner wasn’t able to raise enough money, then that piece of land that was sold will remain under the control of the buyer until the restoration celebration year when it must be returned anyway.
[Leviticus] [25]:[29] If a house inside a walled city is sold, then the right to buy it back will last until one full year after the sale.
[Leviticus] [25]:[30] If it’s not bought back by the original family within that year, then that house in the walled city will then belong permanently to the buyer—it won’t be returned in the restoration celebration year.
[Leviticus] [25]:[31] On the contrary, village houses will be considered as part of the family land, so they’ll be able to be bought back by the family, otherwise they’ll be returned in the restoration celebration year.
[Leviticus] [25]:[32] The Levites’ cities and houses will belong to them permanently—the Levites must always be able to buy them back,
[Leviticus] [25]:[33] but even if they don’t buy them back, they must be returned in the restoration celebration year because the Levites’ houses are their only possession among the Israelis.
[Leviticus] [25]:[34] In addition, they may not sell the pastureland around their cities because that’s their permanent possession.
[Leviticus] [25]:[35] If a fellow citizen becomes poor and is unable to survive beside you, then you must support that person and allow him to live with you like a foreigner might.
[Leviticus] [25]:[36] You mustn’t charge that person any interest or make a profit from him, but you must respect and obey your god, and your fellow citizen can continue to live with you.
[Leviticus] [25]:[37] If you loan him money, don’t charge interest or make a profit from his food.
[Leviticus] [25]:[38] I am your god Yahweh who brought you all out of Mitsrayim (Egypt) to give you the Kena’an (Canaan) region and to be your god.
[Leviticus] [25]:[39] If a fellow citizen becomes poor and selling himself to you, don’t force him to work like a slave—
[Leviticus] [25]:[40] treat him like a hired worker or a temporary resident. He can work with you until the restoration celebration year
[Leviticus] [25]:[41] when he must be released along with his children, and he can return to his family, and to his clan’s land,
[Leviticus] [25]:[42] because they are my slaves that I brought out of Mitsrayim (Egypt) so they mustn’t be sold again as slaves.
[Leviticus] [25]:[43] Don’t rule harshly over them but rather, respect and obey your god.
[Leviticus] [25]:[44] If you want to have male or female slaves, they you can buy them from the surrounding countries,
[Leviticus] [25]:[45] or else from the children or clans of the foreigners who are living among you—you all can own them
[Leviticus] [25]:[46] and then pass them on to your children to own as their inheritance. You all can make them work indefinitely for you, but you mustn’t harshly oppress your fellow Israelis.
[Leviticus] [25]:[47] If a foreigner living among you becomes wealthy, yet your fellow citizen becomes poor and sells himself to that resident foreigner or to a member of their clan,
[Leviticus] [25]:[48] then there’s always the right of redemption even after he’s sold himself, so one of his brothers can buy him back,
[Leviticus] [25]:[49] or his uncle or cousin or another relative from the clan can pay to free him. In fact, he might even be able to buy his own way out.
[Leviticus] [25]:[50] He must work out with his master how many years from when he sold himself, until the restoration celebration year, and figure out the price according to the wages of a hired worker for that many years.
[Leviticus] [25]:[51] If there’s still a lot of years to go, he’d need to repay most of what he sold himself for,
[Leviticus] [25]:[52] but if it’s only a few years to go, the price for his freedom would be proportionally smaller.
[Leviticus] [25]:[53] While he works for the foreign master, he must be treated like an annual hired worker. You others must ensure that he’s not treated harshly.
[Leviticus] [25]:[54] Then even if he’s not bought out, he and his children must be released in the restoration celebration year
[Leviticus] [25]:[55] because the Israelis are my slaves—my slaves because I brought them out of Mitsrayim (Egypt). I am your god Yahweh.
[Leviticus] [26]:[1] You all mustn’t make worthless idols or carved images for yourselves, or set up sacred pillars. In your country, you must never bow down to an engraved stone image, because I am your god Yahweh.
[Leviticus] [26]:[2] You all must observe my rest days and honour my sanctuary. I am Yahweh.
[Leviticus] [26]:[3] If you’ll all follow my instructions and remember my rules and obey them,
[Leviticus] [26]:[4] then I’ll give you all rain in the proper season, and the land will produce crops and the trees in the countryside will produce fruit.
[Leviticus] [26]:[5] The grain threshing will continue until the grape harvest, and the grape harvesting will continue until it’s time to plant new crops, and so you’ll all have plenty of food and you’ll live securely there on your land.
[Leviticus] [26]:[6] Then I’ll give peace in your country so that you’ll all sleep without being afraid. I’ll remove the wild animals from your area and there’ll be no raids or wars in your region.
[Leviticus] [26]:[7] You’ll all be able to chase away your enemies and destroy them—
[Leviticus] [26]:[8] five of you will chase away a hundred, and a hundred of you will chase away ten thousand, and you’ll be able to defeat your enemies.
[Leviticus] [26]:[9] I’ll give you all my attention and bless you with many children, and I’ll maintain my agreement with you all.
[Leviticus] [26]:[10] You’ll all still be eating the previous year’s grain when the new harvest starts, and you’ll have to move out that left-over grain to make room for the new.
[Leviticus] [26]:[11] Then I’ll put my residence among you all and won’t reject you,
[Leviticus] [26]:[12] and I’ll walk among you and be your god, and you’ll all be my people.
[Leviticus] [26]:[13] I am your god Yahweh who brought you all out from being slaves in Mitsrayim (Egypt), and I broke the chains off you so that you all could walk with heads erect.
[Leviticus] [26]:[14] However, if you all won’t listen to me and won’t follow all those instructions,
[Leviticus] [26]:[15] and if you all reject my regulations and my values to the point of hating my commands, thus breaking my agreement,
[Leviticus] [26]:[16] then this is what I’ll do to you all: I’ll send sudden terror to you all, and wasting diseases and sicknesses. You’ll all be wasting your time sowing seeds because your enemies will eat the harvest.
[Leviticus] [26]:[17] I’ll take action against you, and you’ll be defeated by your enemies. You’ll be ruled over by those who hate you, and you’ll all run away frightened even when no one’s chasing you.
[Leviticus] [26]:[18] If you all still won’t listen to me after that, then I’ll continue on to discipline you seven times over for your disobedience.
[Leviticus] [26]:[19] Then I’ll smash your strong pride, and I’ll make the sky like iron with no rain and your land hard like bronze.
[Leviticus] [26]:[20] Your energy spent working your land will be just wasted as your land won’t produce its crops, and the trees won’t produce any fruit.
[Leviticus] [26]:[21] Then if you’re all still being contrary and unwilling to listen to me, then I’ll send seven times more deadly diseases according to your disobedience.
[Leviticus] [26]:[22] Then I’ll send in the wild animals to make you childless and to cut back your livestock, thus diminishing your numbers and leaving your roads desolate.
[Leviticus] [26]:[23] Then after that if you all still won’t accept my discipline and continue to oppose me,
[Leviticus] [26]:[24] then I myself will oppose you all and punish you all seven times over for your disobedience.
[Leviticus] [26]:[25] I’ll send armies against you all to avenge the breaking of our agreement. You’ll be shut into your cities where I’ll send diseases in for you all, and allow your enemies to defeat you.
[Leviticus] [26]:[26] When I limit your food supplies, ten women will bake bread in one oven and it will be rationed by weight—you’ll all eat but never be satisfied.
[Leviticus] [26]:[27] In spite of all that, if you all still won’t listen to me, and continue to oppose me,
[Leviticus] [26]:[28] then I’ll be in a hostile rage against you all and I’ll discipline you seven times more for your disobedience
[Leviticus] [26]:[29] and you’ll start eating your own sons and daughters.
[Leviticus] [26]:[30] I’ll destroy your hilltop shrines and cut down you incense altars, then I’ll pile your corpses on top of your idols’ corpses, and I myself will detest you all.
[Leviticus] [26]:[31] I’ll make your cities into heaps of rubble and I’ll devastate your sanctuaries and no longer smell the pleasing aromas of your sacrifices.
[Leviticus] [26]:[32] I’ll devastate the region, and your enemies who live in it will be appalled.
[Leviticus] [26]:[33] Then I’ll scatter you all among other nations and then armies will come in after you and your land will become desolate and your cities will become rubble,
[Leviticus] [26]:[34] and the land will enjoy all its rest times while it’s desolate and you’re all in your enemies’ countries. The land will stop producing and enjoy its times of resting.
[Leviticus] [26]:[35] It will rest all through its desolation since it didn’t get its rest times when you lived on it.
[Leviticus] [26]:[36] Then those of you who are left in your enemies’ countries, I’ll make you paranoid there—even the sound of a blowing leaf will make them run away as if someone’s chasing them with a sword, and they’ll fall down even when no one’s chasing them.
[Leviticus] [26]:[37] They’ll stumble over each other as if being attacked, but there won’t be anyone chasing them, and then you all won’t have the energy to stand up against your enemies.
[Leviticus] [26]:[38] You’ll die in various countries and your enemies will consume you.
[Leviticus] [26]:[39] Those of you who are left will rot away amongst the wickedness in your enemies’ countries and because of the wickedness of their ancestors.
[Leviticus] [26]:[40] However, if they confess their wickedness and their ancestors’ wickedness, that they’ve disobeyed and neglected me, and been hostile towards me,
[Leviticus] [26]:[41] (and that I became hostile toward them and took their into their enemies’ countries,) and humble their undisciplined hearts and admit their disobedience,
[Leviticus] [26]:[42] then I’ll remember my agreements with Ya’akov (Jacob) and with Yitshak (Isaac) and with Avraham, and I’ll remember this land.
[Leviticus] [26]:[43] The land here will have been deserted by them and will have enjoyed its times of rest, and they’ll accept their wickedness because they rejected my values and they really detested my regulations.
[Leviticus] [26]:[44] Despite that, I won’t reject them in their enemies’ countries, and I won’t detest them enough to completely destroy them and to break my agreement with them, because I am their god Yahweh.
[Leviticus] [26]:[45] I’ll remember the earlier agreement with their ancestors that I brought out of Mitsrayim (Egypt) while all the nations watched me be their god. I am Yahweh.
[Leviticus] [26]:[46] The above are the instructions and values and rules that Yahweh instilled between him and the Israelis through Mosheh (Moses) there at Mt. Sinay.
[Leviticus] [27]:[1] Then Yahweh told Mosheh (Moses):
[Leviticus] [27]:[2] Tell the Israelis that when someone makes a special vow to offer someone to Yahweh,
[Leviticus] [27]:[3] a man between twenty and sixty will be valued at fifty silver coins (according to the sanctuary standard weights)
[Leviticus] [27]:[4] and a woman at thirty coins.
[Leviticus] [27]:[5] If it’s someone between five and twenty, then it’s twenty silver coins for a male and ten for a female.
[Leviticus] [27]:[6] Between one month old and five years, it’s five silver coins for a male and three for a female.
[Leviticus] [27]:[7] For sixty years old and older, it’s fifteen silver coins for a male and ten for a female.
[Leviticus] [27]:[8] If the maker of the vow can’t afford the valuation, then that person must stand in front of the priest and give an account, and then the priest can set a value that they can afford.
[Leviticus] [27]:[9] If it’s an animal that they’re promising as a gift for Yahweh, then that animal becomes sacred—
[Leviticus] [27]:[10] it can’t be exchanged for a different one (either better or worse), but if it does get substituted, then both animals will become sacred.
[Leviticus] [27]:[11] Any ‘unclean’ animal cannot be presented to Yahweh, so if that’s what was promised, the person must take the animal to the priest,
[Leviticus] [27]:[12] and a priest must give a fair valuation according to the quality of the animal—the priest’s decision will be final.
[Leviticus] [27]:[13] However, if it’s later bought back, then an extra twenty percent must be added to that valuation.
[Leviticus] [27]:[14] If someone dedicates their house as sacred to Yahweh, a priest must value it according to its quality—the priest’s decision will be final.
[Leviticus] [27]:[15] However, if that person decides to buy back their house, then an extra twenty percent must be added to the valuation and then it can be theirs again.
[Leviticus] [27]:[16] If someone dedicates part of their farmland as sacred to Yahweh, then it will be valued according to how much seed would be sown in it—fifty silver coins for each 130kg of barley seed required.
[Leviticus] [27]:[17] That would be its value if it was dedicated during the restoration celebration year,
[Leviticus] [27]:[18] but in the years following, the priest must calculate the field’s value depending on how many years remain before the next rest year.
[Leviticus] [27]:[19] However, if that person decides to buy back their land, then an extra twenty percent must be added to the valuation and then it can be theirs again.
[Leviticus] [27]:[20] If the person doesn’t buy back the field but sells it to someone else, then it can’t be bought back again.
[Leviticus] [27]:[21] Then when the field is released at the next rest year, it will be sacred to Yahweh and the priests will take ownership.
[Leviticus] [27]:[22] If someone dedicates to Yahweh some land that they’ve bought (i.e., it’s not part of their clan inheritance),
[Leviticus] [27]:[23] then a priest must calculate the valuation until the next restoration celebration year, and it must be paid that same day —becoming sacred to Yahweh.
[Leviticus] [27]:[24] In that rest year, the land will return to the original owner who has it as part of their clan inheritance.
[Leviticus] [27]:[25] All valuations will be calculated using the standard weights from the sanctuary—the silver coin must weigh twelve grams.
[Leviticus] [27]:[26] Every firstborn domestic animal (including cows and sheep) automatically belongs to Yahweh, and no person can claim to ‘dedicate’ it.
[Leviticus] [27]:[27] However, if it’s an ‘unclean’ animal then it must be bought back by paying its valuation plus an additional twenty percent, but if it’s not bought back, then it must be sold at its valuation price.
[Leviticus] [27]:[28] If someone dedicates something to Yahweh that they own (e.g., a man or an animal, or a field), they can’t then sell it or buy it straight back—everything that’s dedicated like that becomes sacred to Yahweh.
[Leviticus] [27]:[29] Any person who’s dedicated for destruction cannot be bought back—they must be executed.
[Leviticus] [27]:[30] A tenth of all the harvests from the crops and fruit from the trees, belongs to Yahweh. It’s sacred to Yahweh.
[Leviticus] [27]:[31] If someone really wanted to buy back their tenth of their produce, an additional twenty percent must be added to the valuation.
[Leviticus] [27]:[32] Every tenth animal of the mustered domestic cattle and sheep and goats, is sacred to Yahweh.
[Leviticus] [27]:[33] The herder mustn’t pick out good or bad ones, or make substitutions. (If a substitution was made, both animals then become sacred and must not be bought back.)
[Leviticus] [27]:[34] The above are the instructions and rules that Yahweh gave Mosheh (Moses) at Mt. Sinay for the Israelis.
[Census] [1]:[1] In April of the year after the Israeli people escaped from Mitsrayim (Egypt), Yahweh spoke to Mosheh (Moses) in the Sinay wilderness in the sacred tent, saying,
[Census] [1]:[2] “Count all the men who are Yisrael’s (Israel) descendants by their clans and families, being sure to list all their names.
[Census] [1]:[3] Only include those who are twenty or older and able to be recruited as soldiers. You and Aharon (Aaron) must enrol them into military divisions.

[Census] [1]:[6] Shelumiel (Tsurishadai’s son) from Shim’on (Simeon),

[Census] [3]:[1] The following are the descendants of Aharon (Aaron) and Mosheh (Moses) as on the day when Yahweh spoke with Mosheh on Mt. Sinay:
[Census] [3]:[2] Aharon’s sons were: Nadav (the oldest), Avihu, Eleazar, and Itamar.
[Census] [3]:[3] They were all anointed as priests and served in that role,
[Census] [3]:[4] except that Nadav and Avihu died in front of Yahweh when they offered unacceptable fire to him in the Sinay wilderness, and so they had no sons. So Eleazar and Itamar served as priests alongside their father Aharon.
[Census] [3]:[5] Then Yahweh told Mosheh (Moses),
[Census] [3]:[6] “Summon the Levites to come and stand in front of Aharon (Aaron) the priest, so they can assist him.
[Census] [3]:[7] They must perform duties for him and for the entire community at and around the sacred tent,
[Census] [3]:[8] including looking after all of its equipment and fulfilling the obligations of the Israelis.
[Census] [3]:[9] You must assign the Levites to Aharon—out of all the Israelis it’s them who are assigned to serve the priests.
[Census] [3]:[10] Appoint Aharon and his sons as priests and to preserve the priesthood. Any other person who tries to act as a priest must be executed.”
[Census] [3]:[11] Then Yahweh told Mosheh,
[Census] [3]:[12] “Out of all the Israelis, I’ve taken the Levites instead of the oldest son from every family. The Levites will be the ransom for those sons, and so they belong to me,
[Census] [3]:[13] because every firstborn male person and animal is set aside as belonging to me ever since I killed those firstborn males in Mitsrayim (Egypt). I am Yahweh.”

[Census] [3]:[49] So Mosheh collected that ransom money to cover the ransom of the excess not covered by the number of Levites.
[Census] [3]:[50] He collected 1,365 silver coins from the firstborn Israeli males (using the standard weight of silver from the sanctuary)
[Census] [3]:[51] and gave it to Aharon and his sons just as Yahweh had commanded.
[Census] [4]:[1] Then Yahweh told Mosheh (Moses) and Aharon (Aaron),
[Census] [4]:[2] “Take a detailed census of Kohat’s male descendants by their clans and families
[Census] [4]:[3] who are from twenty-five up to fifty years old and who goes into the sacred tent to minister.
[Census] [4]:[4] This is what the Kohatites are responsible for concerning the sacred tent including the inner room:
[Census] [4]:[5] When it’s time to break camp, Aharon and his sons must enter and take down the curtain that veils it, and then use that to cover the box containing the agreement.
[Census] [4]:[6] Then they must cover it with fine leather, followed by a blue cloth, and then put its carrying poles through the rings.
[Census] [4]:[7] They must spread a blue cloth over the sacred bread table, then place the dishes, pans, bowls, and jugs for the drink offerings on top of that, along with the sacred bread.
[Census] [4]:[8] Then they must spread a scarlet cloth over all that, and cover that again with fine leather, and then put its poles through the rings.
[Census] [4]:[9] They must spread a blue cloth over the lampstand with its oil lamps, its tongs and trays, and the oil containers that are used for it.
[Census] [4]:[10] Then they must wrap the lampstand and all its equipment in fine leather, and place it all on its carrying frame.
[Census] [4]:[11] Then the must spread a blue cloth over the gold incense altar, and cover that again with fine leather, and then put its poles through the rings.
[Census] [4]:[12] Then they must get all the other utensils that they use in the sacred tent, and cover that again with fine leather, and place it all on its carrying frame.
[Census] [4]:[13] They need to remove the ashes from the bronze altar and spread a purple cloth over it,
[Census] [4]:[14] and put all the utensils they use on top of it: the trays, meat forks, shovel and basins for the altar. Then they must cover it with fine leather, and then put its poles through the rings.
[Census] [4]:[15] Aharon and his sons must finish covering the sacred tent and all its utensils and equipment when they’re about to move camp. Then the Kohatites can come to carry it all without touching the inner room so they won’t die. That’s the responsibility of Kohat’s descendants—carrying the sacred tent.
[Census] [4]:[16] Eleazar (son of Aharon (Aaron) the priest) is in charge of the lamp oil and the fragrant incense, the regular grain offering, the anointing oil, and the oversight of the sacred tent and the inner room, including everything that’s used inside them.
[Census] [4]:[17] Then Yahweh told Mosheh (Moses) and Aharon,
[Census] [4]:[18] “Don’t allow the Kohatite Levites to get wiped out by mishandling the most sacred items,
[Census] [4]:[19] but take these precautions on their behalf so they won’t die when they approach the most sacred items: Get Aharon and his sons to go and show each of them personally the correct and proper way to do his duties.
[Census] [4]:[20] However, they must never go early to set their eyes on the sacred objects, even briefly, or they’ll die.”
[Census] [4]:[21] Then Yahweh told Mosheh (Moses),
[Census] [4]:[22] “Take a detailed census of Gereshon’s male descendants by their clans and families
[Census] [4]:[23] who are from thirty up to fifty years old and who goes into the sacred tent to minister.
[Census] [4]:[24] This is what the Gershonim are responsible for working with and carrying:
[Census] [4]:[25] They must carry the inner curtains from the sacred tent, the covering, the fine leather covering, the entrance curtain,
[Census] [4]:[26] the courtyard curtains, and the courtyard gate curtain, along with the ropes and other equipment for using them. That will be their ministry.
[Census] [4]:[27] Aharon (Aaron) and his sons will direct the Gershonim in their duties and assign all the items to them.
[Census] [4]:[28] That will be the ministry of Gereshon’s descendants with the sacred tent, and it will all be under the supervision of Aharon’s son Itamar the priest.
[Census] [4]:[29] “Take a detailed census of Merari’s descendants by their clans and families,
[Census] [4]:[30] listing the men who are from thirty to fifty years old and who goes into the sacred tent to minister.

[Census] [4]:[33] That will be the ministry of Merari’s descendants with the sacred tent, and it will all be under the supervision of Aharon’s (Aaron) son Itamar the priest.
[Census] [4]:[34] So Mosheh (Moses) and Aharon (Aaron) and the community leaders listed the Kohatites by their clans and families,

[Census] [4]:[36] and the total for all the clans was 2,750.
[Census] [4]:[37] That was from the Kohatite clans who ministered at the sacred tent and were listed by Mosheh and Aharon just as Yahweh had instructed Mosheh.
[Census] [4]:[38] They counted the Gershonim by their clans and families,
[Census] [4]:[39] counting the men from thirty to fifty years old who go into the sacred tent to minister,

[Census] [4]:[48] and the total came to 8,580.
[Census] [4]:[49] Those were the ones counted by Mosheh following Yahweh’s instructions. Each man’s name was listed by Mosheh, along with his duties and what was his responsibility to carry.
[Census] [5]:[1] Then Yahweh told Mosheh (Moses),
[Census] [5]:[2] “Order the Israelis that anyone with a skin disease or a discharge, and anyone who’s ‘unclean’ because they touched a corpse, must be sent outside the camp.
[Census] [5]:[3] Whether they’re male or female, they must be sent outside the camp so that the whole camp doesn’t become ‘unclean’ because I’m living there right amongst them.”
[Census] [5]:[4] So the Israelis did what Yahweh told Mosheh, and sent those people outside the camp.
[Census] [5]:[5] Then Yahweh told Mosheh (Moses),
[Census] [5]:[6] “Tell the Israelis that when any man or a woman disobeys God by doing any of the things that humans do when they’re unfaithful towards Yahweh, then that person is guilty
[Census] [5]:[7] and they must confess their disobedience. Then that person must make full reparation to whoever they wronged, along with an extra twenty percent of the cost.
[Census] [5]:[8] However, if reparation to the victim isn’t possible for some reason, then it must be paid to Yahweh via a priest, in addition to the ram that will be offered for that person’s atonement.
[Census] [5]:[9] Any sacred contributions by the Israelis that are presented to a priest will belong to him.
[Census] [5]:[10] Each person’s sacred contributions will be their own, but anything given to a priest will belong to him.”
[Census] [5]:[11] Then Yahweh told Mosheh (Moses),
[Census] [5]:[12] “Tell the Israelis that if any man’s wife has an affair and is unfaithful towards him,
[Census] [5]:[13] when another man secretly has sex with her, then she becomes ‘unclean’, even though there’s no witness against her and she wasn’t caught.
[Census] [5]:[14] If the husband becomes suspicious, whether or not she’s actually become ‘unclean’,
[Census] [5]:[15] then he should take her to a priest. He must also bring an offering on her behalf: two litres of barley flour. It must not have any oil or spices mixed into it because it’s a grain offering for suspicion—for determining if unfaithfulness has occurred.
[Census] [5]:[16] Then the priest must lead her forward and stand her in front of Yahweh.
[Census] [5]:[17] He must fill a pottery jar with sacred water, and then mix some dust from the floor of Yahweh’s residence into the water.
[Census] [5]:[18] Then the priest must stand the woman in front of Yahweh and let her hair down, then he must place the suspicion grain offering on her palm. (It’s a grain offering for jealousy.) The priest must be holding the water of bitterness that brings a curse
[Census] [5]:[19] and tell the woman to make this oath: “If no other man slept with you, and if you didn’t dirty yourself while you’re married, then be free from this water of bitterness that brings a curse.
[Census] [5]:[20] But if you have cheated on your husband and become ‘unclean’ and slept with some other guy, there’ll be consequences.
[Census] [5]:[21] Then the priest will make the woman take that curse as an oath, and he’ll tell her, “Yahweh will make your experience a curse and your people will see the results of the oath, when Yahweh gives disease to your genitals and makes your belly swell.
[Census] [5]:[22] This water will invoke the curse to make your belly swell and your genitals shrivel.” Then the woman must say, “Indeed, let it be so.”
[Census] [5]:[23] Then the priest must write those curses on a scroll, then wipe the ink into the water of bitterness.
[Census] [5]:[24] He must make the woman drink that water of bitterness that brings the curse, and it will enter into her.
[Census] [5]:[25] Then he’ll take the grain offering of suspicion from her hand, and hold it up in front of Yahweh, and then take it to the altar.
[Census] [5]:[26] He’ll take some of the grain as a memorial portion and burn it on the altar. Then he’ll make the woman drink the water.
[Census] [5]:[27] After she’s drunk it, if she was ‘unclean’ and unfaithful to her husband, the water will carry that curse into her, and her belly will swell and her genitals will get diseased, and the woman will become a curse among her people.
[Census] [5]:[28] However, if she hadn’t defiled herself and is pure, then she’ll be free and be able to have children.
[Census] [5]:[29] That’s the rule about jealousy when a wife cheats on her husband and defiles herself,
[Census] [5]:[30] or when a husband becomes jealous and suspicious and he stands his wife in front of Yahweh, and the priest applies this ruling to her.
[Census] [5]:[31] Then the husband will be innocent, and that women will bear the consequences of her wrongdoing.
[Census] [6]:[1] Then Yahweh told Mosheh (Moses),
[Census] [6]:[2] “Tell the Israelis that when any man or woman wants to make a solemn vow to separate themself to Yahweh as a Nazirite,
[Census] [6]:[3] they must keep away from wine and strong drink, and even vinegar made from wine or strong drink, plus they mustn’t drink grape juice or eat either grapes or raisins.
[Census] [6]:[4] For the entire time of their separation, they mustn’t eat anything coming from a grapevine, not even the seeds or the skins.
[Census] [6]:[5] “For the entire time of their vow to Yahweh as a Nazirite, they mustn’t cut their hair—they must sacred and grow their hair long.
[Census] [6]:[6] “For the entire time of their separation to Yahweh, they mustn’t approach any dead body,
[Census] [6]:[7] even if it’s their father or mother, or brother or sister. They mustn’t defile themselves with death, because their consecration to their god is on their head.
[Census] [6]:[8] They must remain holy to Yahweh for the whole time.
[Census] [6]:[9] “However, if someone right next to them suddenly died, that would defile their consecrated head, and after the regular seven days of purification, they would have to shave their head.
[Census] [6]:[10] Then on the eighth day, they’d have to take two doves or young pigeons to the priest at the entrance of the sacred tent,
[Census] [6]:[11] and he would take one for a sin offering and the other for a burnt offering—making atonement for their transgression with the corpse. Then they would consecrate their head again that day
[Census] [6]:[12] and restart their days of separation, as well as bringing a one-year old male lamb as a guilt offering. (Their initial days of separation won’t count because they were made ‘unclean’.)
[Census] [6]:[13] “Now these are the instructions for the Nazirites: Once their days of separation are fulfilled, someone must take them to the entrance of the sacred tent
[Census] [6]:[14] and they will present their offerings to Yahweh—an unblemished, one-year old, male lamb as a burnt offering, and an unblemished, one-year old, female lamb as a sin offering, plus an unblemished ram as a peace/fellowship offering,
[Census] [6]:[15] along with a basket of flat breads, flour mixed with oil, and wafers spread with olive oil, and their grain and drink offerings.
[Census] [6]:[16] The priest must present all that to Yahweh, and handle their sin offering and burnt offering.
[Census] [6]:[17] The ram and the basket of flat breads will be offered as a peace offering to Yahweh, and the priest will offer their grain and wine offerings.
[Census] [6]:[18] Then the Nazirite must shave their head of separation at the opening to the sacred tent, and taking the hair, must put it on the fire under their peace offering sacrifice.
[Census] [6]:[19] “The priest will then take the boiled shoulder from the ram, and one flat bread roll and one wafer from the basket, and place them on the palms of that Nazirite with their consecrated head that’s been shaved.
[Census] [6]:[20] Then the priest will raise them as a raised offering to Yahweh. Those raised breads and the shoulder are now sacred and belong to the priest. Then the Nazirite can drink some wine.
[Census] [6]:[21] Those are the instructions for the Nazirite who makes a solemn oath to Yahweh for their separation, plus what they’re able to give. They must do exactly what they promised as per these instructions.”
[Census] [6]:[22] Then Yahweh told Mosheh (Moses),
[Census] [6]:[23] “Tell Aharon (Aaron) and his sons that when the bless the Israelis, this is what they must say:
[Census] [6]:[24] May Yahweh bless you and protect you.
[Census] [6]:[25] May Yahweh give you prosperity and show grace toward you.
[Census] [6]:[26] May he watch over you and give you peace.
[Census] [6]:[27] “In that way, they’ll put my name on the Israelis, and I will bless them.”
[Census] [7]:[1] When Mosheh (Moses) had finished setting up the sacred tent, he anointed it with oil and consecrated it and all its furniture, as well as the altar and all its equipment.

Each of the leaders presented the following offerings: a silver dish (1.5 kg—all weights by the standard temple measurement) and a silver bowl (800g)—both of them full of fine flour mixed with oil as a grain offering, a small gold dish (110g) filled with incense, a young bull, a ram and a one-year-old male lamb for a burnt offering, a male goat for a sin offering, two cows, five rams, five male goats, and five one-year-old rams for the peace offering.
[Census] [7]:[84] That was the dedication of the altar in the day it was anointed, when Yisrael’s (Israel) leaders presented twelve silver dishes, twelve silver bowls, and twelve gold pans.
[Census] [7]:[85] Each silver dish weighed 1.5kg (all weights by the standard temple measurement) and the silver bowls were 800g. The total weight of the silver was around 27 kg.
[Census] [7]:[86] The gold pans that had been filled with incense weighed 110g and their total weight came to 1.3kg.
[Census] [7]:[87] For the burnt offerings there was: twelve bulls, twelve rams, and twelve male one-year-old lambs along with their grain offerings. There were twelve male goats for a sin offering.
[Census] [7]:[88] For the peace offering, there were 24 bulls, 60 rams, 60 male goats, 60 male one-year-old lambs. All of those were part of the dedication offerings for the altar after it was anointed.

[Census] [8]:[17] because every firstborn Israeli male person and animal belongs to me. I set them apart for myself when I killed every other firstborn in Mitsrayim (Egypt),

[Census] [8]:[19] Then I’ve given the Levites out of all the Israelis, to Aharon and his sons to serve the whole country by serving in the sacred tent and making the Israelis innocent in Yahweh’s eyes. That way, a deadly disease won’t strike the Israelis when they approach the sacred tent.”

[Census] [9]:[1] Then Yahweh spoke to Mosheh (Moses) in the Sinay wilderness, in the first month of the second year after they’d left Mitsrayim (Egypt),
[Census] [9]:[2] “The Israelis must observe ‘pass-over’ at the appointed time.
[Census] [9]:[3] You all must celebrate it on the evening of the 14th of this month, following all the instructions that you’ve all been given previously.”
[Census] [9]:[4] So Mosheh ordered the Israelis to prepare the ‘pass-over’,
[Census] [9]:[5] and they celebrated it in the Sinay wilderness starting on the evening of the 14th of that first month, following all the instructions that Yahweh had given Mosheh.
[Census] [9]:[6] However, there were some men who were ‘unclean’ (because they’d touched a dead body) and hence they weren’t able to celebrate the ‘pass-over’ that day, so they approached Mosheh and Aharon (Aaron)
[Census] [9]:[7] and asked them, “We were ‘unclean’ because we’d touched a dead body, but how come we’re excluded from presenting an offering to Yahweh along with the other Israelis?”
[Census] [9]:[8] “Wait here,” Mosheh answered, “and I’ll ask Yahweh what he wants you all to do.”
[Census] [9]:[9] Then Yahweh told Mosheh,
[Census] [9]:[10] “Tell the Israelis that for this and future generations, if a person is ‘unclean’ or far from home, then they can still observe Yahweh’s ‘pass-over’.
[Census] [9]:[11] They can start it on the evening of the 14th of the second month, and eat it as usual with flat bread and bitter herbs.
[Census] [9]:[12] They must not break any of the lambs bones, must not leave any of it until the morning, and must observe it following all the normal instructions.
[Census] [9]:[13] However, any person who isn’t ‘unclean’ or far away, but yet who didn’t celebrate the ‘pass-over’ that first month, must be driven out of the community and will have to bear their own sin.
[Census] [9]:[14] If an outsider is living among you and celebrates the ‘pass-over’, they must also do it according to all the same instructions—there’s only one way to do it whether it’s you all, or a foreigner, or a native of the land.
[Census] [9]:[15] When the sacred tent was dedicated, the cloud covered the inner room of the tent, and every evening it would look like fire above the residence, until morning came.
[Census] [9]:[16] It remained like that continually—the cloud would cover it during the day, and then at night, it would appear like fire.
[Census] [9]:[17] Whenever the cloud would be lifted up from the tent, then the Israelis would leave that place. Then wherever the cloud settled down, that’s where the Israelis would set up camp,
[Census] [9]:[18] so in that way, the Israelis would leave a place whenever Yahweh told them, and would set up camp whenever he told them. As long as the cloud stayed above the residence, they would stay camped in that place.
[Census] [9]:[19] Whenever the cloud remained above the residence for a long time, then the Israelis would follow Yahweh’s guidance and wouldn’t pack up camp.
[Census] [9]:[20] Sometimes the cloud would only remain above the residence for a few days, in which case they’d leave where they’d just camped, and move on as Yahweh commanded.
[Census] [9]:[21] If the cloud was lifted up the next morning, then they’d move on—in fact whether day or night if the cloud was lifted up, then they would move on.
[Census] [9]:[22] Whether it was two days or a month or a year that the cloud stayed above the residence, then the Israeli camp would remain in that place, until eventually moving on when it was lifted up again.
[Census] [9]:[23] In that way, when Yahweh ordered them to camp, they would, and when order to move on, they’d do that—thus they obeyed Yahweh’s instructions to Mosheh (Moses).
[Census] [10]:[1] Then Yahweh told Mosheh (Moses),
[Census] [10]:[2] “Make two hammered silver trumpets for yourself to use for assembling the community and for signalling when it’s time to leave the camp.
[Census] [10]:[3] When both are sounded, the whole community is to assemble in front of you at the entrance to the sacred tent.
[Census] [10]:[4] If just one is sounded, then it’s only the leaders and heads of clans who must assemble.
[Census] [10]:[5] A single blast means that the camps on the eastern side should start moving out.
[Census] [10]:[6] A double blast means that the camps on the southern side should start moving out. So the blasts will signal them to get going.
[Census] [10]:[7] (To assemble the community as above, use long blows, not short blasts.)
[Census] [10]:[8] The priests (Aharon’s (Aaron) descendants) must be the ones to blow the trumpets. That is a permanent regulation.
[Census] [10]:[9] When you need to defend yourselves against an attacker, then you must sound an alarm with the trumpets, and you’ll all be noticed by Yahweh, and you’ll be saved from your enemies.
[Census] [10]:[10] On festival days and at times of celebrations and at the beginning of each new month, then the trumpets will be blown as the burnt offerings and peace offerings are made as a memorial for you all towards your god. I am your god, Yahweh.

[Census] [10]:[20] Deuel’s son Elyasaf led the company from Gad tribe.

[Census] [10]:[22] Efrayim (Ephraim) tribe with their banner was next to leave under the leadership of Amihud’s son Elishama.
[Census] [10]:[23] Pedahtsur’s son Gamliel led the company from Menasheh (Manasseh) tribe.
[Census] [10]:[24] Gid’oni’s son Avidan led the company from Benyamin tribe.
[Census] [10]:[25] Dan tribe with their banner was last to leave as the rear guard under the leadership of Amishaday’s son Ahiezer.
[Census] [10]:[26] Okran’s son Pagiel led the company from Asher tribe.
[Census] [10]:[27] Eynan’s son Ahira led the company from Naftali (Naphtali) tribe.
[Census] [10]:[28] That was the order of the departures of the companies of the Israeli tribes when they set off.
[Census] [10]:[29] Then Mosheh (Moses) told Hovav (son of the Midyanite Re’uel who was Mosheh’s father-in-law), “We’re heading towards the place that Yahweh said he’d give us. Come and join us, and we’ll look after you, because Yahweh has promised to look after Yisrael (Israel).”
[Census] [10]:[30] “Thank you but no,” Hovav replied, “I’ll return to my land and to my relatives.”
[Census] [10]:[31] “Please don’t leave us,” Mosheh insisted, “because you’re the one who knows about camping in the wilderness, and you could be our guide.
[Census] [10]:[32] When you come with us, Yahweh will be blessing us so we’ll also bless you.”
[Census] [10]:[33] Then they left Yahweh’s mountain and travelled for three days, with the box containing Yahweh’s agreement being carried at the front to find a resting place for them,
[Census] [10]:[34] and Yahweh’s cloud was over them each day as they set out from their stop.
[Census] [10]:[35] As the box started moving, Mosheh would say, “Yahweh, take action and then your enemies will scatter, and the ones hating you will flee away from your presence.”
[Census] [10]:[36] Then at the end of the day when it came to rest, he would say, “Yahweh, return to the tens of thousands of Israelis.”
[Census] [11]:[1] One day, the people were complaining about their situation and when Yahweh heard them, it made him angry so he sent a fire that burnt up the edges of their camp.
[Census] [11]:[2] The people cried out to Mosheh (Moses) for help, and he prayed to Yahweh, and the fire stopped,
[Census] [11]:[3] and they named that place Tav’erah (which means ‘burning’) because Yahweh’s fire had burnt among them.
[Census] [11]:[4] However, there was a group of stirrers among the people that badly wanted to have meat and other foods to eat. That spread to all the Israelis who wept and asked, “Who’ll give us meat to eat?
[Census] [11]:[5] We remember the fish that we ate in Mitsrayim (Egypt) for free, as well as the cucumbers, melons, leeks, onions, and garlic,
[Census] [11]:[6] but now our appetite has shrivelled up because we don’t see anything to eat except this ‘stuff’.”
[Census] [11]:[7] (The ‘stuff’ they ate every day was a bit like coriander seed except kind of clear.
[Census] [11]:[8] Each morning the people went around gathering it, then ground it with a stone mill or pounded it in a mortar, then they boiled it and made something like bread rolls with it. They tasted like fresh olive oil.
[Census] [11]:[9] The ‘stuff’ actually descended on the camp during the night with the dew.)
[Census] [11]:[10] Mosheh (Moses) heard the people weeping in their tents (set up by tribe and clan). He thought it was wrong, and it made Yahweh very angry.
[Census] [11]:[11] So Mosheh asked Yahweh, “Why have you caused me, your servant, to be in trouble like this? Don’t you approve of me?. Why has the burden of all this people group landed on me?
[Census] [11]:[12] Was it me who conceived it? Did I carry it to the land promised to their ancestors, like I was a wet-nurse?
[Census] [11]:[13] All these people come to me to ask me to give them meat to eat. Where would I get enough meat to feed all them?
[Census] [11]:[14] I can’t bear the load of this entire people group by myself—it’s too heavy for me.
[Census] [11]:[15] If that’s what you’re doing to me, please kill me now if I’ve found favour in your eyes. Then I wouldn’t have to suffer like this.”
[Census] [11]:[16] Then Yahweh told Mosheh, “Bring me seventy of Yisrael’s (Israel) elders who you know are good leaders, and take them to the sacred tent, and let them take their positions there with you.
[Census] [11]:[17] I’ll come down and talk with you there, and I’ll take some of the spirit that’s on you and put it on them, and then they’ll carry the burden of the people along with you. Then you won’t have to carry it by yourself.
[Census] [11]:[18] Also, tell the people that because they wept in my hearing about not having meat to eat like you all did in Mitsrayim (Egypt), they must purify themselves for tomorrow, because I’ll provide meat for you all to eat.
[Census] [11]:[19] You won’t just have meat for a day or two, or for five, ten, or twenty days,
[Census] [11]:[20] you have it for a whole month until it comes out your nostrils. Yes, it’ll make you all nauseous because you rejected Yahweh who’s among you, and you all wept in front of him, complaining, ‘Why did we ever leave Mitsrayim?’ ”
[Census] [11]:[21] Mosheh queried, “There’s 600,000 able to serve in the army plus women and children, yet you say that you’ll give them all enough meat to eat every day for month!
[Census] [11]:[22] Even if we killed all the cattle and sheep, or caught all the fish in the sea, that wouldn’t be enough meat for all them.”
[Census] [11]:[23] “Do you think that Yahweh’s powerless?” Yahweh replied. “Soon you’ll see whether or not my statement will come true.”
[Census] [11]:[24] So Mosheh went out and passed on Yahweh’s message to the people. Then he gathered seventy men from the Israeli elders and stood them around the tent.
[Census] [11]:[25] Then Yahweh came down in the cloud and spoke to Mosheh, and he took some of the spirit away from him and put it on those seventy elders. As the spirit rested on them, they prophesied (but they never did that again).
[Census] [11]:[26] Two of the men who were listed (named Eldad and Medad), had remained in the main camp (not going to the sacred tent), and the spirit had also rested on them and they prophesied in the camp.
[Census] [11]:[27] A young man ran to Mosheh and told him that Eldad and Medad were prophesying there in the camp.
[Census] [11]:[28] Then Nun’s son Yehoshua (Joshua) (who had helped Mosheh since his youth) responded, “My master Mosheh, stop them from that.”
[Census] [11]:[29] But Mosheh replied, “Are you being jealous on my behalf? I’d be happy if Yahweh would put his spirit on all the people and make them into prophets.”
[Census] [11]:[30] Then Mosheh and the elders went back to their tents.
[Census] [11]:[31] Then Yahweh sent a wind that blew quails from the ocean, and they dropped on the ground a day’s walk in every direction around the camp until they were piled a metre high.
[Census] [11]:[32] So the people went out and collected the quail—each family getting at least the equivalent of ten large barrels full, and they spread the meat around the camp to sun dry.
[Census] [11]:[33] Then when they started to cook and eat some of the fresh meat, Yahweh got very angry and struck the people with a terrible deadly disease before they could even chew it.
[Census] [11]:[34] So that place was named Kivrot-Hata’avah (which means ‘Graves of the cravers’), because that was where they buried the people who had craved meat.
[Census] [11]:[35] From Kivrot-Hata’avah, the people moved on to Hatserot and stayed there.
[Census] [12]:[1] One day, Miryam (Miriam) and Aharon (Aaron) spoke out against Mosheh (Moses) because he’d taken an Kushi (Ethiopian) woman (Kushit) as a wife,
[Census] [12]:[2] and they challenged, “Did Yahweh really only speak through Mosheh? Doesn’t he also speak through us?” Yahweh heard what they said.
[Census] [12]:[3] (Now Mosheh was actually a very humble man—more humble than anyone else alive.)
[Census] [12]:[4] Then Yahweh suddenly told Mosheh, Aharon, and Miryam, “Go out, the three of you, to the sacred tent.” So the three of them went there.
[Census] [12]:[5] and Yahweh descended in a pillar of cloud and stood at the tent opening and called Aharon and Miryam, and the two of them stepped forward,
[Census] [12]:[6] and he said, “Listen to me. When there’s a prophet of Yahweh, I make myself known to him in a vision and speak to him in a dream,
[Census] [12]:[7] but I don’t do that to my servant Mosheh. He’s the most faithful of all my people
[Census] [12]:[8] and I speak to him directly—face-to-face, and not in parables, and he’s able to see my form. So why weren’t you afraid to speak against my servant Mosheh?”
[Census] [12]:[9] So Yahweh was angry at Miryam and Aharon. Then he departed
[Census] [12]:[10] and the cloud moved from the tent. Then wow, Miryam had leprosy—her skin had gone as white as snow. As Aharon turned to her, he saw, wow, she was leprous,
[Census] [12]:[11] and he begged Mosheh, “Please, my master, please don’t make us suffer for our foolish disrespect and disobedience.
[Census] [12]:[12] Don’t let her be like a still-born baby that’s already starting to decompose when its mother gives birth to it.
[Census] [12]:[13] So Mosheh pleaded with Yahweh, “God, please, please heal her!”
[Census] [12]:[14] “If her father had spit in her face, wouldn’t she stay inside in disgrace for seven days?” Yahweh replied. “So she must be put outside the camp for seven days, then after that, she can enter again.”
[Census] [12]:[15] So Miryam was sent outside the camp for seven days, and the people didn’t move on until after she was allowed to return.
[Census] [12]:[16] After that, the people left Hatserot and set up camp in the Paran wilderness.

[Census] [13]:[24] (That place was then called Eshkol, meaning ‘cluster’, because of the cluster of grapes they’d taken from there.)
[Census] [13]:[25] Forty days later, they returned from exploring that land

[Census] [13]:[29] The Amaleki people live in the Negev, and the Hitim, Yevusim, and Amorim live in the hill country, and the Kena’anim (Canaanites) live along the coast and along the Yarden (Jordan) river.”

[Census] [13]:[31] But the men who’d gone in with him argued, “No,, we’re not able to battle against them because they’re stronger than us.”
[Census] [13]:[32] Then they went on to bring out a bad report to the Israelis about the land that they’d explored, saying, “The land that we passed to explore is a land that devours those who live in it. In addition, all the people we saw in there were tall and powerful,
[Census] [13]:[33] plus we saw the Nefilim (descendants of Anak), and we felt as small as grasshoppers compared to them, and that’s how they saw us as well.”
[Census] [14]:[1] The assembled people cried loudly that entire night,
[Census] [14]:[2] and then they started to protest against Mosheh (Moses) and Aharon (Aaron). They were all saying, “If only we’d died in Mitsrayim (Egypt) or back there in this wilderness.

[Census] [14]:[17] So may the power of my master be great, just as you’ve previously said,
[Census] [14]:[18] ‘Yahweh is slow to anger and quick to show loyal commitment, forgiving disobedience and rebellion. Yet he doesn’t leave the guilty unpunished, bringing the consequences of the father’s disobedience onto the next three generations.’

[Census] [14]:[24] However, my servant Kalev (Caleb) has a different spirit with him, and he wholeheartedly followed me, so I’ll take him into the land that he explored, and his descendants will inherit it.

[Census] [15]:[1] Then Yahweh told Mosheh (Moses),

[Census] [15]:[6] For a ram, there must also be a grain offering of two kilograms of fine flour mixed with 1.2 litres of oil
[Census] [15]:[7] plus 1.2 litres of wine, all to be presented as a pleasing aroma to Yahweh.

[Census] [27]:[1] Then the daughters of Tselofehad (son of Hefer, son of Gilead, son of Makir, son of Menasheh (Manasseh)) approached. Their names were Mahlah, Noa, Hoglah, Milkah, and Tirtsah.

[Census] [27]:[5] So Mosheh took their case to Yahweh
[Census] [27]:[6] and he responded,

[Census] [27]:[8] Also, tell the people that if a man dies without sons, then his inheritance should go to his daughter(s).
[Census] [27]:[9] If he had no children, then it should go to his brothers,
[Census] [27]:[10] and if he has no brothers, then it should go to his father’s brothers.
[Census] [27]:[11] However, if his father had no brothers, then the inheritance should go to his nearest blood-relative to become his possession. That will become a permanent regulation for Yisrael (Israel), just as Yahweh has commanded.”

[Census] [30]:[1] Then Mosheh (Moses) gave the Israeli leaders these further instructions from Yahweh,
[Census] [30]:[2] “If a man makes a solemn promise to Yahweh, or makes a binding vow on his own life, he mustn’t dishonour what he said—he must follow whatever came out of his mouth.
[Census] [30]:[3] If a young woman who is still living with her parents solemnly promises to Yahweh to do something,
[Census] [30]:[4] and if her father hears her make the binding vow on her life and he remains silent, then her vow and all her obligations will stand.
[Census] [30]:[5] However, if her father forbids her when he hears her, then that vow and its obligations won’t stand, and Yahweh will forgive her, because her father stepped in.
[Census] [30]:[6] If she gets engaged or married while a vow or thoughtless promise still holds,
[Census] [30]:[7] and her (future) husband hears about it and remains silent that day, then her vow and or thoughtless promise will stand.
[Census] [30]:[8] However, if her (future) husband forbids her when he hears her, then that vow and its obligations won’t stand, and Yahweh will forgive her.
[Census] [30]:[9] If a widow or a woman who has been divorced makes a promise, she must do what she promised.
[Census] [30]:[10] If a married woman makes a solemn promise, or makes a binding vow on her own life,
[Census] [30]:[11] and her husband hears about it but says nothing and doesn’t forbid her, then her vow and all her obligations will stand.
[Census] [30]:[12] However, if he actually nullifies it when he hears about it, any promise that she pronounced or binding vow on her life, won’t stand. Her husband has nullified them and Yahweh will forgive her,
[Census] [30]:[13] so every vow and its obligations can either be nullified or confirmed by her husband.
[Census] [30]:[14] If her husband has stayed silent for several days, that will confirm all her vows and/or obligations because he said nothing.
[Census] [30]:[15] However, if he cancels them sometime after he’d heard about them, then he will bear her guilt.
[Census] [30]:[16] Those are the instructions that Yahweh gave Mosheh (Moses) about promises between a man and his wife, and between a father and his unmarried daughter living at home.
