[Census] [32]:[32] We’ll send armed men across to Kena’an, equipped to fight for Yahweh. However, our inheritance to own will be here on this side of the Yarden river.”
[Census] [32]:[33] So Mosheh gave that region to the tribes of Re’uven and Gad, the half-tribe of Yosef’s (Joseph) son Menasheh (Manasseh), encompassing the kingdoms of the Amori King Sihon and the Bashan’s King Og, plus the surrounding territories.
[Census] [32]:[34] The Gadim rebuilt Divon, Atarot, Aroer,
[Census] [32]:[35] Atrot-Shofan, Yazer, Yagebehah,
[Census] [32]:[36] Beyt-Nimrah, and Beyt-Haran—all fortified cities with pens for their flocks.
[Census] [32]:[37] The Re’uvenim rebuilt Heshbon, El’aleh, Kiryatayim,
[Census] [32]:[38] Nevo, Ba’al-Me’on, and Sivmah, but they renamed some of the cities.
[Census] [32]:[39] The descendants of Menasheh’s son Makir went to Gilead and captured it—driving out the Amorim who lived there.
[Census] [32]:[40] So Mosheh gave Gilead to Menasheh’s son Makir, and his clan lived there.
[Census] [32]:[41] Menasheh’s other son Yair went and captured the Amori villages and named them ‘Yair’s Towns’ (or ‘Havot-Ya’ir’).
[Census] [32]:[42] A man named Novah went and captured Kenat and its villages, and renamed it to ‘Novah’ after himself.
[Census] [33]:[1] The following are the details of the stages of Yisrael’s (Israel) journeys starting from when they exited Mitsrayim (Egypt) tribe-by-tribe under Mosheh (Moses) and Aharon’s (Aaron) leadership.
[Census] [33]:[2] Mosheh, acting on Yahweh’s instructions, had written down their departure points, so these were the legs of their journeys:
[Census] [33]:[3] The day after they celebrated the ‘pass-over’ (around the end of March), they left Ra’meses city, raising one fist in full view of all Mitsrayim.
[Census] [33]:[4] Meanwhile, the Mitsrim (Egyptians) were burying all their oldest sons who’d been struck down by Yahweh who had also totally humiliated their gods.
[Census] [33]:[5] After leaving Ra’meses, the Israelis went to Sukot and camped there.
[Census] [33]:[6] Then they left Sukot and camped at Eytam at the edge of the wilderness.
[Census] [33]:[7] After Eytam, they turned back to Pi-Hahirot (opposite Ba’al-Tsefon) and camped facing Migdal.
[Census] [33]:[8] Then they left Pi-Hahirot and walked through the middle of the sea into the Eytam wilderness and camped at Marah.
[Census] [33]:[9] From Marah, they went to Eylim which had twelve springs with seventy palm trees around them, and they camped there.
[Census] [33]:[10] After Eylam, they camped beside the Red Sea
[Census] [33]:[11] before leaving the sea and camping in the Sin wilderness.
[Census] [33]:[12] Travelling from there, they camped at Dofkah,
[Census] [33]:[13] and then from there, at Alush.
[Census] [33]:[14] After leaving Alush, they camped at Refidim but they didn’t have water there to drink.
[Census] [33]:[15] When they left Refidim, they camped in the Sinay wilderness.
[Census] [33]:[16] From the Sinay wilderness, they went to Kivrot-Hata’avah and camped there.
[Census] [33]:[17] When they left Kivrot-Hata’avah, they camped at Hatserot,
[Census] [33]:[18] and then from there, at Ritmah.
[Census] [33]:[19] From Ritmah, they went to Rimon-Perets to camp,
[Census] [33]:[20] and after that, on to Livnah.
[Census] [33]:[21] Then they left Livnah and camped at Risah,
[Census] [33]:[22] before moving on from there to camp at Kehelatah.
[Census] [33]:[23] From Kehelatah, they camped at Mt. Shefer,
[Census] [33]:[24] then they left the mountain and camped at Haradah.
[Census] [33]:[25] When they left Haradah, they camped at Makhelot,
[Census] [33]:[26] and after that, on to Tahat.
[Census] [33]:[27] From Tahat, they camped at Terah,
[Census] [33]:[28] and then from Terah, they went to Mitkah to camp.
[Census] [33]:[29] After Mitkah, they camped at Hashmonah,
[Census] [33]:[30] and next after that, they camped at Moserot.
[Census] [33]:[31] Then they left Moserot and camped at Beney-Ya’akan.
[Census] [33]:[32] From Beney-Ya’akan, they went to Hor-Hagidgad and camped there,
[Census] [33]:[33] then they left and camped at Yotvatah.
[Census] [33]:[34] Then they left Yotvatah and camped at Avronah.
[Census] [33]:[35] From Avronah, they went to Etsyon-Gever and camped there,
[Census] [33]:[36] then they left and camped in the Tsin (Zin) wilderness, i.e., at Kadesh.
[Census] [33]:[37] Then they left Kadesh and camped at Mt. Hor by the border with Edom.
[Census] [33]:[38] Aharon (Aaron) the priest climbed Mt. Hor following Yahweh’s instructions, and then died there on the 5th of the first month, forty years after the Israelis had left Mitsrayim (Egypt).
[Census] [33]:[39] He was 123 years old when he died there on Mt. Hor.
[Census] [33]:[40] Meanwhile, the Kena’ani (Canaanite) king of Arad who lived in the Negev in Kena’an (Canaan), heard that the Israelis were coming.
[Census] [33]:[41] The Israelis left Mt. Hor and camped at Tsalmonah.
[Census] [33]:[42] When they left Tsalmonah, they camped at Punon,
[Census] [33]:[43] and after that, on to Ovot.
[Census] [33]:[44] From Ovot, they went on to Iyey-Ha’avarim at the Moav (Moab) border.
[Census] [33]:[45] Then they left there and camped at Divon-Gad,
[Census] [33]:[46] before going on to camp at Almon-Divlatayim.
[Census] [33]:[47] From there, they went into the Avarim mountains and camped facing Nevo.
[Census] [33]:[48] After leaving the Avarim mountains, they reached the Moav plains by the Yarden (Jordan) river opposite Yeriho (Jericho).
[Census] [33]:[49] They camped beside the river from Beyt-Hayeshimot to Avel-Hashitim there on the Moav plains.
[Census] [33]:[50] Then Yahweh spoke to Mosheh (Moses) there on the Moav plains beside the Yarden opposite Yeriho,
[Census] [33]:[51] “Tell the Israelis that you’re all about to cross the Yahweh to enter Kena’an (Canaan).
[Census] [33]:[52] Then you all must drive all the land’s inhabitants out ahead of you, and destroy all their carved images and cast metal images, and all their hilltop shrines.
[Census] [33]:[53] Take the land from there and start to live there, because I’ve given it to all of you to own.
[Census] [33]:[54] Use lots to divide the land up for your clans. The larger groups must get more than the smaller groups, then whatever the lot gives, that will be the area to be given within the land for that ancestral tribe.
[Census] [33]:[55] If you don’t drive out the current inhabitants, then they’ll become like barbs in your eyes and thorns in your sides, and they’ll harass you all when you live there.
[Census] [33]:[56] If that happens, then I’ll give you all the punishment that I intended for them.”
[Census] [34]:[1] Then Yahweh told Mosheh (Moses),
[Census] [34]:[2] “Tell the people that you’re all about to enter Kena’an (Canaan)—the land that will become your inheritance. The boundaries will be:
[Census] [34]:[3] “The southern border will extend from the Tsin (Zin) wilderness along the Edom border across to the Salt (Dead) Sea on the east,
[Census] [34]:[4] cross south of the Scorpion Pass, continue to Tsin, and go south of Kadesh-Barnea. Then it will go on to Hatsar-Adar and proceed to Atsmon,
[Census] [34]:[5] From Atsmon it will extend west to the riverbed at the border with Mitsrayim (Egypt), and then across to the Mediterranean Sea.
[Census] [34]:[6] “The western border will be the Mediterranean sea.
[Census] [34]:[7] “The northern border will start at the Mediterranean sea and extend west to Mt. Hor,
[Census] [34]:[8] and then on to Levo-Hamat and onward to Tsedad.
[Census] [34]:[9] From there the border will extend to Zifron, and it will end at Hatsar-Eynan, completing the northern border.
[Census] [34]:[10] “The eastern border will begin at Hatsar-Eynan and extend south to Shefam,
[Census] [34]:[11] then go downhill to Rivlah east of Ayin, then along the hills to the east of Lake Kineret.
[Census] [34]:[12] Then the border will extend south along the Yarden (Jordan) River and end at the Salt (Dead) Sea. “Those will be your country’s borders.”
[Census] [34]:[13] Then Mosheh (Moses) continued, “That will be the land that must be distributed by lot. It’ll be given by Yahweh as an inheritance for the nine tribes and the Menasheh (Manasseh) half-tribe
[Census] [34]:[14] as the Re’uven and Gad tribes and the Menasheh half-tribe have already received their inheritance.
[Census] [34]:[15] Yes, the other two and a half tribes have taken up their inheritance on the eastern side of the Yarden river across from Yeriho (Jericho).
[Census] [34]:[16] Then Yahweh told Mosheh (Moses),
[Census] [34]:[17] “These are the men who will distribute the land: the priest Eleazar and Nun’s son Yehoshua (Joshua),
[Census] [34]:[18] as well as one leader from each tribe to allocate the land that will be their inheritance.
[Census] [34]:[19] Those tribe leaders are: From Yehudah (Judah), Yefuneh’s son Kalev (Caleb),
[Census] [34]:[20] From Shim’on (Simeon), Amihud’s son Shmuel (Samuel),
[Census] [34]:[21] From Benyamin, Kislon’s son Elidad,
[Census] [34]:[22] From Dan, Yogli’s son Buki,
[Census] [34]:[23] From Menasheh (Manasseh), Efod’s son Haniyel,
[Census] [34]:[24] From Efrayim (Ephraim), Shiftan’s son Kemuel,
[Census] [34]:[25] From Zevulun, Parnak’s son Elitsafan,
[Census] [34]:[26] From Yisakar (Issachar), Azan’s son Paltiel,
[Census] [34]:[27] From Asher, Shelomi’s son Ahihud,
[Census] [34]:[28] From Naftali (Naphtali), Amihud’s son Pedahel.”
[Census] [34]:[29] The above are the men that Yahweh put in charge of dividing up Kena’an (Canaan) as the inheritance for the Israelis.
[Census] [35]:[1] While they were there on the Moav (Moab) plains beside the Yarden (Jordan) river, Yahweh told Mosheh (Moses).
[Census] [35]:[2] “Tell the Israelis that out of the land that they’ll own, they must give the Levites cities for them to live in, as well as some pastureland around those cities.
[Census] [35]:[3] The cities will be for them to live in, and that pastureland will be for their herds and their flocks, and for their other animals.
[Census] [35]:[4] The pastureland must extend out half a kilometre around the walls of the Levites cities.
[Census] [35]:[5] Then going out a kilometre in each compass direction, that will also be their land.
[Census] [35]:[6] The Levites must be given forty-two cities to live in, plus you all must designate six refuge cities so that if someone accidentally kills another, they can flee to the refuge city.
[Census] [35]:[7] That would make a total of forty-eight cities, plus their pasturelands, to be given to the Levites.
[Census] [35]:[8] The larger tribes must give more cities than the smaller tribes, according to the area that they inherit.”
[Census] [35]:[9] Then Yahweh told Mosheh (Moses),
[Census] [35]:[10] “Tell the Israelis that when you cross the Yarden (Jordan) river to enter Kena’an (Canaan),
[Census] [35]:[11] you all must choose some cities to become ‘refuge cities’ so that if someone accidentally kills another person, they can flee there.
[Census] [35]:[12] The cities will be places to stay safe from being avenged by the relatives until the killer can be formally tried.
[Census] [35]:[13] You all must allocate six refuge cities—
[Census] [35]:[14] three on the eastern side of the Yarden, and there on the western side in Kena’an.
[Census] [35]:[15] Both Israelis and foreigners living in the country can flee to any of those six cities—anyone who kills another person by accident.
[Census] [35]:[16] “However, if someone strikes another person with a metal object and they die, then that person is a murderer, and murderers must be executed.
[Census] [35]:[17] Similarly, anyone who strikes another person when holding a rock or stone, then that person is a murderer, and murderers must be executed.
[Census] [35]:[18] Again, if someone strikes another person with a piece of wood, then that person is a murderer, and murderers must be executed.
[Census] [35]:[19] The relative who is avenging the spilt blood must execute the murderer as soon as he finds them.
[Census] [35]:[20] “If someone pushes another person in hatred, or lies in wait and then throws something at them,
[Census] [35]:[21] or angrily strikes them with their hand, and then they die, it must be regarded as murder, and when the avenger of their blood finds the murderer, he must execute them.
[Census] [35]:[22] “But if someone pushes another person without any hateful intent, or throws something at them without lying in wait,
[Census] [35]:[23] or drops a rock without noticing someone, and they die but they weren’t that person’s enemy and no harm was intended,
[Census] [35]:[24] then the community must judge between the one who killed and the avenger of the dead person, in accordance with these regulations.
[Census] [35]:[25] If the one who killed is declared innocent, then the community must rescue them from the avenger and return them to the refuge city that they’d fled to, and that accidental killer must live there until after the death of the high priest (who had been anointed with sacred oil).
[Census] [35]:[26] However, if they then ever left the refuge city that they’d fled to,
[Census] [35]:[27] and the avenger found them outside the city boundary, then that relative of the dead person is permitted to kill that person and won’t be accountable for their blood.
[Census] [35]:[28] That’s because the one who killed must remain in that city until the death of the high priest—they can only return to their family home after the high priest’s death.
[Census] [35]:[29] You all must follow these regulations through the generations no matter where you live.
[Census] [35]:[30] “If someone murders another person, they’re to be executed if there’s evidence from witnesses (plural, not just one witness).
[Census] [35]:[31] That sentence can’t be changed to a fine and/or a payment to the deceased’s family—the murderer must be executed.
[Census] [35]:[32] Similarly for the accidental killer who fled to a refuge city, they can’t elect to pay a fine and/or pay compensation in order to be able to return home before the high priest’s death.
[Census] [35]:[33] You mustn’t profane the land that you’re all going to by tolerating murder, because human blood pollutes the ground, and you all can’t restore the land with any sacrifice—only by the blood of the one who shed someone else’s blood.
[Census] [35]:[34] You mustn’t profane the land that you’ll all be living in because I’ll also be living in it, as I will live among you Israelis.”
[Census] [36]:[1] Now the leaders of the Gilead clans (Gilead was the son of Makir, son of Menasheh (Manasseh), one of Yosef’s (Joseph) sons) approached Mosheh (Moses) and the Israeli leaders
[Census] [36]:[2] and said, “Yahweh commanded my master to distribute the land by lot as an inheritance for the people, and my master was also commanded by Yahweh to give our brother Tselofehad’s inheritance to his daughters.
[Census] [36]:[3] However, if they ended up being married by men from other tribes, then their inheritance would pass from our tribe to their husbands’ tribes, so we’d end up with less land as our tribal inheritance.
[Census] [36]:[4] Then when Yisrael (Israel) celebrates the Jubilee Year, then that inheritance will be added to the inheritance of their husbands’ tribes, and be deducted from the inheritance of our ancestral tribe.”
[Census] [36]:[5] Then Mosheh gave a ruling to the Israelis in accordance with what Yahweh had told him, “These Yosefi men are correct.
[Census] [36]:[6] Yahweh’s command to Tselofehad’s daughters is that each of you may marry whoever you want as long as it’s someone from your own tribe.
[Census] [36]:[7] That way, land in Yisrael won’t move from tribe to tribe, because it will always stay as part of the inheritance given to that tribe.
[Census] [36]:[8] Any woman who inherits land can only marry someone from her own tribe, so that the people will always retain ownership of their tribal inheritance.
[Census] [36]:[9] That inheritance mustn’t pass from tribe to tribe, but each Israeli tribe must keep hold of its inheritance.”
[Census] [36]:[10] So Tselofehad’s daughters obeyed what Yahweh had told Mosheh,
[Census] [36]:[11] and the five daughters (Mahlah, Tirtsah, Hoglah, Milkah, and Noa) married their cousins on their father’s side.
[Census] [36]:[12] The men they married were from the Menasheh (Manasseh) tribe (Yosef’s (Joseph) son), so their land continued to belong to their father’s family and tribe.
[Census] [36]:[13] All the above were the commands and regulations that Yahweh ordered Mosheh to tell the Israelis, while they were camped on the Moav (Moab) plains beside the Yarden (Jordan) river opposite Yeriho (Jericho).
[Deuteronomy] [1]:[1] These are the messages that Mosheh (Moses) spoke to Yisrael (Israel) back when they were in the wilderness on the eastern side of the Yarden (Jordan) river, in the desert plain opposite Suf between Paran and Tofel, Lavan (Laban), Hatserot, and Di-Zahav.
[Deuteronomy] [1]:[2] (It takes eleven days to walk from Horev to Kadesh-Barnea via Mt. Se’ir.)
[Deuteronomy] [1]:[3] Forty years after the Israelis had left Mitsrayim (Egypt) Mosheh passed on to them everything that Yahweh had instructed him
[Deuteronomy] [1]:[4] after he’d defeated the Amori King Sihon who lived at Heshbon, and Bashan King Og who lived at Ashtarot in Edre’i.
[Deuteronomy] [1]:[5] On the eastern side of the Yarden river in the Moav (Moab) region, Mosheh began explaining those instructions, saying,
[Deuteronomy] [1]:[6] “Our God Yahweh spoke to us at Horev, saying: You’ve camped here long enough at this mountain.
[Deuteronomy] [1]:[7] Now, pack up and travel to the Amori hill country and the surrounding areas and the river plain, the lowlands and the southern wilderness, the coastal plain, all of Kena’an (Canaan), and Levanon as far north-east as the Perat (Euphrates) river.
[Deuteronomy] [1]:[8] Listen, that area of land ahead of you, I’ve given to you. Go ahead and take possession that land that Yahweh promised to your ancestors Avraham, Yitshak (Isaac), and Ya’akov (Jacob). He promised to give it to them and to their descendants.”
[Deuteronomy] [1]:[9] Then Mosheh (Moses) said, “I told you at that time that I wasn’t able to govern all of you by myself
[Deuteronomy] [1]:[10] because your god Yahweh has multiplied you, and wow, now you’re as numerous as the stars in the sky.
[Deuteronomy] [1]:[11] May your ancestors’ god Yahweh increase you all a thousand times more and bless you all as he’s promised
[Deuteronomy] [1]:[12] but how could I possibly bear all your loads and burdens and disputes by myself?
[Deuteronomy] [1]:[13] So nominate some men from your tribes who I can appoint as your leaders—men who are sensible and wise, and respected by the people,
[Deuteronomy] [1]:[14] and your parents agreed with that suggestion.
[Deuteronomy] [1]:[15] So I took those wise, respected men and appointed them to be your leaders—leaders of thousands, of hundreds, of fifties, and of tens. I also appointed some as your tribal officials.
[Deuteronomy] [1]:[16] Then I instructed your new leaders telling them to listen carefully to both sides of disputes and make fair and honest judgements in conflicts involving either Israelis or foreigners.
[Deuteronomy] [1]:[17] Don’t show partiality when you’re making a judgement—treat important people just the same as the others. Don’t worry about what people will think because fair judgement is a godly activity. And if any matter is too difficult, bring it to me for a decision.
[Deuteronomy] [1]:[18] I also gave you all other instructions at that time.
[Deuteronomy] [1]:[19] “Then we left Horev and went through that wide and dangerous wilderness that you saw on the way to the Amori hill country as our god Yahweh had instructed us, eventually arriving at Kadesh-Barnea.
[Deuteronomy] [1]:[20] Then I told you all, ‘You’ve all come to the Amori hill country, which our god Yahweh is giving us.
[Deuteronomy] [1]:[21] Look, your god Yahweh has given you the land that’s in front of you, so go ahead and take possession of it as Yahweh, your ancestors’ god has told you. Don’t be afraid and don’t be discouraged.’
[Deuteronomy] [1]:[22] Then you all approached me and suggested, ‘We should send some men ahead of us to scout out the place, and they can return and tell us the best way to get inside those cities.’
[Deuteronomy] [1]:[23] That sounded good to me, so I took one man from each of the twelve tribes
[Deuteronomy] [1]:[24] and they went up into the hill country as far as the Eshkol valley, and the scouted it out.
[Deuteronomy] [1]:[25] They picked some fruit from there and brought it back to us, and reported that the land that our god Yahweh is giving us was very good.
[Deuteronomy] [1]:[26] “But your parents were unwilling to proceed and rebelled against your god Yahweh’s command.
[Deuteronomy] [1]:[27] So you all grumbled in your tents, saying that it was because Yahweh hated us that he brought us out of Mitsrayim (Egypt) to hand us over to the Amorim to be destroyed.
[Deuteronomy] [1]:[28] You said that you all didn’t want to enter because the people were so tall and strong and their cities were fortified and powerful with very high walls around them.
[Deuteronomy] [1]:[29] “Then I told your parents, ‘Don’t be terrified or afraid of them.
[Deuteronomy] [1]:[30] Your god Yahweh who goes ahead of you, he’ll fight for you just like everything you saw him do in Mitsrayim
[Deuteronomy] [1]:[31] and in the wilderness, where you saw how your god Yahweh carried you like a father carries his son—getting you through that difficult region until you all eventually arrived here.’
[Deuteronomy] [1]:[32] However, you all didn’t believe your god Yahweh
[Deuteronomy] [1]:[33] who had gone ahead of you to find a good place for you all to make your camp—using fire at night to show you all the way, and cloud in the daytime.
[Deuteronomy] [1]:[34] “Yahweh heard those complaints and got angry and made this promise,
[Deuteronomy] [1]:[35] ‘None of the men of this evil generation will get to enter the good land that I promised to give to your ancestors
[Deuteronomy] [1]:[36] apart from Yefuneh’s son Kalev (Caleb)—he can enter it and I’ll give him and his sons the land that he scouted out because he followed Yahweh whole-heartedly.’
[Deuteronomy] [1]:[37] Yahweh was also angry at me because of you all, and told me that I also wouldn’t be able to enter,
[Deuteronomy] [1]:[38] but that Nun’s son Yehoshua (Joshua) who was standing there in front of me, would be the one to lead Yisrael (Israel) to possess the land.
[Deuteronomy] [1]:[39] “Your children that you thought would be taken captive, and your young sons who don’t yet know right from wrong, they’ll be the ones to enter the land, and I’ll give it to them, and it’ll become theirs.
[Deuteronomy] [1]:[40] But you yourselves need to turn around and go back into the wilderness in the direction of the Red Sea.
[Deuteronomy] [1]:[41] “but they all answered and admitted, ‘Yes, we’ve sinned against Yahweh, but now we’ll fix that by going in to fight and do everything that our god Yahweh has commanded us.’ So every man strapped on his weapons—now thinking it would be easy to take over the hill country.
[Deuteronomy] [1]:[42] “But Yahweh told me to warn them not to go ahead and fight because he wouldn’t help them, and so they’d end up being defeated by their enemies if they proceeded.
[Deuteronomy] [1]:[43] So I told your parents that, but they wouldn’t listen—they rebelled against Yahweh and arrogantly marched up into the hill country
[Deuteronomy] [1]:[44] where the Amorim who lived there came out against them, and chased them like bees and made the warriors scatter in Se’ir as far as Hormah.
[Deuteronomy] [1]:[45] So your parents returned and wept in front of Yahweh, but he didn’t pay any attention to them.
[Deuteronomy] [1]:[46] So that’s why we stayed at Kadesh-Barnea for as long as we all did.
[Deuteronomy] [2]:[1] “Then we turned and went back into the wilderness towards the Red Sea as Yahweh had told us to do, and we spent a long time wandering around Mt. Se’ir.
[Deuteronomy] [2]:[2] “Then Yahweh told me,
[Deuteronomy] [2]:[3] ‘You’ve all been wandering around this hilly area for long enough—now turn and go towards the north
[Deuteronomy] [2]:[4] and tell the people, “You’ll all be crossing the border into Se’ir where your relatives, Esav’s (Esau) descendants, live. They’ll be afraid of you but you’ll all need to stay very alert.
[Deuteronomy] [2]:[5] Don’t attack them because I won’t give you any of their land—not even a footprint size piece because I’ve given Mt. Se’ir to Esav as their inheritance.
[Deuteronomy] [2]:[6] Any food or drink you get from them must be paid for with cash
[Deuteronomy] [2]:[7] because your god Yahweh has blessed all of your labour—he’s always been aware of your travel through that vast wilderness. Your god Yahweh has helped you for those forty years so you’ve all had everything you need.” ’
[Deuteronomy] [2]:[8] “So we passed by our relatives, Esav’s descendants who live in Se’ir. We travelled along the Yarden (Jordan) valley plain from Eylot and Etsyon-Gever, then north through the Moav (Moab) wilderness.
[Deuteronomy] [2]:[9] Then Yahweh told me, ‘Don’t aggravate Moav, and don’t attack them, because I won’t give you any of their land because I’ve given Ar to the sons of Lot, as a possession.’ ”
[Deuteronomy] [2]:[10] (The Emim had lived their previously—there were many of them, and they were tall and strong like the Anakim.
[Deuteronomy] [2]:[11] People also call both the Emim and the Anakim, Refaim but the people of Moav (Moab) call them Emim.
[Deuteronomy] [2]:[12] The Horim had previously lived in Se’ir, but Esav’s (Esau) descendants had killed them and taken over their land, just like the Israelis did later in the land that Yahweh had given them to possess.)
[Deuteronomy] [2]:[13] “Then we crossed the Zered brook as Yahweh had told us to do.
[Deuteronomy] [2]:[14] It had been thirty-eight years since we first left Kadesh-Barnea until we cross the Zered brook, once that generation of warriors had died off, just as Yahweh had told them.
[Deuteronomy] [2]:[15] What’s more, Yahweh had opposed them, so he’d caused them to die.
[Deuteronomy] [2]:[16] “After all the enlistment-aged men had died,

[Deuteronomy] [2]:[18] ‘Today you must travel through the Moav region, near Ar,
[Deuteronomy] [2]:[19] and when you approach the Amoni region, don’t irritate or fight them because I won’t give you any of their land because I’ve given it to Lot’s descendants as a possession.’ ”
[Deuteronomy] [2]:[20] (Also, it’s regarded as the land of the Refaim, who the Amonim call the Zamzumim, who lived there in the past.
[Deuteronomy] [2]:[21] They were as numerous, and as tall and strong as the Anakim, but Yahweh destroyed them in advance of the Anakim who then dispossessed them and lived in their place.
[Deuteronomy] [2]:[22] He had done the same thing for Esav’s (Esau) descendants who live in Se’ir, when he destroyed the Horim ahead of them, and they took over their land and still live there to this day.
[Deuteronomy] [2]:[23] Also the Avim who lived in villages as far south as Azah (Gaza) were destroyed by the Kaftorim who came from Kraitai (Crete), and then lived in their place.)
[Deuteronomy] [2]:[24] “Yahweh had told us, ‘Get ready now and go through the Arnon river valley. I’ll help you defeat the Amori King Sihon from Heshbon. Attack him and begin to take over his land.

[Deuteronomy] [2]:[26] “Then from the Kedemot wilderness, I sent messengers to King Sihon at Heshbon with an offer of peace,

[Deuteronomy] [2]:[30] “However, Heshbon’s King Sihon wouldn’t let us go through his country because your god Yahweh had hardened his spirit and made him stubborn so that you could take his land, which we still have to this day.

[Deuteronomy] [2]:[33] but our god Yahweh helped us to defeat him, and we killed Sihon and his son, and all his people.
[Deuteronomy] [2]:[34] We captured all his cities at that time, and completely destroyed men, women and children in every city, leaving no survivors.
[Deuteronomy] [2]:[35] Only the cattle were taken as plunder for ourselves, along with the goods in the cities we captured.
[Deuteronomy] [2]:[36] Our god Yahweh helped us to capture all their towns from Aroer in the south at the edge of the Arnon River valley, to the Gilead region in the north—none of their city walls were too high for us.
[Deuteronomy] [2]:[37] However, you didn’t go near the Amoni region, the Yabok river area, the hill country towns, or any other place where our god Yahweh told us not to go.
[Deuteronomy] [3]:[1] “Then we turned and went towards the Bashan region but King Og came out with all his warriors to battle against us at Edre’i,
[Deuteronomy] [3]:[2] but Yahweh told me, ‘Don’t be afraid of him, because I’ve given him and all his people and his land over to you, and you’ll do the same to him that you did to the Amori King Sihon who lived at Heshbon.’
[Deuteronomy] [3]:[3] “So our god Yahweh also helped us defeat Bashan’s King Og and all his people, and we killed them all leaving no survivors.
[Deuteronomy] [3]:[4] We captured all sixty of King Og’s cities in the Argov region of Bashan,
[Deuteronomy] [3]:[5] even though they were all fortified with high walls and gates with bars. In addition, there were many rural villages.
[Deuteronomy] [3]:[6] We completely destroyed them like we’d done to Heshbon’s King Sihon—men, women, and children,
[Deuteronomy] [3]:[7] but we plundered all the cattle and the spoil from the cities for ourselves.
[Deuteronomy] [3]:[8] So at that time, we took the land from two of the Amori kings across on the eastern side of the Yarden (Jordan), from the Arnon River in the south, up to Mt. Hermon in the north
[Deuteronomy] [3]:[9] (called Mt. Siryon by the Tsidonim (Sidonians), and Mt. Senir by the Amorim).
[Deuteronomy] [3]:[10] We captured all the cities on the plain and all of the Gilead region, as well as Bashan as far east as Salkah and Edre’i cities, which also belonged to Og’s kingdom.”

[Deuteronomy] [3]:[14] Menasheh’s son Yair had captured the Argov region as far as the borders with the Geshurim and Ma’akatim, renaming Bashan to Havot-Ya’ir as it’s still called to this day.)
[Deuteronomy] [3]:[15] “Then I allocated Gilead to Makir (a clan descended from Menasheh),
[Deuteronomy] [3]:[16] and I gave the southern part of Gilead to the tribes of Re’uven and Gad, extending from the Arnon river (with the middle of it being the boundary) to the Yabok river which borders against the Amonim.
[Deuteronomy] [3]:[17] The border extends from the plain along the east side of the Yarden (Jordan) valley, from Lake Kineret in the north to the Aravah lake (the Salt Sea or Dead Sea) in the south and to the slopes of Mt. Pisgah on the east.
[Deuteronomy] [3]:[18] “Then at that time, I commanded you saying, ‘Your god Yahweh has given this land to you to possess it, however your brave warriors must cross over with the other Israeli tribes to help them conquer the western lands.
[Deuteronomy] [3]:[19] Leave your wives and children and cattle (yes, I know you have many cattle) back here in the cities that I’ve given you
[Deuteronomy] [3]:[20] until Yahweh gives peace to your brother tribes like you have here. Once they’ve taken possession of the land that your god Yahweh is given them across the river, then you’ll all be able to return her to your own inheritance that I’ve allocated to you.’
[Deuteronomy] [3]:[21] “I also instructed Yehoshua (Joshua) at that time, saying, ‘You’ve seen everything that your god Yahweh has done to those two kings. Yahweh will do similar things to all the kingdoms that you’ll be passing through over there.
[Deuteronomy] [3]:[22] Don’t be afraid of them, because your god Yahweh will be the one fighting for you all.
[Deuteronomy] [3]:[23] “At that time, I pleaded with Yahweh,
[Deuteronomy] [3]:[24] ‘My master Yahweh, you’ve begun to show your servant your greatness and your power. What other god in heaven or on earth is there that does works as great and powerful as what you’ve done?
[Deuteronomy] [3]:[25] Please let me cross the Yarden (Jordan) river and see the good land that’s on the other side—that good hill country, and the Levanon region.’
[Deuteronomy] [3]:[26] “But Yahweh was angry at me because of what your parents had done, and he wouldn’t listen to me. Instead, Yahweh told me, ‘Enough from you—don’t talk to me about that again!
[Deuteronomy] [3]:[27] Go up to the top of Mt. Pisgah and look out towards the west and the north and the south and the east. Yes, look with your eyes, because you won’t be crossing this river.
[Deuteronomy] [3]:[28] Instruct Yehoshua (Joshua) and encourage him and strengthen him, because he’s the one who’ll lead the people across, and he’ll lead them to inherit the land that you’ll see.’
[Deuteronomy] [3]:[29] So we remained in the Yarden river valley opposite Beyt-Pe’or.
[Deuteronomy] [4]:[1] “Now Yisrael (Israel), listen to the instructions and regulations that I’ll teach you so that you’ll all go and possess the land that Yahweh, the god of your ancestors, is giving you, and live there.
[Deuteronomy] [4]:[2] Don’t add or subtract from what I tell you, because you all need to follow the instructions from your god Yahweh that I’m telling you.
[Deuteronomy] [4]:[3] You’ve all seen for yourselves what your god Yahweh did at Beyt-Pe’or, when he destroyed all the men who worshipped Ba’al there.
[Deuteronomy] [4]:[4] However, all of you who faithfully continued to follow your god Yahweh are alive here today.
[Deuteronomy] [4]:[5] “Listen, I’ve taught you all the instructions and regulations that my god Yahweh commanded me to, for you all to follow in the land that you’re about to enter and occupy.
[Deuteronomy] [4]:[6] Follow them faithfully because that will lead to wisdom such that people in other countries will notice that this great nation has wisdom and understanding.
[Deuteronomy] [4]:[7] What other great nation is there that has a god near to it like our god Yahweh is whenever we call out to him for help?
[Deuteronomy] [4]:[8] Also, what other nation has rules and regulations that are as sensible and fair as these instructions that I’m giving to you all today?
[Deuteronomy] [4]:[9] “But each of you must take care to guard yourself and your values in case you forget that you’ve seen and those past miracles slip from your minds over the years to come. Yes, make sure that you teach them to your children and your grand-children,
[Deuteronomy] [4]:[10] including the day when you stood in our god Yahweh’s presence at Mt. Sinay (Horev) when he told me, ‘Assemble the people for me, and I’ll make it so they can hear my words, so they’ll learn to honour and respect for their entire lifetimes, and then teach it to their children.’
[Deuteronomy] [4]:[11] “So you all approached the mountain and stood at its base while it blazed with fire that went up into the atmosphere even though the mountain was covered with dark, gloomy clouds.
[Deuteronomy] [4]:[12] Then Yahweh spoke to you from the middle of the flames—you heard the voice even though you couldn’t see anyone,
[Deuteronomy] [4]:[13] and he revealed to you the agreement that he demands you keep: the ten commands that he wrote onto two stone tablets.
[Deuteronomy] [4]:[14] At that time, Yahweh told me to teach you all the instructions and regulations so you’d be able to put them into practice in the land that you’re about to enter and occupy.
[Deuteronomy] [4]:[15] Now remembering that you didn’t see any form at Mt. Sinay (Horev) when Yahweh spoke to you all from the middle of the fire,
[Deuteronomy] [4]:[16] so don’t corrupt yourselves by making an idol to be your god—don’t make anything in the likeness of a man or a woman,
[Deuteronomy] [4]:[17] or of any animal that’s on the earth or bird that flies in the sky,
[Deuteronomy] [4]:[18] or any reptile that creeps along the ground or any fish from the deep oceans.
[Deuteronomy] [4]:[19] Don’t look up to the sky and be tempted to bow down to the sun or the moon or the stars and serve them—your god Yahweh made them to serve every people group in the world.
[Deuteronomy] [4]:[20] Yahweh has brought you all out of the iron-smelting furnace of Mitsrayim (Egypt) to be a people that would belong to him (as you are today),
[Deuteronomy] [4]:[21] but then Yahweh got angry at me because of your parents and determined that I would never enter the land that he’s giving to all of you.
[Deuteronomy] [4]:[22] Instead, I’ll die here in this place. I won’t cross the Yarden (Jordan) river, but you will, and then you’ll all take possession of that good land.
[Deuteronomy] [4]:[23] Take great care that you all don’t forget the agreement with your god Yahweh. Don’t make any idols for yourselves in the form of anything that your god Yahweh has ordered you all not to,
[Deuteronomy] [4]:[24] because your god Yahweh is a consuming fire—he’s a god who gets jealous.
[Deuteronomy] [4]:[25] Even after you’ve had children and grandchildren and then grown old in the land, don’t make an idol in the form of anything, and don’t be corrupt or do evil things that your god Yahweh dislikes and so which will make him angry.
[Deuteronomy] [4]:[26] If you do, I call the heavens and the earth as witnesses against you all today, that you’d die over there in the land that you’re crossing the river to possess. You wouldn’t live there very long, but instead would end up getting destroyed.
[Deuteronomy] [4]:[27] Then Yahweh would scatter the remainder among the nations where you’d remain as a small minority.
[Deuteronomy] [4]:[28] There you would be forced to worship gods that humans have made out of wood or stone and which can’t see, hear, smell, or eat.
[Deuteronomy] [4]:[29] From there you’ll search for your god Yahweh, and you’ll find him when you search for him with determination and total sincerity.
[Deuteronomy] [4]:[30] It’s in the future when you end up in distress there that you’ll return to your god Yahweh and listen to what he tells you,
[Deuteronomy] [4]:[31] because your god Yahweh is a merciful god. He won’t abandon you or destroy you, and he won’t forget what he promised to your ancestors.
[Deuteronomy] [4]:[32] Now, please, consider past times before you were alive, i.e., from when God first created people here on the earth. You could search all through human history and you wouldn’t find anything else as incredible as what Yahweh has done for your ancestors.
[Deuteronomy] [4]:[33] Has any other people group heard God talking from the middle of a fire like you have, and then lived to tell about it?
[Deuteronomy] [4]:[34] Or is their any other nation that God has attempted to take out from the middle of another nation, using miracles and war, and power and terrifying actions, like your god Yahweh did for you all when you were in Mitsrayim (Egypt)?
[Deuteronomy] [4]:[35] You were shown all that so you’d know that Yahweh is the one and only god.
[Deuteronomy] [4]:[36] He allowed you to hear his voice from the skies to instruct you, and on earth you heard his words from the incredible fire that he showed you.
[Deuteronomy] [4]:[37] Because he loved your ancestors, he chose their descendants as his people and used his power and strength to lead you out of Mitsrayim
[Deuteronomy] [4]:[38] and then to drive out nations ahead of you that were greater and more powerful than you—bringing you here today so that you could occupy their land as your inheritance.
[Deuteronomy] [4]:[39] So today you should acknowledge that Yahweh is god of the heavens above and the earth below, and there’s no other god.
[Deuteronomy] [4]:[40] Follow his instructions and obey his regulations that I’m giving you today so that everything will go well for you and your descendants, and so that you’ll live a long time in the land that your god Yahweh is giving you as a permanent possession.”

[Deuteronomy] [5]:[1] Then Mosheh (Moses) summoned all Yisrael (Israel) and told them, “Yisrael, listen to the instructions and the regulations that I will speak in your ears today, and then you must learn them and be careful to follow them.
[Deuteronomy] [5]:[2] Our god Yahweh made an agreement with us at Horev.
[Deuteronomy] [5]:[3] He didn’t make that agreement with our ancestors, but with us ourselves—those of us here today, i.e., with living people.
[Deuteronomy] [5]:[4] Yahweh spoke to you from the middle of the fire—face to face with you all on that mountain.
[Deuteronomy] [5]:[5] Well, it was me who stood between all of you and Yahweh at that time, to reveal Yahweh’s message to you, because you were afraid to approach the fire, and you all didn’t go up the mountain. Yahweh said:
[Deuteronomy] [5]:[6] ‘I am your god Yahweh who brought you all out of Mitsrayim (Egypt)—from the slave-house there.
[Deuteronomy] [5]:[7] Don’t have any other god, other than me.
[Deuteronomy] [5]:[8] Don’t carve any figure for yourself that looks like anything in the sky or on the ground, or in the water below the ground.
[Deuteronomy] [5]:[9] Don’t bow down to them or serve them, because I, your god Yahweh, am a jealous god. I’ll punish the descendants of those who hate me, even for three or four generations,
[Deuteronomy] [5]:[10] but showing loyal commitment to thousands of generations of those who love me and obey my instructions.
[Deuteronomy] [5]:[11] Don’t use the name of your god Yahweh idly, because I won’t fail to punish people who do that.
[Deuteronomy] [5]:[12] Observe the Rest Day on Saturday to sanctify it, as your god Yahweh commanded you.
[Deuteronomy] [5]:[13] There’s six days for labouring and doing all your work,
[Deuteronomy] [5]:[14] but the seventh day is a rest day dedicated to your god Yahweh. Don’t do any work on that day: not you or your children or your slaves, or using any of your cattle, nor any foreigner living with you—your slaves can rest like you.
[Deuteronomy] [5]:[15] Remember that you were a slave in Mitsrayim (Egypt), and that your god Yahweh took action and used my power to take you out of there. Therefore your god Yahweh commands you to keep the Rest Day.
[Deuteronomy] [5]:[16] Honour your father and mother as your god Yahweh has commanded you, so that you’ll have a long life and so that everything will go well in the country that your god Yahweh is giving you.
[Deuteronomy] [5]:[17] Don’t murder anyone.
[Deuteronomy] [5]:[18] Don’t commit adultery.
[Deuteronomy] [5]:[19] Don’t steal anything.
[Deuteronomy] [5]:[20] Don’t tell lies in court about anyone.
[Deuteronomy] [5]:[21] Don’t covet your neighbour’s spouse, or their house or land, or their slaves or livestock, or anything else that they own.’
[Deuteronomy] [5]:[22] Yahweh spoke those words in a booming voice from the middle of the fire, the cloud, and the gloom, to all your assembly on the mountain. That was all he said, and he wrote those instructions on two stone tablets and gave them to me.
[Deuteronomy] [5]:[23] Then when you heard the voice coming out from the darkness and the mountain was blazing with fire, then all the heads of your tribes and the elders approached me
[Deuteronomy] [5]:[24] and said, “Listen, our god Yahweh demonstrated his greatness and power when we heard him speak from the fire. Today, we’ve realised that God talks to people, and that they can stay alive.
[Deuteronomy] [5]:[25] However, we’re still afraid that we’ll die—getting burnt up in that intense fire if we continue hearing our god Yahweh’s voice,
[Deuteronomy] [5]:[26] because when has anybody else ever heard the voice of the living god speak to them from the middle of a blazing fire and they still lived?
[Deuteronomy] [5]:[27] You Mosheh (Moses), go and listen to everything that our god Yahweh says, and tell us everything that he tells you, and we’ll listen to that and obey it.”
[Deuteronomy] [5]:[28] Yahweh heard you all say that to me, and told me, ‘I’ve heard what they said to you and it’s a good idea.
[Deuteronomy] [5]:[29] If only they were sincere in saying that they’d honour me and always follow all my instructions so that everything would go well for them and their descendants forever.
[Deuteronomy] [5]:[30] Go and tell them to return to their tents,
[Deuteronomy] [5]:[31] but then come back up here and I’ll give you all the instructions and rules and regulations for you to teach them, so they can follow them in the land that I’m giving them to take possession of.’
[Deuteronomy] [5]:[32] Make sure that you do everything that your god Yahweh has commanded—don’t deviate from any of them.
[Deuteronomy] [5]:[33] Follow all the instructions from your god Yahweh, and then you’ll all live and things will go well and you’ll all be able to occupy that land for a long time.

[Deuteronomy] [6]:[13] You must honour your god Yahweh and only serve him and only make promises using his name.
[Deuteronomy] [6]:[14] Don’t go trying to follow other gods—the gods of the surrounding countries—

[Deuteronomy] [6]:[22] He did many kinds of miracles that devastated that Mitsri (Egyptian) king and his whole household,

[Deuteronomy] [7]:[1] When your god Yahweh brings you into the land which you’re going to possess, he’ll drive out many people groups ahead of you: the Hitim, Girgashim, Amorim, Kena’anim (Canaanites), Perizim, Hivim, and the Yevusim—seven societies that are more powerful than yourselves.
[Deuteronomy] [7]:[2] When your god Yahweh enables you to defeat them, you must kill them all. You must make no agreement with them, and you must not act mercifully toward them.
[Deuteronomy] [7]:[3] Don’t intermarry with them: don’t allow your daughters to marry their sons, or your sons to marry any of their daughters
[Deuteronomy] [7]:[4] because they’d turn your sons away from me, and they’d end up serving other gods. Then Yahweh would become very angry with you all and would quickly destroy you.
[Deuteronomy] [7]:[5] What you all should do to those people is to break down their altars and smash their stone pillars, cut their Asherah poles to pieces, and burn up their idols.
[Deuteronomy] [7]:[6] You must do that because you’re a group of people who belong only to your god Yahweh. He’s chosen you from all the people groups in the world to be his own special people.
[Deuteronomy] [7]:[7] Yahweh loved you and chose you all, not because you were the most populous nation (in fact, you were the smallest of all the nations),
[Deuteronomy] [7]:[8] but because Yahweh loves you all and because he kept the promise that he’d made to your ancestors. Yahweh used his power to rescue you all from the slavery imposed by Mitsrayim’s (Egypt) King Par’oh (Pharaoh).
