[Deuteronomy] [13]:[14] then you must thoroughly investigate the matter. If it’s actually true that that disgusting thing had been done among you,
[Deuteronomy] [13]:[15] then all the people in that place must be executed by the sword, along with all their livestock.
[Deuteronomy] [13]:[16] Gather all the people’s possessions and pile them up in the city plaza, then burn the place and everything in it like a ‘burnt offering’ to Yahweh. Leave the place as an abandoned heap—it should never be rebuilt again.
[Deuteronomy] [13]:[17] Don’t be tempted to pick anything valuable out from the pile headed for destruction, but obey carefully so that Yahweh’s anger will subside. Then he’ll show compassion to you and mercy, and make you increase like he promised to your ancestors
[Deuteronomy] [13]:[18] when you listen to what he says—following all his instructions and doing what he says is the right thing to do.
[Deuteronomy] [14]:[1] You’re all children of your god Yahweh so don’t cut yourselves or shave the front of your heads for the sake of the dead,
[Deuteronomy] [14]:[2] because you’re a nation that’s set apart for your god Yahweh, and he’s chosen you out of all the other peoples in the world to be his own people.
[Deuteronomy] [14]:[3] Don’t eat anything that Yahweh detests.
[Deuteronomy] [14]:[4] These are the animals that you all can eat: cattle, sheep, goats,
[Deuteronomy] [14]:[5] all kinds of deer, gazelles, wild goats, and mountain sheep,
[Deuteronomy] [14]:[6] i.e., you can eat any of the animals that have split hooves and that also chew the cud.
[Deuteronomy] [14]:[7] But there are other animals that chew the cud that you mustn’t eat: camels, rabbits and hares, and rock badgers. They chew the cud, but don’t have split hooves so they are unacceptable for you to eat.
[Deuteronomy] [14]:[8] Don’t eat pigs—they’re unacceptable for you to eat. They have split hooves, but they don’t chew the cud. Don’t eat the meat of those animals and don’t even touch their dead bodies.
[Deuteronomy] [14]:[9] You all can eat anything that lives in water that has both fins and scales,
[Deuteronomy] [14]:[10] but anything in the water that doesn’t have both is unacceptable for you to eat.
[Deuteronomy] [14]:[11] You all can eat any clean bird,
[Deuteronomy] [14]:[12] but not these: eagles, vultures, ospreys,
[Deuteronomy] [14]:[13] buzzards, kites, falcons,
[Deuteronomy] [14]:[14] any kind of ravens or crows,
[Deuteronomy] [14]:[15] ostriches, owls, seagulls, any kind of hawk,
[Deuteronomy] [14]:[16] any kinds of owls,
[Deuteronomy] [14]:[17] pelicans, carrion vultures, cormorants,
[Deuteronomy] [14]:[18] storks, any kind of heron, hoopoes, or bats.
[Deuteronomy] [14]:[19] You mustn’t eat any insect with wings and which swarm—they’re unacceptable to Yahweh for you to eat,
[Deuteronomy] [14]:[20] but other insects with wings are acceptable to eat.
[Deuteronomy] [14]:[21] Don’t eat any creature that’s died naturally. You may allow foreigners who live among you to eat those things. You may also sell them to other foreigners. But you are a people group that belongs to your god Yahweh. You mustn’t cook a young sheep or goat in its mother’s milk.
[Deuteronomy] [14]:[22] Make sure you set aside a tenth of all the crops that you harvest from your fields.
[Deuteronomy] [14]:[23] You must eat it in the presence of your god Yahweh, in the place that he’ll choose and attach his name to. That’s where you must eat the tenth of your grain, wine, olive oil, and the firstborn male animals from your herd and your flock, so that you’ll learn to always honour your god Yahweh.
[Deuteronomy] [14]:[24] When he blesses you with produce, if the place he chooses to attach his name to is too far for you to be able to carry it to,
[Deuteronomy] [14]:[25] then you can give the equivalent in cash, and carefully take the cash with you all the way to the place that he chooses.
[Deuteronomy] [14]:[26] When you get there, use the money to purchase any kinds of meat or drink that you want, and consume it there in front of your god Yahweh, and celebrate along with your household.
[Deuteronomy] [14]:[27] Be sure not to neglect any Levites that live in your town, because they weren’t given ancestral land for agriculture like you were.
[Deuteronomy] [14]:[28] At the end of every third year, bring the tenth of all your produce for that year and store it in your town
[Deuteronomy] [14]:[29] for the Levites (because they didn’t get land), and for any foreigners, orphans, and widows who live in your towns. They can come and get what they need so that your god Yahweh can bless you in everything that you do.
[Deuteronomy] [15]:[1] At the end of every seven years, you must cancel all debts.
[Deuteronomy] [15]:[2] Handle it like this: Everyone who’s loaned money to their Israeli neighbour must cancel that debt, i.e., they must not insist that it’s paid back, because Yahweh has announced a cancellation.
[Deuteronomy] [15]:[3] You can pressure a foreigner to repay, but you must cancel any debt from a fellow Israeli.
[Deuteronomy] [15]:[4] However, there shouldn’t be any poor among you, because your god Yahweh will bless you in the land that he’s giving you to own as an inheritance,
[Deuteronomy] [15]:[5] as long as you listen to what he says and keep following these instructions that I’m telling you today.
[Deuteronomy] [15]:[6] Because your god Yahweh will bless you (like he promised he would), you’ll lend to many nations rather than borrowing from them, and you’ll rule over many nations rather than them ruling you.
[Deuteronomy] [15]:[7] In the towns that your god Yahweh is giving you, if it so happens that any of your fellow Israelis are poor, then don’t just ignore them and refuse to help them,
[Deuteronomy] [15]:[8] but instead, open your wallet and lend them however much they need.
[Deuteronomy] [15]:[9] Be careful not to quietly think to yourself that the seventh-year reset is close so they won’t have to pay it back. It would be wrong not to help a fellow Israeli, and if you did and he called out to Yahweh for help, then it would be counted against you as disobedience.
[Deuteronomy] [15]:[10] Give generously to the poor without getting resentful inside, because then your god Yahweh can bless you in all your work and all your investments.
[Deuteronomy] [15]:[11] There’ll always be poor people in your country, so I command you to give generously to the poor and needy and your fellow Israelis.
[Deuteronomy] [15]:[12] If a fellow Israeli is sold to you and serves you for six years, then you must free them in the seventh year.
[Deuteronomy] [15]:[13] But when you free them, don’t send them off empty-handed
[Deuteronomy] [15]:[14] but instead, give to them generously from your flock and from your barn and from your wine. In whatever ways your god Yahweh has blessed you, you should give to them.
[Deuteronomy] [15]:[15] Always remember that you were a slave in Mitsrayim (Egypt) and your god Yahweh redeemed you out of there, so that’s why I’m commanding you to do that.
[Deuteronomy] [15]:[16] However, if any slave says that they don’t want to leave you, because they appreciate you and your household, and so they’re better off to stay with you,
[Deuteronomy] [15]:[17] then get an awl and stand them against the doorpost and pierce one of their earlobes with the awl, then that person (male or female) will be your slave forever.
[Deuteronomy] [15]:[18] Don’t complain when you have to release your slaves, because they’ve served you up to six years and been double the value of a regular hired worker, plus your god Yahweh will bless you in whatever you do.
[Deuteronomy] [15]:[19] You must set apart for your god Yahweh, all the firstborn male animals from your herds and your flocks. You mustn’t use the cattle for working, and mustn’t shear the sheep or goats.
[Deuteronomy] [15]:[20] Each year, you and your household must take them to the place that Yahweh will choose, and eat them there in front of him.
[Deuteronomy] [15]:[21] However, any animals that have defects (e.g., lame or blind, or with a severe blemish) mustn’t be sacrificed to your god Yahweh.
[Deuteronomy] [15]:[22] Instead, you can eat those at home whether or not you’re ceremonially ‘clean’, just like you’d eat a wild gazelle or deer.
[Deuteronomy] [15]:[23] However, don’t eat the blood—it must be poured out on the ground like water.
[Deuteronomy] [16]:[1] Each year, honour your god Yahweh in the early spring by celebrating the ‘pass-over’, because it was one night in the early spring that he brought you out of Mitsrayim (Egypt).
[Deuteronomy] [16]:[2] In order to celebrate, go to the place that your god Yahweh will choose to attach his name to, and there sacrifice to him one young animal from your flock or herd.
[Deuteronomy] [16]:[3] Don’t eat any leavened bread with it. For seven days, you must eat flat bread (the bread of suffering) because you came out of Mitsrayim in a rush. That’s how you should remember the day of your exit from Mitsrayim for the rest of your life.
[Deuteronomy] [16]:[4] In fact, for seven days you shouldn’t even have any rising agent within your borders, and none of the meat from the sacrifice on that first evening is allowed to be left until the morning.
[Deuteronomy] [16]:[5] You mustn’t sacrifice the ‘pass-over’ animal within any of your towns that your god Yahweh is giving to you—
[Deuteronomy] [16]:[6] only at the place that your god Yahweh will choose to attach his name to. That’s where you must sacrifice the ‘pass-over’ animal at sunset, which was the time when your ancestors started leaving Mitsrayim.
[Deuteronomy] [16]:[7] You must cook the meat and eat it at the place that Yahweh will choose, then in the morning you can start returning to your homes.
[Deuteronomy] [16]:[8] Then for six days you must only eat flat bread, and the seventh day is a special celebration for your god Yahweh—don’t do any work on that day.
[Deuteronomy] [16]:[9] You must count off seven weeks starting from when the very first harvesting of grain begins.
[Deuteronomy] [16]:[10] Then celebrate the ‘Festival of Weeks’ to honour your god Yahweh by contributing a freewill offering acknowledging however much he has blessed you.
[Deuteronomy] [16]:[11] You should celebrate in Yahweh’s presence, along with your children and your servants, and any Levites living in your town, and the foreigners, orphans, and widows living among you. Take your offerings to the place that your god Yahweh will choose to attach his name to.
[Deuteronomy] [16]:[12] Always remember that you were a slave in Mitsrayim (Egypt), so carefully follow those instructions.
[Deuteronomy] [16]:[13] After you’ve brought in the grain harvest and pressed out the grape juice, you must celebrate the ‘Festival of Shelters’ for seven days.
[Deuteronomy] [16]:[14] You should celebrate along with your children and your servants, as well as any Levites and foreigners and orphans and widows who live in your town.
[Deuteronomy] [16]:[15] Honour your god Yahweh at the place he’ll choose, by celebrating for seven days because he’s blessed your harvest and all your other work.
[Deuteronomy] [16]:[16] In summary, all your men must travel three times each year to the place that your god Yahweh will choose: at the Flat Bread Celebration, at the Festival of Weeks, and at the Festival of Shelters. No man should come empty-handed,
[Deuteronomy] [16]:[17] but rather, each man must give in proportion to the blessings that your god Yahweh has given you during that year.
[Deuteronomy] [16]:[18] You must appoint judges and other officials throughout your tribes, in all the towns that your god Yahweh is giving to you. They must judge the people fairly and correctly.
[Deuteronomy] [16]:[19] You mustn’t pervert justice or give favours. Don’t accept bribes because a bribe causes an otherwise wise person to ignore evil and misrepresents what innocent people say.
[Deuteronomy] [16]:[20] True justice is what you should aim for, so that you’ll occupy and live in the land that your god Yahweh is giving you.
[Deuteronomy] [16]:[21] Never put an Asherah pole near the altar to your god Yahweh that you’ll build for yourself,
[Deuteronomy] [16]:[22] and don’t erect any stone pillars that your god Yahweh hates.
[Deuteronomy] [17]:[1] Don’t sacrifice any animal to your god Yahweh that has any blemish or defect, because he detests that.
[Deuteronomy] [17]:[2] In any of the towns that your god Yahweh is giving you, if you discover any man or woman who does evil by disobeying the agreement that he’s made with you
[Deuteronomy] [17]:[3] and worshipped other gods, or the sun, moon, or stars—all of which I’ve prohibited you from doing,
[Deuteronomy] [17]:[4] and it’s reported to you, and you listen and investigate it thoroughly, and it’s true that this detestable thing was done in Yisrael (Israel),
[Deuteronomy] [17]:[5] you must bring that man or woman out to the town gates, and execute them by throwing rocks at them.
[Deuteronomy] [17]:[6] Note that that person can only be executed if there’s at least two witnesses as evidence—no one can be put to death on the testimony of just one witness.
[Deuteronomy] [17]:[7] The witnesses must be the ones to throw the first rocks then all the other people after that, and that’s how you’ll remove evil from your society.
[Deuteronomy] [17]:[8] If a case is too difficult for you yourselves to judge (e.g., two parties claiming bloodshed, or lawsuits, or assaults, or other disputes within your towns), you must leave town and go to the place that your god Yahweh is going to choose.
[Deuteronomy] [17]:[9] You should go to the Levitical priests and to the judge on duty there and they will produce a judgement.
[Deuteronomy] [17]:[10] Whatever the decision is that’s made at the place Yahweh will choose, that’s the verdict that must be applied to the case—
[Deuteronomy] [17]:[11] accept their judgement and do what they say without making any adjustments to their decision.
[Deuteronomy] [17]:[12] Anyone who shows contempt for the decision of the judge or the priest who’s standing there serving your god Yahweh, then that person must be executed to remove that evil from Yisrael (Israel),
[Deuteronomy] [17]:[13] then all the people will hear about it and be afraid, and it’ll stamp out such arrogance.
[Deuteronomy] [17]:[14] When you enter the land that your god Yahweh is about to give you, then occupy and live in it, and you say that you need a king over you like all the surrounding countries have,
[Deuteronomy] [17]:[15] you can appoint the king over you that Yahweh chooses. Your king must be an Israeli—never allow a foreigner to become your king.
[Deuteronomy] [17]:[16] However, he mustn’t acquire a large number of horses for himself, and he should never send people to Mitsrayim (Egypt) to buy horses, because Yahweh has told you all to never go back that way again.
[Deuteronomy] [17]:[17] He mustn’t take a lot of wives for himself or else he might stop worshipping Yahweh. Nor should he accumulate too much gold and silver.
[Deuteronomy] [17]:[18] Once he’s sitting on his royal throne, he must copy for himself the instructions on the scroll that’s in the custody of the Levitical priests,
[Deuteronomy] [17]:[19] then he must keep it with him and read some of it every day so that he learns to honour his god Yahweh—being careful to follow all the instructions and regulations written in it
[Deuteronomy] [17]:[20] so that he won’t think he’s more valued than his fellow citizens, and so that he doesn’t ignore those instructions even slightly. As a result, him and his descendants will rule as kings in Yisrael (Israel) for many years.
[Deuteronomy] [18]:[1] None of the Levites (including the priests) will receive any land as an inheritance like the other Israelis. Instead, the people’s offerings to Yahweh will be their inheritance to sustain them.
[Deuteronomy] [18]:[2] Yes, unlike fellow Israelis, they won’t have any inherited land—Yahweh is their inheritance like he told them.
[Deuteronomy] [18]:[3] This is the requirement that the people do for the priests: whenever they bring a bull or a sheep as a sacrifice, they must give the shoulder, the cheeks, and the stomach to the priest.
[Deuteronomy] [18]:[4] Also you must give the Levites the firstfruits of your grain, your grape juice, your olive oil, and the wool shorn from your sheep,
[Deuteronomy] [18]:[5] because your god Yahweh chose them out of all your tribes for them and their descendants permanently to serve him.
[Deuteronomy] [18]:[6] If a Levite chooses to move his family from their town in any part of Yisrael (Israel) and sincerely wants to go to the place that Yahweh will choose,
[Deuteronomy] [18]:[7] then he can join the other Levites there to serve his god Yahweh
[Deuteronomy] [18]:[8] and must be given a portion like all the others. (He can keep anything he got from the sale of their family home.)
[Deuteronomy] [18]:[9] When you enter the land that your god Yahweh is about to give you, don’t imitate the disgusting habits of those peoples.
[Deuteronomy] [18]:[10] There mustn’t be anyone among you who passes their son or daughter through fire, or who uses divination or omens to try to tell the future, or who practices sorcery,
[Deuteronomy] [18]:[11] or who puts spells on people, or who tries to talk to spirits of deceased people,
[Deuteronomy] [18]:[12] because anyone who does those things is abhorrent to Yahweh. It’s because of those kinds of things that your god Yahweh will drive those other peoples away ahead of you.
[Deuteronomy] [18]:[13] You must be a blameless nation in the eyes of your god Yahweh,
[Deuteronomy] [18]:[14] because the groups that you’ll expel from the land rely on fortune-tellers and diviners, but your god Yahweh won’t allow you to do that.
[Deuteronomy] [18]:[15] Your god Yahweh will select a man from among you and send him as a prophet like me. You must take notice of him,
[Deuteronomy] [18]:[16] since you begged your god Yahweh from the bottom of Mt. Horev when you said, “We can’t handle directly hearing the voice of our god Yahweh and looking at this terrible fire. Let us go home so we won’t die here.”
[Deuteronomy] [18]:[17] Then Yahweh told me, “They’re right in what they’re saying.
[Deuteronomy] [18]:[18] I’ll choose a prophet from among them and see him. I’ll tell him what to say, and he can pass it on to them,
[Deuteronomy] [18]:[19] and if anyone doesn’t listen to what he says with my authority, I’ll punish that person as if they ignored me.
[Deuteronomy] [18]:[20] However, if the prophet says things that I didn’t tell him to say but claims they came from me, or if he speaks in the name of other gods, then that prophet must die.”
[Deuteronomy] [18]:[21] Now if you ask yourselves, “How can we recognise a message that didn’t come from Yahweh?”
[Deuteronomy] [18]:[22] then when the prophet speaks in Yahweh’s name but that thing doesn’t happen, then you’ll know that it didn’t come from Yahweh. The prophet spoke it assuming that I’d want that, but you don’t need to be afraid of him.
[Deuteronomy] [19]:[1] When your god Yahweh destroys those peoples where he’s giving you the land, and you occupy the land and live in their cities and houses,
[Deuteronomy] [19]:[2] you must select three cities spread across the land that Yahweh is giving you.
[Deuteronomy] [19]:[3] You must define three borders and build roads in the land that your god Yahweh is giving you to inherit. Anyone who kills another person can then flee to one of those cities.
[Deuteronomy] [19]:[4] This is the rule for someone who’s killed another person and flees to live there: if they’ve accidentally killed another person and had no hate for that person from past events,
[Deuteronomy] [19]:[5] (for example, if two men went into the forest to chop wood and an axe head flew off its handle and killed the other man) then that accidental killer can flee to one of those cities and live there.
[Deuteronomy] [19]:[6] Otherwise a friend or relative of the dead person might chase the killer in a sudden rage and overtake and kill the accidental killer if the city was too far away. However, the killer doesn’t deserve death if they hadn’t hated that person from past events—
[Deuteronomy] [19]:[7] that’s why I’m ordering you to select three cities for this.
[Deuteronomy] [19]:[8] Then in the future, if your god Yahweh extends your territory as he promised your ancestors that he would do, and gives you all the land that he told them about,
[Deuteronomy] [19]:[9] and if you’re still following all these instructions that I’m giving you today (loving your god Yahweh and always obeying what he’s said), then you’ll need to add three more refuge cities for your country.
[Deuteronomy] [19]:[10] That’s so innocent people won’t be killed in the land that your god Yahweh is giving you, and so that you won’t be found guilty of the murder of that accidental killer.
[Deuteronomy] [19]:[11] However, if someone hates another person and then ambushes them and kills them, and then flees to one of those cities,
[Deuteronomy] [19]:[12] then the elders from their home town should go and get that person from the refuge city and hand that killer over to the relatives handling the case, and the murderer must be executed.
[Deuteronomy] [19]:[13] You must show no mercy to murderers but they must be executed so that the country isn’t responsible for the blood of innocent people, and then things will go well for you.
[Deuteronomy] [19]:[14] Once you’re in the land that your god Yahweh is giving you to occupy, you mustn’t move the boundary markers which were set between you and your neighbour.
[Deuteronomy] [19]:[15] A single witness must not be used to condemn anyone—a matter must only be considered proven if there’s at least two or three witnesses.
[Deuteronomy] [19]:[16] Suppose that a ‘witness’ brought a false allegation against a man,
[Deuteronomy] [19]:[17] then both parties must go and stand in front of Yahweh—in front of the priests and judges on duty at that time.
[Deuteronomy] [19]:[18] The judges must investigate the case thoroughly, and if the witness is proved to be lying (and so falsely accusing a fellow citizen),
[Deuteronomy] [19]:[19] you must give the false witness the punishment that was planned for the person falsely accused, and that’s how you can remove the evil from among your nation.
[Deuteronomy] [19]:[20] Then the rest of the people will hear about that and be afraid to do that kind of evil thing in your country.
[Deuteronomy] [19]:[21] Don’t pity violent people: it’s a life for a life, an eye for an eye, a tooth for a tooth, a hand for a hand, and a foot for a foot.
[Deuteronomy] [20]:[1] When you go out to battle against your enemies, and see many horses and chariots and a bigger army than yours, don’t be afraid of them, because your god Yahweh who helped you out of Mitsrayim (Egypt) is with you.
[Deuteronomy] [20]:[2] As you approach the place of battle, the high priest must go and stand in front of the warriors,
[Deuteronomy] [20]:[3] and tell them, “Listen, Yisrael (Israel), you’re about to battle against your enemies. Don’t be nervous or afraid, and don’t tremble or be terrified of them,
[Deuteronomy] [20]:[4] because your god Yahweh will go with you to fight for you against your enemies. He’ll give you victory.”
[Deuteronomy] [20]:[5] Then the officers must ask the people, “Is there anyone here who’s just built a new house and hasn’t dedicated it yet? If so, he can go home in case he dies in battle and someone else gets to dedicate his house.
[Deuteronomy] [20]:[6] Is there anyone who’s planted a vineyard and not benefitted from it yet? If so, he can go home in case he dies in battle and someone else enjoys the grape harvest.
[Deuteronomy] [20]:[7] Is there anyone who’s gotten engaged, but not yet married? If so, he can go home in case he died in battle and someone else marries her.”
[Deuteronomy] [20]:[8] Then those officers should also ask, “Is there anyone who’s scared or fearful? If so, he should go home so his fear doesn’t spread to others.”
[Deuteronomy] [20]:[9] Once they’ve finished speaking with the fighting men, they must appoint commanders over them.
[Deuteronomy] [20]:[10] When you approach a city ready to attack it, first call out to offer peace for surrender,
[Deuteronomy] [20]:[11] and if they agree to surrender and open the city gates, then they’ll all be forced to work for you.
[Deuteronomy] [20]:[12] But if they refuse your terms and decide to fight against you, then you should besiege that city.
[Deuteronomy] [20]:[13] Then when your god Yahweh helps you to capture it, you must kill every male in that city.
[Deuteronomy] [20]:[14] However, you can take the women and children and cattle and everything else in the city as plunder for yourself. You can enjoy your enemies’ possessions that Yahweh has given to you.
[Deuteronomy] [20]:[15] That’s how you should treat the cities located far from you—it doesn’t apply to the cities of nearby peoples.
[Deuteronomy] [20]:[16] In contrast, the cities of those peoples that your god Yahweh is giving you as an inheritance, you mustn’t leave a single living thing alive
[Deuteronomy] [20]:[17] because you must complete eliminate the Hitim, the Amorim, the Kena’anim (Canaanites), the Perizim, the Hivim, and the Yevusim. Do that just as your god Yahweh commanded you
[Deuteronomy] [20]:[18] so that they don’t teach you to sin against Yahweh by doing any of their abhorrent activities that they do for their gods.
[Deuteronomy] [20]:[19] When you besiege a city for a lengthy period, battling against it to capture it, you mustn’t use your axes to destroy its trees, because you can eat their fruit. Don’t cut them down because the trees in the countryside aren’t likely to turn around and attack you.
[Deuteronomy] [20]:[20] However, the trees that aren’t fruit trees can be cut down and make ladders and towers to enable you to go over the walls and capture the city that is resisting you.
[Deuteronomy] [21]:[1] If a dead body is found in the land that your god Yahweh is about to give you, and it appears that that person had been killed out in the countryside by some unknown person,
[Deuteronomy] [21]:[2] then your elders and your judges must go out and work out the distance to each of the towns close to that victim.
[Deuteronomy] [21]:[3] Then the elders from that closest town must select a heifer from their herd that’s never been yoked or had to pull anything,
[Deuteronomy] [21]:[4] and take it down into a valley that has a stream but the ground has never been ploughed or planted. They must break its neck there
[Deuteronomy] [21]:[5] and the Levitical priests must approach it because your god Yahweh has chosen them to serve him and pronounce blessings on Yahweh’s behalf, and to give rulings on disputes and assaults.
[Deuteronomy] [21]:[6] Then all the elders from that closest town must wash their hands over the heifer whose neck was broken in the valley,
[Deuteronomy] [21]:[7] and say, “We didn’t murder this person, nor did we see who did it.
[Deuteronomy] [21]:[8] Yahweh, forgive your Israeli people who you rescued from Mitsrayim (Egypt). Don’t count us as guilty for murdering an innocent person.” When they do that, Yisrael (Israel) will be forgiven for that murder.
[Deuteronomy] [21]:[9] That’s how your country will remove from yourselves the guilt of shedding innocent blood, when you do what’s right in Yahweh’s eyes.
[Deuteronomy] [21]:[10] When you go out to battle against your enemies and your god Yahweh helps you defeat them, and you capture some of their people
[Deuteronomy] [21]:[11] and you notice an attractive woman that you’d like to take as a wife,
[Deuteronomy] [21]:[12] then you must publicly take her to your house. There you must shave off her hair and trim her nails,
[Deuteronomy] [21]:[13] and discard the clothes she was wearing when she was captured. She must stay in that house, and be allowed an entire month to mourn for her parents before she’s taken to be your wife.
[Deuteronomy] [21]:[14] If you’re not happy with her, then you can’t sell her—you must release her to go wherever she wants because you’ve already humiliated her.
[Deuteronomy] [21]:[15] If a man has two wives and loves one more than the other, but they’ve both given birth to sons for him but the oldest son is from the wife he dislikes,
[Deuteronomy] [21]:[16] then when he assigns his inheritance to his sons, he mustn’t favour the son of the favourite wife over that eldest son.
[Deuteronomy] [21]:[17] Instead, he must acknowledge the son of the wife he dislikes, and given him double of everything, because that son is the beginning of his strength, and the largest share belongs to him.
[Deuteronomy] [21]:[18] If a person has a stubborn, rebellious son who won’t listen to the voice of his parents, and they tell him off, but he still won’t listen to them,
[Deuteronomy] [21]:[19] then his parents must physically bring him to the elders at the gate of his hometown.
[Deuteronomy] [21]:[20] Then they must tell those elders, “Our son is stubborn and rebellious and pays no attention to what we say—he’s a glutton and a drunkard.”
[Deuteronomy] [21]:[21] Then all the men from that place must execute him by throwing rocks at him, thus removing that evil from among you. Then everyone in Yisrael (Israel) will hear about it and be afraid to imitate him.
[Deuteronomy] [21]:[22] If someone has committed a crime worthy of death, and that person is executed and you hang their body on a tree,
[Deuteronomy] [21]:[23] then the corpse mustn’t remain overnight on the tree—it must be buried that same day, because anyone who’s hanged is cursed by God and you mustn’t defile your country that your god Yahweh is about to give you as an inheritance.
[Deuteronomy] [22]:[1] If you see someone else’s cow or sheep that has strayed away, don’t act as though you didn’t see it. Take it back to its owner.
[Deuteronomy] [22]:[2] However, if the owner doesn’t live near you, or if you don’t know who it is, then take the animal to your house. It can stay with you until the owner comes looking for it, then you must give it to them.
[Deuteronomy] [22]:[3] Similarly if it’s a donkey or clothing or anything else that someone’s lost, don’t pretend that you never saw it.
[Deuteronomy] [22]:[4] If you see someone else’s donkey or cow that’s fallen beside the road, don’t act as though you didn’t see it. You must try to help the owner to get the animal up.
[Deuteronomy] [22]:[5] Women mustn’t wear men’s clothes, and men mustn’t wear women’s clothes. Your god Yahweh hates people who do things like that.
[Deuteronomy] [22]:[6] If you happen to find a bird’s nest in a tree or on the ground, and the mother bird is sitting in the nest on its eggs or with the baby birds, don’t take both the mother bird and the babies.
[Deuteronomy] [22]:[7] You may take the eggs or the baby birds, but you must allow the mother bird to fly away. Do that so that things will go well for you and so that you’ll live in the land for a long time.
[Deuteronomy] [22]:[8] When you build a new house, be sure to include a railing around your flat roof, so you won’t be guilty of having caused someone’s death if a person falls off it and dies.
[Deuteronomy] [22]:[9] Don’t plant a crop in your vineyard, because then the harvest of the crop and the fruit from the vineyard will both be defiled.
[Deuteronomy] [22]:[10] Don’t plough with a cow and a donkey harnessed together.
[Deuteronomy] [22]:[11] Don’t wear clothes with a mix of wool and linen.
[Deuteronomy] [22]:[12] Twist threads together to make tassels and sew them onto the four corners of your cloak.
[Deuteronomy] [22]:[13] If a man takes a wife and sleeps with her, then hates her
[Deuteronomy] [22]:[14] and accuses her of shameful things, destroying her reputation and claiming that she hadn’t been a virgin,
[Deuteronomy] [22]:[15] then the young woman’s parents must show the evidence of her virginity to the elders at the city gate.
[Deuteronomy] [22]:[16] The young woman’s father must tell the elders how he gave his daughter to the man as a wife, but now he’s rejected her
[Deuteronomy] [22]:[17] and made shameful accusations about her not being a virgin. Then the parents must spread out that cloth and show it to the city elders.
[Deuteronomy] [22]:[18] Then the city elders must punish that man
[Deuteronomy] [22]:[19] and fine him a hundred silver coins to be paid to the young woman’s father for defaming an Israeli virgin. Then she’ll remain as his wife and he’ll be prohibited from ever divorcing her.
[Deuteronomy] [22]:[20] However, if the accusation was true and the young woman hadn’t been a virgin,
[Deuteronomy] [22]:[21] then they must take her to the doorway of her father’s house. Then the men from that city must execute her by throwing rocks at her, because she’s done a disgraceful thing in Yisrael (Israel)—committing fornication while she still lived in her father’s house. That’s how you’ll remove evil from your country.
[Deuteronomy] [22]:[22] If a man is discovered sleeping with another man’s wife, then both of them must be executed. That’s how you’ll remove evil from Yisrael.
[Deuteronomy] [22]:[23] If a young woman is engaged to a man, and another man sleeps with her,
[Deuteronomy] [22]:[24] then you must execute both of them at the city gate by throwing rocks at them—the young woman because she didn’t scream, and the man for defiling another man’s fiancée.
[Deuteronomy] [22]:[25] If the man found the young woman out in the countryside and overpowers her and rapes her, then the man must be executed
[Deuteronomy] [22]:[26] but don’t do anything to that woman because she’s not worthy of death. (This is similar to the case of a man murdering another man out in the countryside.)
[Deuteronomy] [22]:[27] When that man found her out in the countryside, then she would have cried out for help, but no one was there to save her.
[Deuteronomy] [22]:[28] If a man overpowers a young woman who’s not engaged, and rapes her, and it’s discovered,
[Deuteronomy] [22]:[29] that man must pay her father fifty silver coins, and she’ll become his wife because he’s violated her. He’ll then be prohibited from ever divorcing her.
[Deuteronomy] [22]:[30] A man must never sleep with any of his father’s wives because that would expose his father’s nakedness.
[Deuteronomy] [23]:[1] No man with crushed testicles or a severed penis is allowed to enter into Yahweh’s assembly.
[Deuteronomy] [23]:[2] No illegitimate child is allowed to enter into Yahweh’s assembly, even down to the tenth generation.
[Deuteronomy] [23]:[3] No Amoni or Moavi is allowed to enter into Yahweh’s assembly, even down past the tenth generation
[Deuteronomy] [23]:[4] since they wouldn’t even sell you bread and water when the people were travelling from Mitsrayim (Egypt) to Kena’an (Canaan). What’s more, they hired Be’or’s son Bil’am (Balaam) (from Petor in Aram-Naharayim) to curse you
[Deuteronomy] [23]:[5] However, your god Yahweh took no notice of Bil’am and turned the curse into a blessing because he loves you,
[Deuteronomy] [23]:[6] so you must never strive for peace or prosperity for the Amonim or the Moavim.
[Deuteronomy] [23]:[7] In contrast, don’t despise the Edomim because they’re your cousins (descendants of your ancestor Yitshak (Isaac) ). And don’t despise the Mitsrim (Egyptians), because you lived there as foreigners.
[Deuteronomy] [23]:[8] The third generation (grandchildren) of any of Edomim or Mitsrim that live among you, may enter Yahweh’s assembly.
[Deuteronomy] [23]:[9] When your warriors are out besieging your enemies, they you must avoid ceremonial impurity.
[Deuteronomy] [23]:[10] If something happens at night to make a man ‘unclean’, then he must stay outside the camp the next day and not join the others.
[Deuteronomy] [23]:[11] That evening, he must wash himself in water, then once the sun has set, he may reenter the camp.
[Deuteronomy] [23]:[12] You must have a place outside your camp where you can go to relieve yourself.
[Deuteronomy] [23]:[13] You must have a spade among your equipment so that when you go to relieve yourself, you can dig a hole and then cover it up afterwards,
[Deuteronomy] [23]:[14] because your god Yahweh walks in your camp to give you victory to defeat your enemies, so your camp must be sacred so he won’t see anything ‘unclean’ and turn away from you.
[Deuteronomy] [23]:[15] You mustn’t return any slaves to their master if they escaped and got to you.
[Deuteronomy] [23]:[16] Allow them to stay in your town and don’t mistreat them.
[Deuteronomy] [23]:[17] Don’t allow any Israeli man or woman to become a religious prostitute.
[Deuteronomy] [23]:[18] Don’t allow anyone woman or man to bring any part of their wages as a secular prostitute into your god Yahweh’s temple, because both female and male prostitution is abhorrent to him.
[Deuteronomy] [23]:[19] You mustn’t charge interest to your fellow Israeli, whether it’s money or food or anything else that’s borrowed.
[Deuteronomy] [23]:[20] You can charge foreigners interest, but not fellow Israelis so that your god Yahweh will bless your society in everything you do in the land that you’re about to occupy.
[Deuteronomy] [23]:[21] When you make a vow to your god Yahweh, don’t put off fulfilling it, because he will hold you accountable and not doing it would count as disobeying him.
[Deuteronomy] [23]:[22] However of course, if you don’t make any vows, then you won’t be guilty,
[Deuteronomy] [23]:[23] but if you’ve spoken your promise out loud to your god Yahweh, then you’re obligated to keep it.
[Deuteronomy] [23]:[24] If you’re walking through someone else’s vineyard, you can eat as many grapes as you like, but you mustn’t pick any to take away in a container.
[Deuteronomy] [23]:[25] Similarly, if you’re going through someone else’s field of grain, you can crunch a few kernels, but you mustn’t cut off any of the stalks.
[Deuteronomy] [24]:[1] When a man marries a woman, then further on he decides he doesn’t want her because of something he found out about her, then he must write a divorce notice and give it to her, and send her out of his house.
[Deuteronomy] [24]:[2] After she leaves that marriage, another man is allowed to marry her.
[Deuteronomy] [24]:[3] If that second husband also decides to divorce her by sending her away with a divorce notice, or if he were to die,
[Deuteronomy] [24]:[4] then the first husband isn’t allow to take her back as his wife. That’s because she’s been defiled and it would be abhorrent to Yahweh, and you mustn’t defile the land that your god Yahweh is giving you.
[Deuteronomy] [24]:[5] When a man is newly married, he mustn’t be called for the army or be given any other responsibilities. He must be free for one year to establish his house and to satisfy his new wife.
[Deuteronomy] [24]:[6] If someone borrows money, the lender mustn’t take their millstone for grinding grain as a pledge, because they need it to stay alive.
[Deuteronomy] [24]:[7] If someone is found to have abducted a fellow Israeli to make them into a slave or to sell them, then that abductor must be executed in order to purge such evils from your country.
[Deuteronomy] [24]:[8] Stay on guard against a deadly skin disease. Always follow what the priests and Levites tell you all to do, as I’ve instructed them.
[Deuteronomy] [24]:[9] Remember what your god Yahweh did to Miryam (Miriam) on the way out of Mitsrayim (Egypt).
[Deuteronomy] [24]:[10] If you’ve lent anything to a neighbour, don’t go into their house to collect their pledge.
[Deuteronomy] [24]:[11] Just wait outside, then the person you’ve lent something to will bring the item out to you.
[Deuteronomy] [24]:[12] However, if that person is poor and gives clothing or a blanket as security, don’t keep it overnight.
[Deuteronomy] [24]:[13] Take it back to them when the sun goes down so they’ll be warm when they sleep. Then they’ll bless you and your god Yahweh will be pleased with you.
[Deuteronomy] [24]:[14] Don’t oppress any poor or needy hired workers, whether they’re fellow Israelis or foreigners who live in your towns.
[Deuteronomy] [24]:[15] At the end of each day, pay them before sunset, because they need it to live on. Then they won’t cry out to Yahweh against you and have him hold you accountable.
[Deuteronomy] [24]:[16] Parents mustn’t be executed for what their children have done, and children mustn’t be executed for what their parents have done. Any person must only be executed for what they themselves have done.
[Deuteronomy] [24]:[17] Don’t pervert justice if it involves foreigners or orphans, and don’t take a widow’s cloak as security for a loan.
[Deuteronomy] [24]:[18] Remember that you were a slave in Mitsrayim (Egypt) and your god Yahweh rescued you from there. That’s why I’m commanding you to do those things—to be considerate about helping other people who are in need.
[Deuteronomy] [24]:[19] When you harvest your crops, if you forget a tied bundle in your field, don’t go back to get it—it’ll be for a resident foreigner or an orphan or widow to pick up, so that your god Yahweh can bless everything that you do.
[Deuteronomy] [24]:[20] When you beat your olive tree to make the fruit fall, don’t go back over it to pick the ones still on the tree. Those will be for the foreigner, or the orphan or widow.
[Deuteronomy] [24]:[21] Similarly, when you pick your grapes in the vineyard, don’t go back over the vines a second time. Those will be for the foreigner, or the orphan or widow.
[Deuteronomy] [24]:[22] Don’t forget that you were a slave in Mitsrayim—that’s why I’m instructing you to do those things.
[Deuteronomy] [25]:[1] If two parties have a dispute, they can request a judgement and the judges will decide who’s right and wrong.
[Deuteronomy] [25]:[2] If the guilty person is deserving of punishment, the judge will order him to lie on the ground where he’ll be whipped in front of the judge as the crime deserves.
[Deuteronomy] [25]:[3] He may not receive more than forty lashes because that would be too degrading.
[Deuteronomy] [25]:[4] Don’t cover your cow’s mouth when it’s pulling the grain threshing sledge.
[Deuteronomy] [25]:[5] If some brothers live on the same property and one of them dies without leaving a son, then the widow mustn’t marry outside of the family. Her brother-in-law must take her as a wife for himself and perform the duty of a brother-in-law.
[Deuteronomy] [25]:[6] If she gives birth to a son in due course, he’ll be considered as the son of the brother who died, so that his family name won’t disappear from Yisrael (Israel).
[Deuteronomy] [25]:[7] But if the dead man’s brother doesn’t want to marry the widow, she must go to the elders at the city gate and explain that her brother-in-law is refusing to do his duty to preserve the dead brother’s family name in Yisrael.
[Deuteronomy] [25]:[8] Then those elders must summon the brother and talk to him. However, if he really doesn’t want to marry her,
[Deuteronomy] [25]:[9] then his late brother’s wife must go up to him in front of those elders, and take his sandal off his foot and spit in his face. Then she must say, ‘That’s what happens to a man who won’t strengthen his brother’s family.’
[Deuteronomy] [25]:[10] After that, the brother will be known in Yisrael as the man who had his sandal taken off.
[Deuteronomy] [25]:[11] If two men are fighting each other, and one man’s wife comes to help her husband, and reaches out and grabs the other man’s private parts,
[Deuteronomy] [25]:[12] then you must cut her hand off. Don’t pity her.
[Deuteronomy] [25]:[13] Don’t keep two stone weights in your bag—a lighter one and a heavier one for when you’re buying and selling.
[Deuteronomy] [25]:[14] Don’t keep two measuring containers in your house—a smaller one and a larger one.
[Deuteronomy] [25]:[15] You must use exact stone weights and measuring containers so that your god Yahweh will prolong your time in the country that he’s giving you—
[Deuteronomy] [25]:[16] he can’t stand people who cheat others.
[Deuteronomy] [25]:[17] Don’t forget what the Amalekim did to you people when you came out of Mitsrayim (Egypt).
[Deuteronomy] [25]:[18] They met you on the road, then attacked you from behind—getting the stragglers who were weak and exhausted. They had no fear of God.
[Deuteronomy] [25]:[19] At some point in the future when your god Yahweh has given you the land to occupy as an inheritance, and you’re no longer being attacked by your enemies, you must eliminate the Amalekim so they won’t be remembered anymore. Don’t forget to do that.
[Deuteronomy] [26]:[1] After you’ve entered the land that your god Yahweh is giving you as an inheritance, and you occupy it and live there,

[Deuteronomy] [26]:[14] I never used any of it at a funeral, or took it in disobedience, or offered it to the dead. I’ve listen to the voice of my god Yahweh and followed all your instructions,
[Deuteronomy] [26]:[15] so look down from your sacred home in the heavens and bless your people Yisrael (Israel) and the land that you’ve given us that’s so fertile, as you had promised our ancestors.
[Deuteronomy] [26]:[16] Today your god Yahweh is commanding you to follow all these instructions and regulations, so follow them sincerely and enthusiastically.
[Deuteronomy] [26]:[17] You have declared today that Yahweh is your god, and that you’ll follow all his instructions and keep his regulations and commands and rules, and listen to his voice.
[Deuteronomy] [26]:[18] Also today, Yahweh has declared that you are his people, like a prized possession, like he told you that you would be. You must follow all his instructions
[Deuteronomy] [26]:[19] and then he’ll make your country greater than all the others that he’s established. You’ll be praised for your reputation and beauty, and you’ll be different from the others—being a sacred people for your god Yahweh, just like he’s said.
