[Yehoshua] [16]:[1] The block for Yosef’s (Joseph) descendants went from the Yarden (Jordan) at Yeriho (Jericho) (Yeriho, east of the springs), through the wilderness into the hill country of Beyt-El (Bethel).
[Yehoshua] [16]:[2] It went out from Beyt-El to Luz then along the border with the Arkim at Atarot.
[Yehoshua] [16]:[3] Then it went west to the border with the Yafletites as far as the border with Lower Beyt-Horon and as far as Gezer, then out to the Mediterranean.
[Yehoshua] [16]:[4] So Yosef’s sons Menasheh (Manasseh) and Efrayim (Ephraim) received an inheritance.
[Yehoshua] [16]:[5] The allotment for Efrayim’s (Ephraim) descendants according to their clans was at Atrot-Adar in the east, going as far as Upper Beyt-Horon
[Yehoshua] [16]:[6] and out to the Mediterranean. From Mikmetat in the north, the border went eastward toward Ta’anat-Shiloh then further east to Yanoah.
[Yehoshua] [16]:[7] From Yanoah it went to Atarot and Na’arah, reached Yeriho (Jericho) then came out at the Yarden (Jordan).
[Yehoshua] [16]:[8] The northern border went from Tapuah to the Kanah riverbed and then out to the Mediterranean. That was the inheritance of Efrayim’s descendants according to their clans,
[Yehoshua] [16]:[9] although some of the cities with their villages for Efrayim’s descendants were actually inside the territory assigned to Menasheh’s (Manasseh) descendants.
[Yehoshua] [16]:[10] But they didn’t capture the land of the Kena’anim (Canaanites) who lived in Gezer, so they’ve lived within Efrayim to this day and were forced to serve as labourers.
[Yehoshua] [17]:[1] The allotment for Menasheh’s (Manasseh) descendants (Yosef’s (Joseph) eldest son) included a special allotment for (Gilead’s father) Makir—he was given Gilead and Bashan because he was a powerful warrior.
[Yehoshua] [17]:[2] The other Menasheh clans that were allocated land were the Aviezer, Helek, Asriel, Shekem, Hefer, and Shemida clans. (They were the sons of Yosef’s son Menasheh who led their own clans.)
[Yehoshua] [17]:[3] But Tselofehad (son of Hefer, son of Gilead, son of Makir, son of Menasheh) had no sons—only daughters who were named Mahlah, Noa, Hoglah, Milkah, and Tirtsah.
[Yehoshua] [17]:[4] They approached the priest Eleazar and Yehoshua (Joshua) and the other leaders and said, “Yahweh told Mosheh (Moses) to give us an inheritance along with our brothers.” So he gave them an inheritance (like he’d given their uncles), as Yahweh had instructed them.
[Yehoshua] [17]:[5] So ten blocks were allocated to Menasheh tribe as well as Gilead and Bashan which were across the Yarden (Jordan)
[Yehoshua] [17]:[6] because Menasheh’s daughters received inheritances along with his sons. The land of Gilead belonged to the rest of Menasheh’s sons.
[Yehoshua] [17]:[7] The border for Menasheh went from Asher to Mikmetat opposite Shekem, then went south towards the spring at Tapuah.
[Yehoshua] [17]:[8] (The Tapuah land was for Menasheh, but Tapuah town was for Efrayim (Ephraim).)
[Yehoshua] [17]:[9] Then the border went south to the Kanah riverbed—the cities there belonged to Efrayim even though they were inside Menasheh’s land—then the border stayed on the north side of the riverbed and extended to the Mediterranean.
[Yehoshua] [17]:[10] So the south was for Efrayim and the north was for Menasheh, and the sea was the western border, meeting Asher from the north and Yisakar (Issachar) from the east.
[Yehoshua] [17]:[11] Menasheh was allocated cities inside both Yisakar’s and Asher’s territories: Beyt-Shean, Yivleam, Dor, Eyn-Dor, Ta’anak, and Megidon along with their surrounding towns.
[Yehoshua] [17]:[12] But Menasheh’s descendants weren’t able to take possession of those cities, so the Kena’anim (Canaanites) continued to live in the region.
[Yehoshua] [17]:[13] When the Israelis strengthened their position, they were able to force those Kena’anim to work for them, but they weren’t able to drive them out.
[Yehoshua] [17]:[14] Then the two half-tribes of Efrayim (Ephraim) and Menasheh (Manasseh) asked Yehoshua (Joshua), “Why have you only given to us one measured allocation as an inheritance when we’re very numerous because Yahweh has already blessed us?”
[Yehoshua] [17]:[15] “If there’s so many of you,” Yehoshua answered, “and if Efrayim’s hill-country is too small for you, go into the forested area of the Perizim and the Refaim and clear some land for yourselves there.”
[Yehoshua] [17]:[16] “The hill country certainly isn’t big enough for all of us,” they responded, “plus the Kena’anim (Canaanites) living in the Yizre’el (Jezreel) valley and in Beyt-Shean and the surrounding towns have iron chariots.”
[Yehoshua] [17]:[17] So Yehoshua told the half-tribes of Efrayim and Menasheh, “Yes, there’s a lot of you and you’re very powerful. One land allotment wouldn’t be enough for you
[Yehoshua] [17]:[18] so the hill country will be yours as well. However, it’s a forest and you’ll have to clear it to the borders. You’ll need to drive out the Kena’anim even if they are strong and with iron chariots.”
[Yehoshua] [18]:[1] Then all the Israelis assembled at Shiloh and set up the sacred tent there. The battles over the land had stopped
[Yehoshua] [18]:[2] but seven of their tribes hadn’t had their inheritances assigned yet.
[Yehoshua] [18]:[3] Yehoshua (Joshua) asked the Israelis, “How much longer are you all going to put off capturing the land that your ancestors’ God Yahweh has given you?
[Yehoshua] [18]:[4] Choose three men from each of those seven tribes and I’ll send them out to scout around and inspect the land and write descriptions of it in terms of potential allocations and bring it to me.
[Yehoshua] [18]:[5] They can divide that land into seven parts. (Yehudah (Judah) will maintain their territory in the south, and Yosef’s (Joseph) tribes in the north.)
[Yehoshua] [18]:[6] You all should write descriptions of the seven parts and bring them here to me, and in front of our god Yahweh, I’ll throw dice for you to allocate them to the seven tribes.
[Yehoshua] [18]:[7] However, the Levites don’t receive a portion, because their inheritance is Yahweh’s priesthood. Gad and Re’uven and the Menasheh (Manasseh) half-tribe have already received their inheritance that Yahweh’s servant Mosheh (Moses) allocated to them on the eastern side of the Yarden (Jordan).
[Yehoshua] [18]:[8] So the chosen men got ready to leave and Yehoshua instructed them, “Go and walk around that land and write a report and bring it back to me. Then I’ll throw dice for you all in front of Yahweh here in Shiloh.”
[Yehoshua] [18]:[9] Then the men left and walked through the area, writing down their recommendations for dividing the seven portions according to the cities in the area, then they returned back to Yehoshua at the camp at Shiloh.
[Yehoshua] [18]:[10] So Yehoshua threw dice for them at Shiloh in front of Yahweh, and so that land was allocated to those remaining seven tribes.
[Yehoshua] [18]:[11] The tribe of Benyamin won the first draw and the area for their clans was between the land assigned to Yehudah (Judah) and that assigned to Efrayim (Ephraim) and Menasheh (Manasseh).
[Yehoshua] [18]:[12] Their northern border went from the Yarden (Jordan) then to the northern side of Yeriho (Jericho) and up into the hill country to the west, coming out in the wilderness at Beyt-Aven.
[Yehoshua] [18]:[13] Then it went across towards Luz (now called Beyt-El (Bethel)) to the southern edge then downhill towards Atrot-Adar beside the hill south of lower Beyt-Horon.
[Yehoshua] [18]:[14] Then the western border turned from that hill and went south, coming out at Kiryat-Ba’al (also called Kiryat-Yearim—a town belonging to Yehudah) thus forming the western side.
[Yehoshua] [18]:[15] The southern border went west from Kiryat-Yearim to the spring at Neftoah,
[Yehoshua] [18]:[16] then downhill to the Ben-Hinom valley (in the valley of the Refaim to the north) then downhill to Hinom valley to the edge of the Yevusim and downhill to Eyn-Rogel.
[Yehoshua] [18]:[17] Then it turned northward and went west to Eyn-Shemesh and across to Gelilot opposite the Adumim pass, before going downhill to the Stone of Bohan (Re’uven’s son).
[Yehoshua] [18]:[18] It extended over to the northern slope of the Yarden valley and then downhill into the actual valley.
[Yehoshua] [18]:[19] It then went east to the northern slope of Beyt-Hoglah before coming out at the north end of the Dead Sea (also called the Salt Sea) where the Yarden river flows into it. That was the southern boundary
[Yehoshua] [18]:[20] and the Yarden borders it on the east. Those were the borders of Benyamin’s descendants’ inheritance according to their clans.
[Yehoshua] [18]:[21] The cities allocated to Benyamin’s descendants and their clans were: Yeriho (Jericho), Beyt-Hoglah, Emek-Ketsits,
[Yehoshua] [18]:[22] Beyt-Ha’aravah, Tsemarayim, Beyt-El (Bethel),
[Yehoshua] [18]:[23] Avim, Parah, Ofrah,
[Yehoshua] [18]:[24] Kefar-Ha’amoni, Ofni, and Geva—a total of twelve cities as well as their surrounding villages.
[Yehoshua] [18]:[25] Also Giveon, Ramah, Be’erot,
[Yehoshua] [18]:[26] Mitspah, Kefirah, Motsah,
[Yehoshua] [18]:[27] Rekem, Yirpe’el, Tar’alah,
[Yehoshua] [18]:[28] Tsela, Haelef, Yevus (now called Yerushalem (Jerusalem)), Giveah, and Kiryat—a total of fourteen cities as well as their surrounding villages. Those were Benyamin’s descendants’ inheritance according to their clans.
[Yehoshua] [19]:[1] The second draw went to Shim’on’s (Simeon) descendants and the land for their clans was in the middle of Yehudah’s (Judah) territory.
[Yehoshua] [19]:[2] Shim’on’s inheritance included: Be’er-Sheva (Beersheba), Moladah,
[Yehoshua] [19]:[3] Hatsar-Shual, Balah, Etsem,
[Yehoshua] [19]:[4] Eltolad, Betul, Hormah,
[Yehoshua] [19]:[5] Tsiklag, Beyt-Hamarkavot. Hatsar-Susah,
[Yehoshua] [19]:[6] Beyt-Leva’ot, and Sharuhen—thirteen cities as well as their surrounding villages.
[Yehoshua] [19]:[7] Also Ayin, Rimon, Eter, and Asha—four cities as well as their surrounding villages,
[Yehoshua] [19]:[8] and all the further villages around those cities as far as Ba’alat-Be’er (also called Ramah of the Negev). That was Shim’on’s descendants’ inheritance according to their clans.
[Yehoshua] [19]:[9] This took away some of Yehudah’s inheritance and gave it to Shim’on’s descendants because Yehudah’s initial area was more than they needed.
[Yehoshua] [19]:[10] The third draw went to Zevulun’s descendants according to their clans. The southern border for their inheritance started at Sarid
[Yehoshua] [19]:[11] and went west to Maralah and Dabeshet then to the riverbed facing Yakeneam.
[Yehoshua] [19]:[12] Also from Sarid it went toward the east beside the border with Kislot-Tavor and then on to Davrat and then to Yafia.
[Yehoshua] [19]:[13] From there it extended east to Gat-Hahefer and Et-Katsin and north to Rimon before turning to Ne’ah.
[Yehoshua] [19]:[14] Then it passed north of Hanaton ending at Yiftah-El valley.
[Yehoshua] [19]:[15] It included the cities of Katat, Nahalal, Shimron, Yid’alah, and Beyt-Lehem (Bethlehem)—a total of twelve cities as well as their surrounding villages.
[Yehoshua] [19]:[16] That was Zevulun’s descendants’ inheritance according to their clans, including those cities as well as their surrounding villages.
[Yehoshua] [19]:[17] The fourth draw went to Yisakar’s (Issachar) descendants according to their clans.
[Yehoshua] [19]:[18] Their land included the cities of Yizre’el (Jezreel), Kesulot, Shunem,
[Yehoshua] [19]:[19] Hafarayim, Shi’on, Anaharat,
[Yehoshua] [19]:[20] Rabbit, Kishyon, Evets,
[Yehoshua] [19]:[21] Remet, Eyn-Ganim, Eyn-Hadah, and Beyt-Patsets.
[Yehoshua] [19]:[22] The border of their allotment met with Tavor, Shahatsimah, and Beyt-Shemesh (Heliopolis), coming out in the east at the Yarden (Jordan)—a total of sixteen cities as well as their surrounding villages.
[Yehoshua] [19]:[23] That was Yisakar’s descendants’ inheritance according to their clans, including those cities as well as their surrounding villages.
[Yehoshua] [19]:[24] The fifth draw went to Asher’s descendants according to their clans.
[Yehoshua] [19]:[25] Their land included the cities of Helkat, Hali, Beten, Akshaf,
[Yehoshua] [19]:[26] Alamelek, Am’ad, and Mish’al. Their western border started at Mt. Karmel and Shihor-Livnat
[Yehoshua] [19]:[27] and turned back to the east to Beyt-Dagon and the border with Zevulun and the Yiftah-El valley to the north. Then it went to Beyt-Emek and Neiel and north to Kavul,
[Yehoshua] [19]:[28] Avdon, Rehov, Hamon and Kanah, as far as Greater Tsidon (Sidon).
[Yehoshua] [19]:[29] The border then turned back to Ramah and to the fortified city of Tsor (Tyre) and turns west to Hosah coming out at the Mediterranean near Akziv.
[Yehoshua] [19]:[30] It also included Umah, Afek, and Rehov—a total of twenty-two cities as well as their surrounding villages.
[Yehoshua] [19]:[31] That was Asher’s descendants’ inheritance according to their clans, including those cities as well as their surrounding villages.
[Yehoshua] [19]:[32] The sixth draw went to Naftali’s (Naphtali) descendants according to their clans.
[Yehoshua] [19]:[33] Their border started in Helef (where there was an oak tree at Tsa’ananim) then Adami-Nekev and Yavne’el and on to Lakum before exiting at the Yarden (Jordan).
[Yehoshua] [19]:[34] Then it turned west to Aznot-Tavor and from there to Hukok, meeting the border with Zevulun on the south, the border with Asher on the west, and the border with Yehudah (Judah) on the east.
[Yehoshua] [19]:[35] The fortified cities were Tsidim, Tser, Hamat, Rakat, Kineret,
[Yehoshua] [19]:[36] Admah, Ramah, Hatsor,
[Yehoshua] [19]:[37] Kedesh, Edre’i, Eyn-Hatsor,
[Yehoshua] [19]:[38] Yir’on, Migdal-El, Horem, Beyt-Anat, and Beyt-Shemesh (Heliopolis)—a total of nineteen cities as well as their surrounding villages.
[Yehoshua] [19]:[39] That was Naftali’s descendants’ inheritance according to their clans, including those cities as well as their surrounding villages.
[Yehoshua] [19]:[40] The final seventh draw went to Dan’s descendants according to their clans.
[Yehoshua] [19]:[41] Their land included the cities of Tsor’ah, Eshtaol, Ir-Shemesh,
[Yehoshua] [19]:[42] Sha’alvim, Ayalon, and Yitlah,
[Yehoshua] [19]:[43] Eylon, Timnah, Ekron,
[Yehoshua] [19]:[44] Elteke, Gibton, Ba’alat,
[Yehoshua] [19]:[45] Yehud, Beney-Berak, Gat-Rimon,
[Yehoshua] [19]:[46] Mey-Hayarkon, Rakon, and the area opposite Yafo (Joppa).
[Yehoshua] [19]:[47] Dan’s border went out from them. Then Dan’s descendants battled against Leshem and captured it and slaughtered their inhabitants. So they took it over and settled in Leshem but they renamed it to ‘Dan’ after their ancestor.
[Yehoshua] [19]:[48] That was Dan’s descendants’ inheritance according to their clans, including those cities as well as their surrounding villages.
[Yehoshua] [19]:[49] After the allocation of the blocks of land to the various tribes, the Israelis gave Yehoshua (Joshua) (Nun’s son) his own inheritance among them.
[Yehoshua] [19]:[50] Following Yahweh’s instructions to give Yehoshua whatever city he asked for, he was given Timnat-Serah in the hill country of Efrayim (Ephraim) and he built up that city and lived in it.
[Yehoshua] [19]:[51] Those were the allotments that Eleazar the priest and Yehoshua (Nun’s son) gave to the leaders of the Israeli tribes as their inheritances. It was done by throwing dice there in Shiloh in front of Yahweh at the opening of the sacred tent, and so the land division was completed.
[Yehoshua] [20]:[1] Then Yahweh told Yehoshua (Joshua),
[Yehoshua] [20]:[2] “Tell the Israelis to select some cities that people can flee to in order to be safe, just as I instructed you through Mosheh (Moses),
[Yehoshua] [20]:[3] so that if someone accidentally kills someone else, they can escape there and be safe from the dead person’s family.
[Yehoshua] [20]:[4] When that person flees to one of these cities, they must stand at the city gate and tell the elders there what happened. Then they should bring the person into the city and give them a place there to live in.
[Yehoshua] [20]:[5] Now if a relative of the deceased comes to avenge the death, the city elders won’t hand over the killer because the death was accidental and didn’t happen because of hate or premeditation.
[Yehoshua] [20]:[6] So then that person must stay in the city until they’re brought before the panel of judges. If they decide that the death wasn’t deliberate, the person must remain in that city until the death of the high priest, then they can freely return to their own city and own home.”
[Yehoshua] [20]:[7] So the Israelis chose Kedesh (in the Galil region in the hill country of Naftali (Naphtali)) and Shekem (in the hill country of Efrayim (Ephraim)) and Kiryat-Arba (now called Hevron, in the hill country of Yehudah (Judah)).
[Yehoshua] [20]:[8] On the other side of the Yarden (Jordan) river, they chose Betser (in the wilderness on the plateau from the tribe of Re’uven), Ramot (in the Gilead from the tribe of Gad), and Golan (in the Bashan from the tribe of Menasheh (Manasseh)).
[Yehoshua] [20]:[9] Those were the appointed cities for both Israelis and foreigners living among them, so that anyone who accidentally killed someone could flee there and be safe from being avenged by the deceased’s relatives until they could receive a proper trial.
[Yehoshua] [21]:[1] Then the leaders of the Levites went to Eleazar the priest and to Yehoshua (Joshua) (Nun’s son) and to the Israeli elders
[Yehoshua] [21]:[2] at Shiloh (in the Kena’an (Canaan) region) and told them, “Yahweh said through Mosheh (Moses) that we should be given cities to live in, along with their surrounding fields for our livestock.”
[Yehoshua] [21]:[3] So the Israeli leaders gave these cities and the fields around them to the Levites for their inheritance as Yahweh had instructed:
[Yehoshua] [21]:[4] The first draw went to those of the Kohat clans who were descendants of Aharon (Aaron) the priest (from the Levites). They were allocated thirteen cities in the regions occupied by Yehudah (Judah), Shim’on (Simeon), and Benyamin.
[Yehoshua] [21]:[5] The remaining Kohat clans were allocated ten cities in the regions occupied by Efrayim (Ephraim), Dan, and the Menasheh (Manasseh) half-tribe.
[Yehoshua] [21]:[6] The Gereshon clans were allocated thirteen cities in the regions occupied by Yisakar (Issachar), Asher, Naftali (Naphtali), and by the Menasheh half-tribe in the Bashan region.
[Yehoshua] [21]:[7] The Merari clans were allocated twelve cities in the regions occupied by Re’uven, Gad, and Zevulun.
[Yehoshua] [21]:[8] So the Israeli leaders gave those cities and their surrounding fields to the Levites, just as Yahweh had instructed through Mosheh (Moses).
[Yehoshua] [21]:[9] These are the names of the cities allocated by the Israeli leaders (from the regions occupied by Yehudah and Shim’on)
[Yehoshua] [21]:[10] that were given to the Levite Kohat clans since they were selected first in the draw:
[Yehoshua] [21]:[11] Kiryat-Arba and the surrounding fields (now called Hevron—Arba was the father of Anak) in Yehudah’s hill country
[Yehoshua] [21]:[12] (although the surrounding countryside and villages had already been given to Yefuneh’s son Kalev (Caleb)).
[Yehoshua] [21]:[13] So Hevron was given to the descendants of Aharon (Aaron) the priest and assigned as a refuge city (for anyone who accidentally kills someone) along with the surrounding fields, along with Livnah,
[Yehoshua] [21]:[14] Yatir, Eshtemoa,
[Yehoshua] [21]:[15] Holon, Devir,
[Yehoshua] [21]:[16] Ayin, Yutah, and Beyt-Shemesh (Heliopolis), all with their surrounding fields—a total of nine cities from within Yehudah and Shim’on’s territories.
[Yehoshua] [21]:[17] From Benyamin’s territories, the Israeli leaders assigned Giveon, Geva,
[Yehoshua] [21]:[18] Anatot, and Almon—four cities and their surrounding fields.
[Yehoshua] [21]:[19] Thus the descendants of Aharon the priests received thirteen cities with their surrounding fields.
[Yehoshua] [21]:[20] The other Levite Kohat clans were allocated cities from within Efrayim’s (Ephraim) territory:
[Yehoshua] [21]:[21] Shekem (which was assigned as a refuge city for anyone who accidentally kills someone), Gezer,
[Yehoshua] [21]:[22] Kivtsayim, and Beyt-Horon—four cities with their surrounding fields.
[Yehoshua] [21]:[23] From Dan’s territory, they were allocated Elteke, Gibton,
[Yehoshua] [21]:[24] Ayalon, and Gat-Rimon—four cities with their surrounding fields.
[Yehoshua] [21]:[25] From the Menasheh half-tribe’s territory, they were allocated Ta’anak and Gat-Rimon—two cities with their surrounding fields.
[Yehoshua] [21]:[26] Thus the other Levite Kohat clans received ten cities with their surrounding fields.
[Yehoshua] [21]:[27] The Levite Gereshon clans were allocated cities from within the Menasheh (Manasseh) half-tribe’s territory: Golan in the Bashan (which was assigned as a refuge city for anyone who accidentally kills someone) and Be’eshterah—two cities with their surrounding fields.
[Yehoshua] [21]:[28] From Yisakar’s (Issachar) territory, they were allocated Kishyon, Davrat,
[Yehoshua] [21]:[29] Yarmut, and Eyn-Ganim—four cities with their surrounding fields.
[Yehoshua] [21]:[30] From Asher’s territory, they were allocated Mish’al, Avdon,
[Yehoshua] [21]:[31] Helkat, and Rehov—four cities with their surrounding fields.
[Yehoshua] [21]:[32] From Naftali’s (Naphtali) territory, they were allocated Kedesh in the Galil (which was assigned as a refuge city for anyone who accidentally kills someone), Hamot-Dor, and Kartan—three cities with their surrounding fields.
[Yehoshua] [21]:[33] Thus the Levite Gereshon clan received thirteen cities with their surrounding fields.
[Yehoshua] [21]:[34] The remaining Levite Merari clans were allocated cities from within Zevulun’s territory: Yakeneam, Kartah,
[Yehoshua] [21]:[35] Dimnah, and Nahalal—four cities with their surrounding fields.
[Yehoshua] [21]:[36] From Re’uven’s territory, they were allocated Betser, Yahats,
[Yehoshua] [21]:[37] Kedemot, and Mofa’at—four cities with their surrounding fields.
[Yehoshua] [21]:[38] From Gad’s territory, they were allocated Ramot in the Gilead (which was assigned as a refuge city for anyone who accidentally kills someone), Mahanayim,
[Yehoshua] [21]:[39] Heshbon, and Yazer—four cities with their surrounding fields.
[Yehoshua] [21]:[40] Thus the Levite Merari clan received twelve cities in the draw, along with their surrounding fields.
[Yehoshua] [21]:[41] So altogether the Levites received forty-eight cities and their surrounding fields from with the territories of the other tribes—
[Yehoshua] [21]:[42] each of those cities had fields around them for their livestock to graze on.
[Yehoshua] [21]:[43] Thus Yahweh gave the Israelis all the land that he’d promised their ancestors would be given and so the people moved into those regions and lived there.
[Yehoshua] [21]:[44] Yahweh gave them peace as he’d promised their ancestors—none of their enemies could stand against them because Yahweh helped them defeat any enemies.
[Yehoshua] [21]:[45] Yahweh kept every promise that he’d made to the Israelis—it all happened just like he’d said.
[Yehoshua] [22]:[1] Then Yehoshua (Joshua) summoned the tribes of Re’uven and Gad, and the Menasheh (Manasseh) half-tribe
[Yehoshua] [22]:[2] and told them, “You yourselves have obeyed everything that Yahweh’s servant Mosheh (Moses) instructed you to do. In addition, you’ve all followed everything that I told you.
[Yehoshua] [22]:[3] You’ve all supported your fellow tribes all this time and fulfilled what your god Yahweh requested of you all,
[Yehoshua] [22]:[4] and now he has enabled these other tribes to rest from battle just like he told them he would. So now, you all may go back to your homes that Yahweh’s servant Mosheh gave you on the other side of the river.
[Yehoshua] [22]:[5] Only do take care to continue to obey the instructions and the law that Yahweh’s servant Mosheh gave you: to love your god Yahweh, to follow him and his instructions, to stay close to him, and to serve him with all your hearts and your inner selves.”
[Yehoshua] [22]:[6] Then Yehoshua blessed them and sent them on their way to return to their homes.
[Yehoshua] [22]:[7] (Mosheh had given the Bashan to the half of the Menasheh half-tribe, and Yehoshua had given land on the western side of the Yarden (Jordan) to the other half.) When he’d blessed them
[Yehoshua] [22]:[8] he’d said, “Go back to your homes with many riches: plenty of livestock, and with silver, gold, bronze, and iron, and with lots of clothing. Share the plunder from your enemies with those who remained behind.”
[Yehoshua] [22]:[9] So the warriors from the tribes of Re’uven, Gad, and the Menasheh half-tribe left the others there at Shiloh in the Kena’an (Canaan) region, and went back to their own land in Gilead across the river which they had taken for themselves with the agreement of Yahweh given through Mosheh.
[Yehoshua] [22]:[10] The warriors from the tribes of Re’uven, Gad, and the Menasheh (Manasseh) half-tribe arrived at the Yarden (Jordan) river (still on the Kena’an (Canaan) side) and they built a very large and noticeable altar there before crossing over to go home.
[Yehoshua] [22]:[11] When the other Israelis heard about it, they said, “Look, the men from the tribes of Re’uven, Gad, and the Menasheh half-tribe have built the altar at the entrance to this Kena’an region down at the Yarden on our side.”
[Yehoshua] [22]:[12] Hearing that, those from the western side of the Yarden assembled at Shiloh to go to battle with the two and a half tribes on the eastern side.
[Yehoshua] [22]:[13] Meanwhile, they sent the priest Pinhas (Eleazar’s son) across into the Gilead region to talk with the leaders from the tribes of Re’uven, Gad, and the Menasheh half-tribe.
[Yehoshua] [22]:[14] Pinhas took ten leaders with him—important leaders from each of the Israeli tribes from the western side.
[Yehoshua] [22]:[15] They crossed over to the Gilead region to talk to the leaders from the tribes of Re’uven, Gad, and the Menasheh half-tribe. They said,
[Yehoshua] [22]:[16] “Yahweh’s people are asking, ‘What’s this unfaithfulness that you all have done unfaithfully against Yisrael’s (Israel) god—turning away from Yahweh when you built an altar for yourselves today in rebellion against Yahweh?
[Yehoshua] [22]:[17] Wasn’t our disobedience at Pe’or bad enough for you? We haven’t gotten over it to this day. Plus there was a deadly disease among Yahweh’s people.
[Yehoshua] [22]:[18] But all of you—are you turning away from Yahweh today? If you all rebel against Yahweh today, tomorrow he’ll be furious at all of us.
[Yehoshua] [22]:[19] But if it’s because you all think this land here is defiled, then cross back over to Yahweh’s own land where he lives in his sacred tent. Either way don’t rebel against Yahweh by building this other altar for yourselves that’s distinct from our god Yahweh’s altar.
[Yehoshua] [22]:[20] Didn’t Akan act unfaithfully taking something that was forbidden and all of us suffered as a result of it? It wasn’t just him alone that died because of that.’ ”
[Yehoshua] [22]:[21] The leaders from the tribes of Re’uven, Gad, and the Menasheh half-tribe answered the other leaders,
[Yehoshua] [22]:[22] “Yahweh is the god of gods. Yahweh is the god of gods. He knows, and as for the Israeli people, let them know also—if it was in rebellion or in unfaithfulness against Yahweh, don’t bother trying to save us today.
[Yehoshua] [22]:[23] If we’d aimed to build an altar for ourselves to turn away from following Yahweh, or if it was to offer burnt offerings or grain offerings on it, or if to make the sacrifices of peace offerings on it, Yahweh himself will handle it.
[Yehoshua] [22]:[24] But no, we did it because we foresaw a potential problem: what if in the future, your descendants ask our descendants over here on this side of the river, ‘What do you lot have to do with Yisrael’s god Yahweh?
[Yehoshua] [22]:[25] Yahweh has given this Yarden (Jordan) river as a border between us, and you descendants of Re’uven and Gad. You all don’t have any part in Yahweh.’ Then your descendants might make our descendants stop worshipping Yahweh.
[Yehoshua] [22]:[26] So we decided to build the altar—not to be used for burnt offerings or for sacrifices,
[Yehoshua] [22]:[27] but as a symbol to remind our future descendants and yours, that we all truly worship Yahweh with our burnt offerings, our sacrifices, and our peace offerings, so your descendants can’t tell our future descendants that we have no business worshipping Yahweh.
[Yehoshua] [22]:[28] If they do say anything like that, then our descendants will be able to reply, ‘See that copy of Yahweh’s altar which isn’t used for burnt offerings or sacrifices, our ancestors built that as a reminder for both you all and us.’
[Yehoshua] [22]:[29] May any idea of rebelling against Yahweh stay far from us. Same with any idea of building any altar apart from our god Yahweh’s genuine altar for burnt offerings, or grain offerings, or other sacrifices.”
[Yehoshua] [22]:[30] So Pinhas the priest and the other community and clan leaders with him, listened to what the descendants of Re’uven, Gad, and Menasheh (Manasseh) told them, and it sounded sensible to them,
[Yehoshua] [22]:[31] so Pinhas (the late Eleazar’s son) told them, “Today we realise that Yahweh is among us and that you all haven’t acted unfaithfully against him, so therefore you’ve prevented Yahweh from needing to punish us.”
[Yehoshua] [22]:[32] Then Pinhas and the other leaders left Gilead and returned back across the Yarden to the Kena’an (Canaan) region where most of the Israelis resided, taking back a good report.
[Yehoshua] [22]:[33] The people were pleased with that news, and they thanked God and stopped talking about going to war with Re’uven and Gad across the river and destroying them.
[Yehoshua] [22]:[34] The descendants of Re’uven and Gad named the altar ‘Reminder’ because it was a reminder between them that Yahweh is God.
[Yehoshua] [23]:[1] A long time passed and Yahweh had given Yisrael (Israel) peace without attacks from their enemies all around, and Yehoshua (Joshua) was now in his old age,
[Yehoshua] [23]:[2] so he summoned all the Israeli elders and leaders, along with the judges and officials. He told them, “Now I’m in my old age,
[Yehoshua] [23]:[3] but you all have seen what Yahweh did to all those kingdoms ahead of you, because he’s the one who fights for you all.
[Yehoshua] [23]:[4] I’ve allocated the remaining kingdoms that you all will defeat as an inheritance for your tribes, alongside those that I conquered from the Yarden (Jordan) to the Mediterranean in the west
[Yehoshua] [23]:[5] Your god Yahweh will push them out ahead of you all and capture their lands for you to possess, just as he told you he would.
[Yehoshua] [23]:[6] Take great care to obey and do everything that Mosheh (Moses) wrote down—don’t deviate from it in any way.
[Yehoshua] [23]:[7] Don’t enter those remaining kingdoms, and don’t mention the name of their gods or make an oath using their names and don’t worship or bow down to them.
[Yehoshua] [23]:[8] Instead you all should cling to your god Yahweh, just as you’ve done until now.
[Yehoshua] [23]:[9] Yes, Yahweh has driven away many great kingdoms ahead of you all, and until this day, none of them have stood against you.
[Yehoshua] [23]:[10] Just one of you can make a thousand men flee, because Yahweh is your god—he’s the one who fights for you just like he said he would.
[Yehoshua] [23]:[11] Make a great effort to guard yourselves that you all continue to love your god Yahweh.
[Yehoshua] [23]:[12] Yes, if you all ever turn away from him and instead cling to those remaining kingdoms or remaining people, and if you intermarry with them or associate with them,
[Yehoshua] [23]:[13] you all will certainly soon find out that your god Yahweh will not continue to drive out these nations ahead of you. Then they will end up trapping and snaring you all, and be like a whip on your sides and like thorns in your eyes, until you all perish from on this good land that Yahweh your god has given you.
[Yehoshua] [23]:[14] Listen, today I’m about to go the way that everyone has to go and you all know with all your heart and with all your soul that not one thing has failed to come true from all the good things that your god Yahweh said about you. Everything has happened as said—down to the very last word.
[Yehoshua] [23]:[15] And just like all those good things came true, so too Yahweh will send all the punishments he promised you all if you disobey him, even if it means that he destroys you all from this good land that he’s given you.
[Yehoshua] [23]:[16] If you ignore the agreement with your god Yahweh and disobey his commands and go and serve other gods and bow down to them, then his anger will flare up against you all and you’ll quickly be wiped out from the good land that he has given you.”
[Yehoshua] [24]:[1] Then Yehoshua (Joshua) assembled all the tribes of Yisrael (Israel) at Shekem. He summoned their elders, leaders, judges, and officers, and they presented themselves before God,
[Yehoshua] [24]:[2] and Yehoshua told all the people, “Yahweh, the god of Yisrael says: Your ancestors including Terah the father of Avraham and Nahor, lived beyond the Perat (Euphrates) river from long ago, but they worshipped other gods.
[Yehoshua] [24]:[3] Then I took your ancestor Avraham from beyond the river and brought him across all the land of Kena’an (Canaan), and I multiplied his descendants, including giving him Yitshak (Isaac).
[Yehoshua] [24]:[4] Then I gave Ya’akov (Jacob) and Esav (Esau) to Yitshak, and I gave Esav the hill country of Se’ir but Ya’akov and his sons went down to Mitsrayim (Egypt).
[Yehoshua] [24]:[5] I sent Mosheh (Moses) and Aharon (Aaron) and I damaged Mitsrayim internally, and then I brought you all out again.
[Yehoshua] [24]:[6] I brought your ancestors out of Mitsrayim, and you all came to the edge of the Red Sea. The Mitsrim (Egyptians) chased after them with chariots and horsemen
[Yehoshua] [24]:[7] and the people cried out to Yahweh, and he placed darkness between you and the Mitsrim. After bringing you all through the sea, he brought the sea over the Mitsri (Egyptian) army and drowned them. Your own eyes saw what I did to Mitsrayim. Then you all lived a long time in the wilderness.
[Yehoshua] [24]:[8] “After that, I brought you to the region of the Amorim who lived on the eastern side of the Yarden (Jordan), and they battled against you all, but I gave you victory over them and I destroyed them from ahead of you and you all took over their land.
[Yehoshua] [24]:[9] Then (Tsipor’s son) King Balak of Moav (Moab) prepared his warriors and fought against you all and he summoned (Be’or’s son) Bil’am (Balaam) to curse you.
[Yehoshua] [24]:[10] But I wasn’t willing to listen to Bil’am, so instead, he blessed you all repeatedly and I rescued you from King Balak.
[Yehoshua] [24]:[11] Then you crossed over the Yarden river and arrived at Yeriho (Jericho). The men of Yeriho fought against you all, as did the Amorim, the Perizim, the Kena’anim (Canaanites), the Hitim, the Girgashim, the Hivim, and the Yevusim but I helped you all to defeat them.
[Yehoshua] [24]:[12] I sent hornets ahead of you all and they drove out the two Amori kings—it wasn’t your swords or bows that did it.
[Yehoshua] [24]:[13] So I gave you all a land which you didn’t earn yourselves and cities to live in that you all didn’t build yourselves. You all are benefitting from vineyards and olive groves that you didn’t plant.”
[Yehoshua] [24]:[14] The Yehoshua (Joshua) continued, “Now you all must respect Yahweh and faithfully serve him with your complete beings. And you all must remove the idols that your ancestors served beyond the Perat (Euphrates) and in Mitsrayim, and only serve Yahweh.
[Yehoshua] [24]:[15] But if you all dislike serving Yahweh, then choose for yourselves today who you will serve: perhaps the gods your fathers once served beyond the Perat, or the gods of the Amori people in whose land you are now living. But as for me and my household, we will serve Yahweh.”
[Yehoshua] [24]:[16] “We’d never even consider leaving Yahweh to serve other gods,” the people responded,
[Yehoshua] [24]:[17] “because Yahweh is our god. He is the one who brought us and our ancestors out from slavery in the land of Mitsrayim, and who did those great miracles right in front of our eyes. Also, he looked after us on our entire journey and among all the people groups that we passed by.
[Yehoshua] [24]:[18] Yahweh drove all the peoples out ahead of us, even the Amorim who lived in that region. So we too we will serve Yahweh because he is our god.”
[Yehoshua] [24]:[19] “You all won’t be able to serve Yahweh,” warned Yehoshua, “because he’s a god who cannot mix with sin. He’s a jealous God—he won’t forgive your rebellion and disobedience.
[Yehoshua] [24]:[20] If you abandon Yahweh and serve the gods of other nations, then he’ll turn and do harm to you all and destroy you, even if he’s previously been good to you all.”
[Yehoshua] [24]:[21] But the people answered Yehoshua, “No, we will worship Yahweh.”
[Yehoshua] [24]:[22] Then Yehoshua cautioned the people, “You all are witnesses against yourselves, that you yourselves have chosen to serve Yahweh.” “We are witnesses,” they confirmed.
[Yehoshua] [24]:[23] “Then you all go right now and remove the foreign gods that you already have, and turn your hearts towards Yahweh, the god of Yisrael (Israel),” said Yehoshua.
[Yehoshua] [24]:[24] “We will serve our god Yahweh, and we will listen to his voice,” the people replied.
[Yehoshua] [24]:[25] So Yehoshua made a formal agreement with the people in Shekem on that day, establishing rules and laws for them.
[Yehoshua] [24]:[26] He wrote them in the book of God’s law. Then he took a large stone and set it up there beneath the oak tree that was by Yahweh’s sacred tent.
[Yehoshua] [24]:[27] “Look at this stone,” Yehoshua said to all the people. “It will be for a witness against us, because it has heard everything that Yahweh has instructed us, and it will be for a witness against you all, in case you act deceptively against your god.”
[Yehoshua] [24]:[28] Then Yehoshua sent all the people off to go to their allotted regions.
[Yehoshua] [24]:[29] After all that, Nun’s son and Yahweh’s servant Yehoshua (Joshua) died at the age of 110.
[Yehoshua] [24]:[30] They buried him in his allotted property at Timnat-Serah which is in the Efrayim (Ephraim) hill country north of Mt. Ga’ash.
[Yehoshua] [24]:[31] The Israelis had served Yahweh all through Yehoshua’s lifetime and throughout the lifetimes of the elders who lived longer than Yehoshua and who had experienced everything that Yahweh had done for Yisrael (Israel).
[Yehoshua] [24]:[32] They buried Yosef’s (Joseph) bones (that they had carried out from Mitsrayim (Egypt)) in Shekem—in the portion of the field that Ya’akov (Jacob) had bought from the sons of Hamor (Shekem’s father) for a hundred coins, and that land became the inheritance of Yosef’s descendants.
[Yehoshua] [24]:[33] Aharon’s (Aaron) son Eleazar also died and was buried at Giveah—the city that belonged to his son Pinhas in the Efrayim hill country.
[Heroes and Guides] [1]:[1] After Yehoshua’s (Joshua) death, the Israelis asked Yahweh, “Which tribe should go first to attack the Kena’anim (Canaanites)?”
[Heroes and Guides] [1]:[2] “Yehudah (Judah) will go first,” Yahweh answered. “Listen, I’ve already determined that they’ll conquer the land.”
[Heroes and Guides] [1]:[3] Then the Yehudah leaders said to the tribe of Shim’on (Simeon), “Come with us into the region that we’ve been allocated and we can fight together against the Kena’anim. Then we’ll do the same in your area.” So the warriors from the two tribes worked together.
[Heroes and Guides] [1]:[4] When they attacked, Yahweh gave them victory over the Kena’anim and the Perizim and they killed ten thousand men at Bezek.
[Heroes and Guides] [1]:[5] They confronted Adoni-Vezek in Bezek and fought against him (then eventually defeating the Kena’anim and the Perizim).
[Heroes and Guides] [1]:[6] Adoni-Vezek tried to flee but they chased him and captured him, cutting off his thumbs and big toes.
[Heroes and Guides] [1]:[7] “Seventy kings had their thumbs and big toes chopped off,” Adoni-Vezek said, “and were gathering scraps of food beneath my table. Just as I have done, so God has repaid to me.” Then they took him to Yerushalem (Jerusalem) and he died there.
[Heroes and Guides] [1]:[8] The warriors from Yehudah (Judah) attacked Yerushalem (Jerusalem) and captured the city, killing the inhabitants and setting the city on fire.
[Heroes and Guides] [1]:[9] Then they fought against the Kena’anim (Canaanites) who lived in the hill country, in the southern wilderness, and in the western foothills.
[Heroes and Guides] [1]:[10] They also fought the Kena’anim in Kiryat-Arba (now known as Hevron) and killed Sheshay, Ahiman, and Talmay.
[Heroes and Guides] [1]:[11] From there they fought against Kiryat-Sefer (now known as Devir).
[Heroes and Guides] [1]:[12] Kalev (Caleb) had said, “The one who attacks Kiryat-Sefer and captures it can marry my daughter Aksah.”
[Heroes and Guides] [1]:[13] Otniel (son of Kalev’s younger brother Kenaz) captured it so Kalev gave his daughter Aksah to him to become his wife.
[Heroes and Guides] [1]:[14] After the wedding, she urged Otniel to ask her father for a field. When she got off her donkey, Kalev asked her, “What can I do for you?”
[Heroes and Guides] [1]:[15] “Give me a blessing,” she requested. “Although you’ve given me land in the southern wilderness, give me some springs of water as well.” So Kalev gave her the upper springs and the lower springs.
[Heroes and Guides] [1]:[16] The Keynim (descendants of Mosheh’s (Moses) father-in-law), left the city of palm trees (Yeriho (Jericho) ) and went with Yehudah’s (Judah) descendants to the southern wilderness near Arad and lived with the people there.
[Heroes and Guides] [1]:[17] Then the warriors of Yehudah and Shim’on (Simeon) conquered the Kena’anim (Canaanites) living at Tsefat and destroyed the city. Now it’s called Hormah (which means ‘complete destruction’).
[Heroes and Guides] [1]:[18] They also captured Azah (Gaza), Ashkelon, and Ekron and all their surrounding territories.
[Heroes and Guides] [1]:[19] Yahweh helped Yehudah and they took possession of the hill country, although they weren’t able to conquer the people living down in the plains because they had iron on their chariots.
[Heroes and Guides] [1]:[20] They gave Hevron to Kalev (Caleb) just as Mosheh had directed, and he dispossessed the three sons of the Anak from there.
[Heroes and Guides] [1]:[21] However Benyamin’s descendants didn’t drive the Yevusim living in Yerushalem (Jerusalem) out, so they have lived among the Benyamites in Yerushalem to this day.
[Heroes and Guides] [1]:[22] Also Yosef’s (Joseph) descendants attacked Beyt-El (Bethel), and Yahweh helped them.
[Heroes and Guides] [1]:[23] They sent spies out to Beyt-El (previously called Luz)
[Heroes and Guides] [1]:[24] and they saw a man coming out of the city and told him, “Please show us an entrance into the city, and we’ll be kind to you.”
[Heroes and Guides] [1]:[25] So he showed them an entrance, and their warriors attacked and killed the inhabitants, but they let the man and his family go free.
[Heroes and Guides] [1]:[26] The man went to the land of the Hitim and founded a city and called it Luz (which it’s still called to this day).
[Heroes and Guides] [1]:[27] However Menasheh’s (Manasseh) descendants didn’t drive out those living in Beyt-Shean, Ta’anak, Dor, Yivleam, or Megidon, because the Kena’anim (Canaanites) were determined to keep living there.
[Heroes and Guides] [1]:[28] (Later, the Israelis became stronger and they forced the Kena’anim to work for them as their slaves, but they didn’t drive them out.)
[Heroes and Guides] [1]:[29] Nor did Efrayim’s (Ephraim) descendants drive the Kena’anim out of Gezer, so they continued to live among them.
[Heroes and Guides] [1]:[30] Zevulun’s descendants didn’t drive the Kena’anim out of Kitron or Nahalal, so they continued to live among them and were forced to work as slaves.
[Heroes and Guides] [1]:[31] Asher’s descendants didn’t drive out those who were living in Ako, Tsidon (Sidon), Ahlav, Akziv, Helbah, Afek, or Rehov,
[Heroes and Guides] [1]:[32] So Asher’s descendants lived with the Kena’anim who still lived in the region because they didn’t drive them out.
[Heroes and Guides] [1]:[33] Naftali’s (Naphtali) descendants didn’t drive out those who were living in Beyt-Shemesh (Heliopolis) or Beyt-Anat, so they continued to live among them and were forced to work as slaves.
[Heroes and Guides] [1]:[34] The Amorim forced Dan’s descendants to live in the hill country, because they didn’t allow them to come down to the plains.
[Heroes and Guides] [1]:[35] The Amorim were determined to live at Mt. Heres, in Ayalon and Sha’alvim (but when Yosef’s (Joseph) descendants became stronger, they forced the Amorim to work as slaves).
[Heroes and Guides] [1]:[36] The Amorim border went from the Scorpion Pass through Sela and upward from there.
[Heroes and Guides] [2]:[1] Then Yahweh’s messenger went from Gilgal to Bokim and told the Israelis, “I brought you all out of Mitsrayim (Egypt) and led you here to this land that I promised to your ancestors. I had said that I wouldn’t ever break my agreement with you all,
[Heroes and Guides] [2]:[2] but that you mustn’t form treaties with the peoples who lived here, rather you must tear down their altars. But you all haven’t obeyed what I said. What have you gone and done?
[Heroes and Guides] [2]:[3] So I’m telling you that I won’t drive your enemies out ahead of you, but they’ll be like thorns in your sides and you’ll all end up being enslaved to their idols.”
[Heroes and Guides] [2]:[4] When Yahweh’s messenger finished saying that, the people wept loudly,
[Heroes and Guides] [2]:[5] so they called that place Bokim (which means ‘weeping’) and they offered sacrifices to Yahweh there.
[Heroes and Guides] [2]:[6] Then Yehoshua (Joshua) dismissed the people and the tribes went to their various regions to take possession of the land.
[Heroes and Guides] [2]:[7] The people obeyed Yahweh as long as Yehoshua and the elders who had seen the great things that Yahweh had done for Yisrael (Israel) , were alive.
[Heroes and Guides] [2]:[8] Then Yahweh’s servant Yehoshua (son of Nun) died at the age of 110
[Heroes and Guides] [2]:[9] and they buried him in his allocated land at Timnat-Heres, inside Efrayim’s (Ephraim) hill country territory north of Mt. Ga’ash.
[Heroes and Guides] [2]:[10] When all of that generation had passed away, the next generation didn’t know Yahweh or even know about what he’d done for the Israelis.
[Heroes and Guides] [2]:[11] They did things that Yahweh considered evil and worshipped Ba’al idols
[Heroes and Guides] [2]:[12] and abandoned the god of their ancestors, Yahweh, the one who brought them out of Mitsrayim (Egypt). Instead they went after other gods—the gods of the people around them. They worshipped them and that made Yahweh angry.
[Heroes and Guides] [2]:[13] They abandoned Yahweh and worshipped the Ba’al and Ashtarot idols.
[Heroes and Guides] [2]:[14] So Yahweh got angry with Yisrael (Israel) so he caused raiders to come and take their property and he allowed their enemies to become more powerful so they could no longer stand against them.
[Heroes and Guides] [2]:[15] Whenever the Israelis went into battle, Yahweh worked against them just like he’d said he would and they became very distressed.
[Heroes and Guides] [2]:[16] Then Yahweh gave them leaders to save them from the raiders.
[Heroes and Guides] [2]:[17] However they wouldn’t listen to those leaders either—continuing to prostitute themselves to other gods and bowing down to idols. They rapidly turned away from their ancestors’ ways and showed no interest in obeying Yahweh’s instructions.
[Heroes and Guides] [2]:[18] Whenever Yahweh gave them a leader, he would support that leader and would save them from their enemies during that leader’s life, because he pitied the people when they groaned from being tormented and oppressed.
[Heroes and Guides] [2]:[19] But then at the death of that leader, they would turn back and behave more corruptly than their ancestors—following other gods and bowing down to idols. They didn’t stop any of their evil activities or their shameless behaviour
[Heroes and Guides] [2]:[20] so Yahweh was very angry at Yisrael and said, “This nation has broken the agreement that I made with their ancestors and haven’t done what I told them to.
[Heroes and Guides] [2]:[21] I won’t keep driving the people groups away that remained when Yehoshua (Joshua) died,
[Heroes and Guides] [2]:[22] so as to use them to test Yisrael to see whether the Israelis will obey my instructions like their ancestors did, or not.
[Heroes and Guides] [2]:[23] So Yahweh allowed those people groups to stay on, and hence they hadn’t been handed over to Yehoshua.
[Heroes and Guides] [3]:[1] The following are the kingdoms which Yahweh allowed to remain so as to test the newer generations of Yisrael (Israel) who hadn’t experienced the battles in Kena’an (Canaan)
[Heroes and Guides] [3]:[2] (if only for the sake of teaching warfare to those generations who hadn’t experienced it):
[Heroes and Guides] [3]:[3] the five Pelishti rulers and the Kena’anim (Canaanites), the Tsidonim (Sidonians), the Hivim that live on Mt. Levanon between Mt. Ba’al-Hermon and Levo-Hamat.
[Heroes and Guides] [3]:[4] They were left to test Yisrael to find out if they would obey Yahweh’s instructions that had been given through Mosheh (Moses) to their ancestors,
[Heroes and Guides] [3]:[5] and so the Israelis lived among the Kena’anim, the Hitim, the Amorim, the Perizim, the Hivim, and the Yevusim.
[Heroes and Guides] [3]:[6] They took their daughters as wives, and gave their own daughters to be married to their sons, and they worshipped their gods.
[Heroes and Guides] [3]:[7] So the Israelis did things considered evil by Yahweh and they forgot about their god Yahweh, instead serving the Ba’al and Asherot idols.
[Heroes and Guides] [3]:[8] Because of that, Yahweh was very angry with Yisrael (Israel), so he handed them over to King Kushan-Rish’atayim of Aram-Naharayim. The Israelis served him for eight years
[Heroes and Guides] [3]:[9] but when they cried out to Yahweh, he sent them a leader to rescue them: Otniel, son of Kalev’s (Caleb) younger brother Kenaz.
[Heroes and Guides] [3]:[10] Yahweh’s spirit empowered him and he led Yisrael. He led them into battle against King Kushan-Rish’atayim of Aram (Syria), and Yahweh helped them defeat him.
[Heroes and Guides] [3]:[11] So the region had peace for forty years, and then Otniel (Kenaz’s son) died.
[Heroes and Guides] [3]:[12] Once again the Israelis started doing things considered evil by Yahweh, so because of that, he strengthened King Eglon of Moav (Moab) against Yisrael (Israel).
[Heroes and Guides] [3]:[13] King Eglon enlisted warriors from the Amonim and the Amalekim, and they attacked Yisrael and captured Yeriho (Jericho), the city of palm trees,
[Heroes and Guides] [3]:[14] so the Israelis served him for eighteen years.
[Heroes and Guides] [3]:[15] But the Israelis cried out to Yahweh, he sent them a leader to rescue them: the left-hander Ehud, son of Gera the Benyamite. The Israelis sent him to carry the tribute payment to King Eglon of Moav.
[Heroes and Guides] [3]:[16] Now Ehud had made himself a double-edged sword—a short one about half a metre long—and he strapped it to his right thigh beneath his clothes.
[Heroes and Guides] [3]:[17] Then he presented the tribute to King Eglon of Moav, who was a very fat man,
[Heroes and Guides] [3]:[18] and after leaving for home, he sent off the people who’d actually carried it all.
[Heroes and Guides] [3]:[19] Then from the stone quarries that they’d reached near Gilgal, he returned and told the king that he had a private message for him. The king told his attendants to be quiet then sent them out of the room.
