[Heroes and Guides] [8]:[10] Now Zevah and Tsalmuna were in Karkor with around fifteen thousand warriors—all that remained out of all of that allied Midyanite camp of eastern people, because one hundred and twenty thousand of their warriors had already been killed.
[Heroes and Guides] [8]:[11] Gid’on approached them unexpectedly via the caravan route east of Novah and Yagebehah, and struck their camp when they were feeling secure.
[Heroes and Guides] [8]:[12] Zevah and Tsalmuna fled, but they chased after those two Midyanite kings and captured them, thus defeating their entire army.
[Heroes and Guides] [8]:[13] The Gid’on (Yoash’s son) and his warriors returned from battle, going through the Heres pass.
[Heroes and Guides] [8]:[14] He captured a young man from Sukot and questioned him—writing down the names of the seventy-seven leaders and elders of Sukot.
[Heroes and Guides] [8]:[15] Then he returned to Sukot and told them, “Look here at Zevah and Tsalmuna—the ones you taunted me about when you asked, ‘Do you already have Zevah and Tsalmuna in your grasp that we should give food to your weary men.’ ”
[Heroes and Guides] [8]:[16] He took the city elders and had them punished with wilderness thorns and briers to teach them a lesson,
[Heroes and Guides] [8]:[17] then they went to Penuel and tore down the tower and executed the city leaders.
[Heroes and Guides] [8]:[18] Then Gid’on asked Zevah and Tsalmuna, “What were the men like that you killed at Tavor?” “They were just like you,” they replied. “They seemed like they could have been a king’s sons.”
[Heroes and Guides] [8]:[19] “They were my brothers—the sons of my mother,” he said. “As Yahweh lives, if only you had let them live, I wouldn’t have killed you.”
[Heroes and Guides] [8]:[20] Then he ordered Yeter, his oldest son, “Go and kill them.” But Yeter didn’t pull out his sword because he was afraid—he was still a youth.
[Heroes and Guides] [8]:[21] Then Zevah and Tsalmuna said, “Come and kill us yourself—be a man and use your own strength.” So Gid’on went over and killed Zevah and Tsalmuna, and then he took the crescent-shaped ornaments that were on their camels’ necks.
[Heroes and Guides] [8]:[22] Then a group of Israeli men said to Gid’on, “We want you and your sons and your future descendants to rule over us, because you have saved us from the Midyanites.”
[Heroes and Guides] [8]:[23] But Gid’on answered, “No, I won’t rule over you myself, nor will my son rule over you. Yahweh will rule over you.”
[Heroes and Guides] [8]:[24] However, he continued, “Let me ask you all for something: that each man give me the earrings from his spoil.” (The enemies had gold earrings because they were Yishmaelim (Ishmaelites).)
[Heroes and Guides] [8]:[25] “We can certainly do that for you,” they replied. So they spread out a garment and each man threw the earrings from his spoil onto it.
[Heroes and Guides] [8]:[26] Now the weight of the gold earrings of gold came to twenty kilograms, and then there were the crescent-shaped ornaments, the pendants, the dyed purple garments that the Midyanite kings had been wearing, as well as the collars that had been around their camels’ necks.
[Heroes and Guides] [8]:[27] Then Gid’on made the gold into an idol and placed it in his home city of Ofrah, and the Israelis prostituted themselves to it there, and so it became like a trap for Gid’on and his household.
[Heroes and Guides] [8]:[28] So Midyan was kept under control by the Israelis and they didn’t continue to oppress the people, and there was peace in the region for forty years during Gid’on’s time.
[Heroes and Guides] [8]:[29] Then Gid’on (Yoash’s son, also known as Yeruba’al) went back and lived in his house,
[Heroes and Guides] [8]:[30] and he fathered seventy sons because he had many wives.
[Heroes and Guides] [8]:[31] He also had a mistress in Shekem—she also bore him a son that he named Avimelek.
[Heroes and Guides] [8]:[32] Gid’on died at a good old age and was buried in the tomb of Yoash his father, at Ofrah of the Abiezerites.
[Heroes and Guides] [8]:[33] However after Gid’on had died, the Israelis turned away again from Yahweh and prostituted themselves to the Baals—making Ba’al-Berit for themselves as a god.
[Heroes and Guides] [8]:[34] They forgot about their god Yahweh—the one who had rescued them from the clutch of all of their enemies all around.
[Heroes and Guides] [8]:[35] They didn’t show lasting loyalty to Gid’on’s family, despite all the good that he’d done within Yisrael (Israel).
[Heroes and Guides] [9]:[1] Now Gid’on’s son Avimelek went to Shekem to his mother’s brothers and spoke to those uncles and to all the extended family of his mother’s father, saying,
[Heroes and Guides] [9]:[2] “Please ask around all the citizens of Shekem: ‘What is better for you: Gid’on’s seventy sons ruling over you, or having a single man in charge?’ Remember that I’m your flesh and bone.”
[Heroes and Guides] [9]:[3] So his uncles working on his behalf, passed that onto all the citizens of Shekem, and they became convinced in Avimelek, because they said, “He’s our brother.”
[Heroes and Guides] [9]:[4] Then they gave him seventy silver coins from the temple of Ba’al-Berit, and Avimelek used them to entice some rough lay-abouts to work for him.
[Heroes and Guides] [9]:[5] Then they went to his father’s house at Ofrah, and he killed his seventy half-brothers (Gid’on’s sons) there on one stone. But Gid’on’s youngest son Yotam (Jotham) survived because he had hidden from them.
[Heroes and Guides] [9]:[6] Then all of the prominent citizens of Shekem and all of Beyt-Milo assembled themselves, and they went and installed Avimelek as king beside an oak tree near the standing pillar that was in Shekem.
[Heroes and Guides] [9]:[7] When they told Yotam (Jotham), he went and stood on the top of Mt. Gerizim and shouted out to them all in a loud voice, “Listen to me, citizens of Shekem, so God will listen to all of you.
[Heroes and Guides] [9]:[8] Once the trees went about in order to appoint a king for themselves, So they said to the olive tree, ‘Reign over us.’
[Heroes and Guides] [9]:[9] But the olive tree replied to them, ‘Have I stopped producing my valuable oil used to honour gods and men, that I should go to sway above the other trees?’
[Heroes and Guides] [9]:[10] So the trees said to the fig tree, ‘You come and reign over us.’
[Heroes and Guides] [9]:[11] But the fig tree answered them, ‘Have I stopped producing my sweetness and my good fruit, that I should go to sway above the other trees?’
[Heroes and Guides] [9]:[12] Then the trees said to the grapevine, ‘You come and reign over us.’
[Heroes and Guides] [9]:[13] But the vine replied, ‘Have I stopped producing my new wine, which cheers gods and man, that I should go to sway over the other trees?’
[Heroes and Guides] [9]:[14] Then all the trees said to the thornbush, ‘You come and reign over us!’
[Heroes and Guides] [9]:[15] The thornbush told the trees, ‘If you all are really wanted to anoint me as king over you, come and take refuge in my shade. But if you all don’t, may the thornbush send out fire to burn up Levanon’s cedar forests.’
[Heroes and Guides] [9]:[16] “Therefore did you all act with honesty and integrity when you installed Avimelek as king? Did you all treat Gid’on’s family well, and did you all repay him appropriately for what he did for you all?
[Heroes and Guides] [9]:[17] My father fought on your behalf, and even risked his life out front when he rescued you all from the Midyanites,
[Heroes and Guides] [9]:[18] but today you’ve all risen up against my father’s family and killed his sons—seventy men on one stone. Then you’ve installed Avimelek, the son of his female servant, as king over the citizens of Shekem because he’s your brother.
[Heroes and Guides] [9]:[19] Now if you’ve all acted with honesty and integrity with towards Gid’on and his family today, be happy with Avimelek, and he’ll also be happy with all of you,
[Heroes and Guides] [9]:[20] but if not, then fire will come out of Avimelek and destroy the citizens of Shekem and Beyt-Milo. Fire will also come out from the Shekem’s citizens and from Beyt-Milo, and it’ll destroy Avimelek.”
[Heroes and Guides] [9]:[21] Then Yotam (Jotham) fled away and escaped and went to Be’er and settled there away from the presence of his half-brother Avimelek.
[Heroes and Guides] [9]:[22] Avimelek ruled over Yisrael (Israel) for three years,
[Heroes and Guides] [9]:[23] then God sent an evil spirit between him and the citizens of Shekem, so the citizens there dealt treacherously with Avimelek.
[Heroes and Guides] [9]:[24] The violent treatment of Gid’on’s seventy sons kept getting brought up, and by it was all blamed on their brother Avimelek who had killed them, and on those of Shekem’s citizens who assisted him in the killing of his brothers.
[Heroes and Guides] [9]:[25] So the Shekem citizens placed men in ambush along the tops of the hills to get him, but they robbed everyone who went passed them along the road, and so it was reported to Avimelek.
[Heroes and Guides] [9]:[26] Then Ga’al (Eved’s son) came along with his brothers and moved into Shekem, and the citizens there began to trust them.
[Heroes and Guides] [9]:[27] They went out into the field, and they picked grapes from their vineyards and pressed them. They celebrated harvest festivals and they went into the house of their gods, then they ate and drank, and they cursed Avimelek.
[Heroes and Guides] [9]:[28] Then Ga’al (Eved’s son) said, “Who’s Avimelek, and who’s Shekem, that we should serve him? Isn’t Avimelek Gid’on’s son, and Zevul is his deputy? Serve the descendants of Shekem’s father Hamor, but why should we serve Avimelek?
[Heroes and Guides] [9]:[29] Who will fight with me to defeat those people and depose Avimelek? Then he said to Avimelek, ‘Gather your army and come and fight.’ ”
[Heroes and Guides] [9]:[30] When Zevul, the prince of the city, heard what Ga’al (Eved’s son) had said, he got very angry
[Heroes and Guides] [9]:[31] and he sent messengers to Avimelek in secret, saying, “Listen, Eved’s son Ga’al and his brothers are coming to Shekem, and wow, they’re inciting the city against you.
[Heroes and Guides] [9]:[32] You and the people who are with you should go out at night and lie in ambush in the countryside.
[Heroes and Guides] [9]:[33] Then when the sun rises in the morning, you all should set out early and spread out in an attack against the city. Keep watch, then when Ga’al and the people with him are coming out toward you to fight, then you can overpower them and treat him however you think fit.”
[Heroes and Guides] [9]:[34] So Avimelek and all the people with him went out in the night and they set up four units in an ambush against Shekem.
[Heroes and Guides] [9]:[35] In the morning, Ga’al (Eved’s son) went out and he stood at the entrance of the city gate. Then Avimelek and his men stood up from their hiding places.
[Heroes and Guides] [9]:[36] When Ga’al saw the people, he said to Zevul, “Look, a group of people is coming down from the tops of the hills!” “You are seeing the shadow of the hills as men,” Zevul responded.
[Heroes and Guides] [9]:[37] But Ga’al said again, “Look, groups of people are coming down from beside the top of the hill, and another group is coming from the way of the ‘oak of the diviners’.”
[Heroes and Guides] [9]:[38] Then Zevul said to him, “Well, you were the one who said, ‘Who is Avimelek that we should serve him?’ Aren’t these the people who you were scorning? Indeed now, go out and fight against them.”
[Heroes and Guides] [9]:[39] So Ga’al went out in front of Shekem’s citizens and fought against Avimelek.
[Heroes and Guides] [9]:[40] Avimelek pursued him, and he had to flee away from him. Many of their men fell fatally wounded as far as the entrance of the city gate.
[Heroes and Guides] [9]:[41] Then Avimelek settled in Arumah, but Zevul drove Ga’al and his brothers away from living in Shekem.
[Heroes and Guides] [9]:[42] Now it so happened that the next day, the people of Shekem went out into the countryside, and it was reported to Avimelek.
[Heroes and Guides] [9]:[43] So he took his men and split them into three units. Then he waited in ambush in the countryside. When he saw and wow, the people were going out of the city, then he attacked and killed them.
[Heroes and Guides] [9]:[44] Avimelek and the units that were with him had spread out and they stood at the entrance of the city gate, and two units spread out against everyone who was in the field and killed them.
[Heroes and Guides] [9]:[45] Avimelek spent that whole day attacking Shekem. He captured the city and they killed the people who were in it. Then he tore it down, and scattered salt on the land.
[Heroes and Guides] [9]:[46] When all the lords of the tower of Shekem heard, they went into the citadel of the temple for El-Berit,
[Heroes and Guides] [9]:[47] but it was reported to Avimelek that all the lords of the Shekem tower had gathered there.
[Heroes and Guides] [9]:[48] So Avimelek and all the people with him, went up to Mt. Tsalmon. He took axes and cut a branch down from the trees, then lifted it onto his shoulder and said to the people who were with him, “What I just did, you all quickly do the same.”
[Heroes and Guides] [9]:[49] So all the people also each cut off a branch and then followed Avimelek. They piled them on top of the underground chamber, and that’s how they burnt out the underground chamber. As a result, all the distinguished people in the tower of Shekem also died—about a thousand men and women.
[Heroes and Guides] [9]:[50] Then Avimelek went to Tevets and set up camp around the city and captured it.
[Heroes and Guides] [9]:[51] But there was a strong tower in the middle of the city, so all of the men and the women and all the prominent citizens fled to it. Once they were all in, they barricaded it up and they went up onto the tower roof.
[Heroes and Guides] [9]:[52] Then Avimelek and his men approached the tower and fought against it, and he came in as close as the tower entrance in order to set fire to it,
[Heroes and Guides] [9]:[53] but a woman threw an upper millstone down onto Avimelek’s head and it crushed his skull.
[Heroes and Guides] [9]:[54] Then he cried out hurriedly to the young man bearing his armour, “Draw out your sword and put me to death, because I don’t want it to be said afterwards that I was killed by a woman.” So his young man stabbed him so that he died.
[Heroes and Guides] [9]:[55] When the Israeli warriors saw that Avimelek was dead, they all returned to their own homes.
[Heroes and Guides] [9]:[56] Thus God avenged the evil of Avimelek that he had done to his father Gid’on by killing his seventy brothers,
[Heroes and Guides] [9]:[57] and God caused all the evil done by Shekem’s men to return back onto their own heads, and the curse of Gid’on’s youngest son Yotam (Jotham), came true on them.
[Heroes and Guides] [10]:[1] Now after Avimelek, Tola (the son of Puah, the son of Dodo, from the tribe of Yisakar (Issachar)) came on the scene to rescue Yisrael (Israel). He settled in Shamir, in the hill country of Efrayim (Ephraim).
[Heroes and Guides] [10]:[2] He led Yisrael for twenty-three years, then he died and was buried in Shamir.
[Heroes and Guides] [10]:[3] After him, Yair the Giladi led Yisrael (Israel) for twenty-two years.
[Heroes and Guides] [10]:[4] He had thirty sons that rode on thirty donkeys. There were thirty cities for them in the Gilead region which they call Yair’s villages to this day.
[Heroes and Guides] [10]:[5] Then Yair died and he was buried in Kamon.
[Heroes and Guides] [10]:[6] The Israelis continued to do what Yahweh considered evil: they worshipped the Ba’als, the Ashtarot, the gods of Aram (Syria), the gods of Tsidon (Sidon), the gods of Moav (Moab), the gods of the sons of Amon, and the gods of the Pelishtim. They forsook Yahweh and didn’t serve him.
[Heroes and Guides] [10]:[7] Yahweh was very angry with Yisrael (Israel), so he allowed the Pelishtim and the Amonim to harass them.
[Heroes and Guides] [10]:[8] They shattered and oppressed the Israelis that year, but it went on for eighteen years for all the Israelis who were on the opposite side of the Yarden (Jordan) in the land of the Amorim, which is in the Gilead.
[Heroes and Guides] [10]:[9] Then the Amonim also crossed over the Yarden to fight against Yehudah (Judah), against Benyamin, and against the half-tribe of Efrayim (Ephraim). This caused incredible distress for the Israelis
[Heroes and Guides] [10]:[10] so they cried out to Yahweh, “We have sinned against you, because we have abandoned our god and we have served the Ba’als.”
[Heroes and Guides] [10]:[11] “Wasn’t it from the Mitsrim (Egyptians),” Yahweh responded, “from the Amorim, from the Amonim, from the Pelishtim,
[Heroes and Guides] [10]:[12] the Tsidonim (Sidonians) and Amalek and Maeon, when they oppressed you that you cried out to me, and I rescued you all from them?
[Heroes and Guides] [10]:[13] Yet you’ve all abandoned me and served other gods. Therefore, I won’t not continue to rescue you.
[Heroes and Guides] [10]:[14] Go and cry out to the gods that you’ve all chosen for yourselves. They should deliver you all at the time of your distress.”
[Heroes and Guides] [10]:[15] Then the Israelis said to Yahweh, “We’ve sinned. You do to us according to all that is good in your eyes. Only please rescue us today.”
[Heroes and Guides] [10]:[16] They removed the foreign gods from among them, and they worshipped Yahweh and so he became concerned with Yisrael’s (Israel) suffering.
[Heroes and Guides] [10]:[17] Now the Amonim had assembled and were camped in Gilead. So the Israelis gathered together and they camped at Mitspah.
[Heroes and Guides] [10]:[18] Then the princes of Gilead said to each other, “Who will lead us to fight against the Amonim? He can become the leader over all of us who live in Gilead.”
[Heroes and Guides] [11]:[1] Now Yiftah (Jephthah) the Giladi was a fierce warrior, but he was a prostitute’s son and his father was Gilead.
[Heroes and Guides] [11]:[2] Gilead’s wife also gave birth to sons for him, and when those sons of the wife grew up, they drove Yiftah out and told him, “You won’t get any inheritance from our father’s estate because you’re a son of another woman.”
[Heroes and Guides] [11]:[3] So Yiftah fled from the presence of his half-brothers and he settled in the Tov region. Unprincipled men associated around Yiftah and went around with him.
[Heroes and Guides] [11]:[4] Some time later, the Amonim battled against Yisrael (Israel).
[Heroes and Guides] [11]:[5] and that was when the elders of Gilead went to summon Yiftah from the Tov region.
[Heroes and Guides] [11]:[6] Then requested Yiftah, “Come and be our commander so we can fight against the Amonim.”
[Heroes and Guides] [11]:[7] “Don’t you all hate me? Yiftah asked them. “Didn’t you yourselves drive me out of my father’s house? So why have you all come to me now when you have troubles?”
[Heroes and Guides] [11]:[8] “Well, true,” the Gilead elders replied, “But now we’ve turned back to you. So join with us and fight against the Amonim, and you’ll become commander over all of who lives in Gilead.”
[Heroes and Guides] [11]:[9] “If you bring me back to fight against the Amonim,” Yiftah asked them, “and if Yahweh helps me defeat them, is it correct that I’ll actually become your leader?”
[Heroes and Guides] [11]:[10] “Yahweh will be a witness between us,” the Gilead elders responded, “that we’ll most certainly do what you just said.”
[Heroes and Guides] [11]:[11] So Yiftah went with the Gilead elders, and the people set him as commander and leader over themselves. (Yiftah had spoken all those words before Yahweh at Mitspah.)
[Heroes and Guides] [11]:[12] Then Yiftah sent messengers to the Amoni king, demanding, “What’s happened with respect to me and to you, that you’ve come against me to fight over my land?”
[Heroes and Guides] [11]:[13] The Amoni king responded to Yiftah’s messengers, “Because the Israelis seized my land when they came out of Mitsrayim (Egypt). It went from the Arnon river up to the Yabok river, and over to the Yarden (Jordan) river. Now return the land peaceably.”
[Heroes and Guides] [11]:[14] Then Yiftah sent messengers back to the Amoni king
[Heroes and Guides] [11]:[15] to tell him, “Yiftah wants you to know that Yisrael (Israel) didn’t take land from Moav (Moab) nor from you Amonim.
[Heroes and Guides] [11]:[16] However in their coming up from Mitsrayim, Yisrael went through the wilderness as far as the Red Sea until arriving at Kadesh.
[Heroes and Guides] [11]:[17] When Yisrael sent messengers to the king of Edom, saying, ‘Please may we pass through your land,’ the king of Edom wouldn’t listen. Yisrael likewise sent to the king of Moav, but he wasn’t willing either, so Yisrael stayed at Kadesh.
[Heroes and Guides] [11]:[18] Then we went through the wilderness and turned away from the land of Edom and the land of Moav, then went the long way around the eastern border of Moav. They camped on the other side of the Arnon river, but they didn’t go within Moav’s borders, because the Arnon was the border of Moav.
[Heroes and Guides] [11]:[19] Yisrael sent messengers to the Amori King Sihon, the king of Heshbon and asked him, ‘Please, let us pass through your land as far as our place.’
[Heroes and Guides] [11]:[20] But King Sihon didn’t trust Yisrael passing through within his border, so he assembled all of his people together and they camped at Yahats, and he battled with Yisrael.
[Heroes and Guides] [11]:[21] Then Yisrael’s god, Yahweh, handed King Sihon and all his people over to Yisrael and we defeated them. Thus Yisrael took possession of all of the land of the Amorim inhabiting that region—
[Heroes and Guides] [11]:[22] everything within the Amori territory from the Arnon river to the Yabok, and from the wilderness as far as the Yarden (Jordan).
[Heroes and Guides] [11]:[23] So since it was Yisrael’s god Yahweh that expelled the Amorim out of the presence of his people Yisrael, do you actually think that you can take it now?
[Heroes and Guides] [11]:[24] Wouldn’t you take possession if your god Kemosh, allowed you to? So too all that our god Yahweh has dispossessed ahead of us, we’ll possess that.
[Heroes and Guides] [11]:[25] Are you really better now than Tsipor’s son, King Balak of Moav? Did he dare contend with Yisrael or did he ever wage war against them?
[Heroes and Guides] [11]:[26] Yisrael lived in Heshbon and in its villages for three hundred years, and in Aroer and in its villages, and in all the cities that are along the banks of the Arnon—so why didn’t you repossess them during that time?
[Heroes and Guides] [11]:[27] I haven’t done anything wrong to you, but you’re doing wrong in dealing with me by fighting against me. Yahweh, the judge, will decide today between the Israelis and the Amonim.”
[Heroes and Guides] [11]:[28] But the Amoni king didn’t take any notice of Yiftah’s message to him.
[Heroes and Guides] [11]:[29] Then Yahweh’s spirit empowered Yiftah (Jephthah), and he passed through the Gilead and Menasheh (Manasseh), and through Mitspah of Gilead, and from there he passed through the Amoni region,
[Heroes and Guides] [11]:[30] and he made a promise to Yahweh, “If you really give me victory over the Amonim,
[Heroes and Guides] [11]:[31] then whoever’s the first person to come out of my house to meet me when I return in peace from the battle against the Amonim, that person will belong to Yahweh, and I will offer him up as a whole burnt offering.”
[Heroes and Guides] [11]:[32] So Yiftah went to the Amoni territory to fight against them, and Yahweh enabled them to defeat them.
[Heroes and Guides] [11]:[33] Then he attacked them from Aroer and as far as the entrance to Minit, twenty cities, and then up to Avel-Keramim, slaughtering a huge number. So the Amonim were subdued by the presence of the Israelis.
[Heroes and Guides] [11]:[34] When Yiftah (Jephthah) got back to his house in the Mitspah area, look, his daughter was coming out to meet him with tambourines and with dancing. She was their only child—he didn’t have any son or daughter apart from her.
[Heroes and Guides] [11]:[35] When he saw her, he tore his clothes and said, “Oh no! My daughter! Indeed, you’ve made me bow in grief, and you’re among those who cause me pain, because I made a vow to Yahweh and I can’t go back on it.”
[Heroes and Guides] [11]:[36] Then she said to him, “My father, you’ve made a vow to Yahweh. Do to me whatever you promised, after what Yahweh has done for you—total vengeance against your Amoni enemies.”
[Heroes and Guides] [11]:[37] But she asked her father, “Just do this one thing for me: release me for two months, so I can go away and take some companions. I’ll fall prostrate on the hills and I’ll weep because I’ll never have a chance to marry.”
[Heroes and Guides] [11]:[38] He agreed and then sent her away for two months. She went with some companions, and she wept on the hills because she’d never be a mother.
[Heroes and Guides] [11]:[39] Then at the end of the two months, she returned to her father and he carried out his vow with respect to her so indeed she never had a chance to marry. After that, it became a custom in Yisrael (Israel)
[Heroes and Guides] [11]:[40] that the young women of Yisrael go to commemorate the daughter of Yiftah the Giladi for four days during the year.
[Heroes and Guides] [12]:[1] Now the men of Efrayim (Ephraim) were summoned and they passed northward and they said to Yiftah (Jephthah), “Why did you pass through in order to fight against the Amonim, but you didn’t call us to go with you? We’re going to burn your house down over you!”
[Heroes and Guides] [12]:[2] “I’ve been involved in very intense disputes—my people against the Amonim,” Yiftah told them. “When I summoned you all, you didn’t come and rescue me from them.
[Heroes and Guides] [12]:[3] When I could see that you weren’t coming to assist, I took my life into my own hands. I advanced against the Amonim, and Yahweh gave me victory over them. So why then have you all come here to fight against me today?”
[Heroes and Guides] [12]:[4] Then Yiftah assembled all of the men of Gilead and they battled against Efrayim. The men of Gilead struck Efrayim because they had said, “You Gilead people are just fugitives from Efrayim—living here in the middle of Efrayim, in the middle of Menasheh (Manasseh).”
[Heroes and Guides] [12]:[5] The Giladim captured the crossing places of the Yarden (Jordan) along Efrayim. Then when any of the survivors from Efrayim would say, “May I cross over,” the men of Gilead would ask, “Are you an Efrati?” If he said, “No,”
[Heroes and Guides] [12]:[6] then they’d demand, “Now say: Shibboleth.” But if he said “Sibboleth” because he didn’t have time to think to pronounce it correctly, they would seize him and would slaughter him at those crossing places of the Yarden. Forty-two thousand from Efrayim fell at that time.
[Heroes and Guides] [12]:[7] Yiftah the Giladi led Yisrael (Israel) for six years, then he died and was buried among the cities of Gilead.
[Heroes and Guides] [12]:[8] Then after him, Ivtsan of Beyt-Lehem (Bethlehem) led Yisrael (Israel).
[Heroes and Guides] [12]:[9] Now he had thirty sons. He gave away thirty daughters to be married to outsiders, and he brought in thirty daughters for his sons from the outside. Ivtsan led Yisrael for seven years,
[Heroes and Guides] [12]:[10] and when he died, he was buried in Beyt-Lehem.
[Heroes and Guides] [12]:[11] After him, Eylon the Zevuluni led Yisrael for ten years.
[Heroes and Guides] [12]:[12] When he died, he was buried in Ayalon in the land of Zevulun.
[Heroes and Guides] [12]:[13] After him, Avdon, the son of Hilel the Pireatoni led Yisrael.
[Heroes and Guides] [12]:[14] He had forty sons and thirty grandsons, who rode on seventy young male donkeys. He led Yisrael for eight years.
[Heroes and Guides] [12]:[15] Then Avdon (the son of Hilel the Pireatoni) died, and he was buried in Pireaton in the land of Efrayim (Ephraim), in the hill country of the Amalekim.
[Heroes and Guides] [13]:[1] The Israelis continued to do what Yahweh considered as evil, so he allowed the Pelishtim to oppress them for forty years.
[Heroes and Guides] [13]:[2] Now there was a man named Manoah from Tsor’ah, of the families of the Danim. His wife was barren so they had no children.
[Heroes and Guides] [13]:[3] One day, Yahweh’s messenger appeared to the wife and told her, “Listen, please, you are barren and have never given birth, but you will conceive and have a son.
[Heroes and Guides] [13]:[4] Now take care that you surely don’t drink wine or strong drink, and that you don’t eat anything prohibited by our rules,
[Heroes and Guides] [13]:[5] because you’ll definitely become pregnant and will give birth to a son. His hair must never be cut because he’ll be a Nazirite to God from his conception. He will begin to rescue Yisrael (Israel) from the oppression of the Pelishtim.”
[Heroes and Guides] [13]:[6] Then the woman went and explained to her husband, “A man of God came to me. He looked like one of God’s messengers—extremely terrifying—so I didn’t like to ask him where he’d come from, and he didn’t tell me his name.
[Heroes and Guides] [13]:[7] Then he told me, ‘You’re definitely pregnant and you’ll give birth to a son. So now, you mustn’t drink wine or strong drink, and you mustn’t eat anything prohibited by our rules, because the boy will be a Nazirite to God from conception until the day of his death.’ ”
[Heroes and Guides] [13]:[8] Then Manoah prayed to Yahweh, “Oh please, my master, please let the man of God that you sent before, come back to us again so he can instruct us about what we must do for this boy who’s going to be born.”
[Heroes and Guides] [13]:[9] The true God listened to Manoah’s request, and God’s messenger came to the woman again when she was sitting out in the field, but her husband Manoah wasn’t with her,
[Heroes and Guides] [13]:[10] so she quickly ran and told her husband, “Look. The man has appeared again who came to me that day.”
[Heroes and Guides] [13]:[11] So Manoah followed his wife, and when he came to the man, he asked him, “Are you the man who spoke to my wife before?” “Yes, it was me,” he replied.
[Heroes and Guides] [13]:[12] “Now may your words come true,” said Manoah. “How should we bring up the boy, and what will his work be?”
[Heroes and Guides] [13]:[13] “Your wife must carefully follow everything I told her,” Yahweh’s messenger replied.
[Heroes and Guides] [13]:[14] “She mustn’t eat or drink anything that comes from the grapevine. She mustn’t drink wine or strong drink, and she mustn’t eat anything prohibited by our rules. She must do everything that I’ve instructed her.”
[Heroes and Guides] [13]:[15] “Please stay a little longer,” Manoah asked Yahweh’s messenger, “so that we can prepare a meal of tender goat meat to honour your presence.”
[Heroes and Guides] [13]:[16] “Even if I stayed longer, I wouldn’t eat your food,” Yahweh’s messenger replied. “But if you wanted to prepare a burnt offering for Yahweh, you may offer it.” (Because Manoah didn’t know that the messenger had come from Yahweh.)
[Heroes and Guides] [13]:[17] “What’s your name,” Manoah asked, “so that we can honour you when your words come true?”
[Heroes and Guides] [13]:[18] “Why are you asking about my name,” Yahweh’s messenger replied. “You simply couldn’t understand.”
[Heroes and Guides] [13]:[19] Then Manoah got their young goat and the other requirements for the offering, and he presented a sacrifice to Yahweh on the rock. Then an amazing thing happened while Manoah and his wife watched—
[Heroes and Guides] [13]:[20] when the flames went up into the sky from the altar, Yahweh’s messenger went up in the flames while Manoah and his wife were watching. When they saw that, they quickly bowed right down to the ground.
[Heroes and Guides] [13]:[21] After that, Manoah and his wife never saw him again, but now Manoah knew that he was Yahweh’s messenger.
[Heroes and Guides] [13]:[22] Manoah said to his wife, “We’ll definitely die now because we’ve seen God!”
[Heroes and Guides] [13]:[23] But his wife replied to him, “If Yahweh had wanted to kill us, he wouldn’t have accepted the entire burnt offering and the grain offering. He wouldn’t have shown us all those things, and he wouldn’t have given us those instructions.”
[Heroes and Guides] [13]:[24] In due course, the woman gave birth to a son and she named him Shimshon (Samson). The boy grew up and Yahweh blessed him,
[Heroes and Guides] [13]:[25] and then Yahweh’s spirit began to stir him when he was in Mahaneh Dan—between Tsor’ah and between Eshtaol.
[Heroes and Guides] [14]:[1] One time when Shimshon (Samson) went to Timnah, he noticed a young, Pelishti woman there,
[Heroes and Guides] [14]:[2] and he went back home and he reported to his parents, “I saw a Pelishti woman in Timnah that I’d like you to get for me as my wife.”
[Heroes and Guides] [14]:[3] “Isn’t there a woman among your relatives?” his parents asked him, “Or among all of our people? Why take a wife from the uncircumcised Pelishtim?” “Get her for me,” Shimshon said to his father, “because I feel she’s right for me.”
[Heroes and Guides] [14]:[4] Now his parents didn’t know that Yahweh was arranging this, because he was seeking an opportunity against the Pelishtim who were oppressing Yisrael (Israel) at that time.
[Heroes and Guides] [14]:[5] Then Shimshon went to Timnah with his parents and when they got to the vineyards there, wow, a young lion roared when it saw him.
[Heroes and Guides] [14]:[6] Yahweh’s spirit rose up in Shimshon, and he tore the lion to pieces with his bare hands like butchering a young goat, but he didn’t mention to his parents what he’d done.
[Heroes and Guides] [14]:[7] Then he continued on and talked with the woman, and he really liked her.
[Heroes and Guides] [14]:[8] Some time later when he returned for the wedding, he turned off the path to look for the lion’s carcass, and to his surprise, a swarm of bees had nested in the carcass and there was honey there.
[Heroes and Guides] [14]:[9] He filled his cupped hands with honey, and continued along—walking and eating as he went to where his parents were. He even gave some to them to try, but he didn’t tell them that he had scooped it out of the carcass of a dead lion.
[Heroes and Guides] [14]:[10] Then his father went to visit the woman, and in the custom of the young men of the time, Shimshon held a party there.
[Heroes and Guides] [14]:[11] When they saw him, they brought thirty close friends to join him.
[Heroes and Guides] [14]:[12] Shimshon said to them, “Let me suggest a riddle for you all. If you’re able to explain it to me during the seven days of the party and you’ve worked it out correctly, I’ll give you all thirty linen coats and thirty sets of clothes.
[Heroes and Guides] [14]:[13] But if you all can’t explain it to me, then you yourselves must give me thirty linen coats and thirty sets of clothes.” “Okay, we’re listening. Tell us the riddle.” they answered.
[Heroes and Guides] [14]:[14] So he said, “Food came out of the eater, and sweetness came out of the strong one.” But three days later, they still couldn’t solve his riddle.
[Heroes and Guides] [14]:[15] Then on the seventh day, they pressured Shimshon’s wife, “Get your husband to tell you the answer of the riddle, otherwise we’ll burn down your father’ house and you as well. Did you invite us to the party just to impoverish us?”
[Heroes and Guides] [14]:[16] Then Shimshon’s wife put on a crying act and said, “You must hate me—you don’t love me because you’ve created a riddle for my relatives, yet you haven’t even told me the answer.” “Listen,” he replied, “I haven’t even told my own parents. Should I tell you?”
[Heroes and Guides] [14]:[17] She continued to cry beside him throughout the seven-day party, and then finally on the seventh day, he gave in and told her because she kept nagging him, so in the end she was able to reveal the answer to her relatives.
[Heroes and Guides] [14]:[18] Then the men of the city said to Shimshon before the sun went down on the seventh day, “What is sweeter than honey? And what’s stronger than a lion?” So he said to them, “If you all hadn’t ploughed with my heifer, you wouldn’t have been able to solve my riddle.”
[Heroes and Guides] [14]:[19] Then Yahweh’s spirit rose up in him, and he went to Ashkelon and killed thirty men there. He took their possessions, and he gave the changes of clothes for the riddle. But he was very angry, so he went back to his parent’s home.
[Heroes and Guides] [14]:[20] Then (unknown to Shimshon), his wife was given to the man who’d been his close friend and companion.
[Heroes and Guides] [15]:[1] Some days later during the wheat harvest, Shimshon visited his wife with a young goat as a present for the family, because he said, “I’ll go into the bedroom with my wife.” But her father wouldn’t allow him to go in,
[Heroes and Guides] [15]:[2] and pleaded, “Truly, I thought that you must hate her, so I gave her to your close friend. But wouldn’t her younger sister be better anyway? Please, would you take her instead.”
[Heroes and Guides] [15]:[3] Shimshon responded, “This time I’m blameless concerning the Pelishtim when I cause trouble for them.”
[Heroes and Guides] [15]:[4] Then he went and captured three hundred foxes and tied them in pairs—tail to tail. He took torches, and tied one torch between the tails of each pair.
[Heroes and Guides] [15]:[5] He lit the torches and let the foxes loose into the grain crops of the Pelishtim. As a result, he burnt both the standing grain plants and also the harvested stacks of sheaves, and even a vineyard and an olive orchard.
[Heroes and Guides] [15]:[6] So the Pelishtim asked, “Who did this?” “Shimshon,” they replied, “the son-in-law of the man from Timnah, because he took Shimshon’s wife and gave her to his close friend.” As a result, the Pelishtim went to Timnah and they burnt both the woman and her father.
[Heroes and Guides] [15]:[7] Then Shimshon told them, “Since you actually did that horrible thing, I certainly won’t stop until I’ve avenged myself against you all.”
[Heroes and Guides] [15]:[8] Then he attacked the Pelishtim and crippled many of them, before going to Eytam’s rock where he lived in a cave.
[Heroes and Guides] [15]:[9] However, the Pelishti warriors went and camped in Yehudah (Judah), and spread out around the town of Lehi.
[Heroes and Guides] [15]:[10] But the men of Yehudah asked them, “Why have you all come here to attack us?” “We’ve come to capture Shimshon (Samson),” they replied. “To give him some of his own back.”
[Heroes and Guides] [15]:[11] Then three thousand men from Yehudah went down to the crevice in Eytam’s rock, and told Shimshon, “Don’t you realise that the Pelishtim are ruling over us? Why are you causing more trouble for us?” “Just as they’ve done to me,” he replied, “so I’ve done to them.”
[Heroes and Guides] [15]:[12] “We’ve come here to tie you up so we can hand you over to the Pelishtim,” they said. “Okay,” Shimshon responded. “But promise me that you all won’t injure me yourselves.”
[Heroes and Guides] [15]:[13] “No, however, we’ll certainly tie you up,” they replied, “and we’ll hand you over to them. But truly we won’t kill you.” Then they tied him up with two new ropes and brought him up from the rocks.
[Heroes and Guides] [15]:[14] When they’d taken him as far as Lehi, the Pelishtim shouted triumphantly when they saw him. Then Yahweh’s spirit rose in Shimshon and the ropes around his arms just seemed as weak as burnt flax stalks when he simply snapped them off him.
[Heroes and Guides] [15]:[15] He saw a fresh donkey’s jawbone lying on the ground, and he reached out his hand and grabbed it, and he slaughtered a thousand Pelishti men with it.
[Heroes and Guides] [15]:[16] Then Shimshon declared, “With a donkey’s jawbone, one heap, two heaps, with a donkey’s jawbone, I’ve slaughtered a thousand men.”
[Heroes and Guides] [15]:[17] When he finished reciting that, he hurled the jawbone away, and he called that place ‘Ramat-Lehi’ (which means ‘jawbone hill’).
[Heroes and Guides] [15]:[18] Then he was very thirsty and cried out to Yahweh, “You yourself have given your servant this great victory, but now must I die with this thirst and get captured by those uncircumcised Pelishtim?”
[Heroes and Guides] [15]:[19] So God split open the little hollow that’s at Lehi, and water came out of it. When he drank, his strength returned and he revived. Because of that, he called it ‘Eyn-Hakore’ (which means ‘the fountain of the one who called out’), which is in Lehi to this day.
[Heroes and Guides] [15]:[20] And so Shimshon led Yisrael (Israel) for twenty years at the time of the Pelishti oppression.
[Heroes and Guides] [16]:[1] Shimshon (Samson) went to Azah (Gaza) city and he saw a prostitute woman there so he went in to spend the night with her.
[Heroes and Guides] [16]:[2] But the Gazim passed around the news, “Shimshon’s in town.” So they encircled the city gate and they laid in wait for him all night. They stayed quiet the whole night, saying, “We’ll kill him when it gets light.”
[Heroes and Guides] [16]:[3] Shimshon stayed with her until the middle of the night, then he got up. He picked up both the gates including the cross-bar and their posts, and hoisted them up onto his shoulders, and he carried them up to the top of the hill which is in front of Hevron.
[Heroes and Guides] [16]:[4] Sometime after that, Shimshon (Samson) fell in love with a Pelishti woman named Dililah who lived in the Sorek valley.
[Heroes and Guides] [16]:[5] The Pelishti leaders came to her and requested, “Make him open up. Find out what makes him strong, and how we can beat him, so that we can tie him up to keep him in our power. Then we’ll each give you one thousand one hundred silver coins.”
[Heroes and Guides] [16]:[6] So Dililah asked Shimshon, “Please, tell me what makes you so strong, and how could someone tie you up to keep you in their power?”
[Heroes and Guides] [16]:[7] “If they’d tie me up with seven green cords that haven’t been dried,” he replied, “then I’d become weak and be just like any other man.”
[Heroes and Guides] [16]:[8] So the Pelishti leaders brought her seven green cords that hadn’t been dried, and she tied him up with them.
[Heroes and Guides] [16]:[9] Now she had an ambush group ready in the next room when she said to him, “The Pelishtim are here to get you, Shimshon!” But he tore the cords to shreds just like a strip of flax fiber is torn to shreds when the fire reaches it, thus they didn’t find out the secret of his strength.
[Heroes and Guides] [16]:[10] Then Dililah said to him, “Listen, you deceived me and lied to me. Now tell me, please, how could someone tie you up?”
[Heroes and Guides] [16]:[11] “Actually, if they would tie me with new ropes which have never been used,” he replied, “I’d become weak and be just like any other man.”
[Heroes and Guides] [16]:[12] So Dililah took new cords and tied him up with them. She said to him, “The Pelishtim are here to get you, Shimshon!” with the ambush group staying in the next room. But he flicked them off his arms like they were just thread.
[Heroes and Guides] [16]:[13] Then Dililah said to Shimshon, “So far you’ve just been deceitful to me and told me lies. Now Tell me how you can be tied up.” So he told her, “It’s if you just weave seven locks of my hair into the loom.”
[Heroes and Guides] [16]:[14] So she did it and fastened it with the pin, and called out, “The Pelishtim are here to get you, Shimshon!” Then he woke up and ripped out the pin, the loom, and his hair from the fabric.
[Heroes and Guides] [16]:[15] Then she said to him, “How can you say, ‘I love you,’ when your heart isn’t with me? You’ve been deceitful to me three times now, and you haven’t revealed to me the secret of your amazing strength.”
[Heroes and Guides] [16]:[16] Day after day she nagged and pestered him until he was sick to death of hearing it.
[Heroes and Guides] [16]:[17] So finally he told her his secret, “My hair has never been cut because I’ve been a Nazirite to God since my birth. If my head would be shaved, then my strength would leave me, and I’d become weak—I’d be just like any other man.”
[Heroes and Guides] [16]:[18] When Dililah perceived that he’d told her his deepest secret, she summoned the Pelishti leaders, “Come here one more time, because he’s told me his secret.” So the Pelishti leaders came, bringing the silver coins with them.
[Heroes and Guides] [16]:[19] Then she made him fall asleep on her knees, and she called in a man to shave off his seven locks of hair, causing him to start to weaken, and his additional strength left him.
[Heroes and Guides] [16]:[20] Then she said, “The Pelishtim are here to get you, Shimshon!” He woke up and thought to himself, “I’ll escape like all the other times and I’ll shake myself loose.” But he didn’t know that Yahweh had left him.
[Heroes and Guides] [16]:[21] So the Pelishtim seized him, and they gouged out his eyes. They brought him to Azah (Gaza) and chained him with a pair of bronze shackles, then they put him to work in prison grinding grain.
[Heroes and Guides] [16]:[22] However, over time his hair began to grow back again.
[Heroes and Guides] [16]:[23] Some time later, the Pelishti leaders gathered together for a celebration and to offer a large sacrifice to their god Dagon, saying, “Our god has helped us capture our terrible enemy, Shimshon (Samson).”
[Heroes and Guides] [16]:[24] When the people saw him, they praised their god, saying, “Our god has helped us capture our enemy—the devastator of our region who killed so many of us.”
[Heroes and Guides] [16]:[25] Later in the celebration when the drink had liberated their thinking, they said, “Call for Shimshon so he can entertain us.” So they brought Shimshon in from the prison and taunted him to get them all laughing. They made him stand among the pillars of the building
[Heroes and Guides] [16]:[26] and he asked the servant who was guiding him by the hand, “Place my hands against the two pillars holding up the building so I can lean on them.”
[Heroes and Guides] [16]:[27] The building was full of the men and the women, including the Pelishti leaders. On the roof there were about three thousand men and women watching the entertainment with Shimshon.
[Heroes and Guides] [16]:[28] Then Shimshon called out to Yahweh, “My master Yahweh, please remember me. Strengthen me please, just this time, oh God, so that I can avenge myself by one last act of vengeance on the Pelishtim to make them pay for my two eyes.”
[Heroes and Guides] [16]:[29] Then he took hold of the two centre pillars on which the building depended, and pressed out against them—one in his right hand and one in his left.
[Heroes and Guides] [16]:[30] Then he exclaimed, “Let me die with the Pelishtim!” He stretched out with his strength and the building fell on their leaders and all of the people in it. So he killed more people at his death than he had killed during his life.
[Heroes and Guides] [16]:[31] Then his brothers and all his father’s household went to Azah (Gaza) and carried his body back. They buried him between Tsor’ah and Eshtaol in the burial place of his father Manoah. He had helped Yisrael (Israel) for twenty years.
[Heroes and Guides] [17]:[1] Now there was a man named Mikah from the hill country of Efrayim (Ephraim)
[Heroes and Guides] [17]:[2] who admitted to his mother, “Those eleven hundred silver coins that were taken from you—when you made a curse, and even said it when I was listening, well listen, I’ve got it all—I took it myself.” His mother said, “May Yahweh bless you, my son.”
[Heroes and Guides] [17]:[3] Then he brought back the eleven hundred silver coins to his mother and she declared, “I will certainly consecrate the money to Yahweh for my son’s benefit. Take it and we’ll use it to have one statue carved and another cast.”
[Heroes and Guides] [17]:[4] So after the money had been returned, his mother gave two hundred silver coins to a silversmith. He made a carved figure and one cast from a mould, and they were placed in Mikah’s house.
[Heroes and Guides] [17]:[5] Now that Mikah had a shrine with gods in it, he made some priestly robes and some household gods, and consecrated one of his sons as his priest.
[Heroes and Guides] [17]:[6] In those days, Yisrael (Israel) didn’t have a king—each person would do whatever seemed right to them.
[Heroes and Guides] [17]:[7] Now there was a young Levite man from the family of Yehudah (Judah) who’d been staying in Beyt-Lehem (Bethlehem) (in Yehudah).
[Heroes and Guides] [17]:[8] He left Beyt-Lehem to find another place to say, and on his way, he ended up arriving at Mikah’s place in the Efrati hill country.
[Heroes and Guides] [17]:[9] “Where have you come from?” Mikah asked him. “I’m a Levite from Beyt-Lehem in Yehudah,” he replied, “and I’m trying to find a good place to stay a while.”
[Heroes and Guides] [17]:[10] “Stay with me,” said Mikah, “and be like a father and a priest to me. I’ll give you ten silver coins a year as well as board and clothing.” So the Levite man went in
[Heroes and Guides] [17]:[11] and agreed to stay with Mikah, eventually becoming like one of Mikah’s own sons.
[Heroes and Guides] [17]:[12] Mikah ordained the Levite, and the young man became like a priest to him, and lived in his house.
[Heroes and Guides] [17]:[13] “Now I know that Yahweh will make everything go well for me,” Mikah said, “because I have this Levite as a priest.”
[Heroes and Guides] [18]:[1] In those days, Yisrael (Israel) didn’t have a king. The tribe of Dan was looking for land to settle in, because up until then, they hadn’t been able to claim their allocated region among the Israeli tribes.
[Heroes and Guides] [18]:[2] So the Danim sent out five capable men (from Tsor’ah and from Eshtaol) to scout out the region and explore it. They had told them, “Go and explore the area.” They came to the Efrati hill country, as far as Mikah’s house, and spent the night there.
[Heroes and Guides] [18]:[3] They’d been near Mikah’s house when they recognized the voice of the young Levite man. So they’d gone in there and they asked him, “Who brought you here? What are you doing in this place? What do you get here?”
[Heroes and Guides] [18]:[4] Then he told them what Mikah had done for him, and how he’d hired him to be like his priest.
[Heroes and Guides] [18]:[5] So they asked him, “Please find out from God if we’ll have success on this expedition we’re on.”
[Heroes and Guides] [18]:[6] “Continue on in peace,” the priest said. “Yahweh has prepared everything ahead of you all.”
[Heroes and Guides] [18]:[7] Then the five men left and went on to Layish. They saw that the people there were living in confidence just like the Tsidonim (Sidonians) were—peacefully and feeling secure. No one in the region was causing trouble for them and they were very settled. They were far away from the Tsidonim and didn’t interact with others.
[Heroes and Guides] [18]:[8] Then they went back to their relatives in Tsor’ah and Eshtaol, who asked them, “How did it go?”
[Heroes and Guides] [18]:[9] “Get ready immediately,” they said, “so that we can go to battle against them! Because we’ve seen the land and listen, it’s incredibly good. Don’t just stay still here—you all need to take action to go in to take possession of the land.
[Heroes and Guides] [18]:[10] When you go, you’ll all come to a people living without suspicion of attack, and the land is spacious in all directions, because God will hand it over to you—a place where there’s no lack of anything that’s on the earth.”
[Heroes and Guides] [18]:[11] So six hundred Dani warriors left Tsor’ah and Eshtaol, carrying their weapons.
[Heroes and Guides] [18]:[12] They set off and camped at Kiryat-Yearim in Yehudah (Judah). That’s why they call that place Mahaneh-Dan (meaning ‘Dan’s camp’) to this day—it’s back behind Kiryat-Yearim.
[Heroes and Guides] [18]:[13] From there, they crossed over into the Efrati hill country, eventually arriving near Mikah’s house.
[Heroes and Guides] [18]:[14] Then the five men who had been here previously scouting out the land said to their group, “Do you know that there’s a house here with a gear for priests, family idols, a carved image, and a cast image? So now, consider what you should do.”
[Heroes and Guides] [18]:[15] So they turned off the main path and they came to the place with the young Levite man in Mikah’s house, and they asked about his welfare.
[Heroes and Guides] [18]:[16] The six hundred Dani men stayed outside at the gate, holding their weapons.
[Heroes and Guides] [18]:[17] The five men who’d gone to scout out the land went in around the back. They took the carved image, the priest’s gear, the family idols, and the cast image, while the priest was standing at the entrance of the gate along with the six hundred armed men.
[Heroes and Guides] [18]:[18] When the priest saw them bringing out all the religious objects, he demanded, “What’s going on?”
[Heroes and Guides] [18]:[19] “Stay quiet,” they told him. “Put your hand over your mouth and come with us, and be like a father and a priest for us. Is it better to be a priest for only one household, or to be a priest for a whole related tribe in Yisrael (Israel)?”
[Heroes and Guides] [18]:[20] The priest liked that idea, so he went along with them—taking the priestly gear and the household idols, and the carved image.
[Heroes and Guides] [18]:[21] Then they went back to the main path and continued on their way with the children, animals, and those carrying the valuable property going in front.
[Heroes and Guides] [18]:[22] When they’d already gone quite some distance from Mikah’s house, Mikah and his neighbours gathered together, then the men ran in a group and caught up with the Danim.
[Heroes and Guides] [18]:[23] They called out to the Danim who turned around to face them and asked Mikah, “What’s the matter? Why has this group come together?”
[Heroes and Guides] [18]:[24] “You all took my gods that I made,” Mikah replied, “And the priest. Then you disappeared and I had nothing left. So how can you all ask me what the matter is!”
[Heroes and Guides] [18]:[25] “I wouldn’t say too much if I was you,” he was told. “Otherwise some of our more fiery men might start to get a bit hostile, then you’d bring about your own death, and that of your companions!”
[Heroes and Guides] [18]:[26] Then Mikah realised that they were too strong for them, so they turned back around and went home. So the Danim continued onward,
[Heroes and Guides] [18]:[27] taking with them the things that Mikah had made, as well as his priest. They came to Layish where the unsuspecting people were living peaceably, and they slaughtered them with their swords and burnt down the city.
[Heroes and Guides] [18]:[28] No one came to rescue them because it was a long way from Tsidon (Sidon) and they did have much involvement with them anyway. (Layish was in the valley near Beyt-Rehov.) They rebuilt the city and then moved into it.
[Heroes and Guides] [18]:[29] They named the rebuilt city Dan (instead of Layish) in honour of their ancestor Dan who was one of Yisrael’s (Israel) sons.
[Heroes and Guides] [18]:[30] The Danim mounted the carved image for themselves to worship. Yonatan (Jonathan) (Gereshom’s son from Menasheh (Manasseh)) became the priest for the Danim (and then his descendants until when the people were eventually exiled from the region).
[Heroes and Guides] [18]:[31] So they set up the carved image that Mikah had made and worshipped it the whole time that God’s tent was at Shiloh.
[Heroes and Guides] [19]:[1] In those days when there was no king over Yisrael (Israel), there was a Levite man who was staying in the remotest parts of the hill country of Efrayim (Ephraim). He took a slave-wife for himself from Beyt-Lehem (Bethlehem) in Yehudah (Judah).
[Heroes and Guides] [19]:[2] However, she started sleeping around, and then she left him and went to her father’s house in Beyt-Lehem where she ended up staying for four months.
[Heroes and Guides] [19]:[3] Then her husband got organised and went after her—to sweet-talk her and persuade her to return with him. He took a young servant man and a team of donkeys. She invited her husband into her father’s house, and when her father saw him, he was glad to meet him.
[Heroes and Guides] [19]:[4] His father-in-law (her father) insisted on offering hospitality, so they ate and drank, and he stayed the night, and ended up staying for three days.
[Heroes and Guides] [19]:[5] Then on the fourth day, they got up early and the Levite prepared to leave, but his father-in-law urged him to eat before they left.
[Heroes and Guides] [19]:[6] So the two of them ate and drank together, and then the woman’s father said, “Please stay another night. Relax and have a good time.”
[Heroes and Guides] [19]:[7] The man got ready to leave, however his father-in-law persisted, so he stayed another night there.
[Heroes and Guides] [19]:[8] He got up early in the morning on the fifth day to get ready to leave, but the father of the young woman said, “Get some energy first.” So they waited until later in the day, and then the two of them ate.
[Heroes and Guides] [19]:[9] When the man stood up to go with his slave-wife and his young man, his father-in-law said, “Listen, the day’s coming to an end soon. Please stay the night. See, it’ll be getting dark soon. Spend the night here and be happy. Then make an early start tomorrow for your journey home.”
[Heroes and Guides] [19]:[10] But the man from the tribe of Levi didn’t want to stay another night. He put saddles on his two donkeys, and started to go with his slave-wife and his servant toward Yevus city (now called Yerushalem (Jerusalem)).
[Heroes and Guides] [19]:[11] They got close to Yevus and the daylight had mostly gone, so the young man said to his master, “Come, please, we should turn aside into this city of the Yevusim so we can spend the night there.”
[Heroes and Guides] [19]:[12] “We won’t go into a city of foreigners,” his master replied. “There’s no Israelis there. Better to keep going until we reach Giveah.”
[Heroes and Guides] [19]:[13] Then he added, “Yes, let’s keep going to reach either Giveah or Ramah to spend the night in.”
[Heroes and Guides] [19]:[14] So they passed Yevus and went on, but the sun went down as they neared Giveah (in Benyamite territory)
[Heroes and Guides] [19]:[15] so they went into Giveah to spend the night there. They went and sat in the open plaza of the city, but no one invited them into their home for the night.
[Heroes and Guides] [19]:[16] But then in late evening, an old man came in from his work in the field. He was from the Efrati hill country but currently staying in the Giveah area where the residents were Benyamites.
[Heroes and Guides] [19]:[17] He looked up and noticed them in the open plaza of the city and asked the man, “Where are you going, and where have you come from?”
[Heroes and Guides] [19]:[18] “We’re passing through from Beyt-Lehem (Bethlehem) in Yehudah (Judah),” the Levite replied. “Going to the remote parts of the Efrati hill country where I’m from. I went to Beyt-Lehem, and I’m going to Shiloh where Yahweh’s house is. However, no one here has invited us into their home.
[Heroes and Guides] [19]:[19] We have our own food and straw for our donkeys, and enough food and wine for the three of us so we don’t need anything else.
[Heroes and Guides] [19]:[20] “Peace to you all,” said the old man. “Let me supply everything you need—only don’t spend the night here in the square.”
[Heroes and Guides] [19]:[21] Then he took them to his house and fed their donkeys. They washed their feet, and they all ate and drank.
[Heroes and Guides] [19]:[22] They were having a good time, but suddenly the men of the city—wicked men—had surrounded the house—pounding repeatedly on the door. They called out to the old man who owned the house, “Hey, bring out the man who came to your place, so we can have fun with him.”
[Heroes and Guides] [19]:[23] The man who owned the house went out to them and said to them, “No, my brothers, please you mustn’t act wickedly. That man is a guest in my house—you all mustn’t do this disgraceful thing.
[Heroes and Guides] [19]:[24] My virgin daughter and his slave-wife are here. Please let me bring them out so you can ravish them and do whatever you want to them. But don’t do that wicked thing to that man.”
[Heroes and Guides] [19]:[25] But the men weren’t willing to listen to him, so the man pushed his slave-wife out to them and they raped her and abused her the whole night until the morning, when they discarded her as it began to dawn.
[Heroes and Guides] [19]:[26] The woman managed to get herself back to the house where her master was, and collapsed at the entrance until it got light.
[Heroes and Guides] [19]:[27] When her master got up and he opened the door to go and continue on his trip, look, his slave-wife had fallen at the entrance and her hands were on the threshold.
[Heroes and Guides] [19]:[28] “Get up,” he told her. “Let’s go.” But she didn’t answer, so he put her on his donkey and headed home.
[Heroes and Guides] [19]:[29] When he arrived, he got a knife and hacked his wife’s body into twelve pieces (including the bones), and he sent them to various places spread across all of Yisrael’s (Israel) territory.
[Heroes and Guides] [19]:[30] Then everyone who saw a piece said, “Nothing has ever happened like this before—we’ve never seen anything like this from the time that the Israelis left Mitsrayim (Egypt) until now. What do we need to do about it? Speak up and make a plan.”
[Heroes and Guides] [20]:[1] Then all the Israelis from Dan in the north to Be’er-Sheva (Beersheba) in the south, and even from Gilead across the Yarden (Jordan), came and assembled before Yahweh at Mitspah with one single, united purpose.
[Heroes and Guides] [20]:[2] The leaders of all the Israeli tribes also came out to show their agreement with the assembly of the people of the true God: four hundred thousand warriors all carrying swords.
[Heroes and Guides] [20]:[3] Meanwhile, the Benyamites had heard that the Israelis had gathered at Mitspah, and everyone asked, “Explain how this wicked thing came to happen.”
[Heroes and Guides] [20]:[4] So the Levite man (the husband of the woman who had been murdered) answered, “I went to the Giveah region (in Benyamin) with my slave-wife to spend the night.
[Heroes and Guides] [20]:[5] The citizens of Giveah conspired together against me. They surrounded the house at night because of me, intending to kill me. Instead, they assaulted and abused my slave-wife so that she died.
[Heroes and Guides] [20]:[6] I took my slave-wife’s body back home and cut her in pieces, and I sent them out into every section of the territory that God gave Yisrael (Israel), because they’ve committed a heinous crime, and a disgrace to Yisrael.
[Heroes and Guides] [20]:[7] Listen, all of you Israelis, what’s your advice? What should we do about it?.”
[Heroes and Guides] [20]:[8] All the people agreed together and started saying, “We won’t go back to our families. We won’t return to our houses.
[Heroes and Guides] [20]:[9] rather this is what we must do to Giveah: choose by lot who will fight against them.
[Heroes and Guides] [20]:[10] Choose a tenth of our men to go and get supplies for the other warriors to travel to Giveah in Benyamin after what they did that outraged Yisrael.
[Heroes and Guides] [20]:[11] So all Yisrael was united together against that city.
[Heroes and Guides] [20]:[12] Then the Israeli tribes sent men across the Benyamite region to ask, “What’s this evil thing that’s been done among you?
[Heroes and Guides] [20]:[13] So now, hand over those worthless men from the Giveah region so that we can put them to death and purge Yisrael of that evil.” But the Benyamites weren’t willing to take the advice of their Israeli relatives.
[Heroes and Guides] [20]:[14] They came out of their cities and assembled at Giveah to the battle against the Israelis.
[Heroes and Guides] [20]:[15] The Benyamites mobilised together twenty-six thousand men from their cities on that day, all carrying swords. In addition, seven hundred chosen men had been mobilised from the Giveah region.
[Heroes and Guides] [20]:[16] Among all of those people were seven hundred chosen left-handers, each of whom could sling a stone at a hair without missing.
[Heroes and Guides] [20]:[17] The Israelis (excluding Benyamites) mustered up for themselves four hundred thousand men—all expert warriors and all carrying swords.
[Heroes and Guides] [20]:[18] The Israelis got ready and went to Beyt-El (Bethel) and asked God, “Who should lead us into battle with the Benyamites?” “It should be Yehudah (Judah) out front,” Yahweh responded.
[Heroes and Guides] [20]:[19] So the Israelis set out in the morning and made camp near Giveah.
[Heroes and Guides] [20]:[20] Then they went out to battle against the Benyamites—setting themselves up for the battle against them at Giveah.
[Heroes and Guides] [20]:[21] But the Benyamites led a surprise attack out of Giveah and killed twenty-two thousand of the Israeli warriors.
[Heroes and Guides] [20]:[22] However the Israelis strengthened themselves and they continued to set up for battle the next day at the same place.
[Heroes and Guides] [20]:[23] Then the Israelis assembled and wept before Yahweh until evening. They asked him, “Should we continue to attack and battle against our cousins the Benyamites?” “Go back against them,” Yahweh replied.
[Heroes and Guides] [20]:[24] So the Israelis went back to battle against the Benyamites again on the second day.
[Heroes and Guides] [20]:[25] Again the Benyamites came out from Giveah, and this time they killed eighteen thousand Israeli swordsmen.
[Heroes and Guides] [20]:[26] Then the Israeli warriors and all the people went back to Beyt-El (Bethel). They wept, and they sat there before Yahweh. They fasted that day until the evening, then they offered burnt offerings and peace offerings to Yahweh.
[Heroes and Guides] [20]:[27] They asked Yahweh (because the box containing the agreement with the true God was there in those days
[Heroes and Guides] [20]:[28] and Pinhas (son of Aharon’s (Aaron) son Eleazar) was serving before it in those days), “Should we continue to go to the battle once more against the our cousins the Benyamites, or should we stop?” “Go back again, because tomorrow I’ll give you victory over them,” Yahweh responded.
[Heroes and Guides] [20]:[29] So the Israelis placed groups of warriors in ambush all around Giveah.
[Heroes and Guides] [20]:[30] Then they took their positions now for the third day against the Benyamites in Giveah.
[Heroes and Guides] [20]:[31] When the Benyamites came out from the city, they were lured away as they began to strike down their enemies like the time before. Around thirty Israelis were killed on the two roads—one going to Beyt-El and the other to Giveah through the countryside.
[Heroes and Guides] [20]:[32] Then the Benyamites said, “We’re starting to defeat them, just like before.” But the Israelis had said, “Let’s flee so that we can draw them away from the city and onto the roads.”
[Heroes and Guides] [20]:[33] Then the main group of Israelis retreated and set up battle lines at Ba’al-Tamar, as the ones hiding in ambush made a surprise attack from their places in Ma’areh-Geva.
[Heroes and Guides] [20]:[34] Ten thousand chosen Israeli warriors came out in the sight of the Giveah region, and the battle was fierce, but the Benyamites hadn’t yet realised that disaster was about to hit them.
[Heroes and Guides] [20]:[35] Yahweh helped the Israelis to defeat the Benyamites that day, and over twenty-five thousand Benyamite swordsmen were killed
[Heroes and Guides] [20]:[36] and they saw that they were defeated. The Israelis had given ground to the Benyamites because they had relied on the ambush placed around Giveah.
[Heroes and Guides] [20]:[37] Then the group hiding in ambush had rushed out and spread out around Giveah, then had gone in and attacked the entire city with their swords.
[Heroes and Guides] [20]:[38] Then they started a fire as the prearranged signal was to be the rising column of smoke up out of the city.
[Heroes and Guides] [20]:[39] Meanwhile the main Israeli force had retreated, and the Benyamites had attacked and killed around thirty men, thinking that they were winning like they’d done twice before.
[Heroes and Guides] [20]:[40] But when the pillar of smoke began to rise from the city, the Benyamites looked behind them and were shocked to see their city going up in smoke.
[Heroes and Guides] [20]:[41] Then the main Israeli force stopped retreating and turned back to attack again. The Benyamites were horrified because they now saw that disaster had struck them.
[Heroes and Guides] [20]:[42] They retreated away from the Israelis into the wilderness, but the battle overtook them, plus the Israelis were coming back out of the cities getting right in amongst them to fight.
[Heroes and Guides] [20]:[43] They surrounded the Benyamites as they tried to flee, and easily ran them down as they tried to escape from the Giveah region towards the east.
[Heroes and Guides] [20]:[44] Eighteen thousand strong Benyamite warriors were killed,
[Heroes and Guides] [20]:[45] and the rest turned and fled into the wilderness towards the Rimon rock. Another five thousand men were killed along the trails. They chased them all the way to Gideom, and killed another two thousand men,
[Heroes and Guides] [20]:[46] so the total number of Benyamite swordsmen who were killed came to twenty-five thousand—all strong warriors.
[Heroes and Guides] [20]:[47] But six hundred men made it to Rimon rock, and they stayed there for four months.
[Heroes and Guides] [20]:[48] Meanwhile, the Israelis went back to the Benyamite region and killed the people with their swords—entire cities including cattle and everything else—then the cities were set on fire.
[Heroes and Guides] [21]:[1] Now back in Mitspah, the Israeli men had promised never to allow their daughters to marry a Benyamite man.
[Heroes and Guides] [21]:[2] But now the Israelis went to Beyt-El (Bethel) and sat there before God until evening—calling out and crying loudly,
[Heroes and Guides] [21]:[3] asking, “Oh Yahweh, God of Yisrael (Israel), why has this happened to Yisrael—for one tribe to be missing from Yisrael now?”
[Heroes and Guides] [21]:[4] The next day, the people got up early and built an altar there, and they offered up burnt offerings and peace offerings.
[Heroes and Guides] [21]:[5] Then the Israelis asked, “Among all the Israeli tribes serving Yahweh, was there any group who didn’t join the battle?” (They asked that because they had previously decided that anyone who didn’t go to Mitspah to fight for Yahweh would be put to death.)
[Heroes and Guides] [21]:[6] Now the Israelis felt sorry for their Benyamite cousins, saying, “An entire tribe has been hacked off Yisrael today.

[Heroes and Guides] [21]:[8] So they asked, “Is there any from our tribes who didn’t show up for Yahweh at Mitspah?” Then listen, no one from Yavesh-Gilead had joined their assembly there.
[Heroes and Guides] [21]:[9] (When the people had checked around themselves, they’d realised that no one from Yavesh-Gilead was there.)
[Heroes and Guides] [21]:[10] So the Israelis sent twelve thousand warriors there, commanding them to use their swords to kill the inhabitants of Yavesh-Gilead, including married women and children—
[Heroes and Guides] [21]:[11] specifically they had to kill every male, and every woman who’s slept with a male.
[Heroes and Guides] [21]:[12] That way they discovered four hundred young virgin women among the inhabitants of Yavesh-Gilead, and brought them back to their camp at Shiloh (in the Kena’an (Canaan) region).
[Heroes and Guides] [21]:[13] Then the entire assembly sent a message to the Benyamites at Rimon rock, saying that they were now ready for peace.
[Heroes and Guides] [21]:[14] So the Benyamites returned and were given the young women from Yavesh-Gilead, but there wasn’t enough of them.
[Heroes and Guides] [21]:[15] The people still felt sorry for the Benyamites, because Yahweh had caused a gap among Yisrael’s (Israel) tribes,
[Heroes and Guides] [21]:[16] so the leaders asked, “How can we provide wives for the remaining Benyamite men since the other Benyamite women were wiped out?”
[Heroes and Guides] [21]:[17] Because they said, “They must be able to procreate so that an entire Israeli tribe isn’t blotted out.
[Heroes and Guides] [21]:[18] But we can’t be the ones to give our daughters to them to marry because we made an oath that anyone who did that would be cursed.”
[Heroes and Guides] [21]:[19] They said, “Listen, there’s a celebration for Yahweh from time to time at Shiloh, which is on the north of Beyt-El (Bethel), east of the road that goes from Beyt-El uphill to Shekem, and on the south of Levonah.”
[Heroes and Guides] [21]:[20] So they told the Benyamites, “Go and hide in those vineyards
[Heroes and Guides] [21]:[21] and watch. When the Shiloh girls come out to perform in the dances, come out of the vineyards and you can each catch a wife for yourselves, then go back home to Benyamin.
[Heroes and Guides] [21]:[22] When their fathers or brothers complain to us, we’ll tell them, “Let them have them since we didn’t find you for them. And you all won’t be guilty of giving them to the Benyamites because they stole them.
[Heroes and Guides] [21]:[23] So that’s what the Benyamites did—they grabbed enough dancing girls to be their wives, then they returned to their allocated land and rebuilt their cities and lived in them.
[Heroes and Guides] [21]:[24] The other Israelis went back to their tribes and their families in the areas that had been allocated to them.
[Heroes and Guides] [21]:[25] In those days, there was no king in Yisrael (Israel)—everyone would just do what seemed right to them.
[Ruth] [1]:[1] Back in the time when the tribal leaders ruled Yisrael (Israel), there was a drought which caused a shortage of food, so a man from the town of Beyt-Lehem (Bethlehem) in the Yehudah (Judah) region went to live in the country of Moav (Moab) for a while, taking his wife and their two sons.
[Ruth] [1]:[2] The man’s name was Elimelek and he was married to No’omi (Naomi), and their sons’ names were Mahlon and Kilyon. (They were part of the clan of Efratah from Beyt-Lehem in Yehudah.) They travelled to the Moav countryside and lived there.
[Ruth] [1]:[3] Then No’omi’s husband Elimelek died, and she was left with her two sons.
[Ruth] [1]:[4] Eventually they married women from there in Moav—Orpah and Ruth. But after No’omi and her sons had lived in Moav for about then years,
[Ruth] [1]:[5] Mahlon and Kilyon both also died, and No’omi was left without her husband or her two sons.
[Ruth] [1]:[6] One day No’omi (Naomi) was in the countryside there in Moav (Moab) when she heard someone telling about how Yahweh had helped his people in Yisrael (Israel) and that now they had plenty of food, so she got ready to return to Beyt-Lehem (Bethlehem) with her two daughters-in-law.
[Ruth] [1]:[7] The three of them left the place where they’d been living in Moav and started walking along the road back to Yehudah (Judah).
[Ruth] [1]:[8] Then No’omi said to her two daughters-in-law, “Both of you should go back to your parents’ homes. I pray that Yahweh will treat you with the same faithfulness that you showed to your now-deceased husbands and to me.
[Ruth] [1]:[9] May Yahweh enable both of you to find new husbands and find peace and happiness in your new homes with them.” Then she kissed them as they all wept aloud.
[Ruth] [1]:[10] But they both said, “No, we’ll go with you as you return to your relatives.”
[Ruth] [1]:[11] But No’omi responded, “No, go back to your homes my daughters. Why would you bother coming with me? It’s not like I could still give birth to more sons to become your husbands.
[Ruth] [1]:[12] Go on back, my daughters, because I’m too old to remarry. Even if I did hope for that and got married tonight and had some sons,
[Ruth] [1]:[13] could you wait for them to grow up so you could be remarried? No, my daughters, what’s hard for me, even more than your hardships, is that Yahweh is using his power against me.”
[Ruth] [1]:[14] Then they wailed and cried again, and Orpah kissed her mother-in-law goodbye and left, but Ruth stayed and clung to No’omi.
[Ruth] [1]:[15] No’omi said, “Look, your sister-in-law is going back to her parents and to her religion. Go back with her.”
[Ruth] [1]:[16] But Ruth replied, “Please don’t insist that I leave you and go back, because wherever you go, I’ll go with you and wherever you live, I’ll live there too. Your people are my people, and your god is my god.
[Ruth] [1]:[17] Wherever you die, I’ll die there too and be buried there. May Yahweh punish me severely if anything other than death separates the two of us.”
[Ruth] [1]:[18] When No’omi saw that Ruth was determined to go with her, she didn’t say any more.
[Ruth] [1]:[19] So the two of them travelled on until they reached Beyt-Lehem (Bethlehem). When they entered Beyt-Lehem, the whole town was curious about them, and the women began asking, “Is that No’omi?”
[Ruth] [1]:[20] But No’omi told them not to call her ‘No’omi’ (which means ‘pleasant’) but to call her ‘Mara’ (meaning ‘miserable’) because she said, “The almighty God has made my life very miserable.
[Ruth] [1]:[21] I went away content with a family, but Yahweh has brought me back with a void. So why call me ‘No’omi’? You see, Yahweh has testified against me—the powerful God has brought misfortune on me.”
[Ruth] [1]:[22] And so No’omi (Naomi) had returned to Yisrael (Israel), along with her daughter-in-law, Ruth the Moavit, and they arrived there in Beyt-Lehem (Bethlehem) at the start of the barley harvest.
[Ruth] [2]:[1] Now there was a relative there of No’omi’s deceased husband. His name was Boaz and he was a very wealthy man from the same clan as Elimelek had been.
[Ruth] [2]:[2] Ruth the Moavit said to No’omi, “Allow me to go to the countryside and pick up any heads of grain that the harvesters drop. I’ll follow any harvester who seems kind.” “Go ahead, my daughter,” No’omi replied.
[Ruth] [2]:[3] So Ruth left and went to the countryside where she picked up heads of grain after the harvesters, and it just so happened that that part of the countryside belonged to Boaz who was Elimelek’s relative.
[Ruth] [2]:[4] Just then, Boaz arrived from the town and greeted the harvesters, “May Yahweh be with you,” to which they replied, “May Yahweh bless you also.”
[Ruth] [2]:[5] Then he asked the foreman of the harvesters, “Whose daughter is that young woman over there?”
[Ruth] [2]:[6] “She’s a young Moavit,” the man replied. “The one who came with No’omi when she returned from Moav (Moab).
[Ruth] [2]:[7] She asked me for permission to follow the harvesters and pick up any heads of grain that drop, and she’s been doing it since early morning until just recently she’s taking a break now in the shelter.
[Ruth] [2]:[8] So Boaz approached Ruth, “Young woman,” he said, “listen here. Don’t leave this place or go to any other field to pick up grain, but just stay close by these young female workers of mine.
[Ruth] [2]:[9] Watch where the men are harvesting and follow along behind them. I’ve told them not to bother you. And whenever you’re thirsty, help yourself from the water jars that the men keep filled.”
[Ruth] [2]:[10] Then she knelt down on the ground and bowed her head low to the ground and said, “Why are you being so kind to me when I’m a foreigner? I wasn’t expecting your attention.”
