[1 Chronicles] [10]:[1] Now the Pelishtim fought against Yisrael (Israel), and the Israeli men fled away from the Pelishtim, and many were killed on Mt. Gilboa.
[1 Chronicles] [10]:[2] Then the Pelishtim pursued Sha’ul (Saul) and his sons, and they killed his sons Yonatan (Jonathan), Avinadav, and Malkishua.
[1 Chronicles] [10]:[3] The battle against Sha’ul was very fierce, and then the archers spotted him and wounded him.
[1 Chronicles] [10]:[4] Then Sha’ul said to his equipment carrier, “Draw your sword and pierce me with it, so those uncircumcised Pelishtim can’t come here and torture me.” But his equipment carrier was very scared and wasn’t willing to do it, so Sha’ul took his sword and fell onto it.
[1 Chronicles] [10]:[5] Then his equipment carrier, seeing that King Sha’ul had died, also fell on his sword and died.
[1 Chronicles] [10]:[6] So Sha’ul and his three sons died, thus ending his family’s rule.
[1 Chronicles] [10]:[7] When all the Israelis living in the valley saw that the army had fled, and that Sha’ul and his sons were dead, they abandoned their cities and fled. Then the Pelishtim came, and they lived there instead.
[1 Chronicles] [10]:[8] The next day, when the Pelishtim came to strip the dead, they found Sha’ul and his sons’ bodies on Mt. Gilboa.
[1 Chronicles] [10]:[9] They stripped him and carried away his head and his armour. Then they sent messengers all around the Pelishti regions to take the news to their idols and the people.
[1 Chronicles] [10]:[10] They put his armour in the temple of their gods, and they hung his head in their god Dagon’s temple.
[1 Chronicles] [10]:[11] When everyone who lived back in Yavesh in the Gilead region heard about everything the Pelishtim had done to Sha’ul,
[1 Chronicles] [10]:[12] all the strong men took action and retrieved the corpses of Sha’ul and his sons, and brought them back to Yavesh. Then they buried them under the large tree in Yavesh, and they fasted for seven days.
[1 Chronicles] [10]:[13] So Sha’ul died because of his disobedience—when he was unfaithful to Yahweh by not following Yahweh’s instructions, and also because he consulted a medium for guidance
[1 Chronicles] [10]:[14] instead of requesting Yahweh’s advice. So Yahweh killed him and handed the kingdom over to Yishay’s (Jesse) son David.
[1 Chronicles] [11]:[1] Then all of Yisrael (Israel) assembled around David at Hevron, saying, “Look, we’re your flesh and blood relatives.
[1 Chronicles] [11]:[2] In the recent past, even when Sha’ul (Saul) was king, you were the one who took Yisrael out and the one who brought us back in. Plus your god Yahweh told you, ‘You yourself will shepherd my people, Yisrael, and you yourself will become the leader of my Israeli people.’ ”
[1 Chronicles] [11]:[3] So all the Israeli elders went to the king at Hevron, and David made a solemn agreement with them at Hevron in front of Yahweh. Then they anointed David as king over Yisrael in accordance with Yahweh’s message that was given through the prophet Shmuel (Samuel).
[1 Chronicles] [11]:[4] Then David and all of Yisrael went to Yerushalem (Jerusalem) (Yerushalem, which was also known as Yevus because the Yevusim were living there).
[1 Chronicles] [11]:[5] The inhabitants inside Yevus said to David, “You won’t be entering this place.” But David captured what became known as the Tsiyon (Zion) stronghold, that is, the city of David.
[1 Chronicles] [11]:[6] He’d said, “The one who strikes down the Yevusim first will become my army commander.” Tseruyah’s son Yoav (Joab) went up over the wall first, and he became head of the army.
[1 Chronicles] [11]:[7] David started living in that stronghold, so then they called it the city of David.
[1 Chronicles] [11]:[8] He built the city up all around, from the terrace to the surrounding walls, and Yoav restored the rest of the city.
[1 Chronicles] [11]:[9] So David became more powerful because Commander-in-chief Yahweh helped him.
[1 Chronicles] [11]:[10] The following were the leaders of David’s powerful warriors who, together with all of Yisrael (Israel), strengthened his kingdom and established him as king, just as Yahweh had said.
[1 Chronicles] [11]:[11] So these are David’s powerful warriors: Yashaveam (a Hakmoni and the leader of the thirty), who once used his spear against three hundred men in a single battle and killed them all.
[1 Chronicles] [11]:[12] Next was Eleazar (an Ahohi, son of Dodo) who was one of the top three powerful warriors.
[1 Chronicles] [11]:[13] He was with David at Pas-Damim when the Pelishtim had assembled there for battle near a part of the countryside where barley was growing. At first, the Israelis fled from the Pelishtim,
[1 Chronicles] [11]:[14] but then they took their stand in the middle of the barley and proceeded to defeat the Pelishtim as Yahweh saved them through a stunning victory.
[1 Chronicles] [11]:[15] Then three of that top thirty went down to David, near the rock at Adulam’s cave. Meanwhile, Pelishtim had encamped in the Refaim Valley.
[1 Chronicles] [11]:[16] David was in that stronghold then, and the Pelishti garrison was in Beyt-Lehem (Bethlehem),
[1 Chronicles] [11]:[17] and David was thirsty and asked, “Who’ll get me water to drink from the well by the Beyt-Lehem gate?”
[1 Chronicles] [11]:[18] So those three broke through the Pelishti camp, and they drew water from the well at the Beyt-Lehem gate, and they brought it back to David. But David wasn’t willing to drink it, and he poured it out on the ground as an offering to Yahweh.
[1 Chronicles] [11]:[19] “Far be it from me to drink this water in front of my god,” he said. “Could I drink the blood of these men who risked their lives to bring it?” So he wasn’t prepared to drink it. Those were some of the things those three powerful warriors did.
[1 Chronicles] [11]:[20] Yoav’s (Joab) brother Avishay was the head of a group of three. He’d killed three hundred people with his spear and had a reputation among the three.
[1 Chronicles] [11]:[21] He was honoured more than the other two and became the leader of that second group of three, but didn’t enter the first Three.
[1 Chronicles] [11]:[22] Yehoyada’s son Benayah from Kavtse’el was a powerful warrior who did amazing things. He struck down Ariel’s two sons from Moav (Moab). Another time, he climbed down into a pit on a snowy day and killed the lion that was trapped in the pit.
[1 Chronicles] [11]:[23] He also killed a huge Mitsri (Egyptian) man—well over two metres tall. The Mitsri was carrying a spear like a weaver’s beam, but Benayah went down to take him on with a staff. He forced the spear from the Mitsri’s grasp, and then killed him with it.
[1 Chronicles] [11]:[24] So that was what Benayah (Yehoyada’s son) did that gave him a reputation among the three powerful warriors.
[1 Chronicles] [11]:[25] Actually, he was honoured more than the Thirty, yet he didn’t make it to the first Three, but David appointed him to have authority over his bodyguards.

[1 Chronicles] [12]:[8] Some Gadim joined David at the wilderness stronghold. They were very strong army warriors, ready for battle with shields and spears. Their faces were fierce like lions, but they could run across the hills like gazelles.
[1 Chronicles] [12]:[9] Their leader was Ezer, then Ovadyah (Obadiah), then Eliav.
[1 Chronicles] [12]:[10] Next was Mishmanah, then Yirmiyah,
[1 Chronicles] [12]:[11] Atay, Eliel,
[1 Chronicles] [12]:[12] Yohanan, Elzavad,
[1 Chronicles] [12]:[13] another Yirmiyah, then the eleventh was Makbanay.
[1 Chronicles] [12]:[14] Those men from the Gad tribe were army leaders—each leading somewhere between a hundred and a thousand men.
[1 Chronicles] [12]:[15] They crossed to the west side of the Yarden (Jordan) River during the spring, at the time of the year when the river floods. They drove out all the people who lived in the valleys on both sides of the river.
[1 Chronicles] [12]:[16] Some other men from the tribes of Benyamin and Yehudah (Judah) also went to David in his stronghold.
[1 Chronicles] [12]:[17] David went out of the cave to meet them, and he told them: “If you’ve come to me in peace, to help me, then I’ll be happy to cooperate with you men. But if you men plan to betray me to my enemies even though I’ve done you no harm, may the god of our ancestors see your motives and judge.”
[1 Chronicles] [12]:[18] Then the spirit empowered Amasay, the head of the thirty, and he said: “To you, David, and with you, son of Yishay (Jesse): peace. Peace to you and peace to the one who helps you, because your god has helped you.” And David received them and appointed them as the heads of the troop.
[1 Chronicles] [12]:[19] Some men from Menasheh (Manasseh) joined David when he accompanied the Pelishtim to battle against King Sha’ul (Saul). (But David and his men didn’t help the Pelishtim, because the Pelishtim’ governors were advised to send them away, as there was a worry that David would feel loyal to his former master, and hence turn on them.)
[1 Chronicles] [12]:[20] As David was going to Tsiklag, the following men from Menasheh joined him: Adnah, Yozavad, Yedieael, Mika’el (Michael), another Yozavad, Elihu, and Tsiletay—the captains of units of thousands from Menasheh.
[1 Chronicles] [12]:[21] They helped David stand against bands of raiders, because they were all powerful warriors and military leaders.
[1 Chronicles] [12]:[22] Every day more men joined David to help him, until his army became very large, like the Israeli people group itself.
[1 Chronicles] [12]:[23] The following are the numbers of the leaders of those equipped for war. They came to David at Hevron to help him obtain Sha’ul’s kingdom as Yahweh had promised.
[1 Chronicles] [12]:[24] From Yehudah (Judah): 6,800 warriors ready for battle with shields and spears.
[1 Chronicles] [12]:[25] From Shim’on (Simeon): 7,100 powerful warriors ready for battle.
[1 Chronicles] [12]:[26] From Levi: 4,600.
[1 Chronicles] [12]:[27] Yehoyada (a leader descended from Aharon (Aaron)) brought 3,700 with him.
[1 Chronicles] [12]:[28] Tsadok, a strong young man, brought twenty-two leaders from his clan.
[1 Chronicles] [12]:[29] From Benyamin (Sha’ul’s (Saul) tribe): 3,000 (most of whom had previously served King Sha’ul).
[1 Chronicles] [12]:[30] From Efrayim (Ephraim): 20,800 powerful warriors who were admired within their own clans.
[1 Chronicles] [12]:[31] From the half-tribe of Menasheh (Manasseh): 18,000 who were known by name came to make David king.
[1 Chronicles] [12]:[32] From Yisakar (Issachar): 200 leaders (with a good understanding of the times and the right thing to do) along with their relatives that they commanded.
[1 Chronicles] [12]:[33] From Zevulun: 50,000 experienced warriors with each kind of weapon, and stoic in attitude, yet loyal.
[1 Chronicles] [12]:[34] From Naftali (Naphtali): 1,000 officers, along with 37,000 men carrying shields and spears.
[1 Chronicles] [12]:[35] From Dan: 28,600 men prepared for battle.
[1 Chronicles] [12]:[36] From Asher: 40,000 warriors prepared for battle.
[1 Chronicles] [12]:[37] From Re’uven, Gad, and the Menasheh (Manasseh) half-tribe across the Yarden (Jordan) river: 120,000 men armed with all kinds of weapons.
[1 Chronicles] [12]:[38] All those enthusiastic and capable warriors came to Hevron to make David king over all of Yisrael (Israel). The rest of Yisrael was also united in wanting to make David king.
[1 Chronicles] [12]:[39] They were there with David three days, eating and drinking, because their families had sent provisions with them.
[1 Chronicles] [12]:[40] Also, people who lived near that area (even as far as the tribal areas belonging to Yisakar (Issachar), Zevulun, and Naftali (Naphtali)) were bringing bread on donkeys and camels, and on mules and on oxen: plentiful supplies of flour, fig cakes, raisin cakes, wine, and oil, as well as oxen and sheep, because Yisrael was celebrating.
[1 Chronicles] [13]:[1] One day David consulted with all his leaders—the commanders of thousands and of hundreds.
[1 Chronicles] [13]:[2] David said to the whole Israeli assembly, “If it sounds good to you, and to our god Yahweh, let’s spread out to all our different regions to recruit our relatives, along with the priests and the Levites in the cities among their pasturelands, so they can join us.
[1 Chronicles] [13]:[3] And let’s return our god’s box back here, because we didn’t use it to ask God for guidance in Sha’ul’s (Saul) time.”
[1 Chronicles] [13]:[4] All the assembled people agreed because everyone could see that it was the right thing to do.
[1 Chronicles] [13]:[5] So David assembled all of Yisrael (Israel), from everywhere from the Shihor river down in Mitsrayim (Egypt) to as far north as Levo-Hamat, to bring in God’s box from Kiryat-Yearim.
[1 Chronicles] [13]:[6] Then David and all of Yisrael went to Kiryat-Yearim (also known as Ba’alah, in Yehudah (Judah)), to bring up from there the box of God Yahweh who sits over the winged creatures. The box is used when calling his name to request help.
[1 Chronicles] [13]:[7] They transported God’s box on a new cart from Avinadav’s house, and Uza and Ahyo were leading the cart,
[1 Chronicles] [13]:[8] and David and all of Yisrael were celebrating in front of God with all their energy, with songs, and with lyres, harps, tambourines, cymbals, and trumpets.
[1 Chronicles] [13]:[9] However, just as they were passing Kidon’s threshing floor, the oxen stumbled and Uza reached out to steady the box.
[1 Chronicles] [13]:[10] That made Yahweh very angry with Uza, and he struck him down because he’d reached out to touch the box, and he died right there in front of God.
[1 Chronicles] [13]:[11] That in turn made David angry because Yahweh had burst out against Uza, and he named that place Perets-Uza (which means ‘outburst against Uza’), which it’s still called, to this day.
[1 Chronicles] [13]:[12] David was afraid of God that day and asked himself, “How can I possibly bring God’s box to where I am in Yerushalem (Jerusalem)?”
[1 Chronicles] [13]:[13] So David gave up on bringing the box to where he was in the city of David, and instead he took it into the nearby house belonging to Oved-Edom the Giti.
[1 Chronicles] [13]:[14] So God’s box stayed at Oved-Edom’s house for three months, and Yahweh blessed Oved-Edom’s home and everything that belonged to him.
[1 Chronicles] [14]:[1] One day King Huram from Tsor (Tyre) sent messengers to David, along with cedar timber and stone masons and carpenters to build a house for him.
[1 Chronicles] [14]:[2] By then David had realised that Yahweh had established him as king over Yisrael (Israel)—that his kingdom was being made more prominent for the sake of Yahweh’s people Yisrael.
[1 Chronicles] [14]:[3] Then David took more wives in Yerushalem (Jerusalem) and he fathered more sons and daughters.
[1 Chronicles] [14]:[4] These are his children who were born there in Yerushalem: Shamua, Shovav, Natan (Nathan), Shelomoh (Solomon),
[1 Chronicles] [14]:[5] Yavehar, Elishua, Elifelet,
[1 Chronicles] [14]:[6] Nogah, Nefeg, Yafia,
[1 Chronicles] [14]:[7] Elishama, Be’elyada, and Elifelet.
[1 Chronicles] [14]:[8] When the Pelishtim heard that David had been anointed as king over all of Yisrael (Israel), the entire Pelishti army went up into the hill country to eliminate him. David got this news and took his army out to meet them.
[1 Chronicles] [14]:[9] Meanwhile, the Pelishtim went and raided the Refaim valley,
[1 Chronicles] [14]:[10] and David asked God, “Should I take on the Pelishtim, and will you give me victory over them?” “Go ahead,” Yahweh answered, “and I’ll enable you to defeat them.”
[1 Chronicles] [14]:[11] Then they went up to what’s now called Ba’al-Peratsim, and David defeated them down there. David said, “God has used me to break through my enemies like a flooded river breaking a dam.” Therefore they named that place Ba’al-Peratsim (which means ‘the master bursts through’).
[1 Chronicles] [14]:[12] The Pelishtim abandoned their idols as they fled, and David ordered them to be burnt.
[1 Chronicles] [14]:[13] But soon the Pelishtim raided the valley again,
[1 Chronicles] [14]:[14] and David asked God’s advice again. “Don’t go uphill after them,” God said, “but circle around them and confront them in front of the balsam trees.
[1 Chronicles] [14]:[15] When you hear the sound of the marching in the tops of the balsam trees, that’s when you should attack, because God will have gone out ahead of you to strike down the Pelishti army.”
[1 Chronicles] [14]:[16] So David did just as God had told him, and he attacked the Pelishtim from Giveon all the way to Gezer.
[1 Chronicles] [14]:[17] So David’s reputation spread everywhere, and Yahweh caused the other nations to be afraid of him.
[1 Chronicles] [15]:[1] David constructed houses for his wives in the city of David. He also prepared a place for God’s sacred box and erected a tent for it.
[1 Chronicles] [15]:[2] Then David ordered, “Only the Levites are allowed to carry God’s box, because Yahweh chose them to carry the box and to minister for him forever.”
[1 Chronicles] [15]:[3] David assembled all of Yisrael (Israel) in Yerushalem (Jerusalem) to bring Yahweh’s box uphill there to the place that he’d prepared for it.
[1 Chronicles] [15]:[4] Then he summoned Aharon’s (Aaron) descendants and these Levites:
[1 Chronicles] [15]:[5] From Kohat’s descendants (Levi’s second son): Uriel the leader and 120 of his relatives.

[1 Chronicles] [15]:[13] The first time we tried, it wasn’t you Levites, so our god Yahweh burst out against us because we hadn’t requested his instruction.”
[1 Chronicles] [15]:[14] So the priests and the Levites consecrated themselves to bring up Yisrael’s (Israel) god Yahweh’s sacred box.
[1 Chronicles] [15]:[15] Then, following Yahweh’s instructions as given to Mosheh (Moses), Levi’s descendants carried God’s sacred box with its poles on their shoulders.
[1 Chronicles] [15]:[16] Meanwhile, David instructed the Levite leaders to assign their brothers as the singers, with accompanying instruments—harps, lyres, and cymbals—playing to raise a sound of celebration.
[1 Chronicles] [15]:[17] The Levites assigned Yoel’s son Heyman and his relative Asaf (son of Berekyah) and Eytan (Kushayah’s son, a descendant of Merari),

[1 Chronicles] [15]:[19] Heyman, Asaf, and Eytan sang and also played bronze cymbals.
[1 Chronicles] [15]:[20] Zekaryah, Aziel, Shemiramot, Yehiel, Uni, Eliav, Ma’aseyah, and Benayah played harps in a certain musical style.
[1 Chronicles] [15]:[21] Matityah, Elifelehu, Mikneyah, Oved-Edom, Yeiel, and Azazyah played lyres in a different musical style.
[1 Chronicles] [15]:[22] Kenanyah, the leader of the musical Levites, directed the singing because he was very capable.
[1 Chronicles] [15]:[23] Berekyah and Elkanah were two of the men who guarded the sacred box.
[1 Chronicles] [15]:[24] The priests Shevanyah, Yoshafat, Netanel, Amasay, Zekaryah, Benayah, and Eliezer were the ones who blew trumpets in front of God’s sacred box. Oved-Edom and Yehiyah also guarded the sacred box.
[1 Chronicles] [15]:[25] So David, the Israeli elders, and the top army commanders went to get the box containing Yahweh’s agreement from Oved-Edom’s house with much celebration.
[1 Chronicles] [15]:[26] Indeed, God helped the Levites carrying the box containing Yahweh’s agreement, and they slaughtered seven bulls and seven rams.
[1 Chronicles] [15]:[27] David was wearing a fine-linen robe, and so were all the Levites carrying the box, and the singers, and the choir director Kenanyah. In addition, David wore a linen chestpiece.
[1 Chronicles] [15]:[28] So all of Yisrael (Israel) brought the box containing Yahweh’s agreement up the hill with happy shouting, and with a sound of a ram’s horn, and with trumpets and cymbals, along with the sound of harps and lyres.
[1 Chronicles] [15]:[29] As the box containing Yahweh’s agreement was being brought inside the city of David, Mikal (Sha’ul’s (Saul) daughter) looked out the window and saw her husband, King David, dancing and celebrating, and she secretly despised him.
[1 Chronicles] [16]:[1] Then they brought in God’s box and put it in the middle of the tent that David had erected for it, and they offered burnt offerings and peace offerings in front of God.
[1 Chronicles] [16]:[2] When David finished presenting the burnt offering and the peace offerings, he blessed the people in Yahweh’s name.
[1 Chronicles] [16]:[3] Then he distributed a loaf of bread, a date cake, and a raisin cake to each man and woman in Yisrael (Israel).
[1 Chronicles] [16]:[4] Then David appointed some Levites to minister in front of Yahweh’s box and to commemorate and to thank and to praise Yisrael’s god Yahweh.
[1 Chronicles] [16]:[5] Asaf was their leader, with Zekaryah (Zechariah) as his assistant. The other Levites who helped were Yeiel, Shemiramot, Yehiel, Matityah, Eliav, Benayah, Oved-Edom, and Yeiel. They played harps and lyres, and Asaf played cymbals.
[1 Chronicles] [16]:[6] Benayah and Yahaziel the priests regularly blew trumpets in front of the box containing God’s agreement.
[1 Chronicles] [16]:[7] On that day David first gave Asaf and his helpers this song to praise Yahweh:

[1 Chronicles] [16]:[9] Sing to him and make music to him. →Tell everyone about all the wonderful things that he’s done.
[1 Chronicles] [16]:[10] Boast about his untarnished reputation. →Those who follow Yahweh should celebrate.
[1 Chronicles] [16]:[11] Ask Yahweh to help you and give you his strength. Constantly ask for his direction.
[1 Chronicles] [16]:[12] Remember the wonderful things that he’s done— his miracles and how he punished those who deserved it.
[1 Chronicles] [16]:[13] You descendants of his servant Yisrael (Israel), you descendants of Ya’akov (Jacob), the one who he chose,
[1 Chronicles] [16]:[14] he is our god, Yahweh. He judges the entire world.
[1 Chronicles] [16]:[15] Remember his agreement forever— the instructions that he gave to a thousand generations,

[1 Chronicles] [16]:[18] saying, “I’ll give the Kena’an (Canaan) region to you— your portion that will then be your inheritance.”
[1 Chronicles] [16]:[19] When your ancestors were still a small group, insignificant, and strangers in the land,
[1 Chronicles] [16]:[20] and they wandered back and forth from nation to nation, and from one kingdom to another,
[1 Chronicles] [16]:[21] God didn’t permit anyone to oppress them, and he rebuked kings on their behalf:
[1 Chronicles] [16]:[22] “Don’t attack my chosen people, and don’t harm my prophets.”
[1 Chronicles] [16]:[23] Sing to Yahweh everybody. →Every day tell others that he’s saved us.
[1 Chronicles] [16]:[24] Tell the other nations about his power. Tell all the people groups about the wonderful things he’s done,
[1 Chronicles] [16]:[25] because Yahweh is great and deserves a lot of praise, and he should be revered more than any other god.
[1 Chronicles] [16]:[26] All those gods of the other people groups are worthless, ^but it was Yahweh who created the heavens.
[1 Chronicles] [16]:[27] His presence emanates splendour and grandeur, and strength and happiness radiate from his place.
[1 Chronicles] [16]:[28] You people in nations all over the world, praise Yahweh— praise him for his splendour and his strength.
[1 Chronicles] [16]:[29] Praise Yahweh for his great reputation. Bring an offering and come into his presence. Worship Yahweh in his splendour and purity.
[1 Chronicles] [16]:[30] Let the entire planet tremble if he comes. The world is firmly established—it can’t be shaken around.
[1 Chronicles] [16]:[31] Let the heavens be glad, and let the earth shout in celebration, and let people in all the nations say, “Yahweh is king.”
[1 Chronicles] [16]:[32] Let the oceans roar along with all the creatures in them. Let the countryside celebrate along with all the creatures that live there.
[1 Chronicles] [16]:[33] Then the trees in the forests should shout happily when Yahweh comes, because he is coming to judge the world.
[1 Chronicles] [16]:[34] Give thanks to Yahweh, because he’s good, because his loyal commitment lasts forever.
[1 Chronicles] [16]:[35] Then say, “Rescue us, God who’s our saviour, and bring us together and save us from attacks by other nations, so that we’ll thank you for your untarnished reputation, and boast about your praiseworthy actions.”

[1 Chronicles] [17]:[1] After a while, when David was living in his house, he said to the prophet Natan (Nathan), “Look, here I am living in a palace made of cedar, but the box containing Yahweh’s agreement is kept in a tent.”
[1 Chronicles] [17]:[2] “Go and do what you’re planning,” Natan replied, “because God is with you.”
[1 Chronicles] [17]:[3] But that night God spoke to Natan,
[1 Chronicles] [17]:[4] “Go and tell my servant David that Yahweh says this: You yourself won’t be the one to build a residence for me to live in,
[1 Chronicles] [17]:[5] because I haven’t lived in a building from the day that I brought Yisrael (Israel) out of Mitsrayim (Egypt) until today—I’ve moved from place to place and tent to tent.
[1 Chronicles] [17]:[6] As I travelled with all the Israelis, did I ever complain to any of Yisrael’s leaders who I’d commanded to shepherd my people, and ask them, ‘Why haven’t you people built a house out of cedar for me?’ ”
[1 Chronicles] [17]:[7] “So now you should tell my servant David that Commander-in-chief Yahweh says this: I myself took you from the pasture, from behind the sheep, to be a leader over my people, Yisrael.
[1 Chronicles] [17]:[8] I’ve always been with you wherever you’ve gone, and I’ve defeated all your enemies who were attacking you, and I’ll make you famous like some of the greatest people in the world.
[1 Chronicles] [17]:[9] I’ll choose a place for my people, Yisrael, and I’ll plant them, and they’ll settle in that place and not need to be fearful again. Violent groups won’t continue to trouble them like they did in the past,
[1 Chronicles] [17]:[10] ever since I first put heroes and leaders over my people, Yisrael. Then I’ll humble all your enemies. In addition, I declare to you that Yahweh will build a dynasty for you.
[1 Chronicles] [17]:[11] When your time on earth is up, and it’s time to join your deceased ancestors, then I’ll raise up one of your sons and establish his kingdom.
[1 Chronicles] [17]:[12] He’ll be the one to build a temple for me and establish a dynasty that will last forever.
[1 Chronicles] [17]:[13] I myself will be a father to him, and he’ll be a son to me, and I won’t cease my loyal commitment to him like I ended it with your predecessor.
[1 Chronicles] [17]:[14] I’ll confirm his rule over my temple and my kingdom forever, and his ruling dynasty will last forever.”
[1 Chronicles] [17]:[15] So Natan (Nathan) passed all of that on to David.
[1 Chronicles] [17]:[16] Then king David went in and sat in front of Yahweh, and asked, “Who am I, Yahweh God, and what is my family, that you’ve brought me to this point?
[1 Chronicles] [17]:[17] This was such a small thing in your eyes, God, and you’ve spoken about the future of your servant’s family, and you’ve blessed me more than I deserve, Yahweh God.
[1 Chronicles] [17]:[18] What more can I, David, say to you about how you’ve honoured your servant? You certainly know me well.
[1 Chronicles] [17]:[19] Yahweh, you’ve done all these great things for the sake of your servant, and done just what you wanted in order to reveal your greatness.
[1 Chronicles] [17]:[20] Yahweh, there’s no one else like you, and no god except you, as we’ve all heard for ourselves.
[1 Chronicles] [17]:[21] There’s no other country like your people, Yisrael (Israel)—the only nation in the world where you, God, rescued the people in order to make them your own. That made you famous, and also feared, as you drove the people groups out ahead of your people who you ransomed out of Mitsrayim (Egypt).
[1 Chronicles] [17]:[22] You took your people, Yisrael, to be your people forever, and you, Yahweh, became our god.
[1 Chronicles] [17]:[23] “And now, Yahweh, may what you said about your servant and his family be confirmed forever, and come to pass just like you’ve said.
[1 Chronicles] [17]:[24] May your reputation be established and increase forever, as people say, ‘Commander-in-chief Yahweh, Yisrael’s god, is god over Yisrael.’ And your servant David’s family has been established as you’ve watched,
[1 Chronicles] [17]:[25] because you, God, have revealed to your servant that you’ll give me a dynasty. That’s why I’m brave enough to pray to you.
[1 Chronicles] [17]:[26] Yes, Yahweh, you are God and you’ve promised these good things to me, your servant.
[1 Chronicles] [17]:[27] And you’ve now decided to bless your servant’s family to be in front of you forever, because you, Yahweh, have blessed us, and so we’ll be blessed forever.
[1 Chronicles] [18]:[1] Sometime afterwards, David attacked and defeated the Pelishtim, subduing them, and he captured the Pelishti city of Gat and its surrounding villages.
[1 Chronicles] [18]:[2] Then he attacked and defeated Moav (Moab), and the Moavim became servants to David—taking him regular tribute.
[1 Chronicles] [18]:[3] Next David attacked and defeated King Hadadezer of Tsovah-Hamat, when that king had tried enforce his control at the Perat (Euphrates) River.
[1 Chronicles] [18]:[4] David captured 1,000 chariots, 7,000 horsemen, and 20,000 foot-soldiers from him. And David hamstrung all but one hundred of the chariot horses.
[1 Chronicles] [18]:[5] When the Arameans (or, Aramim (Syrians) ) came from Damesek (Damascus) to help King Hadadezer, David killed 22,000 of them.
[1 Chronicles] [18]:[6] Then David established forces in the Aramean town of Damesek, and the Arameans became servants to David, taking him regular tribute. So Yahweh helped David wherever he went.
[1 Chronicles] [18]:[7] David took the gold shields that were used by Hadadezer’s servants and brought them to Yerushalem (Jerusalem).
[1 Chronicles] [18]:[8] He also took a lot of bronze from Hadadezer’s cities of Tivhat and Kun. (Later, Shelomoh (Solomon) used it to make the huge bronze basin called ‘the sea’, along with its pillars and other bronze items.)
[1 Chronicles] [18]:[9] When King Toeu from Hamat heard that David had defeated King Hadadezer’s entire army from Tsovah,
[1 Chronicles] [18]:[10] he sent his son Hadoram to King David carrying various items of gold, silver, and bronze. Hadoram went to ask David for peace and to bless him because he’d fought against Hadadezer and struck him down, because Toeu had also been at war with Hadadezer.
[1 Chronicles] [18]:[11] King David set that apart as holy to Yahweh, along with the gold and silver that he’d brought back from other nations: from Edom, from Moav (Moab), from the Amonim, from the Pelishtim, and from the Amalekim.
[1 Chronicles] [18]:[12] Avishay (whose mother was Tseruyah) defeated Edom in the Salt Valley, killing eighteen thousand of them.
[1 Chronicles] [18]:[13] Then David stationed garrisons in Edom, and all of Edom became his servants. And Yahweh saved David wherever he went.
[1 Chronicles] [18]:[14] So David ruled over all of Yisrael (Israel) and administered justice and did what was right for all his people.
[1 Chronicles] [18]:[15] Tseruyah’s son Yoav (Joab) led the army, and Ahilud’s son Yehoshafat (Jehoshaphat) was the record keeper.
[1 Chronicles] [18]:[16] Ahituv’s son Tsadok and Evyatar’s son Ahimelek were priests, and Shavsha was the secretary.
[1 Chronicles] [18]:[17] Yehoyada’s son Benayah supervised the Keretim and Peletim who were David’s bodyguards, and David’s sons were his leading officials.
[1 Chronicles] [19]:[1] Some time later, the Amoni King Nahash died and his son Hanun became their king,
[1 Chronicles] [19]:[2] and David said, “I’ll show loyal commitment to Nahash’s son Hanun, because his father was good to me.” So David sent messengers to comfort him concerning his father’s death. However, when David’s servants entered Amoni territory to comfort Hanun,
[1 Chronicles] [19]:[3] the Amoni leaders asked their new king, “Do you think that David’s really sending comforters to honour your father? Wouldn’t it be more likely that he sent his servants to explore and spy out the land in order to overthrow you?”
[1 Chronicles] [19]:[4] So King Hanun took David’s servants and had their beards shaved off, plus he cut off the bottom half of their robes to expose their buttocks, and then he sent them home.
[1 Chronicles] [19]:[5] Some people quickly informed David what had happened, so he sent messengers to meet the men (because they were very much humiliated) and to tell them, “Stay there in Yeriho (Jericho) until your beards grow out, then return here.”
[1 Chronicles] [19]:[6] By then, the Amonim realised that they’d greatly insulted King David, so King Hanun and the Amonim sent thirty tonnes of silver to hire chariots and horsemen from Aram-Naharayim, Aram-Ma’akah, and Tsovah.
[1 Chronicles] [19]:[7] They hired 32,000 chariots, as well as the king of Ma’akah and his army. They all came and set up their camps near Meydeva, plus they were joined by the Amonim themselves coming out of their cities ready for battle.
[1 Chronicles] [19]:[8] When David heard about that, he sent Yoav (Joab) with the entire army.
[1 Chronicles] [19]:[9] Then the Amonim marched out and deployed ready for battle at the entrance to their city, while the kings who’d come were over in the countryside with their men.
[1 Chronicles] [19]:[10] Yoav quickly realised that he’d have to fight on two fronts, so he chose Yisrael’s (Israel) best warriors and sent them out to face the Arameans (Syrians),
[1 Chronicles] [19]:[11] while he sent the remaining men (under the control of his older brother Avishay) out against the Amonim.
[1 Chronicles] [19]:[12] Yoav told them, “If the Arameans are too strong for me, then you can come to rescue me. But if the Amonim start to gain on you, then I’ll come to rescue you.
[1 Chronicles] [19]:[13] We must be strong and fight hard to defend our people and our cities that belong to our god. Yahweh will do what he considers to be good.”
[1 Chronicles] [19]:[14] So Yoav advanced his troops to attack the Arameans, but the Arameans fled away from them.
[1 Chronicles] [19]:[15] When the Amonim saw that the Arameans had fled, they also fled from Avishay and withdrew into the city, so Yoav went back to Yerushalem (Jerusalem).
[1 Chronicles] [19]:[16] When the Arameans saw that they were defeated by Yisrael, they sent messengers to bring more Arameans from across the Perat (Euphrates) river, led by Shofak, the commander of Hadadezer’s army.
[1 Chronicles] [19]:[17] When that was reported to David, he gathered all of Yisrael and crossed the Yarden (Jordan). They positioned themselves against the Arameans, who then fought against them.
[1 Chronicles] [19]:[18] But the Arameans fled away from the Israelis, and David killed seven thousand chariot drivers and forty thousand men on foot, as well as killing Shofak, their army commander.
[1 Chronicles] [19]:[19] When Hadadezer’s servants saw that Yisrael had defeated them, they made peace with David and became his subjects, so Aram (Syria) wasn’t willing to help the Amonim militarily any more.
[1 Chronicles] [20]:[1] Then, in the spring, when kings often march out to war, Yoav (Joab) led the army out for war, and he devastated the Amonim’ land. Then he reached the capital, Rabah, and he besieged it while David stayed in Yerushalem (Jerusalem). Yoav defeated Rabah and demolished the city.
[1 Chronicles] [20]:[2] Then David took their king’s crown off his head—it was gold with a valuable gemstone set in it, and weighed thirty kilograms. He put the crown on his own head, plus he took a very large amount of plunder out of the city.
[1 Chronicles] [20]:[3] Then they took all the people out of the city and forced them to work with saws, iron picks, and axes. David did that to the people from all the Amoni cities, then he returned to Yerushalem with his army.
[1 Chronicles] [20]:[4] Some time later, war broke out with the Pelishtim at Gezer, then Sibkay the Hushati struck down Sipay, from the descendants of the Refaim, and they were subdued.
[1 Chronicles] [20]:[5] Then there was another battle with the Pelishtim, and Yair’s son Elhanan killed Lahmi the brother of Galyat (Goliath) the Giti (that is, from Gat), even though his spear shaft was as thick as the beam of a weaver’s loom.
[1 Chronicles] [20]:[6] There was also war at Gat, where there was a very tall man with six fingers on each hand and six toes on each foot, who was also a descendant of Rafa.
[1 Chronicles] [20]:[7] When he insulted Yisrael (Israel), Shimea’s son Yonatan (Jonathan) killed him. (Shimea was one of David’s older brothers.)
[1 Chronicles] [20]:[8] Those were the descendants of Rafa from Gat who were killed by David and his men.
[1 Chronicles] [21]:[1] Then a trouble-maker worked against Yisrael (Israel) by encouraging David to take a census of Yisrael,
[1 Chronicles] [21]:[2] so David ordered Yoav (Joab) and the other officials, “Go and count Yisrael from Be’er-Sheva (Beersheba) in the south to all the way as far north as Dan, then come and tell me, so that I’ll know how many warriors I have.”
[1 Chronicles] [21]:[3] “My master, the king, may Yahweh multiply his people one hundred times over. Aren’t they all your servants?” Yoav diplomatically queried, “So why does my master want to do this? Why should he bring judgement on Yisrael?”
[1 Chronicles] [21]:[4] But the king insisted, so Yoav was forced to go and gather statistics on the entire country. Then he returned to Yerushalem (Jerusalem)
[1 Chronicles] [21]:[5] and reported the numbers to David. Yisrael had 1.1 million sword-wielding men, and Yehudah (Judah) had 470 thousand.
[1 Chronicles] [21]:[6] However, Yoav had intentionally not counted the tribes of Levi and Benyamin, because he was horrified by the king’s command.
[1 Chronicles] [21]:[7] God was displeased by what David had ordered, and he punished Yisrael (Israel),
[1 Chronicles] [21]:[8] and David said to God, “I’ve disobeyed you badly by doing that. Please forgive your servant for his disobedience, because I’ve been very stupid.”
[1 Chronicles] [21]:[9] Then Yahweh told David’s prophet Gad,
[1 Chronicles] [21]:[10] “Go and tell David that Yahweh says this: I’ll give you three options—choose one of them and that’s what I’ll do to you.”
[1 Chronicles] [21]:[11] So Gad went to David and told him, “Yahweh says that you must choose one of these punishments:
[1 Chronicles] [21]:[12] either three years of famine, or three months of being overcome by your enemies’ armies, or three days of Yahweh’s ‘sword’ of pestilence in the country and Yahweh’s messenger bringing destruction across all of Yisrael’s territory. So now, tell me what answer I should take back to the one who sent me.”
[1 Chronicles] [21]:[13] “Oh, that’s very distressing,” David replied to Gad, “but please don’t let me fall into my enemies’ hands. Yahweh is very merciful, so please let him be the one to punish me directly.”
[1 Chronicles] [21]:[14] So Yahweh sent a disease throughout Yisrael, and seventy thousand Israeli men died.
[1 Chronicles] [21]:[15] Then God sent a messenger to destroy Yerushalem (Jerusalem), and while the disease was still spreading, Yahweh looked down and relented about the tragedy, and he told the destroying messenger, “Enough! Now stop what you’re doing.” Now Yahweh’s messenger happened to be standing at the threshing floor belonging to Ornan the Yevusi.
[1 Chronicles] [21]:[16] As David looked up, he saw Yahweh’s messenger standing between the earth and the heavens, holding his sword stretched out over Yerushalem. Then David and the elders, who were all dressed in sackcloth, fell to their knees and bowed their faces to the ground.
[1 Chronicles] [21]:[17] Then David asked God, “Wasn’t it me myself who said to count the people? It’s me who disobeyed and clearly did what was wrong, but these sheep, what have they done? Yahweh my god, please direct your punishment against me and my extended family, but don’t continue this deadly disease on your people.”
[1 Chronicles] [21]:[18] Then Yahweh’s messenger told Gad to tell David that he should build an altar to Yahweh at Ornan the Yevusi’s threshing floor.
[1 Chronicles] [21]:[19] So David went up to that place when he heard Gad’s message that was delivered in Yahweh’s name.
[1 Chronicles] [21]:[20] Meanwhile, Ornan was threshing wheat, and he turned and saw Yahweh’s messenger, and he and his four sons who were with him quickly hid behind something.
[1 Chronicles] [21]:[21] When David arrived there, Ornan saw him and left the threshing floor and knelt in front of David, bowing his face to the ground.
[1 Chronicles] [21]:[22] Then David asked Ornan, “Give me this place with its threshing floor, and I’ll build an altar to Yahweh on it. Sell it to me at the full price, so the deadly disease affecting the people will be stopped.”
[1 Chronicles] [21]:[23] “My master the king, take anything you want,” Ornan replied. “Listen, I’ll donate the cattle for the burnt offerings, and the threshing sledges for firewood, and the wheat for the offering—all at no charge.”
[1 Chronicles] [21]:[24] “No, I’ll most definitely pay the full price,” King David responded. “I couldn’t offer a burnt offering to Yahweh if it hadn’t cost me anything.”
[1 Chronicles] [21]:[25] So David paid Ornan six hundred gold pieces for his place,
[1 Chronicles] [21]:[26] and he built an altar to Yahweh there and offered burnt offerings and peace offerings on it. He called to Yahweh, and Yahweh answered him with fire from the heavens on that altar with the burnt offering.
[1 Chronicles] [21]:[27] Then Yahweh spoke to his messenger, who then returned his sword to his sheath.
[1 Chronicles] [21]:[28] When David saw that Yahweh had answered him at Ornan the Yevusi’s threshing floor, he sacrificed there.
[1 Chronicles] [21]:[29] At that time, Yahweh’s sacred tent that Mosheh (Moses) had made in the wilderness, and the altar for burnt sacrifices, were on a hill used for worship near Giveon city.
[1 Chronicles] [21]:[30] David wasn’t able to go there to ask God’s direction because he was terrified of Yahweh’s messenger’s sword.
[1 Chronicles] [22]:[1] Then David said, “This is now the residence of Yahweh God, and this is the altar for Yisrael’s (Israel) burnt offering.”
[1 Chronicles] [22]:[2] Then David said to gather the foreigners who lived in Yisrael (Israel), and he assigned them the job of hewing out cut stones to build the residence for God.
[1 Chronicles] [22]:[3] He prepared a large quantity of iron for the door hinges and fittings, so much brass that it couldn’t be weighed,
[1 Chronicles] [22]:[4] and innumerable cedar logs that the Tsidonim (Sidonians) and the Tsorim (Tyrians) brought in for David.
[1 Chronicles] [22]:[5] David said, “My son Shelomoh (Solomon) is young and not capable, and the house to be built for Yahweh must be impressive for the sake of his reputation and honour everywhere, so I’ll prepare for it now.” So David did a lot of preparation before he died.
[1 Chronicles] [22]:[6] Then David called for his son Shelomoh, and ordered him to build a residence for Yisrael’s god Yahweh.
[1 Chronicles] [22]:[7] David told him, “My son, I wanted to build a temple to honour my god Yahweh,
[1 Chronicles] [22]:[8] but Yahweh gave me this message, ‘You’ve fought a lot of battles and shed a large amount of blood, so you won’t be the one who’ll build a residence to honour me—you’ve shed too much blood on the ground in my sight.’
[1 Chronicles] [22]:[9] He told me, ‘Listen, you’ll have a son who’ll be a man of peace. I’ll give him relief from all his enemies from the surrounding regions. That’s why he’ll be called ‘Shelomoh’ (which sounds like ‘Shalom’—the Hebrew word for peace), and I’ll give peace and quietness to Yisrael during his lifetime.
[1 Chronicles] [22]:[10] He’ll be the one to build a residence for me, and he himself will become my son, and I’ll become his father, and I’ll establish his kingdom’s authority over Yisrael forever.’
[1 Chronicles] [22]:[11] “Now, my son, may Yahweh be with you, and may you be successful and build a residence for Yahweh your god, just as he said you would.
[1 Chronicles] [22]:[12] I also ask Yahweh to give you insight and understanding, and give you charge over Yisrael so that you can keep your god Yahweh’s regulations.
[1 Chronicles] [22]:[13] Then you’ll succeed, if you’re careful to follow the instructions and the directions that Yahweh commanded Mosheh (Moses) concerning Yisrael. Be strong and courageous. Don’t be afraid or discouraged.
[1 Chronicles] [22]:[14] Now, see, despite many battles, I’ve prepared the following for Yahweh’s residence: three thousand tonnes of gold and thirty thousand tonnes of silver, along with too much bronze and iron to weigh, and timber and cut stones. Plus you’ll be able to add more.
[1 Chronicles] [22]:[15] You’ll have plenty of skilled workers, including those who work with stone and those who work with wood.
[1 Chronicles] [22]:[16] Then there’s so many skilled with gold and silver, and bronze and iron. So get organised and get started, and may Yahweh be with you.
[1 Chronicles] [22]:[17] Then David ordered all the Israeli officials to assist his son Shelomoh (Solomon), saying,
[1 Chronicles] [22]:[18] “Isn’t Yahweh your god with you officials, and hasn’t he given you peace on every side? He’s allowed me to take control of this region, and this area has been subdued with the help of Yahweh and his people.
[1 Chronicles] [22]:[19] Now, dedicate your minds and strength to requesting advice from your god Yahweh, then get organised and build Yahweh God’s sanctuary so you can bring the box containing Yahweh’s agreement to the residence to be built to honour Yahweh’s name, and bring God’s sacred items.”
[1 Chronicles] [23]:[1] By then David was old and coming to the end of his life, and he made his son Shelomoh king of Yisrael (Israel).
[1 Chronicles] [23]:[2] Then David gathered all the Israeli officials and the priests and Levites.
[1 Chronicles] [23]:[3] Counting the Levite males that were thirty years old and older, they found there were thirty-eight thousand men.
[1 Chronicles] [23]:[4] David assigned twenty-four thousand of them to supervise the work at Yahweh’s residence, six thousand to be officials and judges,
[1 Chronicles] [23]:[5] four thousand to be gatekeepers, and four thousand to praise Yahweh using the musical instruments that he’d provided.
[1 Chronicles] [23]:[6] So David divided the Levites into divisions according to their ancestry through Levi’s sons Gereshon, Kohat, and Merari.
[1 Chronicles] [23]:[7] The Gershonim included Laedan and Shimei.
[1 Chronicles] [23]:[8] Laedan’s three sons were: Yehiel (the oldest), Zetam, and Yoel (Joel).
[1 Chronicles] [23]:[9] Shimei’s three sons were: Shelomot, Haziel, and Haran. (They were leaders of Laedan’s clans.)
[1 Chronicles] [23]:[10] Shimei’s four sons were: Yahat, Zina, Ye’ush, and Beriah.
[1 Chronicles] [23]:[11] (Yahat was the head, and Zizah was second. Ye’ush and Beriah were grouped together as one family unit because they didn’t have many descendants.)
[1 Chronicles] [23]:[12] Kohat’s four sons were: Amram, Yitshar, Hevron, and Uziel.
[1 Chronicles] [23]:[13] Amram’s sons were Aharon (Aaron) and Mosheh (Moses). Aharon and his future male descendants were permanently appointed to consecrate the most sacred things, to burn incense, to minister to Yahweh, and to bless his name.
[1 Chronicles] [23]:[14] Mosheh was known as a man who served God, and his descendants were included with the other Levites.
[1 Chronicles] [23]:[15] Mosheh’s sons were Gereshom and Eliezer.
[1 Chronicles] [23]:[16] Gereshom’s eldest son was Shevuel.
[1 Chronicles] [23]:[17] Eliezer’s only son was Rehavyah, but Rehavyah went on to have many sons.
[1 Chronicles] [23]:[18] Yitshar’s eldest son was Shelomot.
[1 Chronicles] [23]:[19] Hevron’s sons from oldest to youngest were: Yeriyah, Amaryah, Yahaziel, and Yekameam.
[1 Chronicles] [23]:[20] Uziel’s sons were Mikah and Yishiyah.
[1 Chronicles] [23]:[21] Merari’s sons were Mahli and Mushi, and Mahli’s sons were Eleazar and Kish.
[1 Chronicles] [23]:[22] Eleazar died without having any sons, so his brother Kish’s sons married his daughters (to continue the family name).
[1 Chronicles] [23]:[23] Mushi had three sons: Mahli, Eder, and Yerimot.
[1 Chronicles] [23]:[24] Those were Levi’s descendants by their clans and their appointments, who did the work of serving in Yahweh’s residence once they reached twenty years old,
[1 Chronicles] [23]:[25] because David had said, “Yisrael’s (Israel) god Yahweh has given peace to his people, and he’ll now live forever in Yerushalem (Jerusalem),
[1 Chronicles] [23]:[26] so the Levites won’t need to carry the sacred tent anymore, along with all its equipment.”
[1 Chronicles] [23]:[27] So one of David’s final instructions had been to count the Levite men who were twenty years old and over,
[1 Chronicles] [23]:[28] because their work was to assist Aharon’s (Aaron) descendants in their work in Yahweh’s residence. They were in charge of the courtyards and siderooms, in charge of the purification ceremonies, and did other work at God’s residence.
[1 Chronicles] [23]:[29] They were also in charge of the sacred bread, as well as the fine flour for the offering, the wafers of bread without raising agent, the baking pans, and all the measuring and mixing of ingredients.
[1 Chronicles] [23]:[30] Every morning and every evening the Levites stood and praised Yahweh.
[1 Chronicles] [23]:[31] They would also do that on the rest days, and at the new moon celebrations and during the other religious festivals. There were regulations about how many of them must always be on duty serving Yahweh.
[1 Chronicles] [23]:[32] They were also in charge of the sacred tent and the holy place, and assisting the priests (their relatives, Aharon’s descendants) in their service at Yahweh’s residence.
[1 Chronicles] [24]:[1] Aharon’s (Aaron) sons were: Nadav, Avihu, Eleazar, and Itamar,
[1 Chronicles] [24]:[2] but Nadav and Avihu died before their father and without having any children, so only Eleazar and Itamar became priests.
[1 Chronicles] [24]:[3] David gave Eleazar’s descendant Tsadok, and Itamar’s descendant Ahimelek two different sets of duties to perform.
[1 Chronicles] [24]:[4] There were more leaders among Eleazar’s descendants than there were among Itamar’s descendants, so they appointed sixteen leaders from Eleazar’s descendants and eight from Itamar’s descendants.

(One family from Eleazar’s group was randomly assigned a duty, and then one from Itamar’s group, and so on.)

[1 Chronicles] [25]:[1] Then David and the army chiefs allocated the musical service to the sons of Asaf, Heyman, and Yedutun—the ones prophesying with harps, with lyres, and with cymbals. This is a list of the men they chose for that work:

[1 Chronicles] [28]:[1] Now David called all of Yisrael’s (Israel) leaders to assemble in Yerushalem (Jerusalem): the tribal leaders, the leaders of the various divisions that served the king, the commanders of army units of thousands and of hundreds, and the supervisors of all the property and cattle belonging to the king and his sons, along with the top officials, and the warriors, including their powerful heroes.
[1 Chronicles] [28]:[2] Then King David stood up and spoke, “Listen to me, my brothers and my people, I wanted in my heart to put up a building for the box containing Yahweh’s agreement to rest in. It’s the footstool for our god’s feet, and I’ve made preparations to start building,
[1 Chronicles] [28]:[3] but God told me that I wouldn’t be the one to build a house to honour him, because I’ve been involved in a lot of war and killings.
[1 Chronicles] [28]:[4] “Yet Yisrael’s god Yahweh chose me from all of my father’s family to be king over Yisrael forever, because he chose a leader from the tribe of Yehudah (Judah), my father’s tribe, and among my father’s sons, he was pleased to make me king over all of Yisrael.
[1 Chronicles] [28]:[5] Then out of the many sons that he’s given me, he chose my son Shelomoh (Solomon) to be the next king to rule his kingdom of Yisrael.
[1 Chronicles] [28]:[6] “Then he told me, ‘Your son Shelomoh is the one who’ll build my temple and the courtyards around it, because I’ve chosen him to be like my son, and I’ll be like a father to him.
[1 Chronicles] [28]:[7] I’ll establish his kingdom forever, if he’s diligent at following my instructions and obeying my judgements, like he is at present.’
[1 Chronicles] [28]:[8] “So now, in front of all of Yisrael, Yahweh’s assembly, and in the hearing of our god, I challenge you all to discover and obey all of your god Yahweh’s commands, so that you’ll all possess the good land, and you’ll leave your sons after you to inherit it forever.
[1 Chronicles] [28]:[9] “And you, Shelomoh my son, follow your father’s god and serve him with a whole heart and with a willing life, because Yahweh looks into all hearts, and understands all your motives. If you look for him, he’ll make sure you find him, but if you abandon him, he’ll reject you forever.
[1 Chronicles] [28]:[10] You can now see that you need to be strong and get busy, because Yahweh has chosen you to erect a building to be his sanctuary.”
[1 Chronicles] [28]:[11] Then David gave the plans for the temple to his son Shelomoh, including plans for its porch, its houses, its treasuries, its upper rooms and its inner rooms, and the room to contain the sacred box.
[1 Chronicles] [28]:[12] He also handed over the plans he envisioned for the temple courtyards, all the surrounding apartments, all the treasuries, and all the storerooms for sacred things.
[1 Chronicles] [28]:[13] He included instructions for the divisions of the priests and Levites, for all the services required to operate the temple, and for all the equipment and utensils needed for all that.
[1 Chronicles] [28]:[14] David had determined the weight of gold and silver that would be needed to make all the necessary items that would be used in the regular temple functions,
[1 Chronicles] [28]:[15] including the gold lampstands and lamps and the silver lampstands and lamps,
[1 Chronicles] [28]:[16] and the gold for the display tables, and the silver for the silver tables.
[1 Chronicles] [28]:[17] Also the pure gold meat forks and the jugs and basins, and the weights of the gold and silver bowls.
[1 Chronicles] [28]:[18] Then the weight of refined gold for the incense altar, and for making the winged creatures that spread out across the top of the box containing Yahweh’s agreement.
[1 Chronicles] [28]:[19] He said, “I’ve written down all those plans following Yahweh’s direction, as he gave me instructions for what has to be done.”
[1 Chronicles] [28]:[20] Then David told his son Shelomoh, “Be strong and courageous, and get going. Don’t be afraid or discouraged, because Yahweh God, my god, is with you. He won’t leave you and he won’t abandon you before all the work of constructing Yahweh’s residence and the necessary equipment is finished.
[1 Chronicles] [28]:[21] Listen, the divisions of the priests and the Levites for all the work in God’s house, and all the skilled workmen, will be backing you in all the work. The officials and all the people are ready to follow your instructions.”
[1 Chronicles] [29]:[1] Then King David told the entire assembly, “My son Shelomoh (Solomon) has been chosen by God himself. He’s young and tender, and it’s a huge job, because the temple isn’t being built for people, but for Yahweh God.
[1 Chronicles] [29]:[2] I’ve used all my resources to provide a plentiful supply of materials for my god’s residence: the gold for the gold things, and the silver for the silver things, the bronze for the bronze things, the iron for the iron things, the wood for the wooden parts, onyx stones for inlays, antimony stones and colourful things, and all the rare stones, and alabaster stones.
[1 Chronicles] [29]:[3] What’s more, because I’m excited to have my god’s residence built, I’ve donated my own personal gold and silver on top of everything else that I’ve prepared for the sacred temple:
[1 Chronicles] [29]:[4] 100 tonnes of gold and 2,500 tonnes of refined silver for overlaying the buildings’ walls,
[1 Chronicles] [29]:[5] as well as gold for the gold things, silver for the silver things, and for everything the craftsmen are going to make. So who’s willing to commit themselves today to making a contribution towards Yahweh’s work?
[1 Chronicles] [29]:[6] Then the family leaders and the leaders of the tribes, and the various levels of military commanders, and the king’s construction overseers, all contributed willingly.
[1 Chronicles] [29]:[7] They donated a total of 170 tonnes of gold and 100kg of gold coins, 350 tonnes of silver, 600 tonnes of bronze, and 3,400 tonnes of iron for the temple construction,
[1 Chronicles] [29]:[8] plus anyone who had precious stones donated them to the treasury for the temple. Yehiel (a Gershoni) was in charge of those.
[1 Chronicles] [29]:[9] The people were excited, because they’d all given willingly to Yahweh, and King David was also very pleased.
[1 Chronicles] [29]:[10] Then King David blessed Yahweh in front of the entire assembly, saying, “You are blessed, Yahweh, Yisrael’s (Israel) god, our father, for all time, both past and future.
[1 Chronicles] [29]:[11] Greatness, power, beauty, splendour, and majesty all belong to you, Yahweh, as indeed does everything in the heavens and on the earth. The kingdom and supreme leadership all belong to you, Yahweh.
[1 Chronicles] [29]:[12] Wealth and prestige comes from you, and you rule over everything. You have the power and strength and control to make people great and to strengthen everyone,
[1 Chronicles] [29]:[13] so now, our god, we’re thanking you and praising your beautiful name.
[1 Chronicles] [29]:[14] But who am I, and who are my people, that we should be in a position to be able to donate freely like this? Yes, everything comes from you, and we’ve simply given back from what you gave to us,
[1 Chronicles] [29]:[15] because we’re just strangers on the earth in your eyes, and foreign guests, like all our ancestors. Our time on the earth is like a shadow without any permanence.
[1 Chronicles] [29]:[16] Yahweh our god, all this abundance that we’ve collected in order to build a house for you, for your holy name, originally came from you, and it all belongs to you anyway.
[1 Chronicles] [29]:[17] Yes I know, my god, that you examine our hearts, and you’re pleased when we do what’s right. I’ve freely offered all these gifts as I strive to do what’s right, and now I’m also happy to see your people freely offer gifts to you.
[1 Chronicles] [29]:[18] Yahweh, god of our ancestors Avraham, Yitshak (Isaac), and Yisrael, help your people continue to desire to do things like this forever, and help them remain loyal to you.
[1 Chronicles] [29]:[19] Also, give my son Shelomoh (Solomon) a sincere desire to follow your instructions, your decrees, and your regulations, and to do everything needed to build the temple following all my preparation work.”
[1 Chronicles] [29]:[20] Then David told all the assembled people, “Bless your god Yahweh,” and the entire assembly blessed Yahweh, their ancestors’ god. Then they bowed down to honour both Yahweh and the king.
[1 Chronicles] [29]:[21] Then they offered sacrifices to Yahweh, and sacrificed burnt offerings to Yahweh on the following day: 1,000 bulls, 1,000 rams, 1,000 lambs, plus their drink offerings and sacrifices for all of Yisrael in abundance.
[1 Chronicles] [29]:[22] They ate and drank in Yahweh’s honour that day with great celebration. Then they rededicated David’s son Shelomoh as king, and anointed him as leader on Yahweh’s behalf, and Tsadok as priest.
[1 Chronicles] [29]:[23] Shelomoh sat on Yahweh’s throne as king, replacing his father David, and he prospered, and all of Yisrael listened to him.
[1 Chronicles] [29]:[24] All the leaders and the mighty warriors, as well as all of King David’s sons, pledged allegiance to King Shelomoh.
[1 Chronicles] [29]:[25] Yahweh made Shelomoh exceedingly great in the eyes of all the Israelis, and bestowed a kingdom on him, the majesty of which hadn’t previously been on any king over Yisrael.
[1 Chronicles] [29]:[26] Yishay’s (Jesse) son David was the king who ruled all of Yisrael (Israel),
[1 Chronicles] [29]:[27] and he ruled for forty years: from Hevron city for seven years, and then thirty-three years from Yerushalem (Jerusalem).
[1 Chronicles] [29]:[28] He lived a long life with riches and splendour, and died at a good old age. Then his son Shelomoh (Solomon) replaced him as king.
[1 Chronicles] [29]:[29] The records of everything King David did, from the beginning to his end, were written by the prophets Shmuel (Samuel), Natan (Nathan), and Gad.
[1 Chronicles] [29]:[30] They wrote about his powerful rule, and all the things that happened to him and to the Israeli people, and in the kingdoms of other countries while he was ruling Yisrael.

[2 Chronicles] [1]:[7] That night, God appeared to Shelomoh and told him, “Ask for what you want me to give you.”
[2 Chronicles] [1]:[8] “You showed outstanding loyal commitment to my father David,” Shelomoh replied to God, “and you’ve made me king in his place.
[2 Chronicles] [1]:[9] Now, Yahweh God, may your promise to my father David be confirmed, because you yourself have made me king over a people group as numerous as the dust on the ground.
[2 Chronicles] [1]:[10] Give me wisdom and knowledge now as I come and go in front of these people, because who could make good judgements for this huge people group of yours?”
[2 Chronicles] [1]:[11] “Because that was in your heart,” God replied to Shelomoh “and you didn’t ask for wealth, riches, or fame, or the lives of those who hate you, and also you didn’t ask for a long life, but you’ve asked for wisdom and knowledge for yourself to help you lead my people that I’ve made you king over,
[2 Chronicles] [1]:[12] then I’ll give you that wisdom and knowledge, along with wealth and riches and fame. You’ll have more than any king that preceded you or any that follows.”
[2 Chronicles] [1]:[13] Then Shelomoh (Solomon) left the sacred tent at Giveon and returned to Yerushalem (Jerusalem), where he reigned over Yisrael (Israel).
[2 Chronicles] [1]:[14] Then Shelomoh built up his chariots and horsemen, and soon had 1,400 chariots and 12,000 horsemen, which he stationed in the chariot cities and with him in Yerushalem.
[2 Chronicles] [1]:[15] The king made silver and gold in Yerushalem as common as stones, and he made imported cedar timber as common as the local sycamore trees that were plentiful in the lowlands.
[2 Chronicles] [1]:[16] Shelomoh’s horses were imported from Mitsrayim (Egypt) and from the traders in Kue (in modern southern Türkiye/Turkey).
[2 Chronicles] [1]:[17] Mitsri (Egyptian) chariots cost six hundred silver coins and horses cost one hundred and fifty. (The Hiti and Aramean kings were able to get them for the same price.)

There we’ll burn spiced incense for him, plus we’ll have the regular bread display, and burnt offerings in the morning and in the evening, on rest days and on the new moons, and at Yahweh our god’s other appointed times. Yisrael (Israel) is required to do this forever.
[2 Chronicles] [2]:[5] We want to build an impressive building, because our god is more powerful than all the other gods.
[2 Chronicles] [2]:[6] But who could stay strong enough to build a house for him, since the sky and the heavens of the heavens can’t contain him? And who am I that I could build a house for him—maybe I’m good enough to burn incense for him?

[2 Chronicles] [2]:[12] Blessed be Yisrael’s god Yahweh who made the heavens and the earth, who’s given King David a wise son with insight and understanding, who’ll build a temple for Yahweh and a palace for his kingdom.

[2 Chronicles] [2]:[17] Shelomoh (Solomon) had all the foreign men living in Yisrael (Israel) counted (similar to what his father David had done), and it came to 153,600.
[2 Chronicles] [2]:[18] He conscripted seventy thousand as porters, eighty thousand as stone-cutters, and 3,600 as supervisors to keep the others working.
[2 Chronicles] [3]:[1] Then Shelomoh began to build Yahweh’s temple on Mt. Moriyah in Yerushalem (Jerusalem), where Yahweh had appeared to his father David. It was at Ornan the Yevusi’s threshing floor where David had planned for it,
[2 Chronicles] [3]:[2] and they began the construction in early-May of the fourth year of Shelomoh’s reign.
[2 Chronicles] [3]:[3] The temple foundation was twenty-seven metres long and nine metres wide,
[2 Chronicles] [3]:[4] and the nine metre long front entrance porch was nine metres high. Shelomoh overlaid the inside walls with pure gold.
[2 Chronicles] [3]:[5] For the main building, he overlaid it first with cypress planking, then with pure gold, then carved palm trees and chains along the walls.
[2 Chronicles] [3]:[6] The gold they used came from Parvayim. The main building was also overlaid with valuable gemstones.
[2 Chronicles] [3]:[7] He overlaid the temple beams, thresholds, walls, and doors with gold, and he engraved winged creatures on the walls.
[2 Chronicles] [3]:[8] Then he made the most sacred room inside the temple. It was nine metres long (the full width of the temple) and the same width. He overlaid it with thirty kilograms of pure gold (beaten into thin sheets).
[2 Chronicles] [3]:[9] Each gold nail weighed half a kilogram, and he also overlaid the upper rooms with gold.
[2 Chronicles] [3]:[10] He cast molten metal into two winged creatures in the most sacred room and overlaid them with gold.
[2 Chronicles] [3]:[11] Each of the creatures had two wings, each 2.3 metres long. One of the wings reached the temple wall, and the other wing was stretched out to touch the other creature’s wingtip,
[2 Chronicles] [3]:[12] and the same for its companion,
[2 Chronicles] [3]:[13] so the total span of the two winged creatures was nine metres. They were made standing on their feet, and placed with their faces towards the opening into the main hall.
[2 Chronicles] [3]:[14] The curtain separating the two rooms was made from fine-linen with blue, purple, and red thread, and with winged creatures embroidered onto it.
[2 Chronicles] [3]:[15] For the front of the temple he made two sixteen metre tall pillars, which each had a ‘capital’ topping that was another two metres high.
[2 Chronicles] [3]:[16] Ornamental chains were made for the inner sanctuary and to go around the tops of the pillars, and there were one hundred pomegranate models hanging on the chains.
[2 Chronicles] [3]:[17] There was one pillar on each side of the east-facing entrance—the lefthand one was named Yakin and the righthand one was named Boaz.
[2 Chronicles] [4]:[1] Then he made a square bronze altar, nine metres on each side and 4.5m high,
[2 Chronicles] [4]:[2] and he made the large round metal water tank (called ‘The Sea’), which was 4.5m in diameter and over two metres high.
[2 Chronicles] [4]:[3] Below the outer rim were two rows of small ornamental bulls spaced 45cm apart, which were part of the same casting.
[2 Chronicles] [4]:[4] Supporting ‘The Sea’ were twelve large cast bulls—facing outwards, with three facing each of the four compass points.
[2 Chronicles] [4]:[5] The sides of the tank were eight centimeters thick. The tank’s brim was fashioned like the brim of a cup, resembling a lily blossom. The tank held sixty-six thousand litres of water.
[2 Chronicles] [4]:[6] Then he made ten washbasins, placing five on each side for the priests to rinse the burnt offerings in. The priests used ‘The Sea’ to wash in.
[2 Chronicles] [4]:[7] He made the ten gold lampstands as per their design, and placed them in the temple with five on each side.
[2 Chronicles] [4]:[8] He made ten tables and also placed them in the temple with five on each side, plus he made a hundred gold basins.
[2 Chronicles] [4]:[9] He made the courtyard for the priests, as well as the large courtyard with its doors overlaid with bronze,
[2 Chronicles] [4]:[10] and he placed ‘The Sea’ in the southeast corner.
[2 Chronicles] [4]:[11] Meanwhile, Huram made the tubs and shovels (for the ashes from the altar) and other small bowls. So Huram finished the work for God’s temple that King Shelomoh (Solomon) had assigned to him:
[2 Chronicles] [4]:[12] the two pillars, the bowl-shaped capitals on top of each pillar, the two sets of latticework to cover those two capitals’ bowls,
[2 Chronicles] [4]:[13] and the four hundred pomegranates for the latticework—two rows of pomegranates to cover each of the two bowls of the capitals that decorated the tops of the pillars.
[2 Chronicles] [4]:[14] He also made the washbasins and their stands,
[2 Chronicles] [4]:[15] ‘The Sea’ and the twelve bulls that hold it up,
[2 Chronicles] [4]:[16] and the tubs and shovels, the forks, and other utensils. Those were all items made of polished bronze that Huram-Avi made for King Shelomoh for Yahweh’s temple.
[2 Chronicles] [4]:[17] The king had them cast in the clay between Sukot and Tseredah down by the Yarden (Jordan) River.
[2 Chronicles] [4]:[18] Shelomoh had so many items made that they didn’t even try to weigh all the bronze.
[2 Chronicles] [4]:[19] Shelomoh had all the items for God’s temple made, including the gold altar and the tables for displaying the sacred bread,
[2 Chronicles] [4]:[20] the pure gold lampstands and their lamps for the inner sanctuary according to their designs,
[2 Chronicles] [4]:[21] the pure gold flower ornaments, lamps, tongs,
[2 Chronicles] [4]:[22] the pure gold lamp trimmers, the basins and spoons, and the fire pans. Also the temple entrance, its inner doors into the very sacred room, and the outer temple doors were all gold.
[2 Chronicles] [5]:[1] After all the work which Shelomoh did for Yahweh’s temple was completed, Shelomoh brought in his father David’s sacred things. He put the gold and silver, and all the other items, in the temple treasuries.
[2 Chronicles] [5]:[2] Then Shelomoh (Solomon) assembled the Israeli elders, and all the heads of the tribes, the Israeli clan leaders, in Yerushalem (Jerusalem), to bring the box containing Yahweh’s agreement up the hill from the city of David, that is, Tsiyon (Zion).
[2 Chronicles] [5]:[3] So in October, all those Israeli leaders gathered to be with the king for a feast,
[2 Chronicles] [5]:[4] and once everyone was there, the Levites lifted up the sacred box
[2 Chronicles] [5]:[5] and carried it up towards the temple. The priests (who are also Levites) carried it, along with the sacred tent and everything that had been in it.
[2 Chronicles] [5]:[6] Then King Shelomoh, and all the assembled Israelis with him, gathered in front of the box, sacrificing sheep and cattle which were too many to count.
[2 Chronicles] [5]:[7] The priests then took the box containing Yahweh’s agreement in to its place in the house’s inner room (the holiest place)—to under the winged creatures,
[2 Chronicles] [5]:[8] whose outstretched wings would now be over the sacred box and even over the top of its carrying poles.
[2 Chronicles] [5]:[9] Those long poles stuck out and could be seen from the front of that inner room, but couldn’t be seen from the main room, and they’re still there to this day.
[2 Chronicles] [5]:[10] There was nothing in the box except the two stone tablets that Mosheh (Moses) had put in at Horev, which represented the agreement that Yahweh had made with the Israelis after they’d left Mitsrayim (Egypt).
[2 Chronicles] [5]:[11] Then the priests left the holy place in the temple. All the priests who were there consecrated themselves to do the priestly duties, irrespective of which division they were part of.
[2 Chronicles] [5]:[12] All the Levites who were singers (Asaf, Heyman, Yedutun, and their sons and their brothers) stood on the east side of the altar. They were dressed in fine linen, and had cymbals, and harps and lyres, along with 120 priests playing trumpets.
[2 Chronicles] [5]:[13] The trumpeters and singers performed together to praise and thank Yahweh, with the trumpets and cymbals on the highlights of the song to praise Yahweh: “Yahweh is good to us, because his loyal commitment continues forever.” Then Yahweh’s temple filled with a cloud,
[2 Chronicles] [5]:[14] and the priests weren’t able to stay on their feet and continue ministering, because Yahweh’s brilliance had filled the temple.
[2 Chronicles] [6]:[1] Then Shelomoh (Solomon) prayed, “Yahweh, you said that you would live in a dark cloud,
[2 Chronicles] [6]:[2] but I’ve built a beautiful residence for you—a place for you to live in forever.”
[2 Chronicles] [6]:[3] Then, while all the people stood there, Shelomoh turned toward them and spoke a blessing over them,
[2 Chronicles] [6]:[4] saying, “Yahweh, Yisrael’s (Israel) god, is blessed, who spoke physically to my father David, and then caused it to actually happen, when he said back then,
[2 Chronicles] [6]:[5] ‘When I brought my people out of Mitsrayim (Egypt), I hadn’t chosen a city from all of Yisrael’s tribes as a place to build a house so my name could be there. Nor had I chosen a man to be leader over my people, Yisrael,
[2 Chronicles] [6]:[6] but now I’ve chosen Yerushalem (Jerusalem) to be my place of residence, and I’ve chosen you, David, to be over my people, Yisrael.’
[2 Chronicles] [6]:[7] “My father David wanted to build a temple for Yisrael’s god Yahweh,
[2 Chronicles] [6]:[8] but Yahweh told him, ‘It’s good that you wanted to build a house to honour me,
[2 Chronicles] [6]:[9] but you won’t be the one to build it. It’ll be your own biological son who’ll build the temple to honour my reputation.’
[2 Chronicles] [6]:[10] “Now Yahweh has fulfilled what he said, and I’m here sitting on Yisrael’s throne instead of my father David, just as Yahweh said, and I’ve had this temple built to honour Yisrael’s god Yahweh.
[2 Chronicles] [6]:[11] I’ve placed the sacred box in there—the box that contains the agreement Yahweh made with Yisrael’s descendants.”
[2 Chronicles] [6]:[12] Then Shelomoh (Solomon) stood in front of the altar to Yahweh in front of all the assembled Israelis, and spread out his hands,
[2 Chronicles] [6]:[13] because he’d made a bronze platform and had it placed in the centre of the courtyard. The square platform was just over two metres on each side, and stood just over a metre off the ground. Firstly he stood on it, then he knelt down in front of all the assembled Israelis and spread his hands out to the sky
[2 Chronicles] [6]:[14] and said, “Yahweh, Yisrael’s (Israel) god, there isn’t any god like you in the heavens or on the earth—one who keeps his agreement and shows loyal commitment to your servants who are walking with total integrity as you watch them.
[2 Chronicles] [6]:[15] Everything you verbally told my father David that you’d do, you’ve used your power to make it all happen, including this today.
[2 Chronicles] [6]:[16] And now, Yahweh, Yisrael’s god, keep another promise you made to your servant David my father, when you told him, ‘There’ll always be one of your descendants sitting on Yisrael’s throne, as long as they obey my instructions just like you have.’
[2 Chronicles] [6]:[17] So now, Yahweh, Yisrael’s god, may what you said to your servant, to David, be confirmed.
[2 Chronicles] [6]:[18] “But will God really live with humans here on the earth? Wow, the skies and the heavens of the heavens can’t contain you—how much less this house that I’ve built.
[2 Chronicles] [6]:[19] Nevertheless Yahweh my god, listen to your servant’s prayer and request and take notice.
[2 Chronicles] [6]:[20] Watch over this building where you said you’d be present, and hear my prayers when your servant prays towards this place.
[2 Chronicles] [6]:[21] Listen to what your servant and your Israeli people are requesting when they pray towards this place. Listen from where you live in the heavens, and hear and forgive.
[2 Chronicles] [6]:[22] “If someone is accused of wronging their neighbour, and is forced to make a sworn statement in front of your altar in this temple,
[2 Chronicles] [6]:[23] then listen from the heavens and decide who’s telling the truth. Then punish the guilty party as they deserve, and do good to the other side as a reward for their innocence.
[2 Chronicles] [6]:[24] “And if your Israeli people are defeated by their enemies because they’ve disobeyed you, but they return to you and confess, and pray, and in this place they request your favour,
[2 Chronicles] [6]:[25] then listen to them from the heavens and forgive your Israeli people’s disobedience, and bring them back to this land that you gave to their ancestors and to them.
[2 Chronicles] [6]:[26] “When the clouds hold back and give no rain because your Israeli people have disobeyed you, but then they pray towards this place and acknowledge you and turn away from their disobedience because you’ve punished them,
[2 Chronicles] [6]:[27] then listen to them from the heavens and forgive the disobedience of your servants and your Israeli people. Teach them the right way to live their lives, and give rain to your land which you gave your people as a permanent inheritance.
[2 Chronicles] [6]:[28] “If this land suffers from famine, or if there’s blight or mildew, or locusts or grasshoppers, deadly diseases or sickness, or if an enemy army surrounds them,
[2 Chronicles] [6]:[29] then if any person, or all your Israeli people, stretch out their hands towards this temple with their prayers and requests because they each acknowledge their individual pain and suffering,
[2 Chronicles] [6]:[30] then listen to them from where you live there in the heavens, and forgive them. Reward each person according to their behaviour, because you know people’s motives—only you know what’s in people’s minds.
[2 Chronicles] [6]:[31] Do that so they’ll respect you and live how you want them to, as they live in this country that you gave to our ancestors.
[2 Chronicles] [6]:[32] “Also, any foreigners who don’t belong to your Israeli people, who come to this land because they’ve heard that you’re very great and powerful, if they turn toward this temple and pray,
[2 Chronicles] [6]:[33] then listen to them as well from where you live there in the heavens. Do whatever that foreigner requests from you, so that all the people groups in the world will learn about your reputation, and honour and obey you like your Israeli people do, and know that this temple that I’ve built is called by your name.
[2 Chronicles] [6]:[34] “When you send your people off to battle their enemies, and they pray towards this city that you’ve chosen and this temple that I’ve had built to honour your name,
[2 Chronicles] [6]:[35] then listen from the heavens to their prayer and their requests, and uphold their cause.
[2 Chronicles] [6]:[36] “When they disobey you (and there’s no one who doesn’t), and you’re angry with them and allow an enemy to get the upper hand, and their captors take them to a distant or nearby land as captives,
[2 Chronicles] [6]:[37] and then in that land where they’re captives, they turn and admit their wickedness and their disobedience, and request your favour,
[2 Chronicles] [6]:[38] and they turn to you with total sincerity in that other country, and pray towards the land that you gave their ancestors, and the city that you chose, and toward the temple that I’ve built to honour your name,
[2 Chronicles] [6]:[39] then listen from where you live in the heavens to their prayer and their requests, and uphold their cause and forgive your people who’ve disobeyed you.
[2 Chronicles] [6]:[40] “Now my god, please let your eyes be open and your ears attentive to prayers offered towards this place.
