[2 Chronicles] [6]:[41] “So now Yahweh God, along with the sacred box representing your strength, come and enter your place for resting. Yahweh God, may your priests be dressed in your rescue, and your faithful ones enjoy your goodness.
[2 Chronicles] [6]:[42] Yahweh God, don’t ignore those who you’ve chosen. Remember your servant David’s loyal commitment.”
[2 Chronicles] [7]:[1] When Shelomoh (Solomon) finished praying, fire came down from the skies and consumed the burnt offering and the sacrifices, and Yahweh’s brilliant light filled the temple.
[2 Chronicles] [7]:[2] The priests weren’t able to go into Yahweh’s temple because of Yahweh’s brilliant light,
[2 Chronicles] [7]:[3] and when all the Israelis saw the fire come down and saw the bright light above the temple, they fell to their knees with their faces bowed down low to the stone pavement, and worshipped and thanked Yahweh, saying, “He’s certainly good—his loyal commitment really will continue forever.”
[2 Chronicles] [7]:[4] Then the king and all the people offered sacrifices to Yahweh—
[2 Chronicles] [7]:[5] King Shelomoh sacrificed twenty-two thousand cattle and one hundred and twenty thousand sheep, and so the king and all the people dedicated God’s temple.
[2 Chronicles] [7]:[6] The priests were standing in their positions, as well as the Levites with the instruments King David had made to give thanks to Yahweh. When they assisted David in praising Yahweh, they would sing, “Yes, his loyal commitment continues forever,” and the priests would blow their trumpets in front of them as all the Israelis stood there.
[2 Chronicles] [7]:[7] Then Shelomoh consecrated the middle of the courtyard in front of Yahweh’s temple building so he could offer burnt offerings and the fat of the peace offerings there, because the bronze altar that he’d made wasn’t able to handle the large number of burnt offerings and grain offerings, and the fats.
[2 Chronicles] [7]:[8] Then Shelomoh and all of Yisrael (Israel) feasted for the next seven days—the huge gathering spread from Levo-Hamat in the far north, all the way to the Mitsri (Egyptian) riverbed in the far south.
[2 Chronicles] [7]:[9] On the eighth day, they had a solemn service, because they’d observed seven days of celebration for the altar with seven days of feasting.
[2 Chronicles] [7]:[10] Finally, after some three weeks, Shelomoh sent the people home—they were cheery and encouraged because of the goodness Yahweh had displayed to David and Shelomoh, and to his Israeli people.
[2 Chronicles] [7]:[11] So Shelomoh (Solomon) finished Yahweh’s temple and the king’s palace—he’d succeeded in implementing everything he’d envisaged.
[2 Chronicles] [7]:[12] One night, Yahweh appeared to Shelomoh in a dream and told him, “I’ve heard your prayer, and I’ve chosen this temple to be the place where my people will offer sacrifices to me.
[2 Chronicles] [7]:[13] If I restrain the skies so there’s no rain, or if I command locusts to devour the land, or if I send disease among my people,
[2 Chronicles] [7]:[14] then if my people who are known by my name humble themselves and pray, and request my help and turn away from their evil customs, then I myself will hear them from the heavens, and I’ll forgive their sin and heal their land.
[2 Chronicles] [7]:[15] My eyes will be open and my ears will be attentive to prayers offered towards this place,
[2 Chronicles] [7]:[16] as I’ve chosen and consecrated this temple to be associated with my name forever—I’ll be permanently present there.
[2 Chronicles] [7]:[17] Also, if you’ll obey me like your father David did, and do everything that I’ve instructed you, and keep my rules and regulations,
[2 Chronicles] [7]:[18] then I’ll ensure that your descendants rule your kingdom, just as I promised your father David when I said, ‘You won’t fail to have one of your descendants ruling over Yisrael (Israel).’
[2 Chronicles] [7]:[19] However, if you collectively turn away, and abandon my rules and instructions that I gave you, and decide to serve other gods and worship them,
[2 Chronicles] [7]:[20] then I’ll remove these people from my land that I gave them. Also this temple that I consecrated for myself, I’ll throw it away where I can’t see it, and I’ll make it an object of scorn and ridicule among all the other nations.
[2 Chronicles] [7]:[21] Then this temple, which everyone admires as they pass by, will be devastated, and people will ask, ‘Why did Yahweh do such terrible things to that temple and to that land?’
[2 Chronicles] [7]:[22] ‘It happened because they abandoned Yahweh, their ancestors’ god,’ others will reply. ‘He brought them out from slavery in Mitsrayim (Egypt), but then they obtained other gods and worshipped them and served them—that’s why he sent them all this misery.’ ”
[2 Chronicles] [8]:[1] After the twenty years that it took Shelomoh (Solomon) to build Yahweh’s temple and his palace,
[2 Chronicles] [8]:[2] he rebuilt the cities that King Huram had given to him, and he got Israelis to live in them.
[2 Chronicles] [8]:[3] Then Shelomoh attacked Hamat-Tsovah and captured it.
[2 Chronicles] [8]:[4] He rebuilt Tadmor in the wilderness, and storage cities in the Hamat region.
[2 Chronicles] [8]:[5] He rebuilt the fortified cities of Upper Beyt-Horon and Lower Beyt-Horon with walls and barred gates,
[2 Chronicles] [8]:[6] as well as Ba’alat and all the storage cities, and all the cities for Shelomoh’s chariots and horsemen that he wanted to build in Yerushalem (Jerusalem) and Levanon, and throughout his kingdom.
[2 Chronicles] [8]:[7] All the people who lived in Yisrael (Israel) but who were actually remnants of the Hitim, Amorim, Perizim, Hivim, and Yevusim,
[2 Chronicles] [8]:[8] who were descendants of groups that the Israelis hadn’t completely destroyed, were forced to become Shelomoh’s labourers, and they still continue in that role.
[2 Chronicles] [8]:[9] However, Shelomoh didn’t make the Israelis become labourers, because they became his soldiers, officers, chariot commanders, and horsemen.
[2 Chronicles] [8]:[10] Some 250 Israelis were also King Shelomoh’s chief officials who had authority over the people.
[2 Chronicles] [8]:[11] Shelomoh brought his wife, Par’oh’s (Pharaoh) daughter, up from the city of David to the house he’d built for her, because he said, “My wife mustn’t live in the palace of Yisrael’s King David, because the places where Yahweh’s box has been are sacred.”
[2 Chronicles] [8]:[12] Then Shelomoh sacrificed burnt offerings to Yahweh on the altar that had been built in front of the temple’s porch.
[2 Chronicles] [8]:[13] He followed Mosheh’s (Moses) instructions about the daily sacrifices for the rest days and the new moons, and for the three appointed occasions each year: the Festival of Flat Bread, the Harvest Festival, and the Celebration Living in Shelters.
[2 Chronicles] [8]:[14] Then, as his father David had instructed, he assigned the priests to divisions for their various tasks, and the Levites who would praise and minister in front of the priests and help in their daily tasks, and gatekeepers in their divisions at the various gates. All that was what David, the man of God, had commanded.
[2 Chronicles] [8]:[15] The priests and Levites followed the king’s instructions concerning all their duties, as well as their supervision of the treasuries.
[2 Chronicles] [8]:[16] So now, all of Shelomoh’s work on Yahweh’s temple was completed—from the foundation through to its completion and operation.
[2 Chronicles] [8]:[17] Then Shelomoh went to Etsyon-Gever and to Eylot on the edge of the ocean, in the Edom region.
[2 Chronicles] [8]:[18] King Huram (from Tsor (Tyre) ) sent ships to him, as his servants knew the sea well. Then Shelomoh’s men boarded the ships and sailed with them to Ofir, where they obtained fifteen tonnes of gold and brought it back to King Shelomoh.
[2 Chronicles] [9]:[1] The queen from the Sheva region had heard all about Shelomoh (Solomon), and she came to Yerushalem (Jerusalem) with some hard questions. Her party included a large number of camels carrying lots of spices and gold and valuable gemstones. She came to Shelomoh and discussed with him everything that was on her mind.
[2 Chronicles] [9]:[2] Shelomoh responded to all her queries, and there wasn’t any subject that he wasn’t able to speak about.
[2 Chronicles] [9]:[3] When the queen from Sheva saw Shelomoh’s wisdom, and saw the palace that he’d built
[2 Chronicles] [9]:[4] and the food at his table, as well as his servants’ stations, his well-dressed ministers standing by, his cup-bearers in their uniforms, and the burnt offerings that he sacrificed at Yahweh’s temple, it took her breath away
[2 Chronicles] [9]:[5] and she told the king, “Everything I heard in my own country about you and your wisdom was true.
[2 Chronicles] [9]:[6] I didn’t believe what they reported to me until I saw it with my own eyes, and wow, the reports I heard didn’t even cover half the extent of your wisdom!
[2 Chronicles] [9]:[7] Your men are blessed, and even your servants are blessed to be able to continually stand in front of you and listen to your wisdom.
[2 Chronicles] [9]:[8] Your god Yahweh ought to be blessed—the one who delighted in you and placed you on his throne as his king. Your god loved Yisrael (Israel) and wanted to establish them forever, so he’s placed you over them as king—to give justice and do what’s right.”
[2 Chronicles] [9]:[9] Then she gave the king four tonnes of gold, a very large quantity of spices, and valuable gemstones. Nobody before had ever seen such a large amount of spices as what the queen from Sheva gave to King Shelomoh.
[2 Chronicles] [9]:[10] (Also, King Huram’s servants working together with Shelomoh’s servants brought gold from Ofir, as well as algum wood and valuable gemstones.
[2 Chronicles] [9]:[11] The king made the algum wood into staircases for Yahweh’s temple and for the king’s palace, and into lyres and harps for the singers. Nothing like that had been seen before in Yehudah (Judah).)
[2 Chronicles] [9]:[12] King Shelomoh gave the queen from Sheva everything she wanted—more than what she’d brought to the king. Then she departed with her servants and went back to her country.
[2 Chronicles] [9]:[13] In one year, Shelomoh (Solomon) received about twenty tonnes of gold,
[2 Chronicles] [9]:[14] as well as what the merchants and traders brought in. All the Aravi kings and all the local governors brought gold and silver to Shelomoh.
[2 Chronicles] [9]:[15] King Shelomoh made two hundred large shields of beaten gold—six hundred gold coins’ worth of beaten gold went into each shield.
[2 Chronicles] [9]:[16] Also, three hundred smaller shields—three hundred gold coins’ worth of beaten gold went into each shield.
[2 Chronicles] [9]:[17] Then the king made a large ivory throne and overlaid it with pure gold.
[2 Chronicles] [9]:[18] There were six steps leading up to the throne, and a gold footstool was attached to it. It had an armrest on each side, with a lion statue beside each armrest.
[2 Chronicles] [9]:[19] There were twelve statues of lions standing on the six steps—one at each end of each step. No throne like that existed in any other kingdom.
[2 Chronicles] [9]:[20] All of King Shelomoh’s cups were made of gold, and all the various dishes in ‘The House of the Levanon Forest’ were refined gold. Nothing was made of silver, because during Shelomoh’s reign, silver wasn’t considered valuable,
[2 Chronicles] [9]:[21] because the king’s ships went to Tarshish with Huram’s servants. Every three years the fleet would bring back gold, silver, ivory, and apes and baboons,
[2 Chronicles] [9]:[22] so King Shelomoh became greater than all the other kings in the world, both in wealth and in wisdom.
[2 Chronicles] [9]:[23] Kings from all over the world wanted to come and listen to the wisdom that God had given Shelomoh.
[2 Chronicles] [9]:[24] Each of them would bring gifts: gold and silver items, clothes, myrrh and spices, horses and mules. (This continued year after year.)
[2 Chronicles] [9]:[25] Shelomoh had four thousand stalls for horses and chariots, and twelve thousand horsemen, and he kept some in the chariot cities and some close by in Yerushalem (Jerusalem).
[2 Chronicles] [9]:[26] He ended up ruling over all the kings in the region, from the Perat (Euphrates) River in the northeast, west to the area of the Pelishtim, and south down to the Mitsri (Egyptian) border.
[2 Chronicles] [9]:[27] The king made silver as common as stones, and cedar timber as common as the sycamore fig trees in the lowlands.
[2 Chronicles] [9]:[28] Horses were brought in from Mitsrayim (Egypt) for Shelomoh, and from other countries as well.
[2 Chronicles] [9]:[29] Everything else that Shelomoh (Solomon) did, from the beginning to the end, was written down by the prophet Natan (Nathan), and in the prophecy by Ahiyah (from Shiloh), and the prophet Ido’s visions about Nevat’s son Yarov’am (Jeroboam) were also written down.
[2 Chronicles] [9]:[30] Shelomoh reigned from Yerushalem (Jerusalem) over all of Yisrael (Israel) for forty years,
[2 Chronicles] [9]:[31] then he died and was buried with his father in ‘The City of David’, and his son Rehav’am (Rehoboam) replaced him as king.
[2 Chronicles] [10]:[1] Then Rehav’am (Rehoboam) went to Shekem, where all of Yisrael (Israel) had gathered for his coronation.
[2 Chronicles] [10]:[2] Meanwhile, Nevat’s son Yarov’am (Jeroboam) had fled from King Shelomoh (Solomon) and was down in Mitsrayim (Egypt), but when he heard about the coming coronation, he returned from Mitsrayim.
[2 Chronicles] [10]:[3] So the leaders of the northern tribes summoned Yarov’am, and he went with them to speak to Shelomoh’s son Rehav’am and all of Yisrael, saying,
[2 Chronicles] [10]:[4] “Your father made us work very hard, but now, lighten the demands that your father made on us, and we’ll serve you.”
[2 Chronicles] [10]:[5] “Come back to me in three days.” Rehav’am answered, so the people departed.
[2 Chronicles] [10]:[6] Then King Rehav’am consulted with the older men who’d advised his father Shelomoh when he was still alive, asking them, “How do you advise me to answer the people?”
[2 Chronicles] [10]:[7] “If you’re good to those people and do things that please them, and speak kindly to them,” they answered, “then they’ll serve you for a long time to come.”
[2 Chronicles] [10]:[8] However, Rehav’am rejected their advice, and consulted some of the young men there who’d grown up with him.
[2 Chronicles] [10]:[9] “How would you guys suggest I answer the people who’ve asked me to lighten the burden on them, compared to my father’s time?”
[2 Chronicles] [10]:[10] “Those people tell you that your father was hard on them and that you should lighten their load,” his contemporaries advised him. “But you should tell them that your little finger is thicker than your father’s waist,
[2 Chronicles] [10]:[11] and that whereas he required them to contribute, you’ll be even more demanding. Tell them that he might have whipped them with leather whips, but that you’ll whip them with scorpions!”
[2 Chronicles] [10]:[12] So Yarov’am (Jeroboam) and all the people returned to King Rehav’am on the third day as he’d prearranged,
[2 Chronicles] [10]:[13] and ignoring the advice of the older men, the king answered the people harshly.
[2 Chronicles] [10]:[14] He passed on the younger men’s suggestion, telling the people, “I’ll make your burden even heavier. My father rebuked you people with whips, but I’ll do it with scorpions.”
[2 Chronicles] [10]:[15] So the king took no notice of the people’s request, because it was God turning events around, so that what Yahweh had said to Yarov’am (Nevat’s son) through Ahiyah (from Shiloh) would come to pass.
[2 Chronicles] [10]:[16] When all the Israelis saw that the king hadn’t listened to them, the people from the northern tribes answered the king, “What did David have to do with us anyway? We had nothing to gain from Yishay’s (Jesse) son. You might as well all head home, and then they’ll see what happened to David’s dynasty.” So they all went home,
[2 Chronicles] [10]:[17] and Rehav’am ended up only ruling over the Israelis living in the Yehudah (Judah) region.
[2 Chronicles] [10]:[18] King Rehav’am (still in Shekem) sent out Hadoram, his supervisor of the forced labourers, but the Israelis hurled stones at him and killed him. When he heard about that, King Rehav’am forced his way into his chariot and escaped to Yerushalem (Jerusalem),
[2 Chronicles] [10]:[19] and northern Yisrael (Israel) has rebelled against David’s descendants to this day.
[2 Chronicles] [11]:[1] When Rehav’am (Rehoboam) arrived in Yerushalem (Jerusalem), he assembled Yehudah’s (Judah) and Benyamin’s warriors: 180,000 chosen to fight against Yisrael (Israel) to bring the kingdom back to Rehav’am.
[2 Chronicles] [11]:[2] But Yahweh spoke to the prophet Shemayah, saying,
[2 Chronicles] [11]:[3] “Go and tell this to Shelomoh’s (Solomon) son King Rehav’am of Yehudah, and to all the Israeli people from the Yehudah and Benyamin tribes:
[2 Chronicles] [11]:[4] Yahweh says that you mustn’t go and fight with your relatives. Everyone should just go home again, because everything that’s happened came from me.” So they listened to the message from Yahweh, and called off the planned attack against Yarov’am (Jeroboam).
[2 Chronicles] [11]:[5] So Rehav’am (Rehoboam) lived in Yerushalem (Jerusalem) and fortified the cities throughout Yehudah (Judah):
[2 Chronicles] [11]:[6] Beyt-Lehem (Bethlehem), Eytam, Tekoa,
[2 Chronicles] [11]:[7] Beyt-Tsur, Sokoh, Adulam,
[2 Chronicles] [11]:[8] Gat, Mareshah, Zif,
[2 Chronicles] [11]:[9] Adorayim, Lakish, Azekah,
[2 Chronicles] [11]:[10] Tsor’ah, Ayalon, and Hevron (all in Yehudah and Benyamin).
[2 Chronicles] [11]:[11] He strengthened the fortifications in those cities and towns, appointed an army commander, and stocked their storehouses with food and oil and wine.
[2 Chronicles] [11]:[12] He also equipped each of them with shields and spears, and made sure they were well-protected. So Yehudah and Benyamin were under his control.
[2 Chronicles] [11]:[13] The priests and Levites throughout all of Yisrael (Israel) supported Rehav’am (Rehoboam) from every part of the country.
[2 Chronicles] [11]:[14] The Levites abandoned their property and their pastureland and moved to Yerushalem (Jerusalem) and across the rest of Yehudah (Judah), because Yarov’am (Jeroboam) and his sons stopped them from serving as Yahweh’s priests.
[2 Chronicles] [11]:[15] Instead Yarov’am established his own priests for his hilltop shrines and for the goat and calf idols that he’d made.
[2 Chronicles] [11]:[16] As well as the priests and Levites, people from all the Israeli tribes who wanted to serve Yisrael’s god Yahweh came to Yerushalem to sacrifice to Yahweh, their ancestors’ god.
[2 Chronicles] [11]:[17] So they strengthened the kingdom of Yehudah, and as the people followed David’s and Shelomoh’s (Solomon) examples, they strengthened Rehav’am’s rule for three years.
[2 Chronicles] [11]:[18] Rehav’am (Rehoboam) married Mahalat. She was the daughter of David’s son Yerimot, and her mother was Avihayil, the daughter of Eliav and granddaughter of Yishay (Jesse).
[2 Chronicles] [11]:[19] They had three sons: Ye’ush, Shemaryah, and Zaham.
[2 Chronicles] [11]:[20] After her, he married Avshalom’s (Absalom) daughter Ma’akah, and they had four sons: Aviyah, Atay, Ziza, and Shelomit.
[2 Chronicles] [11]:[21] Rehav’am loved Ma’akah the most out of his eighteen wives and sixty slave-wives. He fathered twenty-eight sons and sixty daughters,
[2 Chronicles] [11]:[22] but he appointed Ma’akah’s son Aviyah to be the leader of his older and younger brothers, because that would mark him as the future king.
[2 Chronicles] [11]:[23] He wisely sent his other sons to fortified cities across all the regions in Yehudah (Judah) and Benyamin, where he set them up generously and asked the local people to give them wives.
[2 Chronicles] [12]:[1] However, after Rehav’am (Rehoboam) had become established and in firm control of his kingdom, he and all the people abandoned Yahweh’s instructions.
[2 Chronicles] [12]:[2] Because they were unfaithful to Yahweh, King Shishak from Mitsrayim (Egypt) came to attack Yerushalem (Jerusalem) in the fifth year of Rehav’am’s reign,
[2 Chronicles] [12]:[3] with 1,200 chariots and sixty thousand horsemen, along with a huge number of troops, including Mitsrim (Egyptians), Luvim (Libyans), Sukim, and Kushim.
[2 Chronicles] [12]:[4] He captured Yehudah’s (Judah) fortified cities, then moved towards Yerushalem.
[2 Chronicles] [12]:[5] Then the prophet Shemayah and the leaders of Yehudah who’d fled to Yerushalem because of Shishak’s attacks came to Rehav’am. Shemayah told them, “Yahweh says that it was you people who abandoned me, so now I’ve also abandoned you to be defeated by Shishak.”
[2 Chronicles] [12]:[6] Then the king and the Israeli leaders humbled themselves and said, “Yahweh always does what’s right and fair.”
[2 Chronicles] [12]:[7] When Yahweh saw that they’d humbled themselves, he gave this message to Shemayah, “They’ve humbled themselves, so I won’t destroy them—my rage won’t pour out on Yerushalem through Shishak’s attack, and I’ll give them a way to recover in the future.
[2 Chronicles] [12]:[8] Nevertheless, they’ll become his servants, and they’ll learn the difference between serving me versus serving other nations’ kings.
[2 Chronicles] [12]:[9] When Mitsrayim’s (Egypt) King Shishak invaded Yerushalem, he took the treasures from Yahweh’s temple and the king’s palace. He took everything valuable, including the gold shields that Shelomoh (Solomon) had made.
[2 Chronicles] [12]:[10] King Rehav’am replaced them with bronze shields, and distributed them to the leaders of the people who guarded the entrance to the king’s palace.
[2 Chronicles] [12]:[11] After that, whenever the king went to Yahweh’s temple, the guards went with him carrying those bronze shields. Then when the king left again, they’d return them to the guardroom.
[2 Chronicles] [12]:[12] Because Rehav’am humbled himself, Yahweh stopped being angry with him and didn’t eliminate him, so things were reasonably good in Yehudah (Judah).
[2 Chronicles] [12]:[13] King Rehav’am consolidated his rule in Yerushalem. He reigned for a total of forty-one years—seventeen of which were from Yerushalem city, which Yahweh had chosen from all the tribes in Yisrael (Israel) as the place to establish his reputation. (Rehav’am’s mother was the Amonit, Na’amah.)
[2 Chronicles] [12]:[14] Rehav’am did evil things because he didn’t make it his priority to get direction from Yahweh.
[2 Chronicles] [12]:[15] The account of everything Rehav’am did while he was king, including genealogical records, was recorded in the scrolls written by the prophets Shemayah and Ido. Rehav’am and Yarov’am (Jeroboam) were at war with each other for his entire reign.
[2 Chronicles] [12]:[16] Then Rehav’am died, he was buried with his ancestors in ‘The City of David’, and his son Aviyah replaced him as king.
[2 Chronicles] [13]:[1] In the eighteenth year of King Yarov’am’s (Jeroboam) reign, Aviyah started his reign over Yehudah (Judah).
[2 Chronicles] [13]:[2] He ruled from Yerushalem (Jerusalem) for three years. (His mother was Uriel’s daughter Mikayah from Giveah.) However, war started between Aviyah and Yarov’am.
[2 Chronicles] [13]:[3] Aviyah launched the attack with four-hundred thousand strong warriors, and Yarov’am drew up in formation against him with eight-hundred thousand strong warriors in his army.
[2 Chronicles] [13]:[4] Aviyah stood on the top of Mt. Tsemarayim in the Efrayim (Ephraim) hill-country and shouted, “Yarov’am and all of Yisrael (Israel), listen to me.
[2 Chronicles] [13]:[5] Don’t you all understand that Yisrael’s god Yahweh made a formal agreement that the kingdom of Yisrael was given forever to David and his descendants?
[2 Chronicles] [13]:[6] But Nevat’s son Yarov’am, who was a servant of David’s son Shelomoh (Solomon), took action and rebelled against his master,
[2 Chronicles] [13]:[7] and a bunch of wicked good-for-nothings gathered around Yarov’am and created a force against Shelomoh’s son, Rehav’am (Rehoboam), when Rehav’am was still an inexperienced, young man and couldn’t stand up to them.
[2 Chronicles] [13]:[8] So now you Israelis are saying that you’ll stand against the kingdom that Yahweh established through David’s descendants. There are certainly many of you, and you have the gold calves that Yarov’am made as gods for you.
[2 Chronicles] [13]:[9] Didn’t you people drive out the Levites, as well as Yahweh’s priests who were Aharon’s (Aaron) descendants? Then you appointed for yourselves ‘priests’ like they have in other countries, so that anyone who comes to consecrate himself by bringing a young bull from the herd and seven rams can become a ‘priest’ of your non-gods.
[2 Chronicles] [13]:[10] “But as for us, Yahweh is our god and we haven’t abandoned him. Our priests who minister to Yahweh are Aharon’s descendants, and the Levites assist them.
[2 Chronicles] [13]:[11] Every morning and every evening, they sacrifice burnt offerings to Yahweh, and spiced incense. There’s sacred bread on the display table, and the lamps in the gold lampstand give light every evening because we’re following our god Yahweh’s instructions, but you people have abandoned him.
[2 Chronicles] [13]:[12] So listen! God is guiding us, and his priests will blast their trumpets to signal battle against you people. Listen, you Israelis: don’t fight against Yahweh, your ancestors’ god, because you won’t succeed.”
[2 Chronicles] [13]:[13] But meanwhile, Yarov’am had sent some men around to ambush them from behind, so they were both in front of the army from Yehudah (Judah) and in ambush behind them.
[2 Chronicles] [13]:[14] When the warriors from Yehudah turned, wow, they realised they were being attacked from in front and from behind. They called out to Yahweh for help while the priests blew their trumpets.
[2 Chronicles] [13]:[15] Then the men from Yehudah shouted a loud battle cry, and God defeated Yarov’am and all of Yisrael in front of Aviyah and Yehudah.
[2 Chronicles] [13]:[16] Yisrael’s soldiers fled away from Yehudah’s army, and God enabled Yehudah to defeat them.
[2 Chronicles] [13]:[17] Aviyah and his men thrashed them badly, and some five-hundred thousand of their chosen warriors were killed.
[2 Chronicles] [13]:[18] So the Israelis were subdued at that time, and the people from Yehudah were victorious because they trusted in Yahweh, their ancestors’ god.
[2 Chronicles] [13]:[19] Aviyah chased after Yarov’am and they captured from Yisrael (Israel) the cities of Beyt-El (Bethel), Yeshanah, and Efron, and their surrounding villages.
[2 Chronicles] [13]:[20] Yarov’am never regained military strength during Aviyah’s reign, and after a time Yahweh struck him with sickness and he died.
[2 Chronicles] [13]:[21] Meanwhile, Aviyah became more powerful. He took fourteen wives for himself, and had twenty-two sons and sixteen daughters.
[2 Chronicles] [13]:[22] The rest of what Aviyah did, including his sayings and his behaviour, was written down by the prophet Ido.
[2 Chronicles] [14]:[1] Then Aviyah died, and they buried him with his ancestors in ‘The city of David’, and his son Asa reigned in his place. During his rule, the country was peaceful for ten years.
[2 Chronicles] [14]:[2] Asa did what was good and right in his god Yahweh’s eyes—
[2 Chronicles] [14]:[3] he removed the pagan altars and the hilltop shrines, smashed the sacred stone pillars, and cut the Asherah poles down.
[2 Chronicles] [14]:[4] He ordered the people in Yehudah (Judah) to worship Yahweh, their ancestors’ god, and to obey his instructions and regulations.
[2 Chronicles] [14]:[5] He removed all the hilltop shrines from Yehudah’s cities, and also the incense altars, and the kingdom was peaceful under his rule.
[2 Chronicles] [14]:[6] He fortified Yehudah’s cities, as the place was quiet without war during those years, because Yahweh had given him peace,
[2 Chronicles] [14]:[7] and he’d told Yehudah, “Let’s build these cities with walls around them, and towers, doors, and bars, while the land’s quiet around us, because we’ve asked our god Yahweh for guidance. We’ve made our request, and he’s given us rest on all our borders.” So they built and they prospered.
[2 Chronicles] [14]:[8] King Asa had an army of three-hundred thousand men from Yehudah who carried large shields and spears, as well as 280,000 men from Benyamin who also carried shields, along with bows and arrows. They were all powerful warriors.
[2 Chronicles] [14]:[9] But then Zerah the Kushi came out against them with an army of a million soldiers and three hundred chariots, and he advanced to Mareshah.
[2 Chronicles] [14]:[10] Asa went out to oppose them, and they deployed for battle in the Tsefat valley near Mareshah.
[2 Chronicles] [14]:[11] Then King Asa called out to his god Yahweh, “Yahweh, it makes no difference to you if there’s one against you, or one million. Help us, Yahweh our god, because we rely on you, and we’ve come against this massive force, trusting in your reputation. Yahweh, you’re our god—don’t let mere humans prevail against you.”
[2 Chronicles] [14]:[12] So Yahweh helped Asa and the army from Yehudah (Judah) to defeat the Kushim, and they fled.
[2 Chronicles] [14]:[13] Asa and his army chased them southwest as far as Gerar. So many Kushim were killed that the rest couldn’t save themselves, because they’d been destroyed in front of Yahweh and his army, and the men of Yehudah carried away a large amount of plunder.
[2 Chronicles] [14]:[14] They struck all the cities around Gerar, because the Kushim there were terrified of Yahweh. The men from Yehudah plundered all those cities, because they contained a lot of valuable goods.
[2 Chronicles] [14]:[15] They also attacked the Kushi cattle herdsmen, as well as capturing lots of sheep and camels before returning to Yerushalem (Jerusalem).
[2 Chronicles] [15]:[1] Then God’s spirit came down onto Oded’s son Azaryah,
[2 Chronicles] [15]:[2] and he went out to King Asa and told him, “Listen to me, Asa, and all of Yehudah (Judah) and Benyamin: Yahweh is with you southerners when you’re with him. And if you look for him, you’ll find him, but if you abandon him, he’ll also abandon you.
[2 Chronicles] [15]:[3] Yisrael (Israel) has been without the true God for a long time, as there hasn’t been a priest teaching, so God’s instructions have been forgotten.
[2 Chronicles] [15]:[4] However, they turned to Yisrael’s god Yahweh when they were in distress, and requested his help, and he helped them.
[2 Chronicles] [15]:[5] “In those times, it wasn’t safe to travel away, because there was wide unrest among the inhabitants of the surrounding regions.
[2 Chronicles] [15]:[6] Nation crushed nation, and city crushed city, because God sent them one trouble after another.
[2 Chronicles] [15]:[7] But you southerners, be strong and don’t give up striving, because your hard work will be rewarded.”
[2 Chronicles] [15]:[8] When King Asa heard those words and the prophecy from the prophet Oded’s son, he took courage and removed all the detestable idols from across Yehudah and Benyamin, and from the cities he’d captured from the Efrayim (Ephraim) hill country. Also, he repaired the altar to Yahweh that stood in front of Yahweh’s temple.
[2 Chronicles] [15]:[9] He assembled all the people from Yehudah and Benyamin, as well as the many people who’d joined them from the tribes of Efrayim, Menasheh (Manasseh), and Shim’on (Simeon). (Many people had emigrated from Yisrael into Yehudah when they realised that his god Yahweh was helping him.)
[2 Chronicles] [15]:[10] They gathered together in Yerushalem (Jerusalem) in June of the fifteenth year of King Asa’s reign
[2 Chronicles] [15]:[11] and sacrificed seven hundred bulls to Yahweh and seven thousand sheep—all of which had come from the recent plunder.
[2 Chronicles] [15]:[12] They solemnly agreed to sincerely and diligently devote themselves to Yahweh, their ancestors’ god.
[2 Chronicles] [15]:[13] They decided that anyone who didn’t worship Yisrael’s god Yahweh must be killed, man or woman, regardless of whether or not they had an important position.
[2 Chronicles] [15]:[14] Together they loudly promised that to Yahweh, then shouted and blew trumpets and horns,
[2 Chronicles] [15]:[15] and all of Yehudah celebrated that promise because they were totally sincere and committed. They asked Yahweh to give them guidance, which he did, and he enabled them to have peace throughout their country.
[2 Chronicles] [15]:[16] King Asa also removed his mother Ma’akah from her position as queen because she made a disgusting Asherah pole. Asa cut down the pole and crushed it, and burnt it at the Kidron brook,
[2 Chronicles] [15]:[17] although they didn’t remove the hilltop shrines from Yisrael. Nevertheless, Asa maintained his singular devotion to Yahweh for his whole life,
[2 Chronicles] [15]:[18] and he brought his father’s sacred things, and his own, into God’s temple—gold and silver items.
[2 Chronicles] [15]:[19] There was no more war in Yehudah until the thirty-fifth year of Asa’s reign.
[2 Chronicles] [16]:[1] In the thirty-sixth year of King Asa’s reign, Yisrael’s (Israel) king Baesha invaded Yehudah (Judah) and built Ramah to prevent anyone from leaving or entering the land controlled by Yehudah’s King Asa.
[2 Chronicles] [16]:[2] Asa took gold and silver from the temple treasuries and the king’s palace, and he sent it to King Ben-Hadad of Aram (Syria) (modern Aram), who lived in Damesek (Damascus), requesting,
[2 Chronicles] [16]:[3] “I want a peace treaty between you and me, and between your family and mine. Listen, I’ve sent gold and silver to you. Go and break your agreement with Yisrael’s King Baesha, so he’ll give up on his attack against me.”
[2 Chronicles] [16]:[4] Ben-Hadad accepted King Asa’s suggestion and sent his army captains to fight against Yisrael’s cities. They struck Iyon, Dan, and Avel-Mayim, and all the storehouses in the Naftali (Naphtali) cities.
[2 Chronicles] [16]:[5] When King Baesha heard about that, he stopped fortifying Ramah and abandoned the project,
[2 Chronicles] [16]:[6] so King Asa took men there from Yehudah. They carried away all the building stones from Ramah, along with the timber which Baesha had been using, and used it all to build Geva and Mitspah (north of Yerushalem (Jerusalem) ).
[2 Chronicles] [16]:[7] At that time, the prophet Hanani went to Yehudah’s (Judah) King Asa and told him, “Because you relied on the king of Aram (Syria) rather than on your god Yahweh, the Aramean king’s army has escaped from being defeated by you.
[2 Chronicles] [16]:[8] Didn’t the Kushim and the Luvim (Libyans) have a vast number of chariots and horsemen? Yet because you relied on Yahweh, he helped you defeat them,
[2 Chronicles] [16]:[9] because Yahweh sees everything that’s happening all over the world, and he strengthens the people who trust him completely. You’ve been foolish in what you’ve just done, so from now on, you’ll be facing wars.”
[2 Chronicles] [16]:[10] But King Asa was angry at the prophet, very angry, and had him put in prison, and after that Asa oppressed some of his people.
[2 Chronicles] [16]:[11] All of Asa’s projects from the beginning of his reign to the end are written in the scroll about the kings of Yehudah (Judah) and Yisrael (Israel).
[2 Chronicles] [16]:[12] King Asa got a disease that started in his feet in the thirty-ninth year of his reign. Even as it got worse, he didn’t try to get Yahweh to help him, only doctors.
[2 Chronicles] [16]:[13] Then Asa died in the forty-first year of his reign,
[2 Chronicles] [16]:[14] and he was buried in the tomb that he’d had carved out in ‘The City of David’. They laid his corpse on a bed of prepared spices and perfumes that had been mixed ready. Then they lit a large bonfire in his honour.
[2 Chronicles] [17]:[1] Then Asa’s son Yehoshafat (Jehoshaphat) replaced him as king, and he strengthened their defenses against Yisrael (Israel).
[2 Chronicles] [17]:[2] He placed troops in all of Yehudah’s (Judah) fortified cities, and posted garrisons across Yehudah and in the cities in Efrayim (Ephraim) that his father Asa had captured.
[2 Chronicles] [17]:[3] Yahweh helped Yehoshafat because he followed his ancestor David’s example at the beginning, and didn’t ask the Baals for guidance,
[2 Chronicles] [17]:[4] because he asked his father’s god, and he followed God’s instructions rather than doing the evil things that were done in Yisrael.
[2 Chronicles] [17]:[5] So Yahweh enabled him to maintain control of his kingdom, and all of Yehudah brought tribute to Yehoshafat, causing him to become very wealthy and highly respected.
[2 Chronicles] [17]:[6] He was completely devoted to doing what pleased Yahweh, even removing the hilltop shrines and the Asherah poles from Yehudah.
[2 Chronicles] [17]:[7] In the third year of his reign he sent his officials, Ben-Hayil, Ovadyah (Obadiah), Zekaryah (Zechariah), Netanel, and Mikayah, to teach in Yehudah’s cities.
[2 Chronicles] [17]:[8] They were accompanied by the Levites Shemayah, Netanyah, Zevadyah, Asahel, Shemiramot, Yonatan (Jonathan), Adoniyah, Toviyah, and Tov-Adoniyah, along with two priests, Elishama and Yehoram (Jehoram).
[2 Chronicles] [17]:[9] They took a scroll with Yahweh’s instructions written on it, and went around Yehudah’s cities teaching the people.
[2 Chronicles] [17]:[10] All the surrounding kingdoms were afraid of Yahweh, so they didn’t attack Yehoshafat (Jehoshaphat).
[2 Chronicles] [17]:[11] Some of the Pelishtim brought tribute to Yehoshafat, including lots of silver. Also, the Aravim brought him flocks totalling 7,700 rams and 7,700 goats.
[2 Chronicles] [17]:[12] So Yehoshafat continued to become more powerful, and he built palaces in Yehudah (Judah), as well as storehouses in the cities.
[2 Chronicles] [17]:[13] He accumulated many supplies in Yehudah’s cities. He also had many powerful warriors in Yerushalem (Jerusalem).
[2 Chronicles] [17]:[14] These are the leaders and numbers from each tribe: From the tribe of Yehudah, Adnah was the commander, and he had three-hundred thousand warriors,
[2 Chronicles] [17]:[15] His assistant Yehohanan commanded 280,000,
[2 Chronicles] [17]:[16] Next was Zikri’s son Amasyah, who volunteered for Yahweh and commanded two-hundred thousand warriors.
[2 Chronicles] [17]:[17] From the tribe of Benyamin, Elyada led two-hundred thousand men equipped with bows and shields,
[2 Chronicles] [17]:[18] next to him was Yehozavad with 180,000 equipped for war.
[2 Chronicles] [17]:[19] Those were the ones who served the king, along with the ones the king had placed in Yehudah’s (Judah) fortified cities.
[2 Chronicles] [18]:[1] King Yehoshafat (Jehoshaphat) became very wealthy, and was highly honoured, but then he allied himself by marriage to Yisrael’s (Israel) King Ahav.
[2 Chronicles] [18]:[2] Some years later, he went up to Ahav in Shomron (Samaria), and Ahav sacrificed lots of sheep and cattle for him and for the people who were with him, and he incited him to attack Ramot-Gilead—
[2 Chronicles] [18]:[3] Yisrael’s King Ahav suggested to Yehudah’s (Judah) King Yehoshafat, “Will you join me to attack Ramot-Gilead?” “Wherever you’ll be, I’ll be there,” he responded. “Your people are like my own people, and we’re with you in battle.”
[2 Chronicles] [18]:[4] Then he added, “But we should get Yahweh’s advice first.”
[2 Chronicles] [18]:[5] So Yisrael’s king gathered four hundred of his prophets and asked them, “Should we attack Ramot-Gilead or not?” “Go ahead,” they answered, “and God will give victory to the king.”
[2 Chronicles] [18]:[6] But Yehoshafat asked, “Is there no prophet of Yahweh here that we can ask?”
[2 Chronicles] [18]:[7] Yisrael’s king told Yehoshafat, “There’s still one man who would ask Yahweh, but personally I hate him because he never prophesies anything good about me—it’s always something evil. He’s Yimla’s son, Mikayah.” “You shouldn’t talk like that,” said Yehoshafat.
[2 Chronicles] [18]:[8] So Yisrael’s king ordered an official, “Get Yimla’s son Mikayah here as quick as possible.”
[2 Chronicles] [18]:[9] Now the kings of Yisrael and Yehudah (Judah) were both clothed in their royal robes and sitting there on their thrones near Shomron’s (Samaria) entrance gate. They were up on a threshing floor, and all the prophets were prophesying in front of them.
[2 Chronicles] [18]:[10] Kena’anah’s son Tsidkiyah (Zedekiah) made himself some iron horns and said, “Yahweh says you’ll use these to gore Aram (Syria) and destroy them.”
[2 Chronicles] [18]:[11] All the rest of Ahav’s prophets agreed, saying, “Yes, go and attack Ramot-Gilead and you’ll succeed—Yahweh will give the king victory.”
[2 Chronicles] [18]:[12] The messenger who went to fetch Mikayah warned him, “Listen, the king is pleased with what the other prophets agreed on. Just say the same as them and give a favourable message.”
[2 Chronicles] [18]:[13] But Mikayah responded, “As sure as Yahweh lives, I’ll only say what my god tells me to say.”
[2 Chronicles] [18]:[14] When he got to the king, King Ahav asked him, “Mikah, should we attack Ramot-Gilead for battle, or should I hold back?” “Go ahead and succeed,” he answered. “You’ll be given victory over them.”
[2 Chronicles] [18]:[15] But the king said to him, “How many times must I keep making you promise that you’ll only say what Yahweh says—not just what I want to hear?”
[2 Chronicles] [18]:[16] So Mikayah responded, “I saw all of Yisrael (Israel) scattered on the hills like sheep without shepherds, and Yahweh said, ‘They don’t have any master, so they’ll all just go home in peace.’ ”
[2 Chronicles] [18]:[17] Ahav remarked to Yehoshafat (Jehoshaphat), “Didn’t I tell you that he wouldn’t prophesy anything good about me—only disaster?”
[2 Chronicles] [18]:[18] But Mikayah continued, “Well, listen to what Yahweh says. I saw Yahweh sitting on his throne, and all the heavenly soldiers standing on each side of him,
[2 Chronicles] [18]:[19] and Yahweh said, ‘Who’ll entice Yisrael’s King Ahav so he’ll attack and then die at Ramot-Gilead?’ Some suggested one thing, and others suggested something else.
[2 Chronicles] [18]:[20] Then a spirit went out and stood in front of Yahweh and said, ‘I myself will entice him.’ ‘How would you do it?’ Yahweh asked him.
[2 Chronicles] [18]:[21] The spirit replied, ‘I’ll go and inspire all of Ahav’s prophets to tell lies.’ Yahweh said, ‘That’ll work. Go and do it.’
[2 Chronicles] [18]:[22] “So now, listen. Yahweh placed a deceiving spirit in the mouths of those prophets of yours, and Yahweh has decreed that you’ll face disaster.”
[2 Chronicles] [18]:[23] Then Kena’anah’s son Tsidkiyah (Zedekiah) went up to Mikayah and slapped him hard on the cheek, saying, “Yeah? Since when did Yahweh’s spirit leave me and start speaking to you?”
[2 Chronicles] [18]:[24] “Well, you’ll find out soon,” answered Mikayah, “on the day when you go room by room in some house to try to hide.”
[2 Chronicles] [18]:[25] “Arrest Mikayah,” ordered King Ahav, “and return him to Amon the city governor, and to my son Yoash.
[2 Chronicles] [18]:[26] Tell them that the king’s ordered that this man be put in prison, and be given only strictly-rationed bread and water until I return safely.”
[2 Chronicles] [18]:[27] “If you return safely,” Mikayah retorted, “then Yahweh mustn’t have spoken to me.”
[2 Chronicles] [18]:[28] So Yisrael’s (Israel) King Ahav and Yehudah’s (Judah) king Yehoshafat (Jehoshaphat) went to Ramot-Gilead.
[2 Chronicles] [18]:[29] Ahav told Yehoshafat, “I’ll get changed, so I’m not recognised, and go into the battle, but you wear your royal robe.” So Yisrael’s king disguised himself, and they went into the battle.
[2 Chronicles] [18]:[30] Meanwhile, Aram’s (Syria) king had ordered his chariot commanders, “Only attack Yisrael’s king—don’t bother fighting anyone else.”
[2 Chronicles] [18]:[31] However, when those chariot commanders saw King Yehoshafat, they mistook him for Yisrael’s king, and wheeled around to fight him, but Yehoshafat cried out to Yahweh for help, and he helped him—God drew them away from him,
[2 Chronicles] [18]:[32] because when the chariot commanders realised that it wasn’t Yisrael’s king, they turned back from chasing him.
[2 Chronicles] [18]:[33] However, one Aramean warrior drew his bow without knowing where Ahav was, and struck Yisrael’s king at a joint in his armour. Ahav ordered the charioteer, “Turn around and get me out of here, because I’ve been seriously wounded.”
[2 Chronicles] [18]:[34] The battle continued for the whole day, and Yisrael’s king was propped up in his chariot to watch the Arameans, but he died as the sun was setting.
[2 Chronicles] [19]:[1] Yehudah’s (Judah) king Yehoshafat (Jehoshaphat) returned safely to his home in Yerushalem (Jerusalem),
[2 Chronicles] [19]:[2] but Hanani’s son, the prophet Yehu (Jehu), confronted him, “Should you have helped the wicked, and befriended those that Yahweh hates? Yahweh’s angry with you because of what you’ve done.
[2 Chronicles] [19]:[3] However, you have some good points, because you removed the Asherah poles from the country, and you’ve been sincere in wanting to follow God.”
[2 Chronicles] [19]:[4] Yehoshafat (Jehoshaphat) lived in Yerushalem (Jerusalem), but one time he went out to the people of Be’er-Sheva (Beersheba) in the Efrayim (Ephraim) hill country and encouraged them back to Yahweh, their ancestors’ god.
[2 Chronicles] [19]:[5] He appointed judges in Yehudah’s (Judah) fortified cities to serve across the country,
[2 Chronicles] [19]:[6] and he told them, “Take care in what you do, because as judges, you’re not serving people, but serving Yahweh when you make judicial decisions.
[2 Chronicles] [19]:[7] So revere Yahweh and judge cases carefully, because our god Yahweh doesn’t tolerate injustice, partiality, or bribery.”
[2 Chronicles] [19]:[8] Yehoshafat also appointed some Levites and priests in Yerushalem, as well as leaders from some Israeli families, to be judges on Yahweh’s behalf based in Yerushalem,
[2 Chronicles] [19]:[9] and he instructed them, “You must revere Yahweh and be trustworthy and sincere.
[2 Chronicles] [19]:[10] When any of your fellow Israelis who live in the cities bring any case to you involving violent crime, or interpreting laws or regulations, and so on, you must caution them so they won’t sin against Yahweh and induce his anger to come against you or them, so do that, and you won’t be guilty.
[2 Chronicles] [19]:[11] And listen, the chief priest Amaryah is superior to you judges in any religious matter, and Yishmael’s (Ishmael) son Zevadyah is Yehudah’s leader for any civil matter concerning the king. Also, you have the Levite officials to assist you judges. Act with courage, and let Yahweh assist people who are doing what’s right.”
[2 Chronicles] [20]:[1] Sometime after that, the Moavim and Amonim, along with some of the Meunim, came to battle against King Yehoshafat (Jehoshaphat).
[2 Chronicles] [20]:[2] Some men came and told Yehoshafat, “A huge army is coming from Aram (Syria) beyond the Dead Sea to attack you, and take note: they’re already in Hatsatson-Tamar, also known as Eyn-Gedi.”
[2 Chronicles] [20]:[3] Yehoshafat was alarmed and decided to request advice from Yahweh, and he ordered that all of Yehudah (Judah) should fast.
[2 Chronicles] [20]:[4] So Yehudah assembled to request Yahweh’s help—they came to Yerushalem (Jerusalem) from all of Yehudah’s cities to ask Yahweh for help.
[2 Chronicles] [20]:[5] Yehoshafat stood in front of all the people from Yerushalem and across Yehudah, in front of the new temple courtyard,
[2 Chronicles] [20]:[6] and prayed, “Yahweh, the god of our ancestors, aren’t you the god who lives in the heavens? And you rule in all the kingdoms around the world, and you have full power and control—no one can stand against you.
[2 Chronicles] [20]:[7] Weren’t you our god who drove the previous inhabitants of this land out ahead of your Israeli people? Didn’t you give it to the descendants of Avraham—the one you loved forever?
[2 Chronicles] [20]:[8] Our ancestors lived in this land and built a temple to honour you, saying,
[2 Chronicles] [20]:[9] ‘If disaster, like war, judgement, epidemic, or famine comes on us, we’ll stand in front of this temple, and in front of you, because your name is honoured here. And we’ll cry to you because of our distress, and you’ll hear and rescue us.’
[2 Chronicles] [20]:[10] You didn’t allow our Israeli ancestors to enter the countries of Amon, Moav (Moab), or Edom when they were travelling from Mitsrayim (Egypt) to Kena’an (Canaan). So our ancestors turned away from those areas and didn’t destroy them, but now they’re coming here to attack us.
[2 Chronicles] [20]:[11] Look how they’re repaying us for not destroying them—they come here to drive us out from the land you gave us as an inheritance.
[2 Chronicles] [20]:[12] So, our god, please punish them, because we’re not strong enough to battle this huge army that’s on its way. We simply don’t know what to do, so we’re looking to you to rescue us.”
[2 Chronicles] [20]:[13] At that time, all of Yehudah (Judah) (men, women, and children) were standing in front of Yahweh,
[2 Chronicles] [20]:[14] and Yahweh’s spirit came on Yahaziel. (Yahaziel was the son of Zekaryah (Zechariah), son of Benayah, son of Yeiel, son of Matanyah the Levite, and a descendant of Asaf.) In the middle of the assembly
[2 Chronicles] [20]:[15] he said, “Pay attention, all of Yehudah, inhabitants of Yerushalem, and King Yehoshafat. Yahweh has this to say to you all, ‘Don’t be afraid, and don’t be dismayed by this huge force, because it’s not your battle, but God’s.
[2 Chronicles] [20]:[16] Tomorrow, go down against them. Listen, they’re coming uphill near the Ascent of Tsits, and you’ll find them at the end of the valley, facing the Yeruel wilderness.
[2 Chronicles] [20]:[17] You won’t need to fight them—just take your positions, people from Yerushalem and wider Yehudah, and watch Yahweh save you. Don’t be afraid or discouraged. Go out there tomorrow and Yahweh will be with you.’ ”
[2 Chronicles] [20]:[18] Then King Yehoshafat (Jehoshaphat) bowed with his face to the ground, and all the people from Yerushalem (Jerusalem) and across Yehudah fell to their knees in front of Yahweh to worship him.
[2 Chronicles] [20]:[19] Then some of the Levites who were descendants of Kohat and Korah stood up to loudly praise Yisrael’s (Israel) god Yahweh.
[2 Chronicles] [20]:[20] They rose early the next morning and went out to the Tekoa wilderness, and as they were leaving, Yehoshafat stood and called out, “Hear me, inhabitants of Yerushalem and Yehudah. Believe in our god Yahweh, and be confident. Believe his prophets and succeed.”
[2 Chronicles] [20]:[21] Then he consulted with the people, and he appointed some to sing to Yahweh and some to praise him for his splendour and sinlessness as they went out in front of the enemy army, and they were saying, “Give thanks to Yahweh, because his loyal commitment endures forever.”
[2 Chronicles] [20]:[22] As they began to sing and praise Yahweh, he sent ambushers against the Amonim, Moavim, and Edomim who were attacking Yehudah, and they were defeated.
[2 Chronicles] [20]:[23] Then the Amonim and Moavim turned on the Edomim and completely annihilated them, and after that they slaughtered each other.
[2 Chronicles] [20]:[24] When Yehudah’s men arrived at the place overlooking the wilderness, wow, they saw corpses all over the ground. No one had escaped.
[2 Chronicles] [20]:[25] Then Yehoshafat and his people went to plunder the spoils, and they found lots of goods among them, as well as clothing, and valuable items. They took that for themselves until there was nothing left to carry away—there was so much plunder that it took three days to collect it all.
[2 Chronicles] [20]:[26] On the fourth day, they assembled in Berakah Valley and praised Yahweh there. That’s why it’s called Berakah Valley (which means ‘praise/blessing’) to this day.
[2 Chronicles] [20]:[27] Then all the men from Yerushalem and across Yehudah returned to Yerushalem with King Yehoshafat leading them—celebrating because Yahweh had enabled them to defeat their enemies.
[2 Chronicles] [20]:[28] When they arrived at Yerushalem, they went to the temple, playing harps, lutes, and trumpets.
[2 Chronicles] [20]:[29] The nearby kingdoms were all very afraid of God when they heard that Yahweh had fought against Yisrael’s (Israel) enemies,
[2 Chronicles] [20]:[30] so Yehoshafat’s kingdom was untroubled, and his god gave him peace from all his neighbours.
[2 Chronicles] [20]:[31] Yehoshafat (Jehoshaphat) was thirty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned over Yehudah (Judah) from Yerushalem (Jerusalem) for twenty-five years. His mother was Shilhi’s daughter, Azuvah.
[2 Chronicles] [20]:[32] He had similar priorities to his father Asa, doing what pleased Yahweh, and he didn’t deviate from that.
[2 Chronicles] [20]:[33] However, he never removed the hilltop shrines, and the people weren’t really serious about obeying their ancestors’ god.
[2 Chronicles] [20]:[34] Everything else that Yehoshafat did, from the beginning to the end of his reign, was written down by Hanani’s son Yehu (Jehu) in the scroll about Yisrael’s (Israel) kings.
[2 Chronicles] [20]:[35] Later on, Yehudah’s King Yehoshafat made an alliance with Yisrael’s King Ahazyah (which was a wicked thing to do),
[2 Chronicles] [20]:[36] and they worked together to make ships at Etsyon-Gever to sail to Tarshish.
[2 Chronicles] [20]:[37] Then Dodavahu’s son Eliezer from Mareshah prophesied against Yehoshafat, saying, “When you allied yourself with Ahazyah, Yahweh destroyed what you created.” In due course, the ships were damaged and unable to sail to Tarshish.
[2 Chronicles] [21]:[1] Then Yehoshafat died and was buried with his ancestors in ‘The City of David’, and his son Yehoram (Jehoram) replaced him as king.
[2 Chronicles] [21]:[2] Yehoram’s (Jehoram) younger brothers were Azaryah, Yehiel, Zekaryah (Zechariah), Azaryah, Mika’el (Michael), and Shefatyah,
[2 Chronicles] [21]:[3] and their father gave them many gifts of gold and silver and precious things, along with fortified cities in Yehudah (Judah), however he handed the kingdom over to Yehoram because he was the oldest son.
[2 Chronicles] [21]:[4] After Yehoram established firm control of his father’s kingdom, he had all his brothers killed, as well as some of Yisrael’s (Israel) leaders.
[2 Chronicles] [21]:[5] Yehoram was thirty-two years old when he became the king, and he ruled from Yerushalem (Jerusalem) for eight years.
[2 Chronicles] [21]:[6] He did many of the evil things that Yisrael’s kings had done, because he married one of King Ahav’s daughters and did things that Yahweh had said were evil.
[2 Chronicles] [21]:[7] Despite that, Yahweh wouldn’t eliminate David’s descendants, because of the promise he’d made with David to ‘keep his lamp burning’ forever.
[2 Chronicles] [21]:[8] Meanwhile, Edom had been under Yehudah’s control, but during Yehoram’s reign they rebelled and appointed their own king.
[2 Chronicles] [21]:[9] Yehoram took his commanders and all his chariots, and crossed the Yarden (Jordan) River, then at nighttime he attacked the Edomim who’d surrounded him and his chariots.
[2 Chronicles] [21]:[10] However, Edom successfully rebelled against Yehudah’s control, then Livnah also did the same, because Yehoram had abandoned Yahweh, his ancestors’ god.
[2 Chronicles] [21]:[11] He also built hilltop shrines around Yehudah, and he caused Yerushalem’s inhabitants to prostitute themselves, and he drove Yehudah away from Yahweh.
[2 Chronicles] [21]:[12] Then King Yehoram received a written message from the prophet Eliyah (Elijah): “Your father David’s god Yahweh says that you decided not to follow your father Yehoshafat’s (Jehoshaphat) example, or good King Asa’s,
[2 Chronicles] [21]:[13] but rather you imitated the behaviour of Yisrael’s (Israel) king, so because of that, you’ve caused Yerushalem’s inhabitants, as well as wider Yehudah, to commit adultery like Ahav’s family did. Also, you’ve killed your own blood brothers—people who were better than you.
[2 Chronicles] [21]:[14] So listen, now Yahweh is going to severely afflict your people, including your sons and your wives, as well as all your possessions,
[2 Chronicles] [21]:[15] and you yourself will get an intestinal disease that’ll get worse every day until your innards fall out.”
[2 Chronicles] [21]:[16] Then Yahweh stirred the Pelishtim up against Yehoram, as well as the Arabs who lived beside the Kushim,
[2 Chronicles] [21]:[17] and they attacked Yehudah. They did a lot of damage and took away everything valuable from the king’s palace. They also took his wives and sons, other than Yehoahaz, his youngest son.
[2 Chronicles] [21]:[18] After that, Yahweh caused an intestinal disease in Yehoram that couldn’t be cured,
[2 Chronicles] [21]:[19] and it progressed day after day until, after two years, his intestines fell out, and he died in a lot of pain. His people didn’t make a bonfire in his honour like they’d done for his ancestors.
[2 Chronicles] [21]:[20] Yehoram was thirty-two when he became king, and he ruled from Yerushalem (Jerusalem) for eight years. No one regretted it when he died, and his body was buried in ‘The City of David’, but not in the royal tombs.
[2 Chronicles] [22]:[1] The inhabitants of Yerushalem (Jerusalem) made his youngest son Ahazyah king in his place, because all his older brothers had been killed by the Aravi invaders. So Yehoram’s (Jehoram) son Ahazyah reigned as Yehudah’s (Judah) king.
[2 Chronicles] [22]:[2] He was twenty-two when he became king, and he reigned from Yerushalem for one year. His mother was Atalyah (Athaliah), a granddaughter of Yisrael’s (Israel) King Omri.
[2 Chronicles] [22]:[3] King Ahazyah behaved just like King Ahav’s family had done, because his mother gave him evil advice,
[2 Chronicles] [22]:[4] so he did what Yahweh had said was evil, just like Ahav’s family, because after his father’s death, they’d become Ahazyah’s advisors, giving destructive suggestions.
[2 Chronicles] [22]:[5] He followed their advice and joined King Yehoram (son of Yisrael’s King Ahav) to fight against Aram’s (Syria) King Hazael at Ramot-Gilead, where Yehoram was wounded by the Arameans.
[2 Chronicles] [22]:[6] Yehoram returned to Yizre’el (Jezreel) to recover, because he’d been wounded at Ramah in the battle against Aram’s King Hazael. So Yehudah’s King Ahazyah went up to Yizre’el to see Yehoram.
[2 Chronicles] [22]:[7] God caused Ahazyah’s downfall through his visit to Yoram (Joram). When Ahazyah arrived, he went with Yehoram to meet Nimshi’s son Yehu (Jehu), who Yahweh had appointed to kill all of Ahav’s descendants.
[2 Chronicles] [22]:[8] While Yehu was executing judgement on Ahav’s descendants, he discovered Yehudah’s officials there, including Ahazyah’s nephews who’d been serving him, and he killed all of them as well.
[2 Chronicles] [22]:[9] Then Yehu went searching for Ahazyah and found him hiding in Shomron (Samaria) city. They captured him and took him to Yehu, and killed him. They did bury him, because they said, “He was the grandson of King Yehoshafat (Jehoshaphat) who tried hard to please Yahweh.” After that, there were no descendants of Ahazyah who were powerful enough to become Yehudah’s king.
[2 Chronicles] [22]:[10] When Ahazyah’s mother Atalyah (Athaliah) found out that her son had died, she took action and destroyed all his family members who could become king of Yehudah (Judah).
[2 Chronicles] [22]:[11] However, a princess named Yehoshav’at took Ahazyah’s son Yoash, and she sneaked him away from among the king’s sons who were about to be killed, and she hid him and his nurse in a bedroom. Yehoshav’at was the daughter of the late King Yehoram (Jehoram) and the wife of Yehoyada the priest (she was Ahazyah’s sister), and she hid Yoash from Atalyah so she couldn’t kill him.
[2 Chronicles] [22]:[12] He stayed in hiding with them in the temple for six years while Atalyah ruled over Yehudah.
[2 Chronicles] [23]:[1] The following year, the priest Yehoyada took courage and made an agreement with the commanders of units of a hundred soldiers: Azaryah (Yehoram’s (Jehoram) son), Yishmael (Ishmael) (Yehohanan’s son), another Azaryah (Oved’s son), Ma’aseyah (Adayah’s son), and Elishafat (Zikri’s son).
[2 Chronicles] [23]:[2] They went throughout Yehudah (Judah) and gathered all the Levites and the clan leaders from all the cities. When they came to Yerushalem (Jerusalem),
[2 Chronicles] [23]:[3] the whole assembly made an agreement with the young king in the temple, and Yehoyada told them, “Listen, the late king’s son will reign, just as Yahweh said about David’s descendants.
[2 Chronicles] [23]:[4] Now this is what you need to do: one third of you priests and Levites who are on duty on the Rest Day must guard the temple entrances.
[2 Chronicles] [23]:[5] Another third of you must guard the king’s palace, and the final third guard the Foundation Gate and all the people in the temple courtyard.
[2 Chronicles] [23]:[6] Don’t let anyone enter Yahweh’s temple other than the priests and the Levites who are on duty, because they’re consecrated. Every one else must respect Yahweh’s instructions not to enter.
[2 Chronicles] [23]:[7] You Levites must be armed and surround the young king. You must kill anyone else who tries to enter the temple, but stay close to the king wherever he goes.
[2 Chronicles] [23]:[8] So the Levites and the other people did everything Yehoyada the priest had instructed. Each leader took his men, both those starting duty on the Rest Day, as well as the others finishing their duties that day, because Yehoyada didn’t dismiss any of the groups.
[2 Chronicles] [23]:[9] Then Yehoyada the priest gave each of those commanders the spears, and the large and small shields which had been put in the temple by King David.
[2 Chronicles] [23]:[10] He stationed all the people, each one holding their weapon, right across the end of the temple, around the altar and the temple, and all around the king.
[2 Chronicles] [23]:[11] Then they brought out young Yoash, put a crown on his head, gave him a scroll with the agreement on it, and proclaimed him as king. Then Yehoyada and his sons anointed him with olive oil and shouted, “Long live the king!”
[2 Chronicles] [23]:[12] When Atalyah (Athaliah) heard the sound of people running, and people praising the king, she went to the temple
[2 Chronicles] [23]:[13] to look, and wow, the young king was standing where previous kings had stood by the pillar at the temple entrance, with the commanders and trumpeters beside him. The people were all cheering and blowing trumpets, and singers with instruments were leading the praise. Then Atalyah tore her robe and shouted out, “Treason! Treason!”
[2 Chronicles] [23]:[14] Then Yehoyada the priest instructed the commanders, “Kill her, but not here at Yahweh’s temple. March her outside and kill anyone who sticks up for her.”
[2 Chronicles] [23]:[15] They seized her as she reached the Horse Gate in front of the palace and killed her there.
[2 Chronicles] [23]:[16] Then Yehoyada the priest got the people to formally agree that they and the king would be loyal to Yahweh,
[2 Chronicles] [23]:[17] so all the people went to Ba’al’s temple and tore it down. They smashed its altars and idols, and killed Ba’al’s priest Matan in front of the altars.
[2 Chronicles] [23]:[18] Then Yehoyada created the roster for the temple duties of the priests and Levites that King David had previously assigned, including offering burnt offerings to Yahweh with happiness and singing, following Mosheh’s (Moses) written instructions.
[2 Chronicles] [23]:[19] He also stationed guards at the temple gates so that no one could enter if they were ceremonially ‘unclean’.
[2 Chronicles] [23]:[20] Then Yehoyada took those commanders, and the nobles and leaders, and all the people, and they brought the king out of the temple and down into the palace through the Upper Gate, and sat him on the royal throne.
[2 Chronicles] [23]:[21] Then all of Yehudah’s (Judah) people celebrated, and then the city was peaceful and quiet, as Atalyah (Athaliah) had been put to death with a sword.
[2 Chronicles] [24]:[1] Yoash was seven years old when he became Yehudah’s (Judah) king, and he reigned from Yerushalem (Jerusalem) for forty years. His mother was Tsivyah from Be’er-Sheva (Beersheba).
[2 Chronicles] [24]:[2] Yoash did what pleased Yahweh throughout the lifetime of Yehoyada the priest.
[2 Chronicles] [24]:[3] Yehoyada procured two wives for him, and they bore him sons and daughters.
[2 Chronicles] [24]:[4] Sometime later, Yoash decided it would be good to repair Yahweh’s residence,
[2 Chronicles] [24]:[5] and he gathered the priests and Levites, and told them, “Go out to Yehudah’s cities and collect enough money across the country to renovate God’s house in the next few years. Make this a priority.” But the Levites didn’t get on to it,
[2 Chronicles] [24]:[6] so the king summoned Yehoyada and demanded, “Why haven’t you followed up on sending the Levites throughout Yerushalem and across Yehudah to collect the annual tax instituted by Yahweh’s servant Mosheh (Moses) for the people to contribute to the costs of the sacred tent?”
[2 Chronicles] [24]:[7] (The wicked Atalyah’s (Athaliah) people had previously broken into Yahweh’s residence and taken some of the sacred items from Yahweh’s temple to use for Ba’al worship.)
[2 Chronicles] [24]:[8] The king ordered that a chest be made and placed outside the main temple entrance.
[2 Chronicles] [24]:[9] They made an announcement in Yerushalem and throughout Yehudah that people were to bring to Yahweh the tax that was instituted by God’s servant Mosheh when they were still in the wilderness.
[2 Chronicles] [24]:[10] All the officials and the people agreed with this policy, so they brought their contributions and dropped them into the chest until it filled up.
[2 Chronicles] [24]:[11] Every day, when the Levites who’d been given oversight over the chest by the king saw that it was full, they’d fetch one of the king’s secretaries along with one of the head priest’s officials, and they’d empty the box and return it to its place, so they amassed a large sum of money.
[2 Chronicles] [24]:[12] The king and Yehoyada the priest gave the collected funds to the people who worked on the temple renovations. They used them to hire stone-workers and carpenters to restore the temple building, as well as for iron and bronze craftsmen.
[2 Chronicles] [24]:[13] So they started on the work, and the temple restoration went ahead. They rebuilt the temple following its original specifications, and strengthened it.
[2 Chronicles] [24]:[14] Whey they’d finished, they brought the remainder of the funds back to the king and Yehoyada, and they made items for the temple, items used in ministry and for burnt offerings, and dishes and gold and silver items. During Yehoyada’s time, they were offering regular burnt sacrifices in Yahweh’s temple.
[2 Chronicles] [24]:[15] By then, Yehoyada was getting old, and he died at the age of 130,
[2 Chronicles] [24]:[16] and they buried him with the kings in ‘The City of David’, because he’d done so much good for Yisrael (Israel), and for God and his temple.
[2 Chronicles] [24]:[17] After Yehoyada’s death, Yehudah’s (Judah) leaders went to young King Yoash and declared their loyalty to him, and he listened to them.
[2 Chronicles] [24]:[18] Then they abandoned the temple of their ancestors’ god Yahweh, and they worshipped the Asherah poles and idols, and God was angry at Yerushalem (Jerusalem) and Yehudah because of their disobedience.
[2 Chronicles] [24]:[19] He sent prophets to tell them to return back to him, and although they warned the people, the people didn’t take any notice.
[2 Chronicles] [24]:[20] Then God’s spirit enveloped Zekaryah (Zechariah), the son of Yehoyada the priest, and he stood up and told the people, “God asks why you people are violating his commands. Because you abandoned Yahweh, he’s abandoned you people.”
[2 Chronicles] [24]:[21] However, the people conspired against Zekaryah, and the king ordered him to be executed by stoning him in the temple courtyard.
[2 Chronicles] [24]:[22] King Yoash disregarded the loyal commitment that Yehoyada had shown to his father, and killed his son. As Zekaryah was dying, he said, “Yahweh will see this and find a way to avenge.”
[2 Chronicles] [24]:[23] Around the end of the year, the Aramean army attacked Yehudah and Yerushalem, and killed all the people’s leaders. They sent all their plunder back to their king in Damesek (Damascus).
[2 Chronicles] [24]:[24] Actually, the Arameans only had a smallish army, but Yahweh allowed them to defeat the much larger army from Yehudah and bring punishment to King Yoash, because they’d abandoned Yahweh, their ancestors’ god.
[2 Chronicles] [24]:[25] When they withdrew, they left Yoash with severe wounds, and then his servants conspired against him because he’d killed the son of the priest Yehoyada. So they killed him in his bed, and although they buried him in ‘The City of David’, he wasn’t buried with the other kings.
[2 Chronicles] [24]:[26] The ones who’d conspired to kill him were: Zavad (a son of the Amoni woman Shim’at) and Yehozavad (a son of the Moavi woman Shimrit).
[2 Chronicles] [24]:[27] The list of King Yoash’s sons, the many prophecies concerning him, and his renovations of the temple, are all written on ‘The Scroll of the Kings’. His son Amatsyah replaced him as king.
[2 Chronicles] [25]:[1] Amatsyah was twenty-five when he became Yehudah’s (Judah) king, and he reigned from Yerushalem (Jerusalem) for twenty-nine years. His mother was Yeho’adin from Yerushalem.
[2 Chronicles] [25]:[2] He mostly followed Yahweh’s instructions, but not whole-heartedly.
[2 Chronicles] [25]:[3] Once his rule was established, he killed those of his servants who’d assassinated his father Yoash.
[2 Chronicles] [25]:[4] However, he didn’t order their sons to be executed, because he obeyed Yahweh’s instructions that had been written down by Mosheh (Moses), “Parents mustn’t die because of what their children did, and children mustn’t die because of what their parents did, but each individual should be punished for their own disobedience.”
[2 Chronicles] [25]:[5] Then Amatsyah summoned Yehudah’s men and appointed some, clan by clan, to be leaders of hundreds and of thousands, for all of Yehudah and Benyamin. They counted three-hundred thousand men who were twenty and over, and suitable for fighting with a spear and shield.
[2 Chronicles] [25]:[6] He also hired a hundred thousand powerful warriors from Yisrael (Israel) for three tonnes of silver.
[2 Chronicles] [25]:[7] However, a man of God came and told him, “Your majesty, don’t let Yisrael’s soldiers go with you, because Yahweh isn’t with Yisrael—those Efrayimim.
[2 Chronicles] [25]:[8] Even if you go and fight courageously in battle, God will cause you to be defeated by the enemy, because God has the power to help and the power to overthrow.”
[2 Chronicles] [25]:[9] “So what should I do about all the silver that I’ve already paid to the troops from Yisrael?” Amatsyah asked. “Yahweh can do much more for you than that,” God’s man replied.
[2 Chronicles] [25]:[10] So King Amatsyah told the troops from Yisrael to go home again, but they were extremely angry with Yehudah, and they got home still feeling furious.
[2 Chronicles] [25]:[11] Then Amatsyah took courage and led his army out to the Salt Valley, where they slaughtered ten thousand Edomi soldiers.
[2 Chronicles] [25]:[12] Yehudah rounded up another ten thousand and herded them to the top of a cliff, where they drove them over to kill them.
[2 Chronicles] [25]:[13] However, during that time, the warriors that Amatsyah had sent back to Yisrael raided Yehudah’s cities all the way from Shomron (Samaria) to Beyt-Horon. They’d killed three thousand people and taken back a large amount of plunder.
[2 Chronicles] [25]:[14] After King Amatsyah returned from fighting the Edomim, he brought back their idols and set them up to be his gods—bowing down to them and offering sacrifices.
[2 Chronicles] [25]:[15] That made Yahweh very angry at Amatsyah, and he sent a prophet to tell him, “Why did you want those gods who weren’t even able to save their own people from your army?”
[2 Chronicles] [25]:[16] While he was still speaking, the king snapped at him, “Who asked you to be my counsellor? Stop right this minute or they’ll strike you down!” So the prophet stopped talking, but then he added, “I know that God has decided to destroy you because you’ve done that, and because you didn’t listen to my advice.”
[2 Chronicles] [25]:[17] Some time later, Yehudah’s (Judah) King Amatsyah consulted his advisors, then sent a challenge to Yisrael’s (Israel) King Yoash (son of Yehoahaz, son of Yehu (Jehu)), “Let’s face each other on the battlefield.”
[2 Chronicles] [25]:[18] But Yisrael’s King Yoash replied, “A thistle in Levanon sent a message to a cedar in Levanon, saying, ‘Give your daughter to my son for a wife,’ but some random animal passed through the Lebanese countryside and trampled the thistle.
[2 Chronicles] [25]:[19] You defeated Edom and now it’s gone to your head. So stay in your chair at home and don’t get over-excited, otherwise both you and Yehudah will be toppled.”
[2 Chronicles] [25]:[20] But King Amatsyah took no notice, because God was planning for him to be defeated for worshipping Edom’s gods.
[2 Chronicles] [25]:[21] So Yisrael’s King Yoash advanced, and the two armies faced each other at Beyt-Shemesh (Heliopolis) in Yehudah,
[2 Chronicles] [25]:[22] and Yehudah was badly defeated by Yisrael, and all their warriors fled back home.
[2 Chronicles] [25]:[23] Yisrael’s King Yoash captured King Amatsyah (son of Yoash, son of Yehoahaz) at Beyt-Shemesh and took him to Yerushalem (Jerusalem). Then he tore down Yerushalem’s wall from the Efrayim Gate to the Corner Gate—a section about 180m long.
[2 Chronicles] [25]:[24] He took back to Shomron (Samaria) all the gold and silver and other valuable items that Oved-Edom had been guarding in the temple, as well as the valuables from the palace and some hostages.
[2 Chronicles] [25]:[25] After the death of Yisrael’s King Yoash (son of Yehoahaz), Yehudah’s King Amatsyah lived for a further fifteen years.
[2 Chronicles] [25]:[26] The account of everything else Amatsyah did was written in the scroll of ‘The Kings of Yehudah and Yisrael’.
[2 Chronicles] [25]:[27] From the time that Amatsyah had turned from following Yahweh, there was a conspiracy to assassinate him in Yerushalem, but he fled to Lakish. However, they traced him to Lakish and killed him there.
[2 Chronicles] [25]:[28] They used horses to carry his body back to Yerushalem, and he was buried with his ancestors in ‘The City of David’.
[2 Chronicles] [26]:[1] Then all the people took sixteen-year-old Uziyah and made him king to replace his father Amatsyah.
[2 Chronicles] [26]:[2] Uziyah restored Eylot City to Yehudah (Judah) and rebuilt it after his father’s death.
[2 Chronicles] [26]:[3] Uziyah was sixteen when he became king, and he reigned from Yerushalem (Jerusalem) for fifty-two years. His mother was Yekaleyah from Yerushalem.
[2 Chronicles] [26]:[4] He did the things that Yahweh said were good, like his father Amatsyah had done.
[2 Chronicles] [26]:[5] He strived to follow God during the lifetime of Zekaryah (Zechariah), who instructed him. During the time that he obeyed Yahweh, God made him successful.
[2 Chronicles] [26]:[6] Uziyah went to attack the Pelishtim, and successfully broke through the walls at Gat, Yavneh, and Ashdod. He rebuilt Ashdod and other cities in the Peleshet region.
[2 Chronicles] [26]:[7] God helped him against the Pelishtim, against the Aravim who were living in Gur-Ba’al, and against the Meunim.
[2 Chronicles] [26]:[8] The Amonim paid tribute to Uziyah, and his fame spread as far as the Mitsri (Egyptian) border because he was becoming more powerful.
[2 Chronicles] [26]:[9] King Uziyah built fortified towers in Yerushalem at the Corner Gate, the Valley Gate, and at the angle in the wall.
[2 Chronicles] [26]:[10] He also built towers in the wilderness, and dug a lot of wells, because he had a lot of cattle—both in the lowlands and in the plains. He was also interested in horticulture, so he had workers stationed in his vineyards and in his fertile fields.
[2 Chronicles] [26]:[11] Uziyah’s army was trained for fighting battles, and organised into divisions set up by Yeiel the scribe and the commander Ma’aseyah, under the supervision of Hananyah, one of the king’s officials.
[2 Chronicles] [26]:[12] There were 2,600 clan leaders who led the powerful warriors,
[2 Chronicles] [26]:[13] and the full force of 37,500 was under their authority, to support the king against his enemies.
[2 Chronicles] [26]:[14] Uziyah supplied shields, spears, helmets, armoured vests, bows, and slingshots for the entire army.
[2 Chronicles] [26]:[15] Using a local invention, he made war machines in Yerushalem to be placed on the towers and corners of the walls to fire arrows and large stones. His fame now spread widely because he’d received a lot of help that had made him very powerful.
[2 Chronicles] [26]:[16] However, at the peak of his strength, he became very arrogant, and that led to his destruction. He disobeyed his god Yahweh and went into the temple to burn incense on the incense altar.
[2 Chronicles] [26]:[17] The high priest Azaryah and eighty other brave priests went in after him.
[2 Chronicles] [26]:[18] They confronted King Uziyah and challenged him, “It’s not permitted for you, Uziyah, to sacrifice to Yahweh, only for Aharon’s (Aaron) descendants the priests—the ones consecrated to sacrifice. Leave the sanctuary, because you’ve disobeyed Yahweh God, so now he won’t honour you.”
[2 Chronicles] [26]:[19] Then Uziyah, who was holding an incense pan, became very angry, but when he started raging at the priests, spots of leprosy suddenly appeared on his forehead while he was still there beside the incense altar in front of the priests.
[2 Chronicles] [26]:[20] The high priest Azaryah looked more closely, and confirming that it was indeed leprosy on his forehead, hurried him outside. The king was now also in a hurry, because Yahweh had afflicted him.
[2 Chronicles] [26]:[21] King Uziyah had leprosy until he died, so he had to live in an isolated residence and wasn’t allowed to approach the temple. His son Yotam (Jotham) stood in for him—supervising the palace and ruling Yehudah (Judah).
[2 Chronicles] [26]:[22] The record of all the other things Uziyah did while he was king was written by the prophet Yeshayah (Isaiah) (son of Amots).
[2 Chronicles] [26]:[23] When Uziyah died, because of his leprosy they buried him with his ancestors in a royal grave in the countryside, and his son Yotam replaced him as king.
[2 Chronicles] [27]:[1] Yotam (Jotham) was twenty-five when he became king, and he reigned from Yerushalem (Jerusalem) for sixteen years. His mother was Yerusha, daughter of the priest Tsadok.
[2 Chronicles] [27]:[2] He did the things that Yahweh said were good like his father Uziyah had done (except that he didn’t trespass in Yahweh’s temple). However, the people were still behaving corruptly.
[2 Chronicles] [27]:[3] He rebuilt the temple’s Upper Gate and extended the Ofel wall.
[2 Chronicles] [27]:[4] He built cities in the Yehudah (Judah) hill country, and built fortresses and towers in the forests.
