[2 Chronicles] [27]:[5] He attacked the Amonim’ king and dominated them. Then for the next three years, the Amonim brought him three tonnes of silver, and 2,000 tonnes each of wheat and barley each year.
[2 Chronicles] [27]:[6] Yotam became more powerful because he’d established a pattern of obeying his god Yahweh.
[2 Chronicles] [27]:[7] The record of all the other things Yotam did while he was king, including all his battles, was written on the scroll ‘The kings of Yisrael (Israel) and Yehudah’.
[2 Chronicles] [27]:[8] He was twenty-five when he became king, and he reigned from Yerushalem for sixteen years.
[2 Chronicles] [27]:[9] Then (at forty-one years old), Yotam died and was buried in ‘The City of David’, and his son Ahaz replaced him as king.
[2 Chronicles] [28]:[1] Ahaz was twenty-five when he became king, and he reigned from Yerushalem (Jerusalem) for sixteen years, but he didn’t do what Yahweh wanted, like his ancestor David had.
[2 Chronicles] [28]:[2] Instead, he followed the example of Yisrael’s (Israel) kings, including casting metal idols for the Ba’al.
[2 Chronicles] [28]:[3] He offered incense in the Ben-Hinom valley and he burnt his children with fire, following the detestable customs of the nations that Yahweh had driven away as the Israelis had entered the region,
[2 Chronicles] [28]:[4] plus he offered sacrifices and burnt incense at the hilltop shrines, and on the hills, and under every large, green tree.
[2 Chronicles] [28]:[5] So his god Yahweh allowed King Ahaz to be defeated by Aram’s (Syria) king—they attacked and took many prisoners back to Damesek (Damascus). In addition, Yahweh allowed Yisrael’s (Israel) king to be victorious, and they slaughtered many fighters.
[2 Chronicles] [28]:[6] Yisrael’s King Pekah (Remalyah’s son) killed 120,000 powerful warriors in Yehudah (Judah) in one day, after they’d abandoned their ancestors’ god.
[2 Chronicles] [28]:[7] A warrior from Efrayim (Ephraim) named Zikri killed King Ahaz’s son Ma’aseyah, Azrikam the palace supervisor, and Elkanah the king’s second-in-command.
[2 Chronicles] [28]:[8] Yisrael’s soldiers captured two-hundred thousand of their relatives, including their wives and children. They also took a lot of plunder back to Shomron (Samaria) with them.
[2 Chronicles] [28]:[9] Now there was a prophet of Yahweh named Oded, and he went out to Yisrael’s (Israel) army as it was returning to Shomron (Samaria), and told them, “Listen, your ancestors’ god, Yahweh, was angry with Yehudah (Judah), so he helped you defeat them. However, you people killed them in rage, and God has taken notice.
[2 Chronicles] [28]:[10] Now you want to keep the people of Yerushalem (Jerusalem) and Yehudah as your own male and female slaves, but that would certainly make you people guilty in your god Yahweh’s view.
[2 Chronicles] [28]:[11] So then, listen to me and return those captives, because they’re your own relatives, and Yahweh is extremely angry at you people.”
[2 Chronicles] [28]:[12] Then some of the leaders of the Efrayim (Ephraim) tribe took action and confronted those returning from battle: Azaryah (Yehohanan’s son), Berekyah (Meshilemot’s son), Yehizkiyah (Shalum’s son), and Amasa (Hadlay’s son)
[2 Chronicles] [28]:[13] told the ones returning, “Don’t bring those captives here, because that would be disobedience, and add to the rest of our disobedience and wrongdoing, because Yahweh’s already angry at us here in Yisrael.”
[2 Chronicles] [28]:[14] So the returning soldiers released the captives in front of the leaders and all the assembled people, and dropped all the plunder there as well.
[2 Chronicles] [28]:[15] Then some men from Yisrael were called out by name to come and search the plunder to find clothes and dress the naked captives from Yehudah and give them sandals. Then they gave them food and drink, as well as oil to rub on their wounds. They gave donkeys to those who couldn’t easily walk, and took them to Yeriho (Jericho) (Yeriho, the Palm City) which was nearer their relatives, then those men returned to Shomron.
[2 Chronicles] [28]:[16] Around that time, King Ahaz requested help from the Assyrian kings,
[2 Chronicles] [28]:[17] because the Edomim had been and attacked Yehudah and taken captives.
[2 Chronicles] [28]:[18] Also the Pelishtim had raided the lowland cities and the Negev, and they’d captured Beyt-Shemesh (Heliopolis), Ayalon, and Gederot, as well as Sokoh, Timnah, and Gimzo with their surrounding villages,
[2 Chronicles] [28]:[19] because Yahweh was humbling Yehudah because King Ahaz had thrown off restraint there and been very unfaithful to Yahweh.
[2 Chronicles] [28]:[20] So the Assyrian King Tiglat-Pileser came, but he ended up adding to his troubles rather than helping.
[2 Chronicles] [28]:[21] Ahaz gave the Assyrian king valuables from the temple and the palace and from other leaders, but that didn’t help.
[2 Chronicles] [28]:[22] While King Ahaz was experiencing those troubles, he disobeyed Yahweh even more
[2 Chronicles] [28]:[23] and sacrificed to the gods of Damesek (Damascus) (because Aram (Syria) had defeated him). He reasoned, “Since the gods of the Aramean kings helped them, I’ll sacrifice to them, and then they’ll help me.” However, that led to Ahaz’s fall, and to the fall of all of Yehudah (Judah).
[2 Chronicles] [28]:[24] Then Ahaz gathered all the furnishings that were used in the temple, and broke them into pieces and locked the temple doors. Then he set up pagan altars at every Yerushalem (Jerusalem) intersection,
[2 Chronicles] [28]:[25] and in every Yehudah city he set up hilltop shrines to make sacrifices to other gods, thus angering Yahweh, his ancestors’ god.
[2 Chronicles] [28]:[26] The record of all the other things Ahaz did while he was king was written on the scroll ‘The kings of Yehudah and Yisrael’ (Israel).
[2 Chronicles] [28]:[27] Then Ahaz died and was buried in ‘The City of David’, but not in the tombs of the other kings of Yisrael. Then his son Hizkiyah (Hezekiah) replaced him as king.
[2 Chronicles] [29]:[1] Hizkiyah (Hezekiah) was twenty-five when he became king, and he reigned from Yerushalem (Jerusalem) for twenty-nine years. His mother was Zekaryah’s (Zechariah) daughter Aviyah.
[2 Chronicles] [29]:[2] He did what pleased Yahweh, like his ancestor King David had done.
[2 Chronicles] [29]:[3] In the very first month of his reign, he unlocked the temple doors and repaired them.
[2 Chronicles] [29]:[4] Then he summoned the priests and the Levites, assembled them in the eastern temple courtyard,
[2 Chronicles] [29]:[5] and told them, “Now you Levites, listen to me. You need to consecrate yourselves now, and consecrate the residence of Yahweh, your ancestors’ god, and remove any defilement from the sacred place,
[2 Chronicles] [29]:[6] because our ancestors were unfaithful and disobeyed our god Yahweh. Then they abandoned him, lost interest in this temple, and turned their back on it all.
[2 Chronicles] [29]:[7] They extinguished the lamps and locked the temple up. After that, they didn’t burn any incense or offer any burnt sacrifices in the sacred place of Yisrael’s (Israel) god.
[2 Chronicles] [29]:[8] That’s why Yahweh was angry at Yerushalem and all of Yehudah (Judah), and allowed us to become a place of terror and horror and scorn, as you’ve all seen with your own eyes.
[2 Chronicles] [29]:[9] As a result, our fathers died in battle, and our wives and children have been captured and taken to other countries.
[2 Chronicles] [29]:[10] Now I sincerely want to make an agreement with Yisrael’s god Yahweh, so that his fierce anger will turn away from us.
[2 Chronicles] [29]:[11] So lads, don’t mess around, because Yahweh has chosen you to stand in his presence to serve him, and to be ministering and burning incense.
[2 Chronicles] [29]:[12] Then these Levites took action: from the Kohatites: Mahat (Amasay’s son) and Yoel (Joel) (Azaryah’s son), from the descendants of Merari: Kish (Avdi’s son) and Azaryah (Yehalel’el’s son), from the Gershonim: Yoah (Zimah’s son) and Eden (Yoah’s son),
[2 Chronicles] [29]:[13] from Elitsafan’s descendants: Shimri and Yeiel, from Asaf’s descendants: Zekaryah (Zechariah) and Matanyah,
[2 Chronicles] [29]:[14] from Heyman’s descendants: Yehiel and Shimei, and from Yedutun’s descendants: Shemayah and Uziel.
[2 Chronicles] [29]:[15] They assembled their relatives and consecrated themselves, then they entered the temple to purify it, as the king had ordered as a result of Yahweh’s message.
[2 Chronicles] [29]:[16] The priests entered the inner part of the temple to purify it, and they took everything they found that shouldn’t be in there and brought it out to the temple courtyard, and then the Levites took it all out to be burnt, down in the Kidron valley.
[2 Chronicles] [29]:[17] They began the purification at the beginning of March and worked outwards, reaching the porch by the eighth, and then it took eight more days for the courtyard, so they finished on the sixteenth.
[2 Chronicles] [29]:[18] Then they reported to King Hizkiyah (Hezekiah), “We’ve purified the whole of Yahweh’s temple, including the altar for burnt offerings and all its utensils, and the bread display table and all its utensils.
[2 Chronicles] [29]:[19] We’ve prepared and consecrated all the items which King Ahaz rejected during his unfaithful reign, and they’re back in front of Yahweh’s altar.”
[2 Chronicles] [29]:[20] Early the next morning, King Hizkiyah (Hezekiah) assembled the city officials and went to Yahweh’s residence,
[2 Chronicles] [29]:[21] taking seven bulls, seven rams, seven male lambs, and seven male goats to be a sin offering for the kingdom, the sanctuary, and Yehudah (Judah). He instructed the priests (Aharon’s (Aaron) descendants) to sacrifice the animals to Yahweh on the altar.
[2 Chronicles] [29]:[22] So they slaughtered the bulls and took the blood and sprinkled it on the altar. Then they did the same for the rams, and then the lambs.
[2 Chronicles] [29]:[23] Finally, they brought the goats for the sin offering to the front, and the king and the people placed their hands on them,
[2 Chronicles] [29]:[24] and then the priests slaughtered them and splashed their blood on the altar so Yahweh would forgive all of Yisrael’s (Israel) disobedience. (The king had ordered the burnt offerings and the sin offering be for all of Yisrael.)
[2 Chronicles] [29]:[25] Then he told the Levites to stand in the temple with cymbals, harps, and lyres—obeying what David and his prophets Gad and Natan (Nathan) had commanded. (Yahweh had actually given those orders through his prophets.)
[2 Chronicles] [29]:[26] The Levites stood with David’s instruments, and the priests with their trumpets,
[2 Chronicles] [29]:[27] then Hizkiyah said to offer the burnt offering on the altar. When they started to slaughter the animals, the people sang and praised Yahweh as the trumpets were blown and the other instruments played.
[2 Chronicles] [29]:[28] The entire assembly were bowing down and worshipping as the singers sang and the trumpeters played, until the burnt offering was completed,
[2 Chronicles] [29]:[29] then the king and everyone with him bowed down and worshipped.
[2 Chronicles] [29]:[30] Then King Hizkiyah and his officials ordered the Levites to sing praises to Yahweh using compositions by David and the prophet Asaf, so they cheerfully sang praises and bowed down and worshipped.
[2 Chronicles] [29]:[31] Then Hizkiyah responded, “You’ve consecrated yourselves to Yahweh, so come near and bring your sacrifices and thanksgiving gifts into Yahweh’s house.” So the assembly brought in their sacrifices and thanksgiving gifts, plus those who wanted to brought their sacrifices to be burnt.
[2 Chronicles] [29]:[32] Altogether they brought seventy bulls, a hundred rams, and two hundred lambs to be completely burnt on the altar,
[2 Chronicles] [29]:[33] as well as six hundred bulls and three thousand sheep as dedicated offerings.
[2 Chronicles] [29]:[34] There weren’t enough priests to skin all the burnt offerings, so their relatives the Levites helped them until the work was finished and until all the priests had consecrated themselves, because the Levites had worked quicker to consecrate themselves than the priests had.
[2 Chronicles] [29]:[35] In addition to the burnt offerings, there was the fat from the peace offerings, and there were drink offerings. So the service in Yahweh’s temple was reinstituted,
[2 Chronicles] [29]:[36] and Hizkiyah and all the people celebrated about what God had prepared for the people, because it had all happened fairly quickly.
[2 Chronicles] [30]:[1] Then King Hizkiyah (Hezekiah) sent invitations to all of Yisrael (Israel) and Yehudah (Judah) (including Efrayim (Ephraim) and Menasheh (Manasseh)) to come to Yahweh’s temple,
[2 Chronicles] [30]:[2] because the king had consulted with his officials and the whole assembly in Yerushalem (Jerusalem) and decided to have a late celebration of the Passover in April.
[2 Chronicles] [30]:[3] (They couldn’t have done it at the proper time because the priests hadn’t consecrated themselves sufficiently then, and so the people hadn’t gathered in Yerushalem.)
[2 Chronicles] [30]:[4] The plan pleased the king and all the people,
[2 Chronicles] [30]:[5] so they sent messages across all of Yisrael and Yehudah, from Be’er-Sheva (Beersheba) in the south to Dan in the far north, for the people to come to Yerushalem to celebrate the Passover to honour Yisrael’s god Yahweh. (They hadn’t previously been observing the written instructions.)
[2 Chronicles] [30]:[6] Runners took the letters from the king and his officials, going to all of Yisrael and Yehudah with the king’s command: “Descendants of Yisrael, return to Yahweh, the god of Avraham, Yitshak (Isaac), and Yisrael, and he’ll return to you—the group that escaped from the control of the Assyrian kings.
[2 Chronicles] [30]:[7] Don’t be like your fathers and brothers who weren’t faithful to Yahweh, their ancestors’ god, provoking him to leave them decimated, as you can see.
[2 Chronicles] [30]:[8] So don’t be stubborn like your ancestors were. Obey Yahweh and come to the sanctuary that he’s consecrated forever, and serve your god Yahweh so he’ll turn his anger away from you.
[2 Chronicles] [30]:[9] If you descendants of Yisrael return to Yahweh, your brothers and sons will be shown mercy by their captors and be able to return to this land, because your god Yahweh is gracious and compassionate, and he won’t ignore you if you’ll turn back to him.
[2 Chronicles] [30]:[10] The messengers went from city to city in the Efrayim (Ephraim) and Menasheh (Manasseh) regions, as far north as Zevulun, but many people there laughed at them and mocked them.
[2 Chronicles] [30]:[11] However, some of the people from Asher, Menasheh, and Zevulun humbled themselves and went to Yerushalem.
[2 Chronicles] [30]:[12] Also in Yehudah, God moved the people to want to obey the king and his officials and Yahweh’s instructions.
[2 Chronicles] [30]:[13] The next month, a huge crowd gathered in Yerushalem (Jerusalem) to celebrate the Festival of Flat Bread.
[2 Chronicles] [30]:[14] They took action and removed the altars to Ba’al in Yerushalem, and all the incense altars, and threw them down into the Kidron valley to be burnt there.
[2 Chronicles] [30]:[15] In the middle of the month, they slaughtered the Passover lambs. The priests and Levites had been ashamed, so they’d consecrated themselves, then they brought the burnt offerings into the temple.
[2 Chronicles] [30]:[16] They stood at their stations, following the instructions written by Mosheh (Moses), then the Levites handed the bowls of blood to the priests to sprinkle on the altar.
[2 Chronicles] [30]:[17] Because many people in the assembly hadn’t consecrated themselves, the Levites assisted them by slaughtering the lambs and consecrating them to Yahweh.
[2 Chronicles] [30]:[18] Although most of the people who’d travelled down from Efrayim (Ephraim), Menasheh (Manasseh), Yisakar (Issachar), and Zevulun hadn’t purified themselves, they ate the Passover food anyway despite the written instructions, because Hizkiyah (Hezekiah) had prayed to Yahweh for them, “May Yahweh, who is good, declare as innocent
[2 Chronicles] [30]:[19] everyone who sincerely wants to honour and obey Yahweh, their ancestors’ god, even if they haven’t completed the formal purification ceremonies for the temple.”
[2 Chronicles] [30]:[20] Yahweh took notice of Hizkiyah’s request, and forgave the people,
[2 Chronicles] [30]:[21] so the Israelis who’d come to Yerushalem celebrated the Festival of Flat Bread for seven days with great excitement. The Levites and priests enthusiastically praised Yahweh every day using their musical instruments.
[2 Chronicles] [30]:[22] Hizkiyah sincerely thanked all the Levites who were very insightful about worshipping Yahweh. Then everyone ate for the prescribed seven days—sacrificing peace offerings and confessing to Yahweh, their ancestors’ god.
[2 Chronicles] [30]:[23] Then the whole group decided to celebrate for seven more days, so they enthusiastically celebrated for another whole week,
[2 Chronicles] [30]:[24] because Yehudah’s (Judah) King Hizkiyah (Hezekiah) had provided a thousand bulls and seven thousand sheep for the people, and the officials had also contributed another thousand bulls and ten thousand sheep. Many more priests also consecrated themselves.
[2 Chronicles] [30]:[25] All the people from Yehudah celebrated, including the priests and Levites, and everyone who’d come down from Yisrael (Israel) to stay in Yehudah (whether just for the occasion, or to live permanently), plus others living in Yehudah.
[2 Chronicles] [30]:[26] Everyone in Yerushalem (Jerusalem) was very happy, because nothing like that had happened in Yerushalem since the time when David’s son Shelomoh (Solomon) was king.
[2 Chronicles] [30]:[27] Finally, the priests and Levites stood up and prayed a blessing on the people, and their voice was heard because their prayer reached God’s holy residence in the heavens.
[2 Chronicles] [31]:[1] When that was all over, all those Israelis went out to Yehudah’s (Judah) cities and shattered the pillars and cut down the Asherah poles, and they tore down the hilltop shrines and altars from the entire Yehudah-Benyamin region, and also up in the Efrayim-Menasheh region. Once they’d finished that, they all returned to their own land and cities.
[2 Chronicles] [31]:[2] King Hizkiyah (Hezekiah) allocated the priests and Levites into divisions for the various different types of duties: for doing burnt offerings and peace offerings, for other services, and for thanksgiving and praise at the temple gates.
[2 Chronicles] [31]:[3] The king contributed some of his own funds for burnt offerings to be sacrificed each morning and evening, as well as for the Rest Days and the New Moon celebrations, and on the other special days as per the written instructions that had come from Yahweh.
[2 Chronicles] [31]:[4] He told the people living in Yerushalem (Jerusalem) to give the prescribed portions to the priests and Levites, so that they could focus on serving Yahweh,
[2 Chronicles] [31]:[5] and as soon as the message reached them, the Israelis started giving the first portions of their harvests of grain, new wine, oil, and honey, and of all the produce from the countryside, so they brought a tenth of the harvests of all their crops.
[2 Chronicles] [31]:[6] The people from Yisrael (Israel) and Yehudah who were living in Yehudah’s cities also brought a tenth of their cattle and sheep, as well as a sacred tenth consecrated to their god Yahweh, and it was all put in big piles.
[2 Chronicles] [31]:[7] That all began in May and was finished by September,
[2 Chronicles] [31]:[8] and when King Hizkiyah and his officials came and saw the piles, they praised Yahweh and his Israeli people.
[2 Chronicles] [31]:[9] When Hizkiyah asked the priests and Levites about the piles,
[2 Chronicles] [31]:[10] Azaryah the chief priest (a descendant of Tsadok) told him, “Since the people started bringing their contributions to the temple, we’ve been eating well, and even had left-overs, because Yahweh has blessed his people, and all this is the remainder.”
[2 Chronicles] [31]:[11] So then Hizkiyah ordered them to prepare the temple storerooms, which they did,
[2 Chronicles] [31]:[12] and they brought in the contributions and the tenths that had been given, and the things faithfully dedicated to Yahweh. A Levite, Konaniyah, was appointed as supervisor, with his brother Shimei as deputy.
[2 Chronicles] [31]:[13] Those two supervised Yehiel, Azazyah, Nahat, Asahel, Yerimot, Yozavad, Eliel, Yismakyah, Mahat, and Benayah, by the arrangement of King Hizkiyah and Azaryah the temple supervisor.
[2 Chronicles] [31]:[14] The Levite Yimnah’s son, Kore, who guarded the temple’s eastern gate, was put in charge of the free-will offering to God—to distribute those offerings that were made to Yahweh, as well as any consecrated items.
[2 Chronicles] [31]:[15] Eden, Minyamin, Yeshua, Shemayah, Amaryah, and Shekanyah faithfully assisted him in the priests’ cities to distribute those things to the different divisions of priests, regardless of their status or size.
[2 Chronicles] [31]:[16] Every male who was at least three years old, and was listed in the genealogical records, received a portion for their service in the temple, as each division performed their assigned duties.
[2 Chronicles] [31]:[17] Each priestly clan kept genealogical records and received a portion, and so did the Levites who were at least twenty years old, all according to their divisions,
[2 Chronicles] [31]:[18] as well as their wives and young children, and sons and daughters whose names were on the genealogies, because they’d also faithfully consecrated themselves for the sacred work.
[2 Chronicles] [31]:[19] Also, there were people chosen by name to give a portion to each male among Aharon’s (Aaron) descendants, the priests, who had pasture land around their cities, as well as to each Levite included on the genealogical records.
[2 Chronicles] [31]:[20] So King Hizkiyah did that throughout Yehudah (Judah), and he continued to faithfully follow his god Yahweh’s instructions.
[2 Chronicles] [31]:[21] He tried hard to be diligent and sincere in whatever he did for the temple operation, as he followed God’s rules and commands, and he prospered.
[2 Chronicles] [32]:[1] After all those acts of faithfulness by Hizkiyah (Hezekiah), the Assyrian King Sanheriv (Sennacherib) invaded Yehudah (Judah). He besieged the fortified cities and prepared to capture them for himself.
[2 Chronicles] [32]:[2] When King Hizkiyah saw that Sanheriv had entered the country and clearly intended to attack Yerushalem (Jerusalem),
[2 Chronicles] [32]:[3] he consulted with his officials and army leaders about blocking up the springs outside the city, and they helped him.
[2 Chronicles] [32]:[4] Many people gathered and blocked the springs from feeding the stream that flowed through the area, saying, “Why should the Assyrian kings come and find plenty of water?”
[2 Chronicles] [32]:[5] Then he strengthened his fortifications, repairing broken sections of the wall, and built towers and an outer wall. He strengthened the supporting wall on the east side of ‘The City of David’. He also manufactured many weapons and shields,
[2 Chronicles] [32]:[6] and he appointed army commanders and assembled them at the plaza by the city gate, and encouraged them with these words,
[2 Chronicles] [32]:[7] “Be strong and be courageous. Don’t be scared or discouraged because of the Assyrian king, or by his massive army, because we have someone on our side who’s more powerful than him.
[2 Chronicles] [32]:[8] They can only rely on human strength, but we have our god Yahweh to help us and fight our battles for us.” So the people took strength from King Hizkiyah’s encouragement.
[2 Chronicles] [32]:[9] Later, when the Assyrian King Sanheriv was surrounding Lakish city with his army, he sent some servants to Yerushalem, to Yehudah’s (Judah) King Hizkiyah and all the residents, saying,
[2 Chronicles] [32]:[10] “I,Sanheriv, the king of Ashur (Assyria), am asking what you’re all trusting in as you’re staying there in Yerushalem while it’s besieged.
[2 Chronicles] [32]:[11] Hizkiyah tells you, ‘Our god Yahweh will rescue us from the Assyrian king,’ but he’s misleading you, and you’ll all die of hunger and thirst!
[2 Chronicles] [32]:[12] Wasn’t it Hizkiyah who removed his hilltop shrines and his altars, and spoke to the people of Yerushalem and all of Yehudah, telling you to bow down at only one altar and offer sacrifices on it?
[2 Chronicles] [32]:[13] Don’t you people know what my ancestors and I have done to the people groups from other countries? Were any of their gods able to save them from me?
[2 Chronicles] [32]:[14] Which one of those nations’ gods which my ancestors destroyed is a precedent showing that your god can rescue anyone from me?
[2 Chronicles] [32]:[15] So don’t let Hizkiyah deceive you or mislead you like this. Don’t believe him, because no god of any nation or kingdom has been able to save his people from my ancestors or from me. So your god certainly won’t be able to protect you from my army.
[2 Chronicles] [32]:[16] Then Sanheriv’s servants said even more against the god Yahweh, and against his servant Hizkiyah,
[2 Chronicles] [32]:[17] plus he wrote letters insulting Yisrael’s (Israel) god Yahweh and speaking against him, writing, “Just like the other nations’ gods couldn’t save their people from me, so too Hizkiyah’s god won’t be able to protect his people from my strength.”
[2 Chronicles] [32]:[18] Then the Assyrians shouted loud threats in Hebrew to the people of Yerushalem who were on the wall, to try to frighten and terrify them so they could capture the city—
[2 Chronicles] [32]:[19] telling them Yerushalem’s god was just another god made by people, and just as useless as other countries’ gods.
[2 Chronicles] [32]:[20] Then King Hizkiyah and Yeshayah (Isaiah) (son of the prophet Amots) called out to the heavens requesting God’s help,
[2 Chronicles] [32]:[21] and Yahweh sent a messenger who destroyed the powerful warriors, and the leaders and chiefs in the Assyrian army, and then their king had to return home in shame. When he went into the temple of his god, some of his sons ran him through with a sword.
[2 Chronicles] [32]:[22] So that’s how Yahweh saved Hizkiyah and Yerushalem’s inhabitants from the Assyrian King Sanheriv, and from the power of other nations, and he gave them peace on all sides.
[2 Chronicles] [32]:[23] Many people came to Yerushalem to bring offerings for Yahweh and valuable gifts for Yehudah’s (Judah) King Hizkiyah, and after all that, he was highly respected by the other nations.
[2 Chronicles] [32]:[24] Some time afterwards, King Hizkiyah (Hezekiah) became very sick and was expected to die, but he prayed to Yahweh, and Yahweh answered him with a miracle.
[2 Chronicles] [32]:[25] However, Hizkiyah was very proud and didn’t thank Yahweh, so his anger fell on Yerushalem (Jerusalem) and Yehudah (Judah).
[2 Chronicles] [32]:[26] Then Hizkiyah and Yerushalem’s inhabitants humbled themselves, and so Yahweh’s anger didn’t affect them during Hizkiyah’s lifetime.
[2 Chronicles] [32]:[27] King Hizkiyah (Hezekiah) had become very wealthy, and he was highly respected. He established treasuries for gold and silver, for gemstones and spices, and for shields and other valuable things,
[2 Chronicles] [32]:[28] as well as storehouses for grain, wine, and olive oil, and stalls for his flocks and all kinds of livestock.
[2 Chronicles] [32]:[29] He built cities for himself, and acquired large numbers of sheep and goats, and also cattle, because God had made him very prosperous.
[2 Chronicles] [32]:[30] Hizkiyah blocked off the upper outlet at the Gihon spring and directed the water down the western side of ‘The City of David’. All his projects were successful,
[2 Chronicles] [32]:[31] and so when the Babylonian leaders sent messengers to ask about the miracle that had been done in the country, God left him alone to test him and see what he really believed.
[2 Chronicles] [32]:[32] The record of all the other things Hizkiyah (Hezekiah) did while he was king, which includes a record of his loyal commitment, was written on the scroll ‘The kings of Yehudah (Judah) and Yisrael’ (Israel).
[2 Chronicles] [32]:[33] Then Hizkiyah died and was buried in the upper tombs with David’s other descendants, and everyone in Yerushalem (Jerusalem) and across Yehudah honoured him. Then his son Menasheh (Manasseh) replaced him as king.
[2 Chronicles] [33]:[1] Menasheh (Manasseh) was twelve when he became king, and he reigned from Yerushalem (Jerusalem) for fifty-five years.
[2 Chronicles] [33]:[2] He did was what Yahweh had said was evil, like the disgusting things of the people groups that Yahweh had driven out ahead of the Israelis.
[2 Chronicles] [33]:[3] The hilltop shrines that his father Hizkiyah (Hezekiah) had torn down, he turned around and rebuilt them and erected altars to the Baals, and he made Asherah poles, and he bowed down to all the stars in the sky and served them.
[2 Chronicles] [33]:[4] He built altars in Yahweh’s temple in Yerushalem that Yahweh had previously said that his name would always be associated with.
[2 Chronicles] [33]:[5] He built altars for all the stars in the sky in both of the temple courtyards,
[2 Chronicles] [33]:[6] and he made his sons pass through the fire in the Ben-Hinom valley, and he practiced fortune-telling and sorcery and magic, and connected with mediums and spirits. He did so much evil in Yahweh’s eyes that it provoked him into getting angry.
[2 Chronicles] [33]:[7] He made an idol and put it in the temple, yes, where God had told David and his son Shelomoh (Solomon), “My name will be associated with that building forever, there in Yerushalem, which was chosen from among all of Yisrael’s (Israel) tribes.
[2 Chronicles] [33]:[8] If Yisrael will be careful to do everything that I’ve instructed them and follow all the regulations and statutes that were given to them through Mosheh (Moses), then I won’t force them to leave the land again that I gave to their ancestors.”
[2 Chronicles] [33]:[9] So Menasheh led Yerushalem’s inhabitants astray, and all of Yehudah (Judah)—doing more evil than the nations that Yahweh had destroyed ahead of the Israelis.
[2 Chronicles] [33]:[10] Then Yahweh spoke to King Menasheh and his people, but they paid no attention,
[2 Chronicles] [33]:[11] so Yahweh brought in the Assyrian king’s army leaders and they captured Menasheh. They put a hook in his nose and bronze chains around his feet, and they took him away to Bavel (Babylon).
[2 Chronicles] [33]:[12] When he was there suffering, he humbled himself in the presence of his ancestors’ god Yahweh, and pleaded with him for help.
[2 Chronicles] [33]:[13] When he prayed, Yahweh listened to him and answered his request and brought him back to Yerushalem to his kingdom. Then Menasheh realised that Yahweh really is God.
[2 Chronicles] [33]:[14] After that, he rebuilt the outer wall for ‘The City of David’ on the west of Gihon to the Fish Gate and around the hill—also making it higher. Then he stationed army commanders in all of Yehudah’s fortified cities.
[2 Chronicles] [33]:[15] He removed the foreign gods and idols from the temple, as well as all the altars that he’d built on the temple mount and throughout Yerushalem, and he dumped them all outside the city.
[2 Chronicles] [33]:[16] Then he rebuilt Yahweh’s altar and sacrificed peace offerings and thank offerings on it, and he told Yehudah to serve Yisrael’s god Yahweh.
[2 Chronicles] [33]:[17] However, the people continued to offer sacrifices at the hilltop shrines, but now only to their god Yahweh.
[2 Chronicles] [33]:[18] The record of all the other things Menasheh did while he was king, including his prayer to his god and the messages spoken to him by the prophets, was written on the scroll ‘The kings of Yisrael’ (Israel).
[2 Chronicles] [33]:[19] It’s written in ‘The Words of Hozay’ about his disobedience and unfaithful activities, and how he built the hilltop shrines and Asherah poles and idols before he humbled himself, as well as the response to his pleading in his prayer.
[2 Chronicles] [33]:[20] Then Menasheh died and was buried at his palace, and his son Amon replaced him as king.
[2 Chronicles] [33]:[21] Amon was twenty-two when he became king, and he ruled from Yerushalem (Jerusalem) for two years.
[2 Chronicles] [33]:[22] He did what Yahweh had said was evil, just like his father Menasheh (Manasseh) had done, and he sacrificed to all the idols his father had made, and served them.
[2 Chronicles] [33]:[23] He didn’t humble himself and turn to Yahweh like his father had, so Amon’s guilt was even worse.
[2 Chronicles] [33]:[24] Then Amon’s servants conspired against him, and assassinated him in his palace,
[2 Chronicles] [33]:[25] but the local people executed everyone who’d conspired against King Amon, and made his son Yoshiyah (Josiah) king in his place.
[2 Chronicles] [34]:[1] Yoshiyah (Josiah) was eight when he became king, and he reigned from Yerushalem (Jerusalem) for thirty-one years.
[2 Chronicles] [34]:[2] He did what Yahweh had said was right, and made similar decisions to his ancestor David—not deviating to the right or the left.
[2 Chronicles] [34]:[3] In the eighth year of his reign, while he was still a teenager, he began to learn more about the god of his ancestor David, and in the twelfth year, he began to remove the hilltop shrines from Yerushalem and across Yehudah (Judah), as well as the Asherah poles, and the carved and cast metal idols.
[2 Chronicles] [34]:[4] He watched while they tore down the altars for the Baals and cut down the incense altars that were above them. He shattered the Asherah poles and the idols, then crushed them to powder, which he scattered over the graves of the people who’d sacrificed to them.
[2 Chronicles] [34]:[5] He burnt the bones of those priests on their altars, and that’s how he purified Yerushalem and all of Yehudah,
[2 Chronicles] [34]:[6] as well as the cities in the tribes of Menasheh (Manasseh), Efrayim (Ephraim), Shim’on (Simeon), and as far north as Naftali (Naphtali), including in the ruins around them.
[2 Chronicles] [34]:[7] He tore down the altars and the Asherah poles, ground the idols into pieces, and cut down the incense altars in all of Yisrael (Israel), before returning to Yerushalem.
[2 Chronicles] [34]:[8] In his eighteenth year as king, in order to purify the land and the temple, he sent Atsalyah’s son Shafan, Ma’aseyah the city official, and Yo’ahaz’s son Yoah the secretary, to repair his god Yahweh’s residence.
[2 Chronicles] [34]:[9] They went to Hilkiyah the high priest and handed over the funds that had been donated for God’s house, which had been collected by the Levites as doorkeepers—the money was from the tribes of Menasheh, Efrayim, and other places in the northern kingdom of Yisrael, as well as from Yerushalem’s inhabitants and people across all of Yehudah and Benyamin.
[2 Chronicles] [34]:[10] The priests then paid the workers who’d been assigned to work in Yahweh’s temple to repair and strengthen it.
[2 Chronicles] [34]:[11] They also paid the carpenters and builders to buy cut stone and timber for the beams and braces which Yehudah’s kings had allowed to deteriorate,
[2 Chronicles] [34]:[12] and the workers did their work faithfully. Their supervisors were Yahat and Ovadyah (Obadiah) (Levites descended from Merari), as well as Zekaryah (Zechariah) and Meshulam (descendants of Levi’s son Kohat), and all the Levites who were good on their musical instruments.
[2 Chronicles] [34]:[13] They also supervised the porters and people working on various other tasks. Some of the Levites were secretaries, officials, and guards.
[2 Chronicles] [34]:[14] When they were bringing the money out of the temple, Hilkiyah the high priest found a scroll containing Yahweh’s instructions that had been given via Mosheh (Moses).
[2 Chronicles] [34]:[15] Hilkiyah informed the scribe Shafan that he’d found a Torah scroll in the temple, and he gave him the scroll.
[2 Chronicles] [34]:[16] Shafan took the scroll with him to the king and reported to him, “Your servants are doing everything they were assigned to do.
[2 Chronicles] [34]:[17] They’ve taken the cash that was in Yahweh’s residence, and passed it on to the supervisors of the workers.”
[2 Chronicles] [34]:[18] Then Shafan told the king, “I’ve brought a scroll that the priest Hilkiyah gave me,” and then he started reading it out to the king.
[2 Chronicles] [34]:[19] When the king heard the words of God’s instructions, he tore his clothes in grief.
[2 Chronicles] [34]:[20] Then he commanded Hilkiyah, Shafan’s son Ahikam, Mikah’s son Avdon, Shafan himself, and the king’s special advisor Asayah,
[2 Chronicles] [34]:[21] “Go and ask Yahweh on my behalf, and on behalf of everyone in Yisrael (Israel) and Yehudah (Judah), what he wants us to do with respect to the instructions on the scroll that’s just been found, because it seems that Yahweh will be very angry at us because our ancestors haven’t followed all of Yahweh’s instructions as they’re written on that scroll.”
[2 Chronicles] [34]:[22] So Hilkiyah and the others went to Yerushalem’s (Jerusalem) Second District, to the prophetess Huldah (wife of Shalum, son of Tokahat, son of Hasrah who took care of the temple robes). They passed on the king’s question,
[2 Chronicles] [34]:[23] and she replied, “Yisrael’s god Yahweh says to tell the king:
[2 Chronicles] [34]:[24] Yahweh says, ‘Listen, I’m going to bring disaster on this place and its inhabitants, as per all the curses written on that scroll that was read to Yehudah’s king,
[2 Chronicles] [34]:[25] because they’ve abandoned me and offered incense to other gods. That’s made me angry, and so my rage will be poured out on this place, and it can’t be prevented.’
[2 Chronicles] [34]:[26] However, Yehudah’s king sent you all to ask for Yahweh’s direction, so tell him, ‘Yisrael’s god Yahweh says that after hearing the scroll’s words,
[2 Chronicles] [34]:[27] you were sincere, and you humbled yourself in front of God when you heard his words about this place and its inhabitants. Yes, Yahweh declares you’ve humbled yourself in front of me and torn your clothes, and wept in front of me, and I’ve personally heard you.
[2 Chronicles] [34]:[28] So listen, I’ll allow you to die and be buried in peace, and so your eyes won’t see the disaster that I’ll send to this place and its inhabitants.’ ” So they took that response back to the king.
[2 Chronicles] [34]:[29] Then the king summoned all the elders from Yerushalem (Jerusalem) and from across Yehudah,
[2 Chronicles] [34]:[30] and they all walked up to the temple, with the inhabitants of Yerushalem and all of Yehudah, and the priests and the Levites, and all the people, irrespective of their standing in the community. Then the king read everything out to them that was on the Torah scroll that had been found in the temple.
[2 Chronicles] [34]:[31] Then the king stood at his normal place and made an agreement with Yahweh: to obey Yahweh and follow his instructions and his regulations and statutes, sincerely and with all his energy—doing what was in the joint understanding that had been written on the scroll.
[2 Chronicles] [34]:[32] Then he had everyone from Yerushalem and Benyamin take a stand in agreement to it, and so Yerushalem’s inhabitants renewed their agreement with their ancestors’ god.
[2 Chronicles] [34]:[33] So King Yoshiyah (Josiah) removed all the disgusting idols from all the Israeli regions, and he made everyone in Yisrael (Israel) serve their god Yahweh—during his lifetime they never turned away from Yahweh, their ancestors’ god.
[2 Chronicles] [35]:[1] Then King Yoshiyah (Josiah) prepared a ‘pass-over’ celebration in Yerushalem (Jerusalem), and they slaughtered the lambs at the end of March.
[2 Chronicles] [35]:[2] He assigned the priests to the various tasks that needed to be done, and encouraged them to do their work well.
[2 Chronicles] [35]:[3] He told the Levites (they’d been separated from the other tribes in order to serve Yahweh) who were teaching all of Yisrael (Israel), “Place the sacred box in the house that was built by David’s son, Yisrael’s King Shelomoh (Solomon)—it won’t be a burden any more for your shoulders. Now serve your god Yahweh and his Israeli people,
[2 Chronicles] [35]:[4] and prepare yourselves in your clan divisions as per the instructions written by Yisrael’s King David and his son Shelomoh.
[2 Chronicles] [35]:[5] Then stand in the temple area, grouped by your clans and ready to help the other tribes.
[2 Chronicles] [35]:[6] Consecrate yourselves and slaughter the ‘pass-over’ lambs for the people as per the instructions given through Mosheh (Moses) by Yahweh.
[2 Chronicles] [35]:[7] King Yoshiyah provided thirty thousand lambs and young goats from his own flocks for the ‘pass-over’ sacrifices, and three thousand bulls from his own herds.
[2 Chronicles] [35]:[8] His officials also contributed for the benefit of the people, priests, and Levites. The chief temple officials Hilkiyah, Zekaryah (Zechariah), and Yehiel donated 2,600 lambs and three hundred cattle to the priests.
[2 Chronicles] [35]:[9] The Levite leaders Konaniyah and his younger brothers Shemayah and Netanel, along with Hashavyah, Yeiel, and Yozavad, together contributed five thousand lambs and three hundred bulls.
[2 Chronicles] [35]:[10] So everything was prepared as the king had commanded, and the priests stood at their places, and the Levites were there in their various divisions,
[2 Chronicles] [35]:[11] and they slaughtered the ‘pass-over’ lambs, then the priests sprinkled the blood while the Levites skinned the animals.
[2 Chronicles] [35]:[12] They set aside the animals to be burnt on the altar, in order to give them to the various family groups to offer to Yahweh, following the instructions Mosheh had written down. They did the same thing with the cattle.
[2 Chronicles] [35]:[13] They roasted the ‘pass-over’ meal over the fire as per the instructions, and they boiled the meat of the sacred offerings in pots and kettles and pans, and served the meat immediately to all the people who were there.
[2 Chronicles] [35]:[14] Afterwards, the Levites prepared the meal for themselves and for the priests (Aharon’s (Aaron) descendants), because the priests had been busy sacrificing the burnt offerings and the fat portions right through to the evening.
[2 Chronicles] [35]:[15] The singers (Asaf’s descendants) were at their posts, as they’d been commanded by King David, Asaf, Heyman, and the king’s prophet Yedutun. The men guarding the gates didn’t have to leave their posts, because their fellow Levites prepared food for them.
[2 Chronicles] [35]:[16] So on that day, everything that needed to be done for worshipping Yahweh was done. They celebrated the ‘pass-over’ festival, and they sacrificed burnt offerings as King Yoshiyah (Josiah) had commanded.
[2 Chronicles] [35]:[17] The Israelis who were there celebrated the ‘pass-over’ that day, then they celebrated the ‘Festival of Flat Bread’ for seven days.
[2 Chronicles] [35]:[18] There hadn’t been a ‘pass-over’ celebration done like that in Yisrael (Israel) since the time of the prophet Shmuel (Samuel), and none of Yisrael’s kings had ever done it like Yoshiyah did, along with the priests and Levites and the people from Yerushalem (Jerusalem) and all of Yehudah (Judah) and Yisrael.
[2 Chronicles] [35]:[19] They celebrated that festival in the eighteenth year of Yoshiyah’s reign.
[2 Chronicles] [35]:[20] After all of Yoshiyah’s (Josiah) work on temple restoration, Mitsrayim’s (Egypt) King Nekoh went to attack Karkemish city on the Perat (Euphrates) river, and Yoshiyah went out to confront him.
[2 Chronicles] [35]:[21] Nekoh sent messengers to tell Yoshiyah, “What’s this got to do with you, King of Yehudah (Judah)? We’re not attacking you at present, because we’re in a different fight, and God told me to hurry. Don’t oppose God, who’s with me, and don’t make him destroy you.”
[2 Chronicles] [35]:[22] However, Yoshiyah wouldn’t listen, but disguised himself before going into battle. He didn’t listen to Nekoh even though he was speaking for God, so he went to fight on the Megidon plain.
[2 Chronicles] [35]:[23] King Yoshiyah was hit by the archers, and he told his servants, “Get me away from here, because I’m badly wounded.”
[2 Chronicles] [35]:[24] So his servants lifted him off his chariot and took him on his reserve chariot back to Yerushalem (Jerusalem), where he died. He was buried in a tomb with his ancestors, and all of Yerushalem and Yehudah mourned over him.
[2 Chronicles] [35]:[25] The prophet Yirmiyah (Jeremiah) wrote a funeral song for him, which the male and female singers still use at funerals to this day. That became a custom in Yisrael (Israel) —the words of that song are written in a scroll of funeral songs.
[2 Chronicles] [35]:[26] The record of all the other things Yoshiyah did while he was king, and his loyal commitment to following Yahweh’s instructions,
[2 Chronicles] [35]:[27] including his actions from the beginning to the end of his reign, was written on the scroll ‘The kings of Yisrael and Yehudah’.
[2 Chronicles] [36]:[1] Then the people of Yehudah (Judah) took Yoshiyah’s (Josiah) son Yehoahaz and made him king in Yerushalem (Jerusalem) to replace his father.
[2 Chronicles] [36]:[2] Yehoahaz was twenty-three when he became king, and he reigned from Yerushalem for only three months.
[2 Chronicles] [36]:[3] Then Mitsrayim’s (Egypt) king deposed him and forced the country to pay an annual tribute of thirty kilograms of gold and three tonnes of silver.
[2 Chronicles] [36]:[4] Mitsrayim’s King Nekoh took Yehoahaz to Mitsrayim, and then the king made his younger brother Elyakim king over Yehudah and Yerushalem, although he changed Elyakim’s name to Yehoyakim.
[2 Chronicles] [36]:[5] Yehoyakim was twenty-five when he became king, and he reigned from Yerushalem (Jerusalem) for eleven years. He did many things that Yahweh had said were evil.
[2 Chronicles] [36]:[6] Bavel’s (Babylon) King Nevukadnetsar (Nebuchadnezzar) attacked and captured Yehoyakim and took him to Bavel in bronze chains,
[2 Chronicles] [36]:[7] along with some items from Yahweh’s temple that were taken to Bavel and placed in the king’s temple there.
[2 Chronicles] [36]:[8] The record of all the other things Yehoyakim did while he was king, including the disgusting things he did, was written on the scroll ‘The kings of Yisrael (Israel) and Yehudah’ (Judah), and his son Yehoyakin replaced him as king.
[2 Chronicles] [36]:[9] Yehoyakin was eighteen when he became king, and he reigned from Yerushalem (Jerusalem) for just ten days. He did many things that Yahweh had said were evil.
[2 Chronicles] [36]:[10] At the beginning of the next year, King Nevukadnetsar (Nebuchadnezzar) sent soldiers to bring him to Bavel (Babylon), bringing valuable items from the temple, and he made his younger brother Tsidkiyah (Zedekiah) king over Yehudah (Judah) and Yerushalem.
[2 Chronicles] [36]:[11] Tsidkiyah (Zedekiah) was twenty-one when he became king, and he reigned from Yerushalem (Jerusalem) for eleven years.
[2 Chronicles] [36]:[12] He did many things that Yahweh had said were evil, in fact, he didn’t even humble himself when the prophet Yirmiyah (Jeremiah) brought him a message from Yahweh.
[2 Chronicles] [36]:[13] He’d become very stubborn and wouldn’t return to Yisrael’s (Israel) god Yahweh, and he also rebelled against King Nevukadnetsar (Nebuchadnezzar), who’d made him promise in front of God to be loyal.
[2 Chronicles] [36]:[14] In addition, all the leaders of the priests and the people of Yehudah (Judah) became more and more unfaithful, doing disgusting things often done in other nations, and then they defiled Yahweh’s residence, which he’d consecrated in Yerushalem.
[2 Chronicles] [36]:[15] So Yahweh, their ancestors’ god, sent many messages via his prophets, because he felt compassion for his people and his residence,
[2 Chronicles] [36]:[16] but they mocked God’s messengers and rejected the messages—ridiculing his prophets until Yahweh became so angry that he couldn’t be stopped.
[2 Chronicles] [36]:[17] So Yahweh sent the Chaldean king against them, and the Kasdim (Chaldeans) ran Yehudah’s young men through with the sword, even in the temple, and they didn’t spare any of the young men or women, or even those who were older or elderly—God allowed Nevukadnetsar to thoroughly defeat them.
[2 Chronicles] [36]:[18] Then he took everything valuable, big or small, from God’s temple, as well as from the king and his officials.
[2 Chronicles] [36]:[19] They set God’s temple on fire, and tore down some of the wall surrounding Yerushalem, burnt all its palaces, and destroyed everything valuable.
[2 Chronicles] [36]:[20] Anyone else who was still alive was taken to Bavel (Babylon), where they became servants to the king and his children until the time when the Persians came to power.
[2 Chronicles] [36]:[21] That fulfilled God’s message that Yirmiyah (Jeremiah) had previously proclaimed, that the land would become desolate to make up for the Rest Days that had been ignored—that took seventy years.
[2 Chronicles] [36]:[22] During the first year that King Koresh (Cyrus) reigned over Paras (Persia), in order to further fulfil what Yahweh had said via the prophet Yirmiyah (Jeremiah), Yahweh worked on the spirit of King Koresh who then wrote this ruling and sent messengers to announce it throughout his kingdom:
[2 Chronicles] [36]:[23] “I, Paras’s King Koresh, declare that Yahweh, the god of the heavens, has given me all these earthly kingdoms, and he’s given me the job of building a house for him in Yerushalem (Jerusalem), which is in Yehudah (Judah). To help with that, anyone who’s from there is allowed to return, and may their god Yahweh be with them and help them.
[Ezra] [1]:[1] In the first year that Koresh (Cyrus) was king of Paras (Persia), Yahweh stirred up his spirit in order to fulfil what he’d spoken through the prophet Yirmiyah (Jeremiah). So the king distributed an official written notice throughout his kingdom, saying,
[Ezra] [1]:[2] “Koresh, king of Paras, declares this: Yahweh, the god of heaven, has given me all the kingdoms in the world, and he’s appointed me to build a residence for him in Yerushalem (Jerusalem) in Yehudah (Judah).
[Ezra] [1]:[3] Anyone among you who’s one of his followers is free to go to Yerushalem (in Yehudah) to help build a temple there for Yisrael’s (Israel) god Yahweh—the god of Yerushalem. May God go with you.
[Ezra] [1]:[4] Those who live near these people but who are not going themselves, should donate gold and silver, and goods and livestock, plus cash as a voluntary offering for God’s temple in Yerushalem.
[Ezra] [1]:[5] Then some of the leaders of Benyamin and Yehudah, and some priests and Levites—all of whom had had their spirits stirred up by God—left to go and build Yahweh’s residence in Yerushalem.
[Ezra] [1]:[6] Their neighbours had helped them by donating gold and silver utensils, goods and livestock, and expensive gifts, as well as the voluntary offerings of cash.
[Ezra] [1]:[7] Then King Koresh brought out the equipment from Yahweh’s temple that Nevukadnetsar (Nebuchadnezzar) had brought all the way from Yerushalem and had put in the house of his gods.
[Ezra] [1]:[8] He put the treasurer Mitredat in charge of bringing them out and Sheshebatsar, the ruler of Yehudah, in charge of accepting them and listing them.
[Ezra] [1]:[9] There were: thirty gold basins, one thousand silver basins, twenty-nine knives,
[Ezra] [1]:[10] thirty gold bowls, 410 silver bowls, and a thousand other utensils,
[Ezra] [1]:[11] coming to a total of 5,400 gold and silver utensils. Sheshebatsar took all of that with the group of exiles going from Bavel (Babylon) to Yerushalem.
