[Ezra] [2]:[59] Another group went from the towns of Tel-Melah, Tel-Harsha, Keruv, Adan, and Imer, but they didn’t know their ancestry from before they were taken as captives.
[Ezra] [2]:[60] There were 652 people who were descendants of Delayah, Toviyah, and Nekoda,
[Ezra] [2]:[61] and from the sons of the priests: the descendants of Havayah; the descendants of Hakots; and the descendants of Barzilay, who took a wife from the daughters of Barzilay the Giladi, so he was called by their name.
[Ezra] [2]:[62] They had searched for their records among the genealogies, but couldn’t find their families listed, so they were disqualified to serve as priests.
[Ezra] [2]:[63] Also the governor told them that they mustn’t eat any of the holiest food until a priest could use the Urim and Tumim to determine their status.
[Ezra] [2]:[64] Altogether in this group, 42,360 people returned to Yehudah (Judah).
[Ezra] [2]:[65] not counting their 7,337 male and female servants, plus 200 male and female musicians.
[Ezra] [2]:[66] They also took 736 horses and 245 mules,
[Ezra] [2]:[67] 435 camels and 6,720 donkeys.
[Ezra] [2]:[68] When some of the heads of families got to Yahweh’s temple in Yerushalem (Jerusalem), they freely donated so that it could be rebuilt.
[Ezra] [2]:[69] They each donated to the treasury according to their individual resources—a total of sixty-one thousand gold coins, five thousand silver bars, and a hundred sets of clothing for the priests.
[Ezra] [2]:[70] So the priests and the Levites, and some of the people, and the singers, and the gatekeepers and the temple servants returned to live in their ancestral cities, and so all the Israeli cities had returnees living in them.
[Ezra] [3]:[1] In the seventh month, the Israelis from their various cities, gathered together in unity in Yerushalem (Jerusalem).
[Ezra] [3]:[2] Then Yotsadak’s son Yeshua and his brothers the priests, and Shealtiyel’s son Zerubavel and his brothers, and they built the altar to offer up burnt offerings to Yisrael’s (Israel) god on it as is written in the law of Mosheh (Moses), the man of God.
[Ezra] [3]:[3] They set the altar up on its foundation because they were worried about trouble from some of the other people groups in the region. Then they offered burnt offerings to Yahweh on it as well as the regular morning and evening burnt offerings.
[Ezra] [3]:[4] Then they observed the Celebration in Shelters as per the written instructions with a burnt offering each day as required.
[Ezra] [3]:[5] After that was over, they kept up the regular burnt offerings, plus those for the new moons and other times that Yahweh required, as well as any free-will offerings to Yahweh.
[Ezra] [3]:[6] Even though the temple foundation rebuilding hadn’t started yet, the people started sacrificing burnt offerings to Yahweh from the beginning of October.
[Ezra] [3]:[7] They donated cash to the stone-workers and carpenters, and food, drink, and oil to the workers from Tsidon (Sidon) and Tsor (Tyre) to float cedar logs along the coast from Levanon into Port Yafo (Joppa) with the permission of Persian King Koresh (Cyrus).
[Ezra] [3]:[8] In the second month of second year since their return to Yerushalem (Jerusalem), Shealtiyel’s son Zerubavel and Yotsadak’s son Yeshua, and the rest of their brothers the priests and the Levites, and everyone except who’d returned to Yerushalem from captivity, began work on God’s residence, and they appointed the Levites who were twenty and over to act as overseers for the work of rebuilding Yahweh’s temple.
[Ezra] [3]:[9] And Yeshua with his brothers and their sons, Kadmiel and his sons, (all descendants of Yehudah (Judah)) cooperated to act as overseers for those doing the work at the temple together with Henadad’s sons and grandsons, and their brothers the Levites.
[Ezra] [3]:[10] When the builders had laid the foundation of Yahweh’s temple, they got the priests to stand there in their robes with their trumpets, and Asaf’s descendants (who were Levites) with their cymbals, to praise Yahweh using the rhythms composed by David, the former Israeli king.
[Ezra] [3]:[11] Then they sang in response—praising and thanking Yahweh: “Yes, he is good, because his loyal commitment to Yisrael (Israel) will continue forever.” Then all the people shouted a great shout in praise to Yahweh because the foundation of Yahweh’s temple had been laid.
[Ezra] [3]:[12] Many of the older priests and Levites, and clan leaders who’d seen the first temple, wept loudly when they witnessed the founding of this one, but others were shouting happily with loud voices.
[Ezra] [3]:[13] So the people couldn’t differentiate the happy sounds from the sound of the people weeping, because the people were shouting very loudly and it could be heard from far away.
[Ezra] [4]:[1] Now the enemies of Yehudah (Judah) and Benyamin heard that the Israelis who’d come back from exile were building a temple for Yisrael’s (Israel) god Yahweh.
[Ezra] [4]:[2] so they went to Zerubavel and to the other clan leaders and they said to them, “Let us help you with the building work, because like you, we worship your god and we’ve been sacrificing to him since the days of the Assyrian king Esar-Hadon—the one who sent us here.”
[Ezra] [4]:[3] But Zerubavel, and Yeshua, and the rest of the Israelis clan leaders said to them, “It’s not for you and for us to build a house for our god, but we ourselves together will build for Yisrael’s god Yahweh, just as the Persian King Koresh (Cyrus) has commanded us.”
[Ezra] [4]:[4] Those local people had been discouraging the people of Yehudah and trying to stop them from building.
[Ezra] [4]:[5] They’d also hired influencers to work against them throughout the reigns of the Persian kings Koresh and Dareyavesh (Darius).
[Ezra] [4]:[6] Now at the beginning of the reign of Ahashverosh (Ahasuerus), they forwarded an accusation against those who lived in Yerushalem (Jerusalem) and throughout Yehudah (Judah).
[Ezra] [4]:[7] And in the days of Persian King Artahshashta (Artaxerxes), Bishlam, Mitredat, Teve’el and the rest of their companions wrote to the king. (The letter was written in Aramit (Syrian) and using that alphabet).
[Ezra] [4]:[8] Rehum the high commissioner and Shimshay the provincial secretary wrote a letter to King Artahshashta against Yerushalem as follows:
[Ezra] [4]:[9] From Rehum the high commissioner and Shimshay the provincial secretary, and the our companions, the judges and the rulers, the officials, the Persians, the Erekites, the Babylonians, the Susaites (that is, the Eylamites),
[Ezra] [4]:[10] and the rest of the nations that the famous and powerful King Asenapar exiled from other nations and forced them to live in the cities of Shomron (Samaria), and the province went of the Perat (Euphrates) river. And now
[Ezra] [4]:[11] this is what the letter said that they sent to him: To Artahshashta the king from your servants on this side of the river. And now
[Ezra] [4]:[12] let it be known to the king that the Yehudim (Jews) who left your region have come to us at Yerushalem to rebuild that rebellious and evil city—they’re currently finishing the walls and repairing the building foundations.
[Ezra] [4]:[13] Now let it be known to the king that if that city is built and the walls are completed, those people won’t pay taxes, or send tributes, and your royal treasury will lose out.
[Ezra] [4]:[14] Now, because we’ve had the favour of the palace, and because we don’t want to see the king dishonoured, that’s why we’ve sent this letter to update the king,
[Ezra] [4]:[15] so that he can search in the official records of the kingdom. You’ll discover and learn that that city of Yerushalem is a rebellious city and one that has caused harm to kings and provinces, and has harboured rebellion there for decades past—that’s why that city was destroyed.
[Ezra] [4]:[16] We are letting the king know that if that city is rebuilt and its walls are completed, then you’ll lose control of this province on this side of the Perat.”
[Ezra] [4]:[17] The king sent this reply: “To Rehum the high commissioner and Shimshay the provincial secretary, and the rest of their companions who live in Shomron (Samaria), and the rest of the people in the province west of the Perat: Peace. And now
[Ezra] [4]:[18] the letter that you all sent to us has been carefully read aloud to me.
[Ezra] [4]:[19] I ordered my officials to search the records and discovered that it’s true that that city has been rebellious and seditious since ancient times.
[Ezra] [4]:[20] Powerful kings have reigned from Yerushalem and ruled the entire region that side of the river, and had taxes and tributes paid to them.
[Ezra] [4]:[21] So command those Yehudim to stop rebuilding the city until such time as I make a decree.
[Ezra] [4]:[22] Don’t be negligent in doing that or the damage to this kingdom might get worse.”
[Ezra] [4]:[23] When King Artahshashta’s (Artaxerxes) letter reached Rehum, Shimshay the secretary, and their companions, and was read aloud to them all, they immediately went to Yerushalem and used force to stop the Yehudim (Jews) from their rebuilding.
[Ezra] [4]:[24] So there was a period when the rebuilding of the temple in Yerushalem stopped, and it remained paused until the second year of King Dareyavesh’s (Darius) reign in Paras (Persia).
[Ezra] [5]:[1] Then the prophet Hagay and Ido’s son Zekaryah (Zechariah) prophesied to the Yehudim (Jews) in Yerushalem (Jerusalem) and across Yehudah (Judah) in the name of Yisrael’s (Israel) god who they served.
[Ezra] [5]:[2] Then Shealtiyel’s son Zerubavel and Yotsadak’s son Yeshua took action and began to rebuild God’s temple in Yerushalem, and the prophets who served God were there with them, supporting them.
[Ezra] [5]:[3] At that time, Tatenay, the governor of the province west of the Perat (Euphrates), and Shetar-Bozenay, and their companions came to them and demanded, “Who gave you all permission to rebuild this temple?”
[Ezra] [5]:[4] They also asked the Yehudim to tell them the names of the men who were working on the building.
[Ezra] [5]:[5] However, God was watching over the Jewish leaders, and they weren’t actually stopped. A report was sent to King Dareyavesh (Darius), then they waited for a response.
[Ezra] [5]:[6] Tatenay, the governor of the province west of the river, and Shetar-Bozenay and his companions, the provincial officials, sent the letter to King Dareyavesh—
[Ezra] [5]:[7] this is what was written in their report: “To King Dareyavesh. All peace.
[Ezra] [5]:[8] Let it be known to the king that we went to the province of Yehudah (Judea), to the temple of the great God, and it is being built with large stones, and timber is being placed in the walls. This work is being done to a high standard and they’re making good progress.
[Ezra] [5]:[9] “Then we asked those elders, ‘Who gave you all permission to rebuild this temple?’
[Ezra] [5]:[10] We also asked them their names, so that we could write down the names of their leaders to inform you.
[Ezra] [5]:[11] “This is the answer they gave us, ‘We are servants of the god of the heavens and earth, and we are rebuilding the temple that was constructed and finished many years ago by a famous Israeli king.
[Ezra] [5]:[12] However, because our ancestors made the god of the heavens angry, he let Babylonian King Nevukadnetsar (Nebuchadnezzar) (Nevukadnetsar, the Chaldean) defeat them, and he destroyed that temple and caused the people to be exiled to Bavel (Babylon).
[Ezra] [5]:[13] But in the first year of the reign of Babylonian King Koresh (Cyrus), he made a decree to rebuild this house of God.
[Ezra] [5]:[14] What’s more, the gold and silver containers that Nevukadnetsar had taken out from that temple that was in Yerushalem and had brought to the temple in Bavel, King Koresh took them out from the temple in Bavel and they were handed over to the man named Sheshebatsar who he’d appointed as governor over Yehudah.
[Ezra] [5]:[15] Koresh had told him to take those containers and put them back in the temple in Yerushalem, and to ensure that the temple got rebuilt in the same place where it had been before.
[Ezra] [5]:[16] So Sheshebatsar came here and laid the foundation of God’s house in Yerushalem, and since then, it’s been being rebuilt but isn’t finished yet.’
[Ezra] [5]:[17] So now, if it pleases the king, let a search be made in the records in the king’s treasure house there in Bavel, if it’s correct that a decree was set by King Koresh to rebuild this house of God in Yerushalem (Jerusalem). Then let the king send his decision on this matter back to us.”
[Ezra] [6]:[1] So King Dareyavesh (Darius) ordered that a search be conducted in all the archives where treasures had been deposited there in Bavel (Babylon),
[Ezra] [6]:[2] and one scroll was found in the fortress at Ahmeta in the province of Maday (Media), and this record had been made:
[Ezra] [6]:[3] “In year one of Koresh (Cyrus) the king, he made a decree about the house of God in Yerushalem (Jerusalem): ‘Let the house be built in the same place where sacrifices were made. Establish its foundations and build it 27m high and 27m wide
[Ezra] [6]:[4] with three layers of large stones and a layer of new timber. That should all be paid for from the royal treasury.
[Ezra] [6]:[5] Also, the gold and silver containers from the house of God that Nevukadnetsar (Nebuchadnezzar) had taken out from the Yerushalem temple and had brought to Bavel, must be returned to their places in the temple in Yerushalem. So you must put them in the house of God.’ ”
[Ezra] [6]:[6] Therefore King Dareyavesh (Darius) wrote: “Now to Governor Tatenay in the province west of the Perat (Euphrates), Shetar-Bozenay, and their companions, the officials who in that province: Keep away from that place.
[Ezra] [6]:[7] Leave alone the work on that house of God. Let the Jewish governor and elders build that temple in its place.
[Ezra] [6]:[8] So here’s my decree about what should be done for those Jewish elders to build that house of God: Using the king’s treasures that come from the tribute of that west-Euphrates province, let those workers costs be regularly reimbursed so that the work doesn’t stop.
[Ezra] [6]:[9] Whatever is needed (including young bulls, or rams, or lambs for burnt offerings to the god of the heavens, wheat, salt, wine, or oil, according to the command of the priests in Yerushalem (Jerusalem)), let it be given to them day by day (that is, without delay),
[Ezra] [6]:[10] so that they can be offering sweet-smelling sacrifices to the god of the heavens and praying for the life of the king and his sons.
[Ezra] [6]:[11] Also I decree that any man who changes this edict should have a beam pulled from his house, and after it’s sharpened and set into the ground, then he should be impaled on it. Then his entire house should be made into a rubbish heap because of what he did.
[Ezra] [6]:[12] May the god who has established his name there overthrow any king or person who makes any attempt to change this decree or to destroy that house of God in Yerushalem. I, Dareyavesh, have made a decree. Let it be done diligently.”
[Ezra] [6]:[13] Then Tatenay, the governor of the region west of the Perat (Euphrates), Shetar-Bozenay, and their companions worked hard to follow the instructions sent by King Dareyavesh (Darius).
[Ezra] [6]:[14] So the Jewish elders continued building, and they were encouraged by the prophesying of the prophet Hagay and Ido’s son Zekaryah (Zechariah). As a result of the decrees of the Persian kings Koresh (Cyrus) , and Dareyavesh and Artahshashta (Artaxerxes), they were able to fulfil God’s decree to rebuild the temple.
[Ezra] [6]:[15] The rebuilt temple was finished in mid-March in the sixth year of King Dareyavesh’s reign.
[Ezra] [6]:[16] Then the Israeli people, the priests, and the Levites, and the ones that had returned from exile, performed the dedication of this house of God with celebrations.
[Ezra] [6]:[17] During the dedication, they offered a hundred bulls, two-hundred rams, and four-hundred lambs, as well as twelve male goats for a sin offering for all Yisrael (Israel) (matching the number of the tribes).
[Ezra] [6]:[18] Then they organised the priests to stand in their divisions and the Levites in their sections to serve the god who resides in Yerushalem (Jerusalem), according to the instructions written by Mosheh (Moses).
[Ezra] [6]:[19] So the people who’d returned from exile celebrated the ‘pass-over’ in late April.
[Ezra] [6]:[20] The priests and Levites all had to be individually purified, and they slaughtered the lambs for all the exiles and for their brothers the priests, and for themselves.
[Ezra] [6]:[21] Then all the Israelis ate the meal—those who’d returned from the exile and every one who’d separated themselves from the uncleanness of the nations of the land in order to search for Yisrael’s (Israel) god Yahweh.
[Ezra] [6]:[22] Then they happily enjoyed the Flat Bread Celebration for seven days, because Yahweh had made them happy, and had caused the Assyrian king to show favour to them, to assist their work rebuilding the house of God, the god of Yisrael.
[Ezra] [7]:[1] Many years later in the reign of Persian King Artahshashta (Artaxerxes), Ezra (son of Serayah, son of Azaryah, son of Hilkiyah,
[Ezra] [7]:[2] son of Shalum, son of Tsadok, son of Ahituv,
[Ezra] [7]:[3] son of Amaryah, son of Azaryah, son of Merayot,
[Ezra] [7]:[4] son of Zerahyah, son of Uzi, son of Buki,
[Ezra] [7]:[5] son of Avishua, the son of Pinhas, the son of Eleazar, the son of Aharon (Aaron) the head priest)
[Ezra] [7]:[6] was a skilled expert in the law that Yisrael’s (Israel) god Yahweh had given through Mosheh (Moses). With the favour of his god Yahweh helping Ezra, the king had granted all his requests, and he travelled from Bavel (Babylon) to Yerushalem (Jerusalem).
[Ezra] [7]:[7] Some Israelis, including some priests and Levites, singers and gatekeepers, and some temple servants travelled to Yerushalem in the seventh year of Artahshashta’s reign.
[Ezra] [7]:[8] They left Bavel on New Year’s Day (in early April) and with God’s favour on the journey, arrived in Yerushalem exactly four months later
[Ezra] [7]:[10] because Ezra had made a firm resolution to study Yahweh’s written instructions, and to carefully follow them, and to teach them in Yisrael.
[Ezra] [7]:[11] King Artahshashta (Artaxerxes) had given a letter for Ezra the priest and scribe and expert in Yahweh’s commands and instructions to take with him, saying:
[Ezra] [7]:[12] Artahshashta, the king of kings, to the priest Ezra, the scribe of the law of the god of heavens: Peace. Now,
[Ezra] [7]:[13] I hereby decree that anyone in my kingdom from Yisrael (Israel) (including priests and Levites) who freely offers to go to Yerushalem (Jerusalem) with you, may go.
[Ezra] [7]:[14] You are sent by the king and his seven counsellors to determine whether the people of Yehudah (Judah) and Yerushalem are following the law of your god which you have a copy of.
[Ezra] [7]:[15] You are also to take the gold and silver that the king and his counsellors have freely offered to the god of Yisrael who lives in Yerushalem,
[Ezra] [7]:[16] along with all the gold and silver that you collect all across Bavel (Babylon), along with the freewill offerings of the people and the priests who freely give towards the house of God in Yerushalem.
[Ezra] [7]:[17] So then you should diligently use those funds to buy bulls, rams, lambs, and supplies for their grain offerings and drink offerings, and you should offer them on the altar at the your god’s house in Yerushalem.
[Ezra] [7]:[18] With the remaining funds, you can use them for whatever seems good to you and your brothers, according to the will of your god.
[Ezra] [7]:[19] Also, make sure that you deliver all those gold and silver containers that were handed over to you for use in your god’s house in Yerushalem.
[Ezra] [7]:[20] Anything else that’s needed for the house of your god that you need to supply can be provided from the king’s treasuries.
[Ezra] [7]:[21] And I, King Artahshashta (Artaxerxes) make a decree for all the treasurers in the province west of the river: that you all diligently help with everything that the priest Ezra (the scribe of the law of the god of the heavens) asks from you all—
[Ezra] [7]:[22] up to three tonnes of silver, five hundred bushels of wheat, two thousand litres of wine and the same amount of olive oil, and as much salt as he needs.
[Ezra] [7]:[23] Everything that the god of the heavens decreed to be done should be done exactly as he specified because there’s no good reason to make him angry at the kingdom of the king and his sons?
[Ezra] [7]:[24] Also, it should be made clear that there is no authority to extract taxes or tribute from any priests or Levites, singers or the gatekeepers, the temple servants or the servants of that house of God.
[Ezra] [7]:[25] As for you, Ezra, use the wisdom that your god has given to you to appoint magistrates and judges who can judge all the people who are in that province beyond the river—everyone who know the laws of your god (plus you should teach those who don’t know them).
[Ezra] [7]:[26] Anyone who refuses to obey your god’s laws and the king’s laws, should receive swift judgement—whether it’s confiscation of goods, or banishment, imprisonment, or the death sentence.”
[Ezra] [7]:[27] Blessed be Yahweh, the god of our fathers who put it into the king’s heart to honour Yahweh’s house in Yerushalem (Jerusalem),
[Ezra] [7]:[28] and showed me his loyal commitment in dealing with the king and his counsellors, and all the powerful officials of the king. And as for me, Yahweh my god blessed me with initiative and the strength to carry it out as I gathered some Israeli leaders to go to Yerushalem with me.
[Ezra] [8]:[1] Now these are the family heads and their descendants by number who went with me from Bavel (Babylon) to Yerushalem (Jerusalem) in the reign of King Artahshashta (Artaxerxes):
[Ezra] [8]:[2] from the descendants of Pinhas: Gereshom, from the descendants of Itamar: Daniyel, from the descendants of David: Hatush,
[Ezra] [8]:[3] from the descendants of Shekanyah and Par’osh: Zekaryah (Zechariah) and a hundred and fifty other men,
[Ezra] [8]:[4] from the descendants of Pahat-Moav: Zerahyah’s son Elyehoeynay and two hundred other men,
[Ezra] [8]:[5] from the descendants of Shekanyah: Yahaziel’s son and three hundred other men,
[Ezra] [8]:[6] from the descendants of Adin: Yonatan’s (Jonathan) son Eved and fifty other men,
[Ezra] [8]:[7] from the descendants of Eylam: Atalyah’s (Athaliah) son Yeshayah (Isaiah) and seventy other men,
[Ezra] [8]:[8] from the descendants of Shefatyah: Mika’el’s (Michael) son Zevadyah and eighty other men;
[Ezra] [8]:[9] from the descendants of Yoav (Joab): Yehiel’s son Ovadyah (Obadiah) and 218 other men,
[Ezra] [8]:[10] from the descendants of Shelomit: Yosifyah’s son and one hundred and sixty other men,
[Ezra] [8]:[11] from the descendants of Bevay: his son Zekaryah (Zechariah) and twenty-eight other men,
[Ezra] [8]:[12] from the descendants of Azgad: Hakatan’s son Yohanan and one hundred and ten other men,
[Ezra] [8]:[13] from the later descendants of Adonikam: Elifelet, Yeiel, and Shemayah, and sixty other men,
[Ezra] [8]:[14] and from the descendants of Bigvay: Utay and Zakur and seventy other men.
[Ezra] [8]:[15] Firstly, I gathered them near the river that goes to Ahava, and we camped there for three days. I interviewed the people and the priests and discovered that we didn’t have any Levites included in the group.
[Ezra] [8]:[16] So I summoned the following leaders: Eliezer, Ariel, Shemayah, Elnatan, Yariv, a second Elnatan, Natan (Nathan), Zekaryah (Zechariah), and Meshulam, as well as the wise men: Yoyariv and a third Elnatan.
[Ezra] [8]:[17] I commanded them to go to Ido, the leader at Kasifya, and I told them to tell Ido and his relatives (temple servants in Kasifya) to send us some Levites who would go to Yerushalem (Jerusalem) to serve in our god’s temple.
[Ezra] [8]:[18] Then since we had God’s favour, they sent us a talented man (from the sons of Mahli, son of Levi, son of Yisrael (Israel)) and eighteen of his sons and other relatives.
[Ezra] [8]:[19] They also sent Hashavyah and Yeshayah (Isaiah) (from Merari’s sons), and their relatives and sons—some twenty men—
[Ezra] [8]:[20] plus two hundred and twenty descendants of Levite temple servants that King David and his officials had appointed for service—all designated by name.
[Ezra] [8]:[21] Then right there by the river Ahava, I proclaimed a fast to humble ourselves in front of our god to request that he’d smooth the way ahead for us, and for our children, and for all our property,
[Ezra] [8]:[22] because I was ashamed to request an army and horsemen from the king to help us from possible enemies on the way. Also, you see, we had previously told the king, “Our god does good to all those who honour him, but his might and his anger are against all those who abandon him.”
[Ezra] [8]:[23] So we fasted and sought wisdom from our god concerning this, and he listened to our requests.
[Ezra] [8]:[24] Then I chose twelve of the leaders of the priests along with Shereveyah and Hashavyah and ten of the other Levites,
[Ezra] [8]:[25] and as they watched, I weighed out the gold and silver, and the valuable utensils—the offering for the house of our god that the king, and his counsellors and officials, and all the exiled Israelis who could be contacted, had offered.
[Ezra] [8]:[26] It came to three tonnes of gold, twenty-one tonnes of silver, and another three tonnes of silver containers,
[Ezra] [8]:[27] as well as twenty gold bowls that weighed another eight kilograms, and two polished bronze containers that were as valuable as gold.
[Ezra] [8]:[28] “You are sacred to Yahweh,” I told them all, “and the containers and utensils are sacred, and the gold and silver are a freewill offering to Yahweh, the god of your ancestors.
[Ezra] [8]:[29] Look after them all carefully until you weigh them out in front of the leaders of the priests and Levites and the leaders of the Israeli elders in the chambers of Yahweh’s house in Yerushalem (Jerusalem).”
[Ezra] [8]:[30] So the priests and the Levites accepted the receipt of the gold and silver, and the containers, to take them to Yerushalem—to the house of our god.
[Ezra] [8]:[31] Then in mid-April, we set out from the river Ahava to go to Yerushalem (Jerusalem), and we had God’s favour as he kept us safe from any enemies or ambushes on the way.
[Ezra] [8]:[32] So we arrived at Yerushalem, and rested there for three days.
[Ezra] [8]:[33] On the fourth day, the gold and silver and the containers and utensils were weighed out in the temple—being handed over to Uriyah’s son Meremot, the priest, and with him was Pinhas’s son Eleazar (and with them were Yeshua’s son Yozavad, and Binuy’s son Noadyah, the Levites).
[Ezra] [8]:[34] They recorded all the items with their weights.
[Ezra] [8]:[35] The descendants of the former captives who had returned from exile offered burnt offerings to Yisrael’s (Israel) god: twelve bulls for all Yisrael, 96 rams, 77 lambs, then twelve male goats for a sin offering. The whole was presented as a burnt offering to Yahweh.
[Ezra] [8]:[36] They relayed the king’s orders to the governors and officials of the province beyond the river, and so they honoured the people and God’s house.
[Ezra] [9]:[1] Now as soon as those things were finished, the leaders came to me, saying, “The people of Yisrael (Israel), and the priests and Levites haven’t kept themselves separate from the idolatry of the peoples of the lands: the Kena’anim (Canaanites) , Hitim, Perizim, the Yevusim, Amonim, Moavim, Mitsrim (Egyptians) , and the Amorim.
[Ezra] [9]:[2] Instead, they’ve taken women from those peoples as wives for themselves and their sons, so they’ve diluted their sacred heritage with the anti-God customs of those peoples. But the worst is that it’s our leaders and officials that have been at the forefront in this unfaithfulness.”
[Ezra] [9]:[3] As soon as I heard that, I tore my clothes and pulled some of the hair out of my head and beard, and I sat down appalled.
[Ezra] [9]:[4] Any others who respectfully followed Yisrael’s god’s instructions and who were concerned about the unfaithfulness of the exiles, joined with me and I sat there appalled until the time of the evening sacrifice.
[Ezra] [9]:[5] So I got up from my position of humiliation with my torn clothes during the evening sacrifice, then I went down on my knees and spread out my palms to my god Yahweh
[Ezra] [9]:[6] and prayed, “My god, I’m ashamed and humiliated to raise my face to you, my god, because our sins have multiplied and risen above our heads, and our guilt has mounted up as high as the sky.
[Ezra] [9]:[7] From back in the time of our ancestors until today, we’ve been very guilty, and in our disobedience, we ourselves, including our kings and our priests, have been killed by the kings of the surrounding countries, or taken captive, or been plundered, or simply put to shame, which is the case right now.
[Ezra] [9]:[8] But now for a brief moment, favour has come from our god Yahweh and given us remaining survivors a stake in his holy place—yes, our god has cheered us up and given us a little relief from our slavery.
[Ezra] [9]:[9] Because we are slaves, yet our god hasn’t abandoned us in our slavery, but he’s used his loyal commitment to us to influence the Persian king to give to us breathing space to rebuild the house of our god from its ruins, and to give to us a ‘wall of protection’ in Yerushalem (Jerusalem) and across Yehudah (Judah).
[Ezra] [9]:[10] “So now, our god, what can we say after that? We’ve abandoned your instructions
[Ezra] [9]:[11] which you gave us via your servants, the prophets, saying, ‘The land that you’re all entering to occupy is a land of impurity, due to the impurity of the current inhabitants with their evil practices that have filled it from one end to the other with their filth.
[Ezra] [9]:[12] So now, don’t give your daughters to their sons to marry, or vice versa. And don’t try to make long-term peace treaties or contracts with them. Then you all will stay in power, and eat the good things of the land, and be able to pass it on to your children for all their future generations.’
[Ezra] [9]:[13] “Yet after everything that’s happened to us as a result our evil actions and our great guilt (even though you, our god, didn’t punish us as harshly as you could have, and you’ve allowed us to survive as we’re here now),
[Ezra] [9]:[14] should we return to disobeying your instructions and to intermarrying with those people groups with their evil practices? You’d rightfully be angry enough with us as to wipe us out completely without leaving any remnant or survivors?
[Ezra] [9]:[15] Yahweh, the god of Yisrael (Israel), you always do what is right, because here we are as survivors even to this day. So, yes, here we are standing in front of you in our guilt, because none of us are innocent enough to stand in front of you because of what we’ve done.”
[Ezra] [10]:[1] When Ezra prayed and confessed like that, weeping and bowing down low in front of the temple, an extremely large number of Israeli men and women and children gathered around him to join in and weep aloud.
[Ezra] [10]:[2] Then Yehiel’s son Shekanyah (from the sons of Eylam) answered and admitted to Ezra, “We ourselves have behaved unfaithfully towards our god and have married foreign women from the other people groups in this region. But there’s still hope for Yisrael (Israel) concerning this.
[Ezra] [10]:[3] So now, let’s make an agreement with our god to send all those women back, along with their children, following the advice of my master and the ones who strive to obey God’s instructions, and as per the law.
[Ezra] [10]:[4] So take action because this is now in your hands, but we’re with you. Lead strongly and make a clear decision.”
[Ezra] [10]:[5] So Ezra took action and made the leaders of the priests and Levites, and all Yisrael, to promise to implement this decision, and they did so.
[Ezra] [10]:[6] Then Ezra left that place there in front of the temple, and he went to Yehohanan’s room (Elyashiv’s son) and went in. He didn’t eat or drink, but continued mourning because of the unfaithfulness of the exiles.
[Ezra] [10]:[7] Then the leaders sent an official written notice throughout Yerushalem (Jerusalem) and all Yehudah (Judah) to all those Yehudim (Jews) who’d returned from captivity, that their men should assemble in Yerushalem.
[Ezra] [10]:[8] They were told that it was the decision of the leaders and elders that anyone who didn’t arrive within three days would then forfeit all their property and would no longer be considered as an Israeli.
[Ezra] [10]:[9] So on the third day (in mid-December), all the men of Yehudah and Benyamin gathered in Yerushalem, and all the people sat in the courtyard in front of the temple. They were shivering because of the rain, and because of the seriousness of the matter.
[Ezra] [10]:[10] Then the priest Ezra stood up and announced, “You yourselves have acted unfaithfully and have married foreign women, thus adding to Yisrael’s guilt in God’s eyes.
[Ezra] [10]:[11] Now however, praise Yahweh, the god of your ancestors, and do what he’s commanded us and separate yourselves from the other religions of the peoples in this region, including not marrying their women.”
[Ezra] [10]:[12] Then all the gathered Israelis answered, “Yes, we do need to do what you’ve said.
[Ezra] [10]:[13] However, it’s the rainy season now, and there’s so many people who can’t stand outside for several days while we try to work all this out, because we’ve done so much wrong.
[Ezra] [10]:[14] So let’s delegate our leaders to make the decisions for all of us. Then we can arrange to meet together by city with our elders and judges to apply the decisions about our foreign wives, until God’s anger towards us about these matters cools down.
[Ezra] [10]:[15] The only ones who were against this plan were Asahel’s on Yonatan (Jonathan) and Tikvah’s son Yahzeyah, with the support of Meshulam and the Levite Shabtay.
[Ezra] [10]:[16] So the exiled Israelis agreed to follow that plan, and the names of the men were written down by each clan leader who then stayed behind with the priest Ezra, and a few days later, they sat down to start working through the lists.
[Ezra] [10]:[17] Some two months later, they had finished considering all the men who had married foreign women.
[Ezra] [10]:[18] Some of the priests’ descendants had married foreign women, i.e., the descendants of Yotsadak’s son Yeshua and his brothers, Ma’aseyah, Eliezer, Yariv, and Gedalyah,
[Ezra] [10]:[19] and they promised to expel their wives, and because of their guilt, each of them sacrificed a ram from their flock.
[Ezra] [10]:[20] Then, also: From Imer’s descendants: Hanani and Zevadyah,
[Ezra] [10]:[21] From Harim’s descendants: Ma’aseyah, Eliyah (Elijah), Shemayah, Yehiel, and Uziyah,
[Ezra] [10]:[22] From Pashhur’s descendants: Elyehoeynay, Ma’aseyah, Yishmael (Ishmael), Netanel, Yozavad, and Eleasah,
[Ezra] [10]:[23] Among the other Levites: Yozavad, and Shimei, and Kelayah (that is, Kelita), Petahyah, Yehudah (Judah), and Eliezer.
[Ezra] [10]:[24] Among the singers: Elyashiv. Among the temple guards: Shalum, Telem, and Uri.
[Ezra] [10]:[25] From the other Israelis: From Par’osh’s descendants: Rameyah, Yiziyah, Malkiyah, Miyamin, Eleazar, Malkiyah, and Benayah.
[Ezra] [10]:[26] From Heylam’s descendants: Matanyah, Zekaryah (Zechariah), Yehiel, Avdi, Yerimot, and Eliyah (Elijah).
[Ezra] [10]:[27] From Zatu’s descendants: Elyehoeynay, Elyashiv, Matanyah, Yerimot, Zavad, and Aziza.
[Ezra] [10]:[28] From Bevay’s descendants: Yehohanan, Hananyah, Zabay, and Atlay.
[Ezra] [10]:[29] From Bani’s descendants: Meshulam, Maluk, Adayah, Yashuv, and Sheal-Yerimot.

[Ezra] [10]:[32] Benyamin, Maluk, and Shemaryah.
[Ezra] [10]:[33] From Hashum’s descendants: Matenay, Matatah, Zavad, Elifelet, Yeremay, Menasheh, and Shimei.

[Nehemyah] [1]:[1] The account by Hakalyah’s son Nehemyah (Nehemiah). In the month of Kislev during the twentieth year of the reign of King Artahshashta (Artaxerxes) over the Persian Empire, I was in the capital city of Shushan (Susa).
[Nehemyah] [1]:[2] Hanani, one of my brothers, came with some other men from Yehudah (Judah), and I asked them about the Yehudim (Jews) who’d escaped and managed to avoid being exiled, and about Yerushalem (Jerusalem),
[Nehemyah] [1]:[3] and he told me, “The ones left behind in the provinces and who avoided the captivity, are in a bad way and feeling depressed. The wall around Yerushalem was torn down, and its gates were burnt.”
[Nehemyah] [1]:[4] When I heard all that, I sat down and I was upset for days. I fasted and cried and prayed to the god of the heavens,
[Nehemyah] [1]:[5] and I said, “Oh Yahweh, God of the heavens, the great and awesome God, who keeps his agreement and is determinedly loyal to those who love him and obey his instructions:
[Nehemyah] [1]:[6] Please listen carefully to your servant’s prayer that I’m presenting to you today, day and night, on account of your servants the Israelis. On behalf of all Israelis, I’m confessing that we’ve sinned against you—both my generation and previous generations.
[Nehemyah] [1]:[7] We’ve acted extremely corruptly—disobeying you by not obeying your commands, statutes, and judgements that you instructed through your servant Mosheh (Moses).
[Nehemyah] [1]:[8] Please remember that you told your servant Mosheh that if we act unfaithfully, you yourself would scatter us among the nations,
[Nehemyah] [1]:[9] but if we’d return to you and obey your instructions, then even if we had been banished to the ends of the earth, you’d gather us back up and bring us back to the place where you’ve established your name and reputation.
[Nehemyah] [1]:[10] “We’re your servants and your people that you rescued from slavery with your incredible power.
[Nehemyah] [1]:[11] Oh, my master, please listen carefully to your servant’s prayer, and to the prayer of your other servants who delight to honour your name. Please cause your servant to succeed today, and give me favour in the king’s eyes.” Now as for me, I was the king’s cupbearer.
[Nehemyah] [2]:[1] In the spring of the twentieth year of King Artahshashta’s (Artaxerxes) reign, I was serving wine to the king. I’d never looked sad before in his presence,
[Nehemyah] [2]:[2] and the king asked me, “Why do you look unhappy? I know that you’re not sick so something must be upsetting you.” I was very scared
[Nehemyah] [2]:[3] and I answered the king, “May the king live forever. I can’t help but look unhappy when the city containing my ancestors’ graves has had its gates burnt down and it’s now abandoned.”
[Nehemyah] [2]:[4] “So what would you like to happen?” the king asked. Then I prayed to the god of heaven
[Nehemyah] [2]:[5] and answered the king, “If I have your favour, and if it seems good to the king, maybe you’d send me to Yehudah (Judah)—to the city of my ancestors’ graves so I could rebuild it.”
[Nehemyah] [2]:[6] Then the king said to me, with the queen sitting beside him, “How long would your journey be? And when would you return?” So I gave him a date and he seemed happy with it, because he released me to go.
[Nehemyah] [2]:[7] Then I made another request, “If it pleases the king, let letters be given to me for the governors of the provinces across the Perat (Euphrates) river to ask them to help me in my travel towards Yehudah.
[Nehemyah] [2]:[8] Also a letter to Asaf, the keeper of the king’s forest, so he’ll give me timber for the beams of the gates of the fortress near the temple, and for the city wall, and for the house that I’ll live in.” Then the king granted those requests, thanks to God’s help on what I was doing.
[Nehemyah] [2]:[9] Then I went to the governors of the provinces across the Perat, and I gave them the king’s letters. The king had sent army officers and horsemen with me.
[Nehemyah] [2]:[10] When Sanvalat the Horoni and the servant Toviyah the Amoni heard my plans, they were very angry that someone would come to help the Israelis.
[Nehemyah] [2]:[11] So I got to Yerushalem (Jerusalem) and was there for three days,
[Nehemyah] [2]:[12] One night, I got up and took a few men with me, without having told anyone what I felt that my god had been telling me to do for Yerushalem. We only had the one horse that I was riding,
[Nehemyah] [2]:[13] and we went out in the dark through the Valley Gate and past the Dragon Well to the Dung Gate. I was carefully inspecting the city walls—noting where they were broken down and which gates had been burnt out.
[Nehemyah] [2]:[14] Then I crossed to the Fountain Gate and the Royal Pool, but there was nowhere that we could get my mount through the rubble.
[Nehemyah] [2]:[15] So I went up the creek bed in the dark, carefully inspecting the wall, before turning back and returning quietly through the Valley Gate.
[Nehemyah] [2]:[16] None of the city officials knew where I’d gone or what I was doing, and up until this point I hadn’t yet told my plans to the Jewish leaders or the priests or nobles or city officials, or hired any workers.
[Nehemyah] [2]:[17] So now I told them, “You call all see the desperate situation that we’re in: Yerushalem is in ruins and its gates have been burnt out. So now, let’s rebuild the city wall and then we’ll no longer be mocked by others.”
[Nehemyah] [2]:[18] I told them how God had helped me so far and what the king had given me permission to do. “Well, let’s get started on the rebuilding,” they said, and got ready to work together.
[Nehemyah] [2]:[19] But then Sanvalat the Horoni, and the Amoni servant Toviyah, and Geshem the Aravi heard, and they mocked and despised us, saying, “What are you guys all up to? Are you all rebelling against the king?”
[Nehemyah] [2]:[20] I answered them by explaining, “The god of the heavens will help us to succeed, and we ourselves, his servants, will do the rebuilding work, but you all will have no part in it, and no rights in Yerushalem.”
[Nehemyah] [3]:[1] The high priest Elyashiv worked together with his brothers the priests, and they rebuilt the Sheep Gate. They themselves dedicated it and installed the doors on it. In addition, they dedicated the section of the wall as far as the Hundred Tower and beyond that to the Hananel Tower.
[Nehemyah] [3]:[2] The men from Yeriho (Jericho) rebuilt the section beside them, and Imri’s son Zakur rebuilt the next section again.
[Nehemyah] [3]:[3] Hasena’ah’s son rebuilt the Fish Gate—laying the beams then installing the doors with their bolts and bars.
[Nehemyah] [3]:[4] Uriyah’s son Meremot (the son of Hakots’s son Uriyah) rebuilt a section, as did Meshulam (son of Mesheyzavel’s son Berekyah) and Ba’ana’s son Tsadok.
[Nehemyah] [3]:[5] The Tekoim worked next to them, but their leaders wouldn’t actually help with the work.
[Nehemyah] [3]:[6] Paseah’s son Yoyada and Besodeyah’s son Meshulam rebuilt the Yeshanah Gate—laying the beams then installing the doors with their bolts and bars.
[Nehemyah] [3]:[7] Next to them was Melatyah the Givoni, Yadon the Meronoti, and men of Giveon and Mitspah rebuilding the section to the residence of the governor of the regions that side of the Perat (Euphrates).
[Nehemyah] [3]:[8] Next again was Harhayah’s son Uziel (one of the goldsmiths), then Hananyah (who was a son of the perfumers) rebuilt as far as the Broad Wall.
[Nehemyah] [3]:[9] Then it was Hur’s son Refayah, the administrator for half of the Yerushalem (Jerusalem) district.
[Nehemyah] [3]:[10] Harumaf’s son Yedayah repaired the section in front of his house, then Hashavneyah’s son Hatush made the next repairs.
[Nehemyah] [3]:[11] Harim’s son Malkiyah and Pahat-Moav’s son Hashuv repaired a section, as well as the Tower of Ovens.
[Nehemyah] [3]:[12] Next to them was Halohesh’s son Shalum, the administrator for another half of the Yerushalem district, helped by his daughters.
[Nehemyah] [3]:[13] Hanun and the inhabitants of Zanoah rebuilt the Valley Gate—installing the doors with their bolts and bars, as well as repairing 500m of wall along to the Dung Gate.
[Nehemyah] [3]:[14] Rekav’s son Malkiyah, the administrator for the Beyt-Hakerem district, rebuilt the Dung Gate—installing the doors with their bolts and bars.
[Nehemyah] [3]:[15] Kal-Hozeh’s son Shalun, the administrator for the Mitspah district, rebuilt the Fountain Gate—he built and covered it, installing the doors with their bolts and bars, and repaired the wall of the Shelah Pool from the king’s garden as far as the stairs that come down from the City of David.
[Nehemyah] [3]:[16] Next to him was Azbuk’s son Nehemyah (Nehemiah), the administrator for half of the Beyt-Tsur district
[Nehemyah] [3]:[17] Next to him were some Levites: Bani’s son Rehum, then Hashavyah (the administrator for half of the Ke’ilah district) did his district,
[Nehemyah] [3]:[18] then Henadad’s son Bavay the administrator for the other half of the Ke’ilah district.
[Nehemyah] [3]:[19] Then there was Yeshua’s son Ezer (the administrator of Mitspah) repaired a section opposite the steps up to the armoury where the wall turned at an angle.
[Nehemyah] [3]:[20] Then Zakay’s son Baruk enthusiastically repaired another section from that angle to the entrance to the house of the high priest Elyashiv.
[Nehemyah] [3]:[21] Next to him was Meremot (son of Hakots’ son Uriyah) who repaired another section from the doorway of Elyashiv’s house to the end of it.
[Nehemyah] [3]:[22] Next to them, some priests from the surrounding area made repairs.
[Nehemyah] [3]:[23] After them Benyamin and Hashuv repaired a section in front of their house, then Azaryah (son of Ananyah’s son Ma’aseyah) repaired beside his house,
[Nehemyah] [3]:[24] Henadad’s son Binuy repaired another section from Azaryah’s house to the corner,
[Nehemyah] [3]:[25] Uzay’s son Palal did opposite the corner and the tower above the palace by the guards’ courtyard, and then Par’osh’s son Pedayah.
[Nehemyah] [3]:[26] The temple servants who lived in Ofel repaired as far as the eastern side of the Water Gate and its tower.
[Nehemyah] [3]:[27] After them, the men from Tekoa repaired another section from opposite that tall tower to the Ofel wall.
[Nehemyah] [3]:[28] The priests repaired the section past the Horse Gate—each of them repairing the section in front of his own house.
[Nehemyah] [3]:[29] Next to them, Imer’s son Tsadok repaired opposite his house, then Shekanyah’s son Shemayah the gatekeeper at the Eastern Gate repaired the next section.
[Nehemyah] [3]:[30] After him was Shelemyah’s son Hananyah with Tsalaf’s sixth son Hanun working on a second section, then Berekyah’s sib Meshulam repairing a section in front of his quarters.
[Nehemyah] [3]:[31] Next was the goldsmiths’ son Malkiyah who repaired as far as the house of the temple servants and the merchants, opposite the Inspection Gate, and up to the upper room in the corner,
[Nehemyah] [3]:[32] and the other goldsmiths and some merchants repaired the last section of the wall from the upper room in the corner to the Sheep Gate.
[Nehemyah] [4]:[1] When Sanvalat heard that we were rebuilding the wall, he got really angry. He mocked the Yehudim (Jews)
[Nehemyah] [4]:[2] and he spoke before in front of his brothers and the army of Shomron (Samaria), “What are those feeble Yehudim doing? Do they think they’ll be able to rebuild that place themselves? Will they sacrifice? Will they get finished one day? Will they form the stones back together from piles of dust, when they’ve been weakened by the heat of the fires?”
[Nehemyah] [4]:[3] Toviyah the Amoni was standing beside him and confirmed, “Yes, even if a fox walked over that stone wall that they’re building, it would make it fall down.”
[Nehemyah] [4]:[4] I prayed, “Our god, listen to how we’re mocked and cause their words to return on their own heads and send them away as captives to become the plunder for another country.
[Nehemyah] [4]:[5] Don’t just cover over their evil, and don’t just ignore their sin, because they’ve repeatedly made the workers get angry.”
[Nehemyah] [4]:[6] So we kept on at building the wall, and eventually all the segments of wall were joined up together up to about half its full height, and so the people were encouraged to keep persevering.
[Nehemyah] [4]:[7] Now when Sanvalat, and Toviyah, and the Aravim, and the Amonim, and the Ashdodim heard that the Yerushalem (Jerusalem) walls were getting repaired and the breaks were beginning to be closed up, it made them extremely angry
[Nehemyah] [4]:[8] and they all got together to come to attack Yerushalem and to throw us into confusion.
[Nehemyah] [4]:[9] So we prayed to our god, as well as setting up a 24-hour guard to watch out for them.
[Nehemyah] [4]:[10] People around Yehudah (Judah) said, “The workers are running out of strength and there’s a lot of rubble still to be moved. Maybe we’re not up to building this wall.”
[Nehemyah] [4]:[11] Then those against us said, “We’ll rush in among them and kill some of them before they even see us or know that we’re coming, then that will bring the work to an end.”
[Nehemyah] [4]:[12] After that, whenever the Yehudim (Jews) living close to them came, they repeatedly warned us, “They’re going to attack us from all directions.”
[Nehemyah] [4]:[13] So I stationed guards behind the lowest places along the wall and where there were still gaps. I also made sure that the families stood guard with their swords, spears, and bows.
[Nehemyah] [4]:[14] I looked then I got organised and told the nobles and the prefects, and the rest of the people, “Don’t be afraid of their threats. Remember my powerful and fearsome master, and fight for your brothers, your sons and your daughters, your wives, and your houses.”
[Nehemyah] [4]:[15] After all that, when our enemies realised that we were aware of their intentions and that God had frustrated their surprise attack plan, we all returned to our work on the wall.
[Nehemyah] [4]:[16] So from that day onwards, half of my young men would work on the rebuilding, while the other half stood guard with spears, shields, and breastplates, and the officials encouraged them all from behind.
[Nehemyah] [4]:[17] Both those who were placing the stones on the wall and those who were carrying the heavy loads to them, always had their weapons with them in case of an attack.
[Nehemyah] [4]:[18] The builders had their swords strapped to their sides as they worked, and the man who would sound the trumpet stayed with me.
[Nehemyah] [4]:[19] Then I told the nobles and prefects, and the rest of the people, “This job is so large and extensive that we’re all separated from each other when we work on the wall,
[Nehemyah] [4]:[20] so whenever you all hear the trumpet blast, join us at that place. Our god will fight for us.”
[Nehemyah] [4]:[21] So we continued the work with half of them keeping their hands on their spears from the beginning of the day until the stars came out at night.
[Nehemyah] [4]:[22] Also at that time, I told the people, “Every worker including servants should spend the night inside the city, so they double as workers during the day and guards at night.”
[Nehemyah] [4]:[23] During that period of construction, none of us, not even our servants, stayed undressed or separated from our weapons, even when washing.
[Nehemyah] [5]:[1] However around then, there was a widespread complaint from the people and their wives against what their fellow Yehudim (Jews) were doing.
[Nehemyah] [5]:[2] Some of them complained, “There’s a lot of us when we include our sons and daughters. We need grain so we can eat and stay alive.”
[Nehemyah] [5]:[3] Others said, “We are mortgaging our fields and vineyards, and our houses so we can get grain during this famine.”
[Nehemyah] [5]:[4] Yet others said, “We’ve borrowed silver to pay the tax on our fields and our vineyards that goes to the tribute to be paid to the foreign king.
[Nehemyah] [5]:[5] We’re Yehudim just like our countrymen, but we’re having to commit our children into bondage as slaves—yes, even our daughters. Now we own nothing at all—not even our fields and vineyards.
[Nehemyah] [5]:[6] I got very angry when I heard their complaints and desperation,
[Nehemyah] [5]:[7] and I couldn’t get it out of my mind. I protested to the nobles and the officials, “You guys are charging interest against your own countrymen.” So I called for a gathering of all the people to deal with them,
[Nehemyah] [5]:[8] and I told them, “Our brothers, the Yehudim, were sold to other countries as slaves and we’ve done all we can to bring them back here. But now even you yourselves are buying and selling your own countrymen to make a profit.” They couldn’t argue against that, so they were just silent.
[Nehemyah] [5]:[9] “It’s not good what you’re doing,” I continued. “Shouldn’t you all respect and obey our god, because otherwise we’ll be despised by the other nations, our enemies.
[Nehemyah] [5]:[10] I myself have lent them money and grain, as have my brothers and my young men, but please let’s forgo charging interest.
[Nehemyah] [5]:[11] Please, even today, return their fields to them, and their vineyards and olive orchards, their houses, and the interest on the money and the grain, the new wine, and the oil that you are charging against them.”
[Nehemyah] [5]:[12] “Okay, we’ll do what you’re asking,” they responded. “We’ll return their property and we won’t impose any more charges on them.” So I called the priests to witness those nobles and officials making an oath to do what they’d said they would do.
[Nehemyah] [5]:[13] Also I shook the folds of my robe and told them, “May God shake you all out of his house like that, and shake every man’s business if he doesn’t do what he just promised—may he be shaken out like that and lose everything.”
[Nehemyah] [5]:[14] Also, from the day that I was appointed to be their governor in the Yehudah (Judah) region (for the twelve years from the Persian King Artahshashta’s (Artaxerxes) 20th year until his 32nd year), I myself didn’t accept the governor’s food allowance, nor did my relatives.
[Nehemyah] [5]:[15] The governors who preceded me had been very hard on the people—demanding bread and wine and forty silver coins. Even their servants oppressed the people. In contrast, I didn’t do that due to desire to honour God.
[Nehemyah] [5]:[16] Also I remained focused on rebuilding the wall, and we didn’t invest in a farm property, and all my servants also contributed to the work.
[Nehemyah] [5]:[17] I regularly fed a hundred and fifty Jewish leaders and city officials, as well as visitors from other countries around us,
[Nehemyah] [5]:[18] so in one day we needed one bull, six choice sheep, and various kinds of poultry, as well as various types of wines every ten days. I didn’t demand any of this from the people because it would have been a heavy burden for them. i
[Nehemyah] [5]:[19] My god, remember me for the good that I’ve done for these people.
[Nehemyah] [6]:[1] Although we didn’t yet have any doors in the gates, when Sanvalat and Toviyah and Geshem the Aravi and the rest of our enemies heard that we’d finished building the wall so it didn’t have any gaps left in it,
[Nehemyah] [6]:[2] Sanvalat and Geshem invited me, “We’d like to arrange to meet with you in one of the villages on the Ono plain.” But they were intending to harm me.
[Nehemyah] [6]:[3] So I sent messengers back to them, “This work is important and extensive, so I can’t afford to abandon it and have the work stop if I travelled down to you on the plain.”
[Nehemyah] [6]:[4] They tried four times to get me to go, but I kept refusing them for those same reasons.
[Nehemyah] [6]:[5] Then Sanvalat sent his servant to me a fifth time with the same request, but this time in an unsealed, open letter
[Nehemyah] [6]:[6] saying, “There’s rumours flying around in nearby countries, and Geshem confirms it, that you and the Yehudim (Jews) are building the wall because you’re all plotting thinking to rebel. Then you’d become their king, according to what we’re hearing.
[Nehemyah] [6]:[7] We’ve also heard that you’ve set up ‘prophets’ to speak out in Yerushalem (Jerusalem) to say about you, ‘There’s a king in Yehudah (Judah).’ By now, all of that will have been heard by the Persian king. So now, come and let’s discuss this together.”
[Nehemyah] [6]:[8] I sent a message straight back, “None of what you’re saying is true. It’s simply your own imagination at work.”
[Nehemyah] [6]:[9] We knew that they were just trying to frighten us so that we’d stop the repairs and it would never get finished. i My god, strengthen my hands.
[Nehemyah] [6]:[10] After that, I entered Shemayah’s house (the son of Meheytavel’s son Delayah) who was confined to his house, and he said, “Let’s set a time to meet in the temple—we’ll shut the temple doors because they’ll be coming to kill you—probably in the night.”
[Nehemyah] [6]:[11] But I disagreed, “Would a man like me run away? Besides that, who’s allowed to live inside the temple? I won’t do that.”
[Nehemyah] [6]:[12] Then I suddenly realised that God hadn’t told him to say that, but rather he was working against me because he’d been paid by Toviyah and Sanvalat.
[Nehemyah] [6]:[13] They must have hired him so that I’d be afraid and take that advice and sin. Then they could have ruined my reputation and discredited me. i
[Nehemyah] [6]:[14] My god, remember what Toviyah and Sanvalat have done, and also the prophetess Noadyah and the other prophets who’ve been trying to scare me.
[Nehemyah] [6]:[15] So the rebuilding of the wall was finished on the 25th of September in just fifty-two days,
[Nehemyah] [6]:[16] and when our enemies heard about it, the surrounding countries were afraid and discouraged because they realised that our god must have helped us.
[Nehemyah] [6]:[17] During that time, the Yehudah (Judah) nobles were sending many letters to Toviyah, and letters from Toviyah were also coming to them,
[Nehemyah] [6]:[18] because many people in Yehudah had ties with him because he was the son-in-law of Arah’s son Shekanyah, plus his son Yehohanan had married Berekyah’s daughter Meshulam.
[Nehemyah] [6]:[19] Those nobles kept telling me about the good things he was doing, and they reported my words back to him. Toviyah also sent letters to try to frighten me.
[Nehemyah] [7]:[1] Once the wall had been rebuilt and the doors hung in the gates, the gatekeepers and the singers and the Levites had been appointed.
[Nehemyah] [7]:[2] I put my brother Hanani and the fortress commander Hananyah in charge over Yerushalem (Jerusalem). (Hananyah was a faithful man and respected God more than many others do.)
[Nehemyah] [7]:[3] I told them, “Don’t open Yerushalem’s gates until broad daylight, and then shut and bar them again while the guards are still on full alert. And assign neighbourhood watch groups among the inhabitants to keep an eye on their own areas.”
[Nehemyah] [7]:[4] Now Yerushalem (Jerusalem) covered a large area but not many people had returned to live there yet, and the houses hadn’t yet been rebuilt.
[Nehemyah] [7]:[5] So God gave me the idea of gathering the leaders and the people grouped by their ancestors. I found the register of those who’d returned from exile to Yerushalem, with this written in it:
[Nehemyah] [7]:[6] “These are the descendants of the people exiled by the Babylonian King Nevukadnetsar (Nebuchadnezzar) , who returned to Yehudah (Judah) and to Yerushalem—each family returning to their own ancestral town.
[Nehemyah] [7]:[7] Their leaders were Zerubavel, Yeshua, Nehemyah (Nehemiah), Azaryah, Ra’amyah, Nahamani, Mordekai, Bilshan, Misperet, Bigvay, Nehum, and Ba’anah. The number of Israeli men:
[Nehemyah] [7]:[8] 2,172 descendants of Par’osh,
[Nehemyah] [7]:[9] 372 descendants of Shefatyah,
[Nehemyah] [7]:[10] 652 descendants of Arah,
[Nehemyah] [7]:[11] 2,818 descendants of Pahat-Moav (descendants of Yeshua and Yoav (Joab)),
[Nehemyah] [7]:[12] 1,254 descendants of Eylam,
[Nehemyah] [7]:[13] 845 descendants of Zatu,
[Nehemyah] [7]:[14] 760 descendants of Zakay,
[Nehemyah] [7]:[15] 648 descendants of Binuy,
[Nehemyah] [7]:[16] 628 descendants of Bevay,
[Nehemyah] [7]:[17] 2,322 descendants of Azgad,
[Nehemyah] [7]:[18] 667 descendants of Adonikam,
[Nehemyah] [7]:[19] 2,067 descendants of Bigvay,
[Nehemyah] [7]:[20] 655 descendants of Adin,
[Nehemyah] [7]:[21] 98 descendants of Ater (from Hizkiyah (Hezekiah)),
[Nehemyah] [7]:[22] 328 descendants of Hashum,
[Nehemyah] [7]:[23] 324 descendants of Betsay,
[Nehemyah] [7]:[24] 112 descendants of Harif,
[Nehemyah] [7]:[25] and 95 descendants of Giveon.
[Nehemyah] [7]:[26] Other men from these towns: 188 from Beyt-Lehem (Bethlehem) and Netofah,

[Nehemyah] [7]:[73] So the priests and the Levites, the gatekeepers and the singers, the temple workers and the rest of the Israelis, all settled in their various ancestral cities.
[Nehemyah] [8]:[1] All the people gathered together in the plaza near the Water Gate and asked Ezra the scribe to bring the scroll with Yahweh’s instructions to Yisrael (Israel) given through Mosheh (Moses).
[Nehemyah] [8]:[2] So it was the beginning of October when Ezra the priest brought the scroll to the gathering of men and women and everyone who wanted to understand it,
[Nehemyah] [8]:[3] and he read it aloud in the plaza near the Water Gate—reading from dawn until the middle of the day in front of those men and women and interested people, who all listened intently.
[Nehemyah] [8]:[4] Ezra the scribe stood on a raised wooden platform that they had made especially for this purpose. Standing on his right were Matityah, Shema, Anayah, Uriyah, Hilkiyah, and Ma’aseyah, and on his left stood Pedayah, Mishael, Malkiyah, Hashum, Hashbadanah, Zekaryah (Zechariah), and Meshulam.
[Nehemyah] [8]:[5] Up on the platform, Ezra opened the scroll in front of all the people, and as he did so, all the people stood up.
[Nehemyah] [8]:[6] Ezra blessed the great God Yahweh and the people raised their arms and responded, “May it be so.” Then they knelt down and bowed to Yahweh with their faces to the ground.
[Nehemyah] [8]:[7] Then Yeshua, Bani, Shereveyah, Yamin, Akuv, Shabtay, Hodiyah, Ma’aseyah, Kelita, Azaryah, Yozavad, Hanan, Pelayah, who were all Levites, explained what had been read to the people standing there.
[Nehemyah] [8]:[8] They read the scroll containing God’s instructions, explaining how it applied so the people could understand it.
[Nehemyah] [8]:[9] Then Nehemyah (Nehemiah) the governor and Ezra the priest & scribe, and the Levites who were explaining it, said to all the people, “Today is a sacred day—it belongs to your god Yahweh. Don’t mourn or weep.” That was because all the people were weeping after they heard Yahweh’s instructions to them.
[Nehemyah] [8]:[10] Then Nehemyah told them, “Go home and eat some special food with sweet drink, and share some with those who can’t afford such things because today is a sacred day that belongs to our master. And don’t grieve, because the happiness from Yahweh will make you all strong.”
[Nehemyah] [8]:[11] The Levites told the people to quieten down, saying, “Don’t grieve today because it’s a sacred day. Stay quiet.”
[Nehemyah] [8]:[12] So all the people went to eat and drink and to take plates of food to others, and to have a big celebration because they understood what had been read to them.
[Nehemyah] [8]:[13] The next day, all the clan leaders, and the priests and Levites, met with Ezra the scribe to study the instructions on the scroll.
[Nehemyah] [8]:[14] They discovered that it was written in the instructions that Yahweh had given through Mosheh (Moses), that the Israelis should live in temporary shelters during the celebration in their seventh month (our September-October).
[Nehemyah] [8]:[15] They should publicly proclaim in Yerushalem (Jerusalem) and in all their towns that the people should go into the hills and bring back branches from olive or wild olive trees, myrtle or palm trees, and/or other leafy trees to make shelters as it’s written.
[Nehemyah] [8]:[16] So the people went out and brought back branches to make shelters for themselves on their roofs or in their courtyards, or in the temple courtyard or in the plazas near the Water Gate and the Efrayim Gate.
[Nehemyah] [8]:[17] Then the whole assembly of people who’d come back from captivity made shelters and lived in them for one week. The Israelis hadn’t done that since the time of Yehoshua’s (Joshua) leadership, and they did it with a lot of celebration.
[Nehemyah] [8]:[18] Ezra read aloud from the scroll of God’s instructions each day of the seven days of celebration, then on the eighth day they all gathered together as per the instructions.
[Nehemyah] [9]:[1] On the 24th of that month, the Israelis dressed in sackcloth, put dust on their heads, fasted, and gathered together.
[Nehemyah] [9]:[2] Those of Jewish descent stood separately from the descendants of foreigners, and they confessed their own sins, as well as those of their ancestors.
[Nehemyah] [9]:[3] They stood and listened to the scroll with Yahweh’s instructions being read for three hours, then for another three hours they confessed and bowed down to Yahweh their god.
[Nehemyah] [9]:[4] Then Yeshua went up the Levites’ stairs with Bani, Kadmiel, Shevanyah, Buni, Shereveyah, another Bani, and Kenani, and they called out loudly to their god Yahweh.
[Nehemyah] [9]:[5] Then some Levites (Yeshua, Kadmiel, Bani, Hashavneyah, Shereveyah, Hodiyah, Shevanyah, and Petahyah) said, “Stand up and bless your eternal God Yahweh: May the peoples bless your wonderful reputation which is greater than anything else that we bless or praise.
[Nehemyah] [9]:[6] Yahweh, you alone are God. You yourself made the heavens, the galaxies in the heavens and all their stars, the earth and all that is on it, the seas and all that is in them. You give life to everything, and all the stars bow down to you.
[Nehemyah] [9]:[7] “You are Yahweh, the god who chose Avram. Then you brought him out from Ur in the Chaldean region, then you renamed him to Avraham (meaning ‘father of many’).
[Nehemyah] [9]:[8] You discovered that he was sincere and faithful to you, and made an agreement with him—to give the Kena’ani (Canaanite), Hiti, Amori, Perizi, Yevusi, and the Girgashi regions to his descendants, and you have ensured that it’s all come to be because you’re righteous.
[Nehemyah] [9]:[9] You noticed the suffering of our ancestors enslaved in Mitsrayim (Egypt), and then you heard their cry for help at the edge of the Red Sea.
[Nehemyah] [9]:[10] “You displayed miracles to Par’oh (Pharaoh), and to all his servants and to all the Mitsri (Egyptian) people, because you knew that they were acting as if you weren’t real, so you got yourself a reputation which you still have to this day.
[Nehemyah] [9]:[11] Then you split the sea open the sea right in front of their eyes, and they walked through the middle of it on dry land. After that, you drowned their pursuers into the deep sea like a stone in a huge lake.
[Nehemyah] [9]:[12] You led them during the day with a pillar of cloud, and during the night with a pillar of fire to illuminate the way that they should go.
[Nehemyah] [9]:[13] “Then you came down to Mt. Sinay and spoke with them from the sky, and you gave to them principles of justice and laws of truth—good statutes and instructions.
[Nehemyah] [9]:[14] You revealed the concept of a rest day to them, and you gave them rules and instructions and laws via your servant Mosheh (Moses).
[Nehemyah] [9]:[15] “You gave them bread from the sky when they were hungry, and you made water come out of a rock when they were thirsty, then eventually you told them to go ahead to possess the land that you had said that you’d give to them.
[Nehemyah] [9]:[16] “But our ancestors were proud and stubborn and they refused to obey your instructions.
[Nehemyah] [9]:[17] Not only did they refuse to listen, they forgot about all the miracles that you’d done for them and they became stubborn and appointed a leader to take them back to their slavery. But you are a god of forgiveness—gracious and compassionate, slow to get angry and generously showing loyal affection, and you didn’t abandon them.
[Nehemyah] [9]:[18] Even when they molded a metal calf for themselves and said, ‘This is your god who brought you out of Mitsrayim’ (Egypt), and they badly insulted you,
[Nehemyah] [9]:[19] you didn’t abandon them in the wilderness because you’re so merciful. You didn’t remove the pillar of cloud that led them on the way during the day, or remove the pillar of fire that shone at night for them to show them which way they should go.
[Nehemyah] [9]:[20] You gave them your good spirit to give them insight. You didn’t withhold your manna for them to eat, and you still gave them water to drink,
[Nehemyah] [9]:[21] yes, you sustained them in the wilderness for forty years—they had everything they needed—their clothes didn’t wear out, and their feet didn’t swell.
[Nehemyah] [9]:[22] “Then you handed kingdoms and people groups over to them, and you let them settle in even the far corners of the regions. They took possession of the King Sihon’s Heshbon region, and King Og’s Bashan region.
[Nehemyah] [9]:[23] You gave our ancestors lots of children so they were like the many stars in the sky, then you brought them into this land which you’d told their ancestors to enter and take ownership of.
[Nehemyah] [9]:[24] Their children went in and took over the land after you went ahead of them and subdued the previous inhabitants, the Kena’anim (Canaanites). You allowed them to defeat them and their kings, and the people groups in the land—letting them do whatever they wanted to do with them.
[Nehemyah] [9]:[25] They captured fortified cities and productive land, and they took over houses full of all good things, stone cisterns, vineyards and olive orchards, and lots of fruit trees. They ate and were satisfied, and grew fat and enjoyed themselves as a result of your amazing goodness.
[Nehemyah] [9]:[26] “But they disobeyed and rebelled against you, and they turned their backs on your instructions. They killed your prophets who testified against them in order to bring them back to you and they badly insulted you.
[Nehemyah] [9]:[27] So you allowed their enemies to harass and conquer them. Then in the time of their distress, they cried out to you, and you yourself heard from heaven. Because you’re so merciful, you sent saviours to them who rescued them from their enemies.
[Nehemyah] [9]:[28] After they’d returned to an era of peace, they reverted to doing evil again in front of you and you left them to submit to their enemies and the oppression that followed. Then they’d return and cry out to you, and you heard from heaven and delivered them many times because you’re merciful.
[Nehemyah] [9]:[29] You showed them their errors so they’d return to following your instructions, but instead they ignored you and didn’t obey your commands. They ignored your values which would have helped them if they’d lived by them and they turned a stubborn shoulder, stiffened their necks, and refused to listen.
[Nehemyah] [9]:[30] Yet you put up with them for many years, and you testified against them with your spirit through the messages of your prophets, but they still didn’t take any notice, so you allowed the other people groups to conquer them.
[Nehemyah] [9]:[31] However, because you’re so merciful, you didn’t abandon them and you didn’t wipe them out completely. Yes, you’re a god who’s gracious and merciful.
[Nehemyah] [9]:[32] “So now God, our amazing, powerful, and awesome God who keeps his agreements due to his loyal commitment, don’t just ignore all our current hardships affecting us, our kings and our leaders, our priests and our prophets, and our ancestors and all your people, from the period of the Assyrian kings until today.
[Nehemyah] [9]:[33] You are totally fair in allowing all that to happen to us, because you have behaved faithfully, but in contrast, we have behaved wickedly—
[Nehemyah] [9]:[34] and our kings, our leaders, our priests, and our ancestors haven’t obeyed your instructions and they haven’t bothered with following your commands or taking notice of your complaints that you made know to them.
[Nehemyah] [9]:[35] They served in their own kingdom and enjoyed the incredible goodness that you poured on them and the wide and prosperous land that you gave them, but they didn’t serve you, and they didn’t turn away from their evil actions.
[Nehemyah] [9]:[36] “Take notice of us today—we’re servants, and the land that you gave to our ancestors so we could eat its fruit and its produce, but look at us now—we’re servants in our own land.
[Nehemyah] [9]:[37] Now its plentiful produce belongs to the kings who you’ve placed over us due to our sins, and who rule over our bodies and over our livestock just however they want to, so we’re terribly distressed.
[Nehemyah] [9]:[38] “So now in all of this, we’re faithfully making an agreement, and our leaders, our Levites, and our priests will even write it down on a document and sign it.”

[Nehemyah] [10]:[28] The rest of the people, the priests, the Levites, the gatekeepers, the singers, the gatekeepers, and all the people who were prepared to dedicate themselves to obeying God rather than the customs of the former inhabitants of the land, their wives, their sons and their daughters, and everyone who was old enough to understand,
[Nehemyah] [10]:[29] were joining with their brothers, their nobles, and were committing to a promise which also had a curse: to obey God’s instructions as given by God’s servant Mosheh (Moses), and to keep and to do all the commands of Yahweh our master, accepting his judgements and his statutes.
[Nehemyah] [10]:[30] They committed to not giving their daughters to the other people groups in the land, and to not taking their daughters for their sons.
[Nehemyah] [10]:[31] On the rest day or other holy day, we won’t buy goods or grain from the peoples of the land (even if they bring it to sell it to us), and we won’t plant or harvest, or reclaim debts, in the seventh year.
[Nehemyah] [10]:[32] We will also pledge to each donate a week’s wages each year to support the temple functions
[Nehemyah] [10]:[33] including the bread displayed in rows, the continual offering and the continual burnt offering, for the rest day offerings and the new moons, for the appointed times and for the holy things, for the sin offerings to cover over Yisrael’s (Israel) guilt, and for all the operation of God’s residence.
[Nehemyah] [10]:[34] Then we threw dice to choose from among the priests, the Levites, and the people to create the roster for bringing firewood to the temple as an offering to be used at the appointed times each year for burning on the altar of Yahweh our god as written in the scrolls.
[Nehemyah] [10]:[35] Every year we will also bring the early produce from our soil and the first harvest from every fruit tree to Yahweh’s temple.
[Nehemyah] [10]:[36] We will dedicate our eldest male sons at the temple, and bring the eldest offspring of our herds and our flocks to the priests who serve at God’s residence.
[Nehemyah] [10]:[37] We will bring our offerings and the first of our flour, and the fruit of every tree, wine, and oil, for the priests, to the temple storerooms, and a tenth of our produce for the Levites. The Levites will be the ones receiving a tenth of our cash income in all the towns where we work.
[Nehemyah] [10]:[38] A priest who’s a descendant of Aharon (Aaron) must be with them when they collect the tenths, then the Levites must take a tenth of that to the temple to be placed in their treasury rooms.
[Nehemyah] [10]:[39] The Israelis and the Levites must bring the offerings of grain, wine, and oil to the storerooms. There must also be utensils for the sanctuary and the priests, for the ones who are ministering and the gatekeepers, and for the singers. We mustn’t neglect our god’s house.
[Nehemyah] [11]:[1] The people’s leaders lived in Yerushalem (Jerusalem), but the rest of the people drew straws to select one out of ten families to reside in Yerushalem the holy city—the other nine settled in the towns,

[Nehemyah] [11]:[3] In the towns in Yehudah (Judah), everyone lived on their own property. That included the Israelis, the priests and Levites, the temple servants, and the descendants of Shelomoh’s (Solomon) servants. The provincial officials lived in Yerushalem,

[Nehemyah] [11]:[32] in Anatot, Nov, and Anayah,
