[Iyov] [42]:[7] After Yahweh had said that to Iyov (Job), he told Elifaz (from Teyman), “I’m angry with you and your two friends, because what you all said about me wasn’t right, like what Iyov said.
[Iyov] [42]:[8] So now get seven bulls and seven rams and go to my servant Iyov and offer them as a burnt offering for yourselves. Then my servant Iyov will pray for you all. I’ll do what he asks and not deal with you like your foolishness deserves, because you all didn’t speak accurately about me like Iyov did.”
[Iyov] [42]:[9] So Elifaz (from Teyman) and Bildad (from Shuah) and Tsofar (from Na’amah) went and did what Yahweh had told them, and Yahweh accepted Iyov’s prayer.
[Iyov] [42]:[10] After Iyov (Job) had prayed for his friends, Yahweh changed his situation and gave him double what he had before.
[Iyov] [42]:[11] Then all of his brothers and sisters and everyone who’d known him before, came to his house and had a meal with him, and they comforted him and consoled him about all the troubles that Yahweh had brought on him. Then they each gave him a silver coin and a gold ring.
[Iyov] [42]:[12] Then Yahweh blessed the second part of Iyov’s life more than the first, and he ended up with 14,000 sheep, 6,000 camels, 1,000 working pairs of cows, and 1,000 female donkeys.
[Iyov] [42]:[13] He also had seven more sons and three more daughters
[Iyov] [42]:[14] who he named Yemimah, Ketsiah, and Keren-Hapuk.
[Iyov] [42]:[15] No one in the whole country was as beautiful as Iyov’s daughters, and as well as their brothers, their father gave them each a piece of land as an inheritance.
[Iyov] [42]:[16] Iyov lived another 140 years after all that, and was even able to see his great-grandchildren.
[Iyov] [42]:[17] Then Iyov died in good circumstances and at a very old age.

[Reflections] [1]:[1] The following are the words of the leader, David’s son, king in Yerushalem (Jerusalem):
[Reflections] [1]:[2] “Totally pointless,” says the leader. “A complete waste of time. Everything’s worthless.”
[Reflections] [1]:[3] What profit does humanity gain from all their hard work in this world?
[Reflections] [1]:[4] Generations come, and generations go, but the world just carries on going.
[Reflections] [1]:[5] The sun rises and the sun sets, then rushes around to its place, rising there again.
[Reflections] [1]:[6] Going to the south then around to the north, the wind is going, changing, turning, then it’s returning on its rounds.
[Reflections] [1]:[7] All the rivers flow into the sea but it never gets full. The place that the rivers are going to, they end up going there again.
[Reflections] [1]:[8] Everything is wearisome—not even worth talking about. The eyes never stop seeing, and your ears never fill up with everything they hear.
[Reflections] [1]:[9] Whatever that was in the past, it will be in the future, and everything that’s happened before, will happen again. There’s nothing new in this world.
[Reflections] [1]:[10] If someone says, “Look at this—it’s new,” well, it was already done long ago before we even got here.
[Reflections] [1]:[11] Things that happened in the past get forgotten, and the same will also happen for future events. People in the future will be exactly the same.
[Reflections] [1]:[12] I, the leader, was king over Yisrael (Israel) in Yerushalem (Jerusalem).
[Reflections] [1]:[13] I used my mind and wisdom to discover and to explore everything that is done in this world. It’s a difficult job that God has given humanity to be busy with.
[Reflections] [1]:[14] I saw everything that gets done in this world, and look—everything’s pointless like chasing after the wind.
[Reflections] [1]:[15] Something that’s bent can’t be straightened again, and what’s missing can’t be counted.
[Reflections] [1]:[16] I spoke with sincerity, saying, “Look at me—I’ve become powerful, and I’ve increased in wisdom relative to everyone who ruled before me here in Yerushalem (Jerusalem). My mind has acquired much knowledge and wisdom.”
[Reflections] [1]:[17] I made it my aim to discover knowledge and wisdom versus madness and folly. I was aware that that also is chasing after the wind
[Reflections] [1]:[18] because having much wisdom leads to much frustration and anyone who’s adding knowledge is also adding pain.
[Reflections] [2]:[1] I said to myself, “Come on, let me find out what’s good and enjoy the pleasure from them.” But look, it was also pointless.
[Reflections] [2]:[2] To laughter, I said, “It’s madness,” and to joy, “What’s the point of this?”
[Reflections] [2]:[3] I explored in myself how to indulge my body with wine, but my mind was guiding me in wisdom. Also, how to grasp foolishness until I could see whether that’s better for humanity to do while they live out their lives here on this earth.
[Reflections] [2]:[4] I expanded my program of works. I built houses for myself. I planted vineyards for myself.
[Reflections] [2]:[5] I made gardens for myself, and royal parks, and I planted all different kinds of fruit trees in them.
[Reflections] [2]:[6] I constructed pools for myself to irrigate a forest of growing trees.
[Reflections] [2]:[7] I acquired male and female servants, and the children born to them belonged to me. Also a large number of sheep and cattle belonged to me— more than all my predecessors in Yerushalem (Jerusalem).
[Reflections] [2]:[8] I also accumulated gold and silver for myself, and treasure from kings and from the provinces. I appointed male and female singers for myself, and the pleasures of the sons of humanity—many women.
[Reflections] [2]:[9] So I became famous, and I added more than all who preceded me in Yerushalem. Also my wisdom stayed with me.
[Reflections] [2]:[10] Everything my eyes wanted, I gave them. I didn’t hold back from anything that would make me happy, because I was happy inside from all my work and that was my reward from all my effort.
[Reflections] [2]:[11] And I turned, I, to all the things that I’d made and to the work that I’d done, and look, everything was pointless and chasing after the wind, and there wasn’t any profit in anything done in this world.
[Reflections] [2]:[12] Then I changed direction to investigate wisdom and madness and folly, because what could any future king do that hasn’t already been done?
[Reflections] [2]:[13] I saw that wisdom is to be preferred over folly, just as light is to be preferred over darkness.
[Reflections] [2]:[14] The wise person uses their eyes, but the fool walks in the darkness, and even I know that the same fate comes to both of them.
[Reflections] [2]:[15] I said to myself, “The fool’s end will also come to me, so what use was it being so wise back then?” Then I told myself that that also is pointless,
[Reflections] [2]:[16] because neither the wise person nor the fool will be remembered forever, as they’ll both be forgotten in the days to come— and how strange it is that the wise die just like the fool!

[Yeshayah] [1]:[1] This is the vision of Yeshayah (Isaiah) (son of Amots), which he saw concerning Yehudah (Judah) and Yerushalem (Jerusalem) in the days of Uziyah, Yotam (Jotham), Ahaz, and Hizkiyah (Hezekiah), kings of Yehudah.
[Yeshayah] [1]:[2] Hear, heavens, and listen, earth, because Yahweh has spoken: “I’ve raised sons and brought them up, ^but they’ve rebelled against me.
[Yeshayah] [1]:[3] The bull knows his owner, and the donkey knows its master’s feeding trough, but Yisrael (Israel) doesn’t know— my people don’t understand.”
[Yeshayah] [1]:[4] This sinful nation won’t come to a good end. these people who excel at disobeying. Descendants of those in the habit of doing evil things. Children who act corruptly. They have abandoned Yahweh. They have despised Yisrael’s holy one. They have estranged themselves from him.
[Yeshayah] [1]:[5] Why do you want more beatings? Why do you keep rebelling? Your whole head is sick, and your motivation is weak.
[Yeshayah] [1]:[6] From the sole of the foot up to the head nothing is healthy. Bruises and sores and fresh wounds haven’t been cleaned out, and they haven’t been bandaged or treated with olive oil.
[Yeshayah] [1]:[7] Your country is totally ruined with your cities all burnt down. Right in front of you, strangers are taking all the harvest from your field— leaving devastation and destruction behind.
[Yeshayah] [1]:[8] Tsiyon’s (Zion) daughter is left isolated like a hut in a vineyard, like a shed in a cucumber field, like a besieged city.
[Yeshayah] [1]:[9] If it wasn’t for the fact that Commander-in-chief Yahweh left a few survivors behind, we would have been wiped out like both Sedom and Amorah (Gomorrah).
[Yeshayah] [1]:[10] Hear what Yahweh has to say, you who are like Sedom’s rulers. Listen to God’s instructions, you who are like Amorah’s people:
[Yeshayah] [1]:[11] “What do your many sacrifices mean to me?” asks Yahweh. “I’ve had enough of the burnt offerings of rams, and the fat of fattened animals, and I’m not pleased by the blood of bulls or lambs or goats.
[Yeshayah] [1]:[12] Who told you all that you had to appear in front of me? Who said that you all should come and trample through my courtyards?
[Yeshayah] [1]:[13] Don’t keep bringing me worthless offerings. They smell terribly bad to me. New moon holidays and sabbaths, calling of assemblies— I can’t stand your disobedience mixed with your festive celebrations.
[Yeshayah] [1]:[14] My spirit hates your religious holidays and your feasts on the calendar. They’ve become a burden to me that I’m tired of carrying.
[Yeshayah] [1]:[15] So when you spread out your hands, I just hide my eyes from you all. Even though you multiply prayers, I don’t listen because your hands are full of blood.
[Yeshayah] [1]:[16] Wash yourselves and get cleaned up. Remove the evil of your actions from in front of me. Stop doing evil things.
[Yeshayah] [1]:[17] Learn to do good. Strive for justice. Correct the oppressor. Serve justice for the fatherless. Stand up for the widow in court.”
[Yeshayah] [1]:[18] Yahweh says, “Come, now, and let’s work things out together. Even though your sins are like scarlet, they’ll become as white like snow. Even though they’re red like crimson, they’ll become like wool.

[Yeshayah] [3]:[15] Why do you crush my people and rub the poor people’s faces into the ground?” That’s the declaration of my master, Commander-in-chief Yahweh.
[Yeshayah] [3]:[16] Then Yahweh said: “Because Tsiyon’s (Zion) daughters are proud, and they walk with their chins stuck out and with flirting eyes— walking and mincing their steps and tinkling their feet,
[Yeshayah] [3]:[17] Then my master will shave the heads of Tsiyon’s daughters, and Yahweh will make their foreheads bald.”
[Yeshayah] [3]:[18] At that time my master will remove their fancy ankle bracelets and headbands, crescent necklaces
[Yeshayah] [3]:[19] and earrings, bracelets and veils,
[Yeshayah] [3]:[20] scarves, armlets, and sashes, perfume bottles and charms,
[Yeshayah] [3]:[21] rings on their fingers and in their noses,
[Yeshayah] [3]:[22] festive robes and capes, veils and purses,
[Yeshayah] [3]:[23] fine clothes and underwear, and their turbans and shawls.
[Yeshayah] [3]:[24] When that happens, there’ll be a stink instead of fragrance, a rope instead of a nice sash, baldness instead of a styled hairdo, sackcloth instead of fancy clothes, brands on the skin instead of beauty,
[Yeshayah] [3]:[25] Your men will die from the sword and your warriors in the battle.
[Yeshayah] [3]:[26] The city gates will mourn and wail, and she’ll end up just sitting their on the ground, alone.
[Yeshayah] [4]:[1] When that happens, seven women will take hold of one man, saying, ‘We’ll eat our food and wear our clothes. Just let us marry you so we can take your name to remove our shame.’
[Yeshayah] [4]:[2] At that time, Yahweh’s branch will become beautiful and glorious, and the produce of the land will be a source of pride and delight for what remains of the Israelis.
[Yeshayah] [4]:[3] All who remain in Tsiyon (Zion), i.e., the remnant in Yerushalem (Jerusalem), will then be his people who are destined to continue to live.
[Yeshayah] [4]:[4] Surely my master will wash away the filth of Tsiyon’s daughters, and clean up the blood stains from the middle of Yerushalem using the spirit of judgement and the spirit of fire.
[Yeshayah] [4]:[5] Then over all of Mt. Tsiyon and her assemblies there, Yahweh will place a canopy over all the splendour—creating cloud during the day, and smoke and the brightness of a flaming fire during the night.
[Yeshayah] [4]:[6] During the day, it’ll be a shelter that gives shade from the heat, as well as being a cover and place to get out of the storm and rain.
[Yeshayah] [5]:[1] Let me sing, please, to my dearest one, a song for my darling about his vineyard. My dearest had a vineyard on very fertile hillside.
[Yeshayah] [5]:[2] He dug it over and cleared it and planted it with choice vines. He built a watchtower in the middle of it and also hewed a wine-pressing pit in a rocky portion. Then he waited for it to produce grapes, but it produced sour, wild grapes.
[Yeshayah] [5]:[3] So now, you who lives in Yerushalem (Jerusalem) and man from Yehudah (Judah), judge, please, between me and between my vineyard.
[Yeshayah] [5]:[4] What more could have been done for my vineyard, that I haven’t already done for it? I waited for it to produce grapes, but why did it produce wild grapes?
[Yeshayah] [5]:[5] So now, listen please, because I’ll tell you what I’m going to do to my vineyard: I’ll remove the hedge around it and burn it in a fire. I’ll tear its wall down so people can trample over it.
[Yeshayah] [5]:[6] Then I’ll allow it to become overgrown. It won’t be pruned or hoed, and thistles and thorns will grow through it. Then I’ll command the clouds not to rain on it any more.
[Yeshayah] [5]:[7] Yes, Commander-in-chief Yahweh’s vineyard is Yisrael (Israel), and the people from Yehudah (Judah) are his nice plants. Then he waited for justice, but look, slaughter came. He waited for people to do what’s right, but listen, screaming came.
[Yeshayah] [5]:[8] Those who acquire houses won’t end well, or those who add to their fields until there’s no room left. →Then the poor are made to remain alone in the middle of the country.
[Yeshayah] [5]:[9] I heard Commander-in-chief Yahweh say: ‘Surely many houses will end up empty— even large and nice ones won’t have anyone living in them.
[Yeshayah] [5]:[10] A large vineyard will produce a measly amount of juice, and ten baskets of seed will only give a harvest of one basket of grain.
[Yeshayah] [5]:[11] Those who get up early in the morning to get a strong drink won’t end well, yes, those who loiter into the night as wine inflames them.
[Yeshayah] [5]:[12] They celebrate with harp and lyre, tambourine and flute and wine, but they don’t care about anything that Yahweh does, in fact, they don’t even know what he’s done for them.
[Yeshayah] [5]:[13] Therefore, my people will be exiled because of their for lack of understanding, and its honourable people are hungry, and the parched crowds are thirsty.
[Yeshayah] [5]:[14] Therefore, the grave has enlarged its appetite and opened its mouth without limit. and its elite and its crowd will descend into it, along with its noisy crowd and those celebrating.
[Yeshayah] [5]:[15] Everyone will be brought into submission and humbled. All the proud people will be humiliated,
[Yeshayah] [5]:[16] and Commander-in-chief Yahweh will be honoured for his justice. God will demonstrate his holiness by doing what is right.
[Yeshayah] [5]:[17] Then the lambs will feed in their pastures, and fattened calves will graze around the houses.
[Yeshayah] [5]:[18] Those who pull in wickedness with cords of lies won’t end well, and nor will those who drag disobedience along behind them with cart ropes.
[Yeshayah] [5]:[19] They say, ‘Let him hurry, let him speed up his work so we can see what he’s doing, and let the counsel of the holy one of Yisrael (Israel) approach, and let it come and let us know.’
[Yeshayah] [5]:[20] Those who call evil good, and good evil, won’t end well. Nor will those who make darkness for light and light for darkness, or who set bitter as sweet and sweet as bitter!
[Yeshayah] [5]:[21] Those who are wise in their own eyes won’t end well, nor those who think they’re clever.
[Yeshayah] [5]:[22] Those who are experts at drinking wine won’t end well, nor those whose strength is mixing strong drinks,
[Yeshayah] [5]:[23] or those who take a bribe then say a wicked person is innocent, or those that deny justice to innocent people.
[Yeshayah] [5]:[24] Therefore, the roots of their families will rot, and their flowers will flower away like dust just like how a tongue of fire devours stubble in a field and the dry grass goes up in flame, because they’ve rejected Commander-in-chief Yahweh’s instructions, and they’ve despised the message from the holy one of Yisrael (Israel).
[Yeshayah] [5]:[25] That’s why Yahweh got very angry at his people, and he’s taken action against them and has struck them. The mountains tremble and their corpses become like garbage in the streets. In all these things, his anger doesn’t subside, and he doesn’t withdraw the actions he’s started.
[Yeshayah] [5]:[26] He’ll signal to faraway nations and will whistle to those at the ends of the earth. Then wow, how quickly they’ll show up.
[Yeshayah] [5]:[27] Those enemy armies won’t get tired or stumble. They won’t stop for a rest or to sleep. They never take their weapons off, or loosen the straps on their sandals.
[Yeshayah] [5]:[28] Their arrows are sharp, and all their bows are strung. Their horses have hooves as hard as flint, and their chariot wheels are like a windstorm.
[Yeshayah] [5]:[29] Their roar sounds like a lion, and they growl like young lions. They seize their prey and carry it off, →and there’s no rescuer in sight.
[Yeshayah] [5]:[30] They will roar above their prey on that day, like the roaring of the ocean. If someone looks across the land they’d only see darkness and distress. The light has been darkened by the clouds.
[Yeshayah] [6]:[1] In the year that King Uziyah died, I saw my master sitting on a tall, elevated throne, and his long robe covered the temple floor.
[Yeshayah] [6]:[2] There were ‘serafs’ standing above him. They each had six wings—they used two to cover their faces, two to cover their feet, and two to fly with.
[Yeshayah] [6]:[3] They were calling out to each other, “Commander-in-chief Yahweh is holy, yes, fully holy. The whole earth is filled with his splendour.”
[Yeshayah] [6]:[4] Whenever one of them spoke, the sound of their voices make the doorways shake, and the temple was filled with smoke,
[Yeshayah] [6]:[5] and I said, “This isn’t going to end well for me. Yes, I’m doomed because I am a man with unclean lips, and I live among a people with unclean lips, and yet my eyes have seen the king: Commander-in-chief Yahweh.”
[Yeshayah] [6]:[6] Then one of the ‘serafs’ flew to me. He was holding a hot coal that he’d taken off the altar with a pair of tongs.
[Yeshayah] [6]:[7] He touched my mouth with that coal and said, “Look, this has touched your lips, and your guilt has been taken away and the price has been paid for your sin.”
[Yeshayah] [6]:[8] Then I heard my master ask, “Who will I send? Who will go on our behalf?” “I’m here,” I answered. “Send me.”
[Yeshayah] [6]:[9] Then he said, “Go and tell that nation: ‘Listen closely, but don’t understand, and see clearly, but don’t perceive.’
[Yeshayah] [6]:[10] Fatten the heart of this people, and dull its ears and dim its eyes. Otherwise it might see with its eyes and hear with its ears and understand with its heart, →and turn and be healed.”
[Yeshayah] [6]:[11] So I asked, “Until when, master?” And he replied: “Until cities are desolate—without inhabitants, and the houses are without people, →and the land is a ruined wasteland,
[Yeshayah] [6]:[12] and Yahweh has driven the people far away, →and the middle of the country is almost totally deserted.
[Yeshayah] [6]:[13] If there’s still a tenth of the people in it, →then disaster will turn back and burn everything. Like an elm or an oak tree that’s been cut down but still has a stump— →so too the sacred remnant is the nation’s stump.”
[Yeshayah] [7]:[1] During the reign of King Ahaz (son of Yotam (Jotham), son of Uziyah) in Yehudah (Judah), King Retsin from Aram (Syria) and King Pekah (son of Remalyah) from Yisrael (Israel), went up to Yerushalem (Jerusalem) attack it, but they weren’t able to conquer it.
[Yeshayah] [7]:[2] Tt was reported to David’s descendants that Aram stands by with Efrayim (Ephraim), and the king and the people trembled just like the trees in the forest shaking in the wind.
[Yeshayah] [7]:[3] Then Yahweh told Yeshayah (Isaiah), “Please go out with your son She’ar-Yashuv to meet Ahaz at the end of the channel from the upper pool, near the road to the field where they wash clothes,
[Yeshayah] [7]:[4] and tell him, ‘Be careful and calm and don’t be afraid. Don’t let your courage melt away because of these two tails of smoldering firebrands, i.e., by the anger of Retsin and Aram and Remalyah’s son.
[Yeshayah] [7]:[5] Yes, they’ve plotted together against you, saying,
[Yeshayah] [7]:[6] “Let’s go up against Yehudah together and terrify her. Let’s break into her and crown Teve’el’s son as king right there in the middle of her.” ’
[Yeshayah] [7]:[7] However, my master Yahweh says: ‘That’s not going to happen. They won’t succeed
[Yeshayah] [7]:[8] because Aram’s capital is Damesek (Damascus) and Damesek’ leader is Retsin. Nevertheless, with sixty-five years Efrayim (Ephraim) (the northern kingdom) will no longer exist as a nation.
[Yeshayah] [7]:[9] Efrayim’s capital is Shomron (Samaria). and Shomron’s leader is Remalyah’s son. If you don’t keep believing, then you’ll end up not standing.’ ”
[Yeshayah] [7]:[10] Later, Yahweh spoke again to Ahaz,
[Yeshayah] [7]:[11] “Ask your god Yahweh for a sign of confirmation for yourself. Request an incredible miracle.”
[Yeshayah] [7]:[12] “No, I won’t ask,” Ahaz replied. “I refuse to test Yahweh.”
[Yeshayah] [7]:[13] Then Yeshayah (Isaiah) said, “You descendants of David need to listen. It’s bad enough that you’re wearing out the people, but why are you also annoying my god?
[Yeshayah] [7]:[14] Because of that, my master will take the initiative himself to choose a sign: listen, a young, virgin woman will become pregnant and give birth to a son, and will name him ‘Imanu-El’ (which means ‘God is with us’.).
[Yeshayah] [7]:[15] He’ll know how to refuse evil and do good by the time that he can eat yoghurt and honey.
[Yeshayah] [7]:[16] However, before the child is old enough to do that, the countries of the two kings that you’re afraid of, will become deserted.
[Yeshayah] [7]:[17] But instead, Yahweh will bring the Assyrian king to attack you and your people, and David’s dynasty will be under its greatest stress since Efrayim (Ephraim) (the northern kingdom) broke away from Yehudah (Judah).”
[Yeshayah] [7]:[18] When that happens, Yahweh will whistle for a fly that’s in Mitsrayim’s (Egypt) distant streams, and for a bee that’s in Ashur (Assyria).
[Yeshayah] [7]:[19] They’ll all come and settle down in deserted valleys and cracks in the rocks, and in all the thornbushes and watering holes.
[Yeshayah] [7]:[20] At that time, my master will use a hired razor from beyond the Perat (Euphrates) to shave the head and legs of the Assyrian king, and to remove his beard.
[Yeshayah] [7]:[21] In those days, a farmer will preserve a single, young cow alive, and a couple of sheep.
[Yeshayah] [7]:[22] However, because they’ll produce so much milk, they’ll produce yoghurt, because everyone left in the country will eat yoghurt and honey.
[Yeshayah] [7]:[23] During that period, every block of land with a thousand grapevines that would have been worth a thousand silver coins, will just be full of thistles and thorns.
[Yeshayah] [7]:[24] Because it’ll be so overgrown with briers, men will hunt there with their bows and arrows.
[Yeshayah] [7]:[25] All the hills that had been cultivated, will now be off limits because of all the thistle and thorns, and sheep and cattle will be left there to tread it down.

[Yeshayah] [36]:[1] In the fourteenth year of the reign of King Hizkiyah (Hezekiah), Ashur’s (Assyria) King Sanheriv (Sennacherib) attacked Yehudah’s (Judah) fortified cities and captured them.
[Yeshayah] [36]:[2] Then from Lakish, the Assyrian king sent his top negotiator to King Hizkiyah in Yerushalem (Jerusalem) with a large army. He stopped by the aqueduct at the upper pool on the road to the field where women wash clothes,
[Yeshayah] [36]:[3] and Hilkiyah’s son Elyakim, the palace supervisor, went out to meet him, taking Shevna the administrator, and Asaf’s son Yoah the secretary.
[Yeshayah] [36]:[4] The negotiator instructed them, “Tell Hizkiyah that Ashur’s powerful king wants to know who or what you think you’re trusting in to rescue you?
[Yeshayah] [36]:[5] Your plan and war preparations are only hot air, so who are you relying on that encourages you to rebel against me?
[Yeshayah] [36]:[6] Listen, if it’s Mitsrayim (Egypt), that’s like trusting a staff made from a splintered reed. If a man were to lean on it, it would pierce his palm—that’s what relying on Mitsrayim’s King Par’oh (Pharaoh) is like for those who put their trust in him.
[Yeshayah] [36]:[7] But if you tell me that you’re relying on your god Yahweh, hasn’t Hizkiyah removed his hilltop shrines and altars, and forced all Yehudah to worship him in front of the altar there in Yerushalem?
[Yeshayah] [36]:[8] “So now, make a deal with my master, the Assyrian king. Let me give you two thousand horses if you can find that many riders for them.
[Yeshayah] [36]:[9] How could you even repel a captain who’s one of the least of my master’s servants since you’ve been relying on Mitsrayim for chariots and horsemen to rescue you?
[Yeshayah] [36]:[10] Also, listen, I didn’t come here to destroy this region without Yahweh—it was Yahweh who told me to come here and destroy this nation.”
[Yeshayah] [36]:[11] Then Elyakim and Shevna and Yoah asked the negotiator, “Please speak Aramit to your servants, because we understand it. Don’t speak to us in Hebrew in the hearing of the people who are up on the wall.”
[Yeshayah] [36]:[12] But the negotiator replied, “Do you think that my master sent me to give this message just to you and your master? Don’t you think that it’s also for the men sitting on the wall who’ll have to join you in eating their own dung and drinking their own urine?”
[Yeshayah] [36]:[13] Then the negotiator stood and looked up, and shouted in Hebrew, “Listen to this message from the great Assyrian king.
[Yeshayah] [36]:[14] The king says not to let your king Hizkiyah deceive you all, because he won’t be able to save you.
[Yeshayah] [36]:[15] Don’t let him make you rely on Yahweh by telling you all that Yahweh will rescue you, and that this city won’t be captured by the Assyrian king.
[Yeshayah] [36]:[16] No, don’t listen to Hizkiyah, because the Assyrian king says that if you all surrender and come out here, you’ll be allowed to continue to harvest your own grapevines and fig trees, and everyone will be able to drink the water from their own wells
[Yeshayah] [36]:[17] until I come and take you to a land like your own that has grain and new wine—a land with bread and vineyards.
[Yeshayah] [36]:[18] “Don’t let Hizkiyah (Hezekiah) mislead you all by saying that Yahweh will rescue you. Did the gods of any other nations saved them from the Assyrian king’s power?
[Yeshayah] [36]:[19] Where were Hamat and Arpad’s gods? Where were Sefarvayim’s gods? Did any gods save Shomron (Samaria) from my power?
[Yeshayah] [36]:[20] From all those regions, which of their gods saved them from my power, so what makes you all think that Yahweh will save Yerushalem (Jerusalem) from me.”
[Yeshayah] [36]:[21] But those on the wall kept silent and didn’t answer him, because King Hizkiyah had ordered them not to respond.
[Yeshayah] [36]:[22] Then Elyakim (Hilkiyah’s son who was the palace supervisor) and Shevna (the administrator) and Yoah (the secretary) returned to Hizkiyah with their clothes torn in grief and passed the negotiator’s messages on to him.
[Yeshayah] [37]:[1] When King Hizkiyah (Hezekiah) heard the report, he torn his clothes too, and covered himself with sackcloth and went into Yahweh’s residence.
[Yeshayah] [37]:[2] Then he sent Elyakim (the palace supervisor) and Shevna (the administrator) and the elders of the priests to go to Yeshayah (Isaiah), the son of Amots the prophet,
[Yeshayah] [37]:[3] and they told him, “King Hizkiyah says that today is a day of distress and rebuke and disgrace, like when children go to their mother who’s about to deliver her baby but she doesn’t have the strength to give birth.
[Yeshayah] [37]:[4] Perhaps your god Yahweh heard the messages from the negotiator who was sent by his master, the Assyrian king, to defy the living god. Perhaps Yahweh will rebuke him for the words that Yahweh heard. So send up a prayer for the remnant of us here.”
[Yeshayah] [37]:[5] When King Hizkiyah’s servants got to Yeshayah,
[Yeshayah] [37]:[6] he told them to tell their master, “Yahweh says not to be afraid because of the words that you heard when the Assyrian king’s servants insulted me.
[Yeshayah] [37]:[7] Listen, I’ll put a spirit in him and he’ll hear a report that he needs to return to his own country, and then I’ll cause him to be assassinated at home.”
[Yeshayah] [37]:[8] Then the Assyrian negotiator returned to find the Assyrian king because he’d heard that he had left Lakish, and he found him fighting against Livnah.
[Yeshayah] [37]:[9] Then the king heard that Kush’s (Ethiopia) King Tirhakah was marching out to attack him, so he sent messengers back to Hizkiyah (Hezekiah) with instructions,
[Yeshayah] [37]:[10] “Tell Yehudah’s (Judah) King Hizkiyah: don’t let your god that you trust in, deceive you by telling you that Yerushalem (Jerusalem) won’t be conquered by the Assyrian king.
[Yeshayah] [37]:[11] Listen, you’ve heard how that the Assyrian kings have destroyed all the other regions. Don’t think that you’ll be saved.
[Yeshayah] [37]:[12] Did the gods of those other nations save them—places like Gozan and Haran and Retsef, and the people of Eden who lived in Telasar?
[Yeshayah] [37]:[13] What happened to the kings of Hamat, Arpad, La’ir, Sefarvayim, Hena, and Ivah?”
[Yeshayah] [37]:[14] Hizkiyah (Hezekiah) accepted the letter brought by the messengers and read it. Then he went into Yahweh’s residence and spread it out in front of Yahweh
[Yeshayah] [37]:[15] and prayed to Yahweh, saying,

[Yeshayah] [38]:[14] I chirp like a swallow and moan like a dove. My eyes feel weak from looking upwards. I’m oppressed, my master, help me out.
[Yeshayah] [38]:[15] What will I say? He told me and then he did it. I’ll walk slowly my remaining years because of my soul’s bitterness.

[Yeshayah] [44]:[12] The blacksmith takes a tool and works on the iron over the coals. He hammers it with his strong arm to form it into shape. But then he gets hungry and feels weaker. If he doesn’t drink water, he’ll feel exhausted.
[Yeshayah] [44]:[13] The carpenter measures a piece of wood. He outlines it with a marker and works it with his chisels. He outlines it with a compass and makes it like the figure of a man— like a good-looking man who might live in a house.
[Yeshayah] [44]:[14] He cuts down cedar trees or selects a cypress or an oak. He lets it grow strong among the trees in the forest. He plants a fir tree and the rain makes it grow.
[Yeshayah] [44]:[15] Then the wood is used by humankind to burn. The carpenter uses some of the wood to warm himself, Yes, he kindles a fire and bakes bread on it. He also makes a god out of it and bows down to it. He makes the wood into an idol and kneels in front of it.
[Yeshayah] [44]:[16] He burns half of the wood for the fire, and roasts meat on that half—he eats the meat and is satisfied. He also warms himself and says ‘Aha, I’m warm,’ as he looks at the fire.
[Yeshayah] [44]:[17] He uses the rest of the wood to make a god. He makes an idol and kneels in front of it. He bows down and prays to it →and says, ‘Rescue me, because you’re my god.’

[Yirmiyah] [1]:[1] These are the messages from Hilkiyah’s son, Yirmiyah (Jeremiah)—one of the priests who were in Anatot in Benyamin’s territory.
[Yirmiyah] [1]:[2] Yahweh’s messages started coming to him when Yehudah’s (Judah) King Yoshiyah (Josiah) (Amon’s son) was in the thirteenth year of his reign.
[Yirmiyah] [1]:[3] It continued through the reign of Yoshiyah’s son, King Yehoyakim until the end of the eleventh year of the reign of Yoshiyah’s son, King Hizkiyah (Hezekiah)—Yerushalem (Jerusalem) was exiled in the fifth month of that year.
[Yirmiyah] [1]:[4] Now Yahweh’s message came to me:
[Yirmiyah] [1]:[5] “Before I formed you in your mother, I already knew you, and before you came out of the womb, I had a plan for you. I appointed you as a prophet to the nations.”
[Yirmiyah] [1]:[6] But I said, “Oh no, Yahweh, my master. Listen, I don’t know how to speak, because I’m just a young lad.”
[Yirmiyah] [1]:[7] but Yahweh told me, “Don’t say that you’re only a child, because you must go to everyone I send you to and you must tell them everything that I command you to say.
[Yirmiyah] [1]:[8] Don’t be afraid of them, because I’ll be with you to rescue you.” That’s Yahweh’s message.
[Yirmiyah] [1]:[9] Then Yahweh stretched out his hand and touched my mouth and said, “Listen, I’ve put my messages into your mouth.
[Yirmiyah] [1]:[10] I’m appointing you today over the nations and kingdoms—to uproot and to break down, to destroy and to pull down, to build and to plant.”
[Yirmiyah] [1]:[11] Another time, Yahweh’s message came to me, saying, “Yirmiyah (Jeremiah), what do you see?” “I see a branch from an almond tree,” I replied.
[Yirmiyah] [1]:[12] Then Yahweh told me, “You’ve done well to see that, because I keep watch on my message to make sure it happens.”
[Yirmiyah] [1]:[13] Then Yahweh asked me a second time what I was seeing, and I replied, “I see a pot full of boiling water and it’s tipping towards the north.”
[Yirmiyah] [1]:[14] “Yes, disaster will come from the north and be released onto all the inhabitants of this region,” Yahweh continued.
[Yirmiyah] [1]:[15] “Listen, I’m about to summon all the clans of the northern kingdoms, and they’ll come and attack the walls around Yerushalem (Jerusalem) and all of Yehudah’s (Judah) other cities, then each king will place his throne at the entrance to Yerushalem’s gates.” That is Yahweh’s declaration.
[Yirmiyah] [1]:[16] “That’s how I’ll judge my people for their wickedness as they’ve abandoned me and sacrificed to other gods and bowed down to idols that they made with their own hands.
[Yirmiyah] [1]:[17] So Yirmiyah (Jeremiah), get yourself ready and go and tell them everything that I’ll tell you. Don’t be scared in front of them or else I’ll scare you right there in front of them!
[Yirmiyah] [1]:[18] And listen, today I’ve you as strong as a fortified city and an iron pillar and bronze walls, as far as the kings of Yehudah are concerned, along with their officials and priests, and the general population.
[Yirmiyah] [1]:[19] They’ll oppose you but they won’t be able to defeat you because I’ll be with you to rescue you,” says Yahweh.

[Yirmiyah] [13]:[16] Give honour to your god Yahweh before he brings darkness, and before he causes you all to stumble on the mountains at twilight, because you’re hoping for light, but he’ll turn the place into deep darkness—into a dark cloud.

[Yirmiyah] [13]:[19] The cities of the Negev have been shut up, and there’s no one to open them again. Yehudah (Judah) has been taken into exile— they’ve all been taken far away.

[Yirmiyah] [13]:[22] Then as a country you’ll ask why those things have happened to you. It’s the magnitude of your disobedience that’s caused your skirt to be lifted and your body to be treated with violence.
[Yirmiyah] [13]:[23] An Kushi (Ethiopian) person can’t change their skin colour and a leopard can’t change its spots. Similarly you all aren’t able to do good as you’re all so accustomed to doing evil.
[Yirmiyah] [13]:[24] I’ll scatter them like straw that’s blown across the wilderness by the wind.
[Yirmiyah] [13]:[25] Yahweh declares that that’s your part of your inheritance as you’ve forgotten me and trusted in lies.
[Yirmiyah] [13]:[26] So I’ll also pull your skirt up over your face and then your shame will become visible.
[Yirmiyah] [13]:[27] I’ve seen your adultery and neighing— the wickedness of your prostitution on the hills and across the countryside. I’ve seen your detestable behaviour. You won’t end well, Yerushalem (Jerusalem). How long will you remain ‘unclean’?
[Yirmiyah] [14]:[1] This is Yahweh’s message to Yirmiyah (Jeremiah) regarding droughts:
[Yirmiyah] [14]:[2] Yehudah (Judah) is in mourning and its gates are neglected. They’re mourning for the land and Yerushalem (Jerusalem) is crying out in distress.
[Yirmiyah] [14]:[3] The leading citizens send their servants out for water, but when they get to the wells, they didn’t find any. They return with empty containers— ashamed and humiliated, and with their heads covered in grief.
[Yirmiyah] [14]:[4] The ground is cracked open because there hasn’t been any rain. The farmers are ashamed—they’ve covered their heads in grief,

[Yirmiyah] [14]:[6] Wild donkeys stand on bare hills and pant for breath like jackals— their eyes have failed because there’s no vegetation.
[Yirmiyah] [14]:[7] Even though our transgressions testify against us, do something, Yahweh, for the sake of your reputation because we sinned against you with our frequent rebellion.
[Yirmiyah] [14]:[8] You are Yisrael’s (Israel) hope—the one who rescues it at a time of distress. Why would you act like a stranger in the land— like a traveller who’s stopped in to stay the night.

[Yirmiyah] [14]:[11] Yahweh told me, “Don’t pray for good to come to this nation
[Yirmiyah] [14]:[12] because even if they fast, I won’t listen to their petition, and when they offer up a burnt offering and a grain offering, I won’t be accepting them, because I’m bringing an end to them by the sword, and famine, and disease.”
[Yirmiyah] [14]:[13] Then I said, “Oh no, my master Yahweh. Listen, the prophets are telling the people that they won’t experience war or famine because you’ll give them ongoing peace in this place.”
[Yirmiyah] [14]:[14] “The prophets use my name but speak deceitfully,” Yahweh answered. “I didn’t appoint them and I didn’t send them, and I didn’t give them a false vision. The worthless prophecies that they’re proclaiming to you all come from their own minds.”
[Yirmiyah] [14]:[15] Therefore Yahweh says, “Now those prophets who I never sent but who are using my name and say that no war or famine will happen in this region, well those prophets will meet their own ends through war and famine.
[Yirmiyah] [14]:[16] Then the people that they prophesied to will be thrown out into Yerushalem’s (Jerusalem) streets because of famine and war. No one will be there to bury them or their wives, sons, or daughters, as I’ll pour their wickedness out onto them.
[Yirmiyah] [14]:[17] Then you’ll pass this message onto them: Day and night the tears run down my eyes. Don’t let them stop, because of the terrible damage as my virgin daughter has been shattered— my people have received a very severe wound.
[Yirmiyah] [14]:[18] If I go out into the countryside, wow, I see those who were killed by the sword. Then if I go into the city, wow, there’s diseases caused by famine, because both prophets and priests have gone into a land that they weren’t familiar with.
[Yirmiyah] [14]:[19] Have you completely rejected Yehudah (Judah)? Do you really hate Tsiyon (Zion)? Why have you struck us when there’s no healing for us? We eagerly hoped for peace, but there was nothing good. We hoped for a time of healing, but wow, we got terror!
[Yirmiyah] [14]:[20] Yahweh, we acknowledge our wickedness— the transgression of our ancestors. Yes, we’ve sinned against you.
[Yirmiyah] [14]:[21] For the sake of your reputation, don’t reject us. Don’t treat the place hosting your wonderful throne with contempt. Remember your agreement with us, and don’t break it.
[Yirmiyah] [14]:[22] Do those useless idols from other countries send rain? Do they cause showers to fall? Isn’t it you, our god Yahweh, who does that? We eagerly wait for you, because you’re the one who does all those things.
[Yirmiyah] [15]:[1] Then Yahweh told me, “Even if Mosheh (Moses) or Shmuel (Samuel) were standing in front of me, I still wouldn’t be in favour of this group of people. Send them out away from me, and let them go away.
[Yirmiyah] [15]:[2] If anyone comes to ask you where they should go, tell them that this is what Yahweh says: Those who are destined for death, will die. Those for the sword, will die in war. Those for famine, will suffer starvation. Those for exile, will be taken away in captivity.
[Yirmiyah] [15]:[3] Yahweh declares that he’ll assign them to four groups: 1. killed by the sword, 2. dragged away by wild dogs, 3. assigned to the birds of prey, and 4. assigned to be devoured and destroyed by wild animals.

[Yirmiyah] [15]:[8] I’ll make more widows for them than sand grains on the beach. I’ll send a destroyer against the mothers of their young men at midday. I’ll make shock and horror fall on them suddenly.

[Yirmiyah] [15]:[10] Poor me, mother, that you gave birth to me— a man of strife and contention throughout the entire region. I haven’t lent money or borrowed it yet they all curse me.
[Yirmiyah] [15]:[11] Yahweh said, Won’t I rescue you for good? Won’t I make your enemies plead with you in a time of evil and distress?
[Yirmiyah] [15]:[12] Can anyone break iron— iron from the north, or bronze?
[Yirmiyah] [15]:[13] I’ll give your wealth and treasures to your enemies as plunder without them having to pay as the price for all your sins committed across all your territories.
[Yirmiyah] [15]:[14] Then I’ll make you serve your enemies in a land that you hadn’t been to before because the fire of my anger towards you all has been kindled and will burn.
[Yirmiyah] [15]:[15] Yahweh, you know my situation. Take note of my situation and bring your vengeance to those harassing me. Don’t be patient with them and let them take me away. Know that I suffer reproach for your sake.
[Yirmiyah] [15]:[16] Your messages were found and I consumed them. Your message to me made me happy and gave me cause for celebration because I bear your name, Commander-in-chief Yahweh, god of armies.
[Yirmiyah] [15]:[17] I didn’t sit among the gathering of the merry makers, but rather, I enjoyed feeling your presence. I sat alone because you’d filled me with indignation.
[Yirmiyah] [15]:[18] Why is my pain ongoing and my wound incurable, refusing to be healed? Will you be like a spring that lets me down when its supply is unreliable?

[Yirmiyah] [15]:[20] I’ll make you like an impenetrable bronze wall to this people, and they’ll fight against you. However, they won’t defeat you, because I’ll be with you to save you, and to rescue you. That is Yahweh’s declaration.
[Yirmiyah] [15]:[21] Then I’ll rescue you from the plots of wicked people and I’ll buy your freedom from the ruthless people.

[Yirmiyah] [17]:[1] Yehudah’s (Judah) sin is written with an iron stylus that has a diamond point. It’s engraved on the tablet which is their hearts, and on the projecting corners of your altars.

[Yirmiyah] [17]:[11] A partridge hatches an egg that it didn’t lay. Someone might get rich by unjust means but right in the middle of their life it’ll leave them and in the end, that person will be a fool.

[Yirmiyah] [17]:[22] Don’t bring a load out from your homes on the rest day. Don’t do any work, but set apart the rest day, just as I instructed your ancestors to do.

[Yirmiyah] [18]:[1] Yahweh’s message came to Yirmiyah (Jeremiah) to say,
[Yirmiyah] [18]:[2] “Get ready and go down to the potter’s house, and I’ll give you my messages there.”
[Yirmiyah] [18]:[3] So I went down to pottery factory, and wow, he was on his potter’s wheel.
[Yirmiyah] [18]:[4] However, the container that he was making with his hand on the clay was ruined, so he started again and make it into another container that he was pleased with.
[Yirmiyah] [18]:[5] Then Yahweh gave me this message:
[Yirmiyah] [18]:[6] Like that potter, shouldn’t I be able to do what I want with you Israelis? Yahweh declares that you Israelis are in my hand like that clay in the potter’s hand.

[Yirmiyah] [18]:[8] and later on, that nation that I spoke to might turn away from its evil, and then I’ll cancel the destruction that I’d planned for them.
[Yirmiyah] [18]:[9] Another time, I might declare that a nation or kingdom will be established, or strengthened,
[Yirmiyah] [18]:[10] however if I see it doing evil and not listening to my voice, then I’ll cancel the good that I’d said I’d do to it.

[Yirmiyah] [24]:[3] Then Yahweh asked me, “Yirmiyah (Jeremiah), what do you see?” “Figs,” I replied. “Some figs that look very good, and others that are so bad they’re inedible.”

[Yirmiyah] [26]:[1] Near the beginning of the reign of Yehoyakim (Yoshiyah’s (Josiah) son), this message came from Yahweh:
[Yirmiyah] [26]:[2] Yahweh says this: Stand in the courtyard of my temple and speak about all of Yehudah’s (Judah) cities who come to worship at my residence. Proclaim all the messages that I’ve commanded you to say to them—don’t hold anything back.
[Yirmiyah] [26]:[3] Maybe they’ll listen and everyone will turn from their wicked ways, and then I would turn back the disaster that I’m planning to send to them because of their wicked behaviour,
[Yirmiyah] [26]:[4] so you need to tell them that Yahweh says this: If you don’t listen to me so as to follow my instructions that I’ve given to you all,
[Yirmiyah] [26]:[5] if you don’t listen to the words of my servants the prophets that I’ve been regularly sending to you, and indeed you haven’t listened,
[Yirmiyah] [26]:[6] then I’ll destroy this house like I did at Shiloh and I’ll turn this city into a curse to/for all the nations in the world.
[Yirmiyah] [26]:[7] The priests, the prophets, and all the people heard Yirmiyah (Jeremiah) proclaiming those words at Yahweh’s temple.
[Yirmiyah] [26]:[8] Then as soon as Yirmiyah had finished saying everything that Yahweh had commanded him to tell all the people, the priests and the prophets and all the people seized him and threatened to kill him, saying:
[Yirmiyah] [26]:[9] Why have you prophesied in Yahweh’s name and said that this temple will be destroyed like Shiloh, and that this city will become desolate, with no inhabitants?” Then all the people gathered together against Yirmiyah at Yahweh’s residence.
[Yirmiyah] [26]:[10] Then Yehudah’s (Judah) officials heard about what was going on, and they went up from the palace to the temple where they sat in the gateway at the New Gate at Yahweh’s residence.
[Yirmiyah] [26]:[11] Then the priests and the prophets spoke to the officials and to all the people, saying, “It’s right for this man to die, because he prophesied against this city, as you’ve all heard with your own ears.”
[Yirmiyah] [26]:[12] So Yirmiyah spoke to all the officials and all the people and said, “Yahweh has sent me out to prophesy to say all the words that you have heard, against both this temple and this city.
[Yirmiyah] [26]:[13] So now, improve your ways and your practices, and listen to the voice of your god Yahweh so that he’ll relent concerning the disaster that he’s proclaimed against you all.
[Yirmiyah] [26]:[14] As for me, here I am in your hands—do to me whatever you think is right and proper.
[Yirmiyah] [26]:[15] However, you must surely know that if you kill me, then you’re all bringing innocent blood on yourselves and on this city and its inhabitants, because Yahweh has truly sent me to you to proclaim all these messages for you all to hear.”
[Yirmiyah] [26]:[16] Then the officials and all the people said to the priests and to the prophets, “This man doesn’t deserve to be sentenced to death, because he’s spoken to us in the name of our god, Yahweh.”
[Yirmiyah] [26]:[17] Then some of Yehudah’s (Judah) elders stepped forward and spoke to all the people who were gathered there,
[Yirmiyah] [26]:[18] “Mikah (from Morashet) prophesied during the lifetime of Yehudah’s King Hizkiyah (Hezekiah), and he told all the people from Yehudah that Commander-in-chief Yahweh says this: Tsiyon (Zion), a field will be ploughed, and Yerushalem (Jerusalem) will become heaps of ruins, and the temple hill will become an overgrown forest.
[Yirmiyah] [26]:[19] Did Yehudah’s King Hizkiyah or anyone else in Yehudah put him to death? Didn’t Hizkiyah respect and honour Yahweh and ask for his favour, and didn’t Yahweh relent from sending the disaster that he had pronounced against them? It seems that we’re about to bring great harm on ourselves.”
[Yirmiyah] [26]:[20] Now there was another man prophesying in Yahweh’s name of Yahweh: Uriyah (son of Shemayah from Kiryat-Yearim) who prophesied against this city and against this land with similar messages to Yirmiyah (Jeremiah).
[Yirmiyah] [26]:[21] When King Yehoyakim and all his warriors and all the officials heard his words, the king wanted to put him to death. However when Uriyah heard about it, he became afraid, and he fled and went to Mitsrayim (Egypt).
[Yirmiyah] [26]:[22] However, King Yehoyakim sent Akbor’s son Elnatan and several other men to Mitsrayim to get Uriyah.
[Yirmiyah] [26]:[23] They brought Uriyah back from Mitsrayim and took him to King Yehoyakim who ran him through with a sword and threw his corpse into the public graveyard.
[Yirmiyah] [26]:[24] However, Shafan’s son Ahikam supported Yirmiyah and didn’t allow the people to kill him.
[Yirmiyah] [27]:[1] At the beginning of the reign of Yehudah’s (Judah) King Yehoyakim (son of Yoshiyah (Josiah) Yoshiyah), this message came to Yirmiyah (Jeremiah) from Yahweh,

[Yirmiyah] [27]:[3] Use it to send messages to the kings of Edom, Moav (Moab), Amon, Tsor (Tyre), and Tsidon (Sidon), through the ambassadors from those countries who’ve come to Yerushalem (Jerusalem) to meet with King Tsidkiyah (Zedekiah)
[Yirmiyah] [27]:[4] to tell them that Yisrael’s (Israel) god, Commander-in-chief Yahweh says to give their masters this message:

[Yirmiyah] [27]:[6] Now I’ve personally handed over all these lands to my servant, the Babylonian King Nevukadnetsar (Nebuchadnezzar), and I’ve also given the animals in the countryside to him to serve him.

[Yirmiyah] [27]:[8] Any nation or kingdom that won’t serve the Babylonian King Nevukadnetsar and that won’t put its neck into his yoke, then I’ll punish that nation with war and famine and disease until I’ve used King Nevukadnetsar to finish them off. That is Yahweh’s declaration,
[Yirmiyah] [27]:[9] so don’t you all keep listening to your ‘prophets’, and to your diviners and dreamers, and to your soothsayers and sorcerers—all those who keep telling you that you all won’t serve the Babylonian king,
[Yirmiyah] [27]:[10] because they’re prophesying lies to you, so as to remove you all far away from on your land. Yes, I will drive you all out and you’ll die in a foreign land.
[Yirmiyah] [27]:[11] However, the nation that brings its neck into the Babylonian king’s yoke and serves him, I’ll let that nation remain on its land, and it will cultivate it and live there. That’s is Yahweh’s declaration.
[Yirmiyah] [27]:[12] Then to Yehudah’s (Judah) King Tsidkiyah (Zedekiah), I passed on those same words, saying, “Put your necks into the yoke of the Babylonian king, and serve him and his people, and live.
[Yirmiyah] [27]:[13] Why would you and your people die from war, famine, and disease, as Yahweh has said will come to any nation that doesn’t serve the Babylonian king?
[Yirmiyah] [27]:[14] So don’t listen to the messages from the prophets who are speaking to you when they tell you all not to serve the king of Bavel (Babylon) as they’re prophesying lies to you
[Yirmiyah] [27]:[15] because I didn’t send them. Yahweh declares that they’re using my name to prophesy lies so that I’ll drive you out, and you’ll all perish—both you and the prophets who are prophesying to you.”
[Yirmiyah] [27]:[16] Then I told the priests and all those people that Yahweh says: Don’t listen to the words of your prophets who are prophesying to you and saying that the utensils from Yahweh’s temple will soon be brought back from Bavel, because they’re prophesying lies to you.
[Yirmiyah] [27]:[17] Don’t listen to them. Serve the Babylonian king and live. Why should this city become a ruin?
[Yirmiyah] [27]:[18] If they were prophets who really have access to Yahweh’s message, then please let them intercede with Commander-in-chief Yahweh so that the utensils remaining in Yahweh’s temple and in Yehudah’s king’s palace and in Yerushalem (Jerusalem) don’t end up being taken to Bavel.
[Yirmiyah] [27]:[19] Yes, Commander-in-chief Yahweh has spoken about the bronze pillars and the large, bronze water basin, and concerning the bronze stands and the rest of the utensils remaining in this city,
[Yirmiyah] [27]:[20] which the Babylonian King Nevukadnetsar (Nebuchadnezzar) didn’t take when he exiled Yehudah’s King Yekaneyah (son of Yehoyakim) from Yerushalem to Bavel, along with all the nobles of Yehudah including Yerushalem.

[Yirmiyah] [28]:[1] In the fifth month of the fourth year of the reign of Yehudah’s (Judah) King Tsidkiyah (Zedekiah), Azur’s son Hananyah who was a ‘prophet’ from Giveon, said to me in Yahweh’s temple as priests and all the people watched, saying,

[Yirmiyah] [31]:[11] because Yahweh has ransomed Yisrael (Ya’akov (Jacob)) and paid the price to free it from the power of a nation that’s stronger than it.
[Yirmiyah] [31]:[12] Then they’ll come and sing on Tsiyon’s (Zion) heights, and they’ll be radiant about Yahweh’s goodness: about the grain, about the new wine and the fresh oil, and about the young from the flock and the herd. Their soul will be like a watered garden, and they won’t be weakened again.
[Yirmiyah] [31]:[13] Then the young women will celebrate with dancing, along with the young and old men together. I’ll turn their mourning into happiness and I’ll comfort them, and I’ll give them reason for celebration rather than sorrow.
[Yirmiyah] [31]:[14] I’ll satisfy the priests’ appetites for good food and my people will be pleased by my goodness. That is Yahweh’s declaration.

[Yirmiyah] [31]:[17] There’s hope for your future, and your children will return to their border. That is Yahweh’s declaration.
[Yirmiyah] [31]:[18] I’ve heard Efrayim (Ephraim) (the northern kingdom) upset at itself, saying, You disciplined me, and I was disciplined like an untrained calf. Restore me so I can return because you’re my god Yahweh.
[Yirmiyah] [31]:[19] Yes, after I turned away, I repented, and after I was instructed, I slapped my thigh. I was ashamed and also humiliated because I still bore the reproach from my youthful rebellion.
[Yirmiyah] [31]:[20] Isn’t Efrayim (Ephraim) (the northern kingdom) a precious son to me, or a child that I really liked? Yes, as often as I speak against him, I still continually remember him. [Yirmiyah] [31]:[21] Set signposts up for yourself. Place markers where you can see them. Set the highway as your goal— the path that you went on. Yisrael’s (Israel) young daughter, return— return to those cities of yours.
[Yirmiyah] [31]:[22] How much longer will you waver, you apostate daughter? Yes, Yahweh has created something new in the land— a woman protects a man.
[Yirmiyah] [31]:[23] Yisrael’s (Israel) god, Commander-in-chief Yahweh says this: When I restore the prosperity of Yehudah (Judah) and its cities, again they’ll restore this saying, ‘May Yahweh bless you— Yahweh who’s the repository of righteousness— mountain of holiness.’
[Yirmiyah] [31]:[24] Then Yehudah and all its cities will live in the land together— farmers, and also shepherds who roam around with their flocks,
[Yirmiyah] [31]:[25] because I satisfy those who are weary, and I refresh everyone who’s become faint.

[Yirmiyah] [31]:[29] Then at that time, they’ll no longer say: ‘The parents ate sour grapes, →but it’s the teeth of the children that are set on edge.’
[Yirmiyah] [31]:[30] because everyone will die for their own disobedience, i.e., whoever eats sour grapes will have their own teeth set on edge.

[Yirmiyah] [31]:[32] It won’t be like the agreement that I made with their ancestors at the time when I took hold of their hand to bring them out from Mitsrayim (Egypt), when they broke my agreement even though I was a husband to them. That is Yahweh’s declaration.

[Yirmiyah] [31]:[35] Yahweh says this: I’m the one who gives the sun for light during the day, and the moon and the stars for light at night. He stirs up the ocean, so that its waves roar, His name is Commander-in-chief Yahweh.

[Yirmiyah] [32]:[1] This was the message that came to Yirmiyah (Jeremiah) from Yahweh in the tenth year of the reign of Yehudah’s (Judah) King Tsidkiyah (Zedekiah), the eighteenth year of Nevukadnetsar’s (Nebuchadnezzar) reign.
[Yirmiyah] [32]:[2] The army of the Babylonian king had besieged Yerushalem (Jerusalem), and the prophet Yirmiyah was imprisoned in the guards’ courtyard at the palace of Yehudah’s king.
[Yirmiyah] [32]:[3] Yehudah’s king Tsidkiyah had imprisoned him there after asking, “Why do you prophesy and say that Yahweh says: Listen, I’m about to hand this city over to the Babylonian king and he’ll capture it.

[Yirmiyah] [32]:[7] Listen, your cousin Hanamel (your uncle Shalum’s son) is coming to see you and will ask you to buy his field in Anatot, because you have the right to buy it.
[Yirmiyah] [32]:[8] Then just as Yahweh had said, my cousin Hanamel came to me in the guards’ courtyard and he asked me, “Buy my field that is in Anatot in the Benyamin region, because you have the right to inherit it so the right to buy it belongs to you. Buy it for yourself.” Then I knew that this was Yahweh’s message.
[Yirmiyah] [32]:[9] So I bought the field in Anatot from my cousin Hanamel, and I weighed out seventeen shekels of silver for him.
[Yirmiyah] [32]:[10] Then I wrote in a scroll and sealed it, and had witnesses witness it and the weight of the silver on the scales.
[Yirmiyah] [32]:[11] Next I took that sealed purchase deed with the price and conditions, as well as an unsealed copy.
[Yirmiyah] [32]:[12] I gave the sealed purchase document to Baruk (son of Neriyah, son of Mahseyah) in front of my cousin Hanamel and the witnesses who’d signed the purchase agreement, as well as all the Yehudim (Jews) who were sitting in the guards’ courtyard.
[Yirmiyah] [32]:[13] Then still in front of them, I instructed Baruk,
[Yirmiyah] [32]:[14] Yisrael’s (Israel) god, Commander-in-chief Yahweh says this: Take these documents, both this receipt of purchase that’s sealed and the unsealed copies, and put them into a clay jar so they’ll last for a long time,
[Yirmiyah] [32]:[15] because Yisrael’s god, Commander-in-chief Yahweh says this: Houses, fields, and vineyards will again be bought in this land.
[Yirmiyah] [32]:[16] After I’d given the purchase deed to Neriyah’s son Baruk, I prayed to Yahweh, saying:
[Yirmiyah] [32]:[17] Oh no, master Yahweh. Listen, you alone made the heavens and the earth by taking action and using your incredible strength. Nothing you say is too difficult for you to do.
[Yirmiyah] [32]:[18] You show loyal commitment to thousands, and pour people’s guilt into their children’s laps after them. You are the strong and powerful god—your name is Commander-in-chief Yahweh.
[Yirmiyah] [32]:[19] You are very wise and do incredible things, because your eyes are open to all the people’s ways—to give each person what their conduct and actions deserve.
[Yirmiyah] [32]:[20] You did miracles and amazing things in Mitsrayim (Egypt), remembered to this day, and you’ve made a name for yourself in Yisrael (Israel) and among humankind.
[Yirmiyah] [32]:[21] You brought your people Yisrael out from Mitsrayim using miracles and amazing things and by taking action and using your incredible strength, along with great terror.
[Yirmiyah] [32]:[22] Then you gave them this land which you had promised their ancestors that you’d give them—a land flowing with milk and honey.
[Yirmiyah] [32]:[23] So they entered and took possession of it, but they didn’t listen to your voice or follow your instructions. They didn’t do anything that you’d ordered them to do so you’ve brought all this calamity onto them.
[Yirmiyah] [32]:[24] Look, the siege mounds have reached up to the city to capture it, and it’s been handed over to the Kasdim (Chaldeans) who’ve been fighting it. Everything you said would happen has, including war, famine, and deadly diseases, and you’re there watching it.
[Yirmiyah] [32]:[25] Then you yourself told me, ‘Use silver to buy yourself a field, and have witnesses witness it, even though this city is being handed over to the Kasdim.’

[Yirmiyah] [34]:[1] Yahweh gave this message to Yirmiyah (Jeremiah) when the Babylonian King Nevukadnetsar (Nebuchadnezzar), along with all the world’s kingdoms, domains, and people groups under his control, was attacking Yerushalem (Jerusalem) and Yehudah’s (Judah) other cities, saying:

[Yirmiyah] [34]:[11] However, after that they changed their minds and retrieved the male and female slaves that they’d freed, then forced them to work as slaves again.
[Yirmiyah] [34]:[12] Then Yahweh gave me this message to tell them:
[Yirmiyah] [34]:[13] Yisrael’s (Israel) god Yahweh says that I personally made an agreement with your ancestors on the day that I brought them out from their lives of slavery in Mitsrayim (Egypt). That was when I said that
[Yirmiyah] [34]:[14] at the end of every seven years, you all must release any fellow Ivrim (Hebrews) who had sold themselves to you and served you for six years, releasing them as free people. However, your ancestors did not listen to me or show any desire to obey me.

[Yirmiyah] [34]:[16] But then you all turned and profaned my name by retrieving your male and female slaves which you’d released as free people, and then forced them to work as slaves again,
