So listen, I’m about to proclaim ‘freedom’ for you: freedom to experience war, deadly diseases, and famine, because I’m going to make you a horrible thing in the sight of every kingdom in the world. That is Yahweh’s declaration.
[Yirmiyah] [34]:[18] Then I’ll deal with the people who’ve broken my agreement, who didn’t respect the intent of the agreement that they established in front of me when they cut a bull in two and walked between the two halves,
[Yirmiyah] [34]:[19] when the leaders of Yehudah (Judah) and Yerushalem (Jerusalem), the officials and the priests, and all the people of the land walked between the two sections of the bull.
[Yirmiyah] [34]:[20] I’ll hand them over to their enemies and to those who want to see them dead. Their bodies will be food for the birds in the skies and the animals on the ground.
[Yirmiyah] [34]:[21] I’ll hand Yehudah’s King Tsidkiyah (Zedekiah) and his leaders over to their enemies and to those who want to see them dead, and to the army of the Babylonian king who’s attacking you.
[Yirmiyah] [34]:[22] This is Yahweh’s declaration: Listen, I’m about to order them back to battle against this city, and they’ll capture it and set it on fire. Then I’ll make Yehudah’s other cities into deserted wastelands.
[Yirmiyah] [35]:[1] Several years earlier, when Yehoyakim son of Yoshiyah (Josiah) was the king of Yehudah (Judah), Yahweh had given Yirmiyah (Jeremiah) this message:
[Yirmiyah] [35]:[2] Go to the Rekavi clan and talk with them, then bring them into one of the rooms in my temple, and give them wine to drink.
[Yirmiyah] [35]:[3] So I took Ya’azanyah (son of Yirmiyah, son of Havatsanyah) and his brothers and his sons, and all the rest of the Rekavi clan,
[Yirmiyah] [35]:[4] and I took them to the rooms of the sons of Hanan (son of Yigdalyah, man of God) at the temple. Those rooms were beside the leaders’ room, which was above the room of Ma’aseyah (Shalum’s son), the gatekeeper.
[Yirmiyah] [35]:[5] Then I placed bowls and cups of wine in front of the Rekavites and told them to drink some.
[Yirmiyah] [35]:[6] But they responded, “We don’t drink wine, because our ancestor, Rekav’s son Yonadav, commanded all of us and our descendants not to ever drink any wine.
[Yirmiyah] [35]:[7] He also told us not to build any houses, or to plant any crops or vineyards, saying that we must always live in tents, so that we’d have long lives in the land that we’re staying in as foreigners.
[Yirmiyah] [35]:[8] We’ve obeyed the voice of our ancestor, Rekav’s son Yonadav in everything that he commanded us and we, our wives, and our children have never drunk wine in our lives.
[Yirmiyah] [35]:[9] We’ll never build houses to live in, or own any vineyards, fields, or seed.
[Yirmiyah] [35]:[10] We’ve lived in tents, and we’ve followed everything that our ancestor Yonadav told us,
[Yirmiyah] [35]:[11] but when the Babylonian King Nevukadnetsar (Nebuchadnezzar) attacked the land, we decided that we must move to Yerushalem (Jerusalem) to escape from the Babylonian and Aramean armies, so now we’re all living in Yerushalem.
[Yirmiyah] [35]:[12] Then Yahweh gave this message to Yirmiyah (Jeremiah), saying that
[Yirmiyah] [35]:[13] Yisrael’s (Israel) god, Commander-in-chief Yahweh says to go and ask the people in Yehudah (Judah), including those who live in Yerushalem: Won’t you all accept correction and listen to my messages? This is Yahweh’s declaration:
[Yirmiyah] [35]:[14] Rekav’s son Yonadav told his descendants not to drink any wine and they’ve followed that to this very day. In contrast, I’ve personally and consistently spoken to all of you but you haven’t taken any notice of what I’ve said.
[Yirmiyah] [35]:[15] I persistently sent all my servants, the prophets, out to you all to tell each person to turn from their wicked behaviour and start doing good instead, and to stop following after other gods and serving them. Then they’d live on the land that I gave to your ancestors and to all of you, however, you all won’t listen to me or pay attention to me.
[Yirmiyah] [35]:[16] Yes, Yonadav’s descendants have followed the instructions that their ancestor gave them, but this people, refuses to obey me,
[Yirmiyah] [35]:[17] so Yisrael’s god, Commander-in-chief Yahweh, says this: Listen, I’m sending all the disasters that I pronounced for Yehudah, including everyone living in Yerushalem. I’m sending them against them because I spoke to them, but they wouldn’t listen. I called to them, but they wouldn’t answer.
[Yirmiyah] [35]:[18] Then Yirmiyah told the Rekavi clan that Yisrael’s god, Commander-in-chief Yahweh says this: You’ve all listened to the commands of your ancestor Yonadav and have kept them all. You’ve obeyed everything that he commanded you all to do,
[Yirmiyah] [35]:[19] so Yisrael’s god, Commander-in-chief Yahweh says this: There’ll always be someone descended from Rekav’s son Yonadav to serve me.
[Yirmiyah] [36]:[1] In the fourth year of the reign Yehudah’s (Judah) King Yehoyakim (son of Yoshiyah (Josiah)), Yahweh gave this message to Yirmiyah (Jeremiah):
[Yirmiyah] [36]:[2] Get a scroll for yourself and write all the messages on it that I’ve told you concerning Yisrael (Israel) and Yehudah, and all the other nations. Do this for everything I have said, back from the time of Yoshiyah until the present time.
[Yirmiyah] [36]:[3] Perhaps Yehudah’s people will hear about all the disasters that I intend to bring on them and then turn away from their wicked ways, so I can forgive them for their wickedness and their disobedience.
[Yirmiyah] [36]:[4] Then Yirmiyah called Neriyah’s son Baruk, and Yirmiyah dictated all the messages that Yahweh had given to him, for Baruk to record on a scroll.
[Yirmiyah] [36]:[5] Then Yirmiyah instructed Baruk saying, “I’m restrained from entering Yahweh’s residence
[Yirmiyah] [36]:[6] so you must go and read from the scroll that you wrote at my dictation. On the day of the fast, you must read Yahweh’s messages so that all the people in the temple will hear them as well as the people from the rest of Yehudah’s cities. Proclaim these messages to them.
[Yirmiyah] [36]:[7] Perhaps Yahweh will take notice of their pleas for mercy. Perhaps everyone will turn from their wicked ways, since the anger and fury that Yahweh has proclaimed against this nation is severe.
[Yirmiyah] [36]:[8] So Neriyah’s son Baruk did everything that the prophet Yirmiyah had told him to—he read Yahweh’s messages aloud at Yahweh’s temple.
[Yirmiyah] [36]:[9] In the ninth month of the next year, all the people in Yerushalem (Jerusalem) and the visitors to the city from the rest of Yehudah, announced a fast to honour Yahweh.
[Yirmiyah] [36]:[10] Again Baruk read Yirmiyah’s messages aloud at Yahweh’s temple, from the room of Gemaryah (son of the scribe Shafan) in the upper courtyard, by the entrance gate to Yahweh’s residence. He did this so that all the people could hear it.
[Yirmiyah] [36]:[11] When Mikayah (son of Gemaryah son of Shafan) heard all Yahweh’s messages from the scroll,
[Yirmiyah] [36]:[12] he went down to the secretary’s room in the palace, and wow, all the officials were sitting there: Elishama the secretary, Shemayah’s son Delayah, Akbor’s son Elnatan, Shafan’s son Gemaryah, and Hananyah’s son Tsidkiyah (Zedekiah), along with all the other officials.
[Yirmiyah] [36]:[13] When Mikayah reported to them all the messages that he’d heard Baruk read aloud for the people to hear,
[Yirmiyah] [36]:[14] the officials sent Yehudi (Jew) (son of Netanyah son of Shelemyah son of Kushi) to Baruk. Yehudi ordered Baruk, “Take the scroll in your hand, the scroll from which you were reading in the hearing of the people, and come.” So Neriyah’s son Baruk took the scroll and went to the officials
[Yirmiyah] [36]:[15] where they told him to sit down and read it to them, so Baruk read out the messages.
[Yirmiyah] [36]:[16] When they heard it all, they were afraid and decided together that they needed to report it all to the king,
[Yirmiyah] [36]:[17] and they asked Baruk, “How come you wrote down all these messages from Yirmiyah (Jeremiah)?”
[Yirmiyah] [36]:[18] “He dictated them to me,” he replied, “and I just wrote them down on the scroll.”
[Yirmiyah] [36]:[19] Then the officials told Baruk, “Go and hide, and Yirmiyah as well. Don’t let anyone know where you two are.”
[Yirmiyah] [36]:[20] Then they left the scroll in the secretary Elishama’s room and went out to the king in the courtyard and told him everything they’d heard.
[Yirmiyah] [36]:[21] The king sent Yehudi (Jew) to get the scroll, and he went and got it from the secretary Elishama’s room. Then Yehudi read it aloud for the king and all the officials who were standing beside him to hear.
[Yirmiyah] [36]:[22] That month, the king was in his winter house and a brazier was burning in front of him.
[Yirmiyah] [36]:[23] Whenever Yehudi had read a couple of columns, the king would slice it off with a knife and toss it into the fire until the entire scroll was gone,
[Yirmiyah] [36]:[24] but neither the king or any of his servants were afraid of the messages (and they didn’t tear their clothes to indicate repentance—
[Yirmiyah] [36]:[25] Elnatan, Delayah, and Gemaryah had urged the king not to burn the scroll, but he hadn’t taken any notice of them).
[Yirmiyah] [36]:[26] Then the king ordered a relative Yerahme’el, Azriel’s son Serayah, and Avdeel’s son Shelemyah to arrest the scribe Baruk and the prophet Yirmiyah (Jeremiah), but Yahweh had hidden them.
[Yirmiyah] [36]:[27] After the king had burnt the scroll with the messages on it that Yirmiyah (Jeremiah) had dictated to Baruk, Yahweh gave this message to Yirmiyah:
[Yirmiyah] [36]:[28] Get yourself another scroll and write down all the messages that were on the original scroll that Yehudah’s (Judah) King Yehoyakim burnt.
[Yirmiyah] [36]:[29] Then you must tell the king that Yahweh says: You burnt that scroll, asking why it was written that the Babylonian king would come and destroy this land and leave it without people or animals.
[Yirmiyah] [36]:[30] Now Yahweh says about King Yehoyakim: No descendant of his will ever sit on David’s throne. As for him, his corpse will be thrown out into the heat of the day and the frost at night.
[Yirmiyah] [36]:[31] I’ll punish him, his descendants, and his servants for their wickedness. The disasters that I’ve threatened them with, but which they ignored, I’ll send onto them and all Yerushalem’s (Jerusalem) inhabitants, and onto every person in the rest of Yehudah.
[Yirmiyah] [36]:[32] So Yirmiyah got another scroll and gave it to Baruk, son of Neriyah the scribe. Yirmiyah again dictated all the messages that had been on the scroll burnt by Yehudah’s King Yehoyakim, and Baruk wrote them onto the scroll, along with several other similar messages.
[Yirmiyah] [37]:[1] By now Yoshiyah’s (Josiah) son Tsidkiyah (Zedekiah) reigned as king instead of Yehoyakim’s son Yehoyakin. The Babylonian King Nevukadnetsar (Nebuchadnezzar) had made Tsidkiyah king over the Yehudah (Judah) region.
[Yirmiyah] [37]:[2] However, Tsidkiyah, his servants, and his people wouldn’t listen to Yahweh’s messages that he’d given via the prophet Yirmiyah (Jeremiah).
[Yirmiyah] [37]:[3] Eventually, King Tsidkiyah, Shelemyah’s son Yehukal, and Tsefanyah (Zephaniah) son of Ma’aseyah the priest, sent a message to the prophet Yirmiyah requesting him, “Pray on our behalf to our god, Yahweh.
[Yirmiyah] [37]:[4] At that time, Yirmiyah was still coming and going among the people, because he hadn’t yet been put in prison.
[Yirmiyah] [37]:[5] Par’oh’s (Pharaoh) army had come out of Mitsrayim (Egypt), and the Babylonians who were besieging Yerushalem (Jerusalem) heard the news about them and retreated from Yerushalem.
[Yirmiyah] [37]:[6] Then Yahweh gave Yirmiyah this message to proclaim:
[Yirmiyah] [37]:[7] Yisrael’s (Israel) god, Yahweh told me that you people should say this to Yehudah’s king who sent you all to consult me: Listen Par’oh’s army which was coming out to help you all is about to return back to its own country, Mitsrayim.
[Yirmiyah] [37]:[8] Then the Babylonians will return and attack this city, then they’ll capture it and burn it down.
[Yirmiyah] [37]:[9] Yahweh says not to deceive yourselves that the Babylonians have left, because they won’t leave,
[Yirmiyah] [37]:[10] because even if you all defeated the entire Babylonian army that’s attacking you so that only wounded men were left in their tents, they would get up and burn down this city.
[Yirmiyah] [37]:[11] Then when the Babylonian army had left Yerushalem (Jerusalem) to avoid Par’oh’s (Pharaoh) army,
[Yirmiyah] [37]:[12] Yirmiyah (Jeremiah) left the city to go to the Benyamin region to take possession of a section of land there among his people.
[Yirmiyah] [37]:[13] As he went through the Benyamin gate, a chief guard named Yiriyah (son of Shelemyah, son of Hananyah) was there. He seized the prophet Yirmiyah and claimed that he was deserting to the Babylonians.
[Yirmiyah] [37]:[14] But Yirmiyah disputed, “That’s a lie—I’m not deserting to the Babylonians.” However Yiriyah wouldn’t listen to him and he arrested him and took him to the officials.
[Yirmiyah] [37]:[15] The officials were angry at Yirmiyah and they had him beaten and put in prison. (The place had been the house of the scribe Yonatan (Jonathan), but it had been converted into a prison.)
[Yirmiyah] [37]:[16] So Yirmiyah was kept there in an underground cell for several days.
[Yirmiyah] [37]:[17] Then King Tsidkiyah (Zedekiah) sent someone to fetch Yirmiyah, and in his house, the king asked him privately, “Is there any message from Yahweh?” “There is a message,” Yirmiyah answered. “You’ll be handed over to the Babylonian king.”
[Yirmiyah] [37]:[18] Then Yirmiyah asked the king, “What crime have I committed against you or your servants or your people, that you’ve had me put in prison?
[Yirmiyah] [37]:[19] Where are all the other prophets who prophesied to you all that the Babylonian king wouldn’t come here?
[Yirmiyah] [37]:[20] But now, my master the king, please listen to this appeal: Don’t return me to the scribe Yonatan’s house, or I’ll die there.”
[Yirmiyah] [37]:[21] So King Tsidkiyah ordered that Yirmiyah be held in the guards’ courtyard, and he was given a loaf of bread every day from the bakers’ street, until the time when all the bread in the city ran out. But Yirmiyah remained confined in the guards’ courtyard.
[Yirmiyah] [38]:[1] Four officials, Matan’s son Shefatyah, Pashhur’s son Gedalyah, Shelemyah’s son Yehukal, and Malkiyah’s son Pashhur heard the messages that Yirmiyah (Jeremiah) was telling all the people, saying:
[Yirmiyah] [38]:[2] Yahweh says this: Anyone who stays in this city will be killed by fighting, famine, or deadly diseases, but anyone who goes out to the Babylonians will survive—they won’t be killed.
[Yirmiyah] [38]:[3] Yahweh says that this city will definitely be taken over and captured by the Babylonian king.
[Yirmiyah] [38]:[4] So those officials went to King Tsidkiyah (Zedekiah) and requested that Yirmiyah be executed because (they claimed) his messages were discouraging their warriors defending the city and discouraging all the people. They claimed that he wasn’t advancing the people’s safety, but causing harm.
[Yirmiyah] [38]:[5] “All right,” King Tsidkiyah replied. “Do whatever you want with him, because no king can argue against all of you.”
[Yirmiyah] [38]:[6] So they took Yirmiyah and put him into the water storage cistern carved out by the king’s son Malkiyah. It was right there in the guards’ courtyard, and they lowered Yirmiyah down with ropes. There wasn’t any water left in the cistern, but it was still muddy at the bottom and he sank down into the mud.
[Yirmiyah] [38]:[7] Now the Kushi Eved-Melek was one of the trusted servants in the king’s house and he heard that they had put Yirmiyah down into the cistern. Meanwhile, the king was sitting at the Benyamin Gate.
[Yirmiyah] [38]:[8] So Eved-Melek left the palace and went and spoke with the king,
[Yirmiyah] [38]:[9] “My master the king, those men have been evil in the way they’ve mistreated the prophet Yirmiyah. They threw him into a cistern so he’d die in it from hunger, since there’s no food left in the city.”
[Yirmiyah] [38]:[10] Then the king ordered Eved-Melek to take command of thirty of the king’s men to go and get the prophet Yirmiyah out of the cistern so he wouldn’t die down there.
[Yirmiyah] [38]:[11] So Eved-Melek led the men to a storeroom for clothing under the king’s house where they got some rags and worn-out clothes. Then they let them down by ropes to Yirmiyah in the cistern
[Yirmiyah] [38]:[12] and told him to use the rags and old clothes under his armpits to protect him from being hurt by the ropes. Yirmiyah did that,
[Yirmiyah] [38]:[13] then they pulled him up with the ropes—that’s how they got him up out from the mud in the cistern. Then he stayed in the guards’ courtyard.
[Yirmiyah] [38]:[14] One day King Tsidkiyah (Zedekiah) summoned the prophet Yirmiyah (Jeremiah) to meet him at the third entrance to the temple and told him, “I want to ask you something. Don’t refuse to answer honestly and truthfully.”
[Yirmiyah] [38]:[15] “Ha, if I tell you the truth, you’ll order me to be executed,” Yirmiyah replied. “And if I give you good advice, you won’t take any notice of what I say.”
[Yirmiyah] [38]:[16] But King Tsidkiyah privately promised Yirmiyah, “As our creator Yahweh lives, I won’t execute you or hand you over to those men who want to see you dead.”
[Yirmiyah] [38]:[17] “Okay,” Yirmiyah answered the king, “Yisrael’s (Israel) god, Commander-in-chief Yahweh says this: If you indeed go out to the Babylonian king’s officials, then you’ll live, and this city won’t be burnt down. You and your family would live.
[Yirmiyah] [38]:[18] But if you don’t go out to his officials, then this city will be handed over to the Babylonians. They’ll burn it down, and you wouldn’t be able to escape from their power.”
[Yirmiyah] [38]:[19] “But I’m afraid of the Yehudim (Jews) who’ve already deserted to the Babylonians,” the king confided to Yirmiyah. “You see, I might be handed over to them and they might treat me cruelly.”
[Yirmiyah] [38]:[20] “The Babylonians won’t hand you over to those Yehudim,” Yirmiyah responded. “Obey Yahweh’s message from Yahweh that I’m passing on to you, so that things will go well for you, and so that you’ll live through this.
[Yirmiyah] [38]:[21] However, if you refuse to surrender, then this is what Yahweh has shown me:
[Yirmiyah] [38]:[22] Listen king of Yehudah (Judah), all the women who are left in your palace will be taken out to the Babylonian king’s commanders. Those women will tell you, ‘You were deceived by your friends—they’ve ruined you. Now your feet are stuck in the mud, and your friends have turned away.’
[Yirmiyah] [38]:[23] Yes, all your wives and children will be taken out to the Babylonians and you yourself won’t escape from them either. You’ll be taken captive by the Babylonian king, and this city will be burnt down.”
[Yirmiyah] [38]:[24] Then Tsidkiyah (Zedekiah) told Yirmiyah, “Don’t tell anyone else what we spoke about or you might die.
[Yirmiyah] [38]:[25] If the officials hear that I’ve have talked with you, and if they come and demand, ‘Tell us what you said to the king—don’t hide it from us or we’ll kill you,’
[Yirmiyah] [38]:[26] then you must tell them, ‘I was just pleading to the king not to return me to the dungeon in Yonatan’s (Jonathan) house or I’d die there.’
[Yirmiyah] [38]:[27] Then sure enough the officials came to Yirmiyah and questioned him and he answered them as the king had instructed him. They couldn’t say anything else because they hadn’t heard the conversation,
[Yirmiyah] [38]:[28] so Yirmiyah remained in the guards’ courtyard until the day that Yerushalem (Jerusalem) was captured.
[Yirmiyah] [39]:[1] In the tenth month of the ninth year of the reign of Yehudah’s (Judah) King Tsidkiyah (Zedekiah), the Babylonian King Nevukadnetsar (Nebuchadnezzar) came against Yerushalem (Jerusalem) with his large army and besieged it.
[Yirmiyah] [39]:[2] On the ninth day of the fourth month of Tsidkiyah’s eleventh year, the city was broken into.
[Yirmiyah] [39]:[3] Then all of the Babylonian king’s officials came and sat at the middle gate, including the top official Nevu-Sar-Sekim, and Samgar-Nevu and Sarsekim.
[Yirmiyah] [39]:[4] When Yehudah’s King Tsidkiyah and all his warriors saw what was happening, they left at nighttime through the gate between the two walls beside the king’s garden and fled towards the Yarden (Jordan) river plains.
[Yirmiyah] [39]:[5] However the Babylonian army chased after them and overtook the king down in the plains near Yeriho (Jericho). They took him back up to the Babylonian King Nevukadnetsar at Rivlah in the Hamat region, and he pronounced his judgement on him.
[Yirmiyah] [39]:[6] The king had Tsidkiyah’s sons slaughtered at Rivlah as their father was forced to watch, and Yehudah’s officials were also executed.
[Yirmiyah] [39]:[7] Then they gouged out Tsidkiyah’s eyes and put him in chains to be taken to Bavel (Babylon).
[Yirmiyah] [39]:[8] Then the Babylonians burnt down the palace and the other houses, and tore down Yerushalem’s walls.
[Yirmiyah] [39]:[9] The rest of the people who’d stayed in the city, including those who’d previously deserted, were exiled to Bavel under the supervision of the chief bodyguard Nevuzar-Adan.
[Yirmiyah] [39]:[10] However, he allowed the poorest people who didn’t own anything to remain in Yehudah—allocating vineyards and fields for them to work.
[Yirmiyah] [39]:[11] Now the Babylonian King Nevukadnetsar (Nebuchadnezzar) had given an order to his chief bodyguard Nevuzar-Adan about finding Yirmiyah (Jeremiah)
[Yirmiyah] [39]:[12] and keeping him safe and unharmed—even to care for him and do anything that he requested.
[Yirmiyah] [39]:[13] So Nevuzar-Adan, the top servant Nevu-Shazban, the high official Nergal-Shar-Etser, and all the Babylonian king’s most important officials
[Yirmiyah] [39]:[14] sent out men to fetch Yirmiyah from the guards’ courtyard. They handed him over to Gedalyah (son of Ahikam, son of Shafan) to take him home, so Yirmiyah stayed there among the people.
[Yirmiyah] [39]:[15] While Yirmiyah (Jeremiah) had still been held in the guards’ courtyard, Yahweh had given him this message:
[Yirmiyah] [39]:[16] Go and tell Eved-Melek the Kushi (Ethiopian) that Yisrael’s (Israel) god, Commander-in-chief Yahweh says this: Listen, I’m about to fulfill my messages against this city for disaster and not for good, and they’ll all come true right in front of your eyes on that day.
[Yirmiyah] [39]:[17] But Yahweh declares that I’ll rescue you from those people that you’re afraid of
[Yirmiyah] [39]:[18] because I’ll definitely save your life. You won’t be killed by the soldiers, but Yahweh declares that because you put your trust in me, your life will be saved.
[Yirmiyah] [40]:[1] The chief bodyguard Nevuzar-Adan had found Yirmiyah (Jeremiah) chained up among all the exiles from Yerushalem (Jerusalem) and the rest of Yehudah (Judah) to be taken to Bavel (Babylon), and had released him at Ramah.
[Yirmiyah] [40]:[2] The chief bodyguard took Yirmiyah aside and told him, “Your god Yahweh decreed this disaster for this place,
[Yirmiyah] [40]:[3] then he caused it to happen. Yahweh did just as he’d decreed, since you people sinned against him and didn’t obey him. That’s why all this has happened to you people.
[Yirmiyah] [40]:[4] But now listen, I’ve released you today from your chains. If you choose to come with me to Bavel, I’ll look after you, but if you don’t want to, then look around and go wherever you think best.
[Yirmiyah] [40]:[5] Or why don’t you return to Gedalyah (son of Ahikam, son of Shafan) who the Babylonian king has put in charge of Yehudah’s cities. Stay among the people with him, or go wherever you think best.” Then the king’s chief bodyguard gave him food and a gift, and sent him away.
[Yirmiyah] [40]:[6] So Yirmiyah went to Gedalyah’s place and stayed with him among the people who were left behind in the land.
[Yirmiyah] [40]:[7] Now some commanders of Yehudi (Jew) soldiers who were still in the countryside, along with their men heard that the Babylonian king had made Ahikam’s son Gedalyah governor over the land. They also heard that he’d put him in charge of the men, women, and children who were the poorest people in the land—those who hadn’t been exiled to Bavel (Babylon).
[Yirmiyah] [40]:[8] So they went to Gedalyah at Mitspah. Those who went were Netanyah’s son Yishmael (Ishmael), Kareah’s sons Yohanan and Yonatan (Jonathan), Tanhumet’s son Serayah, the sons of Ofay the Netofati, and Ma’akati’s son Yezanyah, and their men.
[Yirmiyah] [40]:[9] Gedalyah (son of Ahikam, son of Shafan) made a promise to them and their men, saying, “Don’t be afraid to serve the Babylonian officials. Live in the land and serve the Babylonian king, and it will go well with you.
[Yirmiyah] [40]:[10] See, I’m living in Mitspah to meet with the Babylonians who came to us. So harvest wine, summer fruit, and oil and store them in your containers. Live in the cities that you’ve occupied.”
[Yirmiyah] [40]:[11] Then all the Yehudim (Jews) in Moav (Moab), among the people of Amon, and in Edom, and in every land heard that the Babylonian king had allowed a small number of people to stay in Yehudah (Judah), and that he’d appointed Gedalyah (son of Ahikam, son of Shafan) over them.
[Yirmiyah] [40]:[12] So all the Yehudim from every place that they’d be driven into, came back to Yehudah to Gedalyah at Mitspah, and they harvested a lot of wine and summer fruit.
[Yirmiyah] [40]:[13] Some time later, Kareah’s son Yonatan (Jonathan) and all the army commanders from the countryside, came to Gedalyah at Mitspah,
[Yirmiyah] [40]:[14] and asked him, “Do you realise that the Amoni King Ba’alis has sent Netanyah’s son Yishmael (Ishmael) to assassinate you?” However Ahikam’s son Gedalyah didn’t believe them
[Yirmiyah] [40]:[15] so Kareah’s son Yohanan spoke privately to Gedalyah at Mitspah, “Allow me to go and kill Netanyah’s Yishmael. No one will suspect me. Why should he kill you? Why allow all of Yehudah (Judah) that has been gathered to you to be scattered and the remnant destroyed?”
[Yirmiyah] [40]:[16] However Ahikam’s son Gedalyah replied to Kareah’s son Yohanan, “No, don’t do that, because you’re lying about Yishmael.”
[Yirmiyah] [41]:[1] However, in the seventh month, Yishmael (son of Netanyah, son of Elishama from the royal family) and some officers of the king came—he had ten men with him. They came to Ahikam’s son Gedalyah at Mitspah and had a meal together.
[Yirmiyah] [41]:[2] Then Yishmael and the ten men who were with him, stood up and attacked with their swords. Yishmael killed Gedalyah, who the Babylonian king had put in charge of the region,
[Yirmiyah] [41]:[3] and they killed all the Yehudim (Jews) who were with Gedalyah there at Mitspah, as well as the Babylonian soldiers who were there.
[Yirmiyah] [41]:[4] The next day before anyone found out that Gedalyah had been murdered,
[Yirmiyah] [41]:[5] eighty men from Shekem, Shiloh, and from Shomron (Samaria) came who had shaved off their beards, torn their clothes, and cut themselves in mourning. They were carrying grain offerings and incense to be offered at Yahweh’s residence.
[Yirmiyah] [41]:[6] Netanyah’s son Yishmael went out of Mitspah to meet them, weeping as he went. When he reached them, he told them to come and see what had happened to Ahikam’s son Gedalyah.
[Yirmiyah] [41]:[7] Then as they reached the middle of the town, Yishmael and his men slaughtered them and threw their bodies into a cistern.
[Yirmiyah] [41]:[8] However, ten of them bargained with Yishmael about some wheat, barley, oil, and honey that they’d left out in the countryside, so he didn’t kill them along with the others.
[Yirmiyah] [41]:[9] The water storage cistern when Yishmael had thrown all the bodies of those he’d killed including Gedalyah, had been dug by King Asa in defence against Yisrael’s (Israel) King Baesha. Now Netanyah’s son Yishmael had filled it with dead bodies.
[Yirmiyah] [41]:[10] Next Yishmael captured the remaining people in Mitspah, including the king’s daughters and all the others who the chief bodyguard Nevuzar-Adan had assigned to Ahikam’s son Gedalyah. So Netanyah’s son Yishmael captured them to hand over to the Amonim.
[Yirmiyah] [41]:[11] Meanwhile Kareah’s son Yohanan and all the army commanders with him, heard about all the evil things that Netanyah’s son Yishmael had done,
[Yirmiyah] [41]:[12] so they took all their men to fight against Yishmael. They came across him at the large pool near Giveon city
[Yirmiyah] [41]:[13] When all the people who’d been captured by Yishmael saw Yohanan and all the army commanders they were very relieved.
[Yirmiyah] [41]:[14] So all those people that Yishmael had captured were freed and went back with Kareah’s son Yohanan.
[Yirmiyah] [41]:[15] Unfortunately, Netanyah’s son Yishmael escaped from Yohanan, along with eight of his men, and they went to the Amonim.
[Yirmiyah] [41]:[16] Then Kareah’s son Yohanan and all the army commanders with him, took all the people from Mitspah who’d been rescued from Netanyah’s son Yishmael after he’d killed Ahikam’s son Gedalyah. They took those warriors, and women and children and court-officials that they’d saved at Giveon,
[Yirmiyah] [41]:[17] and went and stayed at Gerut-Kimham near Beyt-Lehem (Bethlehem), getting ready to go to Mitsrayim (Egypt)
[Yirmiyah] [41]:[18] because of the Babylonians. (They worried about their response because Netanyah’s son Yishmael had assassinated Ahikam’s son Gedalyah who’d been appointed in the region by the Babylonian king.)
[Yirmiyah] [42]:[1] Then all the army commanders, as well as Kareah’s son Yohanan, Hoshayah’s son Yezanyah, and all the people from the less prominent to the most important officials approached the prophet Yirmiyah (Jeremiah)
[Yirmiyah] [42]:[2] and asked him, “Please listen to our request. Please ask your god Yahweh our on behalf of all of us who are left here, because there’s not very many of us left as you can see.
[Yirmiyah] [42]:[3] Ask your god Yahweh to tell us what we should do and where we should go.”
[Yirmiyah] [42]:[4] “Sure, I’ve heard your concerns,” the prophet Yirmiyah responded. “Listen, Ill pray to your god Yahweh as you’ve all requested. Whatever Yahweh answers, I’ll tell you. I’ll keep nothing back from you all.”
[Yirmiyah] [42]:[5] “We promise to do everything that your god Yahweh tells us to do,” they told Yirmiyah. “If we don’t, then Yahweh can be a true and faithful witness against us.
[Yirmiyah] [42]:[6] Whether it’s good or bad, we’ll obey the instructions from our god Yahweh who we’re asking you to speak to, so that it may be well with us when we obey his response.”
[Yirmiyah] [42]:[7] After ten days, Yahweh’s response came to Yirmiyah (Jeremiah),
[Yirmiyah] [42]:[8] so he called Kareah’s son Yohanan and all the army commanders, as well as all the people from the less prominent to the most important officials,
[Yirmiyah] [42]:[9] then he told them, “You all sent me to Yisrael’s (Israel) god Yahweh to pass on your requests and here’s his reply:
[Yirmiyah] [42]:[10] If you all stay in this region, then I’ll build you up and not tear you down. I’ll plant you and not pull you all out, because I’m upset about the harm that I’ve done to you all.
[Yirmiyah] [42]:[11] Don’t be afraid of the Babylonian king any more. This is Yahweh’s declaration: Don’t be afraid of him because I’m with you all to save you and to rescue you from his clutches,
[Yirmiyah] [42]:[12] because I’ll give you all mercy. I’ll have compassion on you, and I’ll restore you all back to your country.
[Yirmiyah] [42]:[13] However, suppose that you all decide not to listen to the words of your god Yahweh, and decide not to stay in this region,
[Yirmiyah] [42]:[14] and if you all say that you’ll go to Mitsrayim (Egypt) to live there where there’s no war, and no trumpets signalling, and no shortage of food,
[Yirmiyah] [42]:[15] Now you remaining people listen to Yahweh’s message: Yisrael’s god, Commander-in-chief Yahweh says that if you all do decide to go and stay down in Mitsrayim,
[Yirmiyah] [42]:[16] then the war that you all fear will overtake you in Mitsrayim. The famine that you’re anxious about will follow you all to Mitsrayim, and then you’ll die there,
[Yirmiyah] [42]:[17] i.e., anyone who decides to go to live as foreigners in Mitsrayim, will die from war, famine, or deadly diseases. There won’t be any survivors from the calamities that I’d send onto them.
[Yirmiyah] [42]:[18] Yes, Yisrael’s god, Commander-in-chief Yahweh says this: Just as my anger and rage was poured out on Yerushalem’s (Jerusalem) inhabitants, in the same way my anger would be poured out on all of you if you go to Mitsrayim. You’d become an object of cursing and a horror, something to be used as a curse word, and something dishonourable, and you’d never see this place again.
[Yirmiyah] [42]:[19] Then Yirmiyah (Jeremiah) continued: Yahweh has spoken to you all, the remaining people of Yehudah (Judah). Don’t go down to Mitsrayim as you know that I’ve definitely warned you all against that today.
[Yirmiyah] [42]:[20] Yes, you made a life and death mistake when you sent me to your god Yahweh, and asked me to ask him for instructions for you and when you all said that you’d do everything that he says,
[Yirmiyah] [42]:[21] because I’ve reported all that to you today. However, you haven’t listened to your god Yahweh’s message, or to anything that he sent me to tell you all about.
[Yirmiyah] [42]:[22] So now, you should definitely be aware that you’ll die from war, famine, and deadly diseases where you all wanted to go and live as foreigners.
[Yirmiyah] [43]:[1] When Yirmiyah (Jeremiah) had finished passing on Yahweh’s messages that their god Yahweh had told him to say,
[Yirmiyah] [43]:[2] Hoshayah’s son Azaryah, Kareah’s son Yohanan, and all the arrogant men told Yirmiyah, “You’re lying to us. Our god Yahweh didn’t send you to tell us not to go and live in Mitsrayim (Egypt).
[Yirmiyah] [43]:[3] It’s because Neriyah’s son Baruk is inciting you against us so that we’ll stay here and get captured by the Babylonians to be either put to death or be taken as exiles to Bavel (Babylon).”
[Yirmiyah] [43]:[4] So Kareah’s son Yohanan, all the army officers, and all the rest of the people, refused to take notice of Yahweh’s instructions to remain living in the Yehudah (Judah) region.
[Yirmiyah] [43]:[5] Then Yohanan and all the army commanders gathered all those remaining Yehudi (Jew) people together, who’d come from all the other countries that they’d previously been driven away to and returned to live in Yehudah.
[Yirmiyah] [43]:[6] That included men and women, children, the king’s daughters, and all the people that Nevuzar-Adan, the king’s chief bodyguard Nevuzar-Adan had left with Gedalyah (son of Ahikam, son of Shafan), and including the prophet Yirmiyah and Neriyah’s son Baruk.
[Yirmiyah] [43]:[7] Then they went to Mitsrayim because they took no notice of Yahweh’s instructions and they arrived at Tahfanhes.
[Yirmiyah] [43]:[8] In Tahfanhes, Yahweh gave Yirmiyah a message:
[Yirmiyah] [43]:[9] Get some large stones and while the people from Yehudah are watching, push them into the mortar in the pavement at the entrance to Par’oh’s (Pharaoh) palace at Tahfanhes.
[Yirmiyah] [43]:[10] Then tell the Yehudim (Jews) that Yisrael’s (Israel) god, Commander-in-chief says: Listen, I’m about to send messengers to my servant the Babylonian King Nevukadnetsar (Nebuchadnezzar), to summon him here. I’ll place his throne over the top of those hidden stones, and he’ll spread his royal tent over them.
[Yirmiyah] [43]:[11] He’ll come here to attack Mitsrayim and he’ll kill those that I’ve assigned to die, and similarly for those to be taken captive or run through with a sword.
[Yirmiyah] [43]:[12] Then he’ll light a fire in the temples of Mitsrayim’s gods. Nevukadnetsar will either burn them or carry them away. He’ll clean Mitsrayim out just like shepherds pick lice off their clothes, and then he’ll quietly leave
[Yirmiyah] [43]:[13] after smashing the stone pillars at Beyt-Shemesh (Heliopolis) and burning the temples of Mitsrayim’s gods.
[Yirmiyah] [44]:[1] Yahweh spoke to Yirmiyah (Jeremiah) about all the Yehudim (Jews) who lived in Migdol, Tahfanhes, and Nof (Memphis) in northern/lower Mitsrayim (Egypt), as well as those in Patros in southern/upper Mitsrayim:
[Yirmiyah] [44]:[2] Yisrael’s (Israel) god, Commander-in-chief Yahweh says that you yourselves have seen all the disasters that I sent to Yerushalem (Jerusalem) and Yehudah’s (Judah) other cities. See, they’re just ruins today without anyone living in them.
[Yirmiyah] [44]:[3] That’s because of the wicked things they did to provoke me to anger by going to burn incense and to worship other gods that neither they themselves, nor you, nor your ancestors had ever heard about before.
[Yirmiyah] [44]:[4] I repeatedly sent all my servants, the prophets, to them to tell the people to stop doing those detestable things that I hate,
[Yirmiyah] [44]:[5] but they didn’t listen. They refused to take any notice of it, or to stop their wicked activities like burning incense to other gods.
[Yirmiyah] [44]:[6] So my anger and rage was poured out and burnt in Yehudah’s cities and Yerushalem’s streets like a fire and they’re still desolate ruins to this day.
[Yirmiyah] [44]:[7] So now Yisrael’s god, Commander-in-chief Yahweh asks why you all insist on bringing this terrible harm onto yourselves that’ll see men and women, children and babies from Yehudah, eliminated without even leaving a remnant.
[Yirmiyah] [44]:[8] You’ve provoked me to anger by what you’ve all done with your own two hands, by burning incense to other gods in Mitsrayim where you’ve all gone to live as foreigners. You’ve cut yourselves off so as to become a curse word and a reproach among all the nations in the world.
[Yirmiyah] [44]:[9] Have you all forgotten the wicked things done by your ancestors and also by Yehudah’s kings and their wives? Have you forgotten the evil committed by yourselves and your wives in Yehudah and on Yerushalem’s streets?
[Yirmiyah] [44]:[10] To this day, they still haven’t humbled themselves. They don’t respect the instructions or regulations that I gave them and their ancestors, and so they don’t follow them.
[Yirmiyah] [44]:[11] Therefore Yisrael’s god, Commander-in-chief says this: Listen, I’m about to start working against you all to bring disaster and destroy all Yehudah.
[Yirmiyah] [44]:[12] I’ll eliminate the small group of Yehudim (Jews) that has made up their minds to go to live as foreigners in Mitsrayim. I’ll do that so that they’ll all die there Mitsrayim—from either war or famine, and from the least to the very prominent people they’ll die and will become a curse word, a horror story, and something to ridicule and mock.
[Yirmiyah] [44]:[13] I will punish those living in Mitsrayim just like I punished Yerushalem with war, famine, and deadly diseases
[Yirmiyah] [44]:[14] so that none of the remaining people from Yehudah who’ve gone to live in Mitsrayim will escape or survive or be able to return to Yehudah when they want to return and live there. None of them will return except a few who escaped from there.
[Yirmiyah] [44]:[15] Then all the men who knew that their wives were burning incense to other gods, and all the women who were in the great assembly, and all the people who were living in Lower and Upper Mitsrayim, answered Yirmiyah (Jeremiah):
[Yirmiyah] [44]:[16] Concerning that message that you told us in Yahweh’s name, we’re not listening to you
[Yirmiyah] [44]:[17] because we’ll certainly do everything that we said we’d do. We’ll burn incense to the queen of the skies and pour out drink offerings to her just as we, our ancestors, our kings, and our leaders did in Yehudah’s cities and on Yerushalem’s streets. Then we’ll have plenty of food and will prosper, and won’t experience distress.
[Yirmiyah] [44]:[18] Whenever we didn’t do those things—not offering incense to the queen of the skies and not pouring out drink offerings to her—we were all suffering from poverty and dying from by war and famine.
[Yirmiyah] [44]:[19] The women said, “When we were offering incense to the queen of the skies and pouring out drink offerings to her, and when we were making cakes in her image and pouring out drink offerings to her, did you think we were doing it behind our husbands’ backs?”
[Yirmiyah] [44]:[20] Then Yirmiyah responded to all those who’d answered him including both men and women. He told them all this message:
[Yirmiyah] [44]:[21] Didn’t Yahweh remember the incense that you all burned in Yehudah’s cities and on Yerushalem’s streets—you and your ancestors, your kings and leaders, and the people of the land, and didn’t it come back to his mind?
[Yirmiyah] [44]:[22] Eventually, he could no longer bear it because of your wicked behaviour, i.e., because of the detestable things that you all did. Then your land became a deserted wasteland and a curse, without inhabitants as it is today.
[Yirmiyah] [44]:[23] Because you all burnt incense to other gods and sinned against Yahweh, and because you wouldn’t listen to his voice, his instructions, his regulations, or his promises, this disaster has come against you as you all can see today.
[Yirmiyah] [44]:[24] Then Yirmiyah told all the people, including all those women, “Listen to Yahweh’s message, all of you from Yehudah who are now here in Mitsrayim (Egypt).
[Yirmiyah] [44]:[25] Yisrael’s (Israel) god, Commander-in-chief Yahweh says that both you and your wives have said out loud and confirmed with your actions that you’ll all certainly carry out your vows to worship the queen of the skies and to pour out drink offerings to her. So then, go ahead and do those things to fulfill your wows.
[Yirmiyah] [44]:[26] So then all of Yehudah who’re staying Mitsrayim, listen to Yahweh’s message: Yahweh says, listen, I’ve promised by my powerful name that none of the men from Yehudah who’re living here in Mitsrayim will call on my name any more, i.e., you’ll all no longer say, ‘As our master Yahweh lives.’
[Yirmiyah] [44]:[27] Listen, I’m watching over them for disaster and not for good. Every Yehudi (Jew) person in Mitsrayim will meet their end through war or famine until they’re all eliminated.
[Yirmiyah] [44]:[28] Then a few survivors from the battles will return from Mitsrayim to Yehudah region—only a small number of them. In that way, all the remaining Yehudim (Jews) who went to live in Mitsrayim will know whose word will stand—mine or theirs.
[Yirmiyah] [44]:[29] Yahweh declares that this will be the sign for you all: I’m going to punish you all in this place so that you’ll know that what I’ve said will come to pass, resulting in harm for all of you.
[Yirmiyah] [44]:[30] Yahweh says: Listen, I’m about to hand the Mitsri (Egyptian) king, Par’oh (Pharaoh) Hofra over to his enemies and to those who want to kill him. It’ll be the same as when I handed Yehudah’s King Tsidkiyah (Zedekiah) king of Yehudah over to the Babylonian King Nevukadnetsar (Nebuchadnezzar)—his enemy who wanted him dead.
[Yirmiyah] [45]:[1] This is the message that the prophet Yirmiyah (Jeremiah) dictated to Neriyah’s son Baruk to have it written on a scroll in the fourth year of the reign of Yehudah’s (Judah) King Yehoyakim (son of Yoshiyah (Josiah)):
[Yirmiyah] [45]:[2] Yisrael’s (Israel) god Yahweh says this to you Baruk:
[Yirmiyah] [45]:[3] You’ve said, ‘I’m not doing well because Yahweh has piled sorrow on top of my pain. I’m exhausted from groaning and I can’t find any peace.’
[Yirmiyah] [45]:[4] Yahweh says to tell Baruk, Listen, I’m about to tear down what I’ve built throughout the world, and to pull out what I’ve planted.
[Yirmiyah] [45]:[5] But maybe you’re hoping for great things for yourself? Don’t hope for that, because listen, disaster is coming for all humanity, but wherever you go, I’m giving you your life as your ‘spoil of war’. That is Yahweh’s declaration.
[Yirmiyah] [46]:[1] These are the messages that Yahweh gave the prophet Yirmiyah (Jeremiah) about other nations:
[Yirmiyah] [46]:[2] This is about the army of the Mitsri (Egyptian) king Par’oh (Pharaoh) Nekoh who was at Karkemish by the Perat (Euphrates) river. That was the army that the Babylonian King Nevukadnetsar (Nebuchadnezzar) defeated in the fourth year of the reign of Yehudah’s (Judah) King Yehoyakim, son of Yoshiyah (Josiah):
[Yirmiyah] [46]:[3] Get the small shield and the large shields ready, and go out for battle.
[Yirmiyah] [46]:[4] Harness on the horses to the chariots Mount up on the horses and take your stand with your helmets on. Polish the spears and put on your armour.
[Yirmiyah] [46]:[5] What am I seeing here? They’re filled with terror and they’re retreating, because their warriors will be crushed. They’re fleeing for safety without looking back. Terror is all around. That is Yahweh’s declaration.
[Yirmiyah] [46]:[6] Don’t let the swift one flee, and don’t let the warrior escape. They’ll stumble and fall there in the north by the Perat (Euphrates) River,
[Yirmiyah] [46]:[7] Who’s this coming who rises like the Nile, whose waters surge up and down like the rivers?
[Yirmiyah] [46]:[8] Mitsrayim (Egypt) rises like the Nile, like rivers of water that rise and fall, saying, ‘I’ll go up and I will cover the earth. I’ll destroy cities and their inhabitants.
[Yirmiyah] [46]:[9] Go up, you horses. Be angry, you chariots. Let the soldiers go out, Kush (Ethiopia) and Libya, men skillful with a shield, and Ludia, men skillful at using bows and arrows.’
[Yirmiyah] [46]:[10] That day will be the day of vengeance for the master, Commander-in-chief Yahweh, when he’ll avenge himself on his enemies. The sword will devour and be satisfied—it’ll drink its fill of their blood because there’ll be a sacrifice to the master, Commander-in-chief Yahweh in the northern land by the Perat (Euphrates) River.
[Yirmiyah] [46]:[11] Go up to Gilead and obtain medicine, you virgin daughter of Mitsrayim (Egypt). It’s vain to put that much medicine on yourself—there’s no cure for you.
[Yirmiyah] [46]:[12] The nations have heard about your disgrace. The world is filled with your wailing, because warrior stumbles against warrior— both of them fall together.
[Yirmiyah] [46]:[13] When the Babylonian King Nevukadnetsar (Nebuchadnezzar) was coming to attack Mitsrayim (Egypt), Yahweh gave the prophet Yirmiyah (Jeremiah) this message:
[Yirmiyah] [46]:[14] Announce in Mitsrayim, and proclaim it in Migdol, Nof (Memphis), and Tahfanhes: ‘Take your station and prepare to defend yourself, because everyone around you will be killed.’
[Yirmiyah] [46]:[15] Why are your powerful warriors lying face down on the ground? They can’t stand against the enemy, because I Yahweh, have pushed them to the ground.
[Yirmiyah] [46]:[16] He increases the numbers of those who stumble. Each soldier falls against the next one. They’re saying, ‘Get ready. Let’s go back to our own people, to our native land. Let’s leave this oppressive war.
[Yirmiyah] [46]:[17] There in Mitsrayim (Egypt) they’ll call out, ‘Our King Par’oh (Pharaoh) is all noise— he’s let his opportunity slip away.
[Yirmiyah] [46]:[18] The king whose name is Commander-in-chief Yahweh declares: ‘As surely as I live an invader is coming who’s as tall as Mt. Tavor among the mountains, and like Mt. Karmel by the sea.
[Yirmiyah] [46]:[19] You inhabitants of Mitsrayim, pack your own baggage to carry into exile, because Nof (Memphis) will become a wasteland— it will lie in ruins and no one will live there.
[Yirmiyah] [46]:[20] Mitsrayim is a very beautiful young cow, but a stinging insect is coming from the north. It’s on its way.
[Yirmiyah] [46]:[21] Its hired soldiers are like calves that have been protected and well-fed, but they’ll also turn away and run away. They won’t stand together, because the day of their disaster is coming against them— it’s time for their punishment.
[Yirmiyah] [46]:[22] Mitsrayim hisses like a snake and crawls away, because her enemies are coming with a show of strength. They’re coming toward her like woodcutters with axes.
[Yirmiyah] [46]:[23] Yahweh declares that they’ll cut down the forest so there’ll be nowhere to hide because their soldiers will be more numerous than locusts and no one will even be able to count them.
[Yirmiyah] [46]:[24] Mitsrayim’s inhabitants will be humiliated— they’ll be handed over to those northern people.
[Yirmiyah] [46]:[25] Yisrael’s (Israel) god, Commander-in-chief Yahweh says, “Listen, I’m about to punish Amon the god of No (Thebes) city, Mitsrayim (Egypt) and her other gods, its kings the Par’ohs (Pharaohs), and all those who trust in them.
[Yirmiyah] [46]:[26] I’ll hand them over to those who want them dead, and over to Bavel’s (Babylon) King Nevukadnetsar (Nebuchadnezzar) and his servants. But after that, Mitsrayim will be inhabited as in past times. That is Yahweh’s declaration.
[Yirmiyah] [46]:[27] But you, my servant Ya’akov (Jacob) (meaning Yisrael (Israel) ), don’t be afraid. Don’t be dismayed, Yisrael, because listen, I’m about to bring you back from far away, and your descendants from the land of their captivity. Then Ya’akov will return, find peace, and be secure, and there’ll be no one to terrify him.
[Yirmiyah] [46]:[28] This is Yahweh’s declaration: You, my servant Ya’akov, don’t be afraid, because I’m with you, so I’ll send complete destruction to all the nations that I drove you into. But I won’t completely destroy you, although I’ll discipline you fairly, and I certainly won’t leave you unpunished.”
[Yirmiyah] [47]:[1] This is Yahweh’s message that he gave to the prophet Yirmiyah (Jeremiah) concerning the Pelishtim before Par’oh (Pharaoh) attacked Azah (Gaza).
[Yirmiyah] [47]:[2] Yahweh says this: Listen, armies are rising in the north like floods of water. They’ll be like an overflowing river. Then they’ll overflow the land and everything in it— its cities and its inhabitants. So everyone will shout out for help, and all the land’s inhabitants will wail.
[Yirmiyah] [47]:[3] At the sound of the stamping of their powerful horses’ hooves, at the clattering of their chariots and the noise of their wheels, fathers won’t help their children because of their own helplessness.
[Yirmiyah] [47]:[4] The day is coming that will devastate all of the Pelishtim— to cut every survivor off from Tsor (Tyre) and Tsidon (Sidon) who wants to help them, because Yahweh is devastating the Pelishtim— the remnant who originally came from the island of Kaftor.
[Yirmiyah] [47]:[5] The people of Azah (Gaza) will shave their heads in mourning. The remnant in Ashkelon’s valley will be silenced. How much longer will you cut yourself in mourning for?
[Yirmiyah] [47]:[6] Oh no, sword of Yahweh, how long will it be until you stop? Get back to your scabbard. Stop and be silent.
[Yirmiyah] [47]:[7] How can it stop when Yahweh has commanded it, when he has ordered it to attack Ashkelon and the other cities along the coast?
[Yirmiyah] [48]:[1] Yisrael’s (Israel) god, Commander-in-chief Yahweh says to Moav (Moab): Nevo won’t end well because it’ll be devastated. Kiryatayim has been humiliated and captured. Its fortress has been disgraced and shattered.
[Yirmiyah] [48]:[2] No one will praise Moav again. Their enemies in Heshbon plotted disaster against them, saying, Let’s go and destroy it as a nation. Madmen will be silenced after the sword finishes with you.
[Yirmiyah] [48]:[3] Listen, a cry of distress is coming from Horonayim, where there’s ruin and terrible destruction.
[Yirmiyah] [48]:[4] Moav has been destroyed. Its workers have made their cries heard.
[Yirmiyah] [48]:[5] They weeps as they climb Luhit hill, because on the way down to Horonayim, shouts of distress will heard because of the destruction.
[Yirmiyah] [48]:[6] Flee, save your lives so you’ll be like a juniper bush in the wilderness.
[Yirmiyah] [48]:[7] Because of your trust in your practices and your wealth, you too will be captured. Then Kemosh will go away into captivity, along with its priests and leaders.
[Yirmiyah] [48]:[8] The destroyer will come to every city—no city will escape. The valley will perish and the plain will be devastated, as Yahweh has said.
[Yirmiyah] [48]:[9] Give wings to Moav (Moab), because it must certainly fly away. Its cities will become a wasteland without anyone living in them.
[Yirmiyah] [48]:[10] Anyone who’s slack doing Yahweh’s work should be cursed. Anyone who’s afraid to use his sword to kill should be cursed.
[Yirmiyah] [48]:[11] Moav (Moab) has felt secure since it was young. It’s like its wine that’s never been poured from container to container. It’s never gone into captivity. so it still tastes as good as ever— its nice aroma hasn’t changed.
[Yirmiyah] [48]:[12] But Yahweh declares that the time is coming when I’ll send along those who’ll tip it over and empty out all its pots and smash its jars.
[Yirmiyah] [48]:[13] Then Moav will be ashamed of their god Kemosh just as Yisrael’s (Israel) people were ashamed of the golden calf that they put their trust in at Beyt-El (Bethel).
[Yirmiyah] [48]:[14] How can you Moav soldiers say, ‘We are warriors, powerful fighting men’?
[Yirmiyah] [48]:[15] Moav will be devastated and its cities attacked. Its finest young men have gone down to the place of slaughter. That is the king’s declaration—his name is Commander-in-chief Yahweh.
[Yirmiyah] [48]:[16] Moav’s disaster is coming soon. Calamity is rushing towards it.
[Yirmiyah] [48]:[17] You surrounding nations, wail, and all you who know Moav’s fame, shout ‘Oh no, the strong staff, the splendid rod, has been broken.’
[Yirmiyah] [48]:[18] Come down from your place of honour and sit on the ground that’s dry and thirsty, you daughter living in Divon city, because the one who’ll destroy Moav will attack you— the one who’ll destroy your fortifications.
[Yirmiyah] [48]:[19] You people who live in Aroer city, stand on the road and watch. Ask the escaping men and women what happened there.
[Yirmiyah] [48]:[20] Moav has been humiliated because it’s been shattered. Wail and cry out. Tell the people at the Arnon river that Moav’s been devastated.
[Yirmiyah] [48]:[21] Now punishment has come to Moav’s (Moab) high plateau: to Holon, Yahats, Mofa’at,
[Yirmiyah] [48]:[22] Divon, Nevo, Beyt-Divlatayim,

[Yirmiyah] [51]:[36] Therefore Yahweh says this: Listen, I’m about to plead your case and bring about vengeance for you because I’ll dry up Bavel’s (Babylon) river and make its springs run dry.
[Yirmiyah] [51]:[37] Bavel will become heaps of rubble without any inhabitants— a den of jackals, a horror, and something to whistle at.
[Yirmiyah] [51]:[38] The Babylonians will roar together like young lions. They will growl like lion cubs.
[Yirmiyah] [51]:[39] When they become hot with greed, I’ll make a feast for them and I’ll get them drunk so they can celebrate. →Then they’ll enter into permanent sleep and not wake up. That is Yahweh’s declaration.
[Yirmiyah] [51]:[40] I’ll send them down to the slaughter, like lambs, rams, and male goats.
[Yirmiyah] [51]:[41] Wow, Bavel (Babylon) (Heb. Sheshak) has been captured. The city praised by the whole world has been seized. Wow, Bavel has become a horror among the nations.
[Yirmiyah] [51]:[42] The sea has come up over Bavel. It’s been covered by its violent waves.
[Yirmiyah] [51]:[43] Its cities have become a wasteland, a dry, wilderness region— an area that no one lives in, and no human being even passes through.
[Yirmiyah] [51]:[44] I’ll punish Bavel’s god Bel and I’ll pull what he swallowed back out of his mouth, Then the nations will no longer go streaming to him to placate him. What’s more, Bavel’s walls will fall.
[Yirmiyah] [51]:[45] Come out from Bavel, my people. Each of you should save their own life from Yahweh’s furious anger.
[Yirmiyah] [51]:[46] Don’t be discouraged or afraid due to the report that’s heard in the land, as there’ll be a report one year and the again the year after. There’ll be violence will in the world—ruler will be against ruler.
[Yirmiyah] [51]:[47] Therefore, listen, the time is coming when I’ll punish the Bavel’s carved idols. People across their country will be ashamed, and their slaughtered soldiers will all fall right there in their country.
[Yirmiyah] [51]:[48] Then the heavens and the earth, and everyone in them will celebrate over Bavel’s fall because destroyers from the north will come for it That is Yahweh’s declaration.
[Yirmiyah] [51]:[49] As Bavel has made Yisrael’s (Israel) slain warriors fall, so too their slain will fall in Bavel.
[Yirmiyah] [51]:[50] You all who escaped from being killed in war, go away—don’t stay still. Remember Yahweh even though you’re all far away. Start bringing Yerushalem (Jerusalem) to mind.
[Yirmiyah] [51]:[51] We’re ashamed because we’ve heard insults— our feeling of being disgraced can be seen on our faces, because foreigners have entered the sacred places in Yahweh’s house.
[Yirmiyah] [51]:[52] So Yahweh declares: Listen, the time is coming when I’ll punish Bavel’s (Babylon) carved idols, and their wounded people will groan across that entire region.
[Yirmiyah] [51]:[53] Yes, even if Bavel built tall towers or fortified their highest fortresses, destroyers that I’ve sent would still go there. That is Yahweh’s declaration.
[Yirmiyah] [51]:[54] A cry of distress came from Bavel (Babylon)— terrible destruction from the land of the Kasdim (Chaldeans)
[Yirmiyah] [51]:[55] because Yahweh is about to destroy Bavel. He’s causing its loud voice to die away. Their enemies roar like violent ocean waves— their noise becomes very prominent
[Yirmiyah] [51]:[56] because a destroyer has come against it, against Bavel, and their soldiers have been captured. Their weapons are shattered because Yahweh is a god of vengeance— he’ll definitely repay them fully.
[Yirmiyah] [51]:[57] I’ll make its princes, advisors, officials, and its soldiers drunk, and they will sleep in a permanent stupor and never wake up. That is the king’s declaration—Commander-in-chief Yahweh is his name.
[Yirmiyah] [51]:[58] Commander-in-chief Yahweh says this: Bavel’s (Babylon) thick walls will be completely demolished, and its tall gates will be set on fire. The peoples coming to their aid will waste their time trying— everything that the nations try to do for it will be burnt up.
[Yirmiyah] [51]:[59] This is the message that the prophet Yirmiyah (Jeremiah) commanded Serayah (son of Neriyah, son of Mahseyah) when he went with Yehudah’s (Judah) King Tsidkiyah (Zedekiah) to Bavel (Babylon) in the fourth year of his reign. Now Serayah was a chief officer,
[Yirmiyah] [51]:[60] and Yirmiyah had written on a scroll about all the disaster that was going to come to Bavel— all these messages that were written about Bavel.
[Yirmiyah] [51]:[61] Then Yirmiyah told Serayah, “When you go to Bavel, ensure that you read these messages aloud
[Yirmiyah] [51]:[62] and then pray, ‘Yahweh, you yourself have declared that you would destroy this place, and then that no man or animal will live in it and it’ll be desolate forever.’
[Yirmiyah] [51]:[63] Then when you’ve finished reading out this scroll, tie a stone to it and throw it into the middle of the Perat (Euphrates) River.
[Yirmiyah] [51]:[64] Say, ‘Bavel will sink like that. It won’t ever recover from the disaster that I’m sending against it, and they’ll become irrelevant’ Yirmiyah’s messages end here.
[Yirmiyah] [52]:[1] Tsidkiyah (Zedekiah) was twenty-one when he began to reign and he reigned from Yerushalem (Jerusalem) for eleven years. His mother’s name was Hamutal. (She was the daughter of Yirmiyah (Jeremiah) from Livnah.)
[Yirmiyah] [52]:[2] He did what was evil in Yahweh’s sight just as his father Yehoyakim had done.
[Yirmiyah] [52]:[3] All these events happened in Yerushalem and across the rest of Yehudah (Judah) because of Yahweh’s anger, until he drove them out of his sight. Then Tsidkiyah rebelled against the Babylonian king,
[Yirmiyah] [52]:[4] so on the 10th of the tenth month of the ninth year of King Tsidkiyah’s reign, the Babylonian King Nevukadnetsar (Nebuchadnezzar) came and surrounded Yerushalem with all his army. They took action to put the city under siege
[Yirmiyah] [52]:[5] and the it remained under siege until the eleventh year of King Tsidkiyah’s reign.
[Yirmiyah] [52]:[6] By the 9th of the fourth month, the famine was so severe in the city that there was no more food for the residents.
[Yirmiyah] [52]:[7] Then the city was broken into, and all the fighting men fled out of the city at night by the way of the gate that was between the two walls near the king’s garden, even though the Kasdim (Chaldeans) were all around the city. So they went in the direction of the Aravah plain along the Yarden (Jordan) river.
[Yirmiyah] [52]:[8] But the Chaldean army chased after the king, and overtook Tsidkiyah in the Yarden river plains near Yeriho (Jericho). All his army was then scattered away from him.
[Yirmiyah] [52]:[9] They captured the king and brought him up to the Babylonian king at Rivlah in Hamat region, where he passed sentence on him.
[Yirmiyah] [52]:[10] Then the Babylonian king slaughtered Tsidkiyah’s sons right there in front of his eyes, and he also slaughtered all of Yehudah’s leaders there at Rivlah.
[Yirmiyah] [52]:[11] Then he had Tsidkiyah’s eyes gouged out, shackled him with bronze chains, and took him to Bavel (Babylon) where the Babylonian king put him in prison until he died there.
[Yirmiyah] [52]:[12] Then on the 10th of the fifth month in the nineteenth year of the Babylonian King Nevukadnetsar’s (Nebuchadnezzar) reign, Nevuzar-Adan came to Yerushalem (Jerusalem). He was the commander of the king’s bodyguards and a servant of the Babylonian king.
[Yirmiyah] [52]:[13] He burnt down Yahweh’s house, the king’s palace, and all the homes in Yerushalem, as well as every important building in the city.
[Yirmiyah] [52]:[14] As for the walls all around Yerushalem, they were pulled down by the Babylonian army who were with the commander of the bodyguards.
[Yirmiyah] [52]:[15] Some of the poorer people and the rest of the people who remained in the city, as well as those who’d defected to the Babylonian king, and the rest of the craftsmen were taken into exile by Nevuzar-Adan,
[Yirmiyah] [52]:[16] However, Nevuzar-Adan, the commander of the bodyguards, left some of the poorest people to work the vineyards and the fields.
[Yirmiyah] [52]:[17] As for the bronze pillars that were part of Yahweh’s temple, and the large bronze basin called ‘The Sea’, and the stands that were in it, the Kasdim (Chaldeans) broke them into pieces and carried all the bronze back to Bavel (Babylon).
[Yirmiyah] [52]:[18] The pots, shovels, lamp trimmers, bowls, and all the bronze utensils that the priests had used when serving in the temple, were all taken away by the Kasdim.
[Yirmiyah] [52]:[19] Also, the basins and incense burners, the bowls, pots, lampstands, pans, and basins that were made of gold or silver, were taken away by the commander of the king’s bodyguards.
[Yirmiyah] [52]:[20] The two pillars, the large bronze basin known as ‘The Sea’, and the twelve bronze bulls that were under the stands, things that Shelomoh (Solomon) had made for Yahweh’s temple, contained too much bronze to weigh.
[Yirmiyah] [52]:[21] (Each pillar was eight metres high with a circumference of nearly six metres. Each pillar was hollow with a 8cm thick wall
[Yirmiyah] [52]:[22] with a bronze capital on the top. Each capital was over two metres high, with bronze latticework and bronze pomegranates all around.
[Yirmiyah] [52]:[23] There were ninety-six pomegranates on the sides of each capital, and another hundred pomegranates above the surrounding latticework.)
[Yirmiyah] [52]:[24] The commander of the bodyguards took the high priest Serayah prisoner, along with the second-level priest Tsefanyah (Zephaniah), and the three gatekeepers.
[Yirmiyah] [52]:[25] From the city, he took an army commander prisoner, as well as seven of the king’s advisers who were still in the city. He also took prisoner the king’s army recruitment officer, along with sixty important men from the country who were in the city.
[Yirmiyah] [52]:[26] Then Nevuzar-Adan, the commander of the bodyguards, took them to the Babylonian king at Rivlah,
[Yirmiyah] [52]:[27] and the king put them to death there at Rivlah in the Hamat region. So Yehudah’s (Judah) people were taken out of their country and into exile.
[Yirmiyah] [52]:[28] These were the people who Nevukadnetsar (Nebuchadnezzar) exiled: In Nevukadnetsar’s seventh year, 3,023 Yehudim (Jews).
[Yirmiyah] [52]:[29] In his eighteenth year, he took 832 people from Yerushalem (Jerusalem).
[Yirmiyah] [52]:[30] In his twenty-third year, Nevuzar-Adan, the commander of the king’s bodyguards, exiled 745 Yehudi (Jew) people. All those exiles totalled 4,600 people.
[Yirmiyah] [52]:[31] Some time later on the 25th of the twelfth month of the thirty-seventh year of the exile of Yehudah’s (Judah) King Yehoyakin, Bavel’s (Babylon) King Evil-Merodak (in the first year of his reign) released King Yehoyakin from prison.
[Yirmiyah] [52]:[32] He spoke kindly to him and gave him a seat more honourable than that of the other exiled kings who were with him in Bavel.
[Yirmiyah] [52]:[33] Evil-Merodak supplied new clothes for Yehoyakin to wear, and he ate regularly at the king’s table for the rest of his life.
[Yirmiyah] [52]:[34] He was also given a daily allowance by the king for the rest of his life.
[Sorrows] [1]:[1] Oh dear, how she sits alone, that city, a mighty people. Once powerful among the nations, she’s become like a widow. From being a princess among the provinces, she became a slave.
[Sorrows] [1]:[2] She weeps excessively in the night, and her tears are on her cheeks. Despite having many lovers, no one brings her comfort. All her friends betrayed her—they’ve become her enemies instead.
[Sorrows] [1]:[3] Yehudah (Judah) is exiled and made to experience suffering and harsh slavery. She sits among the nations but finds no rest. All who pursue her, overtake her in the midst of distress.
[Sorrows] [1]:[4] The roads of Tsiyon (Zion) mourn—no one’s coming to the scheduled festivals. All her gates are desolate. Her priests are groaning. Her young women are grieving and she makes herself bitter.
[Sorrows] [1]:[5] Her enemies have become her masters—her enemies prosper because Yahweh has made her suffer due to her frequent disobedience. Her children get taken away as captives by the enemy.
[Sorrows] [1]:[6] All her splendour was sent out from the daughter that’s Tsiyon (Zion). Her leaders have become like deer—they can’t find a pasture so they have very little strength as they flee from the pursuer.
[Sorrows] [1]:[7] Yerushalem (Jerusalem) remembers the days of her suffering and her homelessness, all her treasures which were from former days. When her people fell into the hand of the enemy and there was no one to help her, her enemies saw her—they laughed over her destruction.
[Sorrows] [1]:[8] Yerushalem disobeyed terribly, therefore, she became filth. All her glory is scorned, because they’ve seen her nakedness. Again, she groans and turns away.
[Sorrows] [1]:[9] Her uncleanness is in her skirt. She didn’t remember her end and her descent was marvellous. There wasn’t any comforter for her. “Oh, Yahweh, see my suffering, because the enemy is powerful.”
[Sorrows] [1]:[10] The enemy spread his hand over all her treasures. So, she saw the nations; they entered her sanctuary— those who you had forbidden to enter into your gathering place.
[Sorrows] [1]:[11] All her people are groaning, searching for bread. They give their treasures to restore life with food. “Look and see, Yahweh, because I’ve become worthless.
[Sorrows] [1]:[12] Is it nothing to you, all those going past on the road? Look and see if there is any sorrow like my sorrow, which has been forced on me, which Yahweh inflicted on the day of his fierce anger.
[Sorrows] [1]:[13] He sent fire down from on high into my bones. He spread a net for my feet and turned me away. He made me desolate—feeling faint every day.
[Sorrows] [1]:[14] The yoke of my disobedience is bound. With his hand it’s assembled together and placed on my neck. My strength is gone so now I stumble. My master arranged for me to be captured and I couldn’t defend myself.
[Sorrows] [1]:[15] My master has rejected all my mighty warriors protecting me. He has told us exactly when he plans to destroy my young men. My master has stomped on the grapes for Yehudah’s (Judah) virgin daughter.
[Sorrows] [1]:[16] As a result of those things, I weep. My eyes, oh dear, my eyes overflow with water because the comforter is far from me—one who restores my life. My sons have become desolate, because the enemy is made mighty.”
[Sorrows] [1]:[17] Tsiyon (Zion) has spread her hands wide—there is no comforter for her. Yahweh commanded that those surrounding Ya’akov (Jacob) become his enemies. Yerushalem (Jerusalem) has become filth in the middle of them.
[Sorrows] [1]:[18] “Yahweh is surely righteous, but I disobeyed his command. Hear, all peoples, and see my sorrow. My young men and women have been taken into captivity.
[Sorrows] [1]:[19] I called to my lovers but they deceived me. My priests and my elders perished in the city, while they searched for food to stay alive.
[Sorrows] [1]:[20] Look, Yahweh, because I’m engulfed—my stomach churns. My heart is undone within me, because I’ve disobeyed grievously. Out in the street, the sword bereaves. Inside the house, there’s death.
[Sorrows] [1]:[21] Take notice because I’m groaning. There’s no comforter for me. All my enemies heard my trouble—they rejoiced that you did it. You brought about the day of punishment that you declared, yet may those persecutors become like me.
[Sorrows] [1]:[22] May all their evil be noticed by you, and deal with them just as you have dealt with me because of all my disobedience, because my groans are many and my heart is faint.”

[Sorrows] [4]:[1] Wow, how the gold is tarnished—the pure gold has changed. The holy stones are scattered on the corners of every street.
[Sorrows] [4]:[2] The precious sons of Tsiyon (Zion) were once comparable with fine gold. Now they’re regarded as clay jars—the work of a potter’s hands.
[Sorrows] [4]:[3] Even the jackals offer their teats to suckle their cubs, but my people are fierce like the ostriches in the wilderness.
[Sorrows] [4]:[4] The tongue of the breast-feeding baby sticks to the roof of his mouth with thirst. The children ask for food from those distributing it, but there’s none for them.
[Sorrows] [4]:[5] Those used to eating the finest food are now desolate in the streets. Those once attended by servants wearing scarlet now embrace piles of rubbish.
[Sorrows] [4]:[6] The guilt of my people is greater than Sedom’s sin. That city was overthrown in an instant, but no one shed any tears about it.
[Sorrows] [4]:[7] Her religious leaders were purer than snow—whiter than milk. Their bones were redder than coral—their parts were sapphire.

[Sorrows] [4]:[9] Those slain by the sword were happier than those who died from hunger— those who slowly wasted away as if they were pierced through by the lack of produce from the countryside.

[Sorrows] [4]:[17] Our eyes failed as we waited uselessly for help. From our watchtowers, we expected to see other nations come to rescue us, but no.
[Sorrows] [4]:[18] They tracked our steps, walking in our paths. Our end was coming closer. Our days had been numbered, because our end had come.
[Sorrows] [4]:[19] The ones chasing after us were faster than the eagles in the sky. They chased us over the mountains, then they ambushed us in the wilderness.
