[Yehezkel] [1]:[1] When I was thirty years old, on July 5th, as I was living with the other captives by the Kevar Canal, the skies opened and I saw visions from God.
[Yehezkel] [1]:[2] That was the fifth year since King Yehoyakin had been taken captive.
[Yehezkel] [1]:[3] Yahweh gave me, the priest Yehezkel (Ezekiel) (son of Buzi), this message in the land of the Kasdim (Chaldeans) (often known better as Babylonians) by the Kevar Canal, and Yahweh revealed his strength to me there.
[Yehezkel] [1]:[4] Then I looked, and there was a windstorm coming from the north—a huge cloud with lightning flashing inside it and brilliant light inside it and surrounding it, and fire inside the cloud made it look amber coloured.
[Yehezkel] [1]:[5] In the middle was what seemed to be four living creatures resembling humans,
[Yehezkel] [1]:[6] but each of them had four faces and four wings.
[Yehezkel] [1]:[7] Their legs were straight, but they had hooves like calves’ hooves that gleamed like polished bronze.
[Yehezkel] [1]:[8] They had human hands under their wings on each of their four sides. For each of the four of them,
[Yehezkel] [1]:[9] their wings were touching the wings of the next creature, and they didn’t turn as they went—rather each one went straight forward.
[Yehezkel] [1]:[10] Each one’s front face was like a human face, then they each had a lion’s face on the right, a calf’s face on the left, and the fourth face was an eagle’s face.
[Yehezkel] [1]:[11] Their faces were like that, and their wings were spread out above, so that each creature had a pair of wings that touched another creature’s wings, and also a pair that covered their bodies.
[Yehezkel] [1]:[12] Each went straight forward, so that wherever the spirit directed them to go, they went without turning.
[Yehezkel] [1]:[13] The living creatures resembled burning coals or torches. Bright fire also moved around among the creatures, and there were flashes of lightning.
[Yehezkel] [1]:[14] The living creatures moved rapidly swiftly back and forth, and they looked a bit like lightning.
[Yehezkel] [1]:[15] Then I looked more closely and saw a wheel on the ground beside each of the living creatures with its four faces.
[Yehezkel] [1]:[16] Each of the wheels was the same, and they all shone like chrysolite. Each wheel seemed to have one wheel inside another wheel.
[Yehezkel] [1]:[17] When they moved, they didn’t have to turn to change direction.
[Yehezkel] [1]:[18] The rims of the wheels were awesomely tall, and all four of them were full of eyes around the rim.
[Yehezkel] [1]:[19] Whenever the living creatures moved, the wheels moved beside them. When the living creatures went upwards, the wheels also went up.
[Yehezkel] [1]:[20] Wherever the spirit would go, they went, and the wheels went up beside them, because the spirit of the living creature was in the wheels.
[Yehezkel] [1]:[21] Whenever the creatures moved, the wheels also moved, and when the creatures stood still, the wheels stood still. When the creatures went upwards, the wheels went up beside them, because the spirit of the living creature was in the wheels.
[Yehezkel] [1]:[22] Above the living creatures was something like an awesome crystal dome stretched out over their heads.
[Yehezkel] [1]:[23] Beneath the dome, each of the creatures’ wings stretched out straight and touched another creature’s wings. Each one also had a pair to cover their own body with.
[Yehezkel] [1]:[24] Then I heard the sound of their wings, which was like the noise of a lot of water. When they moved, it was like the voice of the powerful one—like the sound of a rainstorm or an army. Whenever they stood still, they lowered their wings.
[Yehezkel] [1]:[25] Whenever they stopped and lowered their wings, a voice came from under the dome that was above their heads.
[Yehezkel] [1]:[26] Above the dome over their heads was what looked like a sapphire stone that had been made into a throne, and on the thing like a throne was something that looked like a man.
[Yehezkel] [1]:[27] I saw a figure that appeared to have glowing metal with fire in it from his hips upwards, and looking downwards from his hips, I saw the appearance of fire and brightness all around.
[Yehezkel] [1]:[28] The bright light surrounding the throne looked like a rainbow in the clouds on a rainy day—it was the appearance of the likeness of Yahweh’s splendour. When I saw it, I quickly knelt down and bowed my head to the ground, and I heard a voice speaking.
[Yehezkel] [2]:[1] He said to me, “Son of humanity, stand up and then I’ll speak to you.”
[Yehezkel] [2]:[2] Then as he spoke to me, the spirit entered into me and stood me up, and I heard him speaking to me.
[Yehezkel] [2]:[3] He told me, “Son of humanity, I’m sending you to Yisrael’s (Israel) people—two rebellious nations that have rebelled against me. Both they and their ancestors have been sinning against me right up to this very moment.
[Yehezkel] [2]:[4] Their descendants are very stubborn and hardheaded. I’m sending you to them, and you’ll tell them that this is what the master Yahweh is saying to them.
[Yehezkel] [2]:[5] They might listen or might not. They’re a rebellious bunch, but they’ll at least know that a prophet’s been among them.
[Yehezkel] [2]:[6] And you, son of humanity, don’t be afraid of them or their words. Don’t be afraid, even though you’re among briers and thorns, and although you live with scorpions. Don’t fear their words or be dismayed by their faces, since they’re a rebellious bunch.
[Yehezkel] [2]:[7] Pass my messages on to them, whether they listen or not, because they’re quite rebellious.
[Yehezkel] [2]:[8] But you, son of humanity, listen to what I’m telling you. Don’t become rebellious like that rebellious bunch. Open your mouth and eat what I’m about to give you.”
[Yehezkel] [2]:[9] Then I looked and saw a hand extended out to me, and it was holding a scroll with writing on it.
[Yehezkel] [2]:[10] He spread it out in front of me—there was writing on both the front and the back, and it was full of messages about grief, mourning, and sad endings.
[Yehezkel] [3]:[1] He said to me, “Son of humanity, eat what you’ve found. Eat this scroll, then go speak to the Israeli people.”
[Yehezkel] [3]:[2] So I opened my mouth, and he gave me the scroll to eat.
[Yehezkel] [3]:[3] He told me, “Son of humanity, feed your belly and fill your stomach with this scroll that I’ve given you.” So I ate it, and it tasted as sweet as honey.
[Yehezkel] [3]:[4] Then he told me, “Son of humanity, go to the people of Yisrael (Israel) and pass my messages on to them,
[Yehezkel] [3]:[5] because you aren’t being sent to a people group who speak a strange or difficult language, but to the Israeli people—
[Yehezkel] [3]:[6] not to many people groups who speak strange or difficult languages whose words you wouldn’t be able to understand. I’m sure that if it was them that I sent you to, they would’ve listened to you.
[Yehezkel] [3]:[7] But the Israeli people won’t be willing to listen to you, because they’re not willing to listen to me. All the Israeli people are hardheaded and hardhearted.
[Yehezkel] [3]:[8] Listen, I’ll enable you to be as stubborn and tough as they are.
[Yehezkel] [3]:[9] I’ll make you hard like a diamond—harder than flint. Don’t be scared by them or discouraged by the looks they give you, because they’re rebellious people.”
[Yehezkel] [3]:[10] He also told me, “Son of humanity, listen very carefully to what I say, and keep thinking about it.
[Yehezkel] [3]:[11] Then go to any of your people who were brought here as captives, and tell them, ‘This is what the master Yahweh says,’ whether they’ll listen or not.”
[Yehezkel] [3]:[12] Then the spirit lifted me up, and I heard rumbling like a large earthquake behind me. (May Yahweh’s honour in his place be blessed.)
[Yehezkel] [3]:[13] It was the sound of the living creatures’ wings as they touched one another, and the sound of the wheels that were with them, and the sound of a large earthquake.
[Yehezkel] [3]:[14] Then the spirit lifted me up and took me away, and I went with bitterness and rage in my spirit, because Yahweh’s hand was pressing down firmly on me.
[Yehezkel] [3]:[15] Then I went to the captives at Tel-Aviv who lived along the Kevar Canal, and I stayed among them there for seven days, overwhelmed in amazement.
[Yehezkel] [3]:[16] After those seven days were over, Yahweh gave me this message:
[Yehezkel] [3]:[17] “Son of humanity, I’ve made you a guard over the Israeli people, so listen to this message of mine and give them my warning.
[Yehezkel] [3]:[18] When I tell the wicked, ‘You’ll certainly die’ and you don’t warn them about that or give them a warning about their evil actions so they might live—the wicked will die for their sin, but I’ll hold you responsible for their death.
[Yehezkel] [3]:[19] But if you do warn the wicked, and they don’t turn from their wickedness or from their wicked actions, then they’ll die for their sin, but you will have saved your own life.
[Yehezkel] [3]:[20] If a godly person turns from their righteousness and behaves unjustly, and I put a stumbling block in front of that person, they’ll die. Because you didn’t warn them, they’ll die in their sin, and I won’t consider the righteous things they did, but I’ll hold you responsible for their death.
[Yehezkel] [3]:[21] But if you warn the godly person to stop sinning so that they no longer sin, that person will surely live, since they were warned, and you will have saved your own life.”
[Yehezkel] [3]:[22] Then Yahweh’s hand was on me there, and he told me, “Get ready and go out into the plain, and I’ll speak with you there.”

[Yehezkel] [3]:[24] Then the spirit entered me and stood me up on my feet, and spoke with me, telling me: Go and shut yourself up in your house.

[Yehezkel] [7]:[7] Your doom is coming to you who inhabit the land. The time has come. The day of destruction is near, and the mountains will no longer be cheerful.

[Yehezkel] [7]:[9] because I won’t be compassionate and I won’t spare you. Whatever you’ve done in the past, I’ll do to you now, and your disgusting actions will bounce back on you so you’ll know that it’s me, Yahweh, who’s punishing you.
[Yehezkel] [7]:[10] Look here, the day—yes, it’s coming. Doom has gone out. The wooden stick has blossomed. Arrogance has budded.
[Yehezkel] [7]:[11] Violence has grown up into a wooden stick of wickedness, but none of them (even though there’s many of them), and none of their wealth, and none of their importance will continue.
[Yehezkel] [7]:[12] “The time is coming—the day has come close. Don’t let a buyer be happy or a seller be sad, because my anger is directed at the entire large group.
[Yehezkel] [7]:[13] No, the seller won’t return to the land he sold as long as they both live, because the vision concerning the entire group won’t be reversed, and because of their disobedience, none of them will be able to save themselves.
[Yehezkel] [7]:[14] They’ve blown the trumpet and gotten everything ready, but there’s no one marching to battle, since my anger is on the entire large group.
[Yehezkel] [7]:[15] “The sword is on the outside, and deadly diseases and famine are inside the building. People who are in the countryside will die by the sword, while famine and deadly diseases will consume those in the city.
[Yehezkel] [7]:[16] But some survivors will escape from among them, and will go up into the hills. Like the doves that live in the valleys, all of them will moan—each person for their own disobedience.
[Yehezkel] [7]:[17] They won’t be able to use their trembling hands, and their knees will feel like liquid.
[Yehezkel] [7]:[18] They’ll wear sackcloth, but will be covered in terror. Their faces will display their shame, and they’ll shave their heads as a sign of sorrow.
[Yehezkel] [7]:[19] They’ll throw their silver into the streets, and their gold will be like rubbish. Their silver and gold won’t be able to rescue them in the day of Yahweh’s rage. Their lives won’t be saved, and their hunger won’t be satisfied, because their disobedience has become a stumbling block.
[Yehezkel] [7]:[20] In their pride they took his beautiful jewelled ornaments and made them into their idolatrous figures and detestable things. Therefore, I’m going to defile those things.
[Yehezkel] [7]:[21] I’ll hand those things over to strangers and to the earth’s wicked people as plunder, and they’ll defile them.
[Yehezkel] [7]:[22] Then I’ll put my hand over my eyes when they defile my cherished place—bandits will enter it and defile it.
[Yehezkel] [7]:[23] “Make a chain, because the country is filled with judgement for murder, and now the city is full of violence.
[Yehezkel] [7]:[24] I’ll bring the most wicked foreigners here, and they’ll take over the people’s houses, and I’ll bring the pride of the powerful people to an end, because their sacred places will be defiled.
[Yehezkel] [7]:[25] Anguish will be the order of the day, and they’ll wish for peace, but there won’t be any.
[Yehezkel] [7]:[26] Disaster will follow disaster and there’ll be rumour after rumour. Then they’ll be wanting a vision from the prophet, but the priest will no longer teach God’s instructions, and advice from the elders will be useless.
[Yehezkel] [7]:[27] The king will mourn and the prince will be overcome by despair, while the hands of the country’s people will tremble in fear. I’ll do that to them just like they did to others. I’ll judge them by their own standards until they know that I am Yahweh.”
[Yehezkel] [8]:[1] Then in the middle of the sixth year, as I sat in my house, and Yehudah’s (Judah) elders sat in front of me, my master Yahweh’s hands fell on me there again.
[Yehezkel] [8]:[2] I looked, and wow—there was something that looked a bit like a man. From his hips downward there appeared to be fire, and from his hips upward there appeared to be something shining like glowing metal.
[Yehezkel] [8]:[3] Then he reached out something in the shape of a hand and took me by my hair—the Spirit lifted me up between earth and the heavens, and in visions from God, he took me to Yerushalem (Jerusalem), to the entrance of the inner northern gate, where the idol was that made Yahweh very jealous.
[Yehezkel] [8]:[4] Then wow, the brilliant light of Yisrael’s (Israel) god was there, just like the vision that I’d seen on the plain.
[Yehezkel] [8]:[5] Then he told me, “Son of humanity, look towards the north.” So I looked towards the north, and to the north of the gate leading to the altar—there in the entrance—was the idol that caused the jealousy.
[Yehezkel] [8]:[6] So he told me, “Son of humanity, do you see what they’re doing? Those are horribly disgusting things that the Israeli people are doing here to drive me far from my own sanctuary. But you’ll see even more disgusting things soon.”
[Yehezkel] [8]:[7] Then he took me to the courtyard doorway, and I looked, and there was a hole in the wall.
[Yehezkel] [8]:[8] He told me, “Son of humanity, dig into this wall.” So I dug into the wall, and discovered a doorway.
[Yehezkel] [8]:[9] Then he told me, “Go and see the disgustingly wicked things that they’re doing there.”
[Yehezkel] [8]:[10] So I went through and looked, and oh dear, there were shapes of every creeping thing and detestable creature. Pictures of all the Israeli people’s idols were carved into the wall all around.
[Yehezkel] [8]:[11] Seventy elders from the Israeli people were there, and Shafan’s son Ya’azanyah was standing in the middle of them. They were standing in front of the images, and each man was holding his incense burner so that the smell of the cloud of incense went up.
[Yehezkel] [8]:[12] Then he asked me, “Son of humanity, do you see what the Israeli elders are doing in the dark? Each one does this in his idol’s hidden room, because they say, ‘Yahweh doesn’t even notice us. Yahweh’s abandoned this country.’ ”
[Yehezkel] [8]:[13] Then he told me, “Turn again and see the other terribly disgusting things that they’re doing,”
[Yehezkel] [8]:[14] and he took me to the gate at the northern entrance of Yahweh’s temple, and oh dear—there were some women sitting there mourning for the Babylonian Tamuz deity.
[Yehezkel] [8]:[15] Then he said to me, “Son of humanity, do you see that? Turn again, and you’ll see even more disgusting things than those.”
[Yehezkel] [8]:[16] Then he took me into the inner courtyard of Yahweh’s house, and oh no—at the entrance of Yahweh’s temple between the porch and the altar, there were about twenty-five men with their backs toward the temple and their faces toward the east where they were worshipping the sun.
[Yehezkel] [8]:[17] He asked me, “Son of humanity, do you see that? Is it insignificant that Yehudah’s (Judah) people do those disgusting things that they’re doing here? They’ve filled the land with violence and keep provoking me to anger and mocking me.
[Yehezkel] [8]:[18] So I will also do something to them—I won’t have compassion and I won’t spare them. Even if they cry loudly in my ears, I won’t hear them.”
[Yehezkel] [9]:[1] Then I heard Yahweh call out with a loud voice, saying, “Guards, come up to the city, and each one is to bring his destructive weapon.”
[Yehezkel] [9]:[2] Then wow, six men came out from the pathway from the upper gate that faces north, each carrying his weapon of slaughter. There was a man among them dressed in linen with writing equipment at his side. Then they went in and stood beside the bronze altar.
[Yehezkel] [9]:[3] Then the bright light representing Yisrael’s (Israel) god went from the winged creature, where it had been, up to the threshold of the temple. Yahweh called to the man dressed in linen who had the writing equipment at his side.
[Yehezkel] [9]:[4] Yahweh told him, “Go through the middle of Yerushalem (Jerusalem) City, and make a mark on the foreheads of those who complain and despair about all the disgusting things being done there in the middle of the city.”
[Yehezkel] [9]:[5] Then he spoke to the others within my hearing, “Go through the city after him and kill. Don’t let yourselves have compassion, and don’t show any pity.
[Yehezkel] [9]:[6] Slaughter all the old men, young adults, little children, and women, but don’t approach anyone who has the mark on their head. Begin at my sacred place.” So they began with the elders who were in front of the temple.
[Yehezkel] [9]:[7] Yahweh told them, “Defile the temple, and fill its courtyards with the corpses. Now go.” So they went out and started attacking the city.
[Yehezkel] [9]:[8] As they were attacking it, I found myself alone, and I fell to my knees with my head bowed down to the ground, and cried out, and said, “Ah, master Yahweh, will you destroy the entire remnant of Yisrael by pouring out your rage on Yerushalem?”
[Yehezkel] [9]:[9] “The disobedience of the people of Yisrael and Yehudah (Judah) has been extremely bad,” he answered. “The land is full of blood, and the city full of perversions, since they say, ‘Yahweh has forgotten this country,’ and ‘Yahweh won’t take any notice.’
[Yehezkel] [9]:[10] So then, I won’t show compassion, and I won’t spare them, rather I’ll bring it all on their heads.”
[Yehezkel] [9]:[11] Then wow, the man dressed in linen who had the writing equipment by his side came back to report, saying, “I’ve done everything you commanded.”
[Yehezkel] [10]:[1] As I looked toward the dome that was over the heads of the winged creatures, something appeared above them that looked like a sapphire stone that had been made into a throne.
[Yehezkel] [10]:[2] Then Yahweh spoke to the man dressed in linen and said, “Go between the wheels underneath the winged creatures, and fill both your hands with fiery coals from between the winged creatures and scatter them over the city.” Then the man went in as I watched.
[Yehezkel] [10]:[3] The winged creatures stood on the right side of the temple when the man went in, and a cloud filled the inner courtyard.
[Yehezkel] [10]:[4] Yahweh’s brilliant light rose up from the winged creature and stood over the threshold of the temple. It filled the temple with the cloud, and the courtyard was full of the brightness of Yahweh’s splendour.
[Yehezkel] [10]:[5] The sound of the creatures’ wings could be heard as far as the outer courtyard, like the voice of the powerful God when he speaks.
[Yehezkel] [10]:[6] When Yahweh had commanded the man dressed in linen, “Take fire from between the wheels that are between the winged creatures,” the man went in and stood beside a wheel.
[Yehezkel] [10]:[7] A winged creature reached out his hand between the winged creatures to the fire that was among them, and lifted it up and placed it into the hands of the one dressed in linen. The man took it and went back out.
[Yehezkel] [10]:[8] I noticed that the winged creatures had something like a human hand under their wings,
[Yehezkel] [10]:[9] then I looked, and wow, four wheels were beside the winged creatures—one wheel beside each one—and the wheels seemed like shining chrysolite.
[Yehezkel] [10]:[10] They all appeared to be the same, like having a wheel within a wheel.
[Yehezkel] [10]:[11] When they moved, they went in any of their four directions, without turning as they went, because whatever direction the head faced, they went in that direction without turning as they went.
[Yehezkel] [10]:[12] Their whole body (including their backs, their hands, and their wings) was covered with eyes, and there were eyes all around the four wheels, covering them as well.
[Yehezkel] [10]:[13] I heard someone call them ‘the whirling wheels’.
[Yehezkel] [10]:[14] Each one had four faces: the first face was a winged creature’s face, the second was a human face, the third was a lion’s face, and the fourth was an eagle’s face.
[Yehezkel] [10]:[15] Then the living creatures (they were the same ones I’d seen by the Kevar Canal) rose up in the air.
[Yehezkel] [10]:[16] Whenever the winged creatures moved, the wheels would go beside them, and whenever the winged creatures lifted up their wings to take off from the earth, the wheels didn’t turn—they still stayed beside them.
[Yehezkel] [10]:[17] When the winged creatures stood still, the wheels stood still, and when they went up, the wheels went up with them, because the spirit of the living creature was in the wheels.
[Yehezkel] [10]:[18] Then Yahweh’s brilliant light moved out over the temple threshold and stayed over the winged creatures.
[Yehezkel] [10]:[19] The winged creatures lifted up their wings and rose from the ground in my sight when they travelled, and the wheels did the same beside them. They stood at the eastern entrance to Yahweh’s residence, and the brilliant light of Yisrael’s (Israel) god came onto them from above.
[Yehezkel] [10]:[20] Those were the living creatures that I’d seen below Yisrael’s god by the Kevar Canal, so I knew that they were winged creatures.
[Yehezkel] [10]:[21] They each had four faces and four wings, and had something like human hands under their wings,
[Yehezkel] [10]:[22] and their faces resembled the faces that I’d seen in the vision at the Kevar Canal, and each of them went straight ahead.
[Yehezkel] [11]:[1] Then the spirit lifted me up and brought me to the eastern gate of Yahweh’s temple, facing east, and wow, in the doorway of the gate there were twenty-five men. Among them I saw Azur’s son Ya’azanyah and Benayah’s son Pelatyah, who were leaders of the people.
[Yehezkel] [11]:[2] Yahweh told me, “Son of humanity, these are the men who plan to do evil things and who make wicked plans in this city.
[Yehezkel] [11]:[3] They’re saying, ‘This isn’t yet the time to build houses. This city is like a cooking pot, and we’re the meat.’
[Yehezkel] [11]:[4] So, prophesy against them, son of humanity, start prophesying.”
[Yehezkel] [11]:[5] Then Yahweh’s spirit came on me and told me to say: This is what Yahweh says, “That’s what you Israeli people are saying, because I know what goes through your mind.
[Yehezkel] [11]:[6] You’ve killed many people in this city, and filled its streets with them.
[Yehezkel] [11]:[7] Therefore the master Yahweh says: The people you’ve killed, whose bodies you’ve laid in the middle of Yerushalem (Jerusalem), are the meat, and this city is the pot. But you people are going to be brought out from the centre of this city.
[Yehezkel] [11]:[8] You’ve feared the sword, so I’m bringing the sword against you. That’s my master Yahweh’s declaration.
[Yehezkel] [11]:[9] I’ll bring you out from the city, and put you into the hands of foreigners, because I’ll bring judgement against you people.
[Yehezkel] [11]:[10] You’ll be killed by the sword. I’ll judge you within Yisrael’s (Israel) borders so that you people will know that I am Yahweh.
[Yehezkel] [11]:[11] This city won’t be your cooking pot, nor will you be the meat inside it. I’ll judge you people within Yisrael’s borders.
[Yehezkel] [11]:[12] Then you’ll know that I am Yahweh, the one whose instructions you haven’t obeyed and whose regulations you haven’t followed. Instead, you people have imitated the wicked customs of the nations that surround you.”
[Yehezkel] [11]:[13] Then as I was prophesying, Benayah’s son Pelatyah died. So I fell to my knees with my face bowed low to the ground and cried out with a loud voice, “Oh no, my master Yahweh, will you completely eliminate the Israeli people?”
[Yehezkel] [11]:[14] Then Yahweh gave me this message:
[Yehezkel] [11]:[15] “Your brothers, son of humanity, your brothers and all the Israeli people who were exiled—the ones living in Yerushalem (Jerusalem) say about them all, ‘They’re far away from Yahweh. This land was given to us as ours to own.’
[Yehezkel] [11]:[16] So tell them, ‘My master Yahweh says this: ‘Although I’ve removed them far away to other nations, and though I’ve scattered them among those lands, I myself have been a place of security for them for a little while in the lands where they were taken.’
[Yehezkel] [11]:[17] So explain to them, ‘My master Yahweh says this: ‘I’ll gather you from the people groups, and assemble you from the lands where you were scattered, and I’ll give you back the country of Yisrael (Israel).’
[Yehezkel] [11]:[18] Then they’ll go there and remove every detestable and disgusting thing from there,
[Yehezkel] [11]:[19] and I’ll give them one heart, and I’ll put a new spirit in them. I’ll take the rock-hard heart out of them and give them a tender heart,
[Yehezkel] [11]:[20] so that they’ll follow my instructions and obey my regulations. Then they’ll be my people, and I’ll be their god.
[Yehezkel] [11]:[21] But to those who would rather happily choose their detestable and disgusting ways, I’ll make their actions bounce back onto their own heads. That’s the master Yahweh’s declaration.”
[Yehezkel] [11]:[22] Then the winged creatures lifted up their wings and the wheels that were beside them, and the brilliant light of Yisrael’s (Israel) god was up high over them.
[Yehezkel] [11]:[23] Then it went up from the centre of the city and sat above the mountain to the east of the city.
[Yehezkel] [11]:[24] The spirit lifted me up and brought me into the land of the Kasdim (Chaldeans) to the exiles, in the vision from God’s spirit, and the vision that I’d been seeing left me,
[Yehezkel] [11]:[25] and I told the exiles everything Yahweh had shown me.
[Yehezkel] [12]:[1] Then Yahweh gave me this message:
[Yehezkel] [12]:[2] “Son of humanity, you live among a rebellious people group who have eyes to see, yet they don’t see, and who have ears to hear, but don’t listen, because they’re a rebellious people group.
[Yehezkel] [12]:[3] “Therefore, son of humanity, pack up your stuff ready to go into exile, and each day while they’re watching, start going out somewhere, because while they’re watching, I’ll exile you from your place to another place. Perhaps they’ll begin to see, even though they’re such rebellious people.
[Yehezkel] [12]:[4] Each day while they’re watching, bring out your things for an exile, then as they watch in the evening, go out in the way that people do when going into exile.
[Yehezkel] [12]:[5] Dig a hole through the city wall where they’ll see you do it, and go out through it.
[Yehezkel] [12]:[6] While they’re watching, lift your things up onto your shoulder, and bring them out in the darkness. Cover your face, because you mustn’t see this land, since I’ve made you into a sign for the Israeli people.”
[Yehezkel] [12]:[7] So I did just as I was instructed: I brought my things for an exile out in the daytime, and in the evening I dug a hole through the wall by hand. I brought my things out in the dark, and lifted them up onto my shoulder as they watched.
[Yehezkel] [12]:[8] The next morning, Yahweh gave me this message:
[Yehezkel] [12]:[9] “Son of humanity, haven’t those rebellious Israeli people asked you what you’re doing?
[Yehezkel] [12]:[10] Tell them that the master Yahweh says this: ‘this prophetic action concerns the ruler in Yerushalem (Jerusalem) and all the other Israeli people who are there.’
[Yehezkel] [12]:[11] Tell them that you’re a sign to them, and that everything you’ve done will happen to them—they’ll be captured and taken into exile in another country.
[Yehezkel] [12]:[12] Their leader will lift his things up onto his shoulder in the dark, and will go out through the wall. They’ll dig through the wall and take their things out. He’ll cover his face, so he won’t see the place he’s leaving.
[Yehezkel] [12]:[13] I’ll spread my net out over him and he’ll be caught in my trap, then I’ll take him away to Bavel (Babylon) (the land of the Kasdim (Chaldeans)), but he won’t see it, and he’ll die there.
[Yehezkel] [12]:[14] I’ll also scatter all of his assistants in every direction, and I’ll send out a sword after his entire army.
[Yehezkel] [12]:[15] When I scatter them among the nations and disperse them throughout the lands, then they’ll know that I am Yahweh.
[Yehezkel] [12]:[16] But I’ll spare a few of them from the sword, famine, and deadly diseases, so they’ll be able to record all their hardships and ungodly practices in the countries that I take them to, so they’ll know that I am Yahweh.”
[Yehezkel] [12]:[17] Then Yahweh gave me another message:
[Yehezkel] [12]:[18] “Son of humanity, eat your food while trembling with fear, and drink your water while shaking anxiously,
[Yehezkel] [12]:[19] and tell the people in this country, ‘My master Yahweh says this about the inhabitants of Yerushalem (Jerusalem), and the country of Yisrael (Israel), “They’ll anxiously eat their food and fearfully drink their water, since all the abundance from the land will be devastated because of the violence of all the people who live there.
[Yehezkel] [12]:[20] The inhabited cities will become desolate, and the land itself will become a wasteland. Then you’ll know that I am Yahweh.” ’ ”
[Yehezkel] [12]:[21] Then Yahweh gave me another message:
[Yehezkel] [12]:[22] “Son of humanity, what’s that saying that you have in Yisrael (Israel)? It goes, ‘The days seem to go on and on, yet no prophecy ever comes true.’
[Yehezkel] [12]:[23] So tell them, ‘This is what the master Yahweh says: I’m going to prove that what they say isn’t correct, then they’ll never say it again in Yisrael.’ Tell them, ‘It’ll soon be the time when everything that the prophets have predicted will happen,
[Yehezkel] [12]:[24] because there’ll no longer be any false visions or people-pleasing prophecies within Yisrael.
[Yehezkel] [12]:[25] I speak, and I put the words that I speak into action, because I am Yahweh. The matter will no longer be delayed, because I’ll speak this message in your lifetimes, you rebellious people, and then I’ll carry it out!’ That’s the master Yahweh’s declaration.”
[Yehezkel] [12]:[26] Then Yahweh gave me another message:
[Yehezkel] [12]:[27] “Listen, son of humanity, the Israeli people have said, ‘The vision that the prophet sees is for many years from now, and he prophesies about far-off times,’
[Yehezkel] [12]:[28] so tell them, ‘The master Yahweh says this: ‘My words won’t be delayed any longer, but the message that I’ve given will be put into effect. That’s the master Yahweh’s declaration.’ ”
[Yehezkel] [13]:[1] Then Yahweh gave me another message:
[Yehezkel] [13]:[2] “Son of humanity, prophesy against the prophets who are prophesying in Yisrael (Israel), and tell those who are prophesying out of their own imaginations, ‘Listen to Yahweh’s message.
[Yehezkel] [13]:[3] My master Yahweh says this: ‘Foolish prophets who follow their own spirit and haven’t actually seen any vision won’t end well.
[Yehezkel] [13]:[4] Yisrael, your prophets have been like jackals in the wastelands.
[Yehezkel] [13]:[5] You haven’t gone to the breaks in the walls around the Israeli cities and repaired them, in order to be able to defend yourselves well during the battle on Yahweh’s chosen day.
[Yehezkel] [13]:[6] The people have false visions and make false predictions. Yahweh hasn’t sent those who say that they’re bringing Yahweh’s declaration, but nevertheless they’ve made people hope that their messages would come true.
[Yehezkel] [13]:[7] Haven’t you had false visions and made false predictions—all of you who say that you’re bringing Yahweh’s declaration when I myself haven’t spoken?’
[Yehezkel] [13]:[8] Therefore the master Yahweh says this, ‘Because you people have presented false visions and have told lies, this is the master Yahweh’s declaration against you:
[Yehezkel] [13]:[9] I’ll punish the prophets who have lying visions and who make false predictions. They won’t be allowed in the assembly of my people, or enrolled in the record of Yisrael’s descendants. They mustn’t go to the land of Yisrael—that’s how you people will know that I am the master Yahweh.
[Yehezkel] [13]:[10] Also because they led my people astray and said, “Peace,” when there’s no peace, it’s as if they’re building a wall and then whitewashing it.’
[Yehezkel] [13]:[11] Tell the ones who are whitewashing the wall that it’ll fall down. There’ll be a downpour, then I’ll send hailstones to make it fall down, and a strong wind to break it down.
[Yehezkel] [13]:[12] See, the wall will fall down. Haven’t others asked you where the white coating went that you put on it?
[Yehezkel] [13]:[13] Therefore my master Yahweh says this: ‘In my rage, I’ll bring a storm, and in my anger, there’ll be heavy rain causing floods. In my rage, hailstones will completely destroy Yerushalem (Jerusalem).
[Yehezkel] [13]:[14] I’ll tear down the wall that you covered with whitewash, and I’ll demolish it to ground level and expose its foundations. So it’ll fall, and you’ll be annihilated in the middle of it all. Then you people will know that I am Yahweh.
[Yehezkel] [13]:[15] In my rage I’ll annihilate the wall and those who whitewashed it. I’ll tell you, “The wall doesn’t exist anymore, nor do the people who whitewashed it—
[Yehezkel] [13]:[16] those Israeli prophets who prophesied about Yerushalem and had visions of peace for it. But there isn’t any peace! That’s the master Yahweh’s declaration.” ’
[Yehezkel] [13]:[17] So, son of humanity, turn your attention to your people’s daughters and prophesy against them because they invented prophecies in their own imaginations.
[Yehezkel] [13]:[18] Tell them that the master Yahweh says this: ‘The women won’t end well who sew magic charms onto every part of their hands, and make headbands for people of every walk of life that are used to deceive people and hunt them down. Do you people really think you can get away with hunting down my people, but then save your own lives?
[Yehezkel] [13]:[19] You’ve profaned me among my people for handfuls of barley and crumbs of bread. You people have killed people who shouldn’t have died, and saved the lives of those who shouldn’t have continued to live, because of your lies to my people who heard you.
[Yehezkel] [13]:[20] Therefore my master Yahweh says this: ‘I’m against the magic charms that you’ve used to lure the people in as if they were birds. Indeed, I’ll tear them from your arms, and I’ll let the people you’ve trapped like birds go free.
[Yehezkel] [13]:[21] I’ll tear away your headbands and rescue my people from your control so they’ll no longer be trapped in your system. Then you people will know that I am Yahweh.
[Yehezkel] [13]:[22] Because you’ve discouraged the righteous people with lies (even though I didn’t desire their discouragement), and because you people encouraged the actions of the wicked people instead so they won’t change their ways to save their lives,
[Yehezkel] [13]:[23] because of that, you’ll no longer have false visions or continue to make predictions, because I’ll rescue my people out of your control. Then you’ll know that I am Yahweh.’ ”
[Yehezkel] [14]:[1] One day some of the Israeli elders came and sat down to talk,
[Yehezkel] [14]:[2] and Yahweh gave me this message:
[Yehezkel] [14]:[3] “Son of humanity, these men have taken their idols to be their gods, and their choice to disobey makes it very difficult for them to relate to me. Should I even let them ask me anything?
[Yehezkel] [14]:[4] Therefore tell them that the master Yahweh says this: ‘Every Israeli person who makes their idols their priority, or who allows their disobedience to separate them from me, and who then comes to a prophet, I, Yahweh, will answer them according to how many idols they have.
[Yehezkel] [14]:[5] I’ll do that so that I can reclaim the Israeli people whose values are now far from mine due to their idols.
[Yehezkel] [14]:[6] Therefore tell the Israeli people that the master Yahweh says this: ‘Change your behaviour and turn away from your idols. Make a decision to stop disobeying me by doing those evil things.
[Yehezkel] [14]:[7] Any Israeli person or any foreigner residing in Yisrael (Israel) who deserts me, who takes idols to be their gods and allows their disobedience to separate them from me, and who then comes to a prophet to request my guidance, I, Yahweh, will answer that person myself.
[Yehezkel] [14]:[8] I’ll clearly show my disapproval and make that person into a sign for others and into a talking point, and they’ll be isolated from the rest of my people, and you people will know that I am Yahweh.
[Yehezkel] [14]:[9] If a prophet is deceived and speaks a message, then I, Yahweh, will deceive that prophet. I’ll take action against him and destroy him to remove him from among the Israeli people.
[Yehezkel] [14]:[10] Both the prophet and the one who asks him for advice will be guilty, and I’ll punish both of them for their disobedience.
[Yehezkel] [14]:[11] Because of that, the Israeli people will no longer wander away from following me, nor defile themselves any longer through all their disobedience. They’ll be my people, and I’ll be their god. That’s the master Yahweh’s declaration.’ ”
[Yehezkel] [14]:[12] Then Yahweh gave me another message:
[Yehezkel] [14]:[13] “Son of humanity, when a country sins against me by choosing to worship other gods, so that I decide to take action against it, then I’ll break the cycle of food production and send a famine out over it. I’ll punish both people and animals from that land
[Yehezkel] [14]:[14] in such a way that even if Noah, Daniyel, and Iyov (Job) lived in that place, they could only rescue their own lives by being blameless in my sight. That’s the master Yahweh’s declaration.
[Yehezkel] [14]:[15] If I send vicious wild animals through the country and make it barren so that it becomes a wasteland where no one can pass through because of those animals,
[Yehezkel] [14]:[16] then even if those same three men were in it, as I live, declares the master Yahweh, they wouldn’t be able to rescue even their own children—only their own lives would be saved, but the land itself would become a wasteland.
[Yehezkel] [14]:[17] Or if I bring a sword against that country and say, ‘Sword, go through the land and eliminate both the people and domestic animals from it’,
[Yehezkel] [14]:[18] then even if those three men were in it, as I live, declares the master Yahweh, they wouldn’t be able to rescue even their own sons or daughters—only their own lives would be saved.
[Yehezkel] [14]:[19] Or if I send deadly diseases against that country and pour out my rage against it through bloodshed, in order to eliminate both the people and the domestic animals,
[Yehezkel] [14]:[20] as surely as I live, even if Noah, Daniyel, and Iyov were in that country, they wouldn’t be able to rescue even their sons and daughters. They’d save only themselves by being blameless in my sight. That’s the master Yahweh’s declaration.
[Yehezkel] [14]:[21] The master Yahweh says this: ‘I’ll certainly make things worse by sending my four punishments against Yerushalem (Jerusalem) to eliminate both the people and the domestic animals from it: famine, sword, wild animals, and deadly diseases.
[Yehezkel] [14]:[22] But listen! Despite that, a remnant will be left in the city—survivors who’ll go out with sons and daughters. Yes, they’ll go out to you, and you’ll see their behaviour and actions and understand why they deserved the punishment that I sent to Yerushalem, and about everything else that I’ve sent against the country.
[Yehezkel] [14]:[23] The survivors will relieve you people when you see their behaviour and their actions, because you’ll know that all those things that I’ve done against Yerushalem, I didn’t do them without good reason. That’s the master Yahweh’s declaration.”
[Yehezkel] [15]:[1] Then Yahweh gave me another message:
[Yehezkel] [15]:[2] “Son of humanity, how is a vine better than any tree with branches in a forest?
[Yehezkel] [15]:[3] Do people take wood from a vine to make anything? Would anyone use vine wood even to make something to hang a mug on?
[Yehezkel] [15]:[4] If it’s used as firewood, and if the fire burns both ends, and even the middle, is it good wood, or indeed good for anything?
[Yehezkel] [15]:[5] Originally, the vine wood couldn’t be used to make anything, so surely, when the fire’s burnt it, it still can’t do anything useful.
[Yehezkel] [15]:[6] Therefore the master Yahweh says this: ‘Unlike the trees in the forests, I’ve given the vine as fuel for fires. I’ll act in the same way toward Yerushalem’s (Jerusalem) inhabitants,
[Yehezkel] [15]:[7] and I’ll start to take action against them. Even if they get out of the fire, the fire will still consume them, so you people will know that I am Yahweh, when I take action against them.
[Yehezkel] [15]:[8] Then I’ll make the land into an abandoned wasteland because they chose to worship other gods. That’s the master Yahweh’s declaration.”
[Yehezkel] [16]:[1] Then Yahweh gave me another message:
[Yehezkel] [16]:[2] “Son of humanity, inform Yerushalem (Jerusalem) about their detestable behaviour,
[Yehezkel] [16]:[3] and declare that the master Yahweh says this to Yerushalem: Your beginning and your birth took place in the land of Kena’an (Canaan), your father was an Amori, and your mother was a Hiti.
[Yehezkel] [16]:[4] When you were born, your mother didn’t cut your cord, nor did she clean you with water or rub you down with salt, or wrap cloth around you.
[Yehezkel] [16]:[5] No one cared enough about you to do any of these things for you—to be compassionate toward you. Your life was despised and you were thrown out into the open field on the very day that you were born.
[Yehezkel] [16]:[6] But I went past, and I saw you, Yerushalem, writhing in your own blood, so I said to you as you lay there in your blood, “Live!”
[Yehezkel] [16]:[7] I made you grow like a plant in the countryside. You grew up and became tall, and you became the most precious jewel. Your breasts became firm, and your hair grew thick, even though you’d been naked and bare.
[Yehezkel] [16]:[8] I went past again and saw you. Wow, the time of love came for you, so I spread my robe out over you and covered your nakedness. Then I made a promise to you and brought you into a contract and you became mine. That’s the master Yahweh’s declaration.
[Yehezkel] [16]:[9] I washed you, Yerushalem, with water, and rinsed your blood off you, and I put lotion on your skin.
[Yehezkel] [16]:[10] Then I dressed you in embroidered clothes and put leather sandals on your feet. I wrapped you in fine linen, then covered you with silk.
[Yehezkel] [16]:[11] Next I adorned you with jewellery, and I put bracelets on your hands and a chain around your neck.
[Yehezkel] [16]:[12] I put a ring in your nose and earrings in your ears, and a beautiful crown on your head.
[Yehezkel] [16]:[13] So you were adorned with gold and silver, and you were dressed in fine linen, silk, and embroidered clothes. You ate good food made from fine flour, honey, and oil, and you were very beautiful, and you became a queen.
[Yehezkel] [16]:[14] Your reputation, Yerushalem, spread among the nations because of your beauty, because it was perfect in the majesty I’d given you. That’s the master Yahweh’s declaration.
[Yehezkel] [16]:[15] But Yerushalem, you trusted in your own beauty, and you acted like a prostitute because of your reputation. You flirted with everyone going past, and prostituted yourself, so that your beauty became theirs.
[Yehezkel] [16]:[16] Then you took your clothes and made hilltop shrines for yourself with them, decorated in various colours, and there you acted like a prostitute. This shouldn’t have happened, nor should such a thing exist.
[Yehezkel] [16]:[17] You took the fine gold and silver jewellery that I gave you, and you made male sculptures for yourselves, and you behaved with them like a prostitute would.
[Yehezkel] [16]:[18] You took your embroidered garments and covered those idols, and you offered my oils and perfumes to them.
[Yehezkel] [16]:[19] The high-quality bread that I gave you (made with fine flour, oil, and honey), you placed in front of them to be a fragrant aroma, and indeed it was. That’s the master Yahweh’s declaration.
[Yehezkel] [16]:[20] Then you took your sons and daughters that you bore for me, and you sacrificed them to those idols to be devoured as food. Are your acts of prostitution a small matter?
[Yehezkel] [16]:[21] You slaughtered my children for the idols and made them pass through the fire.
[Yehezkel] [16]:[22] In all your evil goings on and your acts of prostitution, you never thought back to the days when you were young, when you were naked and bare as you thrashed about in your own blood.
[Yehezkel] [16]:[23] After all your wickedness, you won’t end well. That’s the master Yahweh’s declaration.
[Yehezkel] [16]:[24] You made yourself a mound and built a raised shrine in every public square.
[Yehezkel] [16]:[25] You built your raised platform at the top of every street and made your beauty a disgrace, and you spread your legs for anyone who passed by, and you multiplied your acts of prostitution.
[Yehezkel] [16]:[26] You’ve acted like a prostitute with your lusty neighbours the Mitsrim (Egyptians), and you committed many more acts of prostitution, provoking me to anger.
[Yehezkel] [16]:[27] Listen, I’ll hit you with my hand and cut off your food supply. I’ll hand your life over to your enemies, the daughters of the Pelishtim, who were ashamed of your obscene behaviour.
[Yehezkel] [16]:[28] You’ve acted like a prostitute with the Assyrians because you couldn’t be satisfied. You acted like a prostitute and still you weren’t satisfied.
[Yehezkel] [16]:[29] So you performed many more acts of prostitution in Bavel (Babylon) (the country of the Chaldean merchants), and even that didn’t satisfy you.
[Yehezkel] [16]:[30] Your heart is so sick that you would do things like that—things that only a shameless prostitute would do. That’s the master Yahweh’s declaration.
[Yehezkel] [16]:[31] You made your mounds at the top of every street and built your tall shrines in every public square, yet you weren’t like a prostitute, in the sense that you scoffed at taking payment.
[Yehezkel] [16]:[32] You adulterous woman, you prefer strangers over your husband.
[Yehezkel] [16]:[33] It’s normal for clients to pay the prostitute, but you do the opposite: you give your wages to all your lovers and bribe them to come to you from all around for your acts of prostitution.
[Yehezkel] [16]:[34] Yes, there’s a difference between you and other women. No one offers payment for you to act as a prostitute. You’re the very opposite—you paid them but nothing was given to you.
[Yehezkel] [16]:[35] Therefore, Yerushalem (Jerusalem), you prostitute, listen to Yahweh’s message.
[Yehezkel] [16]:[36] The master Yahweh says this: ‘Because you’ve poured out your lust and uncovered your nakedness through your acts of prostitution with your lovers and with all your detestable idols, and because you gave them your children’s blood,
[Yehezkel] [16]:[37] then listen: I’ll gather all your lovers that you’ve met, including the ones you loved and the ones you hated—I’ll gather them against you on every side. I’ll uncover your nakedness for them so they see all your nakedness.
[Yehezkel] [16]:[38] Then I’ll punish you for your adultery and the shedding of blood, and I’ll bring on you the bloodshed of my anger and passion.
[Yehezkel] [16]:[39] I’ll allow them to conquer you so they’ll tear apart your mounds and break down your tall shrines, and they’ll strip your clothes off you and take all your jewellery—leaving you naked and bare.
[Yehezkel] [16]:[40] Then they’ll bring a crowd up against you and throw heavy stones at you, and they’ll cut you apart with their swords.
[Yehezkel] [16]:[41] They’ll burn down your houses and punish you in several ways in the sight of many women, because I’ll put a stop to your prostitution, and you’ll no longer pay your lovers.
[Yehezkel] [16]:[42] Then I’ll calm my rage against you. My anger will leave you, because I’ll be satisfied and won’t be angry at you any longer.
[Yehezkel] [16]:[43] Because you didn’t call to mind your younger days, and made me shake with anger because of all those things, therefore, listen: I myself will bring the punishment for what you’ve done down onto your own head. That’s the master Yahweh’s declaration. Haven’t you added prostitution to all your other detestable practices?
[Yehezkel] [16]:[44] Listen, everyone who speaks proverbs about you will say, “Like mother, like daughter.”
[Yehezkel] [16]:[45] You are the daughter of your mother, who detested her husband and her children, and you are the sister of your sisters, who detested their husbands and their children. Your mother was a Hiti, and your father was an Amori.
[Yehezkel] [16]:[46] Your older sister was Shomron (Samaria), and her daughters were the ones living in the north, while your younger sister was the one living south of you, that is, Sedom and her daughters.
[Yehezkel] [16]:[47] Not only did you follow their customs and copy their behaviour and practices, but in everything you did, you’ve been worse than they were.
[Yehezkel] [16]:[48] This is the master Yahweh’s declaration: As I live, your sister Sedom and her daughters didn’t do as much evil as you and your daughters have done.
[Yehezkel] [16]:[49] Listen, your sister Sedom’s sin was that she was arrogant in her leisure, careless and unconcerned about anything. She didn’t assist the poor and needy people.
[Yehezkel] [16]:[50] She was arrogant and performed disgusting actions in front of me, so I took them away, just as you’ve seen.
[Yehezkel] [16]:[51] As for Shomron, they didn’t commit even half of your sins. No, you’ve done many more disgusting things than they did, and you’ve shown that your sisters were better than you, because of all the disgusting things you do.
[Yehezkel] [16]:[52] Also how you display your own shame—you’ve shown that your sisters were better than you by the sins you committed in all those disgusting ways. Your sisters now seem better than you.
[Yehezkel] [16]:[53] From their captivity, I’ll restore the fortunes of Sedom and her daughters, and of Shomron and her daughters, and your fortunes will be similar,
[Yehezkel] [16]:[54] so that you’ll display your shame. You’ll be humiliated because of everything you’ve done, and in that way you’ll be a consolation to Sedom and Shomron.
[Yehezkel] [16]:[55] Your sister Sedom and her daughters will be restored to their former condition, and Shomron and her daughters will be restored similarly. Then you and your daughters will be restored to your former condition.
[Yehezkel] [16]:[56] You never even mentioned your sister Sedom in the period when you were proud,
[Yehezkel] [16]:[57] before your wickedness was revealed. But now you’re an object of scorn to the daughters of Aram (Syria) and to all the daughters of the Pelishtim around her. People all around despise you.
[Yehezkel] [16]:[58] You’ll display your shame and your disgusting actions. That’s Yahweh’s declaration.
[Yehezkel] [16]:[59] The master Yahweh says this: ‘I’ll deal with you as you deserve—you who’ve despised your oath by breaking our agreement.
[Yehezkel] [16]:[60] But I myself will call to mind my agreement with you that was made when you were younger, and I’ll establish a never-ending agreement with you.
[Yehezkel] [16]:[61] Then you’ll call to mind your behaviour and be ashamed when you adopt your older and younger sisters. I’ll give them to you as daughters, but not because of your agreement.
[Yehezkel] [16]:[62] I myself will establish my agreement with you, and you’ll know that I am Yahweh,
[Yehezkel] [16]:[63] so that you’ll call everything to mind and be ashamed. Then you’ll no longer open your mouth to speak, because of your shame, when I’ve forgiven you for everything you’ve done. That’s the master Yahweh’s declaration.’ ”
[Yehezkel] [17]:[1] Then Yahweh gave me another message:
[Yehezkel] [17]:[2] “Son of humanity, present a riddle and tell a parable to the Israeli people.
[Yehezkel] [17]:[3] Tell them, ‘The master Yahweh says this: ‘A large eagle, with large wings full of multi-coloured feathers, and long pinions, went to Levanon and grabbed hold of the top of a cedar tree.
[Yehezkel] [17]:[4] He broke off the top shoot of the tree and took it to Kena’an (Canaan) where he placed it in a city full of merchants.
[Yehezkel] [17]:[5] He also took some of the land’s seed and planted it in fertile soil, beside a large body of water where a willow might grow.
[Yehezkel] [17]:[6] Then the seed sprouted and became a spreading vine low to the ground. Its branches turned toward him, and its roots grew down below, so it became a vine and produced branches and sent out shoots.
[Yehezkel] [17]:[7] But there was another large eagle with large wings and many feathers. Oh wow, that vine turned its roots toward this eagle, and it spread out its branches toward the eagle from the place it had been planted so it might get watered.
[Yehezkel] [17]:[8] It had been planted in good soil beside a large body of water so it would grow branches and produce fruit, to become a magnificent vine.’
[Yehezkel] [17]:[9] Ask the people: ‘The master Yahweh wants to know if it’ll prosper. Won’t it be uprooted and stripped of its fruit so that it withers, and all its fresh growth will dry out? You wouldn’t have to be very strong or get lots of people to help to pull it out by its roots.
[Yehezkel] [17]:[10] So listen. After it had been planted, would it thrive? Wouldn’t it wither up when the eastern wind touches it? Yes, it would wither right up in the garden plot where it sprouted.’ ”
[Yehezkel] [17]:[11] Then Yahweh gave me another message:
[Yehezkel] [17]:[12] “Ask those rebellious people, ‘Don’t you know what those things mean? Listen, the king of Bavel (Babylon) came to Yerushalem (Jerusalem) and captured its king and its princes and took them with him to Bavel.
[Yehezkel] [17]:[13] Then he took a member of the royal family, made an agreement with him—forcing him to make various commitments. Then he took away the country’s former powerful people,
[Yehezkel] [17]:[14] so the kingdom would remain subjected and not be able to become powerful again. However, by keeping the agreement, the country would at least survive.
[Yehezkel] [17]:[15] But the king of Yerushalem rebelled against him by sending his ambassadors to Mitsrayim (Egypt) to acquire horses and an army. Will he succeed? Will the one doing these things escape? If he breaks the agreement, will he survive?
[Yehezkel] [17]:[16] This is the master Yahweh’s declaration: As I live, he’ll definitely die in the land of the king who made him king, the king whose promises he despised, and whose agreement he broke. He’ll die in the middle of Bavel.
[Yehezkel] [17]:[17] Mitsrayim’s Par’oh (Pharaoh) with his mighty army and huge horde won’t help him in battle, when ramps are constructed and siege walls are built up to cut off many lives,
[Yehezkel] [17]:[18] because the king despised his promise by breaking the agreement. Wow, he reached out to make a promise, and yet afterwards he did all those things. He won’t escape.
[Yehezkel] [17]:[19] Therefore the master Yahweh says this: ‘As I live, wasn’t it my promise that he despised and my agreement that he broke? Therefore I’ll cause him to be punished for what he did.
[Yehezkel] [17]:[20] I’ll spread my net out over him, and he’ll be caught in my trap, and I’ll take him to Bavel and handle his judgement there for the treason he committed when he betrayed me.
[Yehezkel] [17]:[21] All of his refugees in his armies will be killed by the sword, and the ones who remain will be scattered in every direction. Then you people will know that I am Yahweh, because I’ve declared that that will happen.”
[Yehezkel] [17]:[22] The master Yahweh says this, ‘So I myself will take away the highest part of the cedar tree, and I’ll plant it away from its tender branches. I’ll break it off, and I myself will plant it on a very high mountain.
[Yehezkel] [17]:[23] I’ll plant it on Yisrael’s (Israel) highest mountain so it’ll grow branches and produce fruit, and it’ll become a majestic cedar so that every winged bird will live under it. They’ll nest in the shade of its branches,
[Yehezkel] [17]:[24] then all the trees in the countryside will know that I am Yahweh. I bring down the high trees and I raise up the low trees. I wither the watered tree and I cause the wilted tree to bloom. I am Yahweh. I’ve declared that that will happen, and I will do it.’ ”
[Yehezkel] [18]:[1] Then Yahweh gave me another message:
[Yehezkel] [18]:[2] “What do you mean, you people who use this proverb about Yisrael (Israel)? You say, ‘Fathers eat sour grapes, but it’s the children’s teeth that are set on edge’.
[Yehezkel] [18]:[3] This is the master Yahweh’s declaration: as I live, there’ll certainly no longer be any occasion for you to use this proverb in Yisrael.
[Yehezkel] [18]:[4] Listen, every life belongs to me: the father’s life as well as the son’s—they belong to me. The one who disobeys is the one who’ll die.
[Yehezkel] [18]:[5] If there’s a godly man who does what’s fair and right,
[Yehezkel] [18]:[6] who doesn’t eat at the hilltop shrines, who doesn’t request help from Yisrael’s (Israel) idols, who doesn’t mess with someone else’s wife or a menstruating woman,
[Yehezkel] [18]:[7] who doesn’t oppress anyone, who gives back to debtors what they put up as security for loans, who doesn’t steal but rather gives his food to the hungry and gives clothes to those without them,
[Yehezkel] [18]:[8] who doesn’t charge too much interest if he lends money, and doesn’t take too much profit for what he sells, who promotes true justice within the community,
[Yehezkel] [18]:[9] who follows my instructions and faithfully obeys my regulations, that man will be acquitted and will definitely live. That’s the master Yahweh’s declaration.
[Yehezkel] [18]:[10] But suppose that godly man has a violent son who kills and sadly goes against all those things above,
[Yehezkel] [18]:[11] not following the example of his godly father, but rather who’s eaten at the hilltop shrines and slept with someone else’s wife,
[Yehezkel] [18]:[12] who oppresses the poor and needy, who steals and robs, who doesn’t return something given as a pledge, who requests help from idols and does disgusting things,
[Yehezkel] [18]:[13] who lends out money at too high interest, and who makes too much profit on what he sells. Should that man live? He certainly won’t! He’ll definitely die, and his blood will be on his own head.
[Yehezkel] [18]:[14] But listen, suppose he has a son, and his son sees all the sins that his father’s committed, and though he sees them, he doesn’t do those things.
[Yehezkel] [18]:[15] He hasn’t eaten at the hilltop shrines, and hasn’t requested help from the Israeli people’s idols, and hasn’t slept with someone else’s wife,
[Yehezkel] [18]:[16] he doesn’t oppress anyone, or keep things given as a pledge, or accept stolen things, but instead gives his food to the hungry and gives clothes to those without them,
[Yehezkel] [18]:[17] he’s turned his back on crime, and doesn’t charge high interest, he follows my instructions and obeys my regulations—he won’t die for his father’s evil actions, but he’ll certainly live.
[Yehezkel] [18]:[18] His father, since he oppressed others by extortion and robbed people, and did evil things among his people—listen, he’ll die in his sin.
[Yehezkel] [18]:[19] But you people ask, ‘Why doesn’t the son also have to pay the cost for his family’s crimes?’ Well it’s because the son promotes justice and godliness and follows all my instructions. He’ll definitely live.
[Yehezkel] [18]:[20] The one who sins is the one who’ll die. The children won’t have to be responsible for their parents’ sin, and the parents won’t be responsible for their children’s sins—the righteousness of those who act rightly will be on themselves, and the wickedness of the wicked will be on themselves.
[Yehezkel] [18]:[21] But if the wicked person turns away from all their disobedience, and follows all my instructions and does what’s right and fair, then that person will certainly live and not die.
[Yehezkel] [18]:[22] All their acts of disobedience won’t be called to mind against them. They’ll live by the right things they do.
[Yehezkel] [18]:[23] That’s the master Yahweh’s declaration. Do I celebrate happily about the death of wicked people, and not about them turning away from their evil behaviour so that they can live?
[Yehezkel] [18]:[24] But if a righteous person turns away from their righteousness, and disobeys and does disgusting things like the wicked people do, then will they live? All the good things that had been done won’t be called to mind when they betray me in their treason, so they’ll die in the sins that they committed.
[Yehezkel] [18]:[25] But you people complain that the master’s way isn’t correct. Please listen, you Israeli people: is it my ways that aren’t correct, or is it your ways?
[Yehezkel] [18]:[26] When the righteous person turns away from their righteousness, and commits injustice and dies because of it, then that person will die in the injustice that they’ve done.
[Yehezkel] [18]:[27] But when a wicked person turns away from the wicked things they’ve done and does what’s fair and what’s right, then that person will preserve their life—
[Yehezkel] [18]:[28] they’ve become aware of all their disobedient behaviours and turned away from them. That person certainly won’t die, but will live.
[Yehezkel] [18]:[29] But the Israeli people insist, ‘The master’s way isn’t fair!’ How is my way not fair, you Israeli people? It’s your ways that aren’t fair.
[Yehezkel] [18]:[30] Therefore I’ll judge each person among you according to their ways, you Israeli people. That’s the master Yahweh’s declaration. Change your direction and turn away from all your disobedient behaviours so that they won’t be stumbling blocks of evil for you.
[Yehezkel] [18]:[31] Throw off all the disobedient things you people have done. Work towards a new heart and a new spirit for yourselves. Why should you die, you Israeli people?
[Yehezkel] [18]:[32] I take no pleasure in the death of someone who dies. That’s the master Yahweh’s declaration, so turn away from your evil behaviour and live.
[Yehezkel] [19]:[1] Now sing a mournful song for Yisrael’s (Israel) leaders,
[Yehezkel] [19]:[2] saying: ‘Who was your mother? A lioness—she lived with a lion’s son. There among the young lions, she reared her cubs.
[Yehezkel] [19]:[3] She’s the one who raised one of her cubs to become a young lion— a lion who learned to tear apart his victims, and then he devoured people.
[Yehezkel] [19]:[4] Then the nations heard about him. He got caught in their trap, and they took him to Mitsrayim (Egypt) with hooks.
