[Yehezkel] [23]:[35] So the master Yahweh says this, ‘Because you’ve forgotten me and thrown me away behind your back, you’ll bear the consequences of your shameful behaviour and your prostitution.’ ”
[Yehezkel] [23]:[36] Yahweh said to me, “Son of humanity, will you judge Oholah and Oholivah? Present them a list of their disgusting actions,
[Yehezkel] [23]:[37] since they’ve committed adultery, and also have blood on their hands. They’ve committed adultery by worshipping their idols, and they’ve even caused their sons to pass through the fire to be considered as food for their idols.
[Yehezkel] [23]:[38] Then on top of that, they defile my sanctuary, and at the same time, they disrespect my rest days.
[Yehezkel] [23]:[39] When they’d slaughtered their children for their idols, then they came to my sanctuary on the same day to desecrate it. So listen, that’s what they’ve done right there in my residence.
[Yehezkel] [23]:[40] You sent messengers to go and bring men from far away. Now look, they indeed came—those who you prepared for by bathing, painting your eyes, and adorning yourself with jewellery.
[Yehezkel] [23]:[41] You sat on a lovely couch bed with a table arranged in front of you where you placed my incense and my olive oil.
[Yehezkel] [23]:[42] Then the sound of a noisy crowd was around her as all kinds of men, even Sava, were brought in from the wilderness, and they put bracelets on their hands and beautiful crowns on their heads.
[Yehezkel] [23]:[43] Then I said about that experienced adulterer, ‘Now they’ll treat her as a prostitute, and she’ll fornicate with them.’
[Yehezkel] [23]:[44] They had sex with her like men do with a prostitute. In that way they had sex with the two immoral women, Oholah and Oholivah.
[Yehezkel] [23]:[45] But righteous men will judge and punish them as adulteresses, and they’ll punish them with the appropriate sentence for those who’ve shed blood, because they’re adulteresses plus they have blood on their hands.
[Yehezkel] [23]:[46] So the master Yahweh says this: I’ll bring a group to attack Shomron (Samaria) and Yerushalem (Jerusalem) and give them up to be terrorized and plundered.
[Yehezkel] [23]:[47] Then that group will stone them with stones and cut them down with their swords. They’ll kill their children and burn down their houses.
[Yehezkel] [23]:[48] That’s how I’ll remove shameful behaviour from the land, and discipline all the women so they’ll no longer act like prostitutes.
[Yehezkel] [23]:[49] They’ll use your shameful behaviour against you. You’ll all bear the guilt of the sins you did with your idols, and in that way you’ll know that I am the master Yahweh.”
[Yehezkel] [24]:[1] Then Yahweh gave me another message on the 15th of January of the ninth year since King Yehoyakin had been taken captive.
[Yehezkel] [24]:[2] “Son of humanity, write down the day and month for yourself, because on this exact day, the Babylonian king started his siege of Yerushalem (Jerusalem).
[Yehezkel] [24]:[3] So tell this parable to the rebellious Israeli people and explain that it comes from the master Yahweh: Pour water into the cooking pot and place it on the fire.
[Yehezkel] [24]:[4] Put in the leg and shoulder of a good sheep, then fill it up with the best bones.
[Yehezkel] [24]:[5] Yes, take the best one from the flock and pile up the fuel underneath it— keeping it boiling to make sure the bones in it cook well.
[Yehezkel] [24]:[6] Now the master Yahweh says this: The city of blood won’t end well—it’s like a cooking pot that has rust in it, and that rust won’t come out of it. Take piece after piece out of it, but don’t be choosy about which pieces,
[Yehezkel] [24]:[7] because the blood the city shed is all the way through its centre. It displayed the blood on a flat rock to be easily seen, rather than pouring it out on the ground where it could be covered over with dust,
[Yehezkel] [24]:[8] so it makes me angry enough to get revenge: I placed the city’s blood on the smooth rock, so it couldn’t be covered.
[Yehezkel] [24]:[9] Therefore, the master Yahweh says this: The city of blood won’t end well. I’ll also enlarge the pile of firewood to put underneath it.
[Yehezkel] [24]:[10] Stack up the wood and kindle the fire. Cook the meat well and mix in the spices and let the bones be charred.
[Yehezkel] [24]:[11] Then put the empty pot onto the hot coals in order to heat and scorch its bronze, so the impurities in it will be melted—its corrosion eaten away.’
[Yehezkel] [24]:[12] That was a lot of work, but the fire didn’t remove the corrosion from it.
[Yehezkel] [24]:[13] Your shameful behaviour is in your uncleanness. Because you wouldn’t accept it when I tried to cleanse you, you won’t be purified anymore until I’ve satisfied my fury against you.
[Yehezkel] [24]:[14] I, Yahweh, have declared it, and I will do it. I won’t relent, nor will I rest from it. You’ll be judged by your own practices and your own behaviour. That’s the master Yahweh’s declaration.”
[Yehezkel] [24]:[15] Then Yahweh gave me another message:
[Yehezkel] [24]:[16] “Listen, son of humanity, I’m taking your cherished wife from you with a deadly disease, but you mustn’t mourn or weep, or let any tears show.
[Yehezkel] [24]:[17] You must groan silently. Don’t organise a funeral when she’s dead. Put on your turban and your sandals, but don’t veil your beard, or eat the bread of men who mourn who’ve lost their wives.”
[Yehezkel] [24]:[18] So I spoke to the people in the morning, and then my wife died in the evening. In the morning I did what I’d been commanded to do.
[Yehezkel] [24]:[19] Then the people asked me, “Won’t you tell us what these things mean—the way that you’re behaving?”
[Yehezkel] [24]:[20] “Yahweh gave me a message,” I answered them,
[Yehezkel] [24]:[21] “to tell the Israeli people that the master Yahweh says this to them: Listen, I’ll desecrate my sanctuary—the pride of your power, the delight of your eyes, and the yearning of your soul—and also your sons and daughters who you left behind there in Yerushalem (Jerusalem) will be killed by the sword.
[Yehezkel] [24]:[22] When that happens, you people will do exactly as I’ve done: you won’t veil your beards, or eat the bread of mourning men,
[Yehezkel] [24]:[23] but instead your turbans will be on your heads, and your sandals on your feet. You won’t mourn or weep, because you’ll melt away due to your disobedience, and everyone will groan for their relatives.
[Yehezkel] [24]:[24] So Yehezkel (Ezekiel) will be a sign for you, because when that time comes, you’ll do exactly the same as he’s doing. Then you people will know that I am the master Yahweh.’ ”
[Yehezkel] [24]:[25] “But you, son of humanity, on the day that I capture their temple, (which is their joy, their pride, and what they see and desire), and when I take away their sons and daughters,
[Yehezkel] [24]:[26] a refugee will come to you here on that day to give you the news.
[Yehezkel] [24]:[27] At that time, your mouth will be opened up to that refugee and you’ll speak again—you’ll no longer be silent. You’ll be a sign for them so that they’ll know that I am Yahweh.”
[Yehezkel] [25]:[1] Then Yahweh gave me another message:
[Yehezkel] [25]:[2] “Son of humanity, keep looking towards the Amonim and prophesy against them.
[Yehezkel] [25]:[3] Tell them to listen to this message because this is what the master Yahweh says: You celebrated my sanctuary being desecrated, and the land of Yisrael (Israel) being desolate, and the kingdom of Yehudah (Judah) going into exile,
[Yehezkel] [25]:[4] so because of that, listen: I’m giving you to a people in the east as their possession. They’ll set up camp against you and set up their tents among you. They’ll eat your fruit and drink your milk.
[Yehezkel] [25]:[5] I’ll make the Amoni capital city, Rabah, into a camel pasture, and the Amoni people into a resting place for flocks. Then you people will know that I am Yahweh.
[Yehezkel] [25]:[6] Because the master Yahweh says this: You clapped your hands and stamped your feet and celebrated with all the contempt within you against the Israeli nation,
[Yehezkel] [25]:[7] therefore, listen Amon. I’ll strike you down and give you as plunder to the other nations. I’ll cut you off from the people groups and make you perish from among the countries. I’ll destroy you, and you’ll know that I am Yahweh.’
[Yehezkel] [25]:[8] The master Yahweh says this, ‘Because Moav (Moab) and Se’ir say that the kingdom of Yehudah (Judah) is just like every other nation,
[Yehezkel] [25]:[9] well listen, I’ll destroy the border cities protecting Moav, starting with the splendour of Beyt-Hayeshimot, Ba’al-Me’on, and Kiryatayim.
[Yehezkel] [25]:[10] I’ll hand them over to the people in the east who’ve already been against the Amonim—I’ll give them up as a possession so that the Amonim won’t be remembered among the nations.
[Yehezkel] [25]:[11] Yes, I’ll execute judgements against Moav, then they’ll know that I am Yahweh.’
[Yehezkel] [25]:[12] The master Yahweh also says, ‘Edom has taken vengeance against the kingdom of Yehudah (Judah) and has done wrong by doing that.
[Yehezkel] [25]:[13] Therefore, the master Yahweh says: I’ll hit Edom with my hand and destroy every person and animal there. I’ll make it a ruined, abandoned place, from Teyman all the way to Dedan—they’ll be killed by the sword.
[Yehezkel] [25]:[14] I’ll use my people Yisrael (Israel) to place my vengeance on Edom, and they’ll apply my anger and fury to Edom so they’ll know my vengeance. That’s the master Yahweh’s declaration.’
[Yehezkel] [25]:[15] The master Yahweh says this, ‘The Pelishtim have chosen hateful vengeance and have put much effort into trying to destroy Yehudah (Judah).
[Yehezkel] [25]:[16] So this is what the master Yahweh says: Listen, I’ll take action against the Pelishtim, and I’ll cut off the Kereti and destroy the remnant along the coast.
[Yehezkel] [25]:[17] I’ll take severe vengeance against them with furious acts to punish them—they’ll know that I am Yahweh, when I take my vengeance on them.’ ”
[Yehezkel] [26]:[1] At the beginning of the month in the eleventh year since King Yehoyakin had been taken captive, Yahweh gave me a message:
[Yehezkel] [26]:[2] “Son of humanity, Tsor (Tyre) has said against Yerushalem (Jerusalem), ‘Nice one! Yerushalem’s gates are broken. It’s going my way—I can take advantage because it’s been destroyed.’
[Yehezkel] [26]:[3] Because of that, the master Yahweh says this: ‘Listen, I’m opposed to you, Tsor, and I’ll raise up many nations against you, just like the sea raises its waves.
[Yehezkel] [26]:[4] They’ll destroy Tsor’s walls and tear down its towers, then I’ll sweep its dust away and make it like a bare rock.
[Yehezkel] [26]:[5] It’ll become a place in the middle of the sea for people to spread their nets out to dry them, since I’ve declared it, and it’ll become plunder for the nations. That’s the master Yahweh’s declaration.
[Yehezkel] [26]:[6] Its young women who are in the countryside will be slaughtered by swords, and then they’ll know that I am Yahweh.’
[Yehezkel] [26]:[7] Yes, this is what Yahweh says: Listen, I’m bringing the Babylonian King Nevukadnetsar (Nebuchadnezzar), king of kings, from the north, against Tsor, with horses and chariots, and with horsemen and a large army.
[Yehezkel] [26]:[8] He’ll kill your daughters in the countryside. He’ll set up a siege program and build a ramp against your walls and lift up shields against you.
[Yehezkel] [26]:[9] He’ll use his battering rams to smash down your walls, and he’ll tear down your towers with his axes.
[Yehezkel] [26]:[10] They’ll have so many horses that their dust will cover you. Your walls will shake with the noise of their horsemen, wagons, and chariots. When he rides through your gates, he’ll pick his way over the stones like men do when entering a city whose walls have been broken down.
[Yehezkel] [26]:[11] The hooves of his horses will trample all of your streets. He’ll slaughter your people with the sword and your mighty stone pillars will be knocked to the ground.
[Yehezkel] [26]:[12] They’ll tear down your walls and destroy your nice homes—plundering your riches and looting your merchandise. Then they’ll throw your building stones, wood, and rubble into the ocean.
[Yehezkel] [26]:[13] I’ll stop the sound of your songs, and the music from your harps won’t be heard anymore.
[Yehezkel] [26]:[14] I’ll make you back into a bare rock—you’ll become a place where nets are spread out to dry. You’ll never be built again, because I, master Yahweh, have spoken. That’s the master Yahweh’s declaration.
[Yehezkel] [26]:[15] The master Yahweh says this to Tsor (Tyre), ‘Won’t the islands shake with the sound of your downfall, and with the groans of the wounded when the terrible slaughter is happening in you?
[Yehezkel] [26]:[16] Then all the leaders of the coastal kingdoms will step down from their thrones and remove their robes and take off their embroidered clothes. Instead, they’ll clothe themselves in fear, they’ll sit on the ground and tremble every moment, and they’ll be appalled because of you.
[Yehezkel] [26]:[17] Then they’ll sing this song of mourning for you and say to you, How you, who were inhabited by sailors, have been destroyed. The famous city that was so strong, it’s now gone from the sea. The ones living in her once spread terror around themselves on everyone who lived nearby.
[Yehezkel] [26]:[18] Now the coastal kingdoms tremble on the day of your downfall. The islands in the sea are terrified by your passing.’
[Yehezkel] [26]:[19] Yes, the master Yahweh says this: When I make you a desolate city, like the other cities that are uninhabited, when I raise up the deep seas against you, and when the great waters cover you,
[Yehezkel] [26]:[20] then I’ll take you down to the pit that ancient people went down to, because I’ll make you live in the lowest realms of the earth like ancient ruins. Because of that, you won’t come back and be splendid in the land of the living.
[Yehezkel] [26]:[21] I’ll send disaster onto you, and you won’t exist anymore. Then people will look for you, but you’ll never be found again. That’s the master Yahweh’s declaration.”
[Yehezkel] [27]:[1] Then Yahweh gave me another message:
[Yehezkel] [27]:[2] “Now you, son of humanity, begin a funeral song about Tsor (Tyre),
[Yehezkel] [27]:[3] and tell Tsor (which is on a coastal island—merchants to people groups on many other islands) that the master Yahweh says this to you: Tsor, you’ve said, ‘My beauty has reached perfection.’
[Yehezkel] [27]:[4] Your borders are surrounded by the ocean. Your builders have perfected your beauty.
[Yehezkel] [27]:[5] They made all your planks with cypress from Mt. Hermon (Senir). They got a cedar from Levanon to make a mast for you.
[Yehezkel] [27]:[6] They made your oars from the oak trees in Bashan. They made your decks out of cypress wood from Kupros (Cyprus), and overlaid them with ivory.
[Yehezkel] [27]:[7] Your sails were made from colourful linen from Mitsrayim (Egypt) that served as your banner. The colours of blue and purple from the coasts of Elishah are used for the awning on your boat.
[Yehezkel] [27]:[8] Those who were living in Tsidon (Sidon) and Arvad were your rowers. The wise men of Tsor (Tyre) were within you—they were your pilots.
[Yehezkel] [27]:[9] Experienced craftsmen from Geval sealed your seams. All the ships and their sailors among you were carrying your merchandise for trade.
[Yehezkel] [27]:[10] Warriors from Paras (Persia), Ludia, and Libya were in your army. They hung their shields and helmets within you. They displayed your splendour.
[Yehezkel] [27]:[11] The men of Arvad and Helek in your army were on your walls surrounding you, and the people from Gamadim were in your towers. They hung up their shields on your walls all around you. They completed your beauty.
[Yehezkel] [27]:[12] “Tarshish was a trading partner with you because of your abundant wealth of goods. They traded silver, iron, tin, and lead for your wares.
[Yehezkel] [27]:[13] Yavan (Greece), Tuval, and Meshek traded slaves, as well as bronze items, for your merchandise.
[Yehezkel] [27]:[14] Beyt-Togarmah provided horses, stallions, and mules in exchange for your products.
[Yehezkel] [27]:[15] People from Dedan were your traders on many coasts. You sent the merchandise and they sent back ivory tusks and ebony wood as payment.
[Yehezkel] [27]:[16] Aram (Syria) was a dealer in your many products—they provided emeralds, purple dye, coloured cloth, fine fabric, pearls, and rubies for your merchandise.
[Yehezkel] [27]:[17] Yehudah (Judah) and Yisrael (Israel) were trading with you. They provided wheat from Minit, cakes, honey, oil, and balsam for your merchandise.
[Yehezkel] [27]:[18] Damesek (Damascus) was a trader of all your products, of all your enormous wealth, and of the wine from Helbon and the wool from Tsahar.
[Yehezkel] [27]:[19] Dan and Yavan from Uzal provided you with merchandise of wrought iron, cinnamon, and fragrant calamus seeds which became your merchandise.
[Yehezkel] [27]:[20] Dedan was your dealer in woven saddle blankets.
[Yehezkel] [27]:[21] Arav and all of Kedar’s leaders were traders with you—they provided you with lambs, rams, and goats.
[Yehezkel] [27]:[22] Traders from Sheva and Ramah came to sell you the best of every spice and all kinds of precious gems—they traded gold for your goods.
[Yehezkel] [27]:[23] Haran, Kaneh, and Eden were traders with you, along with Sheva, Ashur (Assyria), and Kilmad.
[Yehezkel] [27]:[24] Those were your traders in fancy robes made of violet cloth with woven colours, and in blankets of multicoloured, embroidered, and well-woven cloth in your marketplaces.
[Yehezkel] [27]:[25] Tarshish’s ships were the transporters of your merchandise. So you were filled up—heavily laden with cargo there in the heart of the seas.
[Yehezkel] [27]:[26] Your rowers have brought you into vast seas. The east wind has wrecked you in the middle of them.
[Yehezkel] [27]:[27] Your wealth, merchandise, and trade goods, your sailors, pilots, and ship-builders, your traders of merchandise and all the men of war who are in you, and all your crew— they will sink into the depths of the sea at the time of your destruction.
[Yehezkel] [27]:[28] The surroundings will shake when they hear your pilot’s cry of distress.
[Yehezkel] [27]:[29] All the oarsmen will come down off their ships. Mariners and all the pilots on the sea will stand on the land,
[Yehezkel] [27]:[30] then they’ll raise their voices towards you and will wail bitterly. They’ll throw dust up onto their heads. They’ll roll around to get covered in ashes.
[Yehezkel] [27]:[31] They’ll shave their heads bald for you and dress in rough sackcloth, and they’ll weep bitterly over you and they will cry out with loud moans.
[Yehezkel] [27]:[32] They will wail loudly for you and sing funeral songs about you. Who is like the city of Tsor (Tyre), which has now been brought to silence in the middle of the sea?
[Yehezkel] [27]:[33] When your merchandise went ashore from the sea, it pleased many people groups. You enriched kings across the world with your great wealth and merchandise.
[Yehezkel] [27]:[34] But when you were shattered by the seas, by deep waters, your merchandise and all your crew sank.
[Yehezkel] [27]:[35] All the inhabitants of the coastal kingdoms were appalled at you, and their kings shuddered in horror—their faces trembled.
[Yehezkel] [27]:[36] The merchants of the people hiss at you. You’ve become a horror, and you won’t exist anymore.”
[Yehezkel] [28]:[1] Then Yahweh gave me another message:
[Yehezkel] [28]:[2] “Son of humanity, tell Tsor’s (Tyre) ruler that the master Yahweh says this: Your heart is proud and you’ve said, “I’m a god. I’ll sit in the seat of gods in the vital centre of the oceans.” Even though you’re a man and not a god, you tell yourself that you’re a god.
[Yehezkel] [28]:[3] Listen, you king of Tsor, are you wiser than Daniyel was? Are there any secrets that you don’t already know?
[Yehezkel] [28]:[4] You’ve used your wisdom and skill to make yourself wealthy, and amassed gold and silver in your treasuries.
[Yehezkel] [28]:[5] By great wisdom and by your trading, you’ve multiplied your wealth, but now you’ve become arrogant because of your wealth.
[Yehezkel] [28]:[6] Therefore, the master Yahweh says this: Because you’ve convinced yourself that you’re invincible like a god,
[Yehezkel] [28]:[7] I’ll bring foreigners against you—terrifying warriors from other nations. They’ll bring their swords against the beauty of your wisdom, and they’ll defile your splendour.
[Yehezkel] [28]:[8] They’ll send you down to the pit, and you’ll die violently like those who die at sea.
[Yehezkel] [28]:[9] Will you really say, “I’m a god” to the face of one who’s about to kill you? You’re a man and not God, and you’ll be at the mercy of the one who runs you through.
[Yehezkel] [28]:[10] You’ll die like an ungodly person killed by foreigners, because I’ve declared it. That’s the master Yahweh’s declaration.’ ”
[Yehezkel] [28]:[11] Then Yahweh gave me another message:
[Yehezkel] [28]:[12] “Son of humanity, sing a mourning song for the king of Tsor (Tyre) and tell him that the master Yahweh says this: You were the model of perfection, full of wisdom and perfect in beauty.
[Yehezkel] [28]:[13] You were in Eden—God’s garden. Every precious stone covered you: ruby, topaz, emerald, chrysolite, onyx, jasper, sapphire, turquoise, and beryl. Your settings and mountings were made from gold. They were prepared on the very day that you were created.
[Yehezkel] [28]:[14] I placed you on God’s sacred mountain like the winged creatures that I appointed to guard humanity. You were among the fiery stones where you walked around.
[Yehezkel] [28]:[15] You had integrity in your ways from the day you were created until injustice was found within you.
[Yehezkel] [28]:[16] Through your great trade you were filled with violence, and so you sinned. Then I threw you out of God’s mountain, like someone who was defiled, and I destroyed you, guardian winged creature, and drove you from among the fiery stones.
[Yehezkel] [28]:[17] Your heart was arrogant due to your beauty. You ruined your wisdom because of your splendour. I threw you down to the earth. I put you in front of kings so they can see you.
[Yehezkel] [28]:[18] Because of all your disobedience and your dishonest trade, you’ve defiled your sacred places, so I’ve made fire come out from you to consume you. I’ll turn you into ashes on the earth in the sight of everyone who looks at you.
[Yehezkel] [28]:[19] Everyone who knew you among the people groups will shudder to look at you now— they will be horrified, and you won’t exist any longer.’ ”
[Yehezkel] [28]:[20] Then Yahweh gave me another message:
[Yehezkel] [28]:[21] “Son of humanity, look towards Tsidon (Sidon) and prophesy against it.
[Yehezkel] [28]:[22] Tell them that the master Yahweh says this: ‘Listen, I’m against you, Tsidon, because I intend to be praised by you, so your people will know that I am Yahweh, when I execute justice within you and demonstrate my holiness to you.
[Yehezkel] [28]:[23] I’ll send a deadly disease to afflict you, and there’ll be blood in your streets, and people will fall dead all around you. When the sword comes against you from all around, then you’ll know that I am Yahweh.
[Yehezkel] [28]:[24] Then there’ll no longer be pricking briars and painful thorns for the Israeli people from all those around her who despise her, so then they’ll know that I am the master Yahweh.’
[Yehezkel] [28]:[25] The master Yahweh says that when I gather the Jewish people from the nations that they were scattered among, and when they properly honour me so the nations may see, then they’ll make their homes in the land I gave to my servant Ya’akov (Jacob).
[Yehezkel] [28]:[26] Then they’ll live securely within the land and build houses, plant vineyards, and live securely. When I execute justice on all the people all around who now despise them, then they’ll know that I am their god Yahweh.’ ”
[Yehezkel] [29]:[1] At the beginning of January in the twelfth year since King Yehoyakin had been taken captive, Yahweh gave me a message:
[Yehezkel] [29]:[2] “Son of humanity, stand firmly against Mitsrayim’s (Egypt) king Par’oh (Pharaoh). Prophesy against him and against all of Mitsrayim,
[Yehezkel] [29]:[3] telling them that the master Yahweh says this: Listen, I’m against you, Par’oh, king of Mitsrayim—you, the great sea monster that lurks in the middle of the river, who says, “My river is my own. I’ve made it for myself.”
[Yehezkel] [29]:[4] I’ll put hooks into your jaw, and the fish from your streams will cling to the scales on your side. I’ll lift you up from the middle of your river, along with all the river’s fish that cling to your scales.
[Yehezkel] [29]:[5] I’ll fling you into the wilderness—you and all the fish from your river. You’ll fall on the open countryside—your corpse won’t be taken or moved, but rather I’ll give you as food to the birds and wild animals.
[Yehezkel] [29]:[6] Then all of Mitsrayim’s inhabitants will know that I am Yahweh, because they’ve been like a brittle reed to the kingdom of Yisrael (Israel).
[Yehezkel] [29]:[7] When Yisrael grabbed you, you broke and tore open their shoulder, and when they leaned on you, you broke and made their legs unsteady.
[Yehezkel] [29]:[8] Therefore the master Yahweh says this: Listen, I’ll send an army against you that will cut short both people’s and animals’ lives,
[Yehezkel] [29]:[9] and Mitsrayim will become a desolate ruin. Then they’ll know that I am Yahweh. Because the sea monster said, “The river is mine, because I made it,”
[Yehezkel] [29]:[10] listen: I’m against you and against your river, so I’ll give Mitsrayim over to desolation and waste, and you’ll become a wasteland from the Migdol to Seveneh and the borders of Kush (Ethiopia).
[Yehezkel] [29]:[11] No person or domestic animal will pass through it, and it won’t be inhabited for forty years.
[Yehezkel] [29]:[12] I’ll make Mitsrayim a desolation in the middle of uninhabited lands, and its cities will become a desolation in the middle of wasted cities for forty years, then I’ll scatter the Mitsri (Egyptian) people among the nations, and I’ll disperse them through the lands.
[Yehezkel] [29]:[13] But the master Yahweh says this: At the end of forty years I’ll gather Mitsrayim from the people groups they were scattered among,
[Yehezkel] [29]:[14] and I’ll restore Mitsrayim’s fortunes and bring them back to the region of Patros, to their native land. Then they’ll become an insignificant kingdom there.
[Yehezkel] [29]:[15] It’ll be the least significant kingdom, and it won’t become prominent again among the nations. I’ll diminish them so that they’ll no longer dominate other nations.
[Yehezkel] [29]:[16] Requesting help from Mitsrayim will no longer be a reason for the kingdom of Yisrael (Israel) to be confident, instead, Mitsrayim will be a reminder of Yisrael’s disobedience when they turned to Mitsrayim for help. Then they’ll know that I am the master Yahweh.”
[Yehezkel] [29]:[17] At the beginning of May in the 27th year since King Yehoyakin had been taken captive, Yahweh gave me a message:
[Yehezkel] [29]:[18] “Son of humanity, the Babylonian King Nevukadnetsar (Nebuchadnezzar) stationed his army to do hard work against the fortified island city of Tsor (Tyre). Every head was rubbed until it was made bald, and every shoulder was made raw. Yet he and his army received no payment from Tsor for the hard work that he carried out against it,
[Yehezkel] [29]:[19] therefore the master Yahweh says this, ‘Listen, I’m giving Mitsrayim (Egypt) to the Babylonian King Nevukadnetsar and he’ll take away its wealth, plunder its possessions, and carry off everything he finds there—that will be his army’s wages.
[Yehezkel] [29]:[20] I’ve given him the land of Mitsrayim as the wages for the work they did for me. That’s the master Yahweh’s declaration.
[Yehezkel] [29]:[21] On that day I’ll make power sprout up for the kingdom of Yisrael (Israel), and I’ll put you among them to speak out so they’ll know that I am Yahweh.’ ”
[Yehezkel] [30]:[1] Then Yahweh gave me another message:
[Yehezkel] [30]:[2] “Son of humanity, prophesy and say that the master Yahweh says this: ‘Wail now because the coming days won’t go well.
[Yehezkel] [30]:[3] The day is near—the day is near for Yahweh. It’ll be a day of clouds—a time of doom for nations.
[Yehezkel] [30]:[4] Then an army will come against Mitsrayim (Egypt), and there’ll be anguish in Kush (Ethiopia) when the people are killed in Mitsrayim— when they take its wealth, and when its foundations get torn apart.
[Yehezkel] [30]:[5] Kush and Put, Ludia, all Arav, and Libya, together with the people belonging to the agreement—they’ll all be killed by the sword.
[Yehezkel] [30]:[6] Yahweh says this: The ones who support Mitsrayim militarily will fall, and the pride of Mitsrayim’s strength will collapse. From Migdol to Seveneh their combined warriors will be killed by the sword. That’s the master Yahweh’s declaration.
[Yehezkel] [30]:[7] Those allies will be appalled there among the abandoned lands, and their cities will be among all the other ruined cities.
[Yehezkel] [30]:[8] Then they’ll know that I am Yahweh, when I set fire to Mitsrayim, and when all its helpers are destroyed.
[Yehezkel] [30]:[9] At that time, messengers will go out from in front of me in ships to terrorise Kush when they think they’re secure, and there’ll be anguish among them on the day of Mitsrayim’s doom. Yes, take notice, it’s coming.
[Yehezkel] [30]:[10] The master Yahweh says this: I’ll use the Babylonian King Nevukadnetsar (Nebuchadnezzar) to bring Mitsrayim’s multitudes to an end.
[Yehezkel] [30]:[11] He and his army with him, the terror of nations, will be brought in to destroy the land. They’ll draw out their swords against Mitsrayim and fill the land with those they kill.
[Yehezkel] [30]:[12] I’ll make the rivers into dry ground, and I’ll sell the land into the hands of wicked men. I’ll make the land and its abundant produce desolate by the actions of strangers. I, Yahweh, have spoken.
[Yehezkel] [30]:[13] The master Yahweh says this: I’ll destroy idols, and I’ll bring an end to the worthless idols in Nof (Memphis). There won’t be a prince in the land of Mitsrayim any longer, and I’ll put terror into Mitsrayim.
[Yehezkel] [30]:[14] Then I’ll make the Patros region desolate and set fire to Tsoan city, and I’ll execute judgement against No (Thebes) (the capital of southern Mitsrayim).
[Yehezkel] [30]:[15] I’ll pour out my fury on Mitsrayim’s stronghold Sin, and cut off the crowd at No.
[Yehezkel] [30]:[16] Then I’ll set fire to Mitsrayim: Sin will be in great agony, No will be broken up, and Nof will face enemies every day.
[Yehezkel] [30]:[17] The young men of Aven and Pi-Beset cities will be killed by the sword, and their populations will be taken into captivity.
[Yehezkel] [30]:[18] In Mitsrayim’s Tahfanhes, the day will hold back its light when I break Mitsrayim’s power and control there, and its pride in its strength will be finished. There’ll be a cloud covering it, and its daughters will be taken away into captivity.
[Yehezkel] [30]:[19] I’ll execute acts of judgement in Mitsrayim, then they’ll know that I am Yahweh.’ ”
[Yehezkel] [30]:[20] At the beginning of May in the eleventh year since King Yehoyakin had been taken captive, Yahweh gave me a message:
[Yehezkel] [30]:[21] “Son of humanity, I’ve broken the Mitsri (Egyptian) king Par’oh’s (Pharaoh) arm. Listen, it hasn’t been put in a splint, or set to heal with a bandage, so that it’ll become strong enough again to hold a sword.
[Yehezkel] [30]:[22] Therefore the master Yahweh says this, ‘Listen, I’m against the Mitsri king Par’oh and I’ll break both his strong arm and the previously broken one, and I’ll make the sword fall from his grip.
[Yehezkel] [30]:[23] Then I’ll scatter Mitsrayim (Egypt) among the other nations and disperse their people among the lands.
[Yehezkel] [30]:[24] I’ll strengthen the Babylonian king’s arms and place my sword in his hand so that I can destroy Par’oh’s arms. He’ll groan in front of the Babylonian king with the groans of a dying man.
[Yehezkel] [30]:[25] I’ll strengthen the arms of the Babylonian king, while Par’oh’s arms will fall. Then they’ll know that I am Yahweh, when I put my sword into the hand of the king of Bavel (Babylon) and he uses it against Mitsrayim.
[Yehezkel] [30]:[26] I’ll scatter Mitsrayim among the other nations and disperse their people through the lands. Then they’ll know that I am Yahweh.”
[Yehezkel] [31]:[1] At the end of June in the eleventh year since King Yehoyakin had been taken captive, Yahweh gave me a message:
[Yehezkel] [31]:[2] “Son of humanity, ask the Mitsri (Egyptian) king Par’oh (Pharaoh) and his multitudes around him, ‘Who else is as powerful as you and your people?
[Yehezkel] [31]:[3] Listen, Ashur (Assyria) was like a cedar in Levanon with beautiful branches, giving shade to the forest—extremely tall, and the branches formed its treetop.
[Yehezkel] [31]:[4] A deep water supply made it grow tall. Rivers flowed all around its area, because their channels stretched out to all the trees in the countryside.
[Yehezkel] [31]:[5] It grew taller than any of the other trees in the countryside, and its branches grew long and thick because of having plenty of water in its shoots.
[Yehezkel] [31]:[6] Every kind of bird nested in its branches, while every living thing in the countryside gave birth to its young under the foliage of that tree. All the powerful nations lived under its shade.
[Yehezkel] [31]:[7] It was beautiful in its greatness and due to the length of its branches, because its roots had access to many water sources.
[Yehezkel] [31]:[8] Cedar trees in God’s garden couldn’t equal it. None of the cypress trees matched its branches, nor could its branches be equalled by the plane tree. There was no other tree in God’s garden that could compare to its beauty.
[Yehezkel] [31]:[9] I made it beautiful with its many branches, and all the trees in God’s garden in Eden envied it.
[Yehezkel] [31]:[10] Therefore the master Yahweh says this: Because it was so tall, and it set its treetop between its branches, and because it grew proud of its height,
[Yehezkel] [31]:[11] I handed it over to a powerful nation to deal with it according to what its wickedness deserves. I’ve thrown it out,
[Yehezkel] [31]:[12] and foreigners who were the terror of all the nations cut it off and left it to die. Its branches fell onto the mountains and all the valleys, and lay broken in all the land’s ravines. Then all the nations on earth came out from under its shade and went away from it.
[Yehezkel] [31]:[13] All the various kinds of birds rested on the trunk of the fallen tree, and every kind of animal in the countryside came to its branches.
[Yehezkel] [31]:[14] That happened so that no other trees that grow by the waters will raise up their foliage to the height of the tallest trees, and that no other trees that grow beside the waters will reach up to that height. They’ve all been assigned to death, to the earth below, among humanity’s children, with those that go down into the pit.
[Yehezkel] [31]:[15] The master Yahweh says this: On the day when the cedar went down to the place of the dead, I brought mourning to the earth. I covered the deep waters over it, and I held back the oceans. I held back the great waters, and I brought mourning to Levanon for it. So all the trees in the countryside mourned because of it.
[Yehezkel] [31]:[16] I brought shuddering to the nations at the sound of its downfall, when I threw it down to the place of the dead, along with those who went down into the pit. So I comforted all the trees from Eden in the lowest parts of the earth. Those had been the choicest and best trees from Levanon—the trees that drank the waters.
[Yehezkel] [31]:[17] They also went down with the big tree to the place of the dead, to the ones who’d been killed by the sword. Those were its strong arm—those nations who’d lived in its shade.
[Yehezkel] [31]:[18] Mitsrayim (Egypt), which of the trees in Eden was your equal in glory and greatness? You’ll be brought down with Eden’s trees to the lowest parts of the earth among the uncircumcised. You’ll live there with those who were killed by the sword.’ That’s the fate of Par’oh (Pharaoh) and all his multitudes. That’s the master Yahweh’s declaration.”
[Yehezkel] [32]:[1] At the beginning of March in the twelfth year since King Yehoyakin had been taken captive, Yahweh gave me a message:
[Yehezkel] [32]:[2] “Son of humanity, sing a loud mourning song about the Mitsri (Egyptian) King Par’oh (Pharaoh) and tell him, ‘You’re like a young lion among the nations, but you’re like the sea monster in the oceans— you churn up the water— you stir up the waters with your feet, making them muddy.
[Yehezkel] [32]:[3] The master Yahweh says this: I’ll spread my net over you in the assembly of many people groups, and they’ll haul you up in my net.
[Yehezkel] [32]:[4] I’ll abandon you in the land. I’ll throw you into the countryside and cause every kind of bird to settle on you, and animals of every kind of will gorge themselves on you.
[Yehezkel] [32]:[5] I’ll dump your flesh on the hills, and fill the valleys with your corpse.
[Yehezkel] [32]:[6] Then I’ll drench your land with your blood across to the hills, and the ravines will be filled with your blood.
[Yehezkel] [32]:[7] Then when I eliminate you, I’ll cover the heavens and darken their stars. I’ll cover the sun with clouds, and the moon won’t shine its light.
[Yehezkel] [32]:[8] I’ll darken all the shining lights in the skies over you, and I’ll put darkness over your land. That’s the master Yahweh’s declaration.
[Yehezkel] [32]:[9] I’ll disturb the hearts of many people groups in lands that you don’t know about when I bring about your destruction among the nations—among lands you haven’t known.
[Yehezkel] [32]:[10] I’ll shock many people groups with what I’ll do to you. Their kings will shudder in horror concerning you when I swing my sword towards them. On the day of your downfall they’ll be trembling continuously because of you.
[Yehezkel] [32]:[11] Yes, the master Yahweh says this to you, Mitsrayim (Egypt): The Babylonian king’s sword will come against you.
[Yehezkel] [32]:[12] I’ll cause large numbers of you to be killed by warriors’ swords—each warrior a terror of nations. Those warriors will devastate the pride of Mitsrayim and destroy all its many people.
[Yehezkel] [32]:[13] I’ll destroy all the livestock from beside the plentiful waters. No human foot will stir the waters up again, nor will cattle hooves disturb them.
[Yehezkel] [32]:[14] Then I’ll calm their waters and make their rivers run like oil. That’s the master Yahweh’s declaration.
[Yehezkel] [32]:[15] When I make Mitsrayim’s territory into an abandoned place, when the land is stripped of all its produce, when I attack all its inhabitants, they’ll know that I am Yahweh.
[Yehezkel] [32]:[16] There’ll be a funeral song—the daughters of the nations will sing mournful songs about it. They’ll sing sadly about Mitsrayim—over all its multitudes they’ll sing dirges. That’s the master Yahweh’s declaration.’ ”
[Yehezkel] [32]:[17] In the middle of that same month, Yahweh gave me a message:
[Yehezkel] [32]:[18] “Son of humanity, weep for the numerous Mitsrim (Egyptians) and bring them down to the lowest parts of the earth. Bring Mitsrayim (Egypt) and the daughters of majestic nations down along with those who’ve already gone down into the pit.
[Yehezkel] [32]:[19] Ask them: Mitsrayim, are you really more beautiful than anyone else? Go down and lie down with the uncircumcised.
[Yehezkel] [32]:[20] They’ll fall among those who were killed by the sword. The sword has been drawn. Mitsrayim has been handed over to the sword—its enemies will seize it and its multitudes.
[Yehezkel] [32]:[21] The strongest of the warriors in the place of the dead will declare about Mitsrayim and its allies, ‘They’ve come down here. They’ll lie with the uncircumcised—with those who were killed by the sword.’
[Yehezkel] [32]:[22] Ashur (Assyria) is there with all its people, with its graves all around it—all of them were killed by the sword.
[Yehezkel] [32]:[23] Those whose graves are set in the pit’s recesses are there, along with all its people. Its graves surround all of those who were killed by the sword—those who brought terror onto the land of the living.
[Yehezkel] [32]:[24] Eylam is there with all its multitudes, with its graves all around it—all of them were killed. That’s the place for those who were killed by the sword, who’ve gone down uncircumcised to the lowest parts of the earth, who brought their terrors onto the land of the living, and who carry their own shame, together with the ones going down into the pit.
[Yehezkel] [32]:[25] They prepared a bed for Eylam and all its multitudes among those who were slain—its graves surround it. All of them are uncircumcised, pierced by the sword, because they brought their terrors onto the land of the living. So they carry their own shame, together with the ones going down into the pit among all those who’ve been killed, those who are going down into the pit. Eylam is among all those who were killed.
[Yehezkel] [32]:[26] Meshek, Tuval, and all their multitudes are there with their graves all around them. All of them are uncircumcised, killed by the sword, because they brought their terrors onto the land of the living.
[Yehezkel] [32]:[27] They don’t lie with the fallen warriors of the uncircumcised who’ve gone down to the place of the dead with all their weapons of war, and with their swords placed under their heads and their iniquities over their bones, because they were the terror of warriors in the land of the living.
[Yehezkel] [32]:[28] So you, Mitsrayim (Egypt), will be broken amongst the uncircumcised. You’ll lie alongside those who were pierced by the sword.
[Yehezkel] [32]:[29] Edom is also there with its kings and all its leaders. Despite their strength, they’ve been placed with those killed by the sword. They lie there along with the uncircumcised—with those who’ve gone down into the pit.
[Yehezkel] [32]:[30] All the northern leaders are there, along with all the Tsidonim (Sidonians) who went down with the ones who’d been pierced. They were powerful and made others afraid, but now they’re there in shame—uncircumcised along with those who were pierced by the sword. They carry their own shame, together with the ones going down into the pit.
[Yehezkel] [32]:[31] Par’oh (Pharaoh) will look and be comforted about all his multitudes who were pierced by the sword—Par’oh and all his army. That’s the master Yahweh’s declaration.
[Yehezkel] [32]:[32] Yes, I put him there as my agent to terrify those in the land of the living, but Par’oh and all his multitudes will be laid down among the uncircumcised—among those pierced by the sword. That’s the master Yahweh’s declaration.”
[Yehezkel] [33]:[1] Then Yahweh gave me another message:
[Yehezkel] [33]:[2] “Son of humanity, tell this to your people: ‘When I send an army against any country, then the people of that country choose one of their men to become a watchman for them.
[Yehezkel] [33]:[3] He looks for any attacker coming onto the land, and then he blows his horn to warn the people.
[Yehezkel] [33]:[4] If the people hear the sound of the horn but don’t take any notice, and if the attacker comes and kills them, then each one’s blood is on their own head.
[Yehezkel] [33]:[5] Yes, if someone heard the horn but paid no attention, that person’s blood is on them, but if those people do pay attention, they’ll save their own lives.
[Yehezkel] [33]:[6] However, if the watchman sees the attacker coming, but doesn’t blow the horn, that is, if the people weren’t warned, and if the attacker approaches and takes anyone’s life, then that person dies in their own sin, but I’ll require their blood from the watchman.’
[Yehezkel] [33]:[7] Now, talking to you, son of humanity: I’ve made you a watchman for the Israeli people. You’ll hear the words from my mouth and then warn them on my behalf.
[Yehezkel] [33]:[8] If I say to a wicked person, ‘You wicked person, you’re certainly about to die,’ and if you don’t announce it so as to warn that wicked person about their behaviour, then that wicked person will die in their sin, but it’ll be you that I hold responsible for their death.
[Yehezkel] [33]:[9] But if you warn the wicked person about their behaviour, so that they might turn back from it, and if that person doesn’t turn back from their behaviour, then they’ll die in their sin, but you yourself will have saved your own life.
[Yehezkel] [33]:[10] So, son of humanity, you tell the Israeli people, ‘You’re saying this, “Our errors and our disobedience have come back on us and they’re hurting us. How can we go on living like this?” ’
[Yehezkel] [33]:[11] Tell them that this is the master Yahweh’s declaration: ‘As I live, I don’t delight in the death of wicked people. If they turn away from their wicked behaviour, then they’ll live! So turn back, yes turn away from your wicked behaviour. Why should you Israeli people die?’
[Yehezkel] [33]:[12] So now, son of humanity, you tell your people, ‘Righteous people’s righteousness won’t save them if they sin. Wicked people’s wickedness won’t cause them to die if they turn away from their sin. No, the righteous person won’t be able to live because of his righteousness if he sins.
[Yehezkel] [33]:[13] If I say that a righteous person will surely live, and if they trust in their righteousness and then commit injustice, I won’t call to mind any of the good things they did—that person will die for the wickedness they committed.
[Yehezkel] [33]:[14] Again, if I say to the wicked, “You will surely die,” but if they then turn away from their sins and do what’s just and right,
[Yehezkel] [33]:[15] like returning loan guarantees that were wickedly demanded, or like making restitution for what they’ve stolen, and then if they obey the instructions that give life and no longer disobey, then those formerly wicked people will surely live—they won’t die.
[Yehezkel] [33]:[16] None of the sins that they’ve committed will be called to mind against them. Those who’ve acted justly and rightly, will certainly live.
[Yehezkel] [33]:[17] But your people say, “The master’s way isn’t fair!” but it’s your ways that aren’t fair.
[Yehezkel] [33]:[18] When the righteous person turns away from doing what’s right and becomes disobedient, then they’ll die in their sin.
[Yehezkel] [33]:[19] When the wicked person turns away from doing evil and does what’s just and right, they’ll live because of those things.
[Yehezkel] [33]:[20] Yes, you people say, “The master’s way isn’t fair!” but I’ll judge each of you Israeli people according to your behaviour.”
[Yehezkel] [33]:[21] In mid-January of the twelfth year of our captivity in Bavel (Babylon), someone who’d escaped from Yerushalem (Jerusalem) came to me and told me that the city had been captured.
[Yehezkel] [33]:[22] Yahweh had held me in a vision the evening before the fugitive came, but my mouth was opened by the time he came to me at dawn, so by then, I was able to speak again.
[Yehezkel] [33]:[23] Then Yahweh gave me another message:
[Yehezkel] [33]:[24] “Son of humanity, the people inhabiting those ruins back in Yisrael (Israel) are saying, ‘Avraham was only one person, and he inherited the land, but there’s lots of us now. The land has been given to us as an inheritance.’
[Yehezkel] [33]:[25] Therefore tell them that the master Yahweh says this: You eat blood, and you pay your respect to your idols, then you pour out people’s blood. Should you then inherit that land?
[Yehezkel] [33]:[26] You people rely on your swords for protection, and you’ve done disgusting things—each man defiles his neighbour’s wife. Should you really possess that land?’
[Yehezkel] [33]:[27] Tell them that the master Yahweh says this: As I live, surely the ones in the ruins will be killed by swords, and I’ll give those in the countryside to the wild animals as food, and those in fortresses and in caves will die from deadly diseases.
[Yehezkel] [33]:[28] Then I’ll turn the country into a desolation and a horror, and the pride that came from its power will end, because Yisrael’s mountains will be deserted, and there’ll be no one to walk through them.’
[Yehezkel] [33]:[29] Then they’ll know that I am Yahweh, when I make the country a desolation and a wasteland because of all the disgusting things they’ve done.
[Yehezkel] [33]:[30] So now son of humanity, your people are out beside the walls and the gates of their houses talking about you, and they’re all telling each other, ‘Let’s go and listen to the prophet’s message that comes from Yahweh.’
[Yehezkel] [33]:[31] So my people will come to you, as they often do, and will sit in front of you and listen to your words, but they won’t obey them. The right words are on their lips, but their hearts are going after unjust profit.
[Yehezkel] [33]:[32] Yes, you’re like a lovely song to them, a beautiful sound that’s played well on a stringed instrument, so they’ll listen to your words, but none of them will obey them.
[Yehezkel] [33]:[33] So when all that happens, watch out, because it will indeed happen. Then they’ll realise that a prophet’s been among them.”
[Yehezkel] [34]:[1] Then Yahweh gave me another message:
[Yehezkel] [34]:[2] “Son of humanity, prophesy against Yisrael’s (Israel) shepherds. Prophesy and tell them that the master Yahweh says this to the shepherds: Yisrael’s shepherds who are shepherding themselves won’t end well. Shouldn’t shepherds guard the flock?
[Yehezkel] [34]:[3] You eat the best sheep meat and dress in woollen clothes. You slaughter the fat lambs. You don’t shepherd at all.
[Yehezkel] [34]:[4] You haven’t taken care of those with diseases, nor do you heal those who are ill. You don’t bandage up the ones with broken limbs, and you don’t restore the outcasts or search for those who’ve gone missing. Instead, you use strength and violence to rule over them.
[Yehezkel] [34]:[5] Then they were scattered without a shepherd, and after they were scattered, they became food for all the wild animals in the countryside.
[Yehezkel] [34]:[6] My flock has strayed across all the mountains and onto every high hill, and it’s dispersed over the entire surface of the earth, yet no one is searching for them.
[Yehezkel] [34]:[7] Therefore, you shepherds, listen to Yahweh’s message to you:
[Yehezkel] [34]:[8] This is the master Yahweh’s declaration: As I live, my flock has become plunder and food for all the wild animals in the countryside, because there wasn’t any shepherd and because none of my shepherds tried to find any of my flock that had gotten lost. Instead it was themselves that the shepherds looked after, and they didn’t shepherd my flock.
[Yehezkel] [34]:[9] Therefore, you so-called ‘shepherds’, listen to Yahweh’s message:
[Yehezkel] [34]:[10] The master Yahweh says this: Listen, I’m against those shepherds. I’ll require compensation from them for my flock, and then I’ll dismiss them from shepherding the flock. Those shepherds won’t shepherd themselves any longer either, because I’ll take my flock away from their mouths, so that my flock won’t become food for them any longer.
[Yehezkel] [34]:[11] So the master Yahweh says this: Listen, I myself will search for those lost from my flock, and I myself will look after them,
[Yehezkel] [34]:[12] like a shepherd searches for his sheep when he’s among his scattered flock. So I’ll look for my flock and I’ll rescue them from all the places where they were scattered during the dark times.
[Yehezkel] [34]:[13] I’ll bring my people out from among the nations. I’ll gather them from foreign lands and bring them back to their land. I’ll put them in pastures on Yisrael’s (Israel) mountainsides, by the streams, and in every settlement in the land.
[Yehezkel] [34]:[14] I’ll put them in good pastures—Yisrael’s high mountains will be their grazing places. They’ll lie down there in places good for grazing, in abundant pastures, and they’ll graze on Yisrael’s hills.
[Yehezkel] [34]:[15] I myself will shepherd my flock, and I myself will give them rest. That’s the master Yahweh’s declaration.
[Yehezkel] [34]:[16] I’ll search out the lost and restore the outcast. I’ll bandage up those who are broken and heal those who are sick, but I’ll destroy those who are fat and well. I will shepherd with justice.
[Yehezkel] [34]:[17] So now this is what the master Yahweh says, You, my flock, listen, I’ll be a judge between one sheep and another, and between rams and billy goats.
[Yehezkel] [34]:[18] Isn’t it enough to feed on the good pasture? Do you have to trample down any remaining grass? Or drink from clear waters, then muddy the streams with your feet?
[Yehezkel] [34]:[19] Must my flock eat what you’ve trampled and drink what you’ve muddied with your feet?
[Yehezkel] [34]:[20] Therefore the master Yahweh says this to them: Listen, I myself will judge between the fat sheep and the thin ones,
[Yehezkel] [34]:[21] because you shepherds have pushed them with your sides and shoulders, and you’ve gored all the weak ones with your horns until you succeeded in scattering them away from the land.
[Yehezkel] [34]:[22] I’ll save my flock and they’ll no longer be taken as plunder, and I’ll judge between one sheep and the next.
[Yehezkel] [34]:[23] I’ll set one shepherd over them—my servant David. He’ll look after them, and he’ll be their shepherd.
[Yehezkel] [34]:[24] Then I, Yahweh, will be their god, and my servant David will be a leader among them. I, Yahweh, have declared that.
[Yehezkel] [34]:[25] Then I’ll make a peace treaty with them and remove the wild animals from the land, so that they’ll be able to live securely in the wilderness and sleep safely in the forests.
[Yehezkel] [34]:[26] I’ll also bless both them and the places around my hill, and send out showers in the right season—they’ll be showers of blessing.
[Yehezkel] [34]:[27] Then the trees in the countryside will produce their fruit, the soil will yield its produce, and my sheep will be secure in their land. When I break off the ties holding the yoke onto their necks, and when I rescue them from the control of those who enslaved them, then they’ll know that I am Yahweh.
[Yehezkel] [34]:[28] They’ll no longer be plunder for the other nations, and the wild animals on the land will no longer devour them. Then they’ll live securely, and no one will make them afraid.
[Yehezkel] [34]:[29] I’ll provide a land for them that’s known for its crops, so they won’t be victims of famine, and they won’t be mocked by other nations.
[Yehezkel] [34]:[30] Then they’ll know that I, Yahweh their god, am with them. The Israeli people are my people. That’s the master Yahweh’s declaration.
[Yehezkel] [34]:[31] You are my sheep, the flock of my pasture, and my people, and I am your god. That’s the master Yahweh’s declaration.’ ”
[Yehezkel] [35]:[1] Then Yahweh gave me another message:
[Yehezkel] [35]:[2] “Son of humanity, look out towards Mt. Se’ir and prophesy against it.
[Yehezkel] [35]:[3] Tell it that the master Yahweh says this: Listen, I’m against you Edom, represented by Mt. Se’ir, and I’ll work against you to make you a desolation and a waste.
[Yehezkel] [35]:[4] I’ll turn your cities into ruins, and you yourself will become desolate. Then you’ll know that I am Yahweh.
[Yehezkel] [35]:[5] You’ve always been hostile to the Israeli people, and when they were distressed you decided to attack them with swords—at the time their punishment was coming to an end.
[Yehezkel] [35]:[6] Therefore, this is the master Yahweh’s declaration: As I live, I’ll prepare you for bloodshed, and bloodshed will chase after you. Since you didn’t hate bloodshed, bloodshed will come to you.
[Yehezkel] [35]:[7] I’ll make Edom completely desolate when I cut it off so that no one will want to pass through it.
[Yehezkel] [35]:[8] I’ll fill its mountain ranges with people who were killed—those killed by the sword will fall on your high hills and valleys and in all your streams.
[Yehezkel] [35]:[9] I’ll make your land perpetually desolate. Your cities won’t be inhabited, and then you’ll know that I am Yahweh.
[Yehezkel] [35]:[10] You’ve said, “These two nations and these two lands will become mine, and we’ll possess them,” even when Yahweh was there with them.
[Yehezkel] [35]:[11] Therefore, this is the master Yahweh’s declaration: As I live, I’ll act according to your anger and according to your jealousy that you had in your hatred of Yisrael (Israel), and I’ll show myself to them when I judge you—
[Yehezkel] [35]:[12] then you’ll know that I am Yahweh. I’ve heard all the insults you spoke against Yisrael’s hill country, when you said, “They’ve been destroyed—they’ve been given over to us to devour.”
[Yehezkel] [35]:[13] You raised yourselves up against me with what you said, and you multiplied the words you said against me, and I heard all of them.
[Yehezkel] [35]:[14] The master Yahweh says this: I’ll make you into a desolate place while the rest of the world cheers.
[Yehezkel] [35]:[15] Just like you rejoiced over the Israeli people’s inheritance when it was made desolate, I’ll do the same to you. You’ll become a desolation, Mt. Se’ir and all of Edom—all of it. Then they’ll know that I am Yahweh.”
[Yehezkel] [36]:[1] “Now, son of humanity, prophesy to Yisrael’s (Israel) mountains and say, ‘Mountains of Yisrael, listen to Yahweh’s message.
[Yehezkel] [36]:[2] The master Yahweh says this: The enemy has said, “Aha,” when talking about you, and “The ancient hilltop shrines have become ours.” ’
[Yehezkel] [36]:[3] Therefore prophesy and tell them that the master Yahweh says this: Because of your desolation and because of the attacks that came on you from all sides, you’ve ended up belonging to other nations—you’ve been the subject of slanderous lips and tongues, and of people’s stories.
[Yehezkel] [36]:[4] Therefore, mountains of Yisrael, listen to the message from the master Yahweh: The master Yahweh says this to the mountains and the high hills, to the streambeds and valleys, to the places that have been destroyed and are now uninhabited, and to the forsaken cities that have become plunder and a subject of mocking for the other nations that surround them—
[Yehezkel] [36]:[5] the master Yahweh says this: I’ve certainly spoken in the heat of my anger against the other nations, against Edom and everyone who took my land for themselves as a possession—against all those who had both celebration in their heart and disdain in their spirit as they seized my land so they could claim its pasturelands for themselves.’
[Yehezkel] [36]:[6] Therefore, prophesy to Yisrael and tell the mountains and the high hills, the streambeds and the valleys, that the master Yahweh says this: Listen, in my fury and in my anger I’m declaring this because you’ve endured insults from other nations.
[Yehezkel] [36]:[7] Therefore, the master Yahweh says this: I myself will take action and promise that the nations that surround you will certainly be made to carry their own shame.
[Yehezkel] [36]:[8] But you Israeli mountains, you’ll grow branches and bear fruit for my Israeli people, since they’ll soon come back to you,
[Yehezkel] [36]:[9] because, listen, I’m for you, and I’ll treat you favourably—you’ll be ploughed and sown with seed.
[Yehezkel] [36]:[10] I’ll multiply your population—all the Israeli people. The cities will be inhabited again and the ruins rebuilt.
[Yehezkel] [36]:[11] I’ll increase both people and animals on you mountains so that they’ll multiply and be fruitful. Then I’ll cause you to be inhabited like you were previously, and I’ll make you prosper more than you did in the past so that you’ll know that I am Yahweh.
[Yehezkel] [36]:[12] I’ll bring my Israeli people to walk on you. They’ll possess you, and you’ll be their inheritance, and you’ll no longer cause their children to die.

[Yehezkel] [36]:[14] therefore you won’t consume people any longer, and you’ll no longer make your nation mourn their deaths. That’s the master Yahweh’s declaration.
[Yehezkel] [36]:[15] I won’t allow you to hear the insults from the other nations any longer—you’ll no longer have to bear the people groups shaming you, and you won’t cause your nation to stumble. That’s the master Yahweh’s declaration.”
[Yehezkel] [36]:[16] Then Yahweh gave me another message:
[Yehezkel] [36]:[17] “Son of humanity, when the Israeli people inhabited their land, they defiled it with their customs and their activities. In my eyes, their customs were like the uncleanness of a woman’s menstruation,
[Yehezkel] [36]:[18] so I poured out my fury against them for the blood that they’d poured out on the land, and for how they’d polluted it with their idols.
[Yehezkel] [36]:[19] I scattered them among the nations—they were dispersed through the lands. I judged them according to their customs and their actions.
[Yehezkel] [36]:[20] Then they went to those other nations, and wherever they went, they profaned my holy name when people asked about them, ‘Are these really Yahweh’s people? After all, they’ve been thrown out of his land.’
[Yehezkel] [36]:[21] But I had compassion for my holy name that the Israeli people had defiled among the other nations, when they went there.
[Yehezkel] [36]:[22] Therefore tell the Israeli people that the master Yahweh says this: I’m not doing this for the sake of you Israeli people, but for my sacred name, which you’ve profaned among the nations everywhere you’ve gone.
[Yehezkel] [36]:[23] My great name, which you people have profaned among the nations, I’ll make holy even among the nations where you profaned it. Then the nations will know that I am Yahweh, when they see you recognise my holiness. That’s the master Yahweh’s declaration.
[Yehezkel] [36]:[24] I’ll take you back out of those nations and gather you from every land, and I’ll bring you into your land.
[Yehezkel] [36]:[25] Then I’ll sprinkle pure water on you so you’ll be cleaned from all of your impurities, and I’ll purify you from all your idols.
[Yehezkel] [36]:[26] I’ll give you people a new heart and a new spirit in your innermost parts, and I’ll take the stony heart away from your bodies and replace it with a heart of flesh.
[Yehezkel] [36]:[27] I’ll put my spirit in you and enable you Israelis to follow my instructions and keep my regulations.
[Yehezkel] [36]:[28] Then you’ll inhabit the land that I gave to your ancestors—you’ll be my people and I’ll be your god.
[Yehezkel] [36]:[29] I’ll save you from all of your uncleanness, and then I’ll summon the grain and multiply it—I’ll no longer assign famine to you.
[Yehezkel] [36]:[30] I’ll multiply the fruit on the trees and the produce from the soil so that you’ll no longer be shamed by other nations seeing you suffering famine.
[Yehezkel] [36]:[31] Then you’ll think about your wicked customs and your activities that weren’t good, and your faces will display your loathing of your own sins and your disgusting habits.
[Yehezkel] [36]:[32] But make sure you know this: I’m not doing all that for your sake, so you Israeli people should be ashamed and disgraced because of your behaviour. That’s the master Yahweh’s declaration.
[Yehezkel] [36]:[33] The master Yahweh says this: When I purify you from all your disobedience, I’ll enable you to inhabit the cities again and to rebuild the ruined places,
[Yehezkel] [36]:[34] and the idle land will be tilled until it’s no longer a wasteland for everyone to see as they go past.
[Yehezkel] [36]:[35] Then instead they’ll say, “This land was desolate, but it’s become like the garden of Eden—the abandoned cities and the uninhabited ruins that were torn down are now fortified and inhabited.”
[Yehezkel] [36]:[36] Then the other nations around you will know that I am Yahweh, because I built up the ruins and replanted the abandoned places. I, Yahweh, have declared it and I will do it.
[Yehezkel] [36]:[37] The master Yahweh also says this: The Israeli people will again ask me to do this for them: to increase their population like sheep.
[Yehezkel] [36]:[38] Just like the flock that’s kept separate to be used for sacrifices (like the flock in Yerushalem (Jerusalem) at its scheduled feasts), so too the ruined cities will be filled with flocks of people and they will know that I am Yahweh.”
[Yehezkel] [37]:[1] One day Yahweh gave me another vision, and he took me out by his spirit and put me down in the middle of a valley that was full of bones.
[Yehezkel] [37]:[2] Then he led me all around them, and wow, there were so many bones in the valley, and they were totally dried out!
[Yehezkel] [37]:[3] “Son of humanity,” he asked me, “can these bones become living people again?” “My master Yahweh,” I replied, “only you would know that.”
[Yehezkel] [37]:[4] Then he told me, “Prophesy over these bones and tell them, ‘Dry bones. Listen to Yahweh’s message.
[Yehezkel] [37]:[5] The master Yahweh says this to these bones: Listen, I’m about to put breath into you, and you’ll live.
[Yehezkel] [37]:[6] I’ll connect sinews to you and put flesh onto you. I’ll cover you with skin and put breath into you so you’ll live. Then you’ll know that I am Yahweh.’ ”
[Yehezkel] [37]:[7] So I prophesied as I was instructed, and wow, a sound like something rattling started as the bones moved together—bone against bone!
[Yehezkel] [37]:[8] I looked and, wow, the bones now had sinews on them, and flesh grew up over that, and then skin covered them! But there was still no breath in them.
[Yehezkel] [37]:[9] Then Yahweh told me, “Prophesy to the wind, son of humanity, prophesy and tell the air, ‘The master Yahweh commands this: Breath, come from the four compass points, and breathe into these who’ve been killed, so they’ll come to life.’ ”
[Yehezkel] [37]:[10] So I prophesied just like I was commanded. Then breath came into them and they came to life. Then they stood on their feet—a very large army.
[Yehezkel] [37]:[11] Then Yahweh informed me, “Son of humanity, these bones are the entire Israeli population. Listen, they’re saying, ‘Our bones have dried up and our hope is gone. We’ve been cut off.’
[Yehezkel] [37]:[12] Therefore prophesy and tell them, ‘The master Yahweh says this: Listen, I’ll open your graves and lift you, my people, out from them, then I’ll bring you back to Yisrael (Israel).
[Yehezkel] [37]:[13] Then, my people, when I open your graves and bring you out of them, you’ll know that I am Yahweh.
[Yehezkel] [37]:[14] I’ll place my spirit within you so you’ll live, and I’ll cause you to rest in your land when you know that I am Yahweh. I declare it, and I will do it. That is Yahweh’s declaration.’ ”

[Yehezkel] [37]:[25] They’ll live in the land that I’ve given to my servant Ya’akov (Jacob) (also called Yisrael), where your ancestors had stayed. They’ll live in it forever—they, their children, and their grandchildren, and my servant David will be their permanent leader.

[Yehezkel] [38]:[16] Then you’ll attack my Israeli people like a cloud that covers the land. I’ll send you against my land near the end of the era, so that the nations might know me when I show myself through you, Gog—they’ll see with their own eyes that I always demand what’s right.
[Yehezkel] [38]:[17] The master Yahweh says this: Aren’t you the one that I spoke about in the past through my servants, the Israeli prophets who prophesied for years in their own times, that I would bring you against them?

[Yehezkel] [38]:[19] In my zeal and in the fire of my anger, I declare that on that day there’ll be a terrible earthquake in Yisrael,
[Yehezkel] [38]:[20] and the fish in the sea and the birds in the skies, the wild animals in the countryside including all the creatures that crawl on the earth, and every person who’s on the surface of the land will tremble in front of me. The mountains will be thrown down and the cliffs will fall, until every wall falls to the ground.
[Yehezkel] [38]:[21] I’ll summon an army against Gog on all my mountains. Every man’s sword will be against his brother. That’s the master Yahweh’s declaration.
[Yehezkel] [38]:[22] Then I’ll punish Gog with deadly diseases and bloodshed, as well as overwhelming rain and hailstones and burning sulfur that I’ll rain down on him and his troops and the many nations that joined with him.
[Yehezkel] [38]:[23] Yes, I’ll display my greatness and purity, and I’ll make myself known to those many nations, so they’ll know that I am Yahweh.
[Yehezkel] [39]:[1] “Now, son of humanity, prophesy against Gog and say that the master Yahweh says this: Listen, I’m against you, Gog, leader of Meshek and Tuval.
[Yehezkel] [39]:[2] I’ll turn you around and drag you along—I’ll bring you from the far north and take you up to Yisrael’s (Israel) mountains,
[Yehezkel] [39]:[3] Then I’ll knock your bow out of your left hand and make the arrows fall out of your right hand.
[Yehezkel] [39]:[4] You and all your troops and soldiers who are with you will die on Yisrael’s mountains. I’ll give you to the birds of prey and the wild animals in the countryside for food.
[Yehezkel] [39]:[5] You’ll die there in the countryside, because I myself declare it. That’s the master Yahweh’s declaration.
[Yehezkel] [39]:[6] Then I’ll send fire out onto Magog and on those living in safety in the coastal regions, and then they’ll know that I am Yahweh.
[Yehezkel] [39]:[7] I’ll make my holy name known among my people Yisrael, and I’ll no longer allow my holy name to be profaned—the nations will know that I am Yahweh, the holy One in Yisrael.
[Yehezkel] [39]:[8] Listen, the day is coming, and all that will take place. That’s the master Yahweh’s declaration.
[Yehezkel] [39]:[9] The people living in Yisrael’s cities will go out and they’ll use those weapons to kindle and make fires and burn them—small shields, large shields, bows, arrows, the clubs and spears—they’ll make fires with them for seven years.
[Yehezkel] [39]:[10] They won’t need to gather firewood from the countryside or cut down trees from the forests, since they’ll burn the weapons. They’ll take from those invaders who wanted to take from them, and plunder those who wanted to plunder them. That’s the master Yahweh’s declaration.”
[Yehezkel] [39]:[11] Then at that time, I’ll make a grave for Gog there in Yisrael (Israel)—a valley for those who journey to the east of the sea. They’ll bury Gog there with all his multitudes, and they’ll call it the ‘Hamon-Gog’ (or, ‘Gog’s horde’) valley. That mass grave will block people who want to cross over.
[Yehezkel] [39]:[12] It’ll take seven months for the Israelis to bury them to make the area clean—
[Yehezkel] [39]:[13] all the land’s people will bury them. It’ll be a memorable day for them when I’m honoured. That’s the master Yahweh’s declaration.
[Yehezkel] [39]:[14] At the end of the seven months, they’ll designate men to continually go through the region to find people who were travelling through, but who died and their bodies remained above the ground, so that they can bury them to make the land clean.
[Yehezkel] [39]:[15] As those men pass through the land, when they see any human bone, they’ll put a marker by it, until gravediggers come and bury it in the Hamon-Gog valley.
[Yehezkel] [39]:[16] There’ll even be a city there named ‘Hamonah’ (which means, ‘horde’ or ‘multitude’). In that way, they’ll make the land clean again.
[Yehezkel] [39]:[17] Now, son of humanity, the master Yahweh says this to you: Tell all the winged birds and all the wild animals in the countryside, ‘Gather together and come. Gather from all around to the sacrifice that I myself am making for you—a large sacrifice on Yisrael’s mountains, so that you can eat human flesh and drink blood.
[Yehezkel] [39]:[18] You’ll eat warriors’ flesh and drink the blood of the world’s leaders as if they were rams, lambs, goats, and bulls that were all fattened in Bashan.
[Yehezkel] [39]:[19] Then you’ll eat fat until you’re full and drink blood until you’re drunk—that’ll be the sacrifice that I’ll slaughter for you birds and animals.
[Yehezkel] [39]:[20] You’ll be satisfied at my table with horses, chariot drivers, warriors, and every man of war. That’s the master Yahweh’s declaration.’
[Yehezkel] [39]:[21] I’ll display my power among the nations, and all the nations will see my judgement that I’ll put into process and how I’ll put that into action against them.
[Yehezkel] [39]:[22] Then from that time onwards, the Israeli people will know that I am their god Yahweh.
[Yehezkel] [39]:[23] The nations will know that the Israeli people went into captivity because of how they betrayed me with their disobedience, so I distanced myself from them and handed them over to their adversaries so that they all died in the battle.
[Yehezkel] [39]:[24] When I distanced myself from them, I treated them exactly as their defilement and rebellion deserved.
[Yehezkel] [39]:[25] Therefore the master Yahweh says this: Now I’ll restore Ya’akov’s (Jacob) fortunes, and I’ll have compassion on all of Yisrael’s (Israel) descendants, when I act with zeal to protect my pure reputation.
[Yehezkel] [39]:[26] Then they’ll bear their shame and all the treason in which they betrayed me. They’ll forget all that when they rest in their land in safety, with no one to terrify them
[Yehezkel] [39]:[27] when I restore them from the people groups and gather them from their enemies’ lands, and I show myself in the sight of many nations to always do what’s right.
[Yehezkel] [39]:[28] Then they’ll know that I am Yahweh their god, because I sent them into captivity among the other nations, but then I’ll gather them back to their own land. I won’t leave any of them among the nations.
[Yehezkel] [39]:[29] I’ll no longer distance myself from them when I pour out my spirit on the Israeli people. That’s the master Yahweh’s declaration.”
[Yehezkel] [40]:[1] In mid-April of the twenty-fifth year of our captivity (the fourteenth year after Yerushalem (Jerusalem) was captured), Yahweh used his power to take me there,
[Yehezkel] [40]:[2] yes, God took me to Yisrael (Israel) in visions. He put me on a very high mountain where there seemed to be city buildings towards the south,
[Yehezkel] [40]:[3] and he took me there. Then wow, there was a man standing in the city gateway who looked like bronze! He was holding a linen cord and a measuring rod.
[Yehezkel] [40]:[4] The man told me, “Son of humanity, look with your eyes and listen with your ears, and fix your mind on everything that I’m revealing to you, because you were brought here so I could reveal them to you. Report everything you see here to the Israeli people.”
[Yehezkel] [40]:[5] There was a wall surrounding the temple area. The measuring rod in the man’s hand was just over three metres long. (It was six long cubits—each long cubit was a cubit long plus a handbreadth.) So he measured the wall, and it was one measuring rod thick and one high.
[Yehezkel] [40]:[6] Then he went to the temple gate that faced east. He went up its steps and measured the gate’s threshold—one rod across.
[Yehezkel] [40]:[7] The guard chambers were each one rod long and deep, and just under three metres wide. The temple gate threshold by the temple porch was one rod across.
[Yehezkel] [40]:[8] He measured the porch inside the gate and it was one rod long,
[Yehezkel] [40]:[9] and the porch over the gate was one rod deep. The doorposts were each a metre wide. (This was the porch at the gate facing the temple.)
[Yehezkel] [40]:[10] There were three guard chambers on either side of the east gate, and each of them was the same size, and the walls that separated them were the same size.

[Yehezkel] [40]:[18] The pavement reached to the side of the gates, and its width was the same as the gates’ length. That was the lower pavement.
[Yehezkel] [40]:[19] Then the man measured the distance from the front of the lower gate to the front of the inner gate: it was just over fifty metres on the eastern side, and the same on the northern side.
