[Yehezkel] [40]:[41] There were four tables by the gate on each side—they slaughtered animals on those eight tables.
[Yehezkel] [40]:[42] There were four cut-stone tables for the burnt offerings, each just under a metre long and wide, and standing half a metre tall. They kept the tools which they used to slaughter the burnt offerings for the sacrifices on those stone tables.
[Yehezkel] [40]:[43] Some two-pronged hooks a handbreadth in length were fastened all around in the porch, and the flesh of the offerings would be put on the tables.
[Yehezkel] [40]:[44] Within the inner courtyard but on the outside of the inner gate were singers’ rooms—one on the northern side facing south, and the other on the southern side facing north.
[Yehezkel] [40]:[45] Then the man told me, “This room facing south is for the priests who are on duty in the temple.
[Yehezkel] [40]:[46] The room facing north is for the priests on duty at the altar, that is, for Tsadok’s descendants—they’re the only Levites who approach Yahweh to serve him.”
[Yehezkel] [40]:[47] Next he measured the square courtyard at fifty-four metres long and wide, with the altar in front of the temple.
[Yehezkel] [40]:[48] Then the man took me to the temple porch and measured its doorposts—they were each two and a half metres thick. The entryway itself was seven metres wide, and the walls on each side of it were one and a half metres wide.
[Yehezkel] [40]:[49] The porch was eleven metres wide and six metres deep, with steps going up to it and pillars standing on each side of it.
[Yehezkel] [41]:[1] Then the man took me into the temple’s holy place and measured the doorposts at three metres thick on each side.
[Yehezkel] [41]:[2] The doorway was five metres wide and the wall on each side was two and a half metres long. Then the man measured the dimensions of the holy place—twenty-one metres long and eleven metres wide.
[Yehezkel] [41]:[3] Then the man went into the very sacred inner place and measured the door at one metre wide, and the doorway was three metres wide. The walls on either side were nearly four metres wide.
[Yehezkel] [41]:[4] Then he measured the square room’s length and width of eleven metres, measuring to the temple hallway. Then he said to me, “This is the most sacred area.”
[Yehezkel] [41]:[5] Then the man measured the wall of the house at three metres thick. The width of each side room around the house was two metres.
[Yehezkel] [41]:[6] There were side rooms on three levels, one room above another, thirty rooms on each level. There were ledges around the temple wall to support all the side rooms, as the supports weren’t built into the temple wall.
[Yehezkel] [41]:[7] So the side rooms widened and went around going up, because the house went around higher and higher all around—the rooms widened on each higher level, and a stairway went up through the middle level to the highest level.
[Yehezkel] [41]:[8] Then I saw a raised part all around the temple, the foundation for the side rooms. It measured a full rod in height—just over three metres.
[Yehezkel] [41]:[9] The width of the wall of the side rooms on the outside was two and a half metres. There was an open space outside those rooms in the temple.
[Yehezkel] [41]:[10] On the other side of that open space were the priests’ outer side rooms. That space was eleven metres wide all around the temple.
[Yehezkel] [41]:[11] There were doors into the side rooms from another open space with one doorway on the north side, and the other on the south. The width of that open area was two and a half metres all around.
[Yehezkel] [41]:[12] The building that faced the courtyard on the western side was thirty-six metres wide. Its wall was two and a half metres thick all around, and it was forty-seven metres long.
[Yehezkel] [41]:[13] Then the man measured the temple as being fifty-four metres long. The separate building, its wall, and the courtyard combined also measured fifty-four metres across.
[Yehezkel] [41]:[14] The width of the front of the courtyard in front of the temple was also fifty-four metres.
[Yehezkel] [41]:[15] Then the man measured the length of the building behind the temple, to its west, and including the galleries on either side, it came to fifty-four metres. The sacred inner place and the porch,
[Yehezkel] [41]:[16] the inner walls and the windows, including the narrow windows, and the galleries all around on three levels, were all panelled in wood.
[Yehezkel] [41]:[17] Above the entryway to the inner sanctuary and spaced along the walls there was a repeating pattern.
[Yehezkel] [41]:[18] It was decorated with winged creatures and palm trees—with a palm tree between each winged creature, and each winged creature had two faces:
[Yehezkel] [41]:[19] the human face looked toward a palm tree on one side, and the young lion face looked toward a palm tree on the other side. They were carved all around the entire temple.
[Yehezkel] [41]:[20] From the ground to above the doorway, winged creatures and palm trees were carved on the outer wall of the temple.
[Yehezkel] [41]:[21] The door posts of the main temple room were square, all with the same appearance.
[Yehezkel] [41]:[22] The wooden altar was one metre on each side and stood one and a half metres high. Its corner posts, base, and frame were all made of wood. Then the man said to me, “This is the table that stands in Yahweh’s presence.”
[Yehezkel] [41]:[23] Both the main room and the sacred place had double doors—
[Yehezkel] [41]:[24] each consisting of two parts that swung on hinges.
[Yehezkel] [41]:[25] There were carvings of winged creatures and palm trees on the doors, just like on the walls, and there was a wooden roof over the front porch.
[Yehezkel] [41]:[26] There were narrow windows and palm trees on either side of the porch, like the side rooms of the temple, and they also had overhanging roofs.
[Yehezkel] [42]:[1] Next the man sent me out to the outer courtyard on the northern side, and he brought me to rooms in front of the outer courtyard and the northern outer wall.
[Yehezkel] [42]:[2] That building with a north-facing entrance was fifty-four metres long and twenty-seven metres wide.
[Yehezkel] [42]:[3] Some of those rooms faced the inner courtyard and were eleven metres away from the sanctuary. There were three levels of rooms, and the ones above looked down on the ones below and were open to them, having a walkway. Some of the rooms looked out onto the outer courtyard.
[Yehezkel] [42]:[4] A five metre wide passage ran in front of the rooms and was fifty-four metres long. The rooms’ doors faced north.
[Yehezkel] [42]:[5] But the upper halls were smaller, because the walkways there used more space than they did in the bottom and middle levels of the building.
[Yehezkel] [42]:[6] The third storey halls had no pillars (unlike the courtyards), so the rooms at the highest level were smaller than those on the bottom and middle levels.
[Yehezkel] [42]:[7] The outside wall ran along the rooms toward the outer courtyard that was in front of the rooms, and was twenty-seven metres long.

[Yehezkel] [42]:[14] When the priests enter it, they must not go back out of the sacred area to the outer courtyard, without laying aside the clothes in which they served, since those clothes are sacred. So they must dress in other clothes before going back into the public areas.”

[Yehezkel] [42]:[16] He measured each side of the wall with his measuring rod, and it was 270m long on each of the eastern, northern, southern, and western sides.
[Yehezkel] [42]:[20] So the four sides that were measured (and thus the wall around it) was 270m on each side, and the wall separated the sacred area from the public area.
[Yehezkel] [43]:[1] Then the man took me to the gate that opened to the east.
[Yehezkel] [43]:[2] Wow! The splendour of Yisrael’s (Israel) god appeared towards the east. His voice was like the roar of rushing water, and the land shone with his brilliance.
[Yehezkel] [43]:[3] What I saw in this vision was like what I’d seen in my earlier visions, first by the Kevar Canal, then later when he came to destroy Yerushalem (Jerusalem). I fell to my knees with my face to the ground.
[Yehezkel] [43]:[4] So Yahweh’s brightness entered into the temple via the eastern entrance.
[Yehezkel] [43]:[5] Then the spirit lifted me up and brought me into the inner court, and wow, Yahweh’s brilliance was filling the temple.
[Yehezkel] [43]:[6] Then as the man was standing there beside me, I heard someone speak to me from inside the temple,
[Yehezkel] [43]:[7] and the voice told me, “Son of humanity, this is the place where I’ll sit on my throne and rest my feet—where I’ll live in the middle of the Israeli people forever. Yisrael’s descendants and their kings will no longer profane my sacred name with their faithlessness or with the corpses of their kings at their hilltop shrines.
[Yehezkel] [43]:[8] They’ll no longer profane my sacred name by putting their entrance next to my entrance, and their doorposts next to my doorposts, with nothing but a wall between me and them. They profaned my sacred name with their disgusting actions, so I destroyed them with my anger.
[Yehezkel] [43]:[9] Now they’re to remove their prostitution and their kings’ corpses from in front of me, and I’ll live among them forever.
[Yehezkel] [43]:[10] “Son of humanity, describe that temple to the Israeli people so they’ll be ashamed of their disobedience and think about those plans.
[Yehezkel] [43]:[11] If they’re ashamed of everything they’ve done, then reveal the design of that temple to them—its details, its entrances and exits, its complete design, and all its decrees and rules. Then right in front of them, write that down so they’ll see its complete design and all its rules, and then obey them.
[Yehezkel] [43]:[12] This is the regulation for the temple: From the peak of the hill to all the surrounding border around it, it’ll be very sacred. Listen, that’s the regulation for the temple.
[Yehezkel] [43]:[13] These are the altar’s measurements, using the same kind of measuring rod that was used for the temple area: There’s a gutter around the altar that’s both half a metre deep and wide. There’s a rim around it that’s 23cm wide. That’ll be the base for the rest of the altar.
[Yehezkel] [43]:[14] The lower part of the gutter is one metre high to the lower ledge that surrounds the altar. The lower ledge is half a metre wide. From that ledge to the upper ledge, it’s two metres. That ledge is also half a metre wide.
[Yehezkel] [43]:[15] The altar body at the top is another two metres high and has a hornlike projection jutting up from each of its corners.
[Yehezkel] [43]:[16] The sides of the square body are six metres long.
[Yehezkel] [43]:[17] The upper ledge that borders the altar body is also a square, eight metres long on each side, and has a rim all around that’s 27cm wide. There’s a gutter measuring half a metre at the bottom of the altar. There are steps leading up to the east side of the altar.”
[Yehezkel] [43]:[18] Then the man told me, “Son of humanity, the master Yahweh says that those are the dimensions for when they make the altar for presenting the burnt offering on, and for sprinkling blood onto.
[Yehezkel] [43]:[19] You must give a bull from the cattle as a sin offering for the Levitical priests who are Tsadok’s descendants—those who approach me to serve me. That’s the master Yahweh’s declaration.
[Yehezkel] [43]:[20] Then you’ll take some of the bull’s blood and place it on the altar’s ‘horns’ and on the four top edges and the surrounding rim. You’ll purify it and make it allowable in my presence.
[Yehezkel] [43]:[21] Then take that sin offering bull and burn it in the designated part of the temple area outside the sanctuary.
[Yehezkel] [43]:[22] Then on the second day, you’ll get from the goats a male goat without any blemishes, and offer it as a sin offering—the priests will purify the altar just as they purified it with the bull.
[Yehezkel] [43]:[23] When you finish that purification, offer an unblemished bull from the cattle and an unblemished ram from the flock,
[Yehezkel] [43]:[24] and offer them to me, Yahweh. The priests will throw salt onto them and present them as a burnt offering to Yahweh.
[Yehezkel] [43]:[25] Then every day for the next seven days you must bring a billy goat to the priest to be sacrificed for an offering, so I’ll accept the altar. You must also sacrifice a young bull and a ram, each without any defect, that the priests will provide.
[Yehezkel] [43]:[26] They must atone for the altar for seven days and purify it, and in that way they must consecrate it to me.
[Yehezkel] [43]:[27] After doing all that, from the eighth day onward the priests will prepare you people’s burnt offerings and your peace offerings on the altar, and I’ll accept you. That’s the master Yahweh’s declaration.”
[Yehezkel] [44]:[1] Then the man took me back to the outer sanctuary gate facing east, but it was shut,
[Yehezkel] [44]:[2] and Yahweh told me, “This gate has been sealed shut—it won’t be opened. No person will go through it, because Yisrael’s (Israel) god Yahweh entered through it, so it’s now closed.
[Yehezkel] [44]:[3] Only Yisrael’s ruler will sit by it to eat food in front of Yahweh, but he’ll enter via the gate’s porch, and leave the same way.”
[Yehezkel] [44]:[4] Then he took me to the front of the temple by way of the northern gate, and I looked, and wow, Yahweh’s brilliance filled his temple, and I fell to my knees with my face bowed towards the ground.
[Yehezkel] [44]:[5] Then Yahweh told me, “Son of humanity, pay attention and look with your eyes and listen with your ears to everything that I’m declaring to you: all the instructions about Yahweh’s temple and all its regulations. Take special note of the temple’s entrance and exits.
[Yehezkel] [44]:[6] Then tell the rebellious Israelis that the master Yahweh says this: Let all your disgusting actions be enough for you Israeli people—
[Yehezkel] [44]:[7] that you brought foreigners with uncircumcised hearts and uncircumcised flesh to be in my sanctuary, profaning my temple, while you people were offering me food, fat, and blood. You people have broken my agreement with all your disgusting actions.
[Yehezkel] [44]:[8] You haven’t carried out your duties regarding my sacred things, but instead, you people appointed others to take up your duties, and you assigned them to care for my sacred place.
[Yehezkel] [44]:[9] “The master Yahweh says this: No foreigner, from any of those who live among the Israeli people, may enter my sacred place if they’re not physically circumcised or if they haven’t declared themself to be one of my people.
[Yehezkel] [44]:[10] The Levites went far from me—wandering away from me and going after their idols, but they’ll be punished.
[Yehezkel] [44]:[11] They’re still servants in my sanctuary, watching the temple gates and serving inside, and they slaughter the burnt offerings and the people’s sacrifices, and they’ll stand in front of the people and serve them.
[Yehezkel] [44]:[12] However, because they sacrificed to their idols, they became sinful stumbling blocks for the Israeli people, therefore I’ve promised to take action against them, and they’ll pay for their disobedience. That’s the master Yahweh’s declaration.
[Yehezkel] [44]:[13] They mustn’t come near to me to act as my priests or to approach any of my sacred things, the most sacred things. Instead, they’ll bear their shame and their guilt for the disgusting things they’ve done,
[Yehezkel] [44]:[14] but I’ll place them as housekeepers in the temple—for all its mundane duties and all the menial work that’s done in it.
[Yehezkel] [44]:[15] Then the Levitical priests, those descendants of Tsadok who fulfilled the duties of my sanctuary when the Israeli people were wandering away from me, they’ll approach me to worship me. They’ll stand in front of me to offer me the fat and the blood. That’s the master Yahweh’s declaration.
[Yehezkel] [44]:[16] They’ll come to my sanctuary and approach my table to worship me and to fulfill their duties to me.
[Yehezkel] [44]:[17] When they come to the gates of the inner courtyard, they’ll have to dress in linen clothing, because they mustn’t wear wool inside the courtyard gates or in the temple.
[Yehezkel] [44]:[18] They must wear linen turbans on their heads and linen underclothes around their waists. They mustn’t dress in clothing that makes them sweat.
[Yehezkel] [44]:[19] When they go back out to the outer courtyard to go back again to the people, they must take off the clothes they wore when they served—they must take them off and lay them down in a sacred room, so they don’t make other people sacred by contact with their special clothing.
[Yehezkel] [44]:[20] The priests mustn’t shave their heads or allow their hair to hang loosely, but they must keep the hair on their heads neatly trimmed.
[Yehezkel] [44]:[21] No priest should drink wine before he comes to the inner court.
[Yehezkel] [44]:[22] Also, priests can’t marry widows of men who weren’t priests, or women who’ve been divorced—they’re permitted to marry only Israeli women who’ve never been married, or widows of other priests.
[Yehezkel] [44]:[23] They must teach the people the difference between things that are sacred and things that are not, and teach them how to know what things are acceptable to me and what things are not.
[Yehezkel] [44]:[24] In a dispute they must judge in accordance with my instructions and regulations. They must keep my law and my statutes at every religious celebration, and they must observe my sacred rest days.
[Yehezkel] [44]:[25] Priests mustn’t defile themselves by going near a person’s dead body. However, if the dead person was his father or mother, son or daughter, or brother or unmarried sister, then they can defile themselves,
[Yehezkel] [44]:[26] and after they’ve been purified, they must wait for seven days.
[Yehezkel] [44]:[27] Then after that, when he goes into the inner courtyard to serve in the sacred place, he must bring a sin offering for himself. That’s the master Yahweh’s declaration.
[Yehezkel] [44]:[28] The priests must not own any land—I am their inheritance and I’ll be their property.
[Yehezkel] [44]:[29] They’ll have the food offerings, the sin offerings, and the guilt offerings to eat, plus everything in Yisrael (Israel) that’s devoted to Yahweh will be theirs.
[Yehezkel] [44]:[30] The best of the firstfruits from every harvest and every contribution from the people will belong to the priests, and you Israelis will give the first of your bread dough to the priests so that blessing may rest on your home.
[Yehezkel] [44]:[31] Priests must not eat the meat of any bird or animal that’s found dead or that’s been killed by any other animal.
[Yehezkel] [45]:[1] When you throw dice to divide up the land as an inheritance for the tribes, you must make an offering of land to Yahweh. That offering will become a sacred part of the land: thirteen kilometres by ten kilometres in size. That entire area will become sacred.
[Yehezkel] [45]:[2] Within that area, a 270m wide square area that’ll surround the sacred place will be left empty, with a further border around it twenty-seven metres wide.
[Yehezkel] [45]:[3] Inside that first, larger area, measure a rectangle thirteen kilometres by five kilometres for the sanctuary—the most sacred place.
[Yehezkel] [45]:[4] It’ll be a sacred place in the nation for the priests who serve Yahweh, who come near Yahweh to serve him. It’ll be a place for their houses and a sacred area for the sacred place.
[Yehezkel] [45]:[5] The other half, which is also thirteen kilometres long and five kilometres wide, will be for towns for the Levites who serve in the temple.
[Yehezkel] [45]:[6] You’ll designate an area thirteen kilometres long by half a kilometre wide for the city that will be next to the area reserved for the holy place. This city will belong to all the Israeli people.
[Yehezkel] [45]:[7] The leader’s land will be on both sides of the area reserved for the holy place and the city—on the west and the east. Its length will be the same as those portions that it’s parallel to.
[Yehezkel] [45]:[8] That area will belong to Yisrael’s (Israel) leader so the leaders won’t keep oppressing my people, but rather they’ll give the rest of the land to be divided among the tribes.
[Yehezkel] [45]:[9] The master Yahweh says this: That’s plenty for you, leaders of Yisrael! Replace your violence and strife with justice and righteousness. Quit your evictions of my people. That’s the master Yahweh’s declaration.
[Yehezkel] [45]:[10] You Israelis must use accurate scales and measuring containers.
[Yehezkel] [45]:[11] The baskets for measuring dry things and containers for measuring liquids (called an ‘efah’ for dry things and a ‘bath’ for liquids, both a tenth of the large 220 litre ‘homer’) must be the same volume—each must hold twenty-two litres.
[Yehezkel] [45]:[12] For weights, the shekel weight must be ten grams. (Twenty ‘gerahs’ makes one shekel, then sixty shekels makes one ‘mina’.)
[Yehezkel] [45]:[13] You Israelis must present to the leader one measure of wheat or barley for every sixty measures that you harvest,
[Yehezkel] [45]:[14] one measure of olive oil for every one hundred measures that you produce,
[Yehezkel] [45]:[15] plus one sheep or goat from the flock for every two hundred animals from the watered regions of Yisrael (Israel), to be used for any burnt offering or peace offering to make atonement for the people. That’s the master Yahweh’s declaration.
[Yehezkel] [45]:[16] All the people in the country will give that contribution to Yisrael’s leader.
[Yehezkel] [45]:[17] It’ll be the leader’s responsibility to supply the animals for the burnt offerings, the grain offerings, and the drink offerings at the festivals and the new moon celebrations, and on the rest days—all the Israeli people’s scheduled festivals. He’ll provide for the sin offerings, the grain offerings, the burnt offerings, and the peace offerings to make the Israeli people right with God.
[Yehezkel] [45]:[18] The master Yahweh says this: On the first day of the first month of the year, you must take an unblemished bull from the herd and perform a sin offering to purify the temple.
[Yehezkel] [45]:[19] The priest will take some of the blood of that sin offering and place it on the doorposts of the temple and on the four corners of the border of the altar, and on the doorposts of the gate to the inner court.
[Yehezkel] [45]:[20] You’ll do this again on the seventh day of that month for each person’s accidental sin, or sin by ignorance. In that way you’ll make the temple pure in God’s sight.
[Yehezkel] [45]:[21] Then on the fourteenth day of that first month, you Israelis will have a seven-day celebration, when you’ll eat bread made without any raising agent.
[Yehezkel] [45]:[22] That same day, the leader will prepare a bull as a sin offering for himself and for all the people in the country.
[Yehezkel] [45]:[23] For the seven days of the celebration, the leader will prepare a burnt offering for Yahweh: Seven bulls and seven unblemished rams each day for seven days, and a male goat each day as a sin offering.
[Yehezkel] [45]:[24] Then the leader will perform a food offering of twenty-two litres of flour with seven litres of olive oil for each bull and each ram.
[Yehezkel] [45]:[25] On the fifteenth day of the seventh month of the year, at the ‘temporary shelters’ celebration, the leader will perform offerings on those seven days: Sin offerings, burnt offerings, food offerings, and offerings of oil.
[Yehezkel] [46]:[1] The master Yahweh says this: The eastern gate of the inner courtyard will be shut for the six days of work, but it’ll be opened on rest days and on the day of the new moon.
[Yehezkel] [46]:[2] The leader will enter the outer courtyard by the path to that gate and its outside porch, and he’ll stand at the doorposts of the inner gate while the priests perform his burnt offering and peace offering. Then he’ll worship right there at the inner gate and then leave again, but the gate won’t be shut until evening.
[Yehezkel] [46]:[3] The people will also worship in front of Yahweh at the entrance to that gate on rest days and new moons.
[Yehezkel] [46]:[4] The burnt offering that the leader offers to Yahweh on the rest day will be six unblemished lambs and an unblemished ram.
[Yehezkel] [46]:[5] The grain offering that he gives with the ram is twenty-two litres of flour, and with the lambs it should be as much as he pleases, along with one litre of olive oil for every twenty-two litres of flour.
[Yehezkel] [46]:[6] On the day of the new moon he must offer a bull, six lambs, and a ram—all without any defects.
[Yehezkel] [46]:[7] He must also provide a grain offering of twenty-two litres of flour with the bull, the same with the ram, and as much as he wants with the lambs, along with a litre of olive oil with every twenty-two litres of flour.
[Yehezkel] [46]:[8] The leader enters by the path to the gate and its porch, and he must leave by the same path.
[Yehezkel] [46]:[9] But when the land’s people come in front of Yahweh at the scheduled festivals, anyone entering through the north gate to worship must leave through the south gate, and anyone entering through the south gate must leave through the north gate. No one is allowed to turn back to the gate through which they entered, because everyone must keep going straight ahead until they get out.
[Yehezkel] [46]:[10] The leader must be amongst them in their midst—when they go in, he must go in, and when they leave, he must leave.
[Yehezkel] [46]:[11] During the festivals that you hold for me, the king must present twenty-two litres of flour along with a bull or a ram, and as much flour as he wants to with the lambs, along with a litre of olive oil with every twenty-two litres of flour.
[Yehezkel] [46]:[12] When the leader gives a voluntary offering to Yahweh (either a burnt offering or a peace offering), the eastern gate will be opened for him. He’ll offer his burnt offering or his peace offering just like he does on the rest day. Then he must go out, and after he’s gone out, the gate will be shut.
[Yehezkel] [46]:[13] In addition, every morning someone must provide a one year old lamb with no defects to be completely burnt up as an offering to Yahweh.
[Yehezkel] [46]:[14] Also every morning someone must provide an offering of four litres of flour mixed with a litre of olive oil, and that’s a permanent requirement.
[Yehezkel] [46]:[15] They’ll prepare the lamb, the grain offering, and the oil, every morning—a permanent daily burnt offering.
[Yehezkel] [46]:[16] The master Yahweh says this: If the leader gives a gift to any of his sons, it becomes his inheritance—that is, it’ll become his sons’ property because it’s an inheritance.
[Yehezkel] [46]:[17] But if he gives a gift from his inheritance to one of his servants, then it’ll belong to that servant until the year of liberty, and then it’ll return to the leader. His inheritance must definitely be for his own sons.
[Yehezkel] [46]:[18] The leader mustn’t take the people’s inheritance away from them, evicting them from their own property—he must provide for his sons from his own property so that my people won’t be forced off their own inherited land.”
[Yehezkel] [46]:[19] Next the man brought me through the entrance at the gate to the sacred rooms for the priests which were north-facing, and what’s more, there was a place toward the west.
[Yehezkel] [46]:[20] He told me, “That’s the place where the priests must boil the guilt offering and the sin offering and where they must bake the grain offering. They mustn’t bring the offerings into the outer courtyard, because then the people would become sacred (and not be able to leave).”
[Yehezkel] [46]:[21] Then he brought me to the outer courtyard and led me past the four corners of that courtyard, and I saw that in every corner of the courtyard there was another enclosed area,
[Yehezkel] [46]:[22] and each was twenty-two metres long and sixteen metres wide.
[Yehezkel] [46]:[23] Around the inside of each of those enclosed areas was a stone ledge, with cooking hearths all around under the ledge.
[Yehezkel] [46]:[24] The man told me, “Those are the places where the temple workers will boil the people’s sacrifices.”
[Yehezkel] [47]:[1] Then the man took me back to the temple entrance, and there was water flowing out from under the front edge of the building toward the east, and the water was flowing down the south side of the temple, to the right of the altar.
[Yehezkel] [47]:[2] So he took me out through the northern gate and led me around the outside to the eastern gate, and look, the water was flowing from this gate on its south side.
[Yehezkel] [47]:[3] As the man started walking toward the east holding his measuring line in his hand, he measured off five hundred metres and led me through the water, which was ankle-deep.
[Yehezkel] [47]:[4] Then he measured another five hundred metres and led me through the water, which was now knee-deep, and then after another five hundred metres it was up to the waist.
[Yehezkel] [47]:[5] Finally he measured off another five hundred metres, but the water had become deep enough to swim in and too deep to cross—it was now a river that couldn’t be walked through.
[Yehezkel] [47]:[6] The man asked me, “Son of humanity, have you taken note of all this?” Then he led me out and had me return along the riverbank.
[Yehezkel] [47]:[7] As I walked back, wow, now the riverbank had many trees on each side.
[Yehezkel] [47]:[8] The man told me, “This water flows eastward and down into the Rift Valley. It’ll flow into the Dead Sea and will make it into fresh water.
[Yehezkel] [47]:[9] As a result, every kind of living creature that swarms will live where that water flows. There’ll be lots of fish when that water flows into the Dead Sea as it causes the salty water to become fresh water—everything will live wherever that river goes.
[Yehezkel] [47]:[10] Then the fishermen from Eyn-Gedi will stand there by the water, and there’ll be a place to dry out the fishing nets near Eyn-Eglayim. There’ll be many kinds of fish in the Dead Sea—plentiful just like the fish in the Mediterranean Sea.
[Yehezkel] [47]:[11] However, the Dead Sea’s swamps and marshes won’t be made fresh—they’ll be for providing salt.
[Yehezkel] [47]:[12] Beside that river on both banks, all kinds of fruit trees will grow. Their leaves will never wilt, and they’ll never fail to fruit—in fact they’ll bear fruit every month because that water from the temple flows to them. Their fruit will be good to eat, and their leaves will help with healing.
[Yehezkel] [47]:[13] The master Yahweh says that this will be the way that you divide the land up for Yisrael’s (Israel) twelve tribes: Yosef (Joseph) will have a double allocation.
[Yehezkel] [47]:[14] You’re to equally divide the land that I took action to give to your ancestors—from now on that land will come to you Israelis as an inheritance.
[Yehezkel] [47]:[15] These will be the land boundaries: On the north side, it’ll extend from the Mediterranean Sea east along the road towards Hetlon, and then on to Tsedad,
[Yehezkel] [47]:[16] to Berotah, and then on to Sivrayim, which is on the border between Damesek (Damascus) and Hamat. The boundary will run as far as Hatsar-Hatikon, which is on the border of the Havran region.
[Yehezkel] [47]:[17] So the boundary will extend from the Mediterranean Sea to Hatsar-Eynan on the border between Hamat to the north and Damesek to the south. That’ll be the northern boundary.
[Yehezkel] [47]:[18] On the eastern side, the boundary will extend between Havran and Damesek, south along the Yarden (Jordan) River between the Gilead region and Yisrael’s territory, along the Dead Sea as far as Tamar. That’ll be the eastern boundary.
[Yehezkel] [47]:[19] On the southern side, the boundary will extend from Tamar to the springs near Merivah-Kadesh. Then it’ll extend west along the brook of Mitsrayim (Egypt) to the Mediterranean Sea. That’ll be the southern boundary.
[Yehezkel] [47]:[20] On the western side, the boundary will be the Mediterranean Sea, north to a point near Levo-Hamat.
[Yehezkel] [47]:[21] This is how you’ll divide this land for yourselves among Yisrael’s tribes:
[Yehezkel] [47]:[22] You must assign the land as a permanent possession for yourselves and also for any foreigners who are living and raising their children among you. You must consider them to be like native born Israelis, and they must be assigned land among Yisrael’s tribes.
[Yehezkel] [47]:[23] Wherever foreigners are living, you must give them some land to belong to them permanently. That’s the master Yahweh’s declaration.”
[Yehezkel] [48]:[1] Here’s a list of Yisrael’s (Israel) tribes and the territory that each tribe is to receive. The northern boundary of Yisrael will start at the Mediterranean Sea and go east to Hetlon city, then to Levo-Hamat, and farther on to Hatsar-Eynan, which is south of Damesek (Damascus), and it’ll continue to Hamat. Each tribe will receive land that will extend from the eastern boundary of Yisrael west to the Mediterranean Sea. The tribe of Dan will receive land alongside Yisrael’s northern border.
[Yehezkel] [48]:[2] South of their area will be the territory for the tribe of Asher.
[Yehezkel] [48]:[3] South of Asher’s land will be territory for the tribe of Naftali (Naphtali).
[Yehezkel] [48]:[4] South of Naftali’s land will be territory for the tribe of Menasheh (Manasseh).
[Yehezkel] [48]:[5] South of Menasheh’s land will be territory for the tribe of Efrayim (Ephraim).
[Yehezkel] [48]:[6] South of Efrayim’s land will be territory for the tribe of Re’uven.
[Yehezkel] [48]:[7] South of Re’uven’s land will be territory for the tribe of Yehudah (Judah).
[Yehezkel] [48]:[8] South of Yehudah’s (Judah) land will be an area that the entire nation will give to me—you Israelis will set it apart for special use. The temple will be in the middle of the area that’s thirteen kilometres wide and as long as the other land allocations.
[Yehezkel] [48]:[9] The special area that you Israelis will give to Yahweh will be thirteen kilometres long and five kilometres wide.
[Yehezkel] [48]:[10] This special area will be allocated to the priests: you’ll assign them an area of land measuring thirteen kilometres on the northern and southern sides, and five kilometres on the western and eastern sides. Yahweh’s temple will be in the middle of that special area.
[Yehezkel] [48]:[11] The temple area will be for the priests, Tsadok’s descendants, who are dedicated to serving me. (They’re the ones who served me faithfully and didn’t turn away from me like the Levites and the others did.)
[Yehezkel] [48]:[12] The priests’ allocation will be a portion of that very sacred land, extending to the Levites’ border.
[Yehezkel] [48]:[13] The land assigned to the Levites will be the same size as the land that the priests will receive. (So together, these two portions of land will be thirteen kilometres long and about ten kilometres wide.)
[Yehezkel] [48]:[14] They mustn’t sell or barter it—none of this best part of Yisrael’s (Israel) land must ever be used for any other purpose, because it’s all sacred to Yahweh.
[Yehezkel] [48]:[15] Another strip of land thirteen kilometres long and almost three kilometres wide will be allotted for other people living in the special area to use. They may build homes and have pasturelands there, and there’ll be a city in the middle of that area.
[Yehezkel] [48]:[16] The city will be square, over two kilometres long on each side,
[Yehezkel] [48]:[17] with an open area around it, within the special area, that will be about 130m wide in each direction.
[Yehezkel] [48]:[18] Outside the city, there’ll be two strips that’ll extend five kilometres on each of the east and west sides, and the produce from those strips will be food for the people working in the city.
[Yehezkel] [48]:[19] Those who come from the various tribes to work in the city may also work in this farmland.
[Yehezkel] [48]:[20] That entire special area, including the land given for Yahweh’s use and the city, will be a square that’s thirteen kilometres long on each side.
[Yehezkel] [48]:[21] The tracts of land to the east and to the west of Yahweh’s area and the city will belong to the leader. One area will extend thirteen kilometres east to Yisrael’s eastern boundary, and the other will extend thirteen kilometres west to the Mediterranean Sea. Yahweh’s area, which contains the temple, will be in the middle.
[Yehezkel] [48]:[22] The area that belongs to the leader (that surrounds the Levites’ property and the city in the middle of it) will be between the tribe of Yehudah (Judah) to the north and the tribe of Benyamin to the south.
[Yehezkel] [48]:[23] South of Yahweh’s area, each of the other tribes will receive one section of land that extends from the eastern boundary of Yisrael west all the way to the Mediterranean Sea. Just south of Yahweh’s area will be territory for the tribe of Benyamin.
[Yehezkel] [48]:[24] South of Benyamin’s land will be the land for the tribe of Shim’on (Simeon).
[Yehezkel] [48]:[25] South of Shim’on’s land will be the land for the tribe of Yisakar (Issachar).
[Yehezkel] [48]:[26] South of Yisakar’s land will be the land for the tribe of Zevulun.
[Yehezkel] [48]:[27] South of Zevulun’s land will be the land for the tribe of Gad.
[Yehezkel] [48]:[28] Gad’s southern boundary will extend from Tamar south to the waters of Merivah-Kadesh, and farther west to the brook of Mitsrayim (Egypt), and then on to the Mediterranean Sea.
[Yehezkel] [48]:[29] That describes the territory you’ll allocate to Yisrael’s tribes to become their permanent inheritance. That’s the master Yahweh’s declaration.
[Yehezkel] [48]:[30] These will be the exits from the city: On the northern side (which will be just over two kilometres long),
[Yehezkel] [48]:[31] there’ll be three gates named after the tribes of Re’uven, Yehudah (Judah), and Levi.
[Yehezkel] [48]:[32] On the eastern side (the same length) there’ll be three gates named after the tribes of Yosef (Joseph), Benyamin, and Dan.
[Yehezkel] [48]:[33] On the southern side (the same length) there’ll be three gates named after the tribes of Shim’on (Simeon), Yisakar (Issachar), and Zevulun.
[Yehezkel] [48]:[34] On the western side (the same length) there’ll be three gates named after the tribes of Gad, Asher, and Naftali (Naphtali).
[Yehezkel] [48]:[35] The distance around the city will be nine kilometres. From that time onwards, the city’s name will be ‘Yahweh is there’.
[Daniyel] [1]:[1] In the third year of Yehudah’s (Judah) King Yehoyakim’s reign, Bavel’s (Babylon) King Nevukadnetsar (Nebuchadnezzar) came to Yerushalem (Jerusalem) and besieged the city.
[Daniyel] [1]:[2] After two years, the master allowed King Yehoyakim to be defeated by Nevukadnetsar who then took some of the items out of the temple and took them to Shin’ar where he placed them in his god’s temple storerooms.
[Daniyel] [1]:[3] Some time later, King Nevukadnetsar commanded his chief official Ashpenaz to bring him some of the young Israeli men, from both their royal family and from some of the prominent families.
[Daniyel] [1]:[4] They had to be good-looking young men without obvious defects, wise and well-educated, who would be competent for future work in the palace. They would be taught the language and literature of the Kasdim (Chaldeans),
[Daniyel] [1]:[5] and king assigned a daily portion of food and wine for them from his own table. They would be trained for three years before entering the king’s service.
[Daniyel] [1]:[6] Among the young men from Yehudah who were chosen were Daniyel, Hananyah, Mishael, and Azaryah,
[Daniyel] [1]:[7] but Ashpenaz named them Belteshatsar (Belteshazzar), Shadrak, Meyshak, and Aved-Nego respectively.
[Daniyel] [1]:[8] However Daniyel decided that he wouldn’t eat the king’s fancy food or drink his wine because it wasn’t all ‘kosher’, so he requested permission from Ashpenaz to eat an alternative diet.
[Daniyel] [1]:[9] Now God had caused the chief official to like and respect Daniyel,
[Daniyel] [1]:[10] but he queried, “I’m afraid of my master the king, who’s assigned your food and drink—if he saw you guys looking worse than the others of your own age then I’d risk losing my head if the king got angry.”
[Daniyel] [1]:[11] So Daniyel asked the steward that Ashpenaz had assigned over the four of them,
[Daniyel] [1]:[12] “Please test your servants for ten days: let us be given some vegetables to eat and water to drink,
[Daniyel] [1]:[13] then after that, see how we look compared to the other young men who eat the king’s choice food. Then you can make the best decision from the evidence.”
[Daniyel] [1]:[14] So the steward agreed to that and started the ten-day trial.
[Daniyel] [1]:[15] At the end of the ten days, they looked better and healthier than all the young men who’d been eating the king’s fancy food,
[Daniyel] [1]:[16] so after that, the steward just gave them vegetables to eat instead of the choice food and wine.
[Daniyel] [1]:[17] So God gave those four young men knowledge and insight into all literature, and wisdom, and Daniyel was able to interpret any dreams and visions.
[Daniyel] [1]:[18] At the end of the three years when the king ordered them to be brought in, the chief official Ashpenaz brought them in to King Nevukadnetsar (Nebuchadnezzar).
[Daniyel] [1]:[19] The king talked with each of them and realised that none of the others were as capable as Daniyel, Hananyah, Mishael, and Azaryah, so they ended up in the king’s service—
[Daniyel] [1]:[20] in every matter of wisdom and understanding which the king asked them about, he found them ten times better than all the magicians and astrologers from throughout his entire kingdom.
[Daniyel] [1]:[21] Daniyel continued serving there through to the first year of the reign of King Koresh (Cyrus).
[Daniyel] [2]:[1] Back in the second year of King Nevukadnetsar’s (Nebuchadnezzar) reign, the king had had some dreams that troubled him—leaving him unable to sleep.
[Daniyel] [2]:[2] He summoned the magicians, fortune-tellers, sorcerers, and astrologers to explain the dreams to him, so they came in and stood in front of the king.
[Daniyel] [2]:[3] “I’ve had a dream,” the king told them, “and my spirit is anxious to understand it.”
[Daniyel] [2]:[4] The astrologers spoke to the king in Aramit, “Long live King Nevukadnetsar. Tell us what you dreamt, and then we’ll give you the interpretation.”
[Daniyel] [2]:[5] “I’ve already made my decision,” the king replied. “If you all can’t tell me the dream and then give its interpretation, you’ll all be torn limb from limb and your houses made into a rubbish heap.
[Daniyel] [2]:[6] But if you all explain the dream and its interpretation, you’ll receive gifts from me, and a reward and great honour. So tell me the dream and its interpretation.”
[Daniyel] [2]:[7] “Let the king tell his servants the dream,” they insisted, “and we’ll give the interpretation.”
[Daniyel] [2]:[8] “I know for certain that you’re all trying to gain time,” the king answered. “However, I’ve made up my mind
[Daniyel] [2]:[9] that if you all don’t tell me what my dream was, then your fate is already clear because you’ve obviously agreed together to keep feeding me with lies and made-up stories until I give in. So then, tell me what my dream was, and then I’ll be confident that you can give me its interpretation.”
[Daniyel] [2]:[10] “There’s no one in the whole world who could tell the king that,” the astrologers answered the king. “No great and powerful king has asked any magician or enchanter or astrologer to do that before!
[Daniyel] [2]:[11] What you’re requesting, your majesty, is difficult, and no human can tell you what you dreamt—only the gods.”
[Daniyel] [2]:[12] That angered the king, and he got so furious that he ordered for all the Babylonian wise men to be executed.
[Daniyel] [2]:[13] When the decree went out that all the wise men were to be rounded up to be executed, Daniyel and his friends were included.
[Daniyel] [2]:[14] Areyok was the captain of the king’s guards who’d been sent to execute the Babylonian wise men, but Daniyel spoke to him with wise and prudent caution.
[Daniyel] [2]:[15] He asked the king’s commander Areyok, “Why did the king come to that sudden decision?” Areyok explained what had happened,
[Daniyel] [2]:[16] so Daniyel went to the king and requested some time so he would be able to give the interpretation to him.
[Daniyel] [2]:[17] Then Daniyel went back to his house and told his companions Hananyah, Mishael, and Azaryah
[Daniyel] [2]:[18] so they might beg for mercy from the god of the heavens concerning the mystery of the dream, so that all of them might not be executed along with the rest of the Babylonian wise men.
[Daniyel] [2]:[19] Then the mystery was revealed to Daniyel in a vision during the night. Aftewrwards, Daniyel blessed the god of the heavens
[Daniyel] [2]:[20] saying, “Let God’s name be blessed forever and ever, because all wisdom and power belong to him.
[Daniyel] [2]:[21] He moves the times and seasons forwards. He removes some kings and gives power to others. It’s him who gives wisdom to the wise and knowledge to those who have understanding.
[Daniyel] [2]:[22] He reveals the deep and hidden things—he knows what is in the darkness, and the light lives with him.
[Daniyel] [2]:[23] Oh God of my ancestors, I thank you and praise you for the wisdom and power you have given to me. Now you’ve revealed to me what we asked you about because you’ve told us what the king is wanting to know.”
[Daniyel] [2]:[24] So Daniyel went to Areyok, the man that the king had appointed to execute Bavel’s (Babylon) wise men, and told him, “Don’t hurt the wise men in Bavel. Take me in to the king and I’ll tell him the dream and its interpretation.”
[Daniyel] [2]:[25] Areyok quickly took Daniyel in to the king and told him, “I’ve found a man among the exiles from Yehudah (Judah) who will reveal the interpretation of your dream.”
[Daniyel] [2]:[26] “Are you able to tell me the dream that I saw, and its interpretation?” the king asked Daniyel (also called Belteshatsar (Belteshazzar)).
[Daniyel] [2]:[27] “No wise men, enchanters, magicians, or astrologers are able to do what the king has demanded,” replied Daniyel.
[Daniyel] [2]:[28] “However, there is a god in the heavens who reveals mysteries, and he’s the one who’s shown you, King Nevukadnetsar (Nebuchadnezzar), what will happen in the days to come. This was your dream and the visions in your mind while you were in your bed:
[Daniyel] [2]:[29] Oh king, as you lay there your thoughts turned to what would happen in the future, and the one who reveals mysteries showed you what is going to happen.
[Daniyel] [2]:[30] As for me, this mystery was revealed to me, not because I’m wiser than anyone else, but so that the interpretation could be revealed to the king, and so that you can understand what you saw in your mind.
[Daniyel] [2]:[31] “What you were looking at, your majesty, was an incredible, huge statue. It was heavy and shone brightly as it stood there in front of you—a terrifying sight.
[Daniyel] [2]:[32] The statue’s head was made of pure gold, its chest and arms were silver, its belly and thighs were bronze,
[Daniyel] [2]:[33] its legs were made of iron, and its feet were a combination of iron and clay.
[Daniyel] [2]:[34] You continued looking until a stone was supernaturally cut out from a mountain, and it tumbled down and struck the statue on its feet of iron and clay, and it smashed them to pieces.
[Daniyel] [2]:[35] Then the iron, the clay, the bronze, the silver, and the gold were crushed all at the same time and became like the small pieces of dry straw at harvest time in the summer. Then the wind carried them away so that no trace of them could be found, but the stone that struck the statue became a huge mountain that then filled the whole world.
[Daniyel] [2]:[36] “That was the dream, and now we’ll tell the king its meaning:
[Daniyel] [2]:[37] You, your majesty, are the king of kings who has been given the kingdom, the power, the strength, and the splendour by the god of the heavens.
[Daniyel] [2]:[38] Wherever people live, he’s placed you in charge of them, and he’s even put you over the animals in the countryside and the birds in the skies, so you’re the statue’s gold head.
[Daniyel] [2]:[39] But another less prominent kingdom will follow yours, then another kingdom of bronze to rule over all the earth after that.
[Daniyel] [2]:[40] Then there’ll be a fourth kingdom that’s strong as iron—because iron crushes and shatters all things. Like an iron sledge-hammer that smashes things into pieces, it will smash all those others into broken pieces.
[Daniyel] [2]:[41] And as you saw the feet and toes, a mixture of iron and potter’s clay, it will be a divided kingdom—some of the iron’s strength will be in it, just as you saw iron mixed with the soft clay.
[Daniyel] [2]:[42] As the feet were partly iron and partly clay, so that kingdom will be partly strong and partly weak.
[Daniyel] [2]:[43] As you saw the iron mixed with soft clay, so various peoples will make alliances with each other, but they won’t stick together just as iron doesn’t integrate with clay.
[Daniyel] [2]:[44] In the days of those kings, the god of the heavens will establish a kingdom that will never be destroyed or taken over by others. It will crush all those kingdoms and put an end to them, but it will stand forever.
[Daniyel] [2]:[45] Just as you saw that a stone was supernaturally cut out of the mountain, and that it crushed the iron, the bronze, the clay, the silver, and the gold, the powerful God has revealed to the king what will happen in the future. The dream is true, and its interpretation is trustworthy.”
[Daniyel] [2]:[46] Then King Nevukadnetsar (Nebuchadnezzar) fell to his knees with his face to the ground to worship Daniyel, and he commanded that a burnt offering and incense be offered up to him.
[Daniyel] [2]:[47] The king said to Daniyel, “It’s true that your god is the god of gods and the master of masters, and the one who reveals mysteries, because you’ve been able to reveal this mystery.”
[Daniyel] [2]:[48] Then the king gave Daniyel high honours and gave him many great gifts, and he made him ruler over the whole province of Bavel (Babylon) and chief supervisor over all of Bavel’s wise men.
[Daniyel] [2]:[49] Daniyel asked the king to appoint Shadrak, Meyshak, and Aved-Nego over the administration of the Babylonian province, but Daniyel remained at the king’s court.
[Daniyel] [3]:[1] King Nevukadnetsar (Nebuchadnezzar) had a gold statue made that stood nearly thirty metres high and was almost three metres wide, and it was erected on the Dura plain in the Babylonian province.
[Daniyel] [3]:[2] Then King Nevukadnetsar sent for the various levels of governors, the counsellors, the treasurers, the judges, the magistrates, and all the provincial officials, to all come to the dedication of the statue that he’d erected.
[Daniyel] [3]:[3] So all those officials assembled in front of the statue that the king had set up, ready for the dedication.
[Daniyel] [3]:[4] Then the herald loudly proclaimed, “You peoples, nations, and languages are commanded
[Daniyel] [3]:[5] that any time you hear the sound of the horn, flute, lyre, harps, pipes, and other instruments, you all must bow down and worship the gold statue that King Nevukadnetsar has erected.
[Daniyel] [3]:[6] Anyone who refuses to bow down and worship it at that time, will be thrown into a blazing furnace.”
[Daniyel] [3]:[7] So when all those people who had gathered heard the sounds made by the musical instruments, they all bowed down to worship the gold statue.
[Daniyel] [3]:[8] But some Chaldean astrologers went to the king to make trouble for the Yehudim (Jews).
[Daniyel] [3]:[9] They reported to King Nevukadnetsar (Nebuchadnezzar), “Long live the king.
[Daniyel] [3]:[10] Oh king, you’ve made a decree that every man who hears the sound of the musical instruments, must bow down and worship the gold statue,
[Daniyel] [3]:[11] but anyone who doesn’t bow and worship will be thrown into a fiery furnace.
[Daniyel] [3]:[12] Now, there are certain Yehudim who you’ve appointed over the administration of the province of Bavel (Babylon): Shadrak, Meyshak, and Aved-Nego. These men, your majesty, don’t take any notice of you: they don’t serve your gods, or worship the gold statue that you’ve set up.”
[Daniyel] [3]:[13] Then Nevukadnetsar in a furious rage commanded that Shadrak, Meyshak, and Aved-Nego be arrested. Then they were brought to the king
[Daniyel] [3]:[14] who questioned them, “Shadrak, Meyshak, and Aved-Nego, is it true that you won’t serve my gods or worship the gold statue that I set up?
[Daniyel] [3]:[15] Now if you’re ready, as soon as you hear the musical instruments of music, if you all bow down and worship the statue I erected, everything will be okay. But if you don’t, you’ll immediately be thrown into a blazing hot furnace. Then what god could rescue you from my punishment?”
[Daniyel] [3]:[16] “Oh Nevukadnetsar,” the three of them answered the king, “we don’t need to answer that last question.
[Daniyel] [3]:[17] If that’s what happens to us, the god that we serve is able to rescue us from the blazing fire and from your punishment. He will save us, your majesty.
[Daniyel] [3]:[18] But just so it’s clear your majesty, even if he doesn’t, we won’t serve your gods or worship that gold statue.”
[Daniyel] [3]:[19] That made Nevukadnetsar (Nebuchadnezzar) absolutely furious and it could be seen in his face. He ordered that the furnace be made seven times hotter than usual
[Daniyel] [3]:[20] and commanded some of his top warriors to tie up Shadrak, Meyshak, and Aved-Nego and then to throw them into the blazing furnace.
[Daniyel] [3]:[21] So while still fully dressed even with their turbans still on, they were tied up and thrown into the middle of the furnace where the fire was blazing.
[Daniyel] [3]:[22] Unfortunately, because of the king’s insistent command, the furnace was extremely hot and the flames killed the men who threw them in,
[Daniyel] [3]:[23] but Shadrak, Meyshak, and Aved-Nego fell into the roaring flames while still securely tied up.
[Daniyel] [3]:[24] Then King Nevukadnetsar was startled and jumped up and asked his counsellors, “Wasn’t it three who were tied up that were thrown there into the middle of the fire? “Certainly, your majesty,” they replied.
[Daniyel] [3]:[25] “Look there, then!” he responded. “I can see four men walking in the middle of the fire, and they’re not tied up and they’re not hurt, and the fourth one looks like a young god.”
[Daniyel] [3]:[26] Then Nevukadnetsar went over by the furnace door and called out, “Shadrak, Meyshak, and Aved-Nego, servants of the Most High God, come out, and come over here!” Then the three men walked out from the middle of the fire.
[Daniyel] [3]:[27] All the king’s officials gathered around them and saw that the fire hadn’t harmed them—their hair wasn’t even singed, their cloaks weren’t damaged, and they didn’t even smell like smoke.
[Daniyel] [3]:[28] Nevukadnetsar spoke, “Praise the god of Shadrak, Meyshak, and Aved-Nego. He sent his angel and rescued his servants who had put their trust in him. They took objection to the king’s command at the cost of their own lives, rather than serve or worship any god except their god.
[Daniyel] [3]:[29] I hereby make a decree that any people, nation, or language that speaks anything offensive against the god of Shadrak, Meyshak, and Aved-Nego will have their houses made into rubbish heaps and they’ll be torn limb from limb, because there’s no other god who’s able to save people like that.”
[Daniyel] [3]:[30] Then the king gave Shadrak, Meyshak, and Aved-Nego more important positions in Bavel (Babylon) province than they had before.
[Daniyel] [4]:[1] King Nevukadnetsar (Nebuchadnezzar) sent this message to all people groups, nations, and languages that live all over the world: May you have peace and prosperity.
[Daniyel] [4]:[2] It seemed good to me to let you all know about the amazing miracles that the supreme God has done for me.
[Daniyel] [4]:[3] The miracles he does are incredible, and his acts of creation are powerful. His kingdom will last forever, and his authority goes from one generation to another.
[Daniyel] [4]:[4] I, Nevukadnetsar, was doing well at home, and prospering at my work in my palace,
[Daniyel] [4]:[5] but one night as I lay in bed, I had a dream that scared me—the images and visions in my head terrified me.
[Daniyel] [4]:[6] So I summoned all of Bavel’s (Babylon) wise men to come and tell me the interpretation of the dream.
[Daniyel] [4]:[7] When those magicians, fortune-tellers, sorcerers and astrologers arrived, I told them the dream, but they didn’t know the interpretation.
[Daniyel] [4]:[8] Finally, Daniyel came in—he’d been named Belteshatsar (Belteshazzar) after my god’s name. The spirit of the holy gods is in him, and I told him the dream:
[Daniyel] [4]:[9] “Oh Belteshatsar, chief of the magicians, since I know that the spirit of the holy gods is in you and that no mystery is too difficult for you, go through the visions of my dream and tell me their interpretation.
[Daniyel] [4]:[10] This is the vision that was in my mind as a lay in bed: I was looking and was surprised to see a very tall tree growing in the middle of a field.
[Daniyel] [4]:[11] The tree kept growing taller and stronger until its top reached the sky and it could be seen from all over the world.
[Daniyel] [4]:[12] It had beautiful leaves were beautiful and lots of fruit on it. It provided food for everything, the animals in the countryside found shade under it, and the birds of the sky lived in its branches. Every living thing benefitted from it.
[Daniyel] [4]:[13] I was looking at the visions in my mind as I lay in bed, and then, wow, a holy sentinel came down from the heavens.
[Daniyel] [4]:[14] He shouted loudly, ‘Chop that tree down and cut its branches off, strip off its leaves, and scatter its fruit. Let the animals run away from under it and the birds from its branches.
[Daniyel] [4]:[15] But leave the stump with its roots in the ground, and bind it with a band of iron and bronze. Let it become wet with the dew in the tender grass of the field, accompanied only by those animals that live in the grass.
[Daniyel] [4]:[16] Let his mind be changed from a man to an animal as seven periods pass over him.
[Daniyel] [4]:[17] That sentence is by the decree of the sentinels, and the decision is a command of the holy ones, so that the living may know that the highest one is ruler over human kingdoms and gives them to whoever he wants—even to those who seem unimportant.’
[Daniyel] [4]:[18] I, King Nevukadnetsar (Nebuchadnezzar), had this dream. Now you, Belteshatsar (Belteshazzar), tell me the interpretation, because none of the wise men in my kingdom can tell me the interpretation. But you can, because the spirit of the holy gods is in you.”
[Daniyel] [4]:[19] Daniyel (also known as Belteshatsar (Belteshazzar)) was appalled for a while at the meaning of the dream, and worried how to present it. The king saw this and said, Belteshatsar, don’t hold back on being honest about the dream its interpretation.” “My master,” he answered, “If only the dream was for those who hate you, and its interpretation was for your enemies.
[Daniyel] [4]:[20] You saw that tree that grew and became strong, and whose top reached the sky and was visible all over the world,
[Daniyel] [4]:[21] with its beautiful leaves and plentiful fruit. It provided food for everyone, and the animals from the countryside lived under it, and the birds lived in its branches.
[Daniyel] [4]:[22] That was you, your majesty. You’ve grown and become strong—your greatness has grown and reaches to heaven, and your dominion to the ends of the earth.
[Daniyel] [4]:[23] Then the king saw a holy sentinel coming down from heaven and saying, ‘Chop down the tree and destroy it, but leave the stump and the roots in the ground, bound with a band of iron and bronze, in the tender grass of the countryside, and let him be wet with the dew, and let him live with the animals of the fields until seven periods of time pass over him.’
[Daniyel] [4]:[24] “Your majesty, this is the interpretation: It’s actually the decree of what the supreme God has declared will happen to you, my master the king.
[Daniyel] [4]:[25] You will be driven away from society and you’ll live with the animals in the countryside. You’ll be forced to eat grass like a bull, and you’ll sleep on the ground and be wet with dew in the morning for seven years until you acknowledge that the highest one is ruler over humankind and learn that he gives kingdoms to whoever he wants.
[Daniyel] [4]:[26] But just as it was commanded to leave the stump of the tree with its roots, so too your kingdom will be restored to you from the time you recognise that heaven rules over earth.
[Daniyel] [4]:[27] Therefore, your majesty, please consider my advice: stop sinning and do what is right, and stop disobeying God by starting to show mercy to the oppressed, so that perhaps your prosperity might be prolonged.”
[Daniyel] [4]:[28] But all of that did happen to King Nevukadnetsar (Nebuchadnezzar).
[Daniyel] [4]:[29] Twelve months later, he was walking on the upper terrace of the royal palace in Bavel (Babylon)
[Daniyel] [4]:[30] when he looked across and said, “Isn’t that the great Bavel, which I’ve built as a royal residence by the strength of my power and for the glory of my majesty?”
[Daniyel] [4]:[31] He’d only just finished saying that when he heard a voice in the sky, “It’s now decreed to you, King Nevukadnetsar: you’ve just lost your kingdom.
[Daniyel] [4]:[32] You’ll be driven away from other people, and you’ll live will be with the animals out in the countryside where you’ll have to eat grass like a cow. Seven years will pass before you acknowledge that the highest one is ruler over mankind and he gives kingdoms to whoever he wants.”
[Daniyel] [4]:[33] Immediately what had been said in advance happened to Nevukadnetsar. He was driven away from society. He ate grass like a cow, and his body was wet with dew each morning after sleeping on the ground. Eventually his hair had grown long like eagles’ feathers, and his nails were long like birds’ claws.
[Daniyel] [4]:[34] “After the seven years, I, Nevukadnetsar (Nebuchadnezzar) looked up toward heaven and my reason returned to me. Then I praised and honoured the highest one who lives forever, because his authority is everlasting and his kingdom endures through the generations.
[Daniyel] [4]:[35] Compared to him, all the inhabitants of the earth are insignificant like ants—he issues his commands to the heavenly army and to earth’s inhabitants. No one can hold back his hand or has any right to ask him, ‘What have you done?’ ”
[Daniyel] [4]:[36] “At that time my sanity returned to me, and I was reestablished in my kingdom. My majesty and my splendour was restored to me as I became again the respected leader of my kingdom. My counsellors and my nobles wanted to be in my company, and I became even more powerful than I was before.
[Daniyel] [4]:[37] Now I, Nevukadnetsar, praise, extol, and honour the king of the heavens, because everything he does is, and his methods are just, and he’s able to humble those who become proud.
[Daniyel] [5]:[1] Several years later when Belshatsar (Belshazzar) was king, he put on a feast for a thousand of his nobles, and he was drinking wine with them all.
[Daniyel] [5]:[2] As Belshatsar was drinking the wine, he remembered the gold and silver cups that his father Nevukadnetsar (Nebuchadnezzar) had taken from the temple in Yerushalem (Jerusalem), and ordered that they be brought in so that the king and his nobles, and his wives and his concubines, could drink from them.
[Daniyel] [5]:[3] So they brought in the gold cups that had been taken out of God’s residence in Yerushalem, then the king and his nobles, his wives and his concubines, drank from them.
[Daniyel] [5]:[4] They drank the wine and praised the gods of gold and silver, bronze, iron, wood, and stone.
[Daniyel] [5]:[5] Suddenly, the fingers of a human hand appeared and started writing on the plaster on the king’s palace wall, opposite the lampstand. When the king saw the back of the hand that was writing,
[Daniyel] [5]:[6] he was very frightened and the colour drained from his face. His legs felt weak and his knees started knocking together,
[Daniyel] [5]:[7] and he called out for the enchanters, the Kasdim (Chaldeans), and the astrologers to be brought in. The king told those Babylonian wise men, “Anyone who can read this writing and tell me its interpretation will be dressed in royal robes and will have a chain of gold placed around his neck, and he’ll become the third ruler in the kingdom.”
[Daniyel] [5]:[8] When all the king’s wise men of the king got there, none of them could read the writing or tell the king what it meant.
[Daniyel] [5]:[9] Then King Belshatsar became more afraid, his face went whiter still, and his nobles also had no idea what to do.
[Daniyel] [5]:[10] My now the queen had heard about what the king and his noblemen had been saying, so she came into the banquet house and said, “Long live the king. Don’t let this get under your skin. Don’t let it drain you.
[Daniyel] [5]:[11] There’s a man in your kingdom who has the spirit of the holy gods in him. In the days of your father, this man has illumination and insight and wisdom like the wisdom of the gods. Your father King Nevukadnetsar (Nebuchadnezzar) appointed him chief of the magicians, sorcerers, Kasdim, and astrologers,
[Daniyel] [5]:[12] because this Daniyel had an excellent spirit, knowledge, and insight for interpreting dreams, explaining riddles, and solving problems. So summon Daniyel who the king named Belteshatsar (Belteshazzar) and he’ll tell you the interpretation.”
[Daniyel] [5]:[13] So Daniyel was brought in to the king who said to him, “So, you’re that Daniyel—one of the exiles that my father the king brought from Yehudah (Judah).
[Daniyel] [5]:[14] I’ve heard about you—heard that the spirit of the gods is in you, and that you have illumination and insight and excellent wisdom.
[Daniyel] [5]:[15] Now the wise men and enchanters were brought in here to read this writing on the wall and tell me its interpretation, but they couldn’t interpret it.
[Daniyel] [5]:[16] But I’ve heard about you—that you’re able to give interpretations and solve problems. Now, if you’re able to read that writing and tell me what it means, you’ll be clothed with kingly robes and have a chain of gold placed around your neck, and you’ll be made the third-highest ruler in the kingdom.”
[Daniyel] [5]:[17] “I’m not after your gifts, and your rewards can be given to someone else,” Daniyel responded. “But, I’ll read the writing to the king and I’ll tell you the interpretation.
[Daniyel] [5]:[18] “As for you, your majesty, the highest god gave the kingship, power, honour, and majesty, to your father Nevukadnetsar (Nebuchadnezzar).
[Daniyel] [5]:[19] Because of that power, all peoples, nations, and ethnic groups trembled and were afraid when his army approached. He killed whoever he wanted, and he kept alive those he wanted. He promoted whoever he wanted, and he humiliated others when he wanted to.
[Daniyel] [5]:[20] But when he became proud and stubborn and started acting presumptuously, he was disqualified from the throne, and his splendid reputation was deflated.
[Daniyel] [5]:[21] He was driven right out of the community, and he started behaving like an animal—he ended up living with wild donkeys and eating grass like a cow. [Daniyel] [5]:[22] “Yet you, Belshatsar (Belshazzar), his son, haven’t humbled yourself despite already knowing all that.
[Daniyel] [5]:[23] On the contrary, you’ve proudly promoted yourself as being greater than the master of the heavens. You brought the temple cups in here and you and your nobles, your wives and your concubines, have drunk wine from them. You praised the gods made from silver and gold, bronze, iron, wood, and stone, which can’t see, or hear, or know anything, yet you haven’t honoured the god who decides your future and every breath that you take.
[Daniyel] [5]:[24] “So then it’s from his presence that the palm of a hand was sent, and this message was written.
[Daniyel] [5]:[25] This is how it reads, ‘Numbered, numbered, weighed, and divided,’
[Daniyel] [5]:[26] and this is what it means: Numbered: God has numbered your days of leadership and brought them to an end,
[Daniyel] [5]:[27] Weighed: You’ve been weighed on the scales and found deficient, and
[Daniyel] [5]:[28] Divided: Your kingdom has been divided and given to the Madim (Medes) and the Persians.”
[Daniyel] [5]:[29] Then Belshatsar (Belshazzar) gave an order, and they placed a purple robe over Daniyel’s shoulders and a gold chain was placed around his neck, and an official announcement was made that he would now be the third-highest ruler in the kingdom.
[Daniyel] [5]:[30] However, the Chaldean King Belshatsar was killed that very night,
[Daniyel] [5]:[31] and Dareyavesh (Darius) the Madi (Mede) became the new ruler at an age of around sixty-two.
[Daniyel] [6]:[1] The new King Dareyavesh (Darius) decided to divide the kingdom into 120 provinces with a governor over each one.
[Daniyel] [6]:[2] Over them were three higher officials (Daniyel was one of them) that those governors were accountable to so that the king wouldn’t be ripped off,
[Daniyel] [6]:[3] but because Daniyel was exceptionally talented, he became noticed above the other high officials and governors, and the king decided to appoint him over the whole kingdom.
[Daniyel] [6]:[4] That led the high officials and the governors to try to find some fault with Daniyel with regard to his administrative duties. However, they weren’t able to find any misdemeanours or corruption that he could be accused of because he was honest, reliable, and diligent.
[Daniyel] [6]:[5] Then these men concluded, “We won’t find any grounds for making an accusation against this Daniyel unless we find something against him to do with the laws of his god.”
[Daniyel] [6]:[6] So those high officials and governors made a plan and went as a group to the king and made this suggestion, “Long live your majesty, King Dareyavesh.
[Daniyel] [6]:[7] All the high officials of the kingdom, the various leaders, the counsellors, and the governors have consulted together that the king should establish and enforce a law that for thirty days, anyone who makes a request of any god or of any man other than you, your majesty, shall be thrown into the lions’ den.
[Daniyel] [6]:[8] Now, your majesty, sign the document and establish this law so that it can’t then be revoked according to the law of the Madim (Medes) and Persians.”
[Daniyel] [6]:[9] So King Dareyavesh signed the document and it became law.
[Daniyel] [6]:[10] However although Daniyel knew that that law had been passed, he still went into his house (with the windows in his upper room open toward Yerushalem (Jerusalem)), and he continued to kneel three times a day to pray and give thanks to God, just as he’d always done.
[Daniyel] [6]:[11] Then those officials went as a group and found Daniyel praying to his god and presenting him with his requests.
[Daniyel] [6]:[12] Then they approached the king and reminded him about the law, “Didn’t you introduce a law that within thirty days, any man who makes a petition to any god or man, except to you, your majesty, must be thrown into the lions’ den?” “Yes, that’s correct,” answered the king. “It can’t be revoked now according to the law of the Madim and Persians.”
[Daniyel] [6]:[13] Then they informed the king, “Daniyel who was exiled from Yehudah (Judah), pays no attention to you, your majesty, or to the law that you introduced, because he petitions his god three times a day.”
[Daniyel] [6]:[14] When the king heard that, was very upset and for that entire day, he actively tried to think of a way to get Daniyel out of it.
[Daniyel] [6]:[15] However, the group of men returned to the king and said, “You know, your majesty, that it’s a law of the Madim and Persians, that no rule or law that the king establishes can be changed.”
[Daniyel] [6]:[16] So the king gave an order, and Daniyel was brought in and the king responded and told him, “May your god, who you serve continually, save you.” Then Daniyel was thrown down into the lions’ den.
[Daniyel] [6]:[17] A stone was brought and laid over the opening of the den, and the king sealed it with his own signet ring and with the signet rings of his nobles so that no one could sneak Daniyel out.
[Daniyel] [6]:[18] Then the king went to his palace and spent the night without eating. He refused all entertainment, and he couldn’t sleep.
[Daniyel] [6]:[19] Then the king got up at dawn, and hurried out to the lions’ den.
[Daniyel] [6]:[20] As he approached the den, he called out in a worried voice, “Daniyel, Daniyel, servant of the living god. Has your god, who you serve continually, been able to save you from the lions?”
[Daniyel] [6]:[21] “Long live the king,” Daniyel called back.
[Daniyel] [6]:[22] “My god sent his angel and shut the lions’ mouths, and they haven’t hurt me, because he saw that I wasn’t guilty of anything. Also, your majesty, I haven’t wronged you in any way.”
[Daniyel] [6]:[23] Then the king was very happy, and ordered that Daniyel be pulled up out of the den. So Daniyel was lifted out of the den, and he didn’t even have a scratch on him, because he had trusted in his god.
[Daniyel] [6]:[24] Then the king ordered the arrest of the men who had maliciously accused Daniyel, and had them and their wives and children thrown into the lions’ den—they didn’t even reach the bottom of the den before the lions overpowered them and tore them to pieces.
[Daniyel] [6]:[25] Then King Dareyavesh (Darius) wrote to all the peoples, nations, and ethnic groups right across his kingdom: “May you all be enjoying peace and prosperity.
[Daniyel] [6]:[26] I decree that everyone throughout my kingdom is to obey and respect Daniyel’s god, because he is the eternal, living God. His kingdom will never be destroyed, and his rule will continue forever.
[Daniyel] [6]:[27] He delivers and rescues, and he does all kinds of miracles in the heavens and on earth. He’s rescued Daniyel from the strength and power of the lions.”
[Daniyel] [6]:[28] So Daniyel prospered during the reign of Dareyavesh and during the reign of Koresh (Cyrus) the Persian.
[Daniyel] [7]:[1] Previously, in Babylonian King Belshatsar’s (Belshazzar) first year, Daniyel had seen a dream and visions in his mind while lying on his bed. Then he wrote the dream down and gave a summary of it.
[Daniyel] [7]:[2] He explained: In my vision at night I was looking, and suddenly, the four winds were stirring up the massive ocean,
[Daniyel] [7]:[3] and four huge creatures, each one different from the other, were coming up out of it.
[Daniyel] [7]:[4] The first one was like a lion but had the wings of an eagle. But as I watched, its wings were torn off, and it was lifted up and made to stand on two feet like a man, and then it was given a human mind.
[Daniyel] [7]:[5] The second creature resembled a bear with one arm raised. It was chomping on three ribs and it was told to go and gorge itself on more meat.
[Daniyel] [7]:[6] Next I saw another creature that resembled a leopard, but with four wings (like birds’ wings) attached to its back, and with four heads. It was given the authority to rule people.
[Daniyel] [7]:[7] The final creature that I saw in the vision was dreadful and terrifying. It was extremely strong with large iron teeth and it was devouring things then trampling and crushing the remainder. Another difference from the other creatures was that it had ten horns on its head.
[Daniyel] [7]:[8] While I was considering the horns, suddenly another horn, a little one, came up among the others and three of the first horns that were in its way got pulled completely out. Incredibly, this new had eyes like a person and a mouth that had a lot of incredible things to say.
[Daniyel] [7]:[9] I kept looking in the vision while thrones were set up and the ancient one took his seat. His clothing was as white as snow, and his hair looked like pure wool. His throne was flaming with fire, and its wheels were burning fire.
[Daniyel] [7]:[10] A river of fire was coming out and flowing along in front of him. Thousands and thousands served him, and myriads upon myriads were standing in front of him. The court sat in session and the documents were opened.
[Daniyel] [7]:[11] Then I continued looking because of the amazing things that the horn was saying. I kept looking until that final creature was killed and its body destroyed in the fire.
[Daniyel] [7]:[12] As for the other creatures, their authority to rule was taken away, but an extension of life was given to them for a season and a time.

[Hoshea] [1]:[2] When Yahweh first spoke through Hoshea (Hosea), he told him, “Go and get yourself a prostitute for a wife and have children from her, because the country is committing flagrant prostitution by forsaking Yahweh.”
[Hoshea] [1]:[3] So he went and married Divlayim’s daughter Gomer, and she got pregnant and bore him a son.
[Hoshea] [1]:[4] Then Yahweh told him, “Name him Yizre’el (Jezreel), because in a little while I’ll avenge the blood shed in the Yizre’el valley on Yehu’s (Jehu) family, and I’ll put an end to the kingdom of Yisrael (Israel).
[Hoshea] [1]:[5] At that time in the Yizre’el valley, I’ll break Yisrael’s military power.”
[Hoshea] [1]:[6] Then Gomer conceived again and bore a daughter, and Yahweh told Hoshea, “Name her Lo-Ruhamah (which means ‘No mercy’), because I’ll no longer have mercy on the Israelis, and I won’t forgive them at all.
[Hoshea] [1]:[7] But I’ll have mercy on Yehudah’s (Judah) descendants, and I’ll save them so they’ll be able to see that it was their god Yahweh. (I won’t save them using bows, swords, battles, horses, or horsemen.)”
[Hoshea] [1]:[8] After she’d weaned Lo-Ruhamah, she got pregnant again and bore a second son.
[Hoshea] [1]:[9] Then Yahweh said, “Name him Lo-Ami (which means ‘Not my people’) because you’re not my people and I’m not your god.”
[Hoshea] [1]:[10] Yet the number of Israelis will be like the sand on the seashore, which can’t be measured or counted. Then instead of being told, ‘You’re not my people,’ they’ll be told, ‘You are children of the living god.’

[Hoshea] [12]:[1] Efrayim/Yisrael feeds on the wind and pursues the east wind all day. He multiplies lies and violence. They make a covenant with Ashur (Assyria) and olive oil is carried to Mitsrayim (Egypt).

[Hoshea] [13]:[2] Now they disobey God more and more, and they make cast metal images for themselves— idols skillfully made from their silver— all of them the work of craftsmen. They say about them, ‘Those who sacrifice people, kiss calves.’
[Hoshea] [13]:[3] Therefore they’ll be like the morning clouds, and like the dew that goes away early, like the chaff that swirls from the threshing floor, and like smoke exiting an open window.
[Hoshea] [13]:[4] But I’m your god Yahweh who brought you out of Mitsrayim (Egypt), and you were to consider no god except me, because there’s no saviour other than me.
[Hoshea] [13]:[5] I knew you out there in the wilderness, in the region of drought.
[Hoshea] [13]:[6] When they had their pasture, then they became full. They were filled, and their heart became lifted up, so they just forgot me.
