[Hoshea] [13]:[14] Will I ransom them from the hand of the grave? Will I redeem them from death? Death, where are your plagues? Grave, where is your destruction? My eyes won’t be displaying any compassion.”

[Yoel] [1]:[1] This is Yahweh’s message that came to Petuel’s son Yoel (Joel):
[Yoel] [1]:[2] Hear this, you elders, and listen, all you people that live in this country. Has this sort of thing ever happened in your lifetime or in the days of your ancestors?
[Yoel] [1]:[3] Tell your children about it, and your children to their children, and their children to the following generation.
[Yoel] [1]:[4] What the cutting locusts left behind, the swarming locusts have eaten, and what the swarming locusts left behind, the hopping locusts have eaten, and what the hopping locusts left behind, the destroying locusts have eaten.
[Yoel] [1]:[5] Wake up, drunkards, and weep. Yes, wail, all you wine drinkers. Wail about the sweet wine, because it’s all gone now.
[Yoel] [1]:[6] Because a powerful nation (of locusts) with innumerable soldiers has come against my land, Its teeth are like a lion’s teeth, and the fangs are like those of a lioness.
[Yoel] [1]:[7] It’s made my grapevine into a piece of rubbish and my fig tree into splinters. Stripping everything, it’s stripped it and thrown it away. Its branches have become white (without the bark).
[Yoel] [1]:[8] Mourn like a young woman dressed in sackcloth after losing her young husband.
[Yoel] [1]:[9] The grain offering and the drink offering have been discontinued at Yahweh’s temple. The priests mourn—Yahweh’s servants.
[Yoel] [1]:[10] The countryside has been devastated. The soil mourns, because the grain has been destroyed. The new wine dried up, The fresh oil isn’t good.
[Yoel] [1]:[11] Feel shame, farmers, for the wheat and for the barley. Wail, vinedressers, because the harvest from the countryside has perished.
[Yoel] [1]:[12] The grapevine has dried up and the fig tree has been made weak. The pomegranate tree, also the palm tree and the apple tree, all of the trees across the countryside have dried up. →So humanity’s joy has dried up.
[Yoel] [1]:[13] Get dressed in sackcloth and sing dirges, you priests. Wail, you servants of the altar. Come, spend the night in sackcloth, servants of my god, because the grain offering and the drink offering have been withheld from the house of your god.
[Yoel] [1]:[14] Consecrate a fast, call an assembly. Gather the elders and all the residents of the country to the house of Yahweh your god, and cry out to Yahweh.
[Yoel] [1]:[15] What a terrible day, because Yahweh’s day is near, and it will come as destruction from the powerful one.
[Yoel] [1]:[16] Hasn’t our food been cut off right in front of our eyes, and joy and gladness cut off from God’s house?
[Yoel] [1]:[17] The seeds have shrivelled under their clods. The storehouses are in ruins. The granaries have been torn down, because the grain has dried up.
[Yoel] [1]:[18] How the livestock groan. The herds of cattle are perplexed, because there’s no pasture to graze. Also the flocks of sheep have suffered.
[Yoel] [1]:[19] I call for help to you, Yahweh, because fire has devoured the pastures in the wilderness, and the flame has burnt all the trees in the countryside.
[Yoel] [1]:[20] Even the wild animals pant for you, because the streams of water have dried up, and fire has destroyed the pastures in the wilderness.
[Yoel] [2]:[1] Blow the shofar in Tsiyon (Zion), and shout on the mountain of my holiness. Let all of the country’s residents tremble, because Yahweh’s day is coming, yes, it’s close.
[Yoel] [2]:[2] It’ll be a day of darkness and gloom— a day of clouds and thick darkness like the dawn being spread out on the mountains. There hasn’t been a great and mighty army like that since the beginning of time, and after it there won’t be again for many generations.
[Yoel] [2]:[3] A devouring fire goes ahead of it, and behind it a flame is burning. Ahead of it, the land is like the garden of Eden, but behind it is a wilderness of desolation, and indeed, there’s no escape from it.
[Yoel] [2]:[4] At first, it appears like horses, and they run like war horses.
[Yoel] [2]:[5] Like the sound of chariots, they leap along the tops of the hills— like the sound of flames devouring stubble, like a mighty people organised for war.
[Yoel] [2]:[6] People flinch in horror when they see them coming. All of their faces turn dark.
[Yoel] [2]:[7] They run like warriors. Like men of war, they climb the wall. Then they walk, each man choosing his own way forward, and they don’t veer off their paths.
[Yoel] [2]:[8] There’s no jostling each other— each man marches straight forward. They handle those who present weapons against them and their progress isn’t interrupted.
[Yoel] [2]:[9] They rush on the city. They run along the wall. They climb through the windows into the houses like thieves.
[Yoel] [2]:[10] The earth shakes as they approach. The heavens tremble. The sun and the moon become dark, and the stars cease their shining.
[Yoel] [2]:[11] Yahweh speaks in front of his army, because there’s a huge number of them, because those executing his commands are very powerful. Yes, Yahweh’s day is really terrible, and who could possibly survive it?
[Yoel] [2]:[12] Yahweh declares: Even now, return to me with all of your hearts, and with fasting and weeping, and with mourning.
[Yoel] [2]:[13] Yes, tear your hearts and not your clothes, and return to your god Yahweh, because he’s gracious and merciful, slow to get angry, but displaying loyal commitment, and relenting from sending disaster.
[Yoel] [2]:[14] Who knows? He might change his mind and relent and leave a blessing after him: grain and wine that you can all use as offerings for your god Yahweh.
[Yoel] [2]:[15] Blow the shofar in Tsiyon (Zion), declare a fast, announce an assembly.
[Yoel] [2]:[16] Gather the people, consecrate the congregation, assemble the elders, gather the children and the ones suckling the breasts. May the bridegroom come out from his chamber and the bride from her room.
[Yoel] [2]:[17] Let Yahweh’s servants the priests weep between the porch and the altar. And let them say, “Have pity on your people, Yahweh, and don’t allow others to mock the people that you inherited, and then other nations to rule over them. [Amos] [3]:[1] Hear this message that Yahweh has spoken against you, people of Yisrael (Israel), against Ya’akov’s (Jacob) descendants that I brought out of Mitsrayim (Egypt) saying:
[Amos] [3]:[2] “I have chosen only you from all the families of the earth, therefore I’ll punish you all for all your sins.”
[Amos] [3]:[3] Do two people walk together, without first agreeing to meet?
[Amos] [3]:[4] Would a lion roar in the forest when he doesn’t have any prey? Would a young lion growl from his den if he’s caught nothing?
[Amos] [3]:[5] Would a bird fall into a trap on the ground when no bait has been put in it? Would a trap just spring up from the ground when it hasn’t caught anything?
[Amos] [3]:[6] If a warning trumpet sounds in a city, won’t the people start to worry? If disaster comes to a city, wouldn’t it be Yahweh who sent it?
[Amos] [3]:[7] Surely the master Yahweh wouldn’t do anything unless he first reveals his plan to his servants the prophets.
[Amos] [3]:[8] The lion has roared—who won’t be afraid? The master Yahweh has spoken—who won’t prophesy?
[Amos] [3]:[9] Proclaim this in the fortresses at Ashdod, and in the strongholds in Mitsrayim (Egypt), saying, “Assemble yourselves on Shomron’s (Samaria) mountains and see what great confusion is in her, and what oppression is in her.
[Amos] [3]:[10] Yahweh declares that they don’t know how to do right. They store up violence and destruction in their fortresses.”
[Amos] [3]:[11] Therefore, this is what the master Yahweh says: “An enemy will surround the land, and pull down your strongholds and plunder your fortresses.”
[Amos] [3]:[12] This is what Yahweh says: “Just as the shepherd rescues out of the lion’s mouth two legs only, or a piece of an ear, so will the Israelis who live in Shomron (Samaria) be rescued with only the corner of a couch or a piece of a bed.”
[Amos] [3]:[13] Take notice of this and testify against Ya’akov’s (Jacob) descendants. i That is the declaration of the master Yahweh, army commander God.

[Yonah] [1]:[1] Now Yahweh told Yonah (Jonah) (Yonah, Amitay’s son),
[Yonah] [1]:[2] “Go now to the major city of Nineveh, and speak out against it because I’ve noticed how evil they are.”
[Yonah] [1]:[3] But Yonah decided to run away from Yahweh so he went down to Yafo (Joppa) and found a ship about to go to Tarshish. He paid the fare and went aboard to go with them to Tarshish to get away from Yahweh.
[Yonah] [1]:[4] However Yahweh caused a strong wind on the sea and it became a such big storm that they all thought the ship would disintegrate.
[Yonah] [1]:[5] The sailors were afraid and they each cried to their own gods for help, and they threw the cargo overboard to make the ship lighter. But Yonah had gone down into the hold where he had laid down and fallen fast asleep.
[Yonah] [1]:[6] So the ship’s captain approached him and said, “Why are you sleeping? Come on, pray to your god and perhaps he will take notice of us so we won’t die.”
[Yonah] [1]:[7] Then the sailors said to each other, “Let’s draw straws to find out whose fault it is that we are in this predicament.” So they drew straws and Yonah was indicated.
[Yonah] [1]:[8] So they said to him, “Hey, tell us why this disaster is happening to us. What’s your occupation? Where are you from? What country? What nationality are you?”
[Yonah] [1]:[9] And he said to them, “I’m a Ivri (Hebrew) and I fear Yahweh the god of the heavens who made the sea and the land.”
[Yonah] [1]:[10] And the men became really scared and asked him what he had done, because he had told them that he was running from Yahweh.
[Yonah] [1]:[11] So they asked him what they should do to him so that the sea would calm, because the storm was getting worse.
[Yonah] [1]:[12] And he said to them, “Pick me up and throw me into the sea so that the sea will calm down because I know that this terrible storm came because of me.”
[Yonah] [1]:[13] However, the men tried to row but they were not able to return to the land because the sea was very rough and getting worse.
[Yonah] [1]:[14] So they called to Yahweh and said, “We beg you Yahweh: please don’t let us die because of this man, and don’t consider us guilty because you yourself have made this happen.”
[Yonah] [1]:[15] And then they picked up Yonah and threw him into the sea, and the sea became calm.
[Yonah] [1]:[16] The men felt really scared of Yahweh and they sacrificed to him and made vows.
[Yonah] [1]:[17] Then Yahweh commanded a huge fish to swallow Yonah (Jonah) and he stayed in the belly of the fish for three days and three nights.
[Yonah] [2]:[1] And Yonah (Jonah) prayed to Yahweh his god from the belly of the fish.
[Yonah] [2]:[2] And he said, “I called to you Yahweh in my distress and you answered me. I cried for help from the valley of death and you heard my voice.
[Yonah] [2]:[3] You have thrown me right into the deep—the heart of the sea; and a flood surrounds me. All your waves are crashing over me.
[Yonah] [2]:[4] And I said, ‘I have been driven out of your sight however I will look again towards your holy temple.’
[Yonah] [2]:[5] I was up to my neck in the waters; it was deep all around me. There were reeds wrapped around my head.
[Yonah] [2]:[6] I went down to the foundations of the mountains; barred from returning to the land. But you saved my life from the grave, Yahweh my god.
[Yonah] [2]:[7] When my life was draining away from me, I remembered you, Yahweh, and my prayer reached you in your holy temple.
[Yonah] [2]:[8] Those who worship lifeless gods abandon their allegiance to you.
[Yonah] [2]:[9] But I’ll speak out my gratitude as I sacrifice to you. I’ve vowed this and I’ll do it, because Yahweh is my rescuer.”
[Yonah] [2]:[10] Then Yahweh spoke to the fish and it vomited Yonah (Jonah) up onto the land.
[Yonah] [3]:[1] And Yahweh spoke to Yonah (Jonah) a second time saying,
[Yonah] [3]:[2] “Go now to the major city, Nineveh, and announce this declaration which I’ve told you.”
[Yonah] [3]:[3] So Yonah went directly to Nineveh. It was a large city, taking three days to travel across.
[Yonah] [3]:[4] Yonah went one day’s travel into the city and publicly announced, “Nineveh is going to be destroyed in forty days!”
[Yonah] [3]:[5] The people of Nineveh believed in God and announced a time of fasting, and from the least to the most important people, they just wore sackcloth as a sign of contrition.
[Yonah] [3]:[6] The king of Nineveh also heard about it and he got down from his throne, took off his robe and put on sackcloth, then sat in a pile of ashes.
[Yonah] [3]:[7] And he had a statement written out and publicly read throughout Nineveh, saying, “The king and his advisors declare that people and livestock, be it herds or flocks, are prohibited from grazing or eating anything, and even from drinking water.
[Yonah] [3]:[8] Both people and livestock should just wear sacks, and they should use their strength to cry out to God and they should turn away from the evil and violent things they have been doing.
[Yonah] [3]:[9] And maybe God will turn and change his mind and stop his fierce anger, and maybe we won’t die.”
[Yonah] [3]:[10] And God saw their actions in turning away from their evil ways and he changed his mind about the destruction which he had said he would send to them and he didn’t proceed with it.
[Yonah] [4]:[1] But Yonah (Jonah) was very upset and the situation made him angry.
[Yonah] [4]:[2] And he said to Yahweh, “Please Yahweh, wasn’t this what I said would happen when I was still in my own country? That’s why I fled to Tarshish the first time, because I knew that you are a caring forgiving god, who doesn’t get angry quickly; full of kindness and not wanting to cause distress.
[Yonah] [4]:[3] So therefore Yahweh, please kill me because I’d rather die than live like this.”
[Yonah] [4]:[4] But Yahweh said, “Do you think it’s right to be angry like that?”
[Yonah] [4]:[5] And Yonah went outside the city to the east and made himself a shelter and sat there in the shade to see what would happen to the city.
[Yonah] [4]:[6] And Yahweh God commanded a plant and it grew up over Yonah to shade his head and to relieve him from his distress. Yonah was very pleased about the plant.
[Yonah] [4]:[7] Then at dawn the next day God commanded a grub and it attacked the plant which then shrivelled up.
[Yonah] [4]:[8] And when the sun came up, God sent a hot east wind and the sun beat on Yonah’s head. He became faint and asked for his life to end and said, “It’s better for me to die than to live.”
[Yonah] [4]:[9] And God said to Yonah, “Do you think it’s right to be angry about the plant?” And Yonah replied, “Yes, I’m angry enough to die!”
[Yonah] [4]:[10] Then Yahweh said, “You felt sorry for the plant which you didn’t even plant or work for. It came up in a day and died again in a day
[Yonah] [4]:[11] so shouldn’t I feel sorry for the huge city of Nineveh which has so many people in it who don’t know right from wrong—over 120,000 people, not to mention all the livestock!”
[Mikah] [1]:[1] This is Yahweh’s message that came to Mikah (from Morashet) in the days of Yehudah’s (Judah) kings Yotam (Jotham), Ahaz, and Hizkiyah (Hezekiah), that he saw concerning Shomron (Samaria) and Yerushalem (Jerusalem).
[Mikah] [1]:[2] Listen, all you peoples. Let the world and everything in it pay attention. Let my master Yahweh be against you as a witness, my master from his sacred temple
[Mikah] [1]:[3] because wow, Yahweh comes out of his place. He will come down and tread on the high places of the earth.
[Mikah] [1]:[4] The mountains will melt under him. The valleys will break apart, like wax that’s near a fire, like waters that are poured out from a steep place.
[Mikah] [1]:[5] All that is because of Ya’akov’s (Jacob) disobedience, and because of the sins of the Israeli people. What was Ya’akov’s transgression? Isn’t it Shomron (Samaria)? What is Yehudah’s (Judah) high place? Isn’t it Yerushalem (Jerusalem)?

[Mikah] [1]:[7] All her carved statues will be smashed into pieces, and all her wages will be burnt. Yes, I’ll totally destroy all her idols. Since she used prostitutes’ wages to pay for them, the crushed pieces of idols will become prostitutes’ wages again.”

[Mikah] [2]:[4] In that day someone will sing a song against you all. and mourn with a song of wailing, and say, ‘We’re completely ruined. Yahweh changes my people’s territory. How can he remove the land from me? He divides our fields up to give to traitors.’ ”

[Mikah] [2]:[9] You’ve driven our widows out of their pleasant houses. You’ve forever deprived their young children of what I’d blessed them with.

[Mikah] [2]:[13] Someone will go in front of them to break open the way. They’ll force open the gate and go out. Their king will pass on ahead of them. Yahweh will be at their head.
[Mikah] [3]:[1] Then I said, “Now listen, you leaders of Ya’akov (Jacob), and rulers of the house of Yisrael (Israel): Isn’t it your responsibility to understand justice?

[Nahum] [1]:[1] This document is a declaration about Nineveh city which was given to Nahum from Elkosh as a vision.
[Nahum] [1]:[2] Yahweh is a jealous God who avenges. Yahweh avenges and is full of anger. He takes vengeance on his opponents, and he continues to be angry with his enemies.
[Nahum] [1]:[3] Yahweh is slow to get angry, but very powerful. He certainly won’t allow guilty people to go unpunished. He walks among whirlwinds and storms, and clouds are like dust stirred up by his feet.
[Nahum] [1]:[4] He scolds the ocean and makes it sand. He dries up all the rivers. Bashan and Karmel wither up. He makes the flowers wilt in Levanon.
[Nahum] [1]:[5] The mountains shake when he appears, and the hills melt. The ground heaves at his presence— actually the entire world and all its residents.
[Nahum] [1]:[6] What can withstand his indignation? Who can resist his fierce anger? His anger is poured out like fire, and rocks shatter in front of him.
[Nahum] [1]:[7] Yahweh is good at sheltering us when trouble comes. He recognises those go to him for protection.
[Nahum] [1]:[8] He’ll completely destroy his opponents with a rushing flood. He will chase his enemies into the darkness.
[Nahum] [1]:[9] Whatever is plotted against Yahweh, he’ll completely destroy it. Trouble won’t return a second time.
[Nahum] [1]:[10] They’ll get tangled up as if in thorns, and they’ll walk like drunks. They’ll be burnt up completely like dry stubble.
[Nahum] [1]:[11] Someone in Nineveh made a decision, to plot evil against Yahweh. Someone with wicked plans.

[Nahum] [3]:[6] I throw disgusting filth at you and treat you with contempt. I’ll make a spectacle of you.
[Nahum] [3]:[7] Everyone who sees you will run away and say, ‘Nineveh is destroyed.’ Who will weep for her? Where can I find someone who’ll comfort her?
[Nahum] [3]:[8] Are you better than No city was, where the Nile surrounded and protected her? Where the water was one of her secure walls.
[Nahum] [3]:[9] Kush (Ethiopia) and Mitsrayim (Egypt) were her strength, and her strength had no limit. Put and Libya were her allies.
[Nahum] [3]:[10] Yet No was taken as an exile— taken into captivity. Her young children were dashed to pieces at the top of every street. Her captors threw dice for her nobles. All her leading men were bound in chains.
[Nahum] [3]:[11] You, too, will become drunk. You’ll look for places to hide. You’ll try to find somewhere to be safe from your enemies.
[Nahum] [3]:[12] All your fortresses will be like fig trees with the early fruit now ready. When they’re shaken the fruit falls right into the mouth of the eater.
[Nahum] [3]:[13] See, your troops are like weak women. Your city gates will be opened wide to your enemies— their cross-bars will be destroyed by fire.
[Nahum] [3]:[14] Get water from the wells to store for the siege. Strengthen your fortifications. Fetch clay and start working it. Get the molds ready to make bricks.
[Nahum] [3]:[15] Even so, fire will devour you. The sword will cut you down. They’ll chew you up like locusts. You need to multiply like locusts and grasshoppers.
[Nahum] [3]:[16] You have so many merchants— more than the stars in the sky. Like locusts, they strip valuables and then fly away.
[Nahum] [3]:[17] Your many guards are like locusts, and you have a swarm of officials. On a cold morning they settle on the walls, but when the sun rises they fly away to some place that nobody knows about.
[Nahum] [3]:[18] You, king of Ashur (Assyria), your shepherds have fallen asleep. Your nobles have settled down for a break. Your people will be scattered across the hills, with no one to gather them again.
[Nahum] [3]:[19] Your pain will get no relief— your wound is too severe. Everyone who hears the news about you will do a high-five, because there’s no one who hasn’t experienced your cruelty.
[Havakuk] [1]:[1] Here is the message that the prophet Havakuk (Habakkuk) saw:
[Havakuk] [1]:[2] For how long, Yahweh, must I call for help before you listen? I cry out about the violence, but you haven’t rescued me.
[Havakuk] [1]:[3] Why do I have to keep seeing injustice and looking at trouble? Destruction and violence are all around—there’s such strife, and conflicts keep happening.
[Havakuk] [1]:[4] That’s why the law is paralysed and why justice doesn’t prevail— because those who do good are surrounded by wicked people, so justice gets perverted.
[Havakuk] [1]:[5] Watch the other countries and observe them, and be astonished and amazed, because I’m about to do something in your time that no one will believe would happen, even if they were told about it.
[Havakuk] [1]:[6] Listen, I’m about to stir up the Babylonians— that fierce and impetuous empire that marches around the world to seize cities for themselves.
[Havakuk] [1]:[7] They’re dreaded and feared. They go by their own rules to boost their own pride.
[Havakuk] [1]:[8] Their horses are faster than leopards and more menacing than the wolves in the evening. So their horsemen arrive from a great distance, then come charging— they fly like an eagle that’s swift to devour.
[Havakuk] [1]:[9] They all come for violence— hordes of faces advancing like the wind in the wilderness. They gather captives like sand.
[Havakuk] [1]:[10] They scoff at kings, and rulers are just a joke to them. They laugh at fortresses as they pile soil up around them and capture them.
[Havakuk] [1]:[11] Then they sweep past like the wind and move on. They become guilty of thinking that their own strength is their god.
[Havakuk] [1]:[12] Yahweh, aren’t you the eternal God? You’re my heavenly protector who won’t die. Yahweh, you’ve appointed them for judgement. Our rock, you’ve established them for punishment.
[Havakuk] [1]:[13] Your eyes are too pure to endure seeing evil, and you’re not able to look on wrongdoing with favour. Why then have you tolerated those who are treacherous? Why are you silent while the wicked destroy those who are more godly than them?
[Havakuk] [1]:[14] You’ve made those people like the fish of the sea— like reptiles that have no ruler.
[Havakuk] [1]:[15] The invader brings them all up with a fishhook. He drags them up with his fishing net. He catches them all in his drag net, which makes him happily celebrate.
[Havakuk] [1]:[16] Therefore he sacrifices to his fishing net and burns incense to his drag net, because it’s his net that gives him plenty of food, and his food is the richest kind.
[Havakuk] [1]:[17] So will he keep harvesting with his net? Will he continue destroying nations without mercy?
[Havakuk] [2]:[1] I’ll stand at my guard post and station myself on the watchtower, and I’ll wait there to see what he will say to me, and how I should respond when I’m corrected.
[Havakuk] [2]:[2] Yahweh responded, saying: “Write this vision clearly onto tablets so that messengers can run with them and read them aloud.
[Havakuk] [2]:[3] This vision is for a future time, but in the end anyone waiting for it will see it happen, because when it comes, it won’t delay.
[Havakuk] [2]:[4] Listen, those who don’t have noble desires are puffed up, but godly people live by their faith.
[Havakuk] [2]:[5] Wine betrays the arrogant man so that he won’t rest. His appetite becomes like the cemetery—always wanting more, and like death which is never satisfied. The invader takes over all the nations, and captures every people group.
[Havakuk] [2]:[6] Won’t all those peoples create a saying to ridicule the invader and a taunting song and riddles about him? They’ll say ‘It won’t end well for those who take what doesn’t belong to them. As you take more and more, it will become heavier and heavier for you.’
[Havakuk] [2]:[7] Won’t those you’ve taken from suddenly organise themselves— won’t you tremble when they wake up? Then you’ll become spoil for them
[Havakuk] [2]:[8] because you’ve plundered many nations. All the remnants of the nations will plunder you because you’ve taken lives and acted with violence against the land and cities, and everyone who lives in them.
[Havakuk] [2]:[9] It won’t end well for anyone who’s used evil gains to furnish his house. He wanted to set his nest on high to keep himself safe from the hand of evil,
[Havakuk] [2]:[10] but because you’ve destroyed many nations, you’ve brought guilt onto yourself.
[Havakuk] [2]:[11] The stones in the wall will cry out, and the timber rafters will answer them.
[Havakuk] [2]:[12] It won’t end well for anyone who builds a city with blood, or who establishes a town with wickedness.
[Havakuk] [2]:[13] Listen, isn’t it Commander-in-chief Yahweh who ensures that those peoples are just playing with fire and those nations will just get exhausted from their efforts?
[Havakuk] [2]:[14] The world will be filled with the knowledge of Yahweh’s splendour as surely as the oceans are filled with water.
[Havakuk] [2]:[15] It won’t end well for anyone (nation) who forces their neighbour to drink— you’ll pour your anger out on them to make them drunk so that their nakedness becomes exposed.
[Havakuk] [2]:[16] You’ll be filled with shame instead of honour. Now it’s your turn—drink and then your uncircumcision will be exposed. The cup in Yahweh’s powerful right hand is coming around to you, and your honour will be covered over with disgrace.
[Havakuk] [2]:[17] The violence done to Levanon will bounce back and overwhelm you, and the destruction of animals will terrify you, because you’ve taken lives and you’ve acted with violence against the land and the cities, and everyone who lives in them.
[Havakuk] [2]:[18] How can an idol profit you when it was just formed and shaped by its human maker? It’s a teacher of lies because its maker uses his own imagination when he makes these speechless ‘gods’.
[Havakuk] [2]:[19] It won’t end well for anyone who tells the piece of wood to wake up, or for the one who tells that speechless stone to stand up. Can these things teach? Yes, it might be plated with valuable gold and silver, but there’s absolutely no life in it.
[Havakuk] [2]:[20] In contrast, Yahweh is in his sacred temple. Let everyone in the world be silent in his presence.
[Havakuk] [3]:[1] A prayer of the prophet Havakuk (Habakkuk) designed to be sung:
[Havakuk] [3]:[2] Yahweh, I’ve heard the report about what you’ve done, and I’m in awe of your work, Yahweh. Do it again in our times— show us again in this age. Despite your severe anger, remember to have compassion.
[Havakuk] [3]:[3] God came in from Teyman in Edom, and the sinless one from Mt. Paran. (Instrumental break.) His splendour blanketed the skies, and the earth was full of his praise.
[Havakuk] [3]:[4] His brightness was like the light— rays flashed from his hand where he kept his power.
[Havakuk] [3]:[5] Deadly disease went ahead of him, then the plague followed along behind.
[Havakuk] [3]:[6] He stood and measured the earth. He looked and made the nations tremble. Even the ancient mountains were shattered, and the everlasting hills bowed down. His ways are everlasting.
[Havakuk] [3]:[7] I saw the people in tents in Kushan in trouble. The tent curtains in the Midyan region were trembling.
[Havakuk] [3]:[8] Was your rage against the rivers, Yahweh? Was your anger against the rivers, or your fury against the ocean, when you rode in on your horses and your victorious chariots?
[Havakuk] [3]:[9] You got your bow out ready to use. Each arrow was a promise you’d made. (Instrumental break.) You split the earth open with rivers.
[Havakuk] [3]:[10] The mountains saw you and twisted in pain. A storm brought heavy rain down on them. The deep sea raised its voice— it sent up high waves.
[Havakuk] [3]:[11] The sun and moon have stopped in their places with the light from your arrows as they fly by, yes, with the gleam of your flashing spear.
[Havakuk] [3]:[12] You have marched over the world in your fury. You’ve trampled down the nations in anger.
[Havakuk] [3]:[13] You went out to rescue your people— to save your anointed one. You crush the leader of the house of wicked people to strip him from the thigh up to the neck. (Instrumental break.)
[Havakuk] [3]:[14] You have pierced the head of his warriors with his own arrows, since they came like a storm to scatter us— their gloating was like someone who destroys weak people in secret.
[Havakuk] [3]:[15] You trod on top of the sea with your horses— churning the many waters.
[Havakuk] [3]:[16] I heard, and my insides turned to jelly. My lips quivered at the sound. My bones start aching, and my legs tremble beneath me. However, I will wait quietly for the day of distress to hit the people who invaded us.
[Havakuk] [3]:[17] Even if the fig tree doesn’t produce buds and there is no fruit on the grapevines, and although the olive tree stops producing, and the fields yield no food, and although the sheep and goats can’t return to their pens, and there are no cattle in their stalls,
[Havakuk] [3]:[18] I’ll still praise Yahweh. I’ll celebrate because God saves me.
[Havakuk] [3]:[19] I trust my master Yahweh for my strength, and he makes my feet agile like a deer’s feet. He helps me climb up to my high places. For the musical director, on my stringed instruments.
[Tsefanyah] [1]:[1] The message from Yahweh which came to Tsefanyah (Zephaniah) (son of Kush (Ethiopia), son of Gedalyah, son of Amaryah, son of Hizkiyah (Hezekiah)) in the time of Amon’s son, King Yoshiyah (Josiah) of Yehudah (Judah)
[Tsefanyah] [1]:[2] Yahweh declares: I will exterminate everything that lives on the ground.
[Tsefanyah] [1]:[3] Yahweh declares: I’ll bring humans and animals to an end, along with the birds and fish. Wicked people will be destroyed along with their idols and humankind will be cut-off from the earth.
[Tsefanyah] [1]:[4] I will punish the people of Yehudah (Judah), and those living in Yerushalem (Jerusalem). I will wipe all remnants of Ba’al out from this place. No one will even remember the names of those priests who served idols.
[Tsefanyah] [1]:[5] I’ll punish those who bowed down to the stars and planets from their rooftops, and those making promises to Yahweh but then promising to the false god Malkam.
[Tsefanyah] [1]:[6] I’ll punish those who turn back after following me, Yahweh, as well as those who haven’t searched for Yahweh or prayed to me.
[Tsefanyah] [1]:[7] Be silent in the presence of the master Yahweh, because his day is near. Yahweh has prepared a sacrifice, and he’s consecrated his guests.
[Tsefanyah] [1]:[8] On the day of Yahweh’s sacrifice, I will visit their officials and the king’s sons, and all those wearing foreign clothing.
[Tsefanyah] [1]:[9] At that time I will punish all the officials who force their way into people’s homes—the ones filling their masters’ houses using fraud and violence.
[Tsefanyah] [1]:[10] Yahweh declares: On that day a cry of distress will come from the Fish Gate, and wailing from the second district and a loud crash from the hills.
[Tsefanyah] [1]:[11] Wail, you inhabitants of the Maktesh, because all of the people of Kena’an (Canaan) will be destroyed. All the money-counters will be eliminated.
[Tsefanyah] [1]:[12] I will search Yerushalem (Jerusalem) with lamps at that time, and I will punish those who’ve sunk to the bottom— the ones who tell themselves, ‘Yahweh will never take action—either good or bad.’
[Tsefanyah] [1]:[13] Their wealth will be taken as plunder and their houses will be ruined. They’ll build houses, but they won’t get to live in them. They’ll plant vineyards, but won’t get to drink their wine.
[Tsefanyah] [1]:[14] Yahweh’s big day of judgement is near— close and coming quickly. The sound of Yahweh’s day is bitter— even warriors will cry out.
[Tsefanyah] [1]:[15] That day will be a day of anger, a day of distress and anguish, a day of destruction and desolation, a day of darkness and gloom, a day of cloud and thick darkness,
[Tsefanyah] [1]:[16] a day of trumpet blasts and with the battle cry against the fortified cities and against the high towers on their corners.
[Tsefanyah] [1]:[17] I’ll bring distress to the people, and they’ll walk slowly as if they were blind, because they’ve sinned against Yahweh. Their blood will be poured out like dust, and their innards like dung.
[Tsefanyah] [1]:[18] Their silver, and even their gold, won’t be able to save them on the day of Yahweh’s anger. The whole earth will be consumed in the fire of his jealousy because he’ll soon destroy people from all over the world.
[Tsefanyah] [2]:[1] Gather yourselves together, yes, assemble now you shameless nation
[Tsefanyah] [2]:[2] before the decree is made, before the day passes like chaff, before Yahweh’s anger reaches you all, yes, before that day of Yahweh’s anger hits you.
[Tsefanyah] [2]:[3] Search for Yahweh, all you humble people who do his justice. Aim to do what is right and to stay humble. Perhaps you’ll be hidden away on the day Yahweh’s anger.
[Tsefanyah] [2]:[4] Because Azah (Gaza) will become abandoned, and Ashkelon will become a ruin. The people of Ashdod will be driven out by noon, and Ekron will be overthrown.
[Tsefanyah] [2]:[5] The inhabitants of the coastal region are to be pitied, the nation of the Kereti. Yahweh’s decision is against you all, Kena’an (Canaan), land of the Pelishtim. I’ll destroy you until no one remains.
[Tsefanyah] [2]:[6] The coastal region will become pastures of meadows for shepherds and pens for flocks.
[Tsefanyah] [2]:[7] The remaining survivors from Yehudah (Judah) will inhabit that region. They will shepherd their flocks on that land. They’ll lie down in their houses in Ashkelon in the evening, because their god Yahweh will visit them, and he’ll restore their fortune.
[Tsefanyah] [2]:[8] I’ve heard Moav’s (Moab) mocking and the Amonim’ insults. They’ve insulted my people and built up their forces against their border.
[Tsefanyah] [2]:[9] Commander-in-chief Yahweh, Yisrael’s (Israel) god, declares: As certain as I’m alive, Moav will become like Sedom, and the Amonim like Amorah (Gomorrah), overrun by nettles and salt-pits—in ruins forever. The remnant of my people will plunder them, and the remainder of my nation will take possession of them.
[Tsefanyah] [2]:[10] That will be the fruit of their pride, because they mocked and talked themselves up against the people of Commander-in-chief Yahweh.
[Tsefanyah] [2]:[11] The people of Moav (Moab) and Amon will be very scared when Yahweh punishes them. He’ll do that so powerfully that people will stop worshipping all other gods. People in every nation will worship Yahweh instead—each person in their own country.
[Tsefanyah] [2]:[12] Also you, Kushim (Ethiopians) (Kushim), will be killed by my sword.
[Tsefanyah] [2]:[13] Yahweh will punish those in the north. Yes, he’ll destroy Ashur (Assyria). He’ll turn Nineveh into ruins— it’ll become a dry place like the desert.
[Tsefanyah] [2]:[14] Herds of every kind of wild animals will lie down in the middle of it, Various kinds of owls will sit on the pillars still standing. A call will hoot in the window. Rubble will blocking any doorways still upright, because the cedar planks will be exposed.
[Tsefanyah] [2]:[15] This is the proud city where people lived in security. The one with a reputation: “No other city compares with me.” How it’s become a ruin—a home for the wild animals. Every one passing by will hiss at it in derision, and shake their fist remembering their hate for it.
[Tsefanyah] [3]:[1] The one rebelling and being defiled is to be pitied— the city of oppressors.
[Tsefanyah] [3]:[2] She doesn’t listen to what she’s told. She doesn’t take correction. She refuses to trust in Yahweh. She won’t approach her god.
[Tsefanyah] [3]:[3] Her leaders are roaring lions among the flock. Her judges are wolves that approach in the evening. There’s nothing left to eat by the morning.
[Tsefanyah] [3]:[4] Her prophets are insolent, treacherous men. Her priests profane the sanctuary—they violate God’s law.
[Tsefanyah] [3]:[5] Yahweh behaves fairly in her midst. He doesn’t do anything that’s wrong. He makes fair and just judgements every morning. At every dawn, he’s present there, and yet those who are disobedient have no shame.
[Tsefanyah] [3]:[6] I’ve destroyed nations—broken down their walls. I’ve destroyed their streets and now they’re deserted. Their cities are ruined, lifeless, without anyone living in them.
[Tsefanyah] [3]:[7] I said, ‘Surely you will respect me and accept correction. Then she won’t die as a city because of my punishing her.’ Nevertheless, they got up early to do all their corrupt activities.
[Tsefanyah] [3]:[8] Yahweh declares: Wait for me, for when I pounce on the prey, because my decision is to gather nations and assemble kingdoms, to pour my indignation and all my anger out on them, because the whole world will be consumed by the fire of my jealousy.
[Tsefanyah] [3]:[9] Then I’ll be sure to give pure speech to the peoples, so all of them can pray to Yahweh, and serve him side-by-side.
[Tsefanyah] [3]:[10] From across the rivers of Kush (Ethiopia) (Kush), my worshippers, my scattered children will return and bring my offering.
[Tsefanyah] [3]:[11] On that day you won’t feel ashamed about all the times you disobeyed me, because at that time, I’ll remove those proud people from among you, and you won’t continue to be arrogant on my sacred mountain.
[Tsefanyah] [3]:[12] And I’ll leave the poorer and humble people among you, and they’ll trust in Yahweh’s authority.
[Tsefanyah] [3]:[13] The surviving Israelis won’t do what is wrong. They won’t tell lies or deceive others. Instead they’ll eat and sleep in peace, No one will be there to terrify them.
[Tsefanyah] [3]:[14] Tsiyon’s (Zion) daughter, sing happily. All Yisrael (Israel), shout aloud. Daughters of Yerushalem (Jerusalem), be happy and triumphant will all your being.
[Tsefanyah] [3]:[15] Yahweh will stop punishing you. He’s forced your enemy to retreat. Yisrael’s king, Yahweh, is among you. Don’t worry any more about being harmed.
[Tsefanyah] [3]:[16] In that day Yerushalem will be told, “Don’t be afraid, Tsiyon (Zion). Don’t let your hands grow weak.
[Tsefanyah] [3]:[17] Your god Yahweh is right there. A powerful warrior, he’ll save you. He’ll be so happy about you. He’ll be silent in his love. He’ll talk happily about your rescue.”
[Tsefanyah] [3]:[18] I will gather those among you who grieve so they can attend the celebrations. They were taken as tribute and it was a reproach.
[Tsefanyah] [3]:[19] Look, I’ll be dealing with all of your oppressors at that time. I’ll save your people who are disabled or who’ve been shamed. Then I’ll get them praising, and change their shame into a good reputation around the world.
[Tsefanyah] [3]:[20] At that time I will bring you all in— yes, I’ll gather you all together at that time. You’ll have a good reputation and people all over the world will praise you, as I restore your good fortune right in front of your eyes. Yahweh has spoken.
[Hagay] [1]:[1] In Dareyavesh’s (Darius) second year as king of Paras (Persia), on the 1st of the sixth month, the prophet Hagay brought Yahweh’s message to the governor of Yehudah (Judah), Zerubavel (Shealtiyel’s son), and to the high priest, Yehoshua (Joshua) (Yehotsadak’s son), telling them that
[Hagay] [1]:[2] Commander-in-chief Yahweh says, “These people say that it’s not the right time to rebuild Yahweh’s residence.”
[Hagay] [1]:[3] Then Yahweh gave this message to the prophet Hagay to tell the people:
[Hagay] [1]:[4] Is it a time for all of you to live in your panelled houses, while Yahweh’s temple lies in ruins?
[Hagay] [1]:[5] So now Commander-in-chief Yahweh says: “Decide what you’re all going to do.
[Hagay] [1]:[6] You’ve all planted a lot, but only harvested a little. You’ve eaten, but it never fills you. You all drink, but never enough to satisfy you. You put on clothes, but never feel warm enough. You earn wages, but your pockets seem to be full of holes.”
[Hagay] [1]:[7] So Commander-in-chief Yahweh says again: “Decide what you’re all going to do.
[Hagay] [1]:[8] Go up into the hills and bring back timber to build the temple. This will please and honour me,” says Yahweh.
[Hagay] [1]:[9] “You expected much, but gained little. Anything you brought home, I blew away again. Why? Commander-in-chief Yahweh says it’s because my residence is still in ruins, while you’re all busy working on your own houses.
[Hagay] [1]:[10] That’s why the sky withholds the dew and the soil withholds its crops.
[Hagay] [1]:[11] I’ve summoned a drought onto the land and into the hills, onto the grain and the new wine, onto the oil and crops from the ground, onto both people and livestock, and onto everything you all do.”
[Hagay] [1]:[12] Then Shealtiyel’s son Zerubavel and Yehotsadak’s son Yehoshua (Joshua), the high priest, and all the rest of the people listened to the voice of their god Yahweh via the words of the prophet Hagay, because Yahweh their god had sent him, and the people respected Yahweh.
[Hagay] [1]:[13] Then Yahweh’s messenger Hagay passed this message from Yahweh onto the people, “Yahweh declares that I’m with you all.”
[Hagay] [1]:[14] Then Yahweh inspired Shealtiyel’s son Zerubavel, the governor of Yehudah (Judah), inspired Yehotsadak’s son Yehoshua, the high priest, and inspired all the rest of the people, and they came and started work on the temple for their god, Commander-in-chief Yahweh,
[Hagay] [1]:[15] on the twenty-fourth day of the sixth month of the second year of Dareyavesh (Darius) the king of Paras (Persia).
[Hagay] [2]:[1] On the 21st of the seventh month (about a month later), Yahweh spoke again through the prophet Hagay:
[Hagay] [2]:[2] Please ask Shealtiyel’s son Zerubavel, the governor of Yehudah (Judah), and ask Yehotsadak’s son Yehoshua (Joshua), the high priest, and ask the rest of the people,
[Hagay] [2]:[3] “Are there any of you still alive who saw the splendour of the former temple? How does it look to you now? It must now seem pretty much like nothing in comparison.
[Hagay] [2]:[4] Yahweh is telling you now, Zerubavel, to be strong. And be strong, high priest Yehoshua, and be strong all you people of the land. Commander-in-chief Yahweh declares that I’m with you as you work.
[Hagay] [2]:[5] That’s what I promised your ancestors when they came out of Mitsrayim (Egypt), and my spirit remains among you. Don’t be afraid,
[Hagay] [2]:[6] because Commander-in-chief Yahweh says that in a little while, I’ll shake the heavens and the earth, the sea and the dry land, once more.
[Hagay] [2]:[7] I’ll shake all the nations, and they’ll come here bringing their treasure. Then I’ll fill this temple with my splendour, says Commander-in-chief Yahweh.
[Hagay] [2]:[8] Commander-in-chief Yahweh declares that the gold and silver belong to me.
[Hagay] [2]:[9] I declare that this temple will be greater in the future than it was in the past, and also that I will give peace and prosperity to this place.”
[Hagay] [2]:[10] On the 24th of the ninth month in King Dareyavesh’s (Darius) second year (about two months later), Yahweh gave a message to the prophet Hagay:
[Hagay] [2]:[11] Commander-in-chief Yahweh says, “Ask the priests about Mosheh’s (Moses) instructions.
[Hagay] [2]:[12] ‘If a priest took some meat that had been offered to God and carried it wrapped in a piece of clothing, then if the clothing touched some other food, would that other food become holy?’ ” “No, it wouldn’t,” the priests replied.
[Hagay] [2]:[13] Then Hagay asked, “But if a person became unclean by touching a corpse and then touched any of that food, would it become unclean?” “Yes, it would become unclean,” the priests answered.
[Hagay] [2]:[14] “That’s what Yahweh declares about you people,” Hagay continued. “He says that that’s how this country acts towards him. Your actions are dishonourable, and then that same disrespect transfers to your offerings.
[Hagay] [2]:[15] So now think back to before stones were being laid for Yahweh’s temple.
[Hagay] [2]:[16] During that time, when someone went to get twenty containers of grain, there were only ten there, and when someone went to fill fifty jars of wine from the vat, there was only enough for twenty.
[Hagay] [2]:[17] Yahweh declares that he caused blight and mildew and hail to affect your work, but you still didn’t turn to him.
[Hagay] [2]:[18] Think back to the time from when the foundation of Yahweh’s temple was laid, until today (this 24th of the ninth month). Consider that.
[Hagay] [2]:[19] Is any grain left in the storehouse for seed? What’s more, the vines, and the fig trees and pomegranate trees and olive trees, haven’t produced fruit. However, Yahweh will bless you from today onwards.”
[Hagay] [2]:[20] Then Yahweh gave a second message to Hagay on the 24th:
[Hagay] [2]:[21] Tell Zerubavel, the governor of Yehudah (Judah), “I’m about to shake the heavens and the earth.
[Hagay] [2]:[22] I’ll overthrow the thrones of kingdoms, and destroy the strength of the nations. I’ll overthrow chariots and riders—horses and their riders will fall and related tribes will kill each other.
[Hagay] [2]:[23] Commander-in-chief Yahweh declares that on that day he will take Shealtiyel’s son Zerubavel and cause him to place Yahweh’s mark on the nation like a signet ring, because he’s been chosen.”
[Zekaryah] [1]:[1] In the eighth month of the second year of the reign of Persian King Dareyavesh (Darius), Yahweh spoke through the prophet Zekaryah (Zechariah) (Zekaryah, son of Ido’s son Berekyah) saying,
[Zekaryah] [1]:[2] “Yahweh was very angry with your ancestors,
[Zekaryah] [1]:[3] so tell this to the people: Commander-in-chief Yahweh says that if you all turn back to me, I’ll return to you.
[Zekaryah] [1]:[4] Don’t be like your ancestors who’d been told by the prophets that Commander-in-chief Yahweh wanted them to abandon all their evil practices, but they wouldn’t listen or pay attention. That is Yahweh’s declaration.
[Zekaryah] [1]:[5] “So where are you ancestors and the prophets now? Do they live forever?
[Zekaryah] [1]:[6] But your ancestors didn’t obey my words and my decrees that I commanded through my servants the prophets, but they eventually repented and said, ‘Commander-in-chief Yahweh has done to us just what our ways and actions deserved.’ ”
[Zekaryah] [1]:[7] About three months later, Yahweh spoke again through the prophet Zekaryah (Zechariah) (Zekaryah son of Ido’s son Berekyah) saying,

[Zekaryah] [1]:[9] I asked, “What are these things, my master?” Then that heavenly messenger who talked with me told me, “I’ll show you what those things are.”
[Zekaryah] [1]:[10] Then the man who stood among the myrtle trees answered and said, “Those are the ones that Yahweh has sent out to roam throughout the world.”
[Zekaryah] [1]:[11] They answered Yahweh’s messenger who stood among the myrtle trees, telling him, “We’ve been roaming throughout the world, and see, the whole world sits contentedly and is at peace.”
[Zekaryah] [1]:[12] “Commander-in-chief Yahweh,” Yahweh’s messenger asked, “how long before you show compassion to Yerushalem (Jerusalem) and to the cities of Yehudah (Judah), which you’ve been angry with for the past seventy years?”
[Zekaryah] [1]:[13] Then that messenger who’d talked with me was answered by Yahweh with kind and comforting words,
[Zekaryah] [1]:[14] and that messenger told me, “Call out and say, ‘Commander-in-chief Yahweh says this: I’ve been very jealous for Yerushalem and for Tsiyon (Zion).

[Zekaryah] [1]:[18] Then I looked up and wow, I saw four horns.
[Zekaryah] [1]:[19] I asked the messenger who’d talked with me, “What are those?” “Those are the horns that have scattered Yehudah (Judah), Yisrael (Israel), and Yerushalem (Jerusalem).” he answered.
[Zekaryah] [1]:[20] Then Yahweh showed me four craftsmen
[Zekaryah] [1]:[21] and I asked, “What are those people coming to do?” “Those horns are the nations that scattered Yehudah so that everyone went into hiding,” he answered, “But the blacksmiths have come to terrify the horns—to amputate the horns of the nations that attacked Yehudah, scattering the people.”

[Zekaryah] [10]:[8] I’ll whistle to call them and gather them, because I’ll rescue them, and they’ll become as numerous as they were previously.
[Zekaryah] [10]:[9] I scattered them among the nations, but they’ll remember me in distant countries, so they and their children will live and return,
[Zekaryah] [10]:[10] because I’ll bring them back from the land of Mitsrayim (Egypt) and gather them from Ashur (Assyria). I’ll bring them to the land of Gilead and Levanon until the region is filled with them.
[Zekaryah] [10]:[11] Yahweh will lead them through their sufferings. He will strike the waves of that sea and will dry up all the depths of the Nile. The Ashur’s greatness will come to an end, and Mitsrayim’s (Egypt) power will be removed.
[Zekaryah] [10]:[12] I will strengthen them in myself, and they will obey what I’ve instructed them. That is Yahweh’s declaration.”
[Zekaryah] [11]:[1] Open your doors, Levanon, so that fire can devour your cedar trees.
[Zekaryah] [11]:[2] Wail, cypress trees, because the cedar trees have fallen. What was majestic has been devastated. Wail, you Bashan oaks, because the strong forest has come down.
[Zekaryah] [11]:[3] Listen to the shepherds wail, because their pride and joy has been destroyed. Listen to the young lions roaring, because the pride of the Yarden (Jordan) river has been devastated.
[Zekaryah] [11]:[4] My god Yahweh says: “Be like a shepherd who’s watching over the flock that have been marked to be slaughtered.
[Zekaryah] [11]:[5] The ones who buy them, slaughter them and aren’t punished, and the ones who sell them say, ‘Blessed be Yahweh. I’ve become rich.’ because the shepherds working for the flocks’ owners have no pity on them.
[Zekaryah] [11]:[6] This is Yahweh’s declaration: I will no longer feel sorry for the people of this country. Listen, I’m about to allow everyone to be taken over by their neighbours and by their king and allow them to destroy the land, and I won’t rescue anyone from them.”
[Zekaryah] [11]:[7] So I became the shepherd of the flock that had been marked for slaughter—the ones who were suffering the most. I took two shepherd’s staffs—I named one ‘Favour’, and the other I named ‘Unity’, and then I shepherded the flock.
[Zekaryah] [11]:[8] Then I destroyed the three shepherds—in one month I became impatient with them, and they also hated me.
[Zekaryah] [11]:[9] So I said to the owners, “I won’t work for you any longer as a shepherd. The sheep that are dying—let them die. The sheep that are being destroyed—let them be destroyed. Let the sheep that remain start eating each other.”
[Zekaryah] [11]:[10] Then I took my staff named ‘Favour’ and broke it to break the agreement that I’d made with all of my tribes.
[Zekaryah] [11]:[11] So the agreement was broken on that day, and the ones in the flock who were suffering the most and who were watching me, knew that Yahweh had spoken.
[Zekaryah] [11]:[12] Then I told them, “If it seems good to you, give me my wages, but if not, don’t bother.” So they paid me thirty silver coins.
[Zekaryah] [11]:[13] Then Yahweh told me, “Give the money to the potter—the pathetic amount that they valued you at.” So I took the thirty silver coins and tossed them to the potter in Yahweh’s temple.
[Zekaryah] [11]:[14] Then I broke my second staff named ‘Unity’ to break the brotherhood between Yehudah (Judah) and Yisrael (Israel).
[Zekaryah] [11]:[15] After that, Yahweh told me, “Again, take the equipment of a simple shepherd for yourself,
[Zekaryah] [11]:[16] because listen, I’m about to set a shepherd in place in the land who won’t care for those who are dying. He won’t seek out the sheep gone missing, nor will he heal the crippled sheep. He won’t feed the sheep that are healthy, but he’ll tear off the hooves of the fattened sheep and eat them for meat.
[Zekaryah] [11]:[17] The worthless shepherd who abandons the flock won’t end well. May the sword come against his arm and his right eye. May his arm wither away and may his right eye become blind.”
[Zekaryah] [12]:[1] This is a declaration of Yahweh’s message concerning Yisrael (Israel)—a declaration of Yahweh, who stretched out the skies and laid the foundation of the earth, who forms the human spirit that’s inside people,
[Zekaryah] [12]:[2] “Listen, I’m about to make Yerushalem (Jerusalem) into a cup causing all the nations surrounding her to stagger around. It will also be like that for Yehudah (Judah) during the siege against Yerushalem.
[Zekaryah] [12]:[3] At that time, I’ll make Yerushalem into a heavy stone for all the peoples. Anyone trying to lift that stone will hurt himself very much, and all the nations in the world will gather against that city.
[Zekaryah] [12]:[4] This is Yahweh’s declaration: At that time, I will strike every horse with confusion and its rider with madness. I’ll open my eyes over the Yehudah region, but I’ll strike every horse from other countries with blindness.
[Zekaryah] [12]:[5] Then the leaders of Yehudah will say to themselves, ‘The inhabitants of Yerushalem are our strength because of their god, Commander-in-chief Yahweh.’
[Zekaryah] [12]:[6] At that time, I will make the leaders of Yehudah like firepots among wood and like a flaming torch among standing grain, because they’ll devour all the surrounding peoples on their right and on their left. Yerushalem will again live in her own place.”
[Zekaryah] [12]:[7] Yahweh will save Yehudah’s (Judah) tents first, so that the honour of David’s descendants and the honour of Yerushalem’s (Jerusalem) inhabitants won’t be greater than the rest of Yehudah.
[Zekaryah] [12]:[8] At that time, Yahweh will be the defender of the inhabitants of Yerushalem. Those among them who are weak will become strong like David, while the David’s descendants will be like God, like Yahweh’s messenger going ahead of them.
[Zekaryah] [12]:[9] “On that day I will begin to destroy all the nations that fight against Yerushalem.”
[Zekaryah] [12]:[10] But I will pour out a spirit of compassion and pleading on David’s descendants and the inhabitants of Yerushalem, so they will look on me—the one they’ve pierced. They’ll mourn for me, as one mourns for an only son—they will wail bitterly for him like those who wail after the death of a firstborn son.
[Zekaryah] [12]:[11] On that day the wailing in Yerushalem will be like the wailing at Hadad-Rimon in the Megidon plain.
[Zekaryah] [12]:[12] The land will mourn, each clan separate from other clans. The clan of David’s descendants will be separate and their wives will be separate from the men. The clan of Natan’s (Nathan) descendants will be separate and their wives will also be separate from the men.
[Zekaryah] [12]:[13] The clan of Levi’s descendants will be separate and their wives will be separate from the men. The clan of the Shim’im will be separate and their wives will also be separate from the men.
[Zekaryah] [12]:[14] Each of the remaining clans will be separate and the wives will be separate from the men.”
[Zekaryah] [13]:[1] “On that day a spring will be opened for David’s descendants and the other inhabitants of Yerushalem (Jerusalem), to clean them from their sin and impurity.
[Zekaryah] [13]:[2] This is the declaration of Commander-in-chief Yahweh: That same day, I will eliminate the names of the idols from the country and then no one will be able to remember them. I’ll remove the false prophets and the spirit of impurity from the land.
[Zekaryah] [13]:[3] If anyone continues to prophesy, his father and mother will tell him, ‘You can’t be allowed to live because you speak lies using Yahweh’s name’ Then the very father and mother who gave birth to him will run him through when he prophesies.
[Zekaryah] [13]:[4] At that time, each prophet will become ashamed of his vision when he is about to prophesy, so in order to deceive the people, these prophets won’t put on a hairy cloak any more,
[Zekaryah] [13]:[5] and they’ll each say, ‘I’m not a prophet. I’m a man who works the soil—I’ve been doing that since I was young.’
[Zekaryah] [13]:[6] But someone will ask him, ‘What are these wounds between your arms?’ and he’ll answer, ‘I got accidentally wounded in my friends’ house.’ ”
[Zekaryah] [13]:[7] Army command Yahweh declares: Wake up, sword, and work against the one who’s my shepherd and the man who stands close to me. Strike the shepherd and the flock will scatter because I’ll turn my hand against the lowly ones.
[Zekaryah] [13]:[8] Yahweh declares: Then it’ll come about that throughout all the land, that two-thirds of it will be cut off. Those people will die—only one-third will remain there.
[Zekaryah] [13]:[9] I’ll bring that third through the fire and refine them like silver is refined. I’ll test them like gold is tested. They will call out to me for help, and I’ll answer them saying, ‘This is my people.’ and they’ll say, ‘Yahweh is my god.’ ”
[Zekaryah] [14]:[1] Listen, a day is coming for Yahweh, when your plunder will be divided right in front of you,
[Zekaryah] [14]:[2] because I will assemble every country to battle against Yerushalem (Jerusalem) and the city will be captured. The houses will be plundered and the women raped. Half of the city will be led away into captivity, but the remainder of the people won’t be evicted from the city.
[Zekaryah] [14]:[3] Then Yahweh will go out and fight against those nations like when he fights on the day of battle.
[Zekaryah] [14]:[4] On that day, his feet will stand on the Mt. of Olives, which is just east of Yerushalem. The Mt. of Olives will be split in half between the east and the west by a very great valley, and half of the mountain will go back toward the north and half toward the south.
[Zekaryah] [14]:[5] Then you all will flee down the valley between Yahweh’s mountains, because the valley between those mountains will reach to Atsel. You will flee just like you fled from the earthquake in the days of Yehudah’s (Judah) King Uziyah. Then my god Yahweh will come and all the holy ones will be with him.
[Zekaryah] [14]:[6] On that day, there’ll be no light—precious things will freeze together.
[Zekaryah] [14]:[7] On that day (known only to Yahweh), there’ll no longer be day or night, because it’ll stay light at ‘night’.
[Zekaryah] [14]:[8] On that day, living waters will flow out of Yerushalem. Half of them will flow to the eastern sea and half to the western sea, both in summer and in winter.
[Zekaryah] [14]:[9] Yahweh will be king over all the world. On that day there will only be Yahweh, the one God—no other gods.
[Zekaryah] [14]:[10] All the land will be like the plain from Geva to Rimon south of Yerushalem. Yerushalem will continue to be in the hills and remain in its own place, from the Benyamin Gate to the place where the first gate was, to the Corner Gate, and from the Hananel Tower to the king’s wine-pressing pits.
[Zekaryah] [14]:[11] It’ll be inhabited and never completely destroyed again—Yerushalem will live in security.
[Zekaryah] [14]:[12] The deadly disease that Yahweh will use to attack all the nations that fought against Yerushalem will be that their flesh will rot away even while they’re still standing on their feet. Their eyes will rot in their sockets and their tongues will rot in their mouths.
[Zekaryah] [14]:[13] On that day, Yahweh will cause them to panic—they’ll grab hold of each other, and then they’ll start attacking each other.
[Zekaryah] [14]:[14] Yehudah (Judah) will also fight against Yerushalem, and the wealth (gold, silver, and clothing) from all the surrounding countries will be collected together.
[Zekaryah] [14]:[15] That deadly disease will also affect the horses and mules, the camels and donkeys, and all the other animals in those camps.
[Zekaryah] [14]:[16] After that, all who remain in those nations that came against Yerushalem will instead go up from year to year to worship the king (Commander-in-chief Yahweh), and to observe the celebration in shelters.
[Zekaryah] [14]:[17] It will happen that if anyone from all the countries in the world doesn’t go to Yerushalem to worship the king (Commander-in-chief Yahweh) then Yahweh won’t send them any rain.
[Zekaryah] [14]:[18] If Mitsrayim (Egypt) doesn’t go, then they won’t get any rain. A deadly disease from Yahweh will attack the nations that do not go to Yerushalem to observe the celebration in shelters.
[Zekaryah] [14]:[19] That will be the punishment for Mitsrayim and the punishment for every country that doesn’t go to observe that celebration in shelters.
[Zekaryah] [14]:[20] On that day, the horses’ bells will say, “Dedicated to Yahweh,” and the basins in Yahweh’s residence will be like the bowls in front of the altar,
[Zekaryah] [14]:[21] because every pot in Yerushalem and Yehudah (Judah) will be dedicated to Commander-in-chief Yahweh and everyone who brings a sacrifice will eat from them and boil in them. On that day, there will no longer be any traders in Commander-in-chief Yahweh’s residence.
[Malaki] [1]:[1] This is a message that Yahweh gave to Malaki (Malachi) for the Israelis:
[Malaki] [1]:[2] “I have loved you all,” says Yahweh, but you say, “How have you shown your love for us?” “Wasn’t Esav (Esau) Ya’akov’s (Jacob) brother?” declares Yahweh. “Yet I’ve loved Ya’akov
[Malaki] [1]:[3] and rejected Esav. I’ve turned the hills where Esav lived into a wasteland and given his inheritance to the wild jackals.”
[Malaki] [1]:[4] If Esav’s descendants in Edom say, “We’ve been crushed, but we’ll return and rebuild what was destroyed,” then army-commander Yahweh will say, “They might build, but I will tear down. Others will call them ‘The country of wickedness’ and ‘The people who Yahweh is forever angry with.’
[Malaki] [1]:[5] Your own eyes will see it, and you’ll say, ‘Yahweh is great even outside Yisrael’s (Israel) borders.’ ”
[Malaki] [1]:[6] “A son honours his father, and a servant honours his master, so if I’m a father, where is my honour? If I am a master, where is my respect?” says army-commander Yahweh to all you priests who despise my name. “But you say, ‘How have we despised your name?’
[Malaki] [1]:[7] By offering polluted food on my altar. But you say, ‘How have we polluted you?’ By saying that Yahweh’s table can just be disrespected.
[Malaki] [1]:[8] Don’t you think it’s wrong when you sacrifice blind animals? Isn’t it evil when you offer lame or sick animals? Try presenting them to your governor! Will he welcome you or would he be offended?” says army-commander Yahweh.
[Malaki] [1]:[9] So now bring you requests to God and hope to be showered by his grace. Ha, army-commander Yahweh asks how he could treat you all favourably when you’re bringing second-class offerings?
[Malaki] [1]:[10] “Yeah, if only there was one person among you who would shut the temple gates so that you all couldn’t just continue to light worthless fires on my altar. I get no pleasure from you all,” says army-commander Yahweh, “and I won’t accept any offering that you all bring me.
[Malaki] [1]:[11] People in other countries from the east all the way to the west will honour me, and incense and genuine sacrifices will be offered to me, because my reputation in those countries will be praised,” says army-commander Yahweh.
[Malaki] [1]:[12] “But you all are dishonouring my name when you say that the master’s table is polluted, and that its fruit, its food, can be treated with contempt.
[Malaki] [1]:[13] You all also say, ‘How tiresome this is,’ and you snort at it,” says army-commander Yahweh. “You all bring animals for your offering that were killed by a wild animal or is lame or sick. Should I accept those from you?” says Yahweh.
[Malaki] [1]:[14] “May the cheats be cursed who have male animals in their flocks and vow to give them, but instead sacrifices a second-class animal to the master! Yes, I’m a powerful king,” says army-commander Yahweh, “and my name will be carefully respected among the nations.”
[Malaki] [2]:[1] Now you priests, this command is for all of you:
[Malaki] [2]:[2] Army-commander Yahweh says, “If you all won’t listen and won’t decide in your minds to honour to my reputation, then I’ll send a curse on you all—in fact I’ll curse your blessings. Indeed, I’ve already cursed them, because you all are not internalising my instructions.
[Malaki] [2]:[3] Listen, I’m about to rebuke your descendants, and I’ll spread the offal from your festivals on your faces, and you all will be taken away with it.
[Malaki] [2]:[4] That’s so you’ll all know that it’s me who sent this command to you: so that my agreement with the Levites can continue,” says army-commander Yahweh.
[Malaki] [2]:[5] “My agreement with your ancestor Levi was to give life and peace, and I gave them to them. It was an agreement based on respect, and they respected me and honoured my name.
[Malaki] [2]:[6] They taught the people what was right and true—they didn’t tell lies. They worked for me peacefully and loyally, and they encouraged many people to stop disobeying.
[Malaki] [2]:[7] Yes, priests should pass on knowledge and people should look to them for good teaching, because they are army-commander Yahweh’s messengers.
[Malaki] [2]:[8] But you all have turned away from that path and have caused many people to stumble because of what you’ve taught—you all have corrupted the agreement with Levi,” says army-commander Yahweh.
[Malaki] [2]:[9] “So that’s why I’ve caused you all to be despised by all the people and humiliated—because you all haven’t followed me, but rather you’ve been biased in matters of the law.”
[Malaki] [2]:[10] Don’t we all have one father? Didn’t the one God create us all? So why do we cheat each other, thus disrespecting the agreement with our ancestors?
[Malaki] [2]:[11] Our nation of Yehudah (Judah) has been unfaithful to Yahweh and done detestable things in Yisrael (Israel) and in Yerushalem (Jerusalem). Our men have defiled the temple that Yahweh loves by marrying foreign women who worship pagan gods.
[Malaki] [2]:[12] May Yahweh, the one who is awake and the one who answers, banish the men who do this from Yisrael, even if they are bringing an offering to army-commander Yahweh.
[Malaki] [2]:[13] Secondly, you cover Yahweh’s altar with tears from all your weeping and groaning because he still ignores your offerings and won’t accept what you all bring to him.
[Malaki] [2]:[14] So you ask, “Why not?” Well, it’s because Yahweh can testify that you’ve been unfaithful to the wife that you married when you were young, even though she was your companion, and despite your vows.
[Malaki] [2]:[15] Didn’t Yahweh make you and your wife one and give you some of his spirit because he wanted godly children to come from your marriage? So guard yourselves in your spirit, and don’t be unfaithful to the woman you married when you were young.
[Malaki] [2]:[16] “Indeed, I hate divorce,” says Yahweh, the god of Yisrael, “and so-called ‘good people’ who are actually cruel,” says army-commander Yahweh. “So listen to your consciences and don’t be unfaithful.”
[Malaki] [2]:[17] You’ve all wearied Yahweh with your words, and yet you ask, “How have we wearied him?” By saying, “Yahweh is pleased even with those who do evil, and he’s happy with all of them,” or “Where is the god of justice?”
[Malaki] [3]:[1] “Listen, I’m about to send my messenger and he’ll prepare the path ahead of me. Then the master who you’re all looking for will suddenly come to his temple, yes, the messenger who you are all happy about—the party to the agreement—he’ll come,” says army-commander Yahweh.
[Malaki] [3]:[2] But who could survive it when he comes? Who can stand when he appears, because he’ll be like the refiner’s fire and like the cleaners’ powerful soap?
[Malaki] [3]:[3] Yahweh will act as a refiner and purifier of silver, and he will purify Levi’s descendants the priests—yes, he’ll refine you all with fire like gold and silver, and you’ll bring offerings to him that are acceptable.
[Malaki] [3]:[4] After that, the offerings of the people of Yehudah (Judah) and Yerushalem (Jerusalem) will be pleasing to Yahweh, as in ancient times, and as in previous years.
[Malaki] [3]:[5] This is what army-commander Yahweh says, “At that time, I’ll come to you all to judge you. I’ll quickly testify against all those who practice sorcery, against adulterers, against those who lie in court, against those who don’t pay their workers fairly, against those who mistreat widows and orphans, against those who don’t treat the foreigners among you decently, and against those who refuse to honour me.
[Malaki] [3]:[6] “I am Yahweh and I don’t change—that’s the only reason why you descendants of Ya’akov (Jacob) haven’t been destroyed.
[Malaki] [3]:[7] Ever since the time when your ancestors were alive, you all have ignored my commands and refused to obey them. Now return to me—if you all do so, I’ll return to you. That’s what I, army-commander Yahweh, say. But you all ask, ‘How can we return to you?’
[Malaki] [3]:[8] Can a human rob God? Yes, you’re all robbing me, but you ask, ‘How are we robbing you?’ By failing to give a tenth plus offerings.
[Malaki] [3]:[9] You’re all cursed because you’re robbing me—the whole nation of you.
[Malaki] [3]:[10] Bring the full tenth into the temple storeroom, so that there’ll be food in my house for the temple workers,” says army-commander Yahweh. “In fact, you all can test me by doing that and see if I don’t open the windows of heaven for you all and pour out an overflowing blessing for you.
[Malaki] [3]:[11] I’ll rebuke the devourer for you all, so that it won’t destroy your crops, and the fruit off your vines in the countryside won’t be lost,” says army-commander Yahweh.
[Malaki] [3]:[12] “Then all the other countries would say that you’ve all been blessed, because your land would be prosperous,” says army-commander Yahweh.
[Malaki] [3]:[13] “Your words against me have been harsh,” says Yahweh. “But you all say, ‘What have we said among ourselves against you?’
[Malaki] [3]:[14] You’ve all said, ‘It’s a waste of time serving God. What did we gain by keeping his requirements, or by being sorrowful in front of army-commander Yahweh?
[Malaki] [3]:[15] It seems that arrogant people are happier. Evil people not only prosper, but they even challenge God yet nothing happens to them.’ ”
[Malaki] [3]:[16] Then those who still respected Yahweh spoke with one another. Yahweh paid attention and listened, and while he watched, a book of remembrance was written about those who respected Yahweh and honoured his name.
[Malaki] [3]:[17] “They’ll be mine,” says army-commander Yahweh. “On the day when I assemble my treasured possession, I won’t punish those people, just like a father doesn’t punish his son who obeys him.
[Malaki] [3]:[18] Then once again you’ll all be able to see the difference between righteous people and wicked people—between those who serve God and those who don’t.
[Malaki] [4]:[1] “Yes, listen, the day that burns like a furnace is coming, when all the arrogant people and all the evildoers will become useless pieces of dry stalks in a field. The day that is coming will burn them up,” says army-commander Yahweh, “so they’ll be gone without leaving any roots or branches.
[Malaki] [4]:[2] But for you who respect my name, the sun of righteousness will rise and bring healing. You’ll all go out, jumping around like calves let out of their stall,
[Malaki] [4]:[3] and you’ll all trample down the wicked people, because they’ll just be ashes under the soles of your feet on the day that I act,” says army-commander Yahweh.

[Malaki] [4]:[6] He’ll restore harmony between fathers and their children, so that I don’t have to come and strike the earth with complete destruction.”
[Tovi] [1]:[1] The book of the words of Tovi (Tobit), the son of Toviel, the son of Hananiel, the son of Adiel, the son of Gabael, of the seed of Asiyel, of the tribe of Naftali (Naphtali);
[Tovi] [1]:[2] who in the days of the Assyrian King Shalmaneser was carried away captive out of Thisbe, which is on the right hand of Kedesh Naftali in Galil above Asher.
[Tovi] [1]:[3] I, Tovi walked in the ways of truth and righteousness all the days of my life, and I gave to the poor many times to my kindred and my nation, who went with me into the land of the Assyrians, to Nineveh.
[Tovi] [1]:[4] When I was in my own country, in the land of Yisrael (Israel), while I was yet young, all the tribe of Naftali my father fell away from the house of Yerushalem (Jerusalem), which was chosen out of all the tribes of Yisrael, that all the tribes should sacrifice there, and the temple of the habitation of the Most High was hallowed and built there for all ages.
[Tovi] [1]:[5] All the tribes which fell away together sacrificed to the heifer Ba’al, and so did the house of Naftali my father.
[Tovi] [1]:[6] I alone went often to Yerushalem at the feasts, as it’s been ordained to all Yisrael by an eternal decree, having the first fruits and the tenths of my increase, and that which was first shorn; and I gave them at the altar to the priests the sons of Aharon (Aaron).
[Tovi] [1]:[7] I gave a tenth part of all my increase to the sons of Levi, who ministered at Yerushalem. A second tenth part I sold away, and went, and spent it each year at Yerushalem.
[Tovi] [1]:[8] A third tenth I gave to them to whom it was appropriate, as Deborah my father’s mother had commanded me, because I was left an orphan by my father.
[Tovi] [1]:[9] When I became a man, I took as wife Hanah of the seed of our own family. With her, I became the father of Toviyah (Tobias).
[Tovi] [1]:[10] When I was carried away captive to Nineveh, all my kindred and my relatives ate of the bread of the Gentiles;
[Tovi] [1]:[11] but I kept myself from eating,
[Tovi] [1]:[12] because I remembered God with all my soul.
[Tovi] [1]:[13] So the Most High gave me grace and favour in the sight of Shalmaneser, and I was his purchasing agent.
[Tovi] [1]:[14] And I went into Maday (Media), and left ten talents of silver in trust with Gabael, the brother of Gabrias, at Rages of Maday.
[Tovi] [1]:[15] And when Shalmaneser was dead, his son Sanheriv (Sennacherib) reigned in his place. In his time, the highways were troubled, and I could no longer go into Maday.
[Tovi] [1]:[16] In the days of Shalmaneser, I gave to the poor many times to my kindred: I gave my bread to the hungry,
[Tovi] [1]:[17] and my clothes to the naked. If I saw any of my race dead, and thrown out on Nineveh’s wall, I buried him.
[Tovi] [1]:[18] If Sanheriv the king killed any, when he came fleeing from Yehudah (Judea), I buried them privately; for in his anger he killed many; and the bodies were sought for by the king, and weren’t found.
[Tovi] [1]:[19] But one of the Nineuitais went and showed to the king about me, how I buried them, and hid myself; and when I knew that I was sought for to be put to death, I withdrew myself for fear.
[Tovi] [1]:[20] And all my goods were forcibly taken away, and there was nothing left to me, save my wife Hanah and my son Toviyah.
[Tovi] [1]:[21] No more than fifty five days passed before two of his sons killed him, and they fled into the Ararat mountains. And Esar-Hadon his son reigned in his place; and he appointed Ahikar my brother Hanael’s son over all the accounts of his kingdom, and over all his affairs.
[Tovi] [1]:[22] Ahikar requested me, and I came to Nineveh. Now Ahikar was cupbearer, keeper of the signet, steward, and overseer of the accounts. Esar-Hadon appointed him next to himself, but he was my brother’s son.
[Tovi] [2]:[1] Now when I’d come home again, and my wife Hanah was restored to me, and my son Toviyah (Tobias), in the feast of Pentecost, which is the holy feast of the seven weeks, there was a good dinner prepared for me, and I sat down to eat.
[Tovi] [2]:[2] I saw abundance of meat, and I said to my son, “Go and bring whatever poor man you find of our kindred, who’s mindful of the master. Listen, I wait for you.”
[Tovi] [2]:[3] Then he came, and said, “Father, one of our fellow-citizens has been strangled, and his body has been thrown onto the street in the marketplace.”
[Tovi] [2]:[4] Before I’d tasted anything, I sprang up, and took him up into a chamber until the sun had set.
[Tovi] [2]:[5] Then I returned, washed myself, ate my bread in heaviness,
[Tovi] [2]:[6] and remembered the prophecy of Amos, as he said, “Your feasts will be turned into mourning, and all your mirth into lamentation.”
[Tovi] [2]:[7] So I wept: and when the sun had set, I went and dug a grave, and buried him.
[Tovi] [2]:[8] My neighbours mocked me, and said, “He’s no longer afraid to be put to death for this matter; and yet he fled away. Listen, he buries the dead again.”
[Tovi] [2]:[9] The same night I returned from burying him, and slept by the wall of my courtyard, being polluted; and my face was uncovered.
[Tovi] [2]:[10] I didn’t know that there were sparrows in the wall. My eyes were open and the sparrows dropped warm dung into my eyes, and white films came over my eyes. I went to the physicians, and they didn’t help me; but Ahikar nourished me, until I went into Elymais.
[Tovi] [2]:[11] My wife Hanah wove cloth in the women’s chambers,
[Tovi] [2]:[12] and sent the work back to the owners. They on their part paid her wages, and also gave her a kid.
[Tovi] [2]:[13] But when it came to my house, it began to cry, and I said to her, “Where did this kid come from? Is it stolen? Give it back to the owners; for it isn’t lawful to eat anything that’s stolen.”
[Tovi] [2]:[14] But she said, “It’s been given to me for a gift more than the wages.” I didn’t believe her, and I asked her to return it to the owners; and I was ashamed of her. But she replied to me, “What about your gifts to the poor and your righteous actions? Listen, you and all your works are known.”
[Tovi] [3]:[1] I was grieved and wept, and prayed in sorrow, saying,
[Tovi] [3]:[2] “O master, you’re righteous, and all your works and all your ways are mercy and truth, and you judge true and righteous judgement forever.
[Tovi] [3]:[3] Remember me, and look at me. Don’t take vengeance on me for my sins and my ignorances, and the sins of my fathers who sinned before you.
[Tovi] [3]:[4] Because they disobeyed your commandments. You gave us as plunder, for captivity, for death, and for a proverb of reproach to all the nations among whom we’re dispersed.
[Tovi] [3]:[5] Now your judgements are many and true, that you should deal with me according to my sins and the sins of my fathers, because we didn’t keep your commandments, for we didn’t walk in truth before you.
[Tovi] [3]:[6] Now deal with me according to that which is pleasing in your sight. Command my spirit to be taken from me, that I may be released, and become earth.
