Because it’s more profitable for me to die rather than to live, because I’ve heard false reproaches, and there’s much sorrow in me. Command that I be released from my distress, now, and go to the eternal place. Don’t turn your face away from me.”
[Tovi] [3]:[7] The same day it happened to Sarah the daughter of Re’uel in Ahmeta of Maday (Media), that she also was reproached by her father’s female servants;
[Tovi] [3]:[8] because that she’d been given to seven husbands, and Ashmedai the evil spirit killed them, before they’d lain with her. And they said to her, “Don’t you know that you strangle your husbands? You’ve already had seven husbands, and you haven’t borne the name of any one of them.
[Tovi] [3]:[9] Why do you scourge us? If they’re dead, go your ways with them. Let us never see either son or daughter from you.”
[Tovi] [3]:[10] When she heard these things, she was deeply distressed, so that she thought about hanging herself. Then she said, “I’m my father’s only daughter. If I do this, it’ll be a reproach to him, and I’ll bring down his old age with sorrow to the grave.”
[Tovi] [3]:[11] Then she prayed by the window, and said, “Blessed are you, Oh master my god, and blessed is your holy and honourable name forever! Let all your works praise you forever!
[Tovi] [3]:[12] And now, master, I’ve set my eyes and my face towards you.
[Tovi] [3]:[13] Command that I be released from the earth, and that I no longer hear reproach.
[Tovi] [3]:[14] You know, master, that I’m pure from all sin with man,
[Tovi] [3]:[15] and that I never polluted my name or my father’s name in the land of my captivity. I’m the only daughter of my father, and he has no child that’ll be his heir, nor brother near him, nor son belonging to him, that I should keep myself for a wife to him. Seven husbands of mine are dead already. Why should I live? If it doesn’t please you to kill me, command some regard to be had of me, and pity taken of me, and that I hear no more reproach.”
[Tovi] [3]:[16] The prayer of both was heard before the glory of the great God.
[Tovi] [3]:[17] Refael (Raphael) also was sent to heal them both, to scale away the white films from Tovi’s eyes, and to give Sarah the daughter of Re’uel for a wife to Toviyah (Tobias) the son of Tovi; and to bind the evil spirit Ashmedai; because it belonged to Toviyah that he should inherit her. At that very time, Tovi returned and entered into his house, and Sarah the daughter of Re’uel came down from her upstairs room.
[Tovi] [4]:[1] In that day Tovi (Tobit) remembered the money which he’d left in trust with Gabael in Rages of Maday (Media),
[Tovi] [4]:[2] and he said to himself, I’ve asked for death; why don’t I call my son Toviyah, that I may explain to him about the money before I die?
[Tovi] [4]:[3] And he called him, and said, “My child, if I die, bury me. Don’t despise your mother. Honour her all the days of your life, and do that which is pleasing to her, and don’t grieve her.
[Tovi] [4]:[4] Remember, my child, that she’s seen many dangers for you, when you were in her womb. When she’s dead, bury her by me in one grave.
[Tovi] [4]:[5] My child, be mindful of the master our god all your days, and don’t let your will be set to sin and to transgress his commandments: do righteousness all the days of your life, and don’t follow the ways of unrighteousness.
[Tovi] [4]:[6] Because if you do what is true, your activities will prosperously succeed for you, and for all those who do righteousness.
[Tovi] [4]:[7] Give to the poor from your possessions. When you give to the poor, don’t let your eye be envious. Don’t turn away your face from any poor man, and God’s face won’t be turned away from you.
[Tovi] [4]:[8] Give to the poor in proportion to what you have. If you have little, don’t be afraid to give from that little;
[Tovi] [4]:[9] for you lay up a good treasure for yourself against the day of necessity;
[Tovi] [4]:[10] because giving to the poor delivers from death, and doesn’t allow you to come into darkness.
[Tovi] [4]:[11] Giving to the poor is a good gift in the sight of the Most High for all that give it.
[Tovi] [4]:[12] Beware, my child, of all fornication, and take first a wife from your own extended family. Don’t take a strange wife, who isn’t of your father’s tribe; for we’re the descendants of the prophets. Remember, my child, that Noah, Avraham, Yitshak (Isaac), and Ya’akov (Jacob), our fathers of old time, all took wives of their kindred, and were blessed in their children, and their seed will inherit the land.
[Tovi] [4]:[13] And now, my child, love your kindred, and don’t scorn your kindred and the sons and the daughters of your people in your heart, to take a wife of them; for in scornfulness is destruction and much trouble, and in idleness is decay and great lack; for idleness is the mother of famine.
[Tovi] [4]:[14] Don’t let the wages of any man who works for you wait with you, but give it to him out of hand. If you serve God, you’ll be rewarded. Take heed to yourself, my child, in all your works, and be discreet in all your behaviour.
[Tovi] [4]:[15] And what you yourself hate, do to no man. Don’t drink wine to drunkenness, and don’t let drunkenness go with you on your way.
[Tovi] [4]:[16] Give of your bread to the hungry, and of your clothes to those who are naked. Give to the poor from all your abundance. Don’t let your eye be envious when you give to the poor.
[Tovi] [4]:[17] Pour out your bread on the burial of the just, and give nothing to sinners.
[Tovi] [4]:[18] Ask counsel of every man who’s wise, and don’t despise any counsel that’s profitable.
[Tovi] [4]:[19] Bless the master your god at all times, and ask of him that your ways may be made straight, and that all your paths and counsels may prosper; for every nation has no counsel; but the master himself gives all good things, and he humbles whom he will, as he will. And now, my child, remember my commandments, and let them not be blotted out of your mind.
[Tovi] [4]:[20] And now I explain to you about the ten talents of silver, which I left in trust with Gabael the son of Gabrias at Rages of Maday (Media).
[Tovi] [4]:[21] And fear not, my child, because we’re made poor. You have much wealth, if you fear God, and depart from all sin, and do that which is pleasing in his sight.”
[Tovi] [5]:[1] Then Toviyah (Tobias) replied to him, “Father, I’ll do everything that you’ve commanded me.
[Tovi] [5]:[2] But how could I receive the money, since I don’t know him?”
[Tovi] [5]:[3] He gave him the handwriting, and said to him, “Seek a man who’ll go with you, and I’ll give him wages, while I still live; and go and receive the money.”
[Tovi] [5]:[4] He went to seek a man, and found Refael (Raphael) who was an messenger from God
[Tovi] [5]:[5] but he didn’t know it. He said to him, “Can I go with you to Rages in Maday (Media)? Do you know those places well?”
[Tovi] [5]:[6] The messenger said to him, “I’ll go with you. I know the way well. I’ve lodged with our brother Gabael.”
[Tovi] [5]:[7] Toviyah (Tobias) said to him, “Wait for me, and I’ll tell my father.”
[Tovi] [5]:[8] He said to him, “Go, and don’t wait. And he went in and said to his father, “Listen, I’ve found someone who’ll go with me.” But he said, “Call him to me, that I may know of what tribe he is, and whether he be a trustworthy man to go with you.”
[Tovi] [5]:[9] So he called him, and he came in, and they saluted one another.
[Tovi] [5]:[10] And Tovi (Tobit) said to him, “Brother, of what tribe and of what family are you? Tell me.”
[Tovi] [5]:[11] He said to him, “Do you seek a tribe and a family, or a hired man which will go with your son?” And Tovi said to him, “I want to know, brother, your kindred and your name.”
[Tovi] [5]:[12] And he said, “I’m Azaryah, the son of Hananyah the great, of your kindred.”
[Tovi] [5]:[13] And he said to him, “Welcome, brother. Don’t be angry with me, because I sought to know your tribe and family. You’re my brother, of an honest and good lineage; for I knew Hananyah and Jathan, the sons of Shemayah the great, when we went together to Yerushalem (Jerusalem) to worship, and offered the firstborn, and the tenths of our increase; and they didn’t go astray in the error of our kindred. My brother, you’re of a great stock.
[Tovi] [5]:[14] But tell me, what wages should I give you? A drachma a day, and whatever else you need, as to my son?
[Tovi] [5]:[15] And moreover, if you both return safe and sound, I’ll add something to your wages.”
[Tovi] [5]:[16] And so they agreed. And he said to Toviyah (Tobias), “Prepare yourself for the journey. May God prosper you.” So his son prepared what was needful for the journey, and his father said to him, “Go with this man; but God, who lives in heaven, will prosper your journey. May his messenger go with you.” Then they both departed, and the young man’s dog went with them.
[Tovi] [5]:[17] But Hanah his mother wept, and said to Tovi, “Why have you sent away our child? Isn’t he the staff of our hand, in going in and out before us?
[Tovi] [5]:[18] Don’t be greedy to add money to money; but let it be as refuse compared to our child.
[Tovi] [5]:[19] Because what the master has given us to live is enough for us.”
[Tovi] [5]:[20] Tovi (Tobit) said to her, “Don’t worry, my sister. He’ll return safe and sound, and your eyes will see him.
[Tovi] [5]:[21] Because a good messenger will go with him. His journey will be prospered, and he’ll return safe and sound.”
[Tovi] [5]:[22] So she stopped weeping.
[Tovi] [6]:[1] Now as they went on their journey, they came at evening to the river Hidekel, and they lodged there.
[Tovi] [6]:[2] But the young man went down to wash himself, and a fish leapt out of the river, and would have swallowed up the young man.
[Tovi] [6]:[3] But the messenger said to him, “Grab the fish!” So the young man grabbed the fish, and hauled it up onto the land.
[Tovi] [6]:[4] And the messenger said to him, “Cut the fish open, and take the heart, the liver, and the bile, and keep them with you.”
[Tovi] [6]:[5] And the young man did as the messenger commanded him; but they roasted the fish, and ate it. And they both went on their way, till they drew near to Ahmeta.
[Tovi] [6]:[6] The young man said to the messenger, “Brother Azaryah, of what use is the heart, the liver, and the bile of the fish?”
[Tovi] [6]:[7] He said to him, “About the heart and the liver: If a demon or an evil spirit troubles anyone, we must burn those and make smoke of them before the man or the woman, and the affliction will flee.
[Tovi] [6]:[8] But as for the bile, it’s good to anoint a man that has white films in his eyes, and he’ll be healed.”
[Tovi] [6]:[9] But when they drew near to Rages,
[Tovi] [6]:[10] the messenger said to the young man, “Brother, today we’ll lodge with Re’uel. He’s your kinsman. He has an only daughter named Sarah. I’ll speak about her, that she should be given to you for a wife.
[Tovi] [6]:[11] Because her inheritance belongs to you, and you only are of her kindred.
[Tovi] [6]:[12] The maid is fair and wise. And now hear me, and I’ll speak to her father. When we return from Rages we’ll celebrate the marriage; for I know that Re’uel may in no way marry her to another according to Mosheh’s (Moses) law, or else he’d be liable to death, because it belongs to you to take the inheritance, rather than any other.”
[Tovi] [6]:[13] Then the young man said to the messenger, “Brother Azaryah, I’ve heard that this maid has been given to seven men, and that they all perished in the bridal room.
[Tovi] [6]:[14] Now I’m my father’s only son, and I’m afraid that I might go in and die, just like those before me. Because a demon loves her, which harms no man, but those which come to her. Now I fear that I might die, and bring my father’s and my mother’s life to the grave with sorrow because of me. They have no other son to bury them.”
[Tovi] [6]:[15] But the messenger said to him, “Don’t you remember the words which your father commanded you, that you should take a wife of your own kindred? Now hear me, brother; for she’ll be your wife. Don’t worry about the demon; for this night she’ll be given you as wife.
[Tovi] [6]:[16] And when you come into the bridal room, take the ashes of incense, and put on them some of the heart and liver of the fish, and make smoke with them.
[Tovi] [6]:[17] The demon will smell it, and flee away, and never come again any more. But when you go near to her, both of you rise up, and cry to God who’s merciful. He’ll save you, and have mercy on you. Don’t be afraid, for she was prepared for you from the beginning; and you’ll save her, and she’ll go with you. And I suppose that you’ll have children with her.” When Toviyah (Tobias) heard these things, he loved her, and his soul was strongly joined to her.
[Tovi] [7]:[1] They came to Ahmeta, and arrived at Re’uel’s house. But Sarah met them; and she greeted them, and they her. Then she brought them into the house.
[Tovi] [7]:[2] Re’uel said to Edna his wife, “This young man really resembles Tovi (Tobit) my cousin!”
[Tovi] [7]:[3] And Re’uel asked them, “Where are you two from, kindred?” They said to him, “We’re of the sons of Naftali (Naphtali), who are captives in Nineveh.”
[Tovi] [7]:[4] He said to them, “Do you know Tovi our brother?” They said, “We know him.” Then he said to them, “Is he in good health?”
[Tovi] [7]:[5] They said, “He’s both alive, and in good health.” Toviyah (Tobias) said, “He’s my father.”
[Tovi] [7]:[6] And Re’uel sprang up, and kissed him, wept,
[Tovi] [7]:[7] blessed him, and said to him, “You’re the son of an honest and good man.” When he’d heard that Tovi had lost his sight, he was grieved, and wept;
[Tovi] [7]:[8] and Edna his wife and Sarah his daughter wept. They received them gladly; and they killed a ram of the flock, and served them meat. But Toviyah said to Refael (Raphael), “Brother Azaryah, speak of those things of which you talked about in the way, and let the matter be finished.”
[Tovi] [7]:[9] So he communicated the thing to Re’uel. Re’uel said to Toviyah, “Eat, drink, and make merry:
[Tovi] [7]:[10] for it belongs to you to take my child. However I’ll tell you the truth.
[Tovi] [7]:[11] I’ve given my child to seven men of our relatives, and whenever they came in to her, they died in the night. But for the present be merry.” And Toviyah said, “I won’t eat anything here, until you all make an agreement and enter into that covenant with me.”
[Tovi] [7]:[12] Re’uel said, “Take her to yourself from now on according to custom. You’re her relative, and she’s yours. The merciful God will give all good success to you.”
[Tovi] [7]:[13] And he called his daughter Sarah, and took her by the hand, and gave her to be wife of Toviyah, and said, “Listen, take her to yourself after Mosheh’s (Moses) law, and lead her away to your father.” And he blessed them.
[Tovi] [7]:[14] He called Edna his wife, then took a book, wrote a contract, and sealed it.
[Tovi] [7]:[15] Then they began to eat.
[Tovi] [7]:[16] And Re’uel called his wife Edna, and said to her, “Sister, prepare the other chamber, and bring her in there.”
[Tovi] [7]:[17] She did as he asked her, and brought her in there. She wept, and she received the tears of her daughter, and said to her,
[Tovi] [7]:[18] “Be comforted, my child. May the master of heaven and earth give you favour for this your sorrow. Be comforted, my daughter.”
[Tovi] [8]:[1] When they’d finished their supper, they brought Toviyah in to her.
[Tovi] [8]:[2] But as he went, he remembered Refael’s (Raphael) words, and took the ashes of the incense, and put the heart and the liver of the fish on them, and made smoke with them.
[Tovi] [8]:[3] When the demon smelled that smell, it fled into the uppermost parts of Mitsrayim (Egypt), and the messenger bound him.
[Tovi] [8]:[4] But after they were both shut in together, Toviyah rose up from the bed, and said, “Sister, arise, and let’s pray that the master may have mercy on us.”
[Tovi] [8]:[5] And Toviyah began to say, “Blessed are you, Oh God of our fathers, and blessed is your holy and glorious name forever. Let the heavens bless you, and all your creatures.
[Tovi] [8]:[6] You made Adam, and gave him Havah (Eve) his wife for a helper and support. From them came the seed of men. You said, it isn’t good that the man should be alone. Let’s make him a helper like him.
[Tovi] [8]:[7] And now, Oh master, I take not this my sister for lust, but in truth. Command that I may find mercy and grow old with her.”
[Tovi] [8]:[8] She said with him, “Amen.” And they both slept that night.
[Tovi] [8]:[9] Re’uel arose, and went and dug a grave,
[Tovi] [8]:[10] saying, “In case he should also die.”
[Tovi] [8]:[11] And Re’uel came into his house,
[Tovi] [8]:[12] and said to Edna his wife, “Send one of the female servants, and let them see if he’s alive. If not, we’ll bury him, and no man will know it.”
[Tovi] [8]:[13] So the maidservant opened the door, and went in, and found them both sleeping,
[Tovi] [8]:[14] and came out, and told them that he was alive.
[Tovi] [8]:[15] Then Re’uel blessed God, saying, “Blessed are you, Oh God, with all pure and holy blessing! Let your saints bless you, and all your creatures! Let all your messengers and your elect bless you forever!
[Tovi] [8]:[16] Blessed are you, because you’ve made me glad; and it hasn’t happened to me as I suspected; but you have dealt with us according to your great mercy.
[Tovi] [8]:[17] Blessed are you, because you’ve had mercy on two that were the only begotten children of their parents. Show them mercy, Oh master. Fulfil their life in health with gladness and mercy.
[Tovi] [8]:[18] He commanded his servants to fill the grave.
[Tovi] [8]:[19] He kept the wedding feast for them fourteen days.
[Tovi] [8]:[20] Before the days of the wedding feast were finished, Re’uel sware to him, that he shouldn’t depart till the fourteen days of the wedding feast were fulfilled;
[Tovi] [8]:[21] and that then he should take half of his goods, and go in safety to his father; and the rest, he said, when my wife and I die.
[Tovi] [9]:[1] And Toviyah (Tobias) called Refael (Raphael), and said to him,
[Tovi] [9]:[2] “Brother Azaryah, take with you a servant and two camels, and go to Rages of Maday (Media) to Gabael, and receive the money for me, and bring him to the wedding feast,
[Tovi] [9]:[3] because Re’uel has sworn that I mustn’t depart.
[Tovi] [9]:[4] My father counts the days; and if I wait long, he’ll be very grieved.
[Tovi] [9]:[5] So Refael went on his way, and lodged with Gabael, and gave him the handwriting; so he brought forth the bags with their seals, and gave them to him.
[Tovi] [9]:[6] Then they rose up early in the morning together, and came to the wedding feast. Toviyah blessed his wife.
[Tovi] [10]:[1] Tovi (Tobit) his father counted every day. When the days of the journey were expired, and they didn’t come,
[Tovi] [10]:[2] he said, “Could he have been delayed? Or could Gabael have died, and there’s no one to give him the money?”
[Tovi] [10]:[3] He was very grieved.
[Tovi] [10]:[4] But his wife said to him, “The child has perished, seeing he waits long.” She began to bewail him, and said,
[Tovi] [10]:[5] “I care about nothing, my child, since I’ve let you go, the light of my eyes.”
[Tovi] [10]:[6] Tovi said to her, “Relax and stay calm. Don’t worry. He’s in good health.”
[Tovi] [10]:[7] And she said to him, “Relax and stay calm! Don’t deceive me. My child has perished.” And she went out every day into the way by which they went, and ate no bread in the day-time, and didn’t stop bewailing her son Toviyah (Tobias) for whole nights, until the fourteen days of the wedding feast were expired, which Re’uel had sworn that he should spend there. Then Toviyah said to Re’uel, “Send me away, for my father and my mother look no more to see me.”
[Tovi] [10]:[8] But his father-in-law said to him, “Stay with me, and I’ll send to your father, and they’ll declare to him how things go with you.”
[Tovi] [10]:[9] Toviyah said, “No. Send me away to my father.”
[Tovi] [10]:[10] Re’uel arose, and gave him Sarah his wife, and half his goods, servants and cattle and money;
[Tovi] [10]:[11] and he blessed them, and sent them away, saying, “The god of heaven will prosper you, my children, before I die.”
[Tovi] [10]:[12] And he said to his daughter, “Honour your father-in-law and your mother-in-law. They’re now your parents. Let me hear a good report of you.” Then he kissed her. Edna said to Toviyah, “May the master of heaven restore you, dear brother, and grant to me that I may see your children of my daughter Sarah, that I may rejoice before the master. Listen, I commit my daughter to you in special trust. Don’t cause her grief.
[Tovi] [11]:[1] After these things Toviyah also went his way, blessing God because he’d prospered his journey; and he blessed Re’uel and his wife Edna. Then he went on his way until they drew near to Nineveh.
[Tovi] [11]:[2] Refael (Raphael) said to Toviyah, “Don’t you know, brother, how you left your father?
[Tovi] [11]:[3] Let’s run forward before your wife, and prepare the house.
[Tovi] [11]:[4] But bring the fish’s gallbladder with you.” So they went their way, and the dog went after them.
[Tovi] [11]:[5] Hanah sat looking around towards the path for her son.
[Tovi] [11]:[6] She saw him coming, and said to his father, “Listen, your son is coming with the man that went with him!”
[Tovi] [11]:[7] Refael said, “I know, Toviyah, that your father will open his eyes.
[Tovi] [11]:[8] Therefore anoint his eyes with the bile, and being pricked with it, he’ll rub, and will make the white films fall away. Then he’ll see you.”
[Tovi] [11]:[9] Hanah ran to him, and fell onto the neck of her son, and said to him, “I’ve seen you, my child! I’m ready to die.” They both wept.
[Tovi] [11]:[10] Tovi (Tobit) went towards the door and stumbled; but his son ran to him,
[Tovi] [11]:[11] and took hold of his father. He rubbed the bile on his father’s eyes, saying, “Cheer up, my father.”
[Tovi] [11]:[12] When his eyes began to hurt, he rubbed them.
[Tovi] [11]:[13] Then the white films peeled away from the corners of his eyes; and he saw his son, and fell onto his neck.
[Tovi] [11]:[14] He wept, and said, “Blessed are you, Oh God, and blessed is your name forever! Blessed are all your holy messengers!
[Tovi] [11]:[15] Because you scourged, and had mercy on me. Listen, I see my son Toviyah (Tobias).” And his son went in rejoicing, and told his father the great things that’d happened to him in Maday (Media).
[Tovi] [11]:[16] Tovi went out to meet his daughter-in-law at Nineveh’s gate, rejoicing and blessing God. Those who saw him go marvelled, because he’d received his sight.
[Tovi] [11]:[17] Tovi gave thanks before them, because God had shown mercy on him. When Tovi came near to Sarah his daughter-in-law, he blessed her, saying, “Welcome, daughter! Blessed is God who’s brought you to us, and blessed are your father and your mother.” And there was joy among all his kindred who were at Nineveh.
[Tovi] [11]:[18] Ahikar and Nasbas his brother’s son came.
[Tovi] [11]:[19] Toviyah’ wedding feast was kept seven days with great gladness.
[Tovi] [12]:[1] And Tovi called his son Toviyah, and said to him, “See, my child, that the man which went with you have his wages, and you must give him more.”
[Tovi] [12]:[2] And he said to him, “Father, it’s no harm to me to give him the half of those things which I’ve brought;
[Tovi] [12]:[3] for he’s led me for you in safety, and he cured my wife, and brought my money, and likewise cured you.”
[Tovi] [12]:[4] The old man said, “It’s due to him.”
[Tovi] [12]:[5] And he called the messenger, and said to him, “Take half of all that you’ve brought.”
[Tovi] [12]:[6] Then he called them both privately, and said to them, “Bless God, and give him thanks, and magnify him, and give him thanks in the sight of all that live, for the things which he’s done with you. It’s good to bless God and exalt his name, showing forth with honour God’s works. Don’t be slack to give him thanks.
[Tovi] [12]:[7] It’s good to conceal a king’s secret, but to reveal gloriously God’s works. Do good, and evil won’t find you.
[Tovi] [12]:[8] Good is prayer with fasting, giving to the poor, and righteousness. A little with righteousness is better than much with unrighteousness. It’s better to give to the poor than to lay up gold.
[Tovi] [12]:[9] Giving to the poor delivers from death, and it purges away all sin. Those who give to the poor and do righteousness will be filled with life;
[Tovi] [12]:[10] but those who sin are enemies to their own life.
[Tovi] [12]:[11] Surely I’ll conceal nothing from you. I’ve said, ‘It’s good to conceal a king’s secret, but to reveal gloriously God’s works.’
[Tovi] [12]:[12] And now, when you prayed, and Sarah your daughter-in-law, I brought the memorial of your prayer before the Holy One. When you buried the dead, I was with you likewise.
[Tovi] [12]:[13] And when you didn’t delay to rise up, and leave your dinner, that you might go and cover the dead, your good deed wasn’t hidden from me. I was with you.
[Tovi] [12]:[14] And now God sent me to heal you and Sarah your daughter-in-law.
[Tovi] [12]:[15] I’m Refael (Raphael), one of the seven holy messengers which present the prayers of the saints and go in before the glory of the Holy One.”
[Tovi] [12]:[16] And they were both troubled, and fell onto their faces; for they were afraid.
[Tovi] [12]:[17] And he said to them, “Don’t be afraid. You’ll all have peace; but bless God forever.
[Tovi] [12]:[18] Because I came not of any favour of my own, but by your god’s will. Therefore bless him forever.
[Tovi] [12]:[19] All these days I appeared to you. I didn’t eat or drink, but you all saw a vision.
[Tovi] [12]:[20] Now give God thanks, because I ascend to him who sent me. Write in a book all the things which have been done.”
[Tovi] [12]:[21] Then they rose up, and saw him no more.
[Tovi] [12]:[22] They confessed the great and wonderful works of God, and how the master’s messenger had appeared to them.
[Tovi] [13]:[1] And Tovi (Tobit) wrote a prayer for rejoicing, and said, “Blessed is God who lives forever! Blessed is his kingdom!
[Tovi] [13]:[2] Because he scourges, and shows mercy. He leads down to the grave, and brings up again. There’s no one who’ll escape his hand.
[Tovi] [13]:[3] Give thanks to him before the Gentiles, all you children of Yisrael (Israel)! Because he’s scattered us among them.
[Tovi] [13]:[4] Declare his greatness, there. Extol him before all the living, because he’s our master, and God is our Father forever.
[Tovi] [13]:[5] He’ll scourge us for our iniquities, and will again show mercy, and will gather us out of all the nations among whom you’re all scattered.
[Tovi] [13]:[6] If you turn to him with your whole heart and with your whole soul, to do truth before him, then he’ll turn to you, and won’t hide his face from you. See what he’ll do with you. Give him thanks with your whole mouth. Bless the master of righteousness. Exalt the eternal King. I give him thanks in the land of my captivity, and show his strength and majesty to a nation of sinners. Turn, you sinners, and do righteousness before him. Who can tell if he’ll accept you and have mercy on you?
[Tovi] [13]:[7] I exalt my god. My soul exalts the King of heaven, and rejoices in his greatness.
[Tovi] [13]:[8] Let all men speak, and let them give him thanks in Yerushalem (Jerusalem).
[Tovi] [13]:[9] Oh Yerushalem, the holy city, he’ll scourge you for your sons’ works, and will again have mercy on the sons of the righteous.
[Tovi] [13]:[10] Give thanks to the master with goodness, and bless the eternal King, that his tabernacle may be built in you again with joy, and that he may make glad in you those who are captives, and love in you forever those who are miserable.
[Tovi] [13]:[11] Many nations will come from afar to the name of the master God with gifts in their hands, even gifts to the King of heaven. Generations of generations will praise you, and sing songs of rejoicing.
[Tovi] [13]:[12] All those who hate you’re cursed. All those who love you forever will be blessed.
[Tovi] [13]:[13] Rejoice and be extremely glad for the sons of the righteous; for they’ll be gathered together and will bless the master of the righteous.
[Tovi] [13]:[14] Oh blessed are those who love you. They’ll rejoice for your peace. Blessed are all those who mourned for all your scourges; because they’ll rejoice for you when they’ve seen all your glory. They’ll be made glad forever.
[Tovi] [13]:[15] Let my soul bless God the great King.
[Tovi] [13]:[16] Because Yerushalem (Jerusalem) will be built with sapphires, emeralds, and precious stones; your walls and towers and battlements with pure gold.
[Tovi] [13]:[17] Yerushalem’s streets will be paved with beryl, carbuncle, and stones of Ofir.
[Tovi] [13]:[18] All her streets will say, “Hallelujah!” and give praise, saying, “Blessed be God, who’s exalted you forever!”
[Tovi] [14]:[1] Then Tovi (Tobit) finished giving thanks.
[Tovi] [14]:[2] He was fifty-eight years old when he lost his sight. After eight years, he received it again. He gave to the poor and he feared the master God more and more, and gave thanks to him.
[Tovi] [14]:[3] Now he grew very old; and he called his son with the six sons of his son, and said to him, “My child, take your sons. Listen, I’ve grown old, and am ready to depart out of this life.
[Tovi] [14]:[4] Go into Maday (Media), my child, for I surely believe all the things which Yonah (Jonah) the prophet spoke of Nineveh, that it’ll be overthrown, but in Maday there’ll rather be peace for a season. Our kindred will be scattered in the earth from the good land. Yerushalem (Jerusalem) will be desolate, and God’s house in it’ll be burnt up, and will be desolate for a time.
[Tovi] [14]:[5] God will again have mercy on them, and bring them back into the land, and they’ll build the house, but not like to the former house, until the times of that age are fulfilled. Afterward they’ll return from the places of their captivity, and build up Yerushalem with honour. God’s house will be built in it forever with a glorious building, even as the prophets spoke about it.
[Tovi] [14]:[6] And all the nations will turn to fear the master God truly, and will bury their idols.
[Tovi] [14]:[7] All the nations will bless the master, and his people will give thanks to God, and the master will exalt his people; and all those who love the master God in truth and righteousness will rejoice, showing mercy to our kindred.
[Tovi] [14]:[8] And now, my child, depart from Nineveh, because those things which the prophet Yonah spoke will surely happen.
[Tovi] [14]:[9] But you must keep the law and the ordinances, and show yourself merciful and righteous, that it may be well with you.
[Tovi] [14]:[10] Bury me decently, and your mother with me. Don’t stay at Nineveh. See, my child, what Aman did to Ahikar who nourished him, how out of light he brought him into darkness, and all the recompense that he made him. Ahikar was saved, but the other had his recompense, and he went down into darkness. Menasheh (Manasseh) gave to the poor, and escaped the snare of death which he set for him; but Aman fell into the snare, and perished.
[Tovi] [14]:[11] And now, my children, consider what giving to the poor does, and how righteousness delivers.” While he was saying these things, he gave up the ghost in the bed; but he was one hundred and fifty eight years old. Toviyah (Tobias) buried him magnificently.
[Tovi] [14]:[12] When Hanah died, he buried her with his father. But Toviyah departed with his wife and his sons to Ahmeta to Re’uel his father-in-law,
[Tovi] [14]:[13] and he grew old in honour, and he buried his father-in-law and mother-in-law magnificently, and he inherited their possessions, and his father Tovi’s (Tobit).
[Tovi] [14]:[14] He died at Ahmeta of Maday (Media), being one hundred and twenty seven years old.
[Tovi] [14]:[15] Before he died, he heard of the destruction of Nineveh, which Nevukadnetsar (Nebuchadnezzar) and Ahashverosh (Ahasuerus) took captive. Before his death, he rejoiced over Nineveh.
[Yehudit] [1]:[1] In the twelfth year of Nevukadnetsar’s (Nebuchadnezzar) reign, who reigned over the Assyrians in Nineveh, the great city, in the days of Arpakshad, who reigned over the Madim (Medes) in Ahmeta,
[Yehudit] [1]:[2] and built around Ahmeta walls of hewn stones three cubits broad and six cubits long, and made the height of the wall seventy cubits, and its breadth fifty cubits,
[Yehudit] [1]:[3] and set its towers at its gates one hundred cubits high, and its breadth in the foundation was sixty cubits,
[Yehudit] [1]:[4] and made its gates, even gates that were raised to the height of seventy cubits, and their breadth forty cubits, for his mighty army to go out of, and the setting in array of his footmen—
[Yehudit] [1]:[5] in those days King Nevukadnetsar made war with King Arpakshad in the great plain. This plain is on the borders of Ragau.
[Yehudit] [1]:[6] There came to meet him all that lived in the hill country, and all that lived by Perat (Euphrates), Hidekel, and Hudaspes, and in the plain of Areyok the king of the Elymaeans. Many nations of the sons of Chelod assembled themselves to the battle.
[Yehudit] [1]:[7] And Nevukadnetsar king of the Assyrians sent to all who lived in Paras (Persia), and to all who lived westward, to those who lived in Kilikia, Damesek (Damascus), Levanon, Anti-Lebanon, and to all who lived along the sea coast,
[Yehudit] [1]:[8] and to those among the nations that were of Karmel and Gilead, and to the higher Galil and the great plain of Yizre’el (Jezreel),
[Yehudit] [1]:[9] and to all who were in Shomron (Samaria) and its cities, and beyond Yarden (Jordan) to Yerushalem (Jerusalem), Betane, Chellus, Kadesh, the river of Mitsrayim (Egypt), Tahfanhes, Ra’meses, and all the land of Goshen,
[Yehudit] [1]:[10] until you come above Tsoan and Nof (Memphis), and to all that lived in Mitsrayim, until you come to the borders of Kush (Ethiopia).
[Yehudit] [1]:[11] All those who lived in all the land made light of the commandment of Nevukadnetsar king of the Assyrians, and didn’t go with him to the war; for they weren’t afraid of him, but he was before them as one man. They turned away his messengers from their presence without effect, and with disgrace.
[Yehudit] [1]:[12] And Nevukadnetsar was extremely angry with all this land, and he swore by his throne and kingdom that he’d surely be avenged on all the coasts of Kilikia, Damesek, and Aram (Syria), that he’d kill with his sword all the inhabitants of the land of Moav (Moab), the children of Amon, all Yehudah (Judea), and all who were in Mitsrayim, until you come to the borders of the two seas.
[Yehudit] [1]:[13] And he set the battle in array with his army against King Arpakshad in the seventeenth year; and he prevailed in his battle, and turned to flight all Arpakshad’s army, with all his horses and all his chariots.
[Yehudit] [1]:[14] He took possession of his cities. He came to Ahmeta and took the towers, plundered its streets, and turned its beauty into shame.
[Yehudit] [1]:[15] He took Arpakshad in the mountains of Ragau, struck him through with his darts, and utterly destroyed him to this day.
[Yehudit] [1]:[16] He returned with them to Nineveh, he and all his company of sundry nations—a very great multitude of men of war. There he took his ease and banqueted, he and his army, for one hundred and twenty days.
[Yehudit] [2]:[1] In the eighteenth year, the twenty-second day of the first month, there was talk in the house of Nevukadnetsar king of the Assyrians that he should be avenged on all the land, even as he spoke.
[Yehudit] [2]:[2] He called together all his servants and all his great men, and communicated with them his secret counsel, and with his own mouth, recounted the wickedness of all the land.
[Yehudit] [2]:[3] They decreed to destroy all flesh which didn’t follow the word of his mouth.
[Yehudit] [2]:[4] When he’d ended his counsel, Nevukadnetsar king of the Assyrians called Holofernes the chief captain of his army, who was second to himself, and said to him,
[Yehudit] [2]:[5] “The great king, the lord of all the earth, says: ‘Listen, go out from my presence, and take with you men who trust in their strength, to one hundred and twenty thousand footmen and twelve thousand horses with their riders.
[Yehudit] [2]:[6] And go out against all the west country, because they disobeyed the commandment of my mouth.
[Yehudit] [2]:[7] Tell to them that they should prepare earth and water, because I’ll go out in my anger against them, and will cover the whole face of the earth with the feet of my army, who’ll plunder them.
[Yehudit] [2]:[8] Their slain will fill their valleys and brooks, and the river will be filled with their dead until it overflows.
[Yehudit] [2]:[9] I’ll lead them as captives to the utmost parts of all the earth.
[Yehudit] [2]:[10] But go out, and take all their coasts for me first. If they’ll yield themselves to you, then you must reserve them for me until the day of their reproof.
[Yehudit] [2]:[11] As for those who resist, show no mercy; but hand them over to be slain and to be plundered in all your land.
[Yehudit] [2]:[12] Because as I live, and by the power of my kingdom, I’ve spoken, and I’ll do this with my hand.
[Yehudit] [2]:[13] Moreover, don’t disobey any of your lord’s commands, but you must carry them out, as I’ve commanded you. Don’t delay carrying them out.’ ”
[Yehudit] [2]:[14] So Holofernes went out from the presence of his lord, and called all the governors, the captains, and officers of Ashur’s (Assyria) army.
[Yehudit] [2]:[15] He counted chosen men for the battle, as his lord had commanded him, to one hundred and twenty thousand, with twelve thousand archers on horseback.
[Yehudit] [2]:[16] He arranged them as a great multitude is ordered for the war.
[Yehudit] [2]:[17] He took camels, donkeys, and mules for their baggage, a very great multitude, and sheep, oxen, and goats without number for their provision,
[Yehudit] [2]:[18] and a large supply of rations for every man, and a huge amount of gold and silver out of the king’s house.
[Yehudit] [2]:[19] He went out, he and all his army, on their journey, to go before King Nevukadnetsar (Nebuchadnezzar), and to cover all the face of the earth westward with their chariots, horsemen, and chosen footmen.
[Yehudit] [2]:[20] A great company of various nations went out with them like locusts and like the sand of the earth. Because they couldn’t be counted because of their multitude.
[Yehudit] [2]:[21] And they departed out of Nineveh three days’ journey towards the plain of Bectileth, and encamped from Bectileth near the mountain which is at the left hand of the Upper Kilikia.
[Yehudit] [2]:[22] And he took all his army, his footmen, horsemen, and chariots, and went away from there into the hill country,
[Yehudit] [2]:[23] and destroyed Put and Lud, and plundered all the children of Rasses and the children of Yishmael (Ishmael), which were along the wilderness to the south of the land of the Chellians.
[Yehudit] [2]:[24] And he went over Perat (Euphrates), and went through Mesopotamia, and broke down all the high cities that were on the river Arbonai, until you come to the sea.
[Yehudit] [2]:[25] And he took possession of the borders of Kilikia, and killed all who resisted him, and came to the borders of Yefet (Japheth), which were towards the south, opposite Arav.
[Yehudit] [2]:[26] He surrounded all the children of Midyan, and set their tents on fire, and plundered their sheepfolds.
[Yehudit] [2]:[27] He went down into the plain of Damesek (Damascus) in the days of wheat harvest, and set all their fields on fire, and utterly destroyed their flocks and herds, plundered their cities, laid their plains waste, and struck all their young men with the edge of the sword.
[Yehudit] [2]:[28] And the fear and the dread of him fell onto those who lived on the sea coast, on those who were in Tsidon (Sidon) and Tsor (Tyre), those who lived in Sur and Ocina, and all who lived in Yavneh. Those who lived in Azotos and Ashkelon feared him greatly.
[Yehudit] [3]:[1] And they sent to him messengers with words of peace, saying,
[Yehudit] [3]:[2] “Listen, we the servants of Nevukadnetsar (Nebuchadnezzar) the great king lie before you. Use us as it’s pleasing in your sight.
[Yehudit] [3]:[3] Listen, our dwellings, and all our country, and all our fields of wheat, and our flocks and herds, and all the sheepfolds of our tents, lie before your face. Use them as it may please you.
[Yehudit] [3]:[4] Listen, even our cities and those who live in them are your servants. Come and deal with them as it’s good in your eyes.”
[Yehudit] [3]:[5] So the men came to Holofernes, and declared to him according to these words.
[Yehudit] [3]:[6] He came down towards the sea coast, he and his army, and set garrisons in the high cities, and took out of them chosen men for allies.
[Yehudit] [3]:[7] They received him, they and all the country round about them, with garlands and dances and timbrels.
[Yehudit] [3]:[8] He threw down all their borders, and cut down their sacred groves. It’d been given to him to destroy all the gods of the land, that all the nations would worship Nevukadnetsar only, and that all their tongues and their tribes would call on him as a god.
[Yehudit] [3]:[9] Then he came towards Yizre’el (Jezreel) near to Dotan, which is opposite the great ridge of Yehudah (Judea).
[Yehudit] [3]:[10] He encamped between Geva and Beyt-Shean. He was there a whole month, that he might gather together all the baggage of his army.
[Yehudit] [4]:[1] The children of Yisrael (Israel) who lived in Yehudah heard all that Holofernes the chief captain of Nevukadnetsar king of the Assyrians had done to the nations, and how he’d plundered all their temples and destroyed them utterly.
[Yehudit] [4]:[2] They were extremely afraid at his approach, and were troubled for Yerushalem (Jerusalem) and for the temple of the master their god;
[Yehudit] [4]:[3] because they’d newly come up from the captivity, and all Yehudah’s people were recently gathered together; and the vessels, the altar, and the house were sanctified after being profaned.
[Yehudit] [4]:[4] And they sent into every coast of Shomron (Samaria), to Konae, to Beyt-Horon, Belmaim, Yeriho (Jericho), to Choba, Aesora, and to the valley of Shalem;
[Yehudit] [4]:[5] and they occupied beforehand all the tops of the high mountains, fortified the villages that were in them, and stored supplies for the provision of war, for their fields were newly reaped.
[Yehudit] [4]:[6] Yehoyakim the high priest, who was in those days at Yerushalem, wrote to those who lived in Betulia and Betomesthaim, which is opposite Yizre’el (Jezreel) towards the plain that’s near to Dotan,
[Yehudit] [4]:[7] charging them to seize on the ascents of the hill country; because by them was the entrance into Yehudah, and it was easy to stop them from approaching, since the approach was narrow, with space for two men at the most.
[Yehudit] [4]:[8] And the children of Yisrael did as Yehoyakim the high priest had commanded them, as did the senate of all Yisrael’s people, which was in session at Yerushalem.
[Yehudit] [4]:[9] And every man of Yisrael cried to God with great earnestness, and with great earnestness they humbled their souls.
[Yehudit] [4]:[10] They, their wives, their children, their cattle, and every sojourner, hireling, and servant bought with their money put sackcloth on their loins.
[Yehudit] [4]:[11] Every man and woman of Yisrael, including the little children and the inhabitants of Yerushalem, fell prostrate before the temple, threw ashes on their heads, and spread out their sackcloth before the master. They put sackcloth around the altar.
[Yehudit] [4]:[12] They cried to the god of Yisrael earnestly with one consent, that he wouldn’t give their children as prey, their wives as plunder, the cities of their inheritance to destruction, and the sanctuary to being profaned and being made a reproach, for the nations to rejoice at.
[Yehudit] [4]:[13] The master heard their voice, and looked at their affliction. The people continued fasting many days in all Yehudah and Yerushalem before the sanctuary of the master Almighty.
[Yehudit] [4]:[14] And Yehoyakim the high priest, and all the priests who stood before the master, and those who ministered to the master, had their loins dressed in sackcloth and offered the continual burnt offering, the vows, and the free gifts of the people.
[Yehudit] [4]:[15] They had ashes on their turbans. They cried to the master with all their power, that he’d look on all the house of Yisrael for good.
[Yehudit] [5]:[1] Holofernes, the chief captain of Ashur’s (Assyria) army, was told that the children of Yisrael had prepared for war, had shut up the passages of the hill country, had fortified all the tops of the high hills, and had set up barricades in the plains.
[Yehudit] [5]:[2] Then he was extremely angry, and he called all the princes of Moav (Moab), Amon’s captains, and all the governors of the sea coast,
[Yehudit] [5]:[3] and he said to them, “Tell me now, you sons of Kena’an (Canaan), who are these people who live in the hill country? What are the cities that they inhabit? How large is their army? Where is their power and their strength? What king is set over them, to be the leader of their army?
[Yehudit] [5]:[4] Why have they turned their backs, that they shouldn’t come and meet me, more than all who live in the west?”
[Yehudit] [5]:[5] Then Ahior, the leader of all the children of Amon, said to him, “Let my lord now hear a word from your servant’s mouth, and I’ll tell you the truth about these people who live in this hill country, near to the place where you live. No lie will come out of your servant’s mouth.
[Yehudit] [5]:[6] These people are descended from the Kasdim (Chaldeans).
[Yehudit] [5]:[7] They sojourned before this in Mesopotamia, because they didn’t want to follow the gods of their fathers, which were in the land of the Kasdim.
[Yehudit] [5]:[8] They departed from the way of their parents, and worshipped the god of heaven, the god whom they knew. Their parents threw them out from the face of their gods, and they fled into Mesopotamia and sojourned there many days.
[Yehudit] [5]:[9] Then their god commanded them to depart from the place where they sojourned, and to go into the land of Kena’an. They lived there, and prospered with gold and silver, and with very large herds of cattle.
[Yehudit] [5]:[10] Then they went down into Mitsrayim (Egypt), for a famine covered all the land of Kena’an. They sojourned there until they’d grown up. They became a great multitude there, so that one couldn’t count the population of their nation.
[Yehudit] [5]:[11] Then the king of Mitsrayim rose up against them, and dealt subtly with them, and brought them low, making them labour in brick, and made them slaves.
[Yehudit] [5]:[12] They cried to their god, and he struck all the land of Mitsrayim with incurable plagues; so the Mitsrim (Egyptians) threw them out of their sight.
[Yehudit] [5]:[13] God dried up the Red sea before them,
[Yehudit] [5]:[14] and brought them into the way of Sinay Kadesh-Barnea and they threw out all that lived in the wilderness.
[Yehudit] [5]:[15] They lived in the land of the Amorim, and they destroyed by their strength everyone in Heshbon. Passing over Yarden (Jordan), they possessed all the hill country.
[Yehudit] [5]:[16] They threw out before them the Kena’ani (Canaanite), the Perizi, the Yevusi, the Shechemite, and all the Girgashim, and they lived in that country many days.
[Yehudit] [5]:[17] And while they didn’t sin before their god, they prospered, because God who hates iniquity was with them.
[Yehudit] [5]:[18] But when they departed from the way which he appointed them, they were destroyed in many severe battles, and were led captives into a land that wasn’t theirs. Their god’s temple was razed to the ground, and their cities were taken by their adversaries.
[Yehudit] [5]:[19] And now they’ve returned to their god, and have come up from the dispersion where they were dispersed, and have possessed Yerushalem (Jerusalem), where their sanctuary is, and are settled in the hill country; for it was desolate.
[Yehudit] [5]:[20] And now, my lord and master, if there’s any error in this people, and they sin against their god, we’ll find out what this thing is in which they stumble, and we’ll go up and overcome them.
[Yehudit] [5]:[21] But if there’s no lawlessness in their nation, let my lord now pass by, otherwise their master might defend them and their god might take their side, and we’d be disgraced before the whole world.”
[Yehudit] [5]:[22] When Ahior had finished speaking these words, all the people standing around the tent complained. The great men of Holofernes, and all who lived by the sea side and in Moav (Moab), said that he should be cut to pieces.
[Yehudit] [5]:[23] Because, they said, “We won’t be afraid of the children of Yisrael (Israel), because they’re a people that has no power nor might to make the battle strong.
[Yehudit] [5]:[24] Therefore now we’ll go up, and they’ll be a prey to be devoured by all your army, master Holofernes.”
[Yehudit] [6]:[1] And when the disturbance of the men that were around the council had ceased, Holofernes the chief captain of Ashur’s (Assyria) army said to Ahior and to all the children of Moav before all the people of the foreigners:
[Yehudit] [6]:[2] “And who are you, Ahior, and the mercenaries of Efrayim (Ephraim), that you’ve prophesied among us as today, and have said that we shouldn’t make war with the race of Yisrael, because their god will defend them? And who’s God but Nevukadnetsar (Nebuchadnezzar)?
[Yehudit] [6]:[3] He’ll send forth his might, and will destroy them from the face of the earth, and their god won’t deliver them; but we his servants will strike them as one man. They won’t sustain the might of our cavalry.
[Yehudit] [6]:[4] Because with them we’ll burn them up. Their mountains will be drunken with their blood. Their plains will be filled with their dead bodies. Their footsteps won’t stand before us, but they’ll surely perish, says King Nevukadnetsar, lord of all the earth; for he said, ‘The words that I’ve spoken won’t be in vain.’
[Yehudit] [6]:[5] But you, Ahior, hireling of Amon, who’ve spoken these words in the day of your iniquity, will see my face no more from this day, until I’m avenged of the race of those that came out of Mitsrayim (Egypt).
[Yehudit] [6]:[6] And then the sword of my army, and the multitude of those who serve me, will pass through your sides, and you’ll fall among their slain when I return.
[Yehudit] [6]:[7] Then my servants will bring you back into the hill country, and will set you in one of the cities by the passes.
[Yehudit] [6]:[8] You won’t perish until you’re destroyed with them.
[Yehudit] [6]:[9] And if you hope in your heart that they won’t be taken, don’t let your face fall. I’ve spoken it, and none of my words will fall to the ground.”
[Yehudit] [6]:[10] Then Holofernes commanded his servants who waited in his tent to take Ahior, and bring him back to Betulia, and deliver him into the hands of the children of Yisrael (Israel).
[Yehudit] [6]:[11] So his servants took him, and brought him out of the camp into the plain, and they moved from the middle of the plains into the hill country, and came to the springs that were under Betulia.
[Yehudit] [6]:[12] When the men of the city saw them on the top of the hill, they took up their weapons, and went out of the city against them to the top of the hill. Every man that used a sling kept them from coming up, and threw stones at them.
[Yehudit] [6]:[13] They took cover under the hill, bound Ahior, threw him down, left him at the foot of the hill, and went away to their lord.
[Yehudit] [6]:[14] But the children of Yisrael descended from their city, and came to him, untied him, led him away into Betulia, and presented him to the rulers of their city,
[Yehudit] [6]:[15] which were in those days Ozias the son of Mikah, of the tribe of Shim’on (Simeon), and Chabris the son of Otniel, and Charmis the son of Malkiel.
[Yehudit] [6]:[16] Then they called together all the elders of the city; and all their young men ran together, with their women, to the assembly. They set Ahior among all their people. Then Ozias asked him what had happened.
[Yehudit] [6]:[17] He answered and declared to them the words of the council of Holofernes, and all the words that he’d spoken among the princes of the children of Ashur (Assyria), and all the great words that Holofernes had spoken against the house of Yisrael.
[Yehudit] [6]:[18] Then the people fell down and worshipped God, and cried, saying,
[Yehudit] [6]:[19] “Oh master God of heaven, look at their arrogance, and pity the low estate of our race. Look on the face of those who are sanctified to you this day.”
[Yehudit] [6]:[20] They comforted Ahior, and praised him highly.
[Yehudit] [6]:[21] Then Ozias took him out of the assembly into his house, and made a feast for the elders. They called on the god of Yisrael for help all that night.
[Yehudit] [7]:[1] The next day Holofernes commanded all his army and all the people who’d come to be his allies, that they should move their camp towards Betulia, seize the passes of the hill country, and make war against the children of Yisrael.
[Yehudit] [7]:[2] Every mighty man of them moved that day. The army of their men of war was one hundred and seventy thousand footmen, plus twelve thousand horsemen, besides the baggage and the men who were on foot among them—a very great multitude.
[Yehudit] [7]:[3] They encamped in the valley near Betulia, by the fountain. They spread themselves in breadth over Dotan even to Belmaim, and in length from Betulia to Kuamon, which is near Yizre’el (Jezreel).
[Yehudit] [7]:[4] But the children of Yisrael, when they saw the multitude of them, were terrified, and everyone said to his neighbour, “Now these men will lick up the face of all the earth. Neither the high mountains, nor the valleys, nor the hills will be able to bear their weight.
[Yehudit] [7]:[5] Every man took up his weapons of war, and when they’d kindled fires on their towers, they remained and watched all that night.
[Yehudit] [7]:[6] But on the second day Holofernes led out all his cavalry in the sight of the children of Yisrael which were in Betulia,
[Yehudit] [7]:[7] viewed the ascents to their city, and searched out the springs of the waters, seized on them, and set garrisons of men of war over them. Then he departed back to his people.
[Yehudit] [7]:[8] All the rulers of the children of Esav (Esau), all the leaders of the people of Moav (Moab), and the captains of the sea coast came to him and said,
[Yehudit] [7]:[9] “Let our lord now hear a word, that there not be losses in your army.
[Yehudit] [7]:[10] Because this people of the children of Yisrael don’t trust in their spears, but in the height of the mountains wherein they live, for it isn’t easy to come up to the tops of their mountains.
[Yehudit] [7]:[11] And now, my lord, don’t fight against them as men fight who join battle, and there won’t so much as one man of your people perish.
[Yehudit] [7]:[12] Remain in your camp, and keep every man of your army safe. Let your servants get possession of the water spring, which flows from the foot of the mountain,
[Yehudit] [7]:[13] because all the inhabitants of Betulia get their water from there. Then thirst will kill them, and they’ll give up their city. Then we and our people will go up to the tops of the mountains that are near, and will camp on them, to watch that not one man gets out of the city.
[Yehudit] [7]:[14] They’ll be consumed with famine—they, their wives, and their children. Before the sword comes against them they’ll be laid low in the streets where they live.
[Yehudit] [7]:[15] And you’ll pay them back with evil, because they rebelled, and didn’t meet your face in peace.”
[Yehudit] [7]:[16] Their words were pleasing in the sight of Holofernes and in the sight of all his servants; and he ordered them to do as they’d spoken.
[Yehudit] [7]:[17] And the army of the children of Amon moved, and with them five thousand of the children of Ashur (Assyria), and they encamped in the valley. They seized the waters and the springs of the waters of the children of Yisrael.
[Yehudit] [7]:[18] The children of Esav (Esau) went up with the children of Amon, and encamped in the hill country near Dotan. They sent some of them towards the south, and towards the east, near Ekrebel, which is near Chusi, that’s on the brook Mochmur. The rest of the army of the Assyrians encamped in the plain, and covered all the face of the land. Their tents and baggage were pitched on it in a great crowd. They were a very great multitude.
[Yehudit] [7]:[19] The children of Yisrael cried to the master their god, for their spirit fainted; for all their enemies had surrounded them. There was no way to escape out from among them.
[Yehudit] [7]:[20] All Ashur’s army remained around them, their footmen and their chariots and their horsemen, for thirty-four days. All their vessels of water ran dry for all the inhabitants of Betulia.
[Yehudit] [7]:[21] The cisterns were emptied, and they had no water to drink their fill for one day; for they rationed drink by measure.
[Yehudit] [7]:[22] Their young children were discouraged. The women and the young men fainted for thirst. They fell down in the streets of the city, and in the passages of the gates. There was no longer any strength in them.
[Yehudit] [7]:[23] All the people, including the young men, the women, and the children, were gathered together against Ozias, and against the rulers of the city. They cried with a loud voice, and said before all the elders,
[Yehudit] [7]:[24] “God be judge between all of you and us, because you’ve done us great wrong, in that you haven’t spoken words of peace with the children of Ashur.
[Yehudit] [7]:[25] Now we have no helper; but God has sold us into their hands, that we should be laid low before them with thirst and great destruction.
[Yehudit] [7]:[26] And now summon them, and deliver up the whole city as prey to Holofernes’ people, and to all his army.
[Yehudit] [7]:[27] Because it’s better for us to be captured by them. Because we’ll be servants, and our souls will live, and we won’t see the death of our babies before our eyes, and our wives and our children fainting in death.
[Yehudit] [7]:[28] We take to witness against you the heaven and the earth, and our god and the master of our fathers, who punishes us according to our sins and the sins of our fathers. Do what we’ve said today!”
[Yehudit] [7]:[29] And there was great weeping of all with one consent in the assembly; and they cried to the master God with a loud voice.
[Yehudit] [7]:[30] And Ozias said to them, “Brethren, be of good courage! Let us endure five more days, during which the master our god will turn his mercy towards us; for he won’t forsake us utterly.
[Yehudit] [7]:[31] But if these days pass, and no help comes to us, I’ll do what you say.”
[Yehudit] [7]:[32] Then he dispersed the people, every man to his own camp; and they went away to the walls and towers of their city. He sent the women and children into their houses. They were brought very low in the city.
[Yehudit] [8]:[1] In those days Yehudit (Judith) heard about this. She was the daughter of Merari, the son of Ox, the son of Yosef (Joseph), the son of Uziel, the son of Hilkiyah, the son of Hananyah, the son of Gid’on, the son of Raphaim, the son of Ahituv, the son of Elihu, the son of Eliav, the son of Netanel, the son of Shelumiel, the son of Salasadai, the son of Yisrael (Israel).
[Yehudit] [8]:[2] Her husband was Menasheh (Manasseh), of her tribe and of her family. He died in the days of barley harvest.
[Yehudit] [8]:[3] Because he stood over those who bound sheaves in the field, and was overcome by the burning heat, and he fell on his bed, and died in his city Betulia. So they buried him with his fathers in the field which is between Dotan and Ba’al-Hamon.
[Yehudit] [8]:[4] Yehudit was a widow in her house three years and four months.
[Yehudit] [8]:[5] She made herself a tent on the roof of her house, and put on sackcloth on her loins. The clothes of her widowhood were on her.
[Yehudit] [8]:[6] And she fasted all the days of her widowhood, except the eves of the Sabbaths, the Sabbaths, the eves of the new moons, the new moons, and the feasts and joyful days of the house of Yisrael.
[Yehudit] [8]:[7] She was beautiful in appearance, and lovely to look at. Her husband Menasheh had left her gold, silver, male servants, female servants, cattle, and lands. She remained on those lands.
[Yehudit] [8]:[8] No one said anything evil about her, for she feared God greatly.
[Yehudit] [8]:[9] She heard the evil words of the people against the governor, because they fainted for lack of water; and Yehudit heard all the words that Ozias spoke to them, how he swore to them that he’d deliver the city to the Assyrians after five days.
[Yehudit] [8]:[10] So she sent her maid, who was over all things that she had, to summon Ozias, Chabris, and Charmis, the elders of her city.
[Yehudit] [8]:[11] They came to her, and she said to them, “Hear me now, Oh you rulers of the inhabitants of Betulia! Because your word that you’ve spoken before the people this day isn’t right. You’ve set the oath which you’ve pronounced between God and you, and have promised to deliver the city to our enemies, unless within these days the master turns to help you.
[Yehudit] [8]:[12] Now who are you that you’ve tested God this day, and stand in the place of God among the children of men?
[Yehudit] [8]:[13] Now try the master Almighty, and you’ll never know anything.
[Yehudit] [8]:[14] Because you won’t find the depth of the heart of man, and you won’t perceive the things that he thinks. How will you search out God, who’s made all these things, and know his mind, and comprehend his purpose? No, my kindred, don’t provoke the master our god to anger!
[Yehudit] [8]:[15] Because if he hasn’t decided to help us within these five days, he has power to defend us in such time as he will, or to destroy us before our enemies’ face.
[Yehudit] [8]:[16] But don’t you pledge the counsels of the master our god! Because God isn’t like a human being, that he should be threatened, neither is he like a son of man, that he should be won over by pleading.
[Yehudit] [8]:[17] Therefore let’s wait for the salvation that comes from him, and call on him to help us. He’ll hear our voice, if it pleases him.
[Yehudit] [8]:[18] Because there arose none in our age, neither is there any of us today, tribe, or kindred, or family, or city, which worship gods made with hands, as it was in the former days;
[Yehudit] [8]:[19] for which cause our fathers were given to the sword, and for plunder, and fell with a great destruction before our enemies.
[Yehudit] [8]:[20] But we know no other god beside him. Therefore we hope that he won’t despise us, nor any of our race.
[Yehudit] [8]:[21] Because if we’re captured, all Yehudah (Judea) will be captured and our sanctuary will be plundered; and he’ll require our blood for profaning it.
[Yehudit] [8]:[22] The slaughter of our kindred, the captivity of the land, and the desolation of our inheritance, he’ll bring on our heads among the Gentiles, wherever we’ll be in bondage. We’ll be an offence and a reproach to those who take us for a possession.
[Yehudit] [8]:[23] Because our bondage won’t be ordered to favour; but the master our god will turn it to dishonour.
[Yehudit] [8]:[24] And now, kindred, let’s show an example to our kindred, because their soul depends on us, and the sanctuary, the house, and the altar depend on us.
[Yehudit] [8]:[25] Besides all this let’s give thanks to the master our god, who tries us, even as he did our fathers also.
[Yehudit] [8]:[26] Remember all the things which he did to Avraham, and all the things in which he tried Yitshak (Isaac), and all the things which happened to Ya’akov (Jacob) in Mesopotamia of Aram (Syria), when he kept the sheep of Lavan (Laban) his mother’s brother.
[Yehudit] [8]:[27] Because he hasn’t tried us in the fire, as he did them, to search out their hearts, neither has he taken vengeance on us; but the master scourges those who come near to him, to admonish them.”
[Yehudit] [8]:[28] And Ozias said to her, “All that you’ve spoken, you’ve spoken with a good heart. There’s no one who’ll deny your words.
[Yehudit] [8]:[29] Because this isn’t the first day wherein your wisdom is manifested; but from the beginning of your days all the people have known your understanding, because the disposition of your heart is good.
[Yehudit] [8]:[30] But the people were extremely thirsty, and compelled us to do as we spoke to them, and to bring an oath on ourselves, which we won’t break.
[Yehudit] [8]:[31] And now pray for us, because you’re a godly woman, and the master will send us rain to fill our cisterns, and we’ll faint no more.”
[Yehudit] [8]:[32] Then Yehudit (Judith) said to them, “Hear me, and I’ll do a thing, which will go down to all generations among the children of our race.
[Yehudit] [8]:[33] All of you must stand at the gate tonight. I’ll go out with my maid. Within the days after which you said that you’d deliver the city to our enemies, the master will deliver Yisrael (Israel) by my hand.
[Yehudit] [8]:[34] But don’t ask what I’m going to do; for I won’t tell you until the things are finished that I’ll do.”
[Yehudit] [8]:[35] Then Ozias and the rulers said to her, “Go in peace. May the master God be before you, to take vengeance on our enemies.”
[Yehudit] [8]:[36] So they returned from the tent, and went to their stations.
[Yehudit] [9]:[1] But Yehudit fell onto her face, and put ashes on her head, and uncovered the sackcloth with which she was clothed. The incense of that evening was now being offered at Yerushalem (Jerusalem) in God’s house, and Yehudit cried to the master with a loud voice, and said,
[Yehudit] [9]:[2] “Oh master God of my father Shim’on (Simeon), into whose hand you gave a sword to take vengeance on the strangers who loosened the belt of a virgin to defile her, uncovered her thigh to her shame, and profaned her womb to her reproach; for you said, ‘This mustn’t happen;’ and they did so.
[Yehudit] [9]:[3] Therefore you gave their rulers to be slain, and their bed, which was ashamed for her who was deceived, to be dyed in blood, and struck the servants with their masters, and the masters on their thrones;
[Yehudit] [9]:[4] and gave their wives for a prey, and their daughters to be captives, and all their spoils to be divided among your dear children; which were moved with zeal for you, and abhorred the pollution of their blood, and called on you for aid. Oh God, Oh my god, hear me also who am a widow.
[Yehudit] [9]:[5] Because you did the things that were before those things, and those things, and such as come after; and you planned the things which are now, and the things which are to come. The things which you planned happened.
[Yehudit] [9]:[6] Yes, the things which you determined stood before you, and said, ‘Listen, we’re here; for all your ways are prepared, and your judgement is with foreknowledge.’
[Yehudit] [9]:[7] Because the Assyrians are multiplied in their power. They’re exalted with horse and rider. They were proud of the strength of their footmen. They’ve trusted in shield, spear, bow, and sling. They don’t know that you’re the master who breaks the battles. ‘The master’ is your name.
[Yehudit] [9]:[8] Break their strength in your power, and bring down their force in your anger; for they intend to profane your sanctuary, and to defile the tabernacle where your glorious name rests, and to destroy the horn of your altar with the sword.
[Yehudit] [9]:[9] Look at their pride, and send your anger on their heads. Give into my hand, which am a widow, the might that I’ve conceived.
[Yehudit] [9]:[10] Strike by the deceit of my lips the servant with the prince, and the prince with his servant. Break down their arrogance by a woman’s hand.
[Yehudit] [9]:[11] Because your power stands not in numbers, nor your might in strong men, but you’re a God of the afflicted. You’re a helper of the oppressed, a helper of the weak, a protector of the forsaken, a saviour of those who are without hope.
[Yehudit] [9]:[12] Please, please, God of my father, and God of the inheritance of Yisrael, master of the heavens and of the earth, Creator of the waters, King of all your creation, hear my prayer.
[Yehudit] [9]:[13] Make my speech and deceit to be their wound and bruise, who intend hard things against your covenant, your holy house, the top of Tsiyon (Zion), and the house of the possession of your children.
[Yehudit] [9]:[14] Make every nation and tribe of yours to know that you’re God, the god of all power and might, and that there’s no other who protects the race of Yisrael but you.”
[Yehudit] [10]:[1] When she’d ceased to cry to the god of Yisrael (Israel), and had finished saying all these words,
[Yehudit] [10]:[2] that she rose up where she’d fallen down, called her maid, and went down into the house that she lived on the Sabbath days and on her feast days.
[Yehudit] [10]:[3] She pulled off the sackcloth which she’d put on, took off the clothes of her widowhood, washed her body all over with water, anointed herself with rich ointment, braided the hair of her head, and put a tiara on it. She put on her clothes of gladness, which she used to wear in the days of the life of Menasheh (Manasseh) her husband.
[Yehudit] [10]:[4] She took sandals for her feet, and put on her anklet, bracelets, rings, earrings, and all her jewellery. She made herself very beautiful to deceive the eyes of all men who’d see her.
[Yehudit] [10]:[5] She gave her maid a leather container of wine and a flask of oil, and filled a bag with roasted grain, lumps of figs, and fine bread. She packed all her vessels together, and laid them on her.
[Yehudit] [10]:[6] They went out to the gate of the city of Betulia, and found Ozias and the elders of the city, Chabris and Charmis standing by it.
[Yehudit] [10]:[7] But when they saw her, that her face was altered and her clothing was changed, they were greatly astonished by her beauty and said to her,
[Yehudit] [10]:[8] “May the god of our fathers give you favour, and accomplish your purposes to the glory of the children of Yisrael, and to the exaltation of Yerushalem (Jerusalem).” Then she worshipped God,
[Yehudit] [10]:[9] and said to them, “Command that they open the gate of the city for me, and I’ll go out to accomplish the things you spoke with me about.” And they commanded the young men to open to her, as she’d spoken;
[Yehudit] [10]:[10] and they did so. Then Yehudit (Judith) went out, she, and her handmaid with her. The men of the city watched her until she’d gone down the mountain, until she’d passed the valley, and they could see her no more.
[Yehudit] [10]:[11] They went straight onward in the valley. The watch of the Assyrians met her;
[Yehudit] [10]:[12] and they took her, and asked her, “Of what people are you? Where are you coming from? Where are you going?” She said, “I’m a daughter of the Ivrim (Hebrews). I’m fleeing away from their presence, because they’re about to be given you to be consumed.
[Yehudit] [10]:[13] I’m coming into the presence of Holofernes the chief captain of your army, to declare words of truth. I’ll show him a way that he can go and win all the hill country, and there won’t be lacking of his men one person, nor one life.”
[Yehudit] [10]:[14] Now when the men heard her words, and looked at her face, they were astonished by her beauty. They said to her,
[Yehudit] [10]:[15] “You’ve saved your life, in that you’ve hurried to come down to the presence of our master. Now come to his tent. Some of us will guide you until they deliver you into his hands.
[Yehudit] [10]:[16] But when you stand before him, don’t be afraid in your heart, but declare to him what you just said, and he’ll treat you well.”
[Yehudit] [10]:[17] They chose out of them a hundred men, and appointed them to accompany her and her maid; and they brought them to Holofernes’ tent.
[Yehudit] [10]:[18] And there was great excitement throughout all the camp, for her coming was reported among the tents. They came and surrounded her as she stood outside Holofernes’ tent, until they told him about her.
[Yehudit] [10]:[19] They marvelled at her beauty, and marvelled at the children of Yisrael (Israel) because of her. Each one said to his neighbour, “Who’d despise these people, who have among them such women? Because it isn’t good that one man of them be left, seeing that, if they’re let go, they’ll be able to deceive the whole earth.
[Yehudit] [10]:[20] Then the guards of Holofernes and all his servants came out and brought her into the tent.
[Yehudit] [10]:[21] And Holofernes was resting on his bed under the canopy, which was woven with purple, gold, emeralds, and precious stones.
[Yehudit] [10]:[22] And they told him about her; and he came out into the space before his tent, with silver lamps going before him.
[Yehudit] [10]:[23] But when Yehudit (Judith) had come before him and his servants, they all marvelled at the beauty of her face. She fell down on her face and bowed down to him, but his servants raised her up.
[Yehudit] [11]:[1] Holofernes said to her, “Woman, take courage. Don’t be afraid in your heart; for I never hurt anyone who’s chosen to serve Nevukadnetsar (Nebuchadnezzar), the king of all the earth.
[Yehudit] [11]:[2] And now, if your people who live in the hill country hadn’t slighted me, I wouldn’t have lifted up my spear against them; but they’ve done these things to themselves.
[Yehudit] [11]:[3] And now tell me why you fled from them and came to us; for you’ve come to save yourself. Take courage! You’ll live tonight, and in the future;
[Yehudit] [11]:[4] for there’s no one that’ll wrong you, but all will treat you well, as is done to the servants of King Nevukadnetsar my lord.”
[Yehudit] [11]:[5] And Yehudit said to him, “Receive your servant’s words, and let your handmaid speak in your presence, and I won’t lie to my lord tonight.
[Yehudit] [11]:[6] If you’ll follow the words of your handmaid, God will bring the thing to pass perfectly with you; and my lord won’t fail to accomplish his purposes.
[Yehudit] [11]:[7] As Nevukadnetsar king of all the earth lives, and as his power lives, who’s sent you for the preservation of every living thing, not only do men serve him by you, but also the wild animals in the countryside, the cattle, and the birds of the sky will live through your strength, in the time of Nevukadnetsar and of all his house.
[Yehudit] [11]:[8] Because we’ve heard of your wisdom and the subtle plans of your soul. It’s been reported in all the earth that you only are brave in all the kingdom, mighty in knowledge, and wonderful in feats of war.
[Yehudit] [11]:[9] And now as about the matter which Ahior spoke in your council, we’ve heard his words; for the men of Betulia saved him, and he declared to them all that he’d spoken before you.
[Yehudit] [11]:[10] Therefore, Oh lord and master, don’t neglect his word, but lay it up in your heart, for it’s true; for our race won’t be punished, neither will the sword prevail against them, unless they sin against their god.
[Yehudit] [11]:[11] And now, that my lord may not be defeated and frustrated in his purpose, and that death may fall onto them, their sin has overtaken them, wherewith they’ll provoke their god to anger, whenever they do wickedness.
[Yehudit] [11]:[12] Since their food failed them, and all their water was scant, they took counsel to kill their livestock, and determined to consume all those things which God charged them by his laws that they shouldn’t eat.
[Yehudit] [11]:[13] They’re resolved to spend the first fruits of the grain and the tithes of the wine and the oil, which they’d sanctified and reserved for the priests who stand before our god’s face in Yerushalem (Jerusalem), which it isn’t fitting for any of the people so much as to touch with their hands.
[Yehudit] [11]:[14] They’ve sent some to Yerushalem, because they also that live there have done this thing, to bring them permission from the council of elders.
[Yehudit] [11]:[15] When these instructions come to them and they do it, they’ll be given to you to be destroyed the same day.
[Yehudit] [11]:[16] Therefore I your servant, knowing all this, fled away from their presence. God sent me to work things with you, at which all the earth will be astonished, even as many as hear it.
[Yehudit] [11]:[17] Because your servant is religious, and serves the god of heaven day and night. Now, my lord, I’ll stay with you; and your servant will go out by night into the valley. I’ll pray to God, and he’ll tell me when they’ve committed their sins.
[Yehudit] [11]:[18] Then I’ll come and tell you. Then you can go out with all your army, and there’ll be none of them that’ll resist you.
[Yehudit] [11]:[19] And I’ll lead you through the middle of Yehudah (Judea), until you come to Yerushalem. I’ll set your throne in its centre. You’ll drive them as sheep that have no shepherd, and a dog won’t so much as open his mouth before you; for these things were told me according to my foreknowledge, and were declared to me, and I was sent to tell you.”
[Yehudit] [11]:[20] Her words were pleasing in the sight of Holofernes and of all his servants. They marvelled at her wisdom, and said,
[Yehudit] [11]:[21] “There isn’t such a woman from one end of the earth to the other, for beauty of face and wisdom of words.”
[Yehudit] [11]:[22] Holofernes said to her, “God did well to send you before the people, that might would be in our hands, and destruction among those who slighted my lord.
[Yehudit] [11]:[23] And now you’re beautiful in your face, and wise in your words. If you’ll do as you’ve spoken, your god will be my god, and you’ll live in King Nevukadnetsar’s (Nebuchadnezzar) palace, and will be renowned through the whole earth.”
[Yehudit] [12]:[1] He commanded that she should be brought in where his silver vessels were set, and asked that his servants should prepare some of his own delicacies for her, and that she should drink from his own wine.
[Yehudit] [12]:[2] And Yehudit (Judith) said, “I can’t eat it, because that could cause me to sin. I’ll eat from the supplies I brought with me.”
[Yehudit] [12]:[3] And Holofernes said to her, “But if the things that are with you should run out, from where will we be able to give you more like it? Because there’s none of your race with us.”
[Yehudit] [12]:[4] And Yehudit said to him, “As your soul lives, my lord, your servant won’t use up those things that are with me until the master works by my hand the things that he’s determined.”
[Yehudit] [12]:[5] Then Holofernes’ servants brought her into the tent, and she slept until midnight. Then she rose up towards the morning watch,
[Yehudit] [12]:[6] and sent to Holofernes, saying, “Let my lord now command that they allow your servant to go out to pray.”
[Yehudit] [12]:[7] Holofernes commanded his guards that they shouldn’t stop her. She stayed in the camp three days, and went out every night into the valley of Betulia and washed herself at the fountain of water in the camp.
[Yehudit] [12]:[8] And when she came up, she implored the master God of Yisrael (Israel) to direct her way to the triumph of the children of his people.
[Yehudit] [12]:[9] She came in clean and remained in the tent until she ate her food towards evening.
[Yehudit] [12]:[10] On the fourth day, Holofernes made a feast for his own servants only, and called none of the officers to the banquet.
