[Yehudit] [12]:[11] And he said to Bagoas the eunuch, who had charge over all that he had, “Go now, and persuade this Ivri (Hebrew) woman who’s with you that she come to us, and eat and drink with us.
[Yehudit] [12]:[12] Because listen, it’d be a disgrace if we let such a woman go, not having had her company; for if we don’t draw her to ourselves, she’ll laugh us to scorn.”
[Yehudit] [12]:[13] Bagoas went from the presence of Holofernes, and came in to her, and said, “Let this fair lady not fear to come to my lord, and to be honoured in his presence, and to drink wine and be merry with us, and to be made this day as one of the daughters of the children of Ashur (Assyria) who serve in Nevukadnetsar’s (Nebuchadnezzar) palace.”
[Yehudit] [12]:[14] Yehudit (Judith) said to him, “Who am I, that I should contradict my lord? Because whatever would be pleasing in his eyes, I’ll do speedily, and this will be my joy to the day of my death.”
[Yehudit] [12]:[15] She arose, and decked herself with her clothing and all her woman’s attire; and her servant went and laid fleeces on the ground for her next to Holofernes, which she’d received from Bagoas for her daily use, that she might sit and eat on them.
[Yehudit] [12]:[16] Yehudit came in and sat down, and Holofernes’ heart was ravished with her. His passion was aroused, and he greatly desired her company. He was watching for a time to deceive her from the day that he’d seen her.
[Yehudit] [12]:[17] Holofernes said to her, “Drink now, and be merry with us.”
[Yehudit] [12]:[18] Yehudit said, “I’ll drink now, my lord, because my life is magnified in me this day more than all the days since I was born.”
[Yehudit] [12]:[19] Then she took and ate and drank before him what her servant had prepared.
[Yehudit] [12]:[20] Holofernes took great delight in her, and drank a great deal of wine, more than he’d drunk at any time in one day since he was born.
[Yehudit] [13]:[1] But when the evening had come, his servants hurried to depart. Bagoas shut the tent outside, and dismissed those who waited from the presence of his lord. They went away to their beds; for they were all weary, because the feast had been long.
[Yehudit] [13]:[2] But Yehudit was left alone in the tent, with Holofernes lying along on his bed; for he was drunk with wine.
[Yehudit] [13]:[3] Yehudit had said to her servant that she should stand outside her bedchamber, and wait for her to come out, as she did daily; for she said she’d go out to her prayer. She spoke to Bagoas according to the same words.
[Yehudit] [13]:[4] All went away from her presence, and none was left in the bedchamber, small or great. Yehudit, standing by his bed, said in her heart, Oh master God of all power, look in this hour on the works of my hands for the exaltation of Yerushalem (Jerusalem).
[Yehudit] [13]:[5] Because now is the time to help your inheritance, and to do the thing that I’ve purposed to the destruction of the enemies which have risen up against us.
[Yehudit] [13]:[6] She came to the bedpost which was at Holofernes’ head, and took down his sword from there.
[Yehudit] [13]:[7] She drew near to the bed, took hold of the hair of his head, and said, “Strengthen me, Oh master God of Yisrael, this day.”
[Yehudit] [13]:[8] She struck twice on his neck with all her might and cut off his head,
[Yehudit] [13]:[9] tumbled his body down from the bed, and took down the canopy from the posts. After a little while she went out, and gave Holofernes’ head to her maid;
[Yehudit] [13]:[10] and she put it in her bag of food. They both went out together to prayer, according to their custom. They passed through the camp, circled around that valley, and went up to the mountain of Betulia, and came to its gates.
[Yehudit] [13]:[11] Yehudit said afar off to the watchmen at the gates, “Open, open the gate, now. God is with us, even our god, to show his power yet in Yisrael (Israel), and his might against the enemy, as he’s done even this day.”
[Yehudit] [13]:[12] When the men of her city heard her voice, they hurried to go down to the gate of their city, and they called together the elders of the city.
[Yehudit] [13]:[13] They all ran together, both small and great, for it seemed unbelievable to them that she’d come. They opened the gate and received them, making a fire to give light, and surrounded them.
[Yehudit] [13]:[14] She said to them with a loud voice, “Praise God! Praise him! Praise God, who hasn’t taken away his mercy from the house of Yisrael, but has destroyed our enemies by my hand tonight!”
[Yehudit] [13]:[15] Then she took the head out of the bag and showed it, and said to them, “Listen, the head of Holofernes, the chief captain of Ashur’s (Assyria) army, and the canopy under which he laid in his drunkenness. The master struck him by a woman’s hand.
[Yehudit] [13]:[16] And as the master lives, who preserved me in my way that I went, my face deceived him to his destruction, and he didn’t commit sin with me, to defile and shame me.”
[Yehudit] [13]:[17] All the people were extremely amazed, and bowed themselves, and worshipped God, and said with one accord, “Blessed are you, Oh our god, who have this day humiliated your people’s enemies.”
[Yehudit] [13]:[18] Ozias said to her, “Blessed are you, daughter, in the sight of the Most High God, above all the women on the earth; and blessed is the master God, who created the heavens and the earth, who directed you to cut off the head of the prince of our enemies.
[Yehudit] [13]:[19] Because your hope won’t depart from the hearts of people who remember God’s strength forever.
[Yehudit] [13]:[20] May God turn these things to you for a perpetual praise, to visit you with good things, because you didn’t spare your life because of the affliction of our race, but prevented our ruin, walking a straight way before our god.” And all the people said, “Amen! Amen!”
[Yehudit] [14]:[1] Yehudit (Judith) said to them, “Hear me now, my kindred, and take this head, and hang it on the battlement of your wall.
[Yehudit] [14]:[2] As soon as morning comes and the sun rises over the earth, each of you must pick up your weapons, and every brave man must go out of the city. Put a captain in charge of them, as though you’d go down to the plain towards the watch of the children of Ashur (Assyria); but you men mustn’t go down.
[Yehudit] [14]:[3] These will take up their full armour, and will go into their camp and rouse up the captains of Ashur’s army. They’ll run together to Holofernes’ tent. They won’t find him. Fear will fall onto them, and they’ll flee before your face.
[Yehudit] [14]:[4] You men, and all that inhabit every border of Yisrael (Israel), must pursue them and overthrow them as they go.
[Yehudit] [14]:[5] But before you do these things, summon Ahior the Amoni to me, that he may see and know him that despised the house of Yisrael, and that sent him to us, as it were to death.
[Yehudit] [14]:[6] And they called Ahior out of Ozias’ house; but when he came, and saw Holofernes’ head in a man’s hand in the assembly of the people, he fell onto his face, and his spirit failed.
[Yehudit] [14]:[7] But when they’d recovered him, he fell at Yehudit’s feet, bowed down to her, and said, “Blessed are you in every tent of Yehudah (Judah)! In every nation, those who hear your name will be troubled.
[Yehudit] [14]:[8] Now tell me all the things that you’ve done in these days.” And Yehudit declared to him among the people all the things that she’d done, from the day that she went out until the time that she spoke to them.
[Yehudit] [14]:[9] But when she finished speaking, the people shouted with a loud voice, and made a joyful noise in their city.
[Yehudit] [14]:[10] But when Ahior saw all the things that the god of Yisrael had done, he put deep trust in God, and circumcised the flesh of his foreskin, and was joined to the house of Yisrael, to this day.
[Yehudit] [14]:[11] But as soon as the morning arose, they hanged Holofernes’ head on the wall, and every man took up his weapons, and they went forth by bands to the ascents of the mountain.
[Yehudit] [14]:[12] But when the children of Ashur (Assyria) saw them, they sent word to their leaders, and they went to their captains and tribunes, and to every one of their rulers.
[Yehudit] [14]:[13] They came to Holofernes’ tent, and said to him that was over all that he had, “Wake our lord up, now, for the slaves have been bold to come down against us to battle, that they may be utterly destroyed.”
[Yehudit] [14]:[14] Bagoas went in, and knocked at the outer door of the tent; for he supposed that Holofernes was sleeping with Yehudit.
[Yehudit] [14]:[15] But when no one answered, he opened it, went into the bedchamber, and found him thrown on the threshold dead; and his head had been taken from him.
[Yehudit] [14]:[16] He cried with a loud voice, with weeping, groaning, and shouting, and tore his clothes.
[Yehudit] [14]:[17] He entered into the tent where Yehudit lodged, and he didn’t find her. He leapt out to the people, and cried aloud,
[Yehudit] [14]:[18] “The slaves have dealt treacherously! One woman of the Ivrim (Hebrews) has brought shame on King Nevukadnetsar’s (Nebuchadnezzar) house; for Holofernes lies on the ground, and his head isn’t on him!”
[Yehudit] [14]:[19] But when the rulers of Ashur’s army heard this, they tore their tunics, and they were deeply troubled. There were cries and a very great noise in the camp.
[Yehudit] [15]:[1] When those who were in the tents heard, they were amazed at what happened.
[Yehudit] [15]:[2] Trembling and fear fell onto them, and no man dared stay any more in the sight of his neighbour, but rushing out with one accord, they fled into every way of the plain and of the hill country.
[Yehudit] [15]:[3] Those who’d encamped in the hill country round about Betulia fled away. And then the children of Yisrael, every one who was a warrior among them, rushed out on them.
[Yehudit] [15]:[4] Ozias sent to Betomesthaim, Bevay, Choba, and Chola, and to every border of Yisrael, to tell about the things that’d been accomplished, and that all should rush on their enemies to destroy them.
[Yehudit] [15]:[5] But when the children of Yisrael heard this, they all fell onto them with one accord, and struck them to Choba. Yes, and in the same way also, people from Yerushalem and from all the hill country came (for men had told them about what happened in their enemies’ camp), and those who were in Gilead and in Galil fell onto their flank with a great slaughter, until they were past Damesek (Damascus) and its borders.
[Yehudit] [15]:[6] The rest of the people who lived at Betulia fell onto the camp of Ashur, and plundered them, and were enriched greatly.
[Yehudit] [15]:[7] The children of Yisrael returned from the slaughter, and got possession of that which remained. The villages and the cities that were in the hill country and in the plain country took many spoils; for there was a very great supply.
[Yehudit] [15]:[8] Yehoyakim the high priest, and the elders of the children of Yisrael (Israel) who lived in Yerushalem (Jerusalem), came to see the good things which the master had showed to Yisrael, and to see Yehudit (Judith) and to greet her.
[Yehudit] [15]:[9] When they came to her, they all blessed her with one accord, and said to her, “You’re the exaltation of Yerushalem! You’re the great glory of Yisrael! You’re the great rejoicing of our race!
[Yehudit] [15]:[10] You’ve done all these things by your hand. You’ve done with Yisrael the things that are good, and God is pleased with it. May you be blessed by the Almighty master forever!” And all the people said, “Amen!”
[Yehudit] [15]:[11] And the people plundered the camp for thirty days; and they gave Holofernes’ tent to Yehudit, along with all his silver cups, his beds, his bowls, and all his furniture. She took them, placed them on her mule, prepared her wagons, and piled them on it.
[Yehudit] [15]:[12] And all the women of Yisrael ran together to see her; and they blessed her, and made a dance among them for her. She took branches in her hand, and distributed them to the women who were with her.
[Yehudit] [15]:[13] Then they made themselves garlands of olive, she and those who were with her, and she went before all the people in the dance, leading all the women. All the men of Yisrael followed in their armour with garlands, and with songs in their mouths.
[Yehudit] [16]:[1] And Yehudit began to sing this song of thanksgiving in all Yisrael, and all the people sang with loud voices this song of praise.
[Yehudit] [16]:[2] Yehudit said, “Begin a song to my god with timbrels. Sing to my master with cymbals. Make melody to him with psalm and praise. Exalt him, and call on his name.
[Yehudit] [16]:[3] Because the master is the god that crushes battles. Because in his armies among the people, he delivered me out of the hand of those who persecuted me.
[Yehudit] [16]:[4] Ashur (Assyria) came out of the mountains from the north. He came with ten thousands of his army. Its multitude stopped the torrents. Their horsemen covered the hills.
[Yehudit] [16]:[5] He said that he’d burn up my borders, kill my young men with the sword, throw my nursing children to the ground, give my infants up as prey, and make my virgins a plunder.
[Yehudit] [16]:[6] “The Almighty master brought them to nothing by a woman’s hand.
[Yehudit] [16]:[7] Because their mighty one didn’t fall by young men, neither did sons of the Titans strike him. Tall giants didn’t attack him, but Yehudit (Judith) the daughter of Merari made him weak with the beauty of her face.
[Yehudit] [16]:[8] “Because she put off the clothing of her widowhood for the exaltation of those who were distressed in Yisrael (Israel). She anointed her face with ointment, bound her hair in a tiara, and took a linen garment to deceive him.
[Yehudit] [16]:[9] Her sandal ravished his eye. Her beauty took his soul prisoner. The sword passed through his neck.
[Yehudit] [16]:[10] “The Persians quaked at her daring. The Madim (Medes) were daunted at her boldness.
[Yehudit] [16]:[11] “Then my lowly ones shouted aloud. My oppressed people were terrified and trembled for fear. They lifted up their voices and the enemy fled.
[Yehudit] [16]:[12] The children of slave-girls pierced them through, and wounded them as fugitives’ children. They perished by my master’s army.
[Yehudit] [16]:[13] “I’ll sing to my god a new song: Oh master, you’re great and glorious, marvellous in strength, invincible.
[Yehudit] [16]:[14] Let all your creation serve you; for you spoke, and they were made. You sent out your spirit, and it built them. There’s no one who can resist your voice.
[Yehudit] [16]:[15] Because the mountains will be moved from their foundations with the waters, and the rocks will melt as wax at your presence: But you’re yet merciful to those who fear you.
[Yehudit] [16]:[16] Because all sacrifice is little for a sweet savour, and all the fat is very little for a whole burnt offering to you; but he who fears the master is great continually.
[Yehudit] [16]:[17] “Woe to the nations who rise up against my race! The master Almighty will take vengeance on them in the day of judgement and put fire and worms in their flesh; and they’ll weep and feel their pain forever.”
[Yehudit] [16]:[18] Now when they came to Yerushalem (Jerusalem), they worshipped God. When the people were purified, they offered their whole burnt offerings, their free will offerings, and their gifts.
[Yehudit] [16]:[19] Yehudit dedicated all Holofernes’ stuff, which the people had given her, and gave the canopy, which she’d taken for herself out of his bedchamber, for a gift to the master.
[Yehudit] [16]:[20] And the people continued feasting in Yerushalem before the sanctuary for three months, and Yehudit (Judith) remained with them.
[Yehudit] [16]:[21] After these days, everyone departed to his own inheritance. Yehudit went away to Betulia, and remained in her own possession, and was honourable in her time in all the land.
[Yehudit] [16]:[22] Many desired her, but no man knew her all the days of her life from the day that Menasheh (Manasseh) her husband died and was gathered to his people.
[Yehudit] [16]:[23] She became very highly respected; and she grew old in her husband’s house, to one hundred and five years. She let her maid go free. Then she died in Betulia. They buried her in the cave of her husband Menasheh.
[Yehudit] [16]:[24] The house of Yisrael (Israel) mourned for her seven days. She distributed her goods before she died to all those who were nearest of kin to Menasheh her husband, and to those who were nearest of her own kindred.
[Yehudit] [16]:[25] There was no one who made the children of Yisrael afraid any more in the days of Yehudit, nor for a long time after her death.
[Ester (Greek)] [1]:[1] [In the second year of the reign of Ahashverosh (Ahasuerus) the great king, on the first day of Nisan, Mordekai the son of Yair, the son of Shimei, the son of Kish, of the tribe of Benyamin, a Yehudi (Jew) dwelling in the city Shushan (Susa), a great man, serving in the king’s palace, saw a vision. Now he was one of the captives whom Nevukadnetsar (Nebuchadnezzar) king of Bavel (Babylon) had carried captive from Yerushalem (Jerusalem) with Yekaneyah the king of Yehudah (Judea). This was his dream: Listen, voices and a noise, thunders and earthquake, tumult on the earth. And two great serpents came out, both ready for conflict. A great voice came from them. Every nation was prepared for battle by their voice, even to fight against the nation of the just. Listen, a day of darkness and blackness, suffering and anguish, affection and tumult on the earth. And all the righteous nation was troubled, fearing their own afflictions. They prepared to die, and cried to God. Something like a great river from a little spring with much water, came from their cry. Light and the sun arose, and the lowly were exalted, and devoured the honourable. Mordekai, who’d seen this vision and what God desired to do, having arisen, kept it in his heart, and desired by all means to interpret it, even until night. Mordekai rested quietly in the palace with Gabatha and Teresh the king’s two chamberlains, eunuchs who guarded the palace. He heard their conversation and searched out their plans. He learnt that they were preparing to lay hands on King Ahashverosh; and he informed the king about them. The king examined the two chamberlains. They confessed, and were led away and executed. The king wrote these things for a record. Mordekai also wrote about these matters. The king commanded Mordekai to serve in the palace, and gave gifts for this service. But Haman the son of Hamedata the Bugaean was honoured in the sight of the king, and he endeavoured to harm Mordekai and his people, because of the king’s two chamberlains.] And it happened after these things in the days of Ahashverosh, —(this Ahashverosh ruled over one hundred and twenty-seven provinces from Hodu)—
[Ester (Greek)] [1]:[2] in those days, when King Ahashverosh was on the throne in the city of Shushan,
[Ester (Greek)] [1]:[3] in the third year of his reign, he made a feast for his friends, for people from the rest of the nations, for the nobles of the Persians and Madim (Medes), and for the chief of the local governors.
[Ester (Greek)] [1]:[4] After this—after he’d shown them the wealth of his kingdom and the abundant glory of his wealth during one hundred and eighty days—
[Ester (Greek)] [1]:[5] when the days of the wedding feast were completed, the king made a banquet lasting six days for the people of the nations who were present in the city, in the courtyard of the king’s house,
[Ester (Greek)] [1]:[6] which was adorned with fine linen and flax on cords of fine linen and purple, fastened to golden and silver studs on pillars of white marble and stone. There were golden and silver couches on a pavement of emerald stone, and of mother-of-pearl, and of white marble, with transparent coverings variously flowered, having roses arranged around it.
[Ester (Greek)] [1]:[7] There were gold and silver cups, and a small cup of carbuncle set out, of the value of thirty thousand talents, with abundant and sweet wine, which the king himself drank.
[Ester (Greek)] [1]:[8] This banquet wasn’t according to the appointed law, but as the king desired to have it. He charged the stewards to perform his will and that of the company.
[Ester (Greek)] [1]:[9] Also Vashti the queen made a banquet for the women in the palace where King Ahashverosh lived.
[Ester (Greek)] [1]:[10] Now on the seventh day, the king, being merry, told Haman, Bazan, Teresh, Baraze, Zatholtha, Abataza, and Tharaba, the seven chamberlains, servants of King Ahashverosh,
[Ester (Greek)] [1]:[11] to bring in the queen to him, to enthrone her, and crown her with the diadem, and to show her to the princes, and her beauty to the nations, for she was beautiful.
[Ester (Greek)] [1]:[12] But queen Vashti refused to come with the chamberlains; so the king was grieved and angered.
[Ester (Greek)] [1]:[13] And he said to his friends, “This is what Vashti said. Therefore pronounce your legal judgement on this case.”
[Ester (Greek)] [1]:[14] So Arkesaeus, Sarsathaeus, and Malisear, the princes of the Persians and Madim (Medes), who were near the king, who sat chief in rank by the king, drew near to him,
[Ester (Greek)] [1]:[15] and reported to him according to the laws what it was proper to do to queen Vashti, because she hadn’t done the things commanded by the king through the chamberlains.
[Ester (Greek)] [1]:[16] And Memukan said to the king and to the princes, “Queen Vashti hasn’t wronged the king only, but also all the king’s rulers and princes;
[Ester (Greek)] [1]:[17] for he’s told them the queen’s words, and how she disobeyed the king. As she then refused to obey King Ahashverosh,
[Ester (Greek)] [1]:[18] so this day the other wives of the chiefs of the Persians and Madim, having heard what she said to the king, will dare in the same way to dishonour their husbands.
[Ester (Greek)] [1]:[19] If then it seems good to the king, let him make a royal decree, and let it be written according to the laws of the Madim and Persians, and let him not alter it: ‘Don’t allow the queen to come in to him any more. Let the king give her royalty to a woman better than she.’
[Ester (Greek)] [1]:[20] Let the king’s law which he’ll have made be widely proclaimed in his kingdom. Then all the women will give honour to their husbands, from the poor even to the rich.”
[Ester (Greek)] [1]:[21] This advice pleased the king and the princes; and the king did as Memukan had said,
[Ester (Greek)] [1]:[22] and sent into all his kingdom through the several provinces, according to their language, so that men might be feared in their own houses.
[Ester (Greek)] [2]:[1] After this, the king’s anger was pacified, and he no more mentioned Vashti, bearing in mind what she’d said, and how he’d condemned her.
[Ester (Greek)] [2]:[2] Then the king’s servants said, “Let chaste, beautiful young virgins be sought for the king.
[Ester (Greek)] [2]:[3] Let the king appoint local governors in all the provinces of his kingdom, and let them select beautiful, chaste young ladies and bring them to the city Shushan (Susa), into the women’s apartment. Let them be consigned to the king’s chamberlain, the keeper of the women. Then let things for purification and other needs be given to them.
[Ester (Greek)] [2]:[4] Let the woman who pleases the king be queen instead of Vashti.” This thing pleased the king; and he did so.
[Ester (Greek)] [2]:[5] Now there was a Yehudi (Jew) in the city Shushan, and his name was Mordekai, the son of Yair, the son of Shimei, the son of Kish, of the tribe of Benyamin.
[Ester (Greek)] [2]:[6] He’d been brought as a prisoner from Yerushalem (Jerusalem), whom Nevukadnetsar (Nebuchadnezzar) king of Bavel (Babylon) had carried into captivity.
[Ester (Greek)] [2]:[7] He had a foster child, daughter of Aminadav his father’s brother. Her name was Ester. When her parents died, he brought her up to womanhood as his own. This lady was beautiful.
[Ester (Greek)] [2]:[8] And because the king’s ordinance was published, many ladies were gathered to the city of Shushan under Hegay’s hand; and Ester was brought to Hegay, the keeper of the women.
[Ester (Greek)] [2]:[9] The lady pleased him, and she found favour in his sight. He hurried to give her the things for purification, her portion, and the seven maidens appointed her out of the palace. He treated her and her maidens well in the women’s apartment.
[Ester (Greek)] [2]:[10] But Ester didn’t reveal her family or her kindred, for Mordekai had charged her not to tell.
[Ester (Greek)] [2]:[11] But Mordekai used to walk every day by the women’s courtyard, to see what’d become of Ester.
[Ester (Greek)] [2]:[12] Now this was the time for a virgin to go into the king, when she’d completed twelve months; for so are the days of purification fulfilled, six months while they’re anointing themselves with oil of myrrh, and six months with spices and women’s purifications.
[Ester (Greek)] [2]:[13] And then the lady goes in to the king. The officer that he commands to do so will bring her to come in with him from the women’s apartment to the king’s chamber.
[Ester (Greek)] [2]:[14] She enters in the evening, and in the morning she departs to the second women’s apartment, where Hegay the king’s chamberlain is keeper of the women. She doesn’t go in to the king again, unless she’s called by name.
[Ester (Greek)] [2]:[15] And when the time was fulfilled for Ester the daughter of Aminadav the brother of Mordekai’s father to go in to the king, she neglected nothing which the chamberlain, the women’s keeper, commanded; for Ester found grace in the sight of all who looked at her.
[Ester (Greek)] [2]:[16] So Ester went in to King Ahashverosh (Ahasuerus) in the twelfth month, which is Adar, in the seventh year of his reign.
[Ester (Greek)] [2]:[17] The king loved Ester, and she found favour beyond all the other virgins. He put the queen’s crown on her.
[Ester (Greek)] [2]:[18] The king made a banquet for all his friends and great men for seven days, and he highly celebrated the marriage of Ester; and he granted a remission of taxes to those who were under his dominion.
[Ester (Greek)] [2]:[19] Meanwhile, Mordekai served in the courtyard.
[Ester (Greek)] [2]:[20] Now Ester hadn’t revealed her country, for so Mordekai commanded her, to fear God, and perform his commandments, as when she was with him. Ester didn’t change her manner of life.
[Ester (Greek)] [2]:[21] Two chamberlains of the king, the chiefs of the body-guard, were grieved, because Mordekai was promoted; and they sought to kill King Ahashverosh.
[Ester (Greek)] [2]:[22] And the matter was discovered by Mordekai, and he made it known to Ester, and she declared to the king the matter of the conspiracy.
[Ester (Greek)] [2]:[23] And the king examined the two chamberlains and hanged them. Then the king gave orders to make a note for a memorial in the royal library of the goodwill shown by Mordekai, as a commendation.
[Ester (Greek)] [3]:[1] After this, King Ahashverosh highly honoured Haman the son of Hamedata, the Bugaean. He exalted him and set his seat above all his friends.
[Ester (Greek)] [3]:[2] All in the palace bowed down to him, for so the king had given orders to do; but Mordekai didn’t bow down to him.
[Ester (Greek)] [3]:[3] And they in the king’s palace said to Mordekai, “Mordekai, why do you transgress the king’s commands?”
[Ester (Greek)] [3]:[4] They questioned him daily, but he didn’t listen to them; so they reported to Haman that Mordekai resisted the king’s commands; and Mordekai had shown to them that he was a Yehudi (Jew).
[Ester (Greek)] [3]:[5] When Haman understood that Mordekai didn’t bow down to him, he was greatly enraged,
[Ester (Greek)] [3]:[6] and plotted to utterly destroy all the Yehudim (Jews) who were under the rule of Ahashverosh.
[Ester (Greek)] [3]:[7] In the twelfth year of Ahashverosh’s reign, Haman made a decision by casting lots by day and month, to kill the race of Mordekai in one day. The lot fell on the fourteenth day of the month of Adar.
[Ester (Greek)] [3]:[8] So he spoke to King Ahashverosh, saying, “There’s a nation scattered among the nations in all your kingdom, and their laws differ from all the other nations. They disobey the king’s laws. It isn’t expedient for the king to tolerate them.
[Ester (Greek)] [3]:[9] If it seem good to the king, let him make a decree to destroy them, and I’ll remit into the king’s treasury ten thousand talents of silver.”
[Ester (Greek)] [3]:[10] So the king took off his ring, and gave it into Haman’s hands to seal the decrees against the Yehudim.
[Ester (Greek)] [3]:[11] The king said to Haman, “Keep the silver, and treat the nation as you will.”
[Ester (Greek)] [3]:[12] So the king’s recorders were called in the first month, on the thirteenth day, and they wrote as Haman commanded to the captains and governors in every province, from Hodu even to Kush (Ethiopia), to one hundred and twenty-seven provinces; and to the rulers of the nations according to their languages, in King Ahashverosh’s name.
[Ester (Greek)] [3]:[13] The message was sent by couriers throughout Ahashverosh’s kingdom, to utterly destroy the race of the Yehudim on the first day of the twelfth month, which is Adar, and to plunder their goods. [The following is the copy of the letter. “From the great King Ahashverosh to the rulers and the governors under them of one hundred and twenty-seven provinces, from Hodu even to Kush, who hold authority under him: “Ruling over many nations and having obtained dominion over the whole world, I was determined (not elated by the confidence of power, but ever conducting myself with great moderation and gentleness) to make the lives of my subjects continually tranquil, desiring both to maintain the kingdom quiet and orderly to its utmost limits, and to restore the peace desired by all men. When I’d asked my counsellors how this should be brought to pass, Haman, who excels in soundness of judgement among us, and has been manifestly well inclined without wavering and with unshaken fidelity, and had obtained the second post in the kingdom, informed us that a certain ill-disposed people is scattered among all the tribes throughout the world, opposed in their law to every other nation, and continually neglecting the king’s commands, so that the united government blamelessly administered by us isn’t quietly established. Having then conceived that this nation is continually set in opposition to every man, introducing as a change a foreign code of laws, and injuriously plotting to accomplish the worst of evils against our interests, and against the happy establishment of the monarchy, we instruct you in the letter written by Haman, who’s set over the public affairs and is our second governor, to destroy them all utterly with their wives and children by the swords of the enemies, without pitying or sparing any, on the fourteenth day of the twelfth month Adar, of the present year; that the people formerly and now ill-disposed to us having been violently consigned to death in one day, may in the future secure to us continually a well constituted and quiet state of affairs.”]
[Ester (Greek)] [3]:[14] Copies of the letters were published in every province; and an order was given to all the nations to be ready for that day.
[Ester (Greek)] [3]:[15] This business was hastened also in Shushan (Susa). The king and Haman began to drink, but the city was confused.
[Ester (Greek)] [4]:[1] But Mordekai, having perceived what was done, tore his clothes, put on sackcloth, and sprinkled dust on himself. Having rushed forth through the open street of the city, he cried with a loud voice, “A nation that’s done no wrong is going to be destroyed!”
[Ester (Greek)] [4]:[2] He came to the king’s gate, and stood; for it wasn’t lawful for him to enter into the palace wearing sackcloth and ashes.
[Ester (Greek)] [4]:[3] And in every province where the letters were published, there was crying, lamentation, and great mourning on the part of the Yehudim. They wore sackcloth and ashes.
[Ester (Greek)] [4]:[4] The queen’s maids and chamberlains went in and told her; and when she’d heard what was done, she was deeply troubled. She sent clothes to Mordekai to replace his sackcloth, but he refused.
[Ester (Greek)] [4]:[5] So Ester called for her chamberlain Hatak, who waited on her; and she sent to learn the truth from Mordekai.
[Ester (Greek)] [4]:[7] Mordekai showed him what was done, and the promise which Haman had made the king of ten thousand talents to be paid into the treasury, that he might destroy the Yehudim.
[Ester (Greek)] [4]:[8] And he gave him the copy of what was published in Shushan about their destruction to show to Ester; and told him to charge her to go in and entreat the king, and to beg him for the people. “Remember, he said, the days of your humble condition, how you were nursed by my hand; because Haman, who holds the next place to the king, has spoken against us to cause our death. Call on the master, and speak to the king about us, to deliver us from death.”
[Ester (Greek)] [4]:[9] So Hatak went in and told her all these words.
[Ester (Greek)] [4]:[10] Ester said to Hatak, “Go to Mordekai, and say,
[Ester (Greek)] [4]:[11] ‘All the nations of the empire know that any man or woman who goes in to the king into the inner courtyard without being called, that person must die, unless the king stretches out his golden sceptre; then he’ll live. I haven’t been called to go into the king for thirty days.’ ”
[Ester (Greek)] [4]:[12] So Hatak reported to Mordekai all Ester’s words.
[Ester (Greek)] [4]:[13] Then Mordekai said to Hatak, “Go, and say to her, ‘Ester, don’t say to yourself that you alone will escape in the kingdom, more than all the other Yehudim.
[Ester (Greek)] [4]:[14] Because if you keep quiet on this occasion, help and protection will come to the Yehudim from another place; but you and your father’s house will perish. Who knows if you’ve been made queen for this occasion?’ ”
[Ester (Greek)] [4]:[15] And Ester sent the messenger who came to her to Mordekai, saying,
[Ester (Greek)] [4]:[16] “Go and assemble the Yehudim that are in Shushan (Susa), and all of you fast for me. Don’t eat or drink for three days, night and day. My maidens and I’ll also fast. Then I’ll go in to the king contrary to the law, even if I must die.”
[Ester (Greek)] [4]:[17] So Mordekai went and did all that Ester commanded him.
[Ester (Greek)] [4]:[18] [He prayed to the master, making mention of all the master’s works.
[Ester (Greek)] [4]:[19] He said, “master God, you’re king ruling over all, for all things are in your power, and there’s no one who can oppose you in your purpose to save Yisrael (Israel);
[Ester (Greek)] [4]:[20] for you’ve made the heaven and the earth and every wonderful thing under heaven.
[Ester (Greek)] [4]:[21] You’re master of all, and there’s no one who can resist you, master.
[Ester (Greek)] [4]:[22] You know all things. You know, master, that it isn’t in insolence, nor arrogance, nor love of glory, that I’ve done this, to refuse to bow down to the arrogant Haman.
[Ester (Greek)] [4]:[23] Because I’d gladly have kissed the soles of his feet for the safety of Yisrael.
[Ester (Greek)] [4]:[24] But I’ve done this that I might not set the glory of man above God’s glory. I won’t worship anyone except you, my master, and I won’t do these things in arrogance.
[Ester (Greek)] [4]:[25] And now, Oh master God, the King, the god of Avraham, spare your people, for our enemies are planning our destruction, and they’ve desired to destroy your ancient inheritance.
[Ester (Greek)] [4]:[26] Don’t overlook your people, whom you’ve redeemed for yourself out of the land of Mitsrayim (Egypt).
[Ester (Greek)] [4]:[27] Listen to my prayer. Have mercy on your inheritance and turn our mourning into gladness, that we may live and sing praise to your name, Oh master. Don’t utterly destroy the mouth of those who praise you, Oh master.”
[Ester (Greek)] [4]:[28] All Yisrael cried with all their might, for death was before their eyes.
[Ester (Greek)] [4]:[29] And queen Ester took refuge in the master, being taken as it were in the agony of death.
[Ester (Greek)] [4]:[30] Having taken off her glorious clothing, she put on clothes of distress and mourning. Instead of grand perfumes she filled her head with ashes and dung. She greatly humbled her body, and she filled every place of her glad adorning with her tangled hair.
[Ester (Greek)] [4]:[31] She implored the master God of Yisrael, and said, “Oh my master, you alone are our king. Help me. I’m destitute, and have no helper but you,
[Ester (Greek)] [4]:[32] for my danger is near at hand.
[Ester (Greek)] [4]:[33] I’ve heard from my birth in the tribe of my kindred that you, master, took Yisrael out of all the nations, and our fathers out of all their kindred for a perpetual inheritance, and have done for them all that you’ve said.
[Ester (Greek)] [4]:[34] And now we’ve sinned before you, and you’ve delivered us into our enemies’ hands,
[Ester (Greek)] [4]:[35] because we honoured their gods. You’re righteous, Oh master.
[Ester (Greek)] [4]:[36] But now they haven’t been content with the bitterness of our slavery, but have laid their hands on the hands of their idols
[Ester (Greek)] [4]:[37] to abolish the decree of your mouth, and utterly to destroy your inheritance, and to stop the mouth of those who praise you, and to extinguish the glory of your house and your altar,
[Ester (Greek)] [4]:[38] and to open the mouth of the Gentiles to speak the praises of vanities, and that a mortal king should be admired forever.
[Ester (Greek)] [4]:[39] Oh master, don’t surrender your sceptre to those who don’t exist, and don’t let them laugh at our fall, but turn their counsel against themselves, and make an example of him who’s begun to injure us.
[Ester (Greek)] [4]:[40] Remember us, Oh master! Manifest yourself in the time of our affliction. Encourage me, Oh King of gods, and ruler of all dominion!
[Ester (Greek)] [4]:[41] Put harmonious speech into my mouth before the lion, and turn his heart to hate him who fights against us, to the utter destruction of those who agree with him.
[Ester (Greek)] [4]:[42] But deliver us by your hand, and help me who am alone and have no one but you, Oh master.
[Ester (Greek)] [4]:[43] You know all things, and know that I hate the glory of transgressors, and that I abhor the bed of the uncircumcised and of every stranger.
[Ester (Greek)] [4]:[44] You know my necessity, for I abhor the symbol of my proud station, which is on my head in the days of my splendour. I abhor it as a menstruous cloth, and I don’t wear it in the days of my tranquillity.
[Ester (Greek)] [4]:[45] Your handmaid hasn’t eaten at Haman’s table, and I haven’t honoured the banquet of the king, neither have I drunk wine of libations.
[Ester (Greek)] [4]:[46] Neither has your handmaid rejoiced since the day of my promotion until now, except in you, Oh master God of Avraham.
[Ester (Greek)] [4]:[47] Oh god, who has power over all, listen to the voice of the desperate, and deliver us from the hand of those who devise mischief. Deliver me from my fear.]
[Ester (Greek)] [5]:[1] On the third day, when she’d finished praying, she took off her servant’s dress and put on her glorious clothing. Being splendidly dressed and having called on God the Overseer and Preserver of all things, she took her two maids, and she leaned on one, as a delicate female, and the other followed bearing her train. She was blooming in the perfection of her beauty. Her face was cheerful and looked lovely, but her heart was filled with fear. Having passed through all the doors, she stood before the king. He was sitting on his royal throne. He’d put on all his glorious clothing, covered all over with gold and precious stones, and was very terrifying. And having raised his face resplendent with glory, he looked with intense anger. The queen fell, and changed her colour as she fainted. She bowed herself on the head of the maid who went before her. But God changed the king’s spirit to gentleness, and in intense feeling, he sprang from off his throne, and took her into his arms, until she recovered. He comforted her with peaceful words, and said to her, “What’s the matter, Ester? I’m your relative. Cheer up! You won’t die, for our command is openly declared to you: ‘Draw near.’ ”
[Ester (Greek)] [5]:[2] And having raised the golden sceptre, he laid it on her neck, and embraced her. He said, “Speak to me.” So she said to him, “I saw you, my lord, as an angel of God, and my heart was troubled for fear of your glory; for you, my lord, are to be wondered at, and your face is full of grace.” While she was speaking, she fainted and fell. Then the king was troubled, and all his servants comforted her.
[Ester (Greek)] [5]:[3] The king said, “What do you desire, Ester? What’s your request? Ask even to the half of my kingdom, and it’ll be yours.”
[Ester (Greek)] [5]:[4] Ester said, “Today is a special day. So if it seems good to the king, let both him and Haman come to the feast which I’ll prepare this day.”
[Ester (Greek)] [5]:[5] The king said, “Hurry and bring Haman here, that we may do as Ester said.” So they both came to the feast about which Ester had spoken.
[Ester (Greek)] [5]:[6] At the banquet, the king said to Ester, “What’s your request, queen Ester? You’ll have all that you require.”
[Ester (Greek)] [5]:[7] She said, “My request and my petition is:
[Ester (Greek)] [5]:[8] if I’ve found favour in the king’s sight, let the king and Haman come again tomorrow to the feast which I’ll prepare for them, and tomorrow I’ll do as I’ve done today.”
[Ester (Greek)] [5]:[9] So Haman went out from the king very glad and merry; but when Haman saw Mordekai the Yehudi (Jew) in the courtyard, he was greatly enraged.
[Ester (Greek)] [5]:[10] Having gone into his own house, he called his friends, and his wife Zeresh.
[Ester (Greek)] [5]:[11] He showed them his wealth and the glory with which the king had invested him, and how he’d promoted him to be chief ruler in the kingdom.
[Ester (Greek)] [5]:[12] Haman said, “The queen has called no one to the feast with the king but me, and I’m invited tomorrow.
[Ester (Greek)] [5]:[13] But these things don’t please me while I see Mordekai the Yehudi in the courtyard.
[Ester (Greek)] [5]:[14] Then Zeresh his wife and his friends said to him, “Let a fifty cubit tall gallows be made for you. In the morning you speak to the king, and let Mordekai be hanged on the gallows; but you go in to the feast with the king, and be merry.” The saying pleased Haman, and the gallows was prepared.
[Ester (Greek)] [6]:[1] The master removed sleep from the king that night; so he told his servant to bring in the books, the registers of daily events, to read to him.
[Ester (Greek)] [6]:[2] And he found the records written about Mordekai, how he’d told the king about the king’s two chamberlains, when they were keeping guard, and sought to lay hands on Ahashverosh (Ahasuerus).
[Ester (Greek)] [6]:[3] The king said, “What honour or favour have we done for Mordekai?” The king’s servants said, “You haven’t done anything for him.”
[Ester (Greek)] [6]:[4] And while the king was enquiring about Mordekai’s kindness, look, Haman was in the courtyard. The king said, “Who’s in the courtyard? Now Haman had come in to speak to the king about hanging Mordekai on the gallows which he’d prepared.
[Ester (Greek)] [6]:[5] The king’s servants said, “Listen, Haman stands in the courtyard.” And the king said, “Call him!”
[Ester (Greek)] [6]:[6] The king said to Haman, “What should I do for the man whom I wish to honour?” Haman said within himself, “Whom would the king honour but myself?”
[Ester (Greek)] [6]:[7] He said to the king, “As for the man whom the king wishes to honour,
[Ester (Greek)] [6]:[8] let the king’s servants bring the robe of fine linen which the king puts on, and the horse on which the king rides,
[Ester (Greek)] [6]:[9] and let him give it to one of the king’s noble friends, and let him dress the man whom the king loves. Let him mount him on the horse, and proclaim through the streets of the city, saying, “This is what’ll be done for every man whom the king honours!”
[Ester (Greek)] [6]:[10] Then the king said to Haman, “You’ve spoken well. Do so for Mordekai the Yehudi (Jew), who waits in the palace, and let not a word of what you’ve spoken be neglected!”
[Ester (Greek)] [6]:[11] So Haman took the robe and the horse, dressed Mordekai, mounted him on the horse, and went through the streets of the city, proclaiming, “This is what’ll be done for every man whom the king wishes to honour.”
[Ester (Greek)] [6]:[12] Then Mordekai returned to the palace; but Haman went home mourning, with his head covered.
[Ester (Greek)] [6]:[13] Haman related the events that’d happened to him to Zeresh his wife and to his friends. His friends and his wife said to him, “If Mordekai is of the race of the Yehudim (Jews), and you’ve begun to be humbled before him, you’ll assuredly fall; and you won’t be able to withstand him, for the living god is with him.”
[Ester (Greek)] [6]:[14] While they were still speaking, the chamberlains arrived to rush Haman to the banquet which Ester had prepared.
[Ester (Greek)] [7]:[1] So the king and Haman went in to drink with the queen.
[Ester (Greek)] [7]:[2] The king said to Ester at the banquet on the second day, “What’s it, queen Ester? What’s your request? What’s your petition? It’ll be done for you, up to half of my kingdom.”
[Ester (Greek)] [7]:[3] She replied, “If I’ve found favour in the sight of the king, let my life be granted as my petition, and my people as my request.
[Ester (Greek)] [7]:[4] Because both I and my people are sold for destruction, pillage, and genocide. If both we and our children were sold for male and female slaves, I wouldn’t have bothered you, for this isn’t worthy of the king’s palace.”
[Ester (Greek)] [7]:[5] The king said, “Who’s dared to do this thing?”
[Ester (Greek)] [7]:[6] Ester said, “The enemy is Haman, this wicked man!” Then Haman was terrified in the presence of the king and the queen.
[Ester (Greek)] [7]:[7] The king rose up from the banquet to go into the garden. Haman began to beg the queen for mercy, for he saw that he was in serious trouble.
[Ester (Greek)] [7]:[8] The king returned from the garden; and Haman had fallen on the couch, begging the queen for mercy. The king said, “Will you even assault my wife in my house?” And when Haman heard it, his expression changed.
[Ester (Greek)] [7]:[9] And Bigtan, one of the chamberlains, said to the king, “Listen, Haman has also prepared a gallows for Mordekai, who spoke about the king, and a fifty cubit high gallows has been set up on Haman’s property.” The king said, “Let him be hanged on it!”
[Ester (Greek)] [7]:[10] So Haman was hanged on the gallows that’d been prepared for Mordekai. Then the king’s anger was abated.
[Ester (Greek)] [8]:[1] On that day, King Ahashverosh (Ahasuerus) gave to Ester all that belonged to Haman the slanderer. The king called Mordekai, for Ester had told that he was related to her.
[Ester (Greek)] [8]:[2] The king took the ring which he’d taken away from Haman and gave it to Mordekai. Ester appointed Mordekai over all that’d been Haman’s.
[Ester (Greek)] [8]:[3] She spoke yet again to the king, and fell at his feet, and implored him to undo Haman’s mischief and all that he’d done against the Yehudim.
[Ester (Greek)] [8]:[4] Then the king extended the golden sceptre to Ester; and Ester arose to stand near the king.
[Ester (Greek)] [8]:[5] Ester said, “If it seems good to you, and I’ve found favour in your sight, let an order be sent that the letters sent by Haman may be reversed—letters that were written for the destruction of the Yehudim who are in your kingdom.
[Ester (Greek)] [8]:[6] Because how could I see the affliction of my people, and how could I survive the destruction of my kindred?”
[Ester (Greek)] [8]:[7] Then the king said to Ester, “If I’ve given and freely granted you all that was Haman’s, and hanged him on a gallows because he laid his hands on the Yehudim (Jews), what more do you seek?
[Ester (Greek)] [8]:[8] Write in my name whatever seems good to you, and seal it with my ring; for whatever is written at the king’s command, and sealed with my ring, can’t be countermanded.
[Ester (Greek)] [8]:[9] So the scribes were called in the first month, which is Nisan, on the twenty-third day of the same year; and orders were written to the Yehudim, whatever the king had commanded to the local governors and chiefs of the local governors, from Hodu even to Kush—one hundred and twenty-seven local governors, according to the several provinces, in their own languages.
[Ester (Greek)] [8]:[10] They were written by order of the king, sealed with his ring, and the letters were sent by the couriers.
[Ester (Greek)] [8]:[11] In them, he charged them to use their own laws in every city, to help each other, and to treat their adversaries and those who attacked them as they pleased,
[Ester (Greek)] [8]:[12] on one day in all Ahashverosh’s kingdom, on the thirteenth day of the twelfth month, which is Adar.
[Ester (Greek)] [8]:[13] Let the copies be posted in conspicuous places throughout the kingdom. Let all the Yehudim be ready against this day, to fight against their enemies. The following is a copy of the letter containing orders: [The great King Ahashverosh (Ahasuerus) sends greetings to the rulers of provinces in one hundred and twenty-seven local governance regions, from Hodu to Kush (Ethiopia), even to those who are faithful to our interests. Many who’ve been frequently honoured by the most abundant kindness of their benefactors have conceived ambitious designs, and not only endeavour to hurt our subjects, but moreover, not being able to bear prosperity, they also endeavour to plot against their own benefactors. They not only would utterly abolish gratitude from among men, but also, elated by the boastings of men who are strangers to all that’s good, they supposed that they’d escape the sin-hating vengeance of the ever-seeing God. And often evil exhortation has made partakers of the guilt of shedding innocent blood, and has involved in irremediable calamities many of those who’d been appointed to offices of authority, who’d been entrusted with the management of their friends’ affairs; while men, by the false sophistry of an evil disposition, have deceived the simple goodwill of the ruling powers. And it’s possible to see this, not so much from more ancient traditional accounts, as it’s immediately in your power to see it by examining what things have been wickedly perpetrated by the baseness of men unworthily holding power. It’s right to take heed with regard to the future, that we may maintain the government in undisturbed peace for all men, adopting needful changes, and ever judging those cases which come under our notice with truly equitable decisions. Because whereas Haman, a person from Makedonia, the son of Hamedata, in reality an alien from the blood of the Persians, and differing widely from our mild course of government, having been hospitably entertained by us, obtained so large a share of our universal kindness as to be called our father, and to continue the person next to the royal throne, reverenced of all; he however, overcome by pride, endeavoured to deprive us of our dominion, and our life; having by various and subtle artifices demanded for destruction both Mordekai our deliverer and perpetual benefactor, and Ester the blameless consort of our kingdom, along with their whole nation. Because by these methods he thought, having surprised us in a defenceless state, to transfer the dominion of the Persians to the people from Makedonia. But we find that the Yehudim, who’ve been consigned to destruction by the most abominable of men, aren’t malefactors, but living according to the most just laws, and being the sons of the living god, the most high and mighty, who maintains the kingdom, to us as well as to our forefathers, in the most excellent order. You’ll therefore do well in refusing to obey the letter sent by Haman the son of Hamedata, because he who’s done these things has been hanged with his whole family at Shushan’s (Susa) gates, Almighty God having swiftly returned to him a worthy punishment. We enjoin you then, having openly published a copy of this letter in every place, to give the Yehudim permission to use their own lawful customs and to strengthen them, that on the thirteenth of the twelfth month Adar, on the self-same day, they may defend themselves against those who attack them in a time of affliction. Because in the place of the destruction of the chosen race, Almighty God has granted them this time of gladness. Therefore you also, among your notable feasts, must keep a distinct day with all festivity, that both now and in the future it may be a day of deliverance to us and who are well disposed towards the Persians, but to those that plotted against us a memorial of destruction. And every city and province collectively, which won’t do accordingly, will be consumed with vengeance by spear and fire. It’ll be made not only inaccessible to men, but most hateful to wild animals and birds forever.] Let the copies be posted in conspicuous places throughout the kingdom and let all the Yehudim be ready against this day, to fight against their enemies.
[Ester (Greek)] [8]:[14] So the horsemen went forth quickly to perform the king’s commands. The ordinance was also published in Shushan.
[Ester (Greek)] [8]:[15] Mordekai went out robed in royal clothing, wearing a golden crown and a diadem of fine purple linen. The people in Shushan saw it and rejoiced.
[Ester (Greek)] [8]:[16] The Yehudim had light and gladness
[Ester (Greek)] [8]:[17] in every city and province where the ordinance was published. Wherever the official announcement took place, the Yehudim had joy and gladness, feasting and mirth. Many of the Gentiles were circumcised and became Yehudim for fear of the Yehudim.
[Ester (Greek)] [9]:[1] Now in the twelfth month, on the thirteenth day of the month, which is Adar, the letters written by the king arrived.
[Ester (Greek)] [9]:[2] In that day, the adversaries of the Yehudim perished; for no one resisted, through fear of them.
[Ester (Greek)] [9]:[3] Because the chiefs of the local governors, and the princes and the royal scribes, honoured the Yehudim; for the fear of Mordekai was on them.
[Ester (Greek)] [9]:[4] Because the order of the king was in force, that he should be celebrated in all the kingdom.
[Ester (Greek)] [9]:[6] In the city Shushan the Yehudim killed five hundred men,
[Ester (Greek)] [9]:[7] including Pharsannes, Delphon, Phasga,
[Ester (Greek)] [9]:[8] Pharadatha, Barea, Sarbaca,
[Ester (Greek)] [9]:[9] Marmasima, Ruphaeus, Arsaeus, and Zabuthaeus,
[Ester (Greek)] [9]:[10] the ten sons of Haman the son of Hamedata the Bugaean, the enemy of the Yehudim; and they plundered their property on the same day.
[Ester (Greek)] [9]:[11] The number of those who perished in Shushan was reported to the king.
[Ester (Greek)] [9]:[12] Then the king said to Ester, “The Yehudim have slain five hundred men in the city Shushan. What do you think they’ve done in the rest of the country? What more do you ask, that it may be done for you?”
[Ester (Greek)] [9]:[13] Ester said to the king, “Let it be granted to the Yehudim to do the same to them tomorrow. Also, hang the bodies of the ten sons of Haman.”
[Ester (Greek)] [9]:[14] He permitted it to be done; and he gave up to the Yehudim of the city the bodies of the sons of Haman to hang.
[Ester (Greek)] [9]:[15] The Yehudim assembled in Shushan on the fourteenth day of Adar and killed three hundred men, but plundered no property.
[Ester (Greek)] [9]:[16] The rest of the Yehudim who were in the kingdom assembled, and helped one another, and obtained rest from their enemies; for they destroyed fifteen thousand of them on the thirteenth day of Adar, but took no spoil.
[Ester (Greek)] [9]:[17] They rested on the fourteenth of the same month, and kept it as a day of rest with joy and gladness.
[Ester (Greek)] [9]:[18] The Yehudim in the city of Shushan assembled also on the fourteenth day and rested; and they also observed the fifteenth with joy and gladness.
[Ester (Greek)] [9]:[19] On this account then, the Yehudim dispersed in every foreign land keep the fourteenth of Adar as a holy day with joy, each sending gifts of food to his neighbour.
[Ester (Greek)] [9]:[20] Mordekai wrote these things in a book and sent them to the Yehudim, as many as were in Ahashverosh’s (Ahasuerus) kingdom, both those who were near and those who were far away,
[Ester (Greek)] [9]:[21] to establish these as joyful days and to keep the fourteenth and fifteenth of Adar;
[Ester (Greek)] [9]:[22] for on these days the Yehudim obtained rest from their enemies; and in that month, which was Adar, in which a change was made for them from mourning to joy, and from sorrow to a holiday, to spend the whole of it in good days of feasting and gladness, sending portions to their friends and to the poor.
[Ester (Greek)] [9]:[23] And the Yehudim consented to this as Mordekai wrote to them,
[Ester (Greek)] [9]:[24] showing how Haman the son of Hamedata the person from Makedonia fought against them, how he made a decree and threw lots to destroy them utterly;
[Ester (Greek)] [9]:[25] also how he went in to the king, telling him to hang Mordekai; but all the calamities he tried to bring on the Yehudim came on himself, and he was hanged, along with his children.
[Ester (Greek)] [9]:[26] Therefore these days were called Purim, because of the lots (for in their language they’re called Purim) because of the words of this letter, and because of all they suffered on this account, and all that happened to them.
[Ester (Greek)] [9]:[27] Mordekai established it, and the Yehudim took on themselves, on their offspring, and on those who were joined to them to observe it, neither would they on any account behave differently; but these days were to be a memorial kept in every generation, city, family, and province.
[Ester (Greek)] [9]:[28] These days of Purim must be kept forever, and their memorial must never be forgotten in any generation.
[Ester (Greek)] [9]:[29] Queen Ester the daughter of Aminadav and Mordekai the Yehudi (Jew) wrote all that they’d done, and gave the confirmation of the letter about Purim.
[Ester (Greek)] [9]:[31] Mordekai and Ester the queen established this decision on their own, pledging their own well-being to their plan.
[Ester (Greek)] [9]:[32] And Ester established it by a command forever, and it was written for a memorial.
[Ester (Greek)] [10]:[1] The king levied a tax on his kingdom both by land and sea.
[Ester (Greek)] [10]:[2] As for his strength and valour, and the wealth and glory of his kingdom, look, they’re written in the book of the Persians and Madim (Medes) for a memorial.
[Ester (Greek)] [10]:[3] Mordekai was viceroy to King Ahashverosh (Ahasuerus), and was a great man in the kingdom, honoured by the Yehudim (Jews), and lived his life loved by all his nation.
[Ester (Greek)] [10]:[4] [Mordekai said, “These things have come from God.
[Ester (Greek)] [10]:[5] Because I remember the dream which I had about these matters; for not one detail of them has failed.
[Ester (Greek)] [10]:[6] There was the little spring which became a river, and there was light, and the sun and much water. The river is Ester, whom the king married and made queen.
[Ester (Greek)] [10]:[7] The two serpents are Haman and me.
[Ester (Greek)] [10]:[8] The nations are those which combined to destroy the name of the Yehudim.
[Ester (Greek)] [10]:[9] But as for my nation, this is Yisrael (Israel), even those who cried to God and were delivered; for the master delivered his people. The master rescued us out of all these calamities; and God worked such signs and great wonders as haven’t been done among the nations.
[Ester (Greek)] [10]:[10] Therefore he ordained two lots. One for God’s people, and one for all the other nations.
[Ester (Greek)] [10]:[11] And these two lots came for an appointed season, and for a day of judgement, before God, and for all the nations.
[Ester (Greek)] [10]:[12] God remembered his people and vindicated his inheritance.
[Ester (Greek)] [10]:[13] They must observe these days in the month Adar, on the fourteenth and on the fifteenth day of the month, with an assembly, joy, and gladness before God, throughout the generations forever among his people Yisrael.
[Ester (Greek)] [10]:[14] In the fourth year of the reign of Ptolemaios (Ptolemy) and Kleopatra (Cleopatra), Dositheos, who said he was a priest and Levite, and Ptolemaios his son brought this letter of Purim, which they said was authentic, and that Lusimakos the son of Ptolemaios, who was in Yerushalem (Jerusalem), had interpreted.]
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [1]:[1] Love righteousness, all you who are judges of the earth. Think of the master with a good mind. Seek him in singleness of heart,
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [1]:[2] because he’s found by those who don’t put him to the test, and is manifested to those who trust him.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [1]:[3] for crooked thoughts separate from God. His Power convicts when it’s tested, and exposes the foolish;
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [1]:[4] because wisdom won’t enter into a soul that devises evil, nor live in a body that’s enslaved by sin.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [1]:[5] Because a holy spirit of discipline will flee deceit, and will depart from thoughts that are without understanding, and will be ashamed when unrighteousness has come in.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [1]:[6] Because wisdom is a spirit who loves man, and she won’t hold a blasphemer guiltless for his lips, because God is witness of his inmost self, and is a true overseer of his heart, and a hearer of his tongue.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [1]:[7] Because the master’s spirit has filled the world, and that which holds all things together knows what’s said.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [1]:[8] Therefore no one who utters unrighteous things will be unseen; neither will Justice, when it convicts, pass him by.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [1]:[9] Because in his counsels the ungodly will be searched out, and the sound of his words will come to the master to bring his lawless activities to conviction;
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [1]:[10] because a jealous ear listens to all things, and the noise of murmurings isn’t hidden.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [1]:[11] Beware then of unprofitable murmuring, and keep your tongue from slander; because no secret utterance will go on its way void, and a lying mouth destroys a soul.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [1]:[12] Don’t court death in the error of your life. Don’t draw destruction on yourselves by the works of your hands;
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [1]:[13] because God didn’t make death, neither does he delight when the living perish.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [1]:[14] Because he created all things that they might have being. The generative powers of the world are wholesome, and there’s no poison of destruction in them, nor has Haidais royal dominion on earth;
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [1]:[15] for righteousness is immortal,
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [1]:[16] but ungodly men by their hands and their words summon death; deeming him a friend they pined away. They made a covenant with him, because they’re worthy to belong with him.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [2]:[1] Because they said within themselves, with unsound reasoning, “Our life is short and sorrowful. There’s no healing when a man comes to his end, and no one was ever known who was released from Haidais.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [2]:[2] Because we were born by mere chance, and in the future we’ll be as though we’d never been, because the breath in our nostrils is smoke, and reason is a spark kindled by the beating of our heart,
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [2]:[3] which being extinguished, the body will be turned into ashes, and the spirit will be dispersed as thin air.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [2]:[4] Our name will be forgotten in time. No one will remember our works. Our life will pass away as the traces of a cloud, and will be scattered as is a mist, when it’s chased by the rays of the sun, and overcome by its heat.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [2]:[5] Because our allotted time is the passing of a shadow, and our end doesn’t retreat, because it’s securely sealed, and no one turns it back.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [2]:[6] “Come therefore and let’s enjoy the good things that exist. Let’s use the creation earnestly as in our youth.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [2]:[7] Let’s fill ourselves with costly wine and perfumes, and let no spring flower pass us by.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [2]:[8] Let’s crown ourselves with rosebuds before they wither.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [2]:[9] Let none of us go without his share in our proud revelry. Let’s leave tokens of mirth everywhere, because this is our portion, and this is our lot.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [2]:[10] Let’s oppress the righteous poor. Let’s not spare the widow, nor regard the grey hair of the old man.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [2]:[11] But let our strength be a law of righteousness; for that which is weak is proven useless.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [2]:[12] But let’s lie in wait for the righteous man, because he annoys us, is contrary to our works, reproaches us with sins against the law, and charges us with sins against our training.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [2]:[13] He professes to have knowledge of God, and calls himself a child of the master.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [2]:[14] He became to us a reproof of our thoughts.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [2]:[15] He’s grievous to us even to look at, because his life is unlike other men’s, and his paths are strange.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [2]:[16] We were regarded by him as something worthless, and he abstains from our ways as from uncleanness. He calls the latter end of the righteous happy. He boasts that God is his father.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [2]:[17] Let’s see if his words are true. Let’s test what’ll happen at the end of his life.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [2]:[18] Because if the righteous man is God’s son, he’ll uphold him, and he’ll deliver him out of the hand of his adversaries.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [2]:[19] Let’s test him with insult and torture, that we may find out how gentle he is, and test his patience.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [2]:[20] Let’s condemn him to a shameful death, for he’ll be protected, according to his words.”
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [2]:[21] Thus they reasoned, and they were led astray; for their wickedness blinded them,
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [2]:[22] and they didn’t know the mysteries of God, neither did they hope for wages of holiness, nor did they discern that there’s a prize for blameless souls.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [2]:[23] Because God created man for incorruption, and made him an image of his own everlastingness;
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [2]:[24] but death entered into the world by the envy of the devil, and those who belong to him experience it.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [3]:[1] But the souls of the righteous are in God’s hand, and no torment will touch them.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [3]:[2] In the eyes of the foolish they seemed to have died. Their departure was considered a disaster,
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [3]:[3] and their travel away from us ruin, but they’re in peace.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [3]:[4] Because even if in the sight of men they’re punished, their hope is full of immortality.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [3]:[5] Having borne a little chastening, they’ll receive great good; because God tested them, and found them worthy of himself.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [3]:[6] He tested them like gold in the furnace, and he accepted them as a whole burnt offering.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [3]:[7] In the time of their visitation they’ll shine. They’ll run back and forth like sparks among stubble.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [3]:[8] They’ll judge nations and have dominion over peoples. The master will reign over them forever.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [3]:[9] Those who trust him will understand truth. The faithful will live with him in love, because grace and mercy are with his chosen ones.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [3]:[10] But the ungodly will be punished even as their reasoning deserves, those who neglected righteousness and revolted from the master;
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [3]:[11] for he who despises wisdom and discipline is miserable. Their hope is void and their toils unprofitable. Their works are useless.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [3]:[12] Their wives are foolish and their children are wicked.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [3]:[13] Their descendants are cursed. Because the barren woman who’s undefiled is happy, she who hasn’t conceived in transgression. She’ll have fruit when God examines souls.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [3]:[14] So is the eunuch which has done no lawless deed with his hands, nor imagined wicked things against the master; for a precious gift will be given to him for his faithfulness, and a delightful inheritance in the master’s sanctuary.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [3]:[15] Because good labours have fruit of great renown. The root of understanding can’t fail.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [3]:[16] But children of adulterers won’t come to maturity. The seed of an unlawful union will vanish away.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [3]:[17] Because if they live long, they won’t be esteemed, and in the end, their old age will be without honour.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [3]:[18] If they die young, they’ll have no hope, nor consolation in the day of judgement.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [3]:[19] Because the end of an unrighteous generation is always grievous.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [4]:[1] It’s better to be childless with virtue, for immortality is in the memory of virtue, because it’s recognised both before God and before men.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [4]:[2] When it’s present, people imitate it. They long after it when it’s departed. Throughout all time it marches, crowned in triumph, victorious in the competition for the prizes that are undefiled.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [4]:[3] But the multiplying brood of the ungodly will be of no profit, and their illegitimate offshoots won’t take deep root, nor will they establish a sure hold.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [4]:[4] Because even if they grow branches and flourish for a season, standing unsure, they’ll be shaken by the wind. They’ll be uprooted by the violence of winds.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [4]:[5] Their branches will be broken off before they come to maturity. Their fruit will be useless, never ripe to eat, and fit for nothing.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [4]:[6] Because unlawfully conceived children are witnesses of wickedness against parents when they’re investigated.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [4]:[7] But a righteous man, even if he dies before his time, will be at rest.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [4]:[8] Because honourable old age isn’t that which stands in length of time, nor is its measure given by number of years,
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [4]:[9] but understanding is grey hair to men, and an unspotted life is ripe old age.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [4]:[10] Being found well-pleasing to God, someone was loved. While living among sinners he was transported.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [4]:[11] He was caught away, so that evil wouldn’t change his understanding, or guile deceive his soul.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [4]:[12] Because the fascination of wickedness obscures the things which are good, and the whirl of desire perverts an innocent mind.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [4]:[13] Being made perfect quickly, he filled a long time;
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [4]:[14] for his soul was pleasing to the master. Therefore he hurried away from wickedness.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [4]:[15] But the peoples saw and didn’t understand, not considering this, that grace and mercy are with his chosen, and that he visits his holy ones;
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [4]:[16] but a righteous man who’s dead will condemn the ungodly who are living, and youth who’s quickly perfected will condemn the many years of an unrighteous man’s old age.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [4]:[17] Because the ungodly will see a wise man’s end, and won’t understand what the master planned for him, and why he safely kept him.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [4]:[18] They’ll see, and they’ll despise; but the master will laugh them to scorn. After this, they’ll become a dishonoured carcass and a reproach among the dead forever;
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [4]:[19] because he’ll dash them speechless to the ground, and will shake them from the foundations. They’ll lie utterly waste. They’ll be in anguish and their memory will perish.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [4]:[20] They’ll come with coward fear when their sins are counted. Their lawless activities will convict them to their face.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [5]:[1] Then the righteous man will stand in great boldness before the face of those who afflicted him, and those who make his labours of no account.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [5]:[2] When they see him, they’ll be troubled with terrible fear, and will be amazed at the marvel of salvation.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [5]:[3] They’ll speak among themselves repenting, and for distress of spirit they’ll groan, “This was he whom we used to hold in derision, as a parable of reproach.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [5]:[4] We fools considered his life madness, and his end without honour.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [5]:[5] How was he counted among sons of God? How is his lot among saints?
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [5]:[6] Truly we went astray from the way of truth. The light of righteousness didn’t shine for us. The sun didn’t rise for us.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [5]:[7] We took our fill of the paths of lawlessness and destruction. We travelled through trackless deserts, but we didn’t know the master’s way.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [5]:[8] What did our arrogance profit us? What good have riches and boasting brought us?
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [5]:[9] Those things all passed away as a shadow, like a rumour that runs by,
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [5]:[10] like a ship passing through the billowy water, which, when it’s gone by, there’s no trace to be found, no pathway of its keel in the waves.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [5]:[11] Or it’s like when a bird flies through the air, no evidence of its passage is found, but the light wind, lashed with the stroke of its pinions, and torn apart with the violent rush of the moving wings, is passed through. Afterwards no sign of its coming remains.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [5]:[12] Or it’s like when an arrow is shot at a mark, the air it divided closes up again immediately, so that men don’t know where it passed through.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [5]:[13] So we also, as soon as we were born, ceased to be; and we had no sign of virtue to show, but we were utterly consumed in our wickedness.”
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [5]:[14] Because the hope of the ungodly man is like chaff carried by the wind, and as foam vanishing before a tempest; and is scattered like smoke by the wind, and passes by as the remembrance of a guest who stays just a day.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [5]:[15] But the righteous live forever. Their reward is in the master, and the care for them with the Most High.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [5]:[16] Therefore they’ll receive the crown of royal dignity and the diadem of beauty from the master’s hand, because he’ll cover them with his right hand, and he’ll shield them with his arm.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [5]:[17] He’ll take his zeal as complete armour, and will make the whole creation his weapons to punish his enemies:
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [5]:[18] He’ll put on righteousness as a breastplate, and will wear impartial judgement as a helmet.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [5]:[19] He’ll take holiness as an invincible shield.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [5]:[20] He’ll sharpen stern anger for a sword. The universe will go with him to fight against his frenzied foes.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [5]:[21] Shafts of lightning will fly with true aim. They’ll leap to the mark from the clouds, as from a well-drawn bow.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [5]:[22] Hailstones full of anger will be hurled as from a catapult. The water of the sea will be angered against them. Rivers will sternly overwhelm them.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [5]:[23] A mighty wind will encounter them. It’ll winnow them away like a tempest. So lawlessness will make all the land desolate. Their evil-doing will overturn the thrones of princes.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [6]:[1] Hear therefore, you kings, and understand. Learn, you judges of the ends of the earth.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [6]:[2] Give ear, you rulers who have dominion over many people, and make your boast in multitudes of nations,
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [6]:[3] because your dominion was given to you from the master, and your sovereignty from the Most High. He’ll search out your works, and will enquire about your plans,
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [6]:[4] because being officers of his kingdom, you didn’t judge rightly, nor did you keep the law, nor did you walk according to God’s counsel.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [6]:[5] He’ll come on you awfully and swiftly, because a stern judgement comes on those who are in high places.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [6]:[6] Because the man of low estate may be pardoned in mercy, but mighty men will be mightily tested.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [6]:[7] Because the Sovereign master of all won’t be impressed with anyone, neither will he show deference to greatness; because it’s he who made both small and great, and cares about them all;
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [6]:[8] but the scrutiny that comes on the powerful is strict.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [6]:[9] Therefore, my words are to you, Oh princes, that you may learn wisdom and not fall away.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [6]:[10] Because those who’ve kept the things that are holy in holiness will be made holy. Those who’ve been taught them will find what to say in defence.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [6]:[11] Therefore set your desire on my words. Long for them, and you princes will be instructed.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [6]:[12] Wisdom is radiant and doesn’t fade away; and is easily seen by those who love her, and found by those who seek her.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [6]:[13] She anticipates those who desire her, making herself known.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [6]:[14] He who rises up early to seek her won’t have difficulty, for he’ll find her sitting at his gates.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [6]:[15] Because to think on her is perfection of understanding, and he who watches for her will quickly be free from care;
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [6]:[16] because she herself goes around, seeking those who are worthy of her, and in their paths she appears to them graciously, and in every purpose she meets them.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [6]:[17] Because her true beginning is desire for instruction; and desire for instruction is love.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [6]:[18] And love is observance of her laws. To give heed to her laws confirms immortality.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [6]:[19] Immortality brings closeness to God.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [6]:[20] So then desire for wisdom promotes to a kingdom.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [6]:[21] If therefore you delight in thrones and sceptres, you princes of peoples, honour wisdom, that you may reign forever.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [6]:[22] But what wisdom is, and how she came into being, I’ll declare. I won’t hide mysteries from you; but I’ll explore from her first beginning, bring the knowledge of her into clear light, and I won’t pass by the truth.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [6]:[23] Indeed, I won’t travel with consuming envy, because envy will have no fellowship with wisdom.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [6]:[24] But a multitude of wise men is salvation to the world, and an understanding king is stability for his people.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [6]:[25] Therefore be instructed by my words, and you’ll profit.
