[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [7]:[1] I myself am also mortal, like everyone else, and am a descendant of one formed first and born of the earth.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [7]:[2] I moulded into flesh in the time of ten months in my mother’s womb, being compacted in blood from the seed of man and pleasure of marriage.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [7]:[3] I also, when I was born, drew in the common air, and fell onto the kindred earth, uttering, like all, for my first voice, the same cry.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [7]:[4] I was nursed with care in swaddling clothes.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [7]:[5] Because no king had a different beginning,
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [7]:[6] but all men have one entrance into life, and a common departure.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [7]:[7] Because this cause I prayed, and understanding was given to me. I asked, and a spirit of wisdom came to me.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [7]:[8] I preferred her before sceptres and thrones. I considered riches nothing in comparison to her.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [7]:[9] Neither did I liken to her any priceless gem, because all gold in her presence is a little sand, and silver will be considered as clay before her.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [7]:[10] I loved her more than health and beauty, and I chose to have her rather than light, because her bright shining is never laid to sleep.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [7]:[11] All good things came to me with her, and innumerable riches are in her hands.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [7]:[12] And I rejoiced over them all because wisdom leads them; although I didn’t know that she was their mother.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [7]:[13] As I learnt without guile, I impart without grudging. I don’t hide her riches.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [7]:[14] Because she’s a treasure for men that doesn’t fail, and those who use it obtain friendship with God, commended by the gifts which they present through discipline.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [7]:[15] But may God grant that I may speak his judgement, and to conceive thoughts worthy of what’s been given me; because he’s one who guides even wisdom and who corrects the wise.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [7]:[16] Because both we and our words are in his hand, with all understanding and skill in various crafts.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [7]:[17] Because he himself gave me an unerring knowledge of the things that are, to know the structure of the universe and the operation of the elements;
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [7]:[18] the beginning, end, and middle of times; the alternations of the solstices and the changes of seasons;
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [7]:[19] the circuits of years and the positions of stars;
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [7]:[20] the natures of living creatures and the raging of wild animals; the violence of winds and the thoughts of men; the diversities of plants and the virtues of roots.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [7]:[21] All things that are either secret or manifest I learnt,
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [7]:[22] for wisdom, that’s the architect of all things, taught me. Because there’s in her a spirit that’s quick to understand, holy, unique, manifold, subtle, freely moving, clear in utterance, unpolluted, distinct, invulnerable, loving what’s good, keen, unhindered,
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [7]:[23] beneficent, loving towards man, steadfast, sure, free from care, all-powerful, all-surveying, and penetrating through all spirits that are quick to understand, pure, most subtle.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [7]:[24] Because wisdom is more mobile than any motion. Yes, she pervades and penetrates all things because of her purity.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [7]:[25] Because she’s a breath of God’s power, and a pure emanation of the Almighty’s glory. Therefore nothing defiled can find entrance into her.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [7]:[26] Because she’s a reflection of eternal light, an unspotted mirror of the working of God, and an image of his goodness.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [7]:[27] Although she’s one, she has power to do all things. Remaining in herself, she renews all things. Throughout the generations passing into holy souls, she makes friends of God and prophets.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [7]:[28] Because God loves nothing as much as one who lives with wisdom.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [7]:[29] Because she’s fairer than the sun, and above all the constellations of the stars. She’s better than light.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [7]:[30] Because daylight yields to night, but evil doesn’t prevail against wisdom.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [8]:[1] But she reaches from one end to the other with full strength, and orders all things well.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [8]:[2] I loved her and sought her from my youth. I sought to take her for my bride. I became enamoured by her beauty.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [8]:[3] She glorifies her noble birth by living with God. The Sovereign master of all loves her.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [8]:[4] Because she’s initiated into the knowledge of God, and she chooses his works.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [8]:[5] But if riches are a desired possession in life, what’s richer than wisdom, which makes all things?
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [8]:[6] And if understanding is effective, who more than wisdom is an architect of the things that exist?
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [8]:[7] If a man loves righteousness, the fruits of wisdom’s labour are virtues, for she teaches soberness, understanding, righteousness, and courage. There’s nothing in life more profitable for people than these.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [8]:[8] And if anyone longs for wide experience, she knows the things of old, and infers the things to come. She understands subtleties of speeches and interpretations of dark sayings. She foresees signs and wonders, and the issues of seasons and times.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [8]:[9] Therefore I determined to take her to live with me, knowing that she’s one who’d give me good counsel, and encourage me in cares and grief.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [8]:[10] Because of her, I’ll have glory among multitudes, and honour in the sight of elders, though I’m young.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [8]:[11] I’ll be found keen when I give judgement. I’ll be admired in the presence of rulers.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [8]:[12] When I’m silent, they’ll wait for me. When I open my lips, they’ll heed what I say. If I continue speaking, they’ll put their hands on their mouths.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [8]:[13] Because of her, I’ll have immortality, and leave behind an eternal memory to those who come after me.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [8]:[14] I’ll govern peoples. Nations will be subjected to me.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [8]:[15] Dreaded monarchs will fear me when they hear of me. Among the people, I’ll show myself to be good, and courageous in war.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [8]:[16] When I come into my house, I’ll find rest with her. Because conversation with her has no bitterness, and living with her has no pain, but gladness and joy.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [8]:[17] When I considered these things in myself, and thought in my heart how immortality is in kinship to wisdom,
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [8]:[18] and in her friendship is good delight, and in the labours of her hands is wealth that doesn’t fail, and understanding is in her companionship, and great renown in having fellowship with her words, I went about seeking how to take her to myself.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [8]:[19] Now I was a clever child, and received a good soul.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [8]:[20] Or rather, being good, I came into an undefiled body.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [8]:[21] But perceiving that I couldn’t otherwise possess wisdom unless God gave her to me— yes, and to know and understand by whom the grace is given— I pleaded with the master and implored him, and with my whole heart I said:
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [9]:[1] “O God of my ancestors and master of mercy, who made all things by your word;
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [9]:[2] and by your wisdom you formed man, that he should have dominion over the creatures that were made by you,
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [9]:[3] and rule the world in holiness and righteousness, and execute judgement in uprightness of soul,
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [9]:[4] give me wisdom, her who sits by you on your thrones. Don’t reject me from among your servants,
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [9]:[5] because I’m your servant and the son of your handmaid, a weak and short-lived man, with little power to understand judgement and laws.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [9]:[6] Because even if a man is perfect among the sons of men, if the wisdom that comes from you isn’t with him, he’ll count for nothing.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [9]:[7] You chose me to be king of your people, and a judge for your sons and daughters.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [9]:[8] You gave a command to build a sanctuary on your holy mountain, and an altar in the city where you live, a copy of the holy tent which you prepared from the beginning.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [9]:[9] Wisdom is with you and knows your works, and was present when you were making the world, and understands what’s pleasing in your eyes, and what’s right according to your commandments.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [9]:[10] Send her from the holy heavens, and ask her to come from the throne of your glory, that being present with me she may work, and I may learn what pleases you well.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [9]:[11] Because she knows all things and understands, and she’ll guide me prudently in my actions. She’ll guard me in her glory.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [9]:[12] So my works will be acceptable. I’ll judge your people righteously, and I’ll be worthy of my father’s throne.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [9]:[13] Because what man will know God’s counsel? Or who’ll conceive what the master wills?
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [9]:[14] Because the thoughts of mortals are unstable, and our plans are prone to fail.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [9]:[15] Because a corruptible body weighs down the soul. The earthy tent burdens a mind that’s full of cares.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [9]:[16] We can hardly guess the things that are on earth, and we find the things that are close at hand with labour; but who’s traced out the things that are in the heavens?
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [9]:[17] Who gained knowledge of your counsel, unless you gave wisdom, and sent your holy spirit from on high?
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [9]:[18] It was thus that the ways of those who are on earth were corrected, and men were taught the things that are pleasing to you. They were saved through wisdom.”
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [10]:[1] Wisdom guarded to the end the first formed father of the world, who was created alone, and delivered him out of his own transgression,
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [10]:[2] and gave him strength to rule over all things.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [10]:[3] But when an unrighteous man fell away from her in his anger, he perished himself in the rage with which he killed his brother.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [10]:[4] When for his cause the earth was drowning with a flood, wisdom again saved it, guiding the righteous man’s course by a paltry piece of wood.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [10]:[5] Moreover, when nations consenting together in wickedness had been confounded, wisdom knew the righteous man, and preserved him blameless to God, and kept him strong when his heart yearned towards his child.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [10]:[6] While the ungodly were perishing, wisdom delivered a righteous man, when he fled from the fire that descended out of heaven on the five cities.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [10]:[7] To whose wickedness a smoking waste still witnesses, and plants bearing fair fruit that doesn’t ripen, a disbelieving soul has a memorial: a standing pillar of salt.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [10]:[8] Because having passed wisdom by, not only were they disabled from recognising the things which are good, but they also left behind them for their life a monument of their folly, to the end that where they stumbled, they might fail even to be unseen;
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [10]:[9] but wisdom delivered those who waited on her out of troubles.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [10]:[10] When a righteous man was a fugitive from a brother’s anger, wisdom guided him in straight paths. She showed him God’s kingdom, and gave him knowledge of holy things. She prospered him in his toils, and multiplied the fruits of his labour.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [10]:[11] When in their covetousness men dealt harshly with him, she stood by him and made him rich.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [10]:[12] She guarded him from enemies, and she kept him safe from those who lay in wait. Over his severe conflict, she watched as judge, that he might know that godliness is more powerful than every one.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [10]:[13] When a righteous man was sold, wisdom didn’t forsake him, but she delivered him from sin. She went down with him into a dungeon,
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [10]:[14] and in bonds she didn’t depart from him, until she brought him the sceptre of a kingdom, and authority over those that dealt like a tyrant with him. She also showed those who’d mockingly accused him to be false, and gave him eternal glory.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [10]:[15] Wisdom delivered a holy people and a blameless seed from a nation of oppressors.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [10]:[16] She entered into the soul of a servant of the master, and withstood terrible kings in wonders and signs.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [10]:[17] She rendered to holy men a reward of their toils. She guided them along a marvellous way, and became to them a covering in the day-time, and a starry flame through the night.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [10]:[18] She brought them over the Red sea, and led them through much water;
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [10]:[19] but she drowned their enemies, and she threw them up from the bottom of the deep.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [10]:[20] Therefore the righteous plundered the ungodly, and they sang praise to your holy name, Oh master, and extolled with one accord your hand that fought for them,
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [10]:[21] because wisdom opened the mouth of the mute, and made the tongues of babes to speak clearly.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [11]:[1] Wisdom prospered their works in the hand of a holy prophet.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [11]:[2] They travelled through a desert without inhabitant, and they pitched their tents in trackless regions.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [11]:[3] They withstood enemies and repelled foes.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [11]:[4] They thirsted, and they called on you, and water was given to them out of the flinty rock, and healing of their thirst out of the hard stone.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [11]:[5] Because by what things their foes were punished, by these they in their need were benefitted.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [11]:[6] When enemies were troubled with clotted blood instead of a river’s ever-flowing fountain,
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [11]:[7] to rebuke the decree for the slaying of babies, you gave them abundant water beyond all hope,
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [11]:[8] having shown by the thirst which they’d suffered how you punished the adversaries.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [11]:[9] Because when they were tried, although chastened in mercy, they learnt how the ungodly were tormented, being judged with anger.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [11]:[10] Because you tested these as a father admonishing them; but you searched out those as a stern king condemning them.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [11]:[11] Yes and whether they were far off or near, they were equally distressed;
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [11]:[12] for a double grief seized them, and a groaning at the memory of things past.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [11]:[13] Because when they heard that through their own punishments the others benefitted, they recognised the master.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [11]:[14] Because him who long before was thrown out and exposed they stopped mocking. In the end of what happened, they marvelled, having thirsted in another manner than the righteous.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [11]:[15] But in return for the senseless imaginings of their unrighteousness, wherein they were led astray to worship irrational reptiles and wretched vermin, you sent on them a multitude of irrational creatures to punish them,
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [11]:[16] that they might learn that by what things a man sins, by these he’s punished.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [11]:[17] Because your all-powerful hand that created the world out of formless matter didn’t lack means to send on them a multitude of bears, fierce lions,
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [11]:[18] or newly-created and unknown wild animals, full of rage, either breathing out a blast of fiery breath, or belching out smoke, or flashing dreadful sparks from their eyes;
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [11]:[19] which had power not only to consume them by their violence, but to destroy them even by the terror of their sight.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [11]:[20] Yes and without these they might have fallen by a single breath, being pursued by Justice, and scattered abroad by the breath of your power; but you arranged all things by measure, number, and weight.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [11]:[21] Because to be greatly strong is yours at all times. Who could withstand the might of your arm?
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [11]:[22] Because the whole world before you is as a grain in a balance, and as a drop of dew that comes down on the earth in the morning.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [11]:[23] But you have mercy on all men, because you have power to do all things, and you overlook the sins of men to the end that they may repent.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [11]:[24] Because you love all things that are, and abhor none of the things which you made; Because you never would have formed anything if you hated it.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [11]:[25] How would anything have endured unless you’d willed it? Or that which wasn’t called by you, how would it have been preserved?
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [11]:[26] But you spare all things, because they’re yours, Oh Sovereign master, you who love the living.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [12]:[1] Because your incorruptible spirit is in all things.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [12]:[2] Therefore you convict little by little those who fall from the right way, and, putting them in remembrance by the things wherein they sin, you admonish them, that escaping from their wickedness they may believe in you, Oh master.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [12]:[3] Because truly the old inhabitants of your holy land,
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [12]:[4] hating them because they practised detestable works of enchantments and unholy rites—
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [12]:[5] merciless slaughters of children and sacrificial banquets of men’s flesh and of blood—
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [12]:[6] allies in an impious fellowship, and murderers of their own helpless babes, it was your counsel to destroy by the hands of our fathers;
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [12]:[7] that the land which in your sight is most precious of all might receive a worthy colony of God’s servants.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [12]:[8] Nevertheless you even spared these as men, and you sent hornets as forerunners of your army, to cause them to perish little by little.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [12]:[9] Not that you were unable to subdue the ungodly under the hand of the righteous in battle, or by terrible wild animals or by a stern word to make away with them at once,
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [12]:[10] but judging them little by little you gave them a chance to repent, not being ignorant that their nature by birth was evil, their wickedness inborn, and that their manner of thought would never be changed.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [12]:[11] Because they were a cursed seed from the beginning. It wasn’t through fear of any that you left them unpunished for their sins.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [12]:[12] Because who’ll say, “What have you done?” Or “Who’ll withstand your judgement?” Who’ll accuse you for the perishing of nations which you caused? Or who’ll come and stand before you as an avenger for unrighteous men?
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [12]:[13] Because there isn’t any God beside you that cares for all, that you might show that you didn’t judge unrighteously.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [12]:[14] No king or prince will be able to confront you about those whom you’ve punished.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [12]:[15] But being righteous, you rule all things righteously, deeming it a thing alien from your power to condemn one who doesn’t deserve to be punished.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [12]:[16] Because your strength is the source of righteousness, and your sovereignty over all makes you to forbear all.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [12]:[17] Because when men don’t believe that you’re perfect in power, you show your strength, and in dealing with those who think this, you confuse their boldness.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [12]:[18] But you, being sovereign in strength, judge in gentleness, and with great forbearance you govern us; for the power is yours whenever you desire it.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [12]:[19] But you taught your people by such works as these, how the righteous must be kind. You made your sons to have good hope, because you give repentance when men have sinned.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [12]:[20] Because if on those who were enemies of your servants and deserving of death, you took vengeance with so great deliberation and indulgence, giving them times and opportunities when they might escape from their wickedness,
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [12]:[21] with how great care you judged your sons, to whose fathers you gave oaths and covenants of good promises!
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [12]:[22] Therefore while you chasten us, you scourge our enemies ten thousand times more, to the intent that we may ponder your goodness when we judge, and when we’re judged may look for mercy.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [12]:[23] Therefore also the unrighteous that lived in a life of folly, you tormented through their own abominations.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [12]:[24] Because truly they went astray very far in the ways of error, Taking as gods those animals which even among their enemies were held in dishonour, deceived like foolish babes.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [12]:[25] Therefore, as to unreasoning children, you sent your judgement to mock them.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [12]:[26] But those who wouldn’t be admonished by mild correction will experience the deserved judgement of God.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [12]:[27] Because through the sufferings they were indignant of, being punished in these creatures which they supposed to be gods, they saw and recognised as the true God him whom they previously refused to know. Therefore also the result of extreme condemnation came on them.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [13]:[1] Because truly all men who had no perception of God were foolish by nature, and didn’t gain power to know him who exists from the good things that are seen. They didn’t recognise the architect from his works.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [13]:[2] But they thought that either fire, or wind, or swift air, or circling stars, or raging water, or luminaries of heaven were gods that rule the world.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [13]:[3] If it was through delight in their beauty that they took them to be gods, let them know how much better their Sovereign master is than these, for the first author of beauty created them.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [13]:[4] But if it was through astonishment at their power and influence, then let them understand from them how much more powerful he who formed them is.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [13]:[5] Because from the greatness of the beauty of created things, mankind forms the corresponding perception of their Maker.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [13]:[6] But yet for these men there’s but small blame, for they too perhaps go astray while they’re seeking God and desiring to find him.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [13]:[7] Because they diligently search while living among his works, and they trust their sight that the things that they look at are beautiful.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [13]:[8] But again even they aren’t to be excused.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [13]:[9] Because if they had power to know so much, that they should be able to explore the world, how is it that they didn’t find the Sovereign master sooner?
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [13]:[10] But they were miserable, and their hopes were in dead things, who called them gods which are works of men’s hands, gold and silver, skilfully made, and likenesses of animals, or a useless stone, the work of an ancient hand.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [13]:[11] Yes and some woodcutter might saw down a tree that’s easily moved, skilfully strip away all its bark, and fashion it in attractive form, make a useful vessel to serve his life’s needs.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [13]:[12] Burning the scraps from his handiwork to cook his food, he eats his fill.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [13]:[13] Taking a discarded scrap which served no purpose, a crooked piece of wood and full of knots, he carves it with the diligence of his idleness, and shapes it by the skill of his idleness. He shapes it in the image of a man,
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [13]:[14] or makes it like some worthless animal, smearing it with something red, painting it red, and smearing over every stain in it.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [13]:[15] Having made a worthy chamber for it, he sets it in a wall, securing it with iron.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [13]:[16] He plans for it that it may not fall down, knowing that it’s unable to help itself (for truly it’s an image, and needs help).
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [13]:[17] When he makes his prayer about goods and his marriage and children, he isn’t ashamed to speak to that which has no life.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [13]:[18] Yes, for health, he calls on that which is weak. Because life, he implores that which is dead. Because aid, he supplicates that which has no experience. Because a good journey, he asks that which can’t so much as move a step.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [13]:[19] And for profit in business and good success of his hands, he asks ability from that which has hands with no ability.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [14]:[1] Again, one preparing to sail, and about to journey over raging waves, calls on a piece of wood more fragile than the vessel that carries him.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [14]:[2] Because the hunger for profit planned it, and wisdom was the craftsman who built it.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [14]:[3] Your providence, Oh Father, guides it along, because even in the sea you gave a way, and in the waves a sure path,
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [14]:[4] showing that you can save out of every danger, that even a man without skill may put to sea.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [14]:[5] It’s your will that the works of your wisdom shouldn’t be ineffective. Therefore men also entrust their lives to a little piece of wood, and passing through the surge on a raft come safely to land.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [14]:[6] Because in the old time also, when proud giants were perishing, the hope of the world, taking refuge on a raft, your hand guided the seed of generations of the race of men.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [14]:[7] Because blessed is wood through which comes righteousness;
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [14]:[8] but the idol made with hands is accursed, itself and he that made it; because his was the working, and the corruptible thing was called a god.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [14]:[9] Because both the ungodly and his ungodliness are alike hateful to God;
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [14]:[10] for truly the deed will be punished together with him who committed it.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [14]:[11] Therefore also there’ll be a visitation among the idols of the nation, because, though formed of things which God created, they were made an abomination, stumbling blocks to men’s souls, and a snare to the feet of the foolish.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [14]:[12] Because the devising of idols was the beginning of fornication, and the invention of them the corruption of life.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [14]:[13] Because they didn’t exist from the beginning, and they won’t exist forever.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [14]:[14] Because by the boastfulness of men they entered into the world, and therefore a speedy end was planned for them.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [14]:[15] Because a father worn with untimely grief, making an image of the child quickly taken away, now honoured him as a god which was then a dead human being, and delivered to those that were under him mysteries and solemn rites.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [14]:[16] Afterward the ungodly custom, in process of time grown strong, was kept as a law, and the engraved images received worship by the commandments of princes.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [14]:[17] And when men couldn’t honour them in presence because they lived far off, imagining the likeness from afar, they made a visible image of the king whom they honoured, that by their zeal they might flatter the absent as if present.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [14]:[18] But worship was raised to a yet higher pitch, even by those who didn’t know him, urged forward by the ambition of the architect;
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [14]:[19] for he, wishing perhaps to please his ruler, used his art to force the likeness towards a greater beauty.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [14]:[20] So the multitude, allured because of the grace of his handiwork, now consider an object of devotion him that a little before was honoured as a man.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [14]:[21] And this became an ambush, because men, in bondage either to calamity or to tyranny, invested stones and stocks with the Name that shouldn’t be shared.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [14]:[22] Afterward it wasn’t enough for them to go astray about the knowledge of God, but also, while they live in a great war of ignorance, they call a multitude of evils peace.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [14]:[23] Because either slaughtering children in solemn rites, or celebrating secret mysteries, or holding frenzied revels of strange customs,
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [14]:[24] no longer do they guard either life or purity of marriage, but one brings on another either death by treachery, or anguish by adultery.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [14]:[25] And all things confusedly are filled with blood and murder, theft and deceit, corruption, faithlessness, tumult, perjury,
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [14]:[26] confusion about what’s good, forgetfulness of favours, ingratitude for benefits, defiling of souls, confusion of sex, disorder in marriage, adultery and wantonness.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [14]:[27] Because the worship of idols that may not be named is a beginning and cause and end of every evil.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [14]:[28] Because their worshippers either make merry to madness, or prophesy lies, or live unrighteously, or lightly commit perjury.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [14]:[29] Because putting their trust in lifeless idols, when they’ve sworn a wicked oath, they expect not to suffer harm.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [14]:[30] But on both counts, the just doom will pursue them, because they had evil thoughts of God by giving heed to idols, and swore unrighteously in deceit through contempt for holiness.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [14]:[31] Because it isn’t the power of things by which men swear, but it’s the just penalty for those who sin that always visits the transgression of the unrighteous.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [15]:[1] But you, our god, are gracious and true, patient, and in mercy ordering all things.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [15]:[2] Because even if we sin, we’re yours, knowing your dominion; but we won’t sin, knowing that we’ve been accounted yours.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [15]:[3] Because to be acquainted with you is perfect righteousness, and to know your dominion is the root of immortality.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [15]:[4] Because we weren’t led astray by any evil plan of men’s, nor yet by painters’ fruitless labour, a form stained with varied colours,
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [15]:[5] the sight of which leads fools into lust. Their desire is for the breathless form of a dead image.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [15]:[6] Lovers of evil things, and worthy of such hopes, are those who make, desire, and worship them.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [15]:[7] Because a potter, kneading soft earth, laboriously moulds each article for our service. He fashions out of the same clay both the vessels that minister to clean uses, and those of a contrary sort, all in the same way. What’ll be the use of each article of either sort, the potter is the judge.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [15]:[8] Also, labouring to an evil end, he moulds a vain god out of the same clay, he who, having but a little before been made of earth, after a short space goes his way to the earth out of which he was taken, when he’s required to render back the soul which was lent him.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [15]:[9] However he has anxious care, not because his powers must fail, nor because his span of life is short; But he compares himself with goldsmiths and silversmiths, and he imitates moulders in brass, and considers it great that he moulds counterfeit gods.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [15]:[10] His heart is ashes. His hope is of less value than earth. His life is of less honour than clay,
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [15]:[11] because he was ignorant of him who moulded him, and of him that inspired into him an active soul, and breathed into him a vital spirit.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [15]:[12] But he accounted our life to be a game, and our lifetime a festival for profit; for, he says, one must get gain however one can, even if it’s by evil.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [15]:[13] Because this man, beyond all others, knows that he sins, out of earthy matter making brittle vessels and engraved images.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [15]:[14] But most foolish and more miserable than a baby, are your people’s enemies, who oppressed them;
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [15]:[15] because they even considered all the idols of the nations to be gods, which have neither the use of eyes for seeing, nor nostrils for drawing breath, nor ears to hear, nor fingers for handling, and their feet are helpless for walking.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [15]:[16] Because a man made them, and one whose own spirit is borrowed moulded them; for no one has power as a man to mould a god like himself.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [15]:[17] But, being mortal, he makes a dead thing by the work of lawless hands; for he’s better than the objects of his worship, since he indeed had life, but they never did.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [15]:[18] Yes, and they worship the creatures that are most hateful, for, being compared as to lack of sense, these are worse than all others;
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [15]:[19] Neither, as seen beside other creatures, are they beautiful, so that one should desire them, but they’ve escaped both the praise of God and his blessing.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [16]:[1] Because this cause, they were deservedly punished through creatures like those which they worship, and tormented through a multitude of vermin.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [16]:[2] Instead of this punishment, you, giving benefits to your people, prepared quails for food, a delicacy to satisfy the desire of their appetite,
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [16]:[3] to the end that your enemies, desiring food, might for the hideousness of the creatures sent among them, loathe even the necessary appetite; but these, your people, having for a short time suffered lack, might even partake of delicacies.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [16]:[4] Because it was necessary that inescapable lack should come on those oppressors, but that to these it should only be showed how their enemies were tormented.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [16]:[5] Because even when terrible raging of wild animals came on your people, and they were perishing by the bites of crooked serpents, your anger didn’t continue to the uttermost;
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [16]:[6] but for admonition were they troubled for a short time, having a token of salvation to put them in remembrance of the commandment of your law;
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [16]:[7] for he who turned towards it wasn’t saved because of that which was seen, but because of you, the Saviour of all.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [16]:[8] Yes, and in this you persuaded our enemies that you’re he who delivers out of every evil.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [16]:[9] Because the bites of locusts and flies truly killed them. No healing for their life was found, because they were worthy to be punished by such things.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [16]:[10] But your children weren’t overcome by the very fangs of venomous dragons, for your mercy passed by where they were and healed them.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [16]:[11] Because they were bitten to put them in remembrance of your oracles, and were quickly saved, so that they wouldn’t fall into deep forgetfulness and become unable to respond to your kindness.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [16]:[12] Because truly it was neither herb nor poultice that cured them, but your word, Oh master, which heals all people.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [16]:[13] Because you have authority over life and death, and you lead down to Haidais’ gates, and lead up again.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [16]:[14] But though a man kills by his wickedness, he can’t retrieve the spirit that’s departed or release the imprisoned soul.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [16]:[15] But it isn’t possible to escape your hand;
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [16]:[16] for ungodly men, refusing to know you, were scourged in the strength of your arm, pursued with strange rains and hails and relentless storms, and utterly consumed with fire.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [16]:[17] Because, what was most marvellous, in the water which quenches all things, the fire burnt hotter; for the world fights for the righteous.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [16]:[18] Because at one time the flame was restrained, that it might not burn up the creatures sent against the ungodly, but that these themselves as they looked might see that they were chased by God’s judgement.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [16]:[19] At another time even surrounded by water it burns more intensely than fire, that it may destroy the produce of an unrighteous land.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [16]:[20] Instead of these things, you gave your people angels’ food to eat, and you provided ready-to-eat bread for them from heaven without toil, having the virtue of every pleasant flavour, and agreeable to every taste.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [16]:[21] Because your nature showed your sweetness towards your children, while that bread, serving the desire of the eater, changed itself according to every man’s choice.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [16]:[22] But snow and ice endured fire, and didn’t melt, that people might know that fire was destroying the fruits of the enemies, burning in the hail and flashing in the rains;
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [16]:[23] and that this fire, again, so that righteous people may be nourished, has even forgotten its own power.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [16]:[24] Because the creation, ministering to you, its maker, strains its force against the unrighteous for punishment and in kindness, slackens it on behalf of those who trust in you.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [16]:[25] Therefore at that time also, converting itself into all forms, it ministered to your all-nourishing bounty, according to the desire of those who had need,
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [16]:[26] that your children, whom you loved, Oh master, might learn that it isn’t the growth of crops that nourishes a man, but that your word preserves those who trust you.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [16]:[27] Because that which wasn’t destroyed by fire, melted away when it was simply warmed by a faint sunbeam,
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [16]:[28] that it might be known that we must rise before the sun to give you thanks, and must pray to you at the dawning of the light;
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [16]:[29] for the hope of the unthankful will melt as the winter’s hoar frost, and will flow away as water that has no use.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [17]:[1] Because your judgements are great, and hard to interpret; therefore undisciplined souls went astray.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [17]:[2] Because when lawless men had supposed that they held a holy nation in their power, they, prisoners of darkness, and bound in the fetters of a long night, kept close beneath their roofs, lay exiled from the eternal providence.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [17]:[3] Because while they thought that they were unseen in their secret sins, they were divided from one another by a dark curtain of forgetfulness, stricken with terrible awe, and very troubled by apparitions.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [17]:[4] Because neither did the dark recesses that held them guard them from fears, but terrifying sounds rang around them, and dismal phantoms appeared with unsmiling faces.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [17]:[5] And no power of fire prevailed to give light, neither were the brightest flames of the stars strong enough to illuminate that gloomy night;
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [17]:[6] but only the glimmering of a self-kindled fire appeared to them, full of fear. In terror, they considered the things which they saw to be worse than that sight, on which they couldn’t gaze.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [17]:[7] The mockeries of their magic arts were powerless, now, and a shameful rebuke of their boasted understanding:
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [17]:[8] Because those who promised to drive away terrors and disorders from a sick soul, these were sick with a ludicrous fearfulness.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [17]:[9] Because even if no troubling thing frighted them, yet, scared with the creeping of vermin and hissing of serpents,
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [17]:[10] they perished trembling in fear, refusing even to look at the air, which couldn’t be escaped on any side.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [17]:[11] Because wickedness, condemned by a witness within, is a coward thing, and, being pressed hard by conscience, always has added forecasts of the worst.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [17]:[12] Because fear is nothing else but a surrender of the help which reason offers;
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [17]:[13] and from within, the expectation of being less prefers ignorance of the cause that brings the torment.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [17]:[14] But they, all through the night which was powerless indeed, and which came on them out of the recesses of powerless Haidais, sleeping the same sleep,
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [17]:[15] now were haunted by monstrous apparitions, and now were paralysed by their soul’s surrendering; for sudden and unexpected fear came on them.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [17]:[16] So then whoever it might be, sinking down in his place, was kept captive, shut up in that prison which wasn’t barred with iron;
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [17]:[17] for whether he was a farmer, or a shepherd, or a labourer whose toils were in the wilderness, he was overtaken, and endured that inescapable sentence; for they were all bound with one chain of darkness.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [17]:[18] Whether there was a whistling wind, or a melodious sound of birds among the spreading branches, or a measured fall of water running violently,
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [17]:[19] or a harsh crashing of rocks hurled down, or the swift course of animals bounding along unseen, or the voice of wild animals harshly roaring, or an echo rebounding from the hollows of the mountains, all these things paralysed them with terror.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [17]:[20] Because the whole world was illuminated with clear light, and was occupied with unhindered works,
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [17]:[21] while over them alone was spread a heavy night, an image of the darkness that should afterward receive them; but to themselves, they were heavier than darkness.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [18]:[1] But for your holy ones there was great light. Their enemies, hearing their voice but not seeing their form, counted it a happy thing that they too had suffered,
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [18]:[2] yet for that they don’t hurt them, though wronged by them before, they’re thankful; and because they’d been at variance with them, they begged for pardon.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [18]:[3] Therefore you provided a burning pillar of fire, to be a guide for your people’s unknown journey, and a harmless sun for their glorious exile.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [18]:[4] Because the Mitsrim (Egyptians) well deserved to be deprived of light and imprisoned by darkness, they who’d imprisoned your children, through whom the incorruptible light of the law was to be given to the race of men.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [18]:[5] After they’d taken counsel to kill the babes of the holy ones, and when a single child had been abandoned and saved to convict them of their sin, you took away from them their multitude of children, and destroyed all their army together in a mighty flood.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [18]:[6] Our fathers were made aware of that night beforehand, that, having sure knowledge, they might be cheered by the oaths which they’d trusted.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [18]:[7] Salvation of the righteous and destruction of the enemies was expected by your people.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [18]:[8] Because as you took vengeance on the adversaries, by the same means, calling us to yourself, you glorified us.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [18]:[9] Because holy children of good men offered sacrifice in secret, and with one consent they agreed to the covenant of the divine law, that they’d partake alike in the same good things and the same perils, the fathers already leading the sacred songs of praise.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [18]:[10] But the discordant cry of the enemies echoed back, and a pitiful voice of lamentation for children was spread abroad.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [18]:[11] Both servant and master were punished with the same just doom, and the commoner suffering the same as king;
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [18]:[12] Yes, they all together, under one form of death, had corpses without number. Because the living weren’t sufficient even to bury them, Since at a single stroke, their most cherished offspring was consumed.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [18]:[13] Because while they were disbelieving all things because of the enchantments, on the destruction of the firstborn they confessed the people to be God’s children.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [18]:[14] Because while peaceful silence wrapped all things, and night in her own swiftness was half spent,
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [18]:[15] your all-powerful word leapt from heaven, from the royal throne, a stern warrior, into the middle of the doomed land,
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [18]:[16] bearing as a sharp sword your authentic commandment, and standing, it filled all things with death, and while it touched the heaven it stood on the earth.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [18]:[17] Then immediately apparitions in dreams terribly troubled them, and unexpected fears came on them.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [18]:[18] And each, one thrown here half dead, another there, made known why he was dying;
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [18]:[19] for the dreams, disturbing them, forewarned them of this, that they might not perish without knowing why they were afflicted.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [18]:[20] The experience of death also touched the righteous, and a multitude were destroyed in the wilderness, but the anger didn’t last long.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [18]:[21] Because a blameless man hurried to be their champion, bringing the weapon of his own ministry, prayer, and the atoning sacrifice of incense. He withstood the indignation and set an end to the calamity, showing that he was your servant.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [18]:[22] And he overcame the anger, not by strength of body, not by force of weapons, but by his word, he subdued the avenger by bringing to remembrance oaths and covenants made with the fathers.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [18]:[23] Because when the dead had already fallen in heaps one on another, he intervened and stopped the anger, and cut off its way to the living.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [18]:[24] Because the whole world was pictured on his long robe, and the glories of the fathers were on the engraving of the four rows of precious stones, and your majesty was on the diadem on his head.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [18]:[25] The destroyer yielded to these, and they feared; for it was enough only to test the anger.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [19]:[1] But indignation without mercy came on the ungodly to the end; for God also foreknew their future,
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [19]:[2] how, having changed their minds to let your people go, and having sped them eagerly on their way, they’d change their minds and pursue them.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [19]:[3] Because while they were still mourning, and lamenting at the graves of the dead, they made another foolish decision, and pursued as fugitives those whom they’d begged to leave and driven out.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [19]:[4] Because the doom which they deserved was drawing them to this end, and it made them forget the things that’d happened to them, that they might fill up the punishment which was yet lacking from their torments,
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [19]:[5] and that your people might journey on by a marvellous road, but they themselves might find a strange death.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [19]:[6] Because the whole creation, each part in its diverse kind, was made new again, complying with your commandments, that your servants might be kept unharmed.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [19]:[7] Then the cloud that overshadowed the camp was seen, and dry land rising up out of what had been water, out of the Red sea an unhindered highway, and a grassy plain out of the violent surge,
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [19]:[8] by which they passed over with all their army, these who were covered with your hand, having seen strange marvels.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [19]:[9] Because like horses they roamed at large, and they skipped about like lambs, praising you, Oh master, who was their deliverer.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [19]:[10] Because they still remembered the things that happened in the time of their sojourning, how instead of bearing cattle, the land brought forth lice, and instead of fish, the river spewed out a multitude of frogs.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [19]:[11] But afterwards, they also saw a new kind of birds, when, led on by desire, they asked for luxurious dainties;
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [19]:[12] for, to comfort them, quails came up for them from the sea.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [19]:[13] Punishments came on the sinners, not without the signs that were given beforehand by the violence of the thunder, for they justly suffered through their own wickednesses, for the hatred which they practised towards guests was grievous indeed.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [19]:[14] Because while the others didn’t receive the strangers when they came to them, the Mitsrim (Egyptians) made slaves of guests who were their benefactors.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [19]:[15] And not only so, but while punishment of some sort will come on the former, since they received as enemies those who were aliens;
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [19]:[16] because these first welcomed with feastings, and then afflicted with dreadful toils, those who’d already shared with them in the same rights.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [19]:[17] And moreover they were stricken with loss of sight (even as were those others at the righteous man’s doors), when, being surrounded with yawning darkness, they each looked for the passage through his own door.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [19]:[18] Because as the notes of a lute vary the character of the rhythm, even so the elements, changing their order one with another, continuing always in its sound, as may clearly be conjectured from the sight of the things that have happened.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [19]:[19] Because creatures of the dry land were turned into creatures of the waters, and creatures that swim moved on the land.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [19]:[20] Fire kept the mastery of its own power in water, and water forgot its quenching nature.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [19]:[21] On the contrary, flames didn’t consume flesh of perishable creatures that walked among them, neither did they melt the crystalline grains of ambrosial food that were melted easily.
[Wisdom of Shelomoh] [19]:[22] Because in all things, Oh master, you magnified your people, and you glorified them and didn’t lightly regard them, standing by their side in every time and place.
[Sira] [1]:[1] All wisdom comes from the master, and is with him forever.
[Sira] [1]:[2] Who can count the sand of the seas, the drops of rain, and the days of eternity?
[Sira] [1]:[3] Who’ll search out the height of the sky, the breadth of the earth, the deep, and wisdom?
[Sira] [1]:[4] Wisdom has been created before all things, and the understanding of prudence from eternal.
[Sira] [1]:[6] To whom has the root of wisdom been revealed? Who’s known her shrewd counsels?
[Sira] [1]:[8] There’s one wise, greatly to be feared, sitting on his throne: the master.
[Sira] [1]:[9] He created her. He saw and measured her. He poured her out on all his works.
[Sira] [1]:[10] She’s with all flesh according to his gift. He gave her freely to those who love him.
[Sira] [1]:[11] The fear of the master is glory, exultation, gladness, and a crown of rejoicing.
[Sira] [1]:[12] The fear of the master will delight the heart, and will give gladness, joy, and length of days.
[Sira] [1]:[13] All those who fear the master, it’ll go well with him at the last. He’ll be blessed in the day of his death.
[Sira] [1]:[14] To fear the master is the beginning of wisdom. It was created together with the faithful in the womb.
[Sira] [1]:[15] She laid an eternal foundation with men. She’ll be trusted among their offspring.
[Sira] [1]:[16] To fear the master is the fullness of wisdom. She inebriates men with her fruits.
[Sira] [1]:[17] She’ll fill all her house with desirable things, and her storehouses with her produce.
[Sira] [1]:[18] The fear of the master is the crown of wisdom, making peace and perfect health to flourish.
[Sira] [1]:[19] He both saw and measured her. He rained down skill and knowledge of understanding, and exalted the honour of those who hold her fast.
[Sira] [1]:[20] To fear the master is the root of wisdom. Her branches are length of days.
[Sira] [1]:[22] Unjust anger can never be justified, for his anger tips the scale to his downfall.
[Sira] [1]:[23] A man that’s patient will resist for a season, and afterward gladness will spring up to him.
[Sira] [1]:[24] He’ll hide his words until the right moment, and the lips of many will tell of his understanding.
[Sira] [1]:[25] A wise saying is in the treasures of wisdom; but godliness is an abomination to a sinner.
[Sira] [1]:[26] If you desire wisdom, keep the commandments and the master will give her to you freely;
[Sira] [1]:[27] for the fear of the master is wisdom and instruction. Faith and humility are his good pleasure.
[Sira] [1]:[28] Don’t disobey the fear of the master. Don’t come to him with a double heart.
[Sira] [1]:[29] Don’t be a hypocrite in men’s sight. Keep watch over your lips.
[Sira] [1]:[30] Don’t exalt yourself, or you might fall and bring dishonour on your soul. The master will reveal your secrets and will throw you down among the congregation, because you didn’t come to the fear of the master and your heart was full of deceit.
[Sira] [2]:[1] My son, if you come to serve the master, prepare your soul for temptation.
[Sira] [2]:[2] Set your heart aright, constantly endure, and don’t hurry in time of calamity.
[Sira] [2]:[3] Cling to him, and don’t depart, that you may be increased at your latter end.
[Sira] [2]:[4] Accept whatever is brought on you, and be patient when you suffer humiliation.
[Sira] [2]:[5] Because gold is tried in the fire, and acceptable men in the furnace of humiliation.
[Sira] [2]:[6] Put your trust in him, and he’ll help you. Make your ways straight, and set your hope on him.
[Sira] [2]:[7] All you who fear the master, wait for his mercy. Don’t turn aside, or you might fall.
[Sira] [2]:[8] All you who fear the master, put your trust in him, and your reward won’t fail.
[Sira] [2]:[9] All you who fear the master, hope for good things, and for eternal gladness and mercy.
[Sira] [2]:[10] Look at the generations of old, and see: Who ever put his trust in the master, and was ashamed? Or who remained in his fear, and was forsaken? Or who called on him, and he neglected him?
[Sira] [2]:[11] Because the master is full of compassion and mercy. He forgives sins and saves in time of affliction.
[Sira] [2]:[12] Woe to fearful hearts, to faint hands, and to the sinner who goes two ways!
[Sira] [2]:[13] Woe to the faint heart! Because it doesn’t believe. Therefore it won’t be defended.
[Sira] [2]:[14] Woe to you who’ve lost your patience! And what’ll you all do when the master visits you?
[Sira] [2]:[15] Those who fear the master won’t disobey his words. Those who love him will keep his ways.
[Sira] [2]:[16] Those who fear the master will seek his good pleasure. Those who love him will be filled with the law.
[Sira] [2]:[17] Those who fear the master will prepare their hearts, and will humble their souls in his sight.
[Sira] [2]:[18] We’ll fall into the master’s hands, and not into men’s hands; for as his majesty is, so also is his mercy.
[Sira] [3]:[1] Hear me, your father, Oh my children, and do what you hear, that you all may be safe.
[Sira] [3]:[2] Because the master honours the father over the children, and has confirmed the mother’s judgement over her sons.
[Sira] [3]:[3] He who honours his father will make atonement for sins.
[Sira] [3]:[4] He who gives glory to his mother is as one who lays up treasure.
[Sira] [3]:[5] Anyone who honours his father will have joy in his own children. He’ll be heard in the day of his prayer.
[Sira] [3]:[6] He who gives glory to his father will have length of days. He who listens to the master will bring rest to his mother,
[Sira] [3]:[7] and will serve under his parents, as to masters.
[Sira] [3]:[8] Honour your father in deed and word, that a blessing may come on you from him.
[Sira] [3]:[9] Because the blessing of the father establishes children’s houses, but the curse of the mother roots out the foundations.
[Sira] [3]:[10] Don’t glorify yourself in the dishonour of your father, for your father’s dishonour is no glory to you.
[Sira] [3]:[11] Because a man’s glory is from the honour of his father, and a mother in dishonour is a reproach to her children.
[Sira] [3]:[12] My son, help your father in his old age, and don’t grieve him as long as he lives.
[Sira] [3]:[13] If he fails in understanding, have patience with him. Don’t dishonour him in your full strength.
[Sira] [3]:[14] Because the kindness to your father won’t be forgotten. Instead of sins it’ll be added to build you up.
[Sira] [3]:[15] In the day of your affliction it’ll be remembered for you, as fair weather on ice, so your sins will also melt away.
[Sira] [3]:[16] He who forsakes his father is as a blasphemer. He who provokes his mother is cursed by the master.
[Sira] [3]:[17] My son, go on with your business in humility; so you’ll be loved by an acceptable man.
[Sira] [3]:[18] The greater you are, humble yourself the more, and you’ll find favour before the master.
[Sira] [3]:[20] Because the master’s power is great, and he’s glorified by those who are lowly.
[Sira] [3]:[21] Don’t seek things that are too hard for you, and don’t search out things that are above your strength.
[Sira] [3]:[22] Think about the things that have been commanded you, for you have no need of the things that are secret.
[Sira] [3]:[23] Don’t be overly busy in tasks that are beyond you, for more things are shown to you than men can understand.
[Sira] [3]:[24] Because the conceit of many has led them astray. Evil opinion has caused their judgement to slip.
[Sira] [3]:[25] There is no light without eyes. There’s no wisdom without knowledge.
[Sira] [3]:[26] A stubborn heart will do badly at the end. He who loves danger will perish in it.
[Sira] [3]:[27] A stubborn heart will be burdened with troubles. The sinner will heap sin on sins.
[Sira] [3]:[28] The calamity of the proud has no healing, for a weed of wickedness has taken root in him.
[Sira] [3]:[29] The heart of the prudent will understand a proverb. A wise man desires the ear of a listener.
[Sira] [3]:[30] Water will quench a flaming fire; almsgiving will make atonement for sins.
[Sira] [3]:[31] He who repays good turns is mindful of that which comes afterward. In the time of his falling he’ll find a support.
[Sira] [4]:[1] My son, don’t deprive the poor of his living. Don’t make the needy eyes wait long.
[Sira] [4]:[2] Don’t make a hungry soul sorrowful, or provoke a man in his distress.
[Sira] [4]:[3] Don’t add more trouble to a heart that’s provoked. Don’t put off giving to him who’s in need.
[Sira] [4]:[4] Don’t reject a suppliant in his affliction. Don’t turn your face away from a poor man.
[Sira] [4]:[5] Don’t turn your eye away from one who asks. Give no occasion to a man to curse you.
[Sira] [4]:[6] Because if he curses you in the bitterness of his soul, he who made him will hear his supplication.
[Sira] [4]:[7] Endear yourself to the assembly. Bow your head to a great man.
[Sira] [4]:[8] Incline your ear to a poor man. Answer him with peaceful words in humility.
[Sira] [4]:[9] Deliver him who’s wronged from the hand of him who wrongs him; Don’t be hesitant in giving judgement.
[Sira] [4]:[10] Be as a father to the fatherless, and like a husband to their mother. So you’ll be as a son of the Most High, and he’ll love you more than your mother does.
[Sira] [4]:[11] Wisdom exalts her sons, and takes hold of those who seek her.
[Sira] [4]:[12] He who loves her loves life. Those who seek her early will be filled with gladness.
[Sira] [4]:[13] He who holds her fast will inherit glory. Where he enters, the master will bless.
[Sira] [4]:[14] Those who serve her minister to the Holy One. The master loves those who love her.
[Sira] [4]:[15] He who listens to her will judge the nations. He who heeds her will live securely.
[Sira] [4]:[16] If he trusts her, he’ll inherit her, and his generations will possess her.
[Sira] [4]:[17] Because at the first she’ll walk with him in crooked ways, and will bring fear and dread on him, and torment him with her discipline, until she may trust his soul, and try him by her judgements.
[Sira] [4]:[18] Then she’ll return him again to the straight way, and will gladden him, and reveal to him her secrets.
[Sira] [4]:[19] If he goes astray, she’ll forsake him, and hand him over to his fall.
[Sira] [4]:[20] Watch for the opportunity, and beware of evil. Don’t be ashamed of your soul.
[Sira] [4]:[21] Because there’s a shame that brings sin, and there’s a shame that’s glory and grace.
[Sira] [4]:[22] Don’t show partiality, discrediting your soul. Don’t revere any man to your falling.
[Sira] [4]:[23] Don’t refrain from speaking when it’s for safety. Don’t hide your wisdom for the sake of seeming fair.
[Sira] [4]:[24] Because wisdom will be known by speech, and instruction by the word of the tongue.
[Sira] [4]:[25] Don’t speak against the truth and be shamed for your ignorance.
[Sira] [4]:[26] Don’t be ashamed to confess your sins. Don’t fight the river’s current.
[Sira] [4]:[27] Don’t lay yourself down for a fool to tread on. Don’t be partial to one who’s mighty.
[Sira] [4]:[28] Strive for the truth to death, and the master God will fight for you.
[Sira] [4]:[29] Don’t be hasty with your tongue, or slack and negligent in your actions.
[Sira] [4]:[30] Don’t be like a lion in your house, or suspicious of your servants.
[Sira] [4]:[31] Don’t let your hand be stretched out to receive, and closed when you should repay.
[Sira] [5]:[1] Don’t set your heart on your goods. Don’t say, “They’re sufficient for me.”
[Sira] [5]:[2] Don’t follow your own mind and your strength to walk in the desires of your heart.
[Sira] [5]:[3] Don’t say, “Who’ll have dominion over me?” for the master will surely take vengeance on you.
[Sira] [5]:[4] Don’t say, “I sinned, and what happened to me?” for the master is patient.
[Sira] [5]:[5] Don’t be so confident of atonement that you add sin on sins.
[Sira] [5]:[6] Don’t say, “His compassion is great. He’ll be pacified for the multitude of my sins,” for mercy and anger are with him, and his indignation will rest on sinners.
[Sira] [5]:[7] Don’t wait to turn to the master. Don’t put off from day to day; for suddenly the master’s anger will come on you, and you’ll perish in the time of vengeance.
[Sira] [5]:[8] Don’t set your heart on unrighteous gains, for you’ll profit nothing in the day of calamity.
[Sira] [5]:[9] Don’t winnow with every wind. Don’t walk in every path. This is what the sinner who has a double tongue does.
[Sira] [5]:[10] Be steadfast in your understanding. Let your speech be consistent.
[Sira] [5]:[11] Be swift to hear and answer with patience.
[Sira] [5]:[12] If you have understanding, answer your neighbour; but if not, put your hand over your mouth.
[Sira] [5]:[13] Glory and dishonour is in talk. A man’s tongue may be his downfall.
[Sira] [5]:[14] Don’t be called a whisperer. Don’t lie in wait with your tongue; for shame is on the thief, and an evil condemnation is on him who has a double tongue.
[Sira] [5]:[15] Don’t be ignorant in a great or small matter.
[Sira] [6]:[1] Don’t become an enemy instead of a friend; for an evil name will inherit shame and reproach. So it’s with the sinner who has a double tongue.
[Sira] [6]:[2] Don’t exalt yourself in the counsel of your soul, that your soul not be torn in pieces like a bull.
[Sira] [6]:[3] You’ll eat up your leaves, destroy your fruit, and leave yourself like a dry tree.
[Sira] [6]:[4] A wicked soul will destroy him who has it, and will make him a laughing stock to his enemies.
[Sira] [6]:[5] Sweet words will multiply a man’s friends. A gracious tongue will multiply courtesies.
[Sira] [6]:[6] Let those that are at peace with you be many, but your advisers one of a thousand.
[Sira] [6]:[7] If you want to gain a friend, get him in a time of testing, and don’t be in a hurry to trust him.
[Sira] [6]:[8] Because there’s a friend just for an occasion. He won’t continue in the day of your affliction.
[Sira] [6]:[9] And there’s a friend who turns into an enemy. He’ll discover strife to your reproach.
[Sira] [6]:[10] And there’s a friend who’s a companion at the table, but he won’t continue in the day of your affliction.
[Sira] [6]:[11] In your prosperity he’ll be as yourself, and will be bold over your servants.
[Sira] [6]:[12] If you’re brought low, he’ll be against you, and will hide himself from your face.
[Sira] [6]:[13] Separate yourself from your enemies, and beware of your friends.
[Sira] [6]:[14] A faithful friend is a strong defence. He who’s found him has found a treasure.
[Sira] [6]:[15] There’s nothing that can be taken in exchange for a faithful friend. His excellency is beyond price.
[Sira] [6]:[16] A faithful friend is a life-saving medicine. Those who fear the master will find him.
[Sira] [6]:[17] He who fears the master directs his friendship properly; for as he is, so is his neighbour also.
[Sira] [6]:[18] My son, gather instruction from your youth up. Even when you have grey hair you’ll find wisdom.
[Sira] [6]:[19] Come to her as one who ploughs and sows and wait for her good fruit; for your toil will be little in her cultivation, and you’ll soon eat of her fruit.
[Sira] [6]:[20] How extremely harsh she’s to the unlearned! He who’s without understanding won’t remain in her.
[Sira] [6]:[21] She’ll rest on him as a mighty stone of trial. He won’t hesitate to throw her from him.
[Sira] [6]:[22] Because wisdom is according to her name. She isn’t manifest to many.
[Sira] [6]:[23] Give ear, my son, and accept my judgement. Don’t refuse my counsel.
[Sira] [6]:[24] Bring your feet into her fetters, and your neck into her chain.
[Sira] [6]:[25] Put your shoulder under her and bear her. Don’t be grieved with her bonds.
[Sira] [6]:[26] Come to her with all your soul. Keep her ways with your whole power.
[Sira] [6]:[27] Search and seek, and she’ll be made known to you. When you get hold of her, don’t let her go.
[Sira] [6]:[28] Because at the last you’ll find her rest; and she’ll be turned for you into gladness.
[Sira] [6]:[29] Her fetters will be to you for a covering of strength, and her chains for a robe of glory.
[Sira] [6]:[30] Because there’s a golden ornament on her, and her bands are a purple cord.
[Sira] [6]:[31] You’ll put her on as a robe of glory, and will put her on as a crown of rejoicing.
[Sira] [6]:[32] My son, if you’re willing, you’ll be instructed. If you’ll yield your soul, you’ll be prudent.
[Sira] [6]:[33] If you love to hear, you’ll receive. If you incline your ear, you’ll be wise.
[Sira] [6]:[34] Stand in the multitude of the elders. Attach yourself to whomever is wise.
[Sira] [6]:[35] Be willing to listen to every godly discourse. Don’t let the proverbs of understanding escape you.
[Sira] [6]:[36] If you see a man of understanding, get to him early. Let your foot wear out the steps of his doors.
[Sira] [6]:[37] Let your mind live on the ordinances of the master and meditate continually on his commandments. He’ll establish your heart and your desire for wisdom will be given to you.
[Sira] [7]:[1] Do no evil, so no evil will overtake you.
[Sira] [7]:[2] Depart from wrong, and it’ll turn away from you.
[Sira] [7]:[3] My son, don’t sow on the furrows of unrighteousness, and you won’t reap them sevenfold.
[Sira] [7]:[4] Don’t seek preeminence from the master, nor the seat of honour from the king.
[Sira] [7]:[5] Don’t justify yourself in the presence of the master, and don’t display your wisdom before the king.
[Sira] [7]:[6] Don’t seek to be a judge, in case you can’t put an end to wrongdoing, in case you’re intimidated by a powerful person, and lay a stumbling block in the way of your uprightness.
[Sira] [7]:[7] Don’t sin against the multitude of the city. Don’t disgrace yourself in the crowd.
[Sira] [7]:[8] Don’t commit a sin twice, for even in one you won’t be unpunished.
[Sira] [7]:[9] Don’t say, “He’ll look on the multitude of my gifts. When I make an offering to the Most High God, he’ll accept it.”
[Sira] [7]:[10] Don’t be faint-hearted in your prayer. Don’t neglect to give to the poor.
[Sira] [7]:[11] Don’t laugh a man to scorn when he’s in the bitterness of his soul, for there’s one who humbles and exalts.
[Sira] [7]:[12] Don’t devise a lie against your brother, or do the same to a friend.
[Sira] [7]:[13] Refuse to utter a lie, for that habit results in no good.
[Sira] [7]:[14] Don’t babble in the assembly of elders. Don’t repeat your words in your prayer.
[Sira] [7]:[15] Don’t hate hard labour or farm work, which the Most High has created.
[Sira] [7]:[16] Don’t number yourself among the multitude of sinners. Remember that anger won’t wait.
[Sira] [7]:[17] Humble your soul greatly, for the punishment of the ungodly man is fire and the worm.
[Sira] [7]:[18] Don’t exchange a friend for something, neither a true brother for the gold of Ofir.
[Sira] [7]:[19] Don’t deprive yourself of a wise and good wife, for her grace is worth more than gold.
[Sira] [7]:[20] Don’t abuse a servant who works faithfully, or a hireling who gives you his life.
[Sira] [7]:[21] Let your soul love a wise servant. Don’t defraud him of liberty.
[Sira] [7]:[22] Do you have cattle? Look after them. If they’re profitable to you, let them stay by you.
[Sira] [7]:[23] Do you have children? Correct them, and make them obedient from their youth.
[Sira] [7]:[24] Do you have daughters? Take care of their bodies, and don’t be overly indulgent towards them.
[Sira] [7]:[25] Give your daughter in marriage, and you’ll have accomplished a great matter. Give her to a man of understanding.
[Sira] [7]:[26] Do you have a wife who pleases you? Don’t throw her out. But don’t trust yourself to one who’s hateful.
[Sira] [7]:[27] Honour your father with your whole heart, and don’t forget the birth pangs of your mother.
[Sira] [7]:[28] Remember that you were born of them. What’ll you repay them for the things that they’ve done for you?
[Sira] [7]:[29] Fear the master with all your soul; and revere his priests.
[Sira] [7]:[30] With all your strength love him who made you. Don’t forsake his ministers.
[Sira] [7]:[31] Fear the master and honour the priest. Give him his portion, even as it’s commanded you: the first fruits, the trespass offering, the gift of the shoulders, the sacrifice of sanctification, and the first fruits of holy things.
[Sira] [7]:[32] Also stretch out your hand to the poor man, that your blessing may be complete.
[Sira] [7]:[33] A gift has grace in the sight of every living man. Don’t withhold grace for a dead man.
[Sira] [7]:[34] Don’t avoid those who weep, and mourn with those who mourn.
[Sira] [7]:[35] Don’t be slow to visit a sick man, for by such things you’ll gain love.
[Sira] [7]:[36] In all your words, remember eternity, and you’ll never sin.
[Sira] [8]:[1] Don’t contend with a mighty man, or you might fall into his hands.
[Sira] [8]:[2] Don’t strive with a rich man, or he might overpower you; for gold has destroyed many, and turned away the hearts of kings.
[Sira] [8]:[3] Don’t argue with a loudmouthed man. Don’t heap wood on his fire.
[Sira] [8]:[4] Don’t make fun of a rude man, or your ancestors might be dishonoured.
[Sira] [8]:[5] Don’t reproach a man when he turns from sin. Remember that we’re all worthy of punishment.
[Sira] [8]:[6] Don’t dishonour a man in his old age, for some of us are also growing old.
[Sira] [8]:[7] Don’t rejoice over anyone’s death. Remember that we all die.
[Sira] [8]:[8] Don’t neglect the discourse of the wise. Be conversant with their proverbs; for from them you’ll learn discipline and how to serve great men.
[Sira] [8]:[9] Don’t miss the discourse of the aged, for they also learnt from their parents, because from them you’ll learn understanding, and to give an answer in time of need.
[Sira] [8]:[10] Don’t kindle the coals of a sinner, or you might be burnt with the flame of his fire.
[Sira] [8]:[11] Don’t rise up from the presence of an insolent man, or he might lie in wait to trap you by what you say.
[Sira] [8]:[12] Don’t lend to a man who’s stronger than you; and if you lend, count it as a loss.
[Sira] [8]:[13] Don’t be surety beyond your means. If you give surety, think as one who’ll have to pay.
[Sira] [8]:[14] Don’t go to law with a judge; for according to his honour they’ll give judgement for him.
[Sira] [8]:[15] Don’t travel with a reckless man, or he might become a burden to you; for he’ll do as he pleases, and you’ll perish with his folly.
[Sira] [8]:[16] Don’t fight with a wrathful man. Don’t travel with him through the desert, for blood is as nothing in his sight. Where there’s no help, he’ll overthrow you.
[Sira] [8]:[17] Don’t consult with a fool, for he won’t be able to keep a secret.
[Sira] [8]:[18] Do no secret thing before a stranger, for you don’t know what it’ll cause.
[Sira] [8]:[19] Don’t open your heart to every man. Don’t let him return you a favour.
[Sira] [9]:[1] Don’t be jealous over the wife of your bosom, and don’t teach her an evil lesson against yourself.
[Sira] [9]:[2] Don’t give your soul to a woman and let her trample down your strength.
[Sira] [9]:[3] Don’t go to meet a woman who plays the prostitute, or you might fall into her traps.
[Sira] [9]:[4] Don’t associate with a woman who’s a singer, or you might be caught by her tricks.
[Sira] [9]:[5] Don’t gaze at a virgin, or you might stumble and be punished because of her.
[Sira] [9]:[6] Don’t give your soul to prostitutes, that you not lose your inheritance.
[Sira] [9]:[7] Don’t look around in the streets of the city. Don’t wander in its deserted places.
[Sira] [9]:[8] Turn your eye away from a beautiful woman, and don’t gaze at another’s beauty. Many have been led astray by the beauty of a woman; and with this, passion is kindled like a fire.
[Sira] [9]:[9] Don’t dine at all with a woman who has a husband, or revel with her at wine, or your heart might turn towards her, and with your spirit you slide into destruction.
[Sira] [9]:[10] Don’t forsake an old friend; for a new one isn’t comparable to him. A new friend is like new wine: if it becomes old, you’ll drink it with gladness.
[Sira] [9]:[11] Don’t envy the success of a sinner; for you don’t know what his end will be.
[Sira] [9]:[12] Don’t delight in the delights of the ungodly. Remember they won’t go unpunished to the grave.
[Sira] [9]:[13] Keep yourself far from the man who has power to kill, and you won’t be troubled by the fear of death. If you come to him, commit no fault, or he might take your life. Know surely that you go about among traps, and walk on the battlements of a city.
[Sira] [9]:[14] As well as you can, aim to know your neighbours, and take counsel with the wise.
[Sira] [9]:[15] Let your conversation be with men of understanding. Let all your discourse be in the Most High’s law.
[Sira] [9]:[16] Let righteous people be companions at your table. Let your glorying be in the fear of the master.
[Sira] [9]:[17] A work is commended because of the skill of the artisan; so he who rules the people will be considered wise for his speech.
[Sira] [9]:[18] A loudmouthed man is dangerous in his city. He who’s reckless in his speech will be hated.
[Sira] [10]:[1] A wise judge will instruct his people. The government of a man of understanding will be well ordered.
[Sira] [10]:[2] As is the judge of his people, so are his officials. As the city’s ruler is, so are all those who live in it.
[Sira] [10]:[3] An undisciplined king will destroy his people. A city will be established through the understanding of the powerful.
[Sira] [10]:[4] The government of the earth is in the master’s hand. In due time, he’ll raise up over it the right person at the right time.
[Sira] [10]:[5] A man’s prosperity is in the master’s hand. He’ll lay his honour on the person of the scribe.
[Sira] [10]:[6] Don’t be angry with your neighbour for every wrong. Do nothing by works of violence.
[Sira] [10]:[7] Pride is hateful before the master and men. Arrogance is abhorrent in the judgement of both.
[Sira] [10]:[8] Sovereignty is transferred from nation to nation because of injustice, violence, and greed for money.
[Sira] [10]:[9] Why are dirt and ashes proud? Because in life, my body decays.
[Sira] [10]:[10] A long disease mocks the physician. The king of today will die tomorrow.
[Sira] [10]:[11] Because when a man is dead, he’ll inherit maggots, vermin, and worms.
[Sira] [10]:[12] It’s the beginning of pride when a man departs from the master. His heart has departed from him who made him.
[Sira] [10]:[13] Because the beginning of pride is sin. He who keeps it’ll pour out abomination. Because this cause the master brought on them strange calamities and utterly overthrew them.
[Sira] [10]:[14] The master threw down the thrones of rulers and set the lowly in their place.
[Sira] [10]:[15] The master plucked up the roots of nations and planted the lowly in their place.
[Sira] [10]:[16] The master overthrew the lands of nations and destroyed them to the foundations of the earth.
[Sira] [10]:[17] He took some of them away and destroyed them, and made their memory to cease from the earth.
[Sira] [10]:[18] Pride hasn’t been created for men, nor wrathful anger for the offspring of women.
[Sira] [10]:[19] Whose offspring has honour? Human offspring who fear the master. Whose offspring has no honour? Human offspring who break the commandments.
[Sira] [10]:[20] Among relatives he who rules them has honour. Those who fear the master have honour in his eyes.
[Sira] [10]:[22] The rich man, the honourable, and the poor all glory in the fear of the master.
[Sira] [10]:[23] It isn’t right to dishonour a poor man who has understanding. It isn’t fitting to glorify a man who’s a sinner.
[Sira] [10]:[24] The prince, the judge, and the mighty man will be honoured. There isn’t one of them greater than he who fears the master.
[Sira] [10]:[25] Free men will minister to a wise servant. A man who has knowledge won’t complain.
[Sira] [10]:[26] Don’t flaunt your wisdom in doing your work. Don’t boast in the time of your distress.
[Sira] [10]:[27] Better is he who labours and abounds in all things, than he who boasts and lacks bread.
[Sira] [10]:[28] My son, glorify your soul in humility, and ascribe to yourself honour according to your worthiness.
[Sira] [10]:[29] Who’ll justify him who sins against his own soul? Who’ll honour him who dishonours his own life?
