[Sira] [10]:[30] A poor man is honoured for his knowledge. A rich man is honoured for his riches.
[Sira] [10]:[31] But he who’s honoured in poverty, how much more in riches? He who’s dishonoured in riches, how much more in poverty?
[Sira] [11]:[1] The wisdom of the lowly will lift up his head, and make him sit among great men.
[Sira] [11]:[2] Don’t commend a man for his good looks. Don’t abhor a man for his outward appearance.
[Sira] [11]:[3] The bee is little among flying creatures, but what it produces is the best of confections.
[Sira] [11]:[4] Don’t boast about the clothes you wear, and don’t exalt yourself in the day of honour; for the master’s works are wonderful, and his works are hidden among men.
[Sira] [11]:[5] Many kings have sat down on the ground, but one who was never thought of has worn a crown.
[Sira] [11]:[6] Many mighty men have been greatly disgraced. Men of renown have been delivered into other men’s hands.
[Sira] [11]:[7] Don’t blame before you investigate. Understand first, and then rebuke.
[Sira] [11]:[8] Don’t answer before you’ve heard. Don’t interrupt while someone else is speaking.
[Sira] [11]:[9] Don’t argue about a matter that doesn’t concern you. Don’t sit with sinners when they judge.
[Sira] [11]:[10] My son, don’t be busy about many matters; for if you meddle much, you won’t be unpunished. If you pursue, you won’t overtake, and you won’t escape by fleeing.
[Sira] [11]:[11] There’s one who toils, labours, and hurries, and is even more behind.
[Sira] [11]:[12] There’s one who’s sluggish, and needs help, lacking in strength, and who abounds in poverty, but the master’s eyes looked on him for good, and he raised him up from his low condition,
[Sira] [11]:[13] and lifted up his head so that many marvelled at him.
[Sira] [11]:[14] Good things and bad, life and death, poverty and riches, are from the master.
[Sira] [11]:[17] The master’s gift remains with the godly. His good pleasure will prosper forever.
[Sira] [11]:[18] One grows rich by his diligence and self-denial, and this is the portion of his reward:
[Sira] [11]:[19] when he says, “I’ve found rest, and now I’ll eat of my goods!” he doesn’t know how much time will pass until he leaves them to others and dies.
[Sira] [11]:[20] Be steadfast in your covenant and be doing it, and grow old in your work.
[Sira] [11]:[21] Don’t marvel at a sinner’s works, but trust the master and stay in your labour; for it’s an easy thing in the sight of the master to swiftly and suddenly make a poor man rich.
[Sira] [11]:[22] The master’s blessing is in the reward of the godly. He makes his blessing flourish in an hour that comes swiftly.
[Sira] [11]:[23] Don’t say, “What use is there of me? What further good things can be mine?”
[Sira] [11]:[24] Don’t say, “I have enough. What harm could happen to me now?”
[Sira] [11]:[25] In the day of good things, bad things are forgotten. In the day of bad things, a man won’t remember things that are good.
[Sira] [11]:[26] Because it’s an easy thing in the sight of the master to reward a man in the day of death according to his ways.
[Sira] [11]:[27] The affliction of an hour causes delights to be forgotten. In the end, a person’s actions are revealed.
[Sira] [11]:[28] Don’t call anyone happy before their death. A man will be known in his children.
[Sira] [11]:[29] Don’t bring every man into your house, for many are the tricks of a deceitful man.
[Sira] [11]:[30] Like a decoy partridge in a cage, so is the heart of a proud man. Like a spy, he looks for your weakness.
[Sira] [11]:[31] Because he lies in wait to turn things that are good into evil, and assigns blame in things that are praiseworthy.
[Sira] [11]:[32] From a spark of fire, a heap of many coals is kindled, and a sinful man lies in wait to shed blood.
[Sira] [11]:[33] Take heed of an evil-doer, for he plans wicked things, or he might ruin your reputation forever.
[Sira] [11]:[34] Receive a stranger into your house, and he’ll distract you with arguments and estrange you from your own family.
[Sira] [12]:[1] If you do good, know to whom you do it, and your good actions will have thanks.
[Sira] [12]:[2] Do good to a godly man, and you’ll find a reward— if not from him, then from the Most High.
[Sira] [12]:[3] No good will come to him who continues to do evil, nor to him who gives nothing to the poor.
[Sira] [12]:[4] Give to the godly man, and don’t help the sinner.
[Sira] [12]:[5] Do good to one who’s lowly. Don’t give to an ungodly man. Keep back his bread, and don’t give it to him, or he might use it to overpower you; for you’d receive twice as much evil for all the good you’d have done to him.
[Sira] [12]:[6] Because the Most High also hates sinners, and will repay vengeance to the ungodly.
[Sira] [12]:[7] Give to the good man, and don’t help the sinner.
[Sira] [12]:[8] A man’s friend won’t be fully tried in prosperity. His enemy won’t be hidden in adversity.
[Sira] [12]:[9] In a man’s prosperity, his enemies are grieved. In his adversity, even his friend leaves.
[Sira] [12]:[10] Never trust your enemy, for his wickedness is like corrosion in copper.
[Sira] [12]:[11] Though he humbles himself and walks bowed down, still be careful and beware of him. You’ll be to him as one who’s wiped a mirror, to be sure it doesn’t completely tarnish.
[Sira] [12]:[12] Don’t set him next to you, or he might overthrow you and take your place. Don’t let him sit on your right hand, or he might try to take your seat, and at the last you acknowledge my words, and be pricked with my sayings.
[Sira] [12]:[13] Who’ll pity a charmer that’s bitten by a snake, or any who come near wild animals?
[Sira] [12]:[14] Even so, who’ll pity him who goes to a sinner, and is associated with him in his sins?
[Sira] [12]:[15] Because a while he’ll stay with you, and if you falter, he won’t stay.
[Sira] [12]:[16] The enemy will speak sweetly with his lips, and in his heart plan to throw you into a pit. The enemy may weep with his eyes, but if he finds opportunity, he’ll want more blood.
[Sira] [12]:[17] If adversity meets you, you’ll find him there before you. Pretending to help you, he’ll trip you.
[Sira] [12]:[18] He’ll shake his head, clap his hands, whisper much, and change his expression.
[Sira] [13]:[1] He who touches pitch will be defiled. He who has fellowship with a proud man will become like him.
[Sira] [13]:[2] Don’t take up a burden above your strength. Have no fellowship with one who’s mightier and richer than yourself. What fellowship would the earthen pot have with the kettle? The kettle will strike, and the pot will be dashed in pieces.
[Sira] [13]:[3] The rich man does a wrong and threatens. The poor is wronged and apologises.
[Sira] [13]:[4] If you’re profitable, he’ll exploit you. If you’re in need, he’ll forsake you.
[Sira] [13]:[5] If you own something, he’ll live with you. He’ll drain your resources and won’t be sorry.
[Sira] [13]:[6] Does he need you? Then he’ll deceive you, smile at you, and give you hope. He’ll speak kindly to you and say, “What do you need?”
[Sira] [13]:[7] He’ll shame you by his delicacies until he’s made you bare twice or thrice, and in the end he’ll laugh you to scorn. Afterward he’ll see you, will forsake you, and shake his head at you.
[Sira] [13]:[8] Beware that you aren’t deceived and brought low in your enjoyment.
[Sira] [13]:[9] If a mighty man invites you, be reserved, and he’ll invite you more.
[Sira] [13]:[10] Don’t press him, or you might be pushed away. Don’t stand far off, or you might be forgotten.
[Sira] [13]:[11] Don’t try to speak with him as an equal, and don’t believe his many words; for he’ll test you with much talk, and will examine you in a smiling manner.
[Sira] [13]:[12] He who doesn’t keep secrets to himself is unmerciful. He won’t hesitate to harm and to bind.
[Sira] [13]:[13] Keep them to yourself and be careful, for you walk in danger of falling.
[Sira] [13]:[15] Every living creature loves its own kind, and every man loves his neighbour.
[Sira] [13]:[16] All flesh associates with their own kind. A man will stick to people like himself.
[Sira] [13]:[17] What fellowship would the wolf have with the lamb? So is the sinner to the godly.
[Sira] [13]:[18] What peace is there between a hyena and a dog? What peace is there between a rich man and the poor?
[Sira] [13]:[19] Wild donkeys are the prey of lions in the wilderness; likewise poor men are feeding grounds for the rich.
[Sira] [13]:[20] Lowliness is an abomination to a proud man; likewise a poor man is an abomination to the rich.
[Sira] [13]:[21] When a rich man is shaken, he’s supported by his friends, but when the humble is down, he’s pushed away even by his friends.
[Sira] [13]:[22] When a rich man falls, there are many helpers. He speaks things not to be spoken, and men justify him. A humble man falls, and men rebuke him. He utters wisdom, and isn’t listened to.
[Sira] [13]:[23] A rich man speaks, and all keep silence. They extol what he says to the clouds. A poor man speaks, and they say, “Who’s this?” If he stumbles, they’ll help to overthrow him.
[Sira] [13]:[24] Riches are good if they have no sin. Poverty is evil only in the opinion of the ungodly.
[Sira] [13]:[25] A man’s heart changes his face, whether it’s for good or for evil.
[Sira] [13]:[26] A cheerful face is a sign of a prosperous heart. Devising proverbs takes strenuous thinking.
[Sira] [14]:[1] Blessed is the man who hasn’t slipped with his mouth, and doesn’t suffer from sorrow for sins.
[Sira] [14]:[2] Blessed is he whose soul doesn’t condemn him, and who hasn’t given up hope.
[Sira] [14]:[3] Riches aren’t appropriate for a stingy person. What’d a miser do with money?
[Sira] [14]:[4] He who gathers by denying himself gathers for others. Others will revel in his goods.
[Sira] [14]:[5] If one is mean to himself, to whom will he be good? He won’t enjoy his possessions.
[Sira] [14]:[6] There’s none more evil than he who’s grudging to himself. This is a punishment for his wickedness.
[Sira] [14]:[7] Even if he does good, he does it in forgetfulness. In the end, he reveals his wickedness.
[Sira] [14]:[8] A miser is evil. He turns away and disregards souls.
[Sira] [14]:[9] A covetous man’s eye isn’t satisfied with his portion. Wicked injustice dries up his soul.
[Sira] [14]:[10] A miser begrudges bread, and it’s lacking at his table.
[Sira] [14]:[11] My son, according to what you have, treat yourself well, and bring worthy offerings to the master.
[Sira] [14]:[12] Remember that death won’t wait, and that Haidais’ covenant hasn’t been shown to you.
[Sira] [14]:[13] Do good to your friends before you die. According to your ability, reach out and give to them.
[Sira] [14]:[14] Don’t deprive yourself of a good day. Don’t let your share of a desired good pass you by.
[Sira] [14]:[15] won’t you leave your labours to another, and your toils be divided by lot?
[Sira] [14]:[16] Give, take, and treat yourself well, because there’s no seeking of luxury in Haidais.
[Sira] [14]:[17] All flesh grows old like a garment, for the covenant from the beginning is, “You must die!”
[Sira] [14]:[18] Like the leaves flourishing on a thick tree, some it sheds, and some grow, so also are the generations of flesh and blood: one comes to an end and another is born.
[Sira] [14]:[19] Every work rots and falls away, and its builder will depart with it.
[Sira] [14]:[20] Blessed is the man who meditates on wisdom, and who reasons by his understanding.
[Sira] [14]:[21] He who considers her ways in his heart will also have knowledge of her secrets.
[Sira] [14]:[22] Go after her like a hunter, and lie in wait in her paths.
[Sira] [14]:[23] He who peers in at her windows will also listen at her doors.
[Sira] [14]:[24] He who lodges close to her house will also fasten a nail in her walls.
[Sira] [14]:[25] He’ll pitch his tent near at hand to her, and will lodge in a lodging where good things are.
[Sira] [14]:[26] He’ll set his children under her shelter, and will rest under her branches.
[Sira] [14]:[27] By her he’ll be covered from heat, and will lodge in her glory.
[Sira] [15]:[1] He who fears the master will do this. He who has possession of the law will obtain her.
[Sira] [15]:[2] She’ll meet him like a mother, and receive him like a wife married in her virginity.
[Sira] [15]:[3] She’ll feed him with bread of understanding and give him water of wisdom to drink.
[Sira] [15]:[4] He’ll be stayed on her, and won’t be moved. He’ll rely on her, and won’t be confounded.
[Sira] [15]:[5] She’ll exalt him above his neighbours. She’ll open his mouth among the congregation.
[Sira] [15]:[6] He’ll inherit joy, a crown of gladness, and an eternal name.
[Sira] [15]:[7] Foolish men won’t obtain her. Sinners won’t see her.
[Sira] [15]:[8] She’s far from pride. Liars won’t remember her.
[Sira] [15]:[9] Praise isn’t attractive in a sinner’s mouth; for it wasn’t sent to him from the master.
[Sira] [15]:[10] Because praise will be spoken in wisdom; The master will prosper it.
[Sira] [15]:[11] Don’t say, “It’s through the master that I fell away;” for you mustn’t do the things that he hates.
[Sira] [15]:[12] Don’t say, “It’s he that caused me to err;” for he has no need of a sinful man.
[Sira] [15]:[13] The master hates every abomination; and those who fear him don’t love them.
[Sira] [15]:[14] He himself made man from the beginning and left him in the hand of his own counsel.
[Sira] [15]:[15] If you choose, you can keep the commandments. To be faithful is a matter of your choice.
[Sira] [15]:[16] He’s set fire and water before you. You’ll stretch forth your hand to whichever you desire.
[Sira] [15]:[17] Before man is life and death. Whichever he likes, it’ll be given to him.
[Sira] [15]:[18] Because the master’s wisdom is great. He’s mighty in power, and sees all things.
[Sira] [15]:[19] His eyes are on those who fear him. He knows every act of man.
[Sira] [15]:[20] He hasn’t commanded any man to be ungodly. He hasn’t given any man license to sin.
[Sira] [16]:[1] Don’t desire a multitude of unprofitable children, neither delight in ungodly sons.
[Sira] [16]:[2] If they multiply, don’t delight in them unless the fear of the master is in them.
[Sira] [16]:[3] Don’t trust in their life. Don’t rely on their numbers; for one can be better than a thousand, and to die childless than to have ungodly children.
[Sira] [16]:[4] Because from one who has understanding, a city will be populated, but a race of wicked men will be made desolate.
[Sira] [16]:[5] I’ve seen many such things with my eyes. My ear has heard mightier things than these.
[Sira] [16]:[6] In a congregation of sinners, a fire will be kindled. In a disobedient nation, anger is kindled.
[Sira] [16]:[7] He wasn’t pacified towards the giants of old time, who revolted in their strength.
[Sira] [16]:[8] He didn’t spare Lot’s neighbours, whom he abhorred for their pride.
[Sira] [16]:[9] He didn’t pity the people of perdition who were taken away in their sins,
[Sira] [16]:[10] or in the same way, the six hundred thousand footmen who were gathered together in the hardness of their hearts.
[Sira] [16]:[11] Even if there’s one stiff-necked person, it’s a marvel if he’ll be unpunished; for mercy and anger are both with him who’s mighty to forgive, and he pours out anger.
[Sira] [16]:[12] As his mercy is great, so is his correction also. He judges a man according to his works.
[Sira] [16]:[13] The sinner won’t escape with plunder. The perseverance of the godly won’t be frustrated.
[Sira] [16]:[14] He’ll make room for every work of mercy. Each man will receive according to his works.
[Sira] [16]:[17] Don’t say, “I’ll be hidden from the master,” and “Who’ll remember me from on high?” I won’t be known among so many people, for what’s my soul in a boundless creation?
[Sira] [16]:[18] Listen, the heaven, the heaven of heavens, the deep, and the earth, will be moved when he visits.
[Sira] [16]:[19] The mountains and the foundations of the earth together are shaken with trembling when he looks at them.
[Sira] [16]:[20] No heart will think about these things. Who could comprehend his ways?
[Sira] [16]:[21] Like a tempest which no man can see, so, the majority of his works are hidden.
[Sira] [16]:[22] Who’ll declare his works of righteousness? Who’ll wait for them? Because his covenant is afar off.
[Sira] [16]:[23] He who’s lacking in understanding thinks about these things. An unwise and erring man thinks foolishly.
[Sira] [16]:[24] My son, listen to me, learn knowledge, and heed my words with your heart.
[Sira] [16]:[25] I’ll impart instruction with precision, and declare knowledge exactly.
[Sira] [16]:[26] In the master’s judgement are his works from the beginning. From the making of them he determined their boundaries.
[Sira] [16]:[27] He arranged his works for all time, and their beginnings to their generations. They aren’t hungry or weary, and they don’t cease from their works.
[Sira] [16]:[28] No one pushes aside his neighbour. They’ll never disobey his word.
[Sira] [16]:[29] After this also the master looked at the earth and filled it with his blessings.
[Sira] [16]:[30] All manner of living things covered its surface, and they return into it.
[Sira] [17]:[1] The master created mankind out of earth, and turned them back to it again.
[Sira] [17]:[2] He gave them days by number, and a set time, and gave them authority over the things that are on it.
[Sira] [17]:[3] He endowed them with strength proper to them, and made them according to his own image.
[Sira] [17]:[4] He put the fear of man on all flesh, and gave him dominion over animals and birds.
[Sira] [17]:[6] He gave them counsel, tongue, eyes, ears, and heart to have understanding.
[Sira] [17]:[7] He filled them with the knowledge of wisdom, and showed them good and evil.
[Sira] [17]:[8] He set his eye on their hearts, to show them the majesty of his works.
[Sira] [17]:[10] And they’ll praise his holy name, that they may declare the majesty of his works.
[Sira] [17]:[11] He added to them knowledge, and gave them a law of life for a heritage.
[Sira] [17]:[12] He made an eternal covenant with them, and showed them his decrees.
[Sira] [17]:[13] Their eyes saw the majesty of his glory. Their ears heard the glory of his voice.
[Sira] [17]:[14] He said to them, “Beware of all unrighteousness.” So he gave them commandment, each man about his neighbour.
[Sira] [17]:[15] Their ways are ever before him. They won’t be hidden from his eyes.
[Sira] [17]:[17] Because every nation he appointed a ruler, but Yisrael (Israel) is the master’s portion.
[Sira] [17]:[19] All their works are as clear as the sun before him. His eyes are continually on their ways.
[Sira] [17]:[20] Their iniquities aren’t hidden from him. All their sins are before the master.
[Sira] [17]:[22] With him a person’s giving to the poor is as a signet. He’ll keep a man’s kindness as the pupil of the eye.
[Sira] [17]:[23] Afterwards he’ll rise up and repay them, and render their repayment on their head.
[Sira] [17]:[24] However to those who repent he grants a return. He comforts those who are losing hope.
[Sira] [17]:[25] Return to the master, and forsake sins. Make your prayer before his face offend less.
[Sira] [17]:[26] Turn again to the Most High, and turn away from iniquity. Greatly hate the abominable thing.
[Sira] [17]:[27] Who’ll give praise to the Most High in Haidais, in place of the living who return thanks?
[Sira] [17]:[28] Thanksgiving perishes from the dead, as from one who doesn’t exist. He who’s in life and health will praise the master.
[Sira] [17]:[29] How great is the master’s mercy, and his forgiveness to those who turn to him!
[Sira] [17]:[30] Because humans aren’t capable of everything, because the son of man isn’t immortal.
[Sira] [17]:[31] What’s brighter than the sun? Yet even this can be eclipsed. So flesh and blood devise evil.
[Sira] [17]:[32] He looks on the power of the height of heaven, while all men are earth and ashes.
[Sira] [18]:[1] He who lives forever created the whole universe.
[Sira] [18]:[2] The master alone is just.
[Sira] [18]:[4] He’s given power to declare his works to no one. Who could trace out his mighty actions?
[Sira] [18]:[5] Who could measure the strength of his majesty? Who could also proclaim his mercies?
[Sira] [18]:[6] As for the wondrous works of the master, it isn’t possible to take from them nor add to them, neither is it possible to explore them.
[Sira] [18]:[7] When a man has finished, then he’s just at the beginning. When he stops, then he’ll be perplexed.
[Sira] [18]:[8] What’s mankind, and what purpose do they serve? What’s their good, and what’s their evil?
[Sira] [18]:[9] The number of man’s days at the most are a hundred years.
[Sira] [18]:[10] As a drop of water from the sea, and a pebble from the sand, so are a few years in the day of eternity.
[Sira] [18]:[11] Because this cause the master was patient over them, and poured out his mercy on them.
[Sira] [18]:[12] He saw and perceived their end, that it’s evil. Therefore he multiplied his forgiveness.
[Sira] [18]:[13] A man’s mercy is on his neighbour; but the master’s mercy is on all flesh: reproving, chastening, teaching, and bringing back, as a shepherd does his flock.
[Sira] [18]:[14] He has mercy on those who accept chastening, and that diligently seek after his judgements.
[Sira] [18]:[15] My son, don’t add reproach to your good actions, and no harsh words in any of your giving.
[Sira] [18]:[16] Doesn’t the dew relieve the scorching heat? So a word is better than a gift.
[Sira] [18]:[17] Listen, isn’t a word better than a gift? Both are with a gracious person.
[Sira] [18]:[18] A fool is ungracious and abusive. The gift of an grudging person consumes the eyes.
[Sira] [18]:[19] Learn before you speak. Take care of your health before you get sick.
[Sira] [18]:[20] Before judgement, examine yourself, and in the hour of scrutiny you’ll find forgiveness.
[Sira] [18]:[21] Humble yourself before you get sick. In the time of sins, repent.
[Sira] [18]:[22] Let nothing hinder you to pay your vow in due time. Don’t wait until death to be released.
[Sira] [18]:[23] Before you make a vow, prepare yourself. Don’t be like a man who tests the master.
[Sira] [18]:[24] Think about the anger coming in the days of the end, and the time of vengeance, when he turns away his face.
[Sira] [18]:[25] In the days of fullness remember the time of hunger. Remember poverty and lack in the days of wealth.
[Sira] [18]:[26] From morning until evening, the time changes. All things are speedy before the master.
[Sira] [18]:[27] A wise man is cautious in everything. In days of sinning, he’ll beware of offence.
[Sira] [18]:[28] Every man of understanding knows wisdom. He’ll give thanks to him who found her.
[Sira] [18]:[29] They who were of understanding in sayings also became wise themselves, and poured out apt proverbs.
[Sira] [18]:[30] Don’t go after your lusts. Restrain your appetites.
[Sira] [18]:[31] If you give fully to your soul the delight of her desire, she’ll make you the laughing stock of your enemies.
[Sira] [18]:[32] Don’t make merry in much luxury, and don’t be tied to its expense.
[Sira] [18]:[33] Don’t be made a beggar by banqueting with borrowed money when you have nothing in your purse.
[Sira] [19]:[1] A worker who’s a drunkard won’t become rich. He who despises small things will fall little by little.
[Sira] [19]:[2] Wine and women will make men of understanding go astray. He who joins with prostitutes is reckless.
[Sira] [19]:[3] Decay and worms will have him as their heritage. A reckless soul will be taken away.
[Sira] [19]:[4] He who’s hasty to trust is shallow-hearted. He who sins offends against his own soul.
[Sira] [19]:[5] He who rejoices in wickedness will be condemned.
[Sira] [19]:[6] He who hates gossip has less wickedness.
[Sira] [19]:[7] Never repeat what’s told you, and you won’t lose anything.
[Sira] [19]:[8] Whether it’s of friend or foe, don’t tell it. Unless it’s a sin to you, don’t reveal it.
[Sira] [19]:[9] Because if he’s heard you and observed you, when the time comes, he’ll hate you.
[Sira] [19]:[10] Have you heard something? Let it die with you. Be brave: it won’t make you burst!
[Sira] [19]:[11] A fool will travail in pain with a word, as a woman in labour with a child.
[Sira] [19]:[12] As an arrow that sticks in the flesh of the thigh, so is gossip in a fool.
[Sira] [19]:[13] Question a friend; it may be he didn’t do it. If he did something, it may be that he may do it no more.
[Sira] [19]:[14] Question your neighbour; it may be he didn’t say it. If he’s said it, it may be that he may not say it again.
[Sira] [19]:[15] Question a friend; for many times there’s slander. Don’t trust every word.
[Sira] [19]:[16] There’s one who slips, and not from the heart. Who’s he who hasn’t sinned with his tongue?
[Sira] [19]:[17] Reprove your neighbour before you threaten him; and give place to the Most High’s law.
[Sira] [19]:[20] All wisdom is the fear of the master. In all wisdom is the doing of the law.
[Sira] [19]:[22] The knowledge of wickedness isn’t wisdom. The prudence of sinners isn’t counsel.
[Sira] [19]:[23] There’s a wickedness, and it’s an abomination. There’s a fool lacking in wisdom.
[Sira] [19]:[24] Better is one who has little understanding, and fears God, than one who has much intelligence and transgresses the law.
[Sira] [19]:[25] There’s an exquisite subtlety, and it’s unjust. And there’s one who perverts favour to gain a judgement.
[Sira] [19]:[26] There’s one who does wickedly, who hangs down his head with mourning; but inwardly he’s full of deceit,
[Sira] [19]:[27] bowing down his face, and pretending to be deaf in one ear. Where he isn’t known, he’ll take advantage of you.
[Sira] [19]:[28] And if for lack of power he’s hindered from sinning, if he finds opportunity, he’ll do mischief.
[Sira] [19]:[29] A man will be known by his appearance. One who has understanding will be known by his face when you meet him.
[Sira] [19]:[30] A man’s attire, grinning laughter, and the way he walks show what he is.
[Sira] [20]:[1] There’s a reproof that isn’t timely; and there’s a person who’s wise enough to keep silent.
[Sira] [20]:[2] How good is it to reprove, rather than to be angry. He who confesses will be kept back from harm.
[Sira] [20]:[4] As is the lust of a eunuch to deflower a virgin, so is he who executes judgements with violence.
[Sira] [20]:[5] There’s one who keeps silent and is found wise; and there’s one who’s hated for his much talk.
[Sira] [20]:[6] There’s one who keeps silent, for he has no answer to make; And there’s one who keeps silent, knowing when to speak.
[Sira] [20]:[7] A wise man will be silent until his time has come, but the braggart and fool will miss his time.
[Sira] [20]:[8] He who uses many words will be abhorred. He who takes authority for himself will be hated in it.
[Sira] [20]:[9] There’s a prosperity that a man finds in misfortunes; and there’s a gain that turns to loss.
[Sira] [20]:[10] There’s a gift that won’t profit you; and there’s a gift that pays back double.
[Sira] [20]:[11] There are losses because of glory; and there’s one who’s lifted up his head from a low estate.
[Sira] [20]:[12] There’s one who buys much for a little, and pays for it again sevenfold.
[Sira] [20]:[13] He who’s wise in words will make himself beloved; but the pleasantries of fools will be wasted.
[Sira] [20]:[14] The gift of a fool won’t profit you, for he looks for repayment many times instead of one.
[Sira] [20]:[15] He’ll give little and insult much. He’ll open his mouth like a crier. Today he’ll lend, and tomorrow he’ll ask for it back. Such a one is a hateful man.
[Sira] [20]:[16] The fool will say, “I have no friend, and I have no thanks for my good actions. Those who eat my bread have an evil tongue.”
[Sira] [20]:[17] How often, and of how many, will he be laughed to scorn!
[Sira] [20]:[18] A slip on a pavement is better than a slip with the tongue. So the fall of the wicked will come speedily.
[Sira] [20]:[19] A man without grace is a tale out of season. It’ll be continually in the mouth of the ignorant.
[Sira] [20]:[20] A parable from a fool’s mouth will be rejected; for he won’t tell it at the proper time.
[Sira] [20]:[21] There’s one who’s hindered from sinning through lack. When he rests, he won’t be troubled.
[Sira] [20]:[22] There’s one who destroys his soul through bashfulness. By a foolish face, he’ll destroy it.
[Sira] [20]:[23] There’s one who for bashfulness makes promises to his friend; and he makes him his enemy for nothing.
[Sira] [20]:[24] A lie is an ugly blot on a person. It’ll be continually in the mouth of the ignorant.
[Sira] [20]:[25] A thief is better than a man who’s continually lying, but they both will inherit destruction.
[Sira] [20]:[26] The destination of a liar is dishonour. His shame is with him continually.
[Sira] [20]:[27] He who’s wise in words will advance himself. And one who’s prudent will please great men.
[Sira] [20]:[28] He who tills his land will raise his harvest high. He who pleases great men will get pardon for iniquity.
[Sira] [20]:[29] Favours and gifts blind the eyes of the wise, and as a muzzle on the mouth, turn away reproofs.
[Sira] [20]:[30] Wisdom that’s hidden, and treasure that’s out of sight— what profit is in either of them?
[Sira] [20]:[31] Better is a man who hides his folly than a man who hides his wisdom.
[Sira] [21]:[1] My son, have you sinned? Do it no more; and ask forgiveness for your past sins.

[Sira] [21]:[3] All iniquity is as a two-edged sword. Its stroke has no healing.
[Sira] [21]:[4] Terror and violence will waste away riches. So an arrogant man’s house will be laid waste.
[Sira] [21]:[5] Supplication from a poor man’s mouth reaches to the ears of God, and his judgement comes speedily.
[Sira] [21]:[6] One who hates reproof is in the path of the sinner. He who fears the master will repent in his heart.
[Sira] [21]:[7] He who’s mighty in tongue is known far away; but the man of understanding knows when he slips.
[Sira] [21]:[8] He who builds his house with other men’s money is like one who gathers stones for his own tomb.
[Sira] [21]:[9] The congregation of wicked men is as a bundle of tow with a flame of fire at the end of them.

[Sira] [21]:[11] He who keeps the law becomes master of its intent. The fulfilment of the fear of the master is wisdom.
[Sira] [21]:[12] He who isn’t clever won’t be instructed. There’s a cleverness which makes bitterness abound.
[Sira] [21]:[13] The knowledge of a wise man will be made to abound as a flood, and his counsel as a fountain of life.
[Sira] [21]:[14] The inward parts of a fool are like a broken vessel. He’ll hold no knowledge.
[Sira] [21]:[15] If a man of knowledge hears a wise word, he’ll commend it and add to it. The wanton man hears it, and it displeases him, so he throws it away behind his back.
[Sira] [21]:[16] The chatter of a fool is like a burden in the way, but grace will be found on the lips of the wise.
[Sira] [21]:[17] The utterance of the prudent man will be sought for in the congregation. They’ll ponder his words in their heart.
[Sira] [21]:[18] As a house that’s destroyed, so is wisdom to a fool. The knowledge of an unwise man is talk without sense.
[Sira] [21]:[19] Instruction is as fetters on the feet of an unwise man, and as manacles on the right hand.
[Sira] [21]:[20] A fool lifts up his voice with laughter, but a clever man smiles quietly.
[Sira] [21]:[21] Instruction is to a prudent man as an ornament of gold, and as a bracelet on his right arm.
[Sira] [21]:[22] A fool’s foot rushes into a house, but a man of experience will be ashamed of entering.
[Sira] [21]:[23] A foolish man peers into the door of a house, but a man who’s instructed will stand outside.
[Sira] [21]:[24] It’s rude for someone to listen at a door, but a prudent person will be grieved with the disgrace.
[Sira] [21]:[25] The lips of strangers will be grieved at these things, but the words of prudent men will be weighed in the balance.
[Sira] [21]:[26] The heart of fools is in their mouth, but the mouth of wise men is their heart.
[Sira] [21]:[27] When the ungodly curses an adversary, he curses his own soul.
[Sira] [21]:[28] A whisperer defiles his own soul, and will be hated wherever he travels.
[Sira] [22]:[1] A slothful man is compared to a stone that’s defiled. Everyone will hiss at him in his disgrace.

[Sira] [22]:[4] A prudent daughter will inherit a husband of her own. She who brings shame is the grief of her father.
[Sira] [22]:[5] She who’s arrogant brings shame on father and husband. She’ll be despised by both of them.

[Sira] [22]:[8] He who teaches a fool is as one who teaches a man who slumbers. In the end he’ll say, “What’s it?”
[Sira] [22]:[11] Weep for the dead, for he lacks light. Weep for a fool, for he lacks understanding. Weep more sweetly for the dead, because he’s found rest, but the life of the fool is worse than death.
[Sira] [22]:[12] Mourning for the dead lasts seven days, but for a fool and an ungodly man, it lasts all the days of his life.
[Sira] [22]:[13] Don’t talk much with a foolish man, and don’t go to one who has no understanding. Beware of him, or his attack might bring you trouble and defile you. Turn away from him, and you’ll find rest, and you won’t be wearied in his madness.
[Sira] [22]:[14] What’d be heavier than lead? What’s its name, but “Fool”?
[Sira] [22]:[15] Sand, salt, and a mass of iron is easier to bear than a man without understanding.
[Sira] [22]:[16] Timber girded and bound into a building won’t be released with shaking. So a heart established in due season on well advised counsel won’t be afraid.
[Sira] [22]:[17] A heart settled on a thoughtful understanding is as an ornament of plaster on a polished wall.
[Sira] [22]:[18] Fences set on a high place won’t stand against the wind; so a fearful heart in the imagination of a fool won’t stand against any fear.
[Sira] [22]:[19] He who pricks the eye will make tears fall. He who pricks the heart makes it show feeling.
[Sira] [22]:[20] The person who throws a stone at birds, scares them away. He who insults a friend will dissolve friendship.
[Sira] [22]:[21] If you’ve drawn a sword against a friend, don’t despair, for there may be a way back.
[Sira] [22]:[22] If you’ve opened your mouth against a friend, don’t be afraid, for there may be reconciliation, unless it’s for insulting, arrogance, disclosing of a secret, or a treacherous blow— for these things any friend will flee.
[Sira] [22]:[23] Gain trust with your neighbour in his poverty, that in his prosperity you may have gladness. Stay steadfast to him in the time of his affliction, that you may be heir with him in his inheritance.
[Sira] [22]:[24] Before fire is the vapour and smoke of a furnace, so insults precede bloodshed.
[Sira] [22]:[25] I won’t be ashamed to shelter a friend. I won’t hide myself from his face.
[Sira] [22]:[26] If any evil happens to me because of him, everyone who hears it’ll beware of him.
[Sira] [22]:[27] Who’ll set a watch over my mouth, and a seal of shrewdness on my lips, that I may not fall from it, and that my tongue may not destroy me?
[Sira] [23]:[1] Oh master, Father and Master of my life, don’t abandon me to their counsel. Don’t let me fall because of them.
[Sira] [23]:[2] Who’ll set scourges over my thought, and a discipline of wisdom over my heart, that they spare me not for my errors, and not overlook their sins?
[Sira] [23]:[3] Otherwise my errors might be multiplied, and my sins abound, I fall before my adversaries, and my enemy rejoice over me.
[Sira] [23]:[4] Oh master, Father and God of my life, don’t give me a haughty eyes,
[Sira] [23]:[5] and turn away evil desire from me.
[Sira] [23]:[6] Let neither gluttony nor lust overtake me. Don’t give me over to a shameless mind.
[Sira] [23]:[7] Listen, my children, to the discipline of the mouth. He who keeps it won’t be caught.
[Sira] [23]:[8] The sinner will be overpowered through his lips. By them, the insulter and the arrogant will stumble.
[Sira] [23]:[9] Don’t accustom your mouth to an oath, and don’t be accustomed to naming the Holy One,
[Sira] [23]:[10] for as a servant who’s continually scourged won’t lack bruises, so he also who swears and continually utters the Name won’t be cleansed from sin.
[Sira] [23]:[11] A man of many oaths will be filled with iniquity. The scourge won’t depart from his house. If he offends, his sin will be on him. If he disregards it, he’s sinned doubly. If he’s sworn falsely, he won’t be justified, for his house will be filled with calamities.
[Sira] [23]:[12] There’s a manner of speech that’s clothed with death. Let it not be found in the heritage of Ya’akov (Jacob), for all these things will be far from the godly, and they won’t wallow in sins.
[Sira] [23]:[13] Don’t accustom your mouth to gross rudeness, for it involves sinful speech.
[Sira] [23]:[14] Remember your father and your mother, for you sit among great men, that you be not forgetful before them, and become a fool by your bad habit; so you may wish that you hadn’t been born, and curse the day of your birth.
[Sira] [23]:[15] A man who’s accustomed to abusive language won’t be corrected all the days of his life.
[Sira] [23]:[16] Two sorts of people multiply sins, and the third will bring anger: a hot passion, like a burning fire, won’t be quenched until it’s consumed; a fornicator in the body of his flesh will never cease until he has burnt out the fire.
[Sira] [23]:[17] All bread is sweet to a fornicator. He won’t cease until he dies.
[Sira] [23]:[18] A man who goes astray from his own marriage bed says in his heart, “Who sees me? Darkness is around me, and the walls hide me. No one sees me. Of whom am I afraid? The Most High won’t remember my sins.”
[Sira] [23]:[19] Men’s eyes are his terror. He doesn’t know that the master’s eyes are ten thousand times brighter than the sun, seeing all the ways of men, and looking into secret places.
[Sira] [23]:[20] All things were known to him before they were created, and also after they were completed.
[Sira] [23]:[21] This man will be punished in the streets of the city. He’ll be seized where he least expects it.
[Sira] [23]:[22] So also is a wife who leaves her husband, and produces an heir by another man.
[Sira] [23]:[23] Because first, she was disobedient in the Most High’s law. Second, she trespassed against her own husband. Third, she played the adulteress in fornication, and had children by another man.
[Sira] [23]:[24] She’ll be brought out into the congregation. Her punishment will extend to her children.
[Sira] [23]:[25] Her children won’t take root. Her branches will bear no fruit.
[Sira] [23]:[26] She’ll leave her memory for a curse. Her reproach won’t be blotted out.
[Sira] [23]:[27] And those who are left behind will know that there’s nothing better than the fear of the master, and nothing sweeter than to heed the master’s commandments.
[Sira] [24]:[1] Wisdom will praise her own soul, and will proclaim her glory among her people.
[Sira] [24]:[2] She’ll open her mouth in the congregation of the Most High, and proclaim her glory in the presence of his power.
[Sira] [24]:[3] “I came out of the Most High’s mouth, and covered the earth as a mist.
[Sira] [24]:[4] I lived in high places, and my throne is in the pillar of the cloud.
[Sira] [24]:[5] Alone I surrounded the circuit of heaven, and walked in the depth of the abyss.
[Sira] [24]:[6] In the waves of the sea, and in all the earth, and in every people and nation, I obtained a possession.
[Sira] [24]:[7] With all these I sought rest. In whose inheritance will I stay?
[Sira] [24]:[8] Then the Creator of all things gave me a command. He who created me made my tent to rest, and said, ‘Let your dwelling be in Ya’akov (Jacob), and your inheritance in Yisrael (Israel).’
[Sira] [24]:[9] He created me from the beginning, before the ages. Because all ages, I won’t cease to exist.
[Sira] [24]:[10] In the holy tabernacle, I ministered before him. So I was established in Tsiyon (Zion).
[Sira] [24]:[11] In the beloved city, likewise he gave me rest. In Yerushalem (Jerusalem) was my domain.
[Sira] [24]:[12] I took root in a people that was honoured, even in the portion of the master’s own inheritance.
[Sira] [24]:[13] I was exalted like a cedar in Levanon, And like a cypress tree on the mountains of Hermon.
[Sira] [24]:[14] I was exalted like a palm tree on the sea shore, like rose bushes in Yeriho (Jericho), and like a fair olive tree in the plain. I was exalted like a plane tree.
[Sira] [24]:[15] Like cinnamon and aspalathus, I’ve given a scent to perfumes. Like choice myrrh, I spread abroad a pleasant fragrance, like galbanum, onycha, stacte, and as the smell of frankincense in the tabernacle.
[Sira] [24]:[16] Like the terebinth, I stretched out my branches. My branches are glorious and graceful.
[Sira] [24]:[17] Like the vine, I put forth grace. My flowers are the fruit of glory and riches.
[Sira] [24]:[19] “Come to me, all you who desire me, and be filled with my fruits.
[Sira] [24]:[20] Because my memory is sweeter than honey, and my inheritance than the honeycomb.
[Sira] [24]:[21] Those who eat me will be hungry for more. Those who drink me will be thirsty for more.
[Sira] [24]:[22] He who obeys me won’t be ashamed. Those who work with me won’t sin.”
[Sira] [24]:[23] All these things are the book of the Most High God’s covenant, the law which Mosheh (Moses) commanded us for an inheritance for the assemblies of Ya’akov (Jacob).
[Sira] [24]:[25] It’s he who makes wisdom abundant, as Pishon, and as Hidekel in the days of first fruits.
[Sira] [24]:[26] He makes understanding full as the Perat (Euphrates), and as the Yarden (Jordan) in the days of harvest,
[Sira] [24]:[27] who makes instruction shine forth as the light, as Gihon in the days of vintage.
[Sira] [24]:[28] The first man didn’t know her perfectly. In the same way, the last hasn’t explored her.
[Sira] [24]:[29] Because her thoughts are filled from the sea, and her counsels from the great deep.
[Sira] [24]:[30] I came out as a canal stream from a river, and as an irrigation ditch into a garden.
[Sira] [24]:[31] I said, “I’ll water my garden, and will drench my garden bed.” Listen, my stream became a river, and my river became a sea.
[Sira] [24]:[32] I’ll yet bring instruction to light as the morning, and will make these things clear from far away.
[Sira] [24]:[33] I’ll continue to pour out teaching like prophecy, and leave it to all generations.
[Sira] [24]:[34] See that I haven’t laboured for myself only, but for all those who diligently seek wisdom.

[Sira] [25]:[2] But my soul hates three sorts of people, and I’m greatly offended at their life: a poor man who’s arrogant, a rich man who’s a liar, and an old fool who’s an adulterer.
[Sira] [25]:[3] If you gathered nothing in your youth, how could you find anything in your old age?

[Sira] [27]:[16] He who reveals secrets destroys trust, and won’t find a close friend.

[Sira] [27]:[19] As a bird which you’ve released out of your hand, so you’ve let your neighbour go, and you won’t catch him again.
[Sira] [27]:[20] Don’t pursue him, for he’s gone far away, and has escaped like a gazelle out of the snare.
[Sira] [27]:[21] Because a wound may be bound up, and after abuse there may be reconciliation; but he who reveals secrets is without hope.
[Sira] [27]:[22] One who winks the eye contrives evil things; and those who know him will keep their distance.
[Sira] [27]:[23] When you’re present, he’ll speak sweetly, and will admire your words; but afterward he’ll twist his speech and set a trap in your words.

[Sira] [27]:[27] He who does evil things, they’ll roll back on him, and he won’t know where they came from.

[Sira] [28]:[1] He who takes vengeance will find vengeance from the master, and he’ll surely make his sins firm.

[Sira] [28]:[5] He himself, being flesh, nourishes anger. Who’ll make atonement for his sins?

[Sira] [28]:[11] A contention begun in haste kindles a fire; and hasty fighting sheds blood.
[Sira] [28]:[12] If you blow on a spark, it’ll burn; and if you spit on it, it’ll be quenched. Both of these come out of your mouth.

[Sira] [28]:[16] He who listens to it won’t find rest, nor will he live quietly.
[Sira] [28]:[17] The stroke of a whip makes a mark in the flesh, but the stroke of a tongue will break bones.
[Sira] [28]:[18] Many have fallen by the edge of the sword, yet not so many as those who’ve fallen because of the tongue.
[Sira] [28]:[19] Happy is he who’s sheltered from it, who hasn’t passed through its anger, who hasn’t drawn its yoke, and hasn’t been bound with its bands.

[Sira] [28]:[21] Its death is an evil death, and Haidais is better than it.

[Sira] [28]:[23] Those who forsake the master will fall into it. It’ll burn among them, and won’t be quenched. It’ll be sent against them like a lion. It’ll destroy them like a leopard.
[Sira] [28]:[24] As you hedge your possession about with thorns, and secure your silver and your gold,

[Sira] [28]:[26] Be careful not to slip with it, or you might fall before someone lying in wait.
[Sira] [29]:[1] He who shows mercy will lend to his neighbour. He who strengthens him with his hand keeps the commandments.

[Sira] [29]:[3] Confirm your word, and keep faith with him; and at all seasons you’ll find what you need.
[Sira] [29]:[4] Many have considered a loan to be a windfall, and have given trouble to those who helped them.

[Sira] [29]:[6] If he prevails, the creditor will hardly receive half; and he’ll count it as a windfall. If not, he’s deprived him of his money, and he has gotten him for an enemy without cause. He’ll pay him with cursing and railing. Instead of honour, he’ll pay him disgrace.
[Sira] [29]:[7] Many on account of fraud have turned away. They’re afraid of being defrauded for nothing.

[Sira] [29]:[23] With little or with much, be well satisfied.

[Sira] [30]:[4] His father dies, and is as though he hadn’t died; for he’s left one behind him like himself.
[Sira] [30]:[5] In his life, he saw his son and rejoiced. When he died, it was without regret.
[Sira] [30]:[6] He left behind him an avenger against his enemies, and one to repay kindness to his friends.

[Sira] [31]:[21] And if you’ve been forced to eat, rise up in the middle of it, and you’ll have rest.

[Sira] [36]:[18] The belly will eat any food, but one food is better than another.

[Sira] [36]:[20] A contrary heart will cause heaviness. A man of experience will pay him back.

[Sira] [36]:[22] The beauty of a woman cheers the face. A man desires nothing more.
[Sira] [36]:[23] If kindness and humility are on her tongue, her husband isn’t like other sons of men.
[Sira] [36]:[24] He who gets a wife gets his richest treasure, a help meet for him and a pillar of support.

[Sira] [36]:[26] Because who’d trust a nimble robber who skips from city to city? Even so, who’d trust a man who has no nest, and lodges wherever he finds himself at nightfall?
[Sira] [37]:[1] Every friend will say, “I also am his friend”; but there’s a friend which is only a friend in name.
[Sira] [37]:[2] Isn’t there a grief in it even to death when a companion and friend is turned into an enemy?
[Sira] [37]:[3] Oh wicked imagination, why were you formed to cover the dry land with deceit?
[Sira] [37]:[4] There’s a companion who rejoices in the gladness of a friend, but in time of affliction will be against him.
[Sira] [37]:[5] There’s a companion who for the belly’s sake labours with his friend, yet in the face of battle will carry his buckler.
[Sira] [37]:[6] Don’t forget a friend in your soul. Don’t be unmindful of him in your riches.
[Sira] [37]:[7] Every counsellor extols counsel, but some give counsel in their own interest.
[Sira] [37]:[8] Let your soul beware of a counsellor, and know in advance what’s his interest (for he’ll take counsel for himself), in case he casts the lot against you,
[Sira] [37]:[9] and say to you, “Your way is good.” Then he’ll stand near you, to see what’ll happen to you.
[Sira] [37]:[10] Don’t take counsel with one who looks askance at you. Hide your counsel from those who are jealous of you.
[Sira] [37]:[11] Don’t consult with a woman about her rival, with a coward about war, with a merchant about business, with a buyer about selling, with an envious man about thankfulness, with an unmerciful man about kindliness, with a sluggard about any kind of work, with a hireling in your house about finishing his work, or with an idle servant about much business. Pay no attention to these in any matter of counsel.
[Sira] [37]:[12] But rather be continually with a godly man, whom you know to be a keeper of the commandments, who in his soul is as your own soul, and who’ll grieve with you, if you fail.
[Sira] [37]:[13] Make the counsel of your heart stand, for there’s no one more faithful to you than it.
[Sira] [37]:[14] Because a man’s soul is sometimes inclined to inform him better than seven watchmen who sit on high on a watch-tower.
[Sira] [37]:[15] Above all this ask the Most High that he may direct your way in truth.
[Sira] [37]:[16] Let reason be the beginning of every work. Let counsel go before every action.
[Sira] [37]:[17] As a token of the changing of the heart,
[Sira] [37]:[18] four kinds of things rise up: good and evil, life and death. That which rules over them continually is the tongue.
[Sira] [37]:[19] There’s one who’s clever and the instructor of many, and yet is unprofitable to his own soul.
[Sira] [37]:[20] There’s one who’s subtle in words, and is hated. He’ll be destitute of all food.
[Sira] [37]:[21] Because grace wasn’t given to him from the master, because he’s deprived of all wisdom.
[Sira] [37]:[22] There’s one who’s wise to his own soul; and the fruits of his understanding are trustworthy in the mouth.
[Sira] [37]:[23] A wise man will instruct his own people. The fruits of his understanding are trustworthy.
[Sira] [37]:[24] A wise man will be filled with blessing. All those who see him will call him happy.
[Sira] [37]:[25] A man’s life is counted by days. The days of Yisrael (Israel) are innumerable.
[Sira] [37]:[26] The wise man will inherit confidence among his people. His name will live forever.
[Sira] [37]:[27] My son, test your soul in your life. See what’s evil for it, and don’t give in to it.
[Sira] [37]:[28] Because not all things are profitable for all men. Not every soul has pleasure in everything.
[Sira] [37]:[29] Don’t be insatiable in any luxury. Don’t be greedy in the things that you eat.
[Sira] [37]:[30] Because overeating brings disease, and gluttony causes nausea.
[Sira] [37]:[31] Because of gluttony, many have perished, but he who takes heed will prolong his life.
[Sira] [38]:[1] Honour a physician according to your need with the honours due to him, for truly the master has created him.
[Sira] [38]:[2] Because healing comes from the Most High, and he’ll receive a gift from the king.
[Sira] [38]:[3] The skill of the physician will lift up his head. He’ll be admired in the sight of great men.
[Sira] [38]:[4] The master created medicines out of the earth. A prudent man won’t despise them.
[Sira] [38]:[5] Wasn’t water made sweet with wood, that its power might be known?
[Sira] [38]:[6] He gave men skill that he might be glorified in his marvellous works.
[Sira] [38]:[7] With them he heals and takes away pain.
[Sira] [38]:[8] With these, the pharmacist makes a mixture. God’s works won’t be brought to an end. From him, peace is on the face of the earth.
[Sira] [38]:[9] My son, in your sickness don’t be negligent, but pray to the master, and he’ll heal you.
[Sira] [38]:[10] Put away wrong doing, and direct your hands in righteousness. Cleanse your heart from all sin.
[Sira] [38]:[11] Give a sweet savour and a memorial of fine flour, and pour oil on your offering, according to your means.
[Sira] [38]:[12] Then give place to the physician, for truly the master has created him. Don’t let him leave you, for you need him.
[Sira] [38]:[13] There’s a time when in recovery is in their hands.
[Sira] [38]:[14] Because they also will ask the master to prosper them in diagnosis and in healing for the maintenance of life.
[Sira] [38]:[15] He who sins before his Maker, let him fall into the hands of the physician.
[Sira] [38]:[16] My son, let your tears fall over the dead, and as one who suffers grievously, begin lamentation. Wind up his body with due honour. Don’t neglect his burial.
[Sira] [38]:[17] Make bitter weeping and make passionate wailing. Let your mourning be according to his merit, for one day or two, so that people won’t speak badly of you; and so be comforted for your sorrow.
[Sira] [38]:[18] Because from sorrow comes death. Sorrow of heart saps one’s strength.
[Sira] [38]:[19] In calamity, sorrow also remains. A poor man’s life is grievous to the heart.
[Sira] [38]:[20] Don’t give your heart to sorrow. Put it away, remembering the end.
[Sira] [38]:[21] Don’t forget it, for there’s no returning again. You do him no good, and you’d harm yourself.
[Sira] [38]:[22] Remember his end, for so also will yours be: yesterday for me, and today for you.
[Sira] [38]:[23] When the dead is at rest, let his remembrance rest. Be comforted for him when his spirit departs from him.
[Sira] [38]:[24] The wisdom of the scribe comes by the opportunity of leisure. He who has little business can become wise.
[Sira] [38]:[25] How could he become wise who holds the plough, who glories in the shaft of the goad, who drives oxen and is occupied in their labours, and who mostly talks about bulls?
[Sira] [38]:[26] He’ll set his heart on turning his furrows. His lack of sleep is to give his heifers their fodder.
[Sira] [38]:[27] So is every craftsman and master artisan who passes his time by night as by day, those who cut engravings of signets. His diligence is to make great variety. He sets his heart to preserve likeness in his portraiture, and is careful to finish his work.
[Sira] [38]:[28] So too is the smith sitting by the anvil and considering the unwrought iron. The smoke of the fire will waste his flesh. He toils in the heat of the furnace. The noise of the hammer deafens his ear. His eyes are on the pattern of the object. He’ll set his heart on perfecting his works. He’ll be careful to adorn them perfectly.
[Sira] [38]:[29] So is the potter sitting at his work and turning the wheel around with his feet, who’s always anxiously set at his work. He produces his handiwork in quantity.
[Sira] [38]:[30] He’ll fashion the clay with his arm and will bend its strength in front of his feet. He’ll apply his heart to finish the glazing. He’ll be careful to clean the kiln.
[Sira] [38]:[31] All these put their trust in their hands. Each becomes skilful in his own work.
[Sira] [38]:[32] Without these no city would be inhabited. Men wouldn’t reside as foreigners or walk up and down there.
[Sira] [38]:[33] They won’t be sought for in the council of the people. They won’t mount on high in the assembly. They won’t sit on the seat of the judge. They won’t understand the covenant of judgement. Neither will they declare instruction and judgement. They won’t be found where parables are.
[Sira] [38]:[34] But they’ll maintain the fabric of the age. Their prayer is in the handiwork of their craft.
[Sira] [39]:[1] Not so he who’s applied his soul and meditates in the Most High’s law. He’ll seek out the wisdom of all the ancients and will be occupied with prophecies.
[Sira] [39]:[2] He’ll keep the sayings of the men of renown and will enter in amidst the subtleties of parables.
[Sira] [39]:[3] He’ll seek out the hidden meaning of proverbs and be conversant in the dark sayings of parables.
[Sira] [39]:[4] He’ll serve among great men and appear before him who rules. He’ll travel through the land of foreign nations, for he’s learnt what’s good and evil among men.

[Sira] [39]:[18] At his command all his good pleasure is fulfilled. There’s no one who can hinder his salvation.
[Sira] [39]:[19] The works of all flesh are before him. It’s impossible to be hidden from his eyes.
[Sira] [39]:[20] He sees from eternal to eternal. There’s nothing too wonderful for him.
[Sira] [39]:[21] No one can say, “What’s this?” “Why is that?” for all things are created for their own uses.

[Sira] [39]:[27] All these things are for good to the godly, but for sinners, they’ll be turned into evils.
[Sira] [39]:[28] There are winds that are created for vengeance, and in their fury they lay on their scourges heavily. In the time of reckoning, they pour out their strength, and will appease the anger of him who made them.

[Sira] [39]:[30] wild animals’ teeth, scorpions, adders, and a sword punishing the ungodly to destruction.

[Sira] [40]:[1] Great travail is created for every man. A heavy yoke is on the sons of Adam, from the day of their coming forth from their mother’s womb, until the day for their burial in the mother of all things.

[Sira] [40]:[5] there’s anger, jealousy, trouble, unrest, fear of death, anger, and strife. In the time of rest on his bed, his night sleep changes his knowledge.
[Sira] [40]:[6] He gets little or no rest, and afterward in his sleep, as in a day of keeping watch, he’s troubled in the vision of his heart, as one who’s escaped from the front of battle.
[Sira] [40]:[7] In the very time of his deliverance, he awakens, and marvels that the fear is nothing.

[Sira] [40]:[27] The fear of the master is like a garden of blessing and covers a man more than any glory.

[Sira] [40]:[30] Begging will be sweet in the mouth of the shameless, but it kindles a fire in his belly.
[Sira] [41]:[1] Oh death, how bitter is the memory of you to a man who’s at peace in his possessions, to the man who has nothing to distract him and has prosperity in all things, and who still has strength to enjoy food!
[Sira] [41]:[2] Oh death, your sentence is acceptable to a man who’s needy and who fails in strength, who’s in extreme old age, is distracted about all things, is perverse, and has lost patience!
[Sira] [41]:[3] Don’t be afraid of the sentence of death. Remember those who’ve been before you and who come after. This is the sentence from the master over all flesh.
[Sira] [41]:[4] And why do you refuse when it’s the good pleasure of the Most High? Whether life lasts ten, or a hundred, or a thousand years, there’s no enquiry about life in Haidais.

[Sira] [41]:[24] So you’ll be ashamed of the right things and find favour in the sight of every man.
[Sira] [42]:[1] Don’t be ashamed of these things, and don’t sin to save face:
[Sira] [42]:[2] of the law of the Most High and his covenant, of judgement to do justice to the ungodly,
[Sira] [42]:[3] of reckoning with a partner and with travellers, of a gift from the inheritance of friends,

[Sira] [42]:[8] Don’t be ashamed to instruct the unwise and foolish, and one of extreme old age who contends with those who are young. So you’ll be well instructed indeed and approved in the sight of every living man.
[Sira] [42]:[9] A daughter is a secret cause of wakefulness to a father. He loses sleep worrying about her— in her youth, that she might pass the prime of her life; when she’s married, that she might be hated;
[Sira] [42]:[10] in her virginity, that she might be defiled and become pregnant in her father’s house; when she has a husband, that she might do wrong; and when she’s married, that she might be unable to have children.
[Sira] [42]:[11] Keep a strict watch over a headstrong daughter, or she might make you a laughingstock to your enemies, a byword in the city and notorious among the people, and shame you in public.
[Sira] [42]:[12] Don’t gaze at every beautiful body. Don’t sit among women.
[Sira] [42]:[13] Because from clothes comes a moth, and from a woman comes a woman’s wickedness.

[Sira] [42]:[18] He searches out the deep and the heart. He has understanding of their secrets. Because the Most High knows all knowledge. He sees the signs of the world.

[Sira] [42]:[20] No thought escapes him. There isn’t a word hidden from him.

[Sira] [43]:[1] The pride of the heavenly heights is the clear sky, the appearance of heaven, in the spectacle of its glory.
[Sira] [43]:[2] The sun, when it appears, bringing tidings as it rises, is a marvellous instrument, the Most High’s work.
[Sira] [43]:[3] At noon, it dries up the land. Who can stand against its burning heat?
[Sira] [43]:[4] A man tending a furnace is in burning heat, but the sun three times more, burning up the mountains, breathing out fiery vapours, and sending out bright beams, it blinds the eyes.
[Sira] [43]:[5] Great is the master who made it. At his word, he hastens on its course.
[Sira] [43]:[6] The moon marks the changing seasons, declares times, and is a sign for the world.
[Sira] [43]:[7] From the moon is the sign of feast days, a light that wanes when it completes its course.
[Sira] [43]:[8] The month is called after its name, increasing wonderfully in its changing— an instrument of the army on high, shining in the structure of heaven,
[Sira] [43]:[9] the beauty of heaven, the glory of the stars, an ornament giving light in the highest places of the master.
[Sira] [43]:[10] At the word of the Holy One, they’ll stand in due order. They won’t faint in their watches.
[Sira] [43]:[11] Look at the rainbow, and praise him who made it. It’s extremely beautiful in its brightness.
[Sira] [43]:[12] It encircles the sky with its glorious circle. The Most High’s hands have stretched it out.
[Sira] [43]:[13] By his commandment, he makes the snow fall and swiftly sends the lightnings of his judgement.
[Sira] [43]:[14] Therefore the storehouses are opened, and clouds fly out like birds.
[Sira] [43]:[15] By his mighty power, he makes the clouds strong and the hailstones are broken in pieces.
[Sira] [43]:[16] At his appearing, the mountains will be shaken. At his will, the south wind will blow.
[Sira] [43]:[17] The voice of his thunder rebukes the earth. So does the northern storm and the whirlwind. Like birds flying down, he sprinkles the snow. It falls down like the lighting of locusts.
[Sira] [43]:[18] The eye is dazzled at the beauty of its whiteness. The heart is amazed as it falls.
[Sira] [43]:[19] He also pours out frost on the earth like salt. When it’s freezes, it has points like thorns.
[Sira] [43]:[20] The cold north wind blows and ice freezes on the water. It settles on every pool of water. The water puts it on like it was a breastplate.
[Sira] [43]:[21] It’ll devour the mountains, burn up the wilderness, and consume the green grass like fire.
[Sira] [43]:[22] A mist coming speedily heals all things. A dew coming after heat brings cheerfulness.
[Sira] [43]:[23] By his counsel, he’s calmed the deep and planted islands in it.
[Sira] [43]:[24] Those who sail on the sea tell of its dangers. We marvel when we hear it with our ears.
[Sira] [43]:[25] There are also those strange and wondrous works in it— variety of all that has life and the huge creatures of the sea.
[Sira] [43]:[26] Because of him, his messengers succeed. By his word, all things hold together.
[Sira] [43]:[27] We may say many things, but couldn’t say enough. The summary of our words is, “He’s everything!”
[Sira] [43]:[28] How could we have strength to glorify him? Because he’s himself the greater than all his works.
[Sira] [43]:[29] The master is awesome and very great! His power is marvellous!
[Sira] [43]:[30] Glorify the master and exalt him as much as you can! Because even yet, he’ll surpass that. When you exalt him, summon your full strength. Don’t be weary, because you can’t praise him enough.
[Sira] [43]:[31] Who’s seen him, that he may describe him? Who can magnify him as he is?

[Sira] [51]:[12] You saved me from destruction and delivered me from the evil time. Therefore I’ll give thanks and praise to you, and bless the master’s name.
[Sira] [51]:[13] When I was yet young, before I went abroad, I sought wisdom openly in my prayer.
[Sira] [51]:[14] Before the temple I asked for her. I’ll seek her out even to the end.
[Sira] [51]:[15] From the first flower to the ripening grape my heart delighted in her. My foot walked in uprightness. From my youth I followed her steps.
[Sira] [51]:[16] I inclined my ear a little, and received her, and found for myself much instruction.
[Sira] [51]:[17] I profited in her. I’ll give glory to him who gives me wisdom.
[Sira] [51]:[18] Because I determined to practise her. I was zealous for that which is good. I’ll never be put to shame.
[Sira] [51]:[19] My soul has wrestled with her. In my conduct I was exact. I spread out my hands to the heaven above, and bewailed my ignorances of her.
[Sira] [51]:[20] I directed my soul to her. In purity I found her. I got myself a heart joined with her from the beginning. Therefore I won’t be forsaken.
[Sira] [51]:[21] My belly also was troubled to seek her. Therefore I’ve gained a good possession.
[Sira] [51]:[22] The master gave me a tongue for my reward. I’ll praise him with it.
[Sira] [51]:[23] Draw near to me, all you who are uneducated, and live in the house of instruction.
[Sira] [51]:[24] Why therefore are you all lacking in these things, and your souls are very thirsty?
[Sira] [51]:[25] I opened my mouth and spoke, “Get her for yourselves without money.”
[Sira] [51]:[26] Put your neck under the yoke, and let your soul receive instruction. She’s near to find.
[Sira] [51]:[27] See with your eyes how that I laboured just a little and found for myself much rest.
[Sira] [51]:[28] Get instruction with a great sum of silver, and gain much gold by her.
[Sira] [51]:[29] May your soul rejoice in his mercy, and may you all not be put to shame in praising him.
[Sira] [51]:[30] Work your work before the time comes, and in his time he’ll give you your reward.
[Baruk] [1]:[1] These are the words of the book which Baruk the son of Neriyah, the son of Mahseyah, the son of Tsidkiyah (Zedekiah), the son of Hasadyah, the son of Hilkiyah, wrote in Bavel (Babylon),
[Baruk] [1]:[2] in the fifth year, in the seventh day of the month, at the time when the Kasdim (Chaldeans) took Yerushalem (Jerusalem) and burnt it with fire.
[Baruk] [1]:[3] Baruk read the words of this book in the hearing of Yekonias the son of Yehoyakim king of Yehudah (Judah), and in the hearing of all the people who came to hear the book,
[Baruk] [1]:[4] and in the hearing of the mighty men, and of the kings’ sons, and in the hearing of the elders, and in the hearing of all the people, from the least to the greatest, even of all those who lived at Bavel by the river Sud.
[Baruk] [1]:[5] Then they wept, fasted, and prayed before the master.
[Baruk] [1]:[6] They also made a collection of money according to every man’s ability;
[Baruk] [1]:[7] and they sent it to Yerushalem to Yehoyakim the high priest, the son of Hilkiyah, the son of Shalum, and to the priests and to all the people who were found with him at Yerushalem,
[Baruk] [1]:[8] at the same time when he took the vessels of the master’s house, that’d been carried out of the temple, to return them into the land of Yehudah, the tenth day of Sivan—silver vessels which Tsidkiyah the son of Yoshiyah (Josiah) king of Yehudah had made,
[Baruk] [1]:[9] after Nevukadnetsar (Nebuchadnezzar) king of Bavel had carried away Yekonias, the princes, the captives, the mighty men, and the people of the land from Yerushalem, and brought them to Bavel.
[Baruk] [1]:[10] And they said: Listen, we’ve sent you money; therefore buy with the money burnt offerings, sin offerings, and incense, and prepare an oblation, and offer on the altar of the master our god;
[Baruk] [1]:[11] and pray for the life of Nevukadnetsar king of Bavel, and for the life of Belshatsar (Belshazzar) his son, that their days may be as the days of heaven above the earth.
[Baruk] [1]:[12] The master will give us strength and light to our eyes. We’ll live under the shadow of Nevukadnetsar king of Bavel and under the shadow of Belshatsar his son, and we’ll serve them many days, and find favour in their sight.
[Baruk] [1]:[13] Pray for us also to the master our god, for we’ve sinned against the master our god. To this day the anger of the master and his indignation isn’t turned from us.
[Baruk] [1]:[14] Read this book which we’ve sent to you, to make confession in the master’s house on the day of the feast and on the days of the solemn assembly.
[Baruk] [1]:[15] Say: To the master our god belongs righteousness, but to us confusion of face, as at this day—to the men of Yehudah, to the inhabitants of Yerushalem,
[Baruk] [1]:[16] to our kings, to our princes, to our priests, to our prophets, and to our fathers,
[Baruk] [1]:[17] because we’ve sinned before the master.
[Baruk] [1]:[18] We’ve disobeyed him and haven’t listened to the voice of the master our god, to walk in the master’s commandments that he’s set before us.
[Baruk] [1]:[19] Since the day that the master brought our fathers out of the land of Mitsrayim (Egypt) to this present day, we’ve been disobedient to the master our god, and we’ve been negligent in not listening to his voice.
[Baruk] [1]:[20] Therefore the deadly diseases have clung to us, along with the curse which the master declared through Mosheh (Moses) his servant in the day that he brought our fathers out of the land of Mitsrayim to give us a land that flows with milk and honey, as at this day.
[Baruk] [1]:[21] Nevertheless we didn’t listen to the voice of the master our god, according to all the words of the prophets whom he sent to us,
[Baruk] [1]:[22] but we each walked in the imagination of his own wicked heart, to serve strange gods and to do what is evil in the sight of the master our god.
[Baruk] [2]:[1] Therefore the master has made good his word which he pronounced against us, and against our judges who judged Yisrael (Israel), and against our kings, and against our princes, and against the men of Yisrael and Yehudah (Judah),
[Baruk] [2]:[2] to bring terrible deadly diseases onto us such as never happened before under the whole heaven, as it happened in Yerushalem (Jerusalem), according to the things that are written in Mosheh’s law,
[Baruk] [2]:[3] that we should each eat the flesh of our own son, and each eat the flesh of our own daughter.
[Baruk] [2]:[4] Moreover he’s given them to be in subjection to all the kingdoms that are around us, to be a reproach and a desolation among all the people around us, where the master has scattered them.
[Baruk] [2]:[5] Thus they were thrown down and not exalted, because we sinned against the master our god in not listening to his voice.
[Baruk] [2]:[6] To the master our god belongs righteousness, but to us and to our fathers confusion of face, as at this day.
[Baruk] [2]:[7] All these deadly diseases have come onto us which the master has pronounced against us.
[Baruk] [2]:[8] Yet we haven’t asked for the favour of the master by everyone turning from the thoughts of his wicked heart.
[Baruk] [2]:[9] Therefore the master has kept watch over the deadly diseases. The master has brought them onto us, because the master is righteous in all his works which he’s commanded us.
[Baruk] [2]:[10] Yet we haven’t listened to his voice, to walk in the master’s commandments that he’s set before us.
[Baruk] [2]:[11] And now, Oh master, you God of Yisrael (Israel) who’ve brought your people out of the land of Mitsrayim (Egypt) with a mighty hand, with signs, with wonders, with great power, and with a high arm, and have gotten yourself a name, as at this day:
[Baruk] [2]:[12] Oh master our god, we’ve sinned. We’ve been ungodly. We’ve done wrong in all your ordinances.
[Baruk] [2]:[13] Let your anger turn from us, for we’re but a few left among the heathen where you’ve scattered us.
[Baruk] [2]:[14] Hear our prayer, Oh master, and our petition, and deliver us for your own sake. Give us favour in the sight of those who’ve led us away captive,
[Baruk] [2]:[15] that all the earth may know that you’re the master our god, because Yisrael and his posterity is called by your name.
[Baruk] [2]:[16] Oh master, look down from your holy house and consider us. Incline your ear, Oh master, and hear.
[Baruk] [2]:[17] Open your eyes, and see; for the dead that are in Haidais, whose breath is taken from their bodies, will give to the master neither glory nor righteousness;
[Baruk] [2]:[18] but the soul who’s greatly vexed, who goes stooping and feeble, and the eyes that fail, and the hungry soul, will declare your glory and righteousness, Oh master.
[Baruk] [2]:[19] Because we don’t present our supplication before you, Oh master our god, for the righteousness of our fathers and of our kings.
[Baruk] [2]:[20] Because you’ve sent your anger and your indignation onto us, as you’ve spoken by your servants the prophets, saying,
[Baruk] [2]:[21] “The master says, ‘Bow your shoulders to serve the king of Bavel (Babylon), and remain in the land that I gave to your fathers.
[Baruk] [2]:[22] But if you won’t hear the master’s voice to serve the king of Bavel,
[Baruk] [2]:[23] I’ll cause to cease out of the cities of Yehudah (Judah) and from the region near Yerushalem (Jerusalem) the voice of mirth, the voice of gladness, voice of the bridegroom, and the voice of the bride. The whole land will be desolate without inhabitant.’ ”
[Baruk] [2]:[24] But we wouldn’t listen to your voice, to serve the king of Bavel. Therefore you’ve made good your words that you spoke by your servants the prophets, that the bones of our kings and the bones of our fathers would be taken out of their places.
[Baruk] [2]:[25] Listen, they’re thrown out to the heat by day and to the frost by night. They died in great miseries by famine, by sword, and by pestilence.
[Baruk] [2]:[26] You’ve made the house that’s called by your name as it’s today because of the wickedness of the house of Yisrael (Israel) and the house of Yehudah.
[Baruk] [2]:[27] Yet, Oh master our god, you have dealt with us after all your kindness and according to all your great mercy,
[Baruk] [2]:[28] as you spoke by your servant Mosheh (Moses) in the day when you commanded him to write your law in the presence of the children of Yisrael, saying,
[Baruk] [2]:[29] “If you won’t hear my voice, surely this very great multitude will be turned into a small number among the nations where I’ll scatter them.
[Baruk] [2]:[30] Because I know that they won’t listen to me, because they’re a stiff-necked people; but in the land of their captivity they’ll take it to heart,
[Baruk] [2]:[31] and will know that I’m the master their god. I’ll give them a heart and ears to hear.
[Baruk] [2]:[32] Then they’ll praise me in the land of their captivity, and think about my name,
[Baruk] [2]:[33] and will return from their stiff neck and from their wicked actions; because they’ll remember the way of their fathers who sinned before the master.
[Baruk] [2]:[34] I’ll bring them again into the land which I promised to their fathers, to Avraham, to Yitshak (Isaac), and to Ya’akov (Jacob), and they’ll rule over it. I’ll increase them, and they won’t be diminished.
[Baruk] [2]:[35] And I’ll make an eternal covenant with them to be their god, and they’ll be my people. I’ll no more remove my people Yisrael out of the land that I’ve given them.”
[Baruk] [3]:[1] Oh master Almighty, you God of Yisrael, the soul in anguish and the troubled spirit cries to you.
[Baruk] [3]:[2] Hear, Oh master, and have mercy; for you’re a merciful God. Yes, have mercy on us, because we’ve sinned before you.
[Baruk] [3]:[3] Because you’re enthroned forever, and we keep perishing.
[Baruk] [3]:[4] Oh master Almighty, you God of Yisrael, hear now the prayer of the dead Israelis, and of the children of those who were sinners before you, who didn’t listen to the voice of you their god; because of this, these deadly diseases cling to us.
[Baruk] [3]:[5] Don’t remember the iniquities of our fathers, but remember your power and your name at this time.
[Baruk] [3]:[6] Because you’re the master our god, and we’ll praise you, Oh master.
[Baruk] [3]:[7] Because this cause, you’ve put your fear in our hearts, to the intent that we should call on your name. We’ll praise you in our captivity, for we’ve called to mind all the iniquity of our fathers who sinned before you.
[Baruk] [3]:[8] Listen, we’re yet this day in our captivity where you’ve scattered us, for a reproach and a curse, and to be subject to penalty according to all the iniquities of our fathers who departed from the master our god.
[Baruk] [3]:[9] Hear, Oh Yisrael, the commandments of life! Give ear to understand wisdom!
[Baruk] [3]:[10] How is it, Oh Yisrael, that you’re in your enemies’ land, that you’ve become old in a strange country, that you’re defiled with the dead,
[Baruk] [3]:[11] that you’re counted with those who are in Haidais?
[Baruk] [3]:[12] You’ve forsaken the fountain of wisdom.
[Baruk] [3]:[13] If you’d walked in the way of God, you’d have dwelled in peace forever.
[Baruk] [3]:[14] Learn where there’s wisdom, where there’s strength, and where there’s understanding, that you may also know where there’s length of days and life, where there’s the light of the eyes and peace.
[Baruk] [3]:[15] Who’s found out her place? Who’s come into her treasuries?
[Baruk] [3]:[16] Where are the princes of the heathen, and those who ruled the wild animals that are on the earth,
[Baruk] [3]:[17] those who had their pastime with the fowls of the air, and those who hoarded up silver and gold, in which people trust, and of their getting there’s no end?
[Baruk] [3]:[18] Because those who diligently sought silver, and were so anxious, and whose works are past finding out,
[Baruk] [3]:[19] they’ve vanished and gone down to Haidais, and others have come up in their place.
[Baruk] [3]:[20] Younger men have seen the light and lived on the earth, but they haven’t known the way of knowledge,
[Baruk] [3]:[21] nor understood its paths. Their children haven’t embraced it. They’re far off from their way.
[Baruk] [3]:[22] It hasn’t been heard of in Kena’an (Canaan), neither has it been seen in Teyman.
[Baruk] [3]:[23] The sons also of Hagar who seek understanding, which are in the land, the merchants of Merran and Teyman, and the authors of fables, and the searchers out of understanding—none of these have known the way of wisdom or remembered her paths.
[Baruk] [3]:[24] Oh Yisrael (Israel), how great is God’s house! How large is the place of his possession!
[Baruk] [3]:[25] It’s great and has no end. It’s high and unmeasurable.
[Baruk] [3]:[26] Giants were born that were famous of old, great of stature, and expert in war.
[Baruk] [3]:[27] God didn’t choose these, nor did he give the way of knowledge to them,
[Baruk] [3]:[28] so they perished, because they had no wisdom. They perished through their own foolishness.
[Baruk] [3]:[29] Who’s gone up into heaven, taken her, and brought her down from the clouds?
[Baruk] [3]:[30] Who’s gone over the sea, found her, and will bring her for choice gold?
[Baruk] [3]:[31] There’s no one who knows her way, nor any who comprehend her path.
[Baruk] [3]:[32] But he that knows all things knows her, he found her out with his understanding. He who prepared the earth for all time has filled it with four-footed animals.
[Baruk] [3]:[33] It’s he who sends forth the light, and it goes. He called it, and it obeyed him with fear.
[Baruk] [3]:[34] The stars shone in their watches, and were glad. When he called them, they said, “Here we are.” They shone with gladness to him who made them.
[Baruk] [3]:[35] This is our god. No other can be compared to him.
[Baruk] [3]:[36] He’s found out all the way of knowledge, and has given it to Ya’akov (Jacob) his servant and to Yisrael (Israel) who’s loved by him.
[Baruk] [3]:[37] Afterward she appeared on earth, and lived with men.
[Baruk] [4]:[1] This is the book of God’s commandments and the law that endures forever. All those who hold it fast will live, but those who leave it’ll die.
[Baruk] [4]:[2] Turn, Oh Ya’akov, and take hold of it. Walk towards the shining of its light.
