[1 Maccabees] [7]:[47] The Yehudim (Jews) took the spoils and the booty, and they cut off Nikanor’s head and his right hand, which he’d stretched out so arrogantly, and brought them, and hung them up beside Yerushalem.
[1 Maccabees] [7]:[48] The people were extremely glad, and they kept that day as a day of great gladness.
[1 Maccabees] [7]:[49] They ordained to keep this day year by year on the thirteenth day of Adar.
[1 Maccabees] [7]:[50] So the land of Yehudah had rest a few days.
[1 Maccabees] [8]:[1] Yehudah heard of the fame of the Romaios, that they’re valiant men, and have pleasure in all who join themselves to them, and make friends with all who come to them,
[1 Maccabees] [8]:[2] and that they’re valiant men. They told him of their wars and exploits which they do among the Gauls, and how they conquered them, and forced them to pay tribute;
[1 Maccabees] [8]:[3] and what things they did in the land of Spania, that they might take control of the silver and gold mines which were there;
[1 Maccabees] [8]:[4] and how by their policy and persistence they conquered all the place (and the place was extremely far from them), and the kings who came against them from the uttermost part of the earth, until they’d defeated them, and struck them severely; and how the rest give them tribute year by year.
[1 Maccabees] [8]:[5] Filippos (Philip), and Perseus, king of Kitim, and those who lifted up themselves against them, they defeated in battle, and conquered them.
[1 Maccabees] [8]:[6] Antiokos (Antiochus) also, the great king of Asia, came against them to battle, having one hundred and twenty elephants, with cavalry, chariots, and a very great army, and he was defeated by them.
[1 Maccabees] [8]:[7] They took him alive, and decreed that both he and those who reigned after him should give them a great tribute, and should give hostages, and a parcel of land from the best of their provinces:
[1 Maccabees] [8]:[8] the countries of Hodu, Maday (Media), and Ludia. They took them from him, and gave them to King Eumenes.
[1 Maccabees] [8]:[9] Yehudah heard how the Hellains (Greeks) planned to come and destroy them,
[1 Maccabees] [8]:[10] but this became known to them, and they sent against them a general who fought against them, and many of them fell down wounded to death, and they made captive their wives and their children, and plundered them, and conquered their land, and pulled down their strongholds, and plundered them, and brought them into bondage to this day.
[1 Maccabees] [8]:[11] The remaining kingdoms and islands, as many as rose up against them at any time, they destroyed and made them to be their servants;
[1 Maccabees] [8]:[12] but with their friends and those who relied on them they stayed friends. They conquered the kingdoms that were near and those that were far off, and all that heard of their fame were afraid of them.
[1 Maccabees] [8]:[13] What’s more, whoever they desired to help and to make kings, these they make kings; and whoever they desired, they depose. They’re exalted greatly.
[1 Maccabees] [8]:[14] Because all this, none of them ever put on a crown, neither did they clothe themselves with purple, as a display of grandeur.
[1 Maccabees] [8]:[15] Yehudah heard how they’d made for themselves a senate house, and day by day, three hundred and twenty men sat in council, consulting always for the people, to the end they might be well governed,
[1 Maccabees] [8]:[16] and how they commit their government to one man year by year, that he should rule over them, and control all their country, and all are obedient to that one, and there’s neither envy nor emulation among them.
[1 Maccabees] [8]:[17] So Yehudah chose Eupolemos the son of Yohan (John), the son of Hakots, and Yason the son of Eleazar, and sent them to Romai, to establish friendship and alliance with them,
[1 Maccabees] [8]:[18] and that they should free the yoke from themselves; for they saw that the kingdom of the Hellains (Greeks) kept Yisrael (Israel) in bondage.
[1 Maccabees] [8]:[19] Then they went to Romai, a very long journey, and they entered into the senate house, and said,
[1 Maccabees] [8]:[20] “Yehudah, who’s also called Makabi (Maccabaeus), and his kindred, and the people of the Yehudim (Jews), have sent us to you, to make an alliance and peace with you, and that we might be registered as your allies and friends.”
[1 Maccabees] [8]:[21] This thing was pleasing to them.
[1 Maccabees] [8]:[22] This is the copy of the writing which they wrote back again on tables of brass, and sent to Yerushalem (Jerusalem), that it might be with them there for a memorial of peace and alliance:
[1 Maccabees] [8]:[23] “Good success be to the Romaios, and to the nation of the Yehudim, by sea and by land forever. May the sword and the enemy be far from them.
[1 Maccabees] [8]:[24] But if war arises for Romai first, or any of their allies in all their dominion,
[1 Maccabees] [8]:[25] the nation of the Yehudim must help them as allies, as the occasion will indicate to them, with all their heart.
[1 Maccabees] [8]:[26] To those who make war on them, they mustn’t give supplies, food, weapons, money, or ships, as it’s seemed good to Romai, and they must keep their ordinances without taking anything in return.
[1 Maccabees] [8]:[27] In the same way, moreover, if war comes first on the nation of the Yehudim, the Romaios must willingly help them as allies, as the occasion will indicate to them;
[1 Maccabees] [8]:[28] and to those who are fighting with them, there mustn’t be given food, weapons, money, or ships, as it’s seemed good to Romai. They must keep these ordinances, and that without deceit.
[1 Maccabees] [8]:[29] According to these terms, the Romaios made a treaty with the Jewish people.
[1 Maccabees] [8]:[30] But if in the future the one party and the other decide to add or diminish anything, they may do so by mutual agreement, and whatever they add or take away will be ratified.
[1 Maccabees] [8]:[31] About the evils which King Demetrios is doing to them, we’ve written to him, saying, ‘Why have you made your yoke heavy on our friends and allies the Yehudim?
[1 Maccabees] [8]:[32] If therefore they plead any more against you, we’ll do them justice, and fight with you on sea and on land.’ ”
[1 Maccabees] [9]:[1] Demetrios heard that Nikanor had fallen with his forces in battle, and he sent Bakides and Alkimos again into the land of Yehudah (Judah) a second time, and the right wing of his army with them.
[1 Maccabees] [9]:[2] They went by the way that leads to Gilgal, and encamped against Mesaloth, which is in Arbela, and took possession of it, and killed many people.
[1 Maccabees] [9]:[3] The first month of the one hundred and fifty-second year, they encamped against Yerushalem (Jerusalem).
[1 Maccabees] [9]:[4] Then they marched away and went to Beroia with twenty thousand infantry and two thousand cavalry.
[1 Maccabees] [9]:[5] Yehudah was encamped at Elasa with three thousand chosen men.
[1 Maccabees] [9]:[6] They saw the multitude of the forces, that they were many, and they were terrified. Many slipped away out of the army. There weren’t left of them more than eight hundred men.
[1 Maccabees] [9]:[7] Yehudah saw that his army slipped away and that the battle pressed on him, and he was very troubled in spirit, because he had no time to gather them together, and he became faint.
[1 Maccabees] [9]:[8] He said to those who were left, “Let’s arise and go up against our adversaries, if perhaps we may be able to fight with them.”
[1 Maccabees] [9]:[9] They tried to dissuade him, saying, “There’s no way we’re able; but let’s rather save our lives now. Let’s return again with our kindred, and fight against them; but we’re too few.”
[1 Maccabees] [9]:[10] Yehudah said, “Let it not be so that I should do this thing, to flee from them. If our time has come, let’s die in a manly way for our kindred’s sake, and not leave a cause of reproach against our honour.”
[1 Maccabees] [9]:[11] The army marched out from the camp, and stood to encounter them. The cavalry was divided into two companies, and the slingers and the archers went before the army, and all the mighty men that fought in the front of the battle.
[1 Maccabees] [9]:[12] Bakides was in the right wing. The phalanx advanced on the two parts, and they blew with their trumpets.
[1 Maccabees] [9]:[13] The men by Yehudah’ side sounded with their trumpets, and the earth shook with the shout of the armies, and the battle was joined, and continued from morning until evening.
[1 Maccabees] [9]:[14] Yehudah saw that Bakides and the strength of his army were on the right side, and all that were brave in heart went with him,
[1 Maccabees] [9]:[15] and the right wing was defeated by them, and he pursued after them to the mount Azotos.
[1 Maccabees] [9]:[16] Those who were on the left wing saw that the right wing was defeated, and they turned and followed in the footsteps of Yehudah and of those who were with him.
[1 Maccabees] [9]:[17] The battle became desperate, and many on both sides fell wounded to death.
[1 Maccabees] [9]:[18] Yehudah fell, and the rest fled.
[1 Maccabees] [9]:[19] Yonatan (Jonathan) and Shim’on (Simon) took Yehudah their brother, and buried him in the tomb of his ancestors at Modi’in.
[1 Maccabees] [9]:[20] They wept for him. All Yisrael made great lamentation for him, and mourned many days, and said,
[1 Maccabees] [9]:[21] “How is the mighty fallen, the saviour of Yisrael!”
[1 Maccabees] [9]:[22] The rest of the acts of Yehudah, and his wars, and the valiant actions which he did, and his greatness, aren’t written; for they were very many.
[1 Maccabees] [9]:[23] After Yehudah’s death, the lawless emerged within all the borders of Yisrael (Israel). All those who did iniquity rose up.
[1 Maccabees] [9]:[24] In those days there was a very great famine, and the country went over to their side.
[1 Maccabees] [9]:[25] Bakides chose the ungodly men and made them rulers of the country.
[1 Maccabees] [9]:[26] They enquired and searched for Yehudah’s friends, and brought them to Bakides, and he took vengeance on them and used them despitefully.
[1 Maccabees] [9]:[27] There was great suffering in Yisrael, such as wasn’t since the time prophets stopped appearing to them.
[1 Maccabees] [9]:[28] All Yehudah’s friends were gathered together, and they said to Yonatan (Jonathan),
[1 Maccabees] [9]:[29] “Since your brother Yehudah has died, we have no man like him to go out against our enemies and Bakides, and among those of our nation who hate us.
[1 Maccabees] [9]:[30] Now therefore we’ve chosen you this day to be our prince and leader in his place, that you may fight our battles.”
[1 Maccabees] [9]:[31] So Yonatan took the governance on him at that time, and rose up in the place of his brother Yehudah.
[1 Maccabees] [9]:[32] When Bakides found out, he tried to kill him.
[1 Maccabees] [9]:[33] Yonatan, and Shim’on (Simon) his brother, and all who were with him, knew it; and they fled into the wilderness of Tekoa, and encamped by the water of the pool of Asphar.
[1 Maccabees] [9]:[34] Bakides found this out on the Sabbath day, and came—he and all his army—over the Yarden (Jordan).
[1 Maccabees] [9]:[35] Yonatan sent his brother, a leader of the multitude, and implored his friends the Nabataeans, that they might store their baggage, which was much, with them.
[1 Maccabees] [9]:[36] The children of Jambri came out of Meydeva, and seized Yohan (John) and all that he had, and went their way with it.
[1 Maccabees] [9]:[37] But after these things, they brought word to Yonatan and Shim’on his brother that the children of Jambri were celebrating a great wedding, and were bringing the bride, a daughter of one of the great nobles of Kena’an (Canaan), from Nadabath with a large escort.
[1 Maccabees] [9]:[38] They remembered Yohan their brother, and went up, and hid themselves under the cover of the mountain.
[1 Maccabees] [9]:[39] They lifted up their eyes and looked, and saw a great procession with much baggage. The bridegroom came out with his friends and his kindred to meet them with timbrels, musicians, and many weapons.
[1 Maccabees] [9]:[40] They rose up against them from their ambush and killed them, and many fell wounded to death. The remnant fled into the mountain, and the Yehudim (Jews) took all their spoils.
[1 Maccabees] [9]:[41] So the wedding was turned into mourning, and the voice of their musicians into lamentation.
[1 Maccabees] [9]:[42] They avenged fully their brother’s blood, and turned back to the marshes of the Yarden.
[1 Maccabees] [9]:[43] Bakides heard it, and he came on the Sabbath day to the banks of Yarden (Jordan) with a great army.
[1 Maccabees] [9]:[44] Yonatan said to his company, “Let’s stand up now and fight for our lives, for things are different today than they were yesterday and the day before.
[1 Maccabees] [9]:[45] Because the battle is before us and behind us. Moreover the water of the Yarden is on this side and on that side, and marsh and thicket. There’s no place to escape.
[1 Maccabees] [9]:[46] Now therefore cry to heaven, that you may be delivered out of your enemies’ hand.”
[1 Maccabees] [9]:[47] So the battle was joined, and Yonatan stretched out his hand to strike Bakides, and he turned away back from him.
[1 Maccabees] [9]:[48] Yonatan and those who were with him leapt into the Yarden, and swam over to the other side. The enemy didn’t pass over the Yarden against them.
[1 Maccabees] [9]:[49] About a thousand men of Bakides’ company fell that day;
[1 Maccabees] [9]:[50] and he returned to Yerushalem (Jerusalem). They built strong cities in Yehudah (Judea), the stronghold that was in Yeriho (Jericho), and Emmaous, Beyt-Horon, Beyt-El (Bethel), Timnah, Pireaton, and Tephon, with high walls and gates and bars.
[1 Maccabees] [9]:[51] He set garrisons in them to harass Yisrael (Israel).
[1 Maccabees] [9]:[52] He fortified the city Beyt-Tsur, Gezer, and the citadel, and put troops and stores of food in them.
[1 Maccabees] [9]:[53] He took the sons of the chief men of the country for hostages, and put them under guard in the citadel at Yerushalem.
[1 Maccabees] [9]:[54] And in the one hundred and fifty-third year, in the second month, Alkimos gave orders to pull down the wall of the inner courtyard of the sanctuary. He also pulled down the works of the prophets.
[1 Maccabees] [9]:[55] He began to pull down. At that time was Alkimos stricken, and his works were hindered; and his mouth was stopped, and he was taken with a palsy, and he could no more speak anything and give orders about his house.
[1 Maccabees] [9]:[56] Alkimos died at that time with great torment.
[1 Maccabees] [9]:[57] Bakides saw that Alkimos was dead, and he returned to the king. Then the land of Yehudah had rest for two years.
[1 Maccabees] [9]:[58] Then all the lawless men took counsel, saying, “Listen, Yonatan (Jonathan) and his men are dwelling at ease and in security. Now therefore we’ll bring Bakides, and he’ll capture them all in one night.
[1 Maccabees] [9]:[59] They went and consulted with him.
[1 Maccabees] [9]:[60] He marched out and came with a great army, and sent letters secretly to all his allies who were in Yehudah, that they should seize Yonatan and those who were with him; but they couldn’t, because their plan was known to them.
[1 Maccabees] [9]:[61] Yonatan’s men seized about fifty of the men of the country who were authors of the wickedness, and he killed them.
[1 Maccabees] [9]:[62] Yonatan, Shim’on, and those who were with him, went away to Beyt-Basi, which is in the wilderness, and he built up that which had been pulled down, and they made it strong.
[1 Maccabees] [9]:[63] Bakides found out about it, and he gathered together all his multitude, and sent orders to those who were of Yehudah.
[1 Maccabees] [9]:[64] He went and encamped against Beyt-Basi and fought against it many days, and made engines of war.
[1 Maccabees] [9]:[65] Yonatan left his brother Shim’on (Simon) in the city, and went out into the country, and he went with a few men.
[1 Maccabees] [9]:[66] He struck Odomera and his kindred, and the children of Phasiron in their tents.
[1 Maccabees] [9]:[67] They began to strike them, and to go up with their forces. Then Shim’on and those who were with him went out of the city, and set the engines of war on fire,
[1 Maccabees] [9]:[68] and fought against Bakides, and he was defeated by them. They afflicted him severely; for his counsel and expedition was in vain.
[1 Maccabees] [9]:[69] They were very angry with the lawless men who gave him counsel to come into the country, and they killed many of them. Then he decided to depart into his own land.
[1 Maccabees] [9]:[70] Yonatan learnt of this and sent ambassadors to him, to the end that they should make peace with him, and that he should restore to them the captives.
[1 Maccabees] [9]:[71] He accepted the thing, and did according to his words, and swore to him that he wouldn’t seek his harm all the days of his life.
[1 Maccabees] [9]:[72] He restored to him the captives which he’d taken before out of the land of Yehudah (Judah), and he returned and departed into his own land, and didn’t come any more into their borders.
[1 Maccabees] [9]:[73] Thus the sword ceased from Yisrael (Israel). Yonatan lived at Mikmas. Yonatan began to judge the people; and he destroyed the ungodly out of Yisrael.
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[1] In the one hundred sixtieth year, Alexandros (Alexander) Epifanes (Epiphanes), the son of Antiokos (Antiochus), went up and took possession of Ptolemais. They received him, and he reigned there.
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[2] King Demetrios heard about this, and he gathered together very great forces, and went out to meet him in battle.
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[3] Demetrios sent a letter to Yonatan with words of peace, so as to honour him.
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[4] Because he said, “Let’s go beforehand to make peace with them, before he makes peace with Alexandros against us;
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[5] for he’ll remember all the evils that we’ve done against him, and to his kindred and to his nation.”
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[6] So he gave him authority to gather together forces, and to provide weapons, and that he should be his ally. He also commanded that they should release the hostages that were in the citadel to him.
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[7] Yonatan came to Yerushalem (Jerusalem), and read the letter in the hearing of all the people, and of those who were in the citadel.
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[8] They were very afraid when they heard that the king had given him authority to gather together an army.
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[9] Those in the citadel released the hostages to Yonatan, and he restored them to their parents.
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[10] Yonatan lived in Yerushalem and began to build and renew the city.
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[11] He commanded those who did the work to build the walls and encircle Mt. Tsiyon (Zion) with square stones for defence; and they did so.
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[12] The foreigners who were in the strongholds which Bakides had built fled away.
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[13] Each man left his place and departed into his own land.
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[14] Only at Beyt-Tsur, there were left some of those who’d forsaken the law and the commandments, for it was a place of refuge to them.
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[15] King Alexandros (Alexander) heard all the promises which Demetrios had sent to Yonatan. They told him of the battles and the valiant actions which he and his kindred had done, and of the troubles which they’d endured.
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[16] So he said, “Could we find another man like him? Now we’ll make him our friend and ally.”
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[17] He wrote a letter and sent it to him, in these words, saying,
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[18] “King Alexandros to his brother Yonatan, greetings.
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[19] We’ve heard of you, that you’re a mighty man of valour, and worthy to be our friend.
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[20] Now we’ve appointed you this day to be high priest of your nation, and to be called the king’s friend, and to take our side, and to keep friendship with us.” He also sent to him a purple robe and a golden crown.
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[21] And Yonatan put on the holy clothes in the seventh month of the one hundred sixtieth year, at the feast of tabernacles; and he gathered together forces and provided weapons in abundance.
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[22] When Demetrios heard these things, he was grieved and said,
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[23] “What’s this that we’ve done, that Alexandros has gotten ahead of us in establishing friendship with the Yehudim to strengthen himself?
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[24] I also will write to them words of encouragement and of honour and of gifts, that they may be with me to aid me.”
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[25] So he sent to them this message: “King Demetrios to the nation of the Yehudim (Jews), greetings.
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[26] Since as you’ve kept your covenants with us, and continued in our friendship, and haven’t joined yourselves to our enemies, we’ve heard of this, and are glad.
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[27] Now continue still to keep faith with us, and we’ll repay you with good in return for your dealings with us.
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[28] We’ll grant you many immunities and give you gifts.
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[29] “Now I free you and release all the Yehudim from the tributes, from the salt tax, and from the crown levies.
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[30] Instead of the third part of the seed, and instead of half of the fruit of the trees, which falls to me to receive, I release it from this day and from now on, so that I won’t take it from the land of Yehudah (Judah), and from the three districts which are added to it from the country of Shomron (Samaria) and Galil, from this day forth and for all time.
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[31] Let Yerushalem (Jerusalem) be holy and free, with her borders, tithes, and taxes.
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[32] I yield up also my authority over the citadel which is at Yerushalem, and give it to the high priest, that he may appoint in it men whom he chooses to keep it.
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[33] Every soul of the Yehudim who’s been carried captive from the land of Yehudah into any part of my kingdom, I set at liberty without payment. Let all officials also cancel the taxes on their livestock.
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[34] “All the feasts, the Sabbaths, new moons, appointed days, three days before a feast, and three days after a feast, let them all be days of immunity and release for all the Yehudim who are in my kingdom.
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[35] No one has authority to exact anything from any of them, or to trouble them about any matter.
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[36] “Let there be enrolled among the king’s forces about thirty thousand men of the Yehudim, and pay will be given to them, as is due to all the king’s forces.
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[37] Of them, some will be placed in the king’s great strongholds, and some of them will be placed over the affairs of the kingdom, which are positions of trust. Let those who are over them and their rulers be of themselves, and let them walk after their own laws, even as the king has commanded in the land of Yehudah.
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[38] “The three districts that have been added to Yehudah from the country of Shomron (Samaria), let them be annexed to Yehudah, that they may be reckoned to be under one ruler, that they may not obey any other authority than the high priest’s.
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[39] As for Ptolemais and its land, I’ve given it as a gift to the sanctuary that’s at Yerushalem (Jerusalem), for the expenses of the sanctuary.
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[40] I also give every year fifteen thousand shekels of silver from the king’s revenues from the places that are appropriate.
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[41] And all the additional funds which those who manage the king’s affairs didn’t pay as in the first years, they’ll give from now on towards the works of the temple.
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[42] Besides this, the five thousand shekels of silver which they received from the uses of the sanctuary from the revenue year by year is also released, because it belongs to the priests who minister there.
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[43] Anyone who flees to the temple that’s at Yerushalem, and within all of its borders, whether one owe money to the king, or any other matter, let them go free, along with all that they have in my kingdom.
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[44] Because the building and renewing of the structures of the sanctuary, the expense will also be given out of the king’s revenue.
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[45] Because the building of the walls of Yerushalem and fortifying it all around, the expense will also be given out of the king’s revenue, also for the building of the walls in Yehudah.”
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[46] Now when Yonatan (Jonathan) and the people heard these words, they gave no credence to them, and didn’t accept them, because they remembered the great evil which he’d done in Yisrael (Israel), and that he’d afflicted them very severely.
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[47] They were well pleased with Alexandros, because he was the first who spoke words of peace to them, and they were allies with him always.
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[48] King Alexandros (Alexander) gathered together great forces and encamped near Demetrios.
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[49] The two kings joined battle, and Alexandros’ army fled; and Demetrios followed after him, and prevailed against them.
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[50] He strengthened the battle greatly until the sun went down; and Demetrios fell that day.
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[51] Alexandros sent ambassadors to Mitsrayim’s (Egypt) King Ptolemaios (Ptolemy) with this message:
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[52] “Since I’ve returned to my kingdom, and am seated on the throne of my fathers, and have established my dominion, and have overthrown Demetrios, and have taken possession of our country—
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[53] yes, I joined the battle with him, and he and his army were defeated by us, and we sat on the throne of his kingdom—
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[54] now also let’s make friends with one another. Give me now your daughter as my wife. I’ll be joined with you, and will give both you and her gifts worthy of you.”
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[55] King Ptolemaios answered, saying, “Happy is the day you returned to the land of your ancestors and sat on the throne of their kingdom.
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[56] Now I’ll do to you as you’ve written, but meet me at Ptolemais, that we may see one another; and I’ll join with you, even as you’ve said.”
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[57] So Ptolemaios went out of Mitsrayim, himself and Kleopatra (Cleopatra) his daughter, and came to Ptolemais in the one hundred and sixty-second year.
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[58] King Alexandros met him, and he gave him his daughter Kleopatra, and celebrated her wedding at Ptolemais with great pomp, as kings do.
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[59] King Alexandros wrote to Yonatan (Jonathan), that he should come to meet him.
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[60] He went with pomp to Ptolemais, and met the two kings. He gave them and their friends silver and gold, and many gifts, and found favour in their sight.
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[61] Some malcontents out of Yisrael (Israel), men who were transgressors of the law, gathered together against him to complain against him, but the king didn’t pay any attention to them.
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[62] The king commanded that they take off Yonatan’s clothes and clothe him in purple, and they did so.
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[63] The king made him sit with him, and said to his princes, “Go out with him into the middle of the city, and proclaim that no man may complain against him of any matter, and let no man trouble him for any reason.”
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[64] When those who complained against him saw his honour according to the proclamation, and saw him clothed in purple, they all fled away.
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[65] The king gave him honour, and enrolled him among his chief friends, and made him a captain and governor of a province.
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[66] Then Yonatan returned to Yerushalem (Jerusalem) with peace and gladness.
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[67] In the one hundred and sixty-fifth year, Demetrios, son of Demetrios, came out of Kraitai (Crete) into the land of his ancestors.
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[68] When King Alexandros (Alexander) heard of it, he grieved greatly and returned to Antiokeia.
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[69] Demetrios appointed Apolonios, who was over Coele-Syria, and he gathered together a great army, and encamped against Yavneh, and sent to Yonatan the high priest, saying,
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[70] “You alone lift up yourself against us, but I’m ridiculed and in reproach because of you. Why do you assume authority against us in the mountains?
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[71] Now therefore, if you trust in your forces, come down to us into the plain, and let’s match strength with each other there; for the power of the cities is with me.
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[72] Ask and learn who I am, and the rest who help us. They say, ‘Your foot can’t stand before our face; for your ancestors have been put to flight twice in their own land.’
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[73] Now you won’t be able to withstand the cavalry and such an army as this in the plain, where is there’s no stone or pebble, or place to flee.”
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[74] Now when Yonatan heard Apolonios’ words, he was moved in his mind, and he chose ten thousand men, and went out from Yerushalem (Jerusalem); and Shim’on (Simon) his brother met him to help him.
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[75] Then he encamped against Yafo (Joppa). The people of the city shut him out, because Apolonios had a garrison in Yafo.
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[76] So they fought against it. The people of the city were afraid, and opened to him; and Yonatan became master of Yafo.
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[77] Apolonios heard about that, and he gathered an army of three thousand cavalry, and a great army, and went to Azotos as though he were on a journey, and at the same time advanced onward into the plain, because he had a multitude of cavalry which he trusted.
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[78] He pursued him to Azotos, and the armies joined battle.
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[79] Apolonios had secretly left a thousand cavalry behind them.
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[80] Yonatan learnt that there was an ambush behind him. They surrounded his army, and shot their arrows at the people, from morning until evening;
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[81] but the people stood fast, as Yonatan commanded them; and the enemy’s horses grew tired.
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[82] Then Shim’on (Simon) brought forward his army and joined battle with the phalanx (for the cavalry were exhausted), and they were defeated by him and fled.
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[83] The cavalry were scattered in the plain. They fled to Azotos and entered into Beyt-Dagon, their idol’s temple, to save themselves.
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[84] Yonatan burnt Azotos and the cities around it and took their spoils. He burnt the temple of Dagon and those who fled into it with fire.
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[85] Those who’d fallen by the sword plus those who were burnt were about eight thousand men.
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[86] From there, Yonatan left and encamped against Ashkelon. The people of the city came out to meet him with great pomp.
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[87] Yonatan, with those who were on his side, returned to Yerushalem (Jerusalem), having many spoils.
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[88] When King Alexandros heard these things, he honoured Yonatan even more.
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[89] He sent him a gold buckle, as the custom is to give to the king’s kindred. He gave him Ekron and all its land for a possession.
[1 Maccabees] [11]:[1] Then the king of Mitsrayim (Egypt) gathered together great forces, as the sand which is by the sea shore, and many ships, and sought to make himself master of Alexandros’s (Alexander) kingdom by deceit, and to add it to his own kingdom.
[1 Maccabees] [11]:[2] He went out into Aram (Syria) with words of peace, and the people of the cities opened their gates to him and met him; for King Alexandros’s command was that they should meet him, because he was his father-in-law.
[1 Maccabees] [11]:[3] Now as he entered into the cities of Ptolemais, he set his forces for a garrison in each city.
[1 Maccabees] [11]:[4] But when he came near to Azotos, they showed him Dagon’s temple burnt with fire, and Azotos and its pasture lands destroyed, and the bodies thrown out, and those who’d been burnt, whom he burnt in the war, for they’d made heaps of them in his way.
[1 Maccabees] [11]:[5] They told the king what Yonatan had done, that they might throw blame on him; but the king kept silent.
[1 Maccabees] [11]:[6] Yonatan met the king with pomp at Yafo (Joppa), and they greeted one another, and they slept there.
[1 Maccabees] [11]:[7] Yonatan went with the king as far as the river that’s called Eleutherus, then returned to Yerushalem (Jerusalem).
[1 Maccabees] [11]:[8] But King Ptolemaios (Ptolemy) took control of the cities along the sea coast, to Seleukeia which is by the sea, and he devised evil plans about Alexandros.
[1 Maccabees] [11]:[9] He sent ambassadors to King Demetrios, saying, “Come! Let’s make a covenant with one another, and I’ll give you my daughter whom Alexandros has, and you’ll reign over your father’s kingdom;
[1 Maccabees] [11]:[10] for I regret that I gave my daughter to him, for he tried to kill me.
[1 Maccabees] [11]:[11] He accused him, because he coveted his kingdom.
[1 Maccabees] [11]:[12] Taking his daughter from him, he gave her to Demetrios, and was estranged from Alexandros, and their enmity was openly seen.
[1 Maccabees] [11]:[13] Ptolemaios entered into Antiokeia, and put on himself Asia’s crown. He put two crowns on his head, the crown of Mitsrayim (Egypt) and that of Asia.
[1 Maccabees] [11]:[14] But King Alexandros was in Kilikia at that time, because the people of that region were in revolt.
[1 Maccabees] [11]:[15] When Alexandros heard of it, he came against him in war. Ptolemaios marched out and met him with a strong force, and put him to flight.
[1 Maccabees] [11]:[16] Alexandros fled into Arav, that he might be sheltered there; but King Ptolemaios was triumphant.
[1 Maccabees] [11]:[17] Zavdiyel the Aravi took off Alexandros’s head, and sent it to Ptolemaios.
[1 Maccabees] [11]:[18] King Ptolemaios died the third day after, and those who were in his strongholds were slain by the inhabitants of the strongholds.
[1 Maccabees] [11]:[19] Demetrios became king in the one hundred and sixty-seventh year.
[1 Maccabees] [11]:[20] In those days Yonatan (Jonathan) gathered together the Yehudim (Jews) to take the citadel that was at Yerushalem (Jerusalem). He made many engines of war to use against it.
[1 Maccabees] [11]:[21] Some lawless men who hated their own nation went to the king and reported to him that Yonatan was besieging the citadel.
[1 Maccabees] [11]:[22] He heard, and was angry, but when he heard it, he set out immediately, and came to Ptolemais, and wrote to Yonatan, that he shouldn’t besiege it, and that he should meet him and speak with him at Ptolemais with all speed.
[1 Maccabees] [11]:[23] But when Yonatan heard this, he gave orders to continue the siege. He chose some of the elders of Yisrael (Israel) and of the priests, and put himself in peril
[1 Maccabees] [11]:[24] by taking silver, gold, clothing, and various other presents, and went to Ptolemais to the king. Then he found favour in his sight.
[1 Maccabees] [11]:[25] Some lawless men of those who were of the nation made complaints against him,
[1 Maccabees] [11]:[26] and the king did to him even as his predecessors had done to him, and exalted him in the sight of all his friends,
[1 Maccabees] [11]:[27] and confirmed to him the high priesthood, and all the other honours that he had before, and gave him preeminence among his chief friends.
[1 Maccabees] [11]:[28] And Yonatan requested of the king that he’d make Yehudah (Judea) free from tribute, along with the three provinces and the country of Shomron (Samaria), and promised him three hundred talents.
[1 Maccabees] [11]:[29] The king consented, and wrote letters to Yonatan about all these things as follows:
[1 Maccabees] [11]:[30] “King Demetrios to his brother Yonatan, and to the nation of the Yehudim (Jews), greetings.
[1 Maccabees] [11]:[31] The copy of the letter which we wrote to Lasthenes our kinsman about you, we’ve written also to you, that you may see it.
[1 Maccabees] [11]:[32] ‘King Demetrios to Lasthenes his father, greetings.
[1 Maccabees] [11]:[33] We’ve determined to do good to the nation of the Yehudim, who are our friends, and observe what’s just towards us, because of their good will towards us.
[1 Maccabees] [11]:[34] We’ve confirmed therefore to them the borders of Yehudah, and also the three governments of Aphaerema, Lod, and Ramatayim (these were added to Yehudah from the country of Shomron), and all their territory to them, for all who do sacrifice in Yerushalem (Jerusalem), instead of the king’s dues which the king received of them yearly before from the produce of the earth and the fruits of trees.
[1 Maccabees] [11]:[35] As for the other payments to us from now on, of the tithes and the taxes that pertain to us, and the salt pits, and the crown taxes due to us, all these we’ll give back to them.
[1 Maccabees] [11]:[36] Not one of these grants will be annulled from this time forth and forever.
[1 Maccabees] [11]:[37] Now therefore be careful to make a copy of these things, and let it be given to Yonatan, and let it be set up on the holy mountain in a suitable and conspicuous place.’ ”
[1 Maccabees] [11]:[38] When King Demetrios saw that the land was quiet before him, and that no resistance was made to him, he sent away all his troops, each man to his own place, except the foreign troops, which he’d raised from the islands of the Gentiles. So all the troops of his fathers hated him.
[1 Maccabees] [11]:[39] Now Trufon was one of those who previously had been on Alexandros’s (Alexander) side, and he saw that all the forces murmured against Demetrios. So he went to Imalcue the Aravi, who was raising up Antiokos (Antiochus) the young child of Alexandros,
[1 Maccabees] [11]:[40] and urgently insisted to him that he should deliver him to him, that he might reign in his father’s place. He told him all that Demetrios had done, and the hatred with which his forces hated him; and he stayed there many days.
[1 Maccabees] [11]:[41] Now Yonatan sent to King Demetrios, that he should remove the troops of the citadel from Yerushalem, and the troops who were in the strongholds; for they fought against Yisrael (Israel) continually.
[1 Maccabees] [11]:[42] Demetrios sent to Yonatan, saying, “I won’t only do this for you and your nation, but I’ll greatly honour you and your nation, if I find an opportunity.
[1 Maccabees] [11]:[43] Now therefore you’ll do well if you send me men who’ll fight for me; for all my forces have revolted.”
[1 Maccabees] [11]:[44] So Yonatan sent him three thousand valiant men to Antiokeia. They came to the king, and the king was glad at their coming.
[1 Maccabees] [11]:[45] The people of the city gathered themselves together into the middle of the city, to the number of one hundred and twenty thousand men, and they wanted to kill the king.
[1 Maccabees] [11]:[46] The king fled into the palace courtyard, and the people of the city seized the main streets of the city and began to fight.
[1 Maccabees] [11]:[47] The king called the Yehudim (Jews) to help him, and they were gathered together to him all at once, and they dispersed themselves in the city, and killed that day about one hundred thousand.
[1 Maccabees] [11]:[48] They set the city on fire, and seized many spoils that day, and saved the king.
[1 Maccabees] [11]:[49] The people of the city saw that the Yehudim had taken control of the city as they pleased, and they became faint in their hearts, and they cried out to the king with supplication, saying,
[1 Maccabees] [11]:[50] “Give us your right hand, and let the Yehudim cease from fighting against us and the city.”
[1 Maccabees] [11]:[51] They threw away their weapons and made peace. The Yehudim were glorified in the sight of the king, and before all who were in his kingdom. Then they returned to Yerushalem (Jerusalem), having much plunder.
[1 Maccabees] [11]:[52] So King Demetrios sat on the throne of his kingdom, and the land was quiet before him.
[1 Maccabees] [11]:[53] He lied in all that he spoke, and estranged himself from Yonatan (Jonathan), and didn’t repay him according to the benefits with which he had repaid him, and treated him very harshly.
[1 Maccabees] [11]:[54] Now after this, Trufon returned, and with him the young child Antiokos (Antiochus), who reigned and put on a crown.
[1 Maccabees] [11]:[55] All the forces which Demetrios had sent away with disgrace were gathered to him, and they fought against him, and he fled and was routed.
[1 Maccabees] [11]:[56] Trufon took the elephants, and took control of Antiokeia.
[1 Maccabees] [11]:[57] The young Antiokos wrote to Yonatan, saying, “I confirm to you the high priesthood, and appoint you over the four districts, and to be one of the king’s friends.”
[1 Maccabees] [11]:[58] He sent to him golden vessels and furniture for the table, and gave him permission to drink in golden vessels, and to be clothed in purple, and to have a golden buckle.
[1 Maccabees] [11]:[59] He made his brother Shim’on (Simon) governor from the Ladder of Tsor (Tyre) to the borders of Mitsrayim (Egypt).
[1 Maccabees] [11]:[60] Yonatan went out and took his journey beyond the river and through the cities. All the forces of Aram (Syria) gathered themselves to him to be his allies. He came to Ashkelon, and the people of the city met him honourably.
[1 Maccabees] [11]:[61] He departed from there to Azah (Gaza), and Azah’s people shut him out. So he besieged it and burnt its pasture lands with fire, and plundered them.
[1 Maccabees] [11]:[62] Azah’s people pleaded with Yonatan, and he gave them his right hand, and took the sons of their princes for hostages, and sent them away to Yerushalem (Jerusalem). Then he passed through the country as far as Damesek (Damascus).
[1 Maccabees] [11]:[63] Then Yonatan heard that Demetrios’ princes had come to Kedesh, which is in Galil, with a great army, intending to remove him from his office.
[1 Maccabees] [11]:[64] He went to meet them, but he left Shim’on his brother in the country.
[1 Maccabees] [11]:[65] Shim’on encamped against Beyt-Tsur, and fought against it many days, and hemmed it in.
[1 Maccabees] [11]:[66] They asked him to give them his right hand, and he gave it to them. He removed them from there, took possession of the city, and set a garrison over it.
[1 Maccabees] [11]:[67] Yonatan and his army encamped at the water of Gennaisaret, and early in the morning they marched to the plain of Hatsor.
[1 Maccabees] [11]:[68] Listen, an army of foreigners met him in the plain. They laid an ambush for him in the mountains, but they themselves met him face to face.
[1 Maccabees] [11]:[69] But those who lay in ambush rose out of their places and joined battle. All those who were on Yonatan’s side fled.
[1 Maccabees] [11]:[70] Not one of them was left, except Matityah (Mattathias) the son of Avshalom (Absalom), and Yehudah (Judas) the son of Chalphi, captains of the forces.
[1 Maccabees] [11]:[71] Yonatan tore his clothes, put dirt on his head, and prayed.
[1 Maccabees] [11]:[72] He turned again to them in battle, and routed them, and they fled.
[1 Maccabees] [11]:[73] When the men on his side who’d fled saw this, they returned to him and pursued with him to Kedesh to their camp, and they encamped there.
[1 Maccabees] [11]:[74] About three thousand men of the foreigners fell on that day. Then Yonatan returned to Yerushalem (Jerusalem).
[1 Maccabees] [12]:[1] Yonatan saw that the time was favourable for him, so he chose men and sent them to Romai to confirm and renew the friendship that they had with them.
[1 Maccabees] [12]:[2] He also sent similar letters to the Spartans, and to other places.
[1 Maccabees] [12]:[3] They went to Romai, entered into the senate house, and said, “Yonatan the high priest and the nation of the Yehudim have sent us to renew for them the friendship and the alliance, as in former time.”
[1 Maccabees] [12]:[4] They gave them letters to the men in every place, that they should provide safe conduct for them on their way to the land of Yehudah (Judah).
[1 Maccabees] [12]:[5] This is the copy of the letters which Yonatan wrote to the Spartans:
[1 Maccabees] [12]:[6] “Yonatan the high priest, and the senate of the nation, and the priests, and the rest of the people of the Yehudim (Jews), to their kindred the Spartans, greetings.
[1 Maccabees] [12]:[7] Even before this time letters were sent to Honyo (Onias) the high priest from Arius, who was reigning among you, to signify that you’re our kindred, as the copy written below shows.
[1 Maccabees] [12]:[8] Honyo welcomed honourably the man who was sent and received the letters, wherein declaration was made of alliance and friendship.
[1 Maccabees] [12]:[9] Therefore we also, even though we need none of these things, having for our encouragement the holy books which are in our hands,
[1 Maccabees] [12]:[10] have undertaken to send that we might renew our brotherhood and friendship with you, to the end that we shouldn’t become estranged from you altogether; for a long time has passed since you sent your letter to us.
[1 Maccabees] [12]:[11] We therefore at all times without ceasing, both in our feasts, and on the other convenient days, remember you in the sacrifices which we offer, and in our prayers, as it’s right and proper to be mindful of kindred.
[1 Maccabees] [12]:[12] Moreover, we’re glad for your glory.
[1 Maccabees] [12]:[13] But as for ourselves, many afflictions and many wars have encompassed us, and the kings who are around us have fought against us.
[1 Maccabees] [12]:[14] We were unwilling to be troublesome to you, and to the rest of our allies and friends, in these wars;
[1 Maccabees] [12]:[15] for we have the help which is from heaven to help us, and we’ve been delivered from our enemies, and our enemies have been humbled.
[1 Maccabees] [12]:[16] We chose therefore Numenios the son of Antiokos (Antiochus) and Antipater the son of Yason, and have sent them to the Romaios, to renew the friendship that we had with them, and the former alliance.
[1 Maccabees] [12]:[17] We commanded them therefore to go also to you, and to salute you, and to deliver you our letters about the renewing of friendship and our brotherhood.
[1 Maccabees] [12]:[18] And now you’ll do well if you give us a reply.”
[1 Maccabees] [12]:[19] And this is the copy of the letters which they sent to Honyo (Onias):
[1 Maccabees] [12]:[20] “Arius king of the Spartans to Honyo the chief priest, greetings.
[1 Maccabees] [12]:[21] It’s been found in writing, about the Spartans and the Yehudim (Jews), that they’re kindred, and that they’re of the descendants of Avraham.
[1 Maccabees] [12]:[22] Now, since this has come to our knowledge, you’ll do well to write to us of your prosperity.
[1 Maccabees] [12]:[23] We moreover write on our part to you, that your livestock and goods are ours, and ours are yours. We do command therefore that they make report to you accordingly.”
[1 Maccabees] [12]:[24] Now Yonatan (Jonathan) heard that Demetrios’ princes had returned to fight against him with a greater army than before,
[1 Maccabees] [12]:[25] so he marched away from Yerushalem (Jerusalem), and met them in the country of Hamat; for he gave them no opportunity to set foot in his country.
[1 Maccabees] [12]:[26] He sent spies into his camp, and they came again, and reported to him that they were preparing to attack them at night.
[1 Maccabees] [12]:[27] But as soon as the sun was down, Yonatan commanded his men to watch, and to be armed, that all the night long they might be ready for battle. He stationed sentinels around the camp.
[1 Maccabees] [12]:[28] The adversaries heard that Yonatan and his men were ready for battle, and they feared, and trembled in their hearts, and they kindled fires in their camp then withdrew.
[1 Maccabees] [12]:[29] But Yonatan and his men didn’t know it until the morning; for they saw the fires burning.
[1 Maccabees] [12]:[30] Yonatan pursued after them, but didn’t overtake them; for they’d gone over the river Eleutherus.
[1 Maccabees] [12]:[31] Then Yonatan turned towards the Aravim, who are called Zabadaeans, and struck them, and took their spoils.
[1 Maccabees] [12]:[32] He came out from there, and came to Damesek (Damascus), and took his journey through all the country.
[1 Maccabees] [12]:[33] Shim’on (Simon) went out, and took his journey as far as Ashkelon, and the strongholds that were near it. Then he turned towards Yafo (Joppa) and took possession of it;
[1 Maccabees] [12]:[34] for he’d heard that they were planning to hand over the stronghold to Demetrios’ men. He set a garrison there to guard it.
[1 Maccabees] [12]:[35] Then Yonatan returned and called the people’s elders together. He planned with them to build strongholds in Yehudah (Judea),
[1 Maccabees] [12]:[36] and to make Yerushalem’s (Jerusalem) walls higher, and to raise a great mound between the citadel and the city, to separate it from the city, that so it might be isolated, that its garrison might neither buy nor sell.
[1 Maccabees] [12]:[37] They were gathered together to build the city. Part of the wall of the brook that’s on the east side fell down, and he repaired the section called Kafenata.
[1 Maccabees] [12]:[38] Shim’on also built Hadid in the plain country, made it strong, and set up gates and bars.
[1 Maccabees] [12]:[39] And Trufon sought to reign over Asia and to crown himself, and to stretch out his hand against Antiokos (Antiochus) the king.
[1 Maccabees] [12]:[40] He was afraid that Yonatan wouldn’t allow him, and that he’d fight against him; and he sought a way to seize him, that he might destroy him. So he marched out and came to Beyt-Shean.
[1 Maccabees] [12]:[41] Yonatan came out to meet him with forty thousand men chosen for battle, and came to Beyt-Shean.
[1 Maccabees] [12]:[42] Trufon saw that he came with a great army, and he was afraid to stretch out his hand against him.
[1 Maccabees] [12]:[43] He received him honourably, and commended him to all his friends, and gave him gifts, and commanded his forces to be obedient to him, as to himself.
[1 Maccabees] [12]:[44] He said to Yonatan, “Why have you put all this people to so much trouble, seeing there’s no war between us?
[1 Maccabees] [12]:[45] Now send them away to their homes, but choose for yourself a few men who’ll be with you, and come with me to Ptolemais, and I’ll give it to you, and the rest of the strongholds and the rest of the forces, and all the king’s officers. Then I’ll turn around and depart; for this is why I came.”
[1 Maccabees] [12]:[46] He put his trust in him, and did even as he said, and sent away his forces, and they departed into the land of Yehudah (Judah).
[1 Maccabees] [12]:[47] But he reserved to himself three thousand men, of whom he left two thousand in Galil, but one thousand went with him.
[1 Maccabees] [12]:[48] Now as soon as Yonatan entered into Ptolemais, Ptolemais’ people shut the gates and seized him. They killed all those who came in with him with the sword.
[1 Maccabees] [12]:[49] Trufon sent troops and cavalry into Galil, and into the Great Plain, to destroy all Yonatan’s men.
[1 Maccabees] [12]:[50] They perceived that he’d been seized and had perished, along with those who were with him. They encouraged one another and went on their way close together, prepared to fight.
[1 Maccabees] [12]:[51] Those who followed them saw that they were ready to fight for their lives, and turned back again.
[1 Maccabees] [12]:[52] They all came in peace into the land of Yehudah, and they mourned for Yonatan and those who were with him, and they were very afraid. All Yisrael (Israel) mourned with a great mourning.
[1 Maccabees] [12]:[53] And all the Gentiles who were around them sought to destroy them utterly; for they said, “They have no ruler nor anyone to help them. Now therefore let’s fight against them, and take away their memory from among men.”
[1 Maccabees] [13]:[1] Shim’on (Simon) heard that Trufon had gathered together a mighty army to come into the land of Yehudah and destroy it utterly.
[1 Maccabees] [13]:[2] He saw that the people were trembling in great fear. So he went up to Yerushalem (Jerusalem) and gathered the people together.
[1 Maccabees] [13]:[3] He encouraged them, and said to them, “You yourselves know all the things that I, my kindred, and my father’s house have done for the laws and the sanctuary, and the battles and the distresses which we’ve seen.
[1 Maccabees] [13]:[4] Because of this, all my brothers have perished for Yisrael’s sake, and I’m left alone.
[1 Maccabees] [13]:[5] Now be it far from me, that I should spare my own life in any time of affliction, for I’m not better than my kindred.
[1 Maccabees] [13]:[6] However, I’ll take vengeance for my nation, for the sanctuary, and for our wives and children, because all the Gentiles have gathered out of hatred to destroy us.”
[1 Maccabees] [13]:[7] The people’s spirit revived as soon as they heard these words.
[1 Maccabees] [13]:[8] They answered with a loud voice, saying, “You’re our leader in the place of Yehudah and Yonatan (Jonathan) your brothers.
[1 Maccabees] [13]:[9] Fight our battles, and we’ll do all that you tell us to do.”
[1 Maccabees] [13]:[10] He gathered together all the men of war, and hurried to finish Yerushalem’s (Jerusalem) walls. He fortified it all around.
[1 Maccabees] [13]:[11] He sent Yonatan the son of Avshalom (Absalom), and with him a great army, to Yafo (Joppa). He threw out those who were in it, and lived there.
[1 Maccabees] [13]:[12] Trufon left Ptolemais with a mighty army to enter into the land of Yehudah, and Yonatan was with him under guard.
[1 Maccabees] [13]:[13] But Shim’on encamped at Hadid, near the plain.
[1 Maccabees] [13]:[14] Trufon knew that Shim’on had risen up in the place of his brother Yonatan, and meant to join battle with him, so he sent ambassadors to him, saying,
[1 Maccabees] [13]:[15] “It’s for money which Yonatan your brother owed to the king’s treasury, because of the offices which he had, that we’re detaining him.
[1 Maccabees] [13]:[16] Now send one hundred talents of silver and two of his sons for hostages, so that when he’s released he may not revolt against us, and we’ll release him.”
[1 Maccabees] [13]:[17] Shim’on (Simon) knew that they spoke to him deceitfully, but he sent to get the money and the children, to avoid arousing great hostility among the people,
[1 Maccabees] [13]:[18] who might say, “Because I didn’t send him the money and the children, he perished.”
[1 Maccabees] [13]:[19] So he sent the children and the hundred talents, but Trufon lied, and didn’t release Yonatan.
[1 Maccabees] [13]:[20] After this, Trufon came to invade the land and destroy it, and he went around by the way that leads to Adorayim. Shim’on and his army marched near him to every place, wherever he went.
[1 Maccabees] [13]:[21] Now the people of the citadel sent to Trufon ambassadors, urging him to come to them through the wilderness, and to send them food.
[1 Maccabees] [13]:[22] So Trufon prepared all his cavalry to come, but on that night a very heavy snow fell, and he didn’t come because of the snow. He marched off and went into the land of Gilead.
[1 Maccabees] [13]:[23] When he came near to Bascama, he killed Yonatan, and he was buried there.
[1 Maccabees] [13]:[24] Then Trufon turned back, and went away into his own land.
[1 Maccabees] [13]:[25] Shim’on sent, and took the bones of Yonatan his brother, and buried him at Modi’in, the city of his fathers.
[1 Maccabees] [13]:[26] All Yisrael (Israel) made great lamentation over him, and mourned for him many days.
[1 Maccabees] [13]:[27] Shim’on built a monument on the tomb of his father and his kindred, and raised it high so that it could be seen, with polished stone on the front and back.
[1 Maccabees] [13]:[28] He also set up seven pyramids, one near another, for his father, his mother, and his four brothers.
[1 Maccabees] [13]:[29] Because these, he made an elaborate setting, erecting great pillars around them, and on the pillars he made suits of armour for a perpetual memorial, and beside the suits of armour, he carved ships, so that they could be seen by all who sail on the sea.
[1 Maccabees] [13]:[30] This is the tomb which he made at Modi’in. It remains to this day.
[1 Maccabees] [13]:[31] Now Trufon deceived the young King Antiokos (Antiochus) and killed him,
[1 Maccabees] [13]:[32] and reigned in his place. He put on himself the crown of Asia and brought a great calamity on the land.
[1 Maccabees] [13]:[33] Shim’on built up the strongholds of Yehudah (Judea), and walled them all around with high towers, great walls, gates, and bars; and he stored food in the strongholds.
[1 Maccabees] [13]:[34] Shim’on chose men, and sent to King Demetrios with a request that he grant the country an immunity, because all that Trufon did was to plunder.
[1 Maccabees] [13]:[35] King Demetrios sent to him according to these words, and answered him, and wrote a letter to him, as follows:
[1 Maccabees] [13]:[36] “King Demetrios to Shim’on the high priest and friend of kings, and to the elders and nation of the Yehudim (Jews), greetings.
[1 Maccabees] [13]:[37] The golden crown and the palm branch, which you sent, we’ve received. We’re ready to make a steadfast peace with you, yes, and to write to our officers to release you from tribute.
[1 Maccabees] [13]:[38] Whatever things we confirmed to you, they’re confirmed. The strongholds, which you’ve built, let them be your own.
[1 Maccabees] [13]:[39] As for any oversights and faults committed to this day, we forgive them, and the crown tax which you owed us. If there were any other tax collected in Yerushalem (Jerusalem), let it be collected no longer.
[1 Maccabees] [13]:[40] If any among you’re qualified to be enrolled in our court, let them be enrolled, and let there be peace between us.”
[1 Maccabees] [13]:[41] In the one hundred seventieth year, the yoke of the Gentiles was taken away from Yisrael (Israel).
[1 Maccabees] [13]:[42] The people began to write in their instruments and contracts, “In the first year of Shim’on, the great high priest and captain and leader of the Yehudim.”
[1 Maccabees] [13]:[43] In those days Shim’on encamped against Gezer, and surrounded it with troops. He made a siege engine, and brought it up to the city, and struck a tower, and captured it.
[1 Maccabees] [13]:[44] Those who were in the engine leapt out into the city; and there was a great uproar in the city.
[1 Maccabees] [13]:[45] The people of the city tore their clothes, and went up on the walls with their wives and children, and cried with a loud voice, asking Shim’on to give them his right hand.
[1 Maccabees] [13]:[46] They said, “Don’t deal with us according to our wickednesses, but according to your mercy.”
[1 Maccabees] [13]:[47] So Shim’on was reconciled to them, and didn’t fight against them; but he expelled them from the city and cleansed the houses where the idols were, and then entered into it with singing and giving praise.
[1 Maccabees] [13]:[48] He removed all uncleanness out of it, and placed in it men who’d keep the law, and made it stronger than it was before, and built a dwelling place for himself in it.
[1 Maccabees] [13]:[49] But the people of the citadel in Yerushalem (Jerusalem) were hindered from going out and from going into the country, and from buying and selling. So they were very hungry, and a great number of them perished from famine.
[1 Maccabees] [13]:[50] Then they cried out to Shim’on, that he should give them his right hand; and he gave it to them; but he expelled them from there, and he cleansed the citadel from its pollutions.
[1 Maccabees] [13]:[51] He entered into it on the twenty-third day of the second month, in the one hundred and seventy-first year, with praise and palm branches, with harps, with cymbals, and with stringed instruments, with hymns, and with songs, because a great enemy had been destroyed out of Yisrael (Israel).
[1 Maccabees] [13]:[52] Shim’on ordained that they should keep that day every year with gladness. He made the hill of the temple that was by the citadel stronger than before, and he lived there with his men.
[1 Maccabees] [13]:[53] Shim’on saw that his son Yohan (John) was a man, so he made him leader of all his forces; and he lived in Gezer.
[1 Maccabees] [14]:[1] In the one hundred and seventy-second year, King Demetrios gathered his forces together, and went into Maday (Media) to get help, that he might fight against Trufon.
[1 Maccabees] [14]:[2] When Arsakes, the king of Paras (Persia) and Maday, heard that Demetrios had come into his borders, he sent one of his princes to take him alive.
[1 Maccabees] [14]:[3] He went and struck Demetrios’ army, and seized him and brought him to Arsakes, who put him under guard.
[1 Maccabees] [14]:[4] The land had rest all the days of Shim’on. He sought the good of his nation. His authority and his honour was pleasing to them all his days.
[1 Maccabees] [14]:[5] Amid all his honours, he took Yafo (Joppa) for a harbour, and made it an entrance for the islands of the sea.
[1 Maccabees] [14]:[6] He enlarged the borders of his nation and took possession of the country.
[1 Maccabees] [14]:[7] He gathered together a great number of captives, and took control of Gezer, Beyt-Tsur, and the citadel, and he removed its uncleannesses from it. There was no one who resisted him.
[1 Maccabees] [14]:[8] They tilled their land in peace, and the land gave her increase, and the trees of the plains gave their fruit.
[1 Maccabees] [14]:[9] The old men sat in the streets; they all conversed together about good things. The young men put on glorious and warlike clothing.
[1 Maccabees] [14]:[10] He provided food for the cities and furnished them with means of defence, until the glory of his name was known to the end of the earth.
[1 Maccabees] [14]:[11] He made peace in the land, and Yisrael (Israel) rejoiced with great joy.
[1 Maccabees] [14]:[12] Each man sat under his vine and his fig tree, and there was no one to make them afraid.
[1 Maccabees] [14]:[13] No one was left in the land who fought against them. The kings were defeated in those days.
[1 Maccabees] [14]:[14] He strengthened all those of his people who were humble. He searched out the law, and every lawless and wicked person he took away.
[1 Maccabees] [14]:[15] He glorified the sanctuary, and added to the vessels of the temple.
[1 Maccabees] [14]:[16] It was heard at Romai that Yonatan (Jonathan) was dead, and even in Sparta, and they were extremely grieved.
[1 Maccabees] [14]:[17] But as soon as they heard that his brother Shim’on (Simon) was made high priest in his place, and ruled the country and the cities in it,
[1 Maccabees] [14]:[18] they wrote to him on brass tablets to renew with him the friendship and the alliance which they’d confirmed with his brothers Yehudah (Judas) and Yonatan.
[1 Maccabees] [14]:[19] These were read before the congregation at Yerushalem (Jerusalem).
[1 Maccabees] [14]:[20] This is the copy of the letters which the Spartans sent: “The rulers and the city of the Spartans, to Shim’on the high priest, to the elders, the priests, and the rest of the people of the Yehudim (Jews), our kindred, greetings.
[1 Maccabees] [14]:[21] The ambassadors who were sent to our people reported to us about your glory and honour. We were glad for their coming,
[1 Maccabees] [14]:[22] and we registered the things that were spoken by them in the public records as follows: ‘Numenios son of Antiokos (Antiochus), and Antipater son of Yason, the Yehudim’ ambassadors, came to us to renew the friendship they had with us.
[1 Maccabees] [14]:[23] It pleased the people to entertain the men honourably, and to put the copy of their words in the public records, to the end that the people of the Spartans might have a record of them. Moreover they wrote a copy of these things to Shim’on the high priest.’ ”
[1 Maccabees] [14]:[24] After this, Shim’on sent Numenios to Romai with a great shield of gold of weighing one thousand minas, in order to confirm the alliance with them.
[1 Maccabees] [14]:[25] But when the people heard these things, they said, “How can we thank Shim’on and his sons?
[1 Maccabees] [14]:[26] Because he and his brothers and his father’s house have made themselves strong, and have fought and chased away Yisrael’s (Israel) enemies, and confirmed liberty to Yisrael.”
[1 Maccabees] [14]:[27] So they wrote on tablets of brass, and set them on pillars on Mt. Tsiyon (Zion). This is the copy of the writing: “On the eighteenth day of Elul, in the one hundred and seventy-second year, which is the third year of Shim’on the high priest,
[1 Maccabees] [14]:[28] in Asaramel, in a great congregation of priests and people and princes of the nation, and of the elders of the country, it was proclaimed to us:
[1 Maccabees] [14]:[29] ‘Since wars often occurred in the country, Shim’on the son of Matityah (Mattathias), the son of the sons of Yoyariv, and his brothers, put themselves in jeopardy and withstood the enemies of their nation, that their sanctuary and the law might be established, and glorified their nation with great glory.
[1 Maccabees] [14]:[30] Yonatan (Jonathan) rallied the nation, became their high priest, and was gathered to his people.
[1 Maccabees] [14]:[31] Their enemies planned to invade their country, that they might destroy their country utterly, and stretch out their hands against their sanctuary.
[1 Maccabees] [14]:[32] Then Shim’on rose up and fought for his nation. He spent much of his own money to arm the valiant men of his nation and give them wages.
[1 Maccabees] [14]:[33] He fortified the cities of Yehudah (Judea) and Beyt-Tsur that lies on the borders of Yehudah, where the weapons of the enemies were had been stored, and there he placed a garrison of Yehudim (Jews).
[1 Maccabees] [14]:[34] He fortified Yafo (Joppa) which is on the sea, and Gezer which is on the borders of Azotos, where the enemies used to live, and placed Yehudim there, and set in there all things necessary for their restoration.
[1 Maccabees] [14]:[35] The people saw Shim’on’s faith, and the glory which he resolved to bring to his nation, and they made him their leader and high priest, because he’d done all these things, and for the justice and the faith which he kept to his nation, and because he sought by all means to exalt his people.
[1 Maccabees] [14]:[36] In his days, things prospered in his hands, so that the Gentiles were taken away out of their country, and they also who were in the city of David, those who were in Yerushalem (Jerusalem), who’d made themselves a citadel, out of which they used to go, and polluted everything around the sanctuary, and did great damage to its purity.
[1 Maccabees] [14]:[37] He placed Yehudim in it and fortified it for the safety of the country and the city, and made high Yerushalem’s walls.
[1 Maccabees] [14]:[38] King Demetrios confirmed to him the high priesthood according to these things,
[1 Maccabees] [14]:[39] and made him one of his friends, and honoured him with great honour;
[1 Maccabees] [14]:[40] for he’d heard that the Yehudim had been called by the Romaios friends, allies, and kindred, and that they’d met the ambassadors of Shim’on honourably;
[1 Maccabees] [14]:[41] and that the Yehudim and the priests were well pleased that Shim’on should be their leader and high priest forever, until there should arise a faithful prophet;
[1 Maccabees] [14]:[42] and that he should be governor over them, and should take charge of the sanctuary, to set them over their works, and over the country, and over the weapons, and over the strongholds; and that he should take charge of the sanctuary,
[1 Maccabees] [14]:[43] and that he should be obeyed by all, and that all contracts in the country should be written in his name, and that he should be clothed in purple, and wear gold;
[1 Maccabees] [14]:[44] and that it shouldn’t be lawful for any of the people or of the priests to nullify any of these things, or to oppose the words that he should speak, or to gather an assembly in the country without him, or to be clothed in purple, or wear a buckle of gold;
[1 Maccabees] [14]:[45] but anyone who should do otherwise, or nullify any of these things, he’ll be liable to punishment.’ ”
[1 Maccabees] [14]:[46] All the people consented to ordain for Shim’on that he should do according to these words.
[1 Maccabees] [14]:[47] So Shim’on accepted this, and consented to be high priest, and to be captain and governor of the Yehudim and of the priests, and to be protector of all.
[1 Maccabees] [14]:[48] They commanded to put this writing on tablets of brass, and to set them up within the precinct of the sanctuary in a conspicuous place,
[1 Maccabees] [14]:[49] and moreover to put copies of them in the treasury, so that Shim’on and his sons might have them.
[1 Maccabees] [15]:[1] Antiokos (Antiochus) son of Demetrios the king sent a letter from the islands of the sea to Shim’on the priest and governor of the Yehudim, and to all the nation.
[1 Maccabees] [15]:[2] Its contents follow: “King Antiokos to Shim’on the chief priest and governor, and to the nation of the Yehudim, greetings.
[1 Maccabees] [15]:[3] Whereas certain troublemakers have made themselves masters of the kingdom of our fathers, but my purpose is to claim the kingdom, that I may restore it as it was before; and moreover I’ve raised a multitude of foreign soldiers, and have prepared warships;
[1 Maccabees] [15]:[4] moreover I plan to land in the country, that I may punish those who’ve destroyed our country, and those who’ve made many cities in the kingdom desolate;
[1 Maccabees] [15]:[5] now therefore I confirm to you all the tax remissions which the kings who were before me remitted to you, and whatever gifts besides they remitted to you,
[1 Maccabees] [15]:[6] and I permit you to coin money for your country with your own stamp,
[1 Maccabees] [15]:[7] but that Yerushalem (Jerusalem) and the sanctuary should be free. All the weapons that you’ve prepared, and the strongholds that you’ve built, which you have in your possession, let them remain yours.
[1 Maccabees] [15]:[8] Every debt owed to the king, and the things that’ll be owed to the king from now on and forever, let them be remitted to you.
[1 Maccabees] [15]:[9] Moreover, when we’ve established our kingdom, we’ll glorify you and your nation and the temple with great glory, so that your glory will be made manifest in all the earth.
[1 Maccabees] [15]:[10] In the one hundred and seventy-fourth year, Antiokos went into the land of his fathers; and all the forces came together to him, so that there were few men with Trufon.
[1 Maccabees] [15]:[11] King Antiokos pursued him, and he came, as he fled, to Dor, which is by the sea;
[1 Maccabees] [15]:[12] for he knew that troubles had come on him all at once, and that his forces had deserted him.
[1 Maccabees] [15]:[13] Antiokos encamped against Dor, and with him one hundred and twenty thousand men of war and eight thousand cavalry.
[1 Maccabees] [15]:[14] He surrounded the city, and the ships joined in the attack from the sea. He harassed the city by land and sea, and permitted no one to go out or in.
[1 Maccabees] [15]:[15] Numenios and his company came from Romai, having letters to the kings and to the countries, in which were written these things:
[1 Maccabees] [15]:[16] “Lukios, consul of the Romaios, to King Ptolemaios (Ptolemy), greetings.
[1 Maccabees] [15]:[17] The Yehudim’ (Jews) ambassadors came to us as our friends and allies, to renew the old friendship and alliance, being sent from Shim’on (Simon) the high priest, and from the people of the Yehudim.
[1 Maccabees] [15]:[18] Moreover they brought a shield of gold weighing one thousand minas.
[1 Maccabees] [15]:[19] It pleased us therefore to write to the kings and to the countries, that they shouldn’t seek their harm or fight against them, their cities, and their country, or be allies with those who fight against them.
[1 Maccabees] [15]:[20] Moreover, it seemed good to us to receive the shield from them.
[1 Maccabees] [15]:[21] If therefore any troublemakers have fled from their country to you, deliver them to Shim’on the high priest, that he may take vengeance on them according to their law.”
[1 Maccabees] [15]:[22] He wrote the same things to King Demetrios, to Atalos, to Ariarathes, to Arsakes,
[1 Maccabees] [15]:[23] to all the countries, to Sampsames, to the Spartans, to Delos, to Mundos, to Sikuon, to Karia, to Samos, to Pamfulia, to Lukia, to Halikarnasos, to Rodos, to Faselis, to Kos, to Side, to Arvad, Gortuna, Knidos, Kupros (Cyprus), and Kurainai (Cyrene).
[1 Maccabees] [15]:[24] They also wrote this copy to Shim’on the high priest.
[1 Maccabees] [15]:[25] But King Antiokos (Antiochus) encamped against Dor the second day, bringing his forces up to it continually, and making engines of war; and he shut up Trufon from going in or out.
[1 Maccabees] [15]:[26] Shim’on sent him two thousand chosen men to fight on his side, with silver, gold, and instruments of war in abundance.
[1 Maccabees] [15]:[27] He wouldn’t receive them, but nullified all the covenants which he’d made with him before, and was estranged from him.
[1 Maccabees] [15]:[28] He sent to him Athenobios, one of his friends, to confer with him, saying, “You hold possession of Yafo (Joppa), Gezer, and the citadel that’s in Yerushalem, cities of my kingdom.
[1 Maccabees] [15]:[29] You’ve devastated their territory, and done great harm in the land, and control of many places in my kingdom.
[1 Maccabees] [15]:[30] Now therefore hand over the cities which you’ve taken, and the tributes of the places which you’ve taken control of outside of the borders of Yehudah (Judea);
[1 Maccabees] [15]:[31] or else give me for them five hundred talents of silver; and for the harm that you’ve done, and the tributes of the cities, another five hundred talents. Otherwise we’ll come and subdue you.”
[1 Maccabees] [15]:[32] Athenobios, the king’s friend, came to Yerushalem (Jerusalem). When he saw the glory of Shim’on, the cupboard of gold and silver vessels, and his great attendance, he was amazed. He reported to him the king’s words.
[1 Maccabees] [15]:[33] Shim’on answered, and said to him, “We haven’t taken other men’s land nor do we have possession of that which belongs to others, but of the inheritance of our fathers. However, it’d been in possession of our enemies wrongfully for a while.
[1 Maccabees] [15]:[34] But we, having opportunity, firmly hold the inheritance of our fathers.
[1 Maccabees] [15]:[35] As for Yafo and Gezer, which you demand, they did great harm among the people throughout our country. We’ll give one hundred talents for them.” Athenobios didn’t answer even one word,
[1 Maccabees] [15]:[36] but returned in a rage to the king, and reported to him these words, and Shim’on’s glory, and all that he’d seen; and the king was extremely angry.
[1 Maccabees] [15]:[37] Meanwhile, Trufon embarked on board a ship, and fled to Orthosia.
[1 Maccabees] [15]:[38] The king appointed Kendebaios chief captain of the sea coast, and gave him troops of infantry and cavalry.
[1 Maccabees] [15]:[39] He commanded him to encamp against Yehudah (Judea), and he commanded him to build up Kidron, and to fortify the gates, and that he should fight against the people; but the king pursued Trufon.
[1 Maccabees] [15]:[40] So Kendebaios came to Yavneh and began to provoke the people, and to invade Yehudah, and to take the people captive and kill them.
[1 Maccabees] [15]:[41] He built Kidron and stationed cavalry and infantry there, to the end that going out they might make raids on the highways of Yehudah, as the king had commanded him.
[1 Maccabees] [16]:[1] Yohan (John) went up from Gezer and told Shim’on his father what Kendebaios was doing.
[1 Maccabees] [16]:[2] Shim’on called his two oldest sons, Yehudah and Yohan, and said to them, “I and my brothers and my father’s house have fought the battles of Yisrael (Israel) from our youth, even to this day; and things have prospered in our hands, that we’ve often delivered Yisrael.
[1 Maccabees] [16]:[3] But now I’m old, and you moreover, by his mercy, are of a sufficient age. Take the place of me and my brother, and go out and fight for our nation; and let the help which is from heaven be with you.
[1 Maccabees] [16]:[4] He chose out of the country twenty thousand men of war and cavalry, and they went against Kendebaios, and slept at Modi’in.
[1 Maccabees] [16]:[5] Rising up in the morning, they went into the plain, and a great army of infantry and cavalry came to meet them. There was a brook between them.
[1 Maccabees] [16]:[6] He encamped near them, he and his people. He saw that the people were afraid to pass over the brook, and he passed over first. When the men saw him, they passed over after him.
[1 Maccabees] [16]:[7] He divided the people, and placed the cavalry in the middle of the infantry; but the enemies’ cavalry were very many.
[1 Maccabees] [16]:[8] They sounded the trumpets; and Kendebaios and his army were put to flight, and many of them fell wounded to death, but those who were left fled to the stronghold.
[1 Maccabees] [16]:[9] At that time Yehudah, Yohan’s brother, was wounded; but Yohan pursued after them until he came to Kidron, which Kendebaios had built.
[1 Maccabees] [16]:[10] They fled to the towers that are in Azotos’ fields; and he burnt it with fire. About two thousand men of them fell. Then he returned into Yehudah in peace.
[1 Maccabees] [16]:[11] Ptolemaios (Ptolemy) the son of Abubus had been appointed governor over the plain of Yeriho (Jericho), and he had much silver and gold;
[1 Maccabees] [16]:[12] for he was the high priest’s son-in-law.
[1 Maccabees] [16]:[13] His heart was lifted up, and he planned to make himself master of the country, and he made deceitful plans against Shim’on (Simon) and his sons, to do away with them.
[1 Maccabees] [16]:[14] Now Shim’on was visiting the cities that were in the country, and attending to their needs. He went down to Yeriho—himself with Matityah (Mattathias) and Yehudah his sons—in the one hundred and seventy-seventh year, in the eleventh month, which is the month Shevat.
[1 Maccabees] [16]:[15] The son of Abubus received them deceitfully into the little stronghold that’s called Dok, which he’d built, and made them a great banquet, and hid men there.
[1 Maccabees] [16]:[16] When Shim’on and his sons had drunk freely, Ptolemaios and his men rose up, took their weapons, rushed in against Shim’on in the banqueting place, and killed him, his two sons, and some of his servants.
[1 Maccabees] [16]:[17] He committed a great iniquity, and repaid evil for good.
[1 Maccabees] [16]:[18] Ptolemaios wrote these things and sent to the king, that he should send him forces to aid him, and should deliver him their country and the cities.
[1 Maccabees] [16]:[19] He sent others to Gezer to do away with Yohan. To the captains of thousands, he sent letters to come to him, that he might give them silver, gold, and gifts.
[1 Maccabees] [16]:[20] He sent others to take possession of Yerushalem (Jerusalem) and the temple hill.
[1 Maccabees] [16]:[21] One ran before to Gezer, and told Yohan that his father and kindred had perished, and he’s sent to kill you also.
[1 Maccabees] [16]:[22] When he heard, he was greatly shocked. He seized the men who came to destroy him and killed them; for he perceived that they were seeking to destroy him.
