[Matay] [5]:[12] Be happy and praising God because you’ll all have a wonderful reward in the heavens, because in the past they also persecuted the prophets like that.
[Matay] [5]:[13] “You people are the world’s salt, but if the salt is made tasteless, what would you use to salt your food? The salt wouldn’t be useful for anything anymore and would just get thrown out and trampled on by the people.
[Matay] [5]:[14] “You are the world’s light. A city up on a hill can’t be hidden.
[Matay] [5]:[15] No one lights a lamp and puts it under a basket—you put it on a lampstand and it lightens up the house.
[Matay] [5]:[16] In the same way, let your light shine in front of everyone, so that they can see your good behaviour and then might praise your father in the heavens.
[Matay] [5]:[17] “Don’t imagine that I came to criticise the prophets or Mosheh’s (Moses) instructions. I didn’t come to oppose the scriptures, but to fulfil them,
[Matay] [5]:[18] because I can assure you all that until heaven and earth reach their end, not one letter or mark will be taken away from those instructions until everything is fulfilled.
[Matay] [5]:[19] Therefore anyone who breaks even a minor command, and teaches others to do the same, will be seen as one of the least in the heavenly kingdom, but anyone who practices and teaches those instructions will be considered outstanding in the kingdom.
[Matay] [5]:[20] Let me tell all of you, unless you’re more godly than the religious teachers and the Farisaios, there’s no way that you’ll get to enter the heavenly kingdom.
[Matay] [5]:[21] “You’ve all heard that your ancestors were told not to murder, because any murderer will be sentenced.
[Matay] [5]:[22] But I’m telling you that anyone who gets angry at another will be liable for judgement, and anyone who calls another person a numbskull will have to face the court, and if you call them a fool, you’re liable for hellfire.
[Matay] [5]:[23] So if you’re there at the altar to offer your gift and remember that someone has something against you,
[Matay] [5]:[24] leave your gift there at the altar and go and sort that out first, before coming back to offer your gift.
[Matay] [5]:[25] “Resolve things with your opponent as soon as you can, hopefully while you’re still on the way to the court, in case your opponent turns you in to the judge, and the judge to the officer, and then you’ll end up in prison.
[Matay] [5]:[26] I can assure you that you won’t get out of prison until the fine is completely paid.
[Matay] [5]:[27] “You all know that the scriptures say not to commit adultery,
[Matay] [5]:[28] but I’m telling you that if you look at a woman lustfully then you’ve already committed adultery in your mind.
[Matay] [5]:[29] If your right eye is causing you to stumble, then pluck it out and throw it away,
[Matay] [5]:[30] and if your right hand is causing you to stumble, cut it off and throw it away, because it’s better for you that one of your body parts would be taken than for your whole body to end up in the judgement fire.
[Matay] [5]:[31] “It’s said that any man can divorce his wife just by sending her away.
[Matay] [5]:[32] But I’m telling you all that anyone who divorces his wife, except in the case where she’s committed sexual immorality, is causing her to commit adultery, and anyone who marries a wife that’s been sent away is causing her to commit adultery.
[Matay] [5]:[33] “Also, you’ve heard that it was said to our ancestors that you shouldn’t break your oath, but you must do whatever you promised to Yahweh.
[Matay] [5]:[34] But I’m telling you not to make oaths in the first place—don’t swear by heaven because it’s God’s throne,
[Matay] [5]:[35] nor by the earth because it’s God’s footrest, nor by Yerushalem (Jerusalem) because it’s the supreme king’s city.
[Matay] [5]:[36] And don’t swear by your own strength, because you can’t even make one strand of hair grow a different colour.
[Matay] [5]:[37] Just say ‘yes’ when you commit to doing something, and ‘no’ when you don’t, because going beyond that is actually evil.
[Matay] [5]:[38] “You’ve all heard it said that it’s an eye for an eye and a tooth for a tooth,
[Matay] [5]:[39] but I’m telling you not to resist those who want to hurt you. If someone slaps you on your right cheek, turn your left cheek towards them,
[Matay] [5]:[40] and to the person suing you in court and claiming your robe, let them have your coat as well.
[Matay] [5]:[41] And if someone forces you to walk a mile, walk two miles with them.
[Matay] [5]:[42] Give whatever others request from you, and don’t turn away from anyone who wants to borrow from you.
[Matay] [5]:[43] “You’ve all heard it said that you should love your neighbour and hate your enemy,
[Matay] [5]:[44] but I’m telling you to love your enemies and to pray for anyone who’s persecuting you,
[Matay] [5]:[45] so that you might become children of your father in the heavens, because he causes his sun to rise on both evil and good people, and sends the rain for both godly and ungodly people.
[Matay] [5]:[46] If you people just love people who love you, what reward would you expect for that? Don’t even the tax collectors do that?
[Matay] [5]:[47] And if you’re only polite to your own circle, how is that achieving anything? Aren’t non-Jews just the same?
[Matay] [5]:[48] Instead you should all aim to be perfect just like your heavenly father is perfect.
[Matay] [6]:[1] “You people should take care not to only obey God in front of others so they’ll think well of you, because if you do, you’ll certainly get no reward from your father in the heavens.
[Matay] [6]:[2] “So when you’re giving to the poor, don’t make a big display of it like the hypocrites do in the Jewish meeting halls and in the streets so they’ll get the people’s praises. I can assure you that they’ve already received their reward in full.
[Matay] [6]:[3] But when you give to the poor, don’t let your left hand know what your right hand is doing,
[Matay] [6]:[4] so that your giving will be private, yet your father who sees everything you do will give back to you.
[Matay] [6]:[5] “Whenever you pray, don’t be like the hypocrites who love to pray in the Jewish meeting halls and on street corners so everyone will notice them. I can assure you that they’ve already received their reward in full.
[Matay] [6]:[6] Instead, when you pray, go into a private room and shut the door, then pray to your father who’s not visible to you. Then your father who sees everything will reward you.
[Matay] [6]:[7] “And when you do pray, don’t babble away like people of other religions who think they’ll be listened to just because of how much they pray.
[Matay] [6]:[8] There’s no need to be like them, because God your father already knows your needs before you even ask him.
[Matay] [6]:[9] So pray like this: ‘Our father in the heavens, we want your name to be honoured forever.
[Matay] [6]:[10] We want your kingdom to come and your plans to be fulfilled here on earth just like they are in heaven.
[Matay] [6]:[11] Give us everything we need today
[Matay] [6]:[12] and write off what we owe you as we also write off what others owe us.
[Matay] [6]:[13] Don’t bring us to the point of being tempted, but keep us away from doing evil things.’
[Matay] [6]:[14] “Because if you people forgive other people’s wrongs, then your heavenly father will also forgive your wrongs.
[Matay] [6]:[15] But if you don’t forgive other people’s wrongs, then your father won’t forgive your wrongs either.
[Matay] [6]:[16] “Whenever you people are abstaining from food, don’t look miserable like the hypocrites, because they intentionally try to look awful so that everyone will notice that they’re fasting. I can assure you that they’ve already received their reward in full.
[Matay] [6]:[17] Instead, when you fast, comb your hair and wash your face
[Matay] [6]:[18] so that no one will realise that you’re fasting, other than your father who’s not visible to you. Then your father who sees everything will reward you.
[Matay] [6]:[19] “Don’t amass wealth for yourselves here on earth, where insects and corrosion destroy things, and where it can be stolen.
[Matay] [6]:[20] Instead, store your wealth in heaven, where there’s no destructive insects or corrosion or thieves or scammers,
[Matay] [6]:[21] because wherever your wealth is, your values will also be focused there.
[Matay] [6]:[22] “Your eyes are your body’s lamps, so if your eyes are healthy, then your entire body will be bright.
[Matay] [6]:[23] But if your eyes are evil, your entire body will be dark.
[Matay] [6]:[24] “No one can serve two masters, because they’ll either hate one and like the other one, or else will support one and despise the other. So you people can’t serve both God and money.
[Matay] [6]:[25] “So that’s why I’m telling you all not to worry about your worldly life—things like what you’ll eat or drink, or how you look and what you’ll wear. Isn’t life more than food, and the body more than clothing?
[Matay] [6]:[26] Think about the birds in the sky—they don’t plant seeds or harvest crops or gather grain into barns, but it’s your heavenly father who feeds them. Aren’t each of you worth more than them?
[Matay] [6]:[27] Who can add an hour to their lifetime by worrying?
[Matay] [6]:[28] “Why would you worry about clothes? Look how the flowers grow in the fields—they don’t work or make fabric,
[Matay] [6]:[29] but I can tell you that not even King Shelomoh (Solomon) at the peak of his reign was dressed as well as the flowers.
[Matay] [6]:[30] So if God dresses the plants in the fields that are here today and thrown away tomorrow, won’t he care much more for you, you people with little faith?
[Matay] [6]:[31] “That means that you people don’t need to worry about having anything to eat or drink, or having clothes to wear.
[Matay] [6]:[32] People with no trust in God try to obtain all those things, but your heavenly father already knows that you need these things.
[Matay] [6]:[33] So instead you should be striving to enter God’s kingdom and to be guiltless in his eyes, and then all these other things will just follow.
[Matay] [6]:[34] Don’t worry about tomorrow, because tomorrow can worry about itself—today’s problems are enough by themselves.
[Matay] [7]:[1] “Don’t judge others, so that you won’t be judged yourselves,
[Matay] [7]:[2] because you’ll all be judged in the same way that you judge others. Whatever standard you use on others will be the same standard used on you.
[Matay] [7]:[3] And why are you looking at the speck of sawdust in another person’s eye when you have an entire board in your own eye?
[Matay] [7]:[4] How could you offer to get the speck out of their eye, when you still have the board in yours?
[Matay] [7]:[5] What a hypocrite! First get the board out of your own eye, and then you’ll be able to see clearly so that you can help them with their eye.
[Matay] [7]:[6] “Don’t give special things to dogs, and don’t throw pearls to pigs, because they’ll all just trample them underfoot, and then they’re just as likely to turn and attack you.
[Matay] [7]:[7] “Make your requests, and they’ll be given to you. Keep looking, and you’ll find it. Knock on doors, and they’ll be opened.
[Matay] [7]:[8] Everyone who asks for something will get something, and everyone who searches for something will find something, and the door will be opened for everyone who knocks.
[Matay] [7]:[9] If you have a child that asks for something to eat, which of you would give them a stone?
[Matay] [7]:[10] Or if the child asked for some fish, who would give them a snake?
[Matay] [7]:[11] So if evil people know how to give good gifts to their children, how much more will your father in the heavens give good things to those who ask him?
[Matay] [7]:[12] “So in every area, whatever you’d like others to do for you, that’s how you people should be treating them. That’s what Mosheh’s (Moses) instructions and the prophets’ writings were about.
[Matay] [7]:[13] “Come in through the narrow gate, because there’s a big gateway and a wide path that leads away to destruction, and lots of people go that way.
[Matay] [7]:[14] The gateway leading away to life is narrow, and the path has been kept narrow, and not many people find it.
[Matay] [7]:[15] “Watch out for false prophets who come to you in sheep’s clothing, but inside they’re swindling wolves.
[Matay] [7]:[16] You people will know who they are if you observe their fruit. Does anyone pick grapes from thorn bushes, or figs from thistles?
[Matay] [7]:[17] Similarly, every good tree produces good fruit, but the bad tree produces evil fruit.
[Matay] [7]:[18] A good tree can’t produce bad fruit, and a bad tree can’t produce good fruit.
[Matay] [7]:[19] Every tree that doesn’t produce good fruit will be chopped down and thrown into the fire.
[Matay] [7]:[20] So then, you’ll know the false teachers by observing their fruit.
[Matay] [7]:[21] “Not everyone who goes around calling me ‘master’ will enter the heavenly kingdoms—only those who actually do what my father who lives in the heavens wants.
[Matay] [7]:[22] Many people will complain on judgement day saying, ‘Master, master, didn’t we prophesy using your name, and exorcise demons using your name, and do many miracles using your name?’
[Matay] [7]:[23] Then I’ll have to tell them, ‘I don’t even know you. Go away from me, all of you whose behaviour is against God’s laws.’
[Matay] [7]:[24] “Therefore anyone who hears these messages of mine and puts them into practice, they can be likened to a sensible person who built their house on the rock.
[Matay] [7]:[25] When the rains started and the floods came and the winds blew and battered that house, it was stable because its foundation was the rock.
[Matay] [7]:[26] “But anyone who hears these messages of mine and doesn’t put them into practice, they can be likened to a stupid person who built their house on the sand.
[Matay] [7]:[27] When the rains started and the floods came and the winds blew and battered that house, it collapsed with a loud crash.”
[Matay] [7]:[28] When Yeshua (Jesus; Grk. Yesus) had finished sharing all these messages, the crowds were astonished at his teaching
[Matay] [7]:[29] because he taught like someone who had authority, and not like their regular religious teachers.
[Matay] [8]:[1] When Yeshua (Jesus; Grk. Yesus) came down from the hillside, a large crowd followed him,
[Matay] [8]:[2] and then a man with leprosy approached him and knelt down in front of him and asked, “Master, if you’re willing, you’re able to get rid of this disease.”
[Matay] [8]:[3] “I am willing,” said Yeshua as he stretched out his hand and commanded, “Be clean.” The leprosy disappeared immediately,
[Matay] [8]:[4] and Yeshua told him, “Make sure that you don’t tell anyone about this, but you do need to go and show yourself to the priest and make the offering required by Mosheh’s (Moses) law as a testimony to the authorities.”
[Matay] [8]:[5] When Yeshua (Jesus; Grk. Yesus) arrived in Kafarnaoum (Capernaum), a Romaios army commander approached him and pleaded with him,
[Matay] [8]:[6] saying, “Master, I have a slave who’s paralysed and has to stay in bed because he’s being badly tormented.”
[Matay] [8]:[7] “I’ll come and heal him,” Yeshua answered.
[Matay] [8]:[8] “But master,” the commander replied, “I’m not worthy of you coming to my house, but just give the command and my slave will be healed,
[Matay] [8]:[9] because I’m also a man given a position under authority, with soldiers under me, and I tell this one, ‘Come here,’ and he comes, and tell my slave, ‘Do this,’ and he does it.
[Matay] [8]:[10] Yeshua was amazed when he heard that, and said to his followers around him, “I can assure you that I haven’t discovered faith like that from any Israeli.
[Matay] [8]:[11] I’m telling you that many people from all over the world will come and join Avraham and Yitshak (Isaac) and Ya’akov (Jacob) at the table in the heavenly kingdom,
[Matay] [8]:[12] but the ones who thought they were the true children will be thrown out into the distant darkness where there’ll be crying and regrets.
[Matay] [8]:[13] Then he said to the commander, “Go, then, and it’ll happen according to your faith,” and his slave was healed that very moment.
[Matay] [8]:[14] When Yeshua (Jesus; Grk. Yesus) came to Kefa’s (Peter; Grk. Petros) house, he saw Kefa’s mother-in-law lying in bed with a fever.
[Matay] [8]:[15] Yeshua touched her hand and the fever left her. Then she got up and looked after her guest.
[Matay] [8]:[16] In the evening, the people brought many who were possessed by evil spirits, and Yeshua drove out the spirits with a command and healed all the sick people.
[Matay] [8]:[17] This fulfilled what the prophet Yeshayah (Isaiah) had written: ‘He took our sickness and bore our diseases.’
[Matay] [8]:[18] When Yeshua (Jesus; Grk. Yesus) saw the crowd around him, he told his apprentices to take him across to the other side of the lake.
[Matay] [8]:[19] One of the religious teachers came up to Yeshua and told him, “Teacher, I’ll follow you wherever you go.”
[Matay] [8]:[20] “Foxes have burrows,” said Yeshua, “and birds have their nests, but the son of humanity doesn’t even have a place to lay his head.”
[Matay] [8]:[21] Another one of his apprentices said to him, “I’ll follow you, Master, but first let me wait until I can bury my father.”
[Matay] [8]:[22] “Follow after me,” Yeshua responded, “and leave the dead to bury the dead by themselves.”
[Matay] [8]:[23] Then Yeshua (Jesus; Grk. Yesus) and his apprentices followed him and got into the boat and launched it.
[Matay] [8]:[24] Then wow, a huge storm rose up on the lake, and the waves started coming into the boat, but Yeshua was asleep.
[Matay] [8]:[25] They woke him up and pleaded, “Master, save us, we’re going to drown.”
[Matay] [8]:[26] “What are you worried about?” asked Yeshua. “You people don’t have much faith.” Then he stood up and told the winds and the water to stop, and the lake became very calm.
[Matay] [8]:[27] The people were astonished and asked, “What kind of man is this that the winds and the lake just do what he says?”
[Matay] [8]:[28] And when Yeshua (Jesus; Grk. Yesus) arrived in the Gadarainos region on the other side of the lake, he was met by two very dangerous demon-possessed men who were coming out of the cemetery. Because of them, some people weren’t able to travel on that road.
[Matay] [8]:[29] Suddenly the two men yelled out saying, “Son of God, what’s the connection between us and you? Have you come here to cause us pain before the designated time?”
[Matay] [8]:[30] Now there was a large herd of pigs grazing not far away from them,

[Matay] [13]:[4] As he was spreading the seed, some of it fell beside a path, and the birds come and ate that seed.
[Matay] [13]:[5] Some fell on stony ground where there wasn’t much soil, and it sprouted immediately because the thin layer of soil was moist and warm,
[Matay] [13]:[6] but when the sun rose high, it was scorched, and not having any deep roots, it withered up.
[Matay] [13]:[7] Some seed fell in a thistle patch, but the thistles grew over them and choked them out.
[Matay] [13]:[8] However, some seed landed on the good soil, and it grew to bear a harvest—some a hundred times more, some sixty times, and some thirty times.

[Matay] [13]:[10] After this, his apprentices came to him and asked, “Why do you speak to the people in parables?”

[Matay] [13]:[16] “But your eyes are blessed, because they can see, and your ears also, because they can hear,

[Matay] [13]:[18] “So now listen to the meaning of the parable about the person spreading seed.
[Matay] [13]:[19] Everyone who hears the message about the kingdom and doesn’t understand it, the evil one comes and snatches what was sown in that person’s heart. That’s the seed that landed by the path.
[Matay] [13]:[20] The seed that landed on the rocky ground, that’s the person who hears the message and is immediately happy to accept it,
[Matay] [13]:[21] but doesn’t have any roots of their own, so it’s just fleeting—they stumble as soon as there’s any difficulties or persecution because of the message.
[Matay] [13]:[22] The seed that landed among the thorns is the person who hears the message, but the world’s worries and wealth’s seductiveness choke out the message and it becomes unfruitful.
[Matay] [13]:[23] The seed that landed on the good soil is the person who hears the message and understands it and goes on to bear fruit—some people producing a hundred times more, some sixty times, and some thirty times.”
[Matay] [13]:[24] Then Yeshua (Jesus; Grk. Yesus) told them another parable, saying, “The heavenly kingdom is like a farmer who’s planted good seed in his field.
[Matay] [13]:[25] But while everyone was sleeping, his enemy came and spread black-grained ‘wheat’ seeds around his wheat field and left again.
[Matay] [13]:[26] Then when the wheat grew and produced grains, the poisonous ‘wheat’ could also be seen.
[Matay] [13]:[27] The farmer’s slave came and told him, ‘Master, wasn’t it good wheat seed that you planted? So why is there so much false wheat?’
[Matay] [13]:[28] ‘An enemy must have done this,’ the farmer replied. ‘So should we go and pull out the bad stuff?’ asked the slaves.
[Matay] [13]:[29] ‘No,’ said the farmer, ‘because pulling that out might also pull up some of the wheat plants.
[Matay] [13]:[30] Let them all grow together, and then at harvest time I can just tell the harvesters to pull the false wheat plants out first and put them in bundles to be incinerated, and then harvest the wheat to go into my barn.’ ”
[Matay] [13]:[31] Another one of his parables went like this: “The heavenly kingdom is like a mustard seed that a man planted in his field.
[Matay] [13]:[32] Even though it’s a very small seed, it grows larger than most garden plants, and becomes such a large bush that birds even come and nest in its branches.”
[Matay] [13]:[33] In another parable, Yeshua (Jesus; Grk. Yesus) said, “The heavenly kingdom is like yeast, which a woman took and hid in a month’s worth of flour, and eventually all of it rose.”
[Matay] [13]:[34] Yeshua (Jesus; Grk. Yesus) told all these things to the crowds in the form of parables. In fact he said nothing that wasn’t a parable,
[Matay] [13]:[35] so that what had been written by the prophet would be fulfilled: ‘I will be saying things that have been hidden since the creation of the world.’
[Matay] [13]:[36] Then Yeshua (Jesus; Grk. Yesus) left the crowd and went into the house. His apprentices followed him in and asked him for the interpretation of the parable about the poisonous black wheat in the field.
[Matay] [13]:[37] “The farmer spreading the good seed,” Yeshua answered, “is the son of humanity,
[Matay] [13]:[38] and the field is the world, and the good seeds are the heirs to the kingdom. The false wheat seeds are the evil one’s apprentices,
[Matay] [13]:[39] and the enemy who planted them is the devil. The harvest is at the end of this age, and the harvesters are God’s messengers.
[Matay] [13]:[40] Therefore at the end of this age, the false wheat plants will be gathered and incinerated.
[Matay] [13]:[41] The son of humanity will send out his messengers to remove all the temptations out of his kingdom, as well as everyone who doesn’t obey God’s law,
[Matay] [13]:[42] and they’ll throw them into the incinerator, and there’ll be crying and a lot of anguish.
[Matay] [13]:[43] Then the godly people will shine as bright as the sun in their father’s kingdom. Anyone who’s interested in hearing, let them listen.
[Matay] [13]:[44] “The heavenly kingdom is like a field that had had treasure hidden in it. When someone found the treasure, they hid it again, and with great excitement went and sold everything they had so they could buy that field.
[Matay] [13]:[45] “The heavenly kingdom is also like a trader wanting to buy beautiful pearls,
[Matay] [13]:[46] and when they found one outstanding pearl, they went and sold everything they had so they could buy that pearl.
[Matay] [13]:[47] “The heavenly kingdom is also like a dragnet that was thrown into the lake and picked up everything from under the water.
[Matay] [13]:[48] When it was full, they pulled it up onto the beach and sat and sorted the catch—throwing the good catch into containers and throwing out the bad stuff.
[Matay] [13]:[49] It’ll be just like that at the end of this age—God’s messengers will come out and separate the evil people from the godly people,
[Matay] [13]:[50] and they’ll throw the evil ones into the incinerator. There’ll be crying and a lot of anguish.
[Matay] [13]:[51] “Did you all understand all of that?” “Yes,” his apprentices answered.
[Matay] [13]:[52] Then he said to them, “Because of this, every teacher who’s been trained about the heavenly kingdom is like a home owner who gives presents of both new and old things of out their valuables.”
[Matay] [13]:[53] After Yeshua (Jesus; Grk. Yesus) had finished explaining the parables, he left that place,
[Matay] [13]:[54] went to his hometown of Nazaret (Nazareth), and taught the people in the Jewish meeting hall. They were amazed at his teaching, asking each other, “Where did this fellow get his wisdom and his ability to do miracles?
[Matay] [13]:[55] Isn’t he the son of Yosef (Joseph), the carpenter? Don’t we know his mother Maria (Mary; Heb. Miryam; Grk. Maria/Mariam) and his brothers Ya’akov (James; Grk. Yakobos) and Yosef and Shim’on (Simon) and Yehudah (Judas; Grk. Yudas)?
[Matay] [13]:[56] Aren’t his sisters still here in town? So where did he get all these abilities?”
[Matay] [13]:[57] As a result, they didn’t have any respect for him. But Yeshua said to them, “A prophet is not dishonoured except in his own hometown and among his own household.”
[Matay] [13]:[58] So he didn’t do many miracles there because of their disbelief.

[Matay] [14]:[4] Yohan had been saying that it was against God’s law for Herodes to take his brother’s wife.
[Matay] [14]:[5] Herodes had been wanting to have Yohan executed, but he was afraid of the crowd because they considered Yohan to be a prophet.
[Matay] [14]:[6] However at Herodes’s birthday celebration, Herodias’s daughter had danced in front of them all and had pleased Herodes so much
[Matay] [14]:[7] that he promised with an oath to give her anything she requested.
[Matay] [14]:[8] The young woman was urged on by her mother to tell Herodes that she wanted Yohan-the-immerser’s head on a plate.
[Matay] [14]:[9] The king was upset, but because of his oaths in front of the other guests, he commanded it to be so
[Matay] [14]:[10] and sent his soldiers to behead Yohan in prison.
[Matay] [14]:[11] So then his head was brought in on a plate and given to the young woman, who then took it to her mother.

[Matay] [23]:[15] “You religious teachers and Farisaios are hypocrites and will have a bad end, because you’d travel all the way around the world to make one convert, and then you’d make him twice the son of hell that you are yourselves.
[Matay] [23]:[16] “You blind guides will have a bad end. You say that if anyone makes a promise on the temple, it’s worthless, but if they make a promise on the gold in the temple, then they have to honour it.
[Matay] [23]:[17] You’re both stupid and blind, because which is greater: the gold, or the temple which makes the gold sacred?
[Matay] [23]:[18] And you say that if anyone makes a promise on the altar, it’s worthless, but anyone who makes a promise on the gift on the altar has to honour it.
[Matay] [23]:[19] You’re both stupid and blind, because which is greater: the gift, or the altar which makes the gift sacred?
[Matay] [23]:[20] Anyone who makes a promise on the altar is bound by both the altar and the things on it.
[Matay] [23]:[21] Anyone who makes a promise on the temple is bound by both the temple and God who lives in it.
[Matay] [23]:[22] And anyone who makes a promise on heaven is bound by both God’s throne and the one who’s sitting on it.
[Matay] [23]:[23] “You religious teachers and Farisaios are hypocrites and will have a bad end, because you give a tenth of your herbs, but you ignore the weightier parts of God’s commands, like justice, mercy, and faith. It’s good to tithe, but those other things should also be observed, and not left out.
[Matay] [23]:[24] You blind guides! You try to strain out a gnat, and end up swallowing a camel.
[Matay] [23]:[25] “You religious teachers and Farisaios are hypocrites and will have a bad end, because you scrub the outsides of your cups and bowls, but the insides are still full of greed and selfishness.
[Matay] [23]:[26] You blind Farisaios! First you should clean the inside of your cup or dish, so that the outside can also become clean.
[Matay] [23]:[27] “You religious teachers and Farisaios are hypocrites and will have a bad end, because you’re like whitewashed tombs. On the outside they might look nice, but the insides are full of dead people’s bones and all kinds of impurities,
[Matay] [23]:[28] so even though the people might see your godly facade, actually your insides are full of hypocrisy and lawlessness.
[Matay] [23]:[29] “You religious teachers and Farisaios are hypocrites and will have a bad end, because you rebuild the prophets’ tombs and adorn the tombs of godly people,
[Matay] [23]:[30] and you tell yourselves, ‘If we’d lived back in our ancestors’ time, we wouldn’t have had any part with them in killing the prophets.’
[Matay] [23]:[31] By saying that, you’re admitting to yourselves that you’re the descendants of the ones who killed the prophets—
[Matay] [23]:[32] actually you’re just the same as your ancestors.
[Matay] [23]:[33] Bunch of snakes! Brood of vipers! How are you planning to escape being condemned to hell?
[Matay] [23]:[34] Because of that, listen, I’m now sending more prophets and wise preachers and teachers to you people. You’ll kill off some of them and have others executed on posts. You’ll flog some of them in your Jewish meeting halls, and you’ll persecute others from city to city,
[Matay] [23]:[35] so that the judgement for the deaths of all the godly people around the world will fall on you people. This includes the blood of innocent Hevel (Abel) all the way through the centuries to the blood of Zekaryah (Zechariah; Grk. Zakarias) (son of Berekyah) who you people murdered between the temple and the altar.
[Matay] [23]:[36] Yes, I can assure you that all these things will happen to this generation.
[Matay] [23]:[37] “Yerushalem (Jerusalem), Yerushalem, the city that murders the prophets and throws rocks to kill those who are sent to her. How often I wanted to gather your inhabitants like a mother hen gathers her chicks under her wings, but you didn’t want that.
[Matay] [23]:[38] So listen, now your temple will be left uninhabited,
[Matay] [23]:[39] because I’m telling you that you certainly won’t see me again until you can say, ‘The person coming in Yahweh’s name has been blessed.’ ”
[Matay] [24]:[1] When Yeshua (Jesus; Grk. Yesus) left the temple, his apprentices approached him and pointed out the temple buildings.
[Matay] [24]:[2] In response, he asked, “Do you see all this? I can assure you that it’ll be torn down so thoroughly that not a single stone will be left on top of another.”
[Matay] [24]:[3] When Yeshua (Jesus; Grk. Yesus) was sitting on the Mt. of Olives, his apprentices came up to him by themselves, asking, “Tell us when all those things will happen, and what the signs will be of your arrival and of the end of this age.”
[Matay] [24]:[4] “Watch out in case other people mislead you,” Yeshua answered,
[Matay] [24]:[5] “because many will come claiming to be me, saying that they’re the messiah, and misleading many people.
[Matay] [24]:[6] You’ll observe wars and hear reports about wars further away. Don’t be alarmed, but keep watching, because these things need to happen, although that’s not yet the end.
[Matay] [24]:[7] People groups will turn against each other, and countries rise up against one another, and there’ll be famines and earthquakes.
[Matay] [24]:[8] But all of those things are just like the beginning of labour pains.
[Matay] [24]:[9] “Then they’ll hand you apprentices over for persecution, and some of you will be killed. All the people groups will hate you because of my name.
[Matay] [24]:[10] They’ll cause many people to stumble and hand each other over and hate each other.
[Matay] [24]:[11] Also, many false prophets will appear, and they’ll mislead many people,
[Matay] [24]:[12] and as a result, lawlessness will increase, and many people’s love will cool off,
[Matay] [24]:[13] but anyone who lasts until the end will be rescued.
[Matay] [24]:[14] This good message about God’s kingdom will be proclaimed right around the world as a witness statement to all the people groups, and then the end will come.
[Matay] [24]:[15] “So when you apprentices see the irreverent object that the prophet Daniyel wrote about being placed in the holy place (anyone reading this should try to understand it),
[Matay] [24]:[16] those in Yehudah (Judea) should flee to the hills,
[Matay] [24]:[17] anyone outside on the flat roof shouldn’t go back inside to get things out of the house,
[Matay] [24]:[18] and anyone in the field shouldn’t go back to the house to get their coat.
[Matay] [24]:[19] It’ll be very difficult for pregnant women and breast-feeding mothers in those days,
[Matay] [24]:[20] and you should pray that your escape won’t be in winter or on a rest day.
[Matay] [24]:[21] This will be followed by incredible troubles like nothing that’s ever happened in this world, from creation until the present time, and which will never happen again—
[Matay] [24]:[22] in fact, if those days weren’t shortened, nobody would survive. However, because of the chosen people, those days will be shortened.
[Matay] [24]:[23] “At that time, if anyone says, ‘Look, here’s the messiah’ or ‘Here he is’, don’t believe it,
[Matay] [24]:[24] because false messiahs and false prophets will emerge, and they’ll do amazing miracles that would, if possible, mislead even the chosen people.
[Matay] [24]:[25] Listen, I’m telling you apprentices before it happens.
[Matay] [24]:[26] “So if they tell you apprentices, ‘Look, he’s out in the wilderness,’ don’t go out there, or if they say, ‘He’s here in these private rooms,’ don’t believe it,
[Matay] [24]:[27] because when the son of humanity comes, it’ll be like how the lightning goes right across the sky from one side to the other.
[Matay] [24]:[28] “Wherever there’s something dead, that’s where the vultures will gather.
[Matay] [24]:[29] “But immediately after that troubling time, the sun will go dark and the moon won’t shine. The stars will fall from the sky, and the heavenly powers will be shaken.
[Matay] [24]:[30] And then a miracle will appear in the sky as the son of humanity arrives. All of the world’s people groups will be in turmoil, and they’ll see the son of humanity arriving on the clouds in the sky with power and massive splendour.
[Matay] [24]:[31] There’ll be a trumpet blast as he sends out his messengers to bring together all his chosen people from every part of the earth—from one pole to the other.
[Matay] [24]:[32] “So learn the parable about the fig tree: whenever its branches green up and leaves start to sprout out, you know that summer is coming.
[Matay] [24]:[33] In the same way, when you see all those things happening, you’ll know then that the end of this age is very close.
[Matay] [24]:[34] I can assure you that that generation won’t pass away until all of those things happen.
[Matay] [24]:[35] The sky and the earth will pass away, but my messages will certainly not pass away.
[Matay] [24]:[36] “No one knows the exact day or time—not even the messengers in the heavens, or even the son—only the father knows it.
[Matay] [24]:[37] The son of humanity’s arrival will be just like it was in Noah’s time.
[Matay] [24]:[38] In the days leading up to the flood, people were eating and drinking, and marrying and getting engaged—right until the very day that Noah got into the barge.
[Matay] [24]:[39] They didn’t realise that something was coming until the flood came and took everything away. It’ll be just like that when the son of humanity comes.
[Matay] [24]:[40] Two people will be working out on the farm—one will be taken and one left behind.
[Matay] [24]:[41] Two people will be grinding grain—one will be taken and one left behind.
[Matay] [24]:[42] So keep watching, because none of you know exactly when your master will return.
[Matay] [24]:[43] But you do know that if a home-owner knew when a thief was going to come, he’d be there watching, and not allow the thief to break into the house.
[Matay] [24]:[44] Because of that, you apprentices should also get ready, because otherwise you won’t realise when the son of humanity is coming.
[Matay] [24]:[45] “As a result, we’ll see who the faithful and watchful slave is—the one who the master appointed to run all of his household affairs.
[Matay] [24]:[46] That slave will be rewarded if the master finds him working faithfully when he arrives suddenly.
[Matay] [24]:[47] I can assure you that he’ll appoint the slave to supervise everything that he possesses.
[Matay] [24]:[48] But if the evil slave says to himself, ‘Ah, the master won’t be back for a long time yet,’
[Matay] [24]:[49] and starts beating his fellow slaves, and spends time eating and drinking with drunks,
[Matay] [24]:[50] then his master will arrive when he’s not expecting it
[Matay] [24]:[51] and will torture him and send him off with the hypocrites to where there’ll be crying and a lot of anguish.
[Matay] [25]:[1] “The heavenly kingdom can also be likened to ten young women in a wedding party who took their lamps and went off to meet the groom.
[Matay] [25]:[2] Five of them were harebrained and five were sensible.
[Matay] [25]:[3] The less clever ones took their lamps but didn’t take any oil for them,
[Matay] [25]:[4] whereas the sensible ones had oil in containers along with the lamps.
[Matay] [25]:[5] When the groom was delayed, they started nodding off and napping.
[Matay] [25]:[6] “But in the middle of the night there was a shout, ‘Look, the groom’s on his way! Come out and meet him.’
[Matay] [25]:[7] So all the young women got up and trimmed the wicks on their lamps,
[Matay] [25]:[8] and the less sensible ones asked the others, ‘Here, give us some of your oil, because our lamps are starting to splutter.’
[Matay] [25]:[9] But the sensible ones answered, ‘We don’t have enough for everyone. You need to go to the stall and buy some for your lamps.’
[Matay] [25]:[10] However, while they were still away buying oil, the groom appeared, and those who were ready went in with him to the wedding, and the door was shut.
[Matay] [25]:[11] “Later, the other young women arrived and called out, ‘Master, master, let us in!’
[Matay] [25]:[12] But he answered, ‘I can assure you that I don’t know you.’
[Matay] [25]:[13] “So then, be watchful, because you apprentices don’t know the day or the time.
[Matay] [25]:[14] “It’s like a man who was leaving on a trip. He called his slaves and shared his savings among them for them to manage.
[Matay] [25]:[15] He gave five bags of silver to one, two bags to another, and one to the other, according to each slave’s ability, and then he departed.
[Matay] [25]:[16] In his absence, the one with five bags of silver used it for trading and gained five more bags.
[Matay] [25]:[17] Similarly, the one with two bags gained two more bags.
[Matay] [25]:[18] But the one who received the one bag, he went off and dug a hole in the ground and hid his master’s silver.
[Matay] [25]:[19] “Eventually the master of those slaves returned, and he called them in to settle up their accounts.
[Matay] [25]:[20] The slave who’d received five bags of silver approached, also bringing the other five bags, and said, ‘Master, you entrusted me with five bags, and look, I gained another five.’
[Matay] [25]:[21] ‘Well done, good and faithful slave,’ said the master. ‘You were faithful with a few things, so I’ll put you in charge of a lot more things. Come and join your master in celebrating.’
[Matay] [25]:[22] The slave who’d received two bags approached and said, ‘Master, you entrusted me with two bags of silver. Look, I gained another two.’
[Matay] [25]:[23] ‘Well done, good and faithful slave,’ said the master. ‘You were faithful with a few things, so I’ll put you in charge of a lot more things. Come and join your master in celebrating.’
[Matay] [25]:[24] Then the slave with one bag of silver also approached, and he said, ‘Master, I knew that you’re a hard man, harvesting where you didn’t plant, and gathering where you didn’t spread seed.
[Matay] [25]:[25] So because I was afraid, I went and hid your silver in the ground. So look, here’s all of it back.’
[Matay] [25]:[26] ‘You evil and lazy slave,’ his master answered. ‘You know that I harvest where I didn’t plant, and gather where I didn’t spread seed,
[Matay] [25]:[27] so you should’ve at least invested my silver with the bankers, and then I could’ve got it back with some interest.
[Matay] [25]:[28] Therefore take the bag of silver off him and give it to the one with ten bags,
[Matay] [25]:[29] because everyone who has will be given more, and will have plenty, but anyone who doesn’t have, even what they do have will be taken away from them.
[Matay] [25]:[30] So throw that useless slave out into the darkness where there’ll be crying and a lot of anguish.
[Matay] [25]:[31] “But when the son of humanity comes in his glory and all the messengers with him, then he’ll sit down on his splendid throne
[Matay] [25]:[32] and all the nations will be gathered together in front of him. He’ll separate them all from each other, just like a shepherd separates the sheep from the goats.
[Matay] [25]:[33] Then the sheep will be standing on his right, and the goats on his left
[Matay] [25]:[34] and the king will say to the sheep on his right, ‘Come all of you who’ve been blessed by my father. Now you’ll inherit the kingdom that has been prepared for you since the creation of the world
[Matay] [25]:[35] because I was hungry and you gave me something to eat, I was thirsty and you gave me something to drink, I was a stranger and you accommodated me,
[Matay] [25]:[36] I was naked and you gave me clothes, I was sick and you visited me, I was in prison and you came to see me.’
[Matay] [25]:[37] Then those godly people will ask, ‘Master, when did we ever see you hungry and we fed you, or thirsty and we gave you a drink?
[Matay] [25]:[38] And when did we see you as a stranger and accommodate you, or naked and we clothed you?
[Matay] [25]:[39] And when did we see you in prison, and we came to see you?’
[Matay] [25]:[40] Then the king will answer them, ‘I can assure you that whenever you did it to one of the least of these my brothers and sisters, then you did it to me.’
[Matay] [25]:[41] “Then the king will also speak to the ones on his left, ‘Get away from me you who are cursed. You’ll go into the eternal fire which was prepared for the devil and his messengers.
[Matay] [25]:[42] Because I was hungry and you didn’t give me anything to eat, I was thirsty and you didn’t give me anything to drink,
[Matay] [25]:[43] I was a stranger and you didn’t offer me shelter, I was naked and you didn’t give me any clothes, and I was sick and in prison and you never visited me.’
[Matay] [25]:[44] Then they’ll also respond, ‘Master, when did we ever see you hungry or thirsty, or a stranger or naked, or sick or in prison and we didn’t help you?’
[Matay] [25]:[45] ‘I can assure you,’ the king answered, ‘that whenever you failed to help even one of the least of these others, you failed to serve me.’
[Matay] [25]:[46] Then this group will be sent off to eternal punishment, but the guiltless ones will receive eternal life.”
[Matay] [26]:[1] After Yeshua (Jesus; Grk. Yesus) had completed his teaching, he told his apprentices,
[Matay] [26]:[2] “The pass-over celebration is in two more days, and the son of humanity will be handed over to be executed on a stake.”
[Matay] [26]:[3] At that time, the chief priests and the local elders were gathered together in the courtyard of Kayafa (Caiaphas; Grk. Kaiafas), the chief priest,
[Matay] [26]:[4] and they plotted together to devise a way to arrest Yeshua so they could execute him.
[Matay] [26]:[5] However, they decided not to do it during the celebrations so it wouldn’t cause a big public disturbance.
[Matay] [26]:[6] Meanwhile Yeshua (Jesus; Grk. Yesus) arrived in Beyt-Ania (Bethany) at the house of Shim’on (Simon) who had previously had leprosy.
[Matay] [26]:[7] A woman inside the house came up to him carrying a carved alabaster flask of very expensive lotion, which she poured over his head as he was seated,
[Matay] [26]:[8] but some of his followers were upset when they saw this, and complained, “Why all this waste?
[Matay] [26]:[9] That could have been sold and raised a lot of money to give to the poor.”
[Matay] [26]:[10] But Yeshua knew what they were saying and responded, “Why are you all causing problems for this woman, because she did something beautiful for me.
[Matay] [26]:[11] You’ll always have the poor with you, but you won’t always have me around.
[Matay] [26]:[12] This woman put this lotion on my body in a sense as a burial spice.
[Matay] [26]:[13] I can assure you all that wherever the good message about me is retold anywhere in the world, this woman and what she did will also be mentioned as a memorial to her.”
[Matay] [26]:[14] Then one of the twelve named Yehudah (Judas; Grk. Yudas) Iskariot went to the chief priests
[Matay] [26]:[15] and asked, How much are you willing to pay me if I hand him over to you all?” They offered thirty silver coins
[Matay] [26]:[16] so from then on, he was looking for an opportunity to hand him over.
[Matay] [26]:[17] On the first day of the Flat Bread Celebration, the Yeshua’s (Jesus; Grk. Yesus) apprentices approached him and asked, “Where do you want us to prepare the pass-over meal for you?”
[Matay] [26]:[18] “Go into the city to so-and-so,” answered Yeshua, “and tell him that the teacher said, ‘My time is getting close, but I’ll celebrate the pass-over meal with you, along with my apprentices.’ ”
[Matay] [26]:[19] So the apprentices did as Yeshua had instructed them, and then they prepared the pass-over meal.
[Matay] [26]:[20] That evening as Yeshua was sitting with the twelve,
[Matay] [26]:[21] he said to them while they were still eating, “I can assure you that one of you is going to turn me in.”
[Matay] [26]:[22] They were very upset and one by one they asked him, “Surely it won’t be me, master?”
[Matay] [26]:[23] “It’s the one who dipped his bread into the bowl at the same time as I did,” Yeshua answered. “He’s the one who’s going to turn me in.
[Matay] [26]:[24] It’s true that the son of humanity is going to suffer what has already been written about, but on the other hand, the end won’t be good for the man who turns him in, in fact it would have been better for him if he’d never been born.”
[Matay] [26]:[25] “Surely it won’t be me, honoured teacher?” asked Yehudah (Judas; Grk. Yudas), the one who would hand him in. “You said it,” he replied.
[Matay] [26]:[26] Then during the meal, Yeshua (Jesus; Grk. Yesus) took some bread and blessed it, then he broke it into pieces and gave it to his apprentices, saying, “Take this and eat it—it’s my body.”
[Matay] [26]:[27] Then he took a cup of wine and after giving thanks, he shared it with them saying, “Everyone drink some,
[Matay] [26]:[28] because this is my blood of the agreement which is about to be poured out for the forgiveness of the sins of many people.
[Matay] [26]:[29] I can assure you all that I certainly won’t drink this pass-over wine again until I’m able to drink it together with you all in my father’s kingdom.”
[Matay] [26]:[30] Then they sang some songs before heading out of the city to the Mt. of Olives.
[Matay] [26]:[31] Then Yeshua (Jesus; Grk. Yesus) told them, “All of you will flounder tonight concerning me, because it’s been written, ‘I’ll strike the shepherd and the flock will be scattered.’
[Matay] [26]:[32] But after I come back to life, I’ll go to Galil ahead of you all.”
[Matay] [26]:[33] “Even if all the others flounder,” answered Kefa (Peter; Grk. Petros), “I won’t.”
[Matay] [26]:[34] “I can assure you,” responded Yeshua, “that you’ll disown me three times tonight before the rooster crows in the morning.”
[Matay] [26]:[35] “Even if I have to die with you,” said Kefa, “I’d certainly never disown you,” and all the other apprentices said likewise.
[Matay] [26]:[36] Then they went together to a property named Gethsaimanai where he told his apprentices to sit down while he went on a little further to pray.
[Matay] [26]:[37] He took Kefa (Peter; Grk. Petros), Ya’akov (Jacob), and Yohan (John; Grk. Yoannes) with him, and then he was struck by feelings of sorrow and distress
[Matay] [26]:[38] and told them, “My soul is deathly sad. Stay here and look out for me.”
[Matay] [26]:[39] He went on a little further, and knelt with his face to the ground, saying, “My father, if it’s possible, let me avoid this suffering. However, it’s not what I want because I want to do what you want.”
[Matay] [26]:[40] Then he went back to the apprentices, but found them napping and said to Kefa, “Weren’t you even able to stay awake for an hour for me?
[Matay] [26]:[41] Stay alert and pray so that you all don’t fall into temptation. Your spirits are eager, but your endurance is lacking.”
[Matay] [26]:[42] Then he went off a second time and prayed, “My father, if this can’t be done any other way than me having to suffer, then I’ll submit to your will.”
[Matay] [26]:[43] Returning again, he found the apprentices sleeping because they were very tired.
[Matay] [26]:[44] So he left them there and went back a third time, praying in the same way.
[Matay] [26]:[45] Then he went back to his apprentices and told them, “You’re all sleeping to get some rest? But look, it’s time now, and the son of humanity is about to be handed over to sinners.
[Matay] [26]:[46] Get up—we need to move. The one about to turn me in is coming.”
[Matay] [26]:[47] While he was still speaking, Yehudah (Judas; Grk. Yudas), one of the twelve, came and he was accompanied by a large crowd from the chief priests and local elders, and they were carrying swords and clubs.
[Matay] [26]:[48] The one who was turning him in had prearranged a sign that he would kiss the one that they should arrest.
[Matay] [26]:[49] He walked straight up to Yeshua (Jesus; Grk. Yesus) and said, “Greetings, my honoured teacher,” and he kissed him.
[Matay] [26]:[50] “Friend,” Yeshua asked, “why have you come?” Then they came up to Yeshua, and grabbed and arrested him.
[Matay] [26]:[51] But wow, one of Yeshua’s group put out a hand to stop them, then drew his sword and struck at the chief priest’s slave, cutting off his ear.
[Matay] [26]:[52] “Put your sword back in its sheath,” Yeshua said, “because those who fight with the sword, die by the sword.
[Matay] [26]:[53] Don’t you realise that I could just ask my father and he would place over a dozen divisions of heavenly soldiers here in front of me,
[Matay] [26]:[54] however then the scriptures that tell what will happen wouldn’t get fulfilled.”
[Matay] [26]:[55] Then turning to the crowds, Yeshua said, “So you all came out with swords and clubs as if you were arresting a thief?
[Matay] [26]:[56] I was sitting, teaching every day in the temple but you didn’t arrest me there.”
[Matay] [26]:[57] Then the ones who had arrested Yeshua (Jesus; Grk. Yesus) led him away to Kayafa (Caiaphas; Grk. Kaiafas) the chief priest, where the religious teachers and the local elders had gathered together.
[Matay] [26]:[58] Kefa (Peter; Grk. Petros) followed along from a distance, and went inside to the chief priest’s courtyard, where he sat with the attendants and waited to see what would happen.
[Matay] [26]:[59] The chief priests and the whole council tried to find people who would bring false accusations against Yeshua so they could sentence him to death,
[Matay] [26]:[60] but even though many people wanted to try, they couldn’t find anyone suitable. Eventually, two others came up
[Matay] [26]:[61] and said, “We heard this man say, ‘I’m able to demolish God’s temple and rebuild it in three days.’ ”
[Matay] [26]:[62] So the chief priest stood and asked Yeshua, “Don’t you have any respond to what these men are accusing you of?”
[Matay] [26]:[63] But Yeshua stayed silent, so then the chief priest asked him, “I order you by the living God to tell us if you’re the messiah, the son of God.”
[Matay] [26]:[64] “You said it,” Yeshua responded. “However, I can tell you all that from now on, you’ll see the son of humanity sitting beside God in the position of power and coming in the clouds in the sky.”
[Matay] [26]:[65] Then the chief priest tore his robes and said, “He belittled God. Why would we need more witnesses after that? See here, you all heard him slander God.
[Matay] [26]:[66] What do you all think now? “He should get the death penalty,” they answered.
[Matay] [26]:[67] Then they spat in Yeshua’s face and they beat him and slapped him
[Matay] [26]:[68] saying, “Prophesy to us, messiah. Who was it that just slapped you?”
[Matay] [26]:[69] Meanwhile Kefa (Peter; Grk. Petros) was sitting outside in the courtyard when a servant girl went up to him and said, “You were one of the ones with Yeshua (Jesus; Grk. Yesus) from Galil.”
[Matay] [26]:[70] But Kefa disowned Yeshua in front of them all saying, “I’ve got no idea what you’re talking about.”
[Matay] [26]:[71] Then he went out the gate, but someone else saw him and she told the others, “This man was with Yeshua from Nazaret.”
[Matay] [26]:[72] Again, Kefa disowned Yeshua with an oath, “I don’t even know the guy.”
[Matay] [26]:[73] A little while later, another person stood up and went to Kefa, “You must be one of them because we can tell by your accent.”
[Matay] [26]:[74] Kefa began to curse and promise, “I don’t know that man.” Just then the rooster crowed

[Markos] [3]:[29] But anyone who speaks against the Holy Spirit can never be forgiven, but is eternally responsible for their sin.”

[Markos] [4]:[1] Again Yeshua (Jesus; Grk. Yesus) started teaching by the edge of the lake. A huge crowd gathered around him, but he had boarded a boat that was floating in the water, and all the people were there on the shore.

[Markos] [4]:[3] “Listen. Once there was a farmer who went to spread some seed.
[Markos] [4]:[4] As he spread it, some landed on the path, and the birds came and fed on it.
[Markos] [4]:[5] Some landed on a rocky part without a lot of soil, and it quickly sprouted in the warm, shallow soil,
[Markos] [4]:[6] but when the sun came up, it dried out because the roots weren’t deep, and so it just withered up.
[Markos] [4]:[7] Some of the seed landed in a thistle patch, and the thistles grew and choked it out, so the plants never bore a crop.
[Markos] [4]:[8] But some seed landed in fertile soil and it bore a harvest—some of it multiplying thirty times, some sixty, and some a hundred times.”

[Markos] [4]:[14] The person spreading seed is spreading the good message,
[Markos] [4]:[15] and there are some along the path where the good message is being spread, who hear, but Satan turns up immediately and snatches the message that had been planted in them.
[Markos] [4]:[16] Similarly, there’s some seed that falls onto rocky places where the people who hear the good message happily accept it,
[Markos] [4]:[17] but don’t make strong roots—just temporary changes. So when they get mocked or attacked about accepting the good message, they quickly stumble.
[Markos] [4]:[18] Others are the ones where the seed was spread among the thistles. They heard the good message,
[Markos] [4]:[19] but contemporary topics, or the lure of money, or the appetite for other things, choke their good intentions and the message becomes unfruitful in them.
[Markos] [4]:[20] But lastly, the seed that landed on the good soil represents the people who hear the good message, accept it, and are fruitful thirty, sixty, or even a hundred times over.”
[Markos] [4]:[21] Then Yeshua (Jesus; Grk. Yesus) told them, “Obviously no one goes and gets a lamp, and then puts it under a basket or under the bed, but rather they place it somewhere higher on a stand.
[Markos] [4]:[22] You see, nothing is hidden that won’t eventually be disclosed, and there’s no secret that won’t eventually be revealed.
[Markos] [4]:[23] Anyone who wants to understand must listen carefully,”
[Markos] [4]:[24] and he continued, “Take care what you listen to. How much you all judge others, so too will judgement be handed out to you, and even more. DOUBLE-CHECK

[Markos] [4]:[26] And then, “God’s kingdom is like a person throwing some seed onto the ground.

[Markos] [4]:[28] The earth is designed to multiply the seed: first a sprout appears, then a bigger plant, and then the full head of grain.
[Markos] [4]:[29] Then when it’s ripe, the harvester is sent in because it’s ready for harvest.”

[Markos] [8]:[33] Yeshua turned back and looked at the others, then reprimanded Kefa, “Stand back, Satan—you’re applying human values instead of considering God’s plan.”
[Markos] [8]:[34] Calling out to them and to the crowd, he said, “Anyone who wants to follow me must first put aside their own desires and then follow me—even through very difficult times.
[Markos] [8]:[35] Anyone who worries about saving their own life will lose it, but anyone who gives their life due to following me and my teaching will save their life.

[Markos] [8]:[37] What can someone offer in order to buy a home for their soul?
[Markos] [8]:[38] Yes, anyone who’s ashamed of me and my message in front of this adulterous and sinful generation, the son of humanity will likewise be ashamed of them when he comes clearly displaying his father’s greatness and bringing the holy messengers.”

[Markos] [12]:[3] But the tenants grabbed the slave and beat him up, then sent him back empty-handed.

[Markos] [12]:[6] But the owner still had his one, dearly loved son, so finally he sent him to go, thinking that they would now be convinced because it was his son.

[Markos] [12]:[21] So then the second brother took her in, but again died childless, and then too the third.
[Markos] [12]:[22] Eventually all seven brothers died childless, and finally the woman also died.
[Markos] [12]:[23] Now, at the resurrection of the dead, which brother will she be the wife of, because at some point, she was married to each of the seven of them?”
[Markos] [12]:[24] “Actually you’re all quite wrong,” Yeshua answered, “because you ignore the scriptures and also because you haven’t experienced God’s power.
[Markos] [12]:[25] When the dead do come back to life, they won’t be getting engaged or married, but will be like the messengers in the heavens.
[Markos] [12]:[26] But as for the state of those who’ve died, didn’t you all read in the scriptures about Mosheh when God spoke to him in front of the burning thorn bush and said, ‘I am the god of Avraham and the god of Yitshak (Isaac) and the god of Ya’akov’ (Jacob)?
[Markos] [12]:[27] So God is not the god of the dead, but of the living. You Saddoukaios (Sadducees) are very wrong!”
[Markos] [12]:[28] Then one of the religious teachers who had heard their question and Yeshua’s (Jesus; Grk. Yesus) excellent answer, came closer and asked, “Which of God’s commands is the most important?”
[Markos] [12]:[29] “Well,” Yeshua answered, “the most important is this: ‘Listen, Yisrael (Israel). Our God Yahweh is our master.
[Markos] [12]:[30] You must love Yahweh God with all your heart and all your soul, and with all your mind and all your strength.’
[Markos] [12]:[31] And the second is: ‘Love your neighbour like you look after yourself.’ There’s no other commands more important than these.”
[Markos] [12]:[32] The teacher replied to Yeshua, “Yes, teacher, you’re quite right saying there’s only one God and no other,
[Markos] [12]:[33] and saying that we should love him with all our heart and all our intelligence and all our strength, and to be loving our neighbours like we look after ourselves, and all this is more important than all the required temple offerings and sacrifices.”
[Markos] [12]:[34] When Yeshua saw that he’d given such a thoughtful answer, he said, “You’re very close to God’s kingdom!” After that, no one else dared to ask Yeshua any more questions.
[Markos] [12]:[35] Later when Yeshua (Jesus; Grk. Yesus) was teaching in the temple, he asked the people, “How is it that the teachers here say that the messiah is a descendant of King David?
[Markos] [12]:[36] Because David himself said under the inspiration of the holy spirit, ‘Yahweh told my master, “Sit there in the position of honour until I can conquer your enemies.” ’
[Markos] [12]:[37] If David calls the messiah his master, how can the messiah possibly be David’s descendant?” The large crowd was very interested to hear everything that Yeshua had to say.
[Markos] [12]:[38] As Yeshua (Jesus; Grk. Yesus) continued teaching, he said, “Watch out for those religious teachers who like to wear fancy robes and be greeted in the square,
[Markos] [12]:[39] and have the best seats at meetings and the best places at dinners.
[Markos] [12]:[40] Those people trick widows out of their properties, but offer long prayers to cover it up. They will be getting a stricter judgement than others.”
[Markos] [12]:[41] As he sat down in front of the temple treasury, Yeshua (Jesus; Grk. Yesus) watched the crowd as they threw coins into the dish, and some rich people were donating quite valuable silver coins.
[Markos] [12]:[42] Then an impoverished widow came and threw in two small copper coins.
[Markos] [12]:[43] Yeshua called his followers and told them, “Honestly, that hard-up widow gave more than all the others.
[Markos] [12]:[44] You see, most people donate from their excess wealth, but this woman even gave some of the small amount that she needed to live on.”
[Markos] [13]:[1] As they were leaving the temple area, one of Yeshua’s (Jesus; Grk. Yesus) followers noted, “Teacher, look at those large, chiselled stones and those beautiful buildings that they’ve been made into.”
[Markos] [13]:[2] “Yes, incredible buildings,” Yeshua responded, “but the time will come when they’re torn down—not a single piece of stone will be left sitting in its place.”
[Markos] [13]:[3] Later when they were over on the Mt. of Olives overlooking the temple, Kefa (Peter; Grk. Petros) and Ya’akov (James; Grk. Yakobos) and Yohan (John; Grk. Yoannes) and Andreas were with Yeshua (Jesus; Grk. Yesus) and asked
[Markos] [13]:[4] when all that destruction would happen, and what indications there would be that it would be about to happen.
[Markos] [13]:[5] But Yeshua told them, “Be careful so you all aren’t misled by others.
[Markos] [13]:[6] Plenty of people will say that they’re coming because they were sent by me, or that they are me, and they’ll mislead many others.
[Markos] [13]:[7] Also, whenever you all hear about wars or about battles about to begin, don’t be worried—those things will certainly happen, but there’s more to follow.
[Markos] [13]:[8] Countries will take up arms against other countries, and kingdoms against other kingdoms. There’ll be earthquakes in many places and there’ll be famines, but those will be just like the beginning of birth pains.
[Markos] [13]:[9] “So be careful. You’ll be turned over to local councils for questioning, will be whipped in the Jewish meeting halls, and will be stood in front of governors and kings because of following me. However, you’ll be able to present your life stories to them
[Markos] [13]:[10] and it’s right that the good message first be proclaimed to every people group.
[Markos] [13]:[11] But whenever they take you all along to hand you over, don’t worry in advance about what you’re going to say to defend yourselves, but wait until the hearing proceeds and speak what you are given then, because then it won’t be you speaking, but God’s spirit.
[Markos] [13]:[12] In those times, a brother will report on his brother to have him executed, and a father report on his child, and children will be encouraged to report on their own parents and then they’ll be executed as a result.
[Markos] [13]:[13] Then every one will hate you all because they hate my name, but anyone who endures to the end will be saved.
[Markos] [13]:[14] “But whenever you all see the most horrible thing that drives people from God, standing where it shouldn’t be (and you readers should understand that), then anyone in Yehudah (Judea) should flee into the hills,
[Markos] [13]:[15] and anyone upstairs looking outside shouldn’t come down into the bedrooms to get anything,
[Markos] [13]:[16] and anyone working outside shouldn’t go back inside to get a change of clothes.
[Markos] [13]:[17] It will be extremely difficult for pregnant women and for mothers who are breast-feeding their children in those days.
[Markos] [13]:[18] Just pray that it won’t happen in the winter,
[Markos] [13]:[19] because those days will be terrible like nothing that’s ever happened before, all the way back to when God created the world, right until the present time, and won’t ever happen again.
[Markos] [13]:[20] If Yahweh hadn’t shortened that time, no humans would even survive, but he shortened that time so that the chosen ones could be saved.
[Markos] [13]:[21] So don’t believe it if you all hear someone say, ‘Look, the messiah has arrived here.’ or ‘There’s the one that God has sent.’
[Markos] [13]:[22] Plenty of fake messiahs and deceiving prophets will certainly come and even do things that humans can’t normally do, so much so that even the chosen ones would defect if that were possible.
[Markos] [13]:[23] So watch out, but I’ve warned you in advance about all of that.
[Markos] [13]:[24] “After those very difficult times, the sun will go dark and the moon won’t shine at night.
[Markos] [13]:[25] The stars will fall down out of the sky and the powers in the heavens will be shaken up.
[Markos] [13]:[26] Then the people will see the son of humanity in the clouds coming with incredible power and brightness.
[Markos] [13]:[27] He’ll send the messengers out to collect all the chosen people from the four corners of the world—from everywhere between the earth and the sky.
[Markos] [13]:[28] “So learn a lesson from fig trees—whenever the branches green up and start sprouting leaves, then everyone knows that summer is close.
[Markos] [13]:[29] So too whenever you see all those things happening, you know that the end of this current world is close.
[Markos] [13]:[30] I can assure you all that the generation of people who see those things won’t die off before those latter things happen.
[Markos] [13]:[31] The sky and the planet might collapse, but my teachings will never become irrelevant.
[Markos] [13]:[32] “But as for the date or time when all that will happen, only the father knows that—even the son and the messengers in heaven don’t know.
[Markos] [13]:[33] So watch out, observe current events, and be praying, because you won’t know exactly when all this will happen.
[Markos] [13]:[34] It can all be compared to a man who was about to leave his home and go on a trip. Before he leaves, he gives certain jobs and responsibilities to his various slaves, and instructs his security guard to stay alert.
[Markos] [13]:[35] So you all watch and stay alert, because you don’t know when the master of the house might return—perhaps one evening or at midnight, or at dawn or maybe mid-morning.
[Markos] [13]:[36] You certainly don’t want to be caught napping when he comes,
[Markos] [13]:[37] and what I’m telling all of you now, I tell everyone: stay alert and watch.”
[Markos] [14]:[1] Now it was two days before the Passover Feast and the Flat Bread Celebration, and the chief priests and the religious teachers were trying to figure out how they could have Yeshua (Jesus; Grk. Yesus) set up so they could arrest him and have him executed,
[Markos] [14]:[2] but they knew that the Feast wouldn’t be a good time because the people would protest in Yeshua’s favour.
[Markos] [14]:[3] Meanwhile, Yeshua (Jesus; Grk. Yesus) was in Beyt-Ania (Bethany) at the home of Shim’on (Simon) who had previously had leprosy. Yeshua was sitting there when a woman came in with a hand-crafted container of very expensive fragrant lotion. Breaking open the sealed flask, she poured the fragrant oil over Yeshua’s head.
[Markos] [14]:[4] Immediately some in the room started quietly grumbling about the extravagant waste,
[Markos] [14]:[5] then they scolded the woman because a flask of genuine lotion like that could easily fetch almost a year’s wages if it was sold.
[Markos] [14]:[6] But Yeshua spoke up, “What do you think you’re all doing abusing her—leave her alone! She’s done something very good for me.
[Markos] [14]:[7] You’ll always have poor people around, and you can help them whenever you want to, but I won’t be around forever.
[Markos] [14]:[8] She has performed the traditional anointing of my body in advance of my burial,
[Markos] [14]:[9] and I can assure you all, that wherever the good message is proclaimed around the world, what she has done today will be part of the story and she’ll be remembered for it.”
[Markos] [14]:[10] Then Yehudah (Judas; Grk. Yudas) Iskariot, one of Yeshua’s (Jesus; Grk. Yesus) twelve apprentices, visited the chief priests to offer to hand Yeshua over to them.
[Markos] [14]:[11] When they heard that, they were very pleased and promised to pay him well, and Yehudah asked them about the most convenient way for them to get hold of Yeshua.
[Markos] [14]:[12] On the first day of the Flat Bread Celebration when the lambs would be slaughtered ready for the special Passover meal, Yeshua’s (Jesus; Grk. Yesus) apprentices asked him, “Where do you want us to get everything ready for our Passover meal?”
[Markos] [14]:[13] So Yeshua sent off two of them with these instructions, “Go into town and a man carrying a pitcher of water will meet you there. Just follow him
[Markos] [14]:[14] until he goes into a house. Then find the owner of the house and tell him that the teacher wants to know the location of the guestroom where he and his apprentices can celebrate their Passover meal.
[Markos] [14]:[15] He’ll show you a large, furnished room upstairs—that’s where you can get everything ready.”
[Markos] [14]:[16] So the two of them went off into the town, and everything happened there exactly as Yeshua had told them, and so they prepared the special meal there.
[Markos] [14]:[17] As the evening approached, Yeshua (Jesus; Grk. Yesus) went in for dinner with his twelve apprentices.
[Markos] [14]:[18] As they were sitting around eating, he told them, “I’ll tell you frankly that one of you eating with me here will hand me over to be arrested.”
[Markos] [14]:[19] That upset them, and several of them individually asked, “Surely it couldn’t be me?”
[Markos] [14]:[20] Then he continued, “It’s one of you twelve—the one who dips his bread in the sauce at the same time as me.
[Markos] [14]:[21] Indeed it’s written in the scriptures that the son of humanity will be arrested, but on the other hand, what a tragedy it’ll be for the one who hands him over—in fact it would be better for that man if he was never born.”
[Markos] [14]:[22] As they carried on eating, he took some bread, blessed God, broke it apart and gave a piece to them, saying, “Take this bread—it’s my body.”
[Markos] [14]:[23] Then he picked up a cup, gave thanks to God, and passed it around so they could each drink from it,
[Markos] [14]:[24] saying, “That is the blood of my contract that will be poured out for many people.
[Markos] [14]:[25] I can assure you all that I won’t drink anything made from grapes until I drink new juice in God’s kingdom.”
[Markos] [14]:[26] Then after they’d sung some songs, they left the town and went across to the Mt. of Olives.
[Markos] [14]:[27] Then Yeshua (Jesus; Grk. Yesus) continued his teaching, “All of you will stumble because it’s written in the scriptures: ‘I’ll strike down the shepherd and the sheep will get scattered.’
[Markos] [14]:[28] But after I come back to life, I’ll go on ahead of you all back to Galil.”
[Markos] [14]:[29] But Kefa (Peter; Grk. Petros) contradicted him, “Even if everyone else stumbles, I won’t!”
[Markos] [14]:[30] “I can assure you,” Yeshua responded, “that you’ll renounce me three times this very night, before the rooster crows early tomorrow morning.”
[Markos] [14]:[31] But Kefa argued forcibly, “Even if I had to die with you, I would never disown you!” And all the others said similar things.
[Markos] [14]:[32] They walked along until they came to a piece of land called Gethsaimanai where Yeshua (Jesus; Grk. Yesus) told his apprentices to sit down while he prayed.
[Markos] [14]:[33] He took Kefa (Peter; Grk. Petros) and Ya’akov (James; Grk. Yakobos) and Yohan (John; Grk. Yoannes) further in with him where he stared off in a daze but was obviously very distressed.
[Markos] [14]:[34] He told the three of them, “My soul is deathly sad! You guys just stay here and keep alert.”
[Markos] [14]:[35] He went ahead a little way, where he knelt on the ground with his head down and prayed—asking if it was possible to avoid what was ahead of him.
[Markos] [14]:[36] But he said, “Father, I know that you can do anything. Let me avoid this suffering, but yes I do know, it doesn’t matter what I want but rather what you’ve planned.”
[Markos] [14]:[37] Then he went back and found the others sleeping. “Shim’on (Simon), are you asleep?” he asked Kefa. “Couldn’t you stay awake even for a single hour?
[Markos] [14]:[38] You all need to stay alert and be careful not to give into temptation. I know your spirits are enthusiastic on one hand, but it’s still easy to give in to the moment.”
[Markos] [14]:[39] Then he went further in again and prayed as before,
[Markos] [14]:[40] but when he returned again, he found them all asleep because they were tired, but they couldn’t really find any excuse to give.
[Markos] [14]:[41] The third time that Yeshua (Jesus; Grk. Yesus) returned, he said to them, “Ah, you’re all sleeping again and having a good rest. It’s well-earned but look, the time has come for the son of humanity to be handed over to evil men.
[Markos] [14]:[42] Come on—get up—we need to go! Look, the one who’ll hand me over is almost here.”
[Markos] [14]:[43] Even while Yeshua (Jesus; Grk. Yesus) was still speaking, Yehudah (Judas; Grk. Yudas) (one of his twelve apprentices) reached him, followed by a crowd that included some of the chief priests, the religious teachers, and the Jewish elders—many armed with swords and clubs.
[Markos] [14]:[44] Yehudah had prearranged a signal with them that the one he greeted with a kiss, they should grab that person and lead him away under guard.
[Markos] [14]:[45] So he walked right up to Yeshua and said, “My honoured teacher,” and greeted him with a kiss.
[Markos] [14]:[46] Then the others with him grabbed Yeshua and secured him.
[Markos] [14]:[47] But one of the ones with Yeshua that was beside him, drew his sword and struck one of the chief priest’s slaves—cutting off the man’s ear.
[Markos] [14]:[48] Yeshua spoke to the crowd, “Did you all bring swords and clubs to try to capture me like you’d chase down a thief?
[Markos] [14]:[49] I was teaching there in the temple every day and you could have arrested me, but it’s happened this way to ensure that what’s written in scriptures will be fulfilled.”
[Markos] [14]:[50] Meanwhile, the others who’d been with Yeshua had taken off.
[Markos] [14]:[51] One young fellow was wearing a single linen robe, and when the crowd tried to grab him,
