[Markos] [14]:[53] The guards led Yeshua (Jesus; Grk. Yesus) away to the chief priest’s residence, and all the chief priests and the elders and the religious teachers gathered there also.
[Markos] [14]:[54] Kefa (Peter; Grk. Petros) followed along from a distance and went in as far as the courtyard of that residence, where he joined the servants who were sitting around the fire keeping warm.
[Markos] [14]:[55] Inside, the chief priests and all the council were trying to establish a case against Yeshua so he could be sentenced to death, but they weren’t coming up with anything.
[Markos] [14]:[56] Several people were making up charges against him, but none of the accusers’ stories agreed with each other.
[Markos] [14]:[57] Eventually some of them stood up and offered this false charge:
[Markos] [14]:[58] “We heard him say that he would demolish this temple made by many labourers, and within three days he’d build another one without any helpers.”
[Markos] [14]:[59] But even then, they couldn’t get their accusations to align with each other.
[Markos] [14]:[60] Nevertheless, the chief priest in the middle of the council stood up and asked Yeshua, “Aren’t you going to defend yourself? These men are accusing you of those things.”
[Markos] [14]:[61] But Yeshua didn’t say anything, so the chief priest asked again, “Is it true that you’re the chosen one that God promised to send—the son of the blessed God?”
[Markos] [14]:[62] “I am.” Yeshua replied, “and you’ll all see the son of humanity sitting in the honoured position by the powerful God and coming through the clouds in the sky.”
[Markos] [14]:[63] Then the chief priest tore his own robe to show his disgust and shouted, “We certainly don’t need any more witnesses now!
[Markos] [14]:[64] You yourselves all heard him insult God. What sentence does that deserve?” So the leaders there agreed that Yeshua needed to be sentenced to death.
[Markos] [14]:[65] Then various people started spitting on him, and blindfolding him and beating him saying, “Ha, tell us who that was!” Even the servants joined in to slap him.
[Markos] [14]:[66] Meanwhile, Kefa (Peter; Grk. Petros) was down in the courtyard when one of the chief priest’s servant girls came outside,
[Markos] [14]:[67] and seeing Kefa warming himself, she looked more closely and said, “Hey, you were with that Yeshua (Jesus; Grk. Yesus) from Nazaret (Nazareth)!”
[Markos] [14]:[68] But he denied it, “I don’t know him and I don’t know why you think I would!” Then he moved away from the fire.
[Markos] [14]:[69] But the girl that had seen him said to some of the others standing around, “That guy’s one of them.”
[Markos] [14]:[70] But again Kefa denied it. A little while later, some of those standing there said the same thing to him, “You must be one of them because you’re from Galil.”
[Markos] [14]:[71] Now Kefa started swearing and cursing and said, “I’ve never even met that fellow that you’re all talking about!”
[Markos] [14]:[72] Right then the rooster crowed for the second time and Kefa remembered now what Yeshua (Jesus; Grk. Yesus) had told him—how he would renounce Yeshua three times before the rooster crowed—and he broke down and cried.
[Markos] [15]:[1] First thing in the morning, the chief priests called a meeting with the elders and the religious teachers and all the council, and they ordered that Yeshua (Jesus; Grk. Yesus) be tied up and taken over to Governor Pilatos (Pilate).
[Markos] [15]:[2] There Pilatos asked him, “Are you the king of the Yehudim (Jews)?” “You said it,” replied Yeshua.
[Markos] [15]:[3] Then the chief priests started hurling accusations against Yeshua,
[Markos] [15]:[4] so Pilatos asked him again, “Don’t you have anything to say? Listen to all those accusations they’re making against you.”
[Markos] [15]:[5] But Pilatos was astounded that Yeshua didn’t answer any further.
[Markos] [15]:[6] Now at time of the Jewish Passover, at their request, Pilatos (Pilate) would normally pardon one prisoner for them.
[Markos] [15]:[7] There was another prisoner at that time named Bar-Aba (Grk. Barabbas), who was an activist arrested for murder.
[Markos] [15]:[8] By now the crowd had arrived, and asked Pilatos to release a prisoner as usual at Passover,
[Markos] [15]:[9] so he asked them, “Do you all want me to release the King of the Yehudim (Jews) for you?”
[Markos] [15]:[10] (That was because Pilatos was well aware that the chief priests had brought Yeshua (Jesus; Grk. Yesus) because they were jealous of his popularity.)
[Markos] [15]:[11] But the chief priests stirred up the crowd to start saying that it was Bar-Aba that they wanted released,
[Markos] [15]:[12] so Pilatos asked again, “Then what should I do with this man that you call the King of the Yehudim?”
[Markos] [15]:[13] The crowd yelled back, “Execute him on a post.”
[Markos] [15]:[14] “What has he even done wrong?” Pilatos demanded. But they just yelled louder, “Execute him on a post!”
[Markos] [15]:[15] Now Pilatos wanted to placate the crowd, so he had Bar-Aba released while he had Yeshua flogged and then handed over to the execution squad.
[Markos] [15]:[16] So the soldiers led Yeshua (Jesus; Grk. Yesus) inside the palace that was the governor’s residence, and called in the rest of the battalion.
[Markos] [15]:[17] They mocked Yeshua by dressing him in a kingly robe, and after someone twisted some thorns together into a mock crown, they pressed it onto his head,
[Markos] [15]:[18] and began saluting him, “Greetings, king of the Yehudim (Jews).”
[Markos] [15]:[19] They took turns whacking his head with a stick and spitting on him, while others knelt down in front of him and pretended to be bowing to him.
[Markos] [15]:[20] After they’d finished having fun mocking him, they took the purple robe off him, and put his own robe back on him. Then they led him outside towards the execution area.
[Markos] [15]:[21] As they walked out of the city, they came across a man coming in from the country. He was Shim’on (Simon) from Kurainai (Cyrene) (Kurainai—the father of Alexandros (Alexander) and Rufos), and the soldiers forced him to carry the execution post,
[Markos] [15]:[22] and so they all arrived at Golgotha (which means ‘Place of the skull’).
[Markos] [15]:[23] There the soldiers went to give some spiced wine to Yeshua (Jesus; Grk. Yesus), but he declined it.
[Markos] [15]:[24] So they carried out the execution, taking Yeshua’s clothes and drawing straws to see who would get what.
[Markos] [15]:[25] By now it was around 9am, and they affixed Yeshua to the post.
[Markos] [15]:[26] The charge had been written out and attached at the top: “The king of the Yehudim (Jews).”
[Markos] [15]:[27] That morning, two thieves were also executed there—one on each side of Yeshua.
[Markos] [15]:[28] ◘
[Markos] [15]:[29] As people passed by on that path, they insulted Yeshua, shaking their heads and shouting, “Hoy there! You who reckoned you could demolish the temple and rebuild it in three days,
[Markos] [15]:[30] come down from that post and save yourself.”
[Markos] [15]:[31] Similarly the chief priests and the religious teachers laughed together and mocked, “He did miracles for others, but he can’t even save himself.
[Markos] [15]:[32] Now if that so-called ‘chosen one’ or ‘king of Yisrael’ (Israel) would just come down from there, then we’d be able to believe him.” Even the other two being executed with him were deriding him.
[Markos] [15]:[33] At noon, it got dark everywhere, until around 3pm,
[Markos] [15]:[34] when Yeshua (Jesus; Grk. Yesus) shouted loudly, “My god, my god, why have you abandoned me?”
[Markos] [15]:[35] Some of the people standing nearby thought he was calling the prophet Eliyah (Elijah).
[Markos] [15]:[36] One of them ran, and soaked a sponge in some sour wine, then put it on a stick and held it up for Yeshua to drink, saying, “Hang on. Let’s see if Eliyah does come to get him down.”
[Markos] [15]:[37] But just then, Yeshua uttered a loud cry and exhaled his last breath.
[Markos] [15]:[38] (Back in the temple, the curtain tore down the middle from the top to the bottom.)
[Markos] [15]:[39] When Yeshua died, the Romaios commander who had been standing back watching everything said, “That man was definitely God’s son.”
[Markos] [15]:[40] Further back, there was also a group of women observing everything. They included Miryam (Grk. Maria/Mariam) from Magdala, Miryam the mother of young Ya’akov (James; Grk. Yakobos) and Yoseh, and Salome,
[Markos] [15]:[41] and others who had followed Yeshua around Galil and helped look after him, along with many others who had come down to Yerushalem (Jerusalem) with him.
[Markos] [15]:[42] As evening came, it was now the Preparation Day, i.e., the day before the Rest Day.
[Markos] [15]:[43] Yosef (Joseph) (who’d come from Arimathaia city and one who was waiting for the coming of God’s kingdom), a prominent council member, steeled himself up and went in to see the governor to get permission to transfer Yeshua’s (Jesus; Grk. Yesus) body.
[Markos] [15]:[44] Governor Pilatos (Pilate) didn’t think he’d be dead yet, so he called an army commander to find out if Yeshua had indeed died.
[Markos] [15]:[45] As soon as he found out, he gave Yosef permission,
[Markos] [15]:[46] so Yosef and his companions went and bought some linen burial cloth and then, removing Yeshua’s body from the post, wrapped it in the cloth and placed it in a burial chamber that had been chiselled into a rockface. Then they rolled a rock across the opening.
[Markos] [15]:[47] Others were watching and noted where the body had been laid, including Miryam (Grk. Maria/Mariam) from Magdala and Miryam who was Yoseh’ mother.
[Markos] [16]:[1] After the Rest Day was over, Miryam (Grk. Maria/Mariam) from Magdala, Miryam the mother of Ya’akov (James; Grk. Yakobos), and Salome, all went and bought some traditional burial spices that evening to take to the burial chamber and place with the body.
[Markos] [16]:[2] Then very early on Sunday morning they went to the chamber, arriving just as the sun was rising.
[Markos] [16]:[3] Then they realised that they didn’t have anyone with them to roll the rock away that was covering the entrance.
[Markos] [16]:[4] However when they looked, they saw that the very large rock had already been rolled away,
[Markos] [16]:[5] so they went on into the burial chamber and were totally stunned to find a young man dressed in white, sitting in there at the side.
[Markos] [16]:[6] He assured them, “Don’t be surprised. I know you’re looking for Yeshua (Jesus; Grk. Yesus) from Nazaret (Nazareth), the one who was executed on a post. But see there where his body was—he’s not there, because he came back to life.
[Markos] [16]:[7] So you three should go and tell his apprentices, and Kefa (Peter; Grk. Petros) in particular, that he’s going to go up ahead of you all to Galil and you’ll see him up there, just as he already told you all.”
[Markos] [16]:[8] So they left the chamber and took off running, still stunned and shaking, and too scared to stop and talk to anyone.
[Markos] [16]:[9] After coming back to life early on Sunday morning, Yeshua (Jesus; Grk. Yesus) appeared first to Miryam (Grk. Maria/Mariam) from Magdala. (She was the one that he had once commanded seven demons to leave.)
[Markos] [16]:[10] After leaving him, she went and told his followers who were mourning and weeping at his loss.
[Markos] [16]:[11] But when she told them that he is alive again and that she’d seen him, they simply didn’t believe her.
[Markos] [16]:[12] Later on, Yeshua (Jesus; Grk. Yesus) appeared in a different form to two of his followers on the path as they left Yerushalem (Jerusalem) and headed out to the countryside,
[Markos] [16]:[13] but when they hurried back and told the others, no one believed them.
[Markos] [16]:[14] Later again when the eleven apprentices were sitting around eating, Yeshua (Jesus; Grk. Yesus) appeared in the room and scolded them for not believing and for being so stubborn when they hadn’t believed others who had told them that he’d come back from the dead.
[Markos] [16]:[15] Then he instructed them, “Travel around all the world and tell everyone the good message.
[Markos] [16]:[16] Anyone who believes and gets immersed in water will be saved, however, those who refuse to believe will be condemned to death.
[Markos] [16]:[17] Those who believe will be able to do miracles: they’ll be able to use my authority to command demons to leave and to speak new languages,
[Markos] [16]:[18] and they’ll be able to pick up snakes. If they drink anything poisonous, it won’t hurt them, and they will place their hands on people and make them better.”
[Markos] [16]:[19] When Yeshua (Jesus; Grk. Yesus) had finished speaking, he was lifted up into heaven and seated in the honoured place next to God.
[Markos] [16]:[20] Then his followers went around preaching everywhere, and God worked through them and so they were able to confirm the truth of their preaching by doing miracles.
[Lukas] [1]:[1] Several people attempted to write an account about the events that we’re personally certain of

[Lukas] [1]:[5] It started with the priest Zekaryah (Zechariah; Grk. Zakarias) and his wife Elisheva (Elizabeth; Grk. Elisabet) at the time when Herodes (Herod) was the king of Yehudah (Judea). (Zekaryah was in the priestly division of Aviyah, and Elisheva was also a descendant of Aharon (Aaron).)

[Lukas] [1]:[7] Elisheva had never been able to have a child, so there was just the two of them as they were now getting older.

[Lukas] [1]:[10] A lot of people would be praying outside the temple at the time when the incense was burnt.

[Lukas] [1]:[13] But the messenger spoke, “Don’t be scared Zekaryah, because your request has been listened to, and your wife Elisheva will give birth to a son and you’ll name him Yohan (John; Grk. Yoannes).

[Lukas] [3]:[38] the son of Enosh, the son of Shet (Seth), the son of Adam, the son of God.
[Lukas] [4]:[1] Then Yeshua (Jesus; Grk. Yesus), full of the holy spirit, returned from the Yarden (Jordan) region and was led into the wilderness by the spirit
[Lukas] [4]:[2] where he was tested by the devil for forty days. He didn’t eat anything during that time, and was hungry at the end.
[Lukas] [4]:[3] So the devil told him, “If you’re God’s son, just turn this stone into bread.”
[Lukas] [4]:[4] “It’s been written,” Yeshua replied, “that people don’t live just on food.”
[Lukas] [4]:[5] Then the devil brought him up to a high point and in just a moment of time, showed him the vista of all the kingdoms of the world,
[Lukas] [4]:[6] and he said, “I’ll give you this entire domain and the status of these kingdoms because it’s been given to me, and I can give it to anyone I want,
[Lukas] [4]:[7] so just bow down in front of me and it’ll all be yours.”
[Lukas] [4]:[8] “It’s been written,” Yeshua answered, “that we should only bow down to Yahweh our God and only serve him.”
[Lukas] [4]:[9] Then the devil led him to Yerushalem (Jerusalem) and they stood on the highest part of the temple, where he told him, “If you’re God’s son, throw yourself down from here,
[Lukas] [4]:[10] because it’s written that God will command his messengers to guard you
[Lukas] [4]:[11] and they will carry you in their hands, so you won’t even hurt your foot on a stone.”
[Lukas] [4]:[12] “It’s been written,” Yeshua responded, “that we shouldn’t test Yahweh our God.”
[Lukas] [4]:[13] So after completing every temptation, the devil withdrew from him for a time.
[Lukas] [4]:[14] So then Yeshua (Jesus; Grk. Yesus) returned to Galil in the power of the spirit, and the news about him spread into the surrounding region.
[Lukas] [4]:[15] He started teaching in the Jewish meeting halls (Grk. synagogues) and everyone said how good it was.
[Lukas] [4]:[16] When he got to Nazaret (Nazareth) where he grew up, he went into the Jewish meeting hall as usual on the Rest Day and stood up to do the reading.
[Lukas] [4]:[17] The scroll of the prophet Yeshayah (Isaiah) was handed to him, and opening up the scroll, he found the place where it was written,
[Lukas] [4]:[18] “Yahweh’s spirit is on me, because he has chosen and equipped me to preach the good message to the poor. He has sent me out to proclaim freedom for captives and to restore sight to the blind, and for the oppressed to experience freedom.
[Lukas] [4]:[19] He’s sent me to proclaim that this is the year that Yahweh has chosen.”
[Lukas] [4]:[20] Then after rolling up the scroll and giving it back to the attendant, he sat down to give his commentary and every person in the room was studying him
[Lukas] [4]:[21] as he began to speak, “Today this scripture that you’ve just heard has been fulfilled.”
[Lukas] [4]:[22] Later everyone was telling others about him, and they were marvelling at his messages displaying God’s grace, and they asked each other, “Isn’t this Yosef’s (Joseph) son from down the road?”
[Lukas] [4]:[23] Then Yeshua (Jesus; Grk. Yesus) answered them, “I’m sure you’ll all be telling me that parable about the doctor who needed to heal himself, because you’ll be wanting me to do here in my hometown what I did in Kafarnaoum (Capernaum).
[Lukas] [4]:[24] I can assure you all that no prophet is accepted by his own hometown.
[Lukas] [4]:[25] There were certainly many widows in Yisrael (Israel) in the days of Eliyah (Elijah) when God stopped the rain for three and a half years and caused a terrible famine.
[Lukas] [4]:[26] But Eliyah wasn’t sent to any of them—rather he was sent to a foreign widow in Tserefat in the Tsidon (Sidon) region.
[Lukas] [4]:[27] Also there were many people in Yisrael with leprosy in the days of the prophet Elisha and none of them were healed, but only Na’aman from Aram (Syria).”
[Lukas] [4]:[28] By now everyone in the Jewish meeting hall that heard this was furious
[Lukas] [4]:[29] and they all stood up, planning to throw him out of the city. They led him to the edge of the hill that their town was built on, intending to throw him over the edge,
[Lukas] [4]:[30] but somehow he just moved through the middle of them and left.
[Lukas] [4]:[31] After that, Yeshua (Jesus; Grk. Yesus) went to Kafarnaoum (Capernaum), another town in Galil, and taught in the meeting hall there on the Rest Days.
[Lukas] [4]:[32] They were amazed at his teaching, because he presented his message with authority.
[Lukas] [4]:[33] One week there was a man at the Jewish meeting hall with a demon spirit and he yelled out,
[Lukas] [4]:[34] “Ha! What do we have in common with you, Yeshua the man from Nazaret (Nazareth)? Did you come here to destroy us? I know who you are—you’re the holy one from God.”
[Lukas] [4]:[35] Yeshua rebuked the demon, saying, “Be quiet! Now come out of him!” Then the demon threw the man to the floor right in the middle of them, and came out of him, and left him feeling perfectly fine.
[Lukas] [4]:[36] This amazed everyone and they started asking each other, “What is this command that has such authority and power that he orders evil spirits around and they come out?”
[Lukas] [4]:[37] After that, the reports of what he’d done were passed around to every part of the surrounding region.
[Lukas] [4]:[38] After getting up and leaving the Jewish meeting hall, Yeshua (Jesus; Grk. Yesus) went to Shim’on’s (Simon) home where Shim’on’s mother-in-law had been struck with a high fever and they asked Yeshua about it.
[Lukas] [4]:[39] Going over to where she was lying, Yeshua rebuked the fever and it left her, and she stood up straight away and got them something to eat.
[Lukas] [4]:[40] In the evening, anyone who had a relative with any kind of disease brought their sick relatives to Yeshua and he placed his hands on each one of them and healed them.
[Lukas] [4]:[41] Also demons came out from many people, yelling out, “You are God’s son.” But he rebuked them and didn’t allow them to speak because they knew that he was the messiah.
[Lukas] [4]:[42] The next day, Yeshua (Jesus; Grk. Yesus) went off to a quiet place, but the crowds were looking for him and followed after him and insisted that he didn’t leave them,
[Lukas] [4]:[43] but he told them, “I also need to preach this good message about God’s kingdom in other towns, because that’s why I was sent here.”
[Lukas] [4]:[44] So then he went down to Yehudah (Judea) and preached in the Jewish meeting halls there.
[Lukas] [5]:[1] One time when the crowd was pressuring Yeshua (Jesus; Grk. Yesus) that they wanted to hear God’s message as he stood by Lake Galil,
[Lukas] [5]:[2] he saw two boats at the edge of the water, but the fishermen had left the boats so they could wash their nets.
[Lukas] [5]:[3] Yeshua hopped into one of the boats which turned out to be Shim’on’s (Simon), and asked him just to row out a little way from the land. Then Yeshua sat there in the boat and taught the crowds from there.
[Lukas] [5]:[4] Once he’d finished his speaking, he told Shim’on, “Go out to the deeper parts and lower your nets to catch some fish.”
[Lukas] [5]:[5] “Master,” Shim’on answered, “we worked all through the night and didn’t catch anything, but ok, I’ll do what you say and lower the nets.”
[Lukas] [5]:[6] When they lowered the nets, they quickly netted a huge catch of fish, so much so that their nets began to rip
[Lukas] [5]:[7] and they had to signal to their companions in the other boat to come and help. When they got there, they filled both boats with so many fish that the weight began to sink them.
[Lukas] [5]:[8] When Shim’on Kefa (Peter; Grk. Petros) had a moment to realise what had just happened, he knelt in the boat in front of Yeshua and said, “You must leave me, master, because I’m just a sinful man.”
[Lukas] [5]:[9] Kefa and all those with him were stunned at the size of the catch,
[Lukas] [5]:[10] including Ya’akov (James; Grk. Yakobos) and Yohan (John; Grk. Yoannes) (Zavday’s (Grk. Zebedaios) sons) who were his fishing partners. Then Yeshua told Shim’on, “Don’t be afraid—from now on you’ll be catching people.”
[Lukas] [5]:[11] When they got the boats up onto the shore, they left everything there and followed after Yeshua.
[Lukas] [5]:[12] In one of the towns that they visited, a man covered in leprous lesions lay face down in front of Yeshua (Jesus; Grk. Yesus) when he saw him, and implored him, “Master, if you wanted you’d be able to heal me.”
[Lukas] [5]:[13] Yeshua reached out his hand and touched him, saying, “I do want it. Be free from this.” Immediately the man was clear of leprosy.
[Lukas] [5]:[14] “Don’t tell others,” Yeshua instructed, “but go directly to the priest with the offering commanded by Mosheh (Moses) and show yourself to him for clearance and as a testimony to them.”
[Lukas] [5]:[15] However the news about Yeshua was spreading all around, and large crowds were gathering to listen to him and to be healed from their diseases,
[Lukas] [5]:[16] but then he would regularly withdraw into the wilderness to pray.
[Lukas] [5]:[17] Yeshua (Jesus; Grk. Yesus) was teaching one day, and some from the Farisaios party and some religious teachers were sitting there listening. They had come from villages all around Galil and Yehudah (Judea), and also from Yerushalem (Jerusalem), and the power of Yahweh was there enabling Yeshua to heal people.
[Lukas] [5]:[18] Then, look, some men turned up carrying a paralysed man on a stretcher, and they tried to bring him inside and place him in front of Yeshua
[Lukas] [5]:[19] but because of the crowd they couldn’t find a way in. So instead, they went up the stairs to the flat roof and removed some tiles in order to let the stretcher down right in front of Yeshua.
[Lukas] [5]:[20] When he saw their faith, he said, “Man, your sins have been forgiven.”
[Lukas] [5]:[21] “Who’s this guy who’s insulting God?” the teachers and Farisaios started to say among themselves. “Only God is able to forgive sins.”
[Lukas] [5]:[22] But Yeshua knew what they were thinking and saying, and answered them, “Why are you reasoning about this in your minds?
[Lukas] [5]:[23] Which is easier to say: ‘Your sins have been forgiven,’ or ‘Stand up and walk’?
[Lukas] [5]:[24] But I’ll demonstrate to you that the son of humanity does have the authority to forgive sins here on earth.” Then he turned to the paralysed man and told him, “Listen to me. Stand up and pick up your stretcher, then go home.”
[Lukas] [5]:[25] Immediately the man stood up, right there in front of them all, picked up what he’d been lying on, and headed off to his home praising God.
[Lukas] [5]:[26] Everyone was astounded and they too praised God. But there was also a feeling of fear and they said, “We’ve witnessed something out-of-the-normal today!”
[Lukas] [5]:[27] Yeshua (Jesus; Grk. Yesus) went outside after that and he saw a tax-collector named Levi sitting in his office and told him, “Come and follow me.”
[Lukas] [5]:[28] So Levi left everything and went and followed Yeshua.
[Lukas] [5]:[29] Then Levi prepared a large meal in his home for Yeshua, plus there were also a lot of tax-collectors and others who were sitting with them.
[Lukas] [5]:[30] Some from the Farisaios party and religious teachers grumbled at Yeshua’s followers, complaining, “Why are you all eating and drinking with tax collectors and other low-life?”
[Lukas] [5]:[31] But it was Yeshua who answered, “Healthy people don’t need a doctor—only those who are sick.
[Lukas] [5]:[32] I didn’t come to call those who are ‘righteous’, but to call sinners to come and turn away from disobeying God.”
[Lukas] [5]:[33] Then the religious leaders complained, “Yohan’s (John; Grk. Yoannes) followers often fast and bring their needs to God, as do the Farisaios, but your followers are eating and drinking.”
[Lukas] [5]:[34] “You can’t make the groomsmen fast at a wedding,” Yeshua (Jesus; Grk. Yesus) responded, “not while the groom is with them.
[Lukas] [5]:[35] But yes, there will be a future time when the groom will be taken away from them, and then they’ll fast.”
[Lukas] [5]:[36] Then he went on to tell them this parable, “No one repairs their old clothes by putting on a patch of new material. If they did, the new patch will likely tear off again, plus it wouldn’t look right anyway.
[Lukas] [5]:[37] Similarly, no one puts new wine to mature into old wineskins. If they did, the new wine would certainly burst the old wineskin and it would all pour out and the wineskin would be ruined as well.
[Lukas] [5]:[38] New wine needs to be put into a new wineskin.
[Lukas] [5]:[39] And no one who’s used to the old ways wants the new, because he’ll claim that the old is good enough.”
[Lukas] [6]:[1] One Rest Day, Yeshua (Jesus; Grk. Yesus) was walking through some fields of grain and his followers were plucking the heads of grain and rubbing them apart in their hands, then chewing the grains.
[Lukas] [6]:[2] But some from the Farisaios party asked, “Why are you doing that? It’s prohibited to harvest on a Rest Day.”
[Lukas] [6]:[3] “Haven’t you read about David,” Yeshua answered, “when him and his men were hungry and what they did?
[Lukas] [6]:[4] “He went into God’s temple and took the ‘bread of the presence’ and ate some and gave some to his men, even though it’s only priests that are allowed to eat that.”
[Lukas] [6]:[5] Then he added, “The son of humanity is the master of the rest days.”
[Lukas] [6]:[6] On a different Rest Day, Yeshua (Jesus; Grk. Yesus) went into a Jewish meeting hall and was teaching the congregation. There was a man there with a deformed right hand
[Lukas] [6]:[7] and the religious teachers and Farisaios were watching Yeshua closely to see if he might heal the man on the Rest Day so they’d have something to accuse him of.
[Lukas] [6]:[8] But he knew their plans and spoke to the man with the deformed hand, “Stand up and come into the middle.” So the man got up and stood in front of them.
[Lukas] [6]:[9] “I want to ask all of you,” said Yeshua, “whether or not it’s allowable to do good on the Rest Day, or only evil—to save life or to destroy it?”
[Lukas] [6]:[10] Turning slowly and looking at them all, he then said to the man, “Hold out your hand.” The man did it and his hand was healed,
[Lukas] [6]:[11] but the religious leaders were mad with anger and discussed among themselves about what they could do to Yeshua.
[Lukas] [6]:[12] One day Yeshua (Jesus; Grk. Yesus) climbed a hill to pray, and then he spent the night there praying to God.
[Lukas] [6]:[13] In the morning, he called together his followers, and chose twelve of them that he then called ‘missionaries’:
[Lukas] [6]:[14] Shim’on (Simon) (who he also named Kefa (Peter; Grk. Petros)) and his brother Andreas, Ya’akov (James; Grk. Yakobos) and Yohan (John; Grk. Yoannes), Filippos (Philip) and Bar-Talmay (Bartholomew; Grk. Bartholomaios),
[Lukas] [6]:[15] Matay (Matthew; Grk. Matthaios) and Toma (Thomas), Ya’akov (Halfay’ (Grk. Halfaios) son), Shim’on (the one known as a Zealot),
[Lukas] [6]:[16] Yehudah (Judas; Grk. Yudas) (son of Ya’akov), and Yehudah Iskariot (who eventually betrayed him).
[Lukas] [6]:[17] Then coming down the hill with them, Yeshua (Jesus; Grk. Yesus) stood on a flat area along with a large crowd of his followers. There was also a large number of people from all around Yehudah (Judea) and Yerushalem (Jerusalem) and from the coastal areas of Tsor (Tyre) and Tsidon (Sidon)
[Lukas] [6]:[18] who came to hear what he had to say, as well as getting healed from their various diseases.
[Lukas] [6]:[19] All the people in the crowd wanted to touch him, because power would come out from him and he was healing everyone.
[Lukas] [6]:[20] Then looking up at his followers, he said, “Blessed are the poor, because God’s kingdom is yours.
[Lukas] [6]:[21] Blessed are those who don’t have enough to eat now, because you’ll all be satisfied. Blessed are those who are weeping now, because you’ll all be laughing.
[Lukas] [6]:[22] You’re all blessed when people hate you and snub you, and when they deride you and slander your reputations as evil, all on account of the son of humanity.
[Lukas] [6]:[23] Be happy at that time and dance with happiness, because you’ll have a large reward in heaven. Their ancestors did the same sorts of things to the prophets.
[Lukas] [6]:[24] However it’s tragic for all you rich people, because you’ve already enjoyed all those comforts.
[Lukas] [6]:[25] It’s tragic for all of you who are full now, because you’ll all be hungry. It’s tragic for all of you who are laughing now, because you’ll all be mourning and crying.
[Lukas] [6]:[26] It’s tragic for you whenever all the people say they admire you, because their ancestors did the same to the false prophets.
[Lukas] [6]:[27] “But I’ll tell all of you who are listening: Love your enemies and be kind to those who hate you.
[Lukas] [6]:[28] Give a blessing to those who curse you and pray for those who mistreat you.
[Lukas] [6]:[29] When someone slaps you on the face, offer them the other side, and when someone forces you to hand over your coat, don’t resist if they want your shirt as well.
[Lukas] [6]:[30] Give to everyone who asks you for something, and when someone takes your stuff, don’t go demanding it back.
[Lukas] [6]:[31] However you’d all like people to treat you, that’s how you should be treating them.
[Lukas] [6]:[32] “And if you only love those who love you, how good is that? Even those who disobey God love those who love them.
[Lukas] [6]:[33] If you only do good things to people who are good to you, how good is that? Even those who disobey God do that.
[Lukas] [6]:[34] And if you only lend money to people that you’re expecting to repay you, how good is that? Even those who disobey God lend to others like them, knowing they’ll get their money back.
[Lukas] [6]:[35] Instead, you all should love your enemies and do good and lend out even when you expect to get nothing back. Then your reward will be large and you’ll all be children of the highest God because he is good to ungrateful and evil people.
[Lukas] [6]:[36] You should be compassionate towards others, because your father is compassionate.
[Lukas] [6]:[37] “Don’t judge others, then you definitely won’t be judged. Don’t condemn others, then you definitely won’t be condemned.
[Lukas] [6]:[38] Give to others, and then you’ll be given to generously. The returned amount will be really packed in to the container and even overflowing, because however you measure things out for others, that’s how things will be measured out for you.”
[Lukas] [6]:[39] Then Yeshua (Jesus; Grk. Yesus) told them a parable: “Surely a blind person can’t be a guide for someone else who’s blind. Won’t both of them fall into a ditch?
[Lukas] [6]:[40] An apprentice isn’t above their teacher, but can become like their teacher once they’re fully trained.
[Lukas] [6]:[41] “How come you notice the speck in someone else’s eye, yet don’t even notice the log that’s in your own eye?
[Lukas] [6]:[42] How can you tell that person, ‘Hey, let me get that speck out of your eye,’ when you can’t even see the log in your eye? You hypocrite, get the log out of your eye and then you’ll be able to see clearly so you can remove the speck in the other person’s eye.
[Lukas] [6]:[43] “A good tree doesn’t produce bad fruit, and a bad tree doesn’t produce good fruit,
[Lukas] [6]:[44] but each tree is recognised by the fruit it produces. You don’t pick figs from thistles or pick grapes from thorn bushes.
[Lukas] [6]:[45] A good person produces good deeds as a result of all the good things inside them, and an evil person produces evil actions as a result of the evil inside, because what comes out of your mouth originates in your mind.
[Lukas] [6]:[46] “So why do you all call me ‘master, master,’ yet you don’t do what I say?
[Lukas] [6]:[47] Everyone who comes to me and listens to my messages and puts them into practice, I’ll show you who that person is like:
[Lukas] [6]:[48] That person is like a man building a house. He dug and drilled and laid a foundation on the rock, and then when there was a flood that dashed against that house, it didn’t shake it because it was built well.
[Lukas] [6]:[49] But the person who listens but doesn’t put the message into practice is like a man that just built his house on the ground with no foundation, and when the flood dashed against it, the house immediately collapsed and broke into many pieces.”
[Lukas] [7]:[1] After Yeshua (Jesus; Grk. Yesus) had finished sharing those messages with the people, he entered the town of Kafarnaoum (Capernaum).
[Lukas] [7]:[2] A Romaios army commander there had a slave that he valued, but who was sick and expected to die.
[Lukas] [7]:[3] He had heard about Yeshua, so he asked the local Jewish elders to talk to Yeshua on his behalf and to ask him to come to heal his slave.
[Lukas] [7]:[4] When the elders got to Yeshua, they earnestly implored him saying, “The man you’d be helping is worth it
[Lukas] [7]:[5] because he loves us Yehudim (Jews) and he built the local Jewish meeting hall for us.”
[Lukas] [7]:[6] So Yeshua went with them but as they got closer to the house, the commander had sent some friends to tell him, “Master, don’t trouble yourself because I’m not worthy enough to have you enter my home
[Lukas] [7]:[7] and that’s why I never came to you personally. However, just issue a command and then my boy will be healed
[Lukas] [7]:[8] because I’m appointed under authority and have other soldiers under me. When I tell one of them to go, he goes, and when I tell one to come, he comes, and when I tell my slave to do something, he does it.”
[Lukas] [7]:[9] When he heard that, Yeshua was amazed and turned to face the crowd that was following him and said, “I can tell you that never before in all of Yisrael (Israel) have I encountered so much faith!”
[Lukas] [7]:[10] By the time that the commander’s friends had gotten back to the house, they found that the slave was already well again.
[Lukas] [7]:[11] The next day, Yeshua (Jesus; Grk. Yesus) went to a town called Nain, and his followers went with him as well as a large crowd of people.
[Lukas] [7]:[12] As he got near the town gate, look, a dead boy was being carried out to the cemetery. The mother was now a widow and he had been their only son, and a large number of the local residents were with her.
[Lukas] [7]:[13] When he saw her, the master felt sorry for her and said, “Don’t cry.”
[Lukas] [7]:[14] Then he went up closer and touched the coffin, and the pallbearers stopped. Then he spoke, “Young man, I’m talking to you: get up.”
[Lukas] [7]:[15] The dead son sat up and started talking, and Yeshua led him to his mother.
[Lukas] [7]:[16] Everyone felt a bit apprehensive and they praised God saying, “A powerful prophet appeared among us,” and “God has been here with his people.”
[Lukas] [7]:[17] Then the news about Yeshua spread all around Yehudah (Judea) and all the surrounding area.
[Lukas] [7]:[18] The apprentices of Yohan-the-immerser reported all these things back to him and he choose two of his apprentices
[Lukas] [7]:[19] and sent them to Yeshua (Jesus; Grk. Yesus) to ask, “Are you the promised one, or should we wait for someone else?”
[Lukas] [7]:[20] So when they got to Yeshua, the two men told him, “Yohan-the-immerser sent us here to ask you if you’re the promised one, or should we wait for someone else?”
[Lukas] [7]:[21] While they were still there, he healed many people from their diseases and difficulties, as well as evil spirits and some blind people being able to see again,
[Lukas] [7]:[22] so then he answered them, “Go and tell Yohan (John; Grk. Yoannes) everything that you’ve seen and heard here: how blind people can see again, lame people are walking now, people with leprosy are clear, some dead have come back to life, and the good message is being preached to the poor.
[Lukas] [7]:[23] God will bless those who don’t misjudge me.”
[Lukas] [7]:[24] When Yohan’s messengers had left, Yeshua started asking the crowds about Yohan, “What did you all go out into the wilderness to see? A reed waving in the wind?
[Lukas] [7]:[25] Yes, but what did you all go out to see? A man dressed in fine clothes? Well, those in nice clothes and living in luxury are in fine homes.
[Lukas] [7]:[26] So what was it that you went out to see? A prophet? Yes, I’ll tell you that he is more important than any old prophet.
[Lukas] [7]:[27] He is the one that was written about: ‘See, I’m sending my messenger ahead of you and he will prepare your path before you get there.’
[Lukas] [7]:[28] I’m telling all of you, no one who’s been born from a woman is greater than Yohan, yet the lowest person in God’s kingdom is greater than him.”
[Lukas] [7]:[29] (When all the people and the tax-collectors that had been immersed by Yohan heard that, they concurred that God’s way is fair,
[Lukas] [7]:[30] however the Farisaios and the lawyers who had not been immersed by him, they rejected God’s plan for them.)
[Lukas] [7]:[31] “So what can I compare this generation with?” asked Yeshua. “Who are they similar to?
[Lukas] [7]:[32] They’re like little children sitting in the marketplace and calling out to each other, ‘We played the flute for you all but you didn’t dance, then we played a sad song but you all didn’t weep.’
[Lukas] [7]:[33] Because Yohan-the-immerser came and he didn’t eat bread or drink wine, so you all said that he has a demon.
[Lukas] [7]:[34] Then the son of humanity came and ate and drank and you all said, ‘Look, he’s a glutton and a drunkard—a friend of tax-collectors and those who disobey God.’
[Lukas] [7]:[35] But wisdom is justified by all her children.”
[Lukas] [7]:[36] Another time, someone from the Farisaios party invited Yeshua (Jesus; Grk. Yesus) to go to his place for a meal, and so he went there and reclined on a flat couch.
[Lukas] [7]:[37] Then wow, a sinful woman from the city who knew that he was reclining in there, came into the room carrying a beautiful carved stone flask of scented skin-cream.
[Lukas] [7]:[38] She stood weeping behind Yeshua’s feet, wetting his feet with her tears. Then she used her hair to wipe off the tears and kissed his feet and rubbed the lotion into them.
[Lukas] [7]:[39] When the Farisaios who had invited Yeshua saw this, he said to himself, “If that man was a prophet, he’d know who she is and what kind of woman it is that’s touching him, because she breaks God’s laws.”
[Lukas] [7]:[40] “Shim’on (Simon),” Yeshua asked him, “I need to tell you something.” “Tell me, teacher,” he replied.
[Lukas] [7]:[41] Then Yeshua told him this story: “Once there were two people who had borrowed from a money lender: one borrowed five-hundred coins and the other borrowed fifty.
[Lukas] [7]:[42] But neither of them was able to repay him, so he wrote-off both of their debts. Now after that, which one of them do you think would appreciate him more?”
[Lukas] [7]:[43] “I suppose,” answered Shim’on, “that it was the one who was forgiven the biggest debt.” “You’re right,” said Yeshua.
[Lukas] [7]:[44] Then looking at the woman he said to Shim’on, “You see this woman? I came into your house but you didn’t give me any water to wash my feet, yet she wet my feet with her tears and then wiped them off with her hair.
[Lukas] [7]:[45] You didn’t kiss me when I entered, but this woman hasn’t stopped kissing my feet since I came in.
[Lukas] [7]:[46] You didn’t offer olive oil for my head, but she anointed my feet with this lotion,
[Lukas] [7]:[47] so that’s why I’ll tell you this: Her many sins have been forgiven because she showed a lot of love, but the one who has been forgiven little, is loving little.”
[Lukas] [7]:[48] Then he said to the woman, “Your sins have been forgiven.”
[Lukas] [7]:[49] The others who were reclining in the room started to ask to each other, “Who does he think he is to be able to even forgive sins?”
[Lukas] [7]:[50] “Your faith has saved you,” Yeshua (Jesus; Grk. Yesus) said to the woman, “Go in peace.”
[Lukas] [8]:[1] After that, Yeshua (Jesus; Grk. Yesus) started travelling around all the towns and villages—preaching and sharing the good message about God’s kingdom. His twelve apprentices were with him
[Lukas] [8]:[2] along with some women who’d been healed from evil spirits and sicknesses: Miryam (Grk. Maria/Mariam) from Magdala (that seven demons had come out of),
[Lukas] [8]:[3] Yohanah (who’s Kuzas’s wife and one of King Herodes’s (Herod) managers), Shoshanah (Susanna), and many others, who used the group’s assets to look after their needs.
[Lukas] [8]:[4] A large crowd gathered around Yeshua (Jesus; Grk. Yesus), including many who’d travelled out from the city, and he told them this parable:
[Lukas] [8]:[5] “One day a farmer went out to plant some seeds. As he spread the seeds, some of them fell along the path where they got trampled on, and the birds ate them.
[Lukas] [8]:[6] Some of the seeds landed in a rocky area where they sprouted, but then they withered up because they didn’t have enough moisture.
[Lukas] [8]:[7] Some of the seeds landed in a patch of thistles, and as the plants started to grow, they were choked out by the thistles.
[Lukas] [8]:[8] Some of the seeds fell onto good soil, and then the plants grew up to produce a harvest of one hundred times as much.” As he was saying this, he was also telling them, “Anyone who wants to hear, listen carefully.”
[Lukas] [8]:[9] After this, his apprentices asked him, “What’s that parable all about?”
[Lukas] [8]:[10] “You’re permitted to know the mysteries of God’s kingdom,” responded Yeshua (Jesus; Grk. Yesus), “but the others get parables so that when they look, they won’t see, and when they listen, they won’t understand.
[Lukas] [8]:[11] “So this is what the parable means: the seeds are God’s message.
[Lukas] [8]:[12] The seeds along the road are those who hear the message, but afterwards the devil comes along and snatches the message away from their hearts, so that they don’t believe or get saved.
[Lukas] [8]:[13] The seeds among the rocks are those who happily accept the message but don’t put down any roots, so they believe for a short time, and then when temptations come, they pull back from God.
[Lukas] [8]:[14] The seeds among the thistles are those who heard the message but get choked under worries and wealth and the good life, and so they never reach maturity.
[Lukas] [8]:[15] But the seeds in the good soil are those good people with good hearts and after hearing the message, they follow it, and produce fruit from their endurance.
[Lukas] [8]:[16] “No one lights a lamp and then puts a cover over it or puts it under a bed, but rather it’s placed on a lampstand so that everyone coming into the room can see the light.
[Lukas] [8]:[17] “Similarly, nothing is hidden that won’t eventually become visible, and nothing is secret that won’t become known and exposed.
[Lukas] [8]:[18] “So take care in what you listen to, because anyone who has now, will be given more, and anyone who doesn’t have, whatever they think they do have will be taken away from them.”
[Lukas] [8]:[19] Then Yeshua’s (Jesus; Grk. Yesus) mother and brothers arrived but they couldn’t get close to him because of the crowd.
[Lukas] [8]:[20] “Your mother and brothers are standing outside,” someone told him, “and they want to see you.”
[Lukas] [8]:[21] “My mother and my brothers,” Yeshua responded, “are anyone who’s listening to God’s message and who put it into practice.”
[Lukas] [8]:[22] One day Yeshua (Jesus; Grk. Yesus) and his apprentices got into a boat and he asked them to go across to the other side of Lake Galil. So they set off
[Lukas] [8]:[23] but once they were moving, Yeshua fell asleep. Then a big storm descended onto the lake and the boat was being swamped by the waves and they were in danger of sinking.
[Lukas] [8]:[24] The apprentices went and woke Yeshua, “Master, we’re going to drown!” Now awake, he spoke sternly to the wind and the waves in the lake, and they stopped and it became calm.
[Lukas] [8]:[25] “Where’s your faith?” he asked them. From being terrified, they were now astounded and asked each other, “Who is this guy really? He can just tell the wind and the water what to do, and they obey him!”
[Lukas] [8]:[26] Then they sailed across to the region of the Gerasainon, which is across the lake from Galil.
[Lukas] [8]:[27] As they got out of the boat, a demon-possessed man who’d come out of the city met him there. He didn’t live in a house, but lived in a cemetery, and he wasn’t wearing a lot.
[Lukas] [8]:[28] He yelled out when he saw Yeshua (Jesus; Grk. Yesus) and knelt down before him, and spoke loudly, “What business do you and I have together, Yeshua, son of the highest God? I beg you, don’t torture me.”
[Lukas] [8]:[29] He said this because Yeshua had commanded the evil spirit to come out from the man. The demon had animated him many times and he’d needed to be put in chains and shackles, but he would break them off and the demon would drive him into the wilderness.
[Lukas] [8]:[30] “What’s your name?” Yeshua asked. “Thousands,” he answered, because many thousands of demons had entered him
[Lukas] [8]:[31] and now they were pleading with Yeshua not to command them to go back to the bottomless pit.
[Lukas] [8]:[32] They could see a herd of pigs being fed on a hill, and they requested Yeshua to let them go into the pigs, and he agreed to that.
[Lukas] [8]:[33] So the demons rushed out of the man and into the pigs, and all the pigs then rushed down the steep bank into the lake and drowned.
[Lukas] [8]:[34] When the workers feeding the pigs saw this happen, they took off and told everyone in the nearby town and round about.
[Lukas] [8]:[35] So lots of people went there to the edge of the lake to see for themselves, and they found the man who’d been demon-possessed now dressed and sitting at Yeshua’s feet with his full faculties, and they were frightened.
[Lukas] [8]:[36] The people who’d seen it happen told the new-comers how the demon-possessed man had been healed.
[Lukas] [8]:[37] Then all those people from the Gerasainon region asked Yeshua to leave the area, because they were quite terrified, so he got back into the boat and they headed back to the other side.
[Lukas] [8]:[38] The man who the demons had come out of had asked Yeshua if he could go with him, but Yeshua sent him away, saying,
[Lukas] [8]:[39] “Go back to your house and tell them there about what God has done for you.” So he went around the town telling everyone what Yeshua had done for him.
[Lukas] [8]:[40] When Yeshua (Jesus; Grk. Yesus) got back to the other side of the lake, the crowd there had been waiting for him and welcomed him.
[Lukas] [8]:[41] Then, wow, a man named Yair (Jairus) came and knelt down in front of Yeshua. He was the leader at the local Jewish meeting hall and he pleaded for Yeshua to come to his house
[Lukas] [8]:[42] because his only daughter, a twelve-year old, was dying. Then while Yeshua was on his way squeezing through the crowd,
[Lukas] [8]:[43] a woman who’d had internal bleeding for twelve years and who couldn’t be helped by any doctor,
[Lukas] [8]:[44] worked her way up behind Yeshua and touched the edge of his robe. Immediately her bleeding stopped
[Lukas] [8]:[45] and Yeshua stopped and said, “Who touched me?” No one owned up, and Kefa (Peter; Grk. Petros) said, “Master, there’s people all around you and they’re pressing against you.”
[Lukas] [8]:[46] “Someone touched me,” Yeshua responded, “because I felt power going out from me.”
[Lukas] [8]:[47] When the woman now saw that she wouldn’t get away with it, she came to Yeshua shaking, and knelt down at his feet. She told him in front of all the people why she’d touched his clothes and how she’d been immediately healed.
[Lukas] [8]:[48] “Lady,” Yeshua said, “your faith has healed you. Go in peace.”
[Lukas] [8]:[49] While he was still speaking, someone came from the Jewish meeting hall leader’s home and told him, “Don’t bother the teacher any further. Your daughter just passed away.”
[Lukas] [8]:[50] But Yeshua heard this and turned to Yair (Jairus) and said, “Don’t be afraid. Just believe and she’ll be healed.”
[Lukas] [8]:[51] So they continued to the house, but Yeshua didn’t allow anyone inside other than Kefa (Peter; Grk. Petros) and Yohan (John; Grk. Yoannes) and Ya’akov (James; Grk. Yakobos), along with the girl’s parents.
[Lukas] [8]:[52] Everyone was weeping and mourning for her, but he said, “Don’t cry. She isn’t dead—just asleep.”
[Lukas] [8]:[53] But they ridiculed Yeshua because they knew that she’d died.
[Lukas] [8]:[54] He took hold of her hand, and called, “Girl, get up.”
[Lukas] [8]:[55] Then her spirit returned and she got up immediately, and he told them to give her something to eat.
[Lukas] [8]:[56] Her parents were astonished, but he instructed them not to tell anyone what had happened.
[Lukas] [9]:[1] Then Yeshua (Jesus; Grk. Yesus) called together his twelve apprentices and gave them power and authority over all the demons and to heal diseases,
[Lukas] [9]:[2] and then sent them out to preach about God’s kingdom and to heal those who were sick.
[Lukas] [9]:[3] “Don’t take anything for the journey,” he told them. “Don’t take a walking stick or a backpack or food or money or spare clothes.
[Lukas] [9]:[4] When someone invites you into their home, stay in that one house until you leave that place,
[Lukas] [9]:[5] but when the people don’t want to hear from you, shake the dust off your feet as a testimony to them that God will punish them for not receiving his messengers.”
[Lukas] [9]:[6] So they headed off, preaching the good message and healing the people as they walked from village to village.
[Lukas] [9]:[7] Herodes (Herod) the ruler of the Galili quarter heard about everything that was going on and was completely puzzled, because some people said that Yohan (John; Grk. Yoannes) the immerser had come back to life,
[Lukas] [9]:[8] while others said that Eliyah (Elijah) had been spotted, and others that one of the other ancient prophets had come back to life.
[Lukas] [9]:[9] “I beheaded Yohan,” King Herodes said, “so who is this man that I’m hearing so much about?” So he tried to find a way to see him.
[Lukas] [9]:[10] When the twelve apprentices returned back to Yeshua (Jesus; Grk. Yesus), they reported back to him everything they’d done. Then he took them to the town of Beyt-Tsayda for some private time,
[Lukas] [9]:[11] but the crowds saw where he went and followed after them, so he welcomed them and taught them about God’s kingdom as well as healing those who needed it.
[Lukas] [9]:[12] As the day was coming to an end, the twelve approached him and said, “Send the crowd away so that they can go into the nearby towns and countryside to find somewhere to stay and something to eat, because this place is very isolated.”
[Lukas] [9]:[13] But Yeshua told them, “You all give them something to eat.” “We don’t have anything more than just five breadrolls and two fish, unless we go and buy some food for all these people.”
[Lukas] [9]:[14] There were about 5,000 men (not counting women and children). Then he told his apprentices, “Sit them down in rows of about fifty each.”
[Lukas] [9]:[15] So they did that and everyone sat down.
[Lukas] [9]:[16] Then Yeshua took the five breadrolls and the two fish and looking up to the sky, he blessed them and broke them into pieces to give to the apprentices to distribute to the crowd.
[Lukas] [9]:[17] Everyone ate until they were satisfied, and then twelve baskets of leftover pieces were collected up afterwards.
[Lukas] [9]:[18] Later when it was the time to pray and Yeshua (Jesus; Grk. Yesus) and the twelve moved away from the crowd, he asked them, “Who do the crowds say that I am?”
[Lukas] [9]:[19] “Some say Yohan-the-immerser,” they answered, “while others say Eliyah (Elijah), and others say that some other ancient prophet came back to life.”
[Lukas] [9]:[20] “And so who do you guys say I am?” he asked. “You’re the messiah from God,” Kefa (Peter; Grk. Petros) answered.
[Lukas] [9]:[21] Then Yeshua (Jesus; Grk. Yesus) warned them—instructing them not to tell this to anyone else,
[Lukas] [9]:[22] saying, “The son of humanity is destined to suffer many things and to be rejected by the elders and the chief priests and the religious teachers, and then to be executed and to be brought back to life on the third day.”
[Lukas] [9]:[23] Yeshua (Jesus; Grk. Yesus) said, “If anyone wants to become my follower, then that person needs to renounce their own desires and follow me, even in suffering and death,
[Lukas] [9]:[24] because anyone who wants to save their own life will lose it, but anyone who is prepared to lose their life on account of me, they’ll be saving their life.
[Lukas] [9]:[25] How would it benefit a person if they gained the wealth of the whole world, but then ended up lost or destroyed?
[Lukas] [9]:[26] Because anyone who’s ashamed of me and my teachings, the son of humanity will be ashamed of that person when he comes in his splendour and with the splendour of the father and of God’s messengers.
[Lukas] [9]:[27] But I can certainly tell you that some of those who are standing here won’t die until they see God’s kingdom.
[Lukas] [9]:[28] It was about eight days later that Yeshua (Jesus; Grk. Yesus) took Kefa (Peter; Grk. Petros) and Yohan (John; Grk. Yoannes) and Ya’akov (James; Grk. Yakobos), and climbed a hill to pray.
[Lukas] [9]:[29] While he was praying, the appearance of his face changed and his clothes turned brilliant white.
[Lukas] [9]:[30] Then, look, there were two men talking with him—Mosheh (Moses) and Eliyah (Elijah)!
[Lukas] [9]:[31] Those two who’d been in heaven were talking about the end of his time here which was about to be actioned in Yerushalem (Jerusalem).
[Lukas] [9]:[32] Kefa and the others had been exhausted and fallen asleep, but when they woke up they saw the radiance of Yeshua and the other two standing there with him,
[Lukas] [9]:[33] but when it was time for the two to leave, Kefa said to Yeshua, “Master, it’s good that we’re here. We could make three shelters: one for you, one for Mosheh, and one for Eliyah.” (But he didn’t really know what he was saying.)
[Lukas] [9]:[34] While he was still speaking, a cloud appeared and enveloped them and they were afraid as they entered the fog.
[Lukas] [9]:[35] Then a voice came out of the cloud that said, “This is my son, the one that has been chosen. Listen to him.”
[Lukas] [9]:[36] By the time that the voice had spoken, they could only see Yeshua in front of them. After this event, they kept what had happened to themselves and didn’t tell anyone else about what they’d seen.
[Lukas] [9]:[37] When they came back down the hill the next day, a big crowd was waiting for them.
[Lukas] [9]:[38] Then, look, a man in the crowd shouted out, “Teacher, I implore you to come and look at my son, because he’s my only child.
[Lukas] [9]:[39] A spirit takes control of him and suddenly he cries out and it makes him convulse and foam at the mouth, and only leaves him after a long time when he’s bruised and battered.
[Lukas] [9]:[40] I tried to get your apprentices to drive it out, but they couldn’t.”
[Lukas] [9]:[41] “Oh you unbelieving and perverted generation,” Yeshua (Jesus; Grk. Yesus) answered, “how much longer do I have to be with you and put up with all of you? Bring your son here.”
[Lukas] [9]:[42] While they were still approaching, the demon attacked the boy and threw him in a convulsion, but Yeshua rebuked the evil spirit and healed the boy and led him back to his father.
[Lukas] [9]:[43] Everyone there was astounded at God’s power. While all the people were still amazed at what he’d done, Yeshua (Jesus; Grk. Yesus) turned and said to his apprentices,
[Lukas] [9]:[44] “Remember everything that’s been said, because the son of humanity is going to be turned in and placed into the hands of these people.”
[Lukas] [9]:[45] But the apprentices didn’t know what he meant as it was hidden from them so they couldn’t comprehend it, plus they were afraid to ask him to explain further.
[Lukas] [9]:[46] Then the apprentices got themselves into a discussion about which of them might hopefully be considered the greatest.
[Lukas] [9]:[47] But Yeshua (Jesus; Grk. Yesus) knew what was going on, so he took a young child and stood the child there next to him
[Lukas] [9]:[48] and told them, “Anyone who accepts a young child in my name is accepting me, and anyone who accepts me is accepted by the one who sent me here. Because it’s the person who is the least among you who’s at the top.”
[Lukas] [9]:[49] “Master,” Yohan (John; Grk. Yoannes) answered, “we saw someone driving out demons using your name, and we told him to stop because he’s not one of us.”
[Lukas] [9]:[50] “Don’t forbid people like him,” Yeshua (Jesus; Grk. Yesus) replied, “because anyone who’s not against you all, is on your side.”
[Lukas] [9]:[51] It was now coming to the time when the events leading to his ascension would start happening, and Yeshua (Jesus; Grk. Yesus) was completely set in his decision to head to Yerushalem (Jerusalem).
[Lukas] [9]:[52] He sent some of his apprentices ahead of him, and when they arrived at a Shomroni (Samaritan) village, they went to get ready for his arrival.
[Lukas] [9]:[53] However, the people there didn’t welcome them because it was clear that Yeshua was heading to Yerushalem.
[Lukas] [9]:[54] Seeing this, his apprentices Ya’akov (James; Grk. Yakobos) and Yohan (John; Grk. Yoannes) asked, “Master, will you let us call fire down from the sky to burn them up?”
[Lukas] [9]:[55] However, Yeshua turned around and told them off,
[Lukas] [9]:[56] so they headed off to another village.
[Lukas] [9]:[57] As they headed down the road, someone told Yeshua (Jesus; Grk. Yesus), “I’ll follow you wherever you go to.”
[Lukas] [9]:[58] “Foxes have their burrows,” he responded, “and the birds have their nests, but the son of humanity has no home where he can lie down and relax.”
[Lukas] [9]:[59] Later he told a different person, “Follow me.” But the man replied, “Master, just let me go and bury my father first.”
[Lukas] [9]:[60] “Leave those who are dead to bury the dead by themselves,” Yeshua said, “but you go and tell people about God’s kingdom.”
[Lukas] [9]:[61] Also, another person said, “I’ll follow after you, master, but first let me go back and say goodbye to everyone at home.”
[Lukas] [9]:[62] But Yeshua responded, “No one who starts ploughing a field and then starts looking backwards is suitable for God’s kingdom.”
[Lukas] [10]:[1] After all this, the master appointed seventy-two others and he sent them out in pairs to go ahead of him to every town and village that he would pass through.
[Lukas] [10]:[2] He told them, “There’s a large harvest ready, but there’s only a few workers. So ask the owner of the crop to send out more workers to help with his harvest.
[Lukas] [10]:[3] So get moving—see, I’m sending you out like lambs with wolves all around.
[Lukas] [10]:[4] Don’t take a wallet or backpack or spare sandals, and don’t greet people on the road.
[Lukas] [10]:[5] “Whenever you’re welcomed into a home, first say, ‘Peace to this house.’
[Lukas] [10]:[6] And if there’s someone there worthy of peace, then your peace will rest on that home, but if not, your peace will return to you.
[Lukas] [10]:[7] Then stay in that same house and eat and drink what they give you, because the worker is worthy of his compensation. Don’t be moving from house to house.
[Lukas] [10]:[8] Whenever you all go into some place and the locals accept you, then eat what they give you.
[Lukas] [10]:[9] Heal the sick there and tell them that God’s kingdom is near.
[Lukas] [10]:[10] But if you all go into some place and they don’t accept you, then go out to the roads and announce,
[Lukas] [10]:[11] ‘We’re wiping off even the dust from your place that stuck to our footwear, however you all need to know anyway that God’s kingdom is near.’
[Lukas] [10]:[12] I’m telling you that it will be more bearable for the people of Sedom in that day than for the people in that place.
[Lukas] [10]:[13] “You won’t end well, Korazin. And you won’t end well, Beyt-Tsayda. Because if the miracles that were done in your places had been done in Tsor (Tyre) and Tsidon (Sidon), they would have turned around from disobeying God and shown their humility long ago
[Lukas] [10]:[14] hence it will be more tolerable for Tsor and Tsidon on judgement day than it will be for you all.
[Lukas] [10]:[15] And you, Kafarnaoum (Capernaum), don’t think you’ll be heading up to heaven, because it’ll be down to hell for you.
[Lukas] [10]:[16] “Anyone who listens to all of you, will be hearing from me, and anyone who rejects you all will be rejecting me, and anyone who rejects me is rejecting the one who sent me here.
[Lukas] [10]:[17] In time, the seventy-two that had been sent out came back excited, saying, “Master, even the demons listened to us when we used your name and authority.”
[Lukas] [10]:[18] “I saw Satan,” Yeshua (Jesus; Grk. Yesus) replied, “when he fell out of heaven like lightning.
[Lukas] [10]:[19] Listen, I’ve given you all the authority to tread on snakes and scorpions and to overcome the enemy’s power, and nothing at all will be able to injure you.
[Lukas] [10]:[20] However, don’t get excited that the evil spirits obeyed you, but rather be happy that your names have been written down in the heavens.”
[Lukas] [10]:[21] At the same time, the holy spirit got Yeshua (Jesus; Grk. Yesus) excited and he said, “I’m aware father, master of heaven and earth, that you’ve hidden these things away from those who are intelligent and well-educated, and instead revealed them to infants. Yes, father, that was what you decided.
[Lukas] [10]:[22] Everything has been handed over to me by my father, and no one knows who the son is except for the father, and who the father is except for the son and those who the son decides to reveal him to.”
[Lukas] [10]:[23] Then he turned to his apprentices and said discreetly, “Blessed are those who get to see what you all are seeing
[Lukas] [10]:[24] because I can tell you that many prophets and kings wanted to see what you all are seeing, but they didn’t get to see what you’ve seen, nor to hear what you all have heard.”
[Lukas] [10]:[25] Then look, a lawyer stood up to test him, asking, “Teacher, what do I need to do to inherit eternal life?”
[Lukas] [10]:[26] “Well, what’s written in the scriptures?” responded Yeshua (Jesus; Grk. Yesus). “How do you understand them?”
[Lukas] [10]:[27] “You must love your God Yahweh with all your heart and all your soul, and all your strength and all your mind,” he replied. “Also, you must love your neighbour as yourself.”
[Lukas] [10]:[28] “You’ve answered correctly,” answered Yeshua, “so do that and you’ll live forever.”
[Lukas] [10]:[29] But the lawyer wanted to justify his lifestyle, so he asked, “And who’s my neighbour?”
[Lukas] [10]:[30] Yeshua replied with this: “Once a Jewish man was walking downhill from Yerushalem (Jerusalem) to Yeriho (Jericho) when a group of robbers grabbed him and took everything including his clothes, then took off leaving him there wounded and half-dead.
[Lukas] [10]:[31] Then it so happened that a priest came down that same road, but when he saw him he continued past on the other side of the road.
[Lukas] [10]:[32] Similarly, a priestly worker (a Levite) arrived at that place and when he saw him he too passed by on the other side.
[Lukas] [10]:[33] Then a man from Shomron (Samaria) who was on a trip came across him, and when he saw him he felt sorry for him
[Lukas] [10]:[34] and went up to him and bandaged his wounds, pouring olive oil and wine on them, then put him on his own animal and took him to a roadhouse and looked after him.
[Lukas] [10]:[35] The next day he took out two coins and gave them to their host, instructing, ‘Look after this guy and if it costs more than this, I’ll reimburse you on my way back.’
[Lukas] [10]:[36] “So which of those three do you think acted like the neighbour of the one attacked by robbers?”
[Lukas] [10]:[37] “The one who cared for him,” replied the lawyer. “Then you go and do the same,” Yeshua (Jesus; Grk. Yesus) told him.
[Lukas] [10]:[38] When it was time to leave, Yeshua (Jesus; Grk. Yesus) went into a village and there was a woman there named Marta who welcomed him in.

[Yohan] [4]:[4] On the way up, he decided to go through Shomron (Samaria).
