[Yohan] [4]:[6] and ‘Ya’akov’s well’ was there. Yeshua was tired from all the walking and was sitting by the well around midday.
[Yohan] [4]:[7] A woman came from the town to get water from the well, and Yeshua asked her for a drink
[Yohan] [4]:[8] since his followers had gone into the town to buy some lunch.
[Yohan] [4]:[9] The woman said to him, “You’re a Yehudi (Jew). How come you’re asking me for a drink when I’m from Shomron?” (Yehudim (Jews) don’t normally associate with anyone from Shomron.)
[Yohan] [4]:[10] Yeshua answered, “If you’d recognised God’s gift and who it is who’s asking you for a drink, you would have asked me and I would have given you living water to drink.”
[Yohan] [4]:[11] But the woman countered, “Mister, you don’t even have rope and a bucket to reach the water in the deep well. How then could you get ‘living water’?
[Yohan] [4]:[12] I doubt that you’re greater than our ancestor Ya’akov (Jacob) who made this well for us and drank this water along with his children and his animals.”
[Yohan] [4]:[13] Yeshua responded, “Everyone who drinks this water will get thirsty again,
[Yohan] [4]:[14] but anyone who drinks the water that I give them will find a well springing up inside them—springing into eternal life.”
[Yohan] [4]:[15] So the woman said, “Okay, then. Give me some of that water so that I won’t get thirsty and won’t have to keep coming out here to the well.”
[Yohan] [4]:[16] Yeshua said, “First, go and get your husband and then come back here.”
[Yohan] [4]:[17] “Actually, I don’t have a husband!” she retorted. “True enough—indeed you don’t,” Yeshua said.
[Yohan] [4]:[18] “You’ve had five husbands and you’re not married to the man you’re living with, so what you said was true.”
[Yohan] [4]:[19] “Mister, I can see that you’re a prophet,” the woman reacted.
[Yohan] [4]:[20] “Our ancestors worshipped on this mountain, but you Yehudim (Jews) claim that people should only worship there in Yerushalem (Jerusalem).”
[Yohan] [4]:[21] Then Yeshua told her, “You need to believe that I was sent from God, woman, because a day is coming when everyone will be worshipping him neither on this mountain, nor in Yerushalem.
[Yohan] [4]:[22] You people in Shomron (Samaria) don’t even know who you worship, but we do, because people will be saved by means of us Yehudim.
[Yohan] [4]:[23] But a time is coming, starting even now, when the true worshippers will be worshipping the father in spirit and truth, because those are the ones that he is wanting to worship him.
[Yohan] [4]:[24] God is spirit, and the ones worshipping him must worship in spirit and total honesty.”
[Yohan] [4]:[25] The woman said, “I’m aware that the messiah is coming—God’s chosen one. Whenever he appears, he’ll teach us everything.”
[Yohan] [4]:[26] “I am the messiah,” Yeshua responded. “Yes, he’s speaking to you!”
[Yohan] [4]:[27] After this, his followers arrived back, and they were astounded that he was speaking with a woman. However no one dared ask her, “What are you after?” Or to ask him, “Why are you talking with her?”
[Yohan] [4]:[28] So the woman left her water jar there, and went back into the town where she told the people,
[Yohan] [4]:[29] “Come and see a man who knew as much about me as I know myself! He must be the messiah!”
[Yohan] [4]:[30] So they went out from the town to go and see Yeshua.
[Yohan] [4]:[31] Meanwhile, Yeshua’s followers encouraged him, “Teacher, here, eat.”
[Yohan] [4]:[32] But he said, “I’ve had food to eat that you don’t know about.”
[Yohan] [4]:[33] This made his followers ask each other, “Did you see anyone bring him something to eat?”
[Yohan] [4]:[34] “Obeying God who sent me is like food to me, and I plan to finish his work,” Yeshua explained.
[Yohan] [4]:[35] “Don’t you all have a saying about needing to wait four months for a harvest? But I’m telling you that you all should open your eyes and look at the fields, because they’re already lightening up as harvest time approaches.
[Yohan] [4]:[36] The harvester gets paid with a harvest that will last forever so that the ones who plant and the ones who harvest can all celebrate.
[Yohan] [4]:[37] There’s truth in the statement that one person plants and a different person harvests.
[Yohan] [4]:[38] I’ve sent you all out to harvest where you haven’t worked before—others did the groundwork and you benefit from their work.”
[Yohan] [4]:[39] And many people of Shomron (Samaria) came out of that town and believed that Yeshua is God because the woman had told them that he knew everything about her.
[Yohan] [4]:[40] So when they all came, they asked him to stay in their town and they stayed on there for a couple of days.
[Yohan] [4]:[41] As a result of his teaching, many more believed
[Yohan] [4]:[42] so then they told the woman, “We no longer believe just because of what you said, but now that we’ve heard him for ourselves, we can see that he really is the saviour of the world.”
[Yohan] [4]:[43] After his two days in Shomron (Samaria), Yeshua (Jesus; Grk. Yesus) continued on up to Galil.
[Yohan] [4]:[44] He himself had told them that no prophet gets honoured in his own home town.
[Yohan] [4]:[45] When he got to Galil, the people accepted him, having seen everything that he’d done at the feast in Yerushalem (Jerusalem) because they had also been down there.
[Yohan] [4]:[46] So he went again to Kana there in Galil where he had made the water into wine. Now there was a royal official there, whose son in Kafarnaoum (Capernaum) was ill.
[Yohan] [4]:[47] When the official heard that Yeshua was coming up from Yehudah (Judea) to Galil, he went and asked him if he would come and heal his son who was dying.
[Yohan] [4]:[48] Yeshua said to him, “You people won’t believe unless you see miracles and other marvels.”
[Yohan] [4]:[49] But the official begged him, “Sir, please come before my child dies.”
[Yohan] [4]:[50] “Go back there and see,” Yeshua responded. “Your son will recover.” The man believed what Yeshua had told him, and so he started off.
[Yohan] [4]:[51] On his way, his slaves met him and reported that the boy was alive and well.
[Yohan] [4]:[52] So the official asked them what time it was that he got better, and they replied that the fever had subsided around 1pm.
[Yohan] [4]:[53] The father knew that that was the time when Yeshua had told him that his son would recover, and as a result his whole household believed that Yeshua came from God.
[Yohan] [4]:[54] This was the second miracle that Yeshua have done after leaving Yehudah (Judea) and going to Galil.
[Yohan] [5]:[1] After all this, there was another Jewish feast, so Yeshua (Jesus; Grk. Yesus) went down to Yerushalem (Jerusalem).
[Yohan] [5]:[2] In Yerushalem at the Sheep Gate, there’s the Beyt-Tsayda pool that has five alcoves
[Yohan] [5]:[3] and a large number of sick, blind, lame, and paralysed people lie there in them.
[Yohan] [5]:[4] ◘
[Yohan] [5]:[5] One man had been there for thirty-eight years,
[Yohan] [5]:[6] and when Yeshua noticed him and knew that he’d been there for so long, he asked, “Do you want to get better?”
[Yohan] [5]:[7] “Yes mister,” the sick man answered, “but when the water starts moving, I don’t have a companion to lift me into the pool, so someone else always get there before me.”
[Yohan] [5]:[8] Then Yeshua said, “Stand up and pick up your bedroll and start walking.”
[Yohan] [5]:[9] The man immediately stood up, picked up his gear, and started to walk. However, this was the weekly rest day.
[Yohan] [5]:[10] So the religious leaders said to the man, “Hey! It’s against the law for you to carry your bedding on the rest day!”
[Yohan] [5]:[11] But the man answered, “The man who made me better told me to pick up my bedroll and start walking.”
[Yohan] [5]:[12] “Oh. Who was it that told you to take that stuff and start walking?”
[Yohan] [5]:[13] But the man who had been healed didn’t even know who it was, because Yeshua had quickly left when a crowd had formed.
[Yohan] [5]:[14] Later on, Yeshua found the man in the temple and told him, “Look, you’re better now so don’t go on sinning, because you don’t want anything worse to happen to you.”
[Yohan] [5]:[15] The man then went and told the leaders that it was Yeshua who had made him better.
[Yohan] [5]:[16] As a result, the leaders started harassing Yeshua because he had done this on a rest day.
[Yohan] [5]:[17] But Yeshua just replied, “My father is working today, and so I’m also working.”
[Yohan] [5]:[18] Because of this, the leaders became determined that he must be put to death—not just because he broke the rules for the rest day, but most of all because he was calling God his own father, thus making himself equal to God!
[Yohan] [5]:[19] So Yeshua (Jesus; Grk. Yesus) responded to them, “I want to tell you all something: The son can’t initiate anything by himself. He can only do what he sees his father doing, because whatever his father is doing, he also does things like that.
[Yohan] [5]:[20] You see, the father loves his son and shows him everything that he’s doing. In fact, he’ll be showing him even greater things than what he’s done already, so that you all will be amazed.
[Yohan] [5]:[21] Because the father brings the dead back to life, giving them new life, so too the son can give life to anyone who he wants.
[Yohan] [5]:[22] The father won’t be judging anyone, but has already given that task to the son,
[Yohan] [5]:[23] so that the people might honour the son like they honour the father. But anyone who is not honouring the son, is also dishonouring the father who sent him.
[Yohan] [5]:[24] “I assure you that anyone who hears my message and believes that I was sent by God, will live forever and will not be condemned, but has moved from death into life.
[Yohan] [5]:[25] I can also assure you that a time is coming, and in fact is here already, when the dead will be hearing the voice of God’s son and that voice will bring them back to life.
[Yohan] [5]:[26] As the father is the source of life, he gave the power of giving life to the son
[Yohan] [5]:[27] and gave him the authority to be the final judge, because he is the son of humanity.
[Yohan] [5]:[28] Don’t be surprised at this, because a time is coming when everyone in their graves will be hearing his voice,
[Yohan] [5]:[29] and the ones having done what is good will be given new life, and the ones having done what is evil will be condemned.”
[Yohan] [5]:[30] Yeshua (Jesus; Grk. Yesus) continued explaining to the religious leaders, “I don’t do anything in isolation. Whenever I hear from him, only then do I judge and my judgement is correct and impartial because I’m not imposing my desires, but the desire of the one who sent me.
[Yohan] [5]:[31] “If I just testified about myself, my testimony would not be correct or even valid.
[Yohan] [5]:[32] However it’s another one that’s testifying about me, and I know that his testimony about me is true.
[Yohan] [5]:[33] You sent people out to question Yohan (John; Grk. Yoannes) and his testimony was true.
[Yohan] [5]:[34] but I don’t even need any testimony that comes from people, because I am teaching you how to be saved.
[Yohan] [5]:[35] Yohan was a bright and shining light and you appreciated it for a short time.
[Yohan] [5]:[36] But I have a stronger testimony than Yohan’s because the father has entrusted works to me to complete, and which I’m already doing and which clearly show that the father sent me here.
[Yohan] [5]:[37] And since he sent me, he himself has testified about me. You people have never listened to his voice, nor have you ever seen him!
[Yohan] [5]:[38] And his way of thinking is obviously not in your minds, because you don’t believe the one that he sent.
[Yohan] [5]:[39] You look in the Jewish scriptures because you suppose that they’ll lead you to eternal life. Those very scriptures testify about me coming,
[Yohan] [5]:[40] yet you refuse to come to me in order to receive life.
[Yohan] [5]:[41] “I’m not getting any praise from people
[Yohan] [5]:[42] but I do know that you people don’t actually love God in your hearts.
[Yohan] [5]:[43] I have come with my father’s authority and you don’t accept me, but if someone came claiming their own authority, you’d happily accept them.
[Yohan] [5]:[44] How could you possibly believe when you just accept acclamations from each other, but don’t even seek praise from the only God.
[Yohan] [5]:[45] But don’t be assuming that I’ll be accusing you all in front of the father. No, the one who’ll accuse you is Mosheh (Moses) because he’s the one that you’re hoping to please.
[Yohan] [5]:[46] The trouble is that if you actually believed what Mosheh wrote, you would believe me, because Mosheh was writing about me.
[Yohan] [5]:[47] But since you don’t really believe his writings, you’re not at all likely to believe me.”
[Yohan] [6]:[1] After all this, Yeshua (Jesus; Grk. Yesus) crossed the lake in a boat.
[Yohan] [6]:[2] A large crowd followed him because they’d seen his miraculous healings of sick people.
[Yohan] [6]:[3] Yeshua climbed a hill and sat there with his apprentices.
[Yohan] [6]:[4] At that time, it was getting close to the Jewish Festival of Passover.
[Yohan] [6]:[5] When Yeshua looked out and saw the large crowd coming, he asked Filippos (Philip), “Where can we get enough food from to feed all this crowd?”
[Yohan] [6]:[6] But he was only saying this to test Filippos because he already knew what he was going to do.
[Yohan] [6]:[7] Filippos answered, “To buy even just a snack for this many people would take several months’ wages!”
[Yohan] [6]:[8] Now one of Yeshua’s apprentices, Shim’on (Simon) Kefa’s (Peter; Grk. Petros) brother, Andreas, said to Yeshua,
[Yohan] [6]:[9] “There’s a young boy here with five buns and two small cooked fish, but that wouldn’t even start to feed this crowd.”
[Yohan] [6]:[10] But Yeshua told them to get all the people to sit down as there was a large grassy area. So they all sat down—some five thousand men were counted.
[Yohan] [6]:[11] Then he took the buns and gave thanks to God, and started passing around both the buns and the fish, and everyone ate as much as they wanted.
[Yohan] [6]:[12] Once everyone was full, Yeshua got his apprentices to collect the leftover fragments so as not to waste anything.
[Yohan] [6]:[13] So they gathered the leftovers and filled twelve baskets with leftover bread.
[Yohan] [6]:[14] The people who had witnessed this and other miracles said, “This really is the prophet that God promised to send!”
[Yohan] [6]:[15] But Yeshua knew that they intended to come and grab him to proclaim him as their king, so he moved out of the crowd and on up the hill.
[Yohan] [6]:[16] As it moved into evening, Yeshua’s (Jesus; Grk. Yesus) apprentices went back down to the lake
[Yohan] [6]:[17] and having boarded the boat, they set out across the lake toward Kafarnaoum (Capernaum). By then it was dark, and there was still no sign of Yeshua.
[Yohan] [6]:[18] Then a strong wind hit the lake and the water got rough.
[Yohan] [6]:[19] When they had rowed about five kilometres, they saw Yeshua walking on top of the lake and approaching the boat, and they were very scared.
[Yohan] [6]:[20] But he told them, “Don’t worry—it’s me.”
[Yohan] [6]:[21] After that they were willing to let him into the boat, and immediately the boat was at their arrival place.
[Yohan] [6]:[22] The next day, the crowd looked across the lake and saw that only one small boat had crossed, and they knew that only Yeshua’s apprentices had boarded that boat and left, and not Yeshua himself.
[Yohan] [6]:[23] Other boats came across from Tiberias near the place where they had eaten the bread after the master had given thanks.
[Yohan] [6]:[24] So when all the people saw that Yeshua wasn’t around and his apprentices had left, they went off looking for Yeshua in Kafarnaoum.
[Yohan] [6]:[25] When they found him there across the lake, they queried, “Teacher, how did you get here?”
[Yohan] [6]:[26] “Honestly, I know that you’re not looking for me because you saw God working miracles,” Yeshua (Jesus; Grk. Yesus) answered, “but because you all had plenty of food to fill you up.
[Yohan] [6]:[27] Don’t just work for the food which goes off, but for the food which lasts forever—the food which the son of humanity will give to you because God the father has put his mark of approval on him.”
[Yohan] [6]:[28] Puzzled, they asked him, “What should we be doing if we want to work for God?”
[Yohan] [6]:[29] He answered, “Doing God’s work is putting your trust in the one that he sent here.”
[Yohan] [6]:[30] “If so,” they said, “what miracle will you do for us to see so that we can believe that you came from God? What can you do?
[Yohan] [6]:[31] Our ancestors ate the manna out in the wilderness, just like Mosheh (Moses) wrote, ‘He gave them bread from the sky to eat.’ ”
[Yohan] [6]:[32] Yeshua (Jesus; Grk. Yesus) said to them, “Actually I can tell you that it wasn’t Mosheh who gave them bread from heaven, but my father gives you the real bread from heaven,
[Yohan] [6]:[33] because God’s bread is the one who came down from heaven and who gives life to the world.”
[Yohan] [6]:[34] So they requested, “Mister, keep giving us that bread.”
[Yohan] [6]:[35] “I am the bread that gives life,” Yeshua answered, “anyone who comes to me will never hunger, and the one believing in me, will never be thirsty again.
[Yohan] [6]:[36] But as I said already, although you have seen me you refuse to believe me.
[Yohan] [6]:[37] Everyone that the father gives to me will come to me, and I certainly won’t turn away anyone who comes to me,
[Yohan] [6]:[38] because I came down from heaven, not to do what I want, but to do what the one who sent me wants.
[Yohan] [6]:[39] And what he wants is for me to not lose anyone that he’s given to me, but to bring them back to life on the last day.
[Yohan] [6]:[40] My father wants everyone who watches me and believes in me to live forever, because I will bring them back to life on that final day.”
[Yohan] [6]:[41] This little speech made the religious leaders grumble about him because he had said that he was the food that came down from heaven,
[Yohan] [6]:[42] as they figured out, “This is Yeshua the son of Yosef (Joseph) and so we know his parents. So how can he say that he came down from heaven?”
[Yohan] [6]:[43] Yeshua scolded them, “Don’t be grumbling to each other.
[Yohan] [6]:[44] No one can join me unless the father who sent me attracts them, and then I’ll be bringing them back to life on that final day.
[Yohan] [6]:[45] The prophets wrote that the people will be taught by God. And everyone who’s heard and learnt from the father comes to me.
[Yohan] [6]:[46] Not that any person has seen the father—only the one who came from God has seen him.
[Yohan] [6]:[47] I tell you sincerely: anyone who believes in me will live forever.
[Yohan] [6]:[48] I am the bread that gives true life.
[Yohan] [6]:[49] Your ancestors ate manna in the wilderness, but they all went on to die.
[Yohan] [6]:[50] But I am the bread that came down from heaven and anyone who eats this will not die.
[Yohan] [6]:[51] I am the living bread that came down from heaven and if anyone eats this bread, he will live through to the next age.”
[Yohan] [6]:[52] At this point, the religious leaders began to argue with each other, “How could this man give us his flesh to eat?”
[Yohan] [6]:[53] So Yeshua (Jesus; Grk. Yesus) explained, “Indeed if you don’t eat my flesh and drink my blood, you aren’t truly alive!
[Yohan] [6]:[54] Anyone who eats my flesh and drinks my blood will gain eternal life—I will bring them back to life on that final day,
[Yohan] [6]:[55] because my flesh is the true food, and my blood is the true drink.
[Yohan] [6]:[56] Anyone who eats my flesh and drinks my blood lives in me, and I will live in him.
[Yohan] [6]:[57] The father is alive and sent me here, and I am alive because of Him, so also the person who eats me will be alive because of me.
[Yohan] [6]:[58] Unlike your ancestors who ate that bread from the sky and then died, anyone who eats this bread that came down from heaven will live through to the next age.”
[Yohan] [6]:[59] Yeshua (Jesus; Grk. Yesus) taught all of this in the Jewish meeting hall (Grk. synagogue) there in Kafarnaoum (Capernaum).
[Yohan] [6]:[60] But even many of his followers who heard it said, “That’s a difficult teaching—it’s too hard to take.”
[Yohan] [6]:[61] But Yeshua already knew inside that his followers were grumbling about that and asked them, “Do you find that offensive?
[Yohan] [6]:[62] What if you were to see the son of humanity ascending to where he came from?
[Yohan] [6]:[63] It’s the spirit that is the source of life, not the body. The concepts that I’ve taught you are all spiritual and life-giving.
[Yohan] [6]:[64] But there are some here who don’t believe me.” Actually, Yeshua had already known from the beginning just who would believe and which person would betray him
[Yohan] [6]:[65] so he said, “That’s why I told you that no one can come to me unless the father has given them to me.”
[Yohan] [6]:[66] After this, many of his followers went back and no longer accompanied him around.
[Yohan] [6]:[67] So Yeshua said to his twelve apprentices, “Don’t you want to leave as well?”
[Yohan] [6]:[68] “Master,” Shim’on (Simon) answered, “if we went, who would we follow then? You’re the only one who teaches about living forever.
[Yohan] [6]:[69] We believe and know that you are the holy son of God.”
[Yohan] [6]:[70] Yeshua responded, “Didn’t I choose all twelve of you myself? And yet one of you is the devil.”
[Yohan] [6]:[71] (He was talking about Yehudah (Judas; Grk. Yudas), Shim’on Iskariot’s son, because he was the one who would go on to betray him.)
[Yohan] [7]:[1] After all this, Yeshua (Jesus; Grk. Yesus) travelled around Galil. (He didn’t want to travel around Yehudah (Judea) because the leaders there wanted to execute him.)
[Yohan] [7]:[2] As it was now getting close to the Jewish Feast With Tents,
[Yohan] [7]:[3] his brothers said to him, “You should leave this place and go down to Yehudah so that all your followers can see the miracles that you’re doing.
[Yohan] [7]:[4] If you want to become well-known, you don’t do things out of the main stream. If you want to do miracles, go and show yourself to the wider world.
[Yohan] [7]:[5] (You see, not even Yeshua’s own half-brothers believed that he came from God.)
[Yohan] [7]:[6] So Yeshua responded, “Well, you guys can do that any time, but it’s not the right time for me yet.
[Yohan] [7]:[7] All the people won’t hate you guys, but they do hate me because I teach about the evil things they are doing.
[Yohan] [7]:[8] You all go on down to Yerushalem (Jerusalem) ahead of me. I’m not going to the feast yet because it’s not yet the right time for me.”
[Yohan] [7]:[9] After saying this, Yeshua stayed up in Galil.
[Yohan] [7]:[10] But after his half-brothers had left to go down to Yerushalem (Jerusalem), Yeshua (Jesus; Grk. Yesus) also went—not in the public limelight but just incognito so to speak.
[Yohan] [7]:[11] However at the celebrations, the Jewish religious leaders were searching for him, and were asking around where he was.
[Yohan] [7]:[12] Even among the crowds there was a lot of quiet banter with some saying that Yeshua is a good man and others complaining that he was misleading the people.
[Yohan] [7]:[13] Either way, no one was speaking out in public about him, because they were afraid of the reaction of the religious leaders.
[Yohan] [7]:[14] Finally sometime in the middle of the celebrations, Yeshua went into the temple and started teaching in there.
[Yohan] [7]:[15] Even the Jewish leaders were surprised, asking, “How can this man know so much when he hasn’t been trained as a teacher?”
[Yohan] [7]:[16] Yeshua himself responded, “My teaching doesn’t come from me, but from the one who sent me.
[Yohan] [7]:[17] If anyone wants to do God’s will, they’ll soon figure out whether my teaching comes from God or if I’m just making it up myself.
[Yohan] [7]:[18] Any person who just teaches their own thoughts is just seeking their own advancement, but anyone who wants to promote the one who sent them, this is authentic and there’s no hidden self-interest.
[Yohan] [7]:[19] Didn’t Mosheh (Moses) write down God’s commands for you, yet not a single one of you obeys them. Why are you wanting to execute me?”
[Yohan] [7]:[20] “You must be demon-possessed,” said some in the crowd, “Who would be wanting to execute you.”
[Yohan] [7]:[21] Yeshua responded, “I did one miracle and you were all amazed.
[Yohan] [7]:[22] Mosheh gave you the command about circumcision (even though it actually came from before his time), but to obey this, you’ll even circumcise a baby boy on the Rest Day.
[Yohan] [7]:[23] So if a baby boy can be circumcised on the Rest Day so that Mosheh’s commands aren’t broken, they why did you get angry with me because I made a man healthy on the Rest Day?
[Yohan] [7]:[24] Don’t just ‘judge’ things so that you yourselves look good, but judge impartially, seeking the best for others.”
[Yohan] [7]:[25] After this, some of the locals from Yerushalem (Jerusalem) started asking, “Isn’t this the man they were wanting to execute?
[Yohan] [7]:[26] Well, here he is teaching in public, yet they’re not even confronting him. Perhaps the leaders know that he really is the messiah?
[Yohan] [7]:[27] But we even know where this man is from. Surely when the messiah comes, no one would know his family background.”
[Yohan] [7]:[28] So as Yeshua (Jesus; Grk. Yesus) continued teaching, he called out, “Indeed you all know me and my home and my family. But I didn’t come here of my own accord, but the one who sent me here is truthful, even though you don’t even know him.
[Yohan] [7]:[29] I know him, because I came from him, indeed, he was the one who sent me here.”
[Yohan] [7]:[30] So now they really want to arrest him, but no one touched him because it was not yet the proper time.
[Yohan] [7]:[31] Many in the crowd did believe that he was from God and they were saying, “When the messiah comes, would he be doing greater miracles than what we’ve seen this man do?”
[Yohan] [7]:[32] The Farisaios party heard the crowd muttering about these things and sent out some of their servants along with the chief priests to go and arrest Yeshua (Jesus; Grk. Yesus).
[Yohan] [7]:[33] So Yeshua said, “I’ll only be with you all for a short while longer and then I’ll be going to the one who sent me.

[Yohan] [11]:[38] So Yeshua (Jesus; Grk. Yesus) who was still holding back sobs, went to the cemetery. Eleazar’ (Lazarus; Grk. Lazaros) body had been placed in a cave with a stone blocking it,

[Yohan] [11]:[40] But Yeshua responded, “Didn’t I tell you that if you would believe, then you would see God’s power?”
[Yohan] [11]:[41] So they took the stone away and Yeshua looked upwards and said, “Father, I thank you that you listen to me.
[Yohan] [11]:[42] Actually I know that you always hear me, but I said that for the sake of these people so that they will believe that it was you who sent me here.”
[Yohan] [11]:[43] After saying that, he shouted, “Eleazar, come out!”
[Yohan] [11]:[44] Then the man who had died slowly shuffled out—still with linen strips wrapped around his hands and his feet, and a cloth wrapped around his face.
[Yohan] [11]:[45] Because of that, many of the Yehudim (Jews) believed that Yeshua (Jesus; Grk. Yesus) was from God after having followed Miryam (Grk. Maria/Mariam) and seeing what Yeshua did.
[Yohan] [11]:[46] But others went and told the Farisaios party what Yeshua had done.

[Yohan] [11]:[48] If we allow him to continue like this, all the crowds will be believing he’s the messiah, and then the Romaios will come and destroy both our temple and our governance.”
[Yohan] [11]:[49] But one of them, Kayafa (Caiaphas; Grk. Kaiafas) who was chief priest that year, spoke up, “You don’t know anything.
[Yohan] [11]:[50] Don’t you all realise that it’s better for all of us if one man dies so that the people and the nation won’t be destroyed?”
[Yohan] [11]:[51] (He didn’t say this from his own thinking, but being chief priest that year, he was announcing God’s message that Yeshua was going to die for the nation,
[Yohan] [11]:[52] and not only for this nation, but for all of God’s children scattered around the world to become united.)
[Yohan] [11]:[53] As a result, from that day on they decided that Yeshua needed to be executed.
[Yohan] [11]:[54] Because of that, Yeshua no longer walked around Yehudah (Judah) in public, but went out to the town of Efrayim (Ephraim) out in the wilderness and stayed there with his followers.
[Yohan] [11]:[55] At that time, the Jewish Passover celebrations were approaching, and many people from the regions went to Yerushalem (Jerusalem) ahead of the celebrations to purify themselves.

[Yohan] [11]:[57] The chief priests and the Farisaios party had already announced that if anyone knew where Yeshua was, they must inform them so that they could arrest him.

[Yohan] [12]:[15] “Don’t be worried you children of Tsiyon (Zion). Your king is coming mounted on a donkey’s foal.”

[Yohan] [13]:[1] Even before the actual feast part of the Passover celebrations, Yeshua (Jesus; Grk. Yesus) knew that his time had come—the time when he would leave this world and return to the father. He loved his followers who were in the world right through to the end.

[Yohan] [16]:[16] “It won’t be much longer and you won’t be able to see me any more, and then a little while after that, and you’ll see me again.”
[Yohan] [16]:[17] This got his followers asking each other, “What’s all this about seeing him for not much longer, and then seeing him again after a while? And why does he say he’s going to the father?”
[Yohan] [16]:[18] So they were saying, “What’s this about ‘not much longer’? We don’t know what he means.”
[Yohan] [16]:[19] However Yeshua (Jesus; Grk. Yesus) knew what they wanted to ask him, and so he said to them, “You are trying to find out from each other what I meant when I said that you won’t be able to see me after a little while, and then a little while after that you’ll see me again.
[Yohan] [16]:[20] I can assure you that you’ll be weeping and mourning but the world will be elated. You’ll be upset but then your upset will turn into happiness.
[Yohan] [16]:[21] A woman giving birth has pains when the delivery begins, but when she hears that the baby is born, she doesn’t remember those pains any more because she’s so happy that her child was born.
[Yohan] [16]:[22] So too with all of you: you’ll be upset for a while but then I’ll be with you again and you’ll be so happy and no one will be able to take that happiness away from you.
[Yohan] [16]:[23] “When that happens, you won’t be asking me for anything. I can assure you that whatever you request from the father in my name and my authority will be given to you.
[Yohan] [16]:[24] Up until now you haven’t asked him for anything using my authority, but after that time, you’ll be able to make requests and they’ll be answered so that your happiness will be complete.
[Yohan] [16]:[25] “So far I’ve told you these things in parables, however a time is coming when I’ll no longer be speaking in parables but will tell you things about the father quite plainly.
[Yohan] [16]:[26] At that time you’ll have my authority to request from the father. I’m not saying that I’ll be asking him on your behalf,
[Yohan] [16]:[27] no, because he himself loves you all because you have loved me and have believed that I was sent by God.
[Yohan] [16]:[28] I was sent out by the father and I have come into the world, but I’ll be leaving the world again and returning to the father.”
[Yohan] [16]:[29] Yeshua’s (Jesus; Grk. Yesus) followers responded, “Ah, now you’re speaking plainly and not using parables.
[Yohan] [16]:[30] Finally we realise that you know everything already and don’t need to ask anyone else, and so we now believe that you came from God.”
[Yohan] [16]:[31] “So now you all believe?” Yeshua answered.
[Yohan] [16]:[32] “The time is coming and is here already when you will all be scattered in various directions and will leave me by myself, but I won’t be alone because the father is always with me.
[Yohan] [16]:[33] I’ve told you these things so that you can all have peace in me. You will have troubles in this world, but be courageous because I have overcome the world.”
[Yohan] [17]:[1] After Yeshua (Jesus; Grk. Yesus) had finished speaking, he looked up to the sky and said, “Father, it’s now the time for you to honour your son so that the son can honour you.
[Yohan] [17]:[2] You already gave me authority over all people so that I could grant eternal life to everyone that you’ve given me.
[Yohan] [17]:[3] And eternal life means knowing you, the only true God, and knowing me—Yeshua the messiah that you sent.
[Yohan] [17]:[4] I honoured you here on the earth by completing everything that you gave me to do.
[Yohan] [17]:[5] So father, now you yourself can honour me with the greatness that I had when I was together with you before the creation of the world.
[Yohan] [17]:[6] “I revealed your power to the ones that you gave me from this world. They were yours and you gave them to me, and they have obeyed your teaching.
[Yohan] [17]:[7] Now they understand that everything that you gave to me came from you,
[Yohan] [17]:[8] because I passed on to them the messages that you gave to me, and they accepted them. Now they believe that I came from you and that it was you who sent me here.
[Yohan] [17]:[9] “I’m asking about them. It’s not the people of this world that I’m asking about, but about the ones that you gave me because they belong to you.
[Yohan] [17]:[10] Everything that’s mine is yours, and everything that’s your is mine, and I’ve been honoured by their actions.
[Yohan] [17]:[11] I’m about to leave this world and come to you, but they will stay here in it. Holy father, use your power to keep protect the ones that you gave me, so that they might be united just like you and I are one.
[Yohan] [17]:[12] When I was with them, I protected them with the authority that you gave, and I guarded them so that not one of them perished, except the one who chose destruction so that it will indeed happen as the scriptures foretold.
[Yohan] [17]:[13] But soon I’ll be coming to you, and I’m speaking these things in the world so that they will have the same happiness as me and be fulfilled in their lives.
[Yohan] [17]:[14] I’ve passed on your teaching to them, and the world hated them because they don’t belong to this world, just as I don’t.
[Yohan] [17]:[15] I’m not asking you to remove them out of this world, but rather to stop evil from overcoming them.
[Yohan] [17]:[16] They don’t belong to this world just as I don’t.
[Yohan] [17]:[17] Purify them with the truth—your message is that truth.
[Yohan] [17]:[18] In the same way that you sent me out into this world, so I also send them out into the world.
[Yohan] [17]:[19] I’m purifying myself for their sakes so that they also may be made pure by the truth.
[Yohan] [17]:[20] “But it’s not just on behalf of the ones right here that I’m asking, but also for all the others who will believe that I came from you when they hear the message of these ones,
[Yohan] [17]:[21] so that they will all become united, just as you, father, are in me and I am in you. I ask that they will also be in us so that the world will be able to believe that it was you who sent me here.
[Yohan] [17]:[22] And the honour that you’ve given me, I’ve passed on to them so that they can be united just as we are one—
[Yohan] [17]:[23] me in them and you in me so that they can be perfected as one. Then the world will know that you sent me here and that you love them just like you love me.
[Yohan] [17]:[24] Father, I want those that you’ve given me to be with me wherever I am so that they’ll be able to see my greatness—the greatness that you gave me because you loved me even before the creation of the world.
[Yohan] [17]:[25] Righteous father, this world didn’t know you, but I know you and these ones know that you sent me here.
[Yohan] [17]:[26] I revealed your power and authority to them and will continue to do so, so that the love that you love me with might be in them, and I too might be in them.”
[Yohan] [18]:[1] After he’d said all this, Yeshua (Jesus; Grk. Yesus) and his followers left Yerushalem (Jerusalem) proper and over the Kidron stream towards a garden that he and his followers entered.
[Yohan] [18]:[2] And Yehudah (Judas; Grk. Yudas) (the one who would hand him over) also knew the place because Yeshua and his followers often met there.
[Yohan] [18]:[3] Meanwhile Yehudah had met with the soldiers and servants of the chief priests and the Farisaios party, and they all started coming into the garden with lanterns and flaming torches and weapons.
[Yohan] [18]:[4] Yeshua who already knew what was going to happen to him, came forward and asked them, “Who are you all looking for?”
[Yohan] [18]:[5] And they answered, “Yeshua—the one from Nazaret.” Yeshua responded, “I am the one.” Yehudah, the one handing him over, was standing there among them.
[Yohan] [18]:[6] But when Yeshua had said that he is the one, they backed away and fell to the ground.
[Yohan] [18]:[7] So he asked them again, “Who are you all looking for?” And they answered, “Yeshua—the one from Nazaret.”
[Yohan] [18]:[8] Yeshua responded, “I already told you all that I am the one. So if it’s me that you’re looking for, let these others leave.”
[Yohan] [18]:[9] (In this way, the statement was fulfilled that Yeshua had said previously: ‘I didn’t lose any of the ones that you gave me.’)
[Yohan] [18]:[10] Then Shim’on (Simon) Kefa (Peter; Grk. Petros) drew the sword that he was carrying and swiped at the servant of the high priest, cutting off his right ear. The servant’s name was Malkos.
[Yohan] [18]:[11] But Yeshua said to Kefa, “Put your sword back in its sheath. I need to proceed with the plan that the father has prepared for me—I can’t just avoid the suffering.”
[Yohan] [18]:[12] So the soldiers and their commander, and the servants of the Jewish leaders arrested Yeshua (Jesus; Grk. Yesus) and tied him up.
[Yohan] [18]:[13] First they took him to Hanan (Annas; Grk. Hannas), the father-in-law of Kayafa (Caiaphas; Grk. Kaiafas) who was the chief priest that year.
[Yohan] [18]:[14] (Kayafa was the one who had suggested that it was better for the people and the nation if one man should die for all of them.)
[Yohan] [18]:[15] Now Shim’on (Simon) Kefa (Peter; Grk. Petros) and another apprentice were following Yeshua (Jesus; Grk. Yesus), and since that other apprentice was known to the chief priest, he was allowed to enter following Yeshua into the courtyard of the chief priest
[Yohan] [18]:[16] while Kefa waited outside at the door. Then the other apprentice who was known to the chief priest went back and spoke to the woman at the door and brought Kefa in too.
[Yohan] [18]:[17] But the servant girl who was watching the door challenged Kefa, “Aren’t you also one of the followers of that man?” “No, I’m not,” he responded.
[Yohan] [18]:[18] Meanwhile the servants and attendants had made a fire and were standing around it warming themselves, and Kefa also went and stood there to warm himself.
[Yohan] [18]:[19] Now the chief priest interrogated Yeshua (Jesus; Grk. Yesus) about his followers and about his teaching.
[Yohan] [18]:[20] Yeshua answered him, “I’ve spoken openly to the people. I always taught in the meeting halls and in the temple where Jewish people meet. I didn’t speak in secret
[Yohan] [18]:[21] so why are you asking me? Ask the people who heard what I told them—they’re the ones who know what I said.”
[Yohan] [18]:[22] When he said that, one of the attendants standing there slapped Yeshua on the face and said, “You think you can answer the chief priest like that?”
[Yohan] [18]:[23] But Yeshua responded, “If I said anything wrong, tell me my error. But if it was true, why are you hitting me?”
[Yohan] [18]:[24] So Hanan (Annas; Grk. Hannas) sent him away, still tied up, to Kayafa (Caiaphas; Grk. Kaiafas) the chief priest.
[Yohan] [18]:[25] Shim’on (Simon) Kefa (Peter; Grk. Petros) was still standing by the fire warming himself when he was asked, “Aren’t you also one of his followers?” But he denied it, saying, “No, I’m not.”
[Yohan] [18]:[26] One of the servants of the chief priest who was a relative of the man whose ear Kefa had cut off said, “Didn’t I see you in the garden with that Yeshua (Jesus; Grk. Yesus)?”
[Yohan] [18]:[27] But Kefa again denied it, and just then a rooster crowed.
[Yohan] [18]:[28] Then they led Yeshua (Jesus; Grk. Yesus) out from Kayafa’ (Caiaphas; Grk. Kaiafas) place and towards the residence of the governor. It was now the early hours of the morning and as Yehudim (Jews), they didn’t enter the residence of the Romaios governor so they wouldn’t become defiled and thus unable to eat the Passover meal.
[Yohan] [18]:[29] So Governor Pilatos (Pilate) came outside to them and asked, “What charge are you all bringing against this man?”
[Yohan] [18]:[30] “We wouldn’t have brought him to you if he hadn’t committed a serious crime,” they answered.
[Yohan] [18]:[31] So Pilatos said, “You just take him and judge him yourselves according to your own laws.” But the Jewish leaders responded, “We don’t have permission to execute anyone.”
[Yohan] [18]:[32] (This happened to fulfil what Yeshua had said about the way that he was going to die.)
[Yohan] [18]:[33] So Pilatos went back into his governor’s residence and called for Yeshua and asked him, “So you’re the king of the Yehudim?”
[Yohan] [18]:[34] “Are you saying this yourself,” Yeshua asked, “or did others say it about me?”
[Yohan] [18]:[35] Pilatos retorted, “Hoy! I’m not a Yehudi (Jew). It was your own people and the chief priests that handed you over to me. What have you done?”
[Yohan] [18]:[36] “My kingdom isn’t in this world,” Yeshua answered, “because if it was, my supporters would have fought so that I wouldn’t have been handed over to the Jewish leaders. But no, my kingdom isn’t from here.”
[Yohan] [18]:[37] “So you are a king then?” Pilatos responded. “You’re saying that I’m a king,” said Yeshua, “and indeed I was born to be a king. I came into the world so that I could testify to the truth.”
[Yohan] [18]:[38] “Yeah. What is truth?” said Pilatos. After he’d said this, Pilatos (Pilate) went back outside to the Yehudim (Jews) and told them, “I can’t find anything that he’s guilty of.
[Yohan] [18]:[39] But you all have a custom here that the governor can release one prisoner during the Passover. So would you like me to release the king of the Yehudim?”
[Yohan] [18]:[40] But they all yelled back, “No, not this one. Release Bar-Aba (Grk. Barabbas).” (Bar-Aba was a robber.)
[Yohan] [19]:[1] So Pilatos took Yeshua (Jesus; Grk. Yesus) and had him flogged.
[Yohan] [19]:[2] Then the soldiers twisted some thorn branches together into a crown and put it on Yeshua’s head, and they dressed him in a royal purple robe.
[Yohan] [19]:[3] They came up to him and said, “Greetings, you king of the Yehudim,” and then slapped him.
[Yohan] [19]:[4] Then Pilatos went back outside and said to the Yehudim, “Look here. I’m bringing him out to you so that you all can know that I didn’t find him guilty of anything.”
[Yohan] [19]:[5] So they led Yeshua out wearing the thorny crown and the kingly robe, and Pilatos said, “Look. Here’s the man.”
[Yohan] [19]:[6] Now when the chief priests and their supporters saw him, they yelled out, “Execute him on a stake! Execute him on a stake!” “Well you take him and execute him on a stake,” Pilatos answered, “because I haven’t found anything that he’s guilty of.”
[Yohan] [19]:[7] The Yehudim responded, “We have a law and he should be executed according to that law because he said he was the son of God.”
[Yohan] [19]:[8] Now when Pilatos heard that, he became more afraid.
[Yohan] [19]:[9] So he went back inside the residence and asked Yeshua, “Where do you come from?” But Yeshua didn’t answer him.
[Yohan] [19]:[10] So Pilatos said, “Why don’t you answer me? Don’t you realise that I have the authority to release you and I also have the authority to have you executed on a stake?”
[Yohan] [19]:[11] “You have no authority over me,” Yeshua answered, “none at all, except what has been granted to you from above. Because of this, the sin of the person who handed me over to you is greater.”
[Yohan] [19]:[12] After hearing this, Pilatos wanted to release him but the Yehudim yelled out, “If you release that man, you’re no friend of Kaisar. Everyone who claims to be a king is no friend of Kaisar’s.”
[Yohan] [19]:[13] So now Pilatos, having heard all this, brought Yeshua outside again. Pilatos sat down on the judge’s seat at a place called The Stone Pavement (and called Gabatha in Hebrew).
[Yohan] [19]:[14] It was now about noon on the day when the Passover meal is prepared, and Pilatos said to the Yehudim, “Look. Here’s your king.”
[Yohan] [19]:[15] They yelled back, “Take him away. Take him away. Execute him on a stake.” Pilatos asked them, “You want me to have your king executed on a stake?” “We don’t have any king other than Kaisar,” the chief priests answered.
[Yohan] [19]:[16] So Pilatos gave them his permission and handed Yeshua over to them, and they took him away to be executed on a stake.
[Yohan] [19]:[17] Carrying the pole himself, Yeshua (Jesus; Grk. Yesus) arrived at the Place of the Skull (called Golgotha in Hebrew) just out of the city
[Yohan] [19]:[18] where they secured him to a stake along with two others—one stake on each side and with Yeshua on the middle one.
[Yohan] [19]:[19] Pilatos (Pilate) wrote out a title and put it on the stake: Yeshua from Nazaret, the king of the Yehudim (Jews).
[Yohan] [19]:[20] Many Yehudim read this title because the place where Yeshua was executed was near the city, and it had been written in Hebrew, Latin, and Greek.
[Yohan] [19]:[21] But the Jewish chief priests complained to Pilatos, “Don’t write ‘The king of the Yehudim’, but rather ‘The one who said he was king of the Yehudim’.”
[Yohan] [19]:[22] However Pilatos answered, “What I’ve written, I’ve written.”
[Yohan] [19]:[23] After the soldiers had fastened Yeshua to the stake, they took his clothes and placed them in four piles, one for each of them. This left his robe, which had been woven from top to bottom in one piece.
[Yohan] [19]:[24] So they said to each other, “Rather than tearing this, let’s throw a dice to see who will get it.” (This fulfilled what was written in the scriptures that said: they divided my garments among themselves and threw a dice for my clothes.) So they went ahead and did that.
[Yohan] [19]:[25] Meanwhile a group of women had stayed standing near Yeshua on the stake: his mother and his aunt, Miryam (Grk. Maria/Mariam) the wife of Klopas, and Miryam from Magdala.
[Yohan] [19]:[26] When Yeshua saw his mother and also the apprentice that he loved standing nearby, he said to her, “Look, he’ll be your son.”
[Yohan] [19]:[27] And to the apprentice he said, “Look, she’ll be your mother.” And that apprentice took her into his own home from then on.
[Yohan] [19]:[28] Having done this, Yeshua (Jesus; Grk. Yesus) knew that everything had been accomplished, and (in order for the scriptures to be fulfilled) said, “I’m thirsty.”
[Yohan] [19]:[29] There was a container lying there full of vinegary wine, so they placed a sponge on a hyssop stalk, soaked it in the wine, and held it up to his mouth.
[Yohan] [19]:[30] After Yeshua had sucked some wine out, he said, “It is finished.” Then he bowed his head and gave up his spirit.
[Yohan] [19]:[31] Now because it was the preparation day for the coming Rest Day, the Yehudim (Jews) didn’t want the bodies to remain on the stakes after dusk (because it was even a special Rest Day.) So they asked Pilatos (Pilate) to command for their legs to be broken to hasten their deaths and then they could be taken down sooner.
[Yohan] [19]:[32] So the soldiers came and broke the legs of the men on each side of Yeshua (Jesus; Grk. Yesus),
[Yohan] [19]:[33] but when they got to him, they saw that he was already dead so they didn’t break his legs.
[Yohan] [19]:[34] Instead one of the soldiers stabbed his side with a spear and immediately blood and water came out.
[Yohan] [19]:[35] The one who actually saw this happen has testified this and his account is accurate so that you readers can also believe it,
[Yohan] [19]:[36] because these things also happened to fulfil what was written in the scriptures, that ‘none of his bones will be broken,’
[Yohan] [19]:[37] and in another place, ‘they will look at the one that they pierced.’
[Yohan] [19]:[38] After all of this, Yosef (Joseph) from Arimathaia went to Pilatos (Pilate). (Yosef was a follower of Yeshua (Jesus; Grk. Yesus), but secretly because he was afraid of what the Jewish leaders might do.) He asked Pilatos for permission to remove Yeshua’s body, and it was granted to him so they went and got his body.
[Yohan] [19]:[39] Nikodemos (the one who had first visited Yeshua at night) also came, bringing around 30kg of burial spices.
[Yohan] [19]:[40] So they took Yeshua’s body and wrapped it around with linen strips with the spices as per the Jewish burial customs.
[Yohan] [19]:[41] There was a garden out at the place where Yeshua had been executed, and in the garden there was a new tomb that hadn’t been used yet.
[Yohan] [19]:[42] So because it was the preparation day and because the tomb was nearby, they laid his body in there.
[Yohan] [20]:[1] The following Sunday, Miryam (Grk. Maria/Mariam) from Magdala went out to the tomb very early when it was still dark, and she saw that the stone had been removed from the entrance.
[Yohan] [20]:[2] So she ran quickly and went to Shim’on (Simon) Kefa (Peter; Grk. Petros) and the other apprentice that Yeshua (Jesus; Grk. Yesus) loved, and told them, “They’ve taken the master’s body out of the tomb and we don’t know where they’ve put it.”
[Yohan] [20]:[3] So Kefa and the other apprentice went out to the tomb.
[Yohan] [20]:[4] They were running together, but the other apprentice was a bit faster than Kefa and so he got to the tomb first.
[Yohan] [20]:[5] Without going in, he stooped down at the entrance and looked in and saw the linen strips lying there.
[Yohan] [20]:[6] But Kefa came along behind him and went straight into the tomb and also saw the linen strips lying there.
[Yohan] [20]:[7] But the piece of cloth that had been on the head wasn’t lying there with the linen strips, but had been folded and placed separately.
[Yohan] [20]:[8] So now the other apprentice who had arrived first also went inside and he saw it all and believed that Yeshua had risen.
[Yohan] [20]:[9] (At that time they weren’t yet aware of the scripture about him coming back to life.)
[Yohan] [20]:[10] So they went back again to their homes.
[Yohan] [20]:[11] But Miryam (Grk. Maria/Mariam) had stayed there outside the tomb weeping. But when she stooped down and looked into the tomb,
[Yohan] [20]:[12] she saw two messengers dressed in white sitting there—one at the head end and one at the feet end of the slab where Yeshua’s (Jesus; Grk. Yesus) body had been lying.
[Yohan] [20]:[13] They spoke to her, “Woman, why are you crying?” “Because they’ve taken away my master,” she replied, “and I don’t know where they’ve put him.”
[Yohan] [20]:[14] Then she turned back around and saw Yeshua standing there, but she didn’t realise who it was.
[Yohan] [20]:[15] Yeshua asked her, “Woman, why are you crying? Who are you looking for?” Miryam assumed he might be the gardener, so she answered, “Mister, if you took the body, tell me where you put it and I’ll get it taken away for you.”
[Yohan] [20]:[16] Yeshua just answered, “Miryam.” She spun around and said, “My teacher!” (‘Rabboni’ in Hebrew.)
[Yohan] [20]:[17] “Don’t touch me,” Yeshua said to her, “because I haven’t gone back up to the father yet, but go and tell my brothers that I’m going up to my father and the father of you all, and my god and the god of you all.”
[Yohan] [20]:[18] So Miryam went and told the apprentices, “I’ve seen the master,” and she told them what he’d said.
[Yohan] [20]:[19] On Sunday evening Yeshua’s (Jesus; Grk. Yesus) apprentices had met together and had the doors locked because they were afraid of the Jewish leaders, but Yeshua arrived and stood in the middle of the room and said, “Peace to you all.”
[Yohan] [20]:[20] Then he showed them his hands and his side and they were so happy now that they had seen the master.
[Yohan] [20]:[21] Yeshua continued, “Peace to you all. Now I’m sending you all out just like the father sent me out.”
[Yohan] [20]:[22] Then he breathed on them and said, “Receive the holy spirit.
[Yohan] [20]:[23] If you forgive anyone’s sins, then they’ll be forgiven but if you withhold forgiveness, then it will be withheld.”
[Yohan] [20]:[24] But Toma (Thomas), one of the twelve (nicknamed ‘Twin’), wasn’t with them when Yeshua (Jesus; Grk. Yesus) had come
[Yohan] [20]:[25] so the other apprentices told him, “We have seen the master.” But he replied, “I won’t believe that unless I see the mark of the nails in his hands and I can put my finger into the marks and can put my hand into the gash on his side.”
[Yohan] [20]:[26] Eight days later, Yeshua’s apprentices were again together inside, and this time Toma was with them.
[Yohan] [20]:[27] Yeshua came and stood in the middle of the room even though the doors were shut, and said, “Peace to you all.”
[Yohan] [20]:[28] Toma spoke up, “My master and my god!”
[Yohan] [20]:[29] “So you believe now because you’ve seen me,” said Yeshua. “The ones who haven’t seen me, but who believe anyway, will certainly be rewarded.”
[Yohan] [20]:[30] Yeshua (Jesus; Grk. Yesus) went on to do many other miracles in front of his apprentices which aren’t recorded in this account.
[Yohan] [20]:[31] But what has been written here has been recorded so that you might all believe that Yeshua is the messiah, God’s son, and then by believing, so that you might have true life through his power.
[Yohan] [21]:[1] After all this, Yeshua (Jesus; Grk. Yesus) revealed himself again to his apprentices at Lake Galil. It happened like this:
[Yohan] [21]:[2] Shim’on (Simon) Kefa (Peter; Grk. Petros), Toma (Thomas) nicknamed ‘Twin’, Netanel (Nathanael) from Kana in Galil, the sons of Zavday (Grk. Zebedaios), and two other apprentices had gathered together
[Yohan] [21]:[3] when Shim’on Kefa said that he was going fishing and the others said that they’d join him. So they went off and got in the boat, but they didn’t catch anything that night.
[Yohan] [21]:[4] When the dawn was approaching, Yeshua was standing there on the shore, but they didn’t know that it was him.
[Yohan] [21]:[5] He called out, “Hey, young fellas. Don’t you have any fish?” “None.” they answered.
[Yohan] [21]:[6] Then he said, “Throw the net out over the right side of the boat and you’ll find some.” So they did it and they caught so many fish that the net was too heavy to pull back in.
[Yohan] [21]:[7] Now the apprentice that Yeshua loved said to Kefa, “It’s the master!” When Shim’on Kefa heard that, he put on his robe (because he didn’t have it on), and jumped overboard into the lake.
[Yohan] [21]:[8] The other apprentices followed in the little boat dragging the net behind them because they were only about 100m out from the shore.
[Yohan] [21]:[9] When they went up the beach, they saw some bread there and a charcoal fire with fish cooking on it
[Yohan] [21]:[10] and Yeshua told them, “Bring some of the fish that you just caught.”
[Yohan] [21]:[11] So Shim’on Kefa went and dragged the net up onto the beach. Amazingly it hadn’t torn even though it contained 153 large fish.
[Yohan] [21]:[12] Then Yeshua said, “Now, come and have breakfast.” But none of the apprentices dared to ask who he was, because they figured it must be the master.
[Yohan] [21]:[13] Yeshua brought the bread to them and shared it around, and then likewise for the fish.
[Yohan] [21]:[14] This was now the third time that Yeshua had appeared to his apprentices since he’d come back to life.
[Yohan] [21]:[15] While they were eating, Yeshua (Jesus; Grk. Yesus) asked Shim’on (Simon) Kefa (Peter; Grk. Petros), “Shim’on, son of Yohan (John; Grk. Yoannes), do you love me more than these?” Kefa answered, “Yes, master, you know that I love you.” Yeshua responded, “Feed my lambs.”

[Acts] [5]:[31] But God honoured this way-maker and saviour by placing him in the place of honour, to encourage Yisrael (Israel) to repent and then to forgive their sins.
[Acts] [5]:[32] We are witnesses of these messages, along with the holy spirit who God gave to the ones who obey him.”
[Acts] [5]:[33] When the gathered councils heard this, they were enraged and wanted to kill them,
[Acts] [5]:[34] but a certain member of the Farisaios party named Gamliel stood up in the council chamber. He was a law teacher respected by all the community, and he ordered the guards to take them outside for a while,
[Acts] [5]:[35] then he said, “Fellow Israelis, think carefully about what you’re planning to do with these men.
[Acts] [5]:[36] A while back, a man called Theudas became prominent, saying that he was someone important. Eventually about four hundred others joined him, but he was killed and those who’d followed him were dispersed and it all came to nothing.
[Acts] [5]:[37] A bit later on, a Galili man named Yehudah (Judas; Grk. Yudas) became prominent at the time of the census and he attracted people to him. But he also died, and all those who’d been persuaded by him ended up being scattered.
[Acts] [5]:[38] So here’s my advice to you all: pull back from killing these men and allow them to continue, because if this teaching and goings on is man-made, it’ll be overthrown,
[Acts] [5]:[39] but if it’s from God, you all won’t be able to bring them down in case you find yourselves opposing God.” So they were persuaded by Gamliel,
[Acts] [5]:[40] and after calling in the missionaries and having them beaten, they commanded them not to speak using the name and authority of Yeshua (Jesus; Grk. Yesus) and then sent them out.
[Acts] [5]:[41] So the missionaries left the councils, very excited that they were considered worthy to be disgraced because of Yeshua.
[Acts] [5]:[42] After that, they never stopped teaching and preaching the good message about Yeshua the messiah in the temple and in various homes.
[Acts] [6]:[1] However around that time when the number of Yeshua-followers were growing, some of the Greek converts starting grumbling about the Jewish believers because the Greek widows were being overlooked in the daily sharing of food and money.
[Acts] [6]:[2] So the twelve missionaries assembled the believers together and told them, “We’re not pleased about having to take time off sharing the message of God to be serving here at the distribution tables.
[Acts] [6]:[3] So brothers, look around you for seven men who are well known to be full of God’s spirit and wisdom, so we can appoint them to be in charge of this part of the work.
[Acts] [6]:[4] Then we ourselves can continue to pray and share the message.”
[Acts] [6]:[5] This idea pleased the group, so they went ahead and chose Stefanos (a man full of faith and of the holy spirit), Filippos (Philip), Prokoros, Nikanor, Timon, Parmenas, and Nikolaos (a non-Jew from Antiokeia who had previously converted to Youdaismos).
[Acts] [6]:[6] They stood these seven up in front of the missionaries, who prayed and then placed their hands on them.
[Acts] [6]:[7] God’s message continued spreading and the number of followers in Yerushalem (Jerusalem) was rapidly increasing, and a large number of the priests became believers.
[Acts] [6]:[8] Now Stefanos (one of the seven) was full of grace and power and was doing miracles and amazing demonstrations of God’s power among the people.
[Acts] [6]:[9] But a group from the Freedmen Synagogue as well as Yehudim (Jews) from Kurainai (Cyrene), Alexandria, Kilikia, and Asia Minor rose up and started arguing against Stefanos,
[Acts] [6]:[10] but they weren’t able to refute the wisdom that he spoke with the help of the pure spirit.
[Acts] [6]:[11] So they got some men to falsely accuse Stefanos saying, “We heard him denigrating Mosheh (Moses) and God.”
[Acts] [6]:[12] So they stirred up the people and the elders and the law teachers and so they approached Stefanos and arrested him and brought him to the council chambers.
[Acts] [6]:[13] There they produced the false witnesses saying, “This man won’t stop spreading messages against this holy temple and against the law
[Acts] [6]:[14] because we heard him saying that that Yeshua (Jesus; Grk. Yesus) from Nazaret will be tearing down this building and will be changing the traditions that Mosheh gave to us.”
[Acts] [6]:[15] So then the council members looked across at Stefanos and saw that his face was shining like that of one of God’s messengers.
[Acts] [7]:[1] Then the chief priest asked Stefanos, “Is all this true?”
[Acts] [7]:[2] And he replied, “My brothers and fathers, please listen. Our honoured God was seen by our ancestor Avraham in Mesopotamia before he moved to Haran
[Acts] [7]:[3] and he told him, ‘Leave your land and your relatives, and go to the place that I will show you.’
[Acts] [7]:[4] So he left Kasdim and moved to Haran, and then after his father died, he moved again to this land where we now live.
[Acts] [7]:[5] Avraham hadn’t received any land here as an inheritance, in fact he’d never been near this land and nor did he have any children, yet God promised to give this entire country to him and his descendants.
[Acts] [7]:[6] And yet God also told him that his descendants would end up staying in another country where they would be enslaved and mistreated for four hundred years.
[Acts] [7]:[7] However God promised to punish the nation that enslaved them, and told him that in the end they would leave that place and serve him here in this country.
[Acts] [7]:[8] And he contracted with Avraham about being circumcised, and so when Avraham had Yitshak (Isaac), he circumcised him on the eighth day, and then Yitshak went on to have Ya’akov (Jacob), and Ya’akov to have the twelve tribal leaders.
[Acts] [7]:[9] Those brothers went on to become jealous of Yosef (Joseph) and sent him back into Mitsrayim (Egypt) as a slave, but God was with him
[Acts] [7]:[10] and rescued him out of all his troubles there. Then God gave him wisdom and caused him to gain the favour of Par’oh (Pharaoh), the king of Mitsrayim, who then appointed him as the ruler of all Mitsrayim and over Par’oh’s own household.
[Acts] [7]:[11] Then a famine hit all Mitsrayim and Kena’an (Canaan) causing great distress and our ancestors were unable to find enough food.
[Acts] [7]:[12] But Ya’akov heard that grain was available in Mitsrayim, so first, he sent off our tribal leaders.
[Acts] [7]:[13] On their second visit, Yosef revealed himself to them, and so Par’oh became aware of Yosef’s heritage.
[Acts] [7]:[14] Then Yosef sent for his father Ya’akov and all the extended family—some seventy-five of them.
[Acts] [7]:[15] So Ya’akov went to Mitsrayim, where he and the twelve tribal leaders eventually died,
[Acts] [7]:[16] although their bodies were moved to Shekem where they were put into the tomb that Avraham had bought from the sons of Hamor.
[Acts] [7]:[17] But as the time limit promised to Avraham by God was getting closer, our people multiplied in Mitsrayim
[Acts] [7]:[18] until another Par’oh ended up ruling there who had never known Yosef.
[Acts] [7]:[19] He took advantage of us Yehudim (Jews) and mistreated our ancestors, even forcing them apart from their own babies so they wouldn’t live.
[Acts] [7]:[20] Mosheh (Moses) was born during that time and God considered him beautiful. He spent three months in his own father’s house
[Acts] [7]:[21] before being placed outside, from where Par’oh’s daughter took him and brought him up herself as her own son.
[Acts] [7]:[22] So Mosheh was instructed in all the wisdom of the Mitsrim (Egyptians), and was a powerful speaker and project leader.
[Acts] [7]:[23] But when he hit forty, it entered his mind to visit his relatives, the Israelis.
[Acts] [7]:[24] When he noticed one of them being mistreated, he retaliated and while defending the oppressed man, he struck and killed the Mitsri (Egyptian).
[Acts] [7]:[25] He thought his relatives would understand that God was bringing salvation to them via him, but they didn’t see it that way.
[Acts] [7]:[26] So on the following day when he saw two of them quarrelling, he tried to resolve the situation by saying, ‘Men, you’re all brothers. Why are you injuring each other?’
[Acts] [7]:[27] But the bullying one pushed him away and said, ‘Who made you the judge over us?
[Acts] [7]:[28] Do you want to kill me like you killed that Mitsri yesterday?’
[Acts] [7]:[29] When he heard that, Mosheh fled Mitsrayim (Egypt) and became an exile in Midyan where he eventually had two sons.
[Acts] [7]:[30] After another forty years, he was in the wilderness around Mt. Sinay when he saw a messenger in the flame of a burning thorn bush.
[Acts] [7]:[31] Mosheh was amazed at the vision when he saw it, so he approached the bush to look more closely when he heard Yahweh’s voice saying,
[Acts] [7]:[32] ‘I am the god of your ancestors—the god of Avraham and of Yitshak (Isaac) and of Ya’akov (Jacob).’ At that point, Mosheh started trembling and was scared to go any closer to look,
[Acts] [7]:[33] but Yahweh said, ‘Take off your sandals, because the ground you’re standing on is dedicated to God.
[Acts] [7]:[34] I have noticed the mistreatment of my people in Mitsrayim and heard their groaning and so I came down to rescue them, so now I’m going to send you back to Mitsrayim.’
[Acts] [7]:[35] This was the same Mosheh that they had previously rejected and asked who had made him ruler and judge over them. Now God had indeed sent him as ruler and liberator by means of the messenger that he saw in the thorn bush.
[Acts] [7]:[36] So eventually Mosheh led them out of Mitsrayim after doing miracles and signs of God’s power there, and then also at the Red Sea and during the forty years in the wilderness.
[Acts] [7]:[37] This same Mosheh told Israelis that in the future God would raise up another prophet like him from among them.
[Acts] [7]:[38] Now Mosheh was the person that led the assembly of people in the wilderness, was spoken to by one of God’s messengers on Mt. Sinay, and one of our ancestors that received living messages to pass on to us.
[Acts] [7]:[39] “Yet our ancestors didn’t want to obey that man, so they rejected him and started thinking about Mitsrayim again,
[Acts] [7]:[40] saying to Aharon (Aaron), ‘Make some gods for us to lead us because we’ve got no idea what happened to that Mosheh who led us out of Mitsrayim.’
[Acts] [7]:[41] So together they made a calf as an idol to bring sacrifices to, and they were pleased with what they’d achieved.
[Acts] [7]:[42] But God turned and allowed them to serve the heavenly armies, just as the prophets wrote, ‘It wasn’t me that you Israelis sacrificed to for those forty years in the wilderness.
[Acts] [7]:[43] You turned to Molek’s tent and Remfan’s star as your gods by making images of them to bow down to. So for that, I’ll send you all away into exile beyond Bavel (Babylon).’
[Acts] [7]:[44] The tent of evidence was with our ancestors in the wilderness—made to the pattern that God had shown Mosheh.
[Acts] [7]:[45] Our ancestors then carried that tent into the land, having inherited it along with Yehoshua (Joshua) from the possession of the pagans which God drove out ahead of them. The tent remained there until the time of David
[Acts] [7]:[46] who found favour with God and requested to find a tent for the house of Ya’akov (Jacob),
[Acts] [7]:[47] but it was Shelomoh (Solomon) who built the house for God to reside in.
[Acts] [7]:[48] However the highest one doesn’t actually live in structures made by people, but as the prophet wrote,
[Acts] [7]:[49] ‘Heaven is my throne, and the earth is where I place my feet. How could you possibly build a suitable house for me?
[Acts] [7]:[50] Wasn’t it me that created everything?’
[Acts] [7]:[51] You stiff-necked people with uncircumcised hearts and ears! You’re always opposing the holy spirit just like your ancestors were.
[Acts] [7]:[52] Which one of the prophets wasn’t persecuted by your ancestors? Even the ones that foretold the coming of the righteous one were killed off by them in just the same way that you yourselves became his betrayers and murderers!
[Acts] [7]:[53] You’d received the law under the direction of messengers, and yet you didn’t obey it.”
[Acts] [7]:[54] When they heard that, they were raging inside and grating their teeth at him.
[Acts] [7]:[55] But being full of the holy spirit, Stefanos stared up into the sky and was able to see God’s splendour, as well as seeing Yeshua (Jesus; Grk. Yesus) standing there on God’s right.
[Acts] [7]:[56] He said, “I can look through the sky that’s opened up and can see the son of humanity standing at God’s right side.”
[Acts] [7]:[57] At this point, they blocked their ears and rushed together to grab Stefanos, yelling loudly.
[Acts] [7]:[58] They drove him out of the city and then started throwing rocks at him. His accusers left their cloaks in the care of a young man named Sha’ul (Saul; Grk. Saulos/Saul).
[Acts] [7]:[59] As Stefanos was being hit by the rocks, he called out, “Master Yeshua, receive my spirit.”
[Acts] [7]:[60] Then falling to his knees, just before he died he called out loudly, “Master, don’t hold this sin against them.”
[Acts] [8]:[1] (And Sha’ul was agreeing that Stefanos should be executed.) That same day, intense persecution began against the assembly in Yerushalem (Jerusalem), and so the believers fled throughout the regions of Yehudah (Judea) and Shomron (Samaria), except for the twelve who stayed.

[Acts] [8]:[14] When the missionaries in Yerushalem (Jerusalem) heard that many people from Shomron (Samaria) had accepted God’s message, they sent Kefa (Peter; Grk. Petros) and Yohan (John; Grk. Yoannes) out to them

[Acts] [8]:[21] There’s no role for you here and no part for you in our work because your heart isn’t right with God.
[Acts] [8]:[22] You need to turn away from this evil desire and beg the master that maybe he’ll forgive you for your wrong intentions
[Acts] [8]:[23] because I perceive that you have a bitter attitude and ungodly habits.

[Acts] [8]:[25] After that, Kefa (Peter; Grk. Petros) and Yohan (John; Grk. Yoannes) continued to testify and proclaim the good message about the master in many villages around Shomron (Samaria) before they returned to Yerushalem (Jerusalem).
[Acts] [8]:[26] Then a messenger from Yahweh spoke to Filippos (Philip), “Start walking and head south on the road that goes downhill from Yerushalem to Azah (Gaza) through the wilderness.”

[Acts] [8]:[30] So Filippos ran up to the chariot and heard the man reading from the prophet Yeshayah and asked, “Do you know what it is that you’re reading about?”
[Acts] [8]:[31] “How could I know when I don’t have someone to guide me?” he answered, and so he invited Filippos to climb up and sit with him.
[Acts] [8]:[32] Now the particular passage that he was reading was this: ‘He was led away like a sheep being led to the slaughterhouse, and stayed as silent as a lamb being shorn so he never opened his mouth.
[Acts] [8]:[33] He was humiliated by a lack of justice. Who can name his descendants, because his life is being taken from the earth?’
[Acts] [8]:[34] “Now tell me,” said the official, “who was Yeshayah (Isaiah) talking about? Was he talking about himself or someone else?”

[Acts] [8]:[40] As for Filippos, he found himself at the town of Azotos, and as he passed through the coastal towns on the way to Kaisareia, he proclaimed the good message in each town.

[Acts] [9]:[31] After that the assemblies of believers throughout Yehudah (Judea) and Galil and Shomron (Samaria) had peace and grew in their respect and service of the master, as well as increasing in numbers through the encouragement of the holy spirit.

[Acts] [10]:[1] Just up in Kaisareia there was a Romaios army commander named Kornelios (leader of the ‘Italian Regiment’)

[Acts] [10]:[4] Kornelios was scared and looked intently and asked, “What is it, master?” “Your prayers and your helping the poor rose up to God’s notice and attention,” he said.

[Acts] [10]:[7] So as soon as the messenger left, Kornelios called two of his house servants and a godly soldier from his bodyguard,
[Acts] [10]:[8] and after explaining the task to them, he sent them off to Yafo.
[Acts] [10]:[9] The next day as they were approaching the town, Kefa went up onto the flat roof of the house around midday to pray.
[Acts] [10]:[10] But he felt hungry and wanted something to eat, but while it was still being prepared he fell into a trance
[Acts] [10]:[11] and saw the sky open up. Something like a sheet was being lowered down to the earth by the four corners
[Acts] [10]:[12] and it held all kinds of animals and reptiles, as well as birds.
[Acts] [10]:[13] Then he heard a voice saying, “Get up Kefa, and slaughter these and eat them.”
[Acts] [10]:[14] “I can’t, master,” Kefa responded, “because I’ve never eaten anything that’s forbidden.”
[Acts] [10]:[15] But the voice spoke a second time, “Don’t you be treating anything as unclean that God has made clean.”
[Acts] [10]:[16] This vision happened three times and then the sheet thing was lifted back up into the sky.
[Acts] [10]:[17] Now Kefa was still there wondering what the vision was all about when the men sent by Kornelios had tracked down the tanner’s house and arrived outside.
[Acts] [10]:[18] They called out to ask if Shim’on (Simon) Kefa was staying there.
[Acts] [10]:[19] Even as Kefa still continued to ponder about the vision, the spirit said, “Hey, there’s three men here looking for you.
[Acts] [10]:[20] So get up and go downstairs to them. Believe everything they say because I sent them here.”
[Acts] [10]:[21] So he went down and asked the men, “I’m the one you’re looking for, so tell me what you came here for.”
[Acts] [10]:[22] They answered, “We were sent by Kornelios who’s an army commander who worships God and obeys his laws and has a good reputation with you Jewish people. A holy messenger told him to send for you to come to his house so they can listen to what you have to say.”
[Acts] [10]:[23] So Kefa invited them in to stay the night. The next day, Kefa and some of the believers from Yafo (Joppa) started out with them
[Acts] [10]:[24] and they arrived in Kaisareia the following day. Kornelios was expecting them and had also invited some relatives and close friends to join them.
[Acts] [10]:[25] Kefa entered the house and when they met, Kornelios knelt down and worshipped him
[Acts] [10]:[26] but Kefa pulled him up and said, “Stand up. I’m just a man like you.”
[Acts] [10]:[27] After they greeted each other, Kefa went into the main room and found that quite a few people had gathered there.
[Acts] [10]:[28] Then he told them, “You all know that us Yehudim (Jews) are forbidden by our laws to associate with or to enter the house of a non-Jew. However, God showed me that it’s not right to treat other people as being lesser or undesirable.
[Acts] [10]:[29] That’s why I came without any reservations when you sent for me. But I’m still waiting to know what you all want from me?”
[Acts] [10]:[30] So Kornelios answered, “I was praying in my house three days ago in the middle of the afternoon when I suddenly saw a man in shining clothes standing in front of me
[Acts] [10]:[31] and he said, ‘Your prayer has been heard, Kornelios, and God has noticed your gifts to the poor.
[Acts] [10]:[32] Now he wants you to send messengers to get Shim’on (Simon), the one called Kefa, from Yafo (Joppa) where he’s living by the sea in Shim’on the tanner’s house.’
[Acts] [10]:[33] I did that straight away and you kindly came here, so now we’re all here in God’s sight to find out everything that the master has commanded you to say.”
[Acts] [10]:[34] So Kefa (Peter; Grk. Petros) spoke up and said, “Honestly, I’m still just realising that God doesn’t favour only certain people,
[Acts] [10]:[35] but he accepts people from any nation as long as they honour and obey him.
[Acts] [10]:[36] He sent us a message through the descendants of Yisrael (Israel)—a good message that teaches that we can have peace through Yeshua (Jesus; Grk. Yesus) the messiah—everyone’s master.
[Acts] [10]:[37] And you all know the news that started in Galil and spread through all Yehudah (Judea) after the time of Yohan’s (John; Grk. Yoannes) teaching and ministry of immersion—
[Acts] [10]:[38] how God filled Yeshua from Nazaret (Nazareth) with the holy spirit and with power, and who then went around doing good and healing all those oppressed by the devil, because God was with him.
[Acts] [10]:[39] We are witnesses of all the things he did in the Jewish provinces and in Yerushalem (Jerusalem), and then how they executed him by nailing him to a stake.
[Acts] [10]:[40] Then God brought him back to life on the third day and sent him where he could be seen,
[Acts] [10]:[41] not by all the people, but to the witnesses that God had previously appointed—to us who ate with him and drank with him after he’d been raised from the dead.
[Acts] [10]:[42] He commanded us to tell the people, and to testify that he is the one who God has designated to be the judge of the living and the dead.
[Acts] [10]:[43] The writings of all the prophets point towards him, and everyone who believes that he’s God can have their sins forgiven by his authority.”
[Acts] [10]:[44] While Kefa (Peter; Grk. Petros) was still speaking, the holy spirit came down onto everyone who was listening.
[Acts] [10]:[45] The Jewish believers who had come with Kefa were astonished that the gift of the holy spirit had been poured out even on non-Jews
[Acts] [10]:[46] as they heard them speaking in other languages and magnifying God. Then Kefa said,
[Acts] [10]:[47] “Surely no one could argue against them getting immersed in water now that they’ve received the holy spirit just like we did?”
[Acts] [10]:[48] So with the authority of Yeshua (Jesus; Grk. Yesus) the messiah, he commanded for them to be immersed in water. Then they asked him to stay with them for a few more days.
[Acts] [11]:[1] Soon the missionaries and other believers in Yehudah (Judea) heard that non-Jews had also accepted God’s message,
[Acts] [11]:[2] but when Kefa (Peter; Grk. Petros) went to Yerushalem (Jerusalem), the strict Jewish believers were upset with him,
[Acts] [11]:[3] saying that he had gone into the home of uncircumcised pagans and even eaten with them.
[Acts] [11]:[4] But Kefa started explaining from the beginning,
[Acts] [11]:[5] “I was staying in Yafo (Joppa), and as I was praying I saw a vision of an object like a sheet coming down, as if it was being let down out of the sky by its four corners. As it came down to me
[Acts] [11]:[6] I looked at it and saw animals, even wild animals, and reptiles and birds.
[Acts] [11]:[7] I also heard a voice telling me, ‘Kefa, get up and slaughter these and eat them.’
[Acts] [11]:[8] But I said, ‘Master, I can’t because I’ve never eaten anything that’s forbidden.’
[Acts] [11]:[9] But the voice from the sky spoke again, ‘Don’t you be treating anything as unclean that God has made clean.’
[Acts] [11]:[10] This happened three times, and then it was pulled up again into the sky.
[Acts] [11]:[11] Next minute there were three men at the house where I was staying saying that they had been sent from Kaisareia to fetch me,
