[Acts] [25]:[25] But I haven’t discovered anything that he’s done that’s worthy of a death sentence, and since he himself appealed to the emperor, I judged that that’s where he should be sent.
[Acts] [25]:[26] The problem is that I don’t have any charge to write to my master and so I’ve brought the prisoner out in front of you so that after you examine him, I might have something I can write,
[Acts] [25]:[27] because it doesn’t seem logical to me to transport a prisoner to Romai if there’s no charges specified against him.”
[Acts] [26]:[1] So then Agrippas told Paulos, “Okay, you can give your side now then.” So Paulos gestured with his hand and began:
[Acts] [26]:[2] “Concerning all the charges which have been brought against me by the Yehudim (Jews), King Agrippas, I consider myself fortunate
[Acts] [26]:[3] because you’re an expert on Jewish customs and issues, so I ask you to listen to me patiently.
[Acts] [26]:[4] “All the Yehudim know about my early life, from my upbringing in my own country and then in Yerushalem (Jerusalem).
[Acts] [26]:[5] They also know, and could even testify to you if they would admit it, that I followed our religious laws very closely as a member of the Farisaios party.
[Acts] [26]:[6] Yet now I stand judged for believing in the same hope as our ancestors—that hope promised by our God
[Acts] [26]:[7] who we twelve tribes diligently serve day and night in order to obtain—the hope, your majesty, for which I’m being indicted.
[Acts] [26]:[8] So why do you all find it unbelievable that God can raise the dead?
[Acts] [26]:[9] “I too originally thought it necessary to do many things to oppose the cause of this Yeshua (Jesus; Grk. Yesus) from Nazaret.
[Acts] [26]:[10] So in Yerushalem I worked to have many of these innocent believers locked up in prison with the authority of the chief priests, or if they were to be killed, I would add my vote against them.
[Acts] [26]:[11] And in all the Jewish meeting halls, when I found believers I punished them and forced them to curse God and treated them with extreme anger, even travelling to further away towns.
[Acts] [26]:[12] “So it was one time travelling to Damesek (Damascus) carrying permission letters from the chief priests
[Acts] [26]:[13] that in the middle of the day, your majesty, I saw a bright light from the sky—even brighter than the sun—and it shone on me and my companions.
[Acts] [26]:[14] All of us fell down to the ground and I heard a voice speaking to me in Hebrew saying, ‘Sha’ul (Saul; Grk. Saulos/Saul), Sha’ul, why are you persecuting me? Life will be difficult for you if you resist me.’
[Acts] [26]:[15] ‘Who are you, master?’, I asked. “And the master responded, ‘I am Yeshua (Jesus; Grk. Yesus), the one you’re persecuting.
[Acts] [26]:[16] Now get up, because I let you see me in order to appoint you as my servant and my witness—to tell the people what you’ve seen and what you will be shown.
[Acts] [26]:[17] I will rescue you from your own people and from the non-Jews that I’m sending you out to,
[Acts] [26]:[18] to open their minds and for them to turn back from darkness to light and from Satan’s power to God, so that they can be forgiven for their sins and receive an inheritance among the ones who’ve been made guiltless by their faith in me.’
[Acts] [26]:[19] “So then, King Agrippas, I couldn’t disobey that vision
[Acts] [26]:[20] so I preached first to those in Damesek (Damascus) and then in Yerushalem (Jerusalem) and all of Yehudah (Judea), and then in the towns of the non-Jews. I preached about turning from their sins and turning back to God, and then actually living like people who had repented.
[Acts] [26]:[21] It was because of these things that the Yehudim (Jews) grabbed me in the temple and tried to do me in.
[Acts] [26]:[22] So it is that with God’s help until this very day I have stood testifying to commoners and leaders, teaching nothing other than what Mosheh (Moses) and the prophets had already written that would happen—
[Acts] [26]:[23] that the messiah would come and suffer and as the first of the dead to come back to life, he is going to be proclaiming light to both Yehudim and non-Jews.”
[Acts] [26]:[24] Then speaking about Paulos’s defence, Governor Festos said, “Paulos, you’re stark, raving mad! All your education has turned you into an idiot.”
[Acts] [26]:[25] But Paulos said, “I haven’t gone mad, most excellent Festos, but I’m speaking the truth in all seriousness.
[Acts] [26]:[26] The king knows what I’m talking about and that’s why I’m speaking boldly, because none of these things were done in a corner and I’m sure that none of it has escaped his notice.
[Acts] [26]:[27] King Agrippas, do you believe what the prophets wrote? Yes, I’m sure you do.”
[Acts] [26]:[28] But Agrippas answered Paulos, “Do you think you can talk me into becoming a follower of the messiah in just that short time?”
[Acts] [26]:[29] “I hope to God”, said Paulos, “whether it takes a short time or a long time, that both you and the others listening today will become just like me except for these chains.”
[Acts] [26]:[30] Then the king and the governor both stood, along with Bernike and the others sitting with them
[Acts] [26]:[31] and as they left they were saying to each other, “That man hasn’t done anything deserving of death or imprisonment.”
[Acts] [26]:[32] “Yes, he could have been set free,” replied Agrippas, “if he hadn’t appealed to Kaisar.”
[Acts] [27]:[1] So when it was considered the right season to sail to Italia, Paulos and some other prisoners were put under the guard of a centurion named Yulios (from the Augustan Regiment).
[Acts] [27]:[2] We all boarded on a ship from Adramuttainos that was about to sail to various places along the coast of Asia Minor. Aristarkos, a Makedonian man from Thessalonikai, was with us as we departed.
[Acts] [27]:[3] The next day we docked at Tsidon (Sidon) where Yulios very kindly allowed Paulos to visit some of his friends so they could provide for his needs.
[Acts] [27]:[4] When we left again, the ship stayed between Kupros (Cyprus) and the mainland because of the unfavourable winds,
[Acts] [27]:[5] then after sailing past Kilikia and Pamfulia, we docked at Mura in the province of Lukia.
[Acts] [27]:[6] There the centurion found a ship from Alexandria that was sailing to Italia, so he boarded us on that.
[Acts] [27]:[7] After many days of slow and difficult sailing, we came alongside Knidos but the wind wasn’t helpful to us, so we sailed across to Kraitai (Crete) and along the cape of Salmone.
[Acts] [27]:[8] We sailed along it with difficulty until we came to a place called ‘Fair Havens’ which was near the city of Lasaia.
[Acts] [27]:[9] A lot of time had now elapsed and the voyage was starting to become dangerous because we were already heading into winter. Paulos advised those in charge,
[Acts] [27]:[10] telling them, “Men, I perceive that we’re going to encounter a lot of damage on this voyage, with loss not only of the cargo and the ship, but also our lives.”
[Acts] [27]:[11] But the centurion was persuaded by the ship owner and the captain, rather than by what Paulos had said.
[Acts] [27]:[12] They realised that this harbour wasn’t suitable to winter in, so the majority suggested leaving there with the expectation of being able to get to Kraitai to winter in the harbour at Foinix (which was open to both the southwest and the northwest).
[Acts] [27]:[13] When a south wind started blowing gently, they thought they could make it, so they pulled in the anchor and sailed along close to Kraitai (Crete).
[Acts] [27]:[14] However, a short while later the wind turned to a violent north-easter which forced us out to sea.
[Acts] [27]:[15] The ship was driven by the wind and unable to tack to face into it, so the sailors gave up and just let it be driven.
[Acts] [27]:[16] As we passed a small island called Klaudai, we got a brief break and were able to resecure the lifeboat
[Acts] [27]:[17] and then bring it up on board. Then ropes were used to wrap around the ship in case it were to run aground into the shallows at Surtis and the gear was lowered, allowing the wind to drive the ship along.
[Acts] [27]:[18] We were violently tossed around by the storm, and the next day the crew started lightening the ship by tipping some of the cargo overboard.
[Acts] [27]:[19] By the third day, the sailors themselves in desperation were even throwing some of the ship’s gear overboard.
[Acts] [27]:[20] We didn’t see either the sun or the stars for several more days—it wasn’t a minor storm by any means—and by then any remaining hope that we had of staying alive disappeared
[Acts] [27]:[21] and no one had eaten or drunk much at all. Then Paulos stood up in the middle of them and said, “Well, you should have listened to me after all and not left Kraitai, so now we have this damage and loss.
[Acts] [27]:[22] Nevertheless I think we can all cheer up because not a single life will be lost—only the ship—
[Acts] [27]:[23] because last night one of the messengers of the God that I serve came and stood beside me
[Acts] [27]:[24] and told me not to be afraid because I would indeed get to stand before Kaisar and that God has granted your lives to me as well.
[Acts] [27]:[25] So cheer up, fellows, because I’m certain that God will carry out what was told to me
[Acts] [27]:[26] even though we’ll run aground onto an island first.”
[Acts] [27]:[27] So it happened that in the middle of our fourteenth night of being blown across the Adrias Sea, the sailors suspected that we were nearing land.
[Acts] [27]:[28] They dropped a weighted line and measured the ocean depth at around 40 metres and then a bit later it was down to 30 metres.
[Acts] [27]:[29] Worrying that the ship might run aground on rough rocks, they threw out four anchors from the stern as they hoped that daylight would come quickly.
[Acts] [27]:[30] Then the sailors lowered the lifeboat as if planning to pull out some anchors from the bow, but really planning to desert the ship.
[Acts] [27]:[31] However Paulos told the centurion and the soldiers that if the sailors didn’t remain with the ship, everybody couldn’t be sure to be saved,
[Acts] [27]:[32] so the soldiers cut the ropes attaching the lifeboat and allowed it to run aground.
[Acts] [27]:[33] As they waited for the daylight, Paulos encouraged them all to eat something, saying, “Today is our fourteenth day and you’ve had nothing to eat. As we’re waiting,
[Acts] [27]:[34] I urge you to eat something. This will help you to have strength because none of you are going to drown.”
[Acts] [27]:[35] Having said that, he gave thanks to God in front of everyone, and breaking some bread, started eating it.
[Acts] [27]:[36] They all cheered up and also started eating.
[Acts] [27]:[37] There were two hundred and seventy-six of them on the ship,
[Acts] [27]:[38] and when they’d all eaten what they wanted, they lightened the ship more by throwing their wheat into the sea.
[Acts] [27]:[39] Once it became light, they saw that they were close to shore in a bay but didn’t recognise the place. After some discussion, they decided to try to save the ship
[Acts] [27]:[40] so they cut away the anchors that were holding them in the sea and untied the rudder handles. Then raising the foresail, they let the wind blow them into the shore.
[Acts] [27]:[41] But they hit a bank with ocean on both sides of it and the ship ran aground. The bow of the ship was completely stuck but the stern was being broken up by the force of the ocean.
[Acts] [27]:[42] At this point the soldiers decided that they should kill the prisoners in case any of them decided to swim away and escape,
[Acts] [27]:[43] but the centurion wanted to keep Paulos safe so he vetoed that plan. He commanded those who could swim to jump off and swim in to shore,
[Acts] [27]:[44] and for the others to grab floating planks or something off the ship that would float, and so everyone got safely onto the beach.
[Acts] [28]:[1] Once everyone was safe, we discovered that the island is called Melitai.
[Acts] [28]:[2] And the people there showed incredible kindness to us as they welcomed us and lit a fire, as it started raining again and was very cold.
[Acts] [28]:[3] However when Paulos was helping to pick up sticks and putting them on the fire, a viper was driven out by the heat and clamped its jaws down on his hand.
[Acts] [28]:[4] When the islanders saw the snake hanging from his hand they decided that he must be a murderer who had survived the shipwreck but now fate had finally decided his time was up.
[Acts] [28]:[5] However, Paulos just shook the snake off into the fire and wasn’t harmed.
[Acts] [28]:[6] The locals were waiting for his arm to swell up or for him to fall down dead, but after a while when nothing happened they changed their minds and decided that instead, he must be a god.
[Acts] [28]:[7] The area that we had beached in belonged to the leader of the island named Poplios. He welcomed us and looked after us for three days,
[Acts] [28]:[8] but while we were there, his father got sick with dysentery and fever. Paulos went in and placing his hands on him, prayed for him and healed him.
[Acts] [28]:[9] As a result of that, anyone on the whole island who was sick came and was cured
[Acts] [28]:[10] and so the people brought us many gifts and when we left, they supplied us with provisions.
[Acts] [28]:[11] After three months we were able to leave on an Alexandrian ship that had wintered at the island. It was decorated with carvings of the twin ‘gods’.
[Acts] [28]:[12] We stayed three days when we arrived at Surakousai
[Acts] [28]:[13] and then we sailed on to Raigion. The next day a south wind came so we sailed on to Potioloi
[Acts] [28]:[14] where we found some believers and they encouraged us to stay for seven days. Then we finally got to Romai.
[Acts] [28]:[15] The believers in Romai had heard about us, so they came to meet us at the Appios Market and the Three Taverns. Paulos was encouraged to see them and thanked God.
[Acts] [28]:[16] When we got into Romai proper, Paulos was allowed to live by himself, with just a soldier guarding him.
[Acts] [28]:[17] After three days, he called together the leaders of the Yehudim (Jews) in Romai, and when they’d all gathered he spoke to them, “Men, brothers, I have done nothing against my people or against our ancestral customs. I was taken prisoner in Yerushalem (Jerusalem) and handed over to the Romaios
[Acts] [28]:[18] who, after examining me, wanted to release me because I had done nothing worthy of execution.
[Acts] [28]:[19] But in defending myself against the Yehudim there, I felt compelled to appeal to Kaisar, although I myself had no complaint against the Yehudim.
[Acts] [28]:[20] So that was why I called for you and wanted to address you, because I am in chains for the sake of Yisrael’s (Israel) hope—the messiah.”
[Acts] [28]:[21] “We haven’t received any correspondence here about you,” they answered. “Nor have any of our brothers from Yerushalem arrived here to report any crimes of yours.
[Acts] [28]:[22] But we would very much like to hear from you about your thinking, because we’ve certainly heard about this new sect because everyone is speaking out against it.”
[Acts] [28]:[23] Then they set a day when they could visit him where he was staying and so that from morning to evening he could explain about God’s kingdom and show them how Mosheh’s (Moses) law and the prophets’ writings spoke about Yeshua (Jesus; Grk. Yesus).
[Acts] [28]:[24] Afterwards some were persuaded while others didn’t find it believable.
[Acts] [28]:[25] They argued back and forth, and as they were about to leave, Paulos shared this final message, “The holy spirit spoke rightly through Yeshayah (Isaiah) the prophet to your ancestors, saying:
[Acts] [28]:[26] Go to these people and tell them, When you listen you will hear but not understand, and when you look you will see but not perceive it.
[Acts] [28]:[27] Because these people’s minds have become dull and they can barely hear with their ears and they shut their eyes, just in case their eyes might actually see, and their ears might actually hear, and they might understand with their minds, and turn back to me and then I would heal them.
[Acts] [28]:[28] So now let it be known to you all that the message of salvation from God has been sent out to non-Jews and they will listen.”
[Acts] [28]:[29] ◘
[Acts] [28]:[30] Paulos remained in his own rental accommodation in Romai for two whole years and welcomed everyone who went to see him,
[Acts] [28]:[31] telling them about God’s kingdom and boldly teaching about the master Yeshua (Jesus; Grk. Yesus) without any hindrance.
[Romaios] [1]:[1] This letter is from Paulos, a slave of Messiah Yeshua (Jesus; Grk. Yesus) and a chosen ambassador who’s been set apart for God’s good message,
[Romaios] [1]:[2] which God had previously promised through the messages of his prophets in the holy scriptures.
[Romaios] [1]:[3] This good message is about his son, who was conceived as a descendant of David,
[Romaios] [1]:[4] and became known as God’s son according to the spirit of holiness—demonstrating power by coming back to life from the dead. Yes, he’s our master, Yeshua Messiah,
[Romaios] [1]:[5] and it’s through him that we received generous gifts, and also the assignment to faithfully, obediently take his name to all the non-Jews,
[Romaios] [1]:[6] which also includes you non-Jews there who Yeshua Messiah invited.
[Romaios] [1]:[7] This letter is written to all those in Romai that God loves and considers as holy. May you all experience generosity and peace from God our father and from the master Yeshua Messiah.
[Romaios] [1]:[8] I’ll start by thanking my God through Yeshua (Jesus; Grk. Yesus) Messiah for all of you, because the story about your faith has been told in many countries.
[Romaios] [1]:[9] Yes, the God that I serve in my spirit, in the good message about his son, is my witness about how I never stop mentioning you Romaios
[Romaios] [1]:[10] in my prayers—asking that somehow God will favour me by allowing me to come and visit you,
[Romaios] [1]:[11] because I’m longing to see you so that I can share a particular spiritual gift with you in order to strengthen you.
[Romaios] [1]:[12] I want all of us to be encouraged together by each other’s faith—both me and you Romaios.
[Romaios] [1]:[13] Brothers and sisters, I don’t want you to be unaware that I’d planned several times to come to you, but I was vetoed until recently so that I’d also have a harvest among you similar to those among the other non-Jews.
[Romaios] [1]:[14] Whether it’s Hellains (Greeks) or other foreigners, wise people or foolish, I have an obligation,
[Romaios] [1]:[15] and so I’m also eager to talk about the good message to all of you there in Romai.
[Romaios] [1]:[16] I’m not ashamed to talk about the good message, because it conveys God’s power to save everyone who believes it—first Yehudim (Jews) and then non-Jews.
[Romaios] [1]:[17] It explains how God makes us guiltless—by faith leading to more faith—as it’s been written: Godly people will live by faith.
[Romaios] [1]:[18] God’s severe anger is being revealed from heaven on the ungodliness and disobedience of people who limit the truth by their disobedience,
[Romaios] [1]:[19] because the fact that there is a god has been shown to them, because God himself has revealed it.
[Romaios] [1]:[20] Ever since the creation of the world, God’s invisible attributes have been clearly seen through his workmanship—both his eternal power and his divinity—so people have no excuse.
[Romaios] [1]:[21] Even though they know about God, they didn’t honour or thank him, but their theories made them incompetent and their minds turned from perception towards darkness.
[Romaios] [1]:[22] They claimed to be scientific, but instead they believed foolishness,
[Romaios] [1]:[23] and so they changed the greatness of the eternal God into the likeness of an image of a mortal human, or birds or animals or reptiles.
[Romaios] [1]:[24] Therefore God reluctantly let their lusts lead to impurity and the dishonouring of their bodies among themselves,
[Romaios] [1]:[25] as they exchanged God’s truth for a lie, and worshipped and served the creation, instead of the creator, who should be praised throughout all time. May it be so.
[Romaios] [1]:[26] Because of that, God reluctantly let them exercise their dishonourable passions, and their women exchanged natural behaviours for unnatural ones,
[Romaios] [1]:[27] and similarly their men deserted the natural behaviours towards women, and stoked their lusts towards each other—man with man, and the shame that it produces, and then received back in themselves the payment which is appropriate for such deception.
[Romaios] [1]:[28] They didn’t want to know about God, and so he reluctantly let their depraved minds be filled with unhelpful thoughts,
[Romaios] [1]:[29] and so they were filled with disobedience, wickedness, greed, and malice, and full of envy, murder, strife, and deceit, becoming malicious people, gossips,
[Romaios] [1]:[30] slanderers, god-haters, abusers, proud people, braggers, and inventors of evil, unable to be persuaded by their parents,
[Romaios] [1]:[31] unintelligent, untrustworthy, unloving, and unmerciful.
[Romaios] [1]:[32] They know that God must exercise justice towards people doing such things, yet they not only practice those things which will lead to a death sentence, but they also approve when others do them.
[Romaios] [2]:[1] So there’s no excuse for anyone who judges others, because you’re condemning yourselves if you’re doing those same things that you’re judging others for,
[Romaios] [2]:[2] because we know that God’s judgement is based on the factual accounts of what each person is doing.
[Romaios] [2]:[3] But maybe you’re thinking that you can judge others doing these things and yet somehow escape God’s judgement when you do them yourself?
[Romaios] [2]:[4] Or maybe you’re taking advantage of God’s kindness and patience, without realising that his kindness was meant to lead you to turn away from your wrongdoing?
[Romaios] [2]:[5] But it’s your hardness and failure to turn away from wrongdoing that’s causing severe anger to be stored up for God’s judgement day, when all will be revealed, including his severe anger,
[Romaios] [2]:[6] as each person will be judged by their actions.
[Romaios] [2]:[7] Those who’ve persistently done good, expecting praise and honour, and to escape destruction, will be given eternal life,
[Romaios] [2]:[8] but those who’ve lived out their selfish ambition and refused to believe the truth, but let themselves get persuaded by disobedience, will meet with severe anger and rage.
[Romaios] [2]:[9] For every person doing evil, there’ll be trouble and distress—to Yehudim (Jews) first and then to non-Jews,
[Romaios] [2]:[10] but for those who do good, there’ll be praise and honour and peace—to Yehudim first and then to non-Jews,
[Romaios] [2]:[11] because God doesn’t indulge in favouritism.
[Romaios] [2]:[12] Those who weren’t under the Jewish laws and yet sinned, they’ll be judged without the law, and those who knew the laws and sinned will be judged by the law,
[Romaios] [2]:[13] because listening to the law doesn’t make people right with God, but rather it’s those who obey the law who’ll be declared guiltless.
[Romaios] [2]:[14] Whenever other nations don’t have the Jewish laws, but naturally obey what’s in the laws, they show that even without our laws, they have their own law.
[Romaios] [2]:[15] They demonstrate that they effectively have God’s law written in their minds and agreeing with their consciences, and between the two they’ll be either accused or defended
[Romaios] [2]:[16] on the day when God, through Messiah Yeshua (Jesus; Grk. Yesus), judges people’s private lives, as I’ve shared as part of the good message.
[Romaios] [2]:[17] But if you’re a Yehudi (Jew), and trusting in the law, and boasting about being chosen by God
[Romaios] [2]:[18] and knowing his will and knowing what’s important because of familiarity with the law,
[Romaios] [2]:[19] and if you’ve persuaded yourself that you’re a guide for blind people and a light to people who are in darkness,
[Romaios] [2]:[20] and that you’re an instructor to foolish people and a teacher of children, and you appear to be knowledgeable about the truth of the law,
[Romaios] [2]:[21] then why do you teach others when you haven’t even taught yourself? You announce that stealing is wrong, but you’re a thief.
[Romaios] [2]:[22] You teach about not messing with other people’s spouses, yet you do it yourself. You detest idols, but you sneak money out of the temple.
[Romaios] [2]:[23] You boast about being a student of the law, but you dishonour God by breaking the laws.
[Romaios] [2]:[24] Yes, it’s been written: ‘God’s name is slandered among the nations because of you people.’
[Romaios] [2]:[25] Circumcision is of value if you’re keeping the law, but if you’re breaking the laws, then your circumcision means just the same as if you’re uncircumcised,
[Romaios] [2]:[26] so if uncircumcised people groups behave justly according to the law, even though they’re not physically circumcised, God will consider them as his people.
[Romaios] [2]:[27] Yes, those people groups who aren’t circumcised, but keep the law, will be judging you who were given the law in writing and are circumcised, yet break those laws.
[Romaios] [2]:[28] A true Yehudi isn’t just a Yehudi on the outside, and their circumcision isn’t just on the outside of their body,
[Romaios] [2]:[29] but they’re a Yehudi even in their private life and through circumcision of their heart—by the spirit and not by the letter of the law—earning praise not from people, but from God.
[Romaios] [3]:[1] So what advantage is there in being a Yehudi (Jew), and what’s the benefit of circumcision?
[Romaios] [3]:[2] A lot, in every way. Firstly, Yehudim (Jews) were entrusted with the writing down of God’s messages.
[Romaios] [3]:[3] But what if some didn’t believe? Wouldn’t the unbelief of Yehudim make faith that comes from God worthless?
[Romaios] [3]:[4] Absolutely not. Even if every person was a liar, God is truthful, just like it’s been written about him: ‘You will be proved right about what you say, and you’ll prevail when you’re judged in court.’
[Romaios] [3]:[5] But if our sinfulness highlights God’s sinlessness, what can we say about that? Isn’t God, the one inflicting the severe anger, wrong to punish us? (Of course, this is reasoning from a human perspective.)
[Romaios] [3]:[6] Of course not, otherwise how could God be able to judge the world?
[Romaios] [3]:[7] But if my lie exposes God’s truth and so brings him honour, why would he still judge me as a sinner?
[Romaios] [3]:[8] Some people falsely accuse us of saying, ‘Let’s do evil things so that good might follow.’ Those who say that deserve their punishment.
[Romaios] [3]:[9] What then? Do Yehudim (Jews) have any advantage? Definitely not, because we showed earlier that both Yehudim and other nationalities are all under sin’s shadow,
[Romaios] [3]:[10] just like it was written long ago: ‘No one is guiltless, not even one person.
[Romaios] [3]:[11] No one understands, there’s not even one person trying to find God.
[Romaios] [3]:[12] Everyone has turned away, it was a waste of time. No one is being kind, Not even one person.’
[Romaios] [3]:[13] ‘Their words lead to death, their tongues are deceptive.’ ‘Their lips spray out poison.’
[Romaios] [3]:[14] ‘Their mouths are full of cursing and bitterness.’
[Romaios] [3]:[15] ‘They rush off to go and shed blood.
[Romaios] [3]:[16] They leave trails of destruction and misery—
[Romaios] [3]:[17] they don’t know the path that leads to peace.’
[Romaios] [3]:[18] Revering God isn’t at the front of their minds.
[Romaios] [3]:[19] We know that whatever the law says, it’s for everyone that the law applies to, so that no one can speak against it, and the whole world will be bound by God’s judgement.
[Romaios] [3]:[20] No human will be declared guiltless in front of God by their keeping the law, because it’s the law that teaches what sin is.
[Romaios] [3]:[21] But now God has revealed a way to remove guilt that’s not by rules—a way that Mosheh (Moses) and the prophets wrote about.
[Romaios] [3]:[22] We can be made right with God through faith in Yeshua (Jesus; Grk. Yesus) Messiah. This is for everyone who believes, because there’s no distinction between Yehudim (Jews) and others,
[Romaios] [3]:[23] because everyone has sinned and is unable to be honoured by God.
[Romaios] [3]:[24] But even without deserving it, we can be declared guiltless by God’s generosity, by being bought out of slavery to sin by Messiah Yeshua,
[Romaios] [3]:[25] who God placed on the altar as a sacrifice for sin. This happens through faith in his blood, which was a sign of his sinlessness. (God hasn’t yet judged those who sinned in the past,
[Romaios] [3]:[26] because of his patience, waiting for the present time to show his righteousness and to be fair, and to remove the guilt of those with faith in Yeshua.)
[Romaios] [3]:[27] So where does that leave boasting? It’s not in the picture. How come? Through obeying Mosheh’s laws? No, through a law about faith.
[Romaios] [3]:[28] So now we should expect that a person will be made guiltless by faith—not by obeying Mosheh’s laws.
[Romaios] [3]:[29] Or is God only god of the Yehudim? Isn’t he also the god of others? Yes, he is the god of others.
[Romaios] [3]:[30] Indeed, there’s only one God, and he declares people guiltless by faith whether they’re circumcised Yehudim, or non-Jews.
[Romaios] [3]:[31] So does this ‘faith’ cancel the law? Not on your life. In fact, it upholds the law.
[Romaios] [4]:[1] So what did our physical ancestor, Avraham, discover about all this?
[Romaios] [4]:[2] Because if Avraham was declared guiltless because of his actions, maybe he could boast? But not towards God,
[Romaios] [4]:[3] because the scriptures say: ‘Avraham believed in God, so he was considered guiltless.’
[Romaios] [4]:[4] Now for someone who’s working, their wages are considered ‘owed’, not a gift.
[Romaios] [4]:[5] However, someone who’s not working, but having faith that God will declare disobedient people as guiltless, that person’s faith is considered to make them guiltless.
[Romaios] [4]:[6] It’s just like what David said about blessing a person who God declares as guiltless despite their actions:
[Romaios] [4]:[7] ‘Those who’ve been forgiven for their lawlessness will be happy, whose sins have been covered over.
[Romaios] [4]:[8] Anyone who Yahweh declares to have no sin will be happy.’
[Romaios] [4]:[9] Is this favour shown only to circumcised Yehudim (Jews), or is it also for non-Jews? After all, we were saying that Avraham was considered guiltless because of his faith.
[Romaios] [4]:[10] So how did that happen? Because he was circumcised, or when he was still uncircumcised? No, it was before he was circumcised.
[Romaios] [4]:[11] He received circumcision as a sign—proof of the righteousness that he gained from his faith while he was still uncircumcised—becoming the father of everyone who’s uncircumcised but believes so that they’ll be declared guiltless.
[Romaios] [4]:[12] So our ancestor Avraham is the ancestor of us as a circumcised people group, not just because we’re circumcised, but also as we follow the steps of faith he took while uncircumcised.
[Romaios] [4]:[13] It wasn’t because of his obeying the law that it was promised that Avraham or his descendants would inherit the world, but because of his righteousness that came from his faith,
[Romaios] [4]:[14] because if the ones obeying the law can become heirs, then faith would be declared as useless, and the promise would be invalidated,
[Romaios] [4]:[15] because the law produces severe anger, and where there’s no law, there’s nothing to break.
[Romaios] [4]:[16] Because of this, the promise to the descendants is by faith—given not only to the ‘descendants of the law’, but also to the ‘descendants of Avraham’s faith’. This promise is given as a gift, and has been confirmed,
[Romaios] [4]:[17] as it’s been written, ‘I’ve appointed you as a father of many nations.’ He was appointed in front of the god he believed in—the god who brings the dead back to life, and who creates by speaking things into being that didn’t previously exist.
[Romaios] [4]:[18] Without any other evidence, he believed in hope itself, and thus he became the father of many nations, just like he’d been told: ‘Your descendants will be like the sand and the stars.’
[Romaios] [4]:[19] He didn’t falter in his faith, seeing that his body was already infertile, being about a hundred years old, and with Sarah being past menopause.
[Romaios] [4]:[20] He didn’t show unbelief and doubt God’s promise when it was given, but rather he was strengthened in his faith and praised God,
[Romaios] [4]:[21] being quite certain that what God promises, he’s also able to do.
[Romaios] [4]:[22] Therefore his faith was credited to him and he was declared guiltless.
[Romaios] [4]:[23] However, that statement wasn’t written about Avraham only,
[Romaios] [4]:[24] but about us, too, who are also going to receive the same credit, because of our faith in the God who brought our master Yeshua (Jesus; Grk. Yesus) back to life from the dead
[Romaios] [4]:[25] after he was handed over to the executioners because of our sins, and he was brought back to life to make us guiltless.
[Romaios] [5]:[1] So now because we’ve been declared guiltless by our faith, we can have peace with God through our master Yeshua (Jesus; Grk. Yesus) Messiah.
[Romaios] [5]:[2] Through him we also have access by faith into this generosity that we depend on, and we’re boasting in hope of God’s glory. WHAT DOES THIS MEAN?
[Romaios] [5]:[3] Not only that, but we’re also boasting even though we’re still being persecuted, because we know that difficulties produce endurance,
[Romaios] [5]:[4] and endurance shows who we really are, and knowing that produces hope,
[Romaios] [5]:[5] and we’re not disgraced by that hope, because God’s love has been poured out into our hearts through the holy spirit who’s been given to us.
[Romaios] [5]:[6] While we were still weak, and at the right time for ungodly people, the messiah died for us.
[Romaios] [5]:[7] Now it’s rare for someone to offer to die to save a guiltless person, although perhaps someone might offer for the greater good,
[Romaios] [5]:[8] but God demonstrated his love towards us in that the messiah died for us while we were still sinners!
[Romaios] [5]:[9] So now that we’ve been declared guiltless because of his blood, we’ll certainly be spared from his severe anger,
[Romaios] [5]:[10] because if we were reconciled to God through the death of his son while we were still enemies, now that we’ve been reconciled, how much more certain that we’ll be saved by Yeshua’s (Jesus; Grk. Yesus) life!
[Romaios] [5]:[11] And not only that, because of what our master Yeshua Messiah has done so that we might receive that reconciliation, we can now boast in God about it.
[Romaios] [5]:[12] Sin came into the world through one man, and death came as a result of sin, so death spread to everyone because everyone has disobeyed God.
[Romaios] [5]:[13] Sin was in the world before Mosheh’s (Moses) law, but it wasn’t being charged against them, because the law had not yet been given.
[Romaios] [5]:[14] But death reigned from Adam’s time until Mosheh’s time, even over those who didn’t sin in the way that Adam did—Adam who was a pattern of the messiah who would eventually come.
[Romaios] [5]:[15] But the gift is not like the disobedience, because if the disobedience of one man introduced death for many, God’s generosity and the gift that comes from that generosity is much more. That gift is the one man Yeshua (Jesus; Grk. Yesus) Messiah, who’s been given to very many people.
[Romaios] [5]:[16] It only took one man who disobeyed to lead to condemnation, and one act of disobedience to lead to judgement, but the gift is to bring guiltlessness despite many acts of disobedience.
[Romaios] [5]:[17] Because if the disobedience of one man led to death reigning over us through that one man, how much more will the ones receiving an abundance of generosity and the gift of righteousness be reigning in life through the one man Yeshua Messiah.
[Romaios] [5]:[18] So just as one act of disobedience led all people to condemnation, so also one action brought all people to guiltlessness and hence to life.
[Romaios] [5]:[19] The disobedience of one man caused many people to be made sinners, so also the obedience of one man caused many people to be made guiltless.
[Romaios] [5]:[20] The law was introduced so that acts of disobedience would be plentiful, but where sin has been plentiful, generosity has overflowed,
[Romaios] [5]:[21] so that just as sin reigned in death, so also generosity now reigns through righteousness, leading to eternal life through our master Yeshua Messiah.
[Romaios] [6]:[1] So should we continue disobeying so that more of God’s generosity will be displayed?
[Romaios] [6]:[2] Not on your life! We who died to sin, how could we go back to living in it?
[Romaios] [6]:[3] Or didn’t you realise that when we were immersed into Messiah Yeshua (Jesus; Grk. Yesus), we were immersed into his death?
[Romaios] [6]:[4] Therefore we were buried with him through the immersion into death, so that just as Messiah was brought back to life by the father’s power, so too we can live a new life.
[Romaios] [6]:[5] If we’ve taken part in the likeness of his death, then we’ll also take part in the resurrection,
[Romaios] [6]:[6] knowing that the old personality was executed with him so that sin would have no more power over our bodies, and hence we no longer need to serve it,
[Romaios] [6]:[7] because the personality that’s died has been declared free from sin.
[Romaios] [6]:[8] So if we died with Messiah, we also believe that we’ll live with him,
[Romaios] [6]:[9] knowing that now that Messiah has come back to life from the dead, he won’t die again—death has no more power over him.
[Romaios] [6]:[10] When he died, he died to sin once and for all, but now that he lives, he lives to please God.
[Romaios] [6]:[11] So too, you should consider yourselves dead to sin, and at the same time, alive to God in Messiah Yeshua.
[Romaios] [6]:[12] So therefore don’t let sin rule over your mortal bodies in such a way that you’re submitting to its lusts.
[Romaios] [6]:[13] Don’t use any parts of your bodies to sin, as if they’re weapons of disobedience, but instead present yourselves to God as if you came back to life from the dead, and use all your body parts for God, as if they’re weapons of righteousness,
[Romaios] [6]:[14] so that sin won’t take control of you—because you’re not under law, but under generosity.
[Romaios] [6]:[15] What could that mean? That we can sin freely because we’re not under law but under generosity? Not on your life!
[Romaios] [6]:[16] Don’t you know who you’re presenting yourselves to as obedient slaves? Yes, whoever you submit to, you’re their slaves—either slaves of sin that leads to death, or slaves of obedience that leads to righteousness.
[Romaios] [6]:[17] But be thankful to God that although you were slaves to sin, your hearts submitted to what was taught,
[Romaios] [6]:[18] and so, having been freed from sin, you became slaves of righteousness.
[Romaios] [6]:[19] I’m speaking from a human perspective because of your human weakness. Just as you previously used parts of your bodies as slaves to impurity and lawlessness, leading down to further lawlessness, so now present your body parts as slaves to righteousness, leading up to holiness.
[Romaios] [6]:[20] When you were slaves of sin, you were immune to righteousness,
[Romaios] [6]:[21] and so what was the fruit you had back then which you’re now ashamed of? The end result of that lifestyle is death.
[Romaios] [6]:[22] But now that you’re free from slavery to sin, and are God’s slaves instead, you bear the fruit of holiness, and the end result of that is living forever,
[Romaios] [6]:[23] because the wages of sin are death, but God gives eternal life as a gift through our master Yeshua (Jesus; Grk. Yesus) Messiah.
[Romaios] [7]:[1] Brothers and sisters, you know the Law well that I’m talking about, so surely you realise that the law acts as a person’s master for as long as they live?
[Romaios] [7]:[2] For example, a woman who’s married to her husband is bound by the law, but if her husband dies then she’s released from the law concerning her husband.
[Romaios] [7]:[3] So while her husband was still living, he’d call her an adulteress if she slept with another man, but after her husband is deceased, she’s free from the law and doesn’t become an adulteress if she marries another man.
[Romaios] [7]:[4] So, my brothers and sisters, you, too, were made dead to the law through the body of the messiah so that you could join to another—to the one who came back to life from the dead—so that we can bear fruit for God.
[Romaios] [7]:[5] When we were still focused on the physical, the passions aroused by sinning against the law were working in our body parts so that the fruit would be death,
[Romaios] [7]:[6] but now that we’re released from the law which held us—released by dying to it—we can serve in new ways guided by the spirit instead of by the letter of the law.
[Romaios] [7]:[7] So what will we say then? That the law is sin? Not on your life! I wouldn’t have known what sin was if it wasn’t for the Law. For example, I wouldn’t have known what coveting was if the Law hadn’t told me not to covet.
[Romaios] [7]:[8] But sin took the opportunity from that command to produce covetousness in me, because sin would be dead without the Law.
[Romaios] [7]:[9] For a time I was living without the Law, but once God’s command came, sin revived
[Romaios] [7]:[10] and I died, and I discovered that the command, which should lead to life, led to death.
[Romaios] [7]:[11] Sin deceived me when the command gave it an opportunity, and in doing so, it killed me.
[Romaios] [7]:[12] Now the Law is indeed holy, and God’s command is holy and righteous and good,
[Romaios] [7]:[13] so did what’s good turn into death? Not on your life! Rather, it was the good Law that allowed me to see sin as sin and a producer of death, and the command showed me how completely sinful sin really is.
[Romaios] [7]:[14] We know that God’s law is spiritual, but I am physical, having been born into sin.
[Romaios] [7]:[15] I don’t know what’s going on, because I do what I don’t want to do, and I end up doing what I hate.
[Romaios] [7]:[16] So if I do something that I didn’t want to do, then I’m agreeing with the Law that it’s good,
[Romaios] [7]:[17] and it’s no longer me that’s doing it, but the sin that’s in me.
[Romaios] [7]:[18] I’m aware that good isn’t in my physical body, because I want to do good but I can’t.
[Romaios] [7]:[19] I don’t do the good that I want to do, but rather I do the evil that I don’t want to do,
[Romaios] [7]:[20] so if I’m doing what I don’t want to do, then it’s not me doing it, but it’s the sin in me that does it.
[Romaios] [7]:[21] As a result, I’ve discovered the principle that when I want to do good, actually there’s evil in me,
[Romaios] [7]:[22] because I’m happily accepting God’s Law on the inside,
[Romaios] [7]:[23] but I’m observing another law in my body parts, fighting against my mind and keeping me imprisoned in sin’s law, which is in my body parts.
[Romaios] [7]:[24] I’m a miserable person. Who’ll rescue me from this body that’s full of death?
[Romaios] [7]:[25] Thankfully, it’s God, through our master Yeshua (Jesus; Grk. Yesus) Messiah. So I end up with my mind wanting to serve God’s Law, but on the other hand, my body wants to serve sin’s law.
[Romaios] [8]:[1] So now those who are in Messiah Yeshua (Jesus; Grk. Yesus) cannot be condemned,
[Romaios] [8]:[2] because the law of the spirit of life in him freed you from the law of sin and death.
[Romaios] [8]:[3] The law was powerless in that it was faltering through our bodies. God sent his son in a body just like our sinful bodies, and concerning sin, he condemned sin itself in the body,
[Romaios] [8]:[4] so that for those of us who are no longer governed by physical desires, but by the spirit, the law’s just action will be fulfilled in us.
[Romaios] [8]:[5] People who are governed by their physical desires think about physical things, but those who are governed by the spirit think about spiritual things.
[Romaios] [8]:[6] The worldly mindset leads to death, but the spiritual mindset leads to life and peace.
[Romaios] [8]:[7] The worldly mindset is making God your enemy because it’s not being subjected to God’s law, in fact it’s not even able to,
[Romaios] [8]:[8] and those who are worldly aren’t able to do what pleases God.
[Romaios] [8]:[9] And you, brothers and sisters, aren’t worldly, but are in the spirit, if indeed God’s spirit is living in you, but anyone who doesn’t have Messiah’s spirit doesn’t belong to him.
[Romaios] [8]:[10] But if Messiah is in you, while your body is dead because of sin, your spirit has life because it’s been declared guiltless.
[Romaios] [8]:[11] Yes, if the spirit of the one who brought Yeshua (Jesus; Grk. Yesus) back to life is living in you, then the one who brought Messiah Yeshua back to life will also give life to your mortal bodies by means of his spirit living inside you.
[Romaios] [8]:[12] So then, brothers and sisters, we don’t owe anything to our sinful natures, nor do we need to live in worldly ways.
[Romaios] [8]:[13] If your lives, brothers and sisters, are governed by your sinful natures, you’ll die, but if you put bodily practices to death with the help of the spirit, you’ll live,
[Romaios] [8]:[14] because everyone who’s led by God’s spirit becomes one of God’s children.
[Romaios] [8]:[15] You didn’t receive a spirit of slavery to fear again, but rather it was the spirit of adoption as children that you received, and with his help we call out, ‘Dad, dad!’
[Romaios] [8]:[16] God’s spirit himself agrees together with our spirit that we are God’s children,
[Romaios] [8]:[17] and if we’re his children, then we’re also heirs, so we’ll receive an inheritance from God. That makes us fellow-heirs along with Messiah—if we’re suffering with him then we’ll also be honoured along with him.
[Romaios] [8]:[18] I’m sure that any sufferings we experience in this age are nothing in comparison with the coming splendour that’s going to be revealed to us,
[Romaios] [8]:[19] because all of creation is eagerly expecting and waiting for God’s children to be revealed.
[Romaios] [8]:[20] Yes, all of creation has been subjected to lack of purpose, not willingly, but because it was decided by the one who subjected it, but it remains with the hope
[Romaios] [8]:[21] that it too will be freed from the slavery of corruption, and then released into the freedom of the splendour of God’s children,
[Romaios] [8]:[22] because we’re aware that all of creation is groaning and suffering along with us right through to the present time.
[Romaios] [8]:[23] And not only that, but we ourselves who have the initial tastes of the spirit life, we’re also groaning and waiting like children for our bodies to be set free from slavery,
[Romaios] [8]:[24] because we were saved, having hope, but if you can see it then it’s not hope, because you don’t need to hope for something you can already see.
[Romaios] [8]:[25] So we hope for what we can’t yet see, and so we have to patiently keep waiting.
[Romaios] [8]:[26] Similarly, the spirit also helps us with our weaknesses, because we don’t even know what to pray for, but the spirit intercedes with groanings that we can’t put into words.
[Romaios] [8]:[27] The one who searches our hearts knows the mindset of the spirit, because the spirit intercedes for the believers as God desires.
[Romaios] [8]:[28] We know that God makes all things work together for good for everyone who loves him—those who are being invited according to his purpose.
[Romaios] [8]:[29] After all, those he knew in advance, he also determined in advance to be similar to his son’s image, so that his son would become the eldest of many siblings.
[Romaios] [8]:[30] The ones he’d determined in advance he also invited, and the ones he’d invited, he also declared guiltless, and the ones he declared guiltless, he also honoured in heaven.
[Romaios] [8]:[31] So then, what can we say about all this? If God is for us, who’s against us?
[Romaios] [8]:[32] If he didn’t spare his own son, but gave him to be executed for us, won’t they together also give us everything else?
[Romaios] [8]:[33] Who’ll bring charges against people chosen by God? God is the one declaring us guiltless.
[Romaios] [8]:[34] So who’s the one condemning us? Messiah Yeshua (Jesus; Grk. Yesus) (the one who died but came back to life and who’s now sitting beside God) is also pleading for us.
[Romaios] [8]:[35] Who will separate us from Messiah’s love? Troubles or distress or persecution or famine or poverty or danger or execution?
[Romaios] [8]:[36] As it’s been written: ‘We are being put to death all day on your account. We were counted like sheep ready to be slaughtered.’
[Romaios] [8]:[37] But in all that, we’re more than conquerors through the one who loved us.
[Romaios] [8]:[38] Yes, I’ve been persuaded that neither death or life, angels or rulers, present or future events, powers,
[Romaios] [8]:[39] height or depth, or anything else in creation, will be able to separate us from God’s love that’s revealed in our master Messiah Yeshua.
[Romaios] [9]:[1] I’m not lying—I’m speaking truthfully in Messiah, and both my conscience and the holy spirit agree
[Romaios] [9]:[2] that my sorrow is extensive, and the sorrow in my heart just won’t stop,
[Romaios] [9]:[3] because I was hoping that I myself would be a sacrifice from the messiah for my brothers and sisters, my fellow-citizens in this world.
[Romaios] [9]:[4] They’re the descendants of Yisrael (Israel) who’ve been adopted as God’s children, and who God revealed his power to, as well as the agreements, the Law, the temple worship, and the promises.
[Romaios] [9]:[5] The patriarchs are Jewish, and the messiah, who has authority over everything, physically came from them. May God be blessed throughout the ages. May it be so.
[Romaios] [9]:[6] But it’s not that God’s message has failed. Yisrael doesn’t include all of Yisrael’s descendants,
[Romaios] [9]:[7] nor are all of Avraham’s descendants his children, but, ‘It’s through Yitshak (Isaac) that your descendants will be counted.’
[Romaios] [9]:[8] That isn’t talking about biological children—these are God’s children, but the children of the promise are being counted as descendants.
[Romaios] [9]:[9] After all, this message is the promise: ‘I’ll come back, and Sarah will have a son.’
[Romaios] [9]:[10] And not only that, but also Rivkah (Rebecca), from one pregnancy to our ancestor Yitshak, delivered twins.
[Romaios] [9]:[11] Before they were born, and so before they could do anything good or bad, in order that God’s deliberate choice would stand
[Romaios] [9]:[12] (not as a result of effort, but by God’s announcement), she was told, ‘The older child will serve the younger one.’
[Romaios] [9]:[13] As it was written: ‘I loved Ya’akov (Jacob) but I hated Esav (Esau).’
[Romaios] [9]:[14] So what should we say then? Is God unfair? Of course not,
[Romaios] [9]:[15] because he said to Mosheh (Moses): ‘I’ll be merciful to whoever I want to, and I’ll have pity on anyone I want to.’
[Romaios] [9]:[16] In other words, it doesn’t depend on the willingness or activities of the person, but on God’s mercy.
[Romaios] [9]:[17] After all, in the scriptures, God says to the king of Mitsrayim (Egypt): ‘I chose you as king so that I can demonstrate my power through you, and so that my name will be talked about all over the world.’
[Romaios] [9]:[18] In other words, God will be merciful to whoever he wants to, but he hardens whoever he wants to.
[Romaios] [9]:[19] So now you’ll ask me: Then how can God blame us, because how could anyone resist whatever he wants to do?
[Romaios] [9]:[20] Oh human, are you talking back to God? Can the creature that was made talk back to the maker and ask: ‘Why did you make me like this?’
[Romaios] [9]:[21] Doesn’t the potter have the right to split the lump of clay and make a beautiful bowl out of half and a chamber pot out of the other half?
[Romaios] [9]:[22] What if God wanted to display his severe anger and to demonstrate his power, but then showed great patience to the objects of his severe anger that he’d prepared for destruction?
[Romaios] [9]:[23] What if he did that in order to make the riches of his greatness known to the objects of his mercy that he’d prepared for honour?
[Romaios] [9]:[24] Yes, he even called us, not only from among the Yehudim (Jews) but also from non-Jews.
[Romaios] [9]:[25] The prophet Hoshea (Hosea) even wrote: “Those who aren’t my people I will call ‘my people’, and the woman who was never loved is the one I’ll call ‘my love’.
[Romaios] [9]:[26] In the place where they said, ‘You’re not my people’ that’s where they’ll be called ‘children of the living God’.”
[Romaios] [9]:[27] The prophet Yeshayah (Isaiah) announced about Yisrael (Israel): ‘Even though the Israelis are as numerous as grains of sand, only a minority of them will be saved,
[Romaios] [9]:[28] because Yahweh will be abbreviating and terminating his message on the earth.’
[Romaios] [9]:[29] As Yeshayah had previously written: ‘If Commander-in-chief Yahweh hadn’t left us some descendants, we would have become like Sedom and Amorah’s (Gomorrah) people groups.’
[Romaios] [9]:[30] So then, what should we say? That non-Jews who weren’t godly reached out by faith to achieve righteousness,
[Romaios] [9]:[31] but Yehudim (Jews) who chased after righteousness by obeying The Law didn’t achieve it?
[Romaios] [9]:[32] How come? Because they tried to reach it by actions and not by faith. They tripped over the stumbling stone,
[Romaios] [9]:[33] as it’s written: ‘Look, I’m laying down a stumbling stone in Tsiyon (Zion), a rock that causes offence. Anyone who believes in him won’t be disgraced.’
[Romaios] [10]:[1] Brothers and sisters, my heart would be very pleased indeed if Israelis would get rescued, and that’s what I request from God.
[Romaios] [10]:[2] I keep telling them that they’re very zealous for God, yet they lack know-how.
[Romaios] [10]:[3] Because they didn’t know what God’s righteousness is, and they tried to establish their own system, they weren’t covered by his righteousness.
[Romaios] [10]:[4] The fulfilment of The Law is Messiah, leading to righteousness for everyone who believes.
[Romaios] [10]:[5] Mosheh (Moses) wrote this about the Law’s righteousness: ‘The person who practices it will live because of it.’
[Romaios] [10]:[6] But the righteousness based on faith says: ‘Don’t speculate in your mind about who’ll go up to heaven in order to bring Messiah down,
[Romaios] [10]:[7] and don’t ask about who’ll go down to the pit in order to bring Messiah up.’
[Romaios] [10]:[8] So what does the righteousness based on faith say? It says: ‘The message is close to you—it’s in your mouth and heart.’ That’s the message of faith that we’ve been preaching:
[Romaios] [10]:[9] That if you speak out and acknowledge that Yeshua (Jesus; Grk. Yesus) is Yahweh, and you believe in your heart that God brought him back to life from the dead, you will be rescued,
[Romaios] [10]:[10] because it’s the belief in your mind that leads to righteousness, and it’s the acknowledgement from your mouth that leads to rescue.
[Romaios] [10]:[11] As the scriptures say: ‘Anyone who believes in him won’t end up disgraced.’
[Romaios] [10]:[12] There’s no distinction between Yehudi (Jew) and non-Jew, because we all have the same master who gives generously to everyone who makes an appeal to him,
[Romaios] [10]:[13] because everyone who appeals to Yahweh’s authority will be rescued.
[Romaios] [10]:[14] But how could they appeal to a god that they don’t even believe in? And how could they believe if they haven’t even heard about him? And how would they hear if no one told them?
[Romaios] [10]:[15] And who would be there telling them if no one was sent out? Compare what was written: ‘It’s so wonderful that these people came and announced the good message.’
[Romaios] [10]:[16] But not everyone accepted the good message, just like the prophet Yeshayah (Isaiah) wrote: ‘Yahweh, who believed our report?’
[Romaios] [10]:[17] And so faith comes by hearing—listening to Messiah’s message.

[Romaios] [10]:[19] But again I’d ask: Didn’t the Israelis know? Well, firstly Mosheh (Moses) wrote: ‘I’ll be making you all jealous using people who are not even a nation. Then using a foolish nation, I’ll be making you all angry.’
[Romaios] [10]:[20] And Yeshayah (Isaiah) dared to write: ‘The ones who weren’t looking for me found me. I showed myself to the ones not asking about me.’
[Romaios] [10]:[21] But to Yisrael (Israel) he wrote: ‘All day I stretched out my hands to a people who won’t believe and who speak against me.’

[Romaios] [11]:[18] then don’t brag that you’re better than the branches. If you must boast, remember that you’re not supporting the root, but the root is supporting you.
[Romaios] [11]:[19] Ah, but then you’ll say, ‘Branches were broken off so that we could be grafted in.’
[Romaios] [11]:[20] Well you’re right. They were broken off because of their disbelief, and it’s true that you’re there because of your faith. But don’t get a big head—maintain your reverence for God,
[Romaios] [11]:[21] because if he didn’t spare the natural branches when they showed disbelief, then he won’t spare you either.
[Romaios] [11]:[22] So you can see both God’s kindness and his severity—those who disobeyed experienced his severity, but you experienced his kindness. Otherwise you’ll be pruned off, too,
[Romaios] [11]:[23] and also, if they turn away from their disbelief, they’ll be grafted back in, because God has the power to do that.
[Romaios] [11]:[24] If you were cut off an olive tree that’s wild by nature, and contrary to normal practice were grafted into a cultivated olive tree, how much more easily would those who naturally belong be grafted into their own olive tree!
[Romaios] [11]:[25] Brothers and sisters, I don’t want you to be ignorant of this mystery, otherwise you might end up becoming proud: There’s a partial hardening coming to the Yehudim (Jews) until the fullness of the non-Jews comes,

[Romaios] [13]:[1] Everyone should be subject to the authorities who are over them, because there’s no authority except through God, and they’re appointed by God.
[Romaios] [13]:[2] So anyone opposing authority has rebelled against what God has instituted, and everyone who rebels is bringing judgement on themselves,
[Romaios] [13]:[3] because rulers don’t evoke fear in people doing good, just those doing evil. Oh, so you don’t want to be afraid of the authorities? Then do good, and you’ll receive praise from them instead,
[Romaios] [13]:[4] because they’re God’s servants for your good. But if you’re doing evil, then you should rightly be afraid, because the authorities aren’t armed without reason—they’re God’s servants to dispense severe anger to people doing evil.
[Romaios] [13]:[5] Hence it’s necessary to be subject to them, not only to avoid their severe anger, but also because of your consciences.
[Romaios] [13]:[6] That’s also why you believers should pay the taxes that you owe, because the authorities are God’s servants, and they work hard at it.
[Romaios] [13]:[7] So fulfil all of your obligations: if it’s tax then pay it, or revenue then give it, or if it’s respect then show it, or giving honour then do it.
[Romaios] [13]:[8] Don’t be in debt to anyone, other than the debt of love to each other, because people who love each other have fulfilled God’s law,
[Romaios] [13]:[9] which is: Don’t commit adultery. Don’t murder. Don’t steal. Don’t covet what others have. All of those, plus any other commands, can be summarised as: Love your neighbour like you love yourself.

[2 Korinthios] [6]:[5] beatings, imprisonments, riots, labours, sleepless nights, hunger,
[2 Korinthios] [6]:[6] by purity, knowledge, patience, kindness, the holy spirit, genuine love,
[2 Korinthios] [6]:[7] in truthful speech and in the power of God. Hold the weapons of righteousness in both your right and left hands
[2 Korinthios] [6]:[8] whether in victory or dishonour, through bad reports and good reports, even if being called fakes (but being genuine).
[2 Korinthios] [6]:[9] We’re regarded as unknowns despite being well-known, considered to be dying off yet very much alive, being beaten but not yet being killed,
[2 Korinthios] [6]:[10] regarded as sad but always happy, as poor but making many people rich, as having nothing but possessing everything.
[2 Korinthios] [6]:[11] We’ve shared our thoughts with you all from Korinthos and our hearts have been expanded.
[2 Korinthios] [6]:[12] You haven’t been restricted by us, but your own compassions restrict you all.
[2 Korinthios] [6]:[13] In return, you also should be expanded. (Yes, I know it’s like I’m talking to children.)
[2 Korinthios] [6]:[14] Don’t be teamed together with unbelievers, because how can there be a partnership between obeying and disobeying God, or in other words, how can light socialise with darkness?
[2 Korinthios] [6]:[15] So what harmony can Messiah have with Satan, or what does a believer have in common with an unbeliever?
[2 Korinthios] [6]:[16] What agreement can God’s temple have with idols, because we are the temple of the living God? As God said, ‘I will live with them and I will walk among them. I will be their god and they will be my people.’
[2 Korinthios] [6]:[17] Therefore Yahweh says, ‘Come out from among them and be separate. Touch nothing that’s ceremonially prohibited and then I will accept you.
[2 Korinthios] [6]:[18] I will be a Father for you, and you will be my sons and daughters,’ says Yahweh the all-powerful.

[Galatians] [1]:[2] On behalf of all the believers here, I’m writing to the assemblies of believers in Galatia.
[Galatians] [1]:[3] May you all experience the grace and peace that comes from God the father and our master Yeshua the messiah,
[Galatians] [1]:[4] the one who gave himself for our sins to rescue us from this present, evil age, according to God our father’s desire—
[Galatians] [1]:[5] our father who’ll be praised even through future ages. That’s how it is.
[Galatians] [1]:[6] I’m astounded that you people have so quickly replaced the good message that you heard from the one who called you to the messiah’s grace. You’ve replaced it with another narrative
[Galatians] [1]:[7] which is not at all another good message, but rather comes from those who are confusing you and wanting to alter the actual good message about the messiah.
[Galatians] [1]:[8] Even if either we ourselves or even a messenger from heaven were to preach a different ‘good message’ which disagrees with the good message that we first preached to you, then they should be cursed.
[Galatians] [1]:[9] As we’ve previously said, and even now say it again: if anyone preaches a ‘good message’ to you that’s different from what you already heard, let that person be cursed.
[Galatians] [1]:[10] Am I trying to please and persuade people or God? If I was still trying to please people, I wouldn’t be worthy to be one of the messiah’s slaves.
[Galatians] [1]:[11] I’m letting you know, brothers and sisters, that the good message I proclaimed didn’t just come from human ideas.
[Galatians] [1]:[12] It didn’t come from my ideas, nor was I taught it by some other person, but it was revealed to me by Yeshua (Jesus; Grk. Yesus) the messiah.
[Galatians] [1]:[13] Brothers and sisters, you’ve heard about my previous behaviour, when as a strict Yehudi (Jew), I was extreme in persecuting the assembly of God’s people, and was trying to destroy them.
[Galatians] [1]:[14] I was progressing in Youdaismos quicker than many of my contemporaries, being so much more zealous in observing our ancient traditions.
[Galatians] [1]:[15] But God, who’d planned this from even before I was born, called me, because of his grace,
[Galatians] [1]:[16] so that he could reveal his son through me, and I could preach the good message to non-Jews. I didn’t rush to get advice from others,
[Galatians] [1]:[17] nor did I head to Yerushalem (Jerusalem) to consult with the ambassadors there that preceded me, but I went away to Arav and then later returned to Damesek (Damascus).
[Galatians] [1]:[18] Then finally, after three years, I went to Yerushalem to get to know Kefa (Peter; Grk. Petros), and stayed with him for just over two weeks.

[2 Thessalonikai] [1]:[1] This letter is from Paulos, Silas, and Timotheos. It’s written to the assembly of believers in God our father and the master Yeshua (Jesus; Grk. Yesus) Messiah there in Thessalonikai.
[2 Thessalonikai] [1]:[2] May God our father and the master Yeshua Messiah give grace and peace to all of you.
[2 Thessalonikai] [1]:[3] We should be always thanking God for you brothers and sisters, and it’s right that we do, because your faith is growing and you all display plenty of love towards each other.
[2 Thessalonikai] [1]:[4] That’s why we boast about you all in God’s assemblies, because of your endurance and faith despite the persecutions you encounter and the tribulations that you put up with.
[2 Thessalonikai] [1]:[5] This shows God’s righteous judgement in that you’re considered worthy to enter God’s kingdom because of what you’ve had to suffer.
[2 Thessalonikai] [1]:[6] God is righteous, and he’s the one who will repay those who oppress you and make life difficult for you all,
[2 Thessalonikai] [1]:[7] then all of you who’ve been oppressed will be able to relax when the master Yeshua (Jesus; Grk. Yesus) comes back from heaven with his powerful army.
[2 Thessalonikai] [1]:[8] With a fiery flame he’ll judge those who don’t know God and those who haven’t accepted the good message of our master Yeshua Messiah.
[2 Thessalonikai] [1]:[9] They’ll be sentenced to eternal destruction—banished from Yahweh’s presence and from the display of his strength
[2 Thessalonikai] [1]:[10] when he’s honoured by his righteous followers and admired by those who believe in him just as you believed our testimony to all of you.
[2 Thessalonikai] [1]:[11] We’re also praying all the time for you all that you’ll be considered worthy of our god’s calling and will live out your good intentions and demonstrate your faith with power,
[2 Thessalonikai] [1]:[12] so that the reputation of our master Yeshua will be honoured in you all, and you in him, thanks to the grace of our God and of the master Yeshua Messiah.
[2 Thessalonikai] [2]:[1] Now concerning the return of our master Yeshua (Jesus; Grk. Yesus) Messiah and our being gathered together with him, we are asking you all, brothers and sisters,
[2 Thessalonikai] [2]:[2] to not be alarmed or have your thinking jolted back-and-forth by any ‘spirit’ or message or letter that seems to come from us that tries to say that the master has already returned.

[2 Thessalonikai] [2]:[4] who opposes every god or object of worship and puts himself above them all—seating himself in God’s temple and (supposedly) demonstrating that he is God.
[2 Thessalonikai] [2]:[5] Don’t you remember how I told you people this when I was still with you?
[2 Thessalonikai] [2]:[6] Now you know what’s restraining him so that he’ll be revealed at the proper time,
[2 Thessalonikai] [2]:[7] because the mystery of lawlessness is already at work, except that it’s being restrained until he’s taken out of the middle,
[2 Thessalonikai] [2]:[8] and then the lawless man will be revealed. The master Yeshua will kill him with his breath and neutralise him with the appearance of his coming.
[2 Thessalonikai] [2]:[9] The lawless man was coming and working under Satan with his power and signs and false miracles
[2 Thessalonikai] [2]:[10] and with every unrighteous seduction. These deceive those who are perishing, because they never had the love for the truth that could have saved them.
[2 Thessalonikai] [2]:[11] That’s why God is sending deceptive practices to them, so that they can continue to believe in the falsehood,
[2 Thessalonikai] [2]:[12] so that all of those who didn’t believe in the truth, but took pleasure in wicked actions, will be judged and sentenced.
[2 Thessalonikai] [2]:[13] But brothers and sisters, we here should always be thanking God for you who were loved by Yahweh. From the beginning God chose you for salvation in the holiness of the spirit and faith in the truth
[2 Thessalonikai] [2]:[14] which he called you to. That was through the good message that we brought so that you might obtain the power that comes from our master Yeshua (Jesus; Grk. Yesus) Messiah.
[2 Thessalonikai] [2]:[15] So as a result, brothers and sisters, stand firm and keep hold of the practices that we taught you—whether it was spoken or written in our letters.
[2 Thessalonikai] [2]:[16] May our master Messiah Yeshua and God our father who loved us and gives us eternal comfort, and by his grace gives good hope,
[2 Thessalonikai] [2]:[17] comfort your minds and strengthen you all in everything you do and every good message you share.

[2 Thessalonikai] [3]:[2] and so that we might escape from the schemes of perverse and evil people, because not everyone believes this message.
[2 Thessalonikai] [3]:[3] But the master is faithful and will strengthen you all and will keep you from the evil one.

[1 Timotheos] [1]:[5] The outcome of such teaching should be demonstrating love coming from a pure heart, a clean conscience, and selfless faith.

[1 Timotheos] [1]:[7] they want to be religious teachers but they don’t understand what they’re talking about or what they’re agreeing to.
[1 Timotheos] [1]:[8] But we know that the religious law can be good if someone is using it lawfully,
[1 Timotheos] [1]:[9] but other than that, we know that the law isn’t made for those who’ve been forgiven by God. The law was made for those who are disobedient and out of control, those who ignore and disobey God, who don’t honour him but rather profane him, for those who would murder their parents or other people,
