[Ivrim] [4]:[8] Because if Yehoshua (Joshua) had given them rest, God wouldn’t be speaking afterwards about another day.
[Ivrim] [4]:[9] So then, a time of rest is being retained for God’s people,
[Ivrim] [4]:[10] because anyone having come into their rest, also rests from their works, just as God rested from his own works.
[Ivrim] [4]:[11] Therefore we should be earnest about entering that rest, in case someone else falls by following our example of disbelief,
[Ivrim] [4]:[12] because God’s message is living and active and sharper than any high-quality sword, even penetrating to divide the soul and spirit—like separating the bone from sinews—and able to judge a person’s inner thoughts and intentions.
[Ivrim] [4]:[13] There isn’t anything in all of creation that’s hidden from him, but everything is naked and exposed to his sight as he’s the one we have to give an account to.
[Ivrim] [4]:[14] So then, having Yeshua (Jesus; Grk. Yesus) the son of God who came from and returned to the heavens as our high priest, we need to hold firmly to what we say we believe,
[Ivrim] [4]:[15] because we don’t have a high priest who’s not able to sympathise with our weakness, but rather who’s been tempted just like we are, yet he didn’t sin.
[Ivrim] [4]:[16] Therefore we can boldly approach the throne of grace to receive mercy and find grace to help us when we need it.
[Ivrim] [5]:[1] Every high priest is just a person who was selected from the people to work with godly things both by offering gifts to God and sacrificing because of our sins.
[Ivrim] [5]:[2] He’s able to be patient with those who don’t understand and stray from the truth because he also is subject to weakness
[Ivrim] [5]:[3] and because of that, he has to make offerings for his own sins as well as for the people.
[Ivrim] [5]:[4] No one takes that honour onto themself, but they’re called by God like just Aharon (Aaron) was.
[Ivrim] [5]:[5] Similarly the messiah didn’t take the honour of being chief priest onto himself, but the one who spoke to him said: ‘You’re my son; today I have given birth to you.’
[Ivrim] [5]:[6] And in another place he said: ‘You are a priest of the order of Malki-Tsedek (Melchizedek).’
[Ivrim] [5]:[7] During the time when Yeshua (Jesus; Grk. Yesus) lived in a human body, he offered up prayers and petitions with a mighty clamour and tears to the one who was able to save him from death, and he was heard because of his reverence.
[Ivrim] [5]:[8] Although he was a son, he learnt obedience from what he suffered
[Ivrim] [5]:[9] and once he became perfect, he became the source of eternal salvation to all those who submitted to him
[Ivrim] [5]:[10] as he’d been designated by God as the high priest according to the order of Malki-Tsedek.
[Ivrim] [5]:[11] We have a lot to say about that, but it’s hard to explain because you’ve all become lazy at listening.
[Ivrim] [5]:[12] Yes, because you all ought to be teachers by now, yet you still need to have someone teaching you the basics of God’s ways and you’ve become like those who need milk instead of solid food.
[Ivrim] [5]:[13] Everyone who drinks milk doesn’t really understand the message about righteousness, because they’re still infants,
[Ivrim] [5]:[14] but mature people have solid food meaning that their senses have been trained and they can distinguish good from evil.
[Ivrim] [6]:[1] So then, having left the basics of the messiah’s message, we should move on towards maturity—not repeating the foundations of repenting from useless religious actions and faith in God,
[Ivrim] [6]:[2] of teachings about immersion in water and prayerfully placing your hands on people, and the resurrection of the dead followed by eternal judgement.
[Ivrim] [6]:[3] And we’ll be moving on from all that if God permits.
[Ivrim] [6]:[4] It’s impossible for those who’ve understood this and who’ve tasted the heavenly gift and become partakers of the holy spirit
[Ivrim] [6]:[5] and who’ve tasted God’s message and the powers of the coming age
[Ivrim] [6]:[6] and who’ve fallen away, to be brought back to repentance. It’s like they themselves are executing God’s son again and publicly shaming him.
[Ivrim] [6]:[7] The land that soaks in the frequent rains and grows crops suitable for those who are cultivating it, is receiving a blessing from God,
[Ivrim] [6]:[8] but if it’s producing thorns and thistles, then it’s useless and a liability and will end up being burnt off.
[Ivrim] [6]:[9] But dear friends, even though we speak like this, we’ve been convinced to expect better things from you—things that accompany salvation.
[Ivrim] [6]:[10] Yes, God isn’t unjust such that he’d forget about your work and the love that you all displayed towards him, having ministered to other believers as you still do.
[Ivrim] [6]:[11] And our desire is for each of you to be displaying the same earnestness and the full assurance of hope until the end
[Ivrim] [6]:[12] so that you all won’t become sluggish, but become imitators of those who through their faith and patience will be inheriting what God has promised.
[Ivrim] [6]:[13] When God made promises to Avraham, because he didn’t have anyone more powerful to take an oath in front of, he did it in his own name
[Ivrim] [6]:[14] saying: ‘I will certainly bless you and will cause you to have many descendants.’
[Ivrim] [6]:[15] And then after being patient, Avraham received what was promised.
[Ivrim] [6]:[16] Yes, people make oaths in front of someone more powerful and then there’s no controversy, because the oath is the confirmation.
[Ivrim] [6]:[17] In order for God to make the unchanging nature of his purpose very clear to the heirs of what was promised, he guaranteed it with an oath
[Ivrim] [6]:[18] so that by two things that God can’t even change (his promise and his oath), we who have fled to him for refuge can have great confidence as we hold to the hope that lies before us.
[Ivrim] [6]:[19] That hope is an anchor for our souls, being both certain and confirmed, and it will bring us inside the temple curtain
[Ivrim] [6]:[20] where Yeshua (Jesus; Grk. Yesus) went ahead of us according to the order of Malki-Tsedek (Melchizedek)—becoming the high priest for this age.
[Ivrim] [7]:[1] This Malki-Tsedek (Melchizedek) was the king of the city of Shalem and a priest of God, the highest one. He met Avraham who was returning from slaughtering several kings and Malki-Tsedek blessed him,
[Ivrim] [7]:[2] and Avraham gave him a tenth of all the captured goods. The name Malki-Tsedek means ‘king of righteousness’ and then king of Shalem also means ‘king of peace’.
[Ivrim] [7]:[3] There’s no record of his father or mother, no genealogical background, and no record of his being born or dying, but he’s likened to God’s son in that he continually remains as a priest.
[Ivrim] [7]:[4] Notice how great this Malki-Tsedek was, because the patriarch Avraham gave him a tenth of the best of the captured goods.
[Ivrim] [7]:[5] On one hand, the tithing command from Mosheh’s (Moses) law makes the people give a tenth to Levi’s descendants who inherit the priestly office, even though they’re their brothers as fellow descendants of Avraham.
[Ivrim] [7]:[6] On the other hand, Avraham tithed to Malki-Tsedek who can’t be traced as one of them, and he blessed Avraham who had received God’s promises.
[Ivrim] [7]:[7] There’s no doubt that it’s the lessor person that gets blessed by someone greater.
[Ivrim] [7]:[8] So in the first case, the tenth is received by people who die, but in the second case by someone who it’s only testified that he lives.
[Ivrim] [7]:[9] You could even say that even Levi (whose descendants receive the tenths) gave a tenth to Malki-Tsedek through Avraham
[Ivrim] [7]:[10] because Levi’s sperm was still part of his father’s body when Malki-Tsedek met Avraham.
[Ivrim] [7]:[11] Indeed if perfection came from the priesthood from Levi’s tribe which was legislated to help the people, why would there have still been a need for another to rise up as a priest in the order of Malki-Tsedek (Melchizedek) and not just from the order of Aharon (Aaron)?
[Ivrim] [7]:[12] Because if the priesthood is changed, then that law would also need to be changed.
[Ivrim] [7]:[13] The one that we’re talking about here is from another tribe, and no one from that tribe has ever served as a priest at the altar.
[Ivrim] [7]:[14] So it’s quite evident that our master came from Yehudah’s (Judah) tribe but Mosheh (Moses) never mentioned priests coming from that tribe,
[Ivrim] [7]:[15] and it’s even more clear if another priest like Malki-Tsedek rose up
[Ivrim] [7]:[16] who didn’t live by the physical law (of death) but according to the power of indestructible life!
[Ivrim] [7]:[17] Because it’s been testified: ‘You are priest to this age, according to the order of Malki-Tsedek.’
[Ivrim] [7]:[18] In the first case, the command is annulled because it’s weak and unprofitable
[Ivrim] [7]:[19] (because the law made nothing perfect), and in the second case we have the introduction of a better hope by means of which we can approach God.
[Ivrim] [7]:[20] And it wasn’t done without an oath, because although men become priests without an oath,
[Ivrim] [7]:[21] but Yeshua (Jesus; Grk. Yesus) became a priest by an oath from the one that said: ‘Yahweh made an oath and won’t rescind it. You are priest for this age.’
[Ivrim] [7]:[22] Because of that oath, Yeshua became the guarantor of a better agreement.
[Ivrim] [7]:[23] in the first case, there have been many of those priests because death doesn’t allow them to continue on,
[Ivrim] [7]:[24] but in the second case, because Yeshua stays alive for all the age, he can hold the office of priest permanently
[Ivrim] [7]:[25] and thus he’s able to save those who approach God through him—save them to the full extent because he always lives to intercede of their behalf.
[Ivrim] [7]:[26] Such a high priest exactly meets our needs: one who is godly, innocent, pure, set apart from sinners, and honoured above the heavens.
[Ivrim] [7]:[27] Unlike the other high priests, it’s not necessary for him to first make a sacrifice for his own sins before doing it for the sins of the people, because he offered himself—once for everyone.
[Ivrim] [7]:[28] The law appoints those with weaknesses as high priests, but the message from the oath which followed after the law, appointed the son who has been perfected for the age.
[Ivrim] [8]:[1] So here’s the main point in what we’re saying: we have a high priest who sat down in the honoured seat beside the majesty’s throne in the heavens
[Ivrim] [8]:[2] and ministers in the holy places and in the true tent of worship which Yahweh set up, not people.
[Ivrim] [8]:[3] Every high priest is appointed to be offering both gifts and sacrifices, and so it’s necessary for this one to also have something to offer.
[Ivrim] [8]:[4] If he was here on earth, he wouldn’t even be a priest because there are others offering gifts according to Mosheh’s (Moses) law.
[Ivrim] [8]:[5] They serve a copy or shadow of the heavenly realms just as Mosheh was warned when he was about to start making the tent of worship: ‘Make everything according to the pattern that I showed you on the mountain.’
[Ivrim] [8]:[6] But on the contrary, Yeshua (Jesus; Grk. Yesus) has obtained a more special ministry because he’s the mediator of a better agreement which has been legislated with better promises.
[Ivrim] [8]:[7] If the first agreement had been faultless, then there wouldn’t have been any need to find a second one to replace it,
[Ivrim] [8]:[8] but God blamed the people and said: “Listen, Yahweh declares that the time is coming when I will make a new agreement with Yisrael (Israel) and Yehudah (Judah),
[Ivrim] [8]:[9] not like the agreement that I made with their ancestors when they held my hand for me to lead them out of Mitsrayim (Egypt), because they didn’t stay inside my agreement and so I didn’t take any notice of them, says Yahweh.’
[Ivrim] [8]:[10] So this is the agreement that I make with Yisrael after those times, says Yahweh, putting my laws into their minds and writing them onto their hearts, and I will be their God and they will be my people.
[Ivrim] [8]:[11] Then they certainly won’t teach each citizen and their neighbours, saying ‘Know Yahweh,’ because all of them from the smallest to the greatest will all know me.
[Ivrim] [8]:[12] Because I’ll be merciful to them when they disobey, and certainly I won’t remember their sins any longer.”
[Ivrim] [8]:[13] In calling that ‘new’, he’s made the first agreement out-of-date, and what’s out-of-date and getting old is about to disappear.
[Ivrim] [9]:[1] The first agreement had sacred rites and a holy place here on earth,
[Ivrim] [9]:[2] because the tent of worship was set up with a outer room called ‘the holy place’ where both the lampstand and the table were placed and the ‘bread of the presence’.
[Ivrim] [9]:[3] Then past the second curtain was a room called ‘the most holy place’
[Ivrim] [9]:[4] having the golden incense altar and the box of the agreement which was completely gold-plated and which contained a golden jar of manna and Aharon’s (Aaron) staff which had sprouted and the stone tablets inscribed with the commands.
[Ivrim] [9]:[5] On the top of the box were the cherubs OF GLORY with their wings stretched out over the mercy seat which we won’t talk about right now.
[Ivrim] [9]:[6] And then with all of that having been prepared, the priests entered past everything in the first room of the tent to carry out their sacred services.
[Ivrim] [9]:[7] However, only the high priest enters the second room, and then only once a year. He can’t go with taking in blood which he offers for the sins of ignorance done by both himself and by the people.
[Ivrim] [9]:[8] By that, the holy spirit was making it clear that the way into that holy place was not yet open to the public as long as that first tent of worship was still standing.
[Ivrim] [9]:[9] This was an illustration intended for the present time when gifts and sacrifices are still being offered, but are not able to make the conscience of the one serving perfect—
[Ivrim] [9]:[10] only just physical matters of food and drinks and ritual washings—until the reformed system is instigated.
[Ivrim] [9]:[11] But when Messiah came as high priest over what had now become good through the greater and more perfect tent of worship which wasn’t put together by people and isn’t part of this world,
[Ivrim] [9]:[12] he went once-for-all into the holy places—not by the blood of goats and calves but through his own blood—obtaining eternal redemption for us.
[Ivrim] [9]:[13] Because if the blood of goats and bulls, and the sprinkling of defiled people with the ashes of a young cow could make them holy by physical purification,
[Ivrim] [9]:[14] how much more the blood of the messiah who offered himself blameless to God, through the eternal spirit, will then purify your conscience from all useless activities in order that we can serve the living God!
[Ivrim] [9]:[15] So because of that, Yeshua (Jesus; Grk. Yesus) is the mediator of a new agreement, so that his death leads to the ransom payment for those who’ve disobeyed the first agreement, so that now those who are called can receive the eternal inheritance.
[Ivrim] [9]:[16] Where there’s an agreement like a will, it’s necessary for the death of the one who made it,
[Ivrim] [9]:[17] because this type of agreement doesn’t come into effect if the person who made it is still living, but only when they’re confirmed as dead,
[Ivrim] [9]:[18] so even the first agreement wasn’t valid without blood.
[Ivrim] [9]:[19] Hence after telling all the people all the commands according to the law, Mosheh (Moses) then took the blood of calves and goats, along with water and scarlet wool, and hyssop branches, and sprinkled both the scroll and all the people
[Ivrim] [9]:[20] saying: ‘This is the blood of the agreement which God commanded for you all.’
[Ivrim] [9]:[21] Similarly, he sprinkled both the tent itself and all the utensils for the ministry there with blood,
[Ivrim] [9]:[22] and almost everything was declared ‘clean’ according to the law, because there couldn’t be forgiveness without blood.
[Ivrim] [9]:[23] So then it was necessary for these copies of things from the heavens to be purified, but in contrast, the heavenly things will be purified with better sacrifices than that,
[Ivrim] [9]:[24] because Messiah didn’t enter human-made holy places that were only representatives of the true ones, but he entered into heaven where he now appears on our behalf in God’s presence.
[Ivrim] [9]:[25] He didn’t offer himself like the high priest does every year with different blood,
[Ivrim] [9]:[26] otherwise he would have needed to suffer over and over since the creation of the world. Instead he appeared just once throughout all the ages because sin has been annulled by his sacrifice.
[Ivrim] [9]:[27] Just as it’s been determined that people will die once and then there’ll be judgement,
[Ivrim] [9]:[28] so too the messiah was offered once as a sacrifice as an offering for the sins of many people, but will be seen a second time (nothing to do with sin) by those who are eagerly waiting for him.
[Ivrim] [10]:[1] The law is a shadow of the good things coming, not the exact image of them. Every year they offer the same sacrifices—over and over but never getting nearer to perfection,
[Ivrim] [10]:[2] otherwise they could have stopped offering them because once they were fully ‘clean’, they wouldn’t have needed anymore sacrifices to appease the conscience of their sins.
[Ivrim] [10]:[3] But as it is, every year there’s a reminder about their sins
[Ivrim] [10]:[4] because it’s simply not possible for the blood of goats and bulls to take away sins.
[Ivrim] [10]:[5] That’s why when Yeshua (Jesus; Grk. Yesus) came into the world, he said: “You don’t want sacrifice and offering, but you prepared a body for me.
[Ivrim] [10]:[6] You took no pleasure in whole burnt offerings and sacrifices for sin.
[Ivrim] [10]:[7] Then I said, ‘Listen, it’s been written about me in the scroll of the scriptures. I have come, God, to do whatever you want.’ ”
[Ivrim] [10]:[8] Previously he had said, ‘You don’t want sacrifices and offerings and burnt offerings and offerings for sin, and you didn’t take pleasure in them,’ even though they’re offered according to the law.
[Ivrim] [10]:[9] Then he said, ‘Listen, I’m coming to do whatever you want.’ So he was terminating the first agreement in order to be able to establish the second one.
[Ivrim] [10]:[10] By that agreement, we are made holy once-and-for-all through the offering of Yeshua (Jesus; Grk. Yesus) Messiah’s body.
[Ivrim] [10]:[11] In fact, every priest has stood there every day ministering and often offering the same sacrifices, all of which have never been able to remove sins,
[Ivrim] [10]:[12] but this one offered one sacrifice for sins for all time, then sat down on God’s right
[Ivrim] [10]:[13] waiting even now until his enemies are overcome
[Ivrim] [10]:[14] Yes, with one sacrifice, he’s able to make people holy for all time.
[Ivrim] [10]:[15] The holy spirit also testifies to us, having said:
[Ivrim] [10]:[16] ‘Yahweh says: This is the agreement that I will make with them: I will put my laws into their hearts and also I will write them into their minds.’
[Ivrim] [10]:[17] And, ‘I won’t remember their disobedience and their lawlessness any more.’
[Ivrim] [10]:[18] Once there’s been forgiveness, then there’s no longer a need for an offering for sin.
[Ivrim] [10]:[19] Therefore brothers and sisters, we have confidence to enter the holy place by Yeshua’s (Jesus; Grk. Yesus) blood—
[Ivrim] [10]:[20] a new and life-giving path that he initiated for us to go through the curtain, which is his flesh.
[Ivrim] [10]:[21] Since we have an incredible priest presiding over God’s house,
[Ivrim] [10]:[22] we can approach God with sincere hearts in full assurance due to our faith, having our hearts sprinkled to clean us from our guilty consciences and with our bodies having been washed in clean water.
[Ivrim] [10]:[23] We can hold onto the confession of our unwavering hope because the one who made the promise is faithful,
[Ivrim] [10]:[24] and we can be considering how to provoke each other to show love and to do good things—
[Ivrim] [10]:[25] not giving up meeting together as some have, but rather encouraging each other even more as you all see the day of judgement coming closer.
[Ivrim] [10]:[26] If we keep on sinning after learning about the truth, then there’s no sacrifice left for our sins,
[Ivrim] [10]:[27] but the certain expectation of fearful judgement and of a fiery anger that will consume the god-haters.

[Ivrim] [10]:[29] so how much more severe punishment do you all expect might be considered appropriate for someone who trampled God’s son underfoot and who has considered the blood of the agreement as cheap and who has insulted the spirit of grace?
[Ivrim] [10]:[30] Yes, we know who said, ‘Vengeance is mine—I’m the one who’ll repay them,’ and again, ‘Yahweh will be judging his people.’
[Ivrim] [10]:[31] It’s a scary thing to fall into the hands of the living God.
[Ivrim] [10]:[32] Remember those earlier days when you first learnt about Messiah and how you endured a lot of suffering—
[Ivrim] [10]:[33] sometimes being publicly displayed with derision and persecution, and at other times helping others who were being treated like that.
[Ivrim] [10]:[34] You all sympathised with those who were imprisoned and cheerfully accepted the confiscation of your possessions because you knew that you have a better possession that will endure on.
[Ivrim] [10]:[35] So then, don’t toss away your boldness, because it’ll lead to a sizeable reward.
[Ivrim] [10]:[36] Rather you need to endure so that when you’ve done what God wants, you’ll all receive back what was promised
[Ivrim] [10]:[37] because: ‘In still a little while the one coming will come, and won’t be delaying.’
[Ivrim] [10]:[38] And: ‘My righteous one will be living by faith. If he retreats, my soul won’t be pleased with him.’
[Ivrim] [10]:[39] But we aren’t from those retreating back to destruction, but from those with faith that preserves the soul.
[Ivrim] [11]:[1] Now faith is the assurance that the things we hope for will come to pass and the conviction that even what we can’t see is real,
[Ivrim] [11]:[2] because those are what our predecessors were commended for.
[Ivrim] [11]:[3] By faith we understand that time was formed by God’s command because the visible universe was not made from visible materials.
[Ivrim] [11]:[4] By faith Hevel (Abel) offered a more satisfactory sacrifice to God than Kayin (Cain), and as a result, he was declared to be righteous when God testified about his gifts, and through his faith, he still speaks despite being long dead.
[Ivrim] [11]:[5] By faith Hanok (Enoch) was transported directly to heaven without dying. ‘His body was never found because God transported him,’ because before he was transported, it was testified that he pleased God,
[Ivrim] [11]:[6] and without faith it’s impossible to please him. Because it’s necessary for anyone who approaches God to believe that he exists, and that he rewards those who search for him.
[Ivrim] [11]:[7] By faith godly Noah built a box to save his family after he was warned about things that had never been seen before, thus condemning the world and becoming an heir of the righteousness that comes by faith.
[Ivrim] [11]:[8] By faith, Avraham submitted when he was called and travelled to the place that he was going to receive as an inheritance—departing without even knowing where he was going.
[Ivrim] [11]:[9] By faith he camped as a stranger in the promised land, living in tents with Yitshak (Isaac) and Ya’akov (Jacob)—fellow heirs of the same promise—
[Ivrim] [11]:[10] because he was waiting for a city with proper foundations—the city with God as its craftsman and builder.
[Ivrim] [11]:[11] By faith even Sarah herself received the power to conceive a child when she was past that age, because she considered that the one who had made the promise would be faithful to his word.
[Ivrim] [11]:[12] So it was that descendants came from that one man in his old age and they became as numerous as the stars in the sky and uncountable like grains of sand on the beach.
[Ivrim] [11]:[13] All of those people went on to die, not having received everything that was promised but only seeing and welcoming it all from a distance, having admitted that they were strangers and foreigners here on the earth.
[Ivrim] [11]:[14] People who talk like that make it clear that they’re looking for a new place to make their home—
[Ivrim] [11]:[15] if they’d been meaning the place that they left, they would have already had time to go back there—
[Ivrim] [11]:[16] so now they’re aspiring to a better place, i.e., a heavenly home. Therefore God isn’t ashamed of them or of being called their god, because he has prepared a city for them.
[Ivrim] [11]:[17] By faith, Avraham when he was tested offered up Yitshak (Isaac). He had received the promises and offered his only son—
[Ivrim] [11]:[18] the one about which it had been said: ‘Your descendants will be named through Yitshak.’
[Ivrim] [11]:[19] Avraham had reckoned that God was powerful enough to bring him back to life from the dead, and in a manner of speaking, that’s what happened.
[Ivrim] [11]:[20] By faith, Yitshak gave a blessing to Ya’akov (Jacob) and Esav (Esau).
[Ivrim] [11]:[21] By faith, when Ya’akov was dying he gave a blessing to both of Yosef’s (Joseph) sons, and bowed over the top of his walking stick.
[Ivrim] [11]:[22] By faith, when Yosef was dying, he spoke about how Yisrael’s (Israel) descendants would leave Mitsrayim (Egypt) in the future, and gave them instructions about taking his bones.
[Ivrim] [11]:[23] By faith when Mosheh (Moses) was born, his parents hid him for three months when they saw how he was such a beautiful baby, and they weren’t afraid to disobey the king’s ruling.
[Ivrim] [11]:[24] By faith when Mosheh had become powerful, he refused to be called Par’oh’s (Pharaoh) daughter’s son
[Ivrim] [11]:[25] and chose to suffer hardship along with God’s people rather than having the temporary enjoyment of sin.
[Ivrim] [11]:[26] He calculated that enduring derision for the messiah was better than the riches of Mitsrayim because he was considering the future reward.
[Ivrim] [11]:[27] By faith, Mosheh wasn’t afraid of the king’s anger when he left Mitsrayim and persevered because he could see what was invisible.
[Ivrim] [11]:[28] By faith, he initiated the Passover Celebration and the sprinkling of blood, so that the one destroying the eldest offspring wouldn’t touch their families.
[Ivrim] [11]:[29] By faith, they crossed through the Red Sea as if it was dry land, but when the Mitsrim (Egyptians) tried they were drowned.
[Ivrim] [11]:[30] By faith, Yeriho’s (Jericho) walls collapsed after they’d walked around them for seven days.
[Ivrim] [11]:[31] By faith, Rahav the prostitute didn’t die along with all the others in the city who mocked God, because she had peacefully accommodated the spies.
[Ivrim] [11]:[32] So what else should I say? I don’t have time to describe Gid’on, Barak, Shimshon (Samson), and Yiftah (Jephthah), and about David and Shmuel (Samuel) and the prophets
[Ivrim] [11]:[33] who by faith conquered kingdoms, acted righteously, obtained promises, shut lion’s mouths,

[Revelation] [21]:[8] But as for the cowardly and the unbelieving, the abhorred and murderers, fornicators and sorcerers, and idolaters and all liars, their place will be in the lake burning with fire and sulfur, which is the second death.”
[Revelation] [21]:[9] Then one of the seven messengers holding the seven bowls full of the seven last disasters came and spoke to me, saying, “Come, I’ll show you the bride—the lamb’s wife.”
[Revelation] [21]:[10] Then in the spirit, he carried me away to a very large, high mountain and he showed me the HOLY city, Yerushalem (Jerusalem), coming down from God out of heaven,
[Revelation] [21]:[11] shining like God’s splendour—its brilliance being like a very precious stone—like a jasper stone shining like crystal.
[Revelation] [21]:[12] The city had wall that was both wide and high, with twelve gates and twelve messengers at the gates. The gates had the names of the twelve tribes (from Yisrael’s (Israel) twelve sons) written on them.
[Revelation] [21]:[13] There were three gates on the east, three on the north, three on the south, and three on the west.
[Revelation] [21]:[14] The city wall had twelve foundation stones, and they had the names of the lamb’s twelve missionaries written on them.
[Revelation] [21]:[15] The messenger speaking to me had a golden measuring rod so that he could measure the city and its gates and wall.
[Revelation] [21]:[16] The city was laid out square with the length equalling the width. Using the rod, the messenger measured the city at 2.2km on each edge, with the length, width, and height all being equal.
[Revelation] [21]:[17] He also measured the wall to be 70m using normal measurements.
[Revelation] [21]:[18] The wall was made of green jasper stone and the city itself was pure gold but as clear as glass.
[Revelation] [21]:[19] The foundations of the city’s wall were adorned with many different kinds of precious stones. The first foundation was jasper, the second sapphire, the third chalcedony, the fourth emerald,
[Revelation] [21]:[20] the fifth sardonyx, the sixth carnelian, the seventh chrysolite, the eighth beryl, the ninth topaz, the tenth chrysoprase, the eleventh jacinth, and the twelfth amethyst.
[Revelation] [21]:[21] The twelve gates were twelve pearls—each one of the gates individually was from one pearl—and the city street was pure gold—transparent like glass.
[Revelation] [21]:[22] I didn’t see any temple in the city because the all-powerful God Yahweh and the lamb are its temple.
[Revelation] [21]:[23] The city doesn’t need the sun or moon to illuminate it because God’s radiance illuminates it, and its lamp is the lamb.
[Revelation] [21]:[24] The nations will be able to walk around from its light, and the kings on the earth will bring their best into the city.
[Revelation] [21]:[25] It’ll never get dark there, so the city gates will never need to be closed
[Revelation] [21]:[26] and they will bring the prestige and the honour of the nations into it.
[Revelation] [21]:[27] However, nothing that’s ‘unclean’ will ever enter the city, and nor will those with shameful or dishonest behaviour—only those whose names have been written in the lamb’s book of life.
[Revelation] [22]:[1] Then he showed me the river of the water of life that sparkled like crystal. It flowed out of the throne of God and the lamb.
[Revelation] [22]:[2] In the middle of its path and in the middle of the river reaching from one side to the other was the tree of life that produces twelve fruits—a different one each month—and the leaves of the tree are for healing the nations
[Revelation] [22]:[3] and there won’t be a curse any more. The throne for God and the lamb will be in the city, and his slaves will be serving him.
[Revelation] [22]:[4] They will see his face, and his name on their foreheads.
[Revelation] [22]:[5] Nights won’t exist any more and they won’t need the light from a lamp or from the sun because Yahweh God will illuminate them, and they will reign through the ages.
[Revelation] [22]:[6] Then he said to me, “These messages are faithful and true, and Yahweh, the God of the spirits of the prophets, sent his messenger out to show his slaves what’s planned to happen soon.”
[Revelation] [22]:[7] “Yes, listen, I’m coming soon. Anyone who follows the messages of the prophecy on this scroll will be blessed.”
[Revelation] [22]:[8] I, Yohan (John; Grk. Yoannes), am the one who saw and heard all those things, and when I heard and saw them, I knelt down to worship at the feet of the messenger who showed them to me.
[Revelation] [22]:[9] But he told me, Hey, no! I’m a fellow slave of you and of your brothers the prophets and of the ones who obey the words of this book. Worship God.”
[Revelation] [22]:[10] Then he continued, “Don’t seal up the words of the prophecy of this book, because the time is near.
[Revelation] [22]:[11] Those who disobey God can continue to do so and those who are filthy can continue to be so, but those who obey God should continue to obey, and those who are godly should continue to be godly.”
[Revelation] [22]:[12] (Yeshua (Jesus; Grk. Yesus) says,) “Listen, I’m coming back soon, bringing my reward to distribute to each person according to their behaviour.
[Revelation] [22]:[13] I’m the A and the Z—the first and the last—the beginning and the end.
[Revelation] [22]:[14] “Blessed are those who are washing their robes so that they’ll have authority over the tree of life (MEANING???) and so that they’ll be able to enter the city through the gates.
[Revelation] [22]:[15] On the contrary, those outside the city are dogs and sorcerers, the sexually immoral and murderers and idolaters, and everyone loving and exhibiting dishonesty.
[Revelation] [22]:[16] “I, Yeshua, have sent my messenger to explain these things to you concerning the churches. I am both David’s source and his descendant—the bright morning star.”
[Revelation] [22]:[17] The spirit and the bride say, ‘Come.’ Anyone who hears this should also say, ‘Come.’ Anyone who’s thirsty to live forever should come. Anyone who wants it can take the water that gives life free of charge.
[Revelation] [22]:[18] I am testifying to everyone who hears the prophecies written in this document: If anyone adds to these words, then God will add to them the disasters written in this document.
[Revelation] [22]:[19] And if anyone takes away any of this prophetic document, then God will take away their share in the tree of life and in the holy city that’s written about in this document.
